lessons.title: Drilling well control — role and equipment lessons
lessons.body:
# Drilling well control — role and equipment lessons

VUC007. These four lessons extend the embedded eighteen-chapter foundation. All cases are original and fictional. Use paper or configured simulators, never live well controls. The course awards only the specified VNDRLY learning record after actual assessment; it is not an IWCF certificate.

lessons.title: R19 — Read the equipment drawing before trusting a control label
lessons.body:
## R19 — Read the equipment drawing before trusting a control label

The first task is to identify what each component can do in the present geometry. An annular sealing element and a ram assembly are different mechanisms. A pipe ram must suit its specified tubular geometry; a blind closure cannot be assumed usable across an occupied bore. Shearing capability and subsequent sealing depend on the installed design and the object at the cutting position. The manufacturer's documentation supplies these capabilities. A generic BOP name does not.

SLB's [BOP explanation](https://www.slb.com/-/media/files/oilfield-review/defining-bops.ashx) describes annular and ram mechanisms. Use it to understand function, then use the actual equipment specification for limits. Do not infer that an annular element seals every possible shape, that every shear cuts every tool, or that a component's successful movement proves pressure sealing.

### Original functional drawing

```text
                      tubular through bore
                               |
                     sealing function A
                               |
                     sealing function B ---- controlled outlet C
                               |                     |
                     isolation function D     flow restriction E
                               |                     |
                          well source          processing route F

                  hydraulic supply H --> controls A/B/D
                  position feedback J <-- controlled functions
```

This is a functional model, not a recommended stack order. Learners trace the pressure path from the source to every exposed outlet. H supplies actuation energy; J supplies an indication. Neither is a pressure barrier merely because it appears on the drawing. F must be available and suitable for the expected stream before a controlled-flow plan can rely on it.

**Worked case:** B is verified for a 5-inch pipe body. The position record places a 6.5-inch tool joint at B, with no qualified tool-joint sealing capability supplied. A command to close B cannot create that missing capability. The learner identifies the conflict and uses the configured contingency, preserving the correct containment state. Moving the string without assessing the movement's pressure and load consequences is not an acceptable improvised cure.

### Gauges, valves and flow direction

A pressure gauge measures at its communicating point. An isolated or blocked gauge can display a value unrelated to the volume about to be opened. Trace its connection on the drawing. For any controlled flow, distinguish the upstream pressure-containing path, restriction and downstream handling. A hose downstream of a restriction may see a different pressure during normal flow than during a blockage or lineup change. The approved envelope must consider credible states, not just normal operation.

**Practice:** C's position indicator shows CLOSED, but the test evidence does not identify the current assembly and a bypass around C is open. Identify two independent defects. **Answer:** closure indication is not applicable sealing evidence, and the bypass defeats the assumed isolated route. Correcting one does not resolve the other. Draw the bypass and record both issues.

### Drillstring internal controls

The bore inside the drillstring is a separate path from the annulus. An outside seal does not close the inside bore. Appropriate internal control tools must match the connection, pressure/flow envelope and approved installation/use method. A tool stored nearby is not proof it can be deployed under the present condition. Preparation includes access, compatibility, role assignment and the approved contingency. Do not attempt an improvised installation against uncontrolled flow.

**Practice:** the crew has the correct outside sealing element but an incompatible internal safety tool. **Answer:** both flow paths must be addressed; a correct outside barrier cannot compensate for an unmanageable internal path. Resolve compatibility before crediting readiness.

lessons.title: R20 — Casing and cementing change the well-control problem
lessons.body:
## R20 — Casing and cementing change the well-control problem

Running casing changes displacement, flow area and the geometry that pressure-control equipment must accommodate. The crew must know the actual casing size, connections, running tools and available sealing arrangements. A control configured for drillpipe is not automatically suitable for casing or a running assembly. The fluid system must account for displacement, filling and returns throughout movement.

### Worked volume and pressure case

The exercise supplies an approved closed-end displacement of 0.012 bbl/ft for a fictional assembly. Running 300 ft displaces 3.6 bbl. The measured return is 5.1 bbl and no transfer is logged. The 1.5 bbl discrepancy requires the prescribed response and investigation. It does not establish the cause by itself. Do not label it “normal casing displacement” without reconciling the supplied expectation and actual observations.

A different exercise uses 4,000 vertical feet of 10 ppg liquid above 1,000 vertical feet of 14 ppg slurry. Under the explicit static liquid-column assumption, head is 0.052 × (10 × 4,000 + 14 × 1,000) = **2,808 psi**. A single 10 ppg assumption would give 2,600 psi and miss 208 psi. During actual placement, moving interfaces, friction, losses and changing material properties make the pressure profile time-dependent. The worksheet is not a cementing design.

### Float equipment and confirmation

Float equipment provides a specified check function intended to limit reverse flow after displacement. The [SLB float-collar definition](https://glossary.slb.com/en/terms/f/float_collar) explains that function. Presence of a float collar is not proof of its condition or successful operation. If observations suggest reverse flow or an unexpected pressure change, preserve the evidence and follow the approved contingency rather than assuming the valve must be working.

**Original case:** the planned displacement finishes, but the measured returned volume differs from the worksheet. Someone proposes changing the recorded strokes to match the intended total. That would conceal the actual evidence. Record actual delivered and returned volumes, the discrepancy, pressure history and response. Establish what the evidence supports about placement and containment before accepting the job.

### Material transition and the barrier claim

Cement slurry changes as it sets. Its contribution cannot always be treated as a static liquid head throughout that transition. BSEE's [bottom-hole pressure research](https://www.bsee.gov/sites/bsee.gov/files/tap-technical-assessment-program/008ca.pdf) discusses pressure behavior during cement setting. A completed pumping action is not proof of the intended permanent barrier. The approved program supplies waiting, monitoring and verification criteria applicable to the actual material and well.

**Practice:** a coworker says, “We pumped the correct amount, so the barrier is proven.” **Answer:** amount is one piece of evidence. Placement, condition, isolation and required verification remain distinct. The correct closeout records those results rather than substituting elapsed time or a signature.

lessons.title: R21 — The observer, operator and supervisor have different jobs
lessons.body:
## R21 — The observer, operator and supervisor have different jobs

A field-team learner must recognize meaningful evidence, report it promptly and remain within the assigned role. An operator must additionally use the configured response, monitor the actual result and transfer accurate information. A supervisor must evaluate the operating envelope, direct the team, interpret deviations and decide whether the next phase is justified. Titles do not supply competence; the assessment must observe the relevant behavior.

### One event, three role responses

The fictional log shows a sudden drilling-rate change, a return-flow increase and an unexplained active-volume gain. The field-team observer reports the well, time, readings and activity without waiting to prove the mechanism. The operator applies the supplied detection/response procedure and confirms the indicated equipment state. The supervisor checks the reliable shut-in data and the available pressure/volume model before authorizing the next operation. All three preserve uncertainty; none should invent a stabilized pressure simply because the form has an empty box.

**Weak observer response:** “The well is kicking because the tank looks high.” It blends an observation with a diagnosis. **Improved response:** “At 10:14 the active volume increased by the measured amount shown in the log while no transfer was authorized; return flow also increased. I reported the discrepancy and the operator is executing the response procedure.” The message gives usable evidence and action without overstating the cause.

### Operator handover

The operator hands over the current configuration, actual indications, readings with times/units, string position, volume account, actions taken, pending commands and unresolved issues. A requested closure must not be reported as verified isolation until its required verification exists. The supervisor repeats the controlling restrictions so both parties share the same state.

**Practice:** a close command was sent, its position indicator is pending and a pressure trend is still changing. Write the handover. **Model:** “Close commanded at the recorded time; position not yet confirmed. Readings are changing and not accepted as stabilized. Current restrictions remain. Verification/contingency is in progress under the supplied procedure.”

### Supervisor decisions and instructions

Before directing a modeled circulation, state its objective, limits, rate reference, pressure reference, volume checkpoints, communication responsibilities and deviation response. A good instruction is specific enough to be checked. “Keep it safe” is not a control instruction. The operator repeats the instruction; the supervisor tracks the achieved state and any delay rather than assuming instant response.

**Original simulator case:** the approved classroom schedule gives target 520 psi at the current step. The observed value is 590 psi and the model's tolerance is ±10 psi. The supervisor must identify the unexplained mismatch and call the model's hold/verification response. They must not invent a diagnosis or instruct repeated corrections without understanding the resulting pressure distribution. The assessor changes roles on a fresh attempt so memorizing a sentence cannot conceal misunderstanding.

The real equipment's procedure defines the actual control movements. This material teaches the required decision, evidence and communication and supplies independent simulation tasks; it does not invent a universal valve sequence.

lessons.title: R22 — Surface and subsea cases must preserve their different reference points
lessons.body:
## R22 — Surface and subsea cases must preserve their different reference points

A surface pressure reading is not automatically the pressure at a subsea wellhead or at a formation. Hydrostatic contributions, line friction and the locations of restrictions matter. Mark the reference datum on the schematic and calculation sheet. Distinguish the water column outside equipment from the drilling fluid inside the connected flow path; they do not have the same density or necessarily serve the same function.

### Original depth-reference exercise

The model supplies a formation 8,000 vertical feet below the surface reference, a subsea wellhead 2,000 vertical feet below that reference, and a continuous 10 ppg liquid column in the modeled well path. Its total head to the formation is 4,160 psi; the modeled contribution from wellhead to formation is 3,120 psi. Confusing the 6,000-ft below-wellhead interval with the full column loses 1,040 psi in the arithmetic. The exercise does not prescribe the actual riser/return configuration or seawater contribution.

### Changing a return route

At the same model rate, return route A contributes 180 psi pressure loss above a chosen reference point; route B contributes 80 psi. With other terms fixed, the modeled pressure at that reference differs by 100 psi. Copying a pressure schedule across the route change would miss that difference. The approved procedure must account for the transition, measurements, line condition and limits. Do not simply add or subtract a generic “subsea correction” without its model.

**Practice:** route B becomes restricted and its verified model loss rises to 140 psi. **Answer:** compared with its previous state, the pressure contribution increases by 60 psi at that rate under the stated model. This is a changed condition requiring interpretation; it is not permission to turn a control by an inferred amount.

### Emergency functions and actual scope

Emergency shutdown, disconnect and backup actuation functions have different purposes and configuration-dependent effects. A command may involve tool-position restrictions, energy availability, barriers and subsequent well status. The operator must know what the actual assigned system does, who commands it and what confirms the result. A classroom explanation of these functions cannot qualify an unassessed subsea console.

**Original case:** the planned response assumes a qualified cut-and-seal capability, but the tracked position places a nonshearable component at the relevant plane. The response assumption is invalid for that state. Record the limitation and follow the approved contingency. Neither a green panel light nor the existence of a backup button changes the geometry.

For a combined surface/subsea endorsement, the learner must complete the specified configured subsea simulation as well as the common instruction. A surface-only learner still studies the differences so they recognize the boundary, but their record must state surface-only. Do not award combined scope by attendance at the same lecture.


---

lessons.title: Drilling Well Control — formative checks
lessons.body:
# Drilling Well Control — formative checks

Attempt the two checks after each chapter, then review the explanations. Explain your corrected reasoning after any error. These are learning questions, not the final examination.

lessons.title: D01
lessons.body:
## D01

### D01-L1

Why is TVD used for static liquid hydrostatic pressure?

A. It is the pump pressure

B. It measures vertical liquid head

C. It includes pipe friction

D. It is always longer than measured depth

### D01-L2

A circulation-dependent pressure contribution disappears when pumps stop. What must be reconsidered?

A. Only fuel consumption

B. The static pressure balance

C. Only pipe tally

D. The formation pressure becomes zero

### Explained answers

**D01-L1: B — It measures vertical liquid head**

Gravity acts through vertical height. Rework chapter 1 with a deviated-well sketch if you chose a path length.

**D01-L2: B — The static pressure balance**

Annular friction can support circulating bottomhole pressure but is absent in the static calculation. Revisit the 5,200/5,400 psi example.

lessons.title: D02
lessons.body:
## D02

### D02-L1

What additional density balances a verified 260 psi deficit at 5,000 ft TVD?

A. 1.0 ppg

B. 5.0 ppg

C. 10 ppg

D. 0.1 ppg

### D02-L2

Which pressure belongs in the simplified ECD addition?

A. Total pump pressure

B. Annular friction at the evaluation depth and condition

C. The highest gauge anywhere

D. Drillpipe friction alone

### Explained answers

**D02-L1: A — 1.0 ppg**

260/(0.052×5,000)=1.0 ppg. This does not itself approve a circulation plan. Repeat with units if your answer differed.

**D02-L2: B — Annular friction at the evaluation depth and condition**

ECD represents the annular friction contribution as density at a specified depth. Draw the flow path before recalculating.

lessons.title: D03
lessons.body:
## D03

### D03-L1

An approved displacement is 0.008 bbl/ft over 500 ft. Only 2 bbl of fill is observed. What is the discrepancy?

A. 2 bbl more than expected

B. 2 bbl less than expected

C. 4 bbl more than expected

D. No discrepancy

### D03-L2

Why must open-ended and closed-ended pipe conditions be identified?

A. They make trip tanks unnecessary

B. They eliminate swab

C. They change the relevant displacement/fill relationship

D. They change feet into barrels directly

### Explained answers

**D03-L1: B — 2 bbl less than expected**

Expected fill is 4 bbl; actual is 2 bbl. A shortfall demands the approved response and investigation. Reconcile expected versus measured explicitly.

**D03-L2: C — They change the relevant displacement/fill relationship**

The enclosed or drained fluid condition changes the volume relationship. Review chapter 3 and draw the internal pipe volume separately from steel displacement.

lessons.title: D04
lessons.body:
## D04

### D04-L1

Two screens use one failed transmitter. Are they independent confirmation?

A. No, they share the same failed input

B. Only when they agree

C. Yes, if one is newer

D. Yes, if both are digital

### D04-L2

Unexplained gain is dismissed as a probable transfer, but no transfer is confirmed. What is appropriate?

A. Continue until certainty

B. Reset the volume display

C. Edit the log to show a transfer

D. Treat the evidence through the approved response and verify the transfer

### Explained answers

**D04-L1: A — No, they share the same failed input**

Display count is not sensor independence. Trace each reading to its source and identify a valid independent observation.

**D04-L2: D — Treat the evidence through the approved response and verify the transfer**

An unverified explanation cannot erase credible evidence. Rehearse a concise observation-action-assistance report.

lessons.title: D05
lessons.body:
## D05

### D05-L1

What does a successful function test alone establish?

A. The equipment moved as tested

B. Every future configuration is verified

C. All pressure paths are leak-tight

D. All tubulars are shearable

### D05-L2

Closing an annular flow path necessarily closes the internal string path.

A. True for every string

B. False; trace each path and its barriers

C. True if the console says closed

D. True when the mud is heavy

### Explained answers

**D05-L1: A — The equipment moved as tested**

Movement and pressure integrity are different evidence. Review the boundary and acceptance criteria of each test.

**D05-L2: B — False; trace each path and its barriers**

Internal and annular flow paths require their own effective barriers. Redraw chapter 5’s schematic if you conflated them.

lessons.title: D06
lessons.body:
## D06

### D06-L1

Successive pressures are rising. How should the recorder handle them?

A. Keep each timed reading and report the trend

B. Keep only the smallest

C. Keep only the first

D. Replace them with an average called stabilized

### D06-L2

A closure command is shown. What remains necessary?

A. Assume the well is killed

B. Delete the alarm

C. Nothing

D. The procedure-defined verification of actual state and containment

### Explained answers

**D06-L1: A — Keep each timed reading and report the trend**

A time series preserves evidence; an invented stabilized average destroys it. Rework the chapter 6 handover.

**D06-L2: D — The procedure-defined verification of actual state and containment**

Command, position indication, and verified containment are different. Name the configured verification observations.

lessons.title: D07
lessons.body:
## D07

### D07-L1

At 0.1 bbl/stroke, how many strokes nominally move 80 bbl?

A. 8,000

B. 8

C. 80

D. 800

### D07-L2

Observed response departs from a calculated circulation schedule. What governs?

A. Finish the schedule regardless

B. The approved deviation/contingency procedure and verified observations

C. The nearest round number

D. A remembered plan from another well

### Explained answers

**D07-L1: D — 800**

Volume divided by output gives strokes: 80/0.1=800. Recheck dimensions and actual calibration.

**D07-L2: B — The approved deviation/contingency procedure and verified observations**

A model is conditional on its assumptions. Identify which assumptions changed before continuing under the approved method.

lessons.title: D08
lessons.body:
## D08

### D08-L1

Which pressure scale is used in the simple constant-temperature gas volume relationship?

A. Absolute

B. Pump-speed percentage

C. Density

D. Gauge

### D08-L2

Why can more fluid density worsen a loss event?

A. It always reduces hydrostatic pressure

B. It removes all friction

C. It closes the BOP automatically

D. It can increase formation loading beyond the applicable limit

### Explained answers

**D08-L1: A — Absolute**

The relationship uses absolute pressure. Review why gauge zero does not mean no molecular pressure.

**D08-L2: D — It can increase formation loading beyond the applicable limit**

The upper pressure boundary matters. Sketch how loss of fluid can then reduce column support.

lessons.title: D09
lessons.body:
## D09

### D09-L1

Why can choke-line friction matter in a subsea circulation plan?

A. It is always zero

B. It changes pressure relationships along the long flow route

C. It makes remote indication infallible

D. It replaces formation pressure

### D09-L2

An RCD is present. What follows?

A. Its documented function and limits still govern the MPD/well-control interface

B. Unlimited influx can be handled

C. The BOP is unnecessary

D. All transitions are safe

### Explained answers

**D09-L1: B — It changes pressure relationships along the long flow route**

Rate- and fluid-dependent line losses must be included in the specific plan. Trace the subsea flow route.

**D09-L2: A — Its documented function and limits still govern the MPD/well-control interface**

MPD equipment does not remove conventional barrier responsibilities. Review the transition case in chapter 9.

lessons.title: D10
lessons.body:
## D10

### D10-L1

A barrier test failed but gas is no longer seen at surface. May the supervisor declare restart ready?

A. No; resolve the critical barrier failure and other restrictions

B. Yes if a shift ends

C. Only if schedule pressure is high

D. Yes

### D10-L2

Which handover is actionable?

A. Everything looks fine

B. Only the final density

C. Current state, verified barriers, timed trends, restrictions, owner and next permitted action

D. Continue as usual

### Explained answers

**D10-L1: A — No; resolve the critical barrier failure and other restrictions**

Absence of one symptom does not establish barrier integrity. List actual restart evidence.

**D10-L2: C — Current state, verified barriers, timed trends, restrictions, owner and next permitted action**

The receiver must know what may happen next and what must not. Rewrite an ambiguous handover using chapter 10’s structure.

lessons.title: D11
lessons.body:
## D11

### D11-L1

A 5,000 ft TVD shoe has a stipulated 12 ppg equivalent constraint. Replacing a uniform 10 ppg column with 11 ppg changes the simple static surface difference by:

A. An increase of 260 psi

B. A decrease of 2,600 psi

C. A decrease of 260 psi

D. No change

### D11-L2

An ideal mixture combines 50 bbl at 10 ppg and 50 bbl at 12 ppg. What is its predicted density before actual verification?

A. 10 ppg

B. 12 ppg

C. 11 ppg

D. 22 ppg

### Explained answers

**D11-L1: C — A decrease of 260 psi**

The extra hydrostatic support is 0.052×1×5,000=260 psi, consuming that much difference. Review chapter 11’s shoe example.

**D11-L2: C — 11 ppg**

Equal volumes average to 11 ppg under the stated ideal-volume model. Actual fluid testing and compatibility still matter.

lessons.title: D12
lessons.body:
## D12

### D12-L1

A pressure drop occurs before the modelled fluid arrival. What is the sound reasoning?

A. Report the contradiction and follow the configured contingency while checking evidence

B. Delete the model

C. Change every valve until pressure returns

D. Accept density arrival without checking

### D12-L2

Two volume instruments disagree. What should be established first in the investigation?

A. Which display is brighter

B. Whether a shift is nearly over

C. Which reading is more convenient

D. Whether they measure the same inventory boundary and whether their inputs are valid

### Explained answers

**D12-L1: A — Report the contradiction and follow the configured contingency while checking evidence**

A familiar explanation must still fit the evidence. Revisit chapter 12’s competing-explanations case.

**D12-L2: D — Whether they measure the same inventory boundary and whether their inputs are valid**

Different inventory boundaries or faulty sources can explain disagreement. Preserve the discrepancy and required response.

lessons.title: D13
lessons.body:
## D13

### D13-L1

An off-bottom string has an influx below its end. Why question the standard at-bottom worksheet?

A. TVD becomes MD

B. Its assumed pressure connection and circulation coverage may not apply

C. All arithmetic stops working

D. Pressure has no units

### D13-L2

In a uniform vertical classroom annulus, 1 bbl occupies 25 ft. At 10 ppg its liquid hydrostatic equivalent is:

A. 13 psi

B. 1 psi

C. 130 psi

D. 25 psi

### Explained answers

**D13-L1: B — Its assumed pressure connection and circulation coverage may not apply**

A mathematically correct sheet can use the wrong physical model. Mark the string end and influx position before interpreting gauges.

**D13-L2: A — 13 psi**

0.052×10×25=13 psi. This is not a field bleed instruction. Review chapter 13’s missing-input discussion.

lessons.title: D14
lessons.body:
## D14

### D14-L1

A drill is completed quickly but omits containment verification. Is that a pass?

A. No, required correct actions and verification still govern

B. Only if the learner is senior

C. Yes if no one objects

D. Yes, speed is enough

### D14-L2

Which corrective action is measurable?

A. Demonstrate configured containment verification in two changed cases without prompts

B. Read everything again someday

C. Be safer

D. Pay attention

### Explained answers

**D14-L1: A — No, required correct actions and verification still govern**

Speed cannot compensate for a critical missed step. Rehearse verification in a changed simulator case.

**D14-L2: A — Demonstrate configured containment verification in two changed cases without prompts**

A measurable action states the behaviour, conditions and observable standard. Revisit chapter 14’s debrief.

lessons.title: D15
lessons.body:
## D15

### D15-L1

Does porosity alone establish how rapidly formation fluid can enter a well?

A. Only at night

B. Yes

C. No; connected flow pathways and other conditions matter

D. Only if the rock name is known

### D15-L2

Why is a zero gauge on one side of a suspected blockage insufficient for dismantling?

A. Pressure may be trapped elsewhere

B. All blockages are harmless

C. Gauges measure temperature only

D. Zero proves the whole system empty

### Explained answers

**D15-L1: C — No; connected flow pathways and other conditions matter**

Permeability and pressure conditions affect flow. Review the distinction between pore space and connected flow pathways.

**D15-L2: A — Pressure may be trapped elsewhere**

The blockage can isolate pressure. Use the approved isolation/remediation plan and protect against sudden movement or release.

lessons.title: D16
lessons.body:
## D16

### D16-L1

The active system is A+B but the totalizer displays A+C. What is wrong?

A. The monitoring boundary does not match the intended active inventory

B. The fluid density is automatically zero

C. All gauges are broken

D. Nothing if the total is steady

### D16-L2

What does an enabled alarm with a failed input provide?

A. Reliable detection

B. Proof of containment

C. A substitute for independent monitoring

D. No dependable detection from that failed input

### Explained answers

**D16-L1: A — The monitoring boundary does not match the intended active inventory**

A stable wrong inventory is not valid monitoring. Reconcile physical and displayed configuration.

**D16-L2: D — No dependable detection from that failed input**

A working alert path cannot correct a failed measurement. Review all parts of alarm readiness.

lessons.title: D17
lessons.body:
## D17

### D17-L1

What can loss of a separator liquid seal permit?

A. Guaranteed safe circulation

B. Gas entering a route intended for liquid returns

C. Elimination of gas hazards

D. Automatic formation strengthening

### D17-L2

May an emergency subsea sequence be copied from another installation?

A. Yes if it was fast

B. No; actual design, logic, capability and approved procedure govern

C. Yes, names are identical

D. Yes if no one checks

### Explained answers

**D17-L1: B — Gas entering a route intended for liquid returns**

The seal is part of the gas-handling system. Review chapter 17 and trace the unintended gas path.

**D17-L2: B — No; actual design, logic, capability and approved procedure govern**

Function names do not establish identical sequences or conditions. Verify the configured cause-and-effect description.

lessons.title: D18
lessons.body:
## D18

### D18-L1

Why can rapid repeated control adjustments be problematic?

A. Only the screen changes

B. Pressure has no inertia or propagation effects

C. All systems respond instantly

D. Delayed response may lead to overcorrection

### D18-L2

A 0.2 ppg increment over 5,000 ft adds 52 psi. With another 70 psi surface contribution, the total addition is:

A. 70 psi

B. 18 psi

C. 122 psi

D. 52 psi

### Explained answers

**D18-L1: D — Delayed response may lead to overcorrection**

Observe response under the configured control method rather than making uncontrolled repeated changes.

**D18-L2: C — 122 psi**

The simplified contributions add. Review the single pressure-budget example in chapter 18.



---

lessons.title: Role/equipment formative checks
lessons.body:
# Role/equipment formative checks

Attempt independently, then explain corrected reasoning after feedback.

### R19-L1

A sealing function is qualified for pipe body, but a tool joint occupies its position. What matters first?

A. Whether it worked on yesterday's pipe

B. Whether the operator can close it faster

C. Whether its capability covers the actual geometry

D. Whether the button is green

**R19-L1: C — Whether its capability covers the actual geometry**

Capability is geometry-specific. Review R19 and trace the actual object and qualified sealing envelope.

### R19-L2

Why trace an internal drillstring route separately from the annulus?

A. An outside seal does not close the inside bore

B. The inside cannot contain pressure

C. Only the annulus needs monitoring

D. Both routes always have identical barriers

**R19-L2: A — An outside seal does not close the inside bore**

The two pressure paths require their specified controls. Redraw both before reassessment.

### R20-L1

At .012 bbl/ft, what is the supplied displacement over 300 ft?

A. .036 bbl

B. 36 bbl

C. 3.6 bbl

D. 300 bbl

**R20-L1: C — 3.6 bbl**

Multiply capacity by length: .012 × 300 = 3.6 bbl. Keep units.

### R20-L2

What does pumping the intended cement quantity establish by itself?

A. Only a recorded pumping quantity, not every placement and barrier requirement

B. Permanent barrier integrity

C. Approved casing pressure rating

D. Successful float verification

**R20-L2: A — Only a recorded pumping quantity, not every placement and barrier requirement**

Placement, condition and verification are separate. Review R20 before interpreting a completion log.

### R21-L1

A closure command is pending. What should the handover say?

A. Ignore the pending indication

B. Use the previous shift's reading

C. Closure commanded; required confirmation pending

D. Well safely isolated

**R21-L1: C — Closure commanded; required confirmation pending**

Report command and achieved state separately; retain restrictions until required evidence exists.

### R21-L2

Who may invent a stabilized pressure to finish a form?

A. No one

B. The most experienced operator

C. The assessor during a live event

D. The supervisor

**R21-L2: A — No one**

Missing safety-critical data must remain missing until established. Review uncertainty and recording rules.

### R22-L1

A 10 ppg liquid column extends 8000 vertical feet from the stated surface datum. What is its modeled head?

A. 3120 psi

B. 1040 psi

C. 4160 psi

D. 8000 psi

**R22-L1: C — 4160 psi**

0.052 × 10 × 8000 = 4160 psi. Mark the datum before calculating.

### R22-L2

Can surface-only simulation establish a combined subsea endorsement?

A. No; the defined configured subsea demonstration is also required

B. Yes if scores are high

C. Yes if the lecture mentions subsea

D. Yes after sufficient attendance

**R22-L2: A — No; the defined configured subsea demonstration is also required**

Knowledge and configured performance are distinct. Record actual assessed scope.



---

courses.title: VUC007 | Drilling Well Control — practical evaluation packet

content.title: VUC007 | Drilling Well Control — practical evaluation packet
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: Drilling Well Control — practical evaluation packet
lessons.body:
# Drilling Well Control — practical evaluation packet

These original cases are training instruments. Do not connect them to live controls. Assessment outcomes are not prefilled. This packet specifies tasks and observable criteria; equipment-specific console sequences must come from the supplied simulator procedure.

lessons.title: Common assessor instructions
lessons.body:
## Common assessor instructions

Identify learner, pathway, assessor, date, case version, and equipment configuration. Brief the learner on simulator controls, emergency stop, allowed references, and role boundaries. Demonstrate interface use before assessment; assessment is not a test of guessing an unfamiliar interface. Provide the case data and procedure without the answer key. Record time-stamped actions and words, not impressions such as “seemed confident.”

Score each criterion 0 = not demonstrated/incorrect, 1 = demonstrated after prompting, 2 = demonstrated independently. Every safety-critical criterion must score 2 on the final attempt. All other criteria must score at least 1, with an overall score of at least 80%. A prompt during practice is teaching; during assessment it must be recorded. A critical error stops the assessed attempt. Reassessment uses changed numerical inputs or a different fault, not immediate repetition of a memorized answer.

Required tools: calculator, blank calculation and event forms, well schematic, fluid/volume table, equipment and test records, approved simulator procedure, and configured training simulator for operational endorsements. Tabletop-only performance cannot earn a console endorsement.

lessons.title: Station A — pressure and volume worksheet
lessons.body:
## Station A — pressure and volume worksheet

Applicable: introductory, driller, supervisor. Awareness learners discuss the decision meaning without a calculation endorsement.

### Learner data and tasks

Case A is a synthetic vertical conventional surface well: TVD 8,000 ft; measured depth 9,600 ft; uniform original fluid 10.0 ppg; verified stabilized drillpipe pressure 416 psi; pressure connection unobstructed; string at bottom. Recorded reduced-rate pressure with original fluid is 360 psi. The exercise model assumes friction scales with density. String internal volume is 100 bbl; calibrated pump output is 0.10 bbl/stroke. The supplied linear schedule is a training simplification. No operational equipment limits are provided in this calculation-only case.

1. Draw the pressure contributions and state the datum and units.
2. Calculate original hydrostatic pressure, inferred formation pressure under the stated assumptions, balancing density, simplified initial/final circulating pressures, and strokes to bit.
3. Calculate the midpoint pressure in the supplied linear model.
4. State why the worksheet cannot authorize circulation on a real well.
5. Independently check another learner's worksheet and identify an intentional measured-depth substitution planted by the assessor.

### Assessor key and criteria

Hydrostatic 4,160 psi; inferred formation pressure 4,576 psi; balancing density 11.0 ppg; initial circulating pressure 776 psi; simplified final 396 psi; 1,000 strokes; midpoint 586 psi. Accept arithmetic rounding within 1 psi and 0.01 ppg where appropriate, with correct units. The learner must flag the missing pressure window, equipment limits, actual hydraulics, approved method, and procedure. **Critical:** does not authorize real operation from this worksheet; does not use MD for hydrostatic support. Other criteria: accurate equations, units, independent check, transparent assumptions, clear explanation.

lessons.title: Station B — trip discrepancy and recognition
lessons.body:
## Station B — trip discrepancy and recognition

Applicable: all pathways; awareness role reports and withdraws from operational control decisions.

### Case and injects

The approved exercise displacement for the current pipe condition is 0.006 bbl/ft. The crew has pulled 600 ft. Expected fill is 3.6 bbl, but the calibrated trip tank records 1.4 bbl. There is no authorized transfer. At the next inject, a colleague says the tank “always reads low.” At the final inject, the normal pit display reports a sensor fault.

The learner states the discrepancy, identifies the potential influx concern, communicates to the responsible role, and follows the supplied exercise response. Operational candidates execute the appropriate configured simulator response; awareness candidates must not operate controls. The assessor supplies the actual procedure before the exercise and records the version used.

### Criteria

Identifies 2.2-bbl shortfall; does not dismiss it because of informal reassurance; checks independent observations; preserves sensor fault; uses closed-loop communication; follows role and procedure. **Critical:** does not continue pulling simply to average out the discrepancy; does not invent a transfer; does not perform unauthorized control actions. The assessor observes verification of resulting equipment/well state for operational candidates.

lessons.title: Station C — response and incident log
lessons.body:
## Station C — response and incident log

Applicable: driller and supervisor. Introductory learners complete the tabletop record only.

### Simulator setup

Configure a conventional surface training case with known tested barriers, compatible tubular position, an approved response procedure, and instrument ranges suitable for the case. Do not use this case if the configured procedure or pressure limits are unavailable. The assessor records the installed simulator model, response procedure revision, limits, and initial conditions in the blank record below.

Inject unexplained return-flow increase at constant pump strokes and a 3-bbl active gain. Following the learner's response, show closure indication but initially leave containment verification incomplete. Supply pressure readings of 300, 350, and 390 psi at sequential observation times, with an uncertainty about the drillpipe pressure connection. A final inject asks the learner to report a stabilized pressure immediately.

### Criteria

Recognizes and communicates evidence promptly; follows the supplied response without procedural invention; verifies actual state rather than relying on command; records all readings and times; explicitly labels unstable/uncertain data; escalates within role; maintains approved monitoring. **Critical:** does not report an invented stabilized value or authorize a calculation based on an unverified connection. Supervisor additionally assigns roles and protects the crew from conflicting instructions.

lessons.title: Station D — circulation plan and changing conditions
lessons.body:
## Station D — circulation plan and changing conditions

Applicable: driller and supervisor. Requires configured simulator with approved plan and limits.

Use Station A numerical data only after the instructor has supplied compatible simulated formation/equipment limits, hydraulics, and operating procedure. The learner explains the plan, expected fluid-arrival milestones, pressure trend, monitoring roles, and stop/escalation criteria before execution. The assessor then introduces one approved simulator fault: pump output differs from assumed output, a pressure signal fails, or a restriction produces a pressure deviation. Record the selected fault; do not introduce an undocumented physical hazard.

Include a planning discussion of combined margins and surface handling. Give the learner a fictional additional-pressure budget of 100 psi at the stated evaluation location and proposals of 0.1 ppg over 8,000 ft plus 80 psi surface pressure. The expected finding is 121.6 psi combined, exceeding the budget. This tabletop budget must not be used as the simulator's real equipment limit. Then supply a case statement that the separator seal indication is unreliable: the learner must withhold any assumption of verified gas-handling capacity and identify the required resolution. These discussion tasks precede the configured operating exercise.

### Criteria

Checks plan and limits before starting; tracks strokes and actual output; compares expected and observed trends; recognizes departure from the model; follows the supplied contingency; communicates changes and maintains an event record. **Critical:** does not force the operation to a memorized schedule despite contradictory evidence; does not exceed a stated limit; does not conceal the fault. Supervisor must justify whether the plan remains valid and what verification is required before continuation.

lessons.title: Station E — subsea and MPD interface extension
lessons.body:
## Station E — subsea and MPD interface extension

Applicable: candidates seeking those specific practical scope endorsements. Otherwise a tabletop learning case only.

Provide the actual training schematic and approved transition procedure. The learner marks the stack, riser, choke/kill lines, relevant pressure references, control system, MPD equipment if present, and barrier responsibilities. Inject a loss of a planned 200-psi surface-pressure contribution in an MPD case, or a changed choke-line friction condition in a subsea case. The instructor supplies the simulator's validated response model and limits; this packet does not invent a universally safe transition sequence.

Before the inject, ask the candidate to locate the configured emergency-function logic, readiness evidence and available intervention interfaces. Assess whether the candidate distinguishes function names from actual capability, and identifies unresolved tubular compatibility or control-readiness questions. Do not award a subsea endorsement merely because the learner can name deadman, autoshear or emergency disconnect.

### Criteria

Identifies the changed pressure contribution; distinguishes well-control from MPD functions; follows the configured transition/contingency; verifies remote equipment state; accounts for riser and line effects; communicates to the correct authority. **Critical:** does not treat the rotating control device or riser as an unlimited BOP substitute; does not reuse an unmodified surface schedule. Record separate results for subsea and MPD; passing one does not imply passing the other.

lessons.title: Station F — supervisor readiness and restart conference
lessons.body:
## Station F — supervisor readiness and restart conference

Applicable: supervisor. Other learners participate in role-appropriate discussion.

Provide these facts: influx volume reconciled; no further reported surface gas; one barrier test failed; a pressure indication remains unexplained; an incoming shift requests restart; a manager emphasizes lost operating time. The learner chairs a five-minute review, assigns resolution owners, records restrictions, and hands over the current state.

### Criteria

Separates observations from conclusions; retains restrictions; requires barrier and pressure resolution; identifies who may approve restart; responds constructively to challenge; gives the next shift a usable handover. **Critical:** no restart authorization while the stated critical failures remain unresolved. “No gas at surface” is not accepted as proof that all barriers and pressure conditions are satisfactory.

lessons.title: Station G — monitoring setup and alarm verification
lessons.body:
## Station G — monitoring setup and alarm verification

Applicable: driller and supervisor; introductory learners perform on a nonoperational training display.

Provide a simulator inventory diagram specifying Pits A+B as active, a controlled exercise instruction containing the required high/low alarm values, and a test-signal function. The initial display deliberately includes A+C and has the high alarm disabled. The case also includes an unlogged transfer. No universal alarm values are supplied by this packet; the assessor records the configured case values and their source before the exercise.

Learner tasks: compare physical/training lineup with displayed inventory; identify the mismatch; reconcile the transfer; enter the supplied alarm settings through the training procedure; read them back; test the alert path; identify the responsible observer; give a handover stating the corrected setup and any remaining uncertainty.

Criteria: correct inventory boundary, accurate values, functioning alert, reliable input, clear responsibility and record. **Critical:** does not accept a stable total from the wrong pits, leave the required alarm disabled, or silently invent alarm thresholds. A passed test of the alert sound does not excuse a failed measurement input.

lessons.title: Station H — formation/fluid ambiguity and trapped pressure
lessons.body:
## Station H — formation/fluid ambiguity and trapped pressure

Applicable: all pathways within role. No physical pressurized equipment is used.

Inject a small unexplained return after pumps stop. The prior shift recorded one breathing event. The fluid system has since changed. Ask the learner to state the response and what evidence would distinguish hypotheses. Then introduce inconsistent readings across a suspected blocked line and a suggestion to loosen a fitting.

Criteria: retains the unexplained-flow concern; does not treat the old breathing label as proof; identifies fluid and measurement context; follows the approved escalation; recognizes possible isolated pressure; rejects unauthorized dismantling and line-of-fire exposure. **Critical:** no instruction to open, strike or heat the suspected blockage, and no claim that one zero reading proves the whole line safe. The assessor records the learner's actual words and corrective teaching if needed.

courses.title: VUC007 | VUC007 — role-specific practical packet

content.title: VUC007 | VUC007 — role-specific practical packet
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC007 — role-specific practical packet
lessons.body:
# VUC007 — role-specific practical packet

These original cases supplement the embedded foundation stations. No physical pressure or live controls are authorized. Use the actual controlled training-system procedure for console movements; this packet supplies case data, roles, decisions and observable scoring.

lessons.title: P1 — recognize, respond and transfer control
lessons.body:
## P1 — recognize, respond and transfer control

**Preparation:** configured surface simulator, trend display, current well schematic, approved response procedure, event log and role cards. Instructor verifies the normal starting state before the independent attempt.

**Initial case:** fictional Juniper D-7. Active volume stable at 240 bbl. No transfer authorized. Over two observations it rises to 242.0 then 243.5 bbl; return flow increases while the commanded pump state is unchanged. The drill-rate trend also changes. The instructor does not give a cause.

**Observer task:** identify credible evidence and promptly report point/time/units, current activity, uncertainty and assigned action. No unsupported operation of controls. **Operator task:** additionally apply the configured response, verify actual equipment state and hand over recorded observations. **Supervisor task:** accept the handover, distinguish verified and missing data, establish responsibility and authorize only the next supported step.

**Inject:** a closure command has been issued but feedback is pending. Later readings change before stabilizing. The learner must not report immediate verified isolation or use a transient value as stabilized pressure. Instructor releases the confirmation/data cards only when the corresponding specified verification is completed in the simulation.

**Scoring:** five criteria, 0 absent/unsafe, 1 prompted/incomplete, 2 independently correct. Criteria are recognition, action within assigned procedure/role, state verification, accurate communication, preserved log/restrictions. Require 8/10 and independent correctness for action, verification and restrictions. Concealing evidence or operating outside the supplied procedure is critical. Record response times against the configured exercise's stated performance target; do not invent a universal field time limit.

**Debrief:** distinguish a warning from a proven mechanism. Have the learner explain why correct escalation did not require a guessed diagnosis. Fresh attempt uses a trip-volume discrepancy rather than repeating this trend.

lessons.title: P2 — plan, execute the model and verify the end state
lessons.body:
## P2 — plan, execute the model and verify the end state

**Data:** vertical classroom model, TVD 6,000 ft, MD 7,200 ft, full 10 ppg fluid, verified static communicating pressure 312 psi. Original-fluid reduced-rate friction 400 psi. Model assumes friction proportional to density; string volume 60 bbl, pump .1 bbl/stroke. Linear pressure schedule applies only to this supplied model. Instructor supplies the configured simulator's applicable pressure limits and procedure separately before operational assessment.

**Required calculations:** head, modeled formation pressure, balance density, initial/final schedule pressure, strokes to end of string and midpoint. **Key:** 3,120 psi; 3,432 psi; 11 ppg; 712 psi initial; 440 psi final; 600 strokes; midpoint 576 psi. A real field plan needs actual hydraulic, formation, fluid and equipment constraints; these synthetic values are not that plan.

**Stage 1:** supervisor reviews the complete model and states objective, limits, references, roles and stop criteria. Operator repeats and checks readiness. Field-team learner explains the monitoring/reporting contribution without receiving a console endorsement.

**Stage 2:** execute the specified simulated startup and schedule. At 300 strokes, expected pressure is 576 psi; inject 640 psi with unchanged reported rate. The supplied model rule requires hold/verification for unexplained deviation beyond ±10 psi. Learner must detect the mismatch, preserve control through the configured procedure and record uncertainty. Instructor later provides a resolved measurement fault card and approved restart evidence; learner must verify it before continuing.

**Stage 3:** string displacement reaches 600 strokes. The supervisor must not call the entire well displaced merely because fluid reached the modeled string end. Instructor supplies a separate remaining-system volume of 90 bbl and confirms the model uses the same calibrated output. Expected additional displacement is 900 strokes. Actual route/volume evidence remains required.

**Stage 4:** model indicates displacement complete, but one pressure connection is marked UNVERIFIED. Learner retains the restriction and obtains the required verification through the simulation. Only then do they carry out the supplied modeled shutdown and assess the resulting gauges/volume/barrier state. Record what evidence supports the conclusion and any remaining limits.

**Score:** ten criteria 0–2: data/datum, arithmetic, limits/readiness, acknowledged direction, configured startup, monitoring, mismatch response, remaining-volume interpretation, shutdown verification and truthful closeout. Require 16/20 and independent correctness for limits, startup, mismatch response and shutdown/closeout. Instructor records exact control actions against the configured procedure. A tabletop arithmetic pass alone does not satisfy the operator/supervisor console requirement.

**Fresh numerical variant:** 5,000 ft TVD, 10 ppg, 260 psi static, 300 psi friction, 50 bbl string, .1 output. Key: head2600, formation2860, density11, initial560, final330, strokes500, midpoint445. Remaining80bbl means800 additional strokes under the supplied ideal model. Change the injected fault to unexplained return restriction.

lessons.title: P3 — combined subsea scope
lessons.body:
## P3 — combined subsea scope

**Inputs:** configured subsea simulator, actual control/emergency procedure, schematic with explicit surface/wellhead/formation datums and equipment capabilities. No generic disconnect sequence is supplied or accepted.

**Original model:** formation7,000ft below surface, wellhead1,500ft below surface, uniform9ppg column in the specified connected path. Supplied route-A friction160psi; route-B100psi at the same model rate. Nonshearable component position uncertainty overlaps the relevant emergency cutting plane.

**Tasks/key:** total modeled head3276psi; below-wellhead contribution2574psi; upper contribution702psi. Route change reduces the stated loss contribution60psi with other terms fixed. Identify why that does not itself prescribe a control action. Explain the position/capability conflict and demonstrate the actual configuration's permitted contingency in simulation, preserving its stated barriers and authority.

**Score:** five criteria0–2: datums/calculations, route interpretation, geometry/capability, approved contingency, verified state/communication. Require8/10; geometry, contingency and verification must each score2. If the actual configuration cannot be supplied, record combined practical scope not assessed. Do not award it from the worksheet.

lessons.body:
# Drilling Well Control — permitted calculation reference

Use only when the problem states that the simplified model applies. This page is permitted during the controlled knowledge examination. It contains no examination answers. It is not a field operating procedure.

| Quantity | Classroom relationship | Required units / condition |
|---|---|---|
| Liquid hydrostatic pressure | 0.052 × density × TVD | psi; ppg; ft; uniform liquid segment |
| Layered hydrostatic pressure | Sum each segment's hydrostatic contribution | Use vertical thickness for each segment |
| SI liquid hydrostatic pressure | density × g × vertical height | Pa; kg/m³; m/s²; m |
| Pressure gradient | 0.052 × density | psi/ft from ppg |
| Density equivalent of pressure difference | pressure difference ÷ (0.052 × TVD) | ppg; psi; ft |
| Simplified balancing density | original density + verified deficit density equivalent | Requires valid pressure connection and column assumptions |
| Simplified ECD | static density + annular friction ÷ (0.052 × TVD) | Same evaluation depth and flow condition |
| Cylinder volume | diameter² × length ÷ 1,029.4 | bbl; diameter in inches; length in ft |
| Annular volume | (outer diameter² − inner diameter²) × length ÷ 1,029.4 | bbl; diameters in inches; length in ft |
| Expected displacement volume | applicable displacement per length × length | bbl from bbl/ft and ft; pipe condition specified |
| Strokes to move a volume | volume ÷ calibrated output | bbl divided by bbl/stroke |
| Flow rate | calibrated output × stroke rate | bbl/min from bbl/stroke and strokes/min |
| Time at unchanged rate | volume ÷ flow rate | minutes from bbl and bbl/min |
| Simplified initial circulating pressure | verified shut-in drillpipe pressure + original reduced-rate pressure | Conventional training model only |
| Simplified final circulating pressure | original reduced-rate pressure × new density ÷ original density | Stated proportional-friction model only |
| Linear schedule value | initial + fraction travelled × (final − initial) | Use only if linear schedule expressly specified |
| Simplified shoe pressure difference | (stipulated density-equivalent constraint − current uniform density) × 0.052 × shoe TVD | Not a released operating limit; excludes margins and dynamics |
| Ideal mixture density | sum of density × volume for each liquid ÷ total volume | Compatible liquids; additive-volume classroom model |
| Ideal gas volume change | P1 × V1 = P2 × V2 | Absolute pressure, fixed mass, constant temperature |
| Liquid-height equivalent | volume ÷ capacity per vertical length | Uniform vertical geometry |
| Pressure force | pressure difference × effective area | lbf from psi and square inches |
| Circular area | π × diameter² ÷ 4 | Consistent dimensions |

Retain calculation precision until the stated reporting rule is applied. For these written examinations, report pressures to the nearest whole psi, densities to two decimal places where not exact, and volume/strokes to the precision requested. These academic reporting conventions are not field rounding instructions. On an actual approved worksheet, follow that system's specified rules, particularly for minimum required and maximum permitted values.


---

# Drilling Well Control — sources and coverage

Review date: 2026-11-17. This is an original VNDRLY program, not a reproduction of IADC instruction or examinations. Public benchmark documents identify scope; they do not confer accreditation. No proprietary question bank was used.

lessons.title: Source register
lessons.body:
## Source register

1. [IADC WellSharp program](https://iadc.org/accreditation/wellsharp/), live public page inspected on review date. Used to distinguish drilling roles and surface/subsea scope. No claim of approved-provider status.
2. [IADC training and assessment handbook, second edition revision 8, 14 December 2023](https://iadc.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/WSP-01_Handbook-SecondEd_rev8.pdf). Public dated benchmark for pathway distinctions. Not represented as a verified current accreditation contract.
3. [IADC Driller curriculum, second edition revision 1, 19 June 2015](https://iadc.org/wp-content/uploads/2015/06/WSP-02-DO-D_DrillerCurr_2nd-Ed_rev1.pdf). Used only as a historical topic inventory. It predates later additions and is not sufficient to claim current full WellSharp conformity.
4. [IADC announcement of added unconventional concepts, 8 December 2021](https://iadc.org/drillbits/unconventional-well-control-concepts-added-to-wellsharp/). Identifies later additions concerning fluid placement, rotating control devices, and MPD awareness. Covered in chapters 2 and 9; this announcement is not a complete technical standard.
5. [IADC field-unit formula sheet, revision 3, 2018](https://iadc.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/05/WSP-FormulaSheet_FieldUnits_rev3.pdf). Mathematical reference for dimensional checks. All worked case numbers and assessment questions here are original. Formula applicability assumptions are explicitly taught.
6. [SLB equivalent circulating density](https://glossary.slb.com/en/terms/e/equivalent_circulating_density), technical glossary inspected on review date. Supports the distinction between static density and annular-friction contribution.
7. [SLB hydrostatic pressure](https://glossary.slb.com/terms/h/hydrostatic_pressure.aspx), technical glossary inspected on review date. Supports pressure-window reasoning and the risk of excessive formation loading.
8. [California Public Utilities Commission, Pressures in a Well 101](https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/-/media/cpuc-website/files/uploadedfiles/cpuc_public_website/content/news_room/news_and_updates/pressures-in-a-well-101.pdf), undated public introductory sheet inspected on review date. Used for basic pressure categories and TVD. Its simplified statements are not generalized to every MPD or operational condition.
9. [BSEE Early Kick Detection](https://www.bsee.gov/what-we-do/offshore-regulatory-programs/emerging-technologies/bast/early_kick_detection), live public page inspected on review date. Supports the importance of detection and trip monitoring. No new numerical operating threshold is inferred from it.
10. [BSEE well-control regulations FAQ](https://www.bsee.gov/guidance-and-regulations/Regulations/regulatory-reform/bsee-well-control-rule-2019/frequently-asked-questions-well-control-regulations), public explanatory material. Supports site-specific design and monitoring considerations; a historical FAQ does not replace applicable current regulations.
11. [IADC supervisor curriculum, second edition revision 3, Spanish, 26 May 2021](https://iadc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/05/WSP-02-DO-S_SupervisorCurr_2nd-Ed_rev3_SPN.pdf). Used as a dated scope benchmark, including planning, methods and equipment. The full source is not reproduced or translated into the learner package. This review does not certify conformity with an unpublished or later accreditation revision.
12. [IADC introductory curriculum, second edition revision 3, 13 January 2021](https://iadc.org/wp-content/uploads/2021/01/WSP-02-DO-I_IntroCurr-2nd-Ed_rev3.pdf). Public dated scope reference; no claim that the document is the latest accreditation edition.
13. [BSEE Safety Alert 484, 16 April 2024](https://www.bsee.gov/safety-alerts/improperly-depressurizing-piping-to-remove-a-hydrate-causes-injury). Supports the trapped-pressure and blockage-removal hazard taught in chapter 15. The classroom case is original and does not reproduce the incident narrative.
14. [SLB Defining Drilling Fluids, 2013](https://www.slb.com/resource-library/oilfield-review/defining-series/defining-drilling-fluids). Technical background for fluid-system functions and the need to match properties to conditions.
15. [EFC liquid-seal monitor technical description](https://www.efcgroup.net/products/instrumentation-controls/well-control-systems/liquid-seal-monitor-lsm), inspected 2026-11-17. Supports the separator seal-pressure relationship; no product-specific setpoint is generalized.
16. [BSEE ETAC control-system technical assessment](https://www.bsee.gov/sites/bsee.gov/files/research-reports//5018aa.pdf), public technical report. Supports distinguishing emergency control functions and design-dependent sequences. Numerical trigger examples from that report are not taught as universal settings.
17. [SLB below-tension-riser RCD](https://www.slb.com/products-and-services/innovating-in-oil-and-gas/well-construction/rigs-and-equipment/managed-pressure-drilling-equipment/below-tension-riser-rotating-control-device), manufacturer information inspected 2026-11-17. Supports the distinction between sealing/bearing function and other well-control equipment; no product rating is transferred to another installation.

lessons.title: VUC008 — VNDRLY/U Well Intervention Pressure Control
lessons.body:
# VUC008 — VNDRLY/U Well Intervention Pressure Control

Materials version 1.0, 17 November 2026. VNDRLY-owned instruction and assessment. This is not an IWCF-accredited program, IWCF examination preparation guarantee or IWCF certificate. It addresses completion and intervention pressure-control competencies with its own teaching, assessments and boundaries.

lessons.title: Audience, entry and placement
lessons.body:
## Audience, entry and placement

Assistant intervention personnel, equipment operators and supervisors use different pathways. All need arithmetic with units, pressure-versus-force understanding, schematic reading and communication in the delivery language. Operators need the employer's relevant equipment prerequisites; supervisors need relevant intervention experience and authority appropriate to the assessed role. No written examination substitutes for that employer authorization.

Place learners with a short diagnostic: calculate a liquid head from a stated vertical height; distinguish a seal from a restraint; trace tubing and annulus paths; report an uncertain gauge reading without inventing a diagnosis. Teach gaps before advancing. Provide readable diagrams, accessible format and language accommodations that preserve the technical standard. An interpreter may clarify language, not supply answers.

lessons.title: What the learner must demonstrate
lessons.body:
## What the learner must demonstrate

The embedded sixteen-chapter servicing foundation teaches pressure/volume models, barriers, influx recognition, workover, wireline, CT, snubbing, fluids, kill methods, handover, completion accessories, obstructions and controlled transitions. It is valid VNDRLY-owned instruction reused in full, including worked examples and formative explanations. Its original VUC006 labels disclose that reuse. **This guide governs VUC008 assessment and credential pathways**; the old VUC006 course guide is not included.

Six additional chapters teach I17 annulus integrity decisions; I18 direction-specific verification; I19 connected completion functions; I20 role/service transitions; I21 subsea pressure references and system types; I22 emergency capability and restoration. The source/coverage register maps each domain into actual teaching, examination and practical evidence.

All learners study all 22 chapters and complete 44 formative checks with explanations and remediation. This provides context across services. Operational endorsement is limited to the disciplines independently assessed. A subsea pathway requires both wireline and CT assessment in this VNDRLY program and the subsea cases; snubbing remains separate. This is a defined VNDRLY learning path, not a claim to issue an external combined certificate.

lessons.title: Delivery with actual instruction
lessons.body:
## Delivery with actual instruction

Teach S01–S05 foundations first; S06–S09 service functions next; S10–S16 calculations, planning and transitions next. Use the supplied model cards and casebooks, not a slide of chapter titles. Then teach I17–I20 using the new trend, test and equipment exercises, followed by I21–I22 with the subsea interface drawings and emergency case. Have learners solve each worked practice before displaying its explanation, and explain corrected reasoning after errors.

Planning allowance: eight hours foundation instruction/worked calculations, six hours service instruction/model cards, six hours pressure/program and control-system exercises, six hours completion/subsea extensions and six hours case assessments/debrief. Add configured simulator sessions for each operational endorsement and additional practice when needed. These are VNDRLY delivery allowances, not external accreditor minimums. Completion depends on demonstrated objectives, not exhausting a clock.

Use the embedded pressure/program casebook, equipment-selection workbook, six kill-method labs, four functional simulator exercises and control-systems cases as active instruction. Operators and supervisors complete the methods assessment; all pathways complete the systems assessment. Do not reduce a simulator session to a discussion of what someone else would do.

lessons.title: Separate controlled written papers
lessons.body:
## Separate controlled written papers

Each response in the six papers is worth two points: 2 for required result/reasoning, 1 for materially correct but incomplete without unsafe assertion, 0 for absent/incorrect/unsafe. Use the protected item key. The total cannot compensate for failure of a selected paper or a critical error.

| Paper | Items | Maximum | Pass |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Completion Operations | 41 | 82 | 66 |
| Completion Equipment | 10 | 20 | 16 |
| Wireline | 5 | 10 | 8 |
| Coiled Tubing | 5 | 10 | 8 |
| Snubbing | 5 | 10 | 8 |
| Subsea | 8 | 16 | 13 |

Completion Operations and Completion Equipment are required for every pathway, plus each selected service paper. There are 74 unique controlled questions across the whole bank; no duplicate questions are counted as new items. All sixteen foundation domains have three questions and the new domains have four each, except I20's six service-specific questions. For every selected foundation domain require at least 4/6; for each selected new four-item domain require at least 6/8. Each two-item I20 discipline subset requires 3/4. This prevents a strong score elsewhere from concealing a service-transition gap.

For operator/supervisor pathways, methods assessment requires 24/30, at least half credit in each question and no critical failure. All learners' systems assessment requires 16/20, at least 3/5 per case and no critical failure. The embedded instructor-only forms have their own explicit rubrics. Supervisors additionally pass the integrated representative case at 16/20 with all critical criteria satisfied.

The examiner supplies calculator/formula sheet, clean examination paper and response space; no key, coaching or completed practice notes. Allow a nominal 120 minutes for the 41-item paper,45 minutes for equipment,30 minutes per service paper and 45 minutes for subsea; adjust documented accessibility time without changing the standard. These are VNDRLY administration choices, not external examination rules.

lessons.title: Practical evidence and scope
lessons.body:
## Practical evidence and scope

| Pathway | Required observed evidence |
|---|---|
| Assistant — specified service | Foundation A/B/H; new P1/P2; selected service station D, E or F at support/recognition level; P3 assistant role |
| Equipment operator — specified service | Assistant requirements plus selected D/E/F on the configured simulator; relevant functional simulator and kill-method labs; P3 operator role |
| Supervisor — specified service | Common requirements; planning stations C/G/H; P3 supervisor role; integrated representative case; observed oversight of selected D/E/F |
| Subsea extension | Wireline and CT requirements plus P4/P5 using the configured subsea simulator and emergency procedure |

Foundation station letters refer to the embedded practical packet. New P1–P5 are fully supplied in completion-and-subsea-practicals.md. For an assistant, recognizing/reporting a required action does not earn an equipment-operation endorsement. For a supervisor, evaluating a contractor's plan does not automatically qualify operation of that contractor's console.

Each practical has five criteria scored 0/1/2. Pass 8/10 and all critical criteria independently 2. No observation is prefilled. Equipment-specific assessment needs the actual controlled schematic, operating and emergency procedures, ratings, test criteria and competent assessor. The packet supplies complete fictional tasks and rubrics; the delivery provider supplies the identified equipment configuration. Without it, issue only the actually achieved knowledge result, with practical/operational endorsement explicitly not assessed.

lessons.title: Remediation, retakes and credential record
lessons.body:
## Remediation, retakes and credential record

Remediation identifies the failed domain and explains why the response fails, then requires a fresh practice. Do not distribute the final key and immediately repeat the same form. Protected alternate instructions provide changed numerical values and new failure conditions. Record every attempt, changed form, raw scores, domain scores, critical findings and assessor. After two unsuccessful retakes require a documented learning plan and full reassessment of the failed component before completion.

The credential states VNDRLY/U Well Intervention Pressure Control; assistant/operator/supervisor; assessed disciplines; knowledge/practical status; equipment/procedure versions; date and assessor evidence. Do not issue blanket “all intervention” competence from one discipline. Failed nominated components stay incomplete; an independently achieved subset may be recorded accurately without representing the failed combined pathway as passed.

Review competence at least annually as a VNDRLY recommendation, and following relevant incidents, changes or extended absence. Employer/jurisdiction/client requirements control their own acceptance and may be stricter. No external validity period is implied. A refresher requires actual updated learning and reassessment, not opening a document again.

Course-material completion is an authoring record. It is not a learner's attendance, practical pass, external accreditation or software publication.


---
