lessons.title: VUC008 completion/subsea formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC008 completion/subsea formative checks

Answer independently after instruction. Then explain corrections in your own words.

lessons.title: I17-L1
lessons.body:
## I17-L1

Why must an annulus trend name its observation compartment and operating condition?

**Explained answer:** A reading belongs to a particular communicating volume; configuration and temperature/operation can change its interpretation.

**Remediation:** Redraw tubing and separate annuli; identify which route each gauge observes.

lessons.title: I17-L2
lessons.body:
## I17-L2

A model threshold is 300 psi and the observed annulus is 340 psi. A colleague proposes averaging it with an earlier 200 psi reading. Explain the response.

**Explained answer:** Do not average away an exceedance. Preserve 340 and follow the specified hold/escalation response.

**Remediation:** Review the difference between a trend calculation and a limit on the actual state.

lessons.title: I18-L1
lessons.body:
## I18-L1

Why does an outward-pressure test not automatically establish an element can contain inward differential?

**Explained answer:** Direction, element capability and the tested path may differ from the intended service.

**Remediation:** Sketch both loading directions and the approved verification needed.

lessons.title: I18-L2
lessons.body:
## I18-L2

A test volume is replenished during a no-replenishment observation period. What record should be retained?

**Explained answer:** Retain the actual additions and invalid attempt; disposition and fresh testing follow the controlled plan.

**Remediation:** Never alter criteria or erase the attempt to manufacture a pass.

lessons.title: I19-L1
lessons.body:
## I19-L1

Opening a sleeve creates tubing-to-annulus communication. What must change in the barrier review?

**Explained answer:** Redraw the new path and evaluate isolation, exposure and verification before moving.

**Remediation:** A tubing-only valve may no longer contain all routes.

lessons.title: I19-L2
lessons.body:
## I19-L2

A plug fits the bore but its lock is incompatible. Is its seal alone sufficient?

**Explained answer:** No. The required locking, sealing and compatibility functions must all be supported.

**Remediation:** Review load retention as well as pressure containment.

lessons.title: I20-L1
lessons.body:
## I20-L1

Why should a service transition briefing distinguish containment from restraint?

**Explained answer:** A seal does not necessarily restrain axial movement, and a grip does not necessarily contain pressure.

**Remediation:** Trace both functions for the selected service before applying its approved sequence.

lessons.title: I20-L2
lessons.body:
## I20-L2

Calculate the simple upward balance for 1800 psi, 4 square inches effective area and 6500 lbf downward load. Explain its limitation.

**Explained answer:** 7200 minus 6500 = 700 lbf upward. This omits other loads and does not authorize a restraint transfer.

**Remediation:** Show pressure times area and compare force direction, then identify the missing operational model.

lessons.title: I21-L1
lessons.body:
## I21-L1

Why should a subsea sketch show which equipment stays with the well after separation?

**Explained answer:** The retained well barrier and departing equipment contents/loads have different consequences.

**Remediation:** Draw the disconnect boundary rather than assuming every function remains below it.

lessons.title: I21-L2
lessons.body:
## I21-L2

A model gradient is 0.44 psi/ft at 1000 ft and internal pressure is 2200 psi on the same reference. Find the simple differential.

**Explained answer:** External 440 psi; differential 1760 psi. Reference and rating limitations still apply.

**Remediation:** Do not substitute pressure measured at another location without its column correction.

lessons.title: I22-L1
lessons.body:
## I22-L1

A tool connector is not qualified for the available cutting function. Does its brief presence at the cut plane remove the concern?

**Explained answer:** No. The affected transition needs a supported contingency and must not be authorized on duration alone.

**Remediation:** Separate probability arguments from actual emergency capability.

lessons.title: I22-L2
lessons.body:
## I22-L2

Why is a relatch indication not a complete post-disconnect restart check?

**Explained answer:** Required isolation, integrity, trapped volumes and operating conditions must also be verified and authorization obtained.

**Remediation:** List each required function rather than equating connection with readiness.


---

content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VUC006 — practical instruction and assessment packet
lessons.body:
# VUC006 — practical instruction and assessment packet

This packet uses fictional wells and a nonpressurized training console or simulator. It does not direct live-well operations. Classroom completion and equipment-operation endorsement are recorded separately. Never create a practical pass from attendance or a written examination alone.

lessons.title: Delivery preparation
lessons.body:
## Delivery preparation

Provide the supplied worksheets, calculator, blank schematics, clock and a simulator or inert training assembly for the relevant service. For an equipment-specific endorsement, the instructor also supplies the actual manufacturer's controlled operating procedure, component ratings, control diagram, test criteria and approved emergency sequence. These are necessary equipment inputs, not work for learners to invent. If they are unavailable, deliver the classroom exercises and record the operational endorsement as not assessed.

Use an assessor competent in the service and equipment being evaluated. Explain the exercise boundary, stop signal and safe training state. Never pressurize a demonstration assembly or introduce hazardous fluids to make a classroom exercise realistic. A simulation instructor can inject indications verbally or through software. No real customer's data or records are required.

Each station has five scored criteria: 0 = absent/unsafe; 1 = correct only after a prompt or with an unresolved omission; 2 = correct independently with supporting reasoning. Pass requires at least 8/10 and every critical criterion scored 2. A critical failure ends that attempt; restore the training state, teach the gap and assess a fresh attempt. Preserve both results. This is VNDRLY's assessment policy, not an external accreditation rule.

lessons.title: Station A — build the pressure model
lessons.body:
## Station A — build the pressure model

**Input card:** Well Alder-6: 6,000 ft TVD, 7,500 ft MD, full 9.5 ppg liquid column, verified communicating stabilized surface pressure 312 psi. Tubing ID 2.441 inches. The exercise assumes a single liquid column and no friction, gas or temperature correction. No field action is authorized.

**Learner tasks:** draw the pressure path and datum; calculate liquid head, simplified formation estimate and balancing density; calculate tubing internal volume; explain three conditions that would invalidate the result; state why a balance density is not a kill program.

**Assessor key:** 2,964 psi head; 3,276 psi estimate; 10.5 ppg balancing density; approximately 43.41 bbl nominal tubing volume. Accept volume within 0.1 bbl and pressure within 1 psi for rounding. Valid limitations include uncertain liquid level, gas, isolated gauge, unknown communication, temperature/density change and unmodelled friction. Do not accept “add a margin and pump” as an approved operational decision.

**Scored criteria:** correct TVD/MD use (critical); correct arithmetic and units; correct pressure-path assumptions (critical); accurate volume method; appropriate distinction between calculation and field authorization (critical).

**Remediation:** redraw the well with a deviated segment; have the learner explain why gravity uses height while volume uses length. Fresh variant: 5,000 ft TVD, 6,000 ft MD, 10 ppg full column and 260 psi verified communicating surface pressure. Key: 2,600 psi head, 2,860 psi estimate, 11 ppg balance.

lessons.title: Station B — detect and report an unexplained volume
lessons.body:
## Station B — detect and report an unexplained volume

**Input card:** Approved training displacement 0.006 bbl/ft; 500 ft pulled; expected tubing drainage remains unchanged. Fill measured 1.2 bbl. No transfer is logged. The operator is asked to pull another stand because the rig is behind schedule.

**Learner tasks:** calculate expected fill and discrepancy; identify possible causes without choosing an unsupported diagnosis; state the response boundary; deliver a concise radio report; begin an event log.

**Assessor key:** 3.0 bbl expected, 1.8 bbl short. The learner must call the discrepancy and use the approved response before continuing movement. Possible causes include influx, routing/meter error or an invalid drainage assumption. The message includes well, time, state, measurements, uncertainty and action. It must not say the well is safe because no gas is visible.

**Scored criteria:** accurate arithmetic; recognizes stop condition despite schedule pressure (critical); follows supplied response roles (critical); communicates verified facts; preserves the discrepancy in the log (critical).

**Fresh variant:** 400 ft, 0.005 bbl/ft, measured 2.7 bbl. Key: 2.0 expected, 0.7 excess. Excess also requires explanation; it is not automatically proof of influx or harmless overfill.

lessons.title: Station C — workover barrier transition
lessons.body:
## Station C — workover barrier transition

**Input card:** Synthetic diagram: tubing to reservoir; packer separating tubing/annulus; surface tubing isolation valve; annulus outlet; subsurface valve in tubing. Tubing gauge reads zero. Annulus pressure and packer integrity are unknown. Work instruction proposes releasing the packer and opening the tubing hanger. A second page says a tubing leak is suspected.

**Learner tasks:** annotate all potential paths, identify contradictions, mark the proposed transition, list evidence needed before release/opening, and brief the operator representative.

**Assessor key:** the learner must not treat the zero tubing gauge or subsurface valve as proof that all paths are isolated. Missing annulus and integrity evidence prevents the proposed opening. The diagram needs current verification, pressure communication and a staged barrier plan. Mechanical loading must be addressed as well as fluid containment.

**Scored criteria:** identifies separate tubing/annulus paths (critical); detects contradictory integrity information; preserves isolation during transition (critical); includes pressure and mechanical risks; gives an explicit hold and responsible decision owner (critical).

**Fresh variant:** supply a verified packer but an open bypass around two surface valves. The learner must find the bypass, not merely repeat the first answer.

lessons.title: Station D — wireline tool recovery and trapped pressure
lessons.body:
## Station D — wireline tool recovery and trapped pressure

**Input card:** A nonpressurized training stack schematic, manufacturer's relevant procedure, tool string drawing and pressure indications. The job gained a fishing tool after the lubricator-space check. Its position relative to the isolation valve is uncertain. A bleed gauge reads zero, but the simulated bleed passage is reported blocked.

**Learner tasks:** identify the line type and applicable sealing arrangement; distinguish pressure isolation from tool trapping; verify space and position; identify why the zero reading is insufficient; describe and, on the approved simulator, demonstrate the specified safe recovery contingency.

**Assessor key:** no closure through an unverified tool position, no connection opening to check pressure, no assumption that a trap is a pressure barrier. The learner requires a verified arrangement and pressure path before proceeding. Actual control order is scored against the supplied manufacturer procedure, not a generic order in this packet.

**Scored criteria:** correct component functions; confirms tool clearance (critical); verifies pressure communication (critical); uses approved contingency and control sequence (critical); communicates hold/recovery status.

**Fresh variant:** use a known tool position but a failed seal-support supply. Assess response to containment degradation instead of repeating the clearance problem.

lessons.title: Station E — coiled tubing readiness and failure response
lessons.body:
## Station E — coiled tubing readiness and failure response

**Input card:** Inert console with labelled stripper, ram functions, internal check device, injector and emergency controls; actual configuration procedure; synthetic string history; revised bottom-hole assembly containing a nonshearable section. Initial checks show controls move but the required sealing-test record is absent. During the simulation, the instructor reports stripper leakage.

**Learner tasks:** map internal and annular barriers; review string integrity and operating limits; mark the nonshearable interval; reject unsupported readiness; identify the approved response to leakage and demonstrate the permitted sequence on the simulator.

**Assessor key:** distinguish motion/function from sealing evidence. Identify where the emergency function cannot provide the assumed result. The learner must not blindly shear or move the string to a guessed position. Correct actions depend on the supplied configuration and approved contingency. Record the observed procedure steps and indications individually.

**Scored criteria:** maps both flow paths (critical); verifies string and equipment limits; identifies nonshearable position (critical); rejects missing test evidence (critical); demonstrates approved leakage response (critical).

**Fresh variant:** test evidence is valid, but injector control is lost. Use the separate approved contingency; do not reward reuse of an unrelated stripper response.

lessons.title: Station F — snubbing force and controlled transition
lessons.body:
## Station F — snubbing force and controlled transition

**Input card:** Simulator states effective pressure area 4.0 in², differential 2,000 psi, downward effective load 5,000 lbf. Actual equipment sequence and load limits are supplied separately. A tool joint is approaching a ram that seals only on pipe body. One slip-set indication becomes uncertain.

**Learner tasks:** calculate the simplified net force; identify pipe-light condition; state current load-bearing and pressure-containing elements; identify the transition restriction; demonstrate the approved hold/contingency without losing load or pressure control.

**Assessor key:** 8,000 lbf upward pressure force and 3,000 lbf net upward before omitted effects. No use of this simplified number as the equipment's required rated capacity. The learner must preserve verified restraint and containment; an uncertain indication is not confirmation. No improvised valve/slip sequence receives credit.

**Scored criteria:** correct force and units; identifies simplified-model limits; confirms load restraint (critical); preserves pressure containment around joint passage (critical); follows approved uncertainty contingency (critical).

**Fresh variant:** 3.0 in², 1,500 psi, 6,000 lbf downward effective load. Key: 4,500 upward, 1,500 net downward. The learner must still maintain control; pipe-heavy does not mean unrestricted motion.

lessons.title: Station G — kill-program review and return-system limits
lessons.body:
## Station G — kill-program review and return-system limits

**Input card:** A proposed instruction says “pump 10.5 ppg until quiet.” It provides no current fluid profile, return route, weak-point limit, surface processing capacity, pressure checkpoints or verification criteria. A diagram shows an unverified annulus path. The available pump can exceed one connected component's rated pressure.

**Learner tasks:** identify why the instruction is incomplete; prepare a request for specific engineering decisions; identify equipment/route constraints; set a pre-job hold; explain what evidence would be needed to assess completion without writing an unauthorized field procedure.

**Assessor key:** no approval based on density alone. Required decisions include verified pressure communication and fluid state, chosen method, injection/return alignment, operating envelope, applicable limits, compatible fluids, gas/solids handling, monitoring, contingencies and completion verification. Pump capability is not a permitted working limit.

**Scored criteria:** identifies unsupported pressure assumptions (critical); identifies route/weakest-component constraints (critical); includes surface processing; defines meaningful verification; refuses incomplete authorization while assigning resolution (critical).

**Fresh variant:** complete circulation plan, but return processing is unavailable after a maintenance change. Assess change control and readiness rather than density calculation.

lessons.title: Station H — emergency communication, handover and restart
lessons.body:
## Station H — emergency communication, handover and restart

**Input card:** Simulated unexplained annulus pressure rise; another contractor is pressure-testing nearby; radio traffic is congested; the shift changes in ten minutes. No diagnosis is confirmed. The relief crew asks whether it may resume normal work.

**Learner tasks:** announce and manage the simulated stop under the supplied site plan; use closed-loop communication; identify simultaneous-operation conflicts; write a handover; specify restart evidence and decision authority.

**Assessor key:** report facts and uncertainty, preserve restrictions, identify separate pressure sources and communicate with the responsible controllers. A shift change is not a restart criterion. No exposure to a suspected hazardous atmosphere or improvised rescue is acceptable. The handover states exact current condition and what remains prohibited.

**Scored criteria:** prompt response within role (critical); clear acknowledged communication; coordinated simultaneous-work control; truthful complete handover (critical); evidence-based authorized restart criteria (critical).

lessons.title: VUC008 — completion and subsea practical packet
lessons.body:
# VUC008 — completion and subsea practical packet

These five original stations supplement the eight embedded foundation stations. Use only inert/nonpressurized simulation. Supply calculator, blank schematic, observation form, event clock and the cards below. For equipment operation supply the real configuration's controlled drawings/procedures/limits and a competent service assessor. Never use live well exposure as a teaching fault.

Each criterion:0 absent/unsafe,1 correct after prompting or incomplete,2 independent and correct. Pass 8/10 with every **critical** criterion 2. A critical failure stops the attempt; restore the safe simulation, remediate and use a fresh variant. Keep failures and passes separately. Assessor answers are learning/practical rubrics, not the controlled written final.

lessons.title: P1 — annulus history and handover
lessons.body:
## P1 — annulus history and handover

**Input:** Fictional Cypress-8. Tubing gauge T=0; A-annulus readings 140,195,260 psi at 09:00/09:10/09:20. B=0. The mock operating plan requires a hold/escalation above 240 psi. Temperature and gauge communication are not yet verified. A supervisor's draft log says “thermal, all clear.” The next shift plans a completion opening.

**Tasks:** draw the three observation compartments; mark verified facts/uncertainties; identify the threshold event; give a closed-loop report; correct the handover without deleting the original evidence. Explain why the opening cannot rely on “all clear.”

**Expected performance:** actual A exceedance is 260−240=20 psi; zero T/B does not establish A isolation. Temperature-only cause is unproven. Follow the mock hold/escalation and prohibit the affected opening pending approved disposition. Record time, location, readings, uncertainty, restriction and responsible follow-up.

**Criteria:** accurate compartment drawing; preserves all readings; identifies threshold/hold **critical**; rejects unsupported diagnosis **critical**; communicates handover/restrictions **critical**.

**Fresh variant:** A stays below its threshold but its gauge is discovered isolated; assess loss of trustworthy observation rather than threshold arithmetic. The correct result is “unknown,” not a manufactured exceedance or all-clear.

lessons.title: P2 — test direction, communication and changed components
lessons.body:
## P2 — test direction, communication and changed components

**Input:** two-chamber inert model. Lower simulated pressure 2800 psi; planned upper state 600 psi. Plug P separates them. The available chart used pressure from above. The gauge branch is later reported closed. A tool movement has disturbed the plug after that chart. Mock test instructions require verified communication and no replenishment during the defined observation; no actual pressure is applied.

**Tasks:** draw direction/differential; identify why the chart does not establish present readiness; mark the gauge observation invalid; specify the evidence needed from the controlled test plan; respond to an injected fluid-addition event in the mock retest log.

**Expected performance:**2200 psi toward upper chamber in the stated model. Direction, communication and post-test disturbance independently matter. Preserve the chart but do not accept it for present reliance. An addition under no-replenishment criteria invalidates that attempt; record it and follow test disposition. No instruction to open a pressurized fitting is acceptable.

**Criteria:** calculation/reference; direction-specific reasoning **critical**; gauge communication **critical**; changed-state verification **critical**; truthful test disposition/record.

**Fresh variant:** lower 3200,upper 800→2400 psi, with a valid gauge but an unrecorded bypass. Learner must identify the new path rather than repeat the previous gauge diagnosis.

lessons.title: P3 — service transition and role responsibility
lessons.body:
## P3 — service transition and role responsibility

**Setup:** choose the discipline to be endorsed. Use its embedded model card and actual configured simulator for operator endorsement. Give the written contingency before the exercise; do not ask a learner to invent an equipment sequence.

**Wireline card:** usable chamber 4.8 m; required clearance 0.4 m; original tool 4.1 m; added item 0.5 m. Required 5.0 m, excess 0.2 m. Tool-retention indicator is available; chamber pressure communication is not. Hold opening/movement requiring unproven geometry or pressure. A trap is not pressure isolation.

**CT card:** annular seal reports verified; internal check-function evidence is missing. Stripper-support pressure then becomes unavailable in the simulator. Follow the approved contingency, control both paths and verify the required response. No assumption that a sent command equals sealed.

**Snubbing card:** model 2500 psi×3in²=7500 lbf upward; effective downward load 6200 lbf, balance 1300 lbf upward. During planned restraint transfer, one grip's feedback becomes unavailable. Hold under the configured contingency; do not release the verified restraint because an unverified grip is assumed effective. Arithmetic omits other loads and is not a capacity selection.

**Role tasks:** assistant identifies the abnormal state, reports it and carries out only the permitted support task. Operator performs the supplied configured response, with read-back and verification. Supervisor identifies the scope/change decision, coordinates interfaces and states the evidence/authority needed for restart. Score only the role demonstrated; record other roles not assessed.

**Criteria:** identifies service-specific paths/geometry; recognizes fault **critical**; applies correct role and configured response **critical**; verifies rather than assumes control/restraint **critical**; truthful handover and restart restriction.

**Fresh variants:** wireline geometry passes but sealing support fails; CT external control fails while internal evidence is valid; snubbing known grips but changed force direction. Use actual configured procedures. Do not simply repeat the first fault with a new name.

lessons.title: P4 — subsea interface and pressure references
lessons.body:
## P4 — subsea interface and pressure references

**Input:** fictional Reef-8, formation 7200 ft below surface reference; wellhead 1200 ft below it; uniform 10 ppg liquid. Model seawater gradient 0.445 psi/ft; component internal pressure 2600 psi on same reference. Provide three functional cards: riserless lubricator, open-water intervention riser, through-BOP landing string. Each card has a well-retained section, disconnect boundary and vessel-retained section; learner draws the appropriate pressure/tool/control paths from the supplied configured diagram.

**Tasks:** mark retained/departing functions and contents; calculate surface-to-formation and wellhead-to-formation head; calculate model external pressure/differential; identify two hazards of transferring another system's emergency sequence; describe an apparent hydrate blockage without assuming it is safe isolation.

**Expected:**3744 psi full head;3120 psi below wellhead;624 psi upper-column contribution; external 534 psi; simple differential 2066 psi. A wrong reference or unverified path invalidates application. Correct discussion includes actual interfaces, geometry, control authority, trapped contents and vessel/well interaction. The functional drawing is not an approved stack arrangement.

**Criteria:** draws retained/departing functions **critical**; correct pressure datums **critical**; arithmetic/units; identifies configuration-specific sequence **critical**; blockage/contents risk reasoning.

**Fresh variant:** formation 6500,wellhead 1500,9 ppg→3042 total,2340 below,702 upper; external 667.5; internal 2400→1732.5 differential. Same conceptual standard, no memorized numbers.

lessons.title: P5 — emergency capability, loss of feedback and restart
lessons.body:
## P5 — emergency capability, loss of feedback and restart

**Setup:** configured nonpressurized subsea simulator, controlled emergency procedure, rated tool/cut data, position sheet, control-power diagram and mock marine-response plan. Mark fictional section M cuttable and connection N not qualified. Primary/backup controls are initially shown sharing a supply. Do not derive an actual cut sequence from this exercise text.

**Injection 1:** N is at the cut plane during a proposed transition. **Expected:** mark capability unavailable for that geometry, hold readiness and require the approved contingency; no inferred shearability.

**Injection 2:** a predefined marine trigger occurs after the approved training configuration is restored. The configured command is sent but confirmation is absent. **Expected:** follow the supplied missing-confirmation response, distinguish command from verified result, communicate with the marine/well teams, and recognize the shared supply as a common-cause vulnerability where applicable. The instructor supplies actual backup-state evidence rather than requiring guesses.

**Injection 3:** connection is restored; lower isolation verification remains absent. **Expected:** no affected restart merely because the connector relatched; establish required barrier/equipment/test evidence and designated authorization.

**Criteria:** geometry/capability check **critical**; correct configured emergency response **critical**; recognizes common cause and feedback uncertainty **critical**; coordinated timed report; restoration evidence/restriction **critical**.

**Fresh variant:** qualified cutting geometry but secondary feedback disagrees with the primary indication. Assess uncertainty resolution and configured contingency, not automatic preference for whichever display permits work.

lessons.title: VUC006 — functional simulator workbook
lessons.body:
# VUC006 — functional simulator workbook

This workbook teaches verification and sequencing on a **fictional, nonpressurized teaching model**. It is not a procedure for a live well or an actual manufacturer's unit. Buttons represent states, not real hydraulic valves. The model intentionally refuses unsafe transitions so the instructor can expose reasoning errors without applying pressure or moving machinery.

lessons.title: Model board and starting conditions
lessons.body:
## Model board and starting conditions

Draw five boxes: SOURCE, LOWER ISOLATION, TOOL CHAMBER, UPPER CONTAINMENT and CONTROL PANEL. Connect SOURCE to LOWER ISOLATION, then TOOL CHAMBER, then UPPER CONTAINMENT. Add a separate, controlled chamber equalization/recovery route to a labelled closed collection box. The instructor assigns all pressure indications. Use cards for VERIFIED/UNVERIFIED, TOOL CLEAR/TOOL CROSSING, RESTRAINT CONFIRMED/UNKNOWN and CONTROL ENERGY AVAILABLE/LOST.

The source pressure is an arbitrary classroom indication of 100 units; no physical pressure is applied. A second card identifies the pressure in the chamber. The fictitious lower isolation is permitted to close only when TOOL CLEAR is independently confirmed. The chamber may be declared accessible only when lower isolation is confirmed effective, its pressure communication is verified, chamber pressure is confirmed zero and no external pressure source communicates with it. UPPER CONTAINMENT may be declared open only in that accessible state. These are model rules, not real valve instructions.

Use tokens to represent command, indication and verification separately. The learner issues a command; the instructor supplies an indication; the learner must request the relevant verification. This prevents a common misconception: assuming a requested state has been achieved. A pending or contradictory indication leaves the transition incomplete.

### Exercise 1: prepare an entry

Starting state: lower isolation verified effective; chamber pressure zero with communication verified; tool completely in chamber; upper containment not yet verified. The learner must identify that source access cannot be accepted until the specified containment and configuration checks are complete. Have the learner label the containment boundary, confirm tool fit and identify the pressure recovery destination. Only then does the instructor issue the VERIFIED upper-containment card.

Next, the instructor states that the model's approved equalization has made chamber pressure equal to source pressure. The learner records both indications and verifies the intended communication. The instructor then permits the lower-isolation OPEN state, after which the learner moves the tool card to TOOL CROSSING. Ask which element can no longer be assumed closable on clear bore. The answer is the lower isolation; the tool is crossing its boundary. Continue only under the model's verified upper containment.

**Failure injection:** give a zero chamber gauge while a pressure-source card remains connected. The learner must reject the contradictory state, not proceed because the gauge looks favorable. Debrief how isolated gauges and wrong reference points can mislead.

### Exercise 2: recover without trapping an assumption

Starting state: tool crossing lower isolation; upper containment verified; chamber communicates with source. The learner must establish complete tool recovery into the chamber and independent clearance before requesting lower isolation closure. The instructor supplies the closure indication but withholds verification until requested. After effective isolation is confirmed, the learner identifies the approved controlled recovery route and records the instructor's simulated depressurization result.

The learner must verify pressure communication and absence of another source before declaring the chamber accessible. Only then may the upper-containment card be changed to OPEN. Score each distinction: tool position, isolation, recovery route, pressure state and communication. A learner who jumps directly from “closed” to “safe to open” repeats the exercise with a blocked-gauge injection.

**Failure injection:** the simulated recovery route is blocked. Chamber indication becomes UNKNOWN even if one gauge says zero. The correct outcome is a hold and use of the model contingency: retain containment, mark the uncertainty, isolate the exercise and request instructor/technical resolution. There is no “crack the connection” option.

### Exercise 3: internal and external paths

Add an INNER TUBE through the chamber with its own source connection and verified internal check element. The upper containment surrounds the tube but does not close its bore. Ask learners to trace a leak through each path separately. Then mark the internal check UNVERIFIED while the external containment remains VERIFIED. The learner must explain why the assembly cannot be declared controlled solely from the external seal.

Replace the tool card with NONSHEARABLE AT EMERGENCY POSITION. The model's shear function is now unavailable. Require the learner to explain that a command cannot create an equipment capability. Restore the exercise only through a revised instructor-approved model configuration, not by pretending the non-shearable card is ordinary tubing.

### Exercise 4: restraint during a pressure-containing transition

Add two fictional restraint tokens, A and B, and an UPWARD LOAD card. At least one verified, appropriately capable restraint must remain effective throughout the transition. The model permits changing a restraint only after the alternative is independently verified to carry the stated load. The instructor changes an indication to UNKNOWN immediately after a command. The learner must hold rather than release the previously verified restraint.

Now change the load to DOWNWARD. Ask whether restraint is still needed. The correct answer is yes; uncontrolled downward movement is also a loss of control. Repeat with a tool-joint card at the pressure boundary and require simultaneous tracking of load control and containment. Success in one column does not compensate for failure in the other.

lessons.title: Model observation worksheet
lessons.body:
## Model observation worksheet

| Step | Command/request | Indication | Independent verification | Remaining containment | Remaining restraint | Continue/hold and why |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| | | | | | | |

The instructor records the exact step where a learner relied on an assumption. Debrief with three questions: What did you know? What did you assume? What evidence was necessary before the next transition?

lessons.title: Bridge to actual equipment assessment
lessons.body:
## Bridge to actual equipment assessment

After the functional exercises, compare the model with the actual supplied manufacturer diagram. Mark every difference: extra pressure paths, valve functions, fail positions, energy supplies, trapping volumes, geometry and emergency capabilities. Do not transfer model button order to a real console. The actual equipment station uses the actual approved procedure and limits, as specified in the practical packet.

A classroom model pass demonstrates the reasoning observed in that model. It cannot be recorded as a live-equipment or manufacturer-specific operating pass. This distinction must appear in the learner's record.


---

courses.title: VUC008 | VUC006 — service model cards

content.title: VUC008 | VUC006 — service model cards
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC006 — service model cards
lessons.body:
# VUC006 — service model cards

These original diagrams are functional teaching models, not installation drawings or operating sequences. Lines represent possible communication; labels describe functions. They do not specify valve order, rated capacity or a safe field lineup. Use cards with S04 and S06–S09, then use the actual controlled equipment diagram for any equipment-specific assessment.

lessons.title: Card W — completion and workover
lessons.body:
## Card W — completion and workover

```text
                         TUBING GAUGE T
                               |
                      surface tubing valve
                               |
                       tubing to reservoir
                               |
                     subsurface tubing valve
                               |
                +--------- packer ---------+
                |                         |
         annulus below packer      annulus above packer
                |                         |
             reservoir             annulus outlet A
```

The drawing separates a tubing route from an outside-tubing route. The packer is shown as a separation function; its actual sealing and mechanical condition are not established by its symbol. Give each learner four markers: VERIFIED, UNVERIFIED, FAILED and NOT APPLICABLE. They must assign markers from evidence cards, not guess from the drawing.

**Initial evidence:** T reads zero; no current A reading; a tubing leak has been reported; packer status is unknown. The proposed work opens the tubing hanger. **Task:** trace which uncertainties could expose that opening. **Teaching answer:** the zero reading does not characterize all communicating compartments. The suspected tubing leak can invalidate the clean separation assumed in a simple drawing. Before the transition, the approved isolation plan must address the actual pressure paths and load state.

**Change card:** an authorized investigation confirms packer integrity but identifies a bypass around the surface isolation. Have the learner redraw that bypass. The revised issue is not “the packer is bad”; it is that the credited isolation excludes a real path. Correct technical reasoning must change when evidence changes.

lessons.title: Card L — wireline functions
lessons.body:
## Card L — wireline functions

```text
                 line / cable
                      |
          moving-line sealing function
                      |
             tool-containing chamber
              [tool position unknown]
                      |
            well isolation function
                      |
                  well source

  chamber measurement ---- chamber
  controlled discharge --- chamber
  tool retention function: locate from actual model drawing
```

The chamber must contain the actual tool assembly while the required isolation function is available. It is not enough that the tool's nominal length is shorter than a nominal chamber length. Connections, adapters and usable clearances affect the comparison. The functional positions in this model do not prescribe an installed stack.

**Geometry exercise:** the fictional drawing supplies 4.2 m usable chamber space and requires 0.3 m additional clearance. The original assembly is 3.7 m; an added component increases it by 0.4 m. The new required space is 4.4 m, exceeding the supplied usable space by 0.2 m. Do not attempt to close an isolation device across the tool to force a fit.

**Pressure exercise:** chamber measurement reads zero, but the measurement passage is blocked. The reading cannot establish chamber pressure. Have the learner mark the chamber UNVERIFIED and explain why a tool-retention device does not solve the pressure-verification problem.

lessons.title: Card C — coiled-tubing internal and external paths
lessons.body:
## Card C — coiled-tubing internal and external paths

```text
    pumping / internal control               movement control
               |                                  |
          tubing bore                        injector function
               |                                  |
       internal check function          continuous tubing body
               |                                  |
             well                   annular sealing / control
                                                  |
                                                 well
```

Place separate colored traces on the bore and outside-tubing routes. Preventing reverse flow inside the bore is not the same as sealing outside the tubing. Gripping tubing controls movement; it does not establish that either fluid route is isolated. A shear function, if present and qualified for the exact location/material, must be considered together with the subsequent containment state.

**Position exercise:** the fictional location display says a connection is 0.2 m above an emergency cutting plane, with uncertainty ±0.5 m. The connection is outside the verified shear envelope. The uncertainty interval overlaps the cutting plane. A nominal positive separation is not evidence of clearance. The learner must identify the unsupported emergency assumption and preserve the hold while the approved contingency is established.

**Change card:** the displayed position becomes reliable, but required sealing evidence remains absent. Readiness is still not demonstrated. This checks that the learner does not let one corrected defect conceal another.

lessons.title: Card S — snubbing load and pressure functions
lessons.body:
## Card S — snubbing load and pressure functions

```text
          upward pressure-force arrow
                       ↑
                 tubular body
           restraint function R1
           movement function M
           restraint function R2
            pressure function P
                       |
                   well source
                       ↓
          effective downward-load arrow
```

This deliberately nongeometric diagram separates functions; it does not show their installation order. Use the equipment's actual drawing to locate them. Learners must identify both the load-bearing state and pressure-containing state at every simulated hold point.

**Evidence exercise:** R1 indicates HOLD but its independent confirmation is missing. R2 is marked RELEASED. M has been asked to move. P remains verified. The required conclusion is not “pressure is controlled, so move.” Load control is unverified. The learner calls the hold, reports the exact state and follows the approved equipment contingency.

**Transition exercise:** a joint is approaching a component approved only for pipe-body sealing. Ask the learner to identify the geometric conflict and name the evidence required for the approved transition. Do not accept an invented alternating-open sequence. Assessment of actual control actions uses the controlled equipment procedure and an inert/simulated configuration.

lessons.title: Individual model interpretation record
lessons.body:
## Individual model interpretation record

For each card, record: (1) traced pressure paths; (2) assigned function of each element; (3) facts versus unknowns; (4) numerical/geometry result where supplied; (5) justified hold or readiness conclusion. Score each 0–2, requiring 8/10 and no authorization to open, move or exceed an envelope on unverified evidence. Record the learner's explanation, not only a check mark.

Use the model cards for instruction. Do not count repeating the printed teaching answer as independent final performance. Independent assessment uses a changed evidence set and the protected final material.


---
