lessons.title: VUC010 — supervisor technical decisions
lessons.body:
# VUC010 — supervisor technical decisions

These original chapters extend the worker foundation and six supervisor decision lessons. They teach oversight, planning and verification. They do not qualify the learner to perform electrical work, approve engineered safeguards, drive industrial trucks or lead specialist emergency response without the separate required competence and authority.

lessons.title: M17 — Verify energy control and safeguarding through the whole task
lessons.body:
## M17 — Verify energy control and safeguarding through the whole task

A supervisor must understand the work boundary well enough to obtain competent decisions. “Maintenance is handling it” is not a complete coordination plan if production can still operate connected equipment. Identify the exact asset, task, affected people, connected sources and who controls each decision. Distinguish normal operation, setup, cleaning, fault finding and servicing. Different steps can expose different hazards even during one work order.

Start the planning discussion with the authorized servicer and affected workers. Ask them to explain the equipment identity and applicable controlled procedure; identify electrical, pneumatic, hydraulic, gravity, thermal and stored mechanical sources. Ask what verifies the safe state and what would require reverification. The supervisor does not substitute personal confidence for the qualified person's electrical testing or the authorized person's energy-control steps. Record who supplies the evidence and which operations remain prohibited.

Electrical isolation and machine energy control overlap but are not identical. A motor circuit can be deenergized while a connected pneumatic cylinder remains capable of movement. Conversely, a mechanically restrained machine may still have an energized cabinet. Electrical verification requires the applicable qualified work practice; pressing stop or observing no motion is not equivalent. Refer to the embedded G04/G07 sources and instruction for the separate boundaries.

**Worked case:** Packing lineP7 and feederF2 share a control system. The work order says “repairP7” and the diagram shows a separate disconnect, but compressed air and a gravity-fed chute remain connected. Production proposes runningF2 during repair. The supervisor holds the conflicting plan until competent personnel establish the actual isolation and interface. The question is not merely whetherF2 can run; it is whether its operation can defeat the protected state or introduce material/energy intoP7. A separate asset name does not prove independence.

Group work and shift changes need continuity. Identify how each worker remains protected, how status is communicated and how the employer's authorized procedure transfers control. Do not instruct a replacement worker to copy initials or remove an absent worker's lock. Document the unresolved state honestly and obtain the designated process. During temporary testing or repositioning, the applicable procedure governs clearing people/tools, changing the energy state and restoring protection. A supervisor's deadline is not an alternate procedure.

Guarding review begins with the exposure path: point of operation, rotating or nip points, thrown material and bystanders. When production changes feedstock, tool, speed or access, ask whether the existing safeguard still performs its intended function. A signed inspection from last week is not proof for a modified setup. Controls must remain effective during foreseeable access/cleaning as well as normal feeding. Specialist design or validation belongs with qualified personnel.

**Practice:** An interlocked access door causes frequent stoppages. A supervisor is asked to authorize temporary defeat until the new switch arrives. **Explained answer:** reject the bypassed operating state. Determine and correct the cause through authorized maintenance and an approved safe alternative if one exists. Assess production/work arrangements so employees are not pressured to improvise. “Temporary” does not define a protective function.

**Verification exercise:** Write a restart evidence list forP7: correct asset/configuration, completed authorized work, required guards restored/verified, energy-control restoration by the responsible personnel, affected-worker notification and supported safe production conditions. If one item is unknown, record it as unknown with an owner; do not sign a blanket ready status.

lessons.title: M18 — Plan emergencies and PPE for changing work
lessons.body:
## M18 — Plan emergencies and PPE for changing work

Emergency planning must remain usable during maintenance, night shifts and contractor work. Identify how people receive an alarm, how they leave or shelter under the applicable plan, how they are counted and which designated people perform special duties. Verify that temporary work has not blocked routes, changed assembly access or made the alarm ineffective for part of the workforce. Include visitors, temporary workers and people needing an accessible arrangement. Do not assume a posted map proves everyone can use it.

**Worked case:** A packaging facility temporarily closes corridorN during construction. Day staff use an alternate route, but the night cleaning contractor still has the old map. The supervisor coordinates a revised route, communicates it in an understandable format, verifies the physical path and rehearses a tabletop alarm/accountability. Updating the map without telling the contractor leaves the actual failure in place. The contractor must also communicate hazards its cleaning work introduces.

Fire prevention examines combustible loading, ignition sources, storage and work interactions. A hot-work request near a flammable-material transfer cannot be accepted by reviewing two permits independently. Identify common airspaces, spark travel, ventilation, nearby openings and changing conditions; obtain the competent task-specific decision. This course does not supply a universal hot-work distance or override the site program. A fire-watch assignment without training, equipment, authority and the required period of coverage is not a complete control.

Do not silently expand employee firefighting roles. If the employer's policy is evacuation, a supervisor should not direct an untrained person to try an extinguisher because the incident is embarrassing or production is important. If designated response is part of the actual program, establish required competence, equipment, safe conditions and escape. Exercise accountability and emergency communications without a live fire. Preserve failed drill observations and correct their causes rather than recording everyone as successful.

PPE oversight starts with the task hazard assessment, then appropriate selection, fit, condition, training and compatibility. A purchase order is not proof that the PPE works for the task. Substituting a chemical, glove, face protection or work method may invalidate the previous selection. Ensure affected workers understand when protection is needed, how to use it, its limitations and care/replacement. Verify actual use in a safe demonstration rather than only asking whether a training box is checked.

**Practice:** A new eyewear model fits under a face shield but interferes with required hearing protection. **Explained answer:** review the combined arrangement and actual hazard requirements; obtain compatible protection without silently dropping one function. A supervisor cannot resolve the conflict by telling workers to choose whichever is most comfortable while exposed.

**Drill review exercise:** An alarm exercise shows a contractor missing from the list and a worker waiting at the old assembly area. Treat both as system findings. Revise roster ownership and route communication, then verify with the affected groups. Do not punish reporting or rewrite the first drill as a clean pass. A successful retest does not erase the original evidence.

lessons.title: M19 — Design handling and traffic arrangements around real work
lessons.body:
## M19 — Design handling and traffic arrangements around real work

A supervisor should examine the reason people and loads meet, not just order them to pay more attention. Map receiving, storage, picking, replenishment, waste removal and exits. Observe different shifts and peak deliveries. Identify crossing frequency, blind areas, unstable loads, dock interfaces and tasks that require awkward force or reach. Include workers' knowledge of shortcuts; a repeated shortcut may reveal that the designated method is impractical or unavailable.

Prefer removing unnecessary crossings and awkward handling. Relocating a frequently used supply point can reduce exposure more directly than repeating a warning. Check the change for storage compatibility, fire access, floor/rack capacity and replenishment. Physical separation is useful only if it remains effective when doors open, pallets accumulate or another contractor arrives. A gate left open all shift may defeat a carefully drawn pedestrian route.

Truck operators need appropriate equipment/workplace training and evaluation; supervisors verify evidence rather than treat a general certificate as a universal license. A new truck type, attachment, route or task can require additional evaluation under the employer's program. This orientation does not teach or assess driving. If operator competence or equipment condition is uncertain, hold the operation and obtain the responsible qualified decision. Do not borrow an unqualified employee to clear a problem caused by poor planning.

Dock and trailer work adds interfaces: vehicle movement, platform/leveler condition, load stability, edge exposure and communication between driver and dock team. The site's approved method defines restraint/chocking, capacity and verification as applicable. A supervisor should know who confirms readiness and what stops the transfer. Do not substitute a generic checklist for the actual vehicle/equipment arrangement.

**Worked layout:** Workers retrieve cartons40times per shift across a delivery lane. Moving the supply point reduces planned crossings to8. That is32fewer, or80percent reduction in this fictional frequency. It does not make the remaining crossings safe or account for new restocking trips. Observe the actual revised work and apply a controlled crossing arrangement for the residual exposure. Counts are evidence of frequency, not a calculated injury probability.

Storage changes need competent review. A struck rack, new load shape or higher stack can invalidate prior assumptions. Keep people out of the threatened zone; obtain authorized inspection/stabilization and required technical assessment. A supervisor should not instruct workers to climb, push or unload an unstable arrangement without a supported method. Document disposition and verification before reopening the area.

**Practice:** A more compact storage layout reduces walking distance but forces workers to lift18kgpackages from floor to shoulder height with no grips. **Explained answer:** evaluate the whole task—reach, height, grip, force, repetition, route and assistance. Consider changing shelf height, packaging, access or mechanical aid. Reduced walking alone does not establish lower overall risk.

**Worker consultation exercise:** Ask two fictional shift representatives why crossings occur, show the proposed plan, record one objection and revise it. A valid objection might identify that night restocking uses the new pedestrian area. The supervisor must resolve that interaction, not dismiss it because day-shift observations looked good.

lessons.title: M20 — Approve chemical, charging and ergonomic changes with evidence
lessons.body:
## M20 — Approve chemical, charging and ergonomic changes with evidence

A change can reduce one hazard while introducing another. Replacing a cleaner may reduce odor but increase flammability or affect gloves, ventilation, storage and waste handling. Replacing a manual task with powered equipment may change traffic, charging and maintenance needs. Before approval, identify the old assumptions, new exposures, affected people and required competent reviews. Set a trial/verification plan and explicit stop conditions; do not discover incompatibility by exposing workers first.

For a chemical substitution, obtain actual product identity/SDS and use conditions, not only a supplier's marketing description. Review quantity, transfer method, temperature, incompatibilities, ventilation, ignition, exposure routes, PPE and emergency response. Confirm labels, information access and worker training before the change is used. A less hazardous classification in one category does not prove the whole task is safer. Industrial-hygiene support may be needed to assess representative exposure and control effectiveness.

**Worked case:** CleanerA uses an existing exhaust arrangement and glove selection. CleanerB is proposed because it has less odor. Its fictional safety information identifies a new flammability concern, and compatibility with the old gloves is unknown. Hold approval until the relevant exposure/ignition/PPE/storage review is complete. Do not ask a worker to test a small amount during production. Record what evidence supports the final choice and what remains prohibited.

Powered-truck charging or fueling is a distinct work activity. It can introduce electrical, chemical, fire, ventilation and manual-handling hazards. Identify the actual battery/fuel technology and manufacturer's requirements; do not apply instructions for one chemistry to another. Keep the charging arrangement within the employer's assessed program, with designated trained people, suitable equipment and emergency provisions. A spare outlet in a convenient aisle is not a charging-site approval.

**Charging exercise:** A proposed truck charger occupies the emergency route and uses an unverified electrical supply. The operator says the plug fits. The supervisor rejects the location/supply assumption and obtains competent electrical and operational review. Verify access, ventilation and technology-specific requirements before use. No worker is instructed to modify wiring or open a battery during this course.

Ergonomic change review compares actual exposures before and after. Moving a container closer may reduce reach but obstruct an exit or create a pinch point. A powered aid may reduce lifting while introducing pushing, crushing or traffic exposure. Include representative workers, trial the approved arrangement safely and record task frequency, force/reach observations and worker feedback. Symptoms require appropriate reporting/care; a supervisor should not diagnose or dismiss them.

**Practice:** Two jobs alternate every hour, but both require the same wrist force and shoulder reach. **Explained answer:** rotation has not necessarily reduced the relevant exposure. Change the task geometry, tools, assistance or work pattern so the exposure actually changes, then verify. Do not rely on the word “rotation” as evidence.

**Change-release exercise:** Complete five statements: what changed; hazards and assumptions affected; who reviewed each specialist issue; what evidence verifies readiness; and what condition triggers stop/review. For CleanerB, include the unresolved glove evidence and ignition conflict as hold points. For the charging area, include the blocked route and supply review. A decision is complete only when its actual evidence and restrictions are clear.


---

courses.title: VUC010 | VUC009 formative checks

content.title: VUC010 | VUC009 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC009 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC009 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Explain corrected reasoning after each error.

lessons.title: G01-L1
lessons.body:
## G01-L1

Rewrite “unsafe shop” as a useful report about a missing conveyor guard.

**Explained answer:** Identify the machine/location, exposed moving part, people at risk, time and immediate warning/hold; request responsible correction.

**Correction/remediation:** Facts and exposure make the report actionable without unsupported blame.

lessons.title: G01-L2
lessons.body:
## G01-L2

Why are a hazard complaint and a retaliation complaint not interchangeable?

**Explained answer:** They address different events and processes; one does not automatically file the other and deadlines may differ.

**Correction/remediation:** Use the official relevant route promptly rather than waiting on an unrelated process.

lessons.title: G02-L1
lessons.body:
## G02-L1

A ladder user must lean far sideways to finish. What should happen?

**Explained answer:** Stop, descend and reposition or select suitable access; do not compensate by leaning or asking someone to hold an unsuitable setup.

**Correction/remediation:** Keep the body/task within the safe access arrangement.

lessons.title: G02-L2
lessons.body:
## G02-L2

Why is moving a hose from a walkway into a vehicle crossing not necessarily correction?

**Explained answer:** It may transfer exposure to a traffic conflict; verify the whole route and control arrangement.

**Correction/remediation:** A changed object location is not proof that people are protected.

lessons.title: G03-L1
lessons.body:
## G03-L1

A missing coworker was last seen near smoke. What information should you give at assembly?

**Explained answer:** Name/last known location and time, observed conditions and uncertainty; do not re-enter as an untrained rescuer.

**Correction/remediation:** Accountability needs facts, not assumed rescue or an invented all-clear.

lessons.title: G03-L2
lessons.body:
## G03-L2

Does an accessible extinguisher automatically mean you should fight a fire?

**Explained answer:** No; employer policy, designated training, fire conditions and safe escape govern.

**Correction/remediation:** A device nearby is not authorization or competence.

lessons.title: G04-L1
lessons.body:
## G04-L1

Why is a stopped machine not proof that its cabinet is electrically safe?

**Explained answer:** Electrical supply and exposed parts may remain energized; required isolation/verification belongs to qualified authorized work.

**Correction/remediation:** Separate machine motion from electrical state.

lessons.title: G04-L2
lessons.body:
## G04-L2

A protective device trips repeatedly. What is the worker-level response?

**Explained answer:** Stop using the affected equipment, report and obtain qualified evaluation; do not keep resetting to finish.

**Correction/remediation:** Repeated trips may indicate a fault rather than an inconvenience.

lessons.title: G05-L1
lessons.body:
## G05-L1

A glove is thicker than the old model. Is that enough to approve it for a chemical?

**Explained answer:** No; the actual chemical/task compatibility, service conditions, fit and manufacturer information are needed.

**Correction/remediation:** Thickness alone does not determine resistance.

lessons.title: G05-L2
lessons.body:
## G05-L2

What is wrong with treating a user seal check as a replacement for required fit testing?

**Explained answer:** They serve different purposes; fit testing and other program requirements remain necessary where applicable.

**Correction/remediation:** Review selection, medical evaluation, fit and use as separate requirements.

lessons.title: G06-L1
lessons.body:
## G06-L1

An unlabeled bottle left by another shift smells familiar. Can it be used?

**Explained answer:** No; resolve identity and hazard information through the responsible process without sniffing or guessing.

**Correction/remediation:** Familiarity is not reliable identification.

lessons.title: G06-L2
lessons.body:
## G06-L2

For mock ClearSolv-T, why do goggles not solve a nearby ignition source and failed ventilation?

**Explained answer:** They protect a different exposure; ignition and airborne hazards require their own effective controls.

**Correction/remediation:** Map each control to the actual hazard it interrupts.

lessons.title: G07-L1
lessons.body:
## G07-L1

Name two energy hazards that can remain after electrical power is isolated.

**Explained answer:** Examples include trapped hydraulic/pneumatic pressure, gravity load, spring energy or heat.

**Correction/remediation:** Identify actual sources in the machine rather than assuming electricity is the only one.

lessons.title: G07-L2
lessons.body:
## G07-L2

What should an affected employee do when a maintenance lock remains after shift change?

**Explained answer:** Do not remove/bypass/start; contact responsible authorized personnel and follow the documented handover/restoration process.

**Correction/remediation:** A shift boundary does not erase protection.

lessons.title: G08-L1
lessons.body:
## G08-L1

A guard is removed to fit a larger accessory. What two issues need correction?

**Explained answer:** Missing guarding and tool/accessory compatibility; stop the altered setup and obtain suitable authorized correction.

**Correction/remediation:** PPE does not restore either function.

lessons.title: G08-L2
lessons.body:
## G08-L2

Why can normal operation and jam clearing require different controls?

**Explained answer:** Clearing may expose moving/stored energy or require entering the danger zone; servicing decisions must address that changed task.

**Correction/remediation:** Do not assume a brief task remains normal operation.

lessons.title: G09-L1
lessons.body:
## G09-L1

Why does a general safety course not authorize forklift driving?

**Explained answer:** Truck operation requires its own equipment/workplace training and evaluation; this course is pedestrian/recognition orientation.

**Correction/remediation:** Credential scope must match what was actually assessed.

lessons.title: G09-L2
lessons.body:
## G09-L2

Why is package weight alone insufficient to decide whether a lift is safe?

**Explained answer:** Grip, reach, height, route, frequency, posture and assistance also affect exposure.

**Correction/remediation:** Evaluate the complete handling task.

lessons.title: G10-L1
lessons.body:
## G10-L1

Ventilation fails but the air looks clear. What should guide the decision?

**Explained answer:** The prescribed control is unavailable; hold affected exposure and obtain correction/assessment rather than rely on appearance.

**Correction/remediation:** Invisible hazards remain possible.

lessons.title: G10-L2
lessons.body:
## G10-L2

A hot worker becomes confused. What is the appropriate priority?

**Explained answer:** Activate emergency response and trained cooling/care, stay with the person and do not continue work or leave them alone.

**Correction/remediation:** Severe symptoms are an emergency, not a fitness test.


---

courses.title: VUC010 | VUC010 supervisor formative checks

content.title: VUC010 | VUC010 supervisor formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC010 supervisor formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC010 supervisor formative checks

Attempt first, then explain and correct any error. The twenty G-domain checks are embedded separately.

lessons.title: M11-L1
lessons.body:
## M11-L1

What turns “improve traffic safety” into accountable work?

**Explained answer:** Define exposure, interim control, responsible owner, resources, due point and verification under real conditions.

**Correction:** A slogan or assignment to safety alone does not establish an effective correction.

lessons.title: M11-L2
lessons.body:
## M11-L2

Why is purchasing a barrier not sufficient action closure?

**Explained answer:** Installation and effective protection under intended work must be verified, including new hazards and limitations.

**Correction:** Verify the exposure, not spending.

lessons.title: M12-L1
lessons.body:
## M12-L1

Does a fictional risk score of10 automatically make a potentially fatal event acceptable?

**Explained answer:** No; consequence, critical controls, uncertainty and escalation rules still govern.

**Correction:** Ordinal arithmetic does not create permission.

lessons.title: M12-L2
lessons.body:
## M12-L2

What is missing from “isolation checked” as a critical-control statement?

**Explained answer:** Specific sources, arrangement, verification evidence, responsible role and response to failure.

**Correction:** Make performance observable rather than a checkbox.

lessons.title: M13-L1
lessons.body:
## M13-L1

Calculate the original model average for20units over2hours and5units over6hours.

**Explained answer:** 8.75units over8hours.

**Correction:** The arbitrary-unit average is not a real exposure-limit comparison.

lessons.title: M13-L2
lessons.body:
## M13-L2

Why is a lunch-break area measurement insufficient for repeated solvent wiping exposure?

**Explained answer:** It may not represent the task, breathing zone, peaks or actual conditions.

**Correction:** Plan representative competent assessment and route/duration information.

lessons.title: M14-L1
lessons.body:
## M14-L1

Why does “carelessness” fail as the entire explanation of a jam-clearing injury?

**Explained answer:** It does not explain the task, equipment, instructions, production conditions or mechanism needed for effective correction.

**Correction:** Investigate facts and contributing conditions without erasing individual actions.

lessons.title: M14-L2
lessons.body:
## M14-L2

How should a log written after an incident be identified?

**Explained answer:** As a later account, with its actual time/source, not a contemporaneous observation.

**Correction:** Preserve chronology and uncertainty.

lessons.title: M15-L1
lessons.body:
## M15-L1

Two contractors have completed checklists for solvent transfer and nearby hot work. Is combined readiness established?

**Explained answer:** No; evaluate the interaction, shared space/routes and coordinated timing/controls.

**Correction:** Independent plans may conflict.

lessons.title: M15-L2
lessons.body:
## M15-L2

A machine tag changed since the isolation handover. What must happen before reliance?

**Explained answer:** Resolve actual identity/configuration and applicable isolation evidence before proceeding.

**Correction:** Copied initials do not reconcile changed equipment.

lessons.title: M16-L1
lessons.body:
## M16-L1

Training completion is98percent but critical isolation defects remain. What should the review prioritize?

**Explained answer:** The unresolved exposure and effective controls, with owners and verified disposition.

**Correction:** A favorable activity metric cannot hide critical-control failure.

lessons.title: M16-L2
lessons.body:
## M16-L2

Why can more near-miss reports follow improvement?

**Explained answer:** A new reporting channel or greater trust may reveal previously unreported events.

**Correction:** Review conditions and reporting changes before inferring worsening safety.

lessons.title: M17-L1
lessons.body:
## M17-L1

What must be checked when a connected feeder is proposed to run during conveyor service?

**Explained answer:** Whether its energy/material/interface can defeat the protected state; competent procedure and source review.

**Correction:** Different asset names do not establish independence.

lessons.title: M17-L2
lessons.body:
## M17-L2

Why can a guard inspection before a feedstock change be insufficient afterward?

**Explained answer:** New geometry/access or ejection hazards may invalidate its protective function.

**Correction:** Review the changed task and competent safeguard evidence.

lessons.title: M18-L1
lessons.body:
## M18-L1

What failed when a contractor uses an old emergency map after a route change?

**Explained answer:** Coordination and understandable current-plan communication/verification, not just the map file.

**Correction:** Correct the actual affected group’s knowledge and route.

lessons.title: M18-L2
lessons.body:
## M18-L2

Two required PPE items interfere. What should a supervisor verify?

**Explained answer:** Compatible protection for all relevant hazards, actual fit/use and supported task selection.

**Correction:** Do not silently drop one protective function.

lessons.title: M19-L1
lessons.body:
## M19-L1

Crossings fall from40to8per shift. Calculate reduction and state its limit.

**Explained answer:** 32fewer,80percent reduction; remaining/new trips still need safe controls and real observation.

**Correction:** Frequency reduction is not injury-probability proof.

lessons.title: M19-L2
lessons.body:
## M19-L2

A smaller layout creates high awkward lifts. What should the review include?

**Explained answer:** Reach, height, grip, repetition, force, route and aids, not just walking distance.

**Correction:** Evaluate total task exposure.

lessons.title: M20-L1
lessons.body:
## M20-L1

A replacement chemical has less odor but new flammability. What is the readiness decision?

**Explained answer:** Hold until the broader identity/SDS/use, ignition, ventilation, PPE and storage review supports the change.

**Correction:** Odor is not a complete hazard comparison.

lessons.title: M20-L2
lessons.body:
## M20-L2

Does rotating between two equally demanding wrist tasks necessarily reduce exposure?

**Explained answer:** No; the relevant force/posture/repetition may remain unchanged.

**Correction:** Verify actual exposure change and worker feedback.


---

courses.title: VUC010 | VUC009 — applied stations and recording forms

content.title: VUC010 | VUC009 — applied stations and recording forms
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC009 — applied stations and recording forms
lessons.body:
# VUC009 — applied stations and recording forms

Use these original fictional cases in instruction and fresh variants for scored assessment. No hazardous exposure or real complaint/report submission is required. Props are drawings, empty labeled containers, inert PPE and ground-level visual ladder samples. Assessor observes the learner's words, drawings and demonstrations. Do not award attendance as competence.

Each station has five criteria scored0/1/2: absent/unsafe, prompted/incomplete, independent/correct. Pass8/10 with every marked critical criterion2. Stop an unsafe attempt, explain the gap and use the fresh variant after practice. Record each attempt.

lessons.title: A — report the actual exposure and find the right route
lessons.body:
## A — report the actual exposure and find the right route

**Case:** Brook Workshop,11:10. A packing roller's guard is missing; two workers feed cartons beside it. At11:20 one worker reports a hand injury. Later a message alleges that reporting will cost the worker shifts. The training system contains separate hazard, injury and retaliation-information links. Do not submit any real form.

**Tasks:** write a factual urgent warning/report; separate the three records; identify immediate care/reporting and official rights information; explain what is known versus alleged; demonstrate locating the official complaint route.

**Expected:** exact machine/location/exposure and people, safe warning/hold, honest injury record/care, separate retaliation route with prompt current deadline check. No invented motive or decision that the injury is not worth reporting. No real complaint sent.

**Criteria:** specific exposure report; safe warning/position **critical**; separates routes **critical**; preserves facts/privacy; finds official timely resource.

**Fresh variant:** an obstructed access step and a threatened bonus, with no injury. Learner must not fabricate an injury record merely because the first case had one.

lessons.title: B — use chemical information and inspect PPE
lessons.body:
## B — use chemical information and inspect PPE

**Case card:** Empty prop labeled ClearSolv-T, fictional flammable/eye-irritant liquid. Supplied mock extract says specified ventilation, ignition control, task-approved eye protection and compatible gloves are required; designated responders handle spills. Transfer bench is beside a grinder; local exhaust is marked unavailable. SampleA glove has no compatibility data; sampleB has a mock task approval and sound condition; eyewear has one scratched sample and one sound sample. No real chemical is present.

**Tasks:** match identifier, locate hazards/controls, decide readiness, select/inspect and demonstrate fit of approved inert PPE, explain what PPE cannot solve, state spill boundary. Identify information that the limited extract cannot replace in a real task.

**Expected:** no transfer until ignition/exhaust issues are controlled; no guessed glove compatibility; use sound task-approved sample and explain limitations; response follows the designated plan. Demonstration does not constitute a respirator fit test.

**Criteria:** identity/information match **critical**; correct hold/control reasoning **critical**; selects supported PPE; checks condition/fit; response/remaining-information boundary.

**Fresh variant:** label and extract identifiers conflict while ventilation works. Learner must detect the identity problem instead of repeating an exhaust failure that is absent.

lessons.title: C — choose a safe exit and report accountability
lessons.body:
## C — choose a safe exit and report accountability

**Fictional map:** Workbench at center. North route exits through hallN; south route through hallS. AssemblyB is outside the south exit. Smoke blocks hallN; hallS is clear. No firefighting role is assigned. Coworker Lee was last seen at packing bay; current whereabouts unknown. A prop extinguisher is shown near hallN.

**Tasks:** draw evacuation route; give alarm report; reach mock assembly location without actual hazard; report Lee's last known location/uncertainty; explain when reentry is permitted.

**Expected:** use south route and plan; no approach to smoke for extinguisher or untrained rescue; do not mark Lee accounted for; wait for designated reentry authorization rather than alarm silence.

**Criteria:** safe route **critical**; appropriate alarm report; no untrained rescue/fire exposure **critical**; truthful accountability **critical**; controlled reentry.

**Fresh variant:** south route blocked and north is clear, with AssemblyA named in the revised mock plan. Assess current-plan use, not memorized direction.

lessons.title: D — recognize machine, electrical and energy boundaries
lessons.body:
## D — recognize machine, electrical and energy boundaries

**Inert drawing:** Conveyor motor powered from disconnectE; pneumatic actuator from air sourceP; raised component held by gravity restraintG. Start/stop buttons shown separately. Roller guard missing. Electrical cabinet cover is open. A maintenance lock is depicted atE only; other source status unknown. The learner is an affected production employee, not a qualified electrician or authorized servicer.

**Tasks:** mark exposure paths and sources; explain why stop or one lock is insufficient; report/hold the affected task; refuse an instruction to open, reach in or remove the lock; describe who must establish the safe servicing state.

**Expected:** no contact with open electrical parts, no reach into machine, no lock removal; electrical/pneumatic/gravity risks remain distinct. Obtain responsible qualified/authorized personnel and procedure; do not invent control sequence.

**Criteria:** identifies sources; identifies missing guard/electrical boundary; no hazardous contact **critical**; preserves lock/role boundary **critical**; clear report and authorized next step.

**Fresh variant:** all guards intact but a jam requires an exposed cleaning task; no maintenance lock is present. Learner must recognize the changed servicing exposure without inventing a removed guard.

lessons.title: E — route, access and load stability
lessons.body:
## E — route, access and load stability

**Plan:** A pedestrian aisle is blocked by a pallet. Vehicle laneV is active with a reversing truck. RackR has a leaning load after a reported strike. An unmarked panel shifts over a floor opening. A stepladder has a cracked rail. No worker in this case is authorized to drive a forklift.

**Tasks:** mark prohibited exposure zones; propose a controlled route without enteringV or underR; identify access items to remove from use/report; plan authorized correction; explain what evidence reopens each route.

**Expected:** hold conflicting movement through responsible control, separate pedestrians and collapse/opening zones, no ladder use or stepping on panel to test it, no truck operation by the learner. Verified suitable correction includes source/route/control, not just moving the original pallet elsewhere.

**Criteria:** identifies five hazards; avoids transfer of risk **critical**; rejects defective access **critical**; stays within equipment authority **critical**; correction-verification plan.

**Fresh variant:** routes clear but a heavy awkward package must be placed overhead. Assess reach/grip/height/assistance and alternative layout; do not invent active vehicle traffic.

lessons.title: F — occupational health and integrated correction
lessons.body:
## F — occupational health and integrated correction

**Case:** Bag-handling exhaust stops; no visible dust yet. One worker reports shoulder discomfort at a long-reach bench. A different worker in a hot area becomes confused. Supervisor asks the crew to continue while a maintenance ticket waits.

**Tasks:** prioritize the emergency and affected exposure; give separate factual reports; identify control failures and worker-role limits; propose appropriate ergonomic investigation/change; specify verification before resuming the dust task.

**Expected:** activate emergency response for severe heat signs, stay with/obtain trained care for the person; hold exposure dependent on failed exhaust; no guessed respirator replacement; assess task layout/reach rather than dismiss discomfort. Verify restored effective control and any required assessment, not just ticket closure.

**Criteria:** emergency priority **critical**; no abandonment/continued heat exposure **critical**; recognizes invisible dust risk **critical**; task-specific ergonomic reasoning; useful follow-up/verification.

**Fresh variant:** no heat emergency, but noise exposure concerns and a damaged hearing protector. Learner should seek assessment and suitable controls/protection without claiming an emergency that is not present.

lessons.title: Attempt record — duplicate for each station

lessons.title: VUC010 — supervisor casework and observed assessments
lessons.body:
# VUC010 — supervisor casework and observed assessments

All facilities and records below are fictional. Use paper/inert props only. Cases require the learner to produce and defend work decisions; they do not authorize actual specialist work. Supply the worker foundation, technical lessons, blank action/change forms, calculator and these case cards. A competent general-industry safety instructor assesses the reasoning and role boundaries.

Each station has five criteria:0 absent/unsafe,1 incomplete or prompted,2 independently correct. Pass8/10 and every critical criterion2. Preserve failed attempts; teach the gap and use a fresh variant. Learners may consult source material during practice, but scored attempts use clean case cards and relevant controlled references, not worked answers.

lessons.title: S1 — prioritize and own six actions
lessons.body:
## S1 — prioritize and own six actions

**Backlog:** (a) interlock defeated on active machine; (b) faded low-priority notice; (c) daily pedestrian crossing of delivery lane; (d) damaged access ladder in use; (e) missing chemical identity for planned transfer; (f) outdated lunchroom roster. No injuries reported. Budget request is pending; management wants three easy closures today.

**Tasks:** identify immediate exposure controls and operations held; choose a permanent correction for(c); assign owner/resources/due review; design verification; explain why easy closures do not determine priority. Do not invent permission to repair equipment personally.

**Expected:** active(a)/(d) and unidentified(e) need immediate effective protection/hold; traffic(c) requires controlled separation/route and investigation of why crossings occur. Priorities reflect actual exposure/severity, not this list's order. For(c), involve workers, consider supply relocation, account for restocking and verify representative shifts. Unknown information is recorded, not scored away.

**Criteria:** addresses urgent exposures **critical**; defines mechanism/control; assigns empowered owner/resources; interim protection **critical**; objective verification and follow-up.

**Fresh variant:** machine is already isolated and access ladder removed, but new truck traffic defeats the previously protected route. Reprioritize current conditions rather than memorizing the first list.

lessons.title: S2 — risk and fall-control review
lessons.body:
## S2 — risk and fall-control review

**Case:** A six-foot elevated maintenance edge has no verified protection. Proposal lists a harness but no anchorage, clearance or rescue assessment. Local scoring model uses likelihood1–5 and consequence1–5; team chooses2×5=10 and marks “acceptable because no prior incident.” The job can be rescheduled; supervisor is not a fall-system designer.

**Tasks:** define event/exposure, explain score/uncertainty, identify missing control evidence, choose disposition and assign competent review. Write a stop/restart condition.

**Expected:**10is model arithmetic, not proof. Hold affected work; obtain a suitable complete arrangement and required training/rescue evidence through qualified support. Do not select an arbitrary pipe as anchorage. Prior absence of injury does not verify protection.

**Criteria:** defined event; correct model interpretation; no unsupported elevated exposure **critical**; complete control/evidence needs **critical**; appropriate expert/authority and restart.

**Fresh variant:** guardrail exists but has been removed for material access; alternative work platform is proposed with unverified suitability. Evaluate current configuration and alternative rather than repeat “no harness.”

lessons.title: S3 — exposure arithmetic and task representativeness
lessons.body:
## S3 — exposure arithmetic and task representativeness

**Input:** fictional agent in arbitrary units,18for2hours and6for6hours. An area sample during lunch reads1. A supervisor proposes using the lowest number to authorize a changed wiping process. No real exposure limit is supplied. Glove compatibility for the new product is unknown.

**Tasks:** calculate weighted average; identify what the area sample does not show; list three limitations; specify information for a competent evaluator; choose change disposition and control verification.

**Key:**(18×2+6×6)/8=9units. No comparison to a real limit is valid; peaks, skin route, representativeness, agent identity and uncertainty remain. Hold the unsupported change, obtain product/task/PPE/control assessment. Do not select a respirator independently as a substitute.

**Criteria:** arithmetic; representative sampling reasoning; limits/uncertainty **critical**; supported change/role boundary **critical**; verification plan.

**Fresh variant:**24for1hour and8for7hours→10units; new concern is failed source capture rather than unknown gloves. Preserve changed facts.

lessons.title: S4 — investigation and truthful records
lessons.body:
## S4 — investigation and truthful records

**Chronology:**09:00 worn guide reported;09:30 jam repeated;09:40 worker reached around protection;09:41 injury reported;10:15 supervisor wrote “guard checked09:00,” but no original check is available. Production target had been increased the day before. These are statements for investigation, not proof of motive.

**Tasks:** separate facts/accounts/hypotheses; identify two additional evidence needs; protect care/scene/privacy; propose two mechanism-linked corrections; give verification and record-preservation requirements.

**Expected:** preserve original timestamps and source; identify later note as later, investigate guide/jam/usable method/control conditions and production context. Do not erase worker action or stop at blame. Corrections may include competent guide/guard repair and validated safe clearing method, with observed performance. No invented09:00inspection pass.

**Criteria:** source/chronology fidelity **critical**; separates uncertainty; gathers relevant evidence; targeted controls; no altered evidence/privacy breach **critical**.

**Fresh variant:** no injury, but repeated near miss; the equipment repair is documented while training application is uncertain. Investigate current gap, not assumed defective guide.

lessons.title: S5 — coordinate competing work and handover
lessons.body:
## S5 — coordinate competing work and handover

**Schedule:** contractorA hot work10:00–12:00; contractorB solvent transfer10:30–11:30 in adjacent shared airspace; host employees use their shared exit; temporary ventilation unavailable; replacement asset tag differs from the isolation sheet. Both contractors have generic orientation certificates.

**Tasks:** identify conflicts, establish hold/review, propose supported revised sequencing/separation, name communication owners, reconcile asset identity and deliver a shift handover. Do not write a technical hot-work or isolation procedure outside your role.

**Expected:** do not release concurrent conflicting work on two checklists; obtain appropriate combined technical/control review and current identity/isolations. Keep exit available. All affected teams acknowledge revised scope/timing, restrictions and restart authority. No retrospective signature as prework proof.

**Criteria:** finds interactions **critical**; resolves identity before reliance **critical**; workable revised plan with expert inputs; communicates/acknowledges; truthful hold/restart handover.

**Fresh variant:** chemical transfer removed; a crane lift now blocks the exit and overlaps pedestrian access. Adapt the interaction review rather than cite absent solvent.

lessons.title: S6 — energy, guarding and return to service
lessons.body:
## S6 — energy, guarding and return to service

**Input:** modelP7repair, feederF2can discharge intoP7, motor disconnect shown isolated, pneumatic actuator pressure unknown, guard removed for repair. Production requests feeder operation. Shift changes before completion; no authorized restoration evidence supplied.

**Tasks:** trace electrical/material/air/mechanical interfaces; separate supervisor from qualified/authorized tasks; refuse unsupported concurrent operation; plan status handover and required restart evidence.

**Expected:** hold conflicting feed; competent complete-source/procedure evaluation; no assumption from one lock or stopped belt; no lock removal by supervisor merely to meet schedule. Restart needs actual restoration and guards/conditions verified plus affected-worker notification.

**Criteria:** complete interface recognition; preserves protected state **critical**; role/procedure boundary **critical**; truthful shift transfer; adequate restart evidence **critical**.

**Fresh variant:** feeder physically separated but electrical cabinet remains energized for a separate planned task. Do not infer total safe state from mechanical separation.

lessons.title: S7 — emergency and PPE implementation
lessons.body:
## S7 — emergency and PPE implementation

**Input:** routeNclosed, routeSverified clear; night contractor has old map, two temporary workers missing from roster. Employer policy is evacuation-only. New eye/face equipment interferes with required hearing protection. A mock alarm occurs; no real emergency exists.

**Tasks:** coordinate safe route/roster communication, conduct tabletop accountability, preserve deficiencies, reject invented firefighting duties, and resolve combined-PPE issue before affected exposure.

**Expected:** current route reaches all groups; unknown people are not marked accounted for; no untrained fire attack; compatible supported protection rather than choosing one hazard to ignore; corrective retest keeps original findings.

**Criteria:** current accessible route; truthful accountability **critical**; response-role boundary **critical**; PPE compatibility/hold **critical**; implementation verification.

**Fresh variant:** route information correct but alarm is not perceivable in a noisy work area. Address notification effectiveness instead of editing an already-correct map.

lessons.title: S8 — layout, charging and effectiveness review
lessons.body:
## S8 — layout, charging and effectiveness review

**Input:**50crossings/shift before proposed layout,15after; restocking not yet observed. New rack arrangement creates awkward high reaches. Charger is placed in an exit route on an unverified supply. Dashboard reports100percent training completion and30closed actions; struck-rack assessment remains overdue.

**Tasks:** calculate crossing reduction; identify remaining/introduced risks; state operator/charging competence boundaries; select outcome-focused verification and immediate holds; brief management without disguising adverse evidence.

**Key:**35fewer,70percent reduction in the modeled count. Verify residual/restocking exposure. Do not approve unsafe charger location/supply or expose people under an unresolved rack. Evaluate reach/grip/force/frequency and alternative layout/aids. Attendance/closures do not prove safe conditions.

**Criteria:** correct arithmetic/limits; identifies transferred risks; immediate hold on critical unresolved exposure **critical**; qualified operator/electrical boundaries **critical**; balanced effectiveness/worker feedback.

**Fresh variant:**30to12crossings→18fewer,60percent; charger issue resolved but a new chemical substitution has unresolved ignition/PPE evidence. Respond to actual remaining risk.

lessons.body:
# VUC009 — sources, edition and coverage

Author review17November2026. This is an original VNDRLY course addressing general-industry worker orientation. It does not claim OSHA Outreach authorization or issue an OSHA card. Technical/regulatory references are official OSHA sources; apply their scope and current jurisdiction requirements to actual work. Do not assume an orientation replaces a standard's task-specific training.

lessons.title: Scope benchmark
lessons.body:
## Scope benchmark

[OSHA General Industry Outreach Procedures,2024](https://www.osha.gov/sites/default/files/OTP_General_Industry_Procedures_2024.pdf) identifies six required subject families and elective/optional training. This VNDRLY plan teaches the six families for an hour each, then hazardous energy, guarding, handling and industrial hygiene for an hour each. Its own assessment and credential are separate from authorized Outreach delivery. [OSHA Outreach FAQ](https://www.osha.gov/training/outreach/faq) explains program boundaries; [testing-time FAQ](https://www.osha.gov/node/58587) distinguishes testing from instructional time. The VNDRLY plan likewise adds the final outside the ten instructional hours rather than counting examination as teaching.

lessons.title: Source limitations and original material
lessons.body:
## Source limitations and original material

Online standard pages were consulted during authoring; a current live operation must use the applicable current rule and employer program. The SDS format brief describes an earlier HCS format; the current1910.1200 page governs current requirements. No chemical-specific product claim is made from the fictional extract. The2024 pictogram reference is identified by its published revision. State-plan and other legal regimes can differ; the30-day statement is scoped to federal OSH Act retaliation, not all laws.

All course scenarios, prompts, rubrics, times and fake facility/product names are original educational material. Hourly blocks are a delivery design, not recorded attendance. Neither the final nor the practicals certify specialist machinery, electrical, respiratory, rescue or permit-entry competence.


---

The VNDRLY guide supplies its own facilitated 30-hour plan. [Outreach FAQ](https://www.osha.gov/training/outreach/faq) and [testing time](https://www.osha.gov/node/58587) support distinguishing instruction from examination and authorized Outreach from this independent program. No external approval, card or exact examination equivalency is claimed.

|---|---|---|---|

|M17 obtain verified energy/electrical/guarding evidence without exceeding role|[1910.147](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.147), [1910.333](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.333), [1910.212](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.212)|M17 P7/F2 worked case, S6 interfaces|M17-E1–E4|
|M18 implement emergency arrangements and compatible PPE|[1910.38](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.38), [1910.157](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.157), [1910.132](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.132)|M18 current-route and PPE cases, S7|M18-E1–E4|

Every domain also has two explained formative checks. G01–G10 each have four controlled final questions and applied coverage in A–F, as mapped in the embedded worker register. Supervisor case criteria distinguish factual analysis, control decision, authority and verification; critical criteria cannot be compensated by arithmetic totals.

Online sources are guidance or standards in their stated scope, not generic approval of a particular workplace. Check applicable jurisdiction and current employer procedures for actual work. Synthetic exposure units have no real permissible limit; fictional risk scores are ordinal exercises. Case temperatures, hours, counts, product names and equipment IDs do not establish manufacturer instructions. Existing six owned supervisor lessons were reviewed and embedded; the four technical chapters and eight expanded case cards extend their instruction. No licensed external examination was copied.

lessons.title: VUC011 — instructor and credential guide
lessons.body:
# VUC011 — instructor and credential guide

**Program:** VNDRLY/U Construction Worker Safety. Version 1.0, 17 November 2026. Audience: construction workers and new site entrants needing general hazard recognition. Prerequisites: no specialist credential; participation in an understood language with accessible materials. Purpose: identify construction exposures, choose safe worker-level actions, report accurately and recognize tasks requiring additional qualification.

This is VNDRLY-owned training and assessment addressing the source subject. It is not an authorized OSHA Outreach 10-hour course, does not issue an OSHA card and does not substitute for legally required task-specific training. Do not name the awarded credential “OSHA 10.” Material production records no actual attendance or learner competence.

lessons.title: Outcomes and sequence
lessons.body:
## Outcomes and sequence

Teach C01 rights/reporting, C02 falls, C03 electricity, C04 struck-by, C05 caught-in/between, C06 PPE, C07 health, C08 access/scaffolds, C09 excavation and C10 tools/material/emergency decisions. Each written chapter provides explanation, realistic application, common error and worked reasoning. Twenty additional formative questions require attempted answers and correction. The final contains forty different prompts, four per domain. The six applied stations require observable decisions and safe inert demonstrations.

lessons.title: Ten instructional hours
lessons.body:
## Ten instructional hours

This planned delivery comprises six core hours, two elective hours and two expanded-topic hours. It reflects the source topic families while awarding only VNDRLY's credential. Actual facilitated duration must be recorded; document length is not proof of elapsed instruction. Breaks, administration and final/independent practical assessment are additional.

| Session | Minutes | Teaching and learner work |
|---|---:|---|
|C01|60|20 explanation; 20 station A chronology/report; 10 rights/report-route discussion; 10 checks and correction|
|C02|90|30 fall mechanisms/system boundaries; 30 deck/cover cases and diagram; 20 changed delivery opening and defended alternate; 10 checks|
|C03|60|20 electrical paths/program boundaries; 20 cord/overhead/concealed-source cases; 10 emergency boundary; 10 checks|
|C04|60|20 object/vehicle paths; 20 yard route drawing; 10 changed overhead-work access; 10 checks|
|C05|30|10 trapping mechanisms; 10 mixer and swing-gap cases; 10 checks/teach-back|
|C06|30|10 suitability/fit; 10 inert sample compatibility; 10 checks/role boundary|
|C07|30|10 health hazards; 10 cutting/chemical/heat decisions; 10 checks and corrected priorities|
|C08|60|20 access/scaffold instruction; 20 ladder model and post-strike case; 10 task alternative; 10 checks|
|C09|60|20 excavation mechanisms; 20 station E map/travel/protection; 10 changed-depth case; 10 checks|
|C10|120|30 tools/material/entry/emergency instruction; 30 station F integrated decisions; 20 exact-location tabletop call; 20 changed-condition restart review; 20 checks and whole-course teach-back|

C02–C05 total four hours including ninety minutes falls. C08 and C09 provide two distinct electives; C10 expands practical construction hazards for two hours. If more time is needed, extend it; never compress a misunderstood critical decision to meet the plan.

For each exercise ask what mechanism causes injury, what prevents exposure, who can decide specialist details, and what changed fact would invalidate the plan. If a learner repeats “be careful,” request a concrete safe route or hold condition. Provide reading/language support and accessible oral responses without lowering technical criteria or supplying final answers.

lessons.title: Preparation and training safety
lessons.body:
## Preparation and training safety

Instructor needs demonstrated competence in construction hazard recognition and the ability to explain applicable scope limits. Read this package, primary references and protected instruments before teaching. Inert props and synthetic case data are sufficient; do not stage live work at height, energized contact, trench entry, rigging, vehicle movement, chemicals or emergency rescue. No actual complaints, alerts, operational reports or worker assignments are created by training.

Supply coursebook, case cards, paper, calculator and inert PPE/ladder/cord illustrations. Descriptions in the packet can substitute for photographs. Local emergency/contact orientation may be added using actual authorized information, but do not invent it or treat a fictional scenario as a site plan. For real equipment qualifications arrange the separately required authorized training and practical assessment.

lessons.title: Evaluation, scoring and retakes
lessons.body:
## Evaluation, scoring and retakes

All twenty formative checks require an attempt. After an error, revisit the chapter and have the learner explain corrected reasoning in a new situation. Formative answers are intentionally explained; they are not the independent final.

Final: forty constructed responses, two points each. Nominal ninety minutes plus documented accommodations. Calculator and blank paper allowed, no completed exercises or key. Two points for required correct decision and reasoning, one for materially correct but incomplete without unsafe assertion, zero absent/incorrect/unsafe. Pass 64/80 overall and at least 6/8 in every domain. Endorsing unsafe exposure, bypass, unauthorized entry/operation or fabricated evidence identified in the key requires remediation and independent reassessment regardless of total.

Six practical stations A–F each have five observable criteria. Pass 8/10 per station and every critical criterion 2. First scenarios are coached learning; use fresh variants independently. Retain exact variant and observations. A verbal claim to have read the procedure or a completed quiz does not demonstrate the practical decision.

Following failure, teach the gap and provide fresh practice. Protected alternate cards support a new equivalent-demand instrument: four prompts per failed domain, same 6/8 floor. Retain valid same-version independent passing scores and recompute the 64/80 total; otherwise use a full retest. Keep original failures and every attempt. Two unsuccessful retakes require a documented learning plan before reassessing failed components. Do not reveal a key and immediately retest identical answers.

lessons.title: Credential and records
lessons.body:
## Credential and records

Award VNDRLY/U Construction Worker Safety — Orientation after all instruction, corrected formative work, independent final and all six stations pass. Record learner identity, material version, actual dates/hours, domain scores, practical criteria/observations, examiner competence, attempts, accommodations and restrictions. A blank form means pending, never passed.

Recommend annual workplace review and additional learning after changed duties, site hazards/procedures or demonstrated gaps. This is a VNDRLY recommendation, not an external card-expiration rule. Site, employer or jurisdiction requirements may demand an actual authorized Outreach card and specific qualifications. This credential provides none of those by implication. Publication and live learner delivery remain separate from completion of these materials.


---
