content.title: VUC012 | VUC012 — construction leadership instruction
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC012 — construction leadership instruction
lessons.body:
# VUC012 — construction leadership instruction

Six owned VNDRLY lessons reviewed and embedded for this program. Synthetic quantitative models do not approve real equipment or exposure. The VUC012 guide governs completion.

lessons.title: S11 — Construction sequencing, site plans and simultaneous work
lessons.body:
## S11 — Construction sequencing, site plans and simultaneous work

Construction risk changes as the site changes. Map phases, temporary works, access routes, utilities, deliveries and interactions among trades. A safe layout during foundation work may become unsafe when steel erection, lifts and electrical commissioning overlap. The site-specific plan must describe actual means and methods, responsible parties and change triggers rather than copy a generic corporate manual.

Use a job hazard analysis to break work into meaningful steps, identify energy/exposure and select controls. Consider workers performing the task and others nearby. A crane exclusion zone that blocks the only emergency access route creates another hazard; coordinate the layout before execution. Prefer removal or separation of conflicting work over relying on workers to notice one another at the last moment.

Case: overhead pipe installation, mobile equipment travel and scaffold access share a narrow corridor. Sequence work, establish controlled routes and prevent people entering suspended-load areas. Clarify who authorizes changes and how crews learn about them. Signs alone do not physically separate an uncontrolled vehicle route.

Assessment requires a marked logistics plan and a daily coordination briefing for three trades. The assessor checks foreseeable interactions, emergency access, material storage, competent-person assignments and a method to revise the plan after changes. Critical failures include approving work beneath an uncontrolled suspended load or treating yesterday's inspection as proof of today's site conditions.

lessons.title: S12 — Falls, excavations and structural temporary conditions
lessons.body:
## S12 — Falls, excavations and structural temporary conditions

Fall prevention begins with suitable working surfaces, access and collective protection where feasible. Select the applicable standard for the activity; construction thresholds and requirements vary among general fall protection, scaffolds, steel erection and other scopes. A harness alone does not constitute a complete system. Anchorage, connectors, compatibility, clearance, swing-fall exposure and rescue must be addressed.

For a fictional clearance exercise, supplied components are 1.8 m free fall, 1.0 m deceleration, 0.3 m harness/D-ring movement, 1.5 m distance below the D-ring and 1.0 m safety allowance. Their sum is 5.6 m. This simplified example is not a manufacturer-approved design; actual equipment geometry, anchorage height and instructions govern. If available clearance is 4.8 m, the supplied arrangement cannot be accepted.

Excavations require assessment of soil, water, adjacent loads, utilities, access and protective systems by the designated competent person. Temporary forms, shoring and partially completed structures can have load paths unlike the completed design. Do not remove supports because concrete looks hard or a structure appears stable.

Practical assessment uses a safe ground-level fall-system mockup and excavation/temporary-work drawings. The learner identifies missing clearance or rescue information and a changed ground condition. The assessor requires correct arithmetic and referral to the actual design/manufacturer basis. No learner is exposed to a real fall or unprotected trench for assessment.

lessons.title: S13 — Lifting, equipment, electrical and stored-energy interfaces
lessons.body:
## S13 — Lifting, equipment, electrical and stored-energy interfaces

Mobile equipment creates struck-by, caught-between and rollover hazards. Separate pedestrian routes, manage reversing and blind spots, maintain stable travel surfaces and verify operator/equipment suitability. A spotter needs an agreed communication method and a safe position; a spotter is not a substitute for eliminating unnecessary people from the operating envelope.

Lifting requires an actual lift plan, configuration/load-chart review, ground support, rigging and communication. In a simplified symmetric two-leg sling model, tension per leg is W/(2 sin theta), where theta is the angle above horizontal. For a 1000 kg-force equivalent load and theta 30°, each leg carries 1000 kg-force; at 60°, each carries about 577 kg-force. This static model excludes dynamic effects, unequal loading and hardware limits and cannot select production rigging.

Electrical hazards include contact, arc energy and unexpected energization. Identify overhead/underground services and temporary power conditions. Isolation must address all energy sources and stored energy, with verification by the authorized process. An unplugged tool does not establish isolation of connected hydraulic or pneumatic equipment.

Assessment combines a lift sketch, pedestrian route and maintenance task. The learner calculates model sling tension, identifies power-line and pinch exposures and traces multiple energy sources. The assessor checks that the learner does not convert the simplified tension into a rated-capacity approval or treat a switch-off command as verified isolation.

lessons.title: S14 — Construction health exposures and monitoring
lessons.body:
## S14 — Construction health exposures and monitoring

Construction health hazards include silica, welding fumes, lead/asbestos where present, noise, heat/cold, vibration and biological exposures. Identify materials before disturbance and select controls for the actual task. Dust appearance cannot establish respirable concentration or composition. Demolition coatings and insulation may require surveys and specialist controls before work begins.

For silica construction tasks, OSHA's specified-control route requires fully and properly implementing the applicable Table 1 controls and respiratory provisions, or using the alternative exposure-assessment route. Merely owning a vacuum or wet saw does not establish compliance if the configuration or operation differs from the required method. Actual task duration, indoor/outdoor conditions and equipment matter.

For a supplied exposure exercise, two hours at 100 micrograms/m³, four hours at 25 and two hours at 0 give an eight-hour average of (200+100)/8 = 37.5 micrograms/m³. Compare with the applicable limit and action requirements, while retaining task peaks and uncertainty. This arithmetic alone does not establish the entire silica program or substitute for valid sampling.

Assessment asks the learner to inspect a mock dust-control setup, identify missing capture/maintenance elements and develop a task-based sampling question. The assessor checks control selection, instrument purpose, respiratory-program boundaries and health-record privacy. Critical failures include dry disturbance of unidentified hazardous material or treating no visible dust as proof of no exposure.

lessons.title: S15 — Emergency coordination and incident learning
lessons.body:
## S15 — Emergency coordination and incident learning

A construction emergency plan must fit changing site access, elevation, excavation, headcount and communication. Define how to report the emergency, provide precise location, summon appropriate help, evacuate or shelter and account for workers and visitors. Coordinate with external responders about access restrictions and site hazards before an incident. A public emergency number alone does not demonstrate rescue capability for a suspended worker or confined space.

Drills should test realistic failures: blocked gate, unavailable supervisor, radio dead zone or a subcontractor missing from the roster. Record the timeline and decisions, then correct the demonstrated gaps. Response speed is not the only measure; sending untrained people into danger can worsen the event. Medical information and injury details require appropriate confidentiality.

After immediate response, preserve evidence and investigate conditions. A dropped object may involve storage, toe boards, work sequencing, exclusion zones and supervision, not merely a worker's grip. Interview witnesses without leading them to a preferred conclusion. Separate what was observed from assumptions and identify why barriers failed.

Assessment uses a tabletop event with a blocked access route and an injured worker at height. The learner activates the correct response, protects others and tracks accountability without improvising a rescue. The assessor evaluates communication accuracy, role clarity, escalation and restart criteria. A corrective-action plan must name owners and verify effectiveness rather than close everything with a toolbox talk.

lessons.title: S16 — Leadership, inspection records and supervisor capstone
lessons.body:
## S16 — Leadership, inspection records and supervisor capstone

Construction safety technicians influence work through credible field knowledge, clear communication and consistent follow-through. Explain the hazard and required control in language the crew understands, confirm understanding through demonstration or teach-back, and protect the ability to report concerns. A signed attendance sheet does not establish that a worker can perform a critical task.

Inspections should record location, condition, applicable requirement, immediate protection, assigned owner, due date and closure evidence. Prioritize by potential severity and exposure, not merely by how easy an item is to fix. A repeated defect suggests a system problem with procurement, maintenance, planning or supervision. Trend recurrence and verify that the correction persists.

Capstone: a site has good injury statistics but repeated missing edge protection, dust-control failures and late trade coordination. The learner builds a prioritized plan, defines immediate controls and assigns durable corrective actions. The absence of reported injuries does not justify continuing known hazardous conditions. Include a field demonstration and follow-up observation to verify training transfer.

The assessor scores hazard recognition, control selection, calculation accuracy, emergency coordination, documentation and communication. All domains must pass; hiding a critical finding, inventing an inspection or authorizing unsafe exposure is a critical failure. This VNDRLY construction leadership instruction does not establish specialist qualification or employer designation. Actual site authority and task-specific qualifications remain separate.


---

courses.title: VUC012 | VUC012 — technical oversight and coordinated controls

content.title: VUC012 | VUC012 — technical oversight and coordinated controls
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC012 — technical oversight and coordinated controls
lessons.body:
# VUC012 — technical oversight and coordinated controls

These chapters extend C01–C10 and S11–S16. They teach a supervisor to obtain sound decisions, verify implementation and stop unsupported work. They do not appoint the learner as a competent person, qualified designer, entry supervisor, rigger or rescuer. Employer designation and demonstrated competence must match the actual duty.

lessons.title: S17 — PPE, access and supervisory authority
lessons.body:
## S17 — PPE, access and supervisory authority

A title does not establish competence for every construction decision. A competent person must recognize relevant existing/predictable hazards and have authority for prompt correction; a qualified person has demonstrated ability to resolve the particular technical subject. Identify which role each work package requires and who actually holds it. Do not assign an inspection to someone merely because they are available or have completed this course.

PPE oversight starts before procurement: identify the task and hazards, applicable selection and individual fit, interactions with other equipment, inspection, use and replacement. Ask workers to demonstrate safe adjustment and explain limitations. A signature establishes attendance, not fit or effective use. If a replacement model changes compatibility, reassess before exposure. Stocking one nominal size cannot resolve an individual fit problem.

**Worked case:** Roof-access workers need head, eye and hearing protection; the replacement combination dislodges eyewear when they look upward. The supervisor stops the affected exposure and obtains a compatible supported arrangement, tests adjustment in a safe area and records actual findings. Removing eye protection to make other items fit leaves the hazard uncontrolled. The person selecting technical protection must be competent for that task.

Stair and ladder planning includes the task, people, loads, access/egress, stable support and neighboring trades. A ladder may be serviceable but unsuitable for a two-handed sustained force task. Plan a suitable platform or method rather than tell the worker to stretch farther. Keep landings and routes usable throughout deliveries, not only at morning inspection. Inspect and remove defective equipment from use through the employer's procedure.

**Access exercise:** A straight ladder has a twenty-foot supported working length; the one-quarter model gives five feet offset. The proposed base would block an emergency route and lie beneath a delivery path. The correct decision is not “five feet, therefore approved”; resolve the layout or choose suitable alternate access with the responsible people. Do not squeeze the base inward to fit the traffic lane and pretend the arithmetic is unchanged.

A supervisor should review what an inspection proves. A form stating “ladder checked” without identity, condition and actual observations is weak evidence. Distinguish the person who observed the condition from someone later entering data. If a defect appears after inspection, protect current work and preserve the original record. Never backdate a correction to make the first inspection appear complete.

**Practice:** A new foreman is told to sign as scaffold competent person because they completed orientation. **Explained answer:** establish actual required competence and employer authority for that duty; arrange the appropriate person. Orientation provides recognition, not automatic technical designation. Keep affected use on hold while required inspection is unavailable.

lessons.title: S18 — Scaffold and excavation changes need current evidence
lessons.body:
## S18 — Scaffold and excavation changes need current evidence

A scaffold is a temporary structure with a particular configuration and load path. Its condition changes when ties, braces, supports, decks, access or loads change. Ask for design/configuration information, required inspections, user instruction and change authority. Users cannot move a brace for material access and rely on an earlier tag. A supervisor coordinates the work so the intended protection survives actual use.

Review the work platform and access as a system. Materials can overload an area, block access or introduce falling-object hazards. Adjacent mobile equipment and power lines can invalidate the location. Keep unqualified modifications and unverified use on hold; obtain the competent/qualified decisions required by the actual scaffold and activity. The supervisor must not create a capacity from a photograph or use workers as test loads.

**Worked case:** A masonry delivery is proposed on a scaffold deck originally used for hand tools. No load/configuration evidence supports the pallet. The supervisor holds delivery to that platform and obtains the actual capacity and method review. Even if the pallet fits, fit does not establish structural capacity or clear access. The revised plan must include workers below and the delivery transition.

Excavation review covers soil/protective design, water, adjacent structures and loads, utilities, atmosphere, access, equipment and daily/changed-condition inspection. A trench box is not a universal approval. Verify the actual work point lies in the intended protected arrangement and access remains usable. A worker's path to a ladder can be interrupted by installed pipe even though the ladder location did not change.

**Worked case:** Yesterday's five-foot trench was dry; overnight rain enters and a delivery truck is now parked by the edge. A supervisor cannot reuse yesterday's inspection to authorize entry. Obtain current competent assessment and protective decisions addressing changed loading/water/access. Keep affected people out. Do not select soil type by appearance from the office or tell workers to enter to measure the crack first.

The shallow-depth exception for cave-in protection is conditional on competent examination finding no potential indication. A four-foot trench with fresh cracks is not automatically exempt. Likewise, compliant egress distance does not eliminate collapse or atmospheric risk. Keep each control function separate in the review.

**Practice:** A trench has twenty feet travel to an unobstructed ladder, but the proposed work lies outside the shield. **Explained answer:** egress may meet that distance condition while protection at the work point remains unresolved. Hold entry there and obtain the correct protective arrangement. Passing one item cannot compensate for failure of another critical control.

lessons.title: S19 — Fire, material storage and tools across project phases
lessons.body:
## S19 — Fire, material storage and tools across project phases

Fire protection must follow the changing project rather than wait for permanent systems. Identify likely ignition sources, combustible loading, flammable activities, alarm arrangements, accessible suitable equipment and trained response roles. Ensure available fire equipment remains accessible and maintained. A painted extinguisher location on yesterday's plan is not evidence that today's equipment can be reached or used.

Hot work, solvent use and combustible deliveries can conflict even when each trade has a separate permit or checklist. Coordinate their timing, space and control requirements through appropriate competent decisions. Openings can transmit sparks or vapor between areas. Do not invent a universal separation distance or fire-watch duration; obtain the applicable task/site requirements and verify implementation. Do not expand firefighting duties for an untrained worker because stopping is inconvenient.

**Worked case:** Welding is scheduled beside a route where a second contractor will transfer a flammable coating. The coating crew assumes the welder will be finished; the welding crew knows of no delivery. The supervisor holds conflicting work and coordinates a verified sequence/separation, access, atmosphere/ignition review and responsible communication. Two signed documents do not resolve incompatible physical conditions.

Materials create static and changing loads. Check storage support, stability, access and proximity to edges/openings, with competent structural advice where needed. Delivery acceptance must account for unloading and staging, not only final storage. Do not place a heavy load on a temporary floor based on its finished-design appearance. Protect routes from protrusions, falling stacks and waste buildup. Removing a supporting piece can destabilize the remainder.

**Storage case:** A stack is moved closer to a working edge to clear a walkway, but its support and falling-object exposure are unverified. The move may trade one hazard for another. Coordinate an approved storage location and access plan before movement. Do not ask laborers to hold a leaning stack while others pass or allow a rescue impulse to create a crushing casualty.

Tool oversight includes selection, guards, compatible accessories, condition, supply and the trained method for changes or servicing. A repaired cord does not cure a missing guard. An accessory that physically fits does not establish its rating or suitability. Remove unsafe equipment from the operational path using the employer's method, provide suitable replacement and verify that production pressure does not drive improvised use.

**Practice:** A grinder is repaired, but sparks now reach newly delivered packaging. **Explained answer:** equipment repair is only one readiness condition. Reassess the surrounding ignition/exposure path and establish suitable area controls before use. Reopen the affected plan rather than treating the earlier defect ticket as universal clearance.

lessons.title: S20 — Confined-space interfaces, ergonomic changes and release decisions
lessons.body:
## S20 — Confined-space interfaces, ergonomic changes and release decisions

Construction can create or alter confined spaces during the project. A competent person must identify relevant spaces and permit-space hazards before directed work begins. The controlling contractor, host and entry employers have information/coordination roles under the applicable rule. A supervisor should know who evaluates the space, who controls entry, who communicates simultaneous activities and who authorizes a changed condition. A generic orientation card is not entry authorization.

Prevent unauthorized entry into identified permit spaces. If entry is planned, the required written program, roles, controls, testing and rescue arrangements must actually be established for that work. An open hatch, a single acceptable reading, a fan or a harness cannot independently prove safe entry. Alternate procedures and reclassification have conditions that must be demonstrated; a supervisor cannot declare them merely to speed work. This course does not teach entry execution or technical rescue.

**Worked case:** Electrical work is scheduled in a vault while another contractor applies a coating near its opening. The original evaluation considered a different task with no nearby vapor source. Hold entry and coordinate reevaluation of the changed atmosphere and work interfaces through the appropriate program. Communicate restrictions to both crews. Do not send a worker in to see whether the coating can be smelled.

Rescue readiness is more than a telephone number. The actual arrangement must fit location, access, hazards and timely capable response. If a worker collapses, activate that emergency arrangement and prevent impulsive untrained entry. A supervisor who orders a second entrant without controls can worsen the event. Preserve accountability and accurate location/hazard information for responders.

Ergonomic planning examines posture, force, repetition, duration, grip and routes. A lighter individual package can still create greater total handling if deliveries double or access worsens. Include workers in evaluating alternatives and verify the real task. A powered aid can reduce lifting but introduce pinch, crush and traffic paths; competent operators and suitable layout still matter.

**Worked model:** A worker moves thirty packages of twenty kilograms: total handled mass is six hundred kilograms, which is not a safe-lifting limit. Repacking into fifteen-kilogram units and increasing the count to forty preserves six hundred kilograms total. Smaller packages may reduce single-lift load but do not prove the task is safer; reach, grip, frequency, fatigue and aids must also be evaluated. No universal safe weight is supplied by this calculation.

**Practice:** Rotate workers between two tasks with the same overhead reach and wrist force. **Explained answer:** changing job labels may not change the relevant exposure. Redesign task geometry, methods or assistance and verify the approved trial safely with worker feedback. Do not dismiss symptoms because rotation was documented.

**Release exercise:** Write what changed, exposed people, critical controls, actual evidence, competent decision owner, communication and stop/review triggers. For the vault, absent atmospheric/interface/rescue evidence remains a hold; for material handling, unverified aid/traffic interactions remain unresolved. A complete decision honestly states what cannot yet proceed.


---

courses.title: VUC012 | VUC011 formative checks

content.title: VUC012 | VUC011 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC011 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC011 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Explain corrected reasoning after each error.

lessons.title: C01-L1
lessons.body:
## C01-L1

What belongs in a useful opening-hazard report?

**Explained answer:** Observed location/condition/time, people exposed and immediate protection needed, with uncertainty preserved.

**Correction/remediation:** Report facts without entering danger to collect evidence.

lessons.title: C01-L2
lessons.body:
## C01-L2

Does a near miss belong in a fabricated injury record?

**Explained answer:** No; accurately report the near miss separately without inventing injury or treatment.

**Correction/remediation:** Different reporting purposes require truthful facts.

lessons.title: C02-L1
lessons.body:
## C02-L1

Does a harness alone establish a safe fall-arrest arrangement?

**Explained answer:** No; suitable compatible equipment, anchorage, clearance, inspection, training and rescue arrangements remain necessary.

**Correction/remediation:** A component is not a system.

lessons.title: C02-L2
lessons.body:
## C02-L2

Why can a three-foot floor opening still need protection?

**Explained answer:** Stepping/tripping through and other hazards remain; six feet is not a universal exemption.

**Correction/remediation:** Apply the actual opening and task provisions.

lessons.title: C03-L1
lessons.body:
## C03-L1

What should happen after a tool repeatedly trips in wet conditions?

**Explained answer:** Stop affected use and obtain proper fault/supply assessment; do not bypass protection.

**Correction/remediation:** The interruption can indicate unresolved exposure.

lessons.title: C03-L2
lessons.body:
## C03-L2

Does an old services drawing prove drilling is safe?

**Explained answer:** No; establish actual concealed-service risk and controls before drilling.

**Correction/remediation:** An outdated drawing is not current verification.

lessons.title: C04-L1
lessons.body:
## C04-L1

Does seeing the operator establish a safe pedestrian crossing?

**Explained answer:** No; the controlled communication/separation arrangement must be established.

**Correction/remediation:** Do not assume the operator sees or can stop for you.

lessons.title: C04-L2
lessons.body:
## C04-L2

Why is a hard hat insufficient beneath a suspended load?

**Explained answer:** It does not control the load path or prevent crushing; remain outside the exclusion area.

**Correction/remediation:** PPE does not authorize hazardous positioning.

lessons.title: C05-L1
lessons.body:
## C05-L1

Why is a stopped mixer not automatically safe to unjam?

**Explained answer:** Stored energy and unexpected movement/restart may remain; authorized safe servicing is needed.

**Correction/remediation:** No reach based on switch position alone.

lessons.title: C05-L2
lessons.body:
## C05-L2

Name both sides of the trap beside an excavator and a wall.

**Explained answer:** Moving counterweight/equipment and fixed wall, with worker in the closing gap.

**Correction/remediation:** Identify the mechanism, not just the machine name.

lessons.title: C06-L1
lessons.body:
## C06-L1

Why does PPE fit matter?

**Explained answer:** Poor fit can expose the worker, impair grip or interfere with other required protection.

**Correction/remediation:** Select suitable compatible protection, not just a nominal size.

lessons.title: C06-L2
lessons.body:
## C06-L2

Can a worker select a respirator cartridge by odor alone?

**Explained answer:** No; use the applicable assessed respiratory program and required competence/fit/training.

**Correction/remediation:** Smell does not establish contaminant protection.

lessons.title: C07-L1
lessons.body:
## C07-L1

What changes when wet outdoor cutting becomes dry indoor cutting?

**Explained answer:** Exposure/control conditions and environment; hold unsupported work and obtain the appropriate control route.

**Correction/remediation:** Unchanged material does not mean unchanged exposure.

lessons.title: C07-L2
lessons.body:
## C07-L2

A heated worker becomes confused and collapses. What is the priority?

**Explained answer:** Activate emergency help promptly, assist cooling as trained and do not leave them alone.

**Correction/remediation:** Do not wait for routine paperwork or send them away alone.

lessons.title: C08-L1
lessons.body:
## C08-L1

What is the one-quarter base offset for a twelve-foot supported ladder length?

**Explained answer:** Three feet, with actual instructions and all other safe-setup conditions still required.

**Correction/remediation:** Arithmetic alone does not approve a ladder.

lessons.title: C08-L2
lessons.body:
## C08-L2

What happens after equipment strikes an already inspected scaffold?

**Explained answer:** Keep off and obtain competent reassessment for changed integrity.

**Correction/remediation:** The morning tag does not settle the new condition.

lessons.title: C09-L1
lessons.body:
## C09-L1

Does a depth less than five feet always remove cave-in protection concerns?

**Explained answer:** No; the shallow exception requires competent examination finding no potential cave-in indication.

**Correction/remediation:** Fresh cracks invalidate a blanket depth argument.

lessons.title: C09-L2
lessons.body:
## C09-L2

What is wrong with thirty-foot lateral travel to a ladder in a five-foot trench?

**Explained answer:** It exceeds the twenty-five-foot maximum travel arrangement; safe egress must be corrected before affected entry.

**Correction/remediation:** A ladder merely existing is insufficient.

lessons.title: C10-L1
lessons.body:
## C10-L1

Can a worker enter an unassessed vault to retrieve a dropped tool?

**Explained answer:** No; preserve no-entry boundary and use the responsible evaluated process.

**Correction/remediation:** Property retrieval is not an entry authorization.

lessons.title: C10-L2
lessons.body:
## C10-L2

What information improves an emergency location report?

**Explained answer:** Exact site area/elevation or excavation, access point, observed emergency and relevant hazards.

**Correction/remediation:** A street address may not locate the person within the site.


---

courses.title: VUC012 | VUC012 supervisor formative checks

content.title: VUC012 | VUC012 supervisor formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC012 supervisor formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC012 supervisor formative checks

Attempt first, then explain and correct any error. The twenty C-domain checks are embedded separately.

lessons.title: S11-L1
lessons.body:
## S11-L1

Why can a foundation-stage traffic plan fail during steel delivery?

**Explained answer:** Work phases, loads, routes and trade interfaces change; review current conditions and coordinate protection.

**Correction:** A prior plan is not proof of current readiness.

lessons.title: S11-L2
lessons.body:
## S11-L2

An exclusion zone blocks the sole emergency access. What must be resolved?

**Explained answer:** A coordinated layout or sequence protecting both the lifting zone and emergency access.

**Correction:** Do not exchange one uncontrolled hazard for another.

lessons.title: S12-L1
lessons.body:
## S12-L1

Sum the model clearance components 1.8,1.0,0.3,1.5 and1.0 metres.

**Explained answer:** 5.6 metres; it is a supplied model, not actual system approval.

**Correction:** Use all components and preserve model limits.

lessons.title: S12-L2
lessons.body:
## S12-L2

Can temporary supports be removed because concrete looks hard?

**Explained answer:** No; actual authorized design/release criteria govern.

**Correction:** Appearance does not establish load capacity.

lessons.title: S13-L1
lessons.body:
## S13-L1

For model load1000kg-force and symmetric legs at30degrees above horizontal, find tension per leg.

**Explained answer:** 1000kg-force from W/(2sin theta).

**Correction:** Static model excludes unequal/dynamic loading and cannot select rigging.

lessons.title: S13-L2
lessons.body:
## S13-L2

Does switching off electrical power prove all energy is controlled?

**Explained answer:** No; other and stored sources and interfaces require applicable authorized control/verification.

**Correction:** Command state is not a complete protected state.

lessons.title: S14-L1
lessons.body:
## S14-L1

Find eight-hour average for2hours at100,4at25,2at0 micrograms per cubic metre.

**Explained answer:** 37.5 micrograms per cubic metre.

**Correction:** Calculation is not a complete exposure/program assessment.

lessons.title: S14-L2
lessons.body:
## S14-L2

Does owning a dust extractor prove control implementation?

**Explained answer:** No; actual configuration, operation, maintenance and task conditions must match the supported method.

**Correction:** Ownership is not performance.

lessons.title: S15-L1
lessons.body:
## S15-L1

Does a public emergency number establish rescue capability at height?

**Explained answer:** No; actual capable response, access, resources and coordination must be established.

**Correction:** Do not infer technical rescue from contact information.

lessons.title: S15-L2
lessons.body:
## S15-L2

A drill finds a radio dead zone. What closes the corrective action?

**Explained answer:** A corrected arrangement verified under representative conditions, preserving original finding.

**Correction:** Filing the report alone is not correction.

lessons.title: S16-L1
lessons.body:
## S16-L1

Do favorable injury counts justify leaving missing edge protection unresolved?

**Explained answer:** No; known serious exposure requires effective action.

**Correction:** Lagging data cannot override current hazardous conditions.

lessons.title: S16-L2
lessons.body:
## S16-L2

What makes an inspection correction verifiable?

**Explained answer:** Actual condition/control evidence, responsible owner, location, time and effectiveness findings.

**Correction:** A green label or promise is not observed closure.

lessons.title: S17-L1
lessons.body:
## S17-L1

Does orientation appoint someone scaffold competent person?

**Explained answer:** No; subject-specific competence and employer corrective authority must be established.

**Correction:** Title or attendance is not demonstrated capability.

lessons.title: S17-L2
lessons.body:
## S17-L2

Twenty-foot supported ladder length gives what model base offset?

**Explained answer:** Five feet, with actual suitable setup and layout still required.

**Correction:** Do not approve blocked access from arithmetic alone.

lessons.title: S18-L1
lessons.body:
## S18-L1

What changes when a pallet is proposed on a tool-use scaffold?

**Explained answer:** Actual load/configuration/access and falling-object demands require supported review.

**Correction:** Physical fit does not prove capacity.

lessons.title: S18-L2
lessons.body:
## S18-L2

Can yesterday’s dry-trench inspection settle entry after rain and new edge traffic?

**Explained answer:** No; current competent reassessment must address changed conditions.

**Correction:** Old evidence does not describe the new load/water arrangement.

lessons.title: S19-L1
lessons.body:
## S19-L1

Why can two separate permits fail to control welding beside coating transfer?

**Explained answer:** Their simultaneous ignition/vapor/access interactions may be unaddressed.

**Correction:** Coordinate the combined work before exposure.

lessons.title: S19-L2
lessons.body:
## S19-L2

A repaired grinder throws sparks into new packaging. Is the job ready?

**Explained answer:** No; surrounding ignition/exposure conditions still need supported control.

**Correction:** Repair closure is not whole-task clearance.

lessons.title: S20-L1
lessons.body:
## S20-L1

Does a fan and harness establish safe vault entry?

**Explained answer:** No; applicable evaluation/program, competent roles, controls and rescue evidence remain necessary.

**Correction:** Equipment presence is not entry permission.

lessons.title: S20-L2
lessons.body:
## S20-L2

Compare30packages×20kg with40×15kg.

**Explained answer:** Both total600kg handled; neither total nor smaller package alone proves safe ergonomics.

**Correction:** Assess actual force/reach/grip/frequency and aids.


---

courses.title: VUC012 | VUC011 — applied learning and observed worker assessments

content.title: VUC012 | VUC011 — applied learning and observed worker assessments
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC011 — applied learning and observed worker assessments
lessons.body:
# VUC011 — applied learning and observed worker assessments

Use only synthetic drawings, case cards and inert props. Equipment: paper/drawing tool, calculator, inert damaged/serviceable PPE and ladder/cord photographs or the descriptions below. No climbing, energized tools, actual trench entry, chemical handling, live traffic, suspended loads or rescue entry. An instructor competent in construction hazard recognition assesses worker decisions; specialist operation is outside this credential.

First work each case with discussion. Explain the supplied answer. For independent assessment use the fresh variant, with no answer/rubric visible. If already coached on that variant, prepare and retain a new equivalent case. Five criteria each score 0 absent/unsafe, 1 incomplete/prompted, 2 independently correct. Pass 8/10 and every **critical** criterion 2. Stop a hazardous demonstration, record failure and remediate. No score compensates for an unsafe critical decision.

lessons.title: A — report a changing opening and preserve facts
lessons.body:
## A — report a changing opening and preserve facts

**Inputs:** fictional site West Deck; 08:10 rail removed for delivery; 08:20 pedestrian route remains open; no injury reported; 08:35 inspection booked but not performed. Another contractor controls the opening. Worker has a safe alternate ground route. Supervisor asks to record “inspected 08:10.”

**Tasks:** make a 60-second report; select immediate worker action; distinguish observed facts, scheduled inspection and unknowns; draft a truthful record; explain escalation if correction is refused. Do not actually send a complaint or alert.

**Worked answer:** keep away/use approved alternate, report exact opening/time/exposure and seek coordinated protection. Do not backdate inspection or invent injury. Keep reports factual and use the appropriate safety/emergency/rights routes as circumstances require.

**Criteria:** precise factual report; protects exposed access **critical**; identifies contractor coordination; preserves true times **critical**; appropriate escalation rather than unsafe evidence gathering.

**Fresh variant:** rail is restored, but a cover is now displaced for a hose and a new crew was not told. Correct response addresses the current hole/communication; it does not keep reporting the already repaired rail.

lessons.title: B — fall and access decision
lessons.body:
## B — fall and access decision

**Inputs:** sketch a deck seven feet above a lower slab; duct destination near open edge; no approved anchor; pipe nearby; ladder has sixteen-foot supported working length, damaged rung and unstable base; scaffold has a morning tag but was struck at noon. No climbing is required.

**Tasks:** mark three exposures and safe hold areas; calculate the ladder model offset; explain what that does not approve; choose a protected method through the responsible people; list what would require reassessment.

**Worked answer:** hold exposed duct move; do not assume pipe anchorage. Four-foot model offset does not cure damaged ladder/base. Keep off struck scaffold pending competent reassessment. Obtain suitable protected access/work and relevant system/rescue evidence rather than improvise.

**Criteria:** fall mechanism; no invented anchor/exposed work **critical**; ladder arithmetic and limits; respects scaffold changed condition **critical**; supported alternate/restart evidence.

**Fresh variant:** ladder working length twenty feet gives five-foot offset, ladder is serviceable but overhead-line relationship unknown; scaffold base is intact but a brace was removed. Hold unresolved conditions instead of repeating “damaged rung.”

lessons.title: C — electricity, struck-by and trapped-space map
lessons.body:
## C — electricity, struck-by and trapped-space map

**Inputs:** draw a ten-metre-wide yard with a wall at east, excavator swing next to wall, pedestrian crossing through unloading zone, hanging pipe bundle, wet cord with damaged insulation and an unassessed overhead line above the proposed raised-load route. Safe pedestrian route is west of a fixed barrier.

**Tasks:** mark object/contact/crush paths; select worker route; report electrical defect; explain why eye contact and a low load do not suffice; state limits of your role.

**Worked answer:** use west controlled route; keep out of swing/load zone, no squeezing beside wall or passing under bundle. Hold damaged equipment and raised-load uncertainty for competent correction/planning. No touching/repairing live parts or becoming an untrained spotter.

**Criteria:** identifies paths and both crush surfaces; safe route **critical**; no suspended-load entry **critical**; electrical hold/no bypass **critical**; reports and preserves qualified-role boundaries.

**Fresh variant:** overhead issue resolved and cord replaced, but a new cutting operation directs fragments toward west route. Coordinate a verified safe alternative or hold; do not rely on a route that has newly become exposed.

lessons.title: D — PPE and task-health change
lessons.body:
## D — PPE and task-health change

**Inputs:** inert eyewear with loose fit; face shield interfering with hearing protector; unidentified liquid in bottle; mock Seal-R extract from C07; concrete-cutting job moved indoors with failed water feed; worker reports confusion in heat. No real substances or dust.

**Tasks:** inspect/adjust inert PPE or explain why replacement is needed; match information to product; decide cutting disposition; prioritize the heat case; explain respiratory boundary.

**Worked answer:** select compatible fitting protection, no guessed liquid identity or glove compatibility. Hold unsupported dry indoor task and obtain complete assessed method. Severe heat symptoms need immediate emergency assistance and care/cooling as trained. A cabinet mask does not establish respiratory authorization.

**Criteria:** safe fitting/compatibility demonstration; truthful product-information limit; stops unsupported dust exposure **critical**; urgent heat response **critical**; no independent hazardous testing/respirator prescription.

**Fresh variant:** water feed works, but the task/equipment differs from the previously assessed method; PPE fits but is cracked. Reassess actual method and replace damaged protection rather than treating water alone as compliance.

lessons.title: E — excavation entry boundary
lessons.body:
## E — excavation entry boundary

**Inputs:** fictional five-foot trench, worker point thirty feet laterally from ladder, water after overnight rain, spoil at edge, box present but work point outside protected area, utility location unresolved. A supervisor calls it “the same as yesterday.”

**Tasks:** mark entry hold, protection/access/environment uncertainties; calculate excess lateral travel over the twenty-five-foot arrangement; name responsible competent reassessment; state response if someone collapses.

**Worked answer:** no entry into unverified conditions; travel exceeds arrangement by five feet. Box presence is not complete work-point protection. Obtain current competent inspection, utilities/protection/access/water decisions. Call trained emergency response, no untrained entry rescue.

**Criteria:** identifies multiple hazards; no unsupported entry **critical**; correct travel reasoning; competent current reassessment; no improvised rescue **critical**.

**Fresh variant:** depth four-and-a-half feet, travel twenty feet, fresh cracks and damaged protective arrangement. Egress distance is not the failure; shallow depth does not override cave-in indication. Preserve current facts.

lessons.title: F — tools, material and emergency coordination
lessons.body:
## F — tools, material and emergency coordination

**Inputs:** grinder guard missing and accessory unsuitable; stack leaning into exit; unassessed vault with dropped tool; fictional emergency caller knows street but not gate/level. Worker is not a repairer, rigger or rescuer.

**Tasks:** prioritize affected holds, write a coordinated report, rehearse precise emergency call without sending it, explain no-entry/retrieval boundary, describe actual restart evidence.

**Worked answer:** do not run grinder; keep people clear of stack and arrange supported stabilization/alternate route; prevent unauthorized vault entry. Provide exact area, safe gate/access and observed hazard in call. Restart only on actual corrected conditions and appropriate authority; do not invent specialist work to finish the exercise.

**Criteria:** tool hold **critical**; no personal stabilization/unsafe stack approach **critical**; vault no-entry **critical**; usable emergency-location communication; evidence-based restart/coordination.

**Fresh variant:** grinder repaired but delivery blocks exit again, and a new worker offers to enter vault wearing a harness. Keep current access and entry limits; equipment possession does not create rescue/entry capability.

lessons.title: Blank performance record — one per actual attempt
lessons.body:
## Blank performance record — one per actual attempt

Learner____ Version____ Date/time____ Assessor and competence____ Station/variant____ Attempt____

| Criterion | Actual observed response/action | Score 0/1/2 | Critical? | Evidence/notes |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
|1| | | | |
|2| | | | |
|3| | | | |
|4| | | | |
|5| | | | |

Total____/10. Every critical criterion independently 2?____. Result pass/fail/not assessed____. Failed reasoning____. Remediation____. Fresh reassessment inputs____. Assessor signature____. Learner acknowledgment____. Restrictions: orientation decisions only; no specialist authorization.

lessons.title: Blank worker hazard report used in cases
lessons.body:
## Blank worker hazard report used in cases

Exact location/time____ Observed condition____ Who/what could be exposed____ Safe immediate action____ Responsible contact____ Unverified facts____ Required correction/verification____ Current restrictions____ Actual follow-up/time____. Keep fictional reports within the course; never create live operational incidents as a practice action.


---

courses.title: VUC012 | VUC012 — supervisor applied assessments

content.title: VUC012 | VUC012 — supervisor applied assessments
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC012 — supervisor applied assessments
lessons.body:
# VUC012 — supervisor applied assessments

Use synthetic plans, paper, calculator and inert PPE only. No live lifts, height exposure, excavation/space entry, energized work or hazardous material. Instructor must be competent in construction supervision and the mathematical/role limits taught here. This evaluates planning and communication, not specialist operation.

The six embedded worker stations A–F remain required. These eight supervisor stations add direct planning, calculation and implementation decisions. Each uses five criteria scored 0 absent/unsafe, 1 incomplete/prompted, 2 independently correct. Pass 8/10 with every **critical** criterion 2. First cases are coached; independent attempts use fresh variants not previously solved for the learner. Retain actual inputs, responses and failures. A completed worksheet without sound reasoning is not a pass.

lessons.title: P1 — three-trade logistics and instruction
lessons.body:
## P1 — three-trade logistics and instruction

**Input:** fictional North Corridor connects emergency gate to occupied work area. 09:00–11:00 pipe lifting uses its north half; 09:30 masonry delivery crosses it; scaffold access opens into the same zone. Only south route is available, but waste currently blocks it. New crew has not heard the briefing.

**Task:** draw controlled routes and work sequence, state holds, assign coordination owner, brief three trade roles and obtain teach-back. Include a change trigger and required competent inputs.

**Expected:** no exposed pedestrian/delivery overlap or blocked emergency route. Clear/verify suitable alternate before reliance or reschedule conflicting operations. No assumed crane visibility. Communicate actual timing/access/stop authority to new crew; do not claim briefing completion from a signature alone.

**Criteria:** identifies interfaces; protects load zone **critical**; preserves emergency access **critical**; empowered owner/sequence; understandable briefing/teach-back/change trigger.

**Variant:** lifting finishes, but new temporary-power work exposes parts beside the south route. Adapt the plan to current exposure rather than leave the “safe” route unchanged.

lessons.title: P2 — fall and temporary-structure release
lessons.body:
## P2 — fall and temporary-structure release

**Input:** synthetic clearance components 1.8+1.0+0.3+1.5+1.0 metres; available 4.8m. Temporary support blocks delivery. Concrete strength/release evidence absent. Proposed anchor is an unidentified pipe; no rescue arrangement supplied.

**Task:** calculate model total/shortfall; mark unknowns; issue supported hold; request appropriate design/manufacturer/competent evidence; state what cannot be approved from this packet.

**Key:** 5.6m model, 0.8m short. Reject arrangement as supplied; real system needs actual approved basis. No arbitrary pipe anchor or support removal from appearance. Require safe method/rescue and actual structural release evidence.

**Criteria:** arithmetic; no deficient fall arrangement **critical**; no invented anchor/design **critical**; preserves temporary support **critical**; competent evidence/restart decision.

**Variant:** components total 5.2m and available 5.8m. The positive 0.6m difference does not approve actual system: anchor and rescue still unverified. Do not memorize “shortfall” when the new arithmetic differs.

lessons.title: P3 — lift model and stored-energy boundary
lessons.body:
## P3 — lift model and stored-energy boundary

**Input:** ideal symmetric two-leg model W=1000kg-force, angle30° above horizontal; compare60°. Real hardware/rating/ground data absent. Connected feeder can discharge into maintenance area; pneumatic state unknown. Spotter radio fails during the hypothetical setup.

**Task:** calculate two tensions, explain limitations, identify energy/material paths and declare holds/communication response. Do not design actual rigging.

**Key:** 1000kg-force at30°, about577.35 at60°. Smaller angle increases ideal tension. No production selection from model. Hold unsupported lift/movement, restore communication and obtain complete qualified lift/control basis. Control all interfaces through authorized process.

**Criteria:** arithmetic/angle reference; model not capacity **critical**; recognizes connected sources; no unsupported concurrent operation **critical**; agreed communication/stop and competent review.

**Variant:** W=1200kg-force at30° gives1200; electrical power confirmed off but gravity feed remains. Keep that source explicit rather than treating one isolation as complete.

lessons.title: P4 — health-control implementation and privacy
lessons.body:
## P4 — health-control implementation and privacy

**Input:** model2h×100+4h×25+2h×0 micrograms/m³; task now indoors with collector hose disconnected; coating identity unknown. Private medical details appear in a proposed crew-wide report.

**Task:** calculate average; explain why it is not a compliance release; identify actual exposure-control failure and material uncertainty; propose competent assessment questions; restrict medical information appropriately.

**Key:**37.5micrograms/m³. Actual sample representativeness, applicable obligations, routes and control implementation remain. Hold unsupported disturbance; obtain task/material/control basis. Do not send private medical details broadly.

**Criteria:** arithmetic/units; no average-only approval **critical**; failed control/material action **critical**; competent representative assessment; privacy boundary.

**Variant:**2h×80+4h×20+2h×0=30; collector works but material/task does not match supported method. Reassess the match, not just hose connection.

lessons.title: P5 — PPE/access/scaffold readiness
lessons.body:
## P5 — PPE/access/scaffold readiness

**Input:** eyewear dislodged by head/hearing protection; twenty-foot supported ladder would need base in exit; scaffold tag current before brace removal; foreman holds only general orientation certificate.

**Task:** demonstrate inert fit review, calculate model offset, decide access/structure disposition, identify competence/authority gap and record truthful correction requirements.

**Key:** five-foot model offset cannot justify exit obstruction. Obtain compatible properly fitting PPE, suitable alternate access and authorized scaffold reassessment. Orientation does not appoint competent person. No backdated inspection or use before required correction.

**Criteria:** fit/compatibility; safe access decision **critical**; changed scaffold hold **critical**; correct role boundary; truthful evidence/verification.

**Variant:**24-foot supported length gives6-foot offset; scaffold intact but heavy pallet proposed without capacity evidence. Keep load review unresolved even though brace is present.

lessons.title: P6 — excavation and temporary loads
lessons.body:
## P6 — excavation and temporary loads

**Input:** five-foot trench, overnight rain, new truck parked at edge, pipe blocks route to ladder, shield present but work beyond it. Competent inspector unavailable until afternoon. Delivery manager wants entry now.

**Task:** mark exposures, establish hold/alternate schedule, assign current competent review, distinguish separate control functions and explain emergency limits.

**Expected:** no entry until actual water/load/protection/access/utility/atmosphere issues are addressed as applicable. No reliance on yesterday or box presence. Preserve restriction and coordinate responsible review; no untrained rescue if someone collapses.

**Criteria:** identifies changed conditions; entry hold **critical**; actual work-point protection **critical**; usable escape/competent coordination; rescue boundary **critical**.

**Variant:** four-foot depth and clear twenty-foot egress but fresh cracking. Egress improvement does not remove cave-in indication or make shallow exception unconditional.

lessons.title: P7 — fire/material/tool coordination
lessons.body:
## P7 — fire/material/tool coordination

**Input:** welder10:00–12:00; flammable transfer10:30–11:00 shared airspace; extinguisher behind packaging; stack moved toward edge without support review; repaired grinder accessory rating unknown.

**Task:** prioritize holds and shared plan; state fire readiness/role needs; evaluate transferred storage risk; identify actual tool evidence; assign verification owners.

**Expected:** coordinate competent compatible work sequence and controls; restore accessible suitable fire arrangements; no untrained firefighting assignment. No unverified edge storage or accessory use. Verify actual correction rather than close on promises.

**Criteria:** simultaneous-work control **critical**; actual fire readiness; storage support/exposure **critical**; tool suitability **critical**; empowered owners and verified release.

**Variant:** welding complete and extinguisher accessible, but new grinder sparks reach stored coating. Review current ignition path rather than reauthorize from completed welding paperwork.

lessons.title: P8 — vault, handling and investigation capstone
lessons.body:
## P8 — vault, handling and investigation capstone

**Input:** vault evaluation predates coating at opening; single gas reading and fan offered as permission; rescue plan only lists a phone number. Handling changes from30×20kg to40×15kg. Near miss recorded after schedule pressure; manager wants “worker careless” as whole explanation.

**Task:** decide entry hold and coordination; calculate handling comparison with limits; identify evidence needs for investigation; prepare a truthful management brief and verification plan.

**Key:** entry conditions/program/interfaces/rescue require actual capable review; no equipment-only entry approval. Both models600kg total, not equal risk proof. Preserve accounts/times and examine work/control/coordination mechanisms. Assign effective corrections with worker input and test actual outcomes.

**Criteria:** no unsupported entry **critical**; no invented rescue **critical**; arithmetic/ergonomic limits; truthful evidence and causal reasoning; concrete owners/effectiveness verification.

**Variant:** coating removed but rescue remains unestablished; handling24×25kg versus40×15kg still600kg each. Do not let one resolved issue clear all other conditions.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Hazardous Waste Site Operations
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Hazardous Waste Site Operations

VUC013 • Original material package • 2026-11-17 • Counterpart subject: HAZWOPER 40-hour general cleanup worker training.

lessons.title: Audience, boundaries and outcomes
lessons.body:
## Audience, boundaries and outcomes

For workers assigned to covered hazardous-waste cleanup who need the general-site-worker instructional pathway. This is a complete instructional and assessment package for facilitated delivery, not a declaration that its reader has completed forty hours. It does not issue an OSHA card, external accreditation, emergency-response technician qualification, supervisor endorsement, respirator medical approval or site access authorization.

Entry needs: a role-specific training needs review; ability to understand the instruction through suitable language/access accommodations; and readiness for the assigned safe practical activities. Before any actual required respirator use obtain applicable medical evaluation and fit testing. Never solicit clinical histories in classroom worksheets. If equipment practice cannot be performed safely, defer the affected practical and record it incomplete. A paper substitute cannot earn a physical skill sign-off.

By completion the learner can classify the operation; distinguish cleanup, TSD and emergency roles; construct a source/pathway/receptor model; interpret exposure evidence without false clearance; use a site briefing and controls; demonstrate assigned clean monitoring/PPE/decontamination tasks; recognize container and physical hazards; implement communications and withdrawal; report exposure and emergencies; preserve accurate records; and identify requirements still needed before field work. H01–H20 and the coverage map give assessable subobjectives.

lessons.title: Delivery plan: forty actual instructional hours
lessons.body:
## Delivery plan: forty actual instructional hours

Five days of eight instructional hours, excluding breaks, meals and administrative waiting. Days may be divided for accommodations while preserving actual time and learning sequence. Do not award planned hours as attendance. Each two-hour block includes 35 minutes of instruction/demonstration, 55 minutes of individual or rotating practice, 20 minutes of feedback and 10 minutes of learning checks. For final-exam blocks use the allocation specified below. Adjust the division to learner need while maintaining demonstrated outcomes and forty actual hours.

| Day | Four two-hour blocks | Materials and outputs |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Scope/role/records; toxicology and chemical information; characterization and briefing; zones and communication | H01,H05,H07–H09,H13; stations A,B; individual scope, site model and briefing |
| 2 | Monitoring concepts; instrument demonstration and practice; clothing selection; respirator program and equipment | H02,H10–H12; stations C,D,E; each learner operates clean trainer and documents limitations |
| 3 | PPE inspection/donning/doffing; decontamination setup; decontamination repetitions; heat/medical/sanitation | H03,H11,H12,H14,H17; stations D,E,F,G; each learner performs rather than only watches |
| 4 | Containers/sampling; equipment/excavation/space hazards; emergency organization; emergency and handover drill | H04,H06,H15,H16,H18,H19; stations H,I,J; clean mockups only |
| 5 | Integrated changed-condition exercise; individual practical assessment; controlled final exam; feedback, corrections and field-readiness briefing | H20; station K plus independent reassessments; two-hour final; two-hour feedback/field transition |

If eleven individual station assessments and the required repetitions need more time, extend delivery. Do not reduce a station to a group signature to fit the schedule. Skills observed in days 1–4 can be assessed independently after practice; day 5 resolves remaining observations. Knowledge final is 60 constructed responses, nominal 120 minutes; accommodate access needs without coaching answers. A learner requiring more examination time receives it; time extensions do not reduce other instructional hours.

Trainer prerequisites: documented subject competence and instructional capability, familiarity with the applicable site operation and equipment, and ability to recognize when specialist input is required. Arrange industrial-hygiene and respiratory-program expertise for those blocks. Before delivery, the training director approves the equipment-specific procedures, emergency arrangements and adaptation to employer tasks. The generic package cannot pre-fill a real site's hazards or manufacturer instructions.

Adopt the nonmandatory Appendix E ratio recommendations as this program's delivery ceiling: at most30 learners per instructor for classroom work,10 for Level C/D PPE exercises and5 for Level A/B exercises. Use smaller groups where needed for individual observation. These are program delivery choices based on guidance, not a claim that Appendix E is itself mandatory law. Record the PPE levels actually used. Do not advertise hands-on Level A/B if only photographs or paper cards were used.

Equipment: clean suits/gloves/boots in suitable sizes; assigned respirator trainers and manuals; medically suitable conditions for actual wearing; calibrated/maintained monitoring trainers with manufacturer-authorized test equipment and instructions; mock logs/sample labels/containers; cones/tape/site drawing; communications equipment; safe fluorescent contamination surrogate with its safety information; collection trays and clean decontamination supplies; emergency access/first-aid arrangements. Do not use hazardous waste, deliberate oxygen deficiency, live releases, energized equipment, pressurized suspect drums or uncontrolled heat as teaching aids. Assessors may simulate alarms by display cards without impairing life-support equipment.

lessons.title: Assessment and correction
lessons.body:
## Assessment and correction

Forty explained learning checks are practice. Learners attempt before viewing answers; wrong responses require the related lesson, explanation of the consequence and a changed example. The controlled final and answer key are separate instructor files and must not be supplied with the learner package. Score each of60 final responses0–2:2 required findings and reasoning;1 materially correct but incomplete without dangerous assertion;0 wrong, absent or unsafe. Pass96/120 plus at least4/6 in each of20 domains. An endorsement of unprotected hazardous entry, improvised unknown-drum handling, falsified monitoring, unqualified rescue or removal of protection inside the hazard is a critical failure regardless of aggregate score.

Eleven practical stations each have five criteria scored0/1/2. Pass each at8/10 with every starred critical criterion at2. A critical failure stops the unsafe simulated action immediately, is recorded and requires teaching plus a new independently observed run. The instructor can demonstrate during practice; the final observation must be the learner's own performance. Preserve original scores and correction history.

Retake: diagnose specific objectives, reteach with the supplied changed-condition cards, and give a fresh controlled assessment of failed domains plus the integrated decision domain. Retain passing evidence only if it remains applicable; do not erase the initial attempt. Maximum two reassessments before the director establishes an individualized training plan and additional delivery. A changed number alone is not enough if the learner memorized the decision: change the hazard or evidence defect as well. Protected reassessment cards provide explicit prompts and scoring findings.

lessons.title: Credential and field experience rules
lessons.body:
## Credential and field experience rules

The materials package is complete when instruction, assessments, practical tasks, guides and sources are authored and reviewed. No learner completion is asserted by that fact.

Issue a VNDRLY/U off-site instruction completion record only after actual forty-hour participation, required lesson remediation, final pass and all eleven practical passes. Record name, identity verification, dates, actual hours, program/version, instructor and training director, assessment outcomes, PPE/equipment actually demonstrated, and limitations. This record must say supervised field experience and employer authorization are separate if they have not occurred.

For the general cleanup pathway, actual supervised field experience is at least three days under a trained, experienced supervisor. Use the supplied field record for each day and the final review. A blanket three-day signature with no observed tasks is inadequate. Completion of the off-site and field requirements must be certified by the appropriate instructor and trained supervisor as applicable. Do not assign covered work before the applicable prerequisites are satisfied. Other limited-task24-hour pathways and their transition requirements must be separately justified; this package does not silently downgrade an employee to that pathway.

On-site supervisors have additional specialized training requirements; this worker package is not their additional eight-hour supervisor course. Cleanup workers/supervisors covered by the relevant provisions need eight-hour annual refresher training. Record a refresher due date based on actual completion, but do not claim this initial package delivers the refresher. Changed tasks, equipment, deficiencies or site hazards require further training when needed, even before that date. Emergency response follows its own paragraph(q) role/competency framework and TSD operations their paragraph(p) requirements.

Maintain training/assessment records under the employer's applicable retention requirements; program policy is at least five years for training documentation, without shortening any longer required retention. Medical and exposure records have their own requirements and access protections. Routine training files record operational clearance status and restrictions, not unnecessary diagnoses. External peer review, instructor delivery, medical clearances, field attendance and employer approvals are not represented as already performed by this author review.


---
