lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Confined Space Rescue — Rescue-team instruction
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Confined Space Rescue — Rescue-team instruction

This instruction builds on the embedded entry-team coursebook. It is for designated rescue personnel, not bystanders improvising an entry. Actual qualification is limited to the roles, space configurations and equipment independently demonstrated. No reading or written examination establishes physical rescue competence. Training uses representative safe mock spaces and dummies; hazardous atmospheres, engulfment, uncontrolled energy and unprotected suspension are never created for an exercise.

lessons.title: R01 — Decide what rescue capability must exist before entry
lessons.body:
## R01 — Decide what rescue capability must exist before entry

A rescue plan begins with the employer's space inventory, not with a truck full of equipment. For each representative space identify the opening dimensions, vertical or horizontal access, internal restrictions, working location, plausible casualty position, atmosphere, energy sources and material pathways. Determine how an incapacitated person can leave wearing the intended protection. A person who walked through a hatch may not fit through it in a stretcher with breathing equipment and a rescuer beside them.

Match response capability to the harm that can occur. Include notification, mobilization, travel, setup and access to the casualty, rather than quoting only driving time. An atmosphere that can rapidly become IDLH may require the capable rescue team at the entry location. A written promise to call emergency services is not a demonstrated capability. Meet the service, share hazards, verify availability and observe a representative rescue exercise. Record deficiencies and correct them before relying on the arrangement.

Choose the least-exposing effective method. If the entrant can exit safely, direct self-rescue. If an appropriate non-entry system can remove the casualty without increasing overall risk, use it under the plan. If entry is necessary, qualified entry rescuers with protection, support and backup must conduct it. A line that cannot move a casualty around an internal obstruction is not a successful non-entry plan. Neither urgency nor the casualty's identity creates missing equipment or competence.

Worked case: a standby service can arrive in twelve minutes, but the assessed event can incapacitate an entrant within minutes. Do not call twelve minutes “prompt” without comparing it to the hazard. Establish a genuinely suitable response or change the planned work so it is not undertaken under that arrangement. In practice, learners produce a space-specific capability matrix and show which tasks and people were actually evaluated.

lessons.title: R02 — Establish command, roles and a protected scene
lessons.body:
## R02 — Establish command, roles and a protected scene

On an alarm, obtain exact location, number of entrants, last known positions, likely hazards, existing controls and what has already happened. Activate the designated rescue and medical response immediately. Establish a command point in a safe location and prevent spontaneous entry. Retain the entry attendant's accountability function; do not strip that role to create a rescuer without competent relief. Assign rescue lead, safety oversight, entry personnel, outside backup, atmospheric monitoring, rigging operation, communications and medical support according to the plan and scale.

One person may perform compatible duties only when workload and simultaneous needs allow; a title chart does not prove adequate staffing. Outside backup must be able to act, not occupied operating every other essential function. Define the leader who authorizes movement and a stop signal anyone can use. Repeat critical commands and confirm receipt. Establish safe zones, keep access clear for emergency vehicles and prevent process operators from changing isolations or ventilation without coordination.

Develop an initial action plan: protect responders, establish controls and reliable information, select method, prepare patient care and exit route, then authorize the operation. Communicate abort criteria and backup actions before entry. If the scene exceeds available capability, summon appropriate resources and prevent further casualties while maintaining safe actions from outside. This is an operational decision, not abandonment of the casualty.

Worked drill: two coworkers rush toward a hatch after hearing a cry. The assigned responder stops them, summons the designated team and obtains the permit/entrant roster. The safety lead discovers traffic blocking the extraction area and resolves it while the technical team prepares. Assess whether these actions happen concurrently without leaving accountability uncovered. Do not place a learner in a dangerous opening to test courage.

lessons.title: R03 — Stabilize energy, material and atmosphere before rescue entry
lessons.body:
## R03 — Stabilize energy, material and atmosphere before rescue entry

Rescue urgency does not make an agitator, inflow or electrical source harmless. Obtain the isolation boundary and verify it with qualified operators. Consider what failed: the original permit may be invalid, a line may have opened or the casualty may have crossed into an untested area. Record the actual status of each relevant control. Prevent unexpected restoration, gravity movement, pressure release and upstream flow. Where a hazard cannot be made acceptably controlled, choose a method and team specifically capable of it; do not pretend a generic certificate supplies that capability.

Sample from a safe position using instruments suitable for all identified hazards, following transport and response times. Continue monitoring at the rescuers' and casualty's actual locations as required. An oxygen/combustible meter cannot rule out every toxin. Unknown or inadequately characterized respiratory exposure must be treated according to IDLH requirements, not guessed from the absence of odor. Evaluate fire, chemical contact, heat and structural hazards in addition to breathing air.

Ventilate using a clean source with a plan that reaches the occupied area and does not introduce ignition or spread exposure to others. Never use oxygen as ventilation. Atmospheric improvement does not establish mechanical isolation or remove the need for the required protection. Record trends and communicate changes promptly. Rescue entry requires its own authorization and continuing control, not automatic reuse of a canceled work permit.

Worked case: the original entry record lists acceptable oxygen, but the rescue sample is falling and a purge valve status is unknown. The team does not rely on the earlier record. It verifies the purge isolation, applies the required respiratory/other protections and reassesses the rescue method. Practice identifying the unknowns and selecting safe controls, with simulated readings only.

lessons.title: R04 — Select and use respiratory protection as a complete system
lessons.body:
## R04 — Select and use respiratory protection as a complete system

An air-purifying respirator does not supply oxygen and is not the response to an unknown or IDLH atmosphere. OSHA's IDLH selection includes a NIOSH-certified full-face pressure-demand SCBA with at least a thirty-minute rated service life, or a combination full-face pressure-demand supplied-air respirator with auxiliary self-contained supply. Rated duration is a test classification, not guaranteed work time. Selection must also address chemicals, temperature, access and escape. Escape-only equipment is not entry equipment.

Before assignment, verify the respiratory program's medical evaluation, appropriate current fit testing, training and equipment serviceability. Inspect the actual unit, cylinder pressure, facepiece, straps, seals, connections, hoses, regulator and alarms under its instructions. Don the unit in the manufacturer sequence, secure fit without twisted straps and perform the required user seal check. A seal check each donning does not replace fit testing. Facial hair or other equipment interfering with the seal is not corrected by pulling straps harder.

Conduct a buddy check of configuration, air supply, communications and snag hazards before entry. Maintain the protection while in the hazardous area; never remove the facepiece to talk or fit through a restriction. The team must practice the actual model's emergency procedures, supplied-air escape transition where used and communication while masked. An improvised regulator swap between incompatible units can be fatal. Approved breathing-air quality and maintained supply are part of the system, not an assumption about a nearby compressor.

Worked exercise: a rescuer presents a valid course certificate but no current fit-test record for the issued facepiece. Do not assign tight-fitting-respirator entry on that basis. Resolve the prerequisite or use another qualified person. In clean-air supervised practice, each learner demonstrates inspection, donning, seal check, communication, planned withdrawal and safe removal; medical clearance is verified before strenuous respiratory drills.

lessons.title: R05 — Manage air, time and rescuer endurance
lessons.body:
## R05 — Manage air, time and rescuer endurance

Plan air for access, work, removal, exit and contingency. The rescuer with the most limiting supply or condition can govern team withdrawal. Heavy exertion, stress, leaks and patient handling can sharply increase consumption. Low-air alarms are emergency warnings, not the planned moment to begin a long exit. Use the team's approved turn-around/reserve policy, actual pressure readings and observed consumption with conservative allowance for changing workload. Never promise a fixed number of rescue minutes from the cylinder label alone.

For a simple training estimate only, suppose a cylinder starts at 4,500 psi and a synthetic plan requires 1,500 psi left at exit. If measured pressure drops 300 psi per minute under representative work, 3,000 usable psi divided by 300 gives ten minutes for all planned entry, work and exit phases before that reserve. A four-minute approach and four-minute return leaves only two minutes for work, before further contingency. That may be unsuitable. Real compressed-air duration depends on the equipment and conditions; the calculation does not authorize an operation or replace the approved air-management plan.

Record entry time/pressure, agreed checkpoints, current pressure, location and exit decision for each member. Outside personnel monitor trends and communicate impending limits. Relieve teams before fatigue, heat or supply removes their ability to return safely. Maintain backup capability when replacing a team; do not consume all ready personnel in the initial entry. If a rescuer has a malfunction, entanglement, heat symptoms or unexpected restriction, execute the practiced emergency response immediately.

Worked case: an entry pair has similar start pressures, but one member consumes air much faster while moving the casualty. The plan adapts to the limiting member rather than averaging their gauges. Rehearse a clean-air drill with simulated pressure reports and identify the decision point that preserves exit and backup. Never deliberately exhaust a real cylinder with a learner inside a mock restriction.

lessons.title: R06 — Inspect, select and assemble a compatible retrieval system
lessons.body:
## R06 — Inspect, select and assemble a compatible retrieval system

Treat anchorage, high point, connectors, rope/cable, lifting device, harness or stretcher, edge protection and backup as one system. Identify each component, intended function, working limits, inspection history and compatibility. The weakest applicable limit governs. A breaking strength is not a working load limit, a material-handling winch is not automatically rated for people, and a fall-arrest device is not automatically a raising/lowering device. Equipment with unknown history, damage, failed inspection or relevant recall is not used until properly resolved.

Survey the support surface and load direction. A tripod placed on unstable ground or subjected to an unapproved side pull can fail even when its catalog capacity appears sufficient. Set leg lengths, pins, feet/restraint and mounting exactly under the matching instructions. Check overhead clearance, load path and the rescue opening. Secure compatible connectors with gates closed/locked and orient them to avoid cross-loading or pressure on gates. Manage sharp edges and moving lines; padding that can shift away is not reliable protection.

Before a person could depend on the system, a second qualified rescuer checks the load path from anchor to casualty, operating/backup functions and control of every transition. Perform the instructed function/preload checks with a dummy or suitable test arrangement. Keep hands out of pinch points. Do not change gear ratios, bypass brakes or add unapproved power tools because the load is difficult. Unexpected resistance requires stopping and finding the cause, not greater effort.

Worked example: a synthetic planned load is 95 kg casualty, 12 kg packaging and 8 kg attached equipment: 115 kg before any rescuer load. Compare the full intended configuration with every applicable rated limit and its conditions. A 100 kg component fails this comparison; a stronger rope does not fix it. A two-person load needs its own compatible system evaluation. The arithmetic is not a universal design factor or proof that an anchor is suitable.

lessons.title: R07 — Control raising, lowering and transitions
lessons.body:
## R07 — Control raising, lowering and transitions

Establish who operates the device, who controls the backup, who watches the opening and who directs patient movement. Use brief agreed commands: ready, take tension, raise, lower, stop, with acknowledgments before movement. Anyone seeing a danger calls stop. One signal source directs routine motion; contradictory instructions are resolved while the load remains secured. Maintain patient/line observation where possible and reliable communication with entry personnel.

Operate the specific winch or rope-control device according to its inspected setup and current instructions. The operator demonstrates the correct direction, controlled speed, stop/hold function, line management and response to malfunction on a dummy first. Never assume a freewheel control is safe under a person's load. Never release a brake, transfer a connector or remove an anchor while that component is carrying an unsecured load. Before each transfer, establish and verify the receiving support, communicate, transfer gradually and confirm it holds before disconnecting the original support.

Mechanical advantage reduces ideal effort at the cost of travel and adds friction, component loads and reset complexity. A simple ideal four-part system supporting a 120 kg-equivalent load would require about 30 kg-equivalent effort and four metres of hauled rope for one metre of lift, ignoring friction. It does not make the anchor load disappear or authorize arbitrary rigging. Use a competent approved design, inspected hardware and the actual device diagram; this chapter is not a license to invent a rope system.

Worked drill: the casualty package reaches the lip but snags. Stop, secure the load, identify the snag and coordinate the planned edge transition; do not jerk or haul harder. A second run introduces a garbled lower command. The operator holds until the command is confirmed. Record both technical control and team communication, since a perfectly assembled system can still be misoperated.

lessons.title: R08 — Access, communicate and protect the casualty
lessons.body:
## R08 — Access, communicate and protect the casualty

Entry rescuers follow the planned route, maintain protection and communication, and monitor conditions continuously as required. Account for line/air-hose routing so it remains compatible with movement and withdrawal. Do not disconnect protection to get through a restriction. If the expected route is blocked or the casualty is beyond the evaluated configuration, report and reassess rather than improvise an untrained passage. The outside team tracks locations and can act on lost communication.

At contact, assess responsiveness and breathing within the responder's medical competence while addressing immediate environmental threats. Tell a responsive casualty what is happening and provide simple directions that do not encourage unsafe self-movement. Coordinate urgent removal with medical priorities. Do not enter a hazard to deliver treatment that cannot be provided safely, and do not spend prolonged time on nonessential packaging in a rapidly deteriorating environment. Use appropriate respiratory support for the casualty only with equipment and training intended for that purpose; a rescuer's spare mask is not automatically a safe patient air system.

Control major bleeding and protect the airway as feasible under the plan and current first-aid/medical guidance. Suspected spinal injury influences movement but does not override immediate lifesaving needs. Chemical contamination affects both patient contact and the receiving team. Communicate condition, access restrictions and needed equipment before moving. No medical diagnosis or invasive procedure is conferred by this rescue credential.

Worked scenario: the casualty is conscious but panicked, and their clothing catches on a projection. The rescuer communicates, stabilizes the situation within the plan and informs the haul team to stop. They do not command an uncontrolled pull. Practice masked communication and casualty assessment on a dummy, with an instructor speaking the casualty responses. First-aid competence is a prerequisite, not simulated by a correct multiple-choice answer.

lessons.title: R09 — Package for the actual exit path
lessons.body:
## R09 — Package for the actual exit path

Choose a harness, rescue strop or stretcher intended for the casualty condition, orientation and route. A device suitable for a horizontal drag may not be approved for vertical lifting. Check the current model instructions, lifting points, straps and required accessories. The packaging must restrain the casualty without restricting breathing and must remain secure during the actual tilt or transition. Do not attach lifting lines to convenient handles unless those handles are approved load attachments.

Prepare the device outside when practical, inspect it and arrange straps to avoid confusion in the restricted space. Position the dummy or casualty using the trained technique, support vulnerable areas and apply the prescribed restraints in sequence. Check fit, closure, circulation/comfort where appropriate, airway access and loose limbs or equipment. A second rescuer verifies correct attachment and orientation before load is applied. Recheck after movement, since straps can shift and a package can deform through an opening.

Measure the route against the packaged profile, not just the unencumbered person's shoulders. Account for bends, ladders, baffles and the space needed for a rescuer to guide. Use the planned tag/guide arrangement only if it does not entangle or expose another person. At an edge, secure receiving support and coordinate movement before changing orientation. Never remove essential restraints to squeeze a casualty through an unassessed opening.

Worked drill: a package fits a circular hatch horizontally on the floor but cannot make the turn through the vessel neck. The plan must be revised and demonstrated on a representative safe mock-up before reliance. The learner compares a vertical-lift and horizontal-movement device specification, selects the appropriate one, packages a dummy and demonstrates the full route. Passing requires secure movement through the representative geometry, not a neatly strapped stationary mannequin.

lessons.title: R10 — Respond to failure without losing the backup team
lessons.body:
## R10 — Respond to failure without losing the backup team

Preplan loss of communications, deteriorating atmosphere, ventilation failure, respiratory malfunction, snagged line, disabled lifting device, rescuer injury and additional casualties. Define immediate actions, command words, backup personnel and limits. A plan that says “call for help” but identifies no capable available help is incomplete. Outside IDLH personnel must be trained and equipped for effective emergency rescue, maintain communication and follow the notification/assistance provisions before entering to rescue.

On a lost signal, use the agreed backup and withdrawal/emergency response promptly. Do not repeatedly try a dead radio while consuming the entrant's remaining air. On a device fault, secure the load through the trained system and reassess; do not disconnect it in hope another device will catch it. If an entry rescuer becomes impaired, the backup response protects the remaining team and preserves accountability. Rescue commands must clearly identify whether the original casualty, rescuer or both are being moved.

Additional hazards may require stopping the attempted method. Continuing because the team has already committed can convert a manageable problem into multiple casualties. Notify command of the changed facts, preserve safe protection and request appropriate capability. Staffing must remain sufficient for the revised operation; an exhausted team is not a ready backup simply because it is outside.

Worked case: while the first team packages a casualty, the outside monitor detects loss of a required control and the second rescuer reports abnormal air consumption. The correct decision follows the preplanned abort/rescuer-assistance response, not a vote to finish the package. A safe drill uses simulated faults and an instructor-controlled pause; no alarm is disabled and no learner is actually deprived of air.

lessons.title: R11 — Transfer care, decontaminate and restore readiness
lessons.body:
## R11 — Transfer care, decontaminate and restore readiness

At removal, transfer to the designated medical team with the casualty's observed condition, exposure information, duration if known, treatment and changes. Provide relevant safety-data information. Do not delay urgent care for paperwork, but communicate contamination risks before exposing ambulance personnel or the clean treatment area. Establish decontamination appropriate to the substance with qualified guidance; do not improvise chemical neutralization or apply a single wash method to every hazard.

Account for all entrants and rescuers before declaring the operation closed. Keep the space secured and preserve the failed permit/control information for investigation. Quarantine equipment exposed to damaging chemicals, overload, shock or uncertainty. Follow manufacturer cleaning, inspection, retirement and service procedures. Replacing a used cylinder is not the entire readiness check: inspect facepieces, alarms, ropes/cables, packaging, communication and consumables too.

Provide responder medical/exposure follow-up and support after stressful incidents. Record actual actions and times, with unknowns marked honestly. Separate factual observations from interpretations. A review should identify control and system changes with responsible owners, not merely blame an individual or record that the team needs to be more careful. Verify restoration before the team is again relied upon for another entry.

Worked exercise: a successful extraction leaves the only retrieval line contaminated and the backup cylinders partly used. The team is not automatically ready for the next shift. Record the unavailable capability, communicate it to entry operations and restore verified readiness. No rescue service may be represented as available when its critical equipment or personnel are not ready.

lessons.title: R12 — Demonstrate and maintain a real team qualification
lessons.body:
## R12 — Demonstrate and maintain a real team qualification

Assess the team in representative spaces matching opening size, configuration and accessibility, while keeping the exercise environment safe. Measure notification, readiness, access, patient contact, packaging and removal stages, and compare performance with the hazards the team is expected to address. A stopwatch total alone does not show safe technique. Record missed communications, equipment faults, protective violations and patient-control problems even if the dummy exits quickly.

Each member demonstrates assigned tasks independently as well as in the team. Rotate roles only where qualification is sought and preserve restrictions for unassessed duties. Written knowledge, respiratory prerequisites, first-aid competence and physical rescue performance are separate evidence. A course cannot issue unlimited rescue authority for all industries, configurations, loads and equipment. An employer evaluates whether the demonstrated capability meets its actual spaces and expected emergencies.

General-industry employee rescue teams practice at least every twelve months using actual or representative spaces. Construction requires practice before actual rescue and at least annually, with the stated exception for a properly performed recent rescue in the same or a similar space. Do not casually transplant that construction exception into every other program. Relevant changes or observed deficits require further training; a calendar-valid certificate does not excuse a skill gap.

Worked debrief: the extraction time met the target, but the backup operator could not demonstrate a malfunction response and an entrant's pressure report was missed. Record the failed criteria, remediate and conduct a new scenario. The qualification remains pending for those duties until demonstrated. Materials completion supplies instruction and assessment tools; it is not a claim that a team has actually passed them.


---

content.title: VUC018 | Rescue formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: Rescue formative checks
lessons.body:
# Rescue formative checks

Attempt first, then study the reason and correct the error. Explain a changed example before progressing. Safe equipment practice is separate.

lessons.title: R01-L1
lessons.body:
## R01-L1

A service promises a twelve-minute drive. What else must the preplan evaluate?

**Answer:** Notification, mobilization, setup, access, hazard time scale, staffing and equipment capability for this space.

**Reason/remediation:** Arrival is not casualty access. Rework the plan with every stage and compare it with the expected harm.

lessons.title: R01-L2
lessons.body:
## R01-L2

A retrieval line runs around a fixed baffle and will not move a dummy. Is a line alone adequate?

**Answer:** No. Demonstrate an effective safe method and suitable entry-rescue fallback when required.

**Reason/remediation:** A nominal system does not prove a viable path. Trace the whole extraction route.

lessons.title: R02-L1
lessons.body:
## R02-L1

The attendant volunteers to enter because the victim is a friend. What must happen?

**Answer:** Prevent spontaneous entry, retain attendant coverage and activate the designated equipped rescue response.

**Reason/remediation:** Urgency does not create competence or replace accountability. Reassign only with qualified relief and a valid plan.

lessons.title: R02-L2
lessons.body:
## R02-L2

Two people call opposite movement directions. What is the correct command response?

**Answer:** Stop, secure the load and resolve direction through the named movement leader/operator before resuming.

**Reason/remediation:** Ambiguous commands can injure patient and rescuers. Practice acknowledgment before movement.

lessons.title: R03-L1
lessons.body:
## R03-L1

The original permit omitted a purge line. Can rescue use its original isolation approval?

**Answer:** No. Trace and verify the newly identified source and reassess rescue authorization and conditions.

**Reason/remediation:** A signature is not proof that changed conditions are safe. Repeat the source-path review.

lessons.title: R03-L2
lessons.body:
## R03-L2

A four-gas detector has no sensor for the suspected solvent. What does a normal display establish?

**Answer:** Only results within the actual sensors and limitations; it does not establish absence of the solvent.

**Reason/remediation:** Select suitable evaluation and protection. Review detector coverage and unknown-atmosphere decisions.

lessons.title: R04-L1
lessons.body:
## R04-L1

Why is a cartridge respirator unsuitable for oxygen deficiency?

**Answer:** It does not supply oxygen. Use the appropriate atmosphere-supplying system under the respiratory program.

**Reason/remediation:** Filtration cannot restore missing oxygen. Explain the difference between APR and atmosphere-supplying equipment.

lessons.title: R04-L2
lessons.body:
## R04-L2

Does a successful seal check replace the required fit test?

**Answer:** No. Medical evaluation, fit testing, training and each-use seal checking are separate requirements.

**Reason/remediation:** A quick donning check cannot establish fit-test compliance. Identify each prerequisite and its record.

lessons.title: R05-L1
lessons.body:
## R05-L1

Calculate available planning time for 4500 psi start, 1500 psi exit reserve and 300 psi/min consumption.

**Answer:** Ten minutes to that reserve; with four minutes in and four out, only two remain before added contingency.

**Reason/remediation:** Subtract the reserve before dividing. The synthetic result is not permission to use all ten minutes.

lessons.title: R05-L2
lessons.body:
## R05-L2

One rescuer consumes air faster than the other. Whose remaining air governs the team plan?

**Answer:** The limiting member, together with other safety and exit constraints.

**Reason/remediation:** A team average conceals a person at risk. Recalculate withdrawal and contingency needs.

lessons.title: R06-L1
lessons.body:
## R06-L1

A 95 kg casualty, 12 kg package and 8 kg equipment are proposed on a 100 kg rated component. Decide.

**Answer:** Reject: the load is already 115 kg before further system-force considerations.

**Reason/remediation:** Include the whole supported load, not just body weight; verify every component and configuration.

lessons.title: R06-L2
lessons.body:
## R06-L2

Can an unidentified carabiner be used because it looks undamaged?

**Answer:** No. Establish its suitability, rating, history and compatibility or remove it from service.

**Reason/remediation:** Appearance alone does not prove intended use. Trace the entire verified load path.

lessons.title: R07-L1
lessons.body:
## R07-L1

What must happen before the original support is disconnected during a transfer?

**Answer:** The receiving support is established, checked and demonstrably carrying the load under the designed procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** A connection alone is not verified support. Practice the controlled transfer with a dummy.

lessons.title: R07-L2
lessons.body:
## R07-L2

An ideal 4:1 system raises a load one metre. How much haul rope travels, ignoring real losses?

**Answer:** Four metres. Actual friction and system forces require separate evaluation.

**Reason/remediation:** Mechanical advantage changes force and travel; it does not establish component adequacy.

lessons.title: R08-L1
lessons.body:
## R08-L1

The casualty cannot hear through your facepiece. What is the safe response?

**Answer:** Keep protection in place and use trained communication methods or relay while following the plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Removing protection can create another casualty. Practice speech/hand/radio methods while equipped.

lessons.title: R08-L2
lessons.body:
## R08-L2

The route is blocked by equipment not on the drawing. What should the rescuer do?

**Answer:** Stop the unplanned advance, communicate and reassess an authorized safe route and rescue method.

**Reason/remediation:** An improvised squeeze may compromise PPE or trap the rescuer. Review route and withdrawal limits.

lessons.title: R09-L1
lessons.body:
## R09-L1

The packaged dummy fits the hatch but not the internal turn. Did packaging pass?

**Answer:** No. The entire path must work while preserving essential protection and restraints.

**Reason/remediation:** A single aperture test misses the limiting geometry. Demonstrate the full route.

lessons.title: R09-L2
lessons.body:
## R09-L2

Are carrying handles automatically acceptable vertical lifting points?

**Answer:** No. Use the device-specific prescribed attachments and orientation.

**Reason/remediation:** Convenience is not approval for lifting. Locate the actual model instructions and intended points.

lessons.title: R10-L1
lessons.body:
## R10-L1

Radio contact fails during access. Is repeated calling the only action?

**Answer:** No. Implement the planned alternate communication and withdrawal/emergency response promptly.

**Reason/remediation:** Air and hazard exposure continue while waiting. Practice the defined lost-signal response.

lessons.title: R10-L2
lessons.body:
## R10-L2

A lifting device faults with the dummy supported. What is the first principle?

**Answer:** Preserve support through the trained system, stop movement and reassess before any transfer or release.

**Reason/remediation:** Disconnecting an uncertain load can cause a fall. Rehearse the approved secured response.

lessons.title: R11-L1
lessons.body:
## R11-L1

A casualty may carry a chemical contaminant. What must the receiving medical team know?

**Answer:** The suspected substance, exposure information, condition, care and contamination risk, with relevant safety-data information.

**Reason/remediation:** A clean-area transfer can spread harm. Give prioritized factual information and identify unknowns.

lessons.title: R11-L2
lessons.body:
## R11-L2

After a successful rescue, all cylinders are depleted and the only line is contaminated. Is the service ready?

**Answer:** No. Declare the capability unavailable, quarantine/restore equipment and verify readiness before further reliance.

**Reason/remediation:** Success on one event does not replenish capacity. Complete the restoration form.

lessons.title: R12-L1
lessons.body:
## R12-L1

The team is quick, but one member failed a backup task. Can the team score erase that failure?

**Answer:** No. Record and remediate the individual deficit, then independently reassess it and affected team performance.

**Reason/remediation:** A strong partner can conceal a critical skill gap. Qualification is role-specific.

lessons.title: R12-L2
lessons.body:
## R12-L2

Does a course certificate authorize every confined-space rescue configuration?

**Answer:** No. It records demonstrated roles/equipment/configurations; the employer must evaluate actual suitability and designate personnel.

**Reason/remediation:** A paper credential is not universal rescue authority. State exclusions explicitly.


---

content.title: VUC018 | VUC018 sources and objective coverage
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VUC018 sources and objective coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC018 sources and objective coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-17. Scope is an original VNDRLY industrial/construction permit-space rescue program. No IADC, NFPA, OSHA or other organization's certification is claimed. State-plan, sector and employer obligations must be determined for the delivery site. Maritime, diving, collapse and other specialist rescue regimes are not silently included.

Primary references:

1. [29 CFR 1910.146](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.146), particularly (d)–(k): general-industry entry controls, roles, training and rescue capability/equipment/practice. Section(k) is the controlling regulatory text for its scope.
2. [29 CFR 1926.1211](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1211): construction rescue service evaluation, availability, proficiency, practice and retrieval. Read its express recent-rescue exception and pre-actual-rescue practice requirement; do not conflate those with a generic course-expiry rule.
3. [1910.146 Appendix F](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.146AppF): **nonmandatory evaluation guidance**, including initial and performance evaluation and representative configuration. The guidance's discussion of practice does not replace controlling regulation. Response evaluation considers more than travel and configuration evaluation includes the actual limiting route.
4. [29 CFR 1910.134](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134): respiratory selection for unknown/IDLH atmospheres, medical evaluation, fit, use, inspection, air and outside rescue provisions. Its structural-fire two-in/two-out provision is not presented here as a universal confined-space staffing formula. The rescue plan still requires sufficient competent people for all simultaneous essential duties.
5. [1910.146 Appendix B](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.146AppB) and [1926.1204](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1204): atmospheric evaluation/verification, controls and construction monitoring. The embedded entry-team coursebook teaches the paired industry requirements rather than treating one as interchangeable with the other.
6. [Skedco official instruction index](https://skedco.com/skedco-instruction-manuals/) and [Sked-Evac tripod instructions](https://skedco.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/Tripod-Instruction-Updated.pdf), public three-page document linked by the manufacturer at review: supports the limited named-tripod example in station F. Do not use another product's rating or generalize the setup to all high points. No numeric working-load claim is imported from an unseen label.

The actual detector, respiratory apparatus, retrieval/lowering device and stretcher manuals are mandatory equipment-specific teaching aids at delivery. Model/revision, compatible components and the actual observed sequence are recorded. This is normal equipment qualification, not a claim this document can authorize any device. A manufacturer link alone does not demonstrate a learner's operation. No paid textbook, proprietary question bank or unseen current technical standard is represented as reviewed. No generic knot/rope recipe is offered as authorization for arbitrary high-angle rigging.

|Required objective|Original instruction/worked application|Formative / protected final|Physical assessment|Source basis|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|R01 capability and representative preplan|R01, delayed-service/baffle decisions|R01-L1–2 / E1–3|A,L|1,2,3|
|R02 command/accountability/communication|R02, conflicting commands|R02-L1–2 / E1–3|B,L|1,2,4 plus original operational teaching|
|R03 energy/material/atmosphere controls|R03, missing purge and detector coverage|R03-L1–2 / E1–3|C,L|1,2,4,5|
|R04 respiratory equipment/prerequisites|R04, inspection/donning/malfunction|R04-L1–2 / E1–3|D,J,L|4 and actual model instructions|
|R05 air/endurance decisions|R05, synthetic reserve calculation|R05-L1–2 / E1–3|E,J,L|4, original planning exercises, actual equipment plan|
|R06 compatible rigging/load path|R06, total load and unknown equipment|R06-L1–2 / E1–3|F,L|1,2,6 and actual equipment instructions|
|R07 controlled movements/transfers|R07, mechanical advantage and snag|R07-L1–2 / E1–3|G,J,L|1,2; original control principles and actual system instructions|
|R08 access/initial casualty care|R08, blocked path and communication|R08-L1–2 / E1–3|H,L|1,2,4; prerequisite first-aid competence|
|R09 packaging and entire exit path|R09, restriction/turn exercise|R09-L1–2 / E1–3|I,L|1,2,3 and actual stretcher instructions|
|R10 failure/backup response|R10, combined control and air fault|R10-L1–2 / E1–3|J,L|1,2,4|
|R11 handover/decontamination/readiness|R11, depleted/contaminated equipment|R11-L1–2 / E1–3|K,L|1,2,4; applicable substance/manufacturer instructions|
|R12 individual/team qualification|R12, fast drill with unsafe task|R12-L1–2 / E1–3|All, especially L|1,2,3|

Entry foundation is embedded from the reviewed VNDRLY VUC017 coursebook: sixteen C-chapters covering classification, roles, isolation, monitoring, limits, ventilation, access, permits, industry differences, coordination and retrieval. Learners must already have demonstrated entrant proficiency; embedded instruction supports review without substituting a link for content. The new final independently assesses rescue decisions; prior entrant evidence is verified rather than falsely reissued from attendance.

Course hours, class ratio, constructed-response scoring, station thresholds and reassessment limits are VNDRLY delivery policies. They are not alleged statutory values. Synthetic air/load arithmetic is instructional; it is not a manufacturer rating, an engineered system design or an employer-approved rescue plan. Credentials remain explicitly bounded to independently demonstrated duties. Materials authorship does not assert actual attendance, a learner pass, rescue availability or employer designation.

lessons.title: VUC019 — Energy Control: Authorized Employee
lessons.body: # VUC019 — Energy Control: Authorized Employee

lessons.title: Definition, prerequisites and delivery
lessons.body:
## Definition, prerequisites and delivery

Audience: employees designated to isolate machinery for servicing, with affected-worker responsibilities included for coordination. Purpose: independently execute and maintain the employer's equipment-specific energy-control process within the employee's authorized scope. Prerequisites: understand the assigned equipment/task, communicate stop conditions, and receive employer instruction in its actual procedures and devices. This course confers no qualified-electrical-worker status, well-control authority, hot-tapping qualification or permission to improvise isolation hardware.

Objectives E01–E12: distinguish scope/roles; inventory all sources; prepare/notify/shut down; apply suitable devices; control stored/reaccumulating energy; verify the protected state; preserve it during work; coordinate groups/contractors; transfer shifts; conduct testing transitions; restore/handle exceptional removal; recognize narrow exceptions and maintain program proficiency. Each objective has written instruction, worked application, two formative and three final questions. Practical stations below test actual behaviors on a safe trainer and, for employer authorization, the actual equipment-specific procedure in a controlled evaluation.

Eight planned instructional hours excluding breaks: scope/inventory 60 minutes; shutdown/devices 60; stored energy/verification 60; group/contractor/transfer 60; testing/restoration/exceptions 60; supervised practice 90; independent written assessment 45; independent practical assessment/debrief 45. Extend practical time or rotate additional instructors to observe every learner; never award an unobserved skill to meet the clock. Hours are VNDRLY policy, not a statutory course-length requirement.

Instructor: employer-designated authorized employee proficient in the specific machinery, procedures and energy-control devices, with ability to teach and assess. Electrical demonstrations involving exposure require appropriately qualified personnel; ordinary learners use inert replicas. Maximum four learners per directly observed trainer station; assess each learner individually. Demonstrate each sequence, provide coached practice, then remove coaching for assessment. Use only zero-energy/inert simulators with represented hazards, not live voltage, compressed fluid or an unsupported real load. Never loosen actual fittings, defeat a live guard or remove a real worker's lock for class practice.

lessons.title: Examination and credential policy
lessons.body:
## Examination and credential policy

Final: 36 constructed responses, 72 points, pass 58/72 overall and 4/6 each E-domain. Each response:2 correct decision and essential reason;1 safe incomplete;0 wrong/absent/unsafe. Critical unsafe endorsements—working before verified isolation, bypassing another person's protection, unsupported stored-energy exposure or unqualified electrical testing—fail regardless of aggregate score. Forty-five minutes is planned, with reasonable language/access/time accommodation that preserves the safety objective. No keys or coaching during the controlled final.

Eight physical/tabletop stations have five scored criteria each:0 absent/unsafe,1 safe with prompting/incomplete,2 independently correct. Require8/10 at every station and every starred critical criterion at 2. Tabletop exceptions do not qualify actual exceptional-removal authority. A safety intervention ends that attempt. Retain the failed result, teach/practice the deficiency, then reassess a changed example with the same objective. Use protected alternate cards for failed written domains plus E12. Maximum two reassessments before a new targeted training plan and later assessment.

A VNDRLY materials package is not a learner credential. Issue the authorized-employee training/skills credential only after all required written and practical results and equipment-specific competence are recorded. Name the demonstrated equipment/procedures and exclusions; a simulator-only learner receives a conditional training record pending employer equipment demonstration. The employer designates authorization. Review annually alongside procedure inspection as VNDRLY policy, and retrain immediately for relevant changes or deficits. Do not describe annual inspection as a universal annual refresher mandate or renew on attendance alone.

lessons.title: Safe trainer specification and worked procedure
lessons.body:
## Safe trainer specification and worked procedure

Use a tabletop, nonenergized model labelled PRESS-P1. Physical props: manual disconnect D1; closable valve V1; dummy accumulator A1; a supported ram representation; an inert blocking device B1; labelled return-line valve V2 representing an alternate feed; a nonfunctional Start/Stop panel; pressure display cards; dedicated training locks/tags/hasps; lockbox and three distinct personal locks. There is no stored or connected hazardous energy. Instructor announces that any real-machine use requires its own approved procedure; these symbols are not instructions to operate a real press.

Training task: change a part inside the represented ram zone. Energy inventory identifies D1 electrical drive,V1 pneumatic feed,A1 stored hydraulic energy,gravity at the ram and V2 alternate pressure pathway. Device IDs and safe positions are on the trainer-specific drawing. Simulated stored-energy relief is represented by a control card, never a real valve discharge. A card shows whether the specified block is correctly engaged. A qualified-person verification card represents electrical absence-of-voltage testing; the learner must request it and must not pretend a start attempt performs that test.

Worked sequence: identify P1 and the task; compare drawing/props; notify operator and neighboring crew; follow trainer Stop sequence; isolate D1, V1, V2; attach personal devices to hold safe positions; represent approved pressure dissipation and B1 support; verify each source with the named method and appropriate qualified-person input; attempt Start with everyone clear, then restore the control to Stop; record results and reaccumulation monitoring; only then place the work token in the danger zone. If the instructor changes pressure from0 to20 on a card, stop the work token, preserve controls and investigate the pathway before resuming. The numbers are scenario signals, not safe pressure limits.

Restoration: remove work token/tools, verify represented guards/components and all people clear, reconcile group devices, have each owner remove their device through the procedure, notify affected people and perform controlled restart. This complete example is taught before the assessment variations below.

lessons.title: A — Scope and energy walkdown
lessons.body:
## A — Scope and energy walkdown

Props: P1 drawing and trainer, job cards for shop servicing and oilfield well servicing. Learner classifies role/task, identifies the applicable-rule boundary and walks every source. Fault:V2 exists on the trainer but not the first drawing. Correct response stops the planned exposure and resolves the discrepancy rather than relying on the printed procedure.

Criteria: accurately identifies scope/role; lists energy type/magnitude or needed information; *finds every represented source including V2; distinguishes isolation from controls; *does not proceed on an incomplete procedure. Reassessment moves the alternate feed and changes the task boundary.

lessons.title: B — Notification, shutdown and device application
lessons.body:
## B — Notification, shutdown and device application

Props: control-room role card, P1, suitable and deliberately unsuitable training attachments. Learner notifies affected people, carries out orderly shutdown, physically identifies devices and applies assigned locks/tags. Fault: one valve attachment can slip off and allow movement. Correct response rejects it and obtains a suitable device; a tag is not a casual substitute.

Criteria: correct communication; correct shutdown order; *correctly identifies and isolates each required device; *uses suitable secured identifiable personal hardware; verifies attachment prevents intended operation. Assessor observes hands-on attachment rather than accepting a verbal description.

lessons.title: C — Stored energy and verification
lessons.body:
## C — Stored energy and verification

Props: accumulator/ram cards, blocking prop, pressure trend, qualified-electrical-test record card. Learner controls stored energy and identifies verification for each source. Instructor first withholds the qualified electrical result, then presents a valid result after the learner requests qualified help. Later inject pressure reaccumulation.

Criteria: *establishes specified support before exposure; controls all represented stored energy; *requests appropriate verification rather than treating Start as voltage proof; returns controls to safe state; *stops and resolves reaccumulation. No real load is lifted or electrically tested. Repeat with a gauge-discrepancy card instead of a pressure rise.

lessons.title: D — Group and contractor protection
lessons.body:
## D — Group and contractor protection

Props: three personal locks, controlled isolation keys/box, different contractor procedure cards and roster. Learner coordinates the two employers, establishes the group process, joins personally, adds a fourth worker correctly and removes one finishing worker without compromising the others. Worked resolution: everyone exposed retains equivalent personal protection; the lead lock alone is insufficient.

Criteria: reconciles procedures and boundaries; assigns coordination/exposure responsibility; *establishes individual protection for each exposed worker; *prevents key/restoration access while anyone remains protected; records arrivals/departures and verification status. Assessment is individual even when peers play other roles.

lessons.title: E — Shift transfer
lessons.body:
## E — Shift transfer

Props: active group box, outgoing/incoming personnel cards, delayed-arrival inject. Learner demonstrates the approved continuous-protection transfer and verifies incoming understanding. Fault: supervisor asks outgoing staff to remove all locks before incoming staff arrive. Learner keeps the safe state and invokes the documented continuity arrangement rather than a gap.

Criteria: reviews work/energy status; identifies all exposed people; *preserves continuous physical protection; establishes incoming personal protection/verification under procedure; documents transfer and restrictions. Reassessment introduces a contractor who remains working across the shift boundary.

lessons.title: F — Test, position and re-isolate
lessons.body:
## F — Test, position and re-isolate

Props: P1, tool/person tokens, test request. Learner transitions out of lockout for a represented positioning test, then reestablishes the complete controlled state before work. Instructor leaves a person token inside the zone to test whether clearance is real.

Criteria: *clears personnel/tools before release; correct device-owner/removal coordination; controlled defined test; *re-isolates every source and stored energy after test; *re-verifies before work token returns. Stopping the motor after the test is not enough. Repeat with a new source revealed by the test.

lessons.title: G — Restoration and absent-owner case
lessons.body:
## G — Restoration and absent-owner case

Props: completion checklist, personnel board, lock-owner absence/contact records. First demonstrate ordinary owner removal and safe restart. Then present an absent-owner case with contradictory evidence that the person may still be present. Learner refuses casual removal and identifies required employer-directed safeguards and information before any exception. No real device is cut.

Criteria: inspects machine/tools/components; *verifies people clear; normal owner removal and affected notification; *rejects unresolved absence/exposure or informal permission; specifies contact and before-return notification under documented employer procedure. Tabletop success is not authority to approve actual exceptions.

lessons.title: H — Procedure inspection and final complete sequence
lessons.body:
## H — Procedure inspection and final complete sequence

Props: trainer, revised procedure with omitted accumulator, periodic inspection form, training-change case. Learner conducts an independent full sequence on a changed trainer task while the assessor observes, then reviews the flawed procedure. Identify annual inspection by an authorized person other than the users inspected, proper record fields and immediate correction/retraining needs. Do not merely initial every box.

Criteria: *independently completes the full safe sequence; detects procedure/equipment mismatch; identifies independent periodic inspector and required responsibility review; records specific corrective action and retraining; distinguishes actual equipment authorization from simulator attendance. Any critical failed step requires a changed complete reassessment, not just a corrected spoken answer.

lessons.title: Recording forms
lessons.body:

**Energy inventory/procedure:** EquipmentID____ Task/boundary____ Drawing/procedure revision____ Source/type/magnitude____ Isolation device/location/safe position____ Personal/group hardware____ Stored-energy control____ Verification method/qualified person____ Reaccumulation monitoring/stop trigger____ Affected people notified____ Unresolved discrepancy____ Approved by____

**Individual station:** Learner____ Station____ Trainer/equipment____ Scenario revision____ Criterion1__/2;2__/2;3__/2;4__/2;5__/2. Critical criteria all2?____ Total__/10 Outcome____ Actual observed error____ Safety stop____ Remediation____ Changed reassessment____ New result____ Assessor/date____

courses.title: VUC019 | VNDRLY/U Energy Control — Authorized Employee coursebook

content.title: VUC019 | VNDRLY/U Energy Control — Authorized Employee coursebook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Energy Control — Authorized Employee coursebook
lessons.body: # VNDRLY/U Energy Control — Authorized Employee coursebook

lessons.title: E01 — Decide when energy control applies and who may perform it
lessons.body:
## E01 — Decide when energy control applies and who may perform it

Unexpected energy can move a machine, discharge pressure, drop a load, release material, burn a person or energize exposed conductors. Servicing includes cleaning, unjamming, lubrication, adjustment and setup where a person can be exposed—not only work bearing a maintenance work-order label. Normal operation with effective guarding differs from putting a hand into a danger zone or bypassing a guard. A short task can create the same injury mechanism as a long repair.

An authorized employee applies the employer's energy-control procedure for the covered servicing work. An affected employee operates the equipment or works in the area and must understand the controls and prohibition on restart. Other nearby employees also must not defeat controls. A production operator becomes subject to authorized-worker training when their duties include covered servicing. A course certificate alone does not assign equipment-specific authority.

Determine the governing work scope. Federal OSHA 1910.147 excludes construction, agriculture, specified maritime work, exclusive utility installations, electrical utilization exposure covered by Subpart S, and oil-and-gas well drilling and servicing. This matters in VNDRLY's industry: do not label a well-servicing activity compliant with 1910.147 simply because a lock is used. Identify the applicable sector/electrical rules and employer equipment procedure. The exclusion never means uncontrolled energy is acceptable. This course teaches the general-industry authorized-worker method and its boundaries; separate specialist authorization remains necessary.

Worked case: a shop technician clears a jam behind a conveyor guard while the operator holds Stop. The technician is exposed to unexpected movement and stored material. The task requires the applicable energy-control process; an operator's promise is not isolation. In contrast, a worker observing the intact guarded conveyor from outside remains an affected/other worker and must not interfere with another person's controls. Explain the actual exposure, not just the job title.

lessons.title: E02 — Build an energy inventory before touching the equipment
lessons.body:
## E02 — Build an energy inventory before touching the equipment

Confirm the equipment identity, task boundary and current procedure. Walk the system with the approved drawing and competent personnel. Follow every energy source to its isolating device: normal and alternate electrical supplies, hydraulic and pneumatic feeds, accumulators, gravity, springs, flywheels, thermal energy, chemical reactions and material flow. Include connected machines and upstream/downstream processes that can move or refill the serviced equipment. A nameplate identifies a machine, not all its energy pathways.

For each source record type, magnitude or relevant range, hazard, isolation location, safe device position, stored-energy method, verification method and reaccumulation control. Labels must match physical devices. If a drawing and equipment differ, stop and correct the procedure through the employer's process before exposure. Do not guess which of two identical valves serves the machine.

Distinguish a control command from a physical isolating device. A touchscreen stop, PLC command, selector switch, remote disable or emergency stop can fail, reset or be bypassed and is not the required energy isolation. A suitable manually operated disconnect, valve, block or other physical device can prevent transmission when correctly selected and secured. An isolating valve must also be adequate for the actual hazardous substance and leakage potential; a closed handle alone does not establish safe pressure downstream.

Worked inventory: a synthetic shop press has motor supply D1, air supply V1, an accumulator A1 and an elevated ram. Locking D1 prevents motor power but does not release A1 or support the ram. The complete procedure must identify V1, controlled dissipation and specified rated blocking before a person enters the crush zone. Learners draw the four paths and identify what each control accomplishes and what it cannot accomplish.

lessons.title: E03 — Prepare, notify and shut down in a safe sequence
lessons.body:
## E03 — Prepare, notify and shut down in a safe sequence

Before shutdown, review the specific procedure, hazards, work scope and people involved. Obtain the correct dedicated locks, tags, hasps, valve/disconnect attachments and blocking equipment. Confirm their compatibility and condition; a device that can slip off does not protect the isolation. Plan the shutdown's effects on ventilation, cooling, pressure and neighboring operations. Stopping one system may create a different hazard if supporting systems are not managed in the required order.

Notify affected employees before applying energy control. Explain equipment identity, affected operations, purpose and expected restrictions. Coordinate with the control room and other crews, but do not treat a radio message or electronic work permit as a physical lock. If more than one employer or shift is involved, establish the group/transfer arrangement before anyone starts work.

Use the machine's established normal stopping sequence. Wait for required controlled coast-down or process stabilization while staying outside danger zones. Then physically locate and operate every identified isolating device. Verify the identity at the device, not from a memory of a neighboring machine. Keep yourself outside the exposure while isolating; operating electrical equipment may require separate qualified personnel and protective measures under the electrical program.

Worked case: a mixer needs a controlled stop to prevent a hot material surge. Cutting power immediately may defeat the intended safe shutdown. Follow the approved sequence, then isolate and secure all sources. The presence of an emergency does not authorize an untrained worker to open energized electrical equipment. Stop the work and obtain competent help when the procedure cannot be followed safely.

lessons.title: E04 — Apply locks and understand what tags cannot do
lessons.body:
## E04 — Apply locks and understand what tags cannot do

Apply assigned personal energy-control devices to each required isolating point in the safe position. Confirm the attachment physically prevents operation as intended. Dedicated energy-control locks are identifiable and used for that purpose, not borrowed from a toolbox locker. The device and tag must survive the environment and remain legible. Facility standardization supports recognition; the employee's identity must be clear.

Use lockout when the isolating device is capable of being locked, unless the employer has established the applicable full-protection tagout alternative. Tagout is not a worker's shortcut because a lock is missing. A tag warns; it does not physically restrain the device. Where permitted tagout is used, the employer must establish equivalent protection and the required additional measures, training and inspections. Examples such as removing an isolating circuit element or blocking a switch must be appropriate to the system and performed by authorized/qualified personnel—not invented at the job.

Never bypass, ignore or casually remove a tag. A tag that cannot attach directly must be placed as close as safely possible so the prohibition is immediately apparent to someone attempting operation, under the applicable procedure. Secure it with the required durable attachment. A loose string or unreadable paper tag cannot be treated as equivalent to compliant hardware. In 1910.147, attachment requirements include nonreusable, self-locking, hand-attachable/nonreleasable means with at least 50-pound unlocking strength; the employer supplies suitable devices.

For covered equipment installed after January 2, 1990, or undergoing the specified replacement, major repair, renovation or modification, the standard requires energy-isolating devices designed to accept lockout. Report a design deficiency through the employer's program; do not use recurring tagout as an excuse to ignore that requirement.

Worked case: a valve attachment rotates freely and permits the handle to move. A padlock through that attachment does not establish isolation. Stop, obtain the correct approved device and verify its function. If a worker proposes a tag instead to save time, reject the substitution unless the employer's compliant tagout procedure genuinely applies. The assessment uses an inert trainer, never an improvised live-system lockout.

lessons.title: E05 — Control stored energy and prevent its return
lessons.body:
## E05 — Control stored energy and prevent its return

After isolation and device application, make stored or residual energy safe through the specified relief, disconnection, restraint or other control. Sources remain after a motor stops: a rotating flywheel, compressed fluid, elevated carriage, spring, capacitor, hot surface or reactive contents. Control the actual hazardous mechanism rather than looking only for a zero gauge or dark screen.

Use designed bleed/drain/discharge methods with safe routing and appropriate protection. Never loosen a fitting or cut a hose as a pressure test. Support elevated components with the specified rated means before exposing any body part beneath them; a hydraulic valve or jack alone may not be the required restraint. Do not release a spring or remove a support unless its force and movement are controlled by the approved procedure. Electrical discharge and testing require the appropriately qualified person.

Energy can reaccumulate through leaking valves, thermal expansion, connected feeds, gravity, recharge circuits or ongoing process conditions. Where hazardous reaccumulation is possible, verify continued control until servicing is complete or the possibility no longer exists. A single initial zero is not enough. Specify how the condition is monitored, what trigger stops work and who responds. If control is uncertain, withdraw from exposure and resolve it rather than accepting a guessed safe interval.

Worked example: a trapped hydraulic pocket reads zero after an approved bleed but rises again. Possible causes include a second supply or leakage. Stop exposure, communicate the change and correct the isolation/control plan. Repeatedly bleeding while hands remain in the crush zone is not proof of a safe system. A paper pressure trend during training lets learners identify the first unsafe change without releasing real pressure.

lessons.title: E06 — Verify the protected state before work
lessons.body:
## E06 — Verify the protected state before work

Before servicing, the authorized employee verifies that isolation and deenergization are effective. Verification must cover every relevant source and the actual work boundary. Follow the equipment procedure: suitable tests, inspections and a controlled attempt to operate where appropriate, with everyone safely clear. Return controls to the safe position after the attempt so later restoration cannot cause an unexpected start.

A failed start is useful but not universal proof. A motor may not start because its control circuit is disabled while hazardous voltage remains. A pressure gauge may be blocked, failed or connected to the wrong pocket. A blocked ram may still conceal spring force. Match the verification method to the energy. Record actual readings and observations; do not copy a previous shift's result.

Electrical work on exposed deenergized parts has separate qualified-person testing requirements under 1910.333. The qualified person verifies the relevant parts and circuits are deenergized, including induced voltage and unrelated backfeed. The standard expressly requires tester-operation checking immediately before and after testing circuits over 600 volts nominal; employer/manufacturer procedures may require proving the tester at other voltages too. This course does not train an otherwise unqualified person to perform electrical testing or enter an electrical exposure boundary.

Worked case: the start button produces no movement, but a separate heater supply was omitted. The machine is not verified safe for the work. Stop, update isolation and conduct appropriate verification for that supply. The correct answer is not “try Start twice.” A knowledge check asks which hazard each verification addresses and what remains untested.

lessons.title: E07 — Perform work without breaking the protected boundary
lessons.body:
## E07 — Perform work without breaking the protected boundary

Begin servicing only after the planned energy controls and verification are complete and personal protection is established. Keep the work within the authorized scope. If a new task exposes another component, opens a line or requires removing a block, revisit the energy analysis first. A lock does not protect every activity on a connected installation.

Do not lend keys, let another person work under your personal protection without the approved group arrangement, remove your device while still exposed, or operate controlled equipment. Keep guards, components and tools managed so they do not create secondary hazards. An affected employee who needs equipment must contact the responsible authorized person, not attempt to restart it. Access control and communication support the physical isolation but do not replace it.

If a control is disturbed, a lock or tag is missing, an unexpected movement occurs or conditions change, stop and move to a safe position. Notify responsible personnel, preserve evidence and reestablish the approved safe state before resuming. Do not conceal the event by replacing a tag and continuing. When hazardous energy is involved, uncertainty is a reason to resolve the condition before exposure.

Worked case: a technician completes the planned belt change and decides to also free a downstream roller. The downstream equipment has a separate drive and gravity-fed material. The first procedure may not cover it. Expand the approved isolation boundary and verify the additional sources before the extra work; the small size of the added task does not remove the risk.

lessons.title: E08 — Coordinate group work and contractors
lessons.body:
## E08 — Coordinate group work and contractors

Group energy control must give each exposed authorized worker protection equivalent to personal lockout/tagout. The employer assigns an authorized person primary responsibility for a defined group and provides a way to know each member's exposure. When several crews or crafts are involved, overall coordination is assigned so the protective arrangement stays coherent. A supervisor's single lock is not automatically everyone's personal protection.

Under a suitable lockbox method, the designated personnel identify, isolate, secure and verify the equipment; controlled keys are placed in the group box; each exposed worker applies and later removes their personal device under the procedure. Each worker understands the protected boundary and verification arrangements before work. Removal by one person must not allow restoration while another remains exposed. Equivalent protection must persist across additions, departures and changes in scope.

The on-site and outside employers exchange their energy-control procedures before covered contractor servicing. The on-site employer ensures its employees understand and obey the outside program's restrictions. Resolve conflicting colors, key arrangements, device ownership, verification and restoration responsibilities before work. A contractor's signature on a visitor sheet is not procedure coordination.

Worked drill: three workers attach personal locks to a correctly established training lockbox; one finishes and removes their lock. The box remains secured by the other two. Restoration cannot occur until everyone is safely clear and the entire approved release sequence is satisfied. A fourth worker arriving mid-job must join through the procedure, not assume the first three have protected them.

lessons.title: E09 — Transfer protection across shifts and personnel changes
lessons.body:
## E09 — Transfer protection across shifts and personnel changes

Shift changes require an orderly transfer that prevents any unprotected interval. Plan the overlap or other employer-approved continuity method. Incoming personnel review equipment identity, work status, controls, verification and changed conditions, then establish their required personal protection before outgoing protection is removed as the procedure requires. A verbal “you're covered” is not physical continuity.

Document the transfer and reconcile every person's exposure. Account for contractors, temporary workers and personnel who leave unexpectedly. If the incoming shift is delayed, maintain the safe controlled state and use the established procedure; do not remove all devices merely because the shift has ended. Equipment should remain unavailable rather than create an unprotected gap.

An outgoing employee's device is not a convenient permanent substitute for incoming personal protection. The incoming worker must understand the actual boundary and verify protection under the procedure. A work-order status, group board or key count can support the transfer but cannot replace the required protective arrangement.

Worked case: the day crew leaves at 18:00 and the night crew arrives18:15. A plan saying “remove day locks at 18:00; add night locks at 18:15” has a gap. Use an approved continuity arrangement and do not expose anyone until their protection is established. Learners demonstrate the transfer on a trainer and show precisely why no key or restoration path becomes available while a worker is exposed.

lessons.title: E10 — Temporarily energize only through the testing sequence
lessons.body:
## E10 — Temporarily energize only through the testing sequence

Some servicing requires testing or positioning before work can continue. This is a planned transition out of, then back into, the controlled state—not permission to bypass a lock while a person remains in a danger zone. Determine the test boundary, personnel roles, guarding/protection and communication in advance. Energized electrical diagnostics require their own qualified-person work practices; general lockout training does not authorize them.

Under 1910.147's sequence, clear tools and materials, remove employees from the machine/equipment area, remove controls using the authorized removal procedure, energize for the test or positioning, then deenergize and reapply the complete energy-control process before further servicing. Include stored energy and verification again. The fact that the first isolation was correct does not establish the second one after energy has been reintroduced.

Keep the test to its authorized purpose. Communicate clearly that the equipment state is changing, and control access so someone does not assume maintenance protection still exists. If the test reveals a new fault or source, revise the plan before resuming work. Do not leave a temporary jumper or bypass that defeats the restored safety arrangement.

Worked case: a conveyor is positioned for belt alignment, then a worker wants to immediately reach in because the motor has stopped. The system has been energized and must be isolated, secured, stored-energy controlled and verified again. The assessment rejects a partial “stop and reach” sequence even if the learner completed the first lockout perfectly.

lessons.title: E11 — Restore safely and handle absent-owner removal correctly
lessons.body:
## E11 — Restore safely and handle absent-owner removal correctly

Before release, inspect the area and equipment: remove nonessential items, verify required components are intact and ensure employees are safely positioned or removed. Reconcile the work scope and everyone involved. Each energy-control device is normally removed by the employee who applied it. Notify affected employees after removal and before startup as required by the release procedure. Restore using the controlled equipment sequence, watching for abnormal conditions from a safe position.

When the applying employee is unavailable, removal is an employer-directed exception under specific documented procedures and training that provide equivalent safety—not a supervisor's casual permission. Under 1910.147, the minimum safeguards include verifying the employee is not at the facility, making all reasonable efforts to contact them to inform them of removal, and ensuring they know before resuming work at that facility. Those safeguards do not replace the rest of the safe restoration procedure. Do not cut a lock simply because a phone call is unanswered.

Record the authorizing person, basis, absence check, contact efforts, equipment/personnel checks, removal and return-to-work notification. If the person is still in the facility or their exposure cannot be resolved, the required exception conditions are not established. Maintain control and escalate through the employer's process.

Worked case: a worker went home sick and their lock remains. The production deadline is not the exception. Follow the documented process, verify all conditions and record how the returning worker will learn of removal before work resumes. A practical tabletop assessment includes an initially incorrect claim that the person left; learners must resolve the contrary sign-in evidence rather than accept an assumption.

lessons.title: E12 — Recognize narrow exceptions and keep the program effective
lessons.body:
## E12 — Recognize narrow exceptions and keep the program effective

Exceptions have conditions, not convenient labels. Cord-and-plug work requires unplugging to control the relevant unexpected-start hazards and exclusive control of the plug by the servicing employee. If another person can reconnect it or other energy remains, that reasoning is insufficient. Minor servicing during production must be routine, repetitive and integral and use alternative measures providing effective protection; simply being quick is not enough. The hot-tap exception has its own essential-continuity, impractical-shutdown, documented-procedure and proven-protection conditions and does not qualify this learner to perform hot tapping.

The narrow exception from documenting a particular energy-control procedure requires all stated 1910.147 conditions: no dangerous stored/residual energy or reaccumulation; a single readily identified/isolated source; complete deenergization/deactivation by its isolation; isolation and lockout during servicing; one lock achieves protection; exclusive control by the authorized servicing employee; no hazards created for others; and no employer accidents involving unexpected activation/reenergization during such servicing. It is not an exemption from energy control, training or other program duties. Do not use it for a multi-source machine.
