lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Integrated Rigging and Signaling — integration instruction
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Integrated Rigging and Signaling — integration instruction

This course joins routine rigging, advanced rigging, crane-system knowledge and signaling into one assessed work sequence. The complete coursebook physically includes the relevant VNDRLY instructional chapters, rather than asking the learner to obtain earlier programs. These integration chapters address decisions at the boundaries between specialties. This is an original VNDRLY program, not NCCER certification or a substitute for employer task-specific qualification, licensed engineering or crane operator authority.

lessons.title: B01 — Coordinate roles without losing independent safety checks
lessons.body:
## B01 — Coordinate roles without losing independent safety checks

The rigger checks the load, rigging and connections; the operator controls the crane within its configuration and limits; the signaler communicates movement while observing the required route; the lift director coordinates the operation. One person may have more than one demonstrated skill, but that does not mean they can perform competing duties at the same instant. A rigger handling a connection may not be positioned to observe the whole path and give reliable signals. Plan the transition of duties before tensioning.

Start the brief with the actual object and intended sequence. Each role repeats the information it needs: weight and center, rigging configuration, crane setup and governing radius, path, landing, exclusion, communication and hold points. The operator's chart check and the rigger's component check should agree on the supported weights. If one includes a lifting beam and the other omits it, resolve the discrepancy rather than averaging the answers.

Use a deliberate ready-to-lift checkpoint. The rigger confirms the installed configuration and clears the pinch area. The signaler verifies the operator can receive the intended method and that the path is controlled. The operator confirms readiness within the plan. This is not a scripted permission to ignore a new hazard: anybody can call stop. A short checklist works only if its observations are actually made.

Worked case: the same worker finishes placing a sling and immediately signals hoist while still holding the sling at a pinch point. The team stops, establishes safe position and rechecks readiness. Combining titles did not remove the need to clear the connection before take-up. A better sequence assigns a visible transition and lets the operator see that the directing role is established.

Application: draw a responsibility timeline for a lift from initial inspection to rigging removal. Mark periods when a person cannot safely perform two roles. Assign coverage and handoff points rather than adding a generic 'all crew responsible' note that leaves nobody clearly directing.

lessons.title: B02 — Handle pipe, rebar and bundles as loads with internal movement
lessons.body:
## B02 — Handle pipe, rebar and bundles as loads with internal movement

A bundle is not necessarily one rigid object. Individual lengths can slide, roll, telescope or escape the rigging. Shipping bands may organize material without being rated lifting attachments. Verify bundle construction, individual lengths, end alignment, weight and the approved lifting method. Do not hook under a band simply because a forklift previously carried the package that way.

For pipe, consider rolling, surface condition, coating damage, sharp ends and whether contents or attachments change weight. Use the approved number and locations of supports and a retention arrangement that controls the actual material. A hitch that squeezes the outer pieces may not restrain shorter internal pieces. Keep people out of the possible end-ejection and rolling paths. Prepare chocks or a suitable rack at landing before moving the bundle.

Rebar combines flexible lengths, protruding ends and potential slippage. Verify the lifting arrangement supports the intended bundle without unacceptable bending or losing individual bars. Protect slings from sharp contact and keep hands away from closing gaps as the bundle settles. Do not straighten, pull or rearrange a suspended bundle by hand. Land and secure before correcting the arrangement.

Worked case: a bundle includes several short tubes hidden among longer ones. A two-point outer arrangement appears balanced, but the shorter pieces are not actually captured. Hold the lift and obtain an approved containment/rigging method for all pieces. Adding a tag line to one long tube does not restrain the short contents.

Application: on an unloaded tabletop bundle, identify every potential moving piece and the direction it could escape. Develop the landing plan and explain which packaging is organizational versus rated structural support. Actual lifting practice uses a verified safe training bundle with a qualified approved arrangement; the evaluator never secretly adds a loose piece to a live load.

lessons.title: B03 — Use gantries, equalizers and cantilever devices within their configurations
lessons.body:
## B03 — Use gantries, equalizers and cantilever devices within their configurations

A gantry system transfers load through beams, legs, jacks or wheels into the supporting surface. Its apparent symmetry does not prove equal reactions. Verify permitted span, height, bracing, support, travel conditions, lifting-point positions and manufacturer configuration. A device rated for stationary use may not permit rolling under load. Floor capacity and local wheel/jack reactions need separate verification.

An equalizer device can help distribute forces only within its permitted geometry and travel. If a pivot binds or reaches its limit, the expected equalization may disappear. Do not credit equal sharing without considering the complete load path and approved device data. A spreader typically controls compression forces and sling separation; a lifting beam typically carries bending. Their total marked ratings are not interchangeable configurations.

A cantilever lifting bar has a load offset from the support and may rely on a counterweight or specifically designed geometry. Its stability and member forces depend on distances and connections, not only total weight. A home-made counterweight addition is a design change. Verify actual device ratings, attachment points and the approved load location before use.

Worked teaching model: a 2,000-pound force acts 3 feet from a pivot and a balancing force acts 6 feet on the other side. Ideal moment balance requires 1,000 pounds, before device self-weight or any other forces. That arithmetic does not authorize building a cantilever device: structural strength, stability, retention and manufacturer/design limits remain unverified. The exercise teaches why distance matters, not a recipe for a fabricated lifting appliance.

Application: review a supplied gantry/device manual and label its permitted configuration. Introduce a changed span or offset on paper and identify the specific approval/calculation affected. If the actual manual does not cover the proposed arrangement, the correct answer is hold, not interpolation.

lessons.title: B04 — Handle and reeve wire rope without damaging or misapplying it
lessons.body:
## B04 — Handle and reeve wire rope without damaging or misapplying it

Identify rope diameter, construction, core, lay and intended application from traceable documentation. A rope that fits a groove is not necessarily the correct replacement. Strength, flexibility, rotation behavior and termination compatibility affect suitability. Distinguish a wire-rope sling from a crane running rope; their inspection criteria and assembly requirements differ.

Unreeling and installation must follow the actual rope/equipment instructions. Support the reel properly and control its motion. Avoid dragging rope over sharp edges, introducing reverse bends or pulling a loop tight into a kink. Keep hands away from rotating reels, drums, sheaves and tensioned rope. Use an approved method to control rope ends and stored energy; do not cut a tensioned rope or improvise splicing/termination work beyond competence.

Trace the specified reeving path before installation. Confirm the dead end, sheave sequence, supporting parts, drum direction, required rope length and permitted termination. Check groove condition and guards. Incorrect reeving can create interference, uneven winding or a different load path than the chart assumes. Initial spooling/tension and run-in follow manufacturer procedures; the course does not supply universal values.

Worked case: a proposed replacement has the same diameter as the original but its construction and rotation characteristics are unknown. Do not install it. Obtain the specified rope and verify documentation. If the existing rope has a kink or crushed area, straightening it until it looks round does not restore it to service.

Application: use a bench model with slack non-load-bearing line to trace the approved path, identify each support and spot a deliberately wrong route. Inspect isolated wire-rope specimens for damage and state the applicable rope/slings distinction. Actual crane rope installation requires the equipment-specific qualified procedure and is not awarded by a bench exercise alone.

lessons.title: B05 — Read the crane envelope as a rigging team member
lessons.body:
## B05 — Read the crane envelope as a rigging team member

The crane's lifting capacity depends on configuration and the full route. Identify boom type and length, base/support arrangement, counterweight, attachments, operating sector and actual load radius. A telescopic truck, rough-terrain carrier, all-terrain carrier or lattice crawler has configuration-specific data; a familiar appearance does not select the correct chart. A stationary supported chart is not a pick-and-carry chart.

Ask which radius governs, including landing and possible deflection. A range diagram helps establish reach/height but is not a capacity chart. Gross capacity, required deductions and complete suspended weight must be compared consistently. The rigging team supplies the weights of beams, slings and attachments; the operator/qualified plan applies the actual crane's chart conventions. A blank or out-of-range chart condition is not a number to guess.

Original practice data, not a real crane chart: a fictional stationary configuration has gross capacities of 12,000 pounds at 20 feet, 9,000 at 30 feet and 6,000 at 40 feet. For this exercise only, intermediate radii use the next larger listed radius; no interpolation. Required deductions are 700-pound block, 200-pound slings/connectors and 300-pound beam. Reeving limit is 10,000 pounds total suspended. A 5,000-pound payload at a governing 34-foot radius needs 6,200 pounds total; the applicable chart gives 6,000, so the lift fails by 200 pounds even though reeving alone permits it.

Jib or extension erection/stowage changes setup hazards and may affect chart selection/deductions even when the attachment is unused. Follow the actual assembly/disassembly plan, support/pin sequence and responsible direction. Never remove a pin because a diagram seems familiar or stand under an unsupported component to align it. The rigger's contribution is competent handling within the approved sequence, not independent crane configuration approval.

Application: use the fictional data to document governing radius, total suspended weight and the limiting comparison, then explain which actual manufacturer documents are needed for a real task. Inspect a supplied assembly drawing and identify support-before-release hold points without operating a crane or removing real pins.

lessons.title: B06 — Signal overhead cranes and derricks without transplanting the wrong function
lessons.body:
## B06 — Signal overhead cranes and derricks without transplanting the wrong function

An overhead bridge crane moves along a runway, while its trolley traverses the bridge and its hoist raises/lowers the load. These axes differ from a mobile crane's swing and boom functions. A gantry may carry a similar bridge on legs. Establish the operator's orientation and the specific equipment's agreed standard signals before directing movement. Do not use a swing command to describe bridge travel merely because the load goes sideways.

A derrick uses a mast or equivalent supported structure with a hoisting system, sometimes with a boom. Its guying/bracing, anchorage and permitted motions differ from a mobile crane carrier. Know which motions actually exist and which line/function is addressed. The plan and equipment instructions govern; this program does not authorize changing guy tension or anchorage to solve a motion problem.

For overhead signaling, practice distinct hoist, lower, bridge travel, trolley travel, stop, emergency stop and slow movement using the applicable standard/manufacturer chart. Teach the resulting movement on a labeled model, then demonstrate from the operator's view. If a function-specific signal differs from the OSHA mobile/tower reference, obtain and use the actual applicable chart and agreement; do not invent a gesture. This course's supplemental reference supplies an original described practice sequence and cites the primary chart used at delivery.

Worked case: a worker says 'left' while facing a pendant operator from the opposite side of the bay. The intended axis and reference are ambiguous. Stop and identify bridge versus trolley, direction and agreed amount/speed. A clear function command is safer than guessing which sideways movement the worker meant.

Application: move model tokens along perpendicular bridge/trolley axes and produce separate intended commands. For a derrick model, identify hoist and boom movement without treating a fixed mast as a traveling crane. Actual scope on the record identifies the equipment/function charts assessed rather than claiming all crane families from mobile-only practice.

Chart-comparison exercise: Michigan's official overhead/gantry Table1 illustrates bridge travel with a forward open-hand pushing motion and trolley travel with a palm-up directional thumb and horizontal hand motion. It identifies a trolley block by one or two raised fingers before the action. Its stop is a rigid horizontal palm-down arm; emergency stop moves that hand rapidly side to side. Its operator indication for a disconnected magnet spreads the hands, palms up. These are **context-specific overhead examples**, not replacements for the OSHA mobile/tower stop gestures taught in Part III. Compare the actual applicable chart before work. A magnet-disconnected indication is not an electrical isolation procedure or permission to enter beneath an unsecured load. Practice all nine entries in the supplied overhead reference and explicitly name which chart context is in use.

lessons.title: B07 — Manage an integrated change and incident response
lessons.body:
## B07 — Manage an integrated change and incident response

Changes cross specialties. A new sling length changes angle and hook height; a changed crane position changes radius and signal visibility; a new landing rack changes stability and removal access. Stop at the change and identify every affected assumption. The operator, rigger and signaler each recheck their part before the lift director releases the revised operation.

When a hazard appears during movement, issue the stop, maintain communication and use the approved safe securing/return option. Do not create a second emergency by entering beneath a load, touching possibly energized equipment or adjusting a connection under tension. Protect the area and summon the appropriate emergency/qualified assistance. Preserve equipment identities and observations for investigation; no field repair is made simply to avoid delay.

Worked case: a radio interruption occurs while a bundle is approaching a landing rack, and the rack has shifted. Restoring the radio alone is insufficient. The team must also restore or revise the landing support and verify the bundle/control arrangement before restarting. Clearing one symptom does not clear the entire changed condition.

Application: complete a change sheet with original condition, observed change, affected weight/geometry/capacity/communication/support assumptions, required reviewer and restart evidence. Practice the stop verbally on a safe model; never create a real support failure for an exercise.

lessons.title: B08 — Demonstrate the combined work, not three disconnected quizzes
lessons.body:
## B08 — Demonstrate the combined work, not three disconnected quizzes

The combined capstone begins with an original work order for a verified training load and route. The learner checks load/center, chooses and inspects rigging, explains the crane-chart boundary, assembles connections, briefs signals and demonstrates safe take-up, trial, movement and landing. The learner changes roles only at planned safe handoffs. A qualified operator remains responsible for actual crane controls.

The advanced portion uses the separately validated rotation/transfer fixture and its approved stages. The learner identifies changing forces and stops on a simulated discrepancy. The signaling portion requires both recognition and production, hand and voice/radio tasks, and the equipment-specific functions claimed. Bench demonstrations and live tasks are recorded distinctly. No amount of correct arithmetic substitutes for observed safe connection or signaling performance.

Worked grading decision: a learner rigs correctly but gives an ambiguous radio command to the wrong named crane. The combined task fails its safety gate even if the load was never moved because a simulator was used. Correct the communication gap and reassess a changed integrated sequence. Conversely, a learner who deliberately holds on missing capacity data is making the correct safety decision, not failing to 'finish the lift.'

Application: write the final work record with the actual equipment, method, calculated demands, observed stops, evaluator and limits. External NCCER certification is not awarded by this package. The VNDRLY result states the instruction and demonstrated scope without claiming external endorsement, engineering authority or universal job qualification.


---

courses.title: VUC028 | Formative practice

content.title: VUC028 | Formative practice
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: Formative practice
lessons.body:
# Formative practice

Attempt before reading answers. Use named chapter and changed practice for correction.

## R01-L1

Does a crane operator certificate automatically establish rigging qualification?

**Answer:** No; the employer must establish ability for the specific rigging task.

**Reason/remediation:** Different roles require demonstrated task competence.

## R01-L2

What should happen when a routine load changes to an unknown weight?

**Answer:** Hold and obtain current information and an appropriate arrangement.

**Reason/remediation:** The prior routine scope no longer describes the job.

## R02-L1

Name four load facts to verify.

**Answer:** Weight, center of gravity, suitable lifting points and load integrity/contents.

**Reason/remediation:** A strong sling cannot correct unknown or unsuitable load attachment.

## R02-L2

Why prepare dunnage before lifting?

**Answer:** To provide a stable landing and safe rigging removal.

**Reason/remediation:** Landing is part of the plan, not an afterthought.

## R03-L1

For an ideal symmetric4,000lb load at30degrees above horizontal, what is each leg tension?

**Answer:** 4,000lb.

**Reason/remediation:** 4,000/(2×sin30)=4,000.

## R03-L2

Can the design factor be treated as spare lifting capacity?

**Answer:** No; stay within the rated working limit and its conditions.

**Reason/remediation:** Breaking strength is not a usable rating.

## R04-L1

A sling inspected last week now has a cut. Use it?

**Answer:** No; remove/isolate and report it, then correct the damaging condition.

**Reason/remediation:** Current damage overrides a recent inspection.

## R04-L2

What makes an equipment-hold tag useful?

**Answer:** Identity, specific defect, date/reporter and restriction/disposition.

**Reason/remediation:** Another worker must understand why it cannot be used.

## R05-L1

Can ordinary tag-line rope replace a lifting sling?

**Answer:** No; it lacks the required rated lifting assembly/configuration.

**Reason/remediation:** Material resemblance is not lifting identification.

## R05-L2

Why is a soft rag not automatically adequate edge protection?

**Answer:** It may cut, move or fail under the actual contact load.

**Reason/remediation:** Protection must suit the edge, sling and loading.

## R06-L1

A sling is4,000vertical and3,200choker. Can it choke a3,500lb load?

**Answer:** No; it exceeds the applicable choker rating by300lb.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the installed hitch rating.

## R06-L2

A basket can slide along a smooth pipe. Is capacity alone enough?

**Answer:** No; obtain an approved stable arrangement preventing escape/rolling.

**Reason/remediation:** Containment and balance are separate from strength.

## R07-L1

May a convenient bolt replace a missing shackle pin?

**Answer:** No; use the correct identified compatible assembly.

**Reason/remediation:** An arbitrary bolt is not the rated pin.

## R07-L2

Why should a hook latch not carry the load?

**Answer:** It retains the connection; the intended hook bowl carries the load.

**Reason/remediation:** Tip/latch loading can defeat the rated configuration.

## R08-L1

Who may signal stop?

**Answer:** Anyone; it must be obeyed.

**Reason/remediation:** Normal signal assignment does not prevent hazard warnings.

## R08-L2

Is wrapping a tag line around an arm acceptable for grip?

**Answer:** No; keep clear and use the approved controlled handling method.

**Reason/remediation:** A moving load can drag or trap the person.

## R09-L1

What distinguishes the taught inside bowline tail orientation?

**Answer:** The tail is inside the fixed eye after correct dressing.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify structure, not only the knot name.

## R09-L2

Does correct knot tying authorize a knotted sling?

**Answer:** No; the bench knots are for approved nonlifting tasks only.

**Reason/remediation:** Knots do not establish a rated lifting assembly.

## R10-L1

When may rigging be disconnected after landing?

**Answer:** After the load is fully supported, stable and the rigging unloaded under the plan.

**Reason/remediation:** One corner touching is not stable release.

## R10-L2

A sling is trapped under a landed load. Jerk it out?

**Answer:** No; safely re-support/reposition under an approved plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Shock and uncontrolled movement can injure or damage.

## R11-L1

Can a clamp be used outside its specified thickness/orientation?

**Answer:** No; select suitable equipment and revise the method.

**Reason/remediation:** A hook on a device does not make its application universal.

## R11-L2

What does an unexpected snag during lifting require?

**Answer:** Stop and safely resolve it; do not jerk or force the load free.

**Reason/remediation:** Breakout/shock forces may exceed the planned static load.

## R12-L1

A2,600lb load uses a2,400lb choker rating. Decision?

**Answer:** Hold;200lb overload.

**Reason/remediation:** The selected hitch governs.

## R12-L2

The rigging is adequate but a lifting eye is cracked. Continue?

**Answer:** No; hold the complete lift and resolve the load attachment.

**Reason/remediation:** Every part of the load path must be suitable.

## R13-L1

Does a rated hoist prove its supporting beam is adequate?

**Answer:** No; verify the complete support/anchor load path.

**Reason/remediation:** The reaction is carried by the structure.

## R13-L2

What must follow raising a load on a jack?

**Answer:** Prompt suitable blocking/cribbing or other approved secure support.

**Reason/remediation:** Hydraulic pressure alone is not protection beneath a load.

## R14-L1

Can a positioning swivel automatically rotate under load?

**Answer:** No; check the actual device rating/instructions.

**Reason/remediation:** Positioning and loaded rotation are different applications.

## R14-L2

Why not apply crane running-rope wire-break limits to every sling?

**Answer:** Sling and rope types have different applicable criteria.

**Reason/remediation:** Identify the actual product and rule before acceptance.

## A01-L1

Why does turning a known skid upright require a new review?

**Answer:** Rotation changes geometry, force directions, support and stability; obtain an approved staged plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Review A01 and identify the changed assumptions rather than merely increasing sling size.

## A01-L2

Does a rigging certificate authorize every lift?

**Answer:** No; employer task-specific qualification and applicable planning are still required.

**Reason/remediation:** Explain the difference between a training achievement and authority for a particular task.

## A02-L1

Use the supplied density 490 lb/ft³ for a solid 36×24×1 inch plate. Find weight.

**Answer:** 864/1728=0.5 ft³; 245 lb.

**Reason/remediation:** A02: convert cubic units before multiplying; supplied density is an exercise input.

## A02-L2

Where do you count a lifting beam in load accounting?

**Answer:** At every boundary supporting it, including the upper system, not automatically in lower sling demand.

**Reason/remediation:** Draw each load-path boundary and list what hangs below it.

## A03-L1

Find xCG for 2000 lb at x=1 ft and 1000 lb at x=7 ft.

**Answer:** 3000 lb total; (2000+7000)/3000=3 ft.

**Reason/remediation:** Use component centers and weighted moments, not midpoint of length.

## A03-L2

What does unexpected tilt at trial require?

**Answer:** Stop, safely lower and verify actual load, center and installed geometry before authorized adjustment.

**Reason/remediation:** A03: do not correct a suspended imbalance with a person or tag line.

## A04-L1

Find reactions for 12000 lb at x=2 ft between vertical supports at 0 and 8 ft.

**Answer:** Right 3000 lb; left 9000 lb.

**Reason/remediation:** Check both force sum and moment balance.

## A04-L2

Why cannot four connected legs simply be assigned one-quarter weight each?

**Answer:** Stiffness, lengths and geometry affect sharing; use applicable rated data and qualified analysis.

**Reason/remediation:** A04: equilibrium alone may not determine all reactions.

## A05-L1

Find equal leg tensions for 4000 lb at 30° from horizontal.

**Answer:** 4000/(2 sin30°)=4000 lb each.

**Reason/remediation:** Resolve each vertical component to 2000 lb; do not confuse vertical angle.

## A05-L2

For 6000 lb and horizontal angles 30°/60°, give both tensions and a check.

**Answer:** T1=3000 lb, T2≈5196 lb; vertical components 1500+4500=6000, horizontals cancel.

**Reason/remediation:** A05: use a compatible two-force geometry and degree mode.

## A06-L1

A sling is rated 5000 vertical and 4000 choker; demand in choker is 4500. Decision?

**Answer:** Reject that arrangement; the applicable 4000 limit is exceeded.

**Reason/remediation:** Use installed hitch rating, not the largest tag number.

## A06-L2

Can a periodic inspection record replace today’s inspection?

**Answer:** No; inspect before use and isolate current defects or missing identification.

**Reason/remediation:** A06: records and present condition address different times.

## A07-L1

A hoist-ring shoulder is held off its seat by a weld bead. What now?

**Answer:** Hold; obtain an approved connection correction, not extra torque or unauthorized grinding.

**Reason/remediation:** A07: installation geometry is part of suitability.

## A07-L2

Can a similar loose pin replace a missing shackle pin?

**Answer:** Only the approved compatible component; appearance/fit is insufficient.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify identity, retention and manufacturer requirements.

## A08-L1

Ideal fixed return block has two parallel segments at 2000 lb tension. Support force?

**Answer:** 4000 lb before block weight and actual effects.

**Reason/remediation:** Add both rope forces on the block, not just one.

## A08-L2

The hoist is rated but the beam is undocumented. May a low trial prove it?

**Answer:** No; verify the support before loading.

**Reason/remediation:** A08: a trial is not a structural capacity test.

## A09-L1

Why does a flat-sheet vacuum rating not approve corrugated sheet?

**Answer:** Contact/sealing geometry and holding conditions differ; obtain actual suitability evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** A09: weight is only one input.

## A09-L2

Can an equal-capacity spreader replace a lifting beam?

**Answer:** Not without approval of load distribution, top rigging, compression/bending and configuration.

**Reason/remediation:** Identify how each device transmits forces.

## A10-L1

What must be checked during a planned low-clearance trial?

**Answer:** Expected balance/orientation, seating, integrity, holding and clearances from a safe position.

**Reason/remediation:** A10: trial checks a verified setup; it does not excuse unknown weight.

## A10-L2

A tensioned sling needs moving by hand. Action?

**Answer:** Stop, lower to secure support and adjust only after safe unloading and authorization.

**Reason/remediation:** Keep hands out of tension and pinch zones.

## A11-L1

In the warning model RB=1000(0.5−0.25 tanφ), find RB at 45°.

**Answer:** 250 lb; RA=750 lb.

**Reason/remediation:** A11: model assumptions must remain valid.

## A11-L2

Why does a negative computed sling reaction invalidate the model?

**Answer:** A tensile sling cannot provide the required pushing force.

**Reason/remediation:** More capacity does not repair impossible geometry.

## A12-L1

A controlling leg becomes slack early in rotation. Action?

**Answer:** Stop and follow approved safe securing/return, then investigate before continuing.

**Reason/remediation:** A12: do not speed up the other hoist to compensate.

## A12-L2

What must be defined at rotation hold points?

**Answer:** Expected orientation/support/force conditions, checks, release authority and safe recovery.

**Reason/remediation:** The whole path, not just end positions, needs planning.

## A13-L1

What follows a controlled jack raise?

**Answer:** Promptly secure using the planned blocking or other support; do not rely on pressure alone.

**Reason/remediation:** A13: prevent loss-of-support crush exposure.

## A13-L2

Why can a cabinet become unstable on skates after a stable lift?

**Answer:** Support polygon, center projection and movement forces change.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify each transfer and route condition, not only total capacity.

## A14-L1

Required radio communication is lost during movement. Action?

**Answer:** Stop safely and restore agreed communication before continuing.

**Reason/remediation:** A14: guessing a command is not a safe substitute.

## A14-L2

When may rigging be released at landing?

**Answer:** After verified stable intended support and safe unloading/removal conditions.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not pull trapped rigging from an unstable load.

## A15-L1

What makes a calculation reviewable?

**Answer:** Inputs/sources, units, geometry/free-body model, assumptions, calculations and applicable limits.

**Reason/remediation:** A15: a signed answer without its basis cannot be reproduced.

## A15-L2

Demand is 5196 lb and applicable limit 5000. Can it be rounded down?

**Answer:** No; revise and recalculate the approved arrangement.

**Reason/remediation:** Breaking strength/design factor is not spare working capacity.

## A16-L1

Find reactions for 3000 lb at x=3 between vertical supports 0 and 8 ft.

**Answer:** Right 1125 lb; left 1875 lb.

**Reason/remediation:** A16: check 1125×8=3000×3.

## A16-L2

Does passing the level task permit an unplanned rotation?

**Answer:** No; rotation has its own approved staged setup and observed assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** Keep demonstrated scope and authority explicit.

## S01-L1

Does course attendance alone qualify a signaler?

**Answer:** No; required knowledge and practical evaluation plus method-specific documentation are needed.

**Reason/remediation:** Review S01 and distinguish learning participation from evaluated competence.

## S01-L2

Can an employer-only evaluation automatically transfer to another employer?

**Answer:** No; that OSHA evaluation path is not portable.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify the evaluation path and employing organization.

## S02-L1

What is the difference between hoist and raise boom?

**Answer:** Hoist moves the hook by the load line; raise boom changes boom angle and geometry.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the intended function, not an approximate load direction.

## S02-L2

Whose perspective governs directions?

**Answer:** The operator’s perspective.

**Reason/remediation:** Practice from both sides of the model before giving commands.

## S03-L1

How do main/auxiliary selection signals relate to the movement signal?

**Answer:** Select the intended line, then give the regular action signal.

**Reason/remediation:** Selection alone is not a movement command.

## S03-L2

What distinguishes ordinary stop from emergency stop on the chart?

**Answer:** Stop uses one horizontal sweeping arm; emergency stop uses both, palms down.

**Reason/remediation:** Demonstrate the actual movement from the official chart, not a static pose.

## S04-L1

Your position loses the operator’s view behind a column. What now?

**Answer:** Stop the operation requiring signals and restore suitable communication before an understood restart.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not continue on the last visible command.

## S04-L2

Can two signalers direct the same crane simultaneously to be helpful?

**Answer:** No; one directs at a time, with the emergency stop exception.

**Reason/remediation:** Plan a deliberate handoff while safely stopped.

## S05-L1

State the three elements in a voice command.

**Answer:** Function/direction; distance and/or speed; function/stop.

**Reason/remediation:** S05: preserve the order and deliver stop at the appropriate movement point.

lessons.title: S05-L2
lessons.body:
## S05-L2

What is missing from “bring it this way”?

**Answer:** Unambiguous function, operator-perspective direction and movement amount/speed with function-stop.

**Reason/remediation:** Translate conversational intent into agreed crane commands.

lessons.title: S06-L1
lessons.body:
## S06-L1

Where must radio effectiveness be tested?

**Answer:** On site at the positions needed for the operation, before work.

**Reason/remediation:** A near-cab test does not prove reception behind a structure.

lessons.title: S06-L2
lessons.body:
## S06-L2

What receiving arrangement does the operator require?

**Answer:** Hands-free reception in the suitable tested signaling system.

**Reason/remediation:** A handheld phone is not equivalent merely because audio is clear.

lessons.title: S07-L1
lessons.body:
## S07-L1

Why can a load keep moving after a swing command stops?

**Answer:** Suspended-load momentum/pendulum motion persists.

**Reason/remediation:** Anticipate controlled stopping; do not amplify motion by abrupt corrections.

lessons.title: S07-L2
lessons.body:
## S07-L2

The load drags sideways during take-up. Safe response?

**Answer:** Stop and investigate alignment, snagging or changed geometry with the responsible team.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not order extra hoist to force it free.

lessons.title: S08-L1
lessons.body:
## S08-L1

What is two-blocking?

**Answer:** Contact between lower moving hook/block assembly and upper boom-tip/block assembly.

**Reason/remediation:** Recognize clearance loss from hoisting and geometry changes.

lessons.title: S08-L2
lessons.body:
## S08-L2

Does an anti-two-block device replace signaler observation?

**Answer:** No; do not drive to the safeguard or defeat it.

**Reason/remediation:** Stop a developing clearance hazard before contact.

lessons.title: S09-L1
lessons.body:
## S09-L1

Can line voltage be inferred safely from appearance?

**Answer:** No; verify applicable electrical information and controls through responsible planning.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not turn a guessed voltage into an approach clearance.

lessons.title: S09-L2
lessons.body:
## S09-L2

Why can one load require stopping in wind before another nearby load?

**Answer:** Shape, surface area, equipment and plan limits differ.

**Reason/remediation:** No single universal wind number is invented for all lifts.

lessons.title: S10-L1
lessons.body:
## S10-L1

Does crane identification alone make a two-crane lift ready?

**Answer:** No; qualified planning/direction and coordinated sequence are also required.

**Reason/remediation:** Communication is necessary but does not establish load sharing.

lessons.title: S10-L2
lessons.body:
## S10-L2

May a worker ride a cargo load to solve a blind-view problem?

**Answer:** No; reject the improvised personnel lift and establish proper communication/access.

**Reason/remediation:** A visibility problem does not waive personnel-lift requirements.

lessons.title: S11-L1
lessons.body:
## S11-L1

Who may give emergency stop?

**Answer:** Anyone aware of a safety problem.

**Reason/remediation:** The designated-signaler rule does not suppress emergency warnings.

lessons.title: S11-L2
lessons.body:
## S11-L2

A landed load rocks and traps the sling. Release or pull free?

**Answer:** Neither; stop and establish stable support and an approved safe removal.

**Reason/remediation:** Touching the landing is not proof of stability.

lessons.title: S12-L1
lessons.body:
## S12-L1

A learner names signals but cannot produce a discernible stop. Pass?

**Answer:** No; remediate and independently reassess practical performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Recognition does not substitute for application.

lessons.title: S12-L2
lessons.body:
## S12-L2

What signaling scope belongs on the record?

**Answer:** The methods actually evaluated, setup/evaluator and limitations, without invented operator or external certification.

**Reason/remediation:** Record actual evidence, not a broad title.

lessons.title: C01-L1
lessons.body:
## C01-L1

A current certificate lists a crane type. Does it establish competence on every configuration?

**Answer:** No. Employer evaluation must address the actual equipment and assigned tasks.

**Reason/remediation:** Separate external certification from demonstrated equipment/task ability; revisit C01.

lessons.title: C01-L2
lessons.body:
## C01-L2

What changes when a fixed station is replaced by a swing cab?

**Answer:** The station rotates with the upper works, changing sight lines and orientation to the carrier.

**Reason/remediation:** Identify the actual type before transferring control habits.

lessons.title: C02-L1
lessons.body:
## C02-L1

A load is picked at 25 feet and placed at 40 feet. Which radius must planning include?

**Answer:** The 40-foot placement and every intervening loaded condition.

**Reason/remediation:** Capacity at pickup does not establish capacity along the whole path.

lessons.title: C02-L2
lessons.body:
## C02-L2

Why is a boom triangle insufficient to prove hook clearance?

**Answer:** Real pivot offset/height, loaded deflection, block dimensions and clearances must be included.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the actual range diagram, not only ideal geometry.

lessons.title: C03-L1
lessons.body:
## C03-L1

A 48,000-pound reaction acts on 16 square feet. Calculate the simple pressure.

**Answer:** 3,000 pounds per square foot; compare with established support criteria.

**Reason/remediation:** 48,000/16=3,000; this does not establish mat structural adequacy.

lessons.title: C03-L2
lessons.body:
## C03-L2

A previously approved setup flooded overnight. What changes?

**Answer:** Reassess ground/support and level before operation.

**Reason/remediation:** Prior approval does not prove current support.

lessons.title: C05-L1
lessons.body:
## C05-L1

May an operator assume the A/D director role because of an operator certificate?

**Answer:** No. That role requires its own applicable competence/qualification.

**Reason/remediation:** Operating and directing assembly are different duties.

lessons.title: C05-L2
lessons.body:
## C05-L2

A boom pin is fitted but its retainer is missing. May a test lift establish safety?

**Answer:** No. Complete the approved assembly and required inspection before use.

**Reason/remediation:** Motion cannot substitute for configuration integrity.

lessons.title: C07-L1
lessons.body:
## C07-L1

Why is a stronger rope not automatically a valid replacement?

**Answer:** Construction, diameter, rotation, bending, terminations and machine compatibility also govern.

**Reason/remediation:** Use manufacturer selection and authorized installation criteria.

lessons.title: C07-L2
lessons.body:
## C07-L2

The chart allows 30,000 pounds but reeving allows 24,000. Can a 25,000-pound total load proceed?

**Answer:** No. It exceeds the governing reeving limit.

**Reason/remediation:** The lowest applicable limit controls.

lessons.title: C08-L1
lessons.body:
## C08-L1

Can a spotter replace a failed required safety device?

**Answer:** No. Required safety-device failure requires safe stop/out-of-service until corrected.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not confuse device rules with specified operating-aid alternatives.

lessons.title: C08-L2
lessons.body:
## C08-L2

The capacity display says full outriggers but one beam is partial. Which is decisive?

**Answer:** The mismatch must be resolved against an approved actual configuration before lifting.

**Reason/remediation:** A wrong input can make a display dangerously optimistic.

lessons.title: C09-L1
lessons.body:
## C09-L1

Gross capacity is 18,000 and deductions total 1,800. What is the payload allowance?

**Answer:** 16,200 pounds under that chart convention.

**Reason/remediation:** Subtract each required deduction once.

lessons.title: C09-L2
lessons.body:
## C09-L2

A chart has no entry for the installed configuration. What is the next action?

**Answer:** Hold and obtain a valid chart/configuration; do not invent a rating.

**Reason/remediation:** A blank is not permission to interpolate.

lessons.title: C13-L1
lessons.body:
## C13-L1

Does hydraulic-crane experience establish friction-crane control skill?

**Answer:** No. Clutch/brake coordination requires specific training and assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** Power-flow differences affect safe control.

lessons.title: C13-L2
lessons.body:
## C13-L2

Why inspect the actual lattice section order?

**Answer:** It establishes the approved boom configuration and chart/erection limits.

**Reason/remediation:** Overall appearance is not configuration proof.

lessons.title: C14-L1
lessons.body:
## C14-L1

Can a fixed-cab operator assume the same sight lines on a swing cab?

**Answer:** No. Reorient to the rotating station, upper works and carrier hazards.

**Reason/remediation:** Familiarization must match the actual equipment.

lessons.title: C14-L2
lessons.body:
## C14-L2

Does a stowed jib always have no effect on main-boom capacity?

**Answer:** No. Apply the actual chart notes and required deductions.

**Reason/remediation:** Unused attachments may still affect the rating.

lessons.title: B01-L1
lessons.body:
## B01-L1

Why may one qualified worker still need a role handoff?

**Answer:** Rigging contact and route observation/signaling can compete; transition safely before tensioning.

**Reason/remediation:** Map simultaneous duties rather than assuming titles remove conflicts.

lessons.title: B01-L2
lessons.body:
## B01-L2

Rigger includes beam weight but operator does not. Next step?

**Answer:** Resolve supported-weight accounting before releasing the lift.

**Reason/remediation:** Independent checks must agree on the actual load path.

lessons.title: B02-L1
lessons.body:
## B02-L1

Are shipping bands necessarily lifting points?

**Answer:** No; verify rated intended attachments and containment of every piece.

**Reason/remediation:** Packaging may organize material without supporting a lift.

lessons.title: B02-L2
lessons.body:
## B02-L2

Short tubes are hidden in a long bundle. What hazard arises?

**Answer:** They may escape despite outer support; hold for approved containment/rigging.

**Reason/remediation:** Check internal movement, not only bundle balance.

lessons.title: B03-L1
lessons.body:
## B03-L1

Why can equalizer travel limits affect load sharing?

**Answer:** A bound or stopped pivot may no longer distribute forces as assumed.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify actual geometry/range and approved data.

lessons.title: B03-L2
lessons.body:
## B03-L2

Ideal2000 lb at3 ft balanced at6 ft requires what force? Does this approve a device?

**Answer:** 1000 lb; no, structural/stability/retention/design requirements remain.

**Reason/remediation:** Moment balance is not a fabricated-device approval.

lessons.title: B04-L1
lessons.body:
## B04-L1

Does same rope diameter prove replacement compatibility?

**Answer:** No; construction/core/lay/rotation behavior/strength and equipment instructions matter.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify the actual specified rope and termination.

lessons.title: B04-L2
lessons.body:
## B04-L2

May a kink be straightened and treated as repaired?

**Answer:** No; follow proper removal/disposition, not cosmetic repair.

**Reason/remediation:** Damage can remain after appearance changes.

lessons.title: B05-L1
lessons.body:
## B05-L1

Fictional chart at34 ft uses which row?

**Answer:** 40 ft,6000 lb gross under the supplied next-larger-radius rule.

**Reason/remediation:** No interpolation or real-crane use of the exercise chart.

lessons.title: B05-L2
lessons.body:
## B05-L2

With5000 payload and1200 deductions, does that chart permit the lift?

**Answer:** No;6200 total exceeds6000 by200.

**Reason/remediation:** Compare total load consistently with gross rating and other limits.

lessons.title: B06-L1
lessons.body:
## B06-L1

Why distinguish bridge travel and trolley travel?

**Answer:** They move different axes/components and require specific agreed commands.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not substitute mobile swing for any sideways movement.

lessons.title: B06-L2
lessons.body:
## B06-L2

May a mobile stop gesture be assumed identical to every overhead chart?

**Answer:** No; verify the applicable equipment/chart context and agreement.

**Reason/remediation:** The supplied comparison shows meaningful context-specific differences.

lessons.title: B07-L1
lessons.body:
## B07-L1

Radio is restored but landing support changed. Ready?

**Answer:** No; resolve landing and every affected assumption before restart.

**Reason/remediation:** Clearing one fault does not clear all hazards.

lessons.title: B07-L2
lessons.body:
## B07-L2

What goes on a change record?

**Answer:** Observed change, affected assumptions, responsible review and evidence for safe restart.

**Reason/remediation:** Use concrete data rather than a generic approval signature.

lessons.title: B08-L1
lessons.body:
## B08-L1

Rigging is correct but the command addresses the wrong crane. Pass?

**Answer:** No; critical integrated communication failure requires remediation/reassessment.

**Reason/remediation:** An accurate subsystem does not excuse an unsafe combined task.

lessons.title: B08-L2
lessons.body:
## B08-L2

Does this combined program issue NCCER credentials?

**Answer:** No; original VNDRLY achievement with actual demonstrated scope only.

**Reason/remediation:** External certification requires the external provider’s process.


---

courses.title: VUC028 | Foundation practicals — VUC028

content.title: VUC028 | Foundation practicals — VUC028
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: Foundation practicals — VUC028
lessons.body:
# Foundation practicals — VUC028

Apply the combined guide scoring and award rules. These are the full previously authored tasks, with unique prefixes.

lessons.title: RI-A — Job briefing and load verification
lessons.body:
## RI-A — Job briefing and load verification

Task: inspect a supplied known-load work order, explain the assigned routine scope and prepare path/landing controls. Inject unknown contents on a second card. Equipment: actual load documentation, site plan and synthetic qualification record.

Criteria:1 identifies roles/scope;2 verifies weight/CG/lifting points;3 identifies path/landing and exclusion needs;4*holds unknown/changed load;5 communicates the exact unresolved information. Expected decision: similar appearance does not validate changed contents. Record the actual evidence used.

lessons.title: RI-B — Material-specific pre-use inspection
lessons.body:
## RI-B — Material-specific pre-use inspection

Task: examine at least six identified specimens covering chain, wire rope, web, round, fiber and mesh, plus hooks/connectors. Some defects are photographs or isolated samples. Decide serviceable/hold and explain the correct criteria.

Criteria:1 reads identification/rating;2 inspects full accessible material/terminations;3*rejects damaged/unidentified item;4 distinguishes material-specific criteria and periodic versus pre-use inspection;5 tags/isolate/reports with identity and finding. Include a cut web, broken strand/defective rope, distorted chain link, roundsling-cover damage, fiber deterioration and distorted mesh handle. Do not mark 'all slings checked' without individual observations.

lessons.title: RI-C — Hitch installation and edge protection
lessons.body:
## RI-C — Hitch installation and edge protection

Task: demonstrate vertical, basket and choker arrangements on a stable bench/low training load using the supplied approved configuration and ratings. Compare the installed hitch with the correct tag value.

Criteria:1 selects correct hitch/rating;2 seats untwisted sling and protects edges;3*rejects unstable/slipping or overloaded arrangement;4 keeps hands out during controlled slack take-up;5 explains angle/bend/contact limits. Observe every hitch separately. A favorable basket rating does not approve an unstable load.

lessons.title: RI-D — Hardware connection
lessons.body:
## RI-D — Hardware connection

Task: build an approved connection with lifting point, shackle and sling, then identify faults in separate disabled examples: wrong pin, missing retainer, tip-loaded hook, bunched synthetic eye and misaligned eyebolt.

Criteria:1 verifies identity/rating/direction;2 checks compatibility/fit;3*rejects substitute pin or missing required retention;4 installs/seats according to actual instructions;5 explains why side-load/rotation/engagement changes need review. No field-modified hardware or lift proof test is permitted.

lessons.title: RI-E — Rating and geometry laboratory
lessons.body:
## RI-E — Rating and geometry laboratory

Task: solve two supplied known-arrangement cases and a changed-angle hold case. Use actual supplied rating charts for the physical arrangement; synthetic calculations are exercises only.

Criteria:1 identifies units/angle convention;2 selects correct hitch value;3 calculates/checks supplied leg demand;4*holds a component/configuration overload;5 explains that inspection/load integrity/path still govern. Example:3,000 lb symmetric at 30 degrees means 3,000 lb per ideal leg; a 2,500 lb leg rating fails. Assess reasoning, not only arithmetic.

lessons.title: RI-F — Five basic nonlifting knots
lessons.body:
## RI-F — Five basic nonlifting knots

Task: on the bench tie/dress/set an inside bowline, clove hitch, square knot, two half hitches and sheet bend, then distinguish a deliberately wrong configuration. Use appropriate ropes and a post; no suspended load or person is attached.

Criteria:1 identifies ends/standing part and follows sequence;2 produces each correct dressed structure;3 uses appropriate bight/tail orientation;4*rejects knot substitution for rated sling/life-safety equipment;5 explains slipping/cyclic-load/backup limitations and checks the task's instructions. Record each knot individually as pass/pending; aggregate score cannot hide a missing knot. Repeat in a changed order without verbal prompting.

lessons.title: RI-G — Signals, tag line and position
lessons.body:
## RI-G — Signals, tag line and position

Task: rehearse stop/emergency stop/hoist/lower/swing/slow and the actual task signals with disabled equipment, then demonstrate safe tag-line handling during the approved low lift. Inject an ambiguous/lost signal as a card while the load can be safely stopped.

Criteria:1 identifies designated signal role;2 correctly interprets practiced functions;3*obeys stop/holds ambiguity;4*keeps body clear and never wraps the line around it;5 maintains escape path/communication. This is task-signal practice, not a separate signal-person credential.

lessons.title: RI-H — Hoists, jacks and movement devices
lessons.body:
## RI-H — Hoists, jacks and movement devices

Task: inspect a hoist/support connection, demonstrate a suitable low jack-and-secure sequence on a stable training fixture and identify trolley/skate/A-frame hazards from equipment/manuals or scenarios. No body part enters beneath the load; no complex load transfer is attempted.

Criteria:1 checks entire support/anchor system;2 verifies device rating/retention and setup;3*secures raised load rather than relying on pressure;4 identifies travel/side-pull/rolling hazards;5 rejects makeshift extension, unknown beam or unplanned multiple-device operation. Mark physical tasks versus awareness scenarios precisely.

lessons.title: RI-I — Complete known-load lift and landing
lessons.body:
## RI-I — Complete known-load lift and landing

Task: individually inspect, connect and manage the approved routine arrangement with a qualified lifting team; conduct controlled initial lift, guide from a safe position, land on prepared support, release and remove/store gear. The instructor may present a communication-loss card; no real instability is created.

Criteria:1 verifies load/rigging/hardware/path;2 correctly installs and checks slack take-up;3*maintains exclusion/stop decisions and rejects unexpected shift;4*lands stably before releasing;5 removes/stores and reports without jerking trapped gear. All actions must be observed; a spoken checklist is insufficient.

lessons.title: RI-J — Special-device and changed-condition decisions
lessons.body:
## RI-J — Special-device and changed-condition decisions

Task: resolve cards for a clamp outside its thickness range, unknown chemical on webbing, proposed tandem lift, block-support reaction and undocumented swivel-under-load use.

Criteria:1 identifies device-specific restriction;2*rejects damaged/unknown equipment use;3 recognizes higher-level planning boundary;4 identifies reaction/load-direction issue;5 states evidence/person needed to resolve each hold. At least one case uses an actual manufacturer's instruction page; do not accept generic 'be careful' responses.

lessons.title: RA-P01 — Establish scope and validate the object
lessons.body:
## RA-P01 — Establish scope and validate the object

Task: compare an actual training load with its drawing and a work order. A second scenario adds undocumented contents. Tools: drawing, inspection access, synthetic roles sheet.

Criteria: 1 identifies task/roles; 2 compares dimensions/attachments and load identity; 3 distinguishes verified from assumed data; 4*holds the changed/unverified configuration; 5 identifies the required qualified resolution. Expected: original paperwork does not cover new contents or rotation. Record the specific hold, not just 'understands safety.'

lessons.title: RA-P02 — Calculate weight and center
lessons.body:
## RA-P02 — Calculate weight and center

Task: calculate a supplied composite body's weight and two-coordinate center using actual problem units, then explain a changed attachment. Use the original coursebook cases for instruction and changed numbers for assessment.

Criteria: 1 consistent units and defensible inputs; 2 correct volume/weight arithmetic; 3 correct weighted moments; 4 checks physical plausibility and attachment effects; 5*does not treat unresolved material/contents as verified. Expected: sums of weights/moments with coordinates and units, plus a hold for missing inputs. Preserve the worksheet and calculator checks.

lessons.title: RA-P03 — Reactions and bridle forces
lessons.body:
## RA-P03 — Reactions and bridle forces

Task: solve two-support eccentric reactions and an unequal-angle bridle, then inspect a three-leg proposal with unproven sharing.

Criteria: 1 correct free-body model; 2 moment and force balance; 3 correct angle reference and trigonometry; 4 checks component demands against actual configuration limits; 5*rejects negative tensile reactions or unsupported equal sharing. Expected: correct answer is insufficient without a valid model. Preserve diagrams and independent balance checks.

lessons.title: RA-P04 — Inspect and select sling families
lessons.body:
## RA-P04 — Inspect and select sling families

Task: examine identified chain, wire, web, round, mesh and fiber examples plus isolated defects; select a hitch for the approved training task using actual data.

Criteria: 1 reads identity/rating; 2 checks full accessible body/terminations and material-specific damage; 3*isolates every unsafe/unidentified specimen; 4 selects compatible hitch/angle/bend/protection; 5 records item and finding. Observe each family individually. Expected: no use of generic running-rope criteria for sling removal or vertical rating for a choker.

lessons.title: RA-P05 — Install compatible connections
lessons.body:
## RA-P05 — Install compatible connections

Task: install the plan's shackle and lifting-point connection, demonstrate the specified torque/retention and identify bench faults in a turnbuckle, hook and compression termination.

Criteria: 1 component/thread/pin compatibility; 2 correct seating/alignment; 3 correct specified torque/retention; 4*rejects side/tip loading or unapproved termination; 5 documents manual/configuration and final inspection. Expected: no hand-tightening substitution or construction sling-eye clips. No live loaded adjustment is used as a training shortcut.

lessons.title: RA-P06 — Hoists and block support
lessons.body:
## RA-P06 — Hoists and block support

Task: trace a demonstration reeving arrangement, calculate an ideal return-block reaction, inspect the actual hoist/support and demonstrate unloaded controls followed by the approved low-load task.

Criteria: 1 correct rope path/supporting parts; 2 distinguishes ideal calculation from actual rated data; 3 verifies upstream support and hoist condition; 4*stops on side pull, unverified support or abnormal holding; 5 demonstrates normal stop/isolation and recovery communication. Record which manual, lever, electric or air model was actually operated; other types remain awareness-only.

lessons.title: RA-P07 — Below-hook device suitability
lessons.body:
## RA-P07 — Below-hook device suitability

Task: choose among a beam, clamp and vacuum/magnetic device for supplied cases using actual instructions. Include incompatible thickness, eccentric beam loading and unsuitable contact surface.

Criteria: 1 identifies permitted load/material/configuration; 2 includes device weight and support effects; 3 evaluates contact/locking/power-loss limitations; 4*rejects an incompatible case despite sufficient nominal capacity; 5 states inspection and exclusion needs. Expected: three independent selection decisions with cited product evidence. This station does not confer all-device operating authority.

lessons.title: RA-P08 — Level-lift execution
lessons.body:
## RA-P08 — Level-lift execution

Task: independently rig the approved eccentric training load and execute briefing, take-up, trial, movement and landing within the plan's measured tolerance. Use a safe scenario card to introduce an unexpected tilt before continuation.

Criteria: 1 verifies calculations/installed configuration; 2 establishes exclusion/signals; 3 checks trial balance and clearances; 4*stops and safely lowers/reviews the discrepant case; 5 lands stably and releases correctly. Record actual clearance and orientation against the planner's tolerances. Successful movement alone does not pass poor decisions.

lessons.title: RA-P09 — Rotation planning and model limits
lessons.body:
## RA-P09 — Rotation planning and model limits

Task: calculate the A11 warning model at changed assigned angles, identify its invalid range, and compare it with the approved real fixture plan.

Criteria: 1 correctly transforms coordinates; 2 balances moments/reactions; 3 identifies slack/negative/singular conditions; 4*rejects using the hypothetical model as a live 90-degree plan; 5 explains actual fixture stages/force directions and recovery. Expected: mathematical limits and actual approvals are kept distinct. Preserve the plotted values.

lessons.title: RA-P10 — Controlled rotation performance
lessons.body:
## RA-P10 — Controlled rotation performance

Task: independently conduct the validated fixture's rotation from its approved start to finish through all hold points, then respond to a verbally injected early-slack discrepancy.

Criteria: 1 verifies fixture/points/rigging and approved plan; 2 briefs coordinated commands/exclusion; 3 checks each stage against expected orientation and support; 4*stops and follows safe recovery for the discrepancy without improvised opposing movement; 5 secures final support before releasing. Record actual angles and each hold-point observation. No tabletop-only pass; no arbitrary angle range imposed by this course on an unvalidated fixture.

lessons.title: RA-P11 — Jack, secure and transfer
lessons.body:
## RA-P11 — Jack, secure and transfer

Task: use an approved low-height stable load to demonstrate jack placement, controlled raise and prompt securing, then evaluate a skate route and narrow-support tipping case.

Criteria: 1 verifies jack/support/contact/rating; 2 follows planned increments and safe blocking method; 3*never depends on pressure alone or enters the crush area; 4 evaluates route/support polygon/changed load share; 5 lowers/removes equipment in the planned sequence. Expected: each new support state is checked before transfer. Actual rolling may occur only with its separately approved setup.

lessons.title: RA-P12 — Integrated plan, communication and closeout
lessons.body:
## RA-P12 — Integrated plan, communication and closeout

Task: submit the complete advanced training-task plan, brief the team, execute its approved level-lift portion and demonstrate a communication-loss stop. Explain rotation as its separate approved operation, then inspect/store equipment and complete records.

Criteria: 1 reproducible inputs/calculations/component schedule; 2 clear roles/stages/contingency; 3*safe communication-loss and changed-load hold; 4 controlled landing/removal; 5 complete observations/defect reporting and honest qualification scope. Expected: no use of a generic certificate to approve an unassessed complex task.

lessons.title: SG-P01 — Task brief and qualification boundaries
lessons.body:
## SG-P01 — Task brief and qualification boundaries

Task: inspect synthetic qualification documents and a blind-landing work order. Identify the needed signaling method, assigned roles, safe route/position and unresolved prerequisites.

Criteria: 1 recognizes need for signaling; 2 distinguishes attendance, employer and third-party evaluation; 3 identifies documented method and employer applicability; 4*holds an unqualified/undocumented assignment; 5 briefs roles/stop/handoff. Expected: a hand-only record is insufficient evidence for radio duties. Record the actual reasoning and proposed next step.

lessons.title: SG-P02 — Full chart recognition and production
lessons.body:
## SG-P02 — Full chart recognition and production

Task: evaluator prompts every official chart signal in random order, first by demonstrated motion for recognition, then by named function/task for production. Use the chart during teaching, not the independent test. The evaluator uses the original illustrations to judge form and direction.

Criteria: 1 identifies function accurately; 2 correct hand/arm orientation; 3 discernible motion from operator viewpoint; 4*unambiguous stop/emergency stop and no dangerous substituted function; 5 maintains the intended signal and concludes appropriately. In addition to 8/10, every checklist entry must be independently correct in both directions after any documented changed reassessment.

Individual checklist (recognition R / production P / correction record): stop____; emergency stop____; hoist____; lower____; raise boom____; lower boom____; swing____; extend telescope____; retract telescope____; raise boom/lower load____; lower boom/raise load____; dog everything____; move slowly with action____; main select then action____; auxiliary select then action____; travel/tower travel____; crawler both tracks forward/back____; crawler one track with identified locked track____; trolley travel____. Use a model to verify resulting crawler/trolley direction; do not accept motion memorization with the wrong intended equipment response.

Supplemental recognition/production entries: one-hand telescope extension____; one-hand telescope retraction____. Teach from S03's cited manufacturer description and demonstration; require correct thumb-versus-heel chest contact and intended function. Include these two entries in the individual pass requirement rather than assuming two-handed proficiency transfers.

lessons.title: SG-P03 — Visibility, position and handoff
lessons.body:
## SG-P03 — Visibility, position and handoff

Task: choose a safe position on the marked model route, direct a short sequence, then respond to a simulated obstructed view and hand off to another designated signaler while stopped.

Criteria: 1 sees necessary route and is discernible to operator; 2 remains outside marked danger areas; 3 uses operator perspective; 4*stops before required communication is lost and prevents conflicting signalers; 5 deliberately transfers responsibility and resumes only after acknowledgment. Expected: no walking under the represented load or continuing from memory behind an obstacle.

lessons.title: SG-P04 — Ordered voice commands
lessons.body:
## SG-P04 — Ordered voice commands

Task: give independent hoist, swing, telescope and trolley commands for supplied model movements. Each has function/direction, distance or speed and function-stop. Repeat with a second named crane and changed signaler position.

Criteria: 1 correct crane/line identification; 2 correct function and operator-perspective direction; 3 intelligible distance/speed; 4*clear timely function-stop and no ambiguous recipient; 5 observes response and stops/clarifies a deliberately wrong simulated response. Expected: commands are delivered as the movement proceeds, not a rushed recital. Record actual spoken sequence.

lessons.title: SG-P05 — Radio setup and interruption
lessons.body:
## SG-P05 — Radio setup and interruption

Task: inspect/setup radios, demonstrate a dedicated signaling arrangement and hands-free reception, test at required positions, then direct a model task with a simulated transmission failure.

Criteria: 1 battery/spare/channel/device check; 2 on-site/location clarity test; 3 suitable hands-free receiving arrangement; 4*safe stop during interruption with no guessed continuation; 5 re-establishes communication and proper understood command before restart. Expected: a near-cab test alone does not cover a known dead zone. Record each location and method assessed.

lessons.title: SG-P06 — Dynamics and equipment hazards
lessons.body:
## SG-P06 — Dynamics and equipment hazards

Task: use models/diagrams to identify swing lag, boom deflection, side pull, wrong line, two-blocking risk and crane versus trolley/track travel. Choose the safe signaling response to each.

Criteria: 1 explains momentum and controlled stopping; 2 recognizes deflection/alignment effects; 3 distinguishes equipment functions/line selection; 4*stops unsafe side pull/two-blocking rather than driving to an interlock; 5 obtains responsible resolution before restart. Each named hazard requires a documented response, not one generic 'stop' for the whole station.

lessons.title: SG-P07 — Site and specialized-operation decisions
lessons.body:
## SG-P07 — Site and specialized-operation decisions

Task: inspect a synthetic site drawing with electrical boundary, pedestrian path, blind landing and a weather change. Then evaluate two-crane and proposed person-riding-load scenarios.

Criteria: 1 safe position/exclusion/escape selection; 2 identifies applicable electrical plan/roles rather than guessing voltage; 3 accounts for visibility/wind and actual limits; 4*rejects unauthorized personnel lifting or unplanned coordination; 5 identifies qualified planning and communication prerequisites. Expected: do not confuse a signalperson certificate with approval of every lift. All hazards are simulated, not introduced into an active operation.

lessons.title: SG-P08 — Integrated route, stop, landing and record
lessons.body:
## SG-P08 — Integrated route, stop, landing and record

Task: brief and direct a complete approved model or actual low-risk route using hand signals, then voice/radio. Include a controlled stop, handoff or method change while stopped, simulated unexpected response and stable landing verification.

Criteria: 1 complete prebrief/method verification; 2 accurate sustained commands with observation; 3*honors emergency stop from anyone and resolves discrepancy; 4 controlled landing without premature release or danger-area entry; 5 records assessed methods and actual setup honestly. Expected: independent application, not evaluator-led movements. A record must identify simulation versus actual equipment and does not claim crane operator competence.



---

lessons.title: VUC028 — source coverage and provenance
lessons.body:
# VUC028 — source coverage and provenance

Reviewed2026-11-17. Catalog identity is 'NCCER Rigger / Signal Person'; this package is an **original VNDRLY combined curriculum**, not an NCCER course, credential or provider endorsement. Public scope includes routine rigging, advanced rigging and signaling. The package includes those subjects rather than treating the catalog slash as permission to omit one.

lessons.title: Current primary scope sources
lessons.body:
## Current primary scope sources

- [NCCER current certification overview](https://www.nccer.org/rigger-signal-certifications/) and [2025 combined candidate handbook](https://www.nccer.org/media/2025/05/Rigger-Advanced-Rigger-and-Signalperson-Candidate-Handbook_2025.pdf). Current handbook recovered and read; separate knowledge/practical expectations and source credential boundaries identified. External administrative/eligibility language is not transplanted as a VNDRLY claim.
- [Rigger specifications, updated May2025](https://www.nccer.org/media/2024/01/EN_Rigger_Specifications.pdf): routine practices, crane knowledge and wire-rope subjects. The URL's2024 folder does not describe the document's current internal revision.
- [Advanced Rigger specifications, updated May2025](https://www.nccer.org/media/2024/01/Advanced-Rigger.pdf): advanced rigging, crane-system reasoning, plan execution and wire-rope handling. New integration instruction addresses bundles, specialized devices and crew interfaces.
- [Signal Person specifications, updated March2024](https://www.nccer.org/media/2023/03/Signal-Person-Assessment.pdf): communications, crane principles and safety, including broader crane families. Function-specific overhead reference and model tasks supplement mobile/tower instruction.

No proprietary questions or external practical fixture design are reproduced. Historical source pages contain differing administrative wording; no inference about VNDRLY authorization or external examiner eligibility is made from those discrepancies. Full licensed ASME conformity or accreditation is not asserted.

lessons.title: Instructional provenance and coverage
lessons.body:
## Instructional provenance and coverage

Previously authored VNDRLY chapters are incorporated in full, not substituted by links: R01–R14 from Rigger Level I; A01–A16 from Rigger Level II; S01–S12 from Signalperson; selected C01,C02,C03,C05,C07,C08,C09,C13,C14 from Mobile Crane instruction as crane-system awareness; B01–B08 newly authored integration. Their original worked applications and formative explanations are included. The selected C chapters do not award operator performance credit. Repeated safety concepts are intentional because the learner must apply them across roles.

| Subject | Included instruction | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Sling/hardware inspection, hitches, knots, landing | R chapters; A06–A10 | RI stations and R final |
| Weight, center, reactions, angles, rotation | A02–A05,A11–A12 | RA calculations/actual fixture; A final |
| Hoists/jacks/reeving/rolling | R13–R14,A08,A13,B04 | RI/RA, I04, final domains |
| Pipe/rebar/bundle retention | B02 | I02 and B02 questions |
| Gantry/equalizer/cantilever | A09,B03 | I03 plus applicable device cases |
| Crane bases/configurations/support/assembly | selected C chapters,B05 | I05, C/B final papers |
| Charts/deductions/limits and wire-rope distinctions | C07–C09,B04–B05 | I04/I05 and C/B papers |
| Hand/voice/radio and dynamics | S01–S12 | SG all stations/checklist; S paper |
| Overhead/derrick function context | B06 | I06 context-specific demonstrations |
| Multi-crane/personnel boundaries | A01,S10,B01/B07 | case decisions; no unauthorized live specialized task |
| Integrated plan/change/crew execution | B01,B07,B08 | I01/I07/I08 and B paper |

All59 domains have two formative and three independent final questions. Full foundation practical tasks are reproduced in foundation-practicals.md with unique prefixes; eight new integration stations complete the combined assessment. The external provider's exam counts are not represented as this program's structure.

lessons.title: Safety authority and chart references
lessons.body:
## Safety authority and chart references

The incorporated source registers are included in reference/source-registers.md, covering the cited OSHA sling, crane, signaling, electrical, jack and multiple-crane requirements and applicable primary manufacturer references. Use the actual equipment manuals and jurisdictional requirements at delivery. [OSHA1910.179](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.179) and [1910.181](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.181) supply overhead/derrick context.

[Michigan official overhead/gantry rule, Table1 page11](https://www.michigan.gov/leo/-/media/Project/Websites/leo/Documents/MIOSHA/Standards/General_Industry/GI_18/GI_18__02-02-2018.pdf) supplies the separately labeled overhead signal comparison. Its single reference page is included unchanged in reference/overhead-chart-government-reference.pdf. It is a jurisdiction-specific example, not a universal replacement for the OSHA mobile/tower chart. The course explicitly distinguishes stop forms and does not treat magnet indication as energy isolation. Official OSHA mobile/tower chart images and their white-background viewer are also included.

Actual equipment/fixture approval, evaluator competence and learner performance remain delivery evidence. No actual learner qualification, crane operation, external certification, production publication or real-company record mutation is claimed by material completion.
