**Delivery readiness:** course/version____ jurisdiction____ selected variant/model____ manufacturer procedure/revision____ facility plan/revision____ medical pathway verified by/date____ controller____ rescue staff/positions____ ratios/capacity verified____ communications/stop/recovery test results____ water/environment limits/results____ fire trainer check____ medical response/access____ hold items and resolution____ release signature/time____.

**Individual practical:** learner ID____ date____ station/condition____ equipment ID/model____ assessor____ prerequisites checked____ criterion scores 1____2____3____4____5____ total____/10 starred criteria all2 yes/no____ observed actions____ prompts/assistance____ stop/intervention____ result____ remediation____ changed reassessment condition/date/result____ learner acknowledgment____ assessor signature____.

**Water progression:** learner____ variant____ medical clearance reference/restrictions____ day-of declaration____ dry prerequisites____ condition1 plan reference/seat/exit/result____ condition2____ condition3____ additional required conditions____ rescue intervention/details____ symptoms/referral____ final scope actually demonstrated____ evaluator____. Add rows until every condition in the approved delivery plan has an individual result. Blank conditions are not passes.

**Casualty handover:** fictional patient____ event/time____ safe access____ response/breathing____ help called/time____ ventilation/CPR/AED actions and times____ bleeding/cold care____ changes____ transfer to/time____ unknowns____.

**Completion decision:** learner____ program/version____ written____/84 domain minimums____ critical misconceptions resolved____ practical station results____ variant/model/conditions____ outstanding/medical deferrals____ final decision complete/partial/not yet competent____ evaluator/date____ credential ID if earned____ actual scope/limitations____ employer travel acceptance separately verified by____. Retain records securely under the organization's applicable retention policy; restrict health and protected assessment access.


---

courses.title: VUC032 | VUC032 explained learning checks

content.title: VUC032 | VUC032 explained learning checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC032 explained learning checks
lessons.body:
# VUC032 explained learning checks

Attempt before reading the answer. Explain the safer action, correct errors using the named chapter and solve a changed example before progression. Practical demonstration remains separate.

lessons.title: D01-L1
lessons.body:
## D01-L1

A current medical holder develops painful ears before water training. Proceed?

**Answer:** Hold the affected exercise and obtain the designated medical review.

**Reason and remediation:** A new condition can change fitness; an instructor cannot override it. Revisit D01 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D01-L2
lessons.body:
## D01-L2

What does a learner stop signal do to the result?

**Answer:** It triggers safe recovery and review; unfinished work remains unfinished.

**Reason and remediation:** Safety reporting is encouraged, but it does not constitute a skill pass. Revisit D01 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D02-L1
lessons.body:
## D02-L1

Does a helmet permit walking beneath a suspended load?

**Answer:** No; stay out of the exclusion zone.

**Reason and remediation:** PPE does not remove the load hazard. Revisit D02 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D02-L2
lessons.body:
## D02-L2

What changes when an alarm interrupts a permitted task?

**Answer:** Follow the emergency plan and stop/leave as directed.

**Reason and remediation:** The permit does not override changed conditions. Revisit D02 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D03-L1
lessons.body:
## D03-L1

Your destination differs from the manifest. Board first?

**Answer:** No; resolve with dispatch before boarding.

**Reason and remediation:** Manifest accuracy supports accountability and correct transport. Revisit D03 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D03-L2
lessons.body:
## D03-L2

A loose article blows toward the aircraft. Retrieve it?

**Answer:** Stop and tell ground crew; do not chase it.

**Reason and remediation:** Rotor hazards outweigh the value of the article. Revisit D03 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D04-L1
lessons.body:
## D04-L1

A suit fits standing but blocks seated buckle access. Accept it?

**Answer:** No; resolve fit and recheck before travel.

**Reason and remediation:** Essential controls must remain reachable. Revisit D04 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D04-L2
lessons.body:
## D04-L2

Why not inflate the lifejacket inside the cabin?

**Answer:** It can obstruct movement and trap the wearer; follow the taught clearance/inflation sequence.

**Reason and remediation:** Flotation must be deployed at the appropriate stage. Revisit D04 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D05-L1
lessons.body:
## D05-L1

Does a green pressure indication alone prove CA-EBS readiness?

**Answer:** No; complete the model-specific configuration/function checks.

**Reason and remediation:** Indicated pressure does not establish the entire breathing path is usable. Revisit D05 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D05-L2
lessons.body:
## D05-L2

Can rebreather practice automatically qualify someone on CA-EBS?

**Answer:** No; teach and assess the actual variant.

**Reason and remediation:** Equipment function and deployment differ. Revisit D05 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D06-L1
lessons.body:
## D06-L1

Why rehearse release and exits on land first?

**Answer:** To resolve basic control and orientation errors before immersion.

**Reason and remediation:** Water should not be used to discover an avoidable knowledge gap. Revisit D06 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D06-L2
lessons.body:
## D06-L2

Should a learner release restraint immediately on a warning?

**Answer:** No; follow the actual emergency sequence and timing.

**Reason and remediation:** Premature release can cause injury or loss of orientation. Revisit D06 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D07-L1
lessons.body:
## D07-L1

Can this written course authorize private underwater-escape practice?

**Answer:** No; a competent purpose-designed facility and controlled rescue plan are required.

**Reason and remediation:** Uncontrolled restraint/immersion can be fatal. Revisit D07 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D07-L2
lessons.body:
## D07-L2

If a rescue team intervenes, may the attempt be silently marked independent?

**Answer:** No; record intervention and reassess after review.

**Reason and remediation:** An assisted recovery is not proof of independent performance. Revisit D07 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D08-L1
lessons.body:
## D08-L1

What is the immediate priority after cold immersion?

**Answer:** Support the airway with flotation and regain breathing control.

**Reason and remediation:** Immediate uncontrolled swimming can worsen exhaustion and breathing difficulty. Revisit D08 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D08-L2
lessons.body:
## D08-L2

Does an immersion suit guarantee survival for a fixed period?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** Condition, fit, exposure and rescue circumstances differ. Revisit D08 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D09-L1
lessons.body:
## D09-L1

May you answer present for a friend seen earlier?

**Answer:** No; report last known facts and uncertainty.

**Reason and remediation:** False accountability can delay rescue. Revisit D09 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D09-L2
lessons.body:
## D09-L2

Who controls TEMPSC launch?

**Answer:** The authorized coxswain/assigned crew under the emergency plan.

**Reason and remediation:** Passengers are not authorized to operate release mechanisms. Revisit D09 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D10-L1
lessons.body:
## D10-L1

May training water-entry height be chosen from a photograph?

**Answer:** No; use the facility-approved equipment/environment procedure.

**Reason and remediation:** Another installation does not establish safe conditions here. Revisit D10 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D10-L2
lessons.body:
## D10-L2

Why move to an assigned position after raft boarding?

**Answer:** To keep access clear and balance the raft.

**Reason and remediation:** Uncoordinated crowding can impede others and destabilize the situation. Revisit D10 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D11-L1
lessons.body:
## D11-L1

Does a portable-extinguisher lesson authorize smoke entry?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** It does not qualify fire-team operations or atmospheric protection. Revisit D11 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D11-L2
lessons.body:
## D11-L2

What if smoke threatens the escape path?

**Answer:** Withdraw and raise/maintain the alarm.

**Reason and remediation:** A small-fire attempt requires a safe exit. Revisit D11 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D12-L1
lessons.body:
## D12-L1

What should remain available during an authorized extinguisher attempt?

**Answer:** A safe escape route.

**Reason and remediation:** Fire, smoke or heat must not cut off withdrawal. Revisit D12 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D12-L2
lessons.body:
## D12-L2

Can an escape hood authorize entry to rescue a coworker?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** Escape capability is not entry/rescue capability. Revisit D12 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D13-L1
lessons.body:
## D13-L1

Should a rescuer enter dangerous water solely because they know CPR?

**Answer:** No; call capable rescue and use safe aids within competence.

**Reason and remediation:** First-aid training is not aquatic rescue qualification. Revisit D13 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D13-L2
lessons.body:
## D13-L2

Should you try to drain water from lungs before resuscitation?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** It delays effective ventilation and CPR. Revisit D13 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D14-L1
lessons.body:
## D14-L1

Can a written pass cancel a failed critical practical?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** Knowledge and demonstrated performance are separate requirements. Revisit D14 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.

lessons.title: D14-L2
lessons.body:
## D14-L2

What must a credential record about equipment?

**Answer:** The variant/model and conditions actually assessed, with limitations.

**Reason and remediation:** A generic label can overstate capability. Revisit D14 and explain the failure in the rejected approach.


---

lessons.title: VUC032 sources, limits and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC032 sources, limits and coverage

Source review: 17 November 2026. Original VNDRLY instruction, cases and assessments. No proprietary examination reproduced. The public OPITO pages establish broad product scope; the full current product specification is available by request and was not obtained. Therefore this is a complete original VNDRLY materials package within the scope stated here, **not verified clause-by-clause equivalence or OPITO accreditation**. Exact equipment procedures are controlled by the actual manufacturer and delivery facility; no invented universal valve setting, air duration, immersion depth or instructor ratio is supplied.

| Source | Inspected use and boundary |
|---|---|
| [OPITO BOSIET with CA-EBS, 5750](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/basic-offshore-safety-induction-and-emergency-training-bosiet-with-compressed-air-emergency-breathing-system-ca-ebs) | Initial offshore hazards, helicopter escape, sea survival/first aid and fire/self-rescue scope; medical and jurisdiction-specific participation controls. Current public page, not the restricted full specification. |
| [OPITO BOSIET with EBS, 5700](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/basic-offshore-safety-induction-and-emergency-training-bosiet-with-emergency-breathing-system-ebs) | Separately identifies rebreather EBS users. The program records variants rather than claiming automatic conversion. |
| [NOPSEMA pre-flight lifejacket/CA-EBS alert, 8 August 2023](https://www.nopsema.gov.au/sites/default/files/documents/Safety%20Alert%20-%20Pre-flight%20checks%20for%20life%20jackets%20and%20compressed%20air%20emergency%20breathing%20system%20%28CA-EBS%29.pdf) | Readiness case: apparent cylinder pressure did not establish correct supply configuration. Used to teach complete equipment checks, not a generic model operating procedure. |
| [FAA AIM, offshore helicopter operations](https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/publications/atpubs/aim_html/chap10_section_2.html) | Crew-controlled passenger handling and offshore operational interface. Guidance is not a substitute for actual aircraft procedures. |
| [RNLI lifejackets](https://rnli.org/water-safety/lifejackets) and [Float to Live](https://rnli.org/water-safety/float) | Flotation, initial breathing control and heat/energy conservation. Recreational advice is adapted to issued offshore equipment, never substituted for helicopter inflation procedures. |
| [RCUK 2025 adult BLS](https://www.resus.org.uk/professional-library/2025-resuscitation-guidelines/adult-basic-life-support-guidelines) | Adult manikin CPR/AED method and early emergency activation. |
| [RCUK 2025 special circumstances](https://www.resus.org.uk/professional-library/2025-resuscitation-guidelines/special-circumstances-guidelines) | Drowning respiratory priority and safe rescue boundaries. Advanced drugs/ECPR decisions are outside this lay-rescuer course. |
| [RCUK 2025 first aid](https://www.resus.org.uk/professional-library/2025-resuscitation-guidelines/first-aid-guidelines) | Scene safety, early help, care within competence, bleeding and cold-exposure response. Local emergency number and medical arrangements must be briefed. |
| [OSHA portable extinguisher use](https://www.osha.gov/etools/evacuation-plans-procedures/emergency-standards/portable-extinguishers/use) | Alarm, suitable agent, safe exit, controlled discharge and withdrawal. US workplace source used for general technique, not asserted as universal offshore jurisdiction. |

The complete eight-chapter offshore orientation foundation is physically included as `offshore-foundation.md`; its existing source register is included as `foundation-sources.md`. Those reviewed materials cover readiness, access, marine transfer, facility hazards, SEMS participation, environmental protection and emergencies. Statements that the foundation alone does not teach HUET remain accurate; D03–D10 and the supervised stations supply this program's additional survival instruction. No unrelated US clinical course is inserted into the RCUK-based drowning module.

lessons.title: Objective-to-evidence map
lessons.body:
## Objective-to-evidence map

Every D-domain has its named teaching chapter, two explained formative checks, three distinct controlled final items and a changed three-decision reassessment. IDs Dxx-L1/L2, Dxx-E1/E2/E3 and Dxx-R identify them. Instructor key stays in the private directory.

| Domain | Observable objective | Applied assessment |
|---|---|---|
| D01 | Resolve fitness changes and exercise stop rights | P01 medical/stop decision |
| D02 | Recognize barriers and act under facility emergency authority | P02 hazard/route |
| D03 | Verify passenger identity, seat briefing and controls | P03 manifest/seat |
| D04 | Inspect, fit and verify access in survival ensemble | P04 donning/reach |
| D05 | Distinguish EBS/CA-EBS and demonstrate actual system readiness | P05 dry plus applicable water conditions |
| D06 | Demonstrate brace, reference, restraint and exit in dry sequence | P06 dry rehearsal |
| D07 | Perform validated supervised escape conditions | P07 individually recorded water conditions |
| D08 | Maintain flotation/airway, conserve capability and signal | P08 pool survival |
| D09 | Account at muster and board static TEMPSC safely | P09 muster/craft |
| D10 | Board raft and cooperate with rescue interfaces | P10 raft/rescue-device demonstration |
| D11 | Decide attack versus withdrawal and choose suitable agent | P11 fire decision |
| D12 | Operate trainer extinguisher and perform controlled self-rescue | P12 discharge/escape |
| D13 | Recognize deterioration and demonstrate immediate care | P13 measured manikin/AED/cold/bleeding |
| D14 | Integrate response and issue truthful scoped records | P14 integrated decision/record |

lessons.title: Acceptance distinction
lessons.body:
## Acceptance distinction

Materials completion means these written instructional and assessment resources exist and have been author-reviewed. It does not mean a facility has been approved, a real learner has passed, current private OPITO clauses have been verified or travel permission has been granted. Those claims require their own evidence and are not fabricated in this package. The training provider must record actual facility, equipment, medical and evaluator details when delivering; blank forms are reusable evidence instruments, not pre-certified outcomes.


---

content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Offshore Safety — Survival Refresher
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Offshore Safety — Survival Refresher

Original refresher instruction, version 1.0, 17 November 2026. This course refreshes previously learned survival capabilities; it is not an accelerated first course for an untrained person. VNDRLY does not issue OPITO FOET credentials. The complete fourteen-chapter VNDRLY initial-survival teaching is physically included as a reference for correction and practice. The eight chapters below teach the refresher process, changed conditions and recurrent performance decisions.

lessons.title: R01 — Establish a real starting point
lessons.body:
## R01 — Establish a real starting point

A refresher begins with evidence of prior training and current readiness, not confidence alone. Verify identity, previous course, equipment variant, date, scope and relevant employer requirements. A card with an unreadable date or a mismatched name needs resolution. Do not replace the missing record with a colleague's recollection. If foundational training is absent or skills have deteriorated beyond the refresher's safe scope, arrange initial/re-entry training rather than force completion in the refresher timetable.

Review what has changed since the previous course: aircraft seats and exits, breathing equipment, medical condition, employer emergency procedures and the person's own experience. Repetition can hide drift. A worker who has flown hundreds of times may still have never operated the current emergency buckle. Familiarity is useful only when it produces accurate current actions.

Use the confidential medical process before practical exposure and repeat the day-of readiness question. Offshore medical fitness does not automatically settle every shallow-water compressed-air requirement. Report symptoms, recent illness, medication effects or anxiety affecting participation. The instructor refers fitness uncertainty to qualified personnel. A previous successful water exercise does not justify ignoring new symptoms.

Worked case: Omar arrives with an old rebreather certificate and says his employer now issues CA-EBS. The instructor verifies eligibility and scopes the actual equipment training; the learner is not automatically credited with the changed system. If the date is outside the applicable accepted route, the center resolves the correct initial/re-entry pathway. Practice separating three decisions: course entry, medical participation and employer travel acceptance.

lessons.title: R02 — Detect and correct equipment drift
lessons.body:
## R02 — Detect and correct equipment drift

Inspect the actual survival ensemble against its current instructions. Identify the suit, flotation system, breathing system, locator and other fitted components. Confirm size, service status, closures, strap routing and access while seated. A successful check last year is not evidence about today's item. If a hose, mouthpiece, seal or control is defective, stop its use and obtain a verified replacement.

Describe the breathing path rather than merely naming the equipment. Rebreather and compressed-air systems have different deployment and use requirements. For CA-EBS, available pressure and the correct supply configuration both matter. Finite air is for emergency escape, not extended underwater work. The unit's own instructions govern activation, clearing and recovery of a displaced mouthpiece. Practise those actions dry with the instructor before any separately approved water exercise; never experiment underwater to discover a control.

The buddy check is an additional barrier, not a transfer of all responsibility. The wearer confirms that essential controls can be reached and that the complete ensemble works together. If a strap is adjusted afterward, recheck the affected fit. If a colleague gives advice that conflicts with the unit instructions, stop and resolve it with the competent instructor.

Worked case: a worker remembers turning an old unit's control in a particular direction and starts doing the same on an unfamiliar model. Stop the assumption, identify the model and follow its procedure. On an inert trainer, demonstrate deployment with each hand as applicable, a correct seal and the instructed clearing/recovery action. Do not invent a universal control movement.

lessons.title: R03 — Restore the escape sequence before increasing difficulty
lessons.body:
## R03 — Restore the escape sequence before increasing difficulty

Brief the current trainer seat, restraint, exits and brace method. Rehearse on land until the learner independently locates the controls and explains the timing. Do not begin with inversion to discover whether the person remembers. The purpose of progression is to expose and correct errors while their consequences are controlled.

During the validated water sequence, retain orientation through the taught reference and follow the actual restraint/exit procedure. Premature release can displace the person; premature flotation inflation inside the cabin can obstruct escape. A known exit is preferable to a guessed direction toward light. The learner must be able to identify the stop/distress signal and expect immediate competent recovery if needed.

Breathing-system practice and helicopter immersion are not automatically one combined exercise. The authorized plan identifies which equipment is worn in each condition. In particular, do not add CA-EBS to an immersion sequence whose specification excludes it. The separately supervised shallow-water CA-EBS activity has its own medical, breathing, depth, rescue and recovery controls. After breathing compressed air, avoid breath-holding during ascent and follow the instructor's controlled method.

Worked case: the learner performs the first escape but releases too early on a later condition. Record the actual action, recover safely and retrain that sequence. An earlier pass cannot cover a later critical error. Practice a changed approved seat or exit condition only after readiness is restored; no surprise immersion or forced repetition.

lessons.title: R04 — Survive the period after escape
lessons.body:
## R04 — Survive the period after escape

Clearing the cabin is not the end of survival. Establish effective flotation at the correct stage, protect the airway and regain breathing control. Use the taught spray protection and signaling aids where fitted. Cold shock can disrupt breathing; frantic swimming can rapidly exhaust a survivor. Decide on a reachable refuge using the actual current, distance, equipment and rescue plan rather than an optimistic estimate.

Individual conservation and group support must preserve breathing. A posture that puts the mouth under water is unsuitable even if it resembles a diagram. Group arrangements should avoid entanglement and maintain awareness of each person's condition. Alert the rescue team if someone deteriorates. Do not improvise tethers or remove flotation to swim faster.

Approach and board the raft using the taught method. Coordinate assistance, avoid lines and move to a balanced position that leaves boarding space. Follow the assigned survivor/crew lead for canopy, mooring and equipment management. Do not cut lines or operate devices because they look familiar. At recovery, follow the rescue crew's instructions for the actual device, avoiding unapproved attachments or live lifting experiments.

Worked case: a fatigued survivor reaches the raft but cannot climb independently. The group coordinates the demonstrated assistance without pulling only on a loose lifejacket. The assessor records the assistance and checks each learner's own actions. Practice includes both a stable individual response and a group whose member needs help; it does not include deliberately inducing cold shock.

lessons.title: R05 — Refresh the decision to fight or leave
lessons.body:
## R05 — Refresh the decision to fight or leave

The most important firefighting decision may be not to attack. Raise the alarm, identify an exit and assess whether the fire is within the worker's training and authorization. A small developing fire with a suitable extinguisher and protected escape path differs from a pressurized hydrocarbon fire or smoke-filled compartment. If the fire spreads, the route becomes threatened or the first attempt is ineffective, withdraw promptly.

Read current equipment labels. A workplace may use a different fire-class convention from the learner's previous site. Select by fuel, electrical hazard and actual agent suitability rather than color or a remembered letter. Understand the method for each available trainer type and its limitations. CO2 does not remove the hazards of an enclosed atmosphere; water is not a universal choice. Specialist fuel isolation is not granted by a refresher certificate.

Under controlled trainer conditions, demonstrate safe position, effective discharge and withdrawal. Keep the escape route available. After visible flame is gone, remain alert for re-ignition, report the event and replace/replenish used equipment through the proper process. A partially used extinguisher must not quietly return to service as if full.

Worked case: the learner starts an appropriate simulated incipient-fire response, then receives a cue that smoke now threatens the exit. The correct performance is withdrawal, not finishing the extinguisher because the exercise originally asked for discharge. Practice responding to a changing condition rather than demonstrating a fixed movement sequence regardless of danger.

lessons.title: R06 — Escape with limited information
lessons.body:
## R06 — Escape with limited information

Low visibility removes the visual cues on which routine navigation depends. Before an emergency, know the route, alternative and muster destination. During escape use the taught safe reference technique, communicate as briefed and move without creating a collision or losing the route. Do not assume a route is safe because it was open on the last visit.

Use the exact escape device within its limitations. A filter does not create oxygen; an escape device does not authorize entry for rescue or extended work. Donning and seal checks must be rehearsed in safe conditions. An unsuitable or failed device cannot be corrected by holding a hand over a gap and continuing into danger.

In a group exercise, maintain the taught communication and contact arrangement without dangerous entanglement. The lead does not race ahead, and the last person does not silently disappear. Report at muster and identify a missing person from facts, not guesses. If a route is blocked, use the briefed safe alternative or designated refuge/communication plan. Training must remain controlled and recoverable even when learner visibility is obscured.

Worked case: the group emerges with one fewer person than expected. Do not mark the drill complete and search independently in the simulated hazard. Report the discrepancy and last known information so the exercise controller uses the established recovery plan. Practice both individual and group escape, with an observer able to account for every participant throughout.

lessons.title: R07 — Refresh first aid by measured performance
lessons.body:
## R07 — Refresh first aid by measured performance

Recall is not enough for a physical skill such as CPR. Use a feedback manikin to identify shallow compressions, excessive rate, incomplete recoil or over-ventilation. Correct the actual error, then repeat independently. A rescuer who says the right numbers but produces ineffective compressions has a performance gap. The reference chapter D13 gives this package's RCUK-based adult drowning and CPR method; the instructor confirms the local emergency arrangements before class.

Make access safe and summon help early. A first aider does not enter a dangerous atmosphere or water beyond their rescue competence. For an unresponsive casualty, activate emergency help and assess breathing promptly; abnormal gasps require the arrest response. Provide the taught ventilation/CPR sequence and use the AED with safe preparation and clear checks. Do not interrupt care to try to drain water from lungs or debate an uncertain diagnosis.

A rescued survivor who is breathing still needs monitoring and appropriate medical assessment. Protect against further heat loss, handle carefully and report deterioration. Control severe bleeding with the trained method and give a factual handover. A responsive person who becomes confused or breathless is not simply tired. The emergency team needs observations, times and changes, not a guess that the person is fine.

Worked case: the first manikin attempt is too shallow even though the learner passed a course years ago. The instructor coaches correct body position and depth, then observes a new independent two-minute segment and records the feedback. Practice also includes a breathing casualty whose condition changes, so the learner must reassess rather than remain in the first response mode.

lessons.title: R08 — Close gaps without overstating renewal
lessons.body:
## R08 — Close gaps without overstating renewal

A refresher should finish with an evidence-based decision: demonstrated current capability in the stated scope, partial completion with named outstanding work, or not yet competent. The assessor records the actual equipment variant and exercise conditions. One generic tick beside 'water' cannot establish which escape, flotation or breathing actions were observed.

Keep the first attempt, the specific correction and the new observation. If an action required prompting, record it. If rescue intervention was necessary, do not relabel it independent success. If a medical restriction prevented a practical, do not substitute a written answer and issue the same record as someone who completed it. Honest limits protect the learner and the employer who must decide travel readiness.

The next review date comes from the applicable program/employer/authority rules, not an invented extension. A VNDRLY refresher does not renew an OPITO certificate. New equipment or a significant change in health may require review before the calendar date. Assign a clear follow-up owner and record the travel restriction where necessary so an unfinished requirement is not lost between training and dispatch.

Worked case: all classroom and fire work is complete, but an underwater condition remains unobserved. The result names that outstanding condition, schedules the correct safe reassessment and avoids a full-scope credential. Practice writing a concise accurate record that a dispatcher can understand without mistaking participation for completion.


---

lessons.title: VUC033 instructor and practical packet
lessons.body: # VUC033 instructor and practical packet

lessons.title: Entry and scope
lessons.body:
## Entry and scope

This is a VNDRLY refresher for previously trained offshore personnel. Verify a documented initial-survival or accepted refresher background, relevant equipment scope, date, identity and current participation fitness. If records are missing, expired under the applicable acceptance rules or the learner lacks foundational capability, resolve the appropriate initial/re-entry pathway. Do not let a sponsor's desired travel date override the decision. The public OPITO refresher has its own prerequisite rules; VNDRLY completion does not renew an OPITO certificate.

The included full initial-survival reference supplies procedures and explanations for remediation. It is not a requirement to reteach every foundation chapter during a refresher. Start with diagnosis, teach changed or weak skills, demonstrate, allow coached practice, then observe independent performance. No high-risk diagnostic attempt before dry prerequisites.

Plan **16 instructional hours** excluding breaks: readiness and changed equipment R01–R02, 2 hours; escape and post-escape survival R03–R04, 7 hours; fire and self-rescue R05–R06, 4 hours; first aid R07, 2 hours; final assessment/record R08, 1 hour. Add remedial time. This is VNDRLY's allocation, not a representation of OPITO's duration. Schedule adequate recovery between demanding exercises; do not rush immersion to preserve the timetable.

lessons.title: Delivery safeguards and instructor resources
lessons.body:
## Delivery safeguards and instructor resources

Use qualified activity-specific instructors and a purpose-designed survival facility. Establish a controller, immediate water rescue personnel, competent HUET operation/recovery staff, breathing-system competence, fire-training competence and current first-aid instructor capability. The facility's validated plan sets staffing, positions, capacity, water/environment limits and emergency medical response. Record actual assignments; one person cannot perform incompatible simultaneous roles. Missing rescue cover means no water activity.

Before practicals, verify confidential medical clearance and day-of changes, model-specific manufacturer instructions, serviced/hygienic equipment, ensemble compatibility, functional trainer stops/recovery, communications and response access. Dry instruction precedes water. Each learner knows the stop signal; stop for distress, pain, breathing difficulty, unexpected equipment behavior or loss of a control. Recover safely and review before any restart. No surprise inversion, intentional air deprivation, breath-hold contest or forced participation.

Keep the breathing-system water exercise separate from helicopter conditions where that system is excluded. The public OPITO-authored FOET document specifically differentiates these exercise configurations; do not add CA-EBS to every condition merely because the overall course title names it. Use the current approved facility plan for the exact variant. A historical/public document is a planning reference, not permission to ignore updated instructions. Current model-specific clearing and mouthpiece recovery are taught and assessed with competent supervision, never improvised.

Use an engineered extinguisher trainer with competent staff and emergency shutoff. Low-visibility escape is in a monitored recoverable environment with non-toxic simulation and unlocked emergency recovery access. Use manikins and AED trainers for first aid. No live aircraft operation, uncontrolled sea entry, survival-craft launch, real smoke exposure or untrained rescue is authorized.

lessons.title: Assessment policy
lessons.body:
## Assessment policy

Each P-station has five criteria scored 0 unsafe/absent, 1 safe but prompted/incomplete, 2 independently correct. Pass 8/10 and every starred criterion2. Where several conditions are listed, score each condition separately; one overall score cannot hide a failed critical condition. An unsafe action stops the attempt. Retrain the specific gap and use the changed reassessment under the validated safe plan; preserve the original result and assistance.

Written final:24 short-answer questions,45 minutes,48points. Pass 39/48 and at least4/6 in every R-domain; all critical misconceptions resolved. Final key and changed retakes are private. Completion requires both written and all applicable practical conditions. Record actual EBS/CA-EBS variant; no automatic conversion. A medical deferral remains outstanding. Issue only a VNDRLY scoped record after completion, never an OPITO renewal or unverified carrier acceptance.

lessons.title: P01 — Entry, change and readiness review
lessons.body:
## P01 — Entry, change and readiness review

Equipment: fictional prior records, changed-equipment notice, confidential fitness cards and center contact sheet. Learner distinguishes prior training, participation clearance and destination acceptance. Give an unreadable expiry or new symptom; require a hold and correct resolution route.

Criteria: verifies identity/scope/date; identifies change since training; *does not assume medical fitness; *holds unresolved prerequisites; protects confidential information. Reassessment: valid record but newly incompatible equipment scope. Expected result: resolve training/acceptance before exposure rather than issue a generic renewal.

lessons.title: P02 — Current ensemble and breathing system
lessons.body:
## P02 — Current ensemble and breathing system

Equipment: current suit/flotation/selected EBS trainer, official model instructions and a clearly segregated defect sample. Teach inspection, fit, seated reach, deployment and the unit-specific clearing/recovery method dry. Observe each applicable hand/condition. For the CA-EBS in-water component, use separately approved shallow-water conditions after medical clearance and dry prerequisites; record them individually.

Criteria: rejects defects and identifies variant; *completes actual readiness configuration; *fits and accesses controls correctly; demonstrates prescribed deployment/clearing/recovery; *follows breathing/stop/recovery controls in water. Changed attempt: unfamiliar model and a dry scenario card indicating pressure but uncertain supply configuration. Do not create a real surprise failure. Dry success does not pass an unperformed water condition.

lessons.title: P03 — Recurrent helicopter escape
lessons.body:
## P03 — Recurrent helicopter escape

Equipment: validated HUET trainer, ensemble prescribed for each condition, controller and rescue team. Refresh brace/control/reference sequence on land. Record dry emergency preparation, nominated exit and every required partial-submersion/inversion/exit-operation condition in the facility's current refresher plan. Clearly state equipment worn for each.

Criteria: *correct orientation/reference; *correct restraint/exit timing; *complies with condition-specific breathing-equipment rule; clears without premature flotation; reaches designated safe recovery point. Assess every condition individually. Reassessment: another approved seat/exit after review, not a surprise inversion. Rescue intervention or an unseen critical action prevents credit for that attempt.

lessons.title: P04 — Flotation, raft and recovery
lessons.body:
## P04 — Flotation, raft and recovery

Equipment: controlled pool/rescue cover, approved flotation/suit, raft and inert ground-level rescue-device trainer. Observe individual airway/flotation, taught group survival, water-to-raft boarding and coordinated help. Any authorized dry aircraft-to-raft transition uses the facility's isolated trainer procedure. No live winching credit from a ground demonstration.

Criteria: *maintains airway/effective flotation; chooses feasible refuge; avoids entanglement while supporting group; *boards/assists without displacing life-support equipment; follows actual recovery-device instructions. Changed attempt: fatigued group member and shifted boarding position. No deliberate cold shock or unsupervised incapacitation simulation.

lessons.title: P05 — Fire response and discharge
lessons.body:
## P05 — Fire response and discharge

Equipment: labeled training extinguishers representing the site's agent types, engineered trainer and deteriorating-condition cards. Demonstrate the relevant controls for each type; learner selects correctly and operates each required trainer. Include an attack-inappropriate scenario as well as an authorized incipient-fire scenario.

Criteria: *raises alarm; selects suitable agent; *preserves escape/withdraws on deterioration; operates effectively within trainer instructions; reports/replenishes used equipment. Record each agent type and result. Changed attempt: initially safe fire response changes when smoke threatens the exit. Correct response is withdrawal, even if discharge was the original objective.

lessons.title: P06 — Individual and group self-rescue
lessons.body:
## P06 — Individual and group self-rescue

Equipment: escape-device trainers and monitored non-toxic low-visibility environment with safe emergency access. Brief route, alternate, communication and stop method. Independently observe individual reduced-visibility, individual obscured-visibility and small-group obscured-visibility/muster conditions under the approved plan.

Criteria: *device within correct scope/fit; maintains taught route reference; *uses safe alternative when needed; keeps group communication/accountability; reports at muster accurately. Reassessment: primary route blocked with a known safe alternate. Controller retains observation and immediate recovery capability despite learner visibility restrictions.

lessons.title: P07 — Measured emergency first aid
lessons.body:
## P07 — Measured emergency first aid

Equipment: feedback adult manikin, barrier trainer, AED trainer, insulation and handover form. Use the included D13 clinical method with current local emergency arrangements. Observe independent resuscitation segment and separate cold/bleeding/deterioration case. No live compressions or shocks on people.

Criteria: *safe access/early help; *recognizes abnormal breathing and initiates correct sequence; achieves measured CPR/ventilation quality; *uses AED clear checks and resumes care; monitors/protects casualty and gives factual handover. Record rate/depth/recoil/ventilation observations and assistance. Reassessment: initially breathing casualty becomes unresponsive with gasps. Do not award a pass for merely reciting the algorithm.

lessons.title: P08 — Renewal decision and gap closure
lessons.body:
## P08 — Renewal decision and gap closure

Equipment: fictional individual station results, written score, equipment scope and medical deferral. Learner completes a scoped completion decision and handover to dispatch. One case has a written pass but a critical practical failure.

Criteria: reconciles all condition results; *does not average away a critical failure; documents specific remediation/changed reassessment; *does not issue external renewal or unperformed scope; identifies follow-up owner and travel limitation. Reassessment: equipment conversion incomplete although other domains pass.

lessons.title: Reusable forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable forms

**Instructor readiness:** course/version____ jurisdiction____ prior-entry rule and verification____ medical route____ day-of review____ variant/model____ manufacturer instructions/revision____ facility plan/revision____ staff/roles/rescue positions____ environmental limits/results____ equipment service/hygiene____ stop/recovery/communication test____ emergency medical access____ holds/resolution____ controller/time____.

**Individual station/condition:** learner____ station____ condition/seat/exit____ model/equipment configuration____ assessor/date____ prerequisites____ scores1____2____3____4____5____ total____/10 all starred2 yes/no____ observed actions____ assistance____ rescue/stop____ result____ targeted instruction____ changed condition____ reassessment observations/result____ signatures____. Add a row for each condition and agent type; blank rows are not passes.

**Gap and action:** prior scope____ change found____ risk/affected capability____ hold____ correction owner____ evidence needed____ due/review____ independent reassessment____ accepted by____.

**First-aid performance:** scenario____ recognition/help time____ initial sequence____ compression rate/depth/recoil feedback____ ventilation____ AED clear checks/resumption____ deterioration response____ factual handover____ remediation____ independent retest____.

**Completion:** learner____ program/version____ prior record verified____ final____/48 every domain>=4/6____ all critical decisions resolved____ every required practical condition passed____ actual variant/model/conditions____ outstanding restrictions____ complete/partial/not yet competent____ evaluator/date____ record identifier____ employer travel acceptance separate____. Retain first attempts and keys securely under the applicable policy. Do not expose clinical details or protected exam answers to ordinary learners.


---

lessons.title: VUC033 explained formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC033 explained formative checks

Attempt before reading answers. Correct errors using the indicated refresher chapter and included reference. Explain why the unsafe alternative fails and practise a changed case.

lessons.title: R01-L1
lessons.body:
## R01-L1

Does long offshore experience replace an unreadable prior training record?

**Answer:** No; verify the actual scope/date/identity before selecting the pathway.

**Reason/remediation:** Experience does not prove the required prior qualification. Revisit R01 before progression.

lessons.title: R01-L2
lessons.body:
## R01-L2

What does a new health symptom change?

**Answer:** It requires participation review before exposure.

**Reason/remediation:** Past successful training does not establish current fitness. Revisit R01 before progression.

lessons.title: R02-L1
lessons.body:
## R02-L1

Why repeat a buddy check after altering straps?

**Answer:** The inspected configuration changed.

**Reason/remediation:** Correct fit/access must be re-established. Revisit R02 before progression.

lessons.title: R02-L2
lessons.body:
## R02-L2

Should you experiment underwater to find an unfamiliar purge control?

**Answer:** No; learn the actual model method dry first.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncontrolled discovery creates breathing risk. Revisit R02 before progression.

lessons.title: R03-L1
lessons.body:
## R03-L1

Should immersion begin before a reliable dry release demonstration?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Correct control sequence must be established first. Revisit R03 before progression.

lessons.title: R03-L2
lessons.body:
## R03-L2

Can CA-EBS be added to every immersion condition because it is in the course title?

**Answer:** No; follow each approved condition’s equipment configuration.

**Reason/remediation:** Some escape conditions exclude it and separate breathing exercises have their own controls. Revisit R03 before progression.

lessons.title: R04-L1
lessons.body:
## R04-L1

What remains after leaving the cabin?

**Answer:** Effective flotation/airway, breathing control, feasible refuge and rescue coordination.

**Reason/remediation:** Escape alone does not end the exposure. Revisit R04 before progression.

lessons.title: R04-L2
lessons.body:
## R04-L2

Can a helper pull only on a loose lifejacket to board a survivor?

**Answer:** No; use the demonstrated coordinated assistance.

**Reason/remediation:** Pulling may displace flotation and threaten the airway. Revisit R04 before progression.

lessons.title: R05-L1
lessons.body:
## R05-L1

When does an initially suitable fire attempt become a withdrawal?

**Answer:** When smoke/fire threatens escape, conditions exceed capability or the attempt is ineffective.

**Reason/remediation:** The decision must follow changing conditions. Revisit R05 before progression.

lessons.title: R05-L2
lessons.body:
## R05-L2

Does an extinguisher’s color alone establish suitability?

**Answer:** No; read actual agent/fuel/electrical markings.

**Reason/remediation:** Markings and classification conventions differ. Revisit R05 before progression.

lessons.title: R06-L1
lessons.body:
## R06-L1

Can a filter hood supply oxygen in an oxygen-deficient area?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Filtering and supplying breathable atmosphere are different functions. Revisit R06 before progression.

lessons.title: R06-L2
lessons.body:
## R06-L2

Does the first person reaching muster prove the group escaped?

**Answer:** No; account for every person accurately.

**Reason/remediation:** Group completion requires individual accountability. Revisit R06 before progression.

lessons.title: R07-L1
lessons.body:
## R07-L1

Does reciting CPR depth prove effective compressions?

**Answer:** No; observe measured manikin performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Physical output may differ from stated knowledge. Revisit R07 before progression.

lessons.title: R07-L2
lessons.body:
## R07-L2

Can an initially responsive drowning survivor deteriorate?

**Answer:** Yes; monitor, seek medical help and reassess changes.

**Reason/remediation:** Initial conversation is not proof of recovery. Revisit R07 before progression.

lessons.title: R08-L1
lessons.body:
## R08-L1

Can a medically deferred practical be replaced by a written answer for full completion?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The unperformed skill remains outstanding. Revisit R08 before progression.

lessons.title: R08-L2
lessons.body:
## R08-L2

Does VNDRLY renewal extend an OPITO certificate?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** External credential rules and issuer authority remain separate. Revisit R08 before progression.


---

lessons.title: VUC033 source and objective review
lessons.body:
# VUC033 source and objective review

Inspected 17 November 2026. Original VNDRLY recurrent instruction. Public benchmark scope is helicopter emergency performance, fire/self-rescue and first aid. No external credential renewal or proprietary examination is supplied.

- [OPITO FOET with CA-EBS,5850](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/further-offshore-emergency-training-foet-with-compressed-air-emergency-breathing-system-ca-ebs): current public scope, prerequisites, medical participation and variant. OPITO requires its specified in-date prior training; a VNDRLY card is not asserted to satisfy that issuer's entry rule.
- [OPITO FOET with EBS](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/further-offshore-emergency-training-foet-with-emergency-breathing-system-ebs): distinct rebreather variant. No automatic equipment conversion claimed.
- [OPITO-authored FOET CA-EBS product document hosted by Fleetwood Nautical](https://fleetwoodnautical.blackpool.ac.uk/sites/default/files/documents/FOET%20with%20Compressed%20Air%20Emergency%20Breathing%20System%20%28CA-EBS%29%20Product%20Spec%20%285%29.pdf): public technical reference inspected for unit structure and separation of helicopter conditions from additional shallow-water breathing practice. It excludes CA-EBS from specified helicopter/water conditions. Its continuing currency against the latest restricted specification is not certified here. Use current approved facility/model instructions for actual delivery.
- The included `reference-sources.md` preserves the reviewed initial-survival source register: NOPSEMA equipment-readiness alert, FAA passenger management, RNLI flotation, RCUK2025 adult/drowning/first-aid methods and OSHA extinguisher instruction. The entire initial-survival teaching is copied into `survival-reference.md`; no dangling lesson link substitutes for instruction.
