Inspection identifies a condition; engineering and the governing repair process determine an acceptable solution. Separate repair, alteration and rerating according to the applicable code. A change described as 'maintenance' may still change design conditions or pressure-boundary configuration. Identify jurisdictional and authorized-inspector involvement before work starts.

A butt-welded insert replaces an affected section and requires controlled removal geometry, material, fit-up, welding, examination and testing. External weld buildup for internal thinning requires an approved analysis of remaining metal and welding effects. Overlay or clad restoration must address both structural and corrosion-resistant functions. A fillet-welded patch introduces load-transfer and crevice considerations and must not be assumed equivalent to an insert.

Flaw excavation and weld repair require confirmation of flaw removal and acceptable remaining geometry before welding. Flange repair must preserve required dimensions, sealing function and material condition. Shell-and-tube exchanger repairs require review of pressure boundaries, differential pressure and thermal function. Each selected method needs its applicable PCC-2 article and governing in-service requirements; a method title alone is not a repair procedure.

**Worked case.** A contractor proposes covering an uncharacterized crack with a patch. This may conceal an active flaw while adding restraint and stress. Hold the repair, characterize the flaw and obtain an approved design and examination plan. A successful leak test alone would not establish that the concealed crack is acceptable.

**Practice.** Compare insert, buildup and patch options for a synthetic thinning area. State the information needed to select among them, required hold points and the evidence that would reject each option.

### Turn a repair drawing into measurable hold points

Separate dimensions established before removal, during fit-up and after finishing. Once a damaged section is removed, some baseline evidence cannot be recovered. Record the original shape, mapped defect extent, nearby welds and attachments, and reference coordinates before cutting. During fit-up, compare the actual part with the approved detail, not a remembered nominal dimension. After finishing, measure what remains rather than reporting only the amount deposited or machined.

**Original dimensional-control case.** A fictional approved repair drawing requires finished thickness at least 12.0 mm at every marked grid point and a smooth transition within the drawing's specified contour envelope. Deposited thickness is 13.5 mm, but final grinding leaves one point at 11.8 mm. The weld initially contained enough metal; the finished condition nevertheless fails the supplied minimum by 0.2 mm. Do not average the thin point with 12.6 mm readings. Mark its location and obtain an approved correction or technical disposition. These are exercise drawing values, not PCC-2 default limits.

**Inspection-plan exercise.** Build a six-column table: hold point, required record, measured result, acceptance-source revision, disposition and release signature. Add rows for original damage map, removal boundary, replacement identity, fit-up, welding record, final geometry, NDE and required test. A row must not say “pass” when its record is absent. Different responsible parties may sign different stages; a final signature does not retroactively establish a missing observation.

**Changed case.** Finished thickness passes, but the insert interferes with an internal tray support. The mechanical-integrity calculation and internal function are separate requirements. Resolve the actual geometry and attachment effects before closeout. A pressure-boundary repair cannot be accepted as a complete equipment restoration while a necessary internal component remains unusable.

lessons.title: V22 — Control special welding and repair verification
lessons.body:
## V22 — Control special welding and repair verification

In-service welding and hot tapping introduce burn-through, cracking, ignition and process hazards. They require specialized engineering, procedures, qualified personnel and operating controls. This course does not authorize a learner to perform either operation. Inspection review must verify that remaining thickness, material, process conditions, heat removal, weld procedure and emergency arrangements were evaluated by the authorized team.

Cr-Mo repairs require attention to material identity, service degradation, weld consumables, heat treatment and properties. Alternatives to PWHT are not a convenience waiver: applicability, procedure qualification, examination and approval must be established under the relevant provisions. A repair crew cannot substitute a heating blanket schedule from a previous unrelated job.

Develop an inspection and test plan with hold points: original condition documented; material accepted; excavation examined; fit-up accepted; qualifications verified; welding variables recorded; heat treatment reviewed; final NDE accepted; required pressure/tightness test completed or approved alternative justified; protective systems restored; final report approved. NDE in lieu of pressure testing is a controlled code decision, not an automatic trade of 'more UT' for an inconvenient test.

**Worked case.** Final NDE passes, but the heat-treatment chart cannot be linked to the repaired vessel. The repair is not ready for release. Recover traceability and evaluate actual compliance; do not create a retrospective chart. Record the missing evidence and authorized disposition.

**Practice.** Write a repair release checklist that separates completed work, accepted evidence and outstanding conditions. Include a place for the inspector's limitations and the responsible operating-release authority.

lessons.title: V23 — Recognize design checks beyond simple thickness
lessons.body:
## V23 — Recognize design checks beyond simple thickness

External pressure can cause instability even when internal-pressure thickness is adequate. Vacuum can arise during draining, cooling or condensation. Shell geometry, unsupported length, stiffening and material properties matter. Do not use the internal-pressure equation with a negative pressure to assess buckling. Obtain the applicable external-pressure evaluation.

Openings remove load-carrying material and create local stress. Nozzle reinforcement evaluation considers geometry, available reinforcement and applicable limits. Weld dimensions and attachment details matter. For an equal-leg fillet weld, the theoretical throat is approximately 0.707 times leg size; this geometric relationship does not establish that the weld size meets the governing design requirement.

**Worked case.** A drawing specifies a 6 mm equal-leg fillet. Its theoretical throat is about 4.24 mm. An inspector measures a 4 mm leg and records '4 mm throat acceptable.' The record confuses two dimensions. A 4 mm leg has theoretical throat about 2.83 mm. Compare the actual geometry against the approved detail and disposition the discrepancy.

Nozzle loads, supports, thermal expansion and differential pressure can control fitness. A vessel with a calculated internal-pressure margin may still be unfit because of settlement, external loads or fatigue. Report those conditions for the correct analysis rather than forcing every finding into a corrosion spreadsheet.

**Practice.** Identify the additional engineering evaluations needed after adding a larger nozzle, changing to vacuum service or increasing thermal cycling. Explain why a thickness survey alone cannot approve these changes.

lessons.title: V24 — Integrate findings and control return to service
lessons.body:
## V24 — Integrate findings and control return to service

An inspection report must let a qualified reviewer reconstruct what was examined, what was found and why the disposition follows. Include equipment and chamber identity, basis documents, operating history, methods and coverage, personnel/procedures, measurements, indication maps, calculations, assumptions, limitations, repairs, protection review, due dates and approvals. Attach original records rather than replacing them with a summary that hides exceptions.

Rerating requires the applicable engineering calculations, condition assessment, protection changes, documentation and authorization. It does not consist of editing a spreadsheet or changing a relief setting. Consider the weakest component, temperature limits, other loads, service mechanisms and jurisdictional requirements. Preserve the original rating history and approved change basis.

**Integrated case.** Vessel V-410 has a shell calculation supporting 238.80 psi after future allowance, a lower head permitting 220 psi locally thirty feet below the pressure reference, and an upper component permitting 205 psi. The pressure-only reference limit is 205 psi. However, a crack-like weld indication remains unresolved and the installed relief discharge is obstructed. The correct report does not release the vessel at 205 psi. It records that the numerical pressure calculation is only one part of fitness and requires disposition of both unresolved conditions before authorized operation.

Closeout includes repair acceptance, removal of temporary equipment, restored isolation/protection arrangements, required operating instructions, approved limits and inspection schedule. Track each recommendation to an owner and due date. A signed report is not a substitute for completing the actions it requires.

**Practice.** Produce a final report for the integrated case with separate headings for established facts, calculations, unresolved findings, required actions and release decision. State the credential boundary: successfully completing this VNDRLY course demonstrates assessed learning within its documented scope, not API certification or authority to release real equipment independently.


---

lessons.title: VUC035 delivery and applied assessment
lessons.body: # VUC035 delivery and applied assessment

lessons.title: Audience and entry readiness
lessons.body:
## Audience and entry readiness

For personnel developing pressure-vessel inspection knowledge who can read technical drawings, use coherent units and perform algebra. Before enrolment, administer the V08–V13 worked calculations as an unscored diagnostic with changed values. Provide arithmetic/unit remediation before the calculation sessions. Record prior experience; do not infer API eligibility from attendance. API's education/experience requirements and examination are separate.

Instructor: documented pressure-equipment inspection experience, familiarity with the applicable codes and ability to explain the supplied calculations and inspection limitations. Obtain a qualified welding/NDE/materials specialist for questions beyond the instructor's competence. Practical work here uses de-energized training pieces, records and simulations. No live pressure testing, entry, radiography, welding, hot tapping or exposure to operating equipment is authorized by this packet.

lessons.title: Planned 65.25 instructional hours
lessons.body:
## Planned 65.25 instructional hours

| Block | Hours | Work product |
|---|---:|---|
| V01–V06 basis, access, mechanisms, visual | 10 | Basis sheet, M01–M15 mechanism decisions, inspection findings |
| V07–V13 metrology and calculations | 12 | Traceable readings, rates, component/reference limits |
| V14–V20 toughness, welding, NDE, PMI, relief | 10 | Qualification and examination review worksheets |
| V21–V24 repair and disposition | 6 | Repair plan and integrated report |
| Applied station rotations and corrections | 8 | Individual scored evidence at all 24 stations |
| Technical decision workshops T01–T10 | 9.25 | Toughness, nozzle dimensions, welding, protection, NDE, PMI and exchanger decisions |
| Repair decision cases R01–R14 | 6 | Individual repair selection and verification records |
| Controlled final and individual feedback | 4 | Final result and remediation plan |

Breaks excluded. Extend delivery where diagnostic results or practical performance require it; do not compress instruction to meet the schedule. Guided station work begins during the teaching blocks and is assessed during rotations. The planned hours do not claim parity with an external provider's required duration.

lessons.title: Delivery resources
lessons.body:
## Delivery resources

Provide the coursebook, case-packet.md, worked-application-labs.md, damage-mechanism-cases.md, blank forms below, calculator, ruler, vessel/nozzle drawings, synthetic data records, inert coupons, visual photographs with scale, a thickness instrument and suitable reference blocks if conducting hands-on measurement. If equipment is unavailable, record the metrology station as simulation only; do not issue a hands-on measurement endorsement. No consumer pressure container may be pressurized for instruction.

For actual code-lookup exercises, provide authorized controlled copies of the API/ASME editions identified in sources-and-coverage.md. The course's synthetic rules are deliberately labeled and must never replace those standards. Instructor records must identify the edition, clause and resulting decision. The source review does not claim every proprietary clause has been independently verified by the author. Consequently external-equivalence certification remains unestablished; that limitation must appear in the course record and any marketing description.

lessons.title: Common scoring and critical gates
lessons.body:
## Common scoring and critical gates

Each station has five observable criteria scored 0 = absent/wrong, 1 = safe but incomplete, 2 = correct with supporting evidence. Pass at least 8/10 and every starred criterion at 2. A critical error cannot be offset by total points. Stop a real unsafe action immediately. Explain the error, assign the relevant chapter and a changed case, then reassess independently. Retain the first result, correction and reassessment; never overwrite a failed attempt.

Common critical errors: authorizing unsafe access, inventing evidence, releasing unresolved pressure-boundary damage, confusing component/reference pressure, unsupported qualification credit, or representing VNDRLY completion as API authorization. Assessors accept technically defensible alternatives when the learner states assumptions and supporting criteria. They may not relax a safety gate because a learner is experienced.

lessons.title: P01 — Equipment identity and basis
lessons.body:
## P01 — Equipment identity and basis

Supply two synthetic records: V-410 register 250 psi/400°F; plate 225 psi/400°F; rerating approval absent. Task: prepare basis and disposition. Criteria: match equipment/chamber; identify conflicting pressures; list governing records; *hold unsupported rerating; assign responsible resolution and trace affected calculations. Changed case: plate agrees but material record belongs to a different serial number.

lessons.title: P02 — Access and coverage
lessons.body:
## P02 — Access and coverage

Supply a vessel drawing with internal baffle, insulated lower head and unisolated nitrogen connection. Task: mark safe-access and inspection-coverage holds. Criteria: identify energy/atmosphere hazards; *reject entry without approved controls; map expected mechanisms; identify inaccessible surfaces; distinguish access approval from technical alternative-inspection approval. Changed case: entry is safe but baffle obscures the vulnerable weld.

lessons.title: P03 — Metal-loss mechanisms
lessons.body:
## P03 — Metal-loss mechanisms

Supply photographs/descriptions of wet insulation at a support, directional nozzle wear and a condensate low point. Task: plan examination. Criteria: match plausible mechanisms without overdiagnosis; request chemistry/flow history; identify vulnerable locations; select method/coverage; *avoid extrapolating one clean point to the whole surface. Changed case: external appearance is sound but a leaking jacketing seam is documented.

lessons.title: P04 — Cracking and hydrogen damage
lessons.body:
## P04 — Cracking and hydrogen damage

Supply acceptable thickness with linear amine-service weld indications. Task: write an escalation note. Criteria: distinguish cracking from thinning; identify relevant service/stress information; select qualified characterization; *reject remaining-life calculation as sole clearance; preserve evidence and authorize neither grinding nor continued service. Changed case: wet-H2S blisters with suspected internal linking.

lessons.title: P05 — High-temperature mechanism review
lessons.body:
## P05 — High-temperature mechanism review

Supply carbon-steel exchanger history with hydrogen service and past temperature excursions. Task: identify assessment inputs. Criteria: distinguish HTHA from metal loss; collect actual historical conditions; verify material; identify examination capability limits; *avoid declaring safe from current low temperature alone. Changed case: stable temperature but a replacement component has uncertain alloy identity.

lessons.title: P06 — Visual finding quality
lessons.body:
## P06 — Visual finding quality

Supply an inert vessel sketch and three annotated photographs: saddle coating crack, nozzle displacement and liner damage. Task: produce reproducible findings. Criteria: datum/location; scaled evidence; morphology/extent; limitations; *refer deformation/load and liner/base-metal questions rather than declaring thickness-only fitness. Changed case: inaccessible attachment weld.

lessons.title: P07 — Thickness setup and drift
lessons.body:
## P07 — Thickness setup and drift

Supply a 10.0 mm reference, synthetic before reading 10.0 and after reading 10.6; allowed drift 0.1. Task: disposition readings. Criteria: identify setup records; interpret drift; define affected data interval; *quarantine/repeat suspect measurements; document accepted/rejected values. Optional instrument demonstration follows the manufacturer's approved method on inert material. Changed case: stable references but coating mode is inappropriate.

lessons.title: P08 — Rate and life
lessons.body:
## P08 — Rate and life

Supply 12.0 mm/2016, 11.2/2022, 10.0/2026; required 8.4. Task: compute and justify. Criteria: long-term 0.20; short-term 0.30; allowance 1.6; life 5.33 years at justified 0.30; *investigate acceleration and limit result to thinning. Changed case: current 8.3 mm, requiring escalation rather than a usable positive life.

lessons.title: P09 — Interval decision
lessons.body:
## P09 — Interval decision

Supply life six years, exercise internal rule min(half-life, ten years), external min(five years, internal interval), last inspections today. Task: set schedule. Criteria: internal three years; external no later than three; identify rule as synthetic; identify overriding findings; *do not present exercise rule as verified full API code. Changed case: new crack-like indication appears before due date.

lessons.title: P10 — Joint register
lessons.body:
## P10 — Joint register

Supply seam map, uncertain RT record, approved exercise E alternatives 0.85/0.70. Task: determine evidence needed and calculate sensitivity using V10 inputs. Criteria: separate category/type/examination; identify affected seam; trace records; calculate both pressures within 0.1 psi; *withhold unsupported E credit. Changed case: seamless head attached by an undocumented weld.

lessons.title: P11 — Cylinder calculation
lessons.body:
## P11 — Cylinder calculation

Supply P 200 psi, R 24 in, S 20000 psi, E 0.85, future allowance0.060 in, measured0.400. Task: calculate required current thickness and available pressure. Criteria: coherent units; correct equation; required 0.34436 in; pressure 238.80 psi within0.1; *identify component-only/model limits and avoid double allowance. Changed case: same values in coherent SI supplied by instructor.

lessons.title: P12 — Head comparison
lessons.body:
## P12 — Head comparison

Supply hemisphere R 24 and 2:1 ellipsoid D48, P 200,S 20000,E 0.85. Task: calculate pressure thickness. Criteria: identify shapes; hemisphere0.14134; ellipsoid0.28269; separate allowance; *do not use radius for ellipsoid diameter or infer undocumented shape. Changed case: shallow head with no profile record.

lessons.title: P13 — Static head and test plan
lessons.body:
## P13 — Static head and test plan

Supply lower component limit 220 psi at 30 ft below reference and upper limit 205. Task: calculate reference limit and review a test plan. Criteria: head12.99; lower reference207.01; governing205; identify test elevation/temperature/support controls; *no unauthorized test multiplier or pneumatic substitution. Changed case: approved top test300 psi at 40 ft depth gives317.32 psi bottom.

lessons.title: P14 — Toughness evidence
lessons.body:
## P14 — Toughness evidence

Supply synthetic exemption conditions A–D; evidence A–C only; cold test proposed. Task: disposition. Criteria: identify missing D; distinguish material/weld evidence; request applicable clause; identify test restriction; *hold unsupported cold test and never invent impact results. Changed case: material is identified but governing thickness is not.

lessons.title: P15 — Welding controls
lessons.body:
## P15 — Welding controls

Supply approved filler A and field substitution B with no disposition. Task: inspect the repair log. Criteria: identify substitution; locate deposited metal; verify process/temperature records; request qualification review; *hold affected work and avoid treating equal amperage as equivalence. Changed case: correct filler but storage records show unapproved exposure.

lessons.title: P16 — Qualification review
lessons.body:
## P16 — Qualification review

Use V16's synthetic range 3–24 mm, WPS3–30, filler mismatch and SMAW-only welder for GTAW. Task: comparison matrix. Criteria: WPS/PQR distinction; thickness mismatch; filler mismatch; *welder process mismatch; explicit current-code lookup requirement. Changed case: all ranges match but continuity evidence is absent.

lessons.title: P17 — RT record acceptance
lessons.body:
## P17 — RT record acceptance

Supply ten-metre seam requiring full coverage and records covering six metres, unidentified image and valid technician certificate. Task: review. Criteria: four-metre gap; traceability hold; technique/IQI evidence requested; acceptance criteria separated; *no acceptance based on personnel certificate alone. Changed case: all coverage documented but image quality is inadequate.

lessons.title: P18 — Method selection
lessons.body:
## P18 — Method selection

Supply nonferromagnetic stainless surface-crack concern, internal lamination concern and general thinning. Task: method matrix. Criteria: suitable PT consideration; unsuitable MT recognized; distinguish UT flaw/thickness tasks; identify procedure/coverage limits; *no normal thickness override of crack evidence. Changed case: coating blocks penetrant access.

lessons.title: P19 — Material verification
lessons.body:
## P19 — Material verification

Supply alloy-match report without heat traceability or required heat treatment. Task: disposition and traceability plan. Criteria: instrument limits; specification versus alloy distinction; missing records; segregation; *no guessed heat identity or release. Changed case: two alloys require carbon distinction beyond the supplied instrument's capability.

lessons.title: P20 — Relief system
lessons.body:
## P20 — Relief system

Supply passed shop test but blocked discharge and undocumented isolation position. Task: inspection response. Criteria: device/vessel link; installed-system defects; as-found evidence; operational escalation; *no set-pressure increase or unprotected removal. Changed case: rupture disk installation orientation conflicts with approved drawing.

lessons.title: P21 — Repair selection
lessons.body:
## P21 — Repair selection

Supply uncharacterized crack and proposed cover patch. Task: select next decision steps. Criteria: characterize flaw; identify design inputs; compare repair concepts; specify NDE/testing holds; *reject concealment as proof of repair. Changed case: uniform thinning with documented dimensions but unknown material.

lessons.title: P22 — Repair release
lessons.body:
## P22 — Repair release

Supply accepted final NDE, untraceable PWHT chart and no approved test alternative. Task: release matrix. Criteria: link heat-treatment evidence; identify test requirement; establish approvals; preserve original records; *withhold release without fabricating evidence. Changed case: test completed but protection not restored.

lessons.title: P23 — Additional design checks
lessons.body:
## P23 — Additional design checks

Supply proposed vacuum service, larger nozzle and measured4 mm fillet leg where6 required. Task: review. Criteria: external-pressure analysis; opening/load review; throat2.83 mm; compare approved detail; *reject negative-pressure substitution into internal-pressure equation. Changed case: acceptable thickness but saddle settlement.

lessons.title: P24 — Integrated disposition
lessons.body:
## P24 — Integrated disposition

Use V24 case. Task: complete final report. Criteria: correct205 psi pressure-only limit; source/assumption traceability; crack action; relief obstruction action; *no operating release while unresolved. Changed case: both findings resolved with valid records; learner must verify remaining approvals and closeout rather than automatically sign.

lessons.title: Reusable learner/assessor forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable learner/assessor forms

**Basis:** learner____ equipment/chamber____ code/edition____ drawing/revision____ material/record____ dimensions____ conditions____ protection____ unresolved items____ owner/action/date____.

**Finding:** location/datum____ method/procedure____ coverage____ observation____ dimensions____ photos____ limitations____ mechanism hypothesis____ additional evidence____ disposition authority____.

**Calculation:** input/value/unit/source____ equation/applicability____ substitutions____ result/unit____ rounding____ assumptions____ independent check____ governing component/reference____ exclusions____.

**Station:** learner____ station/version____ date____ resources____ simulation or instrument____ criterion scores 1___ 2___ 3___ 4___ 5___ total___/10 critical gates____ result____ evidence file____ assessor____.

**Remediation:** original error____ chapter/task____ instruction provided____ changed case____ new observed performance____ result____ learner/assessor/date____.

**Final report:** identity____ scope____ records____ coverage____ findings____ calculations____ repairs____ protection____ limits____ outstanding actions____ next inspections____ authorization____.

lessons.title: Completion, retention and appeals
lessons.body:
## Completion, retention and appeals

Complete all 24 teaching domains, all 48 formative responses with correction, all stations at the stated criterion, the eight application labs, ten technical decision workshops, fourteen repair decision cases and fifteen damage-mechanism cases at their stated criteria, and the separate controlled final. The planned final has 72 questions scored 0–2: pass 116/144 and at least 4/6 in every domain, with critical errors corrected and reassessed. Record accommodations without changing the competence required. A second assessor reviews contested scoring against the written criteria; retain both decisions and reasons.

Record learner identity, version, dates, assessment evidence, assessor, simulation/hands-on scope and limitations. Issue only a VNDRLY course-completion record describing the assessed scope. Do not issue API510 certification, claim external equivalence established, or imply an employer/jurisdiction has authorized inspection practice. Reassessment after significant scope changes or employer-required intervals is separately recorded. No learner credential has been issued by authoring this material.

lessons.title: Damage-mechanism applied work
lessons.body:
## Damage-mechanism applied work

M01–M15 in damage-mechanism-cases.md extend the V03–V05 teaching block. Complete each original case and changed exercise. Four criteria are scored 0–2: hypothesis/alternative, discriminating evidence, examination coverage/method and disposition boundary. Pass each at 6/8 with no critical error; correct and reassess failures. Retain the case response forms with the P-station records. The planned block includes this work; extend time where needed rather than skipping a mechanism.


---

content.title: VUC035 | VUC035 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC035 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC035 formative checks

Attempt each response before reading the explanation. Correct errors, revisit the linked chapter and solve its changed example. These answers are learning resources, not the controlled final key.

lessons.title: V01-L1
lessons.body:
## V01-L1

Why must chamber identity be recorded?

**Explained answer:** Different chambers can have different conditions and pressure boundaries.

**Reason and remediation:** A common equipment tag does not make shell and tube sides interchangeable. Revisit V01, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V01-L2
lessons.body:
## V01-L2

Does a relief setting establish MAWP?

**Explained answer:** No; establish component strength and approved rating separately.

**Reason and remediation:** Protection setting and structural capability answer different questions. Revisit V01, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V02-L1
lessons.body:
## V02-L1

Why separate access and examination holds?

**Explained answer:** Safe access does not prove adequate damage coverage, and technical coverage does not authorize unsafe entry.

**Reason and remediation:** Both conditions need their own evidence. Revisit V02, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V02-L2
lessons.body:
## V02-L2

How should inaccessible areas appear in a report?

**Explained answer:** Explicitly identified with limitations and approved follow-up or alternative.

**Reason and remediation:** Unseen areas cannot be represented as inspected. Revisit V02, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V03-L1
lessons.body:
## V03-L1

Why inspect insulation penetrations and low points?

**Explained answer:** They can admit/retain moisture and concentrate hidden external corrosion.

**Reason and remediation:** Intact-looking jacketing is not proof of sound metal. Revisit V03, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V03-L2
lessons.body:
## V03-L2

Can historical shell thickness establish a new nozzle corrosion rate?

**Explained answer:** Not without justified comparable geometry/location data.

**Reason and remediation:** Different components can start at different thicknesses and experience different attack. Revisit V03, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V04-L1
lessons.body:
## V04-L1

Why can acceptable thickness coexist with unacceptable cracking?

**Explained answer:** Crack stability and propagation are not resolved by uniform-thinning life.

**Reason and remediation:** Different failure mechanisms need different evaluations. Revisit V04, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V04-L2
lessons.body:
## V04-L2

Are HIC and SSC interchangeable names?

**Explained answer:** No; they describe different hydrogen-related damage forms and susceptibility factors.

**Reason and remediation:** Mechanism identification affects examination and control. Revisit V04, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V05-L1
lessons.body:
## V05-L1

How does HTHA differ from uniform corrosion?

**Explained answer:** It can produce internal metallurgical degradation/fissuring rather than only wall loss.

**Reason and remediation:** Routine thickness surveys alone are insufficient assurance. Revisit V05, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V05-L2
lessons.body:
## V05-L2

Why recover temperature excursions?

**Explained answer:** Accumulated damage depends on historical exposure, not just current conditions.

**Reason and remediation:** Lower current temperature does not reverse past damage. Revisit V05, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V06-L1
lessons.body:
## V06-L1

What makes a visual finding reproducible?

**Explained answer:** Equipment datum, precise location, extent, scaled evidence and method/limitations.

**Reason and remediation:** A vague photograph cannot reliably support trend comparison. Revisit V06, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V06-L2
lessons.body:
## V06-L2

Can a sound liner establish sound base metal?

**Explained answer:** No; evaluate construction and hidden substrate condition with suitable methods.

**Reason and remediation:** The corrosion barrier and pressure boundary may differ. Revisit V06, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V07-L1
lessons.body:
## V07-L1

Does an annual gauge certificate validate today’s setup?

**Explained answer:** No; verify applicable velocity, zero, reference checks and procedure conditions.

**Reason and remediation:** Instrument history differs from field setup validity. Revisit V07, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V07-L2
lessons.body:
## V07-L2

Why retain minimum valid thickness?

**Explained answer:** Localized thinning can control integrity and be concealed by averaging.

**Reason and remediation:** Measurement validity and spatial coverage still require review. Revisit V07, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V08-L1
lessons.body:
## V08-L1

Calculate rate from 12.0 to 10.8 mm over ten years.

**Explained answer:** 0.12 mm/year.

**Reason and remediation:** Loss1.2 divided by ten. Revisit V08, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V08-L2
lessons.body:
## V08-L2

What does zero measured rate not prove?

**Explained answer:** Infinite remaining life.

**Reason and remediation:** Resolution, comparability and mechanism uncertainty remain. Revisit V08, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V09-L1
lessons.body:
## V09-L1

Is remaining life the inspection interval?

**Explained answer:** No; apply governing interval limits, findings and approvals.

**Reason and remediation:** The interval may be substantially shorter. Revisit V09, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V09-L2
lessons.body:
## V09-L2

Does renaming a deferral RBI make it an assessment?

**Explained answer:** No; an approved methodology and documented inputs/results are required.

**Reason and remediation:** Administrative labels do not establish risk analysis. Revisit V09, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V10-L1
lessons.body:
## V10-L1

What is the difference between weld category and type?

**Explained answer:** Category concerns location; type concerns joint construction.

**Reason and remediation:** Neither alone establishes examination extent or efficiency. Revisit V10, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V10-L2
lessons.body:
## V10-L2

May visible weld appearance establish E?

**Explained answer:** No; use applicable provisions and traceable construction/examination evidence.

**Reason and remediation:** Appearance does not prove radiographic coverage. Revisit V10, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V11-L1
lessons.body:
## V11-L1

What units must S and P share?

**Explained answer:** Consistent pressure units, with geometry in coherent length units.

**Reason and remediation:** Mixing MPa and psi invalidates the result. Revisit V11, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V11-L2
lessons.body:
## V11-L2

Why subtract future allowance only once?

**Explained answer:** It reserves the intended future metal loss once; double subtraction misstates available thickness.

**Reason and remediation:** Track current/net thickness explicitly. Revisit V11, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V12-L1
lessons.body:
## V12-L1

Which dimension is used for the standard2:1 ellipsoid formula here?

**Explained answer:** Inside diameter D.

**Reason and remediation:** Substituting radius halves the numerator incorrectly. Revisit V12, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V12-L2
lessons.body:
## V12-L2

Why verify head shape?

**Explained answer:** Different profiles require different applicable equations and conditions.

**Reason and remediation:** A thin measured region cannot establish geometry. Revisit V12, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V13-L1
lessons.body:
## V13-L1

What is water head over 20 vertical feet?

**Explained answer:** 8.66 psi.

**Reason and remediation:** 0.433×20, not sloping shell length. Revisit V13, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V13-L2
lessons.body:
## V13-L2

Why distinguish component and reference pressure?

**Explained answer:** Liquid head creates different local pressures at different elevations.

**Reason and remediation:** Reference allowable pressure must account for depth. Revisit V13, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V14-L1
lessons.body:
## V14-L1

Does carbon steel identify a toughness exemption?

**Explained answer:** No; specification, condition, thickness, temperature and applicable provisions matter.

**Reason and remediation:** A broad material label is insufficient. Revisit V14, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V14-L2
lessons.body:
## V14-L2

Do room-temperature bend tests establish cold toughness?

**Explained answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** The required impact/toughness evidence is distinct. Revisit V14, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V15-L1
lessons.body:
## V15-L1

What does a PQR support?

**Explained answer:** Procedure qualification through actual recorded variables and tests.

**Reason and remediation:** It is not merely a production instruction. Revisit V15, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V15-L2
lessons.body:
## V15-L2

Why control consumable storage?

**Explained answer:** Moisture/condition can affect welding quality and hydrogen-related risks.

**Reason and remediation:** Correct classification alone is not the full control. Revisit V15, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V16-L1
lessons.body:
## V16-L1

Can a valid WPS qualify an individual welder?

**Explained answer:** No; performance qualification is separately required.

**Reason and remediation:** Procedure and individual capability are distinct. Revisit V16, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V16-L2
lessons.body:
## V16-L2

Are nonessential changes undocumented by definition?

**Explained answer:** No; WPS accuracy still requires controlled updates.

**Reason and remediation:** No requalification requirement does not mean no documentation. Revisit V16, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V17-L1
lessons.body:
## V17-L1

Does an IQI guarantee all flaws are detected?

**Explained answer:** No; it demonstrates aspects of technique quality/sensitivity.

**Reason and remediation:** Orientation and geometry still limit detection. Revisit V17, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V17-L2
lessons.body:
## V17-L2

Where do indication acceptance criteria come from?

**Explained answer:** The governing construction/in-service requirements and approved procedure.

**Reason and remediation:** A method standard alone is not every acceptance rule. Revisit V17, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V18-L1
lessons.body:
## V18-L1

What surface condition is necessary for penetrant detection?

**Explained answer:** The discontinuity must be open to a suitable clean nonporous surface.

**Reason and remediation:** Coatings/smearing can prevent access. Revisit V18, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V18-L2
lessons.body:
## V18-L2

Can a thickness gauge substitute for a qualified weld-flaw examination?

**Explained answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** They answer different measurement questions. Revisit V18, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V19-L1
lessons.body:
## V19-L1

Does an alloy match prove heat treatment?

**Explained answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** Chemistry is not all specification/property evidence. Revisit V19, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V19-L2
lessons.body:
## V19-L2

Why maintain identity through cutting?

**Explained answer:** Repair pieces must remain traceable to accepted material records.

**Reason and remediation:** A parent plate certificate is useless if pieces cannot be linked. Revisit V19, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V20-L1
lessons.body:
## V20-L1

Does a bench pass prove installed relief adequacy?

**Explained answer:** No; capacity/design and installation conditions also matter.

**Reason and remediation:** The system can be impaired outside the valve. Revisit V20, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V20-L2
lessons.body:
## V20-L2

Why preserve as-found results?

**Explained answer:** They reveal service degradation, drift or sticking before cleaning/adjustment.

**Reason and remediation:** As-left results alone can hide failure history. Revisit V20, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V21-L1
lessons.body:
## V21-L1

Why characterize a flaw before choosing repair?

**Explained answer:** Mechanism, extent and geometry determine suitable design and acceptance.

**Reason and remediation:** Covering a symptom may leave an active defect. Revisit V21, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V21-L2
lessons.body:
## V21-L2

Is a patch automatically equivalent to an insert?

**Explained answer:** No; load transfer, geometry and limitations differ.

**Reason and remediation:** Method selection requires applicable engineering and code review. Revisit V21, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V22-L1
lessons.body:
## V22-L1

Can extra NDE automatically replace pressure testing?

**Explained answer:** No; an applicable approved alternative must be established.

**Reason and remediation:** Method quantity is not authorization. Revisit V22, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V22-L2
lessons.body:
## V22-L2

Why is live hot tapping outside this course’s authorization?

**Explained answer:** It requires specialized engineering, procedures, personnel and operational controls.

**Reason and remediation:** Course learning does not authorize hazardous live work. Revisit V22, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V23-L1
lessons.body:
## V23-L1

Can negative P in an internal-pressure formula evaluate vacuum buckling?

**Explained answer:** No; use applicable external-pressure evaluation.

**Reason and remediation:** Instability depends on geometry/stiffening and different rules. Revisit V23, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V23-L2
lessons.body:
## V23-L2

What is theoretical throat for a6 mm equal-leg fillet?

**Explained answer:** Approximately4.24 mm.

**Reason and remediation:** 0.707×6; not an acceptance decision by itself. Revisit V23, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V24-L1
lessons.body:
## V24-L1

What should a final report preserve besides its conclusion?

**Explained answer:** Basis, raw evidence, coverage, assumptions, calculations, limitations and action/approval records.

**Reason and remediation:** A reviewer must reconstruct the decision. Revisit V24, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.

lessons.title: V24-L2
lessons.body:
## V24-L2

Does VNDRLY course completion grant API inspector status?

**Explained answer:** No.

**Reason and remediation:** External certification and legal/employer authorization are separate. Revisit V24, identify the mistaken assumption and explain the corrected decision.


---

lessons.title: VUC035 source basis and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC035 source basis and coverage

Review date: 2026-11-17. This is an original VNDRLY instructional package, not reproduced API/ASME courseware. The public body of knowledge and effectivity sheet were downloaded and read. Current copyrighted code clauses and tables have not all been obtained or verified; full external equivalence is **not established**. Code-lookup activities require authorized copies at delivery. Synthetic qualification/interval rules are explicitly teaching data, not actual code requirements.

lessons.title: Governing public scope
lessons.body:
## Governing public scope

- [API 510 body of knowledge, September 2026 / January and May 2027](https://www.api.org/-/media/Files/Certification/ICP/ICP-Certification-Programs/510/2026/Sept%202026%20510%20BOK_final.pdf): inspection, calculations, welding, NDE, damage, repairs and referenced publications. Local text: `.local/certification-115/api510-bok-2026.txt`.
- [API 510 publication effectivity sheet for that window](https://www.api.org/-/media/Files/Certification/ICP/ICP-Certification-Programs/510/2026/Sept%202026_510_Publications%20EffectivitySheet_final.pdf): local text `.local/certification-115/api510-editions-2026.txt`.
- [API certification program directory](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/certifications): external eligibility and certification remain API's responsibility.

The sheet specifies API510 eleventh edition October2022 with March2023 and2025 errata; RP571 third2020; RP572 fifth2023; RP576 fifth2024; RP577 third2020 with September2025 errata; RP578 fourth2023; ASMEBPVC2025 specified portions of V, VIII-1 and IX; PCC-2 2022 specified articles. A newer publication offered for sale does not automatically replace the examination effectivity list or a vessel's legally applicable construction edition.

**Published discrepancy:** BOK's opening reference list includes RP572 AnnexB and excludes other annexes, while its detailed scope includes AnnexesA andB and excludesC. The package does not claim to resolve API's intent. The course covers the broader practical inspection subjects, but exact annex-by-annex equivalence requires clarification/current licensed text. Do not silently delete either reference from an external examination preparation plan.

lessons.title: Supporting primary references
lessons.body:
## Supporting primary references

lessons.title: Controlled code retrieval exercises
lessons.body:
## Controlled code retrieval exercises

### Additional primary-text review receipts — 2026-11-17

These are selected provisions actually viewed, not a claim to have checked an entire publication. The official API examination scope is the edition-selection authority. Publisher-authored text on a third-party host is identified separately from an official controlled copy.

| Source and provenance | Selected material reviewed | Original teaching added |
|---|---|---|
| [ASME VIII-1 2025, publisher text on StudyLib](https://studylib.net/doc/29030014/asme-sec-viii-div1-2025) | UW-51 elongated indications and classification; selected UCS-66 and UW-16 provisions | T01, T02, T08; component versus complete assembly decisions |
| [ASME VIII-1 Appendix 12, 2025, publisher text on StudyLib](https://studylib.net/doc/28231525/asme-bpvc-sec-viii-div1-mandatory-appendix-12--ed.-2025-) | Investigation, classification, acceptance and recording thresholds | T10; separate investigation, rejection and recording decisions |
| [API RP 572 fifth edition, publisher text on StudyLib](https://studylib.net/doc/28311674/api-rp-572---inspection-practices-for-pressure-vessels--2...) | Exchanger arrangements and inspection access; equipment records | T09; original two-circuit coverage and sampling case |
| [ASME Section V 2025 Article 6, publisher text on StudyLib](https://studylib.net/doc/28638988/asme-section-v-2025-liquid-penetrant-examination-guidelines) | Selected temperature, lighting and interpretation-time controls | T05; validity before acceptance |
| [API RP 576 fifth edition, publisher text on StudyLib](https://studylib.net/doc/28051709/api-rp-576--inspection-of-pressure-relieving-devices-2024) | Selected sensing-path, as-found and rupture-disk considerations | T04; protection-system case |
| [PCC-2 2022, publisher text on StudyLib](https://studylib.net/doc/28281618/asme-pcc-2-2022) | Selected scope and limitations for buildup, PWHT alternatives, exchanger repairs and examination alternatives | R01–R14 original repair-decision cases; remaining article-level review is not silently credited |

No source text is supplied as an authorized reproduction of the standards. Learner cases and calculations are original. API RP 577's September 2025 errata was retrieved from the official storefront's DOWNLOAD link and visually checked. It corrects the Section10.8.2 carbon-equivalent equation's percentage notation. V15 and its controlled final now include original calculations using that basis. Official source: https://ecommiddlewareprod.blob.core.windows.net/webstore/addenda-errata/RP_577_E3_EN_E1.pdf. API RP 578 fourth-edition sections 6–9 and Annex A are now accessible in publisher-authored text at https://studylib.net/doc/27679361/pmi-rp-578-e4-en. Method capability, acceptance, component identification and records were reviewed; V19 now includes an original acceptance/traceability exercise. This is a third-party reproduction, not a controlled issuer copy.

Instructor supplies the actual authorized edition. Learner records publication/edition, clause/table, conditions, exceptions and applied decision. Complete: joint efficiency for a supplied real joint; actual interval provisions; pressure-test multiplier/stress-ratio and temperature conditions; impact-test exemption; procedure and welder qualification ranges; RT/PT/MT acceptance; repair/testing alternative requirements. The instructor checks the actual code, not the synthetic classroom answer. An unavailable source or unresolved clause is recorded as an incomplete lookup, not a pass. These exercises support professional preparation but cannot be used to claim that proprietary coverage was author-verified when it was not.

lessons.title: Claims and remaining external verification
lessons.body:
## Claims and remaining external verification

The original course teaches inspection reasoning and supplies assessment materials. It does not reproduce all current technical tables or establish that every API examination clause has been taught to the depth required for external equivalence. Full equivalence remains unverified until current controlled-code coverage and the RP572 annex discrepancy are resolved. No learner examination, physical station or credential issuance has occurred merely because the files exist. Publication/deployment are outside the user's current materials-only scope.

lessons.body:

- ASME Section IX 2025 publisher text: https://studylib.net/doc/29037149/asme-sec-ix-2025 — selected tensile/bend acceptance reviewed for lab E.

All third-party reproductions above were used for selected technical review. None is represented as an authorized distribution of the standard in this course package.

Additional original instruction uses AWS welding-symbol chart (https://app.aws.org/mwf/attachments/64/225364/AWSWeldSymbolchart.pdf), Lincoln arc-welding fundamentals (https://qacd10.lincolnelectric.com/en/Welding-and-Cutting-Resource-Center/Process-and-Theory/Arc-Welding-Fundamentals), National Board process comparison (https://www.nationalboard.org/Index.aspx?ID=528&pageID=164), TWI hydrogen-cracking prevention (https://www.twi-global.com/technical-knowledge/job-knowledge/defects-hydrogen-cracks-in-steels-prevention-and-best-practice-046), LESER chatter explanation (https://www.leser.com/en/leser-update/10-2022/function-chatter) and Emerson Type84 instructions (https://www.emerson.com/is/content/emerson/pt/final-control/pressure-management/documents/manuals-type-84-spring-operated-pressure-relief-valves-anderson-greenwood.pdf). Manufacturer examples support principles and do not authorize applying one model's procedure to every device.


### Additional NDE and weld review receipts

Selected 2025 ASME V T276/T277 and T752 text was read for IQI selection and prod setup; V17/V18 now contain original calculations and changed cases. Selected VIII-1 UW35 text was read for independent undercut/design-thickness/surface checks; V16 includes an original worked calculation. ASTM E797/E797M-21 official public scope was reviewed for V07 applicability instruction. This last receipt is specifically ASTM scope, not a completed comparison of the entire ASME adopted practice.

lessons.title: Thickness-practice edition cross-check
lessons.body:
## Thickness-practice edition cross-check

The publisher-authored 2023 adoption page explicitly identifies SE-797/SE-797M as identical to ASTM E797/E797M-21. The 2025 Section V Summary of Changes lists changes through the adopted standards and does not list a change to SE-797. The teaching basis is therefore the reviewed ASTM2021 practice, supported by this adoption history. This is an edition-continuity inference, not a claim to have compared every character of the2025 adopted pages. Delivery still uses the specified authorized2025 reference and applicable referencing-article requirements.

Sources: [ASME2023 adoption page, indexed publisher text](https://www.west-ti.com/Content/upload/pdf/2022689233/ASME-Sec-V-2023.pdf); [ASME2025 Summary of Changes, publisher text](https://studylib.net/doc/28452860/asme-sec-v-2025-250704-103146). V07 teaches applicability, equipment/probe distinctions, zero/velocity, range standardization, delay, thin-region nonlinearity, echo validity, coverage and records. P07, V07-L1/L2, V07-E1/E2/E3 and the changed reassessment assess those decisions. The BOK's paragraph7 wording is not used to omit the actual2021 standardization procedures in section8.

content.title: VUC035 | VUC035 worked application labs
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC035 worked application labs
lessons.body:
# VUC035 worked application labs

These cases extend the chapter exercises. All equipment and people are fictional. They are calculations and document-review tasks, not operating instructions for an actual pressure system. Use authorized standards for the complete conditions and exceptions; the cited public reproductions support only the identified checks and are not asserted to be controlled copies.

lessons.title: A — A short remaining life changes the interval decision
lessons.body:
## A — A short remaining life changes the interval decision

**Reference check.** API510 eleventh edition, shown with June2025 errata, sections6.4 and6.5 distinguish external, internal/on-stream and thickness-monitoring intervals. The usual non-RBI internal/thickness limit is half remaining life or ten years, whichever is shorter. For remaining life below four years, the provisions permit an interval up to the remaining life, capped at two years, subject to the responsible inspector/engineer and quality system. External inspection generally uses the earlier of five years and the required internal/on-stream interval. Other conditions and approved alternatives still apply. [API-authored text, public reproduction](https://studylib.net/doc/28463865/api-510-pressure-vessel-inspection-code--2025-).

**Case.** A verified uniform-thinning assessment gives3.2 years life. No RBI is supplied. The scheduler sets3.2 years because it is the full remaining life. That exceeds the two-year cap in the cited short-life provision. Under the normal half-life approach the result is 1.6 years. If the responsible authorized decision uses the short-life provision, it may select no more than two years; it is not an automatic extension. Record which path was selected and why. Do not extend operation past a separate crack, protection or jurisdictional constraint.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** Life 1.4 years gives normal half-life 0.7 years. The short-life provision, if validly applied, cannot exceed1.4 years. A two-year interval would exceed the calculated remaining life. Learner must show both candidate results and the approval dependency.

lessons.title: B — Choose the correct efficiency input before calculating
lessons.body:
## B — Choose the correct efficiency input before calculating

The Bureau of Reclamation's unfired-vessel manual presents different efficiency values by joint type and radiographic extent. Its Type1 row gives1.00,0.85 and0.70 for full, spot and no radiography. This supports the teaching distinction; the actual applicable ASME joint description, service restrictions and associated requirements must still be checked. [Federal technical manual, AppendixB](https://www.usbr.gov/power/data/fist/FIST_2-9_%288-2022%29.pdf).

**Case.** A drawing and records establish an applicable Type1 joint with spot examination for the exercise. With S20000 psi, available t0.36 in and R24 in, E0.85 gives P6120/24.216 =252.73 psi. Using1.00 instead gives297.32 psi. The excess is about44.60 psi, arising entirely from unsupported examination credit. A report should show the selected joint/examination record alongside the calculation, not merely the final result.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** If records establish no radiography and the Type1 no-radiography condition is applicable, E0.70 gives5040/24.216 =208.13 psi. If the records are missing rather than proving no examination, distinguish uncertainty from a positively established configuration and obtain authorized disposition.

lessons.title: C — Test temperature affects the pressure calculation
lessons.body:
## C — Test temperature affects the pressure calculation

UG99 and UG100 distinguish hydrostatic and pneumatic pressure bases and use the lowest applicable test-temperature/design-temperature stress ratio. Their general factors are1.3 and1.1 respectively, with additional conditions, bolting exceptions, loading and limits. This is not a complete test procedure. [ASME2025 text, public reproduction, UG99/100](https://studylib.net/doc/29030014/asme-sec-viii-div1-2025).

**Case.** For an exercise explicitly satisfying the applicable conditions, MAWP is 200 psi. MaterialA has allowable stresses20000 psi at test temperature and16000 at design temperature, ratio1.25. MaterialB has22000 and20000, ratio1.10. The lowest ratio is 1.10. The hydrostatic base calculation is 1.3×200×1.10 =286 psi. The pneumatic base calculation would be1.1×200×1.10 =242 psi. Calculating the latter does not authorize choosing a pneumatic test.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** For MAWP150 psi and verified lowest ratio1.20, the hydrostatic base result is 234 psi. If an approved plan uses that value at the top reference and the bottom is twenty feet below in water, bottom pressure is 242.66 psi. The test plan must address local limits and all governing conditions rather than applying the arithmetic blindly.

lessons.title: D — Procedure thickness and deposited thickness are different checks
lessons.body:
## D — Procedure thickness and deposited thickness are different checks

The2025 SectionIX QW451.1 row for a coupon over 3/8 in and below 3/4 in identifies a3/16 in base-metal minimum and2T maximum, with 2t deposited-metal limit, subject to notes and additional variables. [ASME2025 text, public reproduction, QW451.1](https://studylib.net/doc/29037149/asme-sec-ix-2025).

**Case.** A single-process exercise PQR uses T0.500 in coupon and t0.400 in deposited weld metal, excluding reinforcement. Assuming all applicable notes, process variables and other qualifications are satisfied, the base-metal upper range is 1.000 in and deposited-metal upper range 0.800 in. A proposed0.900 in base-metal joint requiring0.850 in deposit is not supported solely by those thickness limits: base thickness passes, deposit exceeds the supplied qualified limit. The learner must evaluate both, not select the favorable base-metal result.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** A proposed0.750 in base thickness with 0.700 in deposit is within those two upper bounds. That result alone does not establish complete WPS qualification: material/filler/process/heat-treatment variables, required tests and any toughness-related restrictions still require review. Do not use this simple row for a different process limitation or a multi-process qualification without the applicable rules.

lessons.title: E — Read a test-result record rather than its cover sheet
lessons.body:
## E — Read a test-result record rather than its cover sheet

**Synthetic acceptance specification for this case:** two tensile specimens each must meet60 ksi; four bend specimens must each have no disallowed open defect under the supplied training acceptance sheet. The laboratory cover says PASS. Results show61 ksi and58 ksi; three bends pass and one is marked NOT TESTED. The cover is contradicted by the underlying record.

**Worked decision.** Reject the record as evidence of a completed passing qualification. One tensile value fails the supplied criterion, and one required bend has no result. Record both separately, preserve the laboratory report and obtain authorized resolution/requalification as applicable. Do not average the tensile results to 59.5 and compare against a lower invented value. Do not assume the missing bend passed because the other three did.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** Both tensile results exceed60, but the fourth bend belongs to another coupon. Qualification evidence remains incomplete because traceability fails. The correct response is record recovery or required testing, not copying the neighboring coupon's pass.

### E extension — Actual qualification acceptance versus a laboratory summary

For an ordinary groove-weld case, review Section IX QW-153.1 and QW-163 in the 2025 edition. Tensile acceptance depends on the applicable specified minimum and the stated exceptions. The base-metal fracture exception is conditional; it is not a blanket five-percent discount for a weld failure. Groove-weld bend evaluation also depends on the defect location and origin, not merely the laboratory's overall PASS label.

**Original record case.** Minimum specified tensile strength is supplied as 70 ksi. Specimen A reaches 68 ksi and breaks in base metal outside the weld and weld interface. Five percent below 70 is 66.5 ksi, so this specimen can satisfy the stated base-metal exception. Specimen B also reaches 68 ksi but breaks in the weld; with no other applicable exception established, the same arithmetic does not make B acceptable. Retain the different fracture locations in the report.

For the accompanying ordinary groove-weld bend, a 0.14 in open discontinuity lies in the weld on the convex surface. It exceeds the 0.125 in criterion and fails. A separate corner opening cannot be ignored until its origin has been evaluated; a corner opening resulting from an internal discontinuity is not automatically exempt. Check specimen identity and that the required weld/heat-affected region was actually within the bend.

**Changed response.** A specimen reaches 67 ksi, but fracture location is blank. The reviewer cannot apply the conditional base-metal exception from strength alone. Obtain the actual test evidence and authorized disposition. For an incorrectly prepared bend that omits the required region, an attractive surface is not a valid passing result. Score strength/exception reasoning, bend reasoning and record validity separately, 0–2 each; require all critical errors corrected within the existing lab criterion.

lessons.title: F — Apply an indication acceptance sheet correctly
lessons.body:
## F — Apply an indication acceptance sheet correctly

**Synthetic examination/acceptance sheet:** a relevant linear indication is unacceptable; a rounded indication above4 mm is unacceptable; any questionable classification requires qualified re-examination. These are classroom limits, not reproduced ASME acceptance criteria. Three observations are:3 mm linear,3 mm rounded,5 mm rounded.

**Worked decision.** The linear indication fails regardless of being smaller than 4 mm. The3 mm rounded indication passes this individual-size criterion only; other required criteria still apply. The5 mm rounded indication fails. Classification comes before applying the correct threshold. A measuring error or invalid technique requires resolution before acceptance; it does not justify choosing the less restrictive category.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** A3 mm indication cannot be confidently classified because excessive background obscures its shape. Repeat or clarify the examination under the qualified procedure. Do not call it rounded merely because that would pass. Record technique validity, characterization and acceptance as separate steps.

lessons.title: G — Develop a complete repair hold-point sequence
lessons.body:
## G — Develop a complete repair hold-point sequence

**Case packet.** V-410 has a mapped local thinning area, no characterized crack, verified base material and an approved insert design. Material pieceM1 is traceable, but welderW2's record supports another process. After correction, a new W2 qualification is recorded. Excavation examination passes. Final NDE passes. The test report is unsigned, and a temporary blind still isolates the relief system.

**Worked sequence.** Initially hold W2's welding assignment until applicable qualification is established. Retain that first hold and its resolution. Verify material/fit-up/excavation and procedure execution. Credit valid final NDE without treating it as a substitute for the incomplete test record. Obtain authorized test acceptance or the applicable alternative. Require removal/restoration of temporary arrangements and verified relief protection. Only then can the responsible authority consider return to service after remaining required reviews. Each record needs equipment identity, date, responsible person and result.

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** The signed test is recovered, but it identifies a different vessel. The test hold remains; a signature cannot cure incorrect identity. Preserve the discrepancy and recover the right evidence or perform required work under an authorized plan.

lessons.title: H — Make a recommendation that can actually be closed
lessons.body:
## H — Make a recommendation that can actually be closed

**Poor recommendation:** 'Monitor corrosion.' It has no location, method, owner or deadline and is not an actionable integrity control.

**Worked revision:** 'Owner integrity engineer to approve a mechanism-specific follow-up plan for V-410 lower-nozzle zoneN2 before the proposed return to service. Plan must identify verified minimum/extent, comparable baseline or justified rate assumption, required thickness basis, examination method/coverage, operating restrictions if applicable, responsible examiner and next due date. Inspection lead to attach approved plan and baseline report to findingF-07 before closure.'

This wording does not fabricate a safe interval when the necessary evidence is absent. It makes the missing technical decision and closure evidence visible. A later completed action must be reviewed against the stated criteria, not closed because an email says 'done.'

**Changed exercise and explained answer.** A finding concerns an obstructed relief discharge rather than corrosion. Replace the monitoring request with authorized protection restoration, installed-path verification and operating disposition. A corrosion survey would not close that finding.

lessons.title: Learner evidence and assessor instructions
lessons.body:
## Learner evidence and assessor instructions

Learner supplies calculations and written decisions forA–H. Score each lab's three elements: correct technical result, applicability/limitations and documented disposition,0–2 each. Pass at least 4/6 in each lab with no unsafe release or fabricated evidence. Use the worked case for instruction and the changed case for reassessment; the separate controlled final remains distinct. Retain worksheet, score, feedback and corrected attempt with the learner record. These eight labs supplement rather than replace the24 applied stations.


---

lessons.title: Record R03 — Service history
lessons.body:
## Record R03 — Service history

Case A: wet insulation repeatedly observed at N2; no documented prior insulation removal. Case B: condensate service, treatment records absent for2019–2022. Case C: amine service, linear surface indications adjacent to a weld despite acceptable thickness. Case D: hydrogen-service exchanger with historical temperature excursions above the current operating point; mechanism-specific assessment absent. These are separate scenarios, not simultaneous claims about V-410's actual service.

lessons.title: Record R04 — Thickness survey
lessons.body:
## Record R04 — Thickness survey

| Location | 2016 mm | 2022 mm | 2026 mm | Note |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| CML-01 |12.0|11.2|10.0|Same identified shell point; valid comparability assumed for P08 |
| N2 |not recorded|not recorded|8.0|No original nozzle baseline supplied |

lessons.title: Record R05 — Qualification packet
lessons.body:
## Record R05 — Qualification packet

PQR TRAIN-A: GTAW, coupon12 mm, filler F-A, no PWHT, backing B. **Synthetic qualification limits for P16 only:** base3–24 mm, fillerF-A, backingB, no PWHT. Test report references TRAIN-A. WPS TRAIN-A revision2: GTAW,3–30 mm, fillerF-B, backingB, no PWHT. Worker W2 record: SMAW only. No GTAW record supplied. These simplified fictional groups are not actual ASME F-numbers or qualification tables.

Separate labD uses the actual table-application inputs stated in that lab, not these fictional limits. Keep the two cases distinguishable on assessment sheets.

lessons.title: Record R06 — Test results for application labE
lessons.body:
## Record R06 — Test results for application labE

Coupon Q-TRAIN-4. Cover sheet: PASS. Required synthetic tensile criterion: each specimen≥60 ksi. T1:61 ksi. T2:58 ksi. Bend B1:acceptable; B2:acceptable; B3:acceptable; B4:NOT TESTED. The learner must evaluate the contradiction rather than edit the cover sheet to create a pass. Retain the original and record disposition.

lessons.title: Record R07 — Examination records
lessons.body:
## Record R07 — Examination records

RT scope: seamB1 ten metres, full coverage specified. Image IDs I01–I06 cover six consecutive one-metre segments; remaining four metres have no image record. Image I07 has no seam/location ID. Personnel certificate is current for the case. Technique quality evidence is not provided; request it. No actual radiographs are included, so the station assesses record review, not image interpretation qualification.

Surface-indication descriptions for labF: A length3 mm, classified linear by qualified examination; B diameter3 mm, rounded; C diameter5 mm, rounded. Apply only the supplied fictional acceptance sheet. A fourth indication D is obscured by excessive background and has uncertain classification. Do not treat D as an established rounded indication.

lessons.title: Record R08 — Materials chain
lessons.body:
## Record R08 — Materials chain

Purchase request specifies material and required heat treatment. Receipt M1 has major-alloy PMI match but no heat number or heat-treatment evidence. Cut pieces C1 and C2 retain traceable identity to accepted plate M2; pieceC3 does not. PMI instrument's stated capability does not include the carbon distinction needed for an alternate-grade decision. Task: segregate unresolved pieces and define evidence needed for release.

lessons.title: Record R09 — Relief and repair closeout
lessons.body:
## Record R09 — Relief and repair closeout

Relief device PRD-410: shop test accepted for this scenario; installed discharge observed blocked. Temporary isolation blind remains installed after maintenance. No alternative protective arrangement documented. Repair insert material accepted; excavation examination accepted; final NDE accepted. Heat-treatment chart has no equipment/coupon linkage. Pressure-test cover identifies V-411 rather thanV-410. Task: credit only valid evidence and list the independent outstanding holds.

lessons.title: Record R10 — Design-change request
lessons.body:
## Record R10 — Design-change request

Request1: cool the vessel in a way that may create vacuum; no external-pressure analysis attached. Request2: increase nozzle size; no opening/reinforcement/load calculation attached. Request3: accept a measured4 mm equal-leg fillet where the approved detail calls for6 mm. Task: identify each different technical gap and calculate the measured theoretical throat. None is resolved by a satisfactory shell corrosion rate.

lessons.title: Instructor model dispositions
lessons.body:
## Instructor model dispositions

R01: basis hold for rating and material identity. R02: entry prohibited until the authorized program resolves missing isolation/atmosphere/rescue evidence. R03: mechanism-specific plans, not one generic thickness check. R04: valid P08 case gives0.20 long,0.30 recent,5.33 years at 8.4 required; drift-case readings are suspect; N2 rate cannot be invented. R05: reject proposed thickness/filler and unsupported worker process. R06: failed tensile plus missing bend. R07: four metres coverage missing, I07 untraceable, technique evidence unestablished; labF A/C fail, B meets only supplied size criterion, D requires clarification. R08: preserve verified chains and hold untraceable/property-unverified material. R09: protection, heat-treatment and test-identity holds remain despite accepted NDE. R10: external-pressure and nozzle analyses required;4 mm leg gives about2.83 mm throat and does not meet6 mm-leg detail.

These are explained practice answers. Controlled final questions use different prompts and values. No actual code-lookup result or practical pass may be invented from this synthetic packet.


---

content.title: VUC035 | VUC035 technical decision workshops
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program.
