content.title: VUC036 | VUC036 workshop records — fictional training issue TR-1
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC036 workshop records — fictional training issue TR-1
lessons.body:
# VUC036 workshop records — fictional training issue TR-1

These records make W01–W08 executable without asking an instructor to invent the scenario. They are not real material certificates, qualifications, engineering approvals or operating permits. Where an actual code table is required, the learner retrieves it from the authorized edition and the assessor independently checks that lookup. Supplied fictional acceptance limits apply only to the specified classroom exercise. Deliberate deficiencies must remain visible until the learner identifies them.

lessons.title: D01 — Boundary, service and locations for W01
lessons.body:
## D01 — Boundary, service and locations for W01

Line LP-21 transports liquefied petroleum gas from Pump P-21 to a pressurized process receiver. The process description states that a loss of containment can rapidly produce a flammable vapor cloud reaching routinely occupied equipment. Current line service is continuous. Drawing revision B omits a two-metre closed bypass observed in the field. There is no completed risk-based inspection assessment. The adopted non-RBI inspection program must be checked in the controlled API 570 edition; no class or interval is preselected for the learner.

Synthetic inspection history: straight point A, 8.0 mm in 2020,7.5 in 2023,7.0 in 2026; required thickness supplied by the training engineering sheet is 5.0 mm. All dates are exactly three years apart. Point B at the bypass has no history. External inspection was due 2026-10-01 and remains unperformed. A planner proposes changing that original due date to 2027-10-01 without a technical review.

**Required output:** establish class reasoning from the stated consequence/service; calculate A's long/recent rate and screening life; obtain the applicable controlled interval provisions; identify bypass coverage and external-overdue issues. **Worked non-code arithmetic:** both rates are 0.1667 mm/year and life is 12 years at A. Those numbers do not establish B's condition or approve the proposed external-inspection deferral. The actual interval answer must include the selected code provision and any applicable restriction, not simply 12 years.

lessons.title: D02 — Straight-pipe material and factors for W02
lessons.body:
## D02 — Straight-pipe material and factors for W02

Fictional material record MR-21 identifies new seamless ASTM A106 Grade B pipe, NPS 6, actual outside diameter 6.625 in. Proposed design pressure is 300 psi; evaluate temperatures 100°F and 400°F. No longitudinal weld is present. Proposed corrosion/mechanical allowance for this exercise is 0.060 in. Purchase specification supplies a 12.5% nominal minus tolerance. The learner must retrieve the applicable stress and factors for this material/temperature and record the actual source notes; do not assume the illustrative S from Q10 is automatically correct for this record.

Available fictional nominal stock choices:0.125 in at cost 100units,0.188 in at 145units,0.280 in at 210units. Costs are training data, not quotations. The exercise asks for the lowest-cost stock satisfying the calculated minimum at both temperatures, with a separate statement that structural and other design checks remain outside this pressure-only selection.

**Deliberate worksheet error:** an attached draft says “E based on 100%girth RT.” The learner must reject that evidentiary basis even if the correct factor for the actual seamless material happens to be the same numerical value. Record manufacturing-route evidence instead. **Changed record:** substitute a longitudinally welded product without its manufacturing/quality documentation. Do not transfer the seamless factor; mark the input unresolved.

lessons.title: D03 — Flange and blank selection for W03
lessons.body:
## D03 — Flange and blank selection for W03

Two fictional purchasing options are ASTM A105 weld-neck flanges, NPS 6: class 150 at 120cost units and class 300 at 190cost units. Service is 200 psi at 400°F. Gasket and bolting are stated to meet the exercise's separate engineering assembly specification; the learner still records that this statement is not a substitute for actual field verification. Use B16.5-2020 to retrieve the actual material-group rating, relevant notes and the appropriate minimum flange dimension. Compare both options and select an acceptable option if one exists. Do not assume the lower price is acceptable before looking up the rating.

Dimensional challenge: after the lookup, the instructor uses the learner's actual retrieved minimum dimension asM. The supplied measured dimension isM−0.020 in. This exact relationship makes the acceptance decision determinate without reproducing a proprietary table: it is below the required minimum by 0.020 in and cannot be accepted merely from its pressure class.

For a separate permanent-blank calculation, the fictional raised-face arrangement has gasket inside diameter 6.20 in, P=200 psi, S=20,000 psi, E=W=1 and allowance 0.050 in. Required thickness by the stated applicable model is approximately 0.31847 in. A verified minimum 0.3125 in plate is insufficient. The gasket diameter is supplied for this configuration; a different gasket style requires its appropriate definition.

lessons.title: D04 — Toughness and heat-treatment evidence for W04
lessons.body:
## D04 — Toughness and heat-treatment evidence for W04

Material coupon TC-21 belongs to fictional heatH-21. The engineering exercise sheet requires an average of at least 27 J, every individual at least 20 J, at −20°C. Laboratory results are 30,29and22 J, but the report's heat field saysH-12. The numbers pass; traceability does not. Learner must identify the mismatch and obtain a valid disposition rather than editing the laboratory identity.

Thermal procedure HT-21 requires, for this exercise only, all three monitored zones to remain 600–620°C for 60continuous minutes. Recorded timeline: minute 0,610/609/607; minute 30,611/608/598; minute 60,612/610/607. Instrument records are otherwise valid. These three snapshots cannot prove a continuous compliant hold, and the 30minute value explicitly violates the supplied band. Obtain the full trace and authorized disposition; averaging zones is not valid.

For the actual code-lookup portion, use the A106GradeB material in D02, governing thickness 0.280 in and proposed minimum metal temperature−20°F. Retrieve the applicable toughness/exemption path and conditions from B31.3-2024. Then evaluate the preheat/PWHT applicability for a matching-material butt weld at the same thickness using the controlled fabrication provisions. The answer must identify actual conditions and exceptions; no field exemption is pre-awarded in this packet.

lessons.title: D05 — Qualification comparison packet for W05
lessons.body:
## D05 — Qualification comparison packet for W05

All identities below are fictional and explicitly marked TRAINING—NOT A QUALIFICATION. Training preparer and verifier fields identify “VNDRLY case author”; there is no claim that welding or testing occurred.

Production jobPJ-21: matching carbon-steel material group supplied asP-No.1; single-process GTAW; groove weld; deposited weld metal 11 mm; argon shielding; matching specified filler family; no required impact qualification in this particular case. The candidate WPS says GTAW,3–10 mm deposited range. Supporting training PQR records GTAW,6 mm deposited test weld, matching material group, required tests recorded as acceptable for the exercise. Candidate personnel documentWPQ-21 records SMAW only, with current continuity for SMAW. A supplemental GTAW personnel record is absent.

**Required review:** the explicit WPS production limit excludes 11 mm, irrespective of what a properly supported revised WPS might allow. Personnel evidence covers the wrong process. The actual IX lookup determines the PQR's applicable qualification range and variable conditions; it does not permit the learner to silently rewrite the WPS or fabricate a GTAW qualification. Hold both mismatches pending valid documentation.

Changed packetPJ-22: production 8 mm within the stated WPS range; a valid GTAW personnel record is supplied for the changed exercise; the execution record lacks required preheat evidence. Explain why qualifications now pass the stated comparison while execution remains unresolved. The assessor records the applicable IX provisions used rather than teaching that these fictional sheets are authentic qualifications.

lessons.title: D06 — Method records for W06
lessons.body:
## D06 — Method records for W06

RT-21: weld mapJ-21, imagesJ-12; required extent whole joint; no identity reconciliation. PT-21: approved procedure range 5–52°C, recorded part 60°C, no alternate temperature qualification. MT-21: ferromagnetic specimen, only one field direction recorded despite the supplied procedure requiring two; equipment check is missing. VT-21: required backside area obscured by a support; report states whole surface examined. LT-21: required jointsA/B/C; bubble-test observation recorded onlyA/B. UT-21: reference checks before work pass; post-check fails; report still releases all intervening values without review.

**Worked review:** each record has a distinct validity/coverage gap before acceptance can be evaluated. ResolveRTidentity; obtain validPTtemperature technique; complete/verifyMTdirections and equipment response; correctVTcoverage statement and arrange missing access/method; examineLTjointC under the approved procedure; quarantine/revalidate affectedUTresults. For each, retrieve the corresponding actual method provision from 2023Section V and record it. No favorable indication statement cures an invalid technique.

Sampling recordSR-21: the supplied designated lot has 20welds by one welder. One initial randomly examined weld fails. Use B31.3-2024 to determine the actual next stage; the instructor then reveals that one additional joint also fails. Continue the actual progressive-sampling path and separately specify verification of each repaired joint. The learner records actual clause-based steps rather than inventing a new sample size.

lessons.title: D07 — Repair proposal review for W07
lessons.body:
## D07 — Repair proposal review for W07

LineRP-21 is a fictional 6 in carbon-steel straight spool at 200 psi/120°C, fully isolated for any training discussion; no live work is performed. Damage is local thinning, with an engineering flag that axial separation must be assessed. ProposalA supplies a sleeve drawing and claims reinforcement and pressure containment, but omits its end-weld design and examination. ProposalB supplies a mechanical clamp rated for sealing at 250 psi/150°C, explicitly excludes axial restraint, and gives no temporary expiry. ProposalC replaces the damaged spool with traceable equivalent material but omits the new support review and test/approved-alternative record.

**Worked review:** none is fully ready for acceptance. A needs an established design/function and execution/examination basis; B lacks the flagged axial function and a controlled temporary plan; C lacks support and test closeout. Use the actual appropriate PCC-2 articles and API 570 requirements to specify the missing evidence. Do not perform a repair design from these deliberately incomplete proposals.

Excavation supplementEX-21: approved minimum after all preparation 8.0 mm; measured after excavation 8.4 mm; required further finishing.5 mm. Net 7.9 mm fails the supplied plan. Identify the hold and appropriate revised disposition. This numerical decision is supplied so the workshop assesses actual reasoning rather than merely listing an article title.

lessons.title: D08 — Test and final-record package for W08
lessons.body:
## D08 — Test and final-record package for W08

Hydrostatic proposalHP-21: design 200 psi; supplied ST/S=1.2; reference-point target calculated using the applicable model; low point 25 ft below; supplied water head.433 psi/ft; low component approved test maximum 365 psi. Reference target 360 psi; low point 370.825 psi exceeds the component limit. The learner must reject the unchanged arrangement and obtain an approved resolution, not reduce a required test arbitrarily.

Pneumatic proposalPN-21: design 200 psi; target 220 psi; independently supplied upper test limit 250 psi; proposed preliminary leak check 110 psi; volume.6 m³. Target satisfies these supplied bounds, but the preliminary check must follow the actual piping rule rather than simply half target. An added.3 m³ vessel raises volume 50% and requires a revised boundary/hazard review. Retrieve all applicable remaining test conditions from the controlled references; these few facts do not establish a safe complete test procedure.

AlternativeALT-21 says only “100%NDE replaces test.” It lacks an applicability basis, approval, method, coverage and acceptance criteria. Record those omissions and identify the relevant controlled provisions. Final reportFR-21 incorrectly says “all work complete” while the support disposition is open. Correct the report status and identify the remaining authority/action, preserving the original version.


---

courses.title: VUC036 | VUC036 controlled-reference workshops

content.title: VUC036 | VUC036 controlled-reference workshops
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC036 controlled-reference workshops
lessons.body:
# VUC036 controlled-reference workshops

These workshops teach the act of selecting and applying a governing requirement, not memorizing a table copied into a course. Use the complete synthetic records in workshop-records.md (D01–D08) and supply authorized copies of the identified editions. D01 corresponds to W01, and so on. Learners record edition, clause/table, applicability, inputs, result and limits. The instructor verifies the actual lookup against that copy. The worked numerical rules below are explicitly synthetic where stated; they teach the decision process and do not replace field code values. A learner must complete both the worked example and the actual reference lookup to pass.

For each workshop score: correct reference and applicability 0–2; technically correct result 0–2; traceable limitations/disposition 0–2. Pass 6/6 after correction. Keep initial and corrected work. A missing controlled reference means the lookup remains incomplete, not that the learner can be credited from a remembered number. None of these tasks authorize work on live equipment.

lessons.title: W01 — Scope, classification and an inspection interval
lessons.body:
## W01 — Scope, classification and an inspection interval

Open API 570 fifth edition and locate its scope, service classification, inspection planning and overdue/deferral provisions. Distinguish an external inspection from thickness monitoring and a special damage-specific examination. Identify the actual basis for a circuit's class rather than choosing the class with the longest interval. Record the owner/inspector responsibilities and conditions attached to an exception before applying it.

**Worked synthetic decision:** the supplied exercise policy uses half-life with a 4 year cap. Life is 10 years, giving 4 years. The external inspection is independently due in 18months. Scheduling thickness monitoring at 4 years cannot close the external task. A proposed deferral needs the applicable assessment and authorization, with the original due date preserved.

**Actual lookup task:** use D01, including its LPG service, occupied-area consequence, omitted bypass and dated records. Record the actual classification reasoning and relevant inspection provisions from the controlled source. Where the description is insufficient, explicitly identify the missing consequence information rather than invent it. Instructor supplies that information and reassesses the completed decision.

**Changed exercise and explanation:** a valid risk-based assessment establishes a different plan. Verify its scope, current inputs and approval; do not mix selected pieces of the RBI and non-RBI paths merely to obtain the longest date. Retain the complete adopted basis.

lessons.title: W02 — Straight-pipe factors and material identity
lessons.body:
## W02 — Straight-pipe factors and material identity

Open B31.3-2024 at 304.1 and its referenced material/quality-factor provisions. Trace each calculation input to the applicable material, manufacturing route and temperature. Check footnotes and the range of the equation. Distinguish the longitudinal seam factor from a production circumferential weld's examination result. Check W and Y rather than silently assuming unity or a familiar value for every material and temperature.

**Worked synthetic decision:** a material record supportsE=.85. A worksheet usesE=1 without qualifying evidence. Using P=300 psi, D=6.625 in, S=20,000, W=1, Y=.4 gives .05805 in withE=.85 and .04939 in withE=1. The higher assumed factor reduces required pressure thickness; therefore the unsupported assumption is consequential. Correct the input and all affected results, then review allowances and other loads.

**Actual lookup task:** use D02, including the named material, manufacturing route, two temperatures and stock choices. Learner retrieves the applicableS, E, W, Y values and footnotes, computes both cases and identifies any range limitation. Assessor verifies every retrieved value against the supplied edition; a guessed factor fails even if the final stock choice happens to remain unchanged.

**Changed exercise:** an examination record is later found. Determine whether it actually qualifies the relevant seam/factor under the applicable provision. Its existence alone is not sufficient; document why it does or does not change the input.

lessons.title: W03 — Flange rating, dimensions and blank geometry
lessons.body:
## W03 — Flange rating, dimensions and blank geometry

Use B16.5-2020 for the exercise's designated material group/class/temperature and B31.3-2024 for the applicable blank configuration. Record the component material marking and supporting record, not only the class. Check how the actual gasket arrangement defines the blank dimension used. Review the flange's dimensional minimum and applicable assembly requirements separately from the pressure-temperature lookup.

**Worked synthetic table:** component familyF permits 28 bar at 100 C and 22 bar at 200 C; interpolation is expressly permitted. At 150 C its limit is 25 bar. FamilyG permits a different pressure and cannot be used for anFmarked component. A requested 24 bar satisfies this numerical F rating, but a measured dimension below the approved minimum still prevents acceptance.

**Actual lookup task:** use the two specified flange options, pressure, temperature, dimensional challenge and blank in D03. Learner identifies the correct table/footnotes, evaluates both, checks one stated dimension and selects the least costly acceptable supplied option. Cost figures are fictional; code ratings come from the controlled source. If neither option meets the requirement, “neither” is the correct selection, not a forced choice.

**Changed exercise:** the temperature rises beyond the supplied table range. Do not extrapolate a rating without an applicable permitted basis. Identify the need for a different component/design assessment.

lessons.title: W04 — Toughness, preheat and heat-treatment applicability
lessons.body:
## W04 — Toughness, preheat and heat-treatment applicability

Use B31.3-2024 material-temperature/toughness and fabrication provisions. Establish material group, governing thickness, temperature and any stated exemption conditions before deciding that impact testing is unnecessary. Record the exact applicability conditions; the word “exempt” without them cannot be checked. For preheat/PWHT, link the requirement to the actual material and weld rather than a shop habit.

**Worked synthetic evidence:** required mean 24 J, individual 18 J at −15 C. Values 29,25,18 J have mean 24 J and satisfy the supplied numerical limits. If the specimen set belongs to another heat, the actual material remains unsupported. If a thermal chart's coldest required zone does not complete the specified hold, the hottest zone cannot compensate for it.

**Actual lookup task:** use D04, including the material/thickness/temperature lookup, impact identity mismatch and thermal record. Learner records the relevant clauses, values, conditions and acceptance decision. Instructor independently verifies the selected path and chart interpretation.

**Changed exercise:** service temperature changes or a thicker repair insert is proposed. Re-evaluate applicability; a previous exemption is not a permanent property of the asset regardless of configuration.

lessons.title: W05 — WPS/PQR/WPQ review and actual execution
lessons.body:
## W05 — WPS/PQR/WPQ review and actual execution

Use the designated 2023Section IX welding provisions and applicable B31.3/API 570 rules. Create a comparison matrix rather than reading only the qualification certificate heading. The matrix contains production process, base material, deposited thickness, joint/backing, filler, position, thermal conditions, qualified ranges and personnel continuity. Identify which variable changes require additional qualification under the applicable rules.

**Worked synthetic package:** production is a single-process weld at 11 mm deposit. The supplied valid procedure range is 3–10 mm; personnel range is 3–16 mm. The welder's range does not extend the procedure's range. Hold the procedure mismatch. If a revised qualified procedure supports 11 mm, separately verify that actual execution follows it; paper qualification cannot prove preheat or consumable control occurred.

**Actual lookup task:** use the explicitly fictional WPS/PQR/WPQ comparison records and changed execution record in D05; they are training evidence, not actual qualifications. Learner determines the applicable ranges from the controlled tables and identifies one deliberately inserted production mismatch. Assessor validates the lookup and the defect. Use a changed mismatch for reassessment, not the same marked document.

**Changed exercise:** all qualification ranges pass, but a required mechanical test result does not. The range arithmetic cannot validate a failed qualification test. Identify the failed evidence and required disposition.

lessons.title: W06 — NDE technique and piping acceptance
lessons.body:
## W06 — NDE technique and piping acceptance

Use 2023Section V articles applicable to the method and B31.3-2024 examination/acceptance provisions. First verify a valid examination: personnel, technique, equipment checks, environmental conditions, coverage and traceability. Then evaluate the indication against the correct service/joint/method criterion. Keep these two stages visible on the worksheet.

**Worked synthetic case:** the procedure requires examination over an identified 180 mm length, but the record establishes 140 mm. Forty millimetres remains unresolved. A favorable result on 140 mm does not satisfy 180 mm. If coverage is corrected but the report uses an acceptance table for another service, the decision still needs correction.

**Actual lookup tasks:** retrieve the applicable RT identification/IQI requirements; PT temperature/viewing/product constraints; MT yoke/prod controls; visual access/lighting controls; bubble-test conditions; and manual UT thickness standardization requirements. Use D06 to find one mismatch per method and work the supplied sampling case. Do not operate radiation equipment or pressurize specimens. Instructor records the actual clause supporting each finding.

**Changed exercise:** random examination detects a defect. Use the actual piping progressive-sampling provision to identify the next lot/personal-work sampling stage and repair examination. A repaired initial weld and an expanded sample are separate evidence. Document both.

lessons.title: W07 — Repair method and the complete applicable article
lessons.body:
## W07 — Repair method and the complete applicable article

Use PCC-2-2022 and the applicable API 570 repair requirements. Select the article for the actual repair configuration, including relevant appendices. Do not treat a table of contents as a design. Review applicability, design, materials, execution, examination, testing and ongoing restrictions as one package. This workshop applies the original R01–R11 cases to the controlled reference.

**Worked synthetic package:** a clamp has a valid sealing design but no axial-load provision. A repair reviewer cannot fill that gap by citing an article title. The actual design must establish the required function and applicable conditions. If the approved repair is temporary, its monitoring and replacement trigger must be present in the work system.

**Actual lookup task:** use the sleeve, clamp, replacement-spool and excavation proposals in D07. Learner identifies each applicable article and relevant appendix, records specific design/execution/examination conditions and identifies one proposal departure. D07 supplies the geometry and service needed to identify its deliberate proposal gaps; learners do not invent the missing engineering design. Record where an engineer's disposition is needed.

**Changed exercise:** the repair method remains the same but the service or remaining geometry changes. Recheck applicability. A previous approval is evidence for its original envelope, not a generic authorization for future conditions.

lessons.title: W08 — Test or authorized alternative and final record
lessons.body:
## W08 — Test or authorized alternative and final record

Use B31.3-2024 testing provisions, API 570 and applicable PCC-2 test/alternative articles. Establish which path applies, then review the complete test boundary. Include temporary components, elevation, weak links, medium, temperature, stored energy and exclusion arrangements. If an alternative to testing is proposed, find the actual applicability and approval conditions and define its methods and coverage.

**Worked synthetic package:** a liquid-test reference point requires 300 psi. A lower component has 30 ft water head and a 310 psi test limit. Its calculated 312.99 psi exceeds that limit. Moving a gauge without changing the physical pressure does not fix the problem. Obtain a revised approved arrangement that satisfies every required point and component.

**Actual lookup task:** produce a test review for the hydrostatic and pneumatic cases in D08, including actual applicable limits and the initial/staged examination sequence. Then review ALT-21 and FR-21 from D08 against the applicable controlled provision. Instructor verifies the complete path; “100%NDE” without an effective method and authorized basis is incomplete.

**Changed exercise:** a late connected-volume change occurs. Revise the boundary and hazard review before execution, then preserve the revision in the final record. Do not silently attach the new volume to an old approval.

lessons.title: Reference worksheet
lessons.body:
## Reference worksheet

Learner____ Workshop____ Date____ Source/title/edition____ Clause/table/appendix____ Applicability conditions____ Supplied facts and records____ Retrieved criteria____ Calculation/decision____ Limits/unresolved items____ Assessor independent check____ Three scores__/2 __/2 __/2 Result____ Remediation____ Changed-case evidence____.


---

courses.title: VUC036 | VUC036 delivery, practical assessment and credential rules

content.title: VUC036 | VUC036 delivery, practical assessment and credential rules
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC036 delivery, practical assessment and credential rules
lessons.body: # VUC036 delivery, practical assessment and credential rules

lessons.title: Entry and teaching arrangements
lessons.body:
## Entry and teaching arrangements

Audience: inspection trainees and personnel responsible for coordinating metallic process-piping integrity work. Prerequisites: basic algebra, units, drawing literacy and industrial safe-work orientation. An instructor reviews the learner's prior inspection experience and conducts this diagnostic: convert 0.125 in to millimetres; calculate loss from 7.5 to 6.9 mm over three years; distinguish a nominal size from actual outside diameter; explain why a zero gauge does not establish isolation. Answers: 3.175 mm; 0.20 mm/year; nominal size is an identifier while actual diameter is a dimension; trapped energy or a blocked sensing path can remain. Remediate each error before related exercises. This is not an API eligibility determination.

The instructor must have documented process-piping inspection experience, familiarity with the referenced codes and the ability to explain the calculations and method limitations. Use qualified NDE, welding, corrosion or engineering specialists for work outside the instructor's competence. An assessor must observe each learner's work and cannot infer performance from a group's answer. Allow accessible formats and additional reading time while preserving the required decisions and practical observations. Translate terminology consistently; do not simplify a safety limit into a different rule.

lessons.title: Planned 64 instructional hours
lessons.body:
## Planned 64 instructional hours

| Block | Hours | Required work |
|---|---:|---|
| Q01–Q06, identity, circuits and damage | 10 | Boundary/circuit records and M01–M15 cases |
| Q07–Q14, measurements and calculations | 12 | Measurement, life, pressure, blank, expansion and material worksheets |
| Q15–Q18, welding, NDE and PMI | 8 | Qualification and examination evidence reviews |
| Q19–Q24, repairs, testing and disposition | 8 | R01–R11 and I01 integrated case |
| Controlled-reference workshops W01–W08 | 8 | Edition/criterion-backed reference decisions |
| Individual applied station assessment | 12 | P01–P24 observable records |
| Final examination and individual review | 4 | Separate final, feedback and remediation assignment |
| Integrated report presentation | 2 | Defensible closeout and oral challenge |

Breaks excluded. Instructional blocks include worked cases and formative checks. Extend delivery for remediation; do not compress individual observations into group attendance. These are VNDRLY planning hours, not a claim of API or external-provider duration equivalence.

lessons.title: Equipment and records
lessons.body:
## Equipment and records

Provide this coursebook, application cases, formative checks, blank forms below, calculator, measuring rule/caliper, marked inert pipe/fitting samples, photographs with scale, drawings, fabricated inspection/material/welding reports and controlled authorized references identified in sources-and-coverage.md. For P07 provide a suitable ultrasonic instrument, probe, couplant, two known-thickness reference blocks and an isolated unpressurizable pipe specimen. The assessor establishes the specimen's reference thicknesses independently and records the instrument-specific procedure and permitted measurement tolerance before assessment.

No live pressure testing, radiography, welding, hot tapping, chemical exposure, energized process manipulation, excavation or confined-space entry is part of these stations. Pressure-test tasks use drawings and inert mockups only. Never connect the mockup to a pressure source. Radiation and spark-producing PMI devices are not operated by learners. P17 and P18 use records; this program does not qualify NDE operators.

If P07 equipment is unavailable, document a simulation result and leave the observed-measurement requirement incomplete. The full course credential requires its actual hands-on measurement observation; a simulation alone cannot satisfy that requirement. The other stations are explicitly document/model-based inspection tasks and are recorded as such.

lessons.title: Scoring and remediation
lessons.body:
## Scoring and remediation

Each P station has five observable criteria, scored 0 = absent, wrong or unsafe; 1 = safe but incomplete; 2 = correct with supporting evidence. Pass each at 8/10 and every starred criterion at 2. Any fabricated record, unsafe intervention or unsupported operating release is a critical failure regardless of total. Stop unsafe conduct immediately. Explain the missed principle, assign the linked chapter and present the changed case for reassessment. Retain both attempts. After two failed reassessments, require an individualized instructor plan and a fresh observed assessment before credit; there is no automatic pass for attendance.

The final consists of 24 independent case questions, each with three scored decisions: 72 decisions and 144 available points. Pass at least 116/144 and at least 4/6 in every domain. Correct and reassess every critical error even when totals pass. Allow 150 minutes for the final within the four-hour review block. Calculator, coursebook and authorized standards are allowed; formative answer sheets and protected keys are not. Proctor verifies identity, permitted resources and independent work. Equivalent defensible answers earn credit when assumptions and evidence are explicit. Retake only after documented remediation, using the protected changed-domain cases. Keep the first result and the retake, not just the better score.

lessons.title: P01 — Boundary and authority record
lessons.body:
## P01 — Boundary and authority record

Supply a sketch showing main M-1 to Vessel A plus an undocumented branch to Skid B; an old report covers only M-1 to A. Learner prepares a boundary record and responsibility list. Observe: identifies main and branch; records drawing discrepancy; identifies missing branch evidence; *withholds unsupported branch acceptance; assigns resolution to the correct owner/technical authority. Changed case: branch drawing exists but field tag disagrees. Expected distinction: document identity remains unresolved until reconciled. Link Q01.

lessons.title: P02 — Component identification
lessons.body:
## P02 — Component identification

Supply inert flange/pipe samples or marked photographs, a component sheet and a gasket drawing with one deliberate mismatch. Learner reconciles identity and dimensions. Observe: distinguishes size from actual diameter; identifies material/class; locates rating basis; detects gasket mismatch; *does not accept from bolt fit alone. Changed case: correct gasket, unknown bolt grade. Link Q02.

lessons.title: P03 — Circuit and location map
lessons.body:
## P03 — Circuit and location map

Supply a hot main, stagnant drain, elbow and mixing junction drawing with existing locations only on straight pipe. Learner marks circuit assumptions and additional coverage. Observe: groups by credible exposure; separates local exceptions; defines reproducible locations; selects mechanism-sensitive coverage; *does not claim unexamined regions covered. Changed case: one drain has a different material. Link Q03.

lessons.title: P04 — Injection change review
lessons.body:
## P04 — Injection change review

Supply old/new injection sketches and operating notes showing altered quill geometry. Learner drafts the revised inspection request. Observe: identifies actual configuration; reviews service history; defines affected-region investigation; seeks qualified mechanism input; *rejects reliance on the old map alone. Changed case: chemical concentration changed without a geometry change. Link Q04.

lessons.title: P05 — Concealed surface plan
lessons.body:
## P05 — Concealed surface plan

Supply wet-insulation and support-contact photographs plus a screening report with a stated blind zone. Learner produces a coverage/limitation plan. Observe: maps water/contact areas; identifies blind zone; selects complementary access/method; plans restoration; *does not authorize lifting/stripping an operating line informally. Changed case: buried transition replaces insulation. Link Q05.

lessons.title: P06 — Mechanism challenge
lessons.body:
## P06 — Mechanism challenge

Use M01, M06 and M11, then ask the learner to contrast a wall-loss and crack hypothesis. Observe: names plausible mechanism without false certainty; links environment/material/stress; identifies discriminating evidence; chooses appropriate examination; *rejects thickness-only clearance of a crack. Changed case: indication is disproved but operating cause remains. Link Q06 and all M cases.

lessons.title: P07 — Hands-on measurement and invalid-data response
lessons.body:
## P07 — Hands-on measurement and invalid-data response

Use the specified instrument, reference blocks and inert specimen. Assessor provides an approved training procedure and independently established reference values. Learner sets up, verifies response, marks locations and takes five repeatable readings. Observe: verifies specimen/probe/procedure; performs valid reference checks; records location and units; explains unexpected echo/coating/geometry effects; *quarantines results when the assessor introduces a failed post-check. Readings must meet the pre-recorded instrument/procedure tolerance; a nominal 0.1 mm tolerance may be used only when suitable for the actual setup. Changed case: introduce a different coating condition and require a revised validated technique. Link Q07. Record real equipment and measured results, not invented successful readings.

lessons.title: P08 — Rate and sensitivity worksheet
lessons.body:
## P08 — Rate and sensitivity worksheet

Supply 8.6 mm six years ago, 7.8 two years ago, 7.2 today; required 5.4. Learner calculates long-term/recent rates, selected-rate life and limitations. Observe: uses comparable locations/dates; obtains 0.233/0.30 mm/year; obtains 6 years using recent rate; states uncertainty/mechanism limits; *does not release the system from arithmetic. Changed case: current lower bound 7.0 gives 5.333 years at the same supplied rate. Link Q08.

lessons.title: P09 — Due-date and deferral record
lessons.body:
## P09 — Due-date and deferral record

Supply life 12 years, exercise half-life rule, four-year cap and a special examination due in two years. Observe: calculates six-year half-life; applies four-year general cap; preserves two-year special requirement; records distinct examination types; *does not erase an overdue original date. Changed case: chemistry changes before either date. Link Q09.

lessons.title: P10 — New pipe selection
lessons.body:
## P10 — New pipe selection

Supply P=200 psi, D=4.5 in, S=20,000 psi, E=W=1, Y=.4, c=.05 in, tolerance 12.5%. Observe: identifies equation/range; obtains t=.022410 in; adds c for .072410 in; obtains nominal≥.082755 in; *does not claim this covers all loads/geometries. Changed case: existing measured pipe instead of new stock; explain why nominal tolerance is not automatically deducted again. Link Q10.

lessons.title: P11 — Future capacity and limiting component
lessons.body:
## P11 — Future capacity and limiting component

Supply current usable .24 in, future loss .04 in, D=8 in, S=20,000, E=W=1, Y=.4 and a 600 psi limiting valve. Observe: obtains future .20 in; computes pipe 1020.408 psi; identifies valve as lower limit; identifies required factor evidence; *rejects proposed 700 psi system operation from pipe result alone. Changed case: temperature changes instead of pressure. Link Q11.

lessons.title: P12 — Blank and flange review
lessons.body:
## P12 — Blank and flange review

Supply dg=5 in, P=200 psi, S=20,000, E=W=1, c=.04 in; actual minimum blank .25 in. Observe: selects correct dg basis; calculates .256506 in; rejects .25 against supplied requirement; distinguishes flange class from psi; *does not authorize isolation/installation from the calculation alone. Changed case: plate is thick enough but untraceable material. Link Q12.

lessons.title: P13 — Movement and support sketch
lessons.body:
## P13 — Movement and support sketch

Supply L=25 m,ΔT=160 C,α=12×10^-6/C and 30 mm clearance. Observe: calculates 48 mm; identifies 18 mm interference; distinguishes free movement from stress; identifies support/fluid-weight considerations; *does not improvise anchor modification. Changed case: clearance 60 mm but nozzle load unresolved. Link Q13.

lessons.title: P14 — Toughness and thermal chart
lessons.body:
## P14 — Toughness and thermal chart

Supply fictional criteria mean≥26 J, each≥19 J at −10 C; results 31,30,18 J; a heat-treatment chart with a below-band zone. Observe: calculates 26.333 J; identifies failed individual; verifies identity/temperature; identifies chart departure; *does not average away either failed requirement. Changed case: all numbers pass but wrong material heat. Link Q14.

lessons.title: P15 — Qualification comparison
lessons.body:
## P15 — Qualification comparison

Supply production GTAW,10 mm deposit; WPS/PQR sheet permits 3–12 mm; personnel sheet SMAW only. Observe: distinguishes three records; confirms procedure range for supplied data; detects personnel mismatch; lists continuity/execution evidence; *holds unsupported personnel credit. Changed case: personnel valid but deposit 14 mm outside supplied range. Link Q15.

lessons.title: P16 — Examination and lot response
lessons.body:
## P16 — Examination and lot response

Supply a report with valid results on only part of required coverage and one rejected sampled joint. Observe: separates validity/acceptance; identifies missing coverage; identifies applicable criterion source; plans lot expansion and repair verification as separate actions; *rejects global acceptance. Changed case: full coverage but wrong acceptance table. Link Q16.

lessons.title: P17 — Technique evidence review
lessons.body:
## P17 — Technique evidence review

Supply image map with mismatched identity, PT report outside its qualified temperature band and a bubble-test report omitting one joint. Observe: detects identity mismatch; detects temperature departure; detects coverage omission; assigns appropriate correction; *does not accept favorable conclusions from invalid evidence. Changed case: identity resolves but IQI evidence is missing. Link Q17.

lessons.title: P18 — Material verification decision
lessons.body:
## P18 — Material verification decision

Supply a low-carbon requirement, an instrument report explicitly excluding carbon measurement and a mixed-batch inventory. Observe: identifies method limit; selects suitable further evidence; defines affected population; preserves traceability; *does not certify unmeasured carbon compliance. Changed case: uncertainty spans the acceptance limit. Link Q18.

lessons.title: P19 — Repair function matrix
lessons.body:
## P19 — Repair function matrix

Supply clamp brochure with sealing capability but no axial restraint, and a temporary repair with no expiry. Observe: distinguishes functions; identifies load-path gap; requests applicable design; assigns monitoring/expiry responsibility; *rejects leak cessation as full structural proof. Changed case: approved temperature exceeded. Link Q19/R01–R06/R09.

lessons.title: P20 — Finished repair acceptance
lessons.body:
## P20 — Finished repair acceptance

Supply required finished overlay 3.5 mm, deposited 4.6 mm, finished 3.2 mm, and a flange with unrecorded final dimensions. Observe: uses finished value; identifies.3 mm shortfall; identifies flange record gap; links corrections to approved process; *does not conceal departure by overwriting original records. Changed case: dimensions pass but material fails. Link Q20/R07–R08.

lessons.title: P21 — Test package challenge
lessons.body:
## P21 — Test package challenge

Supply P=180 psi, ST/S=1.2, low point 20 ft below, given water head.433 psi/ft, local limit 330 psi. Observe: calculates 324 psi reference; calculates 332.66 psi low point; identifies limit exceedance; reviews boundary/support/medium; *holds unsafe or out-of-limit arrangement. Changed case: pneumatic volume increases by half. Link Q21/R10–R11.

lessons.title: P22 — Protection availability
lessons.body:
## P22 — Protection availability

Supply a valid relief bench report and a drawing with an unapproved closed inlet isolation; a check valve has no functional evidence. Observe: distinguishes device/system evidence; identifies unavailable path; identifies check-valve evidence gap; communicates through proper route; *does not manipulate live protection informally. Changed case: path open but changed required capacity. Link Q22.

lessons.title: P23 — Abnormal observation response
lessons.body:
## P23 — Abnormal observation response

Use a photograph and role-play of an unidentified release near an access route. Observe: moves to safe position in simulation; reports asset/location; communicates exposure and uncertainty; preserves observations; *rejects smell-testing or intrusive leak investigation. Changed case: another person labels it harmless without evidence. Link Q23.

lessons.title: P24 — Integrated disposition
lessons.body:
## P24 — Integrated disposition

Use I01 and the learner's station records. Learner produces a concise report and responds to an oral challenge: “The schedule requires startup today.” Observe: correct facts/calculations; explicit limitations; responsible actions/dates; controlled revision approach; *no unsupported release under schedule pressure. Changed case: a late approval resolves one item but another remains. Link Q24.

lessons.title: Forms — reproduce blank for each learner
lessons.body:
## Forms — reproduce blank for each learner

**Station record:** Learner____ Program/version____ Date____ Station____ Attempt____ Assessor/qualification____ Equipment/reference IDs____ Conditions____ Supplied case revision____ Observed work/evidence____ Criterion 1__/2 2__/2 3__/2 4__/2 5__/2 Total__/10 Critical criteria____ Result____ Actual/simulation mode____ Remediation____ Changed case____ Reassessment date/result____ Signatures____.

**Calculation record:** Asset/boundary____ Model and applicability____ Source edition/clause____ Input/value/unit/source____ Assumptions____ Calculation with units____ Independent check____ Sensitivity/uncertainty____ Other governing limits____ Result scope____ Disposition authority____.

**Inspection limitation record:** Location/extent____ Required coverage____ Actual coverage/method____ Blind zone____ Reason____ Alternative/follow-up____ Owner____ Due/trigger____ Current restriction____ Closure evidence____.

**Repair/test review record:** Damage identity____ Approved repair basis____ Materials____ Qualification____ Hold points____ Actual dimensions____ NDE____ Test/authorized alternative____ Boundary/limits____ Departures____ Disposition____ Baseline/monitoring____ Approval____.

**Completion record:** All 24 chapters/checks corrected____ All 27 application cases passed____ All 8 reference workshops passed____ All 24 stations passed____ P07 observed measurement evidence____ Final score__/144 Domains≥4/6____ Critical reassessments resolved____ Instructor/assessor____ Learner____ Credential decision/date____ Limitations____.

lessons.title: Credential and maintenance
lessons.body:
## Credential and maintenance

Award the VNDRLY/U Piping Inspection learning credential only after all required instruction, corrected formative checks, application cases, reference workshops, practical station criteria and final/retake criteria are satisfied. All 27 application cases means 15 mechanism cases,11 repair cases and 1 integrated case. Record actual observed P07 performance separately from document-based stations. An incomplete practical or unresolved critical decision leaves completion pending; do not issue the same credential with a hidden waiver.

The credential describes assessed course competencies, not API authorization, an engineering license or permission to inspect independently. Employer/task authorization and externally required qualifications remain separate. VNDRLY's program policy is a three-year learning review with earlier targeted reassessment after substantial code/task changes, prolonged absence or demonstrated deficiencies. This is a VNDRLY maintenance policy, not an assertion of an external certification's renewal rule. Renewal reviews current practices and references, completes changed cases and repeats affected practical observations; attendance alone is insufficient. Preserve original completion, version and renewal records.


---

courses.title: VUC036 | VUC036 formative checks

content.title: VUC036 | VUC036 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC036 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC036 formative checks

Attempt the response before reading the explanation. Correct missed answers, revisit the linked chapter and solve its changed case. These are learning checks, not the controlled final examination.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

A field tie-in is absent from the current drawing. What must change in the inspection record?

**Explained answer:** Record the boundary discrepancy and obtain the tie-in design, construction and baseline evidence.

**Why and remediation:** A verified old boundary does not cover an undocumented addition. Revisit Q01 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

Can an examiner independently approve a rerating because their measurements are accurate?

**Explained answer:** Only with the separately established authority and required engineering process; measurements alone do not grant it.

**Why and remediation:** Examination evidence and disposition authority are distinct. Revisit Q01 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Does a matching flange bolt pattern establish its rating?

**Explained answer:** No; verify material, class, temperature rating, dimensions and assembly compatibility.

**Why and remediation:** Fit is not pressure-temperature suitability. Revisit Q02 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

Why record the viewing direction for clock-position measurements?

**Explained answer:** So another examiner can reproduce the location.

**Why and remediation:** An ambiguous orientation can corrupt a thickness trend. Revisit Q02 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

What makes a corrosion circuit useful?

**Explained answer:** A defensible common service/material/damage basis with local exceptions identified.

**Why and remediation:** Geographic closeness alone does not establish comparable deterioration. Revisit Q03 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

Can six sound straight-pipe points clear an unexamined elbow?

**Explained answer:** No; examine the elbow using a mechanism-appropriate plan.

**Why and remediation:** Coverage must address the susceptible geometry. Revisit Q03 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Does an intermittently used branch necessarily avoid deadleg behavior?

**Explained answer:** No; review stagnant periods and actual configuration.

**Why and remediation:** Occasional flow does not eliminate accumulated local exposure. Revisit Q04 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

What changes when an injection quill is shortened?

**Explained answer:** Review mixing/impingement conditions and the inspection boundary.

**Why and remediation:** The earlier plan may no longer represent the modified exposure. Revisit Q04 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

What does a sound insulation inspection window prove?

**Explained answer:** The examined area under the stated technique and limits, not all concealed metal.

**Why and remediation:** Unexamined water-entry/contact locations may differ. Revisit Q05 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Why verify insulation restoration after examination?

**Explained answer:** To prevent new water entry and preserve protection.

**Why and remediation:** Inspection access can create a future damage location. Revisit Q05 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Why does a wall-loss forecast not clear a crack?

**Explained answer:** Crack behavior and assessment differ from uniform thinning.

**Why and remediation:** The model does not represent the relevant failure mode. Revisit Q06 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Does disappearance of vibration after shutdown prove the branch is undamaged?

**Explained answer:** No; evaluate accumulated damage and restart loading.

**Why and remediation:** Stopping excitation is not a crack examination. Revisit Q06 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Two 4 and 12 mm blocks read 4.5 and 12.5. What pattern is present?

**Explained answer:** A constant +0.5 mm offset.

**Why and remediation:** Investigate setup and recalibrate; do not merely subtract from production records. Revisit Q07 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

What should follow a failed post-use reference check?

**Explained answer:** Identify affected results, correct the setup and repeat necessary measurements with traceable corrections.

**Why and remediation:** Questionable data cannot support an unqualified integrity decision. Revisit Q07 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

For 8.0 to 7.0 mm over six years, what is the long-term rate?

**Explained answer:** Approximately 0.167 mm/year.

**Why and remediation:** Loss is divided by actual elapsed time at a comparable point. Revisit Q08 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

At 7.0 current, 5.0 required and 0.20 mm/year, what is screening life?

**Explained answer:** 10 years, subject to the model assumptions and other damage.

**Why and remediation:** The calculation is not a release authorization. Revisit Q08 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

An exercise uses half-life capped at five years; life is eight. What interval results?

**Explained answer:** Four years before considering more restrictive conditions.

**Why and remediation:** A maximum is not an automatic recommendation. Revisit Q09 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

Does resetting an overdue date create a valid deferral?

**Explained answer:** No; retain the original date and documented authorized assessment.

**Why and remediation:** A schedule edit is not a risk decision. Revisit Q09 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Where is manufacturing minus tolerance applied when choosing new nominal pipe?

**Explained answer:** To ensure the ordered nominal produces at least the required minimum.

**Why and remediation:** Do not apply a nominal tolerance twice to verified actual in-service thickness. Revisit Q10 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

Can the straight-pipe equation qualify a branch reinforcement?

**Explained answer:** Not by itself; the configuration needs its applicable design basis.

**Why and remediation:** Equation validity is geometry- and load-dependent. Revisit Q10 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Does RT of a girth weld establish a longitudinal seam quality factor?

**Explained answer:** No; obtain evidence applicable to the longitudinal seam and its manufacturing/qualification basis.

**Why and remediation:** Different joints have different evidentiary roles. Revisit Q11 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

Why assess connected components during rerating?

**Explained answer:** The system may be limited by a component other than the calculated straight pipe.

**Why and remediation:** A local calculation cannot raise another component rating. Revisit Q11 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Is class 150 a universal 150 psi rating?

**Explained answer:** No; use material and temperature-specific rating information.

**Why and remediation:** Class is a designation, not a constant pressure. Revisit Q12 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Can a smooth resurfaced flange be accepted without dimensions?

**Explained answer:** No; verify remaining dimensions and approved repair/assembly criteria.

**Why and remediation:** Surface appearance does not establish structural adequacy. Revisit Q12 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

What does αLΔT estimate in the simple exercise?

**Explained answer:** Unrestrained thermal length change under the supplied constant-coefficient assumption.

**Why and remediation:** It is not a flexibility or nozzle-load acceptance calculation. Revisit Q13 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

Why review supports for a water test of a gas line?

**Explained answer:** The added fluid weight may change support loads.

**Why and remediation:** Pressure adequacy does not establish load-path adequacy. Revisit Q13 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

An average impact result passes but one specimen is below the supplied individual minimum. Accept?

**Explained answer:** No; both criteria apply.

**Why and remediation:** A mean can conceal an unacceptable individual result. Revisit Q14 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

Does a warm-temperature impact test prove a colder specified requirement?

**Explained answer:** Not by itself.

**Why and remediation:** The test condition must match the applicable requirement or authorized technical basis. Revisit Q14 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Which record documents actual procedure-qualification test conditions?

**Explained answer:** The PQR.

**Why and remediation:** The WPS provides production instructions; it is not the same record. Revisit Q15 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

Does a process-qualified WPS establish every welder is qualified?

**Explained answer:** No; review personnel qualification and continuity for the production work.

**Why and remediation:** Procedure and performance qualification are distinct. Revisit Q15 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

What must be established before applying an acceptance criterion to NDE results?

**Explained answer:** That the technique, personnel, calibration and coverage produced valid evidence.

**Why and remediation:** Invalid examination cannot support a favorable acceptance result. Revisit Q16 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

Why does repair of one sampled defect not necessarily close the lot?

**Explained answer:** The applicable sampling expansion remains a separate requirement.

**Why and remediation:** Repair and population confidence are different issues. Revisit Q16 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Does an IQI meeting requirements mean the weld has no rejectable flaw?

**Explained answer:** No; it supports image quality, while discontinuities require separate interpretation.

**Why and remediation:** Technique validity and acceptance are distinct. Revisit Q17 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

Can a stable pressure gauge replace required bubble examination?

**Explained answer:** No.

**Why and remediation:** Small leakage may not produce a visible pressure change over the observation period. Revisit Q17 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:
## Q18-L1

Can an alloy-family display establish an unmeasured carbon limit?

**Explained answer:** No.

**Why and remediation:** The method must measure or otherwise validly establish the required characteristic. Revisit Q18 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q18-L2
lessons.body:
## Q18-L2

What happens to identity when a marked parent pipe is cut?

**Explained answer:** Maintain traceability of each relevant piece through controlled marking/records.

**Why and remediation:** Unmarked offcuts cannot inherit identity by assumption. Revisit Q18 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q19-L1
lessons.body:
## Q19-L1

Does a clamp that stops leakage necessarily restore axial capacity?

**Explained answer:** No; establish the design load path and capability.

**Why and remediation:** Leak sealing and structural restraint are different functions. Revisit Q19 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q19-L2
lessons.body:
## Q19-L2

What makes a temporary repair manageable?

**Explained answer:** An approved envelope, monitoring, accountable owner and expiry/replacement trigger.

**Why and remediation:** Temporary must not mean forgotten. Revisit Q19 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q20-L1
lessons.body:
## Q20-L1

An overlay passes deposited thickness but fails finished thickness. Which governs the stated final requirement?

**Explained answer:** The finished condition.

**Why and remediation:** Machining can remove required qualified material. Revisit Q20 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q20-L2
lessons.body:
## Q20-L2

Why record excavation dimensions before welding?

**Explained answer:** They establish the actual substrate and whether the approved repair still applies.

**Why and remediation:** Filling the area cannot erase a changed-condition hold. Revisit Q20 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q21-L1
lessons.body:
## Q21-L1

Why account for elevation in hydrostatic testing?

**Explained answer:** Local pressure varies with liquid head.

**Why and remediation:** A reference gauge can conceal excessive pressure lower in the boundary. Revisit Q21 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q21-L2
lessons.body:
## Q21-L2

Why is adding gas volume a test-plan change?

**Explained answer:** It changes the boundary and stored-energy hazard.

**Why and remediation:** Unchanged pressure does not mean unchanged risk. Revisit Q21 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q22-L1
lessons.body:
## Q22-L1

Does a recent bench certificate prove installed relief protection is available?

**Explained answer:** No; verify the installed path and applicable system conditions.

**Why and remediation:** Isolation or restrictions can defeat a tested device. Revisit Q22 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q22-L2
lessons.body:
## Q22-L2

Can exterior appearance prove a critical check valve closes correctly?

**Explained answer:** No; appropriate functional/maintenance evidence is needed.

**Why and remediation:** Its safety function is internal and scenario-dependent. Revisit Q22 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q23-L1
lessons.body:
## Q23-L1

Should an inspector approach a suspected release to identify it by smell?

**Explained answer:** No; withdraw and use the site response process.

**Why and remediation:** Uncontrolled exposure is not a diagnostic technique. Revisit Q23 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q23-L2
lessons.body:
## Q23-L2

Does a zero gauge prove no trapped pressure?

**Explained answer:** No; use the approved isolation and verification process.

**Why and remediation:** Blocked sensing paths or trapped volumes can invalidate the inference. Revisit Q23 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q24-L1
lessons.body:
## Q24-L1

How should an unexamined region appear in the final report?

**Explained answer:** Explicitly identified with limitations and required follow-up.

**Why and remediation:** A global pass would overstate the evidence. Revisit Q24 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.

lessons.title: Q24-L2
lessons.body:
## Q24-L2

How should a late approval be added?

**Explained answer:** Through a controlled revision retaining original history.

**Why and remediation:** Do not backdate the earlier status. Revisit Q24 and explain the corrected assumption in your own words.


---

courses.title: VUC036 | VUC036 sources, edition basis and coverage

content.title: VUC036 | VUC036 sources, edition basis and coverage
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC036 sources, edition basis and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC036 sources, edition basis and coverage

Author review date: 2026-11-17. This is an original VNDRLY learning program addressing process-piping inspection competencies. It is not an API curriculum, copied exam bank, accredited API credential or a claim of independently verified clause-by-clause external examination equivalence. Applicable law, employer authorization and controlled engineering standards govern actual work. Authoring materials does not establish that any learner has completed an observed practical.

lessons.title: Reference basis and source access
lessons.body:
## Reference basis and source access

S01 — [API 570 program page](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/certifications/api570). Used for external credential boundary and current reference discovery, not to claim VNDRLY awards that credential.

S02 — [Official February/June2027 body of knowledge](https://apidam.widen.net/content/axfqizq8hy/pdf/=c&quality=80&x.app=portals) and [official effectivity sheet](https://apidam.widen.net/content/vj0zycp1wu/pdf/=c&quality=80&x.app=portals), followed from S01. Read during authoring. The next published reference basis retains API 570 fifth2024, RP 571 third2020, RP 574 fifth2024 with March2025 addendum, RP 576 fifth2024, RP 577 third2020, RP 578 fourth2023, BPVC V/IX2023, B16.5-2020 and B31.3-2024, and adds selected PCC-2-2022 repair articles. This program uses that reference set for controlled lookup practice; it does not silently substitute BPVC 2025 from the preceding vessel course. Exam dates/editions can change; confirm the actual external exam window separately.

S03 — API 570, fifth edition, February2024. [Publisher update](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/standards/important-standards-announcements/570-574-tradepress); [primary-authored text consulted via public mirror](https://studylib.net/doc/28069788/api-570-2024). Selected scope, planning, interval, rate and integrity provisions were inspected. Authorized controlled copy required for W01 and field use; the mirror is not the course's distributed standard.

S04 — API RP 574, fifth edition 2024, Addendum1 March2025. [API announcement](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/standards/important-standards-announcements/rp574), [authorized seller edition record](https://store.accuristech.com/standards/api-rp-574?product_id=2581821), [addendum text consulted](https://studylib.net/doc/28065505/api-574-addendum-1--2025). The inspection-planning and structural-screening context informs Q02–Q05/Q13. Tabulated minimums are not reproduced as universal acceptance limits. Use a controlled copy for actual applicability and component practice.

S05 — ASME B31.3-2024. [Primary-authored text consulted](https://studylib.net/doc/28254728/asme-b31.3---2024---process-piping). Selected304.1,304.5.3,341.3 and345.4/345.5 provisions were read. Core calculations in this package are original cases with explicitly supplied inputs. The course does not reproduce design/acceptance tables. Workshops require an authorized edition, correct material/service selection and verification of relevant notes and exceptions.

S06 — ASME B16.5-2020 for the S02 reference set. [Publisher scope](https://www.asme.org/codes-standards/find-codes-standards/b16-5-pipe-flanges-flanged-fittings-nps-1-2-nps-24-metric-inch-standard). Publisher pages may display a newer edition; use the designated2020 copy for W03, not an unidentified web table. The package's rating tables are explicitly fictional teaching data.

S07 — BPVC V/IX2023 for examination methods and welding qualification, as identified by S02. Controlled copies are required for W05/W06. Public course explanations teach method/record distinctions; actual qualification ranges, technique criteria and acceptance decisions must be verified against the designated source. No proprietary table or purported full code text is redistributed.

S08 — API RP 571 third2020. [Primary-authored text consulted](https://studylib.net/doc/27624954/api-571-2020-pdf-version). Mechanism names and selected subject scope were checked against S02. M01–M15 are original investigation cases, not copied damage descriptions or a diagnostic substitute. Their results distinguish hypotheses from confirmed mechanisms.

S09 — API RP 577 third2020 and RP 578 fourth2023. [API catalog description of the material-verification program](https://www.api.org/-/media/files/publications/2024-catalog/2024-refining.pdf); [RP 578 primary-authored text previously reviewed](https://studylib.net/doc/27679361/pmi-rp-578-e4-en). Use controlled copies in the welding/material workshops. Instrument-method capability and material traceability are assessed separately. A displayed alloy name is not treated as full specification evidence.

S10 — PCC-2-2022. [ASME publisher record](https://www.asme.org/codes-standards/find-codes-standards/repair-of-pressure-equipment-and-piping) and [publisher contents](https://www.asme.org/getmedia/6adee048-ce17-4a4e-be87-e3e35e6ab89d/pcc-2_2022_toc.pdf). Selected repair context was reviewed against the newly listed S02 articles. W07/W08 require the complete applicable articles and appendices, not only their titles. R01–R11 are original proposal-review problems, not field repair instructions or fabricated engineering designs.

S11 — [HSE deadleg rupture alert CEMHD2-2019](https://www.hse.gov.uk/safetybulletins/catastrophic-rupture-dead-leg-pipe-work.htm). The alert describes localized damage missed by spot measurements. Q03/Q04 apply that coverage lesson through original cases.

S12 — [HSE pipework guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeaspipework.htm) and [materials/corrosion guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeasmaterial.htm). General design, inspection and environment context. UK guidance is identified as such, not represented as universally applicable US law.

S13 — [CSB Chevron technical findings](https://www.csb.gov/in-cooperation-with-cal-osha-csb-releases-technical-report-on-chevron-2012-pipe-rupture-and-fire-extensive-sulfidation-corrosion-noted/?F_All=y&SID=1). Used for the short M15 lesson on component-level differences and representative inspection. The fictional M15 case does not assert additional facts about the actual incident.

S14 — [Evident velocity/zero calibration tutorial](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/thickness-gauge/zero-calibration). Supports Q07's distinction between offset and scale response. Actual instrument setup follows its own procedure and manufacturer instructions.

S15 — [ASNT PT overview](https://www.asnt.org/what-is-nondestructive-testing/methods/liquid-penetrant-testing), [ASNT MT overview](https://www.asnt.org/what-is-nondestructive-testing/methods/magnetic-particle-testing), [National Board penetrant explanation](https://www.nationalboard.org/Index.aspx?pageID=374). Method principles support Q16/Q17; they do not replace the governing piping acceptance criteria.

S16 — [HSE GS4 fourth edition pressure-test guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/gs4.pdf). Supports stored-energy, boundary and safe-test planning concepts. The course performs no live pressure test and supplies no universal safe stand-off distance.

S17 — [OSHA1910.119](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.119), particularly mechanical integrity, changes and operating safety for covered processes. Applicability must be established; this course does not state that all oil-and-gas operations are covered. Q23/Q24 teach traceable actions and authorized changes without converting every example into a legal applicability conclusion.

S18 — API RP 576 fifth 2024, selected sections identified in S02. Controlled reference for Q22/W08 device inspection and protection review. The course's installed-versus-bench cases do not claim a universal inspection interval or authorize relief-device adjustment.

## Maintenance and boundaries

At each revision, check publisher editions/addenda, effectivity for any advertised external-exam reference window, technical calculation assumptions and practical resources. Do not update an edition label while leaving old criteria unreviewed. Preserve previous course versions and learner records.
