lessons.title: VUC037 advanced calculation and reference labs
lessons.body:
# VUC037 advanced calculation and reference labs

These labs extend the course's technical depth. Every learner must perform the calculations and the stated reference work. The formulas and synthetic project values are supplied for learning; actual use requires the correct standard, edition, scope and conditions. Do not treat successful arithmetic as engineering authorization. The assessor records the actual reference lookup and the learner's explanation of applicability.

lessons.title: T01 — Distinguishing inspection clocks
lessons.body:
## T01 — Distinguishing inspection clocks

**Instruction.** Routine observations, formal external inspection, thickness monitoring and internal inspection answer different questions. An interval for one is not a blanket interval for the others. Calculate each applicable clock, then consider whether a changed condition requires earlier action. Use the same units for remaining allowance and rate. A positive time-to-limit does not guarantee all other mechanisms are controlled.

**Supplied record.** Remaining shell allowance RCA = 1.8 mm; selected rate N = 0.15 mm/year. For this exercise the formal external rule is min(5 years, RCA/(4N)); the thickness-monitoring rule is min(15 years, RCA/(2N)). Internal interval has a separate bottom/RBI basis, not supplied by these two expressions.

**Work and answer.** External = min(5, 1.8/0.6) = 3 years. Thickness monitoring = min(15, 1.8/0.3) = 6 years. The six-year result does not postpone the three-year formal external inspection or establish an internal interval. If rate rises to 0.30, results become 1.5 and 3 years. Update both clocks and review the cause of acceleration.

**Reference task.** Locate API 653 Section 6's applicable inspection types, personnel and interval rules. Explain why an initial internal interval, a subsequent interval and a justified risk-based interval cannot be substituted without meeting their distinct conditions. Record the applicable maximum and supporting credits only when evidence for each credit exists. No credit for an unverified lining/protection system.

**Assessment.** Six points: correct first interval 2; second 2; separate-clock/changed-condition interpretation 2. Require 6/6 after correction. Changed scored case RCA 2.4, N = 0.20 gives 3 and 6 years; unknown rate requires locating the actual applicable rule rather than dividing by zero.

lessons.title: T02 — Reconstructed shell design versus test condition
lessons.body:
## T02 — Reconstructed shell design versus test condition

**Instruction.** Design and hydrotest conditions can use different allowable stresses and liquid properties. Calculate both using the applicable method, then check other required minima and loads. A corrosion allowance belongs to its defined design basis, not indiscriminately to every term. A formula is not valid for every diameter or every construction type.

**Supplied US-customary record.** D=100 ft, H=32 ft, G=.90, Sd=20000 psi, St=22000 psi, CA=.050 in. Supplied one-foot-method expressions are td=2.6D(H−1)G/Sd+CA and tt=2.6D(H−1)/St. The synthetic project minimum is .300 in. Only compare these three values in this exercise; other loads remain a separate review.

**Work and answer.** td=7254/20000+.050=.41270 in. tt=8060/22000=.36636 in. The largest of these and .300 is .41270 in. A proposed .400 in net available plate fails that supplied design comparison. Do not choose the smaller hydrotest value merely because the planned test uses water. If G becomes .70, td=.33210 in and tt=.36636 in, so the test case controls among these inputs.

**SI companion.** Supplied SI form td = 4.9D(H−.3)G/Sd + CA, with D/H in m, S in MPa and result in mm. D = 30, H = 10, G = .9, S = 138, CA = 1.5 gives 10.79935 mm; tt with St = 152 is 9.38092 mm. Keep the SI constant and datum with SI inputs. Do not insert feet into that expression.

**Reference task.** Verify API 650's applicable method, material-table stresses, minimum plate requirements and diameter limit, and API 653's reconstruction provisions. Identify conditions excluded from these simplified exercises. Six points: both calculations 2; controlling-value selection 2; scope/minimum/reference explanation 2; require 6/6 after correction.

lessons.title: T03 — Hot-tap spacing and what it does not authorize
lessons.body:
## T03 — Hot-tap spacing and what it does not authorize

**Instruction.** Spacing is a geometric check, not a complete hot-tap safety assessment. Identify the required datum: weld-toe separation is not nozzle-center spacing. Confirm tank radius and shell thickness use the units required by the supplied relationship. Review material, toughness, contents, operating condition, welding and specialist procedure independently.

**Record.** Tank diameter is 80 ft; shell thickness is .375 in. Supplied spacing expression is √(R×T), with R and T in inches. Proposed weld-toe separation is 12 in.

**Answer.** Radius 40 ft=480 in; √(480×.375)=√180=13.4164 in. Twelve inches fails. If separation becomes 14 in, the numerical spacing passes, but no live operation is authorized. A record stating center spacing 14 in with unspecified nozzle/reinforcement dimensions cannot establish weld-toe clearance.

**Reference task.** Verify API 653 section 9.15's applicability, material/service restrictions, preparatory measurement and specialist procedure requirements. Identify the specific missing evidence in a record whose only completed field is spacing. Scoring: unit conversion 2, spacing 2, authority/scope 2. Changed case D = 60 ft, T = .5 in gives √180 again; the learner must show conversion rather than copy the number.

lessons.title: T04 — Settlement profile reduction
lessons.body:
## T04 — Settlement profile reduction

For the available-source delivery route, also complete C37-1 in available-source-completion.md. Its supplied engineering criteria assess a complete evidence decision without claiming an API chart lookup. The controlled-chart reference task below remains an optional extension until the actual reference is available.

**Instruction.** A reference plane can help distinguish broad tilt from localized departures. Use a valid fitting and evaluation method; do not manipulate the reference to erase a bad point. For this teaching exercise a reference profile is supplied, so no structural acceptance is implied.

**Record.** Eight equally spaced actual elevations in mm: [4, 2, 0, −2, −12, −2, 0, 2]. Supplied fitted-reference values: [4, 2, 0, −2, −4, −2, 0, 2]. Compute actual minus reference. A project review trigger is absolute residual >5 mm; this is not an API settlement acceptance curve.

**Answer.** Residuals are [0, 0, 0, 0, −8, 0, 0, 0]. Station 5 exceeds the supplied review trigger. Do not average −8 across all points and call it acceptable. Repeat/check the survey, refine coverage around station 5 and obtain the required geometric assessment. Changing actual station 5 to −7 gives residual −3, not triggering this particular threshold; other conditions remain.

**Reference task.** Identify the correct Annex B route for shell settlement, edge settlement and near/remote bottom depressions. Use actual controlled figures, correct dimensions and weld orientation. The 2025 errata clarifies a sampling distinction for curve fitting and the settlement calculation; read it before applying the method. Score residual 2, trigger 2, method/limits 2. A numerical chart assessment remains incomplete until all real chart inputs are supplied and evaluated; no invented threshold earns credit.

**Additional worked calculation — remote bottom depression.** The synthetic drawing identifies a local depression remote from the shell in a single-pass lap-welded bottom. Its inscribed-circle radius is 1,200 mm and measured depth is 44 mm. For the applicable simplified comparison, use B = 0.031R with both dimensions in mm. The comparison value is 37.2 mm; 44 mm exceeds it by 6.8 mm. Document the geometry and refer for repair or rigorous assessment. This is not permission to hammer the bottom flat or to continue filling.

**Changed case.** The radius remains 1,200 mm and depth is now 32 mm, but a crack-like indication crosses the depression. The depth lies below 37.2 mm; the separate indication remains unresolved. A depth comparison does not accept a crack. A second changed drawing relocates the depression to the shell edge: do not carry the remote-bottom formula into that different geometry. Select the applicable edge-settlement assessment and required examinations.

**Assessor extension.** Require the learner to identify the inscribed radius, keep units consistent, calculate 37.2 mm, identify exceedance and preserve the separate indication/geometry issues. Record each decision and remediate any missed one before T04 is complete. The reference is API 653 Annex B.3.3; actual applicability and all other conditions must be verified against the controlled standard.

lessons.title: T05 — Penetration height datum and load interpretation
lessons.body:
## T05 — Penetration height datum and load interpretation

**Instruction.** A height variable must use its defined origin. Using floor-to-liquid height where the method calls for penetration-center-to-liquid height creates a different load. Read definitions before substitution. A hydrostatic local pressure comparison also does not establish reinforcement, weld or external-load acceptance.

**Record.** Maximum liquid level is 32 ft above floor; penetration center is 5 ft above floor; SG is .90. The supplied liquid-pressure comparison is p = .433 × G × h in psi. Use the centerline datum.

**Answer.** h = 27 ft, p = 10.5219 psi. Using 32 ft would give 12.4704 psi and would not follow the specified definition. In this comparison the wrong datum is conservative numerically, but that does not make it a valid application of every formula. A changed centerline of 8 ft gives h = 24 ft, p = 9.3528 psi.

**Reference task.** Read the corrected API 653 section 9.9.2 height definition and the applicable API 650/653 penetration detail. Record weld size, spacing, material and examination requirements from the exact detail selected; do not transfer a detail for a different penetration. Score datum 2, calculation 2, detail/scope 2.

lessons.title: T06 — Weld geometry measurement
lessons.body:
## T06 — Weld geometry measurement

**Instruction.** A fillet's leg size and effective throat are different dimensions. A weld gauge reading must correspond to the drawing's specified dimension. For an ideal equal-leg 45° fillet, theoretical throat = leg/√2; actual joint geometry, profile and code criteria still control.

**Record.** Drawing specifies an 8 mm leg. Measured leg is 6 mm. Technician writes “throat 6 mm, acceptable.”

**Answer.** An ideal 6 mm leg corresponds to 4.2426 mm theoretical throat, not 6 mm. The leg itself fails the supplied 8 mm requirement. The ideal 8 mm leg throat would be 5.6569 mm. Recheck the actual profile with the appropriate gauge/procedure; obtain correction and examination. A changed record has an 8 mm leg but undercut is noted: the leg-size pass does not dispose of undercut.

**Reference task.** Locate the selected tank joint detail and its actual weld/examination criteria. Identify whether the drawing calls for fillet dimensions or complete penetration. Score dimensional distinction 2, arithmetic 2, disposition 2.

lessons.title: T07 — Examination quality before acceptance
lessons.body:
## T07 — Examination quality before acceptance

**Instruction.** An image or indication can only support a decision within its technique capability. A missing quality control is not repaired by a favorable indication result. Preserve raw evidence and determine whether valid reevaluation or new examination is required.

**Record.** Synthetic RT procedure requires a visible specified IQI feature and density 2.0–4.0 for its selected film technique. Image A has density 2.6 but the feature is not visible. Image B has density 1.7 and a visible feature. Weld acceptance criteria are separately specified. These numerical limits are exercise inputs, not universal RT limits.

**Answer.** A fails required sensitivity evidence; B fails the supplied density band. Neither image supports acceptance merely because no defect is visible. Restore valid technique and required coverage, then apply the correct weld criteria. A changed image passes quality but shows a linear indication; characterize and evaluate it under the correct criteria rather than simply accepting the image.

**Reference task.** Locate ASME V Article 2's actual requirements for the selected technique and the tank standard's acceptance/coverage. For PT and MT, identify procedure, surface, illumination/field and timing controls and the actual acceptance basis. Score A 2, B 2, separation of quality/acceptance 2.

lessons.title: T08 — Controlled reference qualification review
lessons.body:
## T08 — Controlled reference qualification review

**Instruction.** An exam-oriented simplified qualification case is not an exhaustive qualification rule. For an actual review, identify process-specific variables, applicable thickness/deposit ranges, position and backing restrictions, required tests and additional tank requirements. Distinguish procedure qualification from performance qualification.

**Record.** Supplied PQR mechanical-test requirement: two tensile tests each ≥450 MPa and four bends meeting the approved criterion. Tensile values are 462 and 448 MPa; four bends are acceptable. WPS references PQR correctly; proposed production falls within the otherwise verified range.

**Answer.** The 448 MPa test fails the supplied criterion. Four passing bends and correct referencing do not cure that failure. Follow the actual permitted retest/disposition rules; do not average 462 and 448 to 455 and accept both. Changed values 455 and 460 pass the supplied tensile criterion, but one bend fails; the record still does not pass all required tests.

**Reference task.** Verify actual IX tensile/bend criteria and permitted retest conditions, including any applicable exception rather than assuming the supplied exercise criterion is universal. Identify additional tank standard requirements. Score individual test comparison 2, overall record decision 2, correct reference/authority 2.

lessons.title: Supplemental lab recording form
lessons.body:
## Supplemental lab recording form

Learner____ Lab____ Edition/sections____ Inputs verified____ Work with units____ Answer____ Scope/limits____

Scores__/2 __/2 __/2 Correction____ Changed case____ Assessor/date____

All eight labs must reach 6/6 after correction, including actual reference work. Count them within the scheduled controlled-reference and application blocks; do not add artificial attendance hours. The protected final remains separate.

lessons.title: VUC037 technical workshops and supplied records
lessons.body:
# VUC037 technical workshops and supplied records

All asset names, readings, project limits and approvals below are synthetic. A supplied limit is an exercise input, not a universal code requirement. Work each problem before reading its worked solution. For the controlled-reference portion, use authorized copies of the editions in the source register. Record section, table/figure, units, applicable notes and scope. A successful supplied-data calculation does not earn credit for a reference lookup that was not actually performed.

lessons.title: W01 — Shell loss, critical length and fill height
lessons.body:
## W01 — Shell loss, critical length and fill height

**Record D01.** T-371 is an 80 ft diameter welded tank. The localized assessment includes a vertical joint; the exercise explicitly supplies E = 0.85, S = 20,000 psi, G = 1.0 and required net thickness 0.200 in. Non-pit minimum t2 is 0.130 in. The authorized exercise calculation for critical length is L = min(3.7√(D × t2), 40), using D in feet and t2 in inches, with L in inches. Five equally spaced readings on each of two candidate vertical profiles cover L: A = [0.230, 0.210, 0.130, 0.220, 0.240]; B = [0.220, 0.200, 0.140, 0.210, 0.230]. Future loss over the proposed period is 0.010 in. The supplied acceptance exercise requires future average at least the required net thickness and future minimum at least 60 percent of it.

**Tasks.** Calculate L; choose the controlling profile; test current and future conditions; identify why a passing current condition may not support the proposed period. Use API 653 4.3.2–4.3.3 to verify applicability and any other conditions in an actual reference exercise.

**Worked solution.** L = 3.7√10.4 = 11.9321 in. Profile A average is 0.206 in and B is 0.200 in, so B controls the average. Current average meets 0.200 and current minimum 0.130 exceeds 0.120. Future B average is 0.190 and fails; future minimum is 0.120 and reaches the supplied lower limit. The future-average failure controls. The result cannot be rescued by averaging A and B together.

**Changed record.** B's third reading becomes 0.100. Its mean is 0.192 and the new minimum is 0.100. Both current criteria fail, and the critical length must be reconsidered using the changed minimum. It becomes 3.7√8 = 10.4652 in, so the old profile spacing/extent must be checked against the newly applicable evaluation length. Do not simply reuse an incompatible sampling arrangement.

**Reference completion record.** Edition____ Section____ geometry applicability____ joint-efficiency basis____ other loadings____ corrosion allowance treatment____ assessor____. Credit requires the actual lookup and explanation, not copying these prompts.

lessons.title: W02 — Pitting geometry and an independently failing ligament
lessons.body:
## W02 — Pitting geometry and an independently failing ligament

**Record D02.** The exercise assessment sheet gives required thickness 0.240 in. It permits the isolated-pit screening route only when the remaining ligament is at least max(0.120 in, half required thickness) and the sum of pit dimensions intersected along any assessed 8 in vertical line does not exceed 2.0 in. Line A intersects pits 0.4, 0.6 and 0.7 in long. Line B intersects 0.8, 0.7 and 0.6 in. The lowest remaining ligament is 0.125 in. There is no crack-like indication in the original record.

**Tasks.** Evaluate both lines and ligament. Explain whether a pass on line A disposes of line B. Verify actual applicability against API 653 4.3.2.2 before using this route outside the supplied exercise.

**Worked solution.** Required ligament is 0.120 in; 0.125 passes. A totals 1.7 in and passes; B totals 2.1 in and fails. The isolated-pit screening route does not accept this record. Map the failed line and obtain the permitted further assessment or repair. Pit count alone is irrelevant to this aggregate-length condition.

**Changed record.** B totals only 1.8 in, but the ligament becomes 0.110 in. The geometry change does not cure the ligament failure. If a later examination identifies a crack-like indication, stop using isolated-pit criteria for that indication and obtain characterization.

**Required output.** Scaled sketch with both lines and pits; table of each dimension; criterion calculation; disposition; missing evidence; actual reference row and notes.

lessons.title: W03 — Bottom projection with incomplete coverage
lessons.body:
## W03 — Bottom projection with incomplete coverage

**Record D03.** The bottom map divides 120 plates into 105 fully scanned plates, 10 partially scanned plates and five inaccessible plates. Selected indications were quantified under the approved procedure. Post-repair remaining values supplied for the evaluated region are RTbc = 0.190 in and RTip = 0.210 in. Top-side rate is 0.003 in/year; underside rate 0.005 in/year. Proposed interval is ten years. Supplied minimum for this region is 0.100 in. Separate annular/critical-zone evaluation remains required and is not supplied by this general-region calculation.

**Tasks.** Project the region's thickness, calculate the mathematical time to the supplied limit and write an honest coverage conclusion.

**Worked solution.** Starting lesser value is 0.190. Combined rate is 0.008. Ten-year projection is 0.110 in; time to 0.100 is 11.25 years. This is not a whole-bottom acceptance because the coverage record contains partial and inaccessible regions and the separate junction/annular review is unresolved. The procedure's screening and confirmation capability also matters. Do not call 105/120 = 87.5 percent of plates a precise percentage of bottom area; plate dimensions and partial coverage are not given.

**Changed record.** The underside rate is 0.008. Total rate becomes 0.011 and ten-year projection 0.080 in, failing the supplied minimum. Mathematical time becomes 8.1818 years before other constraints. A shorter interval still needs an applicable basis and authorization; this worksheet cannot authorize it.

**Required output.** Projection sheet, plate coverage register, separate unresolved-region list, proposed next inspection/engineering actions and the controlled-reference review of API 653 bottom and interval requirements.

lessons.title: W04 — Settlement survey integrity and chart selection
lessons.body:
## W04 — Settlement survey integrity and chart selection

**Record D04.** Tank diameter is 60 ft. The synthetic survey plan requires at least eight equally spaced circumferential points and no circumferential gap above 32 ft. Proposed points are eight equally spaced stations. A stable benchmark was checked before and after the survey. A local bottom depression near the shell has measured depth 42 mm over its defined 1.8 m profile. A second depression is remote from the shell, depth 35 mm over a defined 2.4 m profile. Weld orientation is known for the first but missing for the second. No acceptance-chart value is supplied.

**Tasks.** Check circumferential spacing; distinguish the two depression assessments; explain why a numerical pass/fail cannot be invented. Use API 653 Annex B and the relevant current figures to identify the actual evaluation routes and required dimensions.

**Worked solution.** Circumference is π × 60 = 188.496 ft. Eight gaps are approximately 23.562 ft, meeting the supplied spacing rule and eight-point minimum. That establishes only the proposed circumferential arrangement under this exercise rule. Near-shell and remote depressions require their own geometry and applicable method. Depth alone does not establish acceptability; missing geometry or weld conditions must be resolved before a chart is applied.

**Changed record.** Two adjacent stations were inaccessible, creating a gap spanning three intended intervals, approximately 70.686 ft. The record no longer meets the supplied 32 ft gap rule. Do not retain “eight-point survey complete” because the original plan listed eight points. Record actual coverage and arrange the required additional measurements.

**Required output.** Circumferential map; actual/omitted station list; datum check; liquid level; depression profiles; chosen figure and scope; numerical evaluation only after the authorized reference and all inputs support it. An assessor must not award a reference-calculation pass from this incomplete-data example alone; use the complete field/mockup dataset in the practical station.

lessons.title: W05 — Materials and qualification record audit
lessons.body:
## W05 — Materials and qualification record audit

**Record D05.** Proposed repair plate P-5 is 20 mm thick and identified by heat H537. Material certificate H537 matches the approved grade. The supplied impact requirement is mean ≥27 J, each ≥20 J at −10 °C; reported values at −10 °C are 28, 29 and 26 J. WPS W-5 references PQR P-5, which the exercise's controlled qualification sheet confirms supports the process and 6–24 mm base thickness. Welder K's record supports the process and position but has no current continuity evidence. The drawing specifies the same process and 20 mm plate.

**Tasks.** Separate passing material evidence from the open personnel qualification issue. Identify which record must not be rewritten to close the gap. During the reference portion, verify the actual material/toughness and IX ranges instead of treating supplied ranges as universal.

**Worked solution.** Impact mean is 83/3 = 27.667 J, and the minimum is 26 J; supplied energy criteria pass. Identity, test temperature and supplied procedure range agree. Welder continuity remains unresolved. Do not infer it from the procedure qualification or backdate a record. Obtain valid evidence or the required requalification before production work.

**Changed record.** The repair thickness changes to 28 mm. The supplied procedure range now also fails. Resolving continuity alone no longer makes the work ready. Preserve both open issues and obtain the appropriate approved qualification basis.

**Required output.** Material heat trace; impact calculation; WPS/PQR/WPQ comparison; actual code references; hold-point decision and affected weld list.

lessons.title: W06 — Repair layout and NDE traceability
lessons.body:
## W06 — Repair layout and NDE traceability

**Record D06.** The synthetic approved drawing calls for a 400 × 500 mm replacement detail, 100 mm minimum separation from feature F, specified full-penetration joints and complete examination of new weld W6 under procedure N6. The proposed plate is 400 × 500 mm with 110 mm separation. The W6 length is 1,800 mm. Report N6-1 identifies W6 and covers 0–800 mm; N6-2 covers 900–1,800 mm. Both reports give acceptable results for their covered segments.

**Tasks.** Check dimensions and identify the examination gap. Explain why the sum of two accepted reports is not complete acceptance.

**Worked solution.** Supplied dimensions and spacing pass. The interval 800–900 mm is not covered, a 100 mm gap. Obtain required examination or a valid corrected coverage record supported by original evidence. Do not overlap report labels on paper without actual examination. Verify procedure, personnel, technique quality and referencing acceptance criteria before relying on the results.

**Changed record.** Complete coverage is established, but N6-2 identifies weld W9. Resolve weld identity from the raw examination and location records. Merely typing W6 into the report is not valid closure without that evidence.

**Required output.** Weld map, examination intervals, unresolved identity/coverage register, actual repair/NDE reference requirements and closure evidence. For RT, include the technique-quality review; for PT/MT, include surface and process controls.

lessons.title: W07 — Testing and the water-load decision
lessons.body:
## W07 — Testing and the water-load decision

**Record D07.** Tank diameter 24 m, proposed water depth 12 m, water density 1,000 kg/m³. The approved test plan has staged fill levels, maximum permitted differential movement of 8 mm between designated survey points at a stage, and requires the named engineering review if exceeded. At the second stage the difference is 11 mm. No exemption from hydrotesting has been approved.

**Tasks.** Calculate water volume/mass at full depth for scale; decide what the second-stage observation requires; distinguish a test waiver request from an approved exemption.

**Worked solution.** Volume = π × 12² × 12 = 5,428.672 m³, mass approximately 5.429 million kg. At the stage, 11 exceeds the supplied 8 mm stop criterion. Follow the approved stop/safe-condition response and obtain review. The full-volume calculation does not authorize continued filling. A request to replace the hydrotest with a leak check is pending until the applicable exemption conditions and required approvals are satisfied.

**Changed record.** Movement is 6 mm but a leak appears at a repaired junction. The movement pass does not override the leak response. Apply the plan's leak stop condition, preserve location and level data and obtain repair/retest disposition.

**Required output.** Test readiness sheet, water-load arithmetic, stage log, stop decision, responsible contacts, test exemption status and restoration checklist.

lessons.title: W08 — Integrated release with incompatible settings
lessons.body:
## W08 — Integrated release with incompatible settings

**Record D08.** Approved shell review supports maximum level 22 ft at SG ≤0.90. Bottom interval is approved for six years under stated conditions. Roof and vent records are complete. Repair action A8 is verified closed. The current control-system level limit is 24 ft; the operating instruction says 23 ft. The next receipt is SG 0.95. No change-of-service approval exists.

**Tasks.** Identify every contradiction, write the release decision and describe the records required to close it. Do not solve the issue by choosing the lowest displayed level and assuming the denser product is acceptable.

**Worked solution.** Both configured and written levels exceed the approved 22 ft. The proposed SG exceeds 0.90. The approved condition does not cover the planned receipt. Hold the proposed release/receipt under the responsible operating process, reconcile controls and instructions and obtain service-change engineering review. Keep the favorable bottom/roof/vent records; they are valid evidence for their scope, not permission to ignore these conflicts.

**Changed record.** Service remains SG 0.90 and both limits are corrected to 22 ft, but the change has not been independently verified in the active controls. Release stays pending that required verification and authorization. A screenshot of a draft configuration is not proof of the operating configuration.

**Required output.** One-page disposition with identity, operating envelope, passing evidence, open actions, owners, required verification and final authorization field. Record the result as a simulation, not a real tank release.


---

lessons.title: VUC037 mechanism and repair decisions
lessons.body:
# VUC037 mechanism and repair decisions

These original cases extend Q16 and Q20. Answer before reading the discussion. For each case record (a) evidence and plausible mechanism, (b) suitable next examination or assessment and (c) disposition/authority limits. Score each part 0–2; require 5/6 and no critical unsafe or fabricated-acceptance decision. Correct missed reasoning and attempt the changed condition. Cases are synthetic; none authorizes actual work.

lessons.title: M01 — Atmospheric corrosion beneath a damaged coating
lessons.body:
## M01 — Atmospheric corrosion beneath a damaged coating

A shell has a streak of rust below a failed coating edge. The remaining coating looks sound nearby. Operations asks for paint touch-up only. What evidence should precede that work?

**Discussion.** Map the visible condition, assess substrate loss and determine whether moisture has migrated beneath apparently intact coating. Repairing appearance without evaluating steel can hide the condition from the next inspection. Select preparation/examination that safely establishes extent, then apply the approved coating repair after steel disposition. Do not infer a rate from one observation. **Changed condition:** a similar stain originates from an upper leaking nozzle. Investigate the source as well as the coated surface; coating repair alone does not close the leak.

lessons.title: M02 — Brittle-fracture concern during colder service
lessons.body:
## M02 — Brittle-fracture concern during colder service

An old tank has reliable thickness records but incomplete material toughness documentation. The proposed winter service is colder than documented history. Is adequate thickness enough?

**Discussion.** No. Establish the applicable brittle-fracture evaluation, material/thickness/temperature facts and permitted assessment route. Existing service history describes its actual conditions, not every colder condition. Review before filling or testing. Do not improvise a cold hydrotest as a way to find out. **Changed condition:** material certificates are recovered but concern a different heat. Identity remains unresolved; an available certificate is not automatically the right certificate.

lessons.title: M03 — Caustic metal loss after an upset
lessons.body:
## M03 — Caustic metal loss after an upset

A caustic tank shows new localized thinning after an elevated-temperature event. The prior uniform rate was low. What changes in the evaluation?

**Discussion.** Treat the upset as potentially changing the corrosion basis. Confirm comparable measurements, map extent, establish actual chemistry/temperature history and obtain competent mechanism review. Future prediction must address the new condition. Do not average away recent rapid loss by using a much longer benign period. **Changed condition:** thickness is stable but a linear weld indication appears; move to cracking characterization rather than extending a wall-loss calculation.

lessons.title: M04 — Caustic cracking near a repair
lessons.body:
## M04 — Caustic cracking near a repair

A repair weld area in caustic service has fine branched surface indications. The repair's heat-treatment and procedure records are incomplete. What should the report avoid?

**Discussion.** Avoid declaring the indications cosmetic or accepting them from thickness. Preserve morphology/location, review weld/service/stress history and use suitable crack-sensitive examination with qualified interpretation. Establish the applicable engineering disposition. The appearance suggests a concern, not a definitive diagnosis by itself. **Changed condition:** PT was performed over contamination. Technique validity is unresolved; a negative report does not establish absence of cracks.

lessons.title: M05 — Concentration-cell conditions under deposits
lessons.body:
## M05 — Concentration-cell conditions under deposits

Bottom deposits cover regions near a water draw-off. Spot readings on clean exposed steel are satisfactory. Can those readings represent the covered areas?

**Discussion.** Deposits can create local environmental differences and conceal attack. Plan safe cleaning and suitable mapped examination of the affected regions; retain useful deposit/service evidence for mechanism review. The clean-region readings are valid only for their represented locations. **Changed condition:** cleaning exposes deep scattered pits. Characterize remaining thickness and extent using the applicable bottom assessment rather than substituting a shell-pit rule.

lessons.title: M06 — Corrosion under insulation
lessons.body:
## M06 — Corrosion under insulation

Water staining and damaged jacketing appear around a tank penetration. External readings were taken only on an exposed lower band. What is missing?

**Discussion.** The hidden area around the damaged weather barrier is not represented by the exposed band. Review wetting paths and temperature history, select targeted insulation removal or a suitable qualified method and establish extent. Include supports and penetrations where water may collect. Restore the weather barrier after inspection and steel disposition. **Changed condition:** new jacketing has been installed without inspection records. New appearance does not prove the concealed steel was examined.

lessons.title: M07 — Ethanol-service cracking concern
lessons.body:
## M07 — Ethanol-service cracking concern

A tank changed to ethanol-containing service. A recent linear indication is near a weld. The old product's inspection plan used only sparse thickness readings. What should change?

**Discussion.** Review service-specific cracking susceptibility, material and stress history and select appropriate examination with competent corrosion input. Sparse thickness readings may be poorly suited to cracking. Do not apply the old product's mechanism assumptions unchanged. **Changed condition:** no indication has yet been found, but the change review never occurred. Absence of a known defect does not remove the need to review credible mechanisms and inspection strategy.

lessons.title: M08 — Suspected MIC
lessons.body:
## M08 — Suspected MIC

Pits are found beneath sludge and water. Someone labels them “MIC” from a photograph and orders a biocide. What is a more defensible response?

**Discussion.** Preserve relevant samples through the appropriate sampling process, examine service/water history and consider other mechanisms. A mechanism hypothesis does not replace thickness/extent evaluation. A chemical treatment decision needs competent review and does not restore lost metal. **Changed condition:** sampling finds organisms but the pit morphology and chemistry suggest multiple contributors. Record a combined or uncertain diagnosis rather than forcing a single explanation.

lessons.title: M09 — Soil-side loss with CP outage
lessons.body:
## M09 — Soil-side loss with CP outage

The rectifier was off for months and a later bottom survey finds underside loss. Can restoring power close the finding?

**Discussion.** Restore and verify protection through competent personnel, but separately evaluate current metal loss, coverage and a justified future rate. Review foundation moisture, shielding and actual protection distribution. Power restoration is an action, not an integrity disposition. **Changed condition:** rectifier operated throughout, but only one perimeter reading exists. Operating status does not prove protection beneath the entire bottom.

lessons.title: M10 — Sulfuric-acid concentration change
lessons.body:
## M10 — Sulfuric-acid concentration change

A dilution event is followed by thinning near the mixing region. The operator says sulfuric acid tanks are normally stable. What evidence matters?

**Discussion.** Actual concentration, temperature, mixing and exposure history matter more than a generic service label. Map local loss and obtain competent review of the changed environment and materials. Revise future assumptions only with evidence. **Changed condition:** bulk samples have returned to normal but the affected region was exposed during the upset. Present chemistry does not erase historical damage or establish its extent.

lessons.title: R01 — Replacement shell plate and hidden design changes
lessons.body:
## R01 — Replacement shell plate and hidden design changes

A corroded area is removed and a thicker replacement is proposed “for extra strength.” The original material grade is uncertain. **Discussion.** Thickness alone does not resolve material, toughness, weld, fit-up, stress and geometry requirements. Use the approved replacement design and material traceability. The thicker plate may change welding and transition requirements. **Changed condition:** material is correct but plate corners differ from the approved detail; obtain design disposition rather than improvising.

lessons.title: R02 — Lap patch near an existing feature
lessons.body:
## R02 — Lap patch near an existing feature

A patch meets its proposed thickness but overlaps a feature that the selected detail excludes. **Discussion.** Every applicability condition matters. Identify location and geometric conflict, obtain the correct repair design and check associated examination/testing. A patch is not accepted merely because its welds look good. **Changed condition:** the patch is moved clear but no longer covers the mapped damaged area; recheck the entire repair objective.

lessons.title: R03 — Shell-to-bottom weld repair
lessons.body:
## R03 — Shell-to-bottom weld repair

A linear indication is found at the junction during repair preparation. **Discussion.** Characterize and disposition it under the applicable requirements, including effects of local geometry and settlement. Do not weld over an uncharacterized crack to hide it. Establish excavation, verification, repair welding and final examination hold points. **Changed condition:** the crack is removed but the remaining section is below the approved repair basis; removal verification does not establish structural adequacy.

lessons.title: R04 — Bottom patch versus general bottom acceptance
lessons.body:
## R04 — Bottom patch versus general bottom acceptance

A patch closes one leak, but widespread underside loss remains elsewhere. **Discussion.** The local repair addresses its defined area. Reassess the remaining bottom and interval; leak closure does not validate all unexamined plates. Preserve the repair map and separate whole-bottom evaluation. **Changed condition:** leak test passes but a required weld examination is missing; both records must be resolved according to the repair plan.

lessons.title: R05 — Roof repair and support condition
lessons.body:
## R05 — Roof repair and support condition

New roof sheets are installed while corroded supports remain. **Discussion.** New surface material does not restore the complete load path. Evaluate supports, connections and loads under the repair design; establish safe access independently. **Changed condition:** supports are repaired but a floating roof compartment remains untested; do not transfer a fixed-roof completion checklist to a floating-roof system.

lessons.title: R06 — Nozzle replacement with external piping loads
lessons.body:
## R06 — Nozzle replacement with external piping loads

A replacement nozzle matches size and pressure rating, but the connected pipe is misaligned and installers plan to pull it into place. **Discussion.** Check alignment and external-load implications under the approved design. Do not use force to make a connection and then ignore induced loads. Inspect weld/reinforcement and testing requirements. **Changed condition:** alignment is corrected but wrong material is discovered; dimensional fit does not establish material acceptance.

lessons.title: R07 — Foundation leveling
lessons.body:
## R07 — Foundation leveling

The tank is releveled and the shell appears rounder. A previously strained bottom region remains. **Discussion.** Correcting position does not necessarily remove accumulated plastic deformation or cracking. Evaluate affected steel, junctions, nozzles and supports before acceptance. The leveling plan needs competent engineering and controlled stages. **Changed condition:** survey improves but a connected pipe now binds; evaluate the complete system, not just tank elevations.

lessons.title: R08 — Temporary access opening
lessons.body:
## R08 — Temporary access opening

A large shell opening is proposed to accelerate cleaning. **Discussion.** Establish the applicable door-sheet or access-opening requirements, temporary structural support, cutting sequence, material control, weld restoration, examination and testing before work. Convenience does not make the cut minor. **Changed condition:** the original plate is reused but traceability or edge condition was lost; resolve those facts rather than calling reuse automatic.

lessons.title: R09 — Hydrotest exemption request
lessons.body:
## R09 — Hydrotest exemption request

The contractor asks to omit a hydrotest because water disposal is expensive. **Discussion.** Cost explains a request, not eligibility. Evaluate the actual permitted exemption route, required engineering/owner approvals and substitute examination conditions. Until satisfied, the required test remains in scope. **Changed condition:** an engineer's email supports review but the required owner authorization is absent; distinguish recommendation from completed authorization.

lessons.title: R10 — Reconstruction at a new site
lessons.body:
## R10 — Reconstruction at a new site

The rebuilt tank uses traceable plates but the new site has different wind/seismic conditions and a colder climate. **Discussion.** The new conditions require the applicable design review. An old successful operating history cannot stand for the new loading envelope. Preserve dimensional, material, weld, examination and test records in the new dossier. **Changed condition:** engineering completes the new review but operations retains the old limits; reconcile and verify the active instructions and controls.

lessons.title: Applied-case record
lessons.body:
## Applied-case record

Learner____ Case____ Evidence/mechanism____ Examination/assessment____ Decision and authority____

Scores__/2 __/2 __/2 Critical finding____ Correction____ Changed-condition response____ Assessor/date____

All 20 cases are required. They use the existing teaching/application time allocation and do not constitute 20 additional field qualifications.

lessons.title: VUC037 printable station records

# VUC037 printable station records

Use these fictional records with the practical instructions. They are supplied exercise inputs, not real approvals. Blank response fields are learner recording forms, not missing instructional content. Instrument truth values must be established on the actual training equipment by the assessor; do not invent field measurements in advance.

lessons.title: D09 — Identity reconciliation packet for P01
lessons.body:
## D09 — Identity reconciliation packet for P01

| Document | Tank tag | Diameter | Material/history claim | Traceability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Nameplate photo transcript NP37|T-37|60 ft|No readable grade|Photo shows tag and diameter clearly|
|Drawing GA37 rev 2|T-37|64 ft|Unspecified shell grade|Drawing identity matches; geometry conflicts|
|Alteration AL19|T-73|60 ft|Plate replaced in 2019|Different asset; cannot establish T-37 history|
|Field note FN37|T-37|Measurement pending|No material identification performed|Does not resolve diameter or grade|

Learner must write verified facts, disagreements, excluded evidence and affected decisions. Assessor answer: identity is T-37; diameter conflict and material unknown remain; AL19 is not valid alteration evidence for T-37. Do not fill stress/toughness inputs from AL19.

lessons.title: D10 — Tabletop entry permit record for P04
lessons.body:
## D10 — Tabletop entry permit record for P04

Tank T-37 is emptied. Isolation checklist: not verified. Atmospheric reading: yesterday morning, no current test. Ventilation: planned, not confirmed operating. Rescue arrangements: no current briefing recorded. Task request: “enter for two final UT readings.” Responsible permit authority: site entry supervisor. No permit is issued by this record.

Assessor injects verbally: “A worker is unresponsive just inside.” Expected response: prevent unprotected entry, activate the established emergency/rescue process and account for personnel. Do not prompt the learner to physically enter any space. Changed record: valid permit originally issued, ventilation now fails; withdraw and reassess under the procedure.

lessons.title: D11 — Weld map and technique record for P19/P20
lessons.body:
## D11 — Weld map and technique record for P19/P20

W6 starts at station 0 mm and ends at 1800 mm. Report N6-1 covers 0–800 mm, report N6-2 covers 900–1800 mm. Both name W6 and report no rejectable indications in their examined portions. The required coverage is the full weld. Technique sheet RT6 says required IQI identification: **not recorded**. Image-to-location markers: present for the two reported segments. Acceptance reference: synthetic drawing DR6 and its approved examination specification. No conclusion about the missing interval is provided.

```text
W6: 0----------------800   900----------------------1800 mm
    [      N6-1       ] GAP [        N6-2             ]
```

Assessor answer:100 mm unexamined interval and unresolved technique-quality evidence; favorable portion results do not establish complete acceptance. Changed report N6-2 names W9: identity also requires resolution.

Repair drawing DR6 for the layout exercise only: plate 400×500 mm; separation from featureF at least 100 mm, measured edge-to-edge as drawn; proposed 110 mm. Required full-penetration joints and examination per the supplied plan. Do not infer real code dimensions from this synthetic drawing.

lessons.title: D12 — Corrosion-protection and lining records
lessons.body:
## D12 — Corrosion-protection and lining records

CP37 project criterion calls for designated instant-off measurements at locationsCP1–CP4. Available record: one on-reading at perimeterCP0; reference-electrode check absent; rectifier power lamp on. No acceptance potential is supplied. Expected result: method/location/equipment evidence insufficient, competent corrosion review and required valid measurements needed. A numeric criterion must not be invented.

L37 lining project sheet: steel at least 3°C above dew point; DFT400–600 micrometers; specified cure verification required before service. As-found: steel 22°C, dew point 20°C; DFT430,570,650 micrometers; cure field unverified. Expected: environment and one thickness reading fail; cure unresolved. Changed record: steel 24°C/dew point 20°C and all DFT500, but cure still unverified—release remains pending cure.

lessons.title: D13 — Twelve reconstruction segment cards
lessons.body:
## D13 — Twelve reconstruction segment cards

Print/cut rows as cards for P21. The card identity is the exercise evidence; no actual steel is represented.

lessons.title: D14 — Test stage log
lessons.body:
## D14 — Test stage log

Use with D07/P22. The supplied project stop trigger is differential movement above 8 mm between the designated points. Stage 1 records 5 mm, no leak. Stage 2 records 11 mm, no leak. Stage 3 is **not performed**. Exemption request EX37 is “submitted for review,” with no approval. Expected result: apply stop/safe-condition procedure at stage 2 and obtain review; do not enter a stage 3 result or call the exemption approved.

Changed log: stage 2 movement 6 mm, visible leak at repaired junction J2. Apply the leak response despite the movement passing its supplied threshold. This packet does not prescribe a real fill/drain sequence; the actual approved test plan controls.

lessons.title: D15 — Dossier audit and action register
lessons.body:

lessons.body:

lessons.title: VUC037 supplementary bottom-examination qualification case
lessons.body:
# VUC037 supplementary bottom-examination qualification case

Use with Q09, P09 and T07. This is a document-review exercise, not scanner-personnel qualification. Keep its result distinct from operating a scanner successfully on a physical test plate.

lessons.title: Instruction
lessons.body:
## Instruction

RP 575 Annex D is an informative qualification framework. The owner and inspection organization establish the applicable requirements. Review the procedure, equipment configuration and individual examiner's demonstrated scope together. A scanning-only demonstration does not establish prove-up competence. Records must preserve tested variables, results and the responsible sign-offs. Changes outside the qualified scope require disposition before field use. Apply Addendum 2 to the Addendum 1 text; do not retain superseded variable classifications.

lessons.title: Synthetic packet K37
lessons.body:
## Synthetic packet K37

The owner-approved exercise specification requires detection of at least nine of ten designated severe-loss features, location error no greater than 40 mm and agreement within 0.4 mm for all four designated prove-up measurements. These are supplied project criteria, not a reproduction of API acceptance tables. The signed demonstration record identifies scanner A, procedure B revision 3 and examiner C. It covers scanning only. Lift-off was 2 mm; speed was 0.20 m/s. No alternative settings are documented as qualified.

The proposed job uses the same scanner and examiner, procedure B revision 4, lift-off 4 mm and speed 0.35 m/s. Revision 4 changes those settings. A planning note says, “Same equipment, so the old record applies.” The examiner is also listed as performing prove-up, but no prove-up qualification record is attached.

Demonstration results supplied for analysis:

| Measure | Result |
|---|---|
| Designated severe-loss features detected | 8 of 10 |
| Largest location error | 55 mm |
| Reference remaining thicknesses | 2.0, 2.8, 3.4, 4.2 mm |
| Reported remaining thicknesses | 2.2, 3.3, 3.1, 4.3 mm |

lessons.title: Learner task
lessons.body:
## Learner task

Write a readiness decision covering demonstrated scope, changed settings, missing personnel evidence and each numerical criterion. Identify the records needed to resolve the issues. Do not create a signature or infer a pass. Then explain why correcting the numerical results would not automatically resolve the changed settings.

lessons.title: Worked response
lessons.body:
## Worked response

The packet does not support readiness. Eight of ten is 80%, below the supplied 90% requirement. The location error exceeds 40 mm. Absolute thickness errors are 0.2, 0.5, 0.3 and 0.1 mm; the second exceeds 0.4 mm. The old record also does not demonstrate the revised configuration or prove-up scope. Obtain the responsible qualification review and required demonstrations, with the approved procedure revision, tested settings, examiner scope, results and signatures recorded. Retain the original failed results.

lessons.title: Changed case and answer
lessons.body:
## Changed case and answer

New results detect ten of ten, maximum location error is 30 mm and all thickness errors are 0.3 mm or less. The examiner's prove-up record remains absent and the revised settings still lack qualification disposition. The numerical portion now meets the supplied criteria, but readiness remains unsupported. Numerical improvement cannot supply missing scope evidence.

lessons.title: Assessment record
lessons.body:
## Assessment record

Score six decisions 0–2: detection arithmetic; location comparison; four thickness-error calculations; scope separation; changed-variable disposition; traceable resolution records. Pass 10/12 with no unsupported qualification or field-release claim. Correct a missed decision and repeat the changed case before closing this learning exercise.

Learner____ Assessor____ Date____ Six scores____ Critical error____ Remediation____ Changed response____ Final result____

Primary references: API RP 575 fifth edition, Addendum 1 (July 2025), Annex D, and Addendum 2 (June 2026). Consult the current controlled documents for real qualification criteria and variable ranges. The synthetic criteria above do not replace them.


---

content.title: VUC037 | VUC037 delivery guide and practical assessment packet
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program.
