Chemistry, temperature, alloy and hydrodynamics interact. NRC and OECD guidance distinguish FAC from mechanical erosion. [S06] Surface appearance is useful evidence, not a complete diagnosis.

Examine elbows, reducers, downstream restrictions, impingement regions and representative straight runs as required by the mechanism model. Changing flow velocity or materials without checking process performance and other mechanisms can exchange one problem for another. Restoration of nominal thickness does not correct the flow condition.

**Worked decision.** A carbon-steel wet-steam elbow thins without solids in the stream. Lack of abrasive particles does not eliminate FAC. Review water chemistry, steam condition, material and flow distribution, and map susceptible components.

**Transfer.** A pump casing with noise and pitted impeller regions may need cavitation investigation, not merely an inhibitor increase.

lessons.title: Q20 — Dissimilar joints, liquid metals and fabrication interactions
lessons.body:
## Q20 — Dissimilar joints, liquid metals and fabrication interactions

Dissimilar-metal joints combine materials with different thermal expansion, properties and environmental responses. Weld metallurgy, transition geometry and thermal cycling can create local concerns. A joint may have passed fabrication examination yet develop service-related damage later. Separate original fabrication imperfections from deterioration occurring in service, while recognizing that an imperfection can initiate later damage.

Liquid-metal embrittlement is a material/environment-specific interaction in which contact with a liquid metal can produce severe loss of ductility under relevant conditions. Contamination by low-melting metals during fabrication or maintenance therefore deserves control. Do not infer compatibility from the fact that a contaminant amount seems small. Specialized evaluation is required when suspected.

Reheat-related cracking and dissimilar-metal weld cracking require attention to alloy, weld heat treatment, residual stress and service history. A generic surface examination cannot answer every metallurgical question. Preserve consumable, procedure, heat-treatment and repair records so the specialist can reconstruct the actual condition.

**Worked decision.** A hot-service dissimilar joint develops indications after repeated starts. Review differential expansion and weld history as well as corrosion candidates. Replacing one side with a stronger alloy without reviewing the joint can leave the initiating condition unchanged.

**Transfer.** A maintenance contaminant is discovered before restart. Hold the affected decision for a material-specific evaluation instead of assuming cleaning the visible surface closes the issue.

lessons.title: Q21 — Refractory, linings and nonmetallic degradation
lessons.body:
## Q21 — Refractory, linings and nonmetallic degradation

Refractory and linings protect equipment by controlling exposure or temperature, but they can themselves crack, detach, erode or chemically degrade. Their failure may expose a shell to conditions outside its intended envelope. A cold outer surface in one location is not proof of continuous lining integrity elsewhere.

Polymers and composites can degrade through chemical attack, swelling, permeation, aging, ultraviolet exposure, thermal cycling or mechanical loading. Material family names alone are insufficient for compatibility. Resin, reinforcement, cure, temperature and service chemistry can all matter. A steel-wall corrosion technique may not be suitable for a composite or lined component.

Inspection should distinguish the protective layer's condition from the substrate's condition. Repairs need the specified preparation, cure and quality checks. Recoating over contamination or an unassessed crack may hide damage. A holiday test detects particular coating discontinuities under a specified procedure; it does not prove chemical compatibility or structural capacity.

**Worked decision.** A vessel has a new exterior hot spot after an internal refractory repair. Treat the change as evidence requiring investigation and operating review. The repair's completion date is not evidence that the substrate stayed within its temperature limit.

**Transfer.** A lining that passes a discontinuity test can still be unsuitable for a new chemical service. Review compatibility separately.

lessons.title: Q22 — Match inspection to the question
lessons.body:
## Q22 — Match inspection to the question

Write the question before ordering the method: Is wall missing? Is there a surface-connected crack? Is there internal separation? Has the microstructure changed? Is the alloy correct? A method's name is not its capability statement. Geometry, surface preparation, temperature, access, material, flaw orientation, equipment, procedure and operator qualification affect performance.

Visual examination establishes accessible surface condition. Thickness methods sample or map wall under their stated limitations. Surface crack methods detect particular surface or near-surface conditions depending on the technique and material. Volumetric methods can examine internal regions, but coverage and sensitivity are not universal. Chemistry, hardness, metallography and mechanical testing answer additional, different questions.

HSE's NDT guidance stresses matching techniques to damage and recognizing their limits. [S07] A useful report states what was examined, with what procedure, what was found, what could not be examined and what follow-up is required. “No defects” without that context is an unsafe overstatement. Independent review is needed when results conflict with a credible mechanism or process evidence.

**Worked decision.** A report says “UT satisfactory,” but contains only six thickness points on a vessel susceptible to weld cracking. It does not demonstrate a crack examination. Request the actual method/coverage and plan the missing examination.

**Transfer.** A more expensive instrument does not remove the need for a suitable procedure and qualified interpretation.

lessons.title: Q23 — Operating windows, change and mitigation
lessons.body:
## Q23 — Operating windows, change and mitigation

An integrity operating window links a monitored process condition to a damage concern and a defined response. It needs an engineering basis, measurement location, units, responsible role, response time and escalation path. An alarm with no action owner is not a complete control. A window exceedance is evidence to investigate, not automatic proof of damage or automatic proof that equipment is safe afterward.

Management of change must consider feed, chemical treatment, pressure, temperature, throughput, phase distribution, materials, repairs, insulation, instrumentation and operating modes. Temporary changes can matter as much as permanent ones. Include startup and shutdown. Review whether existing inspection locations still represent the altered service.

Mitigation may remove exposure, improve materials, control stress, manage chemistry, restore protective systems or change operation. Verify effectiveness with appropriate evidence. Inspection detects some damage; it does not itself prevent the mechanism. Deferring an action requires the proper authorized risk decision and controls, not a training exercise's score.

**Worked decision.** A chloride alert clears after one normal sample. The event still requires review of duration, local concentration, susceptible materials and inspection needs. Record the excursion and disposition rather than deleting it from history.

**Transfer.** Replacing a failed sensor restores monitoring but does not reconstruct the unmeasured exposure. State the uncertainty and assessment needed.

lessons.title: Q24 — Produce a defensible integrity handover
lessons.body:
## Q24 — Produce a defensible integrity handover

The final review should let another competent person reconstruct the decision. Identify the asset, service period, sources, candidate mechanisms, exclusions with reasons, inspection evidence, uncertainties, required controls, outstanding actions and responsible approvers. Link each significant conclusion to evidence. Separate an observation from an interpretation and an interpretation from an authorization.

Prioritize active leaks, crack-like findings, unexpected rapid loss and conditions outside the established basis through the site's emergency and integrity procedures. Personnel should not approach a leak to collect a better measurement merely to complete a course task. Preserve records and samples safely. Similar-service equipment may require review even when the first finding is isolated to one asset.

A good handover includes disagreement. If process history suggests a mechanism that the examination could not detect, retain the concern and specify the next step. If a mechanism is excluded, state the evidence and the change that would reopen it. A final signature cannot cure missing evidence; it identifies responsibility for an actual decision.

**Worked decision.** The inspection team finds localized loss, operations reports an unrecorded feed change and the maintenance file contains an unverified replacement spool. The handover must combine all three. A wall-loss repair alone does not close material identification or the new service review.

**Transfer.** Write a one-paragraph handover containing a verified fact, a credible mechanism, an uncertainty, an immediate restriction and an owner for follow-up. Avoid declaring an asset fit for service unless the authorized assessment actually establishes that result.


---

courses.title: VUC038 | Specialist mechanism clinics — VUC038

content.title: VUC038 | Specialist mechanism clinics — VUC038
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: Specialist mechanism clinics — VUC038
lessons.body:
# Specialist mechanism clinics — VUC038

These clinics extend the course's grouped chapters. They teach recognition and the evidence needed for specialist disposition. They do not supply unverified API temperature bands, material-selection tables, inspection intervals or chemical-treatment recipes. Each exercise requires a written response; the worked decision is supplied for formative review.

lessons.title: C01 — Ethanol service and cracking
lessons.body:
## C01 — Ethanol service and cracking

Fuel-grade ethanol service can introduce stress corrosion cracking concerns for susceptible steel equipment. It is not adequately screened by saying that the product is less corrosive than an acid. Composition, contaminants, oxygen, stress and operating history require a service-specific assessment. PHMSA-sponsored research documents ethanol-related SCC concerns; NIST research also addresses environmentally assisted fatigue behavior. Those findings are not a universal acceptance rule for every ethanol blend. [S11,S12]

**Exercise.** A carbon-steel tank changes from petroleum product to ethanol service. Its thickness is satisfactory but weld condition and new-service compatibility are unreviewed. **Worked decision:** hold the service-change approval, review material/stress and environment, and specify suitable cracking coverage. A good wall reading does not resolve the new mechanism. **Changed case:** a low-contaminant sample arrives; it establishes only that sample's chemistry, not all future conditions or existing crack condition.

lessons.title: C02 — Polythionic-acid SCC during shutdown
lessons.body:
## C02 — Polythionic-acid SCC during shutdown

Sulfide-containing deposits, air and moisture can produce a damaging shutdown environment for susceptible sensitized stainless material. The exposure can occur when the normal process is no longer running. Metal temperature, material history and scale condition influence the review. MTI's bulletin describes the shutdown reaction and cracking concern. [S08] Prevention must be planned before opening; this course does not prescribe a universal wash or neutralization mixture.

**Exercise.** A hot sulfur-service stainless exchanger is opened to humid air after years of service. “No corrosion in service” is offered as clearance. **Worked decision:** evaluate sensitization, deposits and the shutdown exposure; apply the approved prevention and examination plan. **Changed case:** low-carbon material is documented. That is relevant evidence, not automatic proof that every fabrication and exposure issue is resolved.

lessons.title: C03 — Titanium hydriding and contamination
lessons.body:
## C03 — Titanium hydriding and contamination

Titanium's good performance in many environments does not make it immune to hydrogen-related degradation. Hydrogen can affect properties through material-specific mechanisms, including hydride formation. Welding and cleaning history matter. TWI identifies hydrogen-related degradation and the importance of contamination control in titanium work. [S09] An alloy-chemistry reading does not establish retained ductility or hydride absence.

**Exercise.** A titanium component becomes brittle after an undocumented cleaning operation. **Worked decision:** preserve the history and sample, investigate chemical exposure and hydrogen-related damage with a specialist, and do not authorize re-use from thickness alone. **Changed case:** the cleaning contractor says the process was used successfully on steel. That is not evidence of titanium compatibility.

lessons.title: C04 — Oxygen service and ignition damage
lessons.body:
## C04 — Oxygen service and ignition damage

An oxygen system needs compatible materials, cleanliness and controlled ignition hazards. A component acceptable in air can be unsuitable in oxygen-rich service. Seals, lubricants, particles, compression heating and mechanical contact require system-specific review. NASA and HSE guidance treat compatibility as an end-use assessment, not a property inferred from appearance. [S10,S13]

**Exercise.** A regulator receives a visually identical replacement seal with no oxygen-service traceability. **Worked decision:** do not use it until compatibility and the approved replacement basis are established. **Changed case:** the pressure rating matches; this resolves pressure rating only, not ignition compatibility or cleanliness. No classroom oxygen ignition experiment is permitted.

lessons.title: C05 — Temper embrittlement versus softening
lessons.body:
## C05 — Temper embrittlement versus softening

Temper embrittlement concerns a loss of toughness in susceptible alloy/thermal histories, not necessarily a large decrease in hardness. Softening through other microstructural changes can affect strength. A learner must identify the property under question before choosing evidence. A satisfactory tensile strength or hardness value alone is not a complete toughness assessment.

**Exercise.** An aged low-alloy vessel has normal thickness and hardness; cold startup is proposed. **Worked decision:** review thermal history, toughness and the approved brittle-fracture/startup basis. **Changed case:** new hardness data agree with old values. The toughness question remains. Explain the different information supplied by hardness, impact data and structural assessment.

lessons.title: C06 — Sigma phase and 475°C embrittlement
lessons.body:
## C06 — Sigma phase and 475°C embrittlement

Different alloy systems can undergo different embrittling transformations. Sigma-phase formation and 475°C embrittlement are not interchangeable labels or proof that every alloy held at the named temperature fails. Composition, phase balance, time and thermal history determine susceptibility. Welds and heat-affected zones may have a different history from base material. Examination must establish the relevant microstructural/property condition.

**Exercise.** A duplex component has an undocumented high-temperature excursion. **Worked decision:** obtain actual exposure and fabrication records, request a qualified material-specific evaluation and do not infer fitness from corrosion resistance alone. **Changed case:** chemistry matches the specified grade. Grade identification does not establish phase balance or retained toughness.

lessons.title: C07 — Graphitization versus graphitic corrosion
lessons.body:
## C07 — Graphitization versus graphitic corrosion

Graphitization of susceptible steel concerns transformation of its carbon-bearing microstructure during thermal exposure; location and distribution affect significance. TWI identifies weld heat-affected zones as an important location in welded carbon steels. [S14] Graphitic corrosion of cast iron is selective corrosion that can leave a weakened residual structure. Similar names do not imply similar causes or detection plans.

**Exercise.** Compare a hot steel weld zone with internal structural change against a wet cast-iron pipe whose shape remains but strength is degraded. **Worked decision:** the first needs thermal/metallurgical evaluation; the second needs selective-corrosion condition assessment. **Changed case:** both have normal outside diameter. Geometry does not clear either property concern.

lessons.title: C08 — Spheroidization, decarburization and strength
lessons.body:
## C08 — Spheroidization, decarburization and strength

Spheroidization changes carbide morphology in susceptible steels under suitable thermal histories. Decarburization changes carbon content in affected regions. Both require interpretation against the material and intended service; they are not synonyms for a surface oxide layer. A metallographic observation must be connected to the engineering question, not merely named.

**Exercise.** A hot-service sample shows altered carbides and a softened surface region. **Worked decision:** determine depth, distribution, history and property consequences with qualified analysis. Do not machine away an assumed shallow layer without a repair/design basis. **Changed case:** a surface hardness test is normal elsewhere; it does not characterize the sampled region or full depth.

lessons.title: C09 — Reheat and stress-relaxation cracking
lessons.body:
## C09 — Reheat and stress-relaxation cracking

Cracking can develop during heat treatment or high-temperature service as stresses relax in a susceptible weld/material structure. The relevant combination includes alloy, fabrication, heat treatment, restraint and service history. TWI's research identifies the interaction of loading and microstructure in stress-relaxation cracking. [S15] “Stress relieved” is therefore not universal proof against every cracking mechanism.

**Exercise.** A weld develops indications after an elevated-temperature treatment despite passing the initial examination. **Worked decision:** compare the timing and location with treatment records, characterize the indications and obtain specialist evaluation. **Changed case:** the treatment chart is complete but its thermocouple position is unverified. Preserve that uncertainty rather than declaring the entire weld followed the intended cycle.

lessons.title: C10 — Hydrogen-assisted cracking outside wet sour service
lessons.body:
## C10 — Hydrogen-assisted cracking outside wet sour service

Hydrogen-related cracking can arise in susceptible high-strength materials from sources other than wet H2S, including fabrication or electrochemical processes. Do not require visible rust or a sour-service label before considering it. Material strength/hardness, hydrogen source, stress and time after processing are relevant. Delayed failure can occur after an apparently satisfactory initial inspection.

**Exercise.** High-strength fasteners fail after an undocumented plating operation. **Worked decision:** quarantine the affected batch within the responsible quality process, preserve processing records and request metallurgical analysis. Do not merely replace individual failed bolts from the same unassessed batch. **Changed case:** chemistry matches the grade; processing-related hydrogen and property condition remain unassessed.

lessons.title: C11 — Ammonia, carbonate, amine and caustic SCC distinctions
lessons.body:
## C11 — Ammonia, carbonate, amine and caustic SCC distinctions

These labels identify different environment/material systems, not one common universal cracking threshold. Ammonia-service cracking in steel has a different review basis from ammonia effects on copper alloys. Carbonate, amine and caustic systems require their own chemistry, weld-stress and material review. Local concentration can depart from bulk samples. A control suitable for one service can be ineffective or harmful in another.

**Exercise.** A plant proposes copying its amine crack-inspection plan to a caustic vessel without reviewing temperature, concentration or weld condition. **Worked decision:** retain useful administrative structure but rebuild the mechanism-specific technical basis. **Changed case:** both are carbon steel. Common base alloy does not establish identical exposure, morphology or control requirements.

lessons.title: C12 — Acid-service differentiation
lessons.body:
## C12 — Acid-service differentiation

Sulfuric, hydrochloric, hydrofluoric, phosphoric and organic-acid services cannot share an unqualified material-compatibility decision. Concentration and contaminants can change the mechanism; phase change can concentrate a corrosive liquid; turbulence can remove protective films. HF also requires its specialized exposure controls. Do not instruct a learner to verify compatibility by a field drop test, unprotected sample or trial mixing.

**Exercise.** A supplier gives a compatibility statement without concentration or temperature. **Worked decision:** obtain its exact applicability and the process envelope before acceptance. **Changed case:** normal conditions fit but startup dilution does not appear on the statement. The startup condition requires review; the normal-service statement cannot be extended by assumption.

lessons.title: C13 — Fretting and wear at contact points
lessons.body:
## C13 — Fretting and wear at contact points

Small repeated relative movements at a loaded contact can damage surfaces and initiate cracks. Supports, clamps and attachments deserve attention when vibration or thermal motion exists. A contact scar can coexist with corrosion; finding rust does not prove corrosion alone caused the loss. Inspect the contact geometry, movement history and adjacent crack-prone regions.

**Exercise.** A pipe support has a polished wear band, debris and recurring movement. **Worked decision:** investigate movement and local condition, select suitable examination and have engineering resolve the support/load arrangement. **Changed case:** adding a tighter clamp stops visible movement but changes restraint. That modification needs a stress/thermal-expansion review rather than automatic acceptance.

lessons.title: C14 — Boiling, condensation and concentration cells
lessons.body:
## C14 — Boiling, condensation and concentration cells

Phase change can concentrate dissolved species, expose alternate wet and dry regions or change gas/liquid contact. A boiler-water bulk sample may not represent a deposit-covered tube surface. Condensate can have a different chemistry from feedwater. Local oxygen, pH and flow history matter. Treat boiler-water corrosion, under-deposit attack and steam/condensate concerns as location-specific questions.

**Exercise.** Bulk chemistry is within the site's target while deposits cover a hot tube and localized loss is found. **Worked decision:** investigate local concentration and heat transfer, characterize deposits and metal condition, and review treatment/cleaning through the responsible specialist. **Changed case:** a treatment adjustment improves the sample but does not establish tube integrity or remove old deposits.

lessons.title: C15 — Material-specific high-temperature attack
lessons.body:
## C15 — Material-specific high-temperature attack

Nitriding, carburization, metal dusting and oxidation have different chemical and structural consequences. A hard surface can conceal reduced ductility; loss of metal can coexist with altered substrate properties. Fuel-ash deposits can change the hot-surface environment. Record gas composition, metal temperature, deposits, exposure time and alloy before selecting the candidate set.

**Exercise.** A tube has a hard altered surface and internal carbonaceous exposure. **Worked decision:** investigate carburization and related candidates with suitable analysis rather than assuming hardness means improved service resistance. **Changed case:** a second tube has oxide scale under an oxidizing atmosphere. Rebuild its mechanism model; appearance of a dark scale alone does not make the two cases equivalent.

lessons.title: C16 — Chloride SCC and pitting are not interchangeable
lessons.body:
## C16 — Chloride SCC and pitting are not interchangeable

Localized corrosion can create stress concentration or aggressive chemistry, but a pit and an SCC crack remain different assessment problems. A smooth thickness map does not establish absence of tight cracks. A positive surface indication needs characterization and disposition, not an automatic label based only on chloride exposure. Material susceptibility and stress still matter.

**Exercise.** A stainless weld area has branching indications after wet chloride exposure, while a neighboring region has isolated rounded pits. **Worked decision:** document two morphologies, obtain suitable crack and localized-loss assessments and review their common exposure. **Changed case:** chloride is not detected in a later rinse sample. That does not reconstruct the historic concentrated environment or erase existing indications.

lessons.title: Clinic assessment record
lessons.body:
## Clinic assessment record

For each C01–C16, record: learner/date; two mechanism-specific facts; one missing discriminating observation; one appropriate next action; one prohibited inference; changed-case response. Score each of the five content elements0–2, pass8/10, and require correction of every unsafe intervention or unsupported fitness declaration. The instructor accepts equivalent correct reasoning and records the reason for any0 or1. For reassessment, use the changed case without showing its worked response, then ask what additional evidence would close the specific uncertainty. These are formative applications; they do not replace the controlled final or its separate scoring.


---

courses.title: VUC038 | VUC038 application workbook

content.title: VUC038 | VUC038 application workbook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC038 application workbook
lessons.body:
# VUC038 application workbook

All assets, measurements and acceptance criteria in this workbook are synthetic teaching data. They are not API limits or approval to operate equipment. Work is performed on paper, drawings or inert teaching specimens. No pressurized, hot, chemically contaminated or energized equipment is used. Worked answers teach reasoning; the separate controlled final uses different records.

lessons.title: Lab A — A corrosion-rate record that does not tell the whole story
lessons.body:
## Lab A — A corrosion-rate record that does not tell the whole story

**Record A1.** Carbon steel spool CS-18, same marked location and calibrated procedure: 2022-11-01 9.2 mm; 2024-11-01 8.8 mm; 2026-11-01 8.0 mm. Synthetic engineering minimum for this exercise: 6.0 mm. The feed changed in January 2025. Mapping finds a separate local minimum of 5.7 mm at the six-o'clock position. The mapping report gives that minimum an uncertainty of ±0.2 mm. The routine point has no stated uncertainty in the old report.

**Tasks.** Calculate long- and short-term average rates, a simple arithmetic remaining time at the routine point using each rate, and the difference between local minimum and supplied criterion. Explain which result controls escalation and what the arithmetic cannot establish.

**Worked solution.** Long term: (9.2−8.0)/4 = 0.30 mm/year. Short term: (8.8−8.0)/2 = 0.40 mm/year. Routine-point time is (8.0−6.0)/0.30 = 6.67 years or /0.40 = 5 years. These are extrapolations, not approved intervals. The mapped minimum is 0.3 mm below the supplied criterion; even its upper uncertainty bound of 5.9 mm remains below. The local result needs immediate integrity disposition under the exercise procedure, independent of the favorable routine-point arithmetic. The changed feed also undermines an assumption of stationary loss rate. Request the mechanism review, coverage and approved localized-damage assessment.

**Changed record A2.** Replace the minimum with 6.1±0.2 mm and remove the feed-change record. The interval spans 5.9–6.3 mm; it straddles the criterion. Do not claim a demonstrated pass or average the uncertainty away. Resolve measurement and operating-history uncertainty.

**Scoring, 10 points.** Two each for correct rates, times with limits, local comparison, uncertainty interpretation and actionable handover. Passing requires8/10 and no operating approval based solely on arithmetic. Remediation: compare a point trend with a spatial map, then solve A2 independently.

lessons.title: Lab B — Candidate mechanisms across a real operating cycle
lessons.body:
## Lab B — Candidate mechanisms across a real operating cycle

**Record B1.** E-28 is a stainless process cooler. Normal operation: hot nominally dry gas; outlet cooler than inlet. Shutdown: water wash, two days open to air, no verified drying record. External insulation: coastal exposure, broken seal at a support. Weld heat-treatment and sensitization evidence unavailable. Last inspection: external visual jacket review and six spot thickness readings; no insulation removal or crack examination. A repair proposal says “no general corrosion, return to service.”

**Tasks.** Produce separate internal-operating, shutdown and external candidate lists. Identify facts needed to distinguish candidates and the inadequacy in the repair proposal.

**Worked solution.** Internal candidates depend on condensate and contaminants; obtain actual outlet phase/chemistry rather than assuming the whole exchanger is dry. Shutdown creates a different wet/air exposure; sensitization and deposits must be investigated before excluding relevant shutdown SCC mechanisms. External wet chloride exposure makes pitting and chloride SCC credible for susceptible material. Nothing in the existing spot measurements establishes crack coverage or condition beneath insulation. Request material/weld history, deposit and wash records, targeted surface/volumetric examinations selected by a specialist and an authorized disposition. No single mechanism is confirmed by this record.

**Changed B2.** The stainless material is replaced with carbon steel while the exposure stays the same. Rebuild the candidates: external wet corrosion remains credible, but do not mechanically transfer stainless-specific SCC claims. Explain how material identity changes both mechanism and method selection.

**Scoring.** Five criteria0–2: cycle separation, material specificity, evidence requests, method limits, controlled disposition. Pass8/10 with no claim that thickness clears cracking.

lessons.title: Lab C — Sampling bias in hot-process piping
lessons.body:
## Lab C — Sampling bias in hot-process piping

**Record C1.** A circuit has12 components. Components1,4,7,10 are fittings with traceable composition and thicknesses7.8,7.9,7.7,7.8 mm. The eight pipe segments have unknown traceability; only segment6 has been measured, at4.2 mm. Original nominal wall is8.0 mm. The stream is hot and sulfur-containing. No current approved minimum is supplied. The inspection plan calls all12 components “represented by four fittings.”

**Tasks.** Calculate measured component coverage and fitting-only coverage; identify the unsupported inference; design a follow-up record without inventing a minimum.

**Worked solution.** Five of12 components have a measurement:41.67%. Four of12 are the selected fittings:33.33%. Neither fraction establishes adequate coverage. The large difference at segment6 disproves the assumption that the fittings necessarily represent all pipe. Sulfidation is credible, but additional chemistry and service evidence may identify other contributors. Obtain component-level material and condition evidence, expand examination according to the qualified plan, and obtain the actual engineering criterion. Record7 components unmeasured, not “passed.” Nominal wall is not an acceptance criterion.

**Changed C2.** All12 components are measured once but four have unexamined circumferential regions. Component count is100%; area coverage remains incomplete. Explain why “100% inspected” without defining the coverage unit is misleading.

**Scoring.** Correct fractions2; unsupported inference2; mechanism evidence2; missing criterion2; coverage distinction2. Pass8/10; inventing an allowable wall is a critical error.

lessons.title: Lab D — Hydrogen-service exposure and method selection
lessons.body:
## Lab D — Hydrogen-service exposure and method selection

**Record D1.** A carbon steel exchanger record lists total pressure80 bar absolute, hydrogen mole fraction0.70, normal metal temperature340°C and a recorded excursion of390°C lasting6 hours. The design file's old screening sheet uses40 bar hydrogen partial pressure. Inspection is routine thickness UT. No HTHA-specific assessment is supplied. These temperatures are facts in a synthetic record, not safe/unsafe boundaries.

**Tasks.** Estimate hydrogen partial pressure, compare the stale input, and specify the investigation. Explain the difference between wet sour cracking and HTHA in this record.

**Worked solution.** Ideal-mixture estimate:80×0.70=56 bar absolute,16 bar above the old input, or40% higher. Confirm process-model applicability and actual composition. The record calls for qualified HTHA susceptibility/condition review using actual material and exposure history; routine thickness alone is insufficient. Wet sour mechanisms require their own wet-environment evidence and cannot be substituted merely because hydrogen is involved. Preserve excursion duration and location. Reducing the temperature does not reverse prior metallurgical damage.

**Changed D2.** Total pressure is80 bar gauge and ambient pressure is1 bar for the exercise. Absolute pressure is81 bar; estimated partial pressure56.7 bar. The pressure basis must be corrected before comparison. No safe-service conclusion follows from either calculation.

**Scoring.** Calculation2, pressure basis2, mechanism distinction2, suitable specialist/method request2, irreversible-damage limit2. Pass8/10 with no chart-free declaration of safety.

lessons.title: Lab E — Water/steam thinning: mechanical or chemical?
lessons.body:
## Lab E — Water/steam thinning: mechanical or chemical?

**Record E1.** A carbon-steel wet-steam line has scalloped thinning after a reducer. No abrasive solids are found. Dissolved-oxygen and pH control records show interruptions. A downstream straight run also has loss. The proposed remedy is “install a solids filter.” A pump elsewhere has noise, fluctuating suction conditions and impeller pitting; its chemistry records are stable.

**Tasks.** Build separate candidate models and identify why one remedy cannot address both assets.

**Worked solution.** FAC is credible in the steam line; investigate material, water chemistry, moisture, flow and geometry. The absence of solids does not eliminate chemically driven film dissolution. A filter alone does not address that model. For the pump, cavitation is a candidate needing suction/pressure and hydraulic investigation. Pitting appearance does not conclusively identify it. Inspection and engineering evaluation must characterize each asset before selecting controls. Do not alter water chemistry or pump operation from this classroom record.

**Changed E2.** The line carries a slurry and has directional gouging at the elbow. Mechanical erosion becomes a stronger candidate; corrosion can still interact. Request particle, flow and material evidence rather than forcing the original FAC diagnosis.

**Scoring.** Candidate separation2, physical/chemical distinction2, evidence2, remedy limitations2, safe handover2. Pass8/10.

lessons.title: Lab F — Fatigue and thermal history
lessons.body:
## Lab F — Fatigue and thermal history

**Record F1.** A small-bore branch cracked twice at the same attachment. Repairs used the same detail. Pump speed changed three months before the first crack. The branch vibrates at a measured dominant frequency during one operating mode. No dynamic assessment exists. Another mixing tee experiences120 documented hot/cold transitions per day, versus20 in the original operating assumption. There are no supplied fatigue design curves.

**Tasks.** Identify the likely initiating histories, calculate the change in daily transition count, and state what cannot be calculated.

**Worked solution.** The branch requires vibration/support and local stress evaluation plus crack examination; repeated rewelding does not remove the driver. The tee experiences six times the assumed daily transitions, a500% increase. That does not mean exactly one-sixth life: stress amplitude, sequence, temperature and environment matter. Without a valid fatigue model and inputs, do not calculate remaining life. Escalate both changed service histories.

**Changed F2.** The dominant vibration disappears after a support change, but no post-repair crack examination has occurred. The improved excitation is not proof that the component is free of existing damage or that the support modification is approved.

**Scoring.** Separate drivers2, arithmetic2, fatigue-model limits2, repair/source distinction2, required follow-up2. Pass8/10; fictitious life calculation is critical.

lessons.title: Lab G — Inspection report challenge
lessons.body:
## Lab G — Inspection report challenge

**Record G1.** Report N-38 says “all good.” Its attachment lists eight UT thickness points, no scan map, no procedure revision and no inaccessible-area statement. The asset has a credible weld-cracking mechanism and an internal lining. Chemistry identification was performed on one nozzle only. Operations asks whether the whole vessel can return to service.

**Tasks.** Rewrite the conclusion as defensible statements and issue a focused request for missing evidence.

**Worked solution.** Eight recorded thickness values are available at the stated points; their procedure and representativeness remain unresolved. No demonstrated weld-crack examination is supplied. One nozzle's chemistry does not identify the full vessel. Lining and substrate condition need separate coverage. Request procedure/revision, calibration/qualification, location map, limitations, suitable crack examination, material traceability and authorized acceptance criteria. The report cannot support the requested whole-vessel clearance.

**Changed G2.** A qualified scan map arrives but covers only accessible welds. State precisely which welds remain unassessed and what decision remains held. Do not erase an access limitation by changing “all” to “most.”

**Scoring.** Evidence/claim distinction2, crack-method gap2, material limitation2, access/lining limits2, actionable request2. Pass8/10; whole-vessel approval is critical.

lessons.title: Lab H — Integrity operating window and change control
lessons.body:
## Lab H — Integrity operating window and change control

**Record H1.** Synthetic site window IOW-7 requires an engineering review when a specified monitored contaminant exceeds20 mg/L for more than2 hours. This is a supplied project trigger, not an API threshold. Samples at08:00,10:00,12:00 are24,27,23 mg/L; at14:00 the result is18. The operator closes the event because the last sample is normal. A new feed began at06:00. No continuous record exists.

**Tasks.** Determine what is established, what is uncertain and what the procedure requires.

**Worked solution.** Three samples over four hours exceed the trigger. Continuous duration between samples is not directly measured, but the record cannot justify dismissal; the specified review must be initiated on this evidence and uncertainty. The normal14:00 sample does not assess prior damage. Review feed change, sampling reliability, susceptible assets and any required inspection. Record onset as uncertain rather than asserting06:00 solely because feed changed then.

**Changed H2.** Calibration error invalidates the10:00 sample. The other results and feed change remain. Correct the evidence and reassess; do not treat invalid data as either proof of continuous exceedance or proof of no event.

**Scoring.** Evidence2, duration uncertainty2, response2, change review2, honest record correction2. Pass8/10.

lessons.title: Integrated case I — North Loop unit handover
lessons.body:
## Integrated case I — North Loop unit handover

Synthetic equipment: P-101 hot sulfur-containing carbon-steel circuit with mixed replacement history; E-102 stainless cooler with wet external insulation; V-103 wet sour vessel with weld indications; H-104 hydrogen-service exchanger with a temperature excursion. Operations proposes restarting all four after a two-day outage.

**Evidence packet.** P-101: four fittings measured, pipe traceability incomplete, one pipe segment markedly thinner. E-102: jacket repaired, no substrate examination; shutdown wash and drying records incomplete. V-103: thickness satisfactory, two unresolved linear indications adjacent to a repair weld; hardness report belongs to another weld. H-104: routine UT satisfactory, actual hydrogen composition differs from the old screening sheet; no specialist assessment of excursion. The outage coordinator offers to accept “four satisfactory thickness reports” as clearance.

**Learner deliverable.** Produce one page per asset with candidates, evidence, missing information, immediate decision boundary, inspection request and responsible role; then a one-page management handover prioritizing work. Do not invent operational limits or characterize all findings as the same mechanism.

**Worked review.** P-101 requires component-specific material/condition evidence and appropriate sulfidation/other hot-service review. E-102 needs separate external localized/SCC and shutdown-exposure assessment; jacket repair is not substrate clearance. V-103 needs wet-hydrogen/SCC and weld-condition review using the correct records and crack-capable methods; thickness is insufficient. H-104 needs actual-exposure HTHA review, not a copied pressure input or routine wall result. The coordinator must receive four distinct unresolved dispositions with authorized owners. Restart authorization is outside the learner's role.

**Changed integrated case.** Provide correct material records for P-101, qualified external crack examination for E-102, a corrected hardness report for V-103 and corrected pressure inputs for H-104. None alone necessarily closes each asset: condition/coverage, shutdown exposure, actual indications and specialist damage assessment still require explicit disposition. The learner must close only the specific uncertainty resolved by each new record.

**Rubric, 20 points.** Each asset earns0–4 for a mechanism-specific evidence-to-action chain; management handover earns0–4 for priority, ownership and accurate boundaries. Pass16/20 with no unjustified restart authorization, no dismissal of an unresolved crack, and no substitution of thickness for all damage modes. After feedback, reassess with the changed packet; do not award completion from attendance.


---

courses.title: VUC038 | VUC038 delivery, assessment and credential guide

content.title: VUC038 | VUC038 delivery, assessment and credential guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC038 delivery, assessment and credential guide
lessons.body: # VUC038 delivery, assessment and credential guide

lessons.title: Delivery sequence and prerequisites
lessons.body:
## Delivery sequence and prerequisites

Planned guided study is56 hours:24 chapter discussions at30 minutes each(12 hours);16 specialist clinics at30 minutes(8); eight workbook labs at90 minutes(12);24 application stations at30 minutes(12); integrated case review(3); targeted remediation and consolidation(6); controlled final(3). These are planning allocations, not earned time or proof of competence. Adapt reading/accommodation time without lowering the required decisions. Experienced learners may challenge instruction but must meet the same assessment requirements.

Before starting, check ability to read an equipment record, use units, calculate a percentage and distinguish chemistry identification from a property test. Use these entry tasks: calculate loss from8.0 to7.4 mm in2 years(0.30 mm/year); explain why a certificate for tagB does not identify tagA; identify the missing pressure basis in “80 bar.” If any is missed, teach that skill before the related chapter. This is not an exclusion based on language, disability or job title.

The instructor should have demonstrable corrosion/materials and inspection experience appropriate to the topics and competence in assessment. Use qualified specialists for disputed metallurgical interpretations. The course does not qualify someone to perform UT, surface testing, metallography or destructive sampling. All station work uses supplied records, drawings and inert specimens; field demonstrations are optional and must be separately authorized. No learner must enter equipment, approach a leak, heat a sample, mix chemicals or test oxygen compatibility to pass.

Teach the chapters in order, then the associated clinics and labs. Ask learners to explain a wrong inference, not merely recite a mechanism name. Demonstrate the worked case, hide the solution and issue the changed case. Distinguish recognition from proof: naming a candidate earns no credit for claiming it confirmed without evidence. Record feedback and the learner's corrected reasoning.

lessons.title: Standard station scoring
lessons.body:
## Standard station scoring

Each station has five criteria scored0–2:2 correct and justified,1 safe but incomplete,0 absent/incorrect/unsafe. The criteria are(1) correct use of supplied facts,(2) mechanism-specific reasoning,(3) suitable evidence/method selection,(4) appropriate decision/authority boundary,(5) clear traceable handover. Each station below defines the concrete content expected. Pass8/10, with all critical errors corrected and reassessed using the changed record. Unsupported operating approval, invented evidence, unsafe intervention or disguising an unexamined area is critical regardless of total.

Record learner, assessor, date, version, station, evidence submitted, five scores, critical errors, feedback, changed response and final outcome. An instructor may accept technically correct alternatives if the basis is recorded. Do not score an alternative wrong solely because it names an additional credible mechanism; require a reason and a discriminating observation.

lessons.title: P01 — Operating-cycle map
lessons.body:
## P01 — Operating-cycle map

Use Q01 and B1. Draw normal, wash, shutdown and restart phases. Expected: separate wet exposures; identify the unverified drain/drying record; list evidence and owner; avoid a blanket dry exclusion. Changed record: B2 with carbon steel. Deliverable: one-page phase/candidate map.

lessons.title: P02 — Material evidence audit
lessons.body:
## P02 — Material evidence audit

Use Q02 and C03/C06. Supplied record: nozzle chemistry known, heat treatment absent, parent plate certificate untraceable. Expected: label each known/unknown separately, distinguish chemistry from properties, request exact missing evidence, hold only dependent decisions. Changed: correct plate certificate arrives but weld history stays missing. Deliverable: three-row evidence table.

lessons.title: P03 — Rate and uncertainty calculation
lessons.body:
## P03 — Rate and uncertainty calculation

Use A1. Expected:0.30/0.40 mm/year,6.67/5-year arithmetic projections, local5.7±0.2 comparison, no interval approval. Changed:A2. Deliverable: calculations with units and a short disposition. Assessment includes the difference between a spatial minimum and a time trend.

lessons.title: P04 — Insulation and buried transition plan
lessons.body:
## P04 — Insulation and buried transition plan

Use Q04,B1. Expected: identify water-entry/support regions and stainless cracking concerns; choose a qualified condition plan; distinguish jacket repair from substrate evidence. Changed: carbon-steel soil-air transition with one favorable CP point. Deliverable: annotated location plan and method limitations.

lessons.title: P05 — Galvanic/crevice/selective attack comparison
lessons.body:
## P05 — Galvanic/crevice/selective attack comparison

Use Q05. Records: electrically joined dissimilar metals in water; nonmetal gasket crevice; porous brass region. Expected: three distinct candidate explanations, required evidence, no dimension-only clearance. Changed: electrical isolation is verified for the first record; reconsider galvanic candidate while retaining other exposures. Deliverable: comparison table.

lessons.title: P06 — Deposit investigation request
lessons.body:
## P06 — Deposit investigation request

Use Q06. Expected: MIC as candidate rather than conclusion, representative deposit/metal sampling by approved personnel, treatment/flow history, independent wall assessment. Changed: negative post-treatment bulk sample. Deliverable: laboratory request and remaining-integrity statement; no dosing instructions.

lessons.title: P07 — Wet gas and sour-water review
lessons.body:
## P07 — Wet gas and sour-water review

Use Q07. Record: warm low-loss coupon, cold retained liquid, unknown water chemistry. Expected: local phase evidence and targeted coverage, separate cracking candidates if sour conditions support them, coupon limits. Changed: coupon is moved but old low-point damage is unexamined. Deliverable: revised monitoring/inspection questions.

lessons.title: P08 — Chemical compatibility challenge
lessons.body:
## P08 — Chemical compatibility challenge

Use Q08,C12. Record: chart covers one normal concentration/temperature; startup differs and injection quill changed. Expected: identify applicability gaps and local exposure, route to specialist, no improvised flush. Changed: normal-service vendor letter arrives. Deliverable: focused request covering startup and injection conditions.

lessons.title: P09 — Salt and amine cases
lessons.body:
## P09 — Salt and amine cases

Use Q09. Expected: deposition/wetting/flow model for exchanger; separate weld cracking review for amine vessel; cleaning is not integrity closure. Changed: pressure drop returns to normal after cleaning. Deliverable: two asset-specific follow-up records.

lessons.title: P10 — Sampling coverage audit
lessons.body:
## P10 — Sampling coverage audit

Use C1. Expected:5/12 measured components and4/12 fittings, no representative-pipe assumption, actual criteria requested. Changed:C2. Deliverable: component coverage map distinguishing count, area and damage coverage.

lessons.title: P11 — Hot-surface evidence plan
lessons.body:
## P11 — Hot-surface evidence plan

Use Q11,C15. Record: normal outlet temperature, local scale change, suspected hot spot. Expected: actual metal exposure, gas/deposit/material evidence, distinct corrosion and property questions. Changed: surface hardness increases. Deliverable: investigation plan that does not equate hardness with fitness.

lessons.title: P12 — Shutdown risk review
lessons.body:
## P12 — Shutdown risk review

Use Q12,C02. Expected: wet-air and deposit history, material susceptibility, prevention before opening, suitable examination. Changed: earlier steady-service review is supplied. Deliverable: shutdown-specific open issues and owners.

lessons.title: P13 — SCC evidence triangle
lessons.body:
## P13 — SCC evidence triangle

Use Q13,C11,C16. Map material, environment and stress for ammonia and chloride records. Expected: residual stress considered, crack-capable methods, no thickness-only clearance. Changed: operating pressure is reduced. Deliverable: explanation of which stress evidence remains unresolved.

lessons.title: P14 — Wet-hydrogen morphology review
lessons.body:
## P14 — Wet-hydrogen morphology review

Use Q14. Record: internal separations, weld-adjacent linked indications, uncertain hardness map. Expected: distinguish candidate forms, request qualified characterization, preserve actual weld/plate identity, no drilling of blisters. Changed: new weld procedure approved. Deliverable: separate future-control and existing-condition actions.

lessons.title: P15 — HTHA exposure calculation
lessons.body:
## P15 — HTHA exposure calculation

Use D1. Expected:56 bar absolute estimate,16 bar/40% difference, actual history and specialist review, no ordinary-UT clearance. Changed:D2(56.7 bar). Deliverable: calculation and a method-capability request.

lessons.title: P16 — Fatigue cause/repair distinction
lessons.body:
## P16 — Fatigue cause/repair distinction

Use F1. Expected: vibration and thermal-cycle models kept separate; sixfold count and500% increase; no invented life fraction; cause correction and condition examination. Changed:F2. Deliverable: cause-and-evidence matrix.

lessons.title: P17 — Creep and hot-spot assessment
lessons.body:
## P17 — Creep and hot-spot assessment

Use Q17. Record: bowed tube, deposit, cool-location replica only. Expected: representativeness limits, actual metal-temperature history, dimensional/material evidence and authorized evaluation. Changed: deposits removed. Deliverable: unresolved-condition statement.

lessons.title: P18 — Toughness/property review
lessons.body:
## P18 — Toughness/property review

Use Q18,C05–C08. Expected: separate thickness, hardness, chemistry and toughness evidence; material-specific thermal history; no universal embrittlement threshold. Changed: matching chemistry certificate arrives. Deliverable: property-to-evidence table with held decisions.

lessons.title: P19 — FAC/cavitation/erosion comparison
lessons.body:
## P19 — FAC/cavitation/erosion comparison

Use E1. Expected: distinguish chemical film dissolution from particle removal and bubble-collapse candidate; select relevant process evidence for each. Changed:E2. Deliverable: three-column mechanism/control comparison without operational adjustment instructions.

lessons.title: P20 — Joint and processing history
lessons.body:
## P20 — Joint and processing history

Use Q20,C09,C10. Record: dissimilar hot joint, post-treatment indications, unverified thermocouple position. Expected: identify timing, material/thermal/stress evidence and qualified review; no stress-relief immunity claim. Changed: correct chart supplied but indications remain. Deliverable: evidence chronology.

lessons.title: P21 — Protective-layer versus substrate condition
lessons.body:
## P21 — Protective-layer versus substrate condition

Use Q21. Expected: separate lining discontinuity, compatibility, cure and substrate evidence; refractory hot spot assessed. Changed: holiday test passes after chemical-service change. Deliverable: two distinct acceptance questions and the responsible reviewers.

lessons.title: P22 — NDT claim correction
lessons.body:
## P22 — NDT claim correction

Use G1. Expected: precise limited statement of available results, crack-coverage gap, material scope and access limits, focused evidence request. Changed:G2. Deliverable: corrected report conclusion and action list.

lessons.title: P23 — Window and change record
lessons.body:
## P23 — Window and change record

Use H1. Expected: initiate review on high-sample evidence, preserve uncertain duration, assess changed feed and prior exposure; do not erase after normal sample. Changed:H2. Deliverable: timestamped event record with uncertainties.

lessons.title: P24 — Management handover
lessons.body:
## P24 — Management handover

Use integrated case I. Expected: four distinct asset decisions, urgent concerns escalated safely, open evidence with owners and no invented restart clearance. Changed: use integrated changed packet. Deliverable: concise management summary plus four supporting asset sheets. Score the integrated20-point rubric separately as well as this station's communication criteria.

lessons.title: Assessment administration
lessons.body:
## Assessment administration

All48 formative checks require an attempted response, feedback and correction. Complete16 clinic records, eight labs,24 stations and integrated case. The controlled final is separate:24 cases, three decisions each,144 possible points,180 minutes. Pass116/144 and at least4/6 in every chapter domain; all critical errors must be corrected and reassessed. These are VNDRLY course rules, not API exam rules. An overall passing score cannot hide a failed safety-critical domain.

The instructor keeps the final prompts, answer key and changed reassessment outside the learner package in `.local/private-training/damage-mechanisms-instructor/`. Local file separation is not a claim of encrypted or role-enforced storage; the delivery owner must provide appropriate restricted storage before administering to learners. Issue only the exam form, not the key. Calculator and coursebook may be used; assistance, collaboration and access to the protected key may not. Record accommodations and preserve the reasoning standard. Verify learner identity by the organization's normal privacy-conscious process.

Score each final decision0–2 using its supplied expected reasoning; accept equivalent sound responses. For missed domains, revisit the relevant chapter/clinic, discuss the erroneous assumption and administer the changed case without its answer. Preserve original and changed results. After two unsuccessful reassessments, provide individualized instruction and a fresh equivalent supervised assessment; do not repeatedly expose the same answers until memorized.

lessons.title: Credential and record
lessons.body:
## Credential and record

Issue only after the actual learner meets all requirements. Credential title: “VNDRLY/U Asset Integrity — Damage Mechanisms, available-source learning assessment.” Record learner, version/hash, completion date, assessor, scores, completed practical/application records, limitations and a unique record identifier. This is a learning credential, not API571 certification, an engineering license, an NDE qualification or field operating authorization. It does not assert current-edition equivalence. Suggested VNDRLY review cycle is3 years, sooner after significant role/process/material changes or demonstrated knowledge gaps; this is not an external recertification rule.

Retain the version-specific evidence under the organization's training-record policy. Do not overwrite a failed attempt with a later pass. Permit a documented second-assessor review for disputed scoring and protect assessment keys from learner distribution. Publication and software integration are outside this materials-only task.


---

courses.title: VUC038 | VUC038 formative checks

content.title: VUC038 | VUC038 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC038 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC038 formative checks

Attempt before reading the answer. Correct every missed response, identify the mistaken assumption and revisit the mapped chapter and station. These teaching checks do not replace the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

What makes a mechanism exclusion defensible?

**Answer:** Evidence that a required condition is absent, with the period and limits stated.

**Reason/remediation:** A missing examination is not evidence of absence. Revisit Q01 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

Does a dry-service label cover water washing?

**Answer:** No; evaluate the wash, drainage and shutdown separately.

**Reason/remediation:** Operating modes can create different environments. Revisit Q01 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Does alloy chemistry establish toughness?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Composition, structure and mechanical properties are different evidence. Revisit Q02 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

Why retain weld heat-treatment history?

**Answer:** It can affect local structure and susceptibility.

**Reason/remediation:** Base-metal identity alone does not describe every weld zone. Revisit Q02 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Matched thickness falls from10.0 to9.1 mm in3 years. Rate?

**Answer:** 0.30 mm/year.

**Reason/remediation:** Comparable locations and methods are required. Revisit Q03 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

Why not use a mean thickness to dismiss a deep pit?

**Answer:** The mean can conceal the local remaining ligament.

**Reason/remediation:** Localized geometry needs its own assessment. Revisit Q03 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Does repaired jacketing clear existing CUI?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It changes water entry, not the existing substrate condition. Revisit Q04 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

What additional concern can wet chlorides create on susceptible stainless steel?

**Answer:** Stress corrosion cracking as well as localized loss.

**Reason/remediation:** Thickness alone is not crack clearance. Revisit Q04 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

What completes a galvanic couple besides dissimilar surfaces?

**Answer:** Electrical connection and an electrolyte.

**Reason/remediation:** Exposure and area relationships determine significance. Revisit Q05 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Can a nonmetal gasket create crevice corrosion conditions?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Restricted exchange can matter without a dissimilar metal. Revisit Q05 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Does a positive microbe sample prove MIC caused a pit?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Combine local chemistry, deposits, morphology and history. Revisit Q06 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Can clean bulk water clear deposit-covered metal?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The local environment may differ from the sample. Revisit Q06 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Why distinguish wet and dry CO2 service?

**Answer:** Aqueous corrosion depends on water and local conditions.

**Reason/remediation:** A gas label alone misses condensed/retained liquid. Revisit Q07 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Can a coupon clear hydrogen cracking?

**Answer:** Not by itself.

**Reason/remediation:** Coupon loss is not a qualified crack examination. Revisit Q07 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

Does lower acid concentration always mean less attack?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Compatibility depends on the complete service conditions. Revisit Q08 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

Why inspect an injection zone separately?

**Answer:** Local chemistry and impingement can differ from bulk service.

**Reason/remediation:** Mixing and phase behavior affect exposure. Revisit Q08 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Does a pressure-drop increase measure remaining wall?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Fouling indication and integrity measurement are distinct. Revisit Q09 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

Why can a feed change move a susceptible salt region?

**Answer:** Deposition, condensation and wetting conditions can change.

**Reason/remediation:** An old sample location may no longer represent exposure. Revisit Q09 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Can four fittings represent every pipe component automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Composition and exposure can vary by component. Revisit Q10 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

Does sulfur content alone settle a crude-change review?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Acid characteristics, phase, temperature and other factors can change. Revisit Q10 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Does normal outlet temperature rule out a tube hot spot?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Local metal exposure can differ from bulk fluid. Revisit Q11 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

Does removing scale restore material properties?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Substrate changes require separate evaluation. Revisit Q11 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Which temperature matters for local condensation?

**Answer:** The relevant surface condition as well as gas composition and temperature.

**Reason/remediation:** Bulk gas averages can miss cold spots. Revisit Q12 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Why review opening a sulfur-service stainless unit to wet air?

**Answer:** Shutdown can create a new cracking environment.

**Reason/remediation:** Steady-operation evidence does not cover every shutdown exposure. Revisit Q12 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Must SCC have large wall loss?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Cracking can develop with little general thinning. Revisit Q13 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

Can residual stress matter at low pressure?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Fabrication stress is not represented solely by operating pressure. Revisit Q13 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Are HIC and SSC interchangeable names?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Morphology, stress and material factors differ. Revisit Q14 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

May a learner drill a blister to inspect it?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the controlled specialist investigation and isolation basis. Revisit Q14 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Is HTHA the same as wet sour cracking?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The exposure and metallurgical processes differ. Revisit Q15 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

Does lower temperature reverse existing HTHA?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Existing degradation requires assessment. Revisit Q15 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Why can repeated weld repair fail again?

**Answer:** The cyclic load or stress concentration may remain.

**Reason/remediation:** Repair and cause correction are separate. Revisit Q16 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

Does static strength establish fatigue life?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Cycle history and local stress matter. Revisit Q16 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Can a visually straight tube still need creep evaluation?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** No visible distortion is not proof of unaffected microstructure. Revisit Q17 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

Does repaired refractory undo creep?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It may control future exposure, not erase accumulated damage. Revisit Q17 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:
## Q18-L1

Does unchanged hardness establish toughness?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Different properties require appropriate evidence. Revisit Q18 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q18-L2
lessons.body:
## Q18-L2

Why review cold pressurization of older thick equipment?

**Answer:** Brittle-fracture resistance depends on temperature, material, flaws and stress.

**Reason/remediation:** Wall thickness alone is insufficient. Revisit Q18 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q19-L1
lessons.body:
## Q19-L1

Can FAC occur without abrasive solids?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Film dissolution/transport is not simply mechanical erosion. Revisit Q19 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q19-L2
lessons.body:
## Q19-L2

Why not diagnose cavitation from pitting alone?

**Answer:** Other mechanisms can produce pits.

**Reason/remediation:** Hydraulic history and other evidence are needed. Revisit Q19 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q20-L1
lessons.body:
## Q20-L1

Does fabrication acceptance eliminate later dissimilar-joint damage?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Service exposure and differential movement can create later damage. Revisit Q20 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q20-L2
lessons.body:
## Q20-L2

May a small low-melting-metal contaminant be ignored automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Material-specific liquid-metal interaction may matter. Revisit Q20 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q21-L1
lessons.body:
## Q21-L1

Does a holiday test prove lining compatibility?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Discontinuity detection and chemical suitability are different. Revisit Q21 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q21-L2
lessons.body:
## Q21-L2

Does sound lining prove sound substrate?

**Answer:** Not automatically.

**Reason/remediation:** Both need suitable condition evidence. Revisit Q21 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q22-L1
lessons.body:
## Q22-L1

What must accompany “not detected”?

**Answer:** Method, coverage, limitations and date.

**Reason/remediation:** The claim is bounded by capability and inspected region. Revisit Q22 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q22-L2
lessons.body:
## Q22-L2

Does an advanced instrument replace a qualified procedure?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Capability depends on the complete application. Revisit Q22 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q23-L1
lessons.body:
## Q23-L1

Does a normal sample close a prior excursion?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The past exposure and required response remain to be assessed. Revisit Q23 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q23-L2
lessons.body:
## Q23-L2

What makes an alarm actionable?

**Answer:** A basis, units/location, response, owner and escalation.

**Reason/remediation:** A number alone is not a control system. Revisit Q23 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q24-L1
lessons.body:
## Q24-L1

How should disagreement between process and inspection evidence be handled?

**Answer:** Retain it explicitly and specify the resolving work.

**Reason/remediation:** A favorable result from an unsuitable method cannot cancel credible exposure. Revisit Q24 and explain its changed case in your own words.

lessons.title: Q24-L2
lessons.body:
## Q24-L2

Does a learning credential authorize restart?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Authorization belongs to the designated competent roles. Revisit Q24 and explain its changed case in your own words.


---

lessons.title: VUC038 sources, provenance and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC038 sources, provenance and coverage

Reviewed2026-11-18. Sources below support the stated topics; none is represented as a substitute for the unavailable full current controlled standards. The user directed best effort without pursuing the PDF. No purchase, access request or reading-room dependency is attached to completion of these original materials. No claim of API endorsement or complete clause-by-clause equivalence is made.

lessons.title: Source register
lessons.body:
## Source register

|S01|[API571 certification program](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/certifications/api571)|Public scope identifies entire RP571 third edition2020 as examination basis. Used to establish external-program boundary, not to claim this course reproduces all its content.|
|S02|[HSE corrosion/material selection](https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeasmaterial.htm)|General/localized attack and material-environment selection. Guidance is not a project compatibility approval.|
|S03|[CSB Chevron Richmond investigation](https://www.csb.gov/chevron-richmond-refinery-fire/) and [mechanical-integrity findings](https://www.csb.gov/recommendations/csb-investigations-mechanical-integrity/)|Component variability and sulfidation inspection lessons. Original synthetic case records do not reproduce incident data.|
|S04|[CSB Tesoro Anacortes investigation](https://www.csb.gov/tesoro-anacortes-refinery-fatal-explosion-and-fire-/) and [HTHA safety alert](https://www.csb.gov/assets/1/20/Safety_Alert_HTHA_Final.pdf)|HTHA concern and actual-exposure/assessment limitations. No API941 boundary or safe operating curve is reproduced.|
|S05|[OSHA Technical Manual, pressure vessels](https://www.osha.gov/otm/section-4-safety-hazards/chapter-3)|Ammonia and other environmental cracking examples. Historic technical guidance is not a new numeric service criterion.|
|S06|[NRC aging-mechanism definitions](https://downloads.regulations.gov/NRC-2012-0170-0002/content.pdf) and [OECD-NEA FAC report](https://www.oecd-nea.org/upload/docs/application/pdf/2021-02/csni-r2014-6.pdf)|Distinction between FAC film dissolution and mechanical erosion. Nuclear examples provide mechanism context, not refinery-specific acceptance limits.|

Research summary only; no full-report access claimed.|
|S10|[HSE oxygen-use guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/indg459.pdf)|Oxygen-compatible components and replacement hazards; no oxygen-system design authority.|
|S11|[PHMSA pipeline corrosion report](https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/sites/phmsa.dot.gov/files/docs/technical-resources/pipeline/gas-distribution-integrity-management/65996/finalreportpipelinecorrosion.pdf)|Ethanol SCC and hydrogen-stress-cracking context. Does not establish current acceptance thresholds for a specific asset.|
|S12|[NIST ethanol/bacteria fatigue research](https://www.nist.gov/news-events/news/2011/08/nist-finds-ethanol-loving-bacteria-accelerate-cracking-pipeline-steels)|Environmental interaction with fatigue; research findings are not generalized to every blend.|
|S13|[NASA oxygen hazards analysis guide](https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/19970001787)|End-use compatibility and ignition-source analysis. Abstract-level scope only, no full standards compliance claim.|
|S14|[TWI graphitization explanation](https://www.twi-global.com/technical-knowledge/faqs/faq-what-is-graphitisation)|Graphitization and weld-zone relevance; no life-prediction limits supplied.|
|S15|[TWI stress-relaxation cracking research](https://www.twi-global.com/what-we-do/research-and-technology/research-programmes/joint-industry-projects/assessment-and-prediction-of-stress-relaxation-cracking)|Material/loading/structure interaction; research-project scope is not an operating criterion.|

lessons.title: Original material and unresolved reference limits
lessons.body:
## Original material and unresolved reference limits

The explanatory instruction, invented assets, calculations, case records, scoring rubrics and assessment questions are original VNDRLY teaching materials. Mechanism names are technical terminology. No external exam bank or proprietary standard tables are reproduced. Specific API susceptibility ranges, alloy-selection tables, examination intervals, edition-specific detailed requirements and normative acceptance clauses have not been comprehensively verified. The course therefore teaches mechanism recognition, evidence selection and bounded decisions; live engineering design/acceptance requires the applicable controlled basis.

The broad material groups and mechanism families are treated across the course and specialist clinics. Grouped teaching is not a claim that24 chapters correspond to24 API sections. Less-common mechanisms are addressed at recognition and specialist-referral depth, not by inventing numerical design rules. The evaluator must not infer external examination readiness from completion. Available-source completion means the original package is usable and assessed within its declared scope, not that unavailable references were somehow reviewed.

lessons.title: Objective and assessment map
lessons.body:
## Objective and assessment map

Each Q-domain has two explained formative checks, a three-decision controlled final case, a changed reassessment and an application station. The final/key are kept outside the public assembly. Sources support selected technical facts; the original learning activities assess the stated decision skills.

|---|---|---|---|
