This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Pipeline Construction Inspection
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Pipeline Construction Inspection

VUC042 · Original available-source materials · 2026-11-18

lessons.title: Purpose, audience and authority
lessons.body:
## Purpose, audience and authority

This program teaches construction inspectors and quality personnel to follow a pipeline from approved route and materials through installation, testing, restoration and traceable handover. Learners need industrial safety awareness, drawing literacy and arithmetic; targeted prerequisite teaching is supplied before assessment. The outcome is defensible observation and disposition, not authority to design, weld, rig, excavate, perform NDT or operate a pressure test without the separately applicable qualifications and appointment.

The external subject is API1169 pipeline construction inspection.[S01] This original VNDRLY program does not award API certification or claim comprehensive current API/CSA/ASME standard equivalence. Federal US gas and hazardous-liquid rules differ, and Canadian requirements have their own jurisdictional basis.[S02–S04] Establish actual applicability and approved documents before live decisions. Numerical specifications below are explicitly supplied classroom criteria unless identified as a cited legal example. None is an actual construction or pressure-test procedure.

lessons.title: Q01 — Inspector role and objective evidence
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Inspector role and objective evidence

The inspector observes specified work, compares it with the applicable approved basis, records facts and routes deviations through assigned authority. Observation, interpretation and acceptance are different acts. A contractor's statement may be useful evidence but is not the same as witnessing the activity. Identify the inspected location, time, method, result and limitation so another reviewer can reconstruct what happened.

Understand stop-work and escalation responsibilities before work begins. Do not direct a hazardous operation beyond your competence. Where a condition creates imminent risk, follow the established immediate protection/escalation process; do not continue exposure merely to obtain better photographs. Production pressure cannot justify inventing a pass.

**Worked case.** A foreman asks for a witnessed weld entry while the inspector was at another spread. Record the actual evidence source and required follow-up, not a false witness signature. **Changed case:** a valid NDT report later arrives; it may establish its own result, not retroactive personal observation.

lessons.title: Q02 — Jurisdiction, specifications and change control
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Jurisdiction, specifications and change control

Identify pipeline service, location, regulatory jurisdiction, project approvals and governing specification editions. Gas and hazardous-liquid construction provisions are not interchangeable, and rules for one location or facility type may not apply elsewhere.[S02–S03] The owner establishes the controlled requirements; the inspector verifies against them and escalates conflicts.

Keep drawings and procedures at the correct revision. A field change may affect route, stress, environment, permits, coating or testing. Record who proposed, technically reviewed and authorized it, and what was actually installed. “The new drawing is coming” is not approval, and a redline alone does not prove an approved change.

**Worked case.** A liquid-line project copies a gas-line cover table without checking applicability. Obtain the correct basis rather than use whichever is less restrictive. **Changed case:** a project requirement is more conservative than the applicable minimum; do not silently waive the project requirement.

lessons.title: Q03 — Preconstruction readiness and inspection plan
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Preconstruction readiness and inspection plan

Before mobilization verify available permits, route/access limits, drawings, materials/procedures, qualified personnel, inspection resources and communication paths. The inspection plan should identify stages that will become hidden, hold/witness points and records required for release. An inspector cannot recover an unrecorded buried condition by signing a final checklist.

Coordinate interfaces among civil, welding, coating, NDT, environmental, survey and commissioning teams. Define how incomplete work is handed over between shifts and spreads. Verify actual readiness rather than treat a planned appointment or ordered instrument as available capacity.

**Worked case.** Lowering is scheduled before coating examination resources arrive. Hold the dependent stage under the plan and resolve resources. **Changed case:** an inspector arrives but lacks the required equipment/procedure; attendance alone does not satisfy readiness.

lessons.title: Q04 — Route, survey, stationing and as-built control
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Route, survey, stationing and as-built control

Use the project's coordinate system, datum, station convention and units. A station identifies position along an alignment, not necessarily straight-line distance. Check benchmarks and survey references before comparing elevations or cover. Preserve bends, tie-ins, crossings, weld locations and exceptions in the as-built record.

A coordinate without datum or units can be dangerously ambiguous. Redlines should distinguish approved design changes from observations requiring review. Do not move a route stake or alter a survey value to make installed work appear compliant. Query discrepancies and keep the original evidence.

**Worked case.** In a synthetic metric station system,1+250 means1,250 m;1+430−1+250 is180 m of station difference. **Changed case:** a station equation or different alignment exists; simple subtraction may no longer give actual installed length without reconciliation.

lessons.title: Q05 — Right-of-way and environmental controls
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Right-of-way and environmental controls

Construction authorization includes limits on access, clearing, soil handling, water management, crossings and restoration. The environmental plan must be available and understood by relevant parties; CER guidance explicitly addresses such coordination for its regulated projects.[S04] Do not treat a landowner's informal permission as a substitute for required project/environmental authorization.

Inspect boundaries and protective measures before disturbance. Keep topsoil handling, drainage protection, waste and spill controls traceable to the actual plan. Unexpected water, cultural material or sensitive habitat can require a defined stop/notification response. Record the condition without undertaking unauthorized sampling, removal or relocation.

**Worked case.** Equipment uses an unapproved shortcut through a wet area. Shorter travel does not establish permitted access. **Changed case:** the owner authorizes a route change but the environmental approval has not been checked; both interfaces must be resolved.

lessons.title: Q06 — Existing facilities and damage prevention
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Existing facilities and damage prevention

Plans and surface marks are inputs to a controlled excavation/crossing process, not guarantees of exact buried location. Establish required notifications, current locates, permissions, owner information and safe exposure methods. CER's construction-near-pipelines guidance distinguishes written consent, locating and operator safety information.[S05] Apply the actual local system elsewhere.

When records, marks and exposed facilities disagree, stop the affected work through the established process and reconcile with responsible parties. Do not guess depth or assume an abandoned-looking pipe is harmless. Protect exposed services against loads and damage as required; crossing equipment can create hazards even without digging.

**Worked case.** A marked line is not found at the expected location. That does not prove the area clear. **Changed case:** another unmarked pipe is exposed; identify/control it before continuing affected work rather than assigning it the nearest drawing tag.

lessons.title: Q07 — Pipe and component receipt
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Pipe and component receipt

Verify identity, grade, dimensions, wall, manufacturing/heat records, coating and condition against approved procurement/design requirements. Preserve marking through cutting and installation. A certificate in a folder must link to the actual pipe or component; matching diameter does not establish grade or wall.

Inspect handling damage and report dents, gouges, coating damage, contamination or distorted ends for appropriate disposition. Do not grind away evidence or use an invented acceptance threshold. Separate quarantine status from available stock and record substituted components through actual approval.

**Worked case.** A cut piece has no transferred identity and a nearby pipe has a valid certificate. The certificate cannot simply be assigned to the cut piece. **Changed case:** chemistry matches a grade family, but required mechanical properties and traceability remain unresolved.

lessons.title: Q08 — Transportation, storage and stringing
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Transportation, storage and stringing

Supports, restraints and lifting arrangements should protect pipe geometry, coating and personnel. Observe the approved handling plan and component condition before/after movement. Keep workers clear of suspended loads and pinch zones; inspection does not require standing under a pipe. Stringing sequence should retain joint identity and prevent unintended stress or contamination.

PHMSA's construction issue guidance describes damage that can arise during handling and installation.[S06] Record actual location and extent, not just “minor handling mark.” A later coating repair cannot automatically resolve metal damage beneath it.

**Worked case.** A sling damages coating and leaves a visible gouge. Raise separate coating and base-metal findings. **Changed case:** the coating is restored; the gouge still needs its own technical disposition.

lessons.title: Q09 — Excavation and safe observation
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Excavation and safe observation

Trench hazards include collapse, water, atmosphere, falling loads, adjacent structures and equipment. A construction-inspection credential does not itself appoint the learner as the excavation competent person. Establish that the responsible competent person and applicable protective/access systems are in place. Observe from safe positions; do not enter an unsafe excavation to measure it.

As a US federal example, OSHA1926.651 requires safe egress for trench excavations4 ft or deeper with no more than25 ft lateral travel; protective-system requirements must also be assessed under1926.652.[S07] Shallower depth is not a universal safe-entry exemption. Reinspection after relevant changes is part of the excavation-control system.

**Worked case.** Rain introduces water and sloughing after the morning inspection. Request removal/protection and competent reassessment under the applicable process. **Changed case:** a ladder is added; egress does not by itself resolve collapse or water hazards.

lessons.title: Q10 — Bending and fit-up geometry
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Bending and fit-up geometry

Bends must preserve acceptable pipe shape, wall and coating under the approved procedure/design. Examine identity, bend location, geometry and observations such as wrinkles or flattening using the actual acceptance basis. Do not improvise allowable ovality or bend radius. Cold bending, manufactured bends and other configurations have different qualification/design considerations.

Fit-up must address alignment, bevel, gap, wall transitions and cleanliness before joining. Excessive force to fit an alignment can introduce stress; it is not automatically acceptable because the weld can bridge the gap. Document the condition before it is concealed by joining.

**Worked case.** A synthetic ovality measure uses(Dmax−Dmin)/Dnom×100. Values510,500 and508 mm give1.969%. That is only the stated geometric measure, not a code pass. **Changed case:** a wrinkle exists despite the number meeting a supplied limit; the wrinkle remains a separate finding.

lessons.title: Q11 — Welding procedure and personnel evidence
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Welding procedure and personnel evidence

Verify applicable qualified procedure, personnel scope and actual production parameters through the project welding system. Procedure qualification, welder qualification and production acceptance address different questions. Changes in process, material, thickness or other applicable variables require the actual governing review; an inspector should not invent qualification ranges.

Keep weld identity linked to pipe ends, personnel, date and procedure. Check preparation and environmental/thermal conditions at the required stage. PHMSA construction findings include problems at fit-up and thickness transitions; these must not be hidden by a completed bead.[S06]

**Worked case.** A qualified welder uses an unsupported procedure for the actual wall transition. Welder credentials do not qualify the procedure. **Changed case:** procedure support is corrected, but completed welds made under the unsupported conditions still require disposition.

lessons.title: Q12 — NDT, repairs and weld maps
lessons.body:
## Q12 — NDT, repairs and weld maps

Examination personnel, procedures, method, extent and acceptance must match the actual project requirements. Link each result to the correct weld, repair cycle and final disposition. A report marked acceptable for weld17 cannot clear weld71 because their numbers resemble one another. No learner qualification here replaces required NDT certification or interpretation authority.

Repairs require authorized method and follow-up examination. Keep the original indication/result and each repair/retest record so the final status can be reconstructed. Do not erase a failure once a later report passes, or count a scheduled retest as completed.

**Worked case.** Twenty welds are listed; eighteen have valid final reports, one failed and one lacks a report. Evidence-backed final coverage is90%, not100%. **Changed case:** the failed weld is repaired but retest pending; it remains unresolved for the required final examination.

lessons.title: Q13 — Coating preparation and application
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Coating preparation and application

Coating quality depends on actual surface condition, preparation, environment, materials, application and cure under the approved system. Check instrument suitability and record the measured location/time. Product shelf life and batch identity matter; so do contamination and conditions that differ from the procedure.

A thicker coating is not automatically better, and a favorable average can hide local low/high readings where individual limits apply. Dry-film thickness, cure and adhesion/discontinuity checks are distinct evidence. Do not mix different coating systems or repair methods without approval.

**Worked case.** Synthetic minimum steel-to-dewpoint margin3°C; steel18°C and dewpoint16°C gives2°C,1°C short. **Changed case:** margin improves later, but coating already applied under the earlier condition needs disposition rather than a rewritten application record.

lessons.title: Q14 — Holiday examination and coating repairs
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Holiday examination and coating repairs

Holiday testing seeks coating discontinuities using the applicable qualified method and settings. Voltage, electrode/contact, grounding, travel and safety requirements depend on the coating and procedure; do not invent one universal setting. Identify examination coverage and repairs by location, then perform required verification of the repair.

An indication is evidence requiring classification and action, not proof of a specific metal defect. Conversely, zero indications from an incorrectly configured instrument is not proof of an intact coating. Preserve calibration/function checks and the actual coating thickness/system basis where required.

**Worked case.** Inspector records no holidays but cannot show the required instrument setup/function check. Result validity is unresolved. **Changed case:** setup is verified but the underside was inaccessible; coverage still cannot be reported complete.

lessons.title: Q15 — Lowering-in, support and crossings
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Lowering-in, support and crossings

Lowering must protect personnel, pipe and coating using the approved coordinated plan. Adequate equipment/support, clear communication and the prepared ditch are part of readiness. PHMSA describes how lowering practices can affect pipe stress and coating condition.[S06] Do not direct lifts beyond appointed competence or stand in the load path for a measurement.

At crossings verify approved profile, separation/support and required consents/inspection evidence. A design drawing does not prove the installed elevation. Record pre-burial condition and any unexpected contact, bending or damage. If an unplanned obstruction appears, obtain an authorized solution rather than force the pipe into place.

**Worked case.** Coating passes before a lowering event that drags pipe against rock. Earlier acceptance does not establish the post-event condition. **Changed case:** the exposed top looks sound; inaccessible contact areas still need appropriate evaluation.

lessons.title: Q16 — Backfill, cover and buried records
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Backfill, cover and buried records

Before burial verify required examinations, supports/padding, coating repairs, survey and release records. Backfill material and placement must meet the project system and avoid damaging pipe/coating or creating unsupported sections. Keep the buried route, joints and crossings traceable while measurements remain available.

Cover is generally a vertical relationship to the relevant surface and pipe position under the governing requirement; do not substitute trench depth without accounting for pipe geometry/reference. Applicable requirements vary by service/location.[S02–S03] Use the actual design and law, not a single universal number.

**Worked case.** Supplied ground elevation102.4 m and top-of-pipe101.1 m give1.3 m cover. Synthetic requirement1.2 m is met at that point only. **Changed case:** restored grade becomes102.2 m; cover is1.1 m,0.1 short. Update actual grade/as-built evidence.

lessons.title: Q17 — Pressure-test readiness and exclusion controls
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Pressure-test readiness and exclusion controls

Pressure testing is a high-energy operation requiring an approved plan and competent appointed personnel. The inspector reviews applicable boundary, equipment ratings, medium, pressure/time criteria, instrument calibration, elevation, isolation, exclusion areas, communications and emergency response; this course does not provide an operating procedure. No live test is required for its assessment.

Pressure at one gauge may not equal pressure at every elevation in a liquid-filled section. Air entrapment, thermal effects and instrument uncertainty also matter. Establish that the approved plan addresses relevant constraints before judging a chart. Never tighten a leaking pressurized connection or enter an exclusion area to diagnose a result.

**Worked case.** A proposed test boundary contains a component with an unverified rating. Do not infer suitability from pipe rating. **Changed case:** the component is rated adequately but the elevation correction is absent; that separate basis still needs review.

lessons.title: Q18 — Test records and hydrostatic arithmetic
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Test records and hydrostatic arithmetic

For a static liquid with supplied densityρ, pressure difference isρgΔh. Pressure increases toward lower elevations. Express units consistently and compare high- and low-point conditions to the approved limits. This elementary calculation is not a full pressure-test design or proof of maximum allowable operating pressure.

Review chart identity, instrument calibration, temperatures, duration, interruptions and actual deviations. A pressure change may have several causes and requires the approved interpretation; do not simply label every fall a leak or every stable gauge proof of all construction quality. A passed test does not replace unrelated coating, weld-identity or environmental records.

**Worked case.** Water density1,000 kg/m³, g9.81 and elevation difference20 m gives196,200 Pa=0.1962 MPa. **Changed case:** the gauge is at the low point; the point20 m higher has that much lower static pressure, not higher.

lessons.title: Q19 — Cleaning, dewatering, drying and commissioning interfaces
lessons.body:
## Q19 — Cleaning, dewatering, drying and commissioning interfaces

Precommissioning activities need their own approved procedures, boundaries, equipment, permits and competent teams. Cleaning/pigging introduces moving equipment and stored-pressure hazards; dewatering creates discharge and environmental issues; drying/inerting can introduce oxygen deficiency. Inspection should verify specified evidence without improvising operating steps.

Trace the tested section through tie-ins, cleaning and final configuration. A tie-in outside the tested boundary needs its actual required acceptance route. Record any newly installed components or changes that affect the previous evidence. “Ready for commissioning” must mean the project's conditions are actually satisfied.

**Worked case.** A new spool is installed after the section test; the old chart does not automatically cover it. **Changed case:** its separate acceptance route is complete, but discharge/restoration obligations remain open; report those independently.

lessons.title: Q20 — Cathodic-protection and electrical interfaces
lessons.body:
## Q20 — Cathodic-protection and electrical interfaces

Coating and cathodic protection are related but distinct parts of corrosion control. Construction inspection may include specified test leads, isolation devices, anodes, bonds and their physical installation records. Electrical measurements and acceptance require the appropriate qualified personnel, method and actual criteria. Do not use a remembered potential as a universal pass.

Protect identification and continuity/isolation evidence from later construction damage. A wire present at a test post does not prove correct connection or performance. Coordinate with corrosion specialists and preserve as-built connections and test results.

**Worked case.** Two test leads are swapped in the record. A plausible meter reading cannot establish the intended pipe connection. **Changed case:** labels are corrected but a lead was damaged during backfill; documentation accuracy does not repair continuity.

lessons.title: Q21 — Water, erosion, waste and restoration
lessons.body:
## Q21 — Water, erosion, waste and restoration

Restoration follows actual permits, land agreements and environmental plan, including drainage, soil, erosion controls, waste and monitoring. Inspect what was actually restored rather than mark a spread complete because pipework ended. Temporary controls may need to remain until permanent stabilization is established.

Test-water sourcing/discharge and contaminated material handling require their approved routes. Clear appearance is not proof of permitted discharge quality. Record unresolved erosion or settlement with ownership and follow-up. Do not remove protective measures merely to improve final photographs.

**Worked case.** A ditch is backfilled but runoff bypasses an erosion control into a watercourse. Construction completion does not close environmental response. **Changed case:** the control is repaired; any downstream impact and required reporting still need disposition under the plan.

lessons.title: Q22 — Nonconformance, rework and acceptance
lessons.body:
## Q22 — Nonconformance, rework and acceptance

State the requirement, observation, location, evidence and affected scope for each deviation. Distinguish correction of the physical work from correction of the process that caused it. An authorized disposition may call for repair, replacement, further evaluation or another permitted route; the inspector must not invent acceptance concessions.

Verify actual completion and necessary retesting before closing. Preserve original and revised records. A signed repair plan is not a completed repair; a work-order close is not proof of the required examination. Escalate repeated trends that indicate a broader process problem.

**Worked case.** Several weld-map transpositions recur. Correcting one report does not address why identity errors continue. **Changed case:** the process is fixed prospectively; prior affected records still need reconciliation.

lessons.title: Q23 — Daily reports and defensible quantities
lessons.body:
## Q23 — Daily reports and defensible quantities

Daily reports should identify spread/location, activities, conditions, workforce/resources relevant to observation, inspections/results, hold releases, deviations and pending actions. Quantities need a defined basis: delivered, strung, welded, examined, buried and accepted lengths are different. Do not use one to imply all others.

Photographs need location/time/context and must not replace required measurements. Record limitations honestly, including activities not witnessed. Correct errors through a traceable amendment rather than overwrite inconvenient history. Keep commercial quantity disputes separate from technical acceptance while preserving accurate evidence for both.

**Worked case.** A shift reports500 m strung and400 m welded. Reporting500 m accepted would be unsupported. **Changed case:** all500 m welded next shift but only450 m examined; remaining evidence still matters.

lessons.title: Q24 — Final handover and credential limits
lessons.body:
## Q24 — Final handover and credential limits

The final dossier links route/as-built records, materials, joining/examination, coating, burial, testing, environmental obligations, nonconformances and authorized release to the actual installed asset. Check that documents share correct identifiers and revisions. A binder can be complete by file count yet contain unresolved acceptance conditions.

Present current status, open constraints, responsible owners and follow-up plainly. Employer authorization and any regulatory/role-specific qualifications remain separate from course completion. A VNDRLY learning credential must not imply API1169 certification or permit a learner to approve construction outside appointed competence.

**Worked case.** All charts are filed, but a post-test tie-in and two coating repairs have no final evidence. Do not recommend unconditional handover. **Changed case:** conditional release is actually authorized; retain its exact conditions rather than summarize it as unrestricted completion.


---

courses.title: VUC042 | VUC042 construction inspection workbook

content.title: VUC042 | VUC042 construction inspection workbook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC042 construction inspection workbook
lessons.body:
# VUC042 construction inspection workbook

Every project, limit and test value below is synthetic. These records teach review decisions, not actual excavation, joining, lifting or pressure-test operation. Use the supplied basis; when it is insufficient, state exactly what is missing instead of inventing a pass.

lessons.title: W01 — Route and permission conflict
lessons.body:
## W01 — Route and permission conflict

**Record.** Approved metric alignment runs station1+250 to1+430, datumD1, revision3. A field sketch revision2 shifts30 m of route outside the approved corridor. Landowner verbally permits it; environmental approval and crossing-owner consent are not documented. A survey point uses datumD2 without transformation. Contractor wants quantities certified from the sketch.

**Task.** Compute the simple station difference, identify which other conclusions cannot follow, and draft a change/permission response.

**Worked response.** Station difference180 m under the stated simple convention. It does not establish actual installed length across an unapproved shift or a reconciled coordinate location. Old revision, corridor change, environmental/crossing permissions and datum mismatch need resolution through their responsible authorities. Verbal land access does not establish every permit. Preserve actual observations and do not certify approved construction from that sketch.

**Changed case.** New route approved, but D2 transformation remains unverified. Approval resolves route authorization, not coordinate reliability.

**Rubric10.** Arithmetic1; four distinct issues4; responsible pathway2; honest quantity/coordinate limitation3.

lessons.title: W02 — Pipe tally and identity
lessons.body:
## W02 — Pipe tally and identity

**Record.** Ten nominal12 m joints delivered, IDsJ1–J10. J4 cut into7 m and5 m pieces; only7 m piece retains identity. J8 has a coating gouge with visible metal damage. Eight joints, including both J4 pieces counted as one original joint, are recorded strung. The report states120 m installed/accepted because120 m was delivered.

**Task.** Reconcile nominal delivered and strung lengths, identify identity and damage actions, and correct status wording.

**Worked response.** Delivered120 m. Eight nominal original joints strung represent96 m if actual lengths match the supplied nominal values; J4's pieces total12 m, not24. Delivered/strung is not welded, examined, buried or accepted. Transfer/restore traceability of the5 m piece through evidence; do not borrow another certificate. Separate coating and metal damage disposition for J8. Actual surveyed/tallied lengths govern final quantities, not nominal assumptions alone.

**Changed case.** J8 coating repaired, but metal-damage disposition absent. Close only verified coating work; do not release base metal by implication.

**Rubric.** Lengths3; identity2; independent damage findings2; status distinction3.

lessons.title: W03 — Safe excavation and geometry review
lessons.body:
## W03 — Safe excavation and geometry review

**Record.** Scenario explicitly uses US federal construction excavation requirements. Trench depth5 ft, ladder travel30 ft, water accumulating and soil sloughing after rain. A morning inspection preceded the rain. No current protective-system suitability evidence is available. A nearby buried facility's marks conflict with the drawing. An inspector is asked to enter and measure cover.

**Task.** Identify immediate exposure concerns and the correct role response; calculate the ladder-travel excess relative to the cited25 ft rule.

**Worked response.**30−25=5 ft beyond the stated lateral egress limit, but moving a ladder alone does not resolve collapse, water or protective-system concerns. Do not enter to gather a measurement. Use the employer's removal/protection/escalation process and competent-person reassessment; reconcile facility location through the damage-prevention process before affected excavation. The course does not designate the learner competent person or supply a protective-system design.

**Changed case.** Ladder moved to20 ft. Egress distance improves; water, soil change, protection and facility uncertainty remain independent.

**Rubric.** Arithmetic1; hazard recognition4; competent/authority response3; no unsafe entry2.

lessons.title: W04 — Bend, weld and NDT records
lessons.body:
## W04 — Bend, weld and NDT records

**Record.** Synthetic bend measure(Dmax−Dmin)/Dnom×100 uses510,500,508 mm. Project example permits≤2.0% under that measure, and separately requires no unresolved wrinkle indication. A wrinkle is reported. Weld map has20 welds;18 have valid final NDT reports, one failed awaiting repair and one report references the wrong ID. A qualified welder worked a transition not supported by the provided procedure evidence.

**Task.** Calculate geometry and final-report coverage and list independent release barriers.

**Worked response.**10/508×100=1.9685%, within the supplied numerical criterion; wrinkle remains unresolved. Valid final NDT evidence18/20=90%. Failed weld, wrong report identity and procedure support for the transition need distinct authorized disposition. The geometry number, welder qualification and report count do not cancel these issues. Preserve repair/retest identity and original results.

**Changed case.** Failed weld repaired and retest passes with valid identity, raising final-report evidence to19/20=95%; wrong-ID report and any other unresolved findings remain.

**Rubric.** Calculations3; independent findings4; authority/traceability2; no false overall pass1.

lessons.title: W05 — Coating and post-lowering evidence
lessons.body:
## W05 — Coating and post-lowering evidence

**Record.** Synthetic coating requirement: steel at least3°C above dewpoint; individual thickness450–650 μm. At application, steel18°C/dewpoint16°C. Readings500,440,620 μm. Holiday report shows complete top-side examination only; underside inaccessible. After lowering, a rock-contact event damages an area previously examined. Instrument setup sheet is absent.

**Task.** Calculate margin, individual failure and mean, then distinguish what remains unproven.

**Worked response.** Margin2°C is1°C short.440 μm is10 below minimum; mean520 μm does not cure local failure. Setup validity, underside coverage and post-contact condition remain unresolved, in addition to application conditions and thickness. Map damage and obtain qualified coating/metal evaluation as relevant. Earlier examination does not prove post-lowering condition.

**Changed case.** Setup sheet recovered and valid. It closes setup evidence only; coverage and subsequent damage are unchanged.

**Rubric.** Arithmetic3; five independent concerns5; appropriate record/disposition2.

lessons.title: W06 — Survey, cover and hydrostatic elevation
lessons.body:
## W06 — Survey, cover and hydrostatic elevation

**Record.** At pointA ground102.4 m/top-of-pipe101.1 m; restored ground later102.2 m. Supplied cover minimum1.2 m. A separate water-filled training test section has gauge at its low point and a high point20 m above. Gauge pressure5.00 MPa; density1,000 kg/m³ and g9.81 m/s². Synthetic minimum required at high point4.85 MPa; low-point component maximum5.10 MPa. This arithmetic does not constitute an approved test plan.

**Task.** Calculate original/final cover, high-point pressure and the minimum low-point gauge pressure needed for the supplied high-point criterion; compare with low-point maximum.

**Worked response.** Original cover1.3 m; after grade change1.1 m,0.1 below supplied minimum. Elevation difference gives0.1962 MPa. At5.00 MPa low point, high point4.8038 MPa,0.0462 below required4.85. Meeting that minimum under these simplified assumptions would require5.0462 MPa at the gauge, below5.10 by0.0538 MPa. This small arithmetic margin is not approval to raise pressure: instrument uncertainty, actual density/temperatures, all component limits and the authorized plan still need review.

**Changed case.** Low-point maximum is instead5.02 MPa. The simplified required5.0462 exceeds it by0.0262 MPa; requirements conflict and need authorized test/design resolution, not an operator guess.

**Rubric.** Cover2; pressure calculations4; conflict interpretation2; no live-test authorization2.

lessons.title: W07 — Pressure-chart completeness and tie-in
lessons.body:
## W07 — Pressure-chart completeness and tie-in

**Record.** Supplied test plan requires8 continuous hours of valid records inside its specified limits. Chart runs08:00–16:00 but instrument fails11:00–11:30. Temperature changes are recorded but not evaluated. A spool is added outside the tested boundary afterward. An operator says stable pressure at16:00 proves everything passes.

**Task.** Calculate recorded gap and available valid-duration total; explain why duration addition alone does not establish the continuous requirement or tie-in acceptance.

**Worked response.** Gap30 minutes; valid total7.5 hours, separated into3 and4.5 hours. No8 continuous valid hours are established. Endpoint pressure alone does not resolve the gap, temperature interpretation or post-test spool. Apply the actual authorized test-data disposition and separate tie-in acceptance route; do not prescribe retesting or pressure changes without that authority.

**Changed case.** A separate valid acceptance record covers the spool. Test-chart interpretation remains unresolved; one issue's closure cannot clear the other.

**Rubric.** Time calculations3; continuous-data reasoning2; separate boundaries2; appropriate authority and no invented pass3.

lessons.title: W08 — Restoration and handover status
lessons.body:
## W08 — Restoration and handover status

**Record.** A spread has100 required acceptance items:92 verified,5 repair plans approved but unexecuted,3 environmental follow-ups open. Delivered length1,000 m; welded900; valid final examination850; buried800. A lead wire's as-built label was corrected, but continuity test remains missing. Slide says100% complete because all forms exist.

**Task.** Calculate verified-item percentage, state distinct quantities and draft an honest owner summary.

**Worked response.**92% items verified, not92% safe. Retain1,000/900/850/800 m as different stages; none proves the next. Five planned repairs and three environmental conditions remain open, with owners and completion evidence needed. Correct lead labeling does not prove continuity. File presence is not fulfillment of technical conditions. No unconditional release recommendation is supported by this record.

**Changed case.** Two repairs executed and verified;94% items now verified,3 repair and3 environmental items remain. Lead test remains separately pending unless explicitly included and closed in the item register.

**Rubric.** Percentages2; quantity distinctions2; independent open items3; owners/conditional communication3.

lessons.title: I42 — Spread handover challenge
lessons.body:
## I42 — Spread handover challenge

**Dossier.** SectionA: materials and welding accepted; coating underside examination incomplete before burial. SectionB: coating and burial records valid; one final weld report has transposed ID; test chart covers A/B but has an unexplained sensor gap. SectionC: post-test tie-in with approved procedure but no recorded final examination. Restoration has an eroding outlet; environmental inspector's follow-up not completed. Project manager asks for signed“ready for service”today.

**Task.** Produce section evidence matrix, prioritized issue/action register and a two-minute owner handover. Identify actual limits without specifying unsafe excavation or pressure operations. Distinguish document correction, required investigation and actual corrective work.

**Worked response.** A needs authorized disposition of inaccessible unexamined coating, not a fabricated pre-burial pass. B needs valid weld identity and test-gap interpretation. C's approved procedure does not establish completed final examination or tie-in acceptance. Environmental obligation remains open independently. Record owners/authority and dependencies; do not recommend unconditional service readiness. A safe investigation plan must come from the responsible technical/operating authorities.

**Changed dossier.** B weld identity reconciled; chart gap has a signed technical disposition with conditions not yet fulfilled. C examination passes through its actual approved route. A and restoration unchanged. Close only B identity and C's stated evidence; track chart conditions separately and retain A/environmental issues.

**Rubric30.** Evidence/identity6; technical reasoning6; independent scope/closure6; feasible authorized actions6; clear honest communication6. Pass24 with minimum3 in each dimension and no unresolved critical error.

lessons.title: Reusable forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable forms

**Daily observation:** date/time___ spread/station/datum___ drawing revision___ activity___ actually observed/evidence source___ conditions___ quantity and stage___ inspection result/criterion___ limitations___ open actions/owner___ inspector___.

**Pipe/weld map:** joint/heat___ actual length___ cut-piece transfer___ installed station___ weld ID___ personnel/procedure___ NDT original/repair/final___ coating examination/repair___ burial survey___ test boundary___ exceptions___.

**Test review:** approved plan/revision___ boundary/components___ gauge/sensor locations/elevations___ calibration___ pressure/temperature/time basis___ gaps/deviations___ technical disposition/conditions___ authority/date___.

**Nonconformance:** requirement/source___ actual observation/location___ evidence___ affected scope___ immediate safe response___ authority___ disposition___ actual verification___ residual condition/owner___.

**Handover:** section___ installed/as-built identity___ verified evidence___ open constraint___ responsible owner___ due/trigger___ approval and exact conditions___ actual closure record___.


---

courses.title: VUC042 | VUC042 instructor, practical and credential guide

content.title: VUC042 | VUC042 instructor, practical and credential guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC042 instructor, practical and credential guide
lessons.body: # VUC042 instructor, practical and credential guide

lessons.title: Outcomes and delivery
lessons.body:
## Outcomes and delivery

Learners must identify applicable project requirements, verify route/material/joining/coating/burial evidence, recognize unsafe or unsupported work, interpret supplied measurements/test records, manage nonconformances and communicate defensible handover. This original learning program is not API1169 certification, a regulatory appointment or a license for specialist construction operations.

Instructor needs pipeline-construction inspection experience and knowledge of the job interfaces, with access to qualified welding/NDT/coating/corrosion/environmental/survey specialists when instruction exceeds their competence. Establish learner readiness in units, drawing references, industrial safety and basic report writing. Provide missing prerequisite instruction rather than count an unsupported pass.

Plan48 instructional hours:12 chapter/check teaching,12 workbook practice,12 stations,3 integrated I42,6 targeted remediation/readiness and3 final. Breaks/additional instruction are outside the allocation; no actual attendance is claimed. Follow construction sequence through Q01–Q24 and interleave the matching workbook/station. Require individual records even when teams discuss the case. Ask learners to separate “observed,” “inferred,” “approved,” “performed” and “verified” in every debrief.

No live excavation, suspended load, energized electrical work, pressure test, welding, coating chemicals or NDT radiation is used. Equipment is benign: current course/workbook, calculator, tabletop alignment/pipe map, labeled inert pipe substitutes or blocks, ruler/caliper, safe level or supplied reference elevation cards, inert coating-thickness sample cards, document packets and blank forms. Check all mockups for sharp edges and stable placement. Record assessor reference measurements and instrument resolution before assessment.

Four stations P04/P07/P10/P16 require actual observed benign mapping/measurement demonstrations. Remote assessment requires an observed equivalent setup with known references; if unavailable, mark those outcomes pending, not passed from a quiz. Adapt accessible instruments/response formats while preserving the outcome. These demonstrations qualify only the limited skills tested, not field survey licensure or actual pipeline installation competence.

lessons.title: Station assessment rules
lessons.body:
## Station assessment rules

Score five dimensions0–2: evidence identity, correct technique/calculation, interpretation, safe authority/limitations and traceable communication. Pass8/10 with no zero dimension and no unresolved critical error. Critical errors: invented witness/report evidence, unsafe entry/live-operation instruction, concealing unresolved failures or unsupported unconditional release. Explain the precise failure and provide targeted instruction before changed reassessment.

lessons.title: P01 — Witness versus report
lessons.body:
## P01 — Witness versus report

Use Q01. Learner writes an entry for an event not personally seen but supported by a contractor report. Expected: source and limitation explicit. Changed evidence is an unlabeled photograph; do not convert it into personal observation.

lessons.title: P02 — Requirements conflict
lessons.body:
## P02 — Requirements conflict

Use W01 and the gas/liquid example in Q02. Learner identifies jurisdiction, specification, revision and authorization gaps and the responsible decision route. Change a project requirement to stricter than the legal example; learner must not silently waive it.

lessons.title: P03 — Hold-point readiness
lessons.body:
## P03 — Hold-point readiness

Present lowering scheduled with coating examination pending. Learner documents dependency and missing resources, then receives an instrument without the procedure. Expected: actual qualified capability, not attendance/equipment alone.

lessons.title: P04 — Physical route mapping
lessons.body:
## P04 — Physical route mapping

On a tabletop metric alignment with reference marks, learner locates1+250 and1+430, measures the model distance using a declared scale and records datum/revision. Assessor compares with predeclared reference tolerance. Change one coordinate card to another datum; learner records a conflict instead of forcing alignment.

lessons.title: P05 — Environmental boundary
lessons.body:
## P05 — Environmental boundary

Use W01's corridor shift. Learner maps affected permissions and writes an appropriate stop/referral note. Change landowner consent to written but environmental permission absent; expected independent approvals retained.

lessons.title: P06 — Locate discrepancy
lessons.body:
## P06 — Locate discrepancy

Present two conflicting facility-location cards. Learner describes safe affected-work suspension and owner/locate reconciliation. Change to an unmarked exposed line; no guessed identity or depth-based clearance.

lessons.title: P07 — Physical pipe identity transfer
lessons.body:
## P07 — Physical pipe identity transfer

Use inert labeled blocks representing J4 cut pieces and two candidate heat records. Learner checks actual tags, records missing linkage and traces a supplied valid cutting record when introduced. Expected: no borrowed certificate. This does not qualify live cutting or marking operations.

lessons.title: P08 — Handling damage
lessons.body:
## P08 — Handling damage

Use a benign sketch showing coating scrape and metal gouge. Learner records two findings by location and refers to actual technical acceptance. Change coating repair complete; metal finding persists. No grinding or lifting demonstration.

lessons.title: P09 — Excavation decision
lessons.body:
## P09 — Excavation decision

Use W03. Learner computes5 ft egress excess and identifies water/sloughing/protection/location issues. Expected no unsafe entry and responsible competent-person response. Move ladder to20 ft in changed case; remaining hazards still matter.

lessons.title: P10 — Physical geometry measurement
lessons.body:
## P10 — Physical geometry measurement

Measure two diameters on a benign oval model with checked caliper and declared nominal dimension, record instrument/units and compute the supplied ovality measure. Assessor checks against known dimensions/tolerance. Then use W04's1.9685% result. Introduce a separate wrinkle notation; numerical compliance cannot clear it.

lessons.title: P11 — Welding support
lessons.body:
## P11 — Welding support

Use W04's unsupported transition and qualified welder. Learner separates procedure/personnel/production requirements and maps completed affected welds. New approval applies prospectively; historical work still needs disposition.

lessons.title: P12 — Weld-map reconciliation
lessons.body:
## P12 — Weld-map reconciliation

Use W04 reports. Learner links actual IDs, counts18/20 valid final evidence and preserves failed/wrong-ID records. Changed valid repair/retest yields19/20, not100%. Required interpretation remains with qualified personnel.

lessons.title: P13 — Coating data
lessons.body:
## P13 — Coating data

Use W05. Learner calculates2°C margin,1°C shortfall,440 μm local failure and520 μm mean. Expected: independent application/local criteria, no mean-based acceptance. Change later weather only; earlier work history persists.

lessons.title: P14 — Holiday validity
lessons.body:
## P14 — Holiday validity

Use W05 missing setup/underside coverage. Learner identifies missing validity and coverage evidence without inventing test voltage. Recover setup sheet in changed case; underside and later contact still need disposition.

lessons.title: P15 — Lowering event
lessons.body:
## P15 — Lowering event

Use rock-contact sketch and approved plan excerpt stating inspection required after damage events. Learner records event/location and safe qualified evaluation request. Change top surface appears sound; unseen contact area remains uncertain.

lessons.title: P16 — Physical reference and cover
lessons.body:
## P16 — Physical reference and cover

Use tabletop ground/top-of-pipe markers with known scale. Learner reads elevations from supplied verified benchmark or safe model level, calculates vertical difference and records reference/units. Assessor compares actual readings with reference tolerance. Then W06 changes grade; expected1.3 to1.1 m and0.1 short of supplied minimum. No excavation entry.

lessons.title: P17 — Test readiness review
lessons.body:
## P17 — Test readiness review

Use a document-only test boundary with unknown-rated component, sensor map and missing exclusion plan. Learner lists gaps and responsible test authority. Change rating resolved; unresolved measurement/protection items remain. No live pressure activity.

lessons.title: P18 — Static pressure arithmetic
lessons.body:
## P18 — Static pressure arithmetic

Use W06. Learner calculates0.1962 MPa differential,4.8038 high-point pressure and5.0462 simplified required gauge pressure; recognizes that no field adjustment is authorized. Changed5.02 maximum conflicts by0.0262 MPa. Show work and units.

lessons.title: P19 — Post-test configuration
lessons.body:
## P19 — Post-test configuration

Use W07 added spool. Learner maps old boundary and new component, identifies actual separate acceptance need, and distinguishes cleaning/discharge obligations. Changed spool record closes only that route.

lessons.title: P20 — Corrosion-control interface
lessons.body:
## P20 — Corrosion-control interface

Use switched lead labels and absent continuity result. Learner identifies required qualified verification and as-built correction. Changed labels valid but lead damaged: physical condition remains unresolved. No energized measurements.

lessons.title: P21 — Restoration handover
lessons.body:
## P21 — Restoration handover

Use W08 environmental follow-ups and eroding outlet. Learner records owners/plan conditions and refuses to equate burial with restoration. Change repair complete but downstream follow-up pending; retain independent issue.

lessons.title: P22 — Nonconformance closure
lessons.body:
## P22 — Nonconformance closure

Provide an approved repair plan with no completion evidence. Learner records planned/open status and exact evidence needed to close. Changed work completed but required retest pending; closure remains conditional.

lessons.title: P23 — Quantity integrity
lessons.body:
## P23 — Quantity integrity

Use W08 four stage lengths. Learner writes distinct delivered/welded/examined/buried totals and states need for location matching. Changed aggregate counts increase; no assumption that all refer to the same sections.

lessons.title: P24 — Owner briefing
lessons.body:
## P24 — Owner briefing

Use I42. Learner presents two-minute summary plus section/evidence register. Expected: independent A/B/C/test/environmental issues and authorized response. Changed dossier closes only specific verified elements and preserves release conditions.

lessons.title: Assessments and remediation
lessons.body:
## Assessments and remediation

Correct all48 formative checks with explained reasoning. Pass each of8 workbook labs8/10, all24 stations8/10 with no zero dimension, and I42 at24/30 with minimum3/6 per dimension. Actual physical demonstrations must be observed and recorded for a learner credential. A course author has not performed them on behalf of a student.

Controlled final:24 original cases×3 decisions×2 points=144 maximum;180 minutes; calculator/coursebook allowed, keys/collaboration/outside assistance prohibited. Pass116/144 and at least4/6 per domain, with no unresolved critical error. These are VNDRLY rules, not API's external exam format. Score2 correct/supported,1 safe/incomplete,0 incorrect/missing/unsafe; equivalent sound reasoning accepted.

Preserve first result, teach failed domains and issue changed private prompts without keys. Reassess relevant demonstrated skills as well as written answers when the failure concerns technique. Two unsuccessful changed attempts require individualized teaching and a fresh equivalent supervised assessment. Offer documented appeal and another competent assessor where feasible. Accessible text/instruments or extra time may be approved without removing outcomes or coaching the answer.

lessons.title: Records, credential and maintenance
lessons.body:
## Records, credential and maintenance

Record learner identity, version/hash, actual dates/hours, individual checks/labs/station artifacts, reference measurements/observations, I42, final scores, critical findings, remediation, changed results, accommodations, appeal and completion authority. Form: learner___ activity___ actual evidence___ reference/criterion___ score___ limitation___ feedback___ reassessment___ assessor/date___. Protect private keys and personal records under actual access/retention controls; separate files alone do not enforce protection.

Award **VNDRLY/U Pipeline Construction Inspection — Original Learning Program Completion** only after every gate. Do not claim API1169, professional licensure, welding/NDT/excavation qualifications or employer release authority. Employer role appointment and field-specific competence remain separate. Materials completion means the learning resources exist; it is not an actual learner credential or live construction acceptance.

Review content annually as VNDRLY maintenance and when guidance, project requirements, incident lessons or assessment defects change. This is not an external recertification interval. lessons.title: VUC042 primary sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC042 primary sources and coverage

Reviewed2026-11-18. Original materials using accessible sources; no unavailable-PDF access pursuit. This is not comprehensive API1169/API1104/CSA/ASME equivalence. Actual jurisdiction/project documents govern live work. All workbook limits are synthetic except the explicitly identified OSHA egress example.

- **S01 [API1169 program](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/certifications/api1169).** External program identity and construction-inspection subject. Not proof of clause coverage or external examination readiness; no proprietary questions copied.
- **S02 [49CFR192 SubpartG](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-B/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-192/subpart-G).** US gas transmission/main construction context. Applicability and any other governing subparts must be established; not a universal pipeline specification.
- **S03 [49CFR195 SubpartD](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/subtitle-B/chapter-I/subchapter-D/part-195/subpart-D).** US hazardous-liquid construction context. Kept distinct from gas rules; no universal cover/acceptance table inferred.
- **S04 [CER Onshore Pipeline Regulations guidance](https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/en/about/acts-regulations/cer-act-regulations-guidance-notes-related-documents/onshore-pipeline/guidance-notes-for-the-canada-energy-regulator-onshore-pipeline-regulations.html).** Supports coordination of relevant personnel and environmental plans in the Canadian regulated context. Guidance and actual legal obligations are not collapsed into one universal rule.
- **S05 [CER construction near pipelines](https://www.cer-rec.gc.ca/en/safety-environment/damage-prevention/contractors/construction-near-pipelines/index.html).** Locating, company consent and safety-information interface. Actual applicability/permissions depend on the work and jurisdiction.
- **S06 [PHMSA typical construction issues](https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/technical-resources/pipeline/pipeline-construction/pipeline-construction-typical-construction).** Illustrates handling, fit-up/joining and coating/lowering concerns. Does not supply the fictional workbook criteria or authorize inspection methods.
- **S07 OSHA [1926.651](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.651) and [1926.652](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.652).** US excavation egress, hazards and protective-system context. Four-foot egress trigger and25-foot lateral-travel rule are explicitly cited; no automatic shallow-trench safety exemption is taught.

lessons.body:
## Objective mapping

| Domains | Instruction/application | Reference context |
