courses.title: VUC045 | VUC045 instructor delivery and practical evaluations

content.title: VUC045 | VUC045 instructor delivery and practical evaluations
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC045 instructor delivery and practical evaluations
lessons.body: # VUC045 instructor delivery and practical evaluations

lessons.title: Delivery plan and entry
lessons.body:
## Delivery plan and entry

Use instructors/assessors with demonstrated competence in each method they teach, actual equipment and applicable employer procedure. Course authorship does not appoint an ASNT examiner or Level III. Learners need basic units, arithmetic and safe-work literacy; diagnose these with W02/W05 before instrument work, teach missing foundations and permit appropriate language/access support without supplying examination answers. Verify applicable vision and workplace prerequisites separately.

Planned learning64hours:16instruction/demonstration,12application labs,20supervised method stations,4integrated dossier,8remediation/rehearsal and4controlled final. This is a VNDRLY preparation plan, not a claimed ASNT minimum or guarantee of proficiency. Extend method practice as required. Teach Q01–04 first; demonstrate VT, PT, MT, UT and RT interpretation in their blocks; complete W01–08; integrate coverage/authority in I45; assess independently. All methods are studied, but the learning record lists only those actually demonstrated. No radiation exposure, radioactive source handling or live high-energy test is part of these stations.

lessons.title: Facility and specimen set
lessons.body:
## Facility and specimen set

Provide a supervised benign training space; clean identified mock components; dimensional instruments/light meter; suitable optical/remote viewing equipment; compatible approved PT materials, timers and ventilation/PPE; MT apparatus and known reference specimen under competent supervision; UT instrument/probes/couplant/reference blocks and known training specimens; and legally available pre-existing radiographs/digital images with documented reference findings. Use the relevant equipment manuals and actual approved examination instructions. Do not introduce unsafe equipment faults; use fault cards and isolated demonstrations.

Reference specimen truth must be established independently of the learner: signed map of known features, dimensions/locations and method suitability, retained privately by assessor. A manufactured notch is a training reflector, not proof of sensitivity to every service crack. For actual blind practical evaluation, assessor selects an identified specimen with at least one known relevant feature and one geometry/nonrelevant feature, plus a sound comparison region, appropriate to the chosen method. The supplied tasks and scoring below govern learning; actual instrument/chemical limits come from approved procedures and product instructions. Workbook limits are paper-only.

lessons.title: Scoring and independent performance
lessons.body:
## Scoring and independent performance

Each station scores four listed criteria0–2:2 independent correct action with evidence/reasoning;1 safe incomplete response needing a prompt;0 incorrect, absent or unsafe. Require6/8 in every station and corrected gaps. Critical errors—fabricated coverage/results, unauthorized radiation action, concealed invalid checks or unsupported qualification—fail the attempt. Record demonstration, coached practice and independent assessment separately.

Mandatory observed benign hands-on stations: P05/P06(VT),P07/P08/P09(PT),P10/P11/P12(MT),P13/P14/P15/P16(UT), and P17/P18/P19(RT image interpretation only). Where a learner cannot perform a method's required task, record that method incomplete, not passed by discussion. All other stations require independent supplied-record decisions. No overall practical-preparation completion until all required method learning tasks pass; no external Level II certification is issued. Radiation-operation practical is expressly excluded and requires a separately authorized program.

lessons.title: P01 — Scope and credential distinction
lessons.body:
## P01 — Scope and credential distinction

Use W01 and two sample records, one PT learning-only and one employer-authorized VT record. Candidate identifies each scope and requested-task mismatch. Score record classification, missing evidence, safe assignment decision and accurate credential wording.

lessons.title: P02 — Product and discontinuity reasoning
lessons.body:
## P02 — Product and discontinuity reasoning

Supply a rolled-plate sketch, cast mock component and welded joint with known geometric features. Candidate identifies plausible examination questions and avoids diagnosing solely from appearance. Score product history, expected orientation/location, geometry distinction and appropriate method referral.

lessons.title: P03 — Write a reproducible instruction
lessons.body:
## P03 — Write a reproducible instruction

Using V45 and the supplied task form, candidate prepares a six-face VT instruction with document identity, checks, coverage, measurements, criteria and stop conditions. Score traceability, executable sequence, complete coverage and correct acceptance/authority. A title or list of methods is not an instruction.

lessons.title: P04 — Safe readiness walkdown
lessons.body:
## P04 — Safe readiness walkdown

Candidate inspects the actual training area and responds to solvent/ignition, moving-part and radiation-boundary cards. Score hazard recognition, task authorization, stop/report action and valid restart evidence. Do not physically create the unsafe conditions.

lessons.title: P05 — Lighting and optical setup
lessons.body:
## P05 — Lighting and optical setup

On a benign mock part, candidate measures illumination at required locations, adjusts approved viewing to avoid glare and demonstrates reference-feature visibility. Score actual meter use, viewing/scale plane, resolution check and limitation record. Assessor records observed values; no invented readings.

lessons.title: P06 — VT coverage and measurement
lessons.body:
## P06 — VT coverage and measurement

Candidate independently examines all faces of the identified mock part, measures the assessor-known dimensions and maps features. Score systematic coverage, instrument technique, indication/geometry distinction and comparison with the supplied learning criteria. Use W02 as changed paper case.

lessons.title: P07 — PT system selection
lessons.body:
## P07 — PT system selection

With actual labeled materials and procedure, candidate verifies compatibility, surface suitability and method sequence. Score consumable identity, surface/preclean assessment, process applicability and safe handling. Hold unknown materials or unsuitable surfaces.

lessons.title: P08 — PT execution
lessons.body:
## P08 — PT execution

Candidate performs the approved safe PT process on a known training specimen, timing and recording each required stage. Score preparation, actual timed sequence, controlled removal/development and viewing conditions. Assessor intervenes for safety and records intervention; coached execution does not count as independent assessment.

lessons.title: P09 — PT evaluation
lessons.body:
## P09 — PT evaluation

Candidate maps actual specimen indications, distinguishes relevant/nonrelevant/false possibilities, compares to supplied criteria and records limitations. Score observed detection, location/dimensions, supported interpretation and correct disposition. Missing a known required detectable feature or accepting an invalid process requires reteaching and a changed specimen.

lessons.title: P10 — MT suitability and direction
lessons.body:
## P10 — MT suitability and direction

Using a ferromagnetic reference part and nonferromagnetic label card, candidate establishes suitability and sketches required field directions relative to known feature orientations. Score material decision, directional reasoning, coverage plan and qualification boundary.

lessons.title: P11 — MT setup verification
lessons.body:
## P11 — MT setup verification

Under competent supervision, candidate uses the actual approved yoke/reference procedure and specified checks. Score safe setup, valid performance verification, particle/viewing condition checks and truthful records. This station does not authorize improvised direct-current/prod techniques.

lessons.title: P12 — MT examination and closeout
lessons.body:
## P12 — MT examination and closeout

Candidate examines the known training specimen in required directions and records indications, then performs required cleanup/residual-field verification under the approved instruction. Score actual coverage, supported evaluation, post-controls and report. No pass from one convenient direction when two are required.

lessons.title: P13 — UT time and echo reasoning
lessons.body:
## P13 — UT time and echo reasoning

Using the instrument/reference block, candidate identifies transmitted pulse/appropriate echoes and explains round-trip path and delay correction. Score signal identification, units, correct path model and recognized invalid coupling. Complete W05 arithmetic independently.

lessons.title: P14 — UT standardization and thickness
lessons.body:
## P14 — UT standardization and thickness

Candidate standardizes the actual instrument/probe on suitable references and measures a mapped benign specimen. Score reference suitability, setup/check accuracy, repeated location-based measurements and post-check handling. Use a fault card for drift; do not falsify instrument settings secretly during live assessment.

lessons.title: P15 — UT angle-beam coverage
lessons.body:
## P15 — UT angle-beam coverage

Using an approved reference block and known training geometry under competent supervision, candidate verifies index/angle as required and maps the required scan coverage. Score setup evidence, path/leg interpretation, actual scan discipline and inaccessible-region record. W06 supplements but cannot replace the observed technique task.

lessons.title: P16 — UT indication evaluation
lessons.body:
## P16 — UT indication evaluation

Candidate records responses from the blind training specimen and distinguishes reference/geometry responses from supported relevant indications using the approved method. Score detection, reproducible location/characterization, correct amplitude/reference comparison and bounded disposition. Do not equate amplitude ratio to crack-size ratio.

lessons.title: P17 — RT image validity
lessons.body:
## P17 — RT image validity

Use pre-existing instructor-verified images with component identity, quality evidence and coverage map. Candidate checks validity before interpretation. Score identity, required image quality, projection/coverage limitation and valid-use decision. No radiation-generating device is used.

lessons.title: P18 — RT processing and geometry
lessons.body:
## P18 — RT processing and geometry

Candidate evaluates W07 and a supplied image-artifact example; identifies raw versus processed files and preserves originals. Score geometric calculation, processing-artifact reasoning, original-data preservation and missing-criteria boundary. An enhanced image cannot silently replace the original evidence.

lessons.title: P19 — RT interpretation and safety
lessons.body:
## P19 — RT interpretation and safety

Candidate evaluates a known image feature using the supplied applicable training criteria and responds to an abnormal-radiation alarm scenario. Score supported interpretation, criterion comparison, no unauthorized approach/manipulation and correct escalation. Operation/recovery authority is not earned here.

lessons.title: P20 — Complementary method decision
lessons.body:
## P20 — Complementary method decision

Candidate resolves W01 changed cases, naming the unanswered question and suitable qualified referral. Score material/geometry reasoning, specific limitation, justified alternative and no unsupported competence claim. Awareness of another method is not permission to execute it.

lessons.title: P21 — Coverage and uncertainty
lessons.body:
## P21 — Coverage and uncertainty

Candidate calculates W08 and W02 uncertainty decisions, then draws examined/unexamined/invalid regions. Score denominator, valid-versus-attempted distinction, threshold decision and truthful report. Any claim that unexamined cells passed is a critical error.

lessons.title: P22 — Train without falsifying evidence
lessons.body:
## P22 — Train without falsifying evidence

Candidate gives a short supervised demonstration on benign VT measurement, observes a trainee rehearsal and records coaching. Score clear explanation, observable checks, correction and separation of coached/independent evidence. Do not sign a trainee's incomplete work as fully performed by the supervisor.

lessons.title: P23 — Reconcile the report
lessons.body:
## P23 — Reconcile the report

Candidate completes I45 and correction form, preserving original evidence. Score technical discrepancies, personnel authority, closure evidence and bounded service recommendation. Report acceptance is not an engineering fitness-for-service declaration.

lessons.title: P24 — Learning credential and next authorization
lessons.body:
## P24 — Learning credential and next authorization

Candidate assembles the learning record with actual method demonstrations and simulation-only RT boundaries, and identifies employer/external requirements still separate. Score method scope, evidence chain, maintenance source and honest wording. No course-generated ASNT credential.

lessons.title: Final, remediation and award
lessons.body:
## Final, remediation and award

Separate private final:24 cases×3 decisions×2points=144; pass116 and at least4/6 in every domain, no unresolved critical error;240minutes. Calculator/coursebook permitted, keys/collaboration prohibited. Access accommodations preserve independent reasoning. Explain missed principles, perform targeted changed practice, then administer the separate changed case without its key. After two failed changed attempts, provide individualized teaching and a new equivalent independently assessed task.

Require all48 formative responses with corrected reasoning, each workbook8/10, I45 at least16/20, every station6/8 with gaps corrected and all required observed method tasks. Issue **VNDRLY/U NDT Level II Preparation—learning assessment completed**, listing actual observed methods and “RT image interpretation only; no radiation-operation authority.” This is neither ASNT nor employer Level II certification. Actual training/experience/vision/exam/authorization requirements remain governed by the applicable external/employer route. No attendance-only or written-only practical pass.

Instructor records: learner/version/hash___ method instructor/competence___ approved local procedures___ specimen truth references___ actual observations___ written/workbook scores___ initial failures___ remediation___ changed results___ independent assessor/date___ scope/limitations___. Secure specimen keys and final keys separately from learner materials; filesystem separation alone does not implement access control.


---

courses.title: VUC045 | VUC045 formative checks

content.title: VUC045 | VUC045 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC045 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC045 formative checks

Attempt before reading the response. Explain every correction, revisit its chapter/station and apply the changed case. These checks support instruction and do not replace the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

Does PT training establish UT authorization?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Method competence and employer authorization are specific. Revisit Q01 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

Does no reported indication mean no flaw exists?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Results are bounded by actual capability and coverage. Revisit Q01 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Why review manufacturing history?

**Answer:** It informs likely feature types and orientation.

**Reason/remediation:** Method selection follows the actual examination question. Revisit Q02 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

Is a geometric echo automatically a crack?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Correlate position, geometry and other evidence. Revisit Q02 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Are procedure and acceptance criteria identical?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Execution and disposition requirements serve different purposes. Revisit Q03 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

May a missing acceptance rule be invented after testing?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Resolve the applicable approved basis. Revisit Q03 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Does nondestructive mean hazard-free?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Chemical, electrical, access and radiation hazards may remain. Revisit Q04 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

What follows failed task protection?

**Answer:** Stop affected work and obtain valid correction/restart.

**Reason/remediation:** Schedule pressure cannot replace controls. Revisit Q04 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

Can glare defeat a bright VT image?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Brightness alone does not establish visible detail. Revisit Q05 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Can a scale in another plane prove exact feature size?

**Answer:** Not without valid geometric correction.

**Reason/remediation:** Perspective changes apparent relative dimensions. Revisit Q05 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Can rounding create conformity?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Preserve actual value and decision rule. Revisit Q06 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Is every indication a rejectable defect?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Relevance and acceptance criteria must be established. Revisit Q06 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Can PT exclude wholly buried discontinuities?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It requires accessible suitable surface openings. Revisit Q07 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Are penetrant systems interchangeable?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the approved compatible process. Revisit Q07 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

Can excess removal reduce PT indications?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** A cleaner background is not automatically a valid sensitive test. Revisit Q08 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

Where do process times come from?

**Answer:** Applicable approved procedure/products.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not apply universal invented times. Revisit Q08 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Is PT indication size always actual flaw depth?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Surface indication does not establish depth. Revisit Q09 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

Can reportable and rejectable differ?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Apply each actual threshold separately. Revisit Q09 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Does MT suit every metal?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Material must suit the magnetic method. Revisit Q10 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

Can one field direction guarantee all orientations?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Direction affects sensitivity and coverage. Revisit Q10 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Does a calibration sticker establish task setup?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Actual standardization/performance checks remain. Revisit Q11 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

Is a direction indicator automatically a field-strength meter?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use each device for its specified property. Revisit Q11 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Does switching power off prove demagnetization?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Required residual-field verification is separate. Revisit Q12 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Can residual-field acceptance replace indication acceptance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** They are distinct requirements. Revisit Q12 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Why divide pulse-echo travel by two?

**Answer:** The corrected time covers outward and return paths.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the actual path model. Revisit Q13 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

Does absent useful echo prove sound material?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Coupling/attenuation/geometry may prevent valid examination. Revisit Q13 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Does a new valid setup validate older failed-setup data?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Review the affected interval and required re-examination. Revisit Q14 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

Can few spot readings prove complete wall coverage?

**Answer:** Not automatically.

**Reason/remediation:** Match scan plan and geometry to the required question. Revisit Q14 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Is angle measured from normal in the course geometry?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the stated convention; another convention changes trigonometry. Revisit Q15 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

Does probe travel alone establish examined volume?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Beam geometry, directions and access must support coverage. Revisit Q15 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Does doubling amplitude double flaw size?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Orientation/path/coupling and settings affect amplitude. Revisit Q16 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

Which formula applies to amplitude ratio in dB?

**Answer:** 20log10(A2/A1).

**Reason/remediation:** Do not confuse amplitude and power ratios. Revisit Q16 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Does RT projection reveal every oriented flaw equally?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Orientation and superposition affect detection. Revisit Q17 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

Does an IQI establish every possible flaw is absent?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It supports specified image quality, not universal detection. Revisit Q17 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:
## Q18-L1

Which distance is denominator in the supplied unsharpness model?

**Answer:** Source-to-object distance.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not substitute source-to-detector distance. Revisit Q18 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q18-L2
lessons.body:
## Q18-L2

May image processing discard original evidence?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Preserve raw/original data and processing history. Revisit Q18 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q19-L1
lessons.body:
## Q19-L1

May an image trainee recover a stuck source?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Recovery requires separately authorized specialist response. Revisit Q19 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q19-L2
lessons.body:
## Q19-L2

Does an apparently off device prove source safety?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the actual radiation safety program and authorized clearance. Revisit Q19 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q20-L1
lessons.body:
## Q20-L1

Does knowing a method name confer competence?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use qualified personnel and approved techniques. Revisit Q20 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q20-L2
lessons.body:
## Q20-L2

What should a complementary method address?

**Answer:** A named unresolved examination question.

**Reason/remediation:** More reports do not automatically resolve a limitation. Revisit Q20 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q21-L1
lessons.body:
## Q21-L1

Are attempted cells the same as validly examined cells?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Failed controls can invalidate attempts. Revisit Q21 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q21-L2
lessons.body:
## Q21-L2

Does sample acceptance establish unsampled regions?

**Answer:** Not automatically.

**Reason/remediation:** Coverage and sampling basis must support the conclusion. Revisit Q21 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q22-L1
lessons.body:
## Q22-L1

May a supervisor sign coverage never performed?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Authority cannot create missing evidence. Revisit Q22 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q22-L2
lessons.body:
## Q22-L2

Does coached practice equal independent assessment?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Record assistance and assess independently as required. Revisit Q22 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q23-L1
lessons.body:
## Q23-L1

Can a valid result be assigned to an uncertain serial?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Reliable component identity is essential. Revisit Q23 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q23-L2
lessons.body:
## Q23-L2

Does examiner report authorize fitness for service automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Engineering/service authority is separate. Revisit Q23 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q24-L1
lessons.body:
## Q24-L1

Does payroll job title prove method experience?

**Answer:** Not alone.

**Reason/remediation:** Retain actual method-specific evidence. Revisit Q24 and explain its changed case.

lessons.title: Q24-L2
lessons.body:
## Q24-L2

Does written RT success authorize exposures?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Radiation operation requires a separate authorized program. Revisit Q24 and explain its changed case.


---

courses.title: VUC045 | VUC045 primary sources and coverage

content.title: VUC045 | VUC045 primary sources and coverage
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC045 primary sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC045 primary sources and coverage

Reviewed2026-11-18. Public primary references support concepts; invented tasks and limits are explicitly marked. No unavailable standard PDF is being pursued. Full external-code/examination equivalence is unverified, not claimed. VNDRLY learning assessment is separate from ASNT certification and employer authorization.

|ID|Primary source|Use/limit|
|---|---|---|
|S01|[ASNT Level II examination information](https://certification.asnt.org/certification/examinations/asnt-ndt-level-ii)|Route, method scope and dated outline changes; not copied exam questions. Public page distinguishes VT after18Oct2026 and upcoming MT/UT transitions.|
|S02|[ASNT employer certification explanation](https://www.asnt.org/standards-publications/blog/employer-based-certification-programs)|Employer written-practice authority; course completion does not replace it.|

lessons.title: Review boundaries
lessons.body:
## Review boundaries

Instruction includes the five methods on the public ASNT NDT Level II route and distinguishes related-method awareness. Upcoming outline transitions are not silently called current credential requirements. Actual training hours, experience, vision, employer examinations and maintenance are determined by the applicable route; the64hour VNDRLY plan is not an external eligibility claim. Radiation operations remain a separate qualification.

Physical method demonstrations and independent results are required for this course's practical-preparation award. This authoring work has not tested a real learner. Real training specimens/equipment must be verified by competent assessors; supplied paper cases cannot substitute for them. Private answer/specimen keys need controlled distribution beyond folder separation. Original materials completion, learner completion, external certification and publication remain separate states.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U NDT Level III Technical Leadership Preparation
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U NDT Level III Technical Leadership Preparation

VUC046 · Original available-source course · 2026-11-18

lessons.title: Learning purpose and boundaries
lessons.body:
## Learning purpose and boundaries

This program builds on the included24-chapter NDT method foundation with technical program governance, procedure development/validation, examination design, specialist-method selection, evidence review and audit. It prepares learners to reason about Level III responsibilities; it does not confer ASNT certification or employer appointment. ASNT's actual Level III route requires its Basic examination and at least one method examination, with eligibility requirements.[A01] General familiarity with many methods is not qualification in every method.

Read the included foundation before Q25–40; complete its method tasks and this advanced portfolio. Existing verified equivalent learning may be recognized only through a documented challenge against the same outcomes, not waived by job title. Full external-standard equivalence remains unverified under the user-authorized available-source approach. No unsafe pressure loading, energized industrial access, radiation exposure or source handling is a course exercise.

lessons.title: Q25 — Technical authority and its limits
lessons.body:
## Q25 — Technical authority and its limits

Technical leadership requires knowing both what a person can decide and what must be referred. Separate employer certification authority, method technical responsibility, engineering acceptance, contractual acceptance and radiation licensing. A Level III designation does not make every method or sector interchangeable. Identify appointment, method scope and relevant governing documents before signing a procedure or personnel decision.

When requirements conflict, preserve the conflict and seek an authorized resolution. A customer demand cannot silently override a mandatory safety control or employer written practice. Conversely, an agent or instructor must not invent extra external requirements and call them law. Record which requirement actually controls each decision and who can approve a departure.

**Worked:** a UT technical lead is asked to approve an unfamiliar AE loading procedure. Refer to competent authorized AE and engineering personnel; UT expertise alone is insufficient. **Changed:** AE expert reviews signals but has no authority to prescribe vessel load; test loading still needs the proper engineering approval.

lessons.title: Q26 — Build and maintain the personnel program
lessons.body:
## Q26 — Build and maintain the personnel program

A written practice must identify the employer's actual qualification/certification system: roles, methods/levels, training, experience, examinations, vision, records, authorization, maintenance and treatment of interruptions or revoked status. Use the applicable adopted edition and contractual/regulatory obligations, not a copied old template with the company's name changed. ASNT distinguishes employer-based certification from training documentation.[A02]

Create an evidence matrix for each candidate and method. Every claimed prerequisite needs traceable actual evidence and an authorized decision. Experience logs should identify work and responsible verification; elapsed employment is not automatically method experience. Retain original records when corrections occur. A program change requires an impact review of affected people, procedures and assignments, not blanket backdating.

**Worked:** candidate has500hours employment but only200 documented hours in the requested method. Do not relabel all500 as method experience. **Changed:** actual method experience is verified but required assessment is absent; experience does not substitute for that distinct requirement.

lessons.title: Q27 — Design assessments that test competence
lessons.body:
## Q27 — Design assessments that test competence

Start with observable outcomes: correct selection, setup, examination, evaluation, reporting and safe escalation. Map each to an assessment task and an explicit scoring rule. General knowledge, job-specific application and actual practical performance answer different questions. Use representative known specimens and independent keys, protect answer distribution and define permitted assistance before testing.

Avoid a question bank that only rewards memorized wording. Include changed conditions, invalid evidence and boundary decisions. Review ambiguous questions before administration; if a defect is found afterward, use an authorized documented scoring/remediation decision rather than quietly changing only one candidate's score. Preserve unsuccessful attempts, teaching and changed reassessment. Accommodations should support access while preserving the actual competence being tested.

**Worked:** a trainee memorizes the supplied specimen map and finds every feature. That does not establish blind detection performance. **Changed:** a new equivalent specimen is used but the examiner points to each feature; independence is still absent.

lessons.title: Q28 — Develop and validate a procedure
lessons.body:
## Q28 — Develop and validate a procedure

Translate the examination objective into a bounded procedure: material/geometry, target features, required sensitivity/coverage, method/technique, equipment, reference standards, preparation, variables, controls, evaluation, reporting, cleanup and safety. Explain why the technique is suitable rather than listing instrument settings alone. Validation must represent the claimed use conditions and challenge important failure modes.

Use a documented demonstration plan with known features and sound regions, variation in relevant geometry/orientation, independent truth and acceptance criteria specified beforehand. Retain misses, false calls and invalid runs. Successful detection on one easy artificial notch does not establish service-crack capability across all components. Changes to software, probe, material, surface or geometry require review of whether the validation still applies.

**Worked:** flat-reference success is used to approve a curved component without assessment. The geometry extrapolation is unsupported. **Changed:** curved specimen is tested but only the easiest feature orientation; the claimed orientation range remains unvalidated.

lessons.title: Q29 — Reliability evidence without false certainty
lessons.body:
## Q29 — Reliability evidence without false certainty

Detection studies need a defined population, feature truth, representative conditions and controlled independence. Sensitivity is true positives divided by actual-positive cases; false-positive rate is false positives divided by actual-negative cases. These are different denominators. Overall accuracy can conceal poor detection when positive cases are rare. A favorable point estimate does not establish a high-confidence bound or universal POD curve.

For a simple independent identical Bernoulli illustration with n successes and no failures, a one-sided95% lower bound for success probability is0.05^(1/n). With30/30 successes it is about0.905, not1.00. This calculation is not a complete NDT POD analysis: feature size, orientation, operators and correlation may invalidate the simple model. State assumptions and use an appropriate qualified statistical analysis for real validation.[A03]

**Worked:** repeating the same obvious notch30times is not30representative independent service flaws. **Changed:**30distinct features are used but one operator was coached throughout; independence and operational representativeness still need review.

lessons.title: Q30 — Electromagnetic method selection and signal separation
lessons.body:
## Q30 — Electromagnetic method selection and signal separation

Eddy-current responses depend on conductive material, permeability, frequency, probe geometry, coupling/lift-off and discontinuities. Standard skin depth varies inversely with the square root of frequency when material properties are fixed; increasing frequency fourfold halves that depth.[A04] Skin depth is a field-decay concept, not a hard boundary beyond which no response exists or a guaranteed flaw-detection depth.

A procedure must distinguish target responses from lift-off, geometry and material-property variation using representative references and valid analysis. Remote-field and alternating-current-field measurement techniques have distinct arrangements and assumptions; do not treat them as interchangeable instrument modes. Plan safe access, calibration/standardization, scan speed and coverage. A signal change alone does not establish crack dimensions without the validated interpretation method.

**Worked:** coating thickness changes lift-off and the trace shifts. Investigate geometry/coupling before declaring damage. **Changed:** reference normalization is valid but part permeability differs materially; the transfer of calibration still requires review.

lessons.title: Q31 — Acoustic emission: active sources and noise
lessons.body:
## Q31 — Acoustic emission: active sources and noise

AE observes transient elastic-wave activity generated by active processes during monitored conditions. It is different from sending a UT pulse and receiving its echo. Sensor coupling, spacing, wave velocity, attenuation, thresholds, timing and background noise affect detection/location. A quiet test does not prove absence of a dormant flaw. Loading must be separately authorized and safe; do not increase load simply to create more signals.[A05]

Establish baseline noise and sensor performance before interpreting event clusters. Correlate event timing with legitimate monitored conditions and distinguish friction, impacts or other noise through the approved analysis. For a simple one-dimensional pair of sensors separatedL with speedv and arrival differenceΔt=tB−tA, source position fromA is(L−vΔt)/2. This assumes the source lies between them and the stated propagation model; complex structures need validated location methods.

**Worked:**L=2m,v=4000m/s,Δt=0.0002s givesx=0.6m. **Changed:**noise triggers one channel incorrectly; a mathematically plausible coordinate is not a valid source location.

lessons.title: Q32 — Thermal/infrared interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q32 — Thermal/infrared interpretation

A thermal camera measures radiation, from which temperature is inferred under assumptions. Emissivity, reflected apparent temperature, atmosphere, distance, viewing angle, resolution and load/environment affect interpretation. Low-emissivity reflective surfaces can show a hot reflection rather than the component's true temperature.[A06] A colorful image is not a calibrated temperature map by itself.

Define whether the objective is qualitative comparison or quantitative temperature, and establish comparable operating conditions. Preserve radiometric data and metadata where available, not only a color screenshot. Do not access energized equipment or remove guards without separate authorization. A reference patch/contact comparison must itself be suitable, safe and approved; no technique detail justifies creating an electrical hazard.

**Worked:**one component looks hotter but carries more load than its comparator. Control/record load before diagnosing defect. **Changed:**equal loads but one surface is polished and one painted; emissivity/reflection differences remain.

lessons.title: Q33 — Leak testing and thermodynamic confounders
lessons.body:
## Q33 — Leak testing and thermodynamic confounders

Leak testing asks whether gas/liquid crosses a boundary under defined conditions, and may locate a leak or quantify a rate. Bubble methods, pressure-change methods and tracer-gas detection answer different questions at different sensitivities. Define gas, pressure differential, temperature, volume, stabilization, instrument response and calibration/reference leak before interpreting a rate.[A07]

For a simplified constant-temperature isolated volume, throughput can be estimated as volume×pressure change/time. Pressure change can also reflect temperature, outgassing, permeation or trapped volumes. At fixed amount/volume, ideal-gas absolute pressure scales with absolute temperature; using Celsius directly is wrong. A rate without units or test conditions cannot be compared reliably. Live pressurization/vacuum tasks require separate competent engineering controls; this course uses records only.

**Worked:**10L volume rises0.02mbar in100s:0.002mbar·L/s under the simplified assumptions. **Changed:**temperature drifts significantly; the same arithmetic no longer isolates leakage.

lessons.title: Q34 — Magnetic flux leakage and screening limits
lessons.body:
## Q34 — Magnetic flux leakage and screening limits

MFL applies a magnetic field to suitable material and senses leakage associated with changes such as metal loss. Magnetization, sensor spacing/lift-off, speed, geometry, material and defect morphology influence the signal. A screening indication is not automatically an accurate remaining-thickness value. Define reference features, validated sizing limits and required follow-up measurements.[A08]

A technical leader checks dead zones, edge coverage, saturation assumptions and transfer from calibration piece to component. Map unscanned regions and preserve raw signals. If a follow-up method disagrees, reconcile location and capability rather than choose the favorable report. MFL and MT both involve magnetic phenomena but use different detection approaches; one qualification does not automatically cover the other.

**Worked:**scanner reports possible floor loss near an inaccessible edge. The edge cannot be accepted because central areas were scanned. **Changed:**UT confirmation samples only the center of a broad indication; it may not establish the worst local condition.

lessons.title: Q35 — Neutron radiography and specialist referral
lessons.body:
## Q35 — Neutron radiography and specialist referral

Neutrons interact with materials differently from X-rays, enabling complementary contrast in some assemblies; NIST describes combined neutron/X-ray imaging applications.[A09] Useful contrast depends on actual composition, geometry and imaging conditions, not a simple rule that one radiation sees everything. Image quality, identity and coverage still matter.

Neutron facilities involve specialized radiation protection and access controls. This program teaches selection/review reasoning only, not operation. Define the unanswered materials question and request a qualified feasibility assessment. Do not claim an X-ray qualification includes neutron operation or interpretation expertise. Preserve separate images, registration assumptions and uncertainty when combining datasets.

**Worked:**a hydrogen-containing region inside a metal assembly motivates a neutron feasibility review. It is not permission to expose the part. **Changed:**combined images are misregistered; apparent coincident features may be an alignment artifact.

lessons.title: Q36 — Advanced UT technique validation
lessons.body:
## Q36 — Advanced UT technique validation

Array steering/focusing, encoded scanning and specialized timing techniques can increase information but also add configuration and interpretation risks. Probe/wedge identity, element performance, law setup, material velocity, geometry, calibration, encoder registration and coverage must match the validated technique. A dense image is not proof that the required volume/orientations are interrogated.

Validate with representative known features and adverse conditions, preserve raw data/configuration and distinguish detection from sizing. A software upgrade or changed wedge can affect results even when the screen layout appears unchanged. A conventional-UT qualification does not automatically prove competence in every advanced technique. Evaluate qualifications, procedure and demonstration evidence together.

**Worked:**encoder slip compresses the position scale while signals look normal. Reported feature length is unreliable. **Changed:**encoder corrected but earlier data not re-acquired or validly corrected; the new setup does not repair old position evidence.

lessons.title: Q37 — Control the entire method system
lessons.body:
## Q37 — Control the entire method system

PT, MT, VT and RT performance depends on linked stages. Consumable change, surface preparation, viewing, image processing or software can alter sensitivity without obvious failure. Establish control checks and acceptance criteria for the complete process, not just instrument calibration. Use actual product compatibility and method requirements; do not approve substitutions solely because a label says equivalent.

Define post-check failure response and traceable affected intervals. In film/digital radiography, preserve acquisition/processing controls; in surface methods, retain process timing, viewing and reference performance. Manage control specimens so contamination or wear does not make the check misleading. A system that passes with a known damaged reference may be providing false assurance.

**Worked:**new developer is used with an unverified penetrant system. Familiar appearance does not establish compatibility. **Changed:**compatibility established but reference-panel response has degraded; investigate the panel/system before production acceptance.

lessons.title: Q38 — Change control and technical deviations
lessons.body:
## Q38 — Change control and technical deviations

Classify a change by its effect on the validated examination and governing requirements. Revision numbers alone do not describe impact. Compare before/after material, geometry, equipment/software, consumables, scan plan, personnel and acceptance rules. Identify necessary revalidation, retraining and review of already-issued results. Preserve approval chronology and do not backdate a new procedure to justify old departures.

Temporary deviations need explicit scope, authority, compensating controls, expiration/closure and affected records. An email saying “proceed” is insufficient if its sender lacks authority or critical conditions remain undefined. Distinguish changing a procedure from changing an acceptance standard; the technical lead may not have authority to relax the latter.

**Worked:**new probe has different beam characteristics but the procedure revision only changes its part number. Demonstration coverage must be reviewed. **Changed:**new probe is validated, yet a customer's approval requirement remains; technical and contractual approvals are distinct.

lessons.title: Q39 — Audit, corrective action and effectiveness
lessons.body:
## Q39 — Audit, corrective action and effectiveness

Audit actual practice against the adopted requirements and records. Sample across people, methods, shifts, equipment and adverse conditions rather than only polished examples. Trace a result back to identity, authorization, controls, raw data and disposition. Separate an isolated documentation defect from a systematic capability failure, but do not dismiss a missing critical control as paperwork.

Corrective action has containment, cause analysis, correction, prevention and effectiveness evidence. Retraining attendance alone does not prove the failure mode is removed. Review affected prior work when warranted and verify a changed task is performed correctly. Keep unresolved actions visible and assign accountable owners without fabricating closure.

**Worked:**six reports share an invalid reference setting. Fixing the template contains future error but past results need review. **Changed:**staff retrained, but a blind repeat still uses the wrong reference; effectiveness has not been demonstrated.

lessons.title: Q40 — Defensible technical leadership portfolio
lessons.body:
## Q40 — Defensible technical leadership portfolio

An advanced learning portfolio integrates a written-practice decision, method-selection justification, executable procedure, validation plan/results interpretation, assessment design, report review and corrective-action closure. Each claim needs supporting actual or clearly synthetic evidence and an identified authority. Strong writing cannot replace demonstrated method competence or actual external prerequisites.

The VNDRLY award states preparation completed and names observed methods/portfolio tasks; it does not issue ASNT Level III status or employer appointment. Learners must explain what remains outside their authority and when to obtain specialist review. A portfolio with hidden failed demonstrations or invented approvals is unacceptable regardless of exam score.

**Worked:**candidate's procedure is technically coherent but no validation evidence supports its claimed range. Record the gap and complete a valid demonstration before that claim is accepted. **Changed:**validation passes but the candidate claims every NDT method; restrict recognition to the actual evidence.


---
