content.title: VUC055 | VNDRLY/U Bolted Flange Joint Inspection
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Bolted Flange Joint Inspection
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Bolted Flange Joint Inspection

VUC055 · Original instruction · 2026-11-18

This package includes the twenty-chapter manual assembly foundation and adds eight inspector chapters. Complete the foundation or demonstrate every mapped outcome through documented recognition assessment; a certificate title alone does not waive practical evidence. The combined assessment and award rules here govern. The inspector evaluates another person's work against a supplied approved basis and records the limits of that evaluation. This is not an API BFJI credential, OPITO diploma, engineering design approval or permission for live intervention.

The publicly posted API inspector outline covers pre-assembly, in-process and final inspection, but its stated exam dates end April 2026. Treat it as historical subject context, not a verified current edition specification. Full controlled standards were not reviewed. Original cases supply their own fictional acceptance criteria; learners must use actual approved requirements on real jobs. [I01–03]

lessons.title: Q21 — Inspection planning and authority
lessons.body:
## Q21 — Inspection planning and authority

An inspection plan starts with the actual joint list, applicable documents, work stages and assigned responsibilities. Determine which activities require inspection before proceeding, which require notification or witnessing, and which can be reviewed afterward under the governing quality plan. A hold point cannot be converted to a record review merely because the inspector arrived late. Write the required evidence and release authority before the assembly starts.

Use a joint-by-joint matrix. Include physical identity, work-package revision, component checks, initial geometry, tooling, assembly witness requirements, final inspection and turnover. Clarify access and timing so a gasket check does not become impossible after closure. A photograph can support identification but may not establish surface condition, hidden geometry or a required live observation. Missing access is an inspection limitation, not a passing result.

Independence means reporting evidence faithfully even under schedule pressure. An inspector can identify nonconformance without being authorized to redesign the joint or release the system. Where one person performs and inspects an activity, follow the actual quality-plan rules; do not invent an independent signature. A witnessed event, a reviewed record and an inferred result must remain distinguishable.

**Worked case:** eight joints require pre-assembly release. Six releases exist; two joints are already closed without them. Report six evidenced releases and two missed hold points. Do not backdate observations. **Changed case:** photographs arrive for the two joints. Have the designated authority assess their adequacy and required corrective action; the photographs do not automatically become the originally required observation.

lessons.title: Q22 — Component records and compatibility review
lessons.body:
## Q22 — Component records and compatibility review

Build a traceability chain from physical marking to the specified component and supporting record. For flanges, fasteners, gaskets and any specified blank, compare the actual identifiers with the work package. A certificate can be genuine but belong to a different heat, lot or component. A procurement description can match a nominal size while omitting the facing or material needed for compatibility. Resolve each mismatch rather than accepting a folder because it looks official.

Distinguish a material specification, product standard, drawing and installation procedure. They answer related but different questions. If the work requires mechanical-property evidence, verify the required record and its applicability; visual inspection cannot measure strength. If additional material verification is specified, it needs a qualified method and acceptance basis. This course does not authorize an inspector to substitute a handheld reading for every required material test.

Temporary blanks are part of a controlled configuration. Verify the specified identity, location and installation/removal status through the approved plan. A tag saying removed is not physical proof. The inspector does not choose a blank thickness or pressure rating from a classroom example. Missing technical requirements go to the responsible authority before affected work.

**Worked case:** twelve studs are listed, ten trace to the required heat and two carry a different mark. Ten of twelve have supported identity, not twelve accepted. **Changed case:** the second heat is approved but one nut has damaged threads. Identity closure does not resolve condition. Record the separate finding and disposition reference.

lessons.title: Q23 — Face inspection and measurement limitations
lessons.body:
## Q23 — Face inspection and measurement limitations

Prepare a clean, safely accessible inert surface for training. On a real job, access and cleaning require their actual controls. Inspect the specified area systematically, preserving orientation and joint identity. Locate scratches, corrosion, residue and deformation with a reproducible reference. Describe what was observed before proposing a cause. A radial scratch may matter differently from another surface feature, but the actual gasket and acceptance basis determine disposition.

Choose a method that can support the required decision. A visual estimate does not establish a numerical depth. A surface-finish comparator provides a comparison under its intended conditions, not necessarily a calibrated profilometer result. Instrument settings, reference checks, measurement direction and inaccessible areas belong in the record when relevant. Do not convert one roughness parameter into another without a valid relationship for that measurement. A result in micrometres is not directly comparable with microinches until units are reconciled.

Separate measurement resolution from acceptance. If an instrument cannot resolve the difference around a limit, report that uncertainty and obtain a suitable method or authorized decision rule. Never choose favorable rounding after seeing a failing value. Retain initial measurements when a repeat is made and explain why the repeat is valid.

**Worked case:** supplied teaching finish band is 3.2–6.3 µm for a named mock surface. A valid reading of 6.5 exceeds the upper limit by 0.2 µm. This is not a universal flange finish band. **Changed case:** reading 6.2 with stated uncertainty ±0.3 gives an interval 5.9–6.5. Under the exercise rule requiring the entire interval inside the band, acceptance is not established. Seek a better measurement or authorized disposition rather than declare 6.2 an unconditional pass.

lessons.title: Q24 — Geometry, parallelism and engagement
lessons.body:
## Q24 — Geometry, parallelism and engagement

Plan measurements before the joint becomes inaccessible. Record the specified positions and whether readings describe initial alignment, an intermediate stage or the final condition. Measurements from different stages are not interchangeable. For training, use four clock positions on an inert fixture, a suitable gap tool and a known reference card. Repeat the reading without forcing the tool or moving the assembly. Record actual values rather than a single undocumented “aligned” mark.

A maximum-minus-minimum gap spread describes variation among those readings; it does not prove every other alignment requirement. High/low offset, angular relationship, supports and flange-face condition need their own applicable checks. A well-aligned empty fixture may change when components are installed. Do not use inspection measurements as permission to draw an unsuitable joint into place with bolts.

Check fastener engagement and protrusion against the supplied approved criteria. A visible thread count is not a universal substitute for the actual nut/stud arrangement. Record which end and position was inspected. Do not grind a stud or exchange a nut to satisfy a training number on a real installation. Missing access should be identified explicitly.

**Worked case:** final gaps 2.1, 2.4, 2.2 and 2.6 mm give a spread of 0.5 mm; the fictional maximum is 0.4. Record an exceedance of 0.1. **Changed case:** gaps 2.1, 2.2, 2.2 and 2.4 give 0.3, but one specified engagement check is inaccessible. The spread criterion passes; full final inspection remains incomplete.

lessons.title: Q25 — Tool evidence and calculation review
lessons.body:
## Q25 — Tool evidence and calculation review

Before witnessing tightening, confirm the tool in use matches the documented identification, configuration, range and current verification requirements. Review the relationship between the approved target and the tool's displayed setting. An adapter, different effective length, different hydraulic model or different lubricant can invalidate an assumed relationship. The inspector checks the approved basis and arithmetic; the inspector does not create an engineering target by applying a convenient formula.

Use units throughout. A manual torque setting is not a pump-pressure setting. Manufacturer charts apply to the identified equipment and conditions; a similar-looking tool is insufficient. Review supplied correction factors only within their actual applicability. If a certificate reports an error, use the sign convention stated on that certificate rather than guess whether to add or subtract it. Record the actual method used to decide suitability.

When a tool fails a later check, identify the work performed since its last valid state through records and the applicable quality process. Changing the tool resolves future readiness only. Prior work requires its own technical assessment and disposition. A calibration sticker alone does not close that affected-work review.

**Worked case:** a synthetic indicator reads 100 N·m while the reference is 96. Error relative to reference is (100−96)/96×100=4.1667%. The supplied allowed error is ±3%; it fails. **Changed case:** indicator 98 against reference 96 gives 2.0833%, within that comparison. Wrong serial number on the certificate still prevents evidence from establishing this tool's suitability. Neither example supplies a field setpoint.

lessons.title: Q26 — Witnessing the assembly process
lessons.body:
## Q26 — Witnessing the assembly process

At the planned witness stage, verify that readiness conditions are satisfied and that people understand the approved sequence. Observe the actual tool, locations and stages, without entering a reaction or pinch zone. Record what was personally witnessed and what was established through other evidence. Do not sign for work outside the observed scope. If an unsafe act occurs, use the site's stop-work process rather than continue observing to finish a checklist.

For a benign classroom assembly, the inspector uses the B54 work card while another trained person performs the sequence. Follow each position and stage. A completed final pass does not prove all intermediate stages occurred. If a stage is missed, stop at a safe state and obtain the instructor's controlled recovery. Do not tell the assembler to add an arbitrary turn. Inspect changes in tool or personnel against the actual procedure and record the interruption.

Document coverage in meaningful units. “Twenty-three of twenty-four stage-position events witnessed” describes evidence coverage, not a percentage of joint safety or authorization. If full witnessing is required, the missing event needs disposition. A photograph of the completed joint cannot recreate a torque event. When the plan permits record review, label it accordingly rather than rewriting history as direct observation.

**Worked case:** three stages at eight positions create 24 required events. One event was not witnessed; direct coverage is 23/24=95.8333%. **Changed case:** a fourth final verification pass adds eight events, but the original missing event remains. Coverage is 31/32=96.875%; the hold is not cured by the higher percentage.

lessons.title: Q27 — Nonconformance and repair verification
lessons.body:
## Q27 — Nonconformance and repair verification

A useful finding connects the requirement, actual evidence, affected identity and necessary decision. Write facts without guessing blame. Identify the boundary of the hold so other authorized work can continue safely where appropriate. The disposition may require correction, additional examination or an engineering decision; only the designated authority can approve the relevant option. An inspector verifies that the authorized disposition was actually performed and that its conditions were met.

Rework and repair are not merely synonyms for “fixed.” Use the project's definitions and approval paths. A proposed alteration to a pressure-boundary component may require engineering, qualified personnel and additional examination beyond routine assembly. Do not prescribe field machining, hot bolting or a clamp repair from this course. Preserve removed components and records when needed for investigation.

Closure needs evidence linked to the original issue and the resulting configuration. A signature confirms an action only within its documented scope. The same defect recurring can require broader affected-work review; do not close each record without examining whether a common tool, component lot or procedure is involved. Maintain the original observations and subsequent changes so the decision is auditable.

**Worked case:** ten findings exist, six corrected and verified, two corrected but unverified, two awaiting disposition. Verified closure is 60%, with four open. **Changed case:** one verified item reopens and one awaiting item becomes verified. The count remains six, but the identities and risk may differ. Report the actual register, not only the unchanged percentage.

lessons.title: Q28 — Final dossier and release boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q28 — Final dossier and release boundaries

Turnover should allow another competent person to trace each joint from approved configuration through assembly, inspection, deviations and required testing. Reconcile unique identities instead of counting files. Confirm actual revisions, dates, personnel roles, tool references, observed stages and unresolved limitations. A duplicate report does not create another inspected joint. A signed summary cannot replace missing required underlying evidence.

Keep assembly completion, inspection acceptance, test status and operating release as separate statements. An inspector may verify the first two within assigned scope while the operator retains the last. If testing is pending, say so. If a temporary blank remains in a controlled configuration, carry its actual status into turnover. Do not imply a safe operating state merely because the inspection packet is tidy.

Give a concise verbal handover supported by the register: which system and revision, completed checks, open conditions, who owns each action and what must happen before the next stage. In a disagreement, preserve the requirement and evidence for the defined review or appeal process. Continuing competence includes recognizing changed methods and equipment beyond demonstrated experience.

**Worked case:** twenty joints are assembled, eighteen have supported final inspection, sixteen have required test evidence. Report 20/18/16, not twenty ready for service. **Changed case:** two additional inspection files duplicate existing joints. The inspected total remains eighteen. New original evidence for the two missing joints could change that count; operational release would still require its own authority.


---

courses.title: VUC055 | Retained assembly foundation Q01–20

content.title: VUC055 | Retained assembly foundation Q01–20
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: Retained assembly foundation Q01–20
lessons.body:
# Retained assembly foundation Q01–20

Foundation S references retained; VUC055 combined delivery and award rules govern.

lessons.title: Q01 — The joint as a system
lessons.body:
## Q01 — The joint as a system

A bolted joint combines flanges, gasket, fasteners and the assembly process. Fastener load compresses the gasket while the components respond to load and service conditions. Correct torque does not compensate for an incompatible gasket, damaged face or wrong bolt. Conversely, correct parts do not guarantee correct assembly. Treat the complete joint and final configuration as the unit of work.

Identify the joint tag and service from approved documents. Establish the boundaries of the assembler's role: verify parts and conditions, follow the procedure, record actual work and report deviations. Engineering selects or approves the technical basis; operating personnel control isolation and return to service. Do not convert a training certificate into authority to change the assembly specification.

**Worked case:** B54 joint J1 has the specified fasteners but an unidentified gasket. Keep preparation incomplete and obtain the correct identity; do not proceed because the bolts are right. **Changed case:** gasket identity is resolved but the flange rating is unverified. The independent rating question remains. State which evidence closed and which did not.

lessons.title: Q02 — Work package and joint identity
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Work package and joint identity

The work package should identify the system, joint, drawing revision, component requirements, gasket, lubricant, tools, assembly sequence, target values, inspections and release points. Read the whole package before starting. Similar adjacent joints may have different service or component requirements. Marking a joint for work must agree with the approved system identity and isolation scope.

Resolve contradictions before affected work. A handwritten torque on a box is not necessarily the approved target. A newer drawing may supersede the material list; obtain the designated resolution rather than choose whichever document is convenient. Preserve the final authorized revision in the assembly record so the result is reproducible.

**Worked case:** J1 drawing revision C specifies gasket G2; an older work card says G1. Record the conflict and request resolution. **Changed case:** supervisor confirms G2 verbally but the controlled work package remains unreconciled. Follow the actual document-control process and obtain the required authorization/evidence. Do not invent a signature or silently edit history.

lessons.title: Q03 — Isolation and line-breaking boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Isolation and line-breaking boundaries

Before a pressure-boundary joint is disturbed, the applicable operating and hazardous-energy controls must establish a safe work condition. Stored pressure, temperature, chemicals, trapped sections and possible reaccumulation require attention. A stopped pump, closed valve or zero on one gauge alone does not prove that every hazard is controlled. OSHA's hazardous-energy rule provides a US general-industry framework; actual applicability and site procedures govern.[S04]

The assembler follows their assigned authorized role and verifies the required work clearance; this course does not provide a universal isolation or flange-opening sequence. If isolation evidence conflicts with the observed condition, stop and contact the responsible authority. Do not loosen a nut to test whether a line is pressurized. Keep people out of potential release and movement paths through the approved controls.

**Worked case:** the permit names J2 while the marked joint is J1. Do not begin opening. Resolve the physical/document identity before work. **Changed case:** the tag is corrected but a blocked-in section's condition is unknown. Retain the energy-control question. Classroom work uses an unconnected, unpressurized fixture with no process inventory.

lessons.title: Q04 — Flange types, ratings and facing compatibility
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Flange types, ratings and facing compatibility

Recognize that size, facing and pressure class describe different aspects of a flange. A nominal size is not a complete dimensional or rating specification. Pressure class is not a universal allowable pressure in psi; applicable material, temperature, standard and configuration matter. Raised-face, flat-face and ring-type arrangements use different sealing geometries and component requirements. Do not force visually similar parts together without the approved compatibility basis.

Read markings and correlate them with certificates and drawings. Large-diameter or wellhead equipment can follow different dimensional systems from ordinary piping flanges. A matching bolt count does not establish interchangeability. Refer missing markings, damage or a proposed substitution before assembly.

**Worked case:** two flanges share bolt count and approximate outside diameter but have different specified facing systems. Hold compatibility unresolved. **Changed case:** faces match, yet material/rating records do not. Geometric agreement alone still cannot establish service suitability. Record the exact unresolved property rather than “looks wrong.”

lessons.title: Q05 — Fasteners, nuts and traceability
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Fasteners, nuts and traceability

Fastener selection includes material/grade, diameter, thread, length, condition and associated nut/washer requirements. Compare actual marks and records with the work package. Do not mix metric and inch threads because they initially appear to engage. Cross-threading, damaged threads, bent studs or unidentified substitutions require disposition. Smooth initial engagement is useful evidence of condition, not proof of material grade.

Keep fasteners identifiable through cleaning and assembly. Reuse is a decision under the actual procedure, not a universal right because a stud looks intact. Check required engagement and projection against the specified configuration; this course supplies no universal exposed-thread count. An assembler must not grind or modify a fastener to make an unsupported arrangement fit.

**Worked case:** B54 needs eight matched studs; six have valid identity and two are unmarked. Record two unresolved components and obtain authorized replacements or disposition. **Changed case:** identity is recovered, but one thread is visibly damaged. Traceability resolution does not clear physical condition. Separate each finding and final verification.

lessons.title: Q06 — Gasket selection and handling
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Gasket selection and handling

The gasket must match the specified service, geometry, material and installation method. Nonmetallic sheet, spiral-wound and metallic ring arrangements are not interchangeable simply because their diameters are close. Check identification, dimensions, storage and visible condition against the approved basis. Keep sealing surfaces free of contamination and avoid bending or damaging the gasket during handling.

Do not stack gaskets, reuse a removed gasket or add sealant unless the actual approved procedure explicitly supports that configuration. Such changes can alter seating and load behavior. Manufacturer guidance is product-specific; Garlock's referenced guide covers named product families and is not a universal instruction for every gasket.[S05]

**Worked case:** the specified new gasket is missing, and someone offers a previously compressed one of the same size. Hold the substitution and obtain the approved component. **Changed case:** a new correctly identified gasket has a damaged edge. Identity is correct, condition is not established acceptable. Record the damage and obtain disposition rather than trim it casually.

lessons.title: Q07 — Cleanliness and flange-face condition
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Cleanliness and flange-face condition

Preparation must leave the sealing surfaces in the condition required by the joint procedure. Remove residual material using approved methods that do not damage the face or alter its required finish. Inspect accessible surfaces for contamination, corrosion, scratches, deformation and other relevant damage. Record location and dimensions where the method supports them. A shiny appearance is not proof of an acceptable sealing finish.

Do not invent a permissible scratch depth or machine a face without authorization. Surface finish and defect acceptance depend on the actual joint/gasket basis. Protect cleaned faces while other work proceeds. If preparation exposes a previously hidden defect, treat it as a new finding rather than conceal it beneath the gasket.

**Worked case:** an inert teaching face has residue across one quadrant and a marked radial scratch. Identify both and request the supplied disposition; cleaning does not erase the scratch. **Changed case:** residue is removed, but the scratch's depth cannot be measured by the available tool. Record the measurement limitation and obtain an appropriate assessment. Do not label an unmeasured defect within tolerance.

lessons.title: Q08 — Alignment, support and gaps
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Alignment, support and gaps

Joint alignment includes more than whether bolts enter holes. Compare orientation, gap and parallelism with the approved procedure and inspect the support condition. Uncontrolled loads or forced fit can affect assembly and later service. Do not use bolts as an improvised alignment tool unless the actual engineering procedure specifically provides a controlled method. The assembler does not redesign supports or move connected equipment on personal judgment.

Measure at defined positions with an appropriate tool and record the reference. Uneven gaps can indicate an issue needing investigation, but the readings alone do not identify every cause. Keep alignment acceptance separate from final tightening and any piping-stress or equipment-alignment requirements.

**Worked case:** B54 supplied gap readings are 3.0, 3.2, 3.1, 3.8 mm; fictional maximum spread 0.5 mm. Spread 0.8 exceeds by 0.3 mm. Stop the affected assembly step and seek authorized correction. **Changed case:** readings 3.1, 3.2, 3.0, 3.3 give 0.3 mm spread, meeting that comparison. Missing support approval remains unresolved; a passing gap is not overall installation acceptance.

lessons.title: Q09 — Lubrication and friction
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Lubrication and friction

Applied torque is influenced by friction in threads and bearing surfaces. The approved lubricant, application locations and condition must match the target's basis. Changing lubricant can change achieved load at the same torque. Do not substitute grease, mix products or apply lubricant to a surface not covered by the procedure merely because it makes assembly easier. Check material/service compatibility and product identity.

The classroom relationship T=KFd illustrates sensitivity, where T is torque, F preload, d nominal diameter and K a supplied empirical factor. It is not a field torque-selection formula without a validated basis. Convert diameter to metres for N·m and newtons. A generic K value is not a measured fact about the actual joint.

**Worked case:** supplied K0.20, F10000N, d0.01 m yields 20N·m. At unchanged 20N·m and K0.15, the simplified implied load is 13333.33N, 33.33% higher. **Changed case:**K0.25 gives 8000N, 20% lower. The lesson is to preserve the approved lubrication/target pairing, not to choose field torque from these synthetic examples.

lessons.title: Q10 — Load, elongation and gasket compression
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Load, elongation and gasket compression

Bolts act elastically within their appropriate working range, but the joint's response also involves gasket compression and component stiffness. A torque reading is not a direct universal measurement of preload. Stretch-based or tensioning methods require their own geometry, calibration and procedure. Do not assume equal torque guarantees equal load or that more tightening always improves sealing; excessive load can damage components.

For an idealized classroom elastic bolt, elongationδ=FL/(AE), with consistent units and a supplied effective area. Real threaded assemblies and measurement methods need more detailed treatment. This calculation teaches proportionality and units, not a target for a pressure boundary.

**Worked case:**F10000N, L100 mm, A100 mm², E200000N/mm² givesδ0.05 mm. **Changed case:**F12000N gives 0.06 mm. If measured elongation differs, first examine reference, geometry, temperature and method under the approved process; do not automatically add torque. Gasket stress and service performance require the actual design basis, not this bolt-only model.

lessons.title: Q11 — Manual tools and calibration
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Manual tools and calibration

Select a tool suitable for the required torque, direction, access and fastener. Verify identification, calibration/verification status, range and condition before use. A certificate for another serial number does not establish the tool in hand. Check sockets and adapters for correct fit and approved use. Do not use damaged tools or unapproved handle extensions.

Follow the manufacturer's loading technique and storage instructions. A reading or click is meaningful only when the tool is used as intended. An in-line extension can alter effective lever length; a perpendicular arrangement may behave differently. Use the actual approved correction method rather than assume every adapter has no effect. Classroom calculations are not permission to modify a field tool setup.

**Worked case:** supplied wrench effective length 300 mm, in-line extension 60 mm, desired joint torque 24N·m. Under the stated ideal geometry, setpoint 24×300/360=20N·m. **Changed case:** an approved configuration has zero additional effective length; setpoint remains 24. If geometry or manufacturer approval is unknown, stop and obtain the correct basis instead of applying either answer automatically.

lessons.title: Q12 — Powered torque and reaction hazards
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Powered torque and reaction hazards

Powered torque tools introduce reaction forces, pinch points, hoses, pressure and stored energy. Match tool, socket/cassette, pump and accessories to the manufacturer's approved system. Verify the reaction arrangement, clearances and communication before any authorized operation. Keep hands out of the reaction path; do not use a body part or improvised object to restrain the tool. Enerpac's safety guidance emphasizes proper fit and reaction-arm use for its tools.[S06]

This course uses de-energized identification and planning exercises only. Actual hydraulic/pneumatic operation requires equipment-specific training and the employer's authorization. Do not infer a pump-pressure setting from a generic torque value; use the correct tool's current pressure/torque data and limits. A hose or coupling problem requires the manufacturer's safe depressurization and service process, not a hand search for a pressurized leak.

**Worked case:** a tool's chart belongs to another model and the proposed reaction point is uncertain. Record both gaps and do not energize. **Changed case:** the correct chart arrives, but socket fit is wrong. One corrected document does not make the setup safe. Demonstrate recognition on inert equipment and state the required competent follow-up.

lessons.title: Q13 — Tensioning and special-joint limits
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Tensioning and special-joint limits

Hydraulic tensioning applies load through a different process from torque tightening. Tool engagement, available stud length, hydraulic system, load transfer and the approved sequence matter. A torque target cannot be relabeled as a tensioner pressure. Multi-tool or special-joint methods require their specific procedures and qualifications. Large-diameter, ring-joint or wellhead assemblies may have requirements beyond the benign manual fixture used here.

The assembler must identify when the work exceeds their demonstrated scope. Ask for the actual equipment and joint method rather than extrapolate from another system. Record tool coverage, sequence and final verification according to the approved plan; do not invent compensation factors for load transfer.

**Worked case:** a work package requires tensioning but provides only a manual-torque record and no tensioner setup. Hold the method unresolved. **Changed case:** a tensioner is available but thread engagement evidence is missing. Tool presence is not readiness. This course's completion record distinguishes manual fixture performance from unperformed powered/special-joint qualification.

lessons.title: Q14 — Controlled assembly sequence
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Controlled assembly sequence

After the approved preparation and release checks, position the correct gasket and components without damage, establish the specified initial condition and follow the documented tightening sequence and stages. Track each location so no bolt is omitted or counted twice. The sequence and passes must match the actual procedure; this course's eight-position training pattern is only a benign fixture exercise.

Monitor the specified condition between stages and stop on unexpected movement, damaged components, incorrect readings or loss of tool control. Do not conceal a skipped stage by signing the final column. Manufacturer guidance for the cited gasket families uses staged tightening and a final sequential pass, but actual product/joint instructions govern.[S05]

**Worked case:** B54 classroom target 8N·m with supplied stages 25%, 50%, 100% gives 2, 4, 8N·m. Fixture positions 1–8 are numbered clockwise; exercise cross-pattern 1, 5, 3, 7, 2, 6, 4, 8 is followed at each stage, then the supplied sequential verification. **Changed case:** bolt 6's second-stage record is absent. Stop and obtain the instructor's controlled recovery instruction; do not invent the missing reading. No value here is a field assembly target.

lessons.title: Q15 — In-process observations and interruptions
lessons.body:
## Q15 — In-process observations and interruptions

An interruption can leave the joint at an intermediate condition. Preserve which steps were completed, by whom, with which tool and settings. Protect the assembly against contamination or accidental alteration. Before resuming, reconcile the actual condition with the approved restart instructions. A new shift must not infer completion from a paint mark alone.

Record unexpected friction, damaged threads, gasket movement, unequal gaps or tool issues as observations. Do not diagnose every resistance change as a bad bolt or compensate with unapproved torque. If the tool is found out of tolerance, identify the potentially affected work and obtain the required assessment rather than silently replacing it and continuing.

**Worked case:** a tool check fails after four of eight joints were assembled. Identify those four by records and retain the scope for technical disposition. **Changed case:** the replacement tool is valid, but affected joint evidence has not been reviewed. Future work may have a valid tool; past work is not automatically accepted. Keep the two decisions separate.

lessons.title: Q16 — Post-assembly verification
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Post-assembly verification

Final verification checks the completed configuration and required records against the procedure. Confirm joint identity, components, gasket position where inspectable, specified gaps/engagement, completed sequence and any required inspection sign-off. A checked form is not proof if the actual work or identity is unsupported. Preserve any unresolved deviation before handing the joint to the next stage.

An assembly record and a pressure/leak test answer different questions. Testing requires its own approved plan, boundaries, equipment and authorization. The assembler must not pressurize the classroom fixture or conduct an improvised leak test. A test pass also does not authorize concealment of an assembly deviation that requires separate disposition.

**Worked case:** twelve joints are listed, ten have valid complete assembly records, one has an unresolved gasket deviation and one has the wrong tag. Valid coverage 83.33%; two remain open. **Changed case:** tag corrected with valid evidence yields 11/12=91.67%, but the gasket issue remains. Report the exact open joint rather than rounding the job to complete.

lessons.title: Q17 — Leaks and abnormal conditions
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Leaks and abnormal conditions

A leak or abnormal condition is a reason to follow the operating response and safe isolation process, not to add torque reflexively. Temperature, pressure, component damage and stored energy can make intervention hazardous. The cited Garlock guidance does not recommend retightening its flange connections after temperature or pressure is applied.[S05] This course authorizes no live retightening or hot bolting.

Report location and observed condition from a safe position, protect people through established controls and contact the responsible operator. After the system is made safe under its actual procedure, the authorized investigation can review components, alignment, lubrication, assembly records and service changes. Preserve failed parts or records as directed; do not erase the evidence by an undocumented repair.

**Worked case:** a joint leaks during an authorized test and someone requests “one more turn.” Do not comply; follow the test/emergency controls and responsible authority. **Changed case:** pressure has been removed but residual temperature and trapped inventory are unverified. Safe intervention is still not established. A single zero gauge does not answer all hazards.

lessons.title: Q18 — Disassembly, inspection and reassembly records
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Disassembly, inspection and reassembly records

Disassembly requires the actual authorized work and isolation plan. The course does not prescribe a universal first bolt or opening direction. Once safe access is established by the responsible process, preserve component identity and observations for the investigation. Record damage, gasket condition and relevant assembly history without assuming the cause from one mark.

Reassembly is a new controlled configuration. Determine required replacements, approved reuse, face preparation, support and procedure changes. An old successful record cannot be reused as proof of the new assembly. Retain the relationship between original failure, disposition, actual work and verification.

**Worked case:** a gasket was replaced after a leak, but the record still carries the original assembly date/tool. Create the required traceable reassembly evidence; do not present the old record as current. **Changed case:** all new work is recorded, but the failure investigation imposes a support check that remains pending. Keep that condition open through handover.

lessons.title: Q19 — Records, traceability and quality control
lessons.body:
## Q19 — Records, traceability and quality control

The record should identify joint/system, procedure revision, components, lubricant, tool serial/status, assembler, dates, stage results, interruptions, deviations and verification. Record actual actions, not an intended schedule. Use the designated correction method so changes remain traceable. Blank or illegible entries need resolution, not invented values.

An independent review may compare records with the physical joint and work scope. Help that review by retaining exact IDs and evidence references. Quantity totals should distinguish prepared, assembled, inspected and tested joints. Do not treat these stages as interchangeable or assume all counts refer to the same joints.

**Worked case:** twenty prepared, eighteen assembled, sixteen verified and fourteen tested. Report each stage and its actual identity map; no single “twenty complete” claim is supported. **Changed case:** two more records verified, but they concern joints already counted. Duplicates do not increase verified coverage. Reconcile unique identities before reporting progress.

lessons.title: Q20 — Handover and continuing competence
lessons.body:
## Q20 — Handover and continuing competence

Handover communicates the verified configuration, evidence and remaining restrictions to the designated owner. The assembler can state which assembly tasks were completed under which basis; operating release belongs to the actual authority. Identify unresolved components, interrupted work, failed tool checks and required technical dispositions before the system advances.

Maintain competence within the methods actually demonstrated. A manual fixture assessment is not proof of hydraulic tensioning, energized equipment operation or every special-joint design. Changes in tools, joint types, procedures or observed performance may require additional instruction and assessment. Keep certificates and skill records accurate rather than broadening their wording to cover untested tasks.

**Worked case:** a learner passes manual fixture assembly and de-energized powered-tool hazard identification. Record both outcomes with their limits; do not call the learner a qualified hydraulic operator. **Changed case:** the employer later supplies equipment-specific training and actual assessment. Record that separate evidence and authorization, not a retroactive claim that this course already covered it. Honest scope is part of competent assembly practice.


---

content.title: VUC055 | VUC054 workbook, practical delivery and credential
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC054 workbook, practical delivery and credential
lessons.body: # VUC054 workbook, practical delivery and credential

lessons.title: Instructor, equipment and delivery
lessons.body:
## Instructor, equipment and delivery

Instructor must be competent in the actual manual assembly method and the training fixture, with access to qualified bolting/engineering specialists for questions beyond that scope. Assess safety, reading, units and arithmetic prerequisites; supply instruction before assessment. Use the combined VUC055 60-hour delivery plan; foundation final and award rules are superseded. Breaks and extra remediation are additional; record actual attendance, not just the plan.

Use a purpose-built stable, unconnected, unpressurized eight-position training fixture, compatible reusable training gasket, identified fasteners, benign approved training lubricant, correct sockets, a suitable verified low-range manual torque tool, ruler/caliper/feeler gauges, reference cards and printed records. Instructor confirms fixture/component/tool suitability for the supplied 8N·m maximum and records the manufacturer's setup instructions. If that suitability cannot be established, use a different documented benign fixture with its approved values and reissue all exercise references; never apply 8N·m blindly. Guard pinch points and secure the fixture. No fluid, pressure, live process, powered hydraulic operation, hot work or line breaking occurs.

Training-only reusable gasket/fixture is not an example permitting field gasket reuse. Clearly label it. Actual observed stations P04–P08, P11, P14 and P16 plus integrated I54 are mandatory. Remote delivery requires supervised equivalent equipment and known references; otherwise affected outcomes remain pending. Other stations use supplied records or de-energized equipment/images. Safe accessible tools/response formats may be substituted while preserving outcomes. No unassessed powered-tool endorsement is awarded.

lessons.title: B54 approved classroom work card
lessons.body:
## B54 approved classroom work card

Joint J1; procedureT54 revision 1; eight positions numbered 1–8 clockwise. Instructor fills actual fixture, tool serial, component IDs, lubricant and reference dimensions before issue. Supplied training stages 2/4/8N·m use pattern 1, 5, 3, 7, 2, 6, 4, 8; final sequential verification 1–8 at 8N·m. These are fixture-only values. Instructor verifies the tool is suitable at every stage or supplies a separately approved low-range tool. Require gasket centering and supplied initial condition before stages. Monitor hands/fixture, gaps and component condition throughout. Unexpected movement or damaged parts stops the exercise.

For an interrupted/missing stage, the learner stops and reports actual state. Instructor inspects the fixture and supplies a documented safe recovery instruction; do not improvise a universal field recovery rule. For reassessment, disassemble/reset only under the instructor's safe fixture instructions, issue changed identification/defect cards and require a fresh complete record. The instructor's known reference list is withheld during scored performance but is available for debrief.

Forms:

- Preparation: learner/date, joint/system, procedure/revision, isolation/fixture status, parts/marks, gasket/condition, faces, gaps/support, lubricant, tool serial/range/status, hold release.
- Stage sheet: bolt position, stage target, actual completion/reading as method permits, tool, operator, time, interruption and disposition. Never invent a continuous measured torque when the tool only supplies a setpoint/click indication.
- Deviation: observation, requirement, affected joints, safe hold, authority, disposition, actual correction and verification.
- Handover: unique joint IDs, assembly records, inspection status, testing status, open conditions, owner and release boundary.
- Assessment: original response, score, critical error, feedback, remediation, changed attempt, actual equipment/reference, assessor/date/version.

Labs use five dimensions 0–2: identity, calculation/method, comparison, safety/authority and traceable communication. Pass 8/10 with no zero or unresolved critical error. Correct all formative answers with reasoning and revisit the chapter/changed case. Keep unsuccessful attempts and targeted instruction.

lessons.title: W01 — Preparation and identity
lessons.body:
## W01 — Preparation and identity

**Packet:** J1 drawing C specifies G2; work card B says G1. Six of eight studs are identified, two unmarked. Permit names J2. Prepare a readiness register.

**Worked response:** three independent gaps: document/gasket basis, two fastener identities and actual isolation/joint scope. Do not open or assemble. Obtain controlled resolution from the designated owners, preserving the original discrepancies.

**Changed packet:** correct permit and G2 work card issued; both stud identities recovered, but one thread damaged. Close only supported identity issues; physical condition remains. Demonstrate actual component/mark matching on the inert fixture.

lessons.title: W02 — Face, gasket and alignment
lessons.body:
## W02 — Face, gasket and alignment

**Packet:** residue and marked scratch on inert face; correct new gasket with damaged edge. Gap readings 3.0/3.2/3.1/3.8 mm, supplied maximum spread 0.5 mm. Record each finding and comparison.

**Worked response:** spread 0.8 mm, 0.3 above supplied limit. Residue, scratch, gasket damage and gap are separate. Do not clean away the evidence or force alignment; follow the instructor's approved disposition. Real joint criteria are not supplied by this exercise.

**Changed packet:** cleaned face, sound correct gasket, gaps 3.1/3.2/3.0/3.3; spread 0.3 passes, but scratch assessment is missing. Retain that limitation. Physically measure the benign model and record actual positions/reference.

lessons.title: W03 — Friction and elastic sensitivity
lessons.body:
## W03 — Friction and elastic sensitivity

**Packet:** supplied T=KFd; K=.20, F=10000 N, d=.01 m. Elastic model L=100 mm, A=100 mm², E=200000 N/mm². Calculate torque and elongation; explain why neither is a field target.

**Worked response:** 20 N·m and .05 mm. K is supplied, not verified for a real joint; ideal geometry/material assumptions exclude actual gasket/component behavior.

**Changed packet:** same 20 N·m with K=.15 implies 13333.33 N, 33.33% higher; K=.25 implies 8000 N, 20% lower. Elastic F=12000 N gives .06 mm. Do not change field torque to chase classroom numbers; preserve the approved lubricant/target pairing.

lessons.title: W04 — Tool setup and staged values
lessons.body:
## W04 — Tool setup and staged values

**Packet:** ideal wrench effective length 300 mm, in-line extension 60 mm, desired 24 N·m. Separate B54 fixture target 8 N·m with 25/50/100% stages. Calculate both and check actual tool suitability.

**Worked response:** ideal setpoint 20 N·m; fixture stages 2/4/8 N·m. The extension correction does not authorize an unapproved adapter. Verify tool serial, range, direction, status and manufacturer instructions before demonstration.

**Changed packet:** authorized geometry has zero extra effective length, so 24 N·m setpoint. Fixture tool range 4–20 N·m cannot validly cover the 2 N·m stage; obtain an approved suitable tool or revised validated fixture procedure. Never use outside range and claim a valid result.

lessons.title: W05 — Powered-method readiness
lessons.body:
## W05 — Powered-method readiness

**Packet:** hydraulic tool chart for another model, uncertain reaction point, wrong-size socket. A separate job requires tensioning but only a manual torque card exists. Make method-specific readiness decisions.

**Worked response:** none is ready. Correct chart alone will not resolve reaction/fit. Tensioning needs its own approved setup, engagement, sequence and qualified personnel; manual target is not pump pressure.

**Changed packet:** chart and fit resolved; reaction still unverified. Tensioner available but engagement unknown. Retain both holds. Identify hazards using de-energized equipment/images only; no hydraulic actuation is performed.

lessons.title: W06 — Interruption and affected-work scope
lessons.body:
## W06 — Interruption and affected-work scope

**Packet:** stage 2 entry for bolt 6 missing; tool verification fails after four joints. Records identify J1–J4 as affected. Write hold and handover entries.

**Worked response:** stop and report actual fixture state; obtain instructor recovery, do not invent an entry. Preserve J1–J4 for technical assessment. Replacement tool validity does not accept past work.

**Changed packet:** replacement tool valid and J1/J2 disposition completed; J3/J4 unresolved. Report two of four closed, 50%, with actual IDs. Do not infer closure from the new tool alone. Reperform the fixture sequence under supplied safe recovery before completion.

lessons.title: W07 — Verification and stage counts
lessons.body:
## W07 — Verification and stage counts

**Packet:** 12 joints, 10 valid assembly records, 1 gasket deviation, 1 wrong tag. Separate job has 20 prepared, 18 assembled, 16 verified, 14 tested. Provide unique identity-based status.

**Worked response:** 10/12=83.3333% valid, 2 open; stage counts remain 20/18/16/14 and must match actual IDs. Preparation is not testing or operational release.

**Changed packet:** wrong tag validly resolved, 11/12=91.6667%, gasket issue open. Two added verification files are duplicates; verified count remains 16. Record actual evidence, not file count.

lessons.title: W08 — Leak response and reassembly
lessons.body:
## W08 — Leak response and reassembly

**Packet:** joint leaks during authorized test; request one more turn. Later gasket replaced, but record is old; support follow-up remains. Draft response and closure conditions.

**Worked response:** no live tightening. Follow operator/test controls and safe isolation; no zero-gauge-only assumption. New assembly requires its own record. Support condition remains independent.

**Changed packet:** pressure zero, but temperature/trapped inventory unknown; still no safe intervention established. When actual safe condition and new assembly evidence are provided, close only those elements; retain unmet support condition and owner decision.

lessons.title: Stations and scoring
lessons.body:
## Stations and scoring

Each station uses the lab five-dimension rubric, 8/10 minimum, no zero/critical error. Critical errors: attempting to open or tighten a live/unknown joint, defeating fixture controls, hands in reaction/pinch path, fabricated completion, concealing failed components or unsupported operational release. Stop unsafe practice, teach the reason and require changed observed performance.

| Station | Performance/evidence | Changed case |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Explain system and role boundaries using J1 | Correct gasket but unknown flange rating |
| P02 | Resolve drawing/work-card conflict | Verbal resolution without required controlled evidence |
| P03 | Match permit to physical joint, identify unknown energy | Correct tag with trapped-section uncertainty |
| P04 **actual** | Identify fixture flange geometry and supplied markings | Similar bolt pattern with mismatched facing card |
| P05 **actual** | Match eight fasteners/marks and inspect inert samples | Identity resolved but one damaged thread sample |
| P06 **actual** | Handle/center training gasket and identify condition | Correct identity with marked damage |
| P07 **actual** | Inspect inert face and record residue/scratch | Clean face with unmeasured defect |
| P08 **actual** | Measure gaps at named positions | Passing spread with support approval absent |
| P09 | Calculate friction sensitivity and preserve lubricant basis | Different supplied K at same torque |
| P10 | Calculate ideal elongation and explain limits | Increased load and uncertain actual reference |
| P11 **actual** | Check tool identity/range and demonstrate safe manual use | Tool outside range for first stage; reject setup |
| P12 | Identify powered-tool reaction/fit/chart hazards, de-energized | Correct chart but wrong fit |
| P13 | Distinguish tensioning and special-joint scope | Tensioner present with unknown engagement |
| P14 **actual** | Complete staged fixture sequence under work card | Instructor introduces missing-stage record and safe recovery |
| P15 | Scope affected work after failed tool check | Two dispositions close; other IDs remain open |
| P16 **actual** | Compare final fixture/configuration with its record | Wrong-tag or incomplete entry must be resolved |
| P17 | State safe response to leak request | Zero pressure but other hazards unverified |
| P18 | Build new reassembly record linked to prior failure | Signed work with open support condition |
| P19 | Reconcile unique IDs and four stage counts | Duplicate files do not increase coverage |
| P20 | Give restricted handover and accurate competence scope | Additional employer training is separate evidence |

lessons.title: I54 — Complete manual fixture assembly
lessons.body:
## I54 — Complete manual fixture assembly

Learner receives the B54 card, actual identified fixture/components and seeded documentation/condition discrepancies. First resolve the mismatches through the instructor's controlled issue process; do not assume they are harmless because it is training. Demonstrate preparation, component checks, gasket position, gap measurement, tool checks, staged manual assembly and final verification. Record actual work, including any interruption. Give handover with unperformed powered methods and field release explicitly excluded.

Assessor scores six dimensions 0–2: identity/preparation, component/face checks, measurement/tool setup, sequence/control, final record, and safety/authority. Pass 10/12 with no zero or unresolved critical error. All mandatory actual stations must also pass. For changed assessment reset the fixture under its instructions, change component/record defects and require a fresh sequence. Never seed a physical hazard; simulated defects use clearly safe inert samples or cards.



---

courses.title: VUC055 | VUC055 practical workbook and delivery

content.title: VUC055 | VUC055 practical workbook and delivery
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC055 practical workbook and delivery
lessons.body: # VUC055 practical workbook and delivery

lessons.title: Delivery plan and equipment
lessons.body:
## Delivery plan and equipment

Plan 60 instructional/assessment hours: the foundation's 10 instruction, 8 labs, 14 stations and 4 integrated practice hours (36); then 6 inspector instruction, 4 inspector labs, 6 inspector stations, 3 integrated inspection and 5 combined final hours (24). Do not administer the superseded foundation final in addition to this combined final. Breaks and additional remediation are outside the plan. Record actual participation. Assess reading, units, arithmetic and foundational safety before specialist exercises; provide targeted prerequisite teaching.

Instructor must demonstrate competence in manual assembly and joint inspection, tool verification and the actual training equipment. Obtain qualified technical support for questions beyond that scope. Keep the approved benign B54 fixture, training-only reusable gasket, identified components, low-range manual tool and safe setup from the foundation. Add an inert face-condition sample, a calibrated or verified surface-measurement instrument suitable for the supplied reference, gap tools, reference specimens/cards and instructor-controlled discrepancy packets. No process pressure, live equipment, hydraulic actuation, line breaking or destructive repair is performed.

The instructor measures and records reference specimens and equipment IDs before delivery. Synthetic numerical examples are not substitutes for actual instrument performance. If an appropriate surface instrument is unavailable, P23 remains pending; a photograph cannot earn the measurement outcome. Accessible equipment and response formats may be used if they preserve the outcome and safety requirements. A second trained person assembles the inert fixture for the inspection witness; learner and assembler roles must be identified separately.

Retain all foundation W01–08 and P01–20, with eight actual stations P04–08, P11, P14 and P16. Add W09–12 and P21–28 below. P23–26 require actual supervised instrument/fixture performance, bringing mandatory actual stations to twelve. Complete I54 manual assembly and I55 inspection. Prior learning may be credited only through mapped evidence and a demonstrated equivalent assessment; never waive missing outcomes based on job title.

lessons.title: W09 — Plan and traceability exercise
lessons.body:
## W09 — Plan and traceability exercise

**Packet:** J01–J08 require a pre-assembly hold release. J01–J06 have dated releases; J07/J08 are closed with no release. Twelve studs for J08 have ten matching heat records and two different marks. A drawing requires blank B4 but the register calls it B3.

**Task:** build a joint/stage matrix and a finding register. Distinguish direct observation, reviewed records and unknowns. State which steps must wait and who resolves each gap.

**Worked response:** six of eight required releases are evidenced; two missed hold points remain. Ten of twelve studs have supported identity. The blank requirement conflicts. Preserve joint IDs and revisions, obtain authorized dispositions, and do not backdate observations or infer suitability from appearance. Percentages 75% releases and 83.3333% stud identity are evidence summaries, not safety ratings.

**Changed packet:** approved second heat record arrives, but one nut is damaged; blank conflict resolved; photographs arrive for missed holds. Close supported identity/document issues only. Damage and the missed-hold disposition remain. Write a real record-review entry, not a fabricated witness signature.

lessons.title: W10 — Measurement and uncertainty exercise
lessons.body:
## W10 — Measurement and uncertainty exercise

**Packet:** named teaching face has fictional acceptance band 3.2–6.3 µm. Valid reading 6.5. Changed reading 6.2 with stated uncertainty ±0.3; exercise decision rule requires the whole interval inside the band. Separate final gaps are 2.1/2.4/2.2/2.6 mm, maximum spread 0.4. Changed gaps 2.1/2.2/2.2/2.4, with one inaccessible engagement check.

**Task:** calculate comparisons, state limitations, then physically measure the supplied inert reference specimen and fixture. Use actual values in the performance record rather than copying the case numbers.

**Worked response:** finish exceeds upper limit by 0.2 µm; changed interval 5.9–6.5 crosses the limit and does not meet the supplied decision rule. Initial gap spread 0.5 exceeds by 0.1; changed spread 0.3 passes that check only. Engagement still needs evidence. Record instrument, reference, units, positions, repeat results and limits. Obtain improved measurement or authorized disposition; do not round into acceptance.

**Changed practical:** instructor changes the safe sample or position labels and withholds its known reference until scoring. Learner identifies any measurement limits and completes a fresh report. No physical damage is created on operating equipment.

lessons.title: W11 — Tool and witness exercise
lessons.body:
## W11 — Tool and witness exercise

**Packet:** synthetic indicator 100 N·m, reference 96, allowed error ±3% relative to reference. Changed indicator 98, reference 96, but certificate serial differs. Three stages across eight positions require 24 witness events; one is missing. Later eight final-pass events are witnessed.

**Task:** assess tool evidence and build a stage-position record; then witness the actual benign B54 assembly by a second person. Stand clear of pinch/reaction paths. Stop unsafe or unexplained deviations using the instructor's safe recovery procedure.

**Worked response:** initial error 4.1667% fails; changed 2.0833% passes the numerical comparison but cannot establish the wrong-serial tool's validity. Witness coverage begins 23/24=95.8333%, later 31/32=96.875%. Missing original event remains; extra evidence does not recreate it. Do not energize a hydraulic tool or derive pump pressure.

**Changed practical:** instructor introduces a record discrepancy, never an unsafe physical setup. Learner distinguishes personally witnessed work from reviewed documentation, raises the discrepancy and verifies the controlled recovery. Record actual tool/fixture/operator/time and events observed.

lessons.title: W12 — Nonconformance and turnover exercise
lessons.body:
## W12 — Nonconformance and turnover exercise

**Packet:** ten findings: six corrected/verified, two corrected/unverified, two awaiting disposition. Twenty joints assembled, eighteen finally inspected, sixteen have test evidence. Two extra inspection reports duplicate known joints.

**Task:** reconcile the register and write a handover to the designated owner, with stage counts, limitations and action ownership.

**Worked response:** 60% verified closure, four open. Duplicate files do not increase eighteen inspected. Counts 20/18/16 remain distinct. No operating release is established by the packet. Corrected/unverified work still needs actual inspection evidence, and pending dispositions require authorized decisions.

**Changed packet:** one verified finding reopens and one pending finding becomes verified. Count stays six but update identities and restrictions. New test evidence for one previously untested joint raises tested count to seventeen; inspection and operating-release questions remain separate.

lessons.title: Station rubric and inspector stations
lessons.body:
## Station rubric and inspector stations

All labs/stations: five dimensions, each 0–2: identity/basis, method/calculation, comparison/limitations, safety/authority, and traceable report. Pass 8/10, no zero and no unresolved critical error. Critical errors include live/unknown-joint intervention, bypassing a required hold, unsafe equipment handling, fabricated witnessing and unauthorized operating release. Stop unsafe practice, teach the reason, and require changed observed performance. Arithmetic tolerance is 0.01 of the stated unit or percentage point, never rounding a failing criterion into a pass.

| Station | Required performance | Changed evidence |
|---|---|---|
| P21 | Build inspection-stage matrix and identify missed holds using W09 | Photographs arrive but required disposition is absent |
| P22 | Trace components and blank identity to requirements | Identity resolved with damaged nut remaining |
| P23 **actual** | Inspect inert face, use suitable instrument/reference and record units/limits | Different known specimen or uncertainty interval crossing supplied limit |
| P24 **actual** | Measure fixture at defined positions and assess supplied gap/engagement rules | Gap passes but engagement access remains incomplete |
| P25 **actual** | Match tool serial/range/reference and demonstrate correct verification setup without unsafe loading | Wrong certificate or unsuitable first-stage range; reject setup |
| P26 **actual** | Witness another person's complete B54 manual sequence and make contemporaneous record | Seeded record discrepancy and instructor-directed safe recovery |
| P27 | Write requirement/evidence/disposition/verification register | One closure reopens while another closes |
| P28 | Reconcile unique joint dossier and give restricted handover | Duplicates plus one genuine new test record |

lessons.title: I55 — Independent inspection of a training assembly
lessons.body:
## I55 — Independent inspection of a training assembly

Issue the approved B54 card and W09–12 records. The instructor supplies actual fixture/tool/sample identities and safe discrepancies. Learner plans inspection, checks documentation and components, measures the benign surface and geometry, verifies tooling, witnesses the second person's manual sequence, reconciles final evidence and hands over restrictions. No pressure test occurs. Do not simulate a dangerous condition by creating one; use safe cards or inert samples for defects.

Six dimensions score 0–2: inspection plan/identity, component traceability, measurement/tool evidence, witness accuracy, nonconformance closure, final handover/safety. Pass 10/12, no zero/critical error. A missed actual performance remains pending even if written answers are excellent. Changed reassessment resets the safe fixture per its instructions, changes the discrepancy cards and requires fresh measurement and witnessing. Record original and changed attempts separately.

lessons.title: Assessment, remediation and credential rules
lessons.body:
## Assessment, remediation and credential rules

Combined final has 28 cases, three decisions each, two points per decision: 168 points. Allow 300 minutes and calculator/coursebook; prohibit keys, collaboration and external assistance. Pass at least 135/168 and 4/6 in every domain, with no unresolved critical error. Score 2 for correct supported reasoning, 1 for safe incomplete response, 0 for wrong/missing/unsafe. The changed form has independently changed facts. After targeted remediation use changed cases and reobserve failed practical work. After two unsuccessful changed attempts, provide individualized instruction and a fresh equivalent supervised assessment. Preserve unsuccessful attempts and allow evidence-based appeal to another competent assessor where feasible.

Award requires all 28 chapters and 56 explained checks, 12 labs, 28 stations including twelve actual stations, both integrated cases and the combined final. Record identity, actual hours, version/hash, actual equipment/references, results, critical issues, remediation, assessor and restrictions. Separate private files do not themselves provide delivery access control; the provider must protect answer keys and personal records.

Issue “VNDRLY/U Bolted Flange Joint Inspection — training-fixture inspection assessment completion.” This is not API BFJI, ASME or OPITO certification, powered-tool operation qualification, engineering authorization or live-system release. Apply a 24-month VNDRLY review and earlier reassessment after changed methods or demonstrated gaps. Actual employer qualification remains separate.

lessons.title: Reusable evidence forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable evidence forms

- Plan: joint ID; drawing/procedure revision; stage; requirement; hold/witness/review basis; responsible person; required record; release signature/date.
- Measurement: sample/joint; location/stage; instrument/serial/reference; units; raw and repeat readings; uncertainty/limits; criterion; comparison; disposition.
- Witness: joint; assembler; inspector; tool/setting; stage/position; time; personally observed action; record-reviewed action; missing event; safe hold; recovery authority.
- Finding: unique issue; requirement; evidence; affected joints; status; owner; disposition; correction evidence; actual verification; closure/reopening history.
- Handover: unique joint stage counts; unresolved IDs; test status; temporary components; restrictions; owner; next release authority.
- Assessment: learner; outcome; equipment; original score; critical finding; instruction supplied; changed case; observed result; assessor/date/version; appeal outcome.


---

content.title: VUC055 | VUC055 formative checks
