courses.title: VUC060 | VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Crack Height Sizing

content.title: VUC060 | VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Crack Height Sizing
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Crack Height Sizing
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Crack Height Sizing

VUC060 · Original materials · 2026-11-18

lessons.title: Scope and prerequisites
lessons.body:
## Scope and prerequisites

This specialist course addresses conventional ultrasonic sizing of planar features connected to the surface opposite the scanning surface, including weld-root geometry. It preserves the catalog's legacy QUSE scope while distinguishing it from the currently listed API QUTE programs. The available QUSE orientation is dated July 2015; it is historical context, not proof of current external examination rules. [S60-01] VNDRLY completion is not API certification, employer UT qualification or fitness-for-service acceptance.

Require demonstrated conventional UT competence, geometry/arithmetic, safe instrument handling and applicable vision/prerequisite records before independent scored work. The instructor supplies an approved specimen-specific technique and manufacturer instructions. Beginners receive foundation teaching rather than being signed off on advanced sizing. All work uses cool, stable, depressurized training specimens. Actual practical performance is required; course creation is not a claim that any learner has performed it.

lessons.title: Q01 — Define the quantity before measuring
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Define the quantity before measuring

Crack height, depth to tip, remaining ligament and length along the weld are different quantities. Establish the scanning surface and the connected surface on a section drawing. For a feature connected to the opposite surface of a flat plate of local thickness t, if the tip lies at depth d from the scanning surface, height h=t−d. That equation assumes correct feature identity and the stated geometry. A numerical difference cannot establish those assumptions.

Write the required report quantity and units at the top of the worksheet. If the request says “depth,” clarify whether it means distance from the scanning surface or penetration from the far surface. Do not let an ambiguous column heading propagate into engineering decisions.

**Worked:** local thickness 20 mm, established tip depth 14 mm gives height 6 mm and near-surface ligament 14 mm. **Changed:** the feature is near-surface connected instead. The same depth no longer supports the original far-surface subtraction. Redraw the connection and use the applicable method before reporting. P01 tests the definition, not memorized subtraction.

lessons.title: Q02 — Procedure, role and safe readiness
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Procedure, role and safe readiness

Identify the approved sizing technique, material/thickness range, probe/wedge, reference standards, calibration, scanning pattern and reporting limits. The procedure must be suitable for the actual feature and geometry. A technique that detects a response may not resolve the tip accurately enough for sizing. Production acceptance belongs to its authorized decision maker; the examiner reports supported measurements and limitations.

Inspect the bench arrangement, instrument/cable condition, specimen stability, sharp edges and couplant handling. Use compatible materials and safe electrical practices under the equipment manual. Do not test hot, moving, pressurized or energized process equipment on this course's authority. Record interrupted work so a restart does not skip the affected region.

**Worked:** a learner has a conventional detection procedure but no validated sizing method for the specimen. Hold scored sizing and obtain the appropriate technique. **Changed:** the method is supplied but a heavy sample is unsecured. Correct the physical setup before work. P02 requires a completed readiness/authority checklist with actual observations.

lessons.title: Q03 — Material, weld root and geometry
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Material, weld root and geometry

Review local thickness, surface contour, weld crown/root and reference direction. Geometry can create strong echoes that mask or resemble feature responses. A nominal drawing is a starting point, not proof of the actual specimen profile. Verify accessible dimensions with the approved method and preserve deviations. Do not grind a crown simply to make interpretation easier unless explicitly authorized for that specimen.

Separate known geometric responses from possible crack-related responses through controlled probe movement and corroboration. The strongest echo may be a corner or root, not the crack tip. A complicated root cannot be dismissed as “noise” when it prevents reliable sizing. Report the actual limitation and obtain an appropriate technique or access solution.

**Worked:** nominal thickness 20 mm but verified local thickness 19 mm. With the same established tip depth 14 mm, height is 5 mm, not 6 mm. **Changed:** local thinning varies across the crack length. Pair each tip depth with the corresponding local thickness; do not subtract all depths from a single favorable nominal value.

lessons.title: Q04 — Sound path and corrected travel time
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Sound path and corrected travel time

For a simple pulse-echo material path, S=vt/2 using the correct mode velocity and material-only round-trip transit time. Wedge/electronic delay must be handled by the approved calibration. Use consistent units and name the path. An angle-beam path is longer than its normal-depth component; reporting S as depth can greatly overstate or understate the intended quantity.

Keep raw readings, applied configuration and calculations together. If the velocity or zero changes, determine which prior measurements are affected. Do not correct only the final printed number while leaving the stored setup inconsistent.

**Worked:** corrected transit 10 µs at 3.2 mm/µs gives 16 mm path. **Changed:** raw transit 12 µs contains 2 µs delay; corrected path is still 16 mm, while using raw time gives 19.2 mm. The 3.2 mm error is not a tolerance to ignore. P04 links an actual reference check to this calculation.

lessons.title: Q05 — Angle, depth and leg interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Angle, depth and leg interpretation

For a flat first-leg ray at angle θ from the normal, d=S cosθ and offset=S sinθ. Draw the ray before using the formulas. Reflected paths require the proper leg treatment and actual boundary geometry. Curved surfaces require an appropriate model; the flat formula cannot be extended by simply changing the thickness number.

Angle error influences depth. Near a sizing boundary, a small geometric error may materially change reported height. Demonstrate the method on suitable known references over the range used. Do not choose the angle that makes an unknown feature agree with an expected answer.

**Worked:** S=20 mm at 60° gives d=10 mm; in 20 mm plate with a valid far-surface feature, h=10 mm. **Changed:** at 55° the same S gives d=11.4715 mm and h=8.5285 mm. This illustrates sensitivity to angle, not permission to change angles arbitrarily. P05 requires a labeled sketch and verification of the actual configuration.

lessons.title: Q06 — Probe selection and reference suitability
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Probe selection and reference suitability

Select the approved probe/wedge and settings for the expected depth, resolution and geometry. Frequency, pulse characteristics and beam behavior affect whether separate responses can be resolved. A more precise display does not improve physical resolution. Reference blocks must be identified and suitable for the method; a shallow notch alone does not prove deep-tip performance throughout the intended range.

Inspect wear and contact. Record actual system identifiers and software/settings. Any changed probe, wedge or relevant configuration requires the procedure's applicable checks. A previous operator's saved file can assist setup but cannot replace the learner's demonstration.

**Worked:** the packet specifies reference features at three depths, but only the shallow one is checked. Range performance is not established. **Changed:** all references are checked, then the wedge is replaced. Assess and perform required new checks rather than carrying old evidence forward unquestioned. P06 requires actual inventory and reference selection.

lessons.title: Q07 — Calibration and independent verification
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Calibration and independent verification

Calibration establishes the measurement relationship; verification tests whether it remains suitable. Use known positions across the relevant range, identify the reference and record actual readings. For each point, signed error is measured minus reference. Evaluate against the announced training criterion and its decision rule. Do not average a high and low error into an apparent pass if each point must comply.

The reference truth must be more reliable than the measurement performance being assessed. Unknown notch depth or unsupported documentation cannot serve as a precise grading standard. If independent truth is inadequate, the specimen cannot be used for scored sizing until resolved.

**Worked:** reference depths 5/15 mm read 5.2/15.8. Errors+0.2/+0.8; against fictional±0.5 mm, the second fails. **Changed:** readings 4.8/15.2 both meet the numerical band, but reference identity is missing. Numeric agreement does not establish traceability. P07 requires actual calibration and a separately recorded verification.

lessons.title: Q08 — Locating a tip-diffracted response
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Locating a tip-diffracted response

A feature tip can produce a diffracted response whose arrival helps locate the tip. It may be much weaker than a corner response; mistaking geometry or another mode for the tip creates a false height. Manufacturer teaching illustrates the distinct corner and tip responses, but the actual specimen requires a demonstrated technique. [S60-02]

Follow the approved probe movement, range and evaluation settings to seek a repeatable response consistent with the feature geometry. Corroborate location using permitted positions/directions. Preserve the observed waveform and the reasoning for identification. If a unique tip cannot be established, report sizing as unresolved rather than selecting a convenient small echo.

**Worked:** strong corner echo and earlier weak response are present, but the weak response does not track consistently with probe movement. It is not yet a proven tip. **Changed:** repeated approved observations establish a consistent tip location. Record that evidence and then calculate height; do not claim the initial uncertainty never existed. P08 uses actual known-feature specimens under supervision.

lessons.title: Q09 — Amplitude sizing and equivalent reflectors
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Amplitude sizing and equivalent reflectors

Amplitude-drop and equivalent-reflector approaches describe response behavior under particular assumptions. Beam width, orientation, shape and coupling influence the result. BINDT notes limitations when flaw geometry/orientation is complex. [S60-03] Equivalent reflector size is not automatically the actual physical height of a crack; DGS relates response to a reference model. [S60-04]

Use amplitude information only as the approved sizing technique permits. A half-amplitude point is about−6.02 dB relative to the peak, but finding it does not by itself validate the physical boundary. Document reference, evaluation gain, clipping and beam conditions. Do not switch methods mid-examination solely to obtain a more favorable number.

**Worked:** peak 80% and comparison 40% give ratio 0.5 and−6.0206 dB. **Changed:** the peak was clipped. The ratio is no longer established from that display; restore a valid approved measurement basis and repeat. P09 demonstrates the response limitation on a reference, without awarding crack-height accuracy from amplitude alone.

lessons.title: Q10 — Scan the full feature and find maximum height
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Scan the full feature and find maximum height

A crack can vary in height along its length. A single favorable section does not establish the maximum. Use the procedure's scan pattern over the entire assigned feature, maintain contact and track position. Record local thickness and identified tip depth at each required location. The maximum supported height is the largest valid local height, not the average.

If contact or interpretation fails at an interval, that interval remains unresolved. A high confidence result elsewhere does not fill the gap. Rescan under valid conditions and preserve the original coverage record. Do not silently exclude a difficult crown or edge.

**Worked:** valid local heights 3.2, 4.1, 3.8 mm have maximum 4.1 mm. **Changed:** an unexamined interval lies between the first two locations. The maximum of measured values remains 4.1, but the whole-feature maximum is not established. P10 requires actual systematic scanning and an explicit coverage map.

lessons.title: Q11 — Multiple tips, branching and ambiguous boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Multiple tips, branching and ambiguous boundaries

More than one plausible tip response may occur. Do not select the smallest height by preference or assume every extra response belongs to a separate crack. Compare repeatability, geometry and approved corroborating evidence. Report the greatest supported height within the procedure's definition, while preserving uncertainty about unresolved features.

Separate resolution limits from absence of a feature. If two responses merge, adding decimal places does not identify their true boundaries. An alternative approved technique may be needed; invoking its name without actual qualification and performance does not resolve the result.

**Worked:** far-surface feature in 20 mm plate has established tips at depths 14 and 12 mm; corresponding heights 6 and 8 mm. Maximum supported height 8 mm. **Changed:** the 12 mm response is later proven geometric. Withdraw that interpretation with a traceable revision; 6 mm remains supported only if the remaining feature and full coverage are valid. P11 requires evidence-based reasoning, not guessing a maximum.

lessons.title: Q12 — Repeatability, bias and uncertainty
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Repeatability, bias and uncertainty

Repeat measurements can show consistency without proving correctness. Three readings all displaced by a wrong zero may agree closely. Compare against independent known truth as well as repeatability. Record signed errors to reveal systematic over- or undersizing. Do not treat average zero error as proof that every measurement meets tolerance.

Uncertainty describes limitations in the measurement and reference basis; it is not a discretionary allowance to add or subtract until a result passes. Use the predeclared decision rule. Where the evidence cannot resolve whether a criterion is met, state that rather than rounding away the issue.

**Worked:** errors+1,−1,+1,−1 mm have mean 0 but RMS 1 mm. **Changed:** all four errors+0.8 mm have RMS 0.8 and mean+0.8, showing bias despite smaller RMS. These are training calculations, not API scoring rules. P12 compares actual repeat readings with protected reference truth after the attempt.

lessons.title: Q13 — Units, conversion and report precision
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Units, conversion and report precision

Keep the instrument, worksheet and final report units consistent. One inch is exactly 25.4 mm. A height expressed as a decimal fraction of an inch is not the same number in millimeters. Retain sufficient intermediate precision and round only according to the reporting instruction. Never use rounding to move a failed measured error inside its limit.

Record the measured quantity explicitly, such as far-surface-connected height, rather than an unlabeled “depth.” Include coordinate convention and local thickness basis. If a conversion reveals an implausible result, revisit the source reading rather than silently altering it.

**Worked:**0.25 in equals 6.35 mm. **Changed:**0.20 in equals 5.08 mm, difference 1.27 mm. A worksheet containing 6.35 under an “inches” heading is not a harmless cosmetic error. P13 requires a checked dual-unit report with a second calculation or independent review.

lessons.title: Q14 — Drift, changes and recovery
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Drift, changes and recovery

Perform verification at required intervals and after relevant changes. A failed check identifies a potentially affected examination period; assess records since the last valid check under the procedure. A successful later correction does not validate old results automatically. Preserve the failure, affected IDs, corrective action and actual repeat examination.

Changes to probe, wedge, velocity, range or evaluation method may affect prior data differently. Identify the real dependency rather than repeating unrelated work or overlooking affected work. Do not erase original measurements to make the file look clean.

**Worked:** last valid 10:00, failure 12:00; five specimens scanned between. All five require affected-scope assessment. **Changed:** only the fifth is repeated after correction. The first four remain unresolved unless the approved disposition specifically establishes their validity. P14 uses a safe instructor-issued drift condition and actual recovery records.

lessons.title: Q15 — Reporting to engineering without overclaiming
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Reporting to engineering without overclaiming

Provide specimen/component identity, procedure, actual equipment, configuration, references, coverage, measured quantity/units, maximum supported height and limitations. Distinguish the recorded result from an acceptance decision. A sizing examiner does not independently convert a height into remaining life or safe operating pressure without the relevant authority and assessment.

Make revisions traceable. If later evidence changes tip identification or local thickness, show the original value, new basis, affected result and recipient notification through the authorized workflow. Do not bury a meaningful limitation in a generic disclaimer.

**Worked:** report says “crack depth 6 mm, acceptable” without surface convention or acceptance basis. Correct the quantity/coordinate statement and remove unsupported disposition. **Changed:** authorized engineering acceptance arrives for a named condition. Attach it with its scope; do not imply it applies to another component or changed measurement.

lessons.title: Q16 — Blind performance and continuing competence
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Blind performance and continuing competence

Independent assessment requires an unseen specimen set with protected, validated truth and adequate range of feature heights/geometry. The learner sets up, verifies, scans and reports without coaching. Written answers and familiar demonstration specimens cannot replace it. Scoring must be announced before the attempt and must not be altered after seeing results.

Use the outcome to diagnose errors: wrong quantity, calibration bias, tip confusion, coverage gap or reporting error. Teach the cause and reassess on changed specimens. Retain evidence of failed and successful attempts. Course completion records only the actual demonstrated scope; employer qualification and production authorization remain separate.

**Worked:** nine of ten heights meet the announced band, but one specimen was never scanned and its value was copied. This is an integrity failure, not 90% competence. **Changed:** the learner honestly reports an unresolved size. That avoids fabrication but still requires remediation and a valid changed demonstration before the practical can pass. I60 assesses actual performance, not confidence.


---

courses.title: VUC060 | VUC060 delivery, applied learning and award

content.title: VUC060 | VUC060 delivery, applied learning and award
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC060 delivery, applied learning and award
lessons.body: # VUC060 delivery, applied learning and award

lessons.title: Instructor and equipment
lessons.body:
## Instructor and equipment

Plan 48 hours: 12 instruction/checks, 8 labs, 16 supervised stations, 8 integrated practice/blind practical and 4 written final/review. Record actual attendance; extra remediation and breaks are additional. Instructor must be competent in conventional UT sizing and the selected procedure/equipment. The responsible UT technical authority validates the technique, specimen truth and grading basis. This is not a prescribed API training-hour requirement.

Provide conventional UT flaw detector, suitable approved probes/wedges/cables, manufacturer instructions, identified reference standards, safe couplant/SDS, ruler/caliper as appropriate, removable tape and stable cool carbon-steel training specimens. Use no live plant, heat, pressure, radiation or hazardous access. Inspect cables and bench stability; control spill/slip and handling hazards. The learner physically performs setup and sizing. No simulator or written calculation substitutes for the actual stations.

Diagnostic: draw far-surface connection, distinguish height/ligament, compute t−d, convert inches/mm, calculate pulse-echo path, explain why a weak echo is not automatically a tip. Teach missing prerequisites before scored work. Demonstrate one known specimen with reasoning, then use different practice specimens. Accessible benches, larger displays and equivalent response formats are permitted without removing the measured performance requirement.

lessons.title: S60 specimen sets and controlled procedure
lessons.body:
## S60 specimen sets and controlled procedure

Teaching set includes known far-surface-connected planar features at differing heights, root/crown geometry and a deliberately ambiguous example for learning limitations. Independent set A and changed set B each contain ten resolvable sizing specimens/regions spanning at least two thickness groups and both flush and retained-crown geometries. Assign unique aliases; keep feature height truth hidden. These are original training specifications, not a statement that physical hardware already exists or API uses this configuration.

The technical authority establishes truth from suitable independent characterization/certified records, records uncertainty and confirms the approved technique resolves each scored feature. If truth is inadequate or the method cannot resolve a scored feature, replace/validate it before scoring; do not manufacture an answer. Include one known non-sizing geometric teaching region outside the scored ten to assess honest limitation. No exam specimen data from another organization are used.

Complete actual technique sheet before delivery: material/local thickness/geometry; instrument and software; probe/wedge/cable; mode/velocity; reference blocks; calibration and verification sequence; scanning pattern; tip-identification corroboration; height calculation; coverage; report format; verification intervals/recovery. Use the actual manufacturer's button sequence. Learner independently establishes and demonstrates setup; a saved file alone is insufficient.

Fictional S60 teaching criteria: reference depth error no more than±0.5 mm at each specified point; final height error no more than±1.0 mm on every designated scored specimen; complete assigned coverage and valid verification records; correct quantity/units and no unresolved safety/integrity error. Reference truth uncertainty must be sufficiently smaller, documented by the authority, with a conservative decision rule set before testing. These are VNDRLY training thresholds, not current API grading or production acceptance criteria.

lessons.title: W01 — Quantity, local thickness and readiness
lessons.body:
## W01 — Quantity, local thickness and readiness

Input: flat plate nominal 20 mm, verified local 19 mm, established far-surface tip depth 14 mm; detection-only procedure supplied. Task: draw quantity definitions, compute height and identify readiness gap. Worked response: height 5 mm, ligament 14 mm; nominal subtraction would give 6 mm; sizing procedure must be established before scored work. Changed: feature near-surface connected and sample unsecured. Redraw applicability and stabilize safely; do not reuse far-surface formula. Submit actual readiness form and corrected sketch.

lessons.title: W02 — Time and ray geometry
lessons.body:
## W02 — Time and ray geometry

Input: raw 12 µs, delay 2 µs, velocity 3.2 mm/µs; separate ray 20 mm at 60° in 20 mm plate. Worked response: corrected 10 µs, path 16 mm; raw-time path 19.2 mm is 3.2 mm high. Separate ray depth 10 mm and far-surface height 10 mm. Changed: angle 55° gives depth 11.4715 mm, height 8.5285 mm. State these are separate cases and assumptions, not interchangeable readings. Draw each geometry and label units/mode/leg.

lessons.title: W03 — System and calibration
lessons.body:
## W03 — System and calibration

Input: required shallow/mid/deep reference checks, only shallow done; known 5/15 mm read 5.2/15.8 against±0.5. Worked response: range insufficient; errors+0.2/+0.8, second fails. Changed: 4.8/15.2 pass numerically but reference identity absent; wedge then changes. Obtain traceable reference and perform applicable new system checks. Learner actually inventories, calibrates and verifies on suitable references; instructor records observations rather than supplying passing values.

lessons.title: W04 — Tip and amplitude discrimination
lessons.body:
## W04 — Tip and amplitude discrimination

Input: strong corner echo plus unstable weak candidate; amplitude example 80%/40%. Worked response: weak candidate not established as tip; ratio 0.5,−6.0206 dB, not proof of physical height. Changed: consistent tip corroborated but original amplitude peak clipped. Record valid tip evidence separately from invalid amplitude comparison; restore approved amplitude basis if needed. Physically demonstrate on known teaching features and preserve an annotated response record.

lessons.title: W05 — Maximum height and multiple responses
lessons.body:
## W05 — Maximum height and multiple responses

Input: valid local heights 3.2/4.1/3.8 mm; second case 20 mm plate with established tip depths 14/12 mm. Worked response: first maximum 4.1 mm; second heights 6/8 mm, max 8. Changed: first has unexamined interval, so whole-feature max unresolved; second 12 mm response proves geometric, so revise interpretation while preserving history. Actual scan must cover assigned length and record local thickness/tip pairs, not just one favorable point.

lessons.title: W06 — Bias, repeatability and units
lessons.body:
## W06 — Bias, repeatability and units

Input: errors+1/−1/+1/−1 mm; 0.25 in height. Worked response: mean 0, RMS 1 mm; 6.35 mm conversion. Changed: all errors+0.8 mm produce mean+0.8, RMS 0.8; 0.20 in=5.08 mm, difference 1.27 mm. Compare repeatability and independent truth separately. Learner performs repeated actual sizing and retains every reading; no selective deletion or changing the rubric after results.

lessons.title: W07 — Drift and report repair
lessons.body:
## W07 — Drift and report repair

Input: last valid 10:00, failed 12:00, five specimens scanned; report says “depth 6 mm, acceptable” without basis. Worked response: assess all five affected specimens, define quantity/surface and remove unsupported acceptance. Changed: only fifth repeated; engineering disposition covers one named component. Four measurements remain unresolved unless validly disposed; engineering decision is not universal. Preserve original/revised records and actual repeat evidence.

lessons.title: W08 — Independent assessment decisions
lessons.body:
## W08 — Independent assessment decisions

Input: ten specimens, nine within±1 mm, one unscanned with copied value. Worked response: integrity failure, not 90% pass. Changed: learner honestly reports unresolved size. Honest limitation is required but does not satisfy sizing performance; teach and repeat on changed validated set. Prepare a complete report with actual inventory, reference checks, coverage, local thickness, tip evidence, height and limits. No credit for invented hardware observations.

lessons.title: Stations and rubric
lessons.body:
## Stations and rubric

Score five dimensions 0–2 each: identity/basis, method/setup, measurement/interpretation, safety/authority, traceable record. Pass 8/10, no zero or unresolved critical issue. Critical errors: unsafe handling, fabricated observation, hidden invalid calibration, unexamined scope represented as complete, unsupported production release. Stop unsafe action, teach and reobserve on changed conditions. Arithmetic tolerance 0.01 stated unit; physical grading uses S60 criteria and prior decision rule, not rounding into compliance.

| Station | Required evidence | Changed task |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Draw height/depth/ligament definitions | Changed surface connection |
| P02 **actual** | Safe bench and procedure readiness | Unsecured specimen/changed technique |
| P03 **actual** | Establish actual geometry/local thickness basis | Variable thickness along feature |
| P04 | Correct transit/path calculation | Delay included in raw reading |
| P05 | Draw angle/leg/depth relationship | Changed angle or invalid leg |
| P06 **actual** | Inventory system and select proper references | Wedge/probe replacement |
| P07 **actual** | Calibrate and independently verify | Second reference fails |
| P08 **actual** | Identify/corroborate tip response | Ambiguous geometry response |
| P09 **actual** | Demonstrate amplitude/reference limitation | Clipped peak |
| P10 **actual** | Scan whole feature and record maximum | Interrupted coverage |
| P11 **actual** | Resolve multiple-response interpretation | One candidate proven geometric |
| P12 **actual** | Repeat sizing and compare protected truth | Consistent biased readings |
| P13 | Produce correct dual-unit report | Wrong unit heading |
| P14 **actual** | Verification failure and actual recovery record | Only part of affected set repeated |
| P15 | Report measured scope without engineering overclaim | Narrow authorized disposition |
| P16 **actual** | Independent sizing/report on unseen practice set | Fresh feature identities |

lessons.title: I60 — Blind sizing practical
lessons.body:
## I60 — Blind sizing practical

Four-hour original practical within the integrated block, with breaks/setup planning separately scheduled. Use set A; changed assessment uses set B. Learner inventories, sets up, verifies, scans all ten, identifies appropriate tip evidence and reports maximum far-surface-connected height. Instructor observes without revealing feature truth or coaching probe placement. Required actual records link every specimen to valid setup and verification.

Pass requires every designated height within fictional±1.0 mm; every assigned region examined; all required setup/reference checks valid; correct quantity, units and coordinate basis; no unresolved critical error. Instructor compares signed errors to protected validated truth using the preannounced decision rule. A missing value cannot be silently omitted from denominator. Ambiguous teaching specimen is assessed for honest limitation separately, not inserted into scored set as an impossible sizing task.

Private truth record fields: alias___ material/thickness/geometry___ actual height truth___ independent method/uncertainty___ validated technique___ scored status___ actual learner height___ signed error___ decision-rule result___ setup/coverage link___ assessor/date___ . Store truth separately from learner packet and never use protected external exam samples.

lessons.title: Final, remediation and credential
lessons.body:
## Final, remediation and credential

16 cases, three decisions each, 2 points each: 96 points. Three hours within final/review block. Pass 77/96 and 4/6 in each domain, no unresolved critical error. Calculator/coursebook permitted; keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Each decision 2 correct supported, 1 safe incomplete, 0 wrong/missing/unsafe. Changed Form B uses changed facts. Written pass never offsets failed actual sizing.

Require 16 chapters/32 formative checks, 8 labs, 16 stations including 11 actual, I60 and written final. Teach failed concepts, require corrected explanation and changed observed performance; after two unsuccessful changed attempts, individualized instruction and fresh equivalent supervised assessment. Preserve all attempts and permit review by another competent assessor where feasible. If safe equipment or validated truth is unavailable, learner practical remains pending.

Award “VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Crack Height Sizing: training assessment completion.” Record learner/prerequisite evidence, actual hours, version/hash, equipment/technique, specimen-set version, results, remediation, assessor and scope. No API/ASNT/employer qualification or fitness-for-service authority conferred. VNDRLY review 24 months or earlier after changed method/requirements or competence gaps; internal policy only.

lessons.title: Learner record forms
lessons.body:
## Learner record forms

**Readiness/technique:** operator/date___ specimen/geometry___ procedure/revision___ quantity/surface convention___ safe setup___ actual instrument/probe/wedge/cable___ mode/velocity___ reference/checks___ scan/sizing method___ verification/recovery___

**Sizing:** specimen/position___ local thickness/basis___ actual tip response/evidence___ path/angle/leg___ depth___ height/calculation/units___ coverage___ repeat readings___ uncertainty/limit___ saved record___

**Recovery/report:** last valid___ failed check___ affected IDs___ disposition___ actual repeats___ original retained___ revised value/basis___ authorized recipient___

**Assessment:** learner/version___ original evidence/score___ critical issue___ instruction___ changed specimen/case___ result___ assessor/date___ appeal___ award/pending reason___


---

lessons.title: VUC060 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC060 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

Is height always depth from the scanning surface?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Define surface connection and quantity. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

Does subtraction establish tip identity?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence must establish the geometry first. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Does a detection procedure always qualify sizing?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Sizing suitability must be established. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

Does this course authorize live plant inspection?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Bench training scope only. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Can nominal thickness replace known local thickness indiscriminately?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the corresponding actual basis. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

May a weld crown be ground without authorization?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Preparation must preserve authorized scope. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Must wedge delay be addressed?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Raw time may include nonmaterial travel. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

Is sound path necessarily normal depth?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Angle/leg geometry matters. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

Are angles measured from normal here?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Surface-angle substitution changes result. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Can a flat first-leg formula silently handle every reflected path?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use actual geometry. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Does a shallow reference alone prove deep-range sizing?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Required range must be demonstrated. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Does a saved file replace setup demonstration?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Actual system checks required. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Can opposite errors average into a per-point pass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Each required point must meet its criterion. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Is unidentified reference truth sufficient?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Traceability and dimensions required. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

Is every weak early echo a tip?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Identification requires corroboration. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

Should an unresolved tip be assigned a guessed height?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Report limitation and resolve method. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Is equivalent reflector size automatically crack height?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It describes a model response. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

Does half amplitude alone validate the physical edge?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Technique assumptions matter. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Does one section establish maximum height over the whole feature?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Complete required scan needed. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

Is maximum the average of local heights?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use largest supported value with full coverage. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Must the smallest plausible height be selected?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence determines supported feature extent. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

Can extra decimal places resolve merged tips?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Physical resolution governs. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Does repeatability prove accuracy?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Consistent bias is possible. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Is uncertainty a discretionary pass allowance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use prior decision rule. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Is one inch exactly 25.4 mm?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Use correct unit conversion. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

May rounding turn an exceeded limit into a pass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Preserve applicable decision rule. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Does correction validate earlier scans automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Affected interval requires assessment. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

May failed checks be deleted?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Preserve history and recovery. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Does a sizing result alone establish safe operating pressure?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Authorized engineering assessment is separate. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

Can a narrow disposition cover another component automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Identity and scope govern. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Can familiar practice specimens replace blind performance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Fresh independent set required. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

Can an honest unresolved size be counted as a successful measurement?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Honesty is necessary but performance remains pending. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: VUC060 source and outcome register
lessons.body:
# VUC060 source and outcome register

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original VNDRLY instruction/cases, not reproduced examination material. No full proprietary standard or current external exam equivalence claim.

**S60-01 Legacy API scope/current context:** https://www.api.org/~/media/files/certification/icp/icp-certification-programs/ut%20programs/quse/api%20quse_candidate%20orientation_rev-072415.pdf . The document itself is July 2015. It describes far-surface-connected crack-height performance demonstration, distinguishing height from remaining ligament. Used only to identify legacy catalog scope. Current https://landing.api.org/qute-icp lists QUTE (M), QUTE (PA), QUTE-TM and LSP; no claim that legacy QUSE registration/scoring is currently available. Historical limits are not imported as current VNDRLY or production criteria.

**S60-02 Tip response:** https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/flaw-detection/tip-diffraction . Supports distinct corner/tip response interpretation and geometry-based tip location. Original cases teach that actual identity must be demonstrated; no universal weak-echo rule or automatic height calculation.

**S60-03 Sizing limitations:** https://www.bindt.org/What-is-NDT/Ultrasonic-flaw-detection/?cookie-accept=1 . Supports dependence of sizing on beam/flaw geometry and limits of amplitude techniques. No quoted accuracy is promised for this course or an unknown specimen.

**S60-04 Equivalent reflector distinction:** https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/flaw-detection/dgs-avg . Primary indexed excerpt describes equivalent-reflector modeling. Used only to distinguish that quantity from actual crack height; no DGS procedure/acceptance curve reproduced.

**S60-05 Amplitude-drop caution:** https://www.fhwa.dot.gov/publications/research/infrastructure/structures/04042/02.cfm . Historical FHWA guidance explains geometric assumptions behind amplitude-drop sizing. It concerns a different application and is not used as an oilfield acceptance standard. Course examples are original mathematical demonstrations.

**S60-06 Credential boundary:** https://www.asnt.org/me/26/0/advisory-on-snt-tc-1a-certification-practices-and-use-of-asnt-credentials . Supports separating training-provider completion from employer certification. No ASNT logo or external credential conferred.

lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Phased-Array Crack Height Sizing

VUC061 · Original instruction · 2026-11-18

lessons.title: Audience, scope and learning contract
lessons.body:
## Audience, scope and learning contract

This advanced course develops phased-array measurement of opposite-surface-connected planar feature height in cool carbon-steel weld training specimens. It is distinct from broad phased-array detection training and conventional single-probe sizing. Learners must already demonstrate conventional UT fundamentals, phased-array setup and safe equipment use. A coursebook is not an employer qualification or an API credential. The catalog's QUSEPA name is treated as legacy scope; current external program availability and examination requirements are not inferred from an old candidate guide. [S61-01]

By completion, the learner must independently establish a valid array setup, verify the relevant laws, distinguish actual tip evidence from misleading images, scan the whole assigned feature, calculate and report its maximum supported height, recover from invalid measurements and defend an honest limitation. Written knowledge and observed practical performance are separate requirements. This package specifies training equipment and specimen evidence; it does not claim that hardware has been supplied or a learner has performed the tasks.

lessons.title: Q01 — Height is a defined physical quantity
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Height is a defined physical quantity

Start with a cross-section showing the scanning surface, opposite surface, local wall thickness and crack connection. For a flat far-surface-connected feature, height equals local thickness minus normal depth to its established tip. Remaining near-surface ligament equals that tip depth. Length along the weld is a third dimension. A display cursor labeled depth must not be copied into a height field without determining its reference.

State the coordinate convention before scanning. If the feature is embedded or connected to the scanning surface, the far-surface equation is inapplicable. Establish both boundaries or use the appropriate approved method. No software label can establish a feature's surface connection.

**Worked:** local thickness 22 mm, verified tip depth 15 mm: height 7 mm, ligament 15 mm. **Changed:** connection is unknown. The arithmetic remains 7 but is not a supported height. Draw the alternatives, investigate the connection and report unresolved sizing until evidence supports one. P01 requires this distinction in a sketch and report.

lessons.title: Q02 — Safe readiness and technical authority
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Safe readiness and technical authority

Confirm the material, geometry, thickness range and feature class covered by the sizing technique. A generic PAUT detection procedure cannot automatically support crack-height measurement. The responsible UT authority approves the actual technique and references; the instructor assesses performance against it. Production acceptance and engineering remaining-life decisions remain outside this training award.

Use stable, cool, depressurized bench specimens. Inspect sharp edges, cable insulation, connectors, couplant compatibility and spill controls. Secure heavy samples before positioning the probe. Stop if the physical arrangement becomes unsafe. Do not use this course to justify hot work, process access or energized electrical repair.

**Worked:** technically suitable setup, unstable sample. Secure the sample before scanning; a valid procedure does not cure a handling hazard. **Changed:** stable sample but alloy outside the technique. Obtain an applicable validated technique rather than borrowing the steel velocity. P02 records both technical and physical readiness.

lessons.title: Q03 — Array identity, active aperture and element condition
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Array identity, active aperture and element condition

Record instrument/software, array serial number, element count/pitch, wedge, cable and active aperture. The programmed probe definition must match the connected hardware. Verify element performance using the approved manufacturer method; document failed or weak channels and apply the actual procedure's disposition. An attractive image does not prove every required element is functioning.

Do not silently reduce the aperture to hide a defective channel. That changes the beam and may invalidate focusing, calibration and demonstrated sizing performance. Save the original finding, obtain an authorized configuration and repeat applicable checks. A spare probe requires its own identity and validation.

**Worked:** a 16-element aperture includes one nonresponsive channel. Record the condition and hold use pending the specified disposition; do not declare a universal allowable percentage. **Changed:** replacement array passes its checks. Reestablish the relevant setup and reference evidence. P03 is an actual equipment task, not a screenshot quiz.

lessons.title: Q04 — Focal laws, focus and demonstrated range
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Focal laws, focus and demonstrated range

Focal laws control element timing and the intended beam directions/focus. Document aperture, angle range, increment and focus definition. A focus entered as sound path is not the same as normal depth. Establish the actual instrument convention and validate the resulting response on suitable references throughout the required region. A beam drawing is a planning aid, not proof that a small tip is resolvable.

Increasing the number of angles can affect acquisition performance. More laws do not repair inadequate access, incorrect material velocity or unsupported focus. Use a demonstrated set rather than adding laws until the image looks convincing. Any substantive change requires the procedure's applicable verification.

**Worked:** 40° through 70° inclusive at 1° increments gives 31 laws; at 0.5° it gives 61. **Changed:** the second setup has the same nominal sector but slower refresh. Recheck scanning performance and required coverage rather than assuming equivalence. P04 documents configuration, focus convention and actual reference demonstration.

lessons.title: Q05 — Wedge delay and depth accuracy
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Wedge delay and depth accuracy

The displayed depth depends on a valid time origin, mode velocity and geometry. Wedge delay is not material travel. Verify the required laws over the intended depth range; a correct middle-angle response does not prove edge-angle accuracy. Manufacturer guidance emphasizes calibration across the sequence. [S61-02]

Use known references with documented truth. Record measured versus reference positions and the configuration used. If a point fails the announced band, resolve the cause and repeat the affected checks. Do not offset the report by a guessed constant while leaving the setup wrong.

**Worked:** known 8 and 18 mm depths read 8.2 and 18.7: errors +0.2 and +0.7 mm. Against this course's fictional ±0.5 mm check band, the second fails. **Changed:** only a central law is corrected. Edge laws remain unsupported until verified. P05 requires actual readings and retained failed evidence.

lessons.title: Q06 — Sensitivity normalization and TCG are not geometry calibration
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Sensitivity normalization and TCG are not geometry calibration

Sensitivity normalization addresses differences in response among laws; TCG addresses amplitude response versus path under the selected method. These are different from establishing accurate coordinates. A normalized image may still have incorrect depth, and a geometrically correct setup may have inadequate tip visibility. Treat the checks separately and preserve both records. [S61-02]

Use only the specified reference reflectors and applicable gain method. Ensure signals are not clipped and the noise level remains usable. Increasing gain indiscriminately can display noise as apparent structure. Changing evaluation sensitivity requires the technique's controls; it does not authorize selecting whatever setting produces the smallest crack.

**Worked:** comparable reference response rises from 20% to 40%, an amplitude factor of 2 or 6.0206 dB. This does not show a doubled flaw size. **Changed:** the new response clips at full scale. Restore a valid measurement range before comparison. P06 records actual normalization and the separate depth check.

lessons.title: Q07 — Ray path, depth and coordinate validity
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Ray path, depth and coordinate validity

For a flat first-leg path S at angle θ from normal, depth d=S cosθ and lateral offset x=S sinθ. These formulas require the assumed mode, leg and geometry. A reflected ray or curved part needs the applicable treatment. When measuring a far-surface-connected feature, use local thickness at the actual position, not an unrelated nominal dimension.

Explain every cursor coordinate in the report. A sloping distance in an image is not necessarily vertical height. If the display switches between sound path and true depth, confirm the saved data and report headings remain coherent.

**Worked:** S=24 mm at 60° gives d=12 mm and x=20.7846 mm. In local 22 mm thickness, supported height is 10 mm. **Changed:** at 50° the same path gives d=15.4269 mm and height 6.5731 mm. Verify the real angle; do not choose the value yielding a preferred result.

lessons.title: Q08 — Read A-scan evidence behind the image
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Read A-scan evidence behind the image

An S-scan or reconstructed view organizes acquired responses; its pixels are not a photograph of the physical crack. Select the relevant law and examine its waveform, gate, range and coordinate basis. Keep the raw response and setup linked to any annotated image. Manufacturer descriptions distinguish manual views from encoded position-linked imaging. [S61-03]

Color palettes, interpolation, persistence and display saturation can change apparent boundaries. Use the approved sizing evidence rather than a color transition chosen by eye. A cursor with two decimal places does not establish physical accuracy to two decimals.

**Worked:** an operator measures a 6 mm colored streak without identifying its waveform or law. That is an image measurement, not yet a supported crack height. **Changed:** the streak changes with palette while the waveform timing stays fixed. Preserve the actual response basis and investigate; do not average the two visual sizes. P08 requires an annotated image linked to its A-scan and configuration.

lessons.title: Q09 — Tip, corner and branch identification
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Tip, corner and branch identification

Opposite-surface features can produce a strong base/corner response and a weaker tip response. Weakness alone is not proof of a tip. Corroborate the candidate through approved probe movements, laws and geometric consistency. Complex branching can introduce additional echoes or hide deeper boundaries. The manufacturer application study illustrates these difficulties, not a universal sizing guarantee. [S61-04]

Do not automatically use the brightest response as the tip or pick the deepest pixel. Identify the physical meaning of each candidate and record why it is accepted or rejected. When a unique boundary cannot be supported, report the limitation and obtain an appropriate validated approach.

**Worked:** a weak candidate appears at one law but fails to track consistently with approved movement. Tip identity remains unresolved. **Changed:** repeated permitted observations establish its location. Calculate from that evidence and preserve the resolution history. P09 uses real known teaching features before blind specimens.

lessons.title: Q10 — Beam width and amplitude boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Beam width and amplitude boundaries

An amplitude-defined edge depends on the technique, beam response, orientation and reference. It is not automatically the physical crack boundary. Treat any amplitude-drop method as a procedure-dependent measurement requiring validation on suitable specimens. It cannot be substituted for a tip method merely because the tip is hard to see.

Record peak validity, threshold, evaluation settings and geometric assumptions. If the peak is clipped, the fraction of peak is not known. Coupling changes can move apparent endpoints without any change in the crack. Repeat under valid conditions and explain the limitation instead of writing a precise but unsupported result.

**Worked:** 72% and 36% valid comparable responses have ratio 0.5, or −6.0206 dB. **Changed:** the peak is actually above display range. The visible ratio no longer establishes the intended drop. P10 compares known-feature response behavior; no physical height is awarded from the ratio alone.

lessons.title: Q11 — Access, crown and local thickness
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Access, crown and local thickness

Plan probe positions that can interrogate the required feature along its full extent. A retained weld crown may restrict position or contact. Use the validated technique and actual accessible surfaces; do not imply that nominal beam coverage overcame a physical access barrier. Record the local profile and thickness basis used for each calculation.

Do not modify a specimen or production surface without authorization. If an approved alternate access direction is available, demonstrate its validity rather than treating it as interchangeable by name. An unresolved region stays unresolved until actually examined under a valid method.

**Worked:** nominal thickness 24 mm, actual local 23 mm, valid tip depth 16 mm: height 7 mm rather than nominal 8 mm. **Changed:** crown blocks one required probe position. State the missing scope and obtain a demonstrated alternative or leave the result incomplete. P11 includes flush and retained-crown training conditions.

lessons.title: Q12 — Scan acquisition and coverage
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Scan acquisition and coverage

Maintain contact, required movement and complete assigned length. For encoded acquisition, verify position direction/scale and the procedure's acquisition settings. Missing data are not sound material. For manual acquisition, retain the required position map and response evidence; a stationary screen capture cannot prove the entire feature was scanned.

Estimate acquisition spacing using actual effective full-sequence rate, not a headline pulser specification. The simple spacing model is speed divided by completed frames per second; confirm performance using the actual instrument and method. Data dropout, lift-off or excess speed requires scope assessment and valid repeat scanning.

**Worked:** 60 mm/s at 120 complete frames/s gives 0.5 mm between frames. **Changed:** actual full-sequence rate is 60/s, giving 1 mm. Whether either meets the method depends on its predeclared requirement. P12 records measured acquisition performance and actual coverage, not merely theoretical arithmetic.

lessons.title: Q13 — Track maximum supported height
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Track maximum supported height

Crack height may vary along the weld. Calculate local height from valid local thickness and established tip depth at each required position. The greatest supported height is not the average. Preserve position labels so the maximum can be relocated and reviewed.

If an interval is missing or a tip is ambiguous, distinguish maximum among measured points from maximum of the whole feature. A good measurement elsewhere does not resolve the gap. Complete required coverage and retain both original and repeat records.

**Worked:** supported heights 5.4, 6.1 and 5.8 mm yield maximum 6.1 mm. **Changed:** one unexamined interval remains. Report 6.1 only as the largest measured value, not the final whole-feature maximum. P13 requires a complete position/height table and an explanation of the controlling observation.

lessons.title: Q14 — Multiple responses and limits of transfer
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Multiple responses and limits of transfer

Separate genuine feature tips from mode-converted, geometric or secondary responses using the approved evidence. Two plausible tips do not justify selecting the smaller height. Conversely, the highest apparent response is not necessarily the actual crack boundary. Preserve the interpretation trail, including rejected candidates.

A method validated on simple opposite-surface weld features does not automatically qualify corrosion cracking networks, different alloys, curved parts, TFM, PCI or TOFD. These require their own applicability and performance basis. An instrument's ability to display a mode is not permission or evidence of competence in it.

**Worked:** in 24 mm local thickness, established tip depths 17 and 14 mm correspond to 7 and 10 mm heights; greatest supported height is 10 mm. **Changed:** the 14 mm response is proven geometric. Revise the interpretation traceably and verify the remaining feature and coverage before reporting 7 mm.

lessons.title: Q15 — Repeatability, bias and uncertainty
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Repeatability, bias and uncertainty

Repeatability asks whether repeated readings agree; accuracy requires comparison with independent truth. Shared setup error can make every reading consistently wrong. Compute signed errors and inspect their pattern before summarizing. An average near zero can hide large over- and undersizing.

Apply the declared uncertainty/decision rule to the actual reference and measurement. Do not invent an allowance after seeing a failure. Where the evidence cannot support a pass, preserve the uncertainty and remediate the method or specimen basis. Truth uncertainty must be suitable for the precision being assessed.

**Worked:** errors +0.6, −0.6, +0.6, −0.6 mm have zero mean and RMS 0.6 mm. **Changed:** four +0.4 mm errors have mean +0.4 and RMS 0.4, indicating consistent positive bias. Neither summary alone proves every required individual result is acceptable. P15 retains all repeated readings, not a favorable subset.

lessons.title: Q16 — Drift and configuration change recovery
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Drift and configuration change recovery

Perform the procedure's checks at required intervals and after relevant changes. A failed verification identifies a potentially affected period. Determine which specimens and laws depended on the invalid condition, preserve the records, correct the cause and perform the required repeat work. A later passing check does not retroactively validate earlier sizing.

Changes to wedge, array, focal law, velocity, focus or processing can affect different parts of the evidence. Use an explicit dependency record. Never overwrite the old setup or measurements to make a failed sequence disappear.

**Worked:** four specimens were measured after the last valid check before failure. All four require affected-scope assessment. **Changed:** two are repeated validly. The other two remain unresolved absent a supported authorized disposition. P16 includes an instructor-controlled safe verification fault and actual recovery evidence.

lessons.title: Q17 — Unit conversion and report precision
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Unit conversion and report precision

Use a consistent report quantity and units across instrument, worksheet and submission. One inch is exactly 25.4 mm. Keep intermediate precision and round only as the report rule permits. A value can look plausible while being wrong by a unit factor or by confusing height with ligament.

Have the learner independently check a conversion and the coordinate label. Do not use rounding to turn an exceeded tolerance into a pass. The report must identify what was actually measured, not merely include a number in a column.

**Worked:** 0.28 in equals 7.112 mm. **Changed:** 0.24 in equals 6.096 mm, a 1.016 mm difference. A 7.112 value under an inches heading requires a traceable correction, not a cosmetic dismissal. P17 requires paired-unit reporting and explanation of the physical quantity.

lessons.title: Q18 — Independent demonstration and defensible handover
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Independent demonstration and defensible handover

Blind assessment uses unfamiliar specimens with protected, independently supported truth. The learner must establish the setup, verify, scan, interpret and report without coaching. Familiar practice results do not demonstrate independent competence. Keep failed attempts and require a changed set after remediation.

Report component identity, actual technique/configuration, verification, coverage, maximum supported height, reference convention and limitations. Engineering disposition is separate. Preserve raw records and revisions under the training record policy; old external exam memory-erasure instructions are not a reason to destroy VNDRLY learner evidence.

**Worked:** nine valid measurements and one copied value do not constitute a 90% practical pass; fabrication is critical. **Changed:** the tenth is honestly unresolved. That is proper disclosure but still leaves required performance incomplete. I61 requires both integrity and actual sizing competence before the training award.


---
