lessons.title: VUC061 instructor, application and credential guide
lessons.body: # VUC061 instructor, application and credential guide

lessons.title: Delivery and prerequisites
lessons.body:
## Delivery and prerequisites

Plan 56 hours: 14 instruction/formative work, 9 application labs, 19 supervised stations, 10 integrated practice/assessment and 4 written final/review. Breaks and additional remediation are extra. This is a VNDRLY delivery plan, not API or employer-prescribed training hours. Instructor must have documented competence in the actual PAUT sizing technique, equipment and assessment. A responsible UT technical authority approves the specimen/technique and reference-truth basis.

Diagnostic before entry: distinguish height from ligament; calculate sound path and first-leg depth; identify aperture/focus settings; demonstrate safe array connection, reference calibration and raw-data retrieval. Missing fundamentals require prerequisite instruction before advanced scored work. Allow accessible benches, enlarged screens, breaks and equivalent response formats without removing actual sizing requirements. Demonstrate one known sample with reasoning, then change the sample and geometry for practice.

Equipment: suitable PAUT instrument/software, compatible identified array/wedge/cables, safe couplant and SDS, manufacturer instructions, identified calibration references, stable cool carbon-steel weld specimens, removable marking tape, dimension tools and a scanner/encoder where the chosen acquisition method uses one. Do not introduce live pressure, heat, energized plant or hazardous access. Inspect cables and handling arrangements, secure samples, and control sharp edges and spills. Practical records must describe actual equipment observations, not fictional passing values.

lessons.title: S61 specimen design and technique controls
lessons.body:
## S61 specimen design and technique controls

Teaching samples must permit demonstration of known base/tip responses, differing heights, retained-crown and flush conditions, local-thickness effects, and an ambiguous geometry response. Supply a separate non-scored difficult example to teach honest limitations. Blind set A and changed set B each require ten resolvable opposite-surface-connected planar features across at least two thickness groups, with both crown conditions. They must be unfamiliar to the learner and technically comparable in difficulty; no protected external exam specimens or remembered answers may be used.

The authority establishes each reference height using suitable independent characterization or certified records, documents uncertainty and confirms the selected PAUT technique can resolve it. Do not treat an unsupported machining label as exact truth. If the reference basis or resolvability is inadequate, repair the assessment set before scoring; do not make up a truth value. Record specimen aliases and keep the truth record separate from learner materials. This design specifies what delivery requires; it does not claim specimens have already been obtained.

Complete the actual technique sheet: material/thickness/geometry scope; system and software; array/wedge/cable; active aperture and element disposition; angle range/increment; focus convention; mode/velocity; references; wedge-delay, sensitivity and position checks; acquisition pattern/rate; tip corroboration; height definition/calculation; verification intervals; reporting and recovery. Manufacturer-specific button operations must match the actual equipment manual. A saved configuration assists setup but does not replace independent demonstration.

Fictional VNDRLY S61 criteria, announced before assessment: each required reference depth within ±0.5 mm; each of ten blind height results within ±1.0 mm of validated truth using the prior decision rule; complete assigned coverage and valid setup/verification evidence. These are original training criteria, not API exam rules or production acceptance limits. The authority must document suitably smaller reference uncertainty and a conservative decision rule before use. No retroactive tolerance changes or rounding into compliance.

lessons.title: W01 — Define the task and stop unsafe work
lessons.body:
## W01 — Define the task and stop unsafe work

Input: local 22 mm plate, established far-surface tip depth 15 mm, unstable bench sample. Draw the quantities and readiness sequence. Worked: height 7 mm and ligament 15 mm, but physical work stops until the sample is secured. Changed: sample secured, feature connection unknown. The equation cannot establish connection; investigate and report unresolved height until supported. Submit sketch, actual readiness form and authority boundary. Instructor checks that the learner does not mistake successful arithmetic for permission to work.

lessons.title: W02 — Array and focal-law setup
lessons.body:
## W02 — Array and focal-law setup

Input: required 16-element aperture includes a failed channel; planned sector 40°–70° inclusive at 1°. Worked: 31 laws, but failed-channel disposition must follow the actual procedure before use. No universal allowed-failure percentage is supplied. Changed: replacement array and 0.5° increment give 61 laws. Recheck relevant calibration and acquisition performance. Learner physically inventories the system, verifies elements and records focus convention and range performance. A copied setup file alone earns no actual-performance credit.

lessons.title: W03 — Separate depth accuracy and amplitude normalization
lessons.body:
## W03 — Separate depth accuracy and amplitude normalization

Input: known depths 8/18 mm read 8.2/18.7; comparable response 20% becomes 40%. Worked: errors +0.2/+0.7 mm, second exceeds fictional ±0.5; amplitude factor 2 equals 6.0206 dB but says nothing about depth validity. Changed: center law corrected, edge laws unchecked, signal clips. Resolve all required law checks and restore valid amplitude range. Submit separate actual depth and sensitivity records; instructor must not accept a brighter image as geometry proof.

lessons.title: W04 — Geometry and image interpretation
lessons.body:
## W04 — Geometry and image interpretation

Input: first-leg S=24 mm at 60°, local wall 22 mm; operator instead measures a colored streak. Worked: normal depth 12 mm, offset 20.7846 mm, supported height 10 mm only with valid tip identity. The streak alone is insufficient. Changed: 50° yields depth 15.4269 and height 6.5731 mm. Confirm actual angle and waveform, not preferred appearance. Submit labeled ray sketch and an actual A-scan-linked image showing configuration/cursor meaning.

lessons.title: W05 — Tip and response-boundary discrimination
lessons.body:
## W05 — Tip and response-boundary discrimination

Input: weak candidate fails geometric tracking; amplitude comparison 72%/36%. Worked: tip unresolved; ratio 0.5 or −6.0206 dB does not establish a physical crack edge. Changed: corroborated tip appears but original peak is clipped. Preserve tip evidence separately from invalid amplitude measurement; repeat any required amplitude work correctly. Learner performs actual permitted movements on known samples and explains accepted/rejected responses without declaring every weak echo a tip.

lessons.title: W06 — Access, scan rate and maximum
lessons.body:
## W06 — Access, scan rate and maximum

Input: nominal 24 mm, local 23 mm, tip depth 16 mm; speed 60 mm/s, full-sequence rate 120/s; local heights 5.4/6.1/5.8. Worked: height 7 mm, nominal would give 8; acquisition spacing 0.5 mm; largest recorded height 6.1. Changed: rate 60/s gives 1 mm spacing, crown blocks an interval. Apply actual method criteria and rescan unresolved scope. Do not claim whole-feature maximum from partial coverage. Submit actual access/coverage map and acquisition verification.

lessons.title: W07 — Multiple candidates and statistical honesty
lessons.body:
## W07 — Multiple candidates and statistical honesty

Input: local thickness 24 mm, established tip depths 17/14; errors +0.6/−0.6/+0.6/−0.6. Worked: heights 7/10 mm, maximum 10 when both identities valid; mean error 0, RMS 0.6 mm. Changed: 14 mm echo proven geometric; separate readings all +0.4 yield mean/RMS +0.4/0.4. Revise interpretation traceably and recognize bias. Actual repeats must all be retained; no cherry-picking or automatic transfer to complex SCC/TFM methods.

lessons.title: W08 — Recovery and report units
lessons.body:
## W08 — Recovery and report units

Input: four specimens between valid and failed verification; 0.28 in reported height. Worked: assess all four, conversion 7.112 mm. Changed: only two validly repeated; remaining two unresolved absent supported disposition; 0.24 in equals 6.096 mm, difference 1.016 mm. Preserve original failure/configuration and correct unit headings traceably. Learner performs actual controlled recovery, not just an arithmetic answer.

lessons.title: W09 — Blind demonstration and handover
lessons.body:
## W09 — Blind demonstration and handover

Input: ten required specimens, ninth valid and tenth copied without scanning. Worked: critical integrity failure, not a percentage pass. Changed: tenth honestly unresolved. Honest reporting is required but does not complete the sizing requirement; remediate and assess a changed validated set. Assemble a report linking actual setup, references, scanned positions, maximum height, limitations and revisions. Instructor distinguishes technical measurement from engineering acceptance and records actual learner performance only.

lessons.title: Stations and scoring
lessons.body:
## Stations and scoring

Each station uses five 0–2 dimensions: correct identity/basis; valid method/setup; interpretation/calculation; safe authority-bound action; traceable evidence. Pass 8/10, no zero, no unresolved critical error. Critical errors include unsafe handling, fabricated observations, concealed failed checks, unexamined scope represented as examined, and unauthorized production release. Stop unsafe actions immediately; teach the cause and reobserve a changed task. Numerical answers tolerate 0.01 of the stated unit; physical results use S61 criteria and the prior decision rule without rounding into a pass.

| Station | Evidence required | Changed assessment |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Height/depth/ligament sketch | Unknown surface connection |
| P02 **actual** | Safe bench and applicable technique | Unstable sample or changed material |
| P03 **actual** | Array identity and element check | Failed channel/replacement array |
| P04 **actual** | Focal laws/focus and reference demonstration | Changed increment/focus |
| P05 **actual** | Depth checks across required laws | Edge-law failure |
| P06 **actual** | Sensitivity and separate depth records | Clipped response |
| P07 | Correct ray/coordinate calculation | Different angle/leg |
| P08 **actual** | Image linked to waveform/configuration | Palette changes apparent extent |
| P09 **actual** | Corroborated tip evidence | Geometric candidate |
| P10 **actual** | Known-feature amplitude limitation | Clipped peak |
| P11 **actual** | Access/local-thickness basis | Retained crown limits access |
| P12 **actual** | Actual scan/position/acquisition coverage | Lift-off or missed interval |
| P13 **actual** | Full-feature maximum-height record | Local high point and gap |
| P14 **actual** | Multiple-response interpretation | Geometric echo excluded traceably |
| P15 **actual** | Repeats against independent truth | Consistent bias |
| P16 **actual** | Verification failure and recovery | Partial repeat work |
| P17 | Correct dual-unit report | Wrong unit heading |
| P18 **actual** | Independent unseen practice/report | Fresh feature identities |

lessons.title: I61 — Independent sizing practical
lessons.body:
## I61 — Independent sizing practical

Five-hour original practical inside the integrated block; breaks and setup planning separately scheduled. Use blind set A; changed reassessment uses B. Learner independently inventories equipment, establishes applicable configuration, verifies relevant laws, scans all ten required features and reports maximum supported height. Instructor observes actual operations without revealing truth or coaching cursor/probe positions. An annotated screenshot alone cannot replace setup and coverage evidence.

Pass requires every designated height within S61's fictional ±1.0 mm band under the declared decision rule, all required reference checks valid, complete assigned coverage, correct quantity/units and no critical issue. Do not exclude a missing result from the denominator. The difficult non-scored teaching example remains separate from the ten resolvable blind specimens; assess honest limitation there without using an impossible item as an undisclosed trap.

Private truth form: set/version___ alias___ material/geometry/thickness___ independent truth method/value/uncertainty___ validated technique___ actual learner value___ signed error___ decision rule/result___ coverage/check links___ assessor/date___ . Keep truth and final keys outside learner distribution. Directory separation alone does not establish application access permissions.

lessons.title: Controlled final and remediation
lessons.body:
## Controlled final and remediation

18 cases, three decisions each, 2 points each: 108 points. Three-hour written final inside the four-hour final/review block. Pass 87/108 and at least 4/6 in every domain, with no unresolved critical error. Calculator/coursebook permitted; keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Each decision: 2 correct with supported reasoning; 1 safe but incomplete; 0 wrong/missing/unsafe. Changed Form B tests changed facts and decisions. Written success cannot offset missing actual performance.

Require 18 chapters/36 explained formative checks, nine labs, all 18 stations including 15 actual, I61 and final. For failure, identify setup, interpretation, arithmetic, coverage or integrity cause; teach it, obtain corrected reasoning and observe a changed task. After two unsuccessful changed attempts, use individualized instruction and a fresh equivalent supervised assessment. Preserve attempts. Another competent assessor may review an appeal. No learner completion is issued while equipment, validated truth or required practical evidence is missing.

lessons.title: Credential and records
lessons.body:
## Credential and records

Award “VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Phased-Array Crack Height Sizing: training assessment completion.” Record identity/prerequisites, actual hours, material version/hash, technique/equipment, specimen-set version, original/changed results, remediation, assessor and demonstrated scope. It does not confer API/ASNT credentials, employer certification, engineering acceptance or authorization for other imaging methods. Internal review at 24 months or earlier after significant method changes or competence gaps; this is VNDRLY policy, not an external validity period.

**Readiness/setup:** learner/date___ technique/revision___ specimen/material/geometry___ safe arrangement___ instrument/software/array/wedge/cable___ element disposition___ aperture/laws/focus/mode/velocity___ references___ depth/sensitivity checks___ scan plan___ recovery intervals___

**Sizing evidence:** alias/position___ local thickness/basis___ law/waveform/tip corroboration___ cursor reference___ depth/height/units___ coverage___ largest supported value___ limitations___ saved record___

**Recovery/revision:** last valid___ failed check/change___ affected specimens/laws___ corrective action___ actual repeats___ old record retained___ revised report/recipient___

**Assessment:** attempt/version___ actual observed evidence___ domain scores___ critical issue___ remediation___ changed task/set___ result___ assessor/date___ appeal___ award or pending reason___

lessons.title: VUC061 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC061 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

Is a depth cursor automatically crack height?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Define its surface reference and feature connection. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

Does subtraction prove the feature connects to the far surface?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Geometry and identity require evidence. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Can a PAUT detection procedure automatically support height sizing?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Technique must be suitable and validated for sizing. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

May a good calibration excuse an unsecured sample?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Physical safety is independently required. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Does a clean image prove all required channels work?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Actual element checks are required. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

May the learner silently change aperture to hide a failed channel?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** That changes beam/configuration validity. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Are focus depth and sound-path focus interchangeable?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Confirm actual definition. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

Do more angles alone prove better sizing?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Validate coverage/resolution and acquisition. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

Does one central law prove edge-law depth accuracy?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Check required law range. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

May a report offset replace a corrected setup?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Resolve setup and preserve evidence. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Does sensitivity normalization establish correct depth?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Coordinate and amplitude checks differ. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Does gain doubling mean flaw height doubles?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Response amplitude is not physical size. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Is θ from the normal in the given first-leg formula?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Use stated convention. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Can a reflected path silently use the same flat first-leg equation?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Actual leg/geometry required. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

Is an S-scan a photograph of a crack?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It displays acquired responses through a model. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

Does extra cursor precision prove physical accuracy?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Validity and resolution must be demonstrated. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Is every weak response a tip?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Corroborate identity and geometry. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

Must the brightest response define tip height?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It may be base/corner geometry. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Can an amplitude boundary automatically replace a physical tip?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Technique-specific validation needed. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

Can a clipped peak support a valid fraction-of-peak comparison?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** True peak is unknown. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Can crown access limits be erased by a beam sketch?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Actual access and performance govern. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

May a crown be removed without authorization?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Preparation scope must be approved. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Does missing acquired data mean sound material?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Missing coverage remains unknown. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Is advertised pulser rate necessarily full-sequence frame rate?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify effective acquisition. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Is whole-feature maximum the average of measured heights?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Largest valid value with complete required coverage. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

Does a valid local maximum cover an unscanned interval?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Whole-feature claim remains unsupported. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Should the smaller of two plausible heights be preferred?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence determines supported extent. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

Does PAUT training authorize TFM/PCI/TOFD automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Each needs its own applicability and competence basis. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Does repeatability guarantee accuracy?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Shared bias may persist. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

May uncertainty be invented after failure to obtain a pass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use prior decision rule. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Does a later passing check validate all earlier data?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Affected scope requires disposition. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

May the old configuration be overwritten to hide a failure?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Keep history and recovery evidence. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Is inch-to-mm factor exactly 25.4?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Use consistent quantity and units. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

May rounding turn an exceeded band into a pass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Apply declared decision rule. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:
## Q18-L1

Can familiar specimen answers replace independent performance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Unseen validated set required. Revisit Q18 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L2
lessons.body:
## Q18-L2

Does honest unresolved sizing fulfill the measurement requirement?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Disclosure is correct but performance remains pending. Revisit Q18 and perform its changed application.


---

lessons.title: VUC061 source and coverage register
lessons.body:
# VUC061 source and coverage register

Reviewed 2026-11-18. This is original VNDRLY material on an available-source basis. Full proprietary standards and current external exam equivalence are not claimed. Worked cases and grading thresholds are original teaching designs.

**S61-01 — Legacy scope and current context.** [API QUSE-PA candidate orientation](https://www.api.org/-/media/files/certification/icp/icp-certification-programs/ut%20programs/qusepa/api%20quse-pa%20candidate%20orientation.pdf) identifies phased-array opposite-surface crack-height demonstration, equipment/configuration and reporting context. Its historical text contains incomplete/ambiguous grading language; those values are not adopted. [Current API exam information](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/schedule-exams) lists QUTE (M), QUTE (PA), QUTE-TM and LSP. A legacy directory entry is not proof of current registration availability. The course retains the user's catalog scope without representing itself as a currently approved API course.

**S61-02 — Calibration distinctions.** [Evident calibration and normalization](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/calibration/calibrationnormalization) supports separating law-dependent wedge-delay/sensitivity checks and amplitude compensation. Used for conceptual distinctions only, not an instrument-specific operating procedure or universal acceptance threshold.

**S61-03 — Display and acquisition.** [Evident phased-array specifications](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/calibration/specifationspa) describes manual versus encoded views, waveform information, cursors and acquisition considerations. No product performance promise or automatic cursor accuracy is imported. Actual hardware settings must follow its approved manual/technique.

**S61-04 — Interpretation limits.** [Evident crack imaging application](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/applications/ultrasounds-hidden-stress-corrosion-cracking) illustrates base/tip/branch responses and geometry-dependent difficulties. The specialized SCC examples are not converted into general qualification for SCC, TFM, PCI or TOFD. The course's scope remains validated conventional PAUT sizing of specified training features.

No copied external exam questions, protected specimen values or proprietary standard tables are included. Formula exercises are independently derived under explicitly stated assumptions. The original material goes beyond source summaries to teach safe reasoning, records, recovery and learner demonstration; it does not claim comprehensive verification against inaccessible standards.

| Outcomes | Chapters | Labs | Stations | Controlled final/changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Quantity/readiness | Q01–02 | W01 | P01–02 | Q01–02 F/R |
| Array/law configuration | Q03–04 | W02 | P03–04 | Q03–04 F/R |
| Depth/sensitivity | Q05–06 | W03 | P05–06 | Q05–06 F/R |
| Geometry/image evidence | Q07–08 | W04 | P07–08 | Q07–08 F/R |
| Tip/amplitude limitations | Q09–10 | W05 | P09–10 | Q09–10 F/R |
| Access/acquisition/maximum | Q11–13 | W06 | P11–13 | Q11–13 F/R |
| Complex responses/bias | Q14–15 | W07 | P14–15 | Q14–15 F/R |
| Recovery/units | Q16–17 | W08 | P16–17 | Q16–17 F/R |
| Independent performance/report | Q18 | W09 | P18/I61 | Q18 F/R |

Each chapter has two explained formative checks. The actual practical cannot be replaced by answers or reading. Specimen design, equipment list, technique fields, protected-truth record, grading rules and changed assessment are specified. Actual hardware validation and learner observations remain delivery obligations, not invented evidence in this package.

content.title: VUC062 | VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Detection and Characterization
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Detection and Characterization
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Detection and Characterization

VUC062 · Original materials · 2026-11-18

lessons.title: Course scope and entry requirements
lessons.body:
## Course scope and entry requirements

This course addresses manual conventional ultrasonic detection, characterization and location of discontinuities in carbon-steel plate and pipe weld training specimens. It retains the catalog's legacy QUTE detection emphasis. Current QUTE (M) has separate current documentation and is the next catalog program; this package does not claim an old orientation is today's examination specification. [S62-01, S62-02]

Learners need established UT fundamentals, safe instrument handling, basic weld geometry and calculation ability. The instructor verifies those prerequisites before independent scored work. Training completion is not API certification, employer NDT qualification or production acceptance authority. Learners must actually perform scanning on validated specimens; reading and written answers cannot establish detection competence.

lessons.title: Q01 — Detection is evidence, not an alarm
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Detection is evidence, not an alarm

An indication is a recorded response that requires evaluation. A reportable discontinuity is an interpretation supported by the applicable method and reporting criterion. A defect is an acceptance classification under a specified criterion and authorized process; do not use the words interchangeably. An alarm can be caused by a geometric response or invalid setup, while a significant feature may not produce the largest amplitude.

Start with examination scope, reporting threshold and required evidence. Record enough position, response and configuration information for another competent examiner to understand what was found. Neither “beeped” nor “screen looked clear” establishes a complete examination.

**Worked:** a gated echo appears, but the gate covers a known corner response. Investigate and document geometry rather than automatically reporting a crack. **Changed:** a repeatable response meets the reporting criterion but type is unresolved. Report the supported indication and limitation; do not omit it because a precise type is uncertain. P01 evaluates this decision chain.

lessons.title: Q02 — Procedure and safe bench readiness
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Procedure and safe bench readiness

Confirm material, weld geometry, thickness, access and equipment are within the approved examination technique. Identify reporting versus acceptance rules and who can authorize disposition. The responsible UT authority must establish the actual technique and reference basis; a course title is not an inspection procedure.

Use cool, depressurized, stable training samples. Inspect sharp edges, cables, connectors, couplant compatibility and slip risks. Secure pipe sections against rolling. Stop when handling or electrical condition is unsafe. This course does not authorize process entry, high-temperature examination or live electrical repair.

**Worked:** suitable UT setup but unsecured pipe section. Secure it before positioning the probe. **Changed:** stable part but alloy outside the technique. Resolve applicability instead of assuming carbon-steel settings. P02 requires actual readiness observations and a clear stop/resolve record.

lessons.title: Q03 — Weld geometry and coordinate convention
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Weld geometry and coordinate convention

Identify the weld centerline, start datum, positive direction, examination side and inside/outside surfaces. The crown can be offset from the actual joint centerline; do not use appearance alone as a coordinate system. Draw the weld preparation, root, thickness and known geometric features from supported records and accessible measurements.

Keep the same convention through scan notes and final report. If the part is turned, reestablish orientation before continuing. A correctly detected response reported on the wrong side can lead follow-up examination to the wrong location.

**Worked:** start 35 mm, stop 57 mm from the same datum gives length 22 mm. **Changed:** the stop was measured from the opposite end of a 100 mm segment. Convert it to 43 mm from the first datum before calculating the 8 mm interval. State both original readings and the corrected basis.

lessons.title: Q04 — Probe, wedge and material selection
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Probe, wedge and material selection

Select the approved probe/wedge and mode for the weld volume and likely reflector orientations. A straight beam and an angle beam serve different geometries; one cannot simply replace the other because both produce echoes. Record frequency, size, angle definition, cable and actual equipment identity. Manufacturer teaching explains why weld orientation can require angle-beam examination. [S62-03]

Check wear, contact and wedge condition. Use the actual material velocity and verified refracted angle. A wedge label is a nominal selection aid, not proof of the angle in every material. Replacing hardware requires the applicable new checks.

**Worked:** a planned angle-beam pass is replaced with straight beam solely for convenience. Required directional coverage is not established. **Changed:** an approved alternative is demonstrated on suitable references. Record its scope and validation rather than pretending the original method was used. P04 requires actual inventory and selection reasoning.

lessons.title: Q05 — Time base and distance calibration
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Time base and distance calibration

Calibrate using suitable known references spanning the relevant path range. Separate zero/delay from velocity as required by the instrument and method. Manufacturer guidance describes angle-beam setup using known sound paths; use the actual manual for button operations. [S62-04] A single favorable point cannot establish the entire range.

For simple material-only pulse-echo transit, path S=vt/2. Raw transit containing wedge/electronic delay is not material-only time. Preserve reference identity and actual readings. If verification fails, fix the setup and assess affected work; do not change only the final report.

**Worked:** corrected 20 µs at 3.2 mm/µs gives path 32 mm. **Changed:** raw time 22 µs includes 2 µs delay; uncorrected path 35.2 mm is 3.2 mm high. P05 requires actual calibration and independent range verification, with arithmetic used to explain the result.

lessons.title: Q06 — Index point, angle and first-leg location
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Index point, angle and first-leg location

Establish the beam exit/index point and actual refracted angle using the prescribed reference method. Position is measured from the correct index, not automatically the wedge front edge. For flat first-leg path S and angle θ from normal, depth is S cosθ and surface offset is S sinθ. Label the assumptions on the sketch.

An error in probe position propagates into reported reflector position. Preserve the actual index value and any front-edge-to-index offset used. Do not compensate by moving the drawing to a more plausible weld location.

**Worked:** S=30 mm at 60° gives depth 15 mm and offset 25.9808 mm. **Changed:** the recorded probe reference is displaced 4 mm from the intended index. Correct the coordinate traceably using the actual direction; do not alter depth to hide the position error. P06 requires actual index/angle checks and a plotted response.

lessons.title: Q07 — Reflected legs and full-volume planning
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Reflected legs and full-volume planning

A sound beam reflected from the back surface can interrogate another portion of the weld. Determine the applicable leg before calculating depth. For a flat plate of thickness t and a second-leg path, unfolded normal travel is S cosθ; within the second leg, actual depth is 2 t−S cosθ. This requires correct mode, geometry and leg identification.

Plan scan limits and required directions against the actual weld cross-section. A theoretical ray line is not evidence that the probe could reach each position or that the relevant feature orientations were interrogated.

**Worked:** t=20 mm, θ=60°, S=60 mm gives unfolded normal travel 30 mm and second-leg depth 10 mm. **Changed:** using first-leg depth would place the reflector at 30 mm, outside the plate. Resolve the leg instead of accepting an impossible location. P07 uses a labeled sketch and actual reference verification.

lessons.title: Q08 — Reference sensitivity and reporting levels
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Reference sensitivity and reporting levels

Set and verify reference sensitivity using the required reflector, path and method. Distinguish reference level, scanning sensitivity, evaluation sensitivity and reporting threshold. Record applied corrections explicitly. A large echo at excessive gain is not automatically a large flaw; a weak echo at inadequate sensitivity cannot support a clear examination.

Avoid clipping and preserve usable signal-to-noise conditions. A dB change is a response ratio, not a direct physical size change. Do not lower sensitivity to eliminate difficult indications or raise it until every region appears flawed.

**Worked:** increasing a comparable amplitude from 25% to 50% is a factor of 2, or 6.0206 dB. **Changed:** the peak clips after adjustment. Reestablish a valid range before evaluation. P08 requires actual sensitivity records, including the level used for final evaluation.

lessons.title: Q09 — Scan patterns and directional coverage
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Scan patterns and directional coverage

Use the approved pattern to interrogate the required volume and reflector orientations. Coverage requires deliberate probe movement, controlled indexing and contact. A pass across the surface is not proof that the whole volume has been examined. Manufacturer examples discuss patterns for longitudinal and transverse features; actual procedure requirements govern the learner's work. [S62-05]

Record direction, side, limits and interruptions. Resume from a known overlap after loss of contact rather than guessing where coverage stopped. Do not treat a required second direction as optional because the first direction found nothing.

**Worked:** a training plan specifies 12 mm effective swath and 6 mm index spacing, giving 50% overlap. **Changed:** actual spacing becomes 15 mm, leaving a 3 mm geometric gap in this simplified model. Rescan deficient scope; a clean screen does not establish coverage. P09 observes actual movement and records its limits.

lessons.title: Q10 — Coupling, surfaces and curved parts
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Coupling, surfaces and curved parts

Check contact and stable response throughout the movement. Couplant quantity, roughness and wedge fit affect transmission. Loss of signal can be poor coupling rather than absence of discontinuities. Curvature changes contact and ray geometry; flat-plate calculations cannot automatically represent pipe examination.

Use an appropriate validated wedge/technique for the curvature and access. Record any inaccessible area. Do not claim a favorable isolated reading proves the whole curved surface was adequately coupled. Stop and correct an unsafe or uncontrolled setup.

**Worked:** a flat wedge rocks on a small pipe, with intermittent reference response. The examination basis is unstable. **Changed:** suitable contoured arrangement is supplied. Verify actual performance and coordinate model before examination. P10 requires observed contact checks and a traceable limitation where coverage cannot be established.

lessons.title: Q11 — Geometry versus discontinuity
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Geometry versus discontinuity

Compare a response with known root, crown, mismatch and boundary geometry. Use approved probe movements and plotting to test whether the response fits a geometric explanation. A location near the root does not automatically prove either harmless geometry or a crack. Preserve observations that support or contradict each interpretation.

Do not label every uncertain echo as a flaw to avoid misses; false calls can misdirect repairs. Conversely, do not dismiss a repeatable reportable response as geometry without evidence. Escalate unresolved classification while reporting the supported finding.

**Worked:** echo position agrees with a known boundary and tracks consistently through permitted movements. Record the geometric interpretation and evidence. **Changed:** an additional response persists at a distinct location inconsistent with that boundary. Evaluate it separately rather than hiding it under the original explanation. P11 uses known sound and flawed teaching regions.

lessons.title: Q12 — Planar feature characterization
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Planar feature characterization

Planar features can respond strongly or weakly depending on beam orientation. Evaluate position, directional response, surface connection and relationship to the weld preparation. Distinguish supported characterization from an unsupported label. Lack of sidewall fusion, root-related conditions and cracking may demand different evidence and follow-up.

Do not equate amplitude with severity or assume a low-amplitude feature is harmless. A plausible type assignment needs the technique's evidence. When feature identity remains uncertain, report what is established and seek appropriate corroboration rather than inventing a precise mechanism.

**Worked:** repeated evidence places a planar response on the fusion face. State the supported location and characterization basis. **Changed:** another view suggests a surface-connected feature instead. Resolve the inconsistency and retain both observations; do not average incompatible categories. P12 requires an explanation grounded in actual teaching-specimen responses.

lessons.title: Q13 — Volumetric indications and laminations
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Volumetric indications and laminations

Distributed or irregular responses may support a volumetric interpretation, but waveform appearance alone is not a universal classifier. Compare response behavior, position and applicable method evidence. Straight-beam examination may reveal laminar features that affect sound access to the weld; the region behind a reflector is not automatically examined.

Separate detecting a lamination from proving the weld behind it is clear. Use the approved response to access limitations and report unresolved scope. Do not relabel an inconvenient planar response as porosity merely because that category seems less serious.

**Worked:** a laminar response interrupts the expected backwall and blocks required interrogation. Record the feature and affected coverage. **Changed:** alternate validated access examines the missing volume. Add that actual evidence and revise coverage; do not erase the original limitation. P13 includes a known laminar teaching condition and interpretation discussion.

lessons.title: Q14 — Position, start/stop and length
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Position, start/stop and length

Use the method's endpoint definition and record start and stop from a consistent datum. The measured response length is technique-dependent; do not imply unvalidated physical boundaries. Record the response criterion, gain and probe orientation used. Oversizing can wrongly implicate adjacent sound regions.

Check ordering, units and coordinate direction before calculating length. A reversed datum or mixed inches/millimeters can produce plausible but wrong values. Preserve raw endpoint observations so a reviewer can reconstruct the result.

**Worked:** start 42 mm, stop 71 mm gives 29 mm response length. **Changed:** revised valid stop 68 mm gives 26 mm, a 3 mm reduction. Document why the endpoint changed. P14 requires actual endpoint work under the supplied technique and a relocated indication check.

lessons.title: Q15 — Misses, false calls and denominator discipline
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Misses, false calls and denominator discipline

Independent detection performance needs both known flawed regions and known sound regions. Detection rate uses actual known flaws as denominator; false-call rate uses the defined sound regions. Reporting everything as flawed can inflate apparent detection while failing discrimination. Counting only the flaws the learner found hides misses.

Separate characterization and positioning outcomes from initial detection. State the denominator for each measure. Training scores are not a statistically established probability-of-detection curve or a guarantee on production components.

**Worked:** 9 of 10 known flaws detected gives 90%; two false calls in 20 sound regions gives 10% false-call rate. **Changed:** only eight of the nine detections are characterized correctly: conditional characterization is 8/9=88.8889%, not 80% unless using all ten known flaws and labeling that different measure. P15 requires explicit denominators and error analysis.

lessons.title: Q16 — Verification failure and affected-scope recovery
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Verification failure and affected-scope recovery

Perform checks at required intervals and after relevant changes. A failure makes the dependent examination period suspect; identify affected specimens, configurations and recorded results. Correct the cause and repeat required work under valid conditions. Do not erase the failed check or call all prior results valid merely because the new check passes.

Use evidence to bound the affected interval. If the last valid check is unknown, do not invent a convenient start time. Record authorized disposition, actual repeat work and remaining gaps.

**Worked:** six specimens since the last valid check before failure require affected-scope assessment. **Changed:** two are validly repeated; four remain unresolved absent supported disposition. P16 includes a safe instructor-issued check fault and actual recovery records, not only a written response.

lessons.title: Q17 — Report, review and acceptance boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Report, review and acceptance boundaries

Provide identity, procedure/version, equipment, calibration, scan coverage, indications with coordinates, characterization basis, endpoints and limitations. Differentiate “no reportable indications within examined scope” from “no defects anywhere.” A valid UT report does not automatically establish fitness for service or authorize repair.

Review coherence before handover: every indication belongs to the correct specimen, coordinates use the same datum, limitations are visible and original records remain linked. Correct errors traceably rather than replacing the old report invisibly.

**Worked:** a report says “clear” despite a documented inaccessible quadrant. Rewrite it to state examined scope and unresolved quadrant. **Changed:** authorized engineering disposition addresses that exact limitation. Attach its conditions without pretending the missing UT examination occurred. P17 assesses a complete evidence-based report.

lessons.title: Q18 — Blind demonstration and remediation
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Blind demonstration and remediation

Use unfamiliar, independently validated specimens with protected truth. The learner establishes the setup, examines all assigned scope and submits records without coaching or knowing flaw counts/locations. Familiar practice samples and written tests cannot substitute. Practical failures require diagnosis and changed demonstration, not repeated guessing of the same specimen answers.

Analyze whether the cause was setup, access, direction, interpretation, position or reporting. Teach that cause and preserve unsuccessful attempts. A course completion record describes the actual demonstrated scope and does not transfer to other techniques or external credentials.

**Worked:** learner reports every region as flawed, finding all ten true flaws but producing twenty false calls. Detection alone is not a pass. **Changed:** a changed set is examined with sound discrimination and valid evidence. Score all announced categories independently; do not retroactively lower criteria to compensate for the original failure.


---

lessons.title: VUC062 delivery and application guide
lessons.body: # VUC062 delivery and application guide

lessons.title: Instructor, prerequisites and equipment
lessons.body:
## Instructor, prerequisites and equipment

Plan 56 hours: 14 instruction/checks, 9 application labs, 19 supervised stations, 10 integrated practice/assessment, 4 final/review. Breaks and extra remediation are additional. This is an original VNDRLY plan, not prescribed external certification hours. Instructor must have documented competence in the selected conventional UT techniques and equipment; the responsible UT technical authority validates actual specimen truth, procedures and assessment conditions.

Entry diagnostic: distinguish indication/discontinuity/defect, sketch weld coordinates, explain pulse-echo path, calculate a first-leg location, safely connect the actual equipment and retrieve reference echoes. Teach missing foundations before advanced scored work. Use an enlarged display, accessible bench and equivalent response formats as needed without waiving actual scanning. Demonstrate on known examples, then provide different practice material.

Provide conventional flaw detector, approved straight/angle-beam probes and wedges, identified cables, manufacturer instructions, suitable reference blocks, ruler/plotting tools, removable tape, couplant/SDS, stable cool plate and pipe weld training specimens and protected specimen-truth records. Secure curved specimens against rolling. No hot, pressurized, energized or hazardous-access work is included. Inspect physical condition and control spills/edges. Learners must perform actual calibration and scanning; supplied answer sheets cannot substitute.

lessons.title: S62 teaching and blind specimen design
lessons.body:
## S62 teaching and blind specimen design

Teaching examples include known geometric responses, planar and volumetric indications, a laminar condition and sound regions. Independent set A and changed set B contain plate and pipe geometry, at least two thickness groups, ten validated reportable flaws and twenty known sound grading regions. Include surface-connected and embedded planar conditions and representative volumetric conditions resolvable by the approved technique. Counts and locations are protected from the learner; this is a specimen-design requirement, not a claim that physical specimens already exist.

Authority establishes truth by suitable independent characterization/certified records, documents coordinate/endpoint uncertainty and validates examination access and reportability. Match each intended flaw to one defined grading region and prevent ambiguous scoring from overlapping regions. Validate realistic geometric responses in sound regions. The authority supplies the exact appropriate technique and reporting threshold; no inaccessible standard limits are invented. Replace inadequately validated specimens before grading.

Technique sheet must specify scope/material/geometry; instrument/probe/wedge/cable; mode/velocity; index/angle; reference paths and sensitivity; scan directions/limits/indexing/contact checks; relevant curved-part treatment; indication evaluation/endpoint definition; reporting criteria; verification intervals; recovery and records. Teach hardware operations from the actual manual. Learner independently demonstrates setup rather than relying solely on preloaded settings.

Fictional VNDRLY S62 practical criteria: detect at least 9/10 known reportable flaws, including every predesignated critical planar feature; no more than one false call across twenty sound regions; correctly characterize at least 90% of detected flaws, rounding the required number up; locate every detected flaw within ±5 mm of the validated datum-based reference position; record endpoints within ±5 mm of validated technique-based endpoints for each detected feature; valid setup and complete assigned coverage. Truth uncertainty and a conservative decision rule must be set beforehand. These are original training criteria, not API examination or production acceptance rules. No rounding a failed physical error into compliance.

lessons.title: W01 — Evidence and safe readiness
lessons.body:
## W01 — Evidence and safe readiness

Input: gated response coincides with a known boundary; unsecured pipe sample. Worked: do not equate alarm with defect; stabilize before further scanning and evaluate the response under the technique. Changed: stable sample, separate repeatable response meets reporting threshold but type unresolved. Report supported indication and limitation rather than omit it. Deliver actual readiness record and an evidence/interpretation table. Instructor checks that the learner separates technical uncertainty from safety and acceptance authority.

lessons.title: W02 — Datum and equipment selection
lessons.body:
## W02 — Datum and equipment selection

Input: 100 mm segment, start 35 mm from datum A, stop 57 mm from datum B at opposite end; planned angle pass replaced by straight beam. Worked: stop is 43 mm from A, interval 8 mm; required directional coverage is not established by unapproved substitution. Changed: both readings are from A, giving 22 mm; valid alternative method is demonstrated. Record actual datum and technique evidence. Learner physically inventories probes/wedges and locates the reference direction.

lessons.title: W03 — Time, index and ray geometry
lessons.body:
## W03 — Time, index and ray geometry

Input: raw 22 µs includes 2 µs delay at 3.2 mm/µs; separate first-leg path 30 mm at 60°. Worked: corrected path 32 mm versus raw 35.2; depth 15 mm and offset 25.9808 mm for the separate ray. Changed: probe coordinate is 4 mm displaced from index. Correct position using the known direction; do not adjust depth arbitrarily. Learner actually calibrates paths, index and angle and attaches a labeled plot. Cases are separate, not inconsistent measurements of one feature.

lessons.title: W04 — Leg and sensitivity
lessons.body:
## W04 — Leg and sensitivity

Input: plate 20 mm, path 60 mm at 60°; reference amplitude changes 25% to 50%. Worked: unfolded normal travel 30 mm, second-leg depth 10 mm; factor 2 is 6.0206 dB and not flaw size. Changed: waveform clips after gain change. Restore valid range before evaluation. Show leg sketch and actual sensitivity record. Instructor rejects an impossible 30 mm depth inside a 20 mm plate without an explanatory geometry correction.

lessons.title: W05 — Scan coverage and curved contact
lessons.body:
## W05 — Scan coverage and curved contact

Input: simplified effective swath 12 mm, index 6 mm; flat wedge rocks on small pipe. Worked: 50% geometric overlap in the simplified swath model; unstable coupling prevents a valid pipe examination. Changed: index 15 mm leaves 3 mm gap; contoured validated arrangement supplied. Recheck actual geometry/contact and rescan gaps. Submit observed movement, direction, limits and interrupted-area record. No claim that simple swath arithmetic alone proves volumetric coverage.

lessons.title: W06 — Geometry and planar interpretation
lessons.body:
## W06 — Geometry and planar interpretation

Input: one response matches a known boundary, another lies near fusion face. Worked: evaluate separately using actual position and directional evidence; do not dismiss both as geometry or call both cracks. Changed: a permitted view suggests surface connection inconsistent with initial classification. Resolve and document observations, retaining uncertainty if needed. Learner examines known sound and flawed teaching regions and explains why each interpretation is supported. Instructor records real performance, not a canned expected waveform.

lessons.title: W07 — Volumetric/laminar limits and endpoints
lessons.body:
## W07 — Volumetric/laminar limits and endpoints

Input: laminar response blocks required interrogation; separate feature start 42 mm and stop 71 mm. Worked: report lamination/coverage limitation; response length 29 mm. Changed: validated alternate access resolves missing volume; revised valid stop 68 mm gives 26 mm, 3 mm shorter. Record actual added coverage and endpoint criterion. Do not erase limitation history or assume a detected lamination proves the weld behind it sound.

lessons.title: W08 — Denominators and recovery
lessons.body:
## W08 — Denominators and recovery

Input: 9/10 true flaws detected, two false calls in twenty sound regions, eight of nine detections characterized correctly; six specimens affected by failed verification. Worked: 90% detection, 10% false-call rate, 88.8889% conditional characterization; all six need assessment. Changed: two validly repeated leaves four unresolved absent valid disposition. Explain why a high detection score cannot offset false calls or invalid setup. Submit separate metric denominators and actual recovery records.

lessons.title: W09 — Report and blind decisions
lessons.body:
## W09 — Report and blind decisions

Input: report says “clear” despite inaccessible quadrant; independent learner labels all thirty regions flawed. Worked: qualify examination scope; ten true detections plus twenty false calls fails discrimination. Changed: engineering disposition covers exactly the inaccessible area; a fresh blind assessment has valid evidence. Preserve engineering scope separately from actual UT and score the changed attempt using announced criteria. Final report includes actual identity, setup, coverage, response/location/type evidence, endpoints and limitations.

lessons.title: Station rubric
lessons.body:
## Station rubric

Five dimensions scored 0–2: identity/basis, valid technique, actual interpretation/calculation, safe authority-bound behavior, traceable record. Pass 8/10, no zero, no unresolved critical issue. Critical issues: unsafe handling, invented observations, hidden invalid setup, unscanned volume represented as examined, unauthorized production release. Stop unsafe acts, teach cause and reobserve a changed task. Written arithmetic tolerance 0.01 stated unit/percentage point; physical S62 criteria and predeclared decision rule remain separate.

| Station | Required evidence | Changed task |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Indication/reportability/acceptance decision | Unresolved type at reporting level |
| P02 **actual** | Safe bench/procedure readiness | Rolling pipe or changed material |
| P03 **actual** | Datum and specimen orientation | Opposite-end reading |
| P04 **actual** | Actual probe/wedge inventory/selection | Approved alternative hardware |
| P05 **actual** | Path calibration and verification | Raw-time delay error |
| P06 **actual** | Index/angle and plotted location | Changed index reference |
| P07 | Correct leg/coverage sketch | Impossible first-leg depth |
| P08 **actual** | Reference/evaluation sensitivity | Clipped response |
| P09 **actual** | Complete directional scan | Missed interval/direction |
| P10 **actual** | Stable curved-part contact | Unsuitable wedge fit |
| P11 **actual** | Geometry/indication distinction | Additional distinct response |
| P12 **actual** | Planar characterization evidence | Conflicting surface connection |
| P13 **actual** | Volumetric/laminar evaluation | Shadowed examination volume |
| P14 **actual** | Actual start/stop/length record | Changed endpoint |
| P15 | Correct performance denominators | High detection with false calls |
| P16 **actual** | Failed check/recovery record | Partial valid repeat |
| P17 | Complete scoped report | Narrow engineering disposition |
| P18 **actual** | Unseen practice examination/report | Fresh specimen identities |

lessons.title: I62 — Independent detection practical
lessons.body:
## I62 — Independent detection practical

Five-hour original practical within integrated block; breaks/setup planning separately scheduled. Use set A, changed reassessment B. Learner independently establishes setup, examines all assigned plate/pipe scope and records indications, geometry, type, position and endpoints. Do not reveal the number/location of flawed or sound regions during the attempt. Instructor observes without coaching probe positions or interpretations.

Apply all S62 categories independently. If nine flaws detected, at least nine correctly characterized are required because ceiling(0.9×9)=9; if ten detected, at least nine correctly characterized. All predesignated critical planar flaws must be detected regardless of total. One false call in twenty sound regions is 5%; two fails the one-call limit. Every detected feature must satisfy position/endpoint criteria and records. Complete coverage and valid setup cannot be offset by scores. These thresholds are original training rules, not statistically demonstrated production POD.

Protected truth record: alias/region___ flaw or sound___ independently established type/location/endpoints___ uncertainty___ critical designation___ validated reportability/technique___ actual learner report___ matched detection___ characterization___ position/endpoint errors___ false-call result___ setup/coverage links___ assessor/date___ . Resolve scoring ambiguities before examination, not after seeing answers.

lessons.title: Controlled written assessment and remediation
lessons.body:
## Controlled written assessment and remediation

18 cases ×3 decisions ×2 points =108. Three-hour final inside four-hour final/review block. Pass 87/108 and at least 4/6 each domain, with no critical error. Calculator/coursebook allowed; keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Each decision: 2 correct supported reasoning, 1 safe incomplete, 0 wrong/missing/unsafe. Changed Form B uses changed facts. Keys and blind truth remain outside learner distribution; folder placement alone is not an application-access-control claim.

Require all 18 chapters/36 explained checks, nine labs, 18 stations including 14 actual, I62 and written final. Written success never replaces actual detection. Diagnose failed cause, reteach, obtain corrected reasoning and changed observed performance. After two unsuccessful changed attempts, individualized instruction and fresh equivalent supervised assessment. Keep attempts and permit review by another competent assessor where feasible. Inadequate equipment or validated specimen truth means practical delivery remains pending, not fabricated completion.

lessons.title: Award and record forms
lessons.body:
## Award and record forms

Award “VNDRLY/U Ultrasonic Examination — Detection and Characterization: training assessment completion.” Record learner/prerequisites, actual hours, material version/hash, equipment/technique, specimen-set version, results/denominators, remediation, assessor and demonstrated scope. It does not confer API/ASNT or employer certification, repair authority or fitness-for-service approval. VNDRLY internal review at 24 months or earlier after changed methods/requirements or competence concerns; not an external credential term.

**Readiness:** learner/date___ specimen/geometry/material___ procedure/version___ safe setup___ instrument/probe/wedge/cable___ reference/mode/velocity/index/angle___ actual calibration/sensitivity___ scan plan/datum___

**Examination:** alias/position___ actual direction/coverage___ coupling/limits___ response/evaluation level___ geometry/type evidence___ start/stop/units___ location plot___ saved waveform___ limitation___

**Recovery:** last valid___ failed check/configuration change___ affected IDs___ correction___ actual repeats___ unresolved scope___ old record retained___

**Assessment:** original attempt/evidence___ scores/denominators___ critical issue___ remediation___ changed set/result___ assessor/date___ appeal___ completion or pending reason___


---

lessons.title: VUC062 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC062 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

Does an alarm automatically establish a defect?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Evaluate response, reportability and acceptance separately. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

May an unresolved type justify hiding a reportable indication?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Report supported evidence and uncertainty. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Does course completion authorize production acceptance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Authority and criteria are separate. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

May a pipe sample remain unsecured during scanning?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Prevent rolling and unsafe handling. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Is crown center always the established weld datum?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify actual coordinate basis. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

Must orientation be reestablished after turning a part?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Preserve consistent side/direction. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Can straight beam replace required angle coverage without validation?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Direction and geometry matter. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

Does wedge label prove angle in every material?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify actual material/configuration. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

Can one favorable reference establish the full path range?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Required range needs verification. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Does raw transit always equal material transit?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Delay may be included. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Should wedge front edge be assumed beam index?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Establish actual index/offset. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Is first-leg angle measured from normal here?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Use explicit convention. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Can second-leg normal travel be reported directly as depth?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Account for reflection geometry. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Does theoretical ray coverage prove physical access?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Demonstrate actual required scan. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

Does gain change directly measure flaw size?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Amplitude and physical geometry differ. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

May sensitivity be lowered to erase difficult indications?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Follow approved reference/evaluation rules. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Does a surface pass prove full volume examined?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Required directions/contact/limits matter. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

May a required second direction be omitted after a clean first pass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Different orientation may reveal different features. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Does unstable coupling establish absence of flaws?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Transmission may be inadequate. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

May flat geometry automatically represent a curved pipe?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use applicable validated model/fit. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Is every root-region echo harmless geometry?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence must distinguish responses. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

Does calling every uncertain echo a flaw prove competence?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** False calls also matter. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

Does low amplitude prove harmlessness?

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Can incompatible characterizations be averaged?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Resolve evidence and uncertainty. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Does detecting a lamination prove the weld behind it clear?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It may block required interrogation. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

Is waveform appearance alone a universal type classifier?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use position and method evidence. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Must endpoints share datum and units?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Mixed references invalidate length. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

Is response length automatically physical flaw length?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Depends on validated method/criterion. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Does detection denominator include only found flaws?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use all known reportable flaws. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

Can high detection offset unlimited false calls?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Assess each category independently. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Does later correction validate prior examinations automatically?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Affected scope needs supported disposition. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

May last-valid time be invented if missing?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use evidence and disclose uncertainty. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Does no reportable indication mean no defect anywhere?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Statement is limited by examined scope/method. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

Does UT measurement itself authorize engineering release?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Separate authority/criteria required. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:

Can known practice answers replace blind examination?

lessons.title: VUC062 sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC062 sources and coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original available-source instruction, examples and assessment. No external certification equivalence or complete proprietary-standard conformity claimed.

**S62-01 Legacy detection context:** [API QUTE candidate orientation, July 2015](https://www.api.org/~/media/files/certification/icp/icp-certification-programs/ut%20programs/qute/api%20qute_candidate%20orientation_rev-072015.pdf). Used for historical scope of detection, characterization, positioning and false calls on plate/pipe welds. Old approximate grading percentages, sample dimensions and administration are not asserted as current. S62 thresholds are independently defined VNDRLY training criteria.

**S62-02 Current boundary:** [API QUTE (M)](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/certifications/api-qute-m). Current page identifies hands-on conventional single/dual-element work and four error categories, but one introductory sentence inconsistently calls it phased array. The inconsistency is disclosed rather than used to redefine manual conventional technique. #63 addresses the separately cataloged current manual scope; #62 retains legacy detection emphasis. No claim of API approval is made.

**S62-03 Beam/application concept:** [Evident angle-beam inspection](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/flaw-detection/weld-inspection). Supports choosing beam geometry appropriate to weld/reflector orientation. No manufacturer example is copied into a universal operating procedure or acceptance criterion.

**S62-04 Calibration concept:** [Evident angle-beam setup](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/flaw-detection/straight-beam-delay). Supports suitable known-path references and material-aware calibration. Actual instrument operations and tolerances must come from the approved technique/manual.

**S62-05 Coverage and contact:** [Evident common test practices](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/learn/ndt-tutorials/flaw-detection/common-test-practices). Supports deliberate directional coverage and attention to curved-surface contact/access. No example index distance or wedge contour is treated as a universal rule. Original swath arithmetic is explicitly a simplified teaching model, not proof of volumetric coverage.

| Outcome | Chapters | Labs | Stations | Final/changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Evidence/readiness | Q01–02 | W01 | P01–02 | Q01–02 F/R |
| Geometry/equipment | Q03–04 | W02 | P03–04 | Q03–04 F/R |
| Path/index/angle | Q05–06 | W03 | P05–06 | Q05–06 F/R |
| Legs/sensitivity | Q07–08 | W04 | P07–08 | Q07–08 F/R |
| Coverage/curvature | Q09–10 | W05 | P09–10 | Q09–10 F/R |
| Geometry/planar character | Q11–12 | W06 | P11–12 | Q11–12 F/R |
| Volumetric limits/endpoints | Q13–14 | W07 | P13–14 | Q13–14 F/R |
| Error measures/recovery | Q15–16 | W08 | P15–16 | Q15–16 F/R |
| Reporting/independence | Q17–18 | W09 | P17–18/I62 | Q17–18 F/R |

Every chapter has two explained formative checks. Actual stations and I62 require real equipment and validated unfamiliar specimens. The package supplies the design, controls, forms and rubric; it does not invent learner results or claim physical reference specimens already exist. Proprietary acceptance tables and protected external exam data are not reproduced.
