content.title: VUC066 | VNDRLY/U Long Seam Pipeline Examination
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Long Seam Pipeline Examination
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Long Seam Pipeline Examination

VUC066. Original advanced training and assessment package for long-seam feature detection, characterization, sizing and traceable handover. Its practical pathway uses a declared validated UT/PAUT method with suitable supplementary observations. It does not award API LSP, employer NDT qualification, excavation competence or permission to operate or repair a pipeline. Actual demonstrated methods and limitations appear on the training record.

Prerequisites: established UT fundamentals, ability to configure and verify the selected instrument, dimensional arithmetic and interpretation of section drawings. The instructor diagnoses gaps before advanced work. This course is not a substitute for missing basic method training. Learning outcomes are to establish a defensible seam examination plan, demonstrate setup, distinguish feature evidence from geometry, measure supported dimensions, reconcile field/ILI coordinates and produce an independent report. Complete teaching, checks, labs, observed stations and the separate final assessments.

lessons.title: Q01 — Define what the examination can decide
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Define what the examination can decide

The examiner supplies trustworthy observations and measurements to the operator's integrity process. Detection, characterization and sizing are distinct tasks. A successful indication search does not prove accurate height sizing; a correct height on one feature does not establish coverage of the entire seam. Identify the required volume, methods, reporting rules and decision authority before starting.

Record pipe identity, seam evidence, material and geometry information, accessible area and the actual procedure revision. If the supplied history is uncertain, keep that uncertainty visible. Do not turn a guessed manufacturing process into a fact. An examination finding is not itself an engineering acceptance calculation or repair instruction.

Worked: the assignment requests 600 mm of seam, but only 450 mm is accessible. The examined fraction is 75%, with 150 mm unresolved. Changed: a different method reaches part of the gap but has no demonstrated sensitivity to the required feature. Access alone does not complete the assignment. P01 requires a scope matrix that identifies what each method can and cannot establish.

lessons.title: Q02 — Understand seam manufacture without overdiagnosis
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Understand seam manufacture without overdiagnosis

Electric-resistance joining and filler-metal seam welding produce different local geometry and material histories. Examine the available manufacturing records and the actual seam profile. Distinguish the central joining region, adjacent affected material and surrounding pipe body. Avoid assuming that a visible ridge marks every relevant subsurface feature.

Historical process information helps identify plausible threats but does not prove a particular defect exists. Nor does newer manufacture guarantee absence of relevant features. A technician should describe the observed location, orientation and response, then assign a supported category with stated confidence. Mixed or uncertain evidence remains unresolved pending appropriate investigation.

Worked: records identify ERW, but the exposed surface shows an unexpected deposited weld profile. Verify identity and repair history before using the original seam model. Changed: records cannot resolve the discrepancy. Develop an authorized examination plan for the actual demonstrated geometry and label the history uncertainty. P02 uses original section sketches and record cards, not a claim that visual appearance alone identifies manufacturing process.

lessons.title: Q03 — Establish safe access and preparation boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Establish safe access and preparation boundaries

An in-ditch examination depends on safe access arranged by the operator. This course does not authorize excavation entry, pressure changes, grinding, coating removal or contact with an unsafe line. Confirm the site's access controls, competent-person decisions and permitted surface preparation. If conditions change, stop the affected work and use the designated communication path.

Training uses supported cool nonpressurized coupons. Control sharp edges, lifting, unstable curved pieces, cables, couplant and chemicals. Preserve specimen identification and protected truth. Do not remove material to make an indication easier to interpret; a production removal could change both integrity and evidence.

Worked: a seam region is covered by a coating whose removal is not authorized. Record the restriction and obtain the approved method or preparation instruction. Changed: a supervisor verbally suggests using a grinder without the required controls. The examination assignment does not supply that authority. P03 is a simulated access/preparation decision and safe bench setup, with no hazardous field task performed.

lessons.title: Q04 — Choose a primary method and its supporting evidence
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Choose a primary method and its supporting evidence

Select a method whose performance has been demonstrated for the assigned feature types, orientations, depths and geometry. Define what supplementary methods contribute: surface connection, local profile, thickness or an independent response. Combining methods can improve evidence, but two unsuitable methods do not make a suitable examination.

Use the learner's actual qualified method scope. A person unfamiliar with a technique cannot add it to the certificate by mentioning it in a report. Inventory and verify each used system. If a supplementary method is unavailable, evaluate the lost evidence and state the resulting limitation rather than crediting an observation that was never made.

Worked: UT detects a response, and a surface method is proposed to establish external connection. Until the supplementary examination is validly performed, external connection remains unconfirmed. Changed: the surface method is negative but lacks suitable orientation/sensitivity. That result cannot rule out a connected feature. P04 produces a method-to-output matrix and demonstrates the selected primary setup.

lessons.title: Q05 — Model the curved section correctly
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Model the curved section correctly

Long-seam scanning crosses curved inner and outer surfaces. The geometry changes beam paths and displayed position. Establish actual diameter/radius, local thickness, probe position and surface contour within the technique's supported range. A flat-plate display can misplace a response when applied without suitable correction to curved pipe.

Software correction is only as credible as its inputs and validation. Check the actual probe/wedge and relevant reference targets. Do not treat a visually plausible image as a calibrated section. Preserve the coordinate convention and distinguish sound path, normal depth and circumferential offset.

Worked: a setup file assumes 300 mm outside diameter, while the specimen is 250 mm. Correct the input and perform the applicable checks before interpretation. Changed: the diameter is corrected but the wedge is still the wrong contour. The configuration remains unverified. P05 requires an actual section/setup comparison and demonstrated location of known references on representative curvature.

lessons.title: Q06 — Calibrate the system for detection and sizing
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Calibrate the system for detection and sizing

Identify the instrument, software, probe, wedge, cable and reference blocks. Establish the required range/position and sensitivity checks for the actual method. A strong known reflector does not verify a height-sizing method; include suitable depth/height references and the required response states. Record achieved values, not merely checked boxes.

Use the applicable approved equipment instructions rather than a universal button recipe. If the instrument or technique cannot demonstrate required performance, do not use it for that assigned output. Replacing a probe or changing relevant laws/settings triggers the prescribed revalidation. A stored file does not substitute for independent setup competence.

Worked: known normal depths 3 and 8 mm display 3.0 and 8.7. Under fictional ±0.3 mm reference tolerance, the second fails. Changed: an adjustment gives 3.5 and 8.0. The lower reference now fails; the range is still unverified. P06 requires actual setup and reference evidence for every method used in the integrated practical.

lessons.title: Q07 — Locate the seam and preserve the coordinate convention
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Locate the seam and preserve the coordinate convention

Establish a reproducible axial origin, positive direction, circumferential reference and viewing direction. State whether clock position is viewed upstream or downstream. Verify the seam location with suitable evidence rather than relying on an arbitrary surface mark. Keep the examination coordinates linked to the operator's reference system.

Reversing a coupon or viewing direction can invert positions without changing the feature. Record transformations explicitly. A result cannot be compared to an ILI feature merely because both numbers are near each other. Match identity, origin, units and direction first.

Worked: on a 600 mm segment, a feature extends 120–170 mm from the left reference. Its length is 50 mm; from the opposite end it extends 430–480 mm. Changed: the report preserves 120–170 while labeling the opposite origin. The dimensions are numerically plausible but the location is wrong. P07 requires a physical relocation from the report alone by another observer.

lessons.title: Q08 — Cover the seam volume rather than the predicted target
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Cover the seam volume rather than the predicted target

Plan the required scan directions, offsets, tracks and supplementary views against the actual feature orientations and access. An ILI indication can guide correlation, but it must not cause the examiner to ignore the rest of the assigned region. Record contact loss, obstructed paths and excluded volume.

Validate the plan on representative references/targets. One-sided access may leave important orientations poorly interrogated; do not assume an opposite surface response proves all intervening features would be detected. A coverage map should show actual acquisition and limitations, not just planned tracks.

Worked: an assigned 500 mm length has coupling loss from 210 to 235 mm. The 25 mm interval needs valid recovery under the technique. Changed: it is rescanned at a different offset that does not interrogate the same volume. The original gap remains. P08 demonstrates coverage and recovery, preserving both failed and corrected evidence.

lessons.title: Q09 — Separate geometry from a reportable discontinuity
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Separate geometry from a reportable discontinuity

Offset, residual trim and surface profile can generate responses. Compare the response to actual geometry, movement with probe position and permitted corroborating views. Do not label every strong signal a crack. Equally, a known geometric reflector does not explain away a separate nearby response.

Map evidence before assigning a name. Keep observed signal behavior separate from interpretation. A response that cannot be resolved should be reported with its uncertainty and required follow-up, not deleted to reduce false calls. False calls and missed relevant features are separate error dimensions.

Worked: a response follows a known ridge, while a second persists away from the ridge under suitable alternate views. Investigate and record both; the ridge does not dismiss the second. Changed: the second disappears when a setup error is corrected. Retain the interpretation revision and evidence rather than silently erasing the original call. P09 uses known geometry and adjacent-feature specimens.

lessons.title: Q10 — Characterize bondline and planar indications
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Characterize bondline and planar indications

A planar response at the joining region may support a bondline discontinuity interpretation. Establish its position relative to the seam, orientation, extent and connection evidence. Similar response patterns can arise from different conditions. Do not claim metallurgy or fabrication cause solely from a screen image.

Check the full assigned feature and preserve intermittent or stacked responses. A single strong segment does not establish the maximum extent. Sensitivity and orientation influence visibility, so absence under one view is not proof of absence. Use the validated interpretation procedure and record unresolved boundaries.

Worked: a response follows the joining plane in two separated axial intervals. Record both intervals before applying an explicit interaction rule. Changed: a third shallow response is seen only in an unverified law. Do not add it as established height until that state is verified. P10 requires actual known planar-feature interpretation with supporting views and a clear confidence limit.

lessons.title: Q11 — Examine hook-shaped and laminar features
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Examine hook-shaped and laminar features

A laminar feature near a formed seam can change orientation through the wall. A hook-like feature may therefore require more than one view to establish its geometry. Do not expect every feature to produce a textbook hook image. Distinguish a supported shape description from proof of an active crack or propagation mechanism.

Map normal depths and lateral extent using validated geometry. An intermediate reflector can block or redirect sound and hide another region. Retain unresolved volume. When multiple apparent tips exist, establish which are real boundaries and which are geometry or mode artifacts before calculating maximum height.

Worked: a planar feature is nearly parallel to the surface away from the seam and turns toward it near the joining region. Describe the supported orientation change and investigate its connection. Changed: the apparent turn occurs only in an incorrect flat-geometry display. Correct the model and reassess before calling a hook feature. P11 uses independently characterized teaching examples and changed orientations.

lessons.title: Q12 — Distinguish inclusions, surface marks and contact effects
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Distinguish inclusions, surface marks and contact effects

Volumetric responses, manufacturing surface marks and localized contact-related features require evidence appropriate to their scale and position. Record whether a feature is visible, acoustically detected or both. A familiar appearance does not establish harmlessness. Nearby planar evidence must be assessed separately.

Surface examination can help describe a mark, but it does not automatically establish its subsurface extent. Do not remove or polish a feature without authorization. Where the method cannot establish composition or origin, use a descriptive category and state the uncertainty rather than a confident unsupported label.

Worked: several short surface marks lie beside the seam and one has a separate supported subsurface response. Report the visible marks and the subsurface finding distinctly. Changed: an operator requests “normal manufacturing marks” as the report description without supporting evidence. Preserve the actual findings and refer disposition to the authorized reviewer. P12 combines safe visual/profile observations with actual UT corroboration.

lessons.title: Q13 — Assess metal loss and trim without double counting
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Assess metal loss and trim without double counting

Local thinning, raised trim and edge offset have different physical meanings. Establish the actual local section and datum before computing loss. A deeper surface depression and a crack-like response can coexist; record the basis for each dimension and avoid assuming their depths can simply be added.

Measure remaining wall with a suitable validated technique and distinguish it from depth to an internal reflector. A nominal manufacturing thickness may differ from actual nearby sound wall. State which baseline is used in a percentage calculation. Do not convert percentage loss into an operating decision without the governing engineering criteria.

Worked: local reference wall 10 mm and supported remaining wall 8 mm imply 2 mm loss, or 20% of that reference. Changed: a separate crack height is measured from a different surface datum. Do not add 2 mm and the crack height until the geometry and required engineering convention are established. P13 requires a section sketch with all measured and inferred quantities labeled.

lessons.title: Q14 — Establish endpoints and apply only the assigned interaction rule
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Establish endpoints and apply only the assigned interaction rule

Measure axial start and stop under the validated endpoint technique and preserve the origin. Length is stop minus start only when both share the same coordinate system. Nearby features may need to be reported separately and also grouped under a governing interaction rule. Grouping does not erase individual observations.

Use the actual assigned rule, including whether equality is included. A training interaction threshold is not automatically a production rule. A gap between features must itself be adequately examined before being treated as clear material. Report ambiguous separation rather than choosing the grouping that looks more favorable.

Worked: features 40–70 and 85–110 mm have lengths 30 and 25, a 15 mm gap and 70 mm overall span. Under an explicitly fictional rule to group gaps less than 20 mm, group and retain the two components. Changed: the gap is exactly 20 mm. The strict “less than” rule does not group equality. P14 measures actual endpoints and performs a separate paper rule comparison.

lessons.title: Q15 — Measure height, ligament and surface connection
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Measure height, ligament and surface connection

Establish normal-depth coordinates and validated feature boundaries before arithmetic. For a far-surface-connected feature in a locally flat section, height equals local wall minus depth to its established near tip. For an embedded feature, height is the difference between its established boundary depths; remaining ligament to the scanning surface is the shallower depth. Curvature and other geometry must be handled by the validated method.

Surface connection is an evidence-based classification. A tip near a surface is not automatically connected. An amplitude image extent is not necessarily physical height. If a boundary cannot be resolved, report the limitation rather than entering zero or a convenient estimate.

Worked: local wall 12 mm and established far-surface-connected tip at normal depth 8 mm give height 4 mm and near-surface ligament 8 mm. Changed: two embedded boundaries at 4 and 8 mm give height 4, near ligament 4 and far ligament 4 mm. Identical heights can represent different geometry. P15 requires actual supported sizing and section sketches for both cases.

lessons.title: Q16 — Search for maximum extent and control uncertainty
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Search for maximum extent and control uncertainty

Scan the full feature and pair each valid boundary measurement with its local section. Maximum measured height is not automatically the full-feature maximum when an interval is unexamined. Verify candidate tips with the approved method and preserve rejected interpretations. Report the largest supported value and limitations honestly.

Use declared truth uncertainty and a preannounced decision rule in training. Do not let a highly precise cursor hide poor boundary identification. Signed error, absolute error and uncertainty serve different purposes. Reassessment must test a new feature, not memorization of the disclosed maximum.

Worked: supported heights 3.0, 3.8 and 3.4 mm give a measured maximum 3.8 mm. Changed: a section between those positions is missing. The whole-feature maximum remains unresolved. A separate grading example has error 0.4 mm plus truth uncertainty 0.1; against fictional guarded tolerance 0.6 it passes at 0.5. An error 0.55 plus 0.1 fails at 0.65. P16 records raw evidence and the conservative decision.

lessons.title: Q17 — Reconcile field findings with ILI without changing them to match
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Reconcile field findings with ILI without changing them to match

Match pipe identity, weld reference, axial offset, clock convention and units before pairing an in-ditch finding with an ILI call. Keep the original ILI result and the independent field result. Differences may reflect location mismatch, different measured quantities or method uncertainty, not necessarily a defect in one system.

Do not adjust the field number to agree with the predicted value. Document the matching rationale, actual difference and unresolved alternatives. Operator specialists determine the implications for ILI performance and integrity assessment. One matched feature is not a complete statistical validation of a tool population.

Worked: ILI height estimate 5.0 mm and independently measured field height 4.2 yield field-minus-ILI difference −0.8 mm, if they describe the same feature and quantity. Changed: the field location is one joint away. Withdraw the match; the subtraction no longer supports a sizing comparison. P17 uses synthetic records and a traceable correlation table, with no live operational records altered.

lessons.title: Q18 — Detect verification failure and recover data
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Detect verification failure and recover data

Perform prescribed reference checks and event-based revalidation. Record the last valid state, failure time and affected acquisition IDs. Stop using an invalid configuration. Correct the cause, reverify and determine the repeat or disposition required by the responsible authority.

A successful later check does not retroactively validate earlier scans. Preserve failed and original data, even if a revised report is issued. Recover all potentially affected regions, not just the last convenient specimen. If recovery cannot be completed, make the remaining limitation visible at handover.

Worked: valid 09:00, failed 12:00, four seam regions examined in between. All four may be affected. Changed: one is repeated after correction at 12:30. Three remain unresolved unless an authorized supported disposition addresses them. P18 uses harmless controlled training discrepancies and separate files; no production configurations or records are erased.

lessons.title: Q19 — Produce an actionable examination record
lessons.body:
## Q19 — Produce an actionable examination record

For each finding preserve unique ID, specimen/pipe reference, start/stop/length, circumferential position, normal depths/height/ligament as applicable, supported type/connection, method/setup and limitations. Link the evidence used for detection separately from evidence used for sizing when they differ. Record the required geometric anomalies as well as flaws under the assignment rules.

Inspect the actual exported report for missing rows, incorrect units, truncated limitations and accidental default setup IDs. A complete-looking form can still contain unsupported measurements. Communicate credible significant findings through the designated path without inventing a repair or pressure decision.

Worked: five findings use setup S2, but two rows default to S1. Correct them against actual acquisition evidence. Changed: the corrected export drops the longest limitation. Repair and inspect again; a save message is not proof of a usable handover. P19 requires actual report entry/export and a simulated communication record, with no outside alert sent.

lessons.title: Q20 — Demonstrate independent competence in the declared method
lessons.body:
## Q20 — Demonstrate independent competence in the declared method

The final performance combines valid setup, full coverage, feature detection, characterization, dimensions, false-call control and reporting. Score each dimension independently. A high detection percentage cannot compensate for invented tip measurements or omitted areas. The training award lists only methods actually demonstrated under observation.

Use unfamiliar validated specimens with protected truth. Teach failures after the attempt and reassess on changed specimens of comparable scope. Preserve original scores and critical issues. A written pass or prior certificate cannot replace the actual integrated demonstration required by this course.

Worked: nine of ten relevant features found, but a designated critical planar feature is the one missed. The critical condition fails despite 90% detection. Changed: all ten are found, but three false calls are entered among twenty sound regions when the training maximum is one. Detection is 100%; false-call performance still fails. I66 requires both conditions and all assigned dimensions before a completion record is issued.


---

content.title: VUC066 | VUC066 delivery, application and assessment
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC066 delivery, application and assessment
lessons.body: # VUC066 delivery, application and assessment

lessons.title: Preparation and schedule
lessons.body:
## Preparation and schedule

Plan 64 hours: 16 instruction/checks, 10 application labs, 20 observed stations, 12 integrated practice/independent performance and remediation, 6 written final/review. Breaks/additional remediation separate; record actual hours. Instructor must be competent in the declared seam examination method and selected equipment. A responsible UT Level III or equivalently authorized technical authority validates procedures, physical references/specimens, truth and scoring before delivery. Authoring this package does not constitute that physical validation.

Diagnostic: identify normal depth versus path, read a curved section, reproduce a basic approved UT/PAUT setup, calculate length/percentage and explain an unresolved boundary. Teach missing fundamentals before advanced assessment. Demonstrate a complete known seam example with reasoning, then let learners examine a changed known example. Do not disclose final specimen truth or coach during independent attempts.

Provide actual selected instrument/software, compatible probes/wedges/cables, representative calibration references with known locations/depths, suitable scanner/encoder if used, rulers/profile tools, compatible couplant/SDS, removable marking materials, stable coupon supports and training computer. Supplementary surface methods require their own qualified instructor, suitable procedure and safety controls; the default pathway uses safe visual/profile observations plus UT/PAUT. No radiography, live pressure work, excavation entry, hot work or unauthorized coating removal is part of the exercise. Preserve production configurations and data; use separate training files rather than factory resets.

lessons.title: S66 original practical design
lessons.body:
## S66 original practical design

Teaching set T must include known examples of planar joining-region features, hook/laminar geometry, volumetric response, offset/trim, surface mark and metal loss. Where a safe artificial target is used, label its representational limits; do not claim it reproduces every response of a real service defect. Include supplementary original section drawings and known feature evidence for concepts that the actual bench cannot demonstrate. Written drawings do not replace required physical performance.

Protected sets A and B each contain at least five supported curved seam coupons across two geometries/thickness groups within the validated method range. Provide ten independently established reportable features and twenty designated sound regions; at least four of the ten are critical planar features, including a resolvable near-seam changing-orientation feature. Include an internal and an external connected feature, embedded feature, geometric anomaly and local loss. Five designated features have resolvable required height/ligament targets; all ten have defined endpoints. The technical authority validates that each declared primary method can interrogate them. Sets A/B must be distinct from T and each other.

Document specimen IDs, material/process evidence, local dimensions, feature truth and uncertainty, reference method, safe handling and validated detection/sizing technique. Obtain adequate independent qualified characterization or certified truth documentation. Do not derive protected truth from the same unvalidated scan being assessed. If the claimed feature type cannot be established, revise the training target before use or select another specimen; never invent truth to fill the matrix.

Technique sheet: scope/material/geometry; actual method and supplementary methods; probe/wedge/configuration; reference range/position/sensitivity checks; curved-geometry treatment; scan directions/offsets/speed/coverage validation; endpoint/height/ligament techniques; explicit reporting/interaction rules; verification events/intervals; recovery/reporting; authority/revision. Actual equipment button sequence comes from approved instructions. Every learner demonstrates setup rather than merely loading a file.

Original S66 requirements, announced before testing: reference position/depth guarded error ≤0.30 mm, where guarded error is absolute error plus declared reference uncertainty. Sensitivity reference within ±10 percentage points of its assigned 80% level where that level is appropriate to the validated method. Verify before/after each specimen and after relevant changes. All failed checks must be resolved with required recovery.

All assigned seam volume must be examined with limitations explicitly recorded. Detect at least nine of ten features and all four critical planar features. Correctly characterize at least nine of ten truth features, including applicable surface connection; a missed feature counts as incorrect, not removed from denominator. No more than one false feature call in the twenty sound regions. Endpoint guarded errors ≤3 mm and length guarded error ≤4 mm on at least nine of ten features, including all critical ones. Each of the five designated height and ligament targets must have guarded error ≤0.60 mm; no missing dimension is removed from denominator. Establish truth uncertainty ≤0.10 mm for height/ligament and ≤0.50 mm for endpoints/length. These are original training criteria, not API grading or production limits.

S66 reporting: record all validated features meeting the explicitly assigned response basis and length ≥5 mm; record required geometric anomalies and all five designated sizing targets. For the original training grouping exercise only, group axial gaps strictly less than 20 mm while retaining individual start/stop records. Equality does not group. This rule does not claim external or production applicability. No examiner may authorize operation, grinding or repair from a training score.

lessons.title: W01 — Scope and identity
lessons.body:
## W01 — Scope and identity

Packet: 600 mm assigned, 450 accessible; manufacturing card says ERW, apparent deposited repair visible. Worked: 75% physically accessible, 150 mm unresolved; verify identity/history and actual geometry before using assumed model. Changed: records unavailable. Preserve uncertainty and obtain authorized technique for actual geometry. Learner submits scope/method matrix and original section sketch. Instructor challenges an unsupported claim that visual access or a manufacturing label proves examinability.

lessons.title: W02 — Setup and curved geometry
lessons.body:
## W02 — Setup and curved geometry

Packet: file diameter 300 mm, actual 250; references 3/8 mm display 3.0/8.7 against fictional ±0.3. Worked: diameter mismatch and high reference +0.7 require correction and full applicable recheck. Changed: new readings 3.5/8.0; low end +0.5 still fails. Actual lab inventories system, verifies representative curvature and locates reference targets. No production files erased and no universal equipment sequence invented.

lessons.title: W03 — Coordinates and coverage
lessons.body:
## W03 — Coordinates and coverage

Packet: 600 mm segment, interval 120–170; coupling gap 210–235 on separate scan. Worked: feature length 50, reverse interval 430–480, gap 25 mm. Changed: gap rescanned at wrong offset. Coverage still unresolved. Learner physically relocates a feature from a written report and executes an approved scan/recovery, retaining actual acquisition evidence and the interpretation of clock/view direction.

lessons.title: W04 — Geometry versus planar evidence
lessons.body:
## W04 — Geometry versus planar evidence

Packet: known ridge response plus separate persistent indication away from ridge. Worked: explain geometry response but independently investigate second feature. Changed: corrected setup eliminates second response. Preserve revision and causal evidence; do not silently erase it. Actual known specimens combine geometry and a relevant feature, with changed locations for reassessment. Learner distinguishes observation, hypothesis, corroboration and final supported category.

lessons.title: W05 — Hook/laminar and surface-feature interpretation
lessons.body:
## W05 — Hook/laminar and surface-feature interpretation

Packet: changing-orientation response near joining region, surface marks beside seam, unverified flat-display image. Worked: correct geometry, map supported orientation and separately assess surface/subsurface evidence. Changed: no surface connection can be established. Report connection unresolved; do not call an embedded or surface-connected feature solely for scoring convenience. Actual lab uses validated specimens and safe supplementary visual/profile examination. Unknown metallurgy remains unknown.

lessons.title: W06 — Loss, endpoints and grouping
lessons.body:
## W06 — Loss, endpoints and grouping

Packet: local wall 10, remaining 8 mm; features 40–70 and 85–110. Worked: 2 mm loss/20%; lengths 30/25, gap 15, span 70; group under fictional gap <20 rule and retain components. Changed: gap exactly 20. Do not group equality. A separate crack value with another datum cannot simply be added to loss. Learner measures actual profile/endpoints and draws each quantity on the section.

lessons.title: W07 — Height and ligament
lessons.body:
## W07 — Height and ligament

Packet: local wall 12 mm, validated far-surface tip depth 8. Worked: height 4, near ligament 8. Changed: embedded boundaries 4/8 give height 4, near ligament 4 and far ligament 4. Actual work establishes boundaries with the selected validated method and preserves corroborating evidence. If a teaching boundary is unresolvable, honest limitation is assessed separately; final designated targets must be genuinely resolvable.

lessons.title: W08 — Maximum and guarded error
lessons.body:
## W08 — Maximum and guarded error

Packet: established heights 3.0/3.8/3.4 mm; one feature interval missing. Worked: measured maximum 3.8, whole-feature maximum unresolved. Changed: full valid coverage supports 4.1 elsewhere. Update maximum/location. Error examples: 0.4+0.1 uncertainty=0.5 passes 0.6; 0.55+0.1=0.65 fails. Learner performs actual full-feature sizing, records rejected candidate tips and applies the predeclared rule without favorable rounding.

lessons.title: W09 — ILI correlation and drift
lessons.body:
## W09 — ILI correlation and drift

Packet: ILI height 5.0, field 4.2, same matched feature; last valid 09:00, failed 12:00, four regions scanned. Worked: difference −0.8 mm only with matching quantity/location; all four potentially affected by drift. Changed: match is one joint off and one region repeated after correction. Withdraw unsupported correlation and identify three unresolved regions. Learner produces synthetic correlation/recovery records; no live data modified.

lessons.title: W10 — Reporting and independent score
lessons.body:
## W10 — Reporting and independent score

Packet: five findings use S2, two default to S1; ten detected features, three false calls among twenty sound regions. Worked: correct two setup links against evidence; detection 100%, false-call rate 15%, exceeds S66 maximum one. Changed: export truncates limits and a missing height is copied. Both report and integrity conditions fail. Learner enters/export-checks actual training findings and drafts a simulated handover without sending any outside message.

lessons.title: Station rubric
lessons.body:
## Station rubric

Score identity/basis, setup/method, result reasoning, safety/limits and reproducible evidence 0–2 each. Pass 8/10, no zero or unresolved critical issue. Fabrication, unsafe action, hidden invalid calibration/coverage and unsupported operational authority are critical. Stop unsafe work, teach and require changed observed performance. Written arithmetic tolerance 0.01 stated unit/percentage point; physical grading uses S66 guarded errors.

| Station | Required evidence | Changed task |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Scope and output/method matrix | Blocked assigned volume |
| P02 | Manufacturing/section evidence and uncertainty | Conflicting repair history |
| P03 | Safe access/preparation scenario and bench plan | Unauthorized removal request |
| P04 **actual** | Primary-method setup and supplementary limits | Missing corroboration |
| P05 **actual** | Curvature/configuration/reference location | Different diameter/wedge |
| P06 **actual** | Range/sensitivity/sizing checks | Second reference fails |
| P07 **actual** | Reproducible physical coordinates | Reverse origin/view |
| P08 **actual** | Coverage and coupling-gap recovery | Wrong offset repeat |
| P09 **actual** | Geometry plus independent feature | Setup artifact disappears |
| P10 **actual** | Planar joining-region interpretation | Intermittent feature |
| P11 **actual** | Hook/laminar orientation and limits | Changed orientation |
| P12 **actual** | Surface/subsurface evidence separation | Unsupported benign label |
| P13 **actual** | Local loss and datum/profile | Mixed feature geometry |
| P14 **actual** | Endpoints and explicit grouping rule | Equality boundary |
| P15 **actual** | Height/ligament/connection evidence | Embedded versus connected |
| P16 **actual** | Maximum search and guarded error | Missing interval |
| P17 | Synthetic ILI correlation | Wrong joint |
| P18 **actual** | Verification failure/recovery records | Multiple affected regions |
| P19 **actual** | Actual report/export and simulated handover | Wrong setup/hidden limit |
| P20 **actual** | Independent practice and evidence package | Changed protected set |

lessons.title: I66 independent examination
lessons.body:
## I66 independent examination

Allow six hours actual setup, scan, verification and report work, with breaks outside scored time. This is VNDRLY timing, not an external exam promise. Use protected set A and declared method. Assessor observes without indicating feature locations, probe positions or correct interpretation. All S66 conditions must pass separately. Genuine failure to complete is recorded, not filled with nominal or copied values.

Truth/scoring record: learner/method/version___ specimen/region___ feature truth/method/uncertainty___ critical designation___ actual detected/type/connection___ endpoints/length actual and truth___ height/ligament actual and truth___ guarded errors___ sound-region false call___ coverage/check evidence___ critical issue___ result___ assessor/date___. Keep private truth separate from learner forms. Document the twenty sound-region denominator and all ten expected features, including missed ones.

After failure, teach the concept/technique and use changed set B with comparable validated challenge. Do not count memorized disclosed coordinates as independent performance. Required actual stations and I66 cannot be satisfied with screenshots alone. Missing equipment, safe specimens or credible truth leaves practical delivery pending; it never converts to a written-only award.

lessons.title: Written final and credential
lessons.body:
## Written final and credential

Twenty cases, three decisions each, 120 points, 180 minutes. Pass 96 and ≥4/6 each domain, no unresolved critical error. Calculator/coursebook permitted; keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Two points correct with supported reasoning, one safe incomplete, zero wrong/missing/unsafe. Separate changed Form B retains necessary context but no answers. Written pass does not offset failed practical.

Require twenty chapters/forty explained checks, ten labs, twenty stations including sixteen actual, I66 and written final. Diagnose failures, teach, require corrected explanation and changed performance. After two unsuccessful reassessments use individualized instruction and fresh equivalent supervised assessment. Preserve attempts and allow independent competent grading review where feasible.

Record learner identity, prerequisites, actual hours, version/hash, actual methods/equipment, specimen set, all results, remediation, assessor and limits. Award: “VNDRLY/U Long Seam Pipeline Examination — training assessment completion,” listing only demonstrated methods. No API/ASNT logo or external qualification claim. Employer qualification, production procedure and operator disposition remain separate. Internal review at 24 months or earlier after changed methods/requirements or demonstrated gaps; no claim this is an external renewal term.

lessons.title: Reusable learner forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable learner forms

Scope: component/history evidence___ seam/geometry___ assigned volume___ origin/direction/view___ primary/supplementary methods___ outputs/limits___ authority___

Setup: instrument/software/probe/wedge/cable___ actual geometry inputs___ references/truth/uncertainty___ checks/guarded errors___ sensitivity___ technique revision___ operator/time___

Coverage: specimen/track/direction___ interval/offset___ contact gaps___ excluded volume___ recovery___ source file/check linkage___

Finding: uniqueID___ location/start/stop/length___ normal depth/height/ligament___ supported type/connection___ observed evidence___ grouping rule/components___ setup IDs for detection/sizing___ uncertainty/limits___

Correlation: ILI original ID/coordinates/quantity___ field ID/coordinates/quantity___ match basis___ difference___ uncertainty/unmatched alternatives___ reviewer___

Recovery/report: last valid___ failed___ affectedIDs___ correction/repeat/disposition___ originals retained___ exported rows/units/limits checked___ simulated escalation___

Assessment: task/evidence___ scores___ critical issue___ instruction___ changed set/result___ assessor/date___ appeal___ award or pending reason___

lessons.title: VUC066 source review and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC066 source review and coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original VNDRLY teaching and assessments based on available primary public sources. No external specimen truth or examination questions reproduced. No full proprietary-standard equivalence or external qualification claimed. S66 limits, examples, specimen matrix and scoring are independently stated training choices.

L01 — [API current LSP page](https://www.api.org/products-and-services/individual-certification-programs/certifications/apilsp). Supports the program's seam detection/characterization/sizing scope, practical emphasis and method-specific credential boundary. Public descriptions emphasize ERW and mention other seam processes. This VNDRLY package records actual demonstrated methods/geometries instead of claiming automatic qualification for every process.

L02 — [Currently linked characterization guide](https://apidam.widen.net/content/m7r8yqa6cb/pdf/=c&quality=80&x.app=portals). Supports considering location, connection, geometry and feature evidence separately. Terminology includes both hook crack and hook flaw; the course avoids claiming active cracking or a specific cause from shape alone. The guide's generalized detection/propagation language is not adopted as a universal safety or acceptance guarantee. Full API 5T1 text was not reviewed; no complete clause-by-clause equivalence is claimed.

L03 — [Currently linked candidate orientation](https://apidam.widen.net/content/cfbwwp9ism/pdf/=c&quality=80&x.app=portals), internally effective 2020. Supports independently demonstrated primary-method setup and separate performance categories. The document remains linked but is not assumed to settle every current administrative detail. Its external thresholds, data-reset rules and security procedures are not instructions to alter this workspace or production instruments. VNDRLY supplies separate explicit assessment rules and preserves training/production data.

L04 — [PHMSA-hosted historical seam evaluation](https://www.phmsa.dot.gov/sites/phmsa.dot.gov/files/docs/technical-resources/pipeline/gas-transmission-integrity-management/65266/tto05lowfrequencyerwfinalreportrev3april2004.pdf), April 2004. Historical context for legacy seam features and the need to match examination capability to threats. It is not presented as current regulation, a modern acceptance standard or proof of a specific pipe's condition.

L05 — [Sonatest long-seam application note](https://sonatest.com/resources/application-notes/long-seam-weld-inspection-encoded-semi-automatic). Supports the importance of curved geometry and actual system configuration. Product examples do not establish performance of every instrument or qualify a learner. The course requires representative reference verification rather than assuming software correction is sufficient.

L06 — [Evident long-seam scanning application](https://ims.evidentscientific.com/en/applications/inspecting-long-seam-welds-efficiently-and-easily-using-the-axseam-scanner). Supports acoustic/mechanical challenges of axial seam scanning. It does not provide universal scan spacing, acceptance limits or guaranteed detection. S66 requires a validated actual technique.

| Maximum/uncertainty | Q16/W08 | P16 | Q16-F/R |
| ILI correlation | Q17/W09 | P17 | Q17-F/R |
| Recovery/traceability | Q18/W09 | P18 | Q18-F/R |
| Report/export/handover | Q19/W10 | P19 | Q19-F/R |
| Independent completion | Q20/W10 | P20/I66 | Q20-F/R |

Two explained formative checks accompany each chapter. The delivery guide specifies actual equipment work, protected specimen truth, independent practical conditions, forms, remediation and credential rules. Instructor final forms/keys are kept outside the public learner package. Physical apparatus, actual learner performance, employer qualifications and operating decisions are not asserted by material completion.

content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC067 — Tower Crane Operation
lessons.body: # VUC067 — Tower Crane Operation

lessons.title: Program boundary and learning outcome
lessons.body:
## Program boundary and learning outcome

This original VNDRLY/U program teaches planning, inspection, controlled load handling and safe securing of tower cranes. Completion records the exact crane type and observed activities. It is not CCO certification, a license, an erection-director qualification or an employer's equipment/task evaluation. A written or simulated result alone earns a knowledge-only record. Actual operating assessment requires suitable equipment, authorized supervision and the performance evidence in the workbook.

Read each chapter, work its example and complete the corresponding two checks before its application. Bring uncertainty to the instructor rather than filling missing load, configuration or procedure information by assumption. The governing operating information is the actual manufacturer's current instructions for the installed configuration, together with applicable rules and authorized site procedures. All numerical charts and limits labeled T67 are fictional classroom data, never operating instructions for a real crane.

lessons.title: Q01 — Roles, readiness and stop authority
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Roles, readiness and stop authority

A tower operator controls machine motion but depends on several independently competent people: the assembly/disassembly director manages that operation, qualified technical personnel resolve design and configuration questions, riggers arrange the load, signal personnel communicate movements, and management establishes site control. Certification, training and employer evaluation are different evidence. A course completion cannot substitute for demonstrated competence on the equipment and work assigned.

Before accepting a shift identify your authorization, crane identity, task, supervisor, signal channel and means of safe access. Review previous defects and restrictions. Fatigue, impairment, a missing familiarization or inability to understand the signal system can make an otherwise trained person unready. Report the condition and obtain relief or training; do not begin merely because a schedule is urgent. Anyone's emergency stop must receive an appropriate safe stop, not an argument about who normally signals.

Worked case: a learner has passed this written course and is assigned alone to a luffing crane after practice only on a simulator. The missing evidence is actual competence and required employer authorization/evaluation, not another signature on the written score. Arrange supervised training on the actual type. Changed application: an experienced operator receives an unfamiliar control layout. Experience does not remove familiarization and evaluation needs.

lessons.title: Q02 — Crane types, components and power flow
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Crane types, components and power flow

A hammerhead crane generally changes radius with a trolley on a substantially horizontal jib. A luffing crane changes jib angle to alter radius; geometry and out-of-service configuration differ. A self-erecting crane may use a distinct base, outrigger and unfolding arrangement. Identify mast, slewing assembly, jib, counterjib where fitted, trolley or luffing machinery, hoist, reeving, hook block, ballast and electrical supply on the specific machine rather than assuming every type has every component.

Trace operator command through control, drive, transmission and brake to load movement. Electrical, hydraulic and mechanical systems can retain energy after normal controls stop. A brake is not a substitute for isolation, and an emergency stop is not proof of zero energy. Operator observation and permitted maintenance stay within the manual and employer authorization; electrical repair belongs to authorized personnel. Never bridge a limit device to diagnose a nuisance trip.

Worked case: a control produces no motion, but the drive cabinet is energized and the load is suspended. Treat this as a malfunction with stored energy, control exposure and summon qualified help. Do not enter the cabinet or release a brake. Changed application: power returns unexpectedly. Prevent an unplanned restart using the approved recovery procedure before resuming.

lessons.title: Q03 — Site and supporting system
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Site and supporting system

The site plan must address the entire operating and out-of-service envelope: load path, counterjib, other cranes, structures, roads, public access, underground services, overhead conductors and space needed during erection. Air rights and property boundaries are constraints, not clearance assumptions. Foundation and supporting structure adequacy require the prescribed manufacturer/engineering basis. Operators identify damage, flooding, excavation, settlement or unauthorized alterations and report them; they do not certify foundation design by visual judgment.

For self-erecting equipment, verify the specified setup geometry, support and outrigger arrangements through the approved procedure. A large-looking mat does not prove capacity. Keep foundations, anchors, drainage and access protected from site changes. Electrical supply, isolation, grounding and lightning provisions must be established by appropriate authorized personnel. Do not infer their adequacy from the crane powering on.

Worked case: yesterday's accepted foundation now has an excavation immediately beside it and water collecting around anchors. Hold operations and refer the changed support condition to the responsible authority. Yesterday's approval describes yesterday's condition. Changed application: no visible movement exists. Lack of visible movement is not proof that support capacity is unchanged.

lessons.title: Q04 — Erection and dismantling interfaces
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Erection and dismantling interfaces

Erection and dismantling are planned sequences with changing centers of gravity and support conditions. The assembly/disassembly director must have the required competence and qualifications. Crew members need their task, hazards and communication arrangements before movement. The operator follows the authorized sequence and does not improvise a shortcut because a component appears nearly balanced. Pins or bolts may be carrying loads that are not visually obvious.

Identify temporary supports, assist-crane capacity at the actual radius, rigging, connection specifications and the point at which each component becomes stable. Keep people clear of crush zones and suspended components. If a worker moves out of view into an exposure area, establish communication and stop the relevant motion until their position and safety are known. Structural connections use the specified components, installation and verification process; generic torque values or substitute bolts are unacceptable.

Worked case: a connection pin resists removal while the crew says the section is supported. Stop and verify the engineered support/load-transfer state; do not add force or move the hoist experimentally. Changed application: the pin frees suddenly. That does not validate the sequence; evaluate movement and stability before continuing under the director.

lessons.title: Q05 — Climbing, ties, ballast and plumb
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Climbing, ties, ballast and plumb

Climbing changes the support arrangement of the crane. Internal climbing frames, collars, beams and wedges, or an external climbing unit and ties, must match the specified configuration and sequence. The operator must understand the commanded balance condition and communication plan, but this course does not qualify the learner to design ties or direct climbing. Do not use a remembered balance load, tie spacing or permissible free-standing height from another crane.

Verify the approved mast height, tie locations, supported height above ties, ballast arrangement and post-climb position of the climbing equipment. Both insufficient and excessive ballast can be unsafe. Host-structure attachments require the appropriate engineering basis. Plumb is checked by the prescribed method and tolerance. A generic arithmetic exercise cannot establish the real crane's acceptance. After erection or relevant changes, the specified inspection and testing must be completed before ordinary lifting.

Worked T67 exercise: an assigned fictional plumb limit is 1: 500 over 40 m. The displacement limit is 40, 000/500 = 80 mm; a 92 mm displacement exceeds it by 12 mm. The decision is a hold for correction/technical review, not to move ballast until it looks straight. Changed application: the manufacturer specifies 60 mm. That stricter applicable instruction governs the exercise instead of the generic value.

lessons.title: Q06 — Shift inspection and defect disposition
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Shift inspection and defect disposition

An inspection is an organized search for conditions affecting safety, not a form completed from memory. Follow the actual inspection scope: structure and connections visible from safe access, support changes, fluids and leaks, controls, brakes, guards, hoist system, rope path, hook and latch, electrical condition, operational aids, safety devices and access. Check required records and outstanding restrictions. Use safe functional checks specified by the manufacturer; do not create an overload or disable a device to prove it operates.

Distinguish a shift inspection from periodic or annual inspections, post-assembly inspection and special inspection after a change or event. The operator cannot extend an expired inspection merely by finding no obvious defect. Record what was observed, where, when and the restriction communicated. A defect that creates a safety hazard requires the appropriate removal from service and repair process. A replacement part does not establish readiness until the required checks and authorized release are complete.

Worked case: the checklist is signed, but the hook latch is damaged and the rope appears to have jumped a sheave. Suspend the lift and report the actual conditions. A signed checklist does not override the equipment. Changed application: a colleague says it ran this morning. Previous movement does not prove continued safe condition.

lessons.title: Q07 — Wire rope, reeving and hooks
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Wire rope, reeving and hooks

Inspect the rope where deterioration can concentrate: sheaves, drums, repetitive bending locations, terminations and sections exposed to abrasion or heat. Look for distortion, broken wires, corrosion, diameter change, damaged terminations and evidence of crushing or kinking. Use the applicable rope type and removal criteria; a single remembered broken-wire count cannot cover all ropes or all defects. Do not handle moving rope, run fingers along damaged strands, or climb into an unprotected reeving area.

Reeving determines both load capability and available hook travel. Confirm line parts, permitted line pull, block and hook capacity, drum capacity and required remaining wraps against the actual manual. More parts do not automatically make every chart rating larger. Check that rope is seated and spooled correctly and that the hook/block has the appropriate identity and inspection status. Never straighten a hook, weld a fitting or substitute a rope because its diameter is similar.

Worked T67 example: permitted line pull is 2.0 t and four parts give a simplified ideal 8.0 t force ceiling, but the configuration chart permits only 6.5 t. The 6.5 t limit still governs before all other applicable deductions/limits. This simplified multiplication is a classroom comparison, not a reeving design. Changed application: only two parts are installed. Reassess the actual configuration rather than retaining the four-part rating.

lessons.title: Q08 — Capacity charts and configuration
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Capacity charts and configuration

A valid chart decision begins with identity: crane model, jib length/type, mast/support configuration, reeving and chart revision. Determine the operating radius from the correct reference, the full planned path and the governing worst condition. Do not substitute jib length for load radius. Follow the actual chart's conventions for intermediate values, deductions and gross/net load. Never interpolate or extrapolate unless explicitly permitted by the governing information.

T67 fictional chart: at radii 15, 20, 25 and 30 m, gross suspended-load capacities are respectively 8.0, 6.5, 5.0 and 4.0 t. The classroom instruction requires the next larger listed radius for intermediate radii and includes hook, rigging and attachments in gross suspended load. These conventions belong only to this chart. For a 23 m path use 25 m and 5.0 t, not an average between columns. An unavailable or mismatched chart is a stop condition.

Worked: payload 4.2 t, hook 0.3 t, rigging 0.2 t and beam 0.4 t total 5.1 t. At 23 m the permitted T67 gross load is 5.0 t, so the lift fails by 0.1 t. Moving slowly does not repair insufficient capacity. Changed: the path extends to 28 m; the 30 m column gives 4.0 t and the deficiency increases. Replan with authorized information before lifting.

lessons.title: Q09 — Load weight, center of gravity and rigging
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Load weight, center of gravity and rigging

Obtain reliable weight information for the actual object, including retained contents and attached equipment. A shipping weight for an empty vessel may not describe a wet or partly filled vessel. Determine center of gravity and approved lifting points. Rigging capacity depends on its identity, configuration, angle, condition and how the load is distributed. A qualified rigger must resolve the actual arrangement. The operator verifies the information needed for the lift rather than assuming a crane's load display will safely discover an unknown weight.

For classroom understanding only, two equal symmetric sling legs carrying a static load W at angle theta above horizontal have ideal tension W/(2 sin theta) in each leg. As the angle becomes shallower, tension rises. Real rigging selection also depends on component ratings, connection factors, unequal loading and manufacturer instructions. Never use this simplified equation to authorize an unreviewed arrangement.

Worked: a 4.0 t load with ideal equal legs at 30 degrees above horizontal produces 4.0 t tension per leg, not 2.0 t. At 60 degrees it is about 2.31 t. Changed: the center of gravity shifts. Equal load sharing is no longer justified. Stop to correct the plan before the load is suspended, and perform only the approved initial check lift to confirm balance and rigging behavior.

lessons.title: Q10 — Signals and blind lifts
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Signals and blind lifts

Agree on the signal system before movement. The designated signal person needs the required qualification for the signals used. The operator and signaler must share the meaning of directions, identify the crane when more than one can hear the channel, and test communications. Use standardized hand signals as applicable; agree on any necessary nonstandard signal beforehand. Stop if a signal is unclear or communication needed for safe movement is lost.

Blind lifting needs planned communication and control of the hidden area, not merely a radio. Confirm who sees the load, travel path and landing area, how a transfer between signalers works, and who controls exclusion zones. Only one person normally directs motion at a time; emergency stop signals from others remain valid. Describe directions from the agreed operator perspective and use an unambiguous command sequence. A camera or anti-collision device supplements rather than automatically replaces required signaling.

Worked: the radio breaks up after a command to lower a load behind a wall. Stop safely; do not finish the remembered command while waiting for the signal to return. Re-establish communication and confirm conditions before resuming. Changed: two voices give conflicting directions. Resolve control of signaling with the load secure instead of choosing the louder voice.

lessons.title: Q11 — Controlled motion and load placement
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Controlled motion and load placement

Start with familiarization inside the permitted practice envelope and no unsupported assumptions about control response. Lift vertically over the load's center of gravity, take slack in a controlled way and make the prescribed initial balance/brake check close to the support surface. Keep the load and hook under control through hoisting, radius change and slewing. Avoid abrupt acceleration and reversal that amplify swing. A load's momentum does not stop when the control returns to neutral.

Plan a clear route, adequate clearance and a prepared landing area. Never side-pull or drag a load with the crane. Use tag lines only under an appropriate plan where they can be handled without entanglement, pinch or electrical exposure; do not wrap a line around the body. Keep people out from under the load and prevent hands entering crush points during placement. Slack and disconnect only after the load is supported and stable and the rigger directs the next step.

Worked: the hook is two metres to the side of a load snagged behind a pallet. Pulling would apply side force and might suddenly free the load. Stop, reposition and resolve the obstruction through an authorized plan. Changed: the load begins to swing. Use the taught machine-specific controlled recovery, protect the path and land when safe; do not chase swing with aggressive commands.

lessons.title: Q12 — Devices, zoning and multiple cranes
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Devices, zoning and multiple cranes

Know which installed devices are safety devices and which are operational aids under the governing requirements. A failure does not create permission to invent a workaround. Safety-device failures require the prescribed stop/removal-from-service response; some operational-aid provisions allow specified temporary alternatives and repair periods, but only under the applicable rule and authorized implementation. The operator must know the particular provision, condition and restrictions before any continued use.

Confirm the configured limits match the actual crane and site. Anti-collision or zoning systems depend on correct geometry, settings and communications; they cannot justify an otherwise unsafe overlapping envelope. Multiple cranes require coordination for jibs, towers, ropes and loads, including out-of-service positions and wind effects. Keep changes controlled. Do not silence alarms or increase a limit because another crane appears farther away on a screen.

Worked case: the indicator shows a 40 m jib, while the installed configuration is 50 m. Stop and have the configuration corrected and verified. A plausible displayed capacity is not proof of a valid model. Changed: an anti-collision alarm repeatedly trips at the same location. Investigate the actual envelope and settings through authorized personnel; do not bypass the system to maintain output.

lessons.title: Q13 — Wind, weather and out-of-service position
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Wind, weather and out-of-service position

Obtain the specific limits and procedures for operation, erection, climbing, dismantling and parking. These can differ. Wind at the crane and gusts may differ from a ground weather report. Large surface-area loads can become uncontrollable before a nominal machine limit is reached. Lightning, poor visibility, ice and temperature can require additional restrictions. Monitor conditions and plan enough time to land and secure before a hazardous threshold is reached.

Parking is an engineered configuration, not a universal instruction to lock or release slew. Follow the exact crane's out-of-service jib angle/radius, hook position, slew/brake arrangement and restraints. Some cranes require weather-vaning; preventing it can create dangerous loads. Others have different arrangements. Never use a practical-test instruction to set a brake as the complete real-world overnight parking procedure. Verify the manufacturer's instructions for the installed machine and surrounding structures.

Worked T67 case: a fictional lift plan stops lifting at 12 m/s, and observed gusts reach 13 m/s although the average is 9. Stop the exercise and secure under its plan. Do not average away the exceedance. Changed: a broad panel becomes difficult to control at 8 m/s. Stop for loss of control even though the numeric limit has not been reached.

lessons.title: Q14 — Electrical hazards and exclusion zones
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Electrical hazards and exclusion zones

Identify overhead lines and establish the required work-zone assessment, voltage information and protective measures before operations. Treat lines as energized unless the utility owner/operator confirms the required de-energized and grounding condition. An observer saying a line looks unused is insufficient. The OSHA assessment triggers, clearance tables and special arrangements are not interchangeable; do not teach one distance as safe for every voltage and circumstance.

Plan for every part of the equipment, rigging and load, including swing and wind movement. Barriers, warning lines and designated observers or other measures must match the selected compliant method. If line contact occurs, stop movements, warn people away and get emergency/utility assistance through the site response plan. Do not approach or touch the equipment to help someone while it may be energized. The operator follows the emergency procedure; evacuation when fire or other immediate danger requires it needs trained action, not experimentation.

Worked: the lift plan assesses the boom but ignores the long suspended steel load extending toward a line. The plan is incomplete. Reassess the complete envelope before the lift. Changed: a spotter leaves. If that measure is required for the selected method, suspend the operation until compliant protection is restored. All course electrical scenarios are tabletop; no energized-line approach is used for practice.

lessons.title: Q15 — Special lifts and travel
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Special lifts and travel

Personnel lifting, underwater loads, traveling with suspended loads and multiple-crane lifts introduce additional requirements and may be prohibited for the configuration. They are not authorized by passing ordinary load-placement practice. Obtain the specific applicable procedure, equipment suitability, planning and approvals. For personnel platforms, ordinary cargo rigging and a confident operator are not enough; applicable personnel-hoisting requirements must be satisfied. This program uses planning cases only for personnel lifting.

An underwater load may include suction, trapped material, changing buoyancy or snagging. Do not use crane capacity as an experimental breakout force. Rail travel requires the specified track condition, stops, clearances and control arrangements. Self-erecting setup or travel must follow the actual manufacturer's limits. A suspended load can shift the effective envelope and ground/support demand; evaluate the whole operation rather than only the lifting position.

Worked: a submerged object has a recorded dry weight below chart capacity, but its release force and contents are unknown. Hold for a qualified plan; the dry weight alone is not adequate. Changed: a supervisor proposes using a cargo basket to lift a worker for a quick repair. Refuse the improvised personnel lift and use an authorized access method or properly planned compliant operation.

lessons.title: Q16 — Malfunctions and emergencies
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Malfunctions and emergencies

Know how to stop and secure under the actual crane's emergency procedures, who to call and how the site protects the affected zone. A malfunction with a suspended load needs controlled isolation of the hazard and qualified recovery, not an improvised repair by the operator. Do not leave controls with a suspended load except as required by the emergency situation and approved response. Communicate the load's location and condition so responders do not enter blindly.

Fire, smoke, a failing brake, loss of power or a medical emergency in the cab may require distinct actions. Establish a rescue plan for elevated access before the shift; calling emergency services without crane location, height or access information is incomplete preparation. Never perform live fault creation or an unplanned rescue drill to make training realistic. Use a simulator or tabletop for failures and an authorized separate rescue program for actual rescue techniques.

Worked: a load drifts down with the hoist control neutral. Warn and protect the area and execute the trained equipment-specific safe response; report the brake/control fault and remove the equipment from operation until appropriately repaired and released. Changed: the fault disappears on restart. Intermittent failure still requires investigation; absence of a repeated symptom is not proof of repair.

lessons.title: Q17 — Maintenance, access and handover
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Maintenance, access and handover

Before access or maintenance, identify gravity, electrical, hydraulic and mechanical energy and use the authorized isolation procedure. Controls turned off do not demonstrate isolation. Fall protection and access arrangements must match the actual equipment and work; no climbing practice occurs without the separately established access/rescue controls and competent supervision. Operator maintenance is limited to authorized tasks in the instructions, not structural repair or limit calibration by intuition.

A handover must preserve what the next shift needs: crane/configuration, work status, weather restrictions, defects, repairs and release evidence, inspection status, unusual events and parked condition. Clearly distinguish observed facts from diagnosis. A verbal note alone may not satisfy required reporting and records. Store the defect record where the incoming operator and responsible management can actually retrieve it. Never delete an unresolved restriction because a new shift begins.

Worked: the outgoing operator reports a recurring trolley fault but the log says normal. Record the discrepancy and maintain the appropriate hold while it is resolved. Changed: a technician replaced a component but release checks are not documented. Obtain the required verification before use; the repair action and return-to-service decision are separate.

lessons.title: Q18 — Integrated lift decision
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Integrated lift decision

A sound lift decision integrates authority, site, configuration, condition, load, route, communication and recovery. Passing each topic on a different hypothetical crane is not proof that today's combined lift is ready. Use a repeatable pre-lift briefing: identify equipment and controlling documents; confirm inspection and restrictions; calculate the governing capacity; verify rigging and exclusion zone; agree signals and weather limits; identify stop conditions; establish landing and securing sequence.

Worked T67 case: at a maximum radius of 24 m, payload 3.8 t plus hook 0.3, rigging 0.2 and beam 0.4 gives 4.7 t against the 5.0 t fictional gross rating. Capacity passes by 0.3 t, but a failed required device and missing landing signaler still prevent the lift. A passing arithmetic result is only one condition. Changed case: after those issues are resolved the planned radius changes to 27 m. Now the 4.0 t rating is insufficient. Reassess every material change; never carry forward a stale approval.

The final practical requires controlled actual operation, not just this analysis. Record the observed crane type and limits. If actual equipment or safe supervision is unavailable, finish the knowledge record honestly and leave operational performance unawarded until it can be demonstrated.


---
