A stopped head is not necessarily isolated. On a jam, unusual movement or uncertain holding, stop and obtain the approved recovery method. Maintain control during vertical and inclined placement; gravity acts differently when supports are repositioned.

Worked: a clamp is opened before the string's alternate support is confirmed. The string can drop or slide. Stop and restore the approved holding arrangement. Changed: alternate support is confirmed, but a helper puts a hand between the rod and mast to align it. Resolve the pinch exposure using the approved handling/alignment method before motion.

lessons.title: Q16 — Air, water, grout and pressure systems
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Air, water, grout and pressure systems

Identify actual pressure ratings, compatible couplings, restraints, relief devices, isolation and depressurization points. The lowest component rating limits the system; a high pump rating does not authorize a lower-rated hose. Secure and inspect lines and protect their routes from damage. Never loosen a connection to check whether pressure remains or look for a pinhole leak with a hand. Follow qualified procedures for blockage and stored-energy release.

Manage returns and grout under the approved containment plan. Cementitious materials can harm skin and eyes; use suitable PPE, washing facilities and the actual SDS/emergency response. Promptly remove exposure and seek appropriate medical help for injury or eye contact. Do not improvise chemical neutralizers from an informal toolbox suggestion. Respiratory protection must follow the applicable exposure assessment/program, not a blanket dust-mask assumption.

Worked F71: pump limit 200 bar, hose 150 and fitting 120 give a supplied system ceiling no higher than 120 bar, before other restrictions. A proposed 140 bar exceeds it by 20. Changed: the fitting is upgraded to 180 but the hose remains 150. The new comparison ceiling is 150, not 180 or 200.

lessons.title: Q17 — Dust, noise, weather and the work environment
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Dust, noise, weather and the work environment

Assess dust from drilling, spoil and cement handling. Where construction silica requirements apply, implement the appropriate complete control method or assessed alternative; a partly working shroud or absent water flow cannot be treated as fully implemented control. Maintain the specified cab, ventilation or suppression system and housekeeping. Required respirators need the appropriate program, training and fit/medical provisions; this course does not authorize selection by guesswork.

Use actual controls for noise, visibility, lighting, wind, temperature and fatigue. Stop when conditions prevent safe control even if one numerical limit passes. Keep access clear of slurry and hoses and use appropriate hearing/eye protection. Hidden fabric, discarded rope or loose material near an auger can entangle and pull a person toward it; clear the work zone through a safe isolated process.

Worked: drilling begins with a broken dust-control hose and a worker says the wind will carry dust away. Stop and restore the required exposure controls; wind direction is not a substitute. Changed: dust control is restored but poor lighting hides a clamp zone. Resolve the visibility hazard before continuing.

lessons.title: Q18 — Emergencies, isolation and maintenance
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Emergencies, isolation and maintenance

Brief responses for power contact, instability, fire, flooding, control/travel failure, a fall into a shaft, pressure release and injury. Stop and protect people using the actual emergency plan. Do not rush into a potentially energized zone or shaft to attempt an unplanned rescue. Emergency stop does not guarantee release of hydraulic, pneumatic, gravity or rotational stored energy.

Service work requires authorized isolation, verification and support of components. Operators perform only the maintenance allowed by their competence and actual instructions; qualified personnel handle critical repair/adjustment. Record defects, actions and separate return-to-service verification. Preserve restrictions through handover. Do not erase an incident because the machine eventually functioned normally.

Worked: a hydraulic hose fails and a suspended component remains held by residual pressure. Keep people clear and obtain the approved supported recovery/isolation procedure; do not disconnect more fittings. Changed: the component is safely supported but a worker reports a tiny puncture from the jet. Activate immediate professional medical response for suspected injection injury.

lessons.title: Q19 — Shutdown, securing and records
lessons.body:
## Q19 — Shutdown, securing and records

For a break, end of shift or transport, follow the appropriate actual sequence. Land/support tools, secure strings and open shafts, set controls and brakes, isolate/secure access as required and stow the mast/attachments only in the permitted configuration. End-of-day security is different from a brief operational pause. Do not leave an unsupported rod or unsecured hole for the next crew.

Record shaft/anchor identity, actual location/alignment/depth, equipment/tool configuration, relevant strata/groundwater observations, interruptions, defects and unresolved technical decisions. Distinguish measured facts from estimates. Foundation acceptance is made by the authorized inspection/design process; the operator's log supports it but does not replace it. Handover requires the receiving party to understand remaining restrictions.

Worked: depth was estimated because the instrument failed, but the outgoing report labels it measured. Correct the record and require valid verification. Changed: depth is verified, but the shaft protection is removed for a delivery. Protect the opening immediately through the approved arrangement; a complete log does not guard a physical hazard.

lessons.title: Q20 — Independent integrated decisions
lessons.body:
## Q20 — Independent integrated decisions

Combine scope, site, platform, utilities, equipment, tooling, load limits, signals, drilling and securing as one coherent operation. A pass in arithmetic cannot cancel missing locate information, and a good inspection cannot authorize a changed tool or trajectory. Rebrief changes and record the actual basis for proceeding. Safe voluntary stops show judgment; hiding uncertainty does not.

F71 integrated paper case: pipe 1, 400 kg plus handling equipment 250 at 5 m totals 1, 650 against the fictional 1, 800 chart, margin 150. An unverified platform extension still holds the move. Changed: extension is validated but retained material adds 200; total becomes 1, 850, failing by 50. Replan before motion rather than relying on the previous calculation.

Actual integrated assessment has two separately scored routes: foundation rig inspection/setup, pipe handling and controlled digging; anchor/micropile rig inspection/travel, steel joint and vertical/inclined positioning. A full combined operating award requires both routes. A knowledge-only or single-route record states its limits explicitly. Successful authored materials do not constitute actual operator qualification or a completed foundation.


---

courses.title: VUC071 | VUC071 — Delivery, applications and observed assessment

content.title: VUC071 | VUC071 — Delivery, applications and observed assessment
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC071 — Delivery, applications and observed assessment
lessons.body: # VUC071 — Delivery, applications and observed assessment

lessons.title: Delivery preparation
lessons.body:
## Delivery preparation

Plan 88 hours for the combined program: 18 instruction/checks, 10 application labs, 32 supervised stations, 20 integrated practice/assessment, 4 controlled examination/review and 4 remediation/records. Extend practice when needed; record actual hours. A single-route course must explicitly identify the omitted operating route and cannot issue the combined award. Instructors and assessors require appropriate actual rig/task competence, with qualified site, lifting, geotechnical and utility personnel fulfilling their responsibilities.

Provide an inspected foundation rig and anchor/micropile rig with actual manuals/charts, approved tools/steel/casing/handlers, compatible inspected rigging, validated platform and travel paths, nonhazardous verified loads, safe cleared drilling medium, supported pipe/rod racks and alignment fixtures, measuring instruments, barriers, radios, emergency supplies and forms. Actual training drilling has predeclared safe location, geometry and maximum depth; nobody enters a shaft. Do not create live utility, collapsing ground, equipment failure or pressurized blockage to demonstrate a fault. Use photographs/tabletop cases for those conditions.

Validate machine configuration, ground reactions/platform, tool/rod retention, actual capacity and line limits, control function, clearances, utility/structure information, drilling plan and protection before delivery. Mechanical handling must be approved for the actual item and rig. Learners receive necessary data before assessment; essential operating limits cannot be hidden in the answer key.

Diagnostic: read a configuration chart, distinguish radius from tool length, interpret an angle datum, calculate weight/pressure, identify emergency stop and explain rotation/clamp exposure. Teach by explanation and a complete safe demonstration, then supervised practice with a changed case, then independent performance. Do not award from attendance or a trainer operating the controls for the learner.

lessons.title: F71 paper data
lessons.body:
## F71 paper data

Auxiliary lift gross ratings at 2/4/6 m are 4, 000/2, 800/1, 800 kg. Select next larger radius; no extrapolation; all listed suspended components count. Other limits are explicitly supplied in each case. These numbers are fictional, not actual manufacturer data. Trigonometric angles are from the stated datum, with calculations in degrees. Real rig work uses its actual validated limits.

lessons.title: Ten application labs
lessons.body:
## Ten application labs

### W01 — Scope, roles and job analysis

Packet: foundation-rig operator assigned an inclined micropile rig, public route beside the rod rack and an unassigned platform validator. Worked: identify separate operating scope, protect the complete handling/travel area and obtain platform validation. Changed: the rig is familiar but the task includes an unapproved attachment. Learner writes role/scope matrix and a job analysis with hold points, responsible parties and restart evidence. Generic statements such as be careful are insufficient controls.

### W02 — Platform and access

Paper reaction 720 kN, supplied allowable pressure 240 kPa, effective area 2.4 m². Worked ideal area 3.0 m²; actual average 300 kPa fails. Changed effective area 3.6 m² gives 200 kPa, but an adjacent new trench requires fresh review. Learner submits arithmetic and an actual validated platform/travel inspection, identifying drainage, boundaries, voids and safe setup. No actual overloaded platform is created.

### W03 — Underground trajectory and openings

Packet: entry point cleared but an inclined path crosses a service corridor; open shaft temporarily covered by an unverified panel. Worked: stop drilling for full-path verification and obtain proper opening protection. Changed: location is confirmed but nearby footing depth is unresolved. Learner marks the complete influence/trajectory and writes a change/shaft-handover record. A clear entry mark or warning tape does not automatically resolve these hazards.

### W04 — Inspection, controls and mast setup

Packet: missing tool lock, faulty emergency-stop check, ambiguous head/travel signal and unverified mast-raising clearance. Worked: each condition requires resolution before affected operation. Changed: all corrected except inspection release after repair. Hold remains. Actual lab identifies controls/manuals, safely inspects and follows approved setup/function checks. Faults remain photos or verbal injects; no protection is disconnected for realism.

### W05 — Charts and handling

Paper pipe 1, 300 kg, lifting head 250, rigging 150 at 5 m totals 1, 700 kg, leaving 100 under the 1, 800 chart. A supplied line ceiling of 1, 600 independently fails by 100. Changed pipe 1, 100 makes total 1, 500; chart margin 300 and line margin 100, subject to all remaining limits. Learner plans full path, actual approved handling method and stable laydown; demonstrates controlled actual handling with safe verified loads.

### W06 — Foundation drilling

Packet: validated training point and target depth 1.00 m ±0.04 m; safe measurement 0.93 m. Worked interval 0.96–1.04 and shortfall 0.03. Changed depth 0.99 passes, but unexpected water/formation change requires review. Actual exercise uses the instructor's independently validated dimensions, not necessarily these paper values. Learner positions, drills, withdraws/cleans safely, measures without entry and protects the opening; records all interruptions and actual results.

### W07 — Anchor/micropile geometry and steel

Paper 8 m trajectory at 30 degrees below horizontal has vertical component 4.0 m and horizontal 6.928 m. Changed angle is 30 degrees from vertical: vertical 6.928, horizontal 4.0. Learner resolves datum before setup. Actual lab demonstrates approved steel handling, vertical joint make/break and vertical/inclined positioning in a protected fixture with confirmed support at each clamp transfer. No hand alignment beside moving rotation.

### W08 — Pressure and material exposure

Paper pump 180 bar, hose 160, fitting 130: supplied ceiling 130; proposed 145 fails by 15. Changed fitting 170 leaves hose ceiling 160, subject to actual system restrictions. Learner identifies real isolation/pressure verification points without opening live lines, checks PPE/SDS/washing/containment and writes response to a simulated grout splash. No actual exposure or pressure fault is introduced. Do not improvise household chemical treatment.

### W09 — Changes, emergencies and repairs

Packet: broken dust suppression, settling track, unknown utility contact and an unexplained control restart. Worked: distinguish each stop, exposure control, emergency notification and qualified release path. Changed: utility owner clears its installation but rig damage remains. Actual lab locates emergency controls/access and performs only safe manufacturer-prescribed checks; emergencies are tabletop. Learner records facts without claiming a restart erased the incident.

### W10 — Combined handover and limits

Paper total 1, 750 kg at 5 m has 50 kg chart margin. Added retained material 120 produces 1, 870 and deficiency 70. Changed material is removed but travel leaves the validated platform. Learner submits a full changed-plan decision and separately completes actual safe securing on both rigs. Handover identifies depth measurement basis, opening protection, defects and scope earned. A foundation-rig pass cannot fill an anchor-rig observation blank.

lessons.title: Observation rubric and stations
lessons.body:
## Observation rubric and stations

Score five dimensions 0–2: correct equipment/basis, preparation/method, controlled result, safety/limits and traceable record. Zero wrong/absent/unsafe, one safe but incomplete, two complete and supported. Each station needs at least 8/10 with no zero or unresolved critical error. Unsafe rotation/clamp exposure, unsupported loads, ignored utility/platform uncertainty, capacity violation, bypass, unauthorized shaft entry or fabrication is critical. Stop actual unsafe work, record the first result, remediate and reassess with a changed case. Numerical tolerance 0.01 stated unit unless an actual approved task specifies otherwise; never round a failure into a pass.

| Station | Required evidence | Changed application |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Scope/role/authority matrix | Different rig or attachment |
| P02 actual | Site analysis and entire influence zone | Changed delivery route |
| P03 actual | Validated platform/setup inspection | Different approved location |
| P04 actual | Utility/structure verification and opening protection | Changed cleared trajectory |
| P05 actual | Both rigs' inspection and safe access | Photographic critical defect |
| P06 actual | Actual controls, signals and emergency-stop check | Different safe instruction sequence |
| P07 actual | Approved forward/reverse tramming | Changed validated route |
| P08 actual | Approved setup/alignment and mast sequence | Different safe setup point |
| P09 actual | Actual chart/configuration plan | Changed load/path |
| P10 actual | Rope/rigging/handler inspection and use | Different verified item |
| P11 actual | Tool identity, installation and retention | Different approved tool |
| P12 actual | Foundation positioning/drilling/spoil cycle | Changed safe drilling point |
| P13 | Formation/casing/extraction decision | Unexpected groundwater |
| P14 actual | Anchor-rig vertical/inclined setup | Changed specified angle |
| P15 actual | Actual steel joint, holding and placement | Different approved section |
| P16 | Pressure/SDS/isolation decision | Lower-rated connection |
| P17 actual | Exposure/weather/access controls | Simulated control loss |
| P18 | Emergency and qualified release plan | Utility clearance with rig defect |
| P19 actual | Both rigs' actual shutdown/secure/handover | End-of-day instead of brief pause |
| P20 actual | Independent integrated F71/AMP71 routes | Physical set B |

Sixteen stations require actual evidence. Recorded scopes distinguish shared observations from each rig's required performance; using one rig cannot substitute for actual inspection, control, handling and securing on the other.

lessons.title: Independent practical I71
lessons.body:
## Independent practical I71

Prepare teaching set T and assessment sets A/B separately. Qualified instructor/site personnel validate actual rig/manual/chart, tool and load IDs/weights, support/reactions, safe trajectories, approved handling fixtures and all capacity/line limits. Provide a known safe drilling medium with complete facility clearance, no shaft entry and protected holes. State actual drill location, diameter, depth, alignment tolerances and maximum safe limit in the learner packet before work. These are assessed exercise targets, not foundation design prescriptions.

Use generous capacity margins, lightweight boundary markers, supported laydown racks and adequate clearance for the actual rig/tool/load. No person is an obstacle or suspended-load guide by bodily force. Familiarization is separate from assessment. Schedule about four hours per route plus practice as required; safety and accurate performance, not speed, determine pass.

**Foundation route F71:** independently inspect and identify controls/emergency stop; review/brief platform, utilities and influence area; perform approved setup/alignment; verify actual capacity and handling arrangement; pick up a supported test pipe, place it at two approved target supports and lay it down under controlled support; position the approved drilling tool; complete two controlled drilling/withdrawal/spoil cycles within the validated target and safe maximum; safely measure and record results without entry; protect the hole and perform the appropriate shutdown/handover.

**Anchor/micropile route AMP71:** independently inspect/identify controls; verify platform and route; tram forward in approved configuration to the validated station; set up and align; handle steel using the approved system; make and break one vertical joint while maintaining confirmed support and protected hands; place steel into the validated vertical fixture and the separate inclined fixture at the declared datum/tolerance; safely secure steel and mast; reverse-tram along the approved path; shut down and hand over. Actual pressurized grouting, anchor proof testing and production foundation acceptance are outside this operator exercise.

Pass criteria for both: correct configuration and actual limits; effective signals and stop response; no person exposed to rotation, clamp, fall or track hazards; no collision, uncontrolled swing, side pull or unplanned dropped/dragged item; all required targets/tolerances met and safely supported before release; drilling remains within approved location/geometry and maximum; opening protected; all restrictions and actual results recorded. Every listed element must pass. Safe voluntary pauses are permitted and recorded; assessor intervention to prevent danger fails independent performance.

Set B changes load/target path and safe drill point for F71, or steel length/fixture angle and approved travel route for AMP71, within equivalent validated conditions. Recalculate/rebrief. Weather/equipment interruption is recorded separately from learner error; restore conditions and repeat the complete affected task. A different machine requires fresh familiarization/configuration and a complete route attempt. Retain failed evidence and retest observations.

lessons.title: Controlled assessment, remediation and credential rules
lessons.body:
## Controlled assessment, remediation and credential rules

Form A and changed Form B each have twenty original cases, three scored decisions per case, 120 points. Allow 180 minutes with calculator/coursebook, no keys or assistance. Pass at least 96/120 and at least 4/6 in every domain with no unresolved critical error. These are original VNDRLY assessments, not external CCO core/specialty examinations. Protect keys outside the learner packet; provide original situation context with changed reassessment questions.

Require all corrected formative checks, ten labs, twenty stations, written final and the actual route(s) for the award. Combined scope requires both F71 and AMP71. If only one route is demonstrated, issue a precisely named single-route record; incomplete actual work supports knowledge-only status. Never claim CCO certification, engineering authority, shaft-entry competence, well-control competence or unassessed equipment categories.

Remediation names the error, reteaches the principle with a worked example, includes changed supervised practice and then independent changed examination/performance. Keep critical-failure and correction history. Accommodations may change access or communication but cannot remove essential safe operation. VNDRLY uses a one-year review reminder, not a claim about external certification duration; reassess sooner for material task/equipment change or unsafe performance.

lessons.title: Reproducible record forms
lessons.body:
## Reproducible record forms

**Enrollment:** learner ID, diagnostic findings, prior experience, requested F71/AMP71 scope, accommodations, instructor/assessor competence, actual hours and version.

**Delivery validation:** machine/manual/chart IDs, configuration/tool/handler/rigging IDs, actual loads and limits, platform basis/validator, locate/structure information, drilling/trajectory plan and tolerances, barriers, support fixtures, weather/exposure/emergency arrangements and date.

**Observed performance:** station/route/set, actual actions and instrument readings, five rubric scores, critical error/intervention, safe stop, result, assessor/date, remediation and changed retest. Separate columns for foundation and anchor/micropile rigs where both are required.

**Drilling/handover:** work ID, location/angle datum/depth and measurement method, tooling, strata/water observations, spoil/return containment, shaft protection, deviations and authorized disposition, defects, secure state, receiving acknowledgment.

**Credential decision:** checks/labs/stations/final/route evidence, unresolved failures, exact earned scope and exclusions, version/hash, reviewer/date and review triggers. Do not prefill actual results or real site approvals.


---

courses.title: VUC071 | VUC071 formative checks

content.title: VUC071 | VUC071 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC071 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC071 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

Does a foundation-rig practical pass prove anchor/micropile rig competence?

**Answer:** No. Assess the separate rig and operating route.

**Reason/remediation:** Clamps, steel handling and inclined operation differ. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

May an operator redesign the foundation because drilling becomes difficult?

**Answer:** No. Report conditions and obtain authorized technical disposition.

**Reason/remediation:** Operating authority does not confer engineering design authority. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Is the carrier footprint the complete hazard boundary?

**Answer:** No. Include mast, swing, tool, pipe, spoil, opening and traffic interactions.

**Reason/remediation:** Hazards extend beyond the tracks. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

What should trigger a renewed job briefing?

**Answer:** A material change in work, conditions, equipment or interacting personnel.

**Reason/remediation:** A previous plan may no longer control the actual risks. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Does average track pressure establish the maximum working-platform demand?

**Answer:** No. Actual reactions and operating states must be assessed.

**Reason/remediation:** Mast position, extraction and geometry change pressure and stability. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

Can rain require a platform reassessment?

**Answer:** Yes. Drainage and ground support may change.

**Reason/remediation:** Previous acceptance is not proof after deterioration. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

Does a cleared entry point prove an inclined subsurface path is clear?

**Answer:** No. Verify the full planned trajectory.

**Reason/remediation:** The drill can intersect installations away from the entry. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

Is warning tape automatically sufficient protection for an open shaft?

**Answer:** No. Use the required approved protection arrangement.

**Reason/remediation:** A warning alone does not prevent a fall or support a load. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

Does a daily check replace a required post-repair inspection?

**Answer:** No. Their purposes and evidence differ.

**Reason/remediation:** Readiness requires all applicable checks. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Can a disappearing alarm be recorded as repaired?

**Answer:** No. Preserve the symptom until appropriate cause/correction and release are established.

**Reason/remediation:** Restart success alone is not defect closure. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Should an unfamiliar control be tried beside a helper to identify it?

**Answer:** No. Identify it from actual instructions and safe familiarization.

**Reason/remediation:** Unexpected motion can crush or entangle the helper. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Must the operator obey an emergency stop from someone other than the directing signaler?

**Answer:** Yes.

**Reason/remediation:** Immediate danger takes precedence over ordinary directing responsibility. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Can a rig always tram with its mast in the drilling position?

**Answer:** No. Follow its actual travel configuration and limits.

**Reason/remediation:** Stable drilling setup does not establish travel stability. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Does a clear route mean it has adequate bearing support?

**Answer:** No. Verify the actual route/platform basis.

**Reason/remediation:** Visual clearance does not establish ground capacity. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

May hydraulic pressure be assumed to support a mast during pin removal?

**Answer:** No. Use the actual required support and isolation procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Stored energy or failure can produce sudden movement. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

Why recheck the exclusion zone after setup?

**Answer:** Deployment changes the working envelope.

**Reason/remediation:** The transport footprint is not the operating footprint. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Can auxiliary-hoist capacity be inferred from maximum pullback?

**Answer:** No. Use the actual applicable lifting data and permission.

**Reason/remediation:** Extraction and hoisting systems/limits differ. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

May a paper chart be extrapolated beyond its largest radius?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** No rating is supplied for that condition. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Does a rod handler suit every same-diameter rod?

**Answer:** No. Verify actual compatibility, grip, weight and approved use.

**Reason/remediation:** Material, geometry and configuration affect retention. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

Does a strong winch compensate for an unidentified swivel?

**Answer:** No. Every load-bearing component must be suitable.

**Reason/remediation:** System strength is limited by each component in context. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Does a pin fitting a hole prove it is approved?

**Answer:** No. Verify its specified identity and retention.

**Reason/remediation:** Dimensions alone do not establish material or strength. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

Can a jammed Kelly be freed by uncontrolled swinging?

**Answer:** No. Stop and use the approved qualified recovery procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Impact or sudden release can cause failure or dropped tooling. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Does counting tool passes establish actual hole depth?

**Answer:** No. Use the approved measurement method.

**Reason/remediation:** Penetration per pass varies. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

May a learner enter a shaft to measure the exercise?

**Answer:** No. This course prohibits shaft entry.

**Reason/remediation:** Measurement does not waive entry/rescue hazards. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Does free casing weight establish required extraction force?

**Answer:** No. Soil resistance and other effects may be additional and unknown.

**Reason/remediation:** A lifting rating cannot be treated as breakout permission. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

Who approves a change from the dry drilling method to casing or fluid support?

**Answer:** The responsible authorized technical/site process.

**Reason/remediation:** The operator reports observations rather than inventing design changes. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Why record whether an angle is from horizontal or vertical?

**Answer:** The same number produces different trajectories.

**Reason/remediation:** A datum error can reach a utility or miss the design location. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

Does correct bore geometry establish anchor holding capacity?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Installation and engineering acceptance require separate evidence. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

May a helper hand-thread steel while the head rotates?

**Answer:** No. Use the approved protected handling/jointing method.

**Reason/remediation:** Rotating joints can entangle and crush. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

What must be established before opening a holding clamp?

**Answer:** The prescribed alternate support and sequence must be confirmed.

**Reason/remediation:** The string can drop or slide when support is transferred. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Can a fitting be loosened to determine whether a line is pressurized?

**Answer:** No. Use the authorized isolation/depressurization/verification method.

**Reason/remediation:** Loosening can release stored energy violently. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

Does wearing gloves make wet-grout exposure harmless?

**Answer:** No. Prevent contamination and use suitable PPE/hygiene/SDS response.

**Reason/remediation:** Grout inside gloves can prolong harmful exposure. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Is wind carrying dust away a substitute for required exposure controls?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The complete applicable control method or assessed alternative must be implemented. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

Can hidden landscaping fabric create auger danger?

**Answer:** Yes. It can wrap and pull material or people toward rotation.

**Reason/remediation:** Inspect and clear the work area through a safe process. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:
## Q18-L1

Does emergency stop remove all stored energy?

**Answer:** No. Hydraulic, pneumatic and gravity energy may remain.

**Reason/remediation:** Service requires actual isolation/support verification. Revisit Q18 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L2
lessons.body:
## Q18-L2

Should a tiny puncture from a hydraulic jet wait until the end of shift?

**Answer:** No. Activate immediate professional medical response.

**Reason/remediation:** Severe internal injection injury may initially look minor. Revisit Q18 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q19-L1
lessons.body:
## Q19-L1

Can an estimated depth be labeled measured?

**Answer:** No. Record the actual basis and obtain required verification.

**Reason/remediation:** False precision conceals missing quality evidence. Revisit Q19 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q19-L2
lessons.body:
## Q19-L2

Does a complete log replace physical shaft protection?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Records and physical hazard controls serve different purposes. Revisit Q19 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q20-L1
lessons.body:
## Q20-L1

Does a chart pass cancel unverified ground support?

**Answer:** No. All essential conditions must be satisfied.

**Reason/remediation:** Safe operation is not an average of passing and failing checks. Revisit Q20 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q20-L2
lessons.body:
## Q20-L2

Can a trainer's demonstration replace the learner's independent route?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Demonstration teaches; observed independent performance establishes the learner result. Revisit Q20 and perform its changed application.


---

courses.title: VUC071 | VUC071 — Source review and coverage

content.title: VUC071 | VUC071 — Source review and coverage
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC071 — Source review and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC071 — Source review and coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Current public CCO handbook DRO CH REV 01/25 was retrieved and its core outline and both practical routes reviewed. VNDRLY writes its own instruction, cases, exercises and assessments; this does not reproduce external exam content or claim CCO approval.

| Primary reference | Application |
|---|---|
| [Current drill-rig handbook](https://ccocert.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/drill-rig-operator-candidate-handbook_112024-en.pdf) | Scope across site/pre-operation, operation, technical knowledge, tooling and communications; distinct foundation and anchor/micropile practical functions. |
| [ADSC working-platform position](https://www.adsc-iafd.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/ADSC-Position-Statement-FINAL-Letterhead.pdf) | Q03: actual rig loads and geotechnical platform evaluation; industry guidance, not itself a new regulation. |
| [OSHA excavation requirements](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.651) | Q04: installation location and protection, changing excavation conditions. |
| [OSHA earth-boring hazard bulletin](https://www.osha.gov/publications/hib19900604) | Q05–06,11,15: rotating-component exposure and protective systems; historical hazard illustration, not a current machine-specific procedure. |
| [OSHA auger hazard bulletin](https://www.osha.gov/sites/default/files/publications/SHIB041608A.pdf) | Q12,17: hidden fabric and other entanglement hazards; no reliance on obsolete electrical citations in that older bulletin. |
| [ADSC anchor/micropile reminders](https://www.adsc-iafd.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/Tieback-Anchor-Micropile-Safet-Reminders.pdf) | Q15–16: hands clear of rotating steel, mechanized handling and pressure connections. Its generic clearance/manual-lift statements are not used as universal limits. |
| [OSHA construction silica](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1153) | Q17: task-appropriate complete controls or assessed alternative, not blanket respirator selection. |
| [OSHA concrete worker guidance](https://www.osha.gov/sites/default/files/publications/3221_CONCRETE.pdf) | Q16: cement skin/eye exposure prevention and prompt washing/medical response. Actual SDS and emergency procedures govern treatment. |
| [OSHA cement hygiene interpretation](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/standardinterpretations/2010-10-18) | Q16: accessible washing provisions and appropriate hygiene. No improvised chemical-neutralization instruction. |
| [HSE hydraulic injection alert](https://www.hse.gov.uk/safetybulletins/hydraulic-injection-injury.htm) | Q18: immediate professional medical response to suspected injection injury. |

Coverage: rig scope/types Q01; worksite/structures/brief Q02, 04; working platform/stability Q03; inspection/manuals/access Q05; controls/signage/safety functions/signals Q06; loading/travel Q07; assembly/setup Q08; capacity/stability charts Q09; line/rigging/mechanical handling Q10; rotary/Kelly/drifter/attachments Q11; foundation drilling/spoil Q12; groundwater/casing/formation changes Q13; AMP geometry/setup Q14; steel joints/holding/placement Q15; auxiliary fluids/pressure/grout Q16; dust/noise/weather Q17; emergencies/maintenance Q18; securing/records Q19; independent routes Q20/I71. Actual foundation and AMP observations remain separately recorded.

The handbook's summary and detailed foundation practical pages number some tasks differently. Coverage follows the functions (inspection, site controls, control identification, pipe pickup/placement/laydown, positioning/drilling and securing), not copied numbering or timing. Our original routes add explicit setup and changed-condition decisions and do not purport to be the external examination.

Full current proprietary ANSI/ASSP drilling standards and every model-specific manual were not available for clause-complete review. Actual manuals, site engineering, qualifications and observed learner performance remain required for delivery. The public ADSC cement-grout toolbox sheet was also reviewed; its suggestion to add household neutralizers was not adopted. Use the actual SDS and suitable emergency/medical instructions instead. No unsupported external-equivalence or real learner-pass claim is made. Publication and software releases are outside this materials task.

courses.title: VUC072 | VUC072 — Concrete Pump Operation

content.title: VUC072 | VUC072 — Concrete Pump Operation
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC072 — Concrete Pump Operation
lessons.body: # VUC072 — Concrete Pump Operation

lessons.title: Purpose and scope
lessons.body:
## Purpose and scope

This original VNDRLY/U program develops safe truck-mounted concrete boom-pump preparation, setup, controlled placement, cleanout and securing. The operating award requires actual machine and controlled pumping performance on the recorded equipment. It is not CCO or ACPA certification, a commercial driving license, engineering approval for supports or authority to operate every line pump, separate placing boom or high-rise system. Record actual equipment and unassessed limits.

Use current actual manufacturer instructions, applicable requirements and the validated site/pour plan. P72 numbers are fictional learning data, not real equipment ratings or engineering designs. The instructor validates equipment, ground, pipeline, concrete and training conditions before actual work. Learners must stop for missing essential information instead of guessing. Independent performance follows taught examples, checks and supervised changed practice.

lessons.title: Q01 — Responsibilities and pre-trip planning
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Responsibilities and pre-trip planning

Confirm the job's location, pour type, reach, volume, mix, planned rate, access, expected duration and cleanup arrangements. Coordinate with the pour supervisor, controlling entity and placing crew before dispatch. Identify who provides verified ground information, traffic control, pipeline support, electrical clearance and authorized mix decisions. An operator can refuse an unsafe setup; schedule pressure does not establish missing conditions.

Select actual compatible hoses, clamps, gaskets, safety pins, pads/dunnage, spill materials, tools, approved spare parts, manuals and required paperwork. Prepare appropriate PPE, weather clothing, drinking water and charged communication/remote batteries. A spare part that looks similar is not necessarily rated or approved. Plan contingencies for a delayed truck, changing weather or an unavailable washout location.

Worked: a pump arrives with enough reach but no approved location for primeout or washout. Do not improvise discharge into a storm drain; resolve containment before pumping. Changed: containment is arranged, but the specified hose and gasket sizes do not match. Fix compatibility rather than assume the clamp can compensate.

lessons.title: Q02 — Truck inspection, road readiness and route
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Truck inspection, road readiness and route

Inspect the vehicle and review required defect/repair information before driving. Confirm brakes, tires, steering, lights, mirrors, horn, emergency equipment and secure loads as applicable. Check actual travel height, width, mass, axle/route limits and permits. Driving qualifications, medical/duty-status and other applicable carrier requirements remain separate from pump operation. Do not assume a special-purpose vehicle is exempt from every road requirement.

Plan access and exit for the pump's actual dimensions, including bridges, overhead lines, weight restrictions and turning room. Avoid distractions and drive for the vehicle's stability and stopping distance. A route that worked with a different machine may not fit this one. Stop safely rather than continue under an uncertain clearance. Public-road assessment requires a separately qualified driver/assessor; this course's controlled-site maneuvers do not grant a license.

Worked P72: travel height is 4.00 m and a route has a verified 3.85 m clearance. The vehicle exceeds it by 0.15 m; choose a verified lawful alternate. Changed: alternate clearance is adequate but the bridge's permitted weight is unknown. Height alone does not approve the route. Preserve actual inspection and restriction records instead of marking ready from appearance.

lessons.title: Q03 — Pump, boom and safety-system inspection
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Pump, boom and safety-system inspection

Match actual equipment identity, manual revision, boom configuration and installed delivery system. Inspect boom sections, pins/retention, hydraulics, pipe/elbows, clamps/gaskets, hose condition, outriggers, locks, hopper guards, interlocks, controls and required emergency functions. Follow actual inspection intervals and qualified wear-measurement procedures; a pre-use glance does not replace periodic examination or a required thickness check.

Keep hands away from moving or pressure-exposed components. A worn elbow, missing clamp safety pin, faulty guard/interlock or unintended boom movement is not cured by slower pumping. Record precise symptoms and remove affected operation from service for qualified correction and required release. Do not operate a failed protection just to see whether it really matters. Water box, lubrication and fluid checks are performed under safe manufacturer procedures.

Worked: an elbow shows unusual external wear and its inspection record is overdue. Hold until suitability is established rather than assume no leak means adequate wall thickness. Changed: the elbow is replaced, but a boom retention pin is missing. Resolve the separate structural defect before operation.

lessons.title: Q04 — Site review, ground information and pour coordination
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Site review, ground information and pour coordination

Meet the responsible pour personnel and verify information rather than accepting a vague all clear. Inspect underground features, excavations, slabs, fill, soft ground, overhead obstructions, traffic, public exposure and truck staging. Include the full deployed boom, hose and delivery-truck envelope. A paved surface can conceal a vault or unsupported slab. Identify a safe operator position with sight of the work and suitable communication where visibility is limited.

Agree pour sequence, startup exclusion, hand signals, designated signaler, stopping process, concrete delivery, primeout/restart discharge area, cleanup and emergency access. Keep people out of backing and outrigger pinch zones. Reassess if another trade enters or the work moves to a different part of the structure. The setup point must serve the entire planned pour safely, not merely the first discharge location.

Worked: the initial pour is reachable, but the far end requires the boom to pass under an overhead service. Hold and revise the complete plan. Changed: the boom route is safe, but mixer trucks now need to reverse across a public walkway. Traffic/backing controls must be established separately.

lessons.title: Q05 — Outriggers, support and level
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Outriggers, support and level

Use actual maximum outrigger reactions and appropriately assessed ground/support information. Do not divide vehicle mass equally among legs. Pads and dunnage must have adequate structural capacity, effective bearing and stable placement. Excavation edges, buried services and slopes require appropriate assessment; a simple one-to-one sketch or pocket penetrometer reading alone cannot approve every ground condition. Follow the actual permissible setup distance and engineering requirements.

Deploy outriggers in the prescribed sequence with people clear and verify required extension, support and level. Partial deployment is permitted only where the actual manufacturer system and work-sector limitations authorize it; never invent a reduced-capacity rule or falsify the sensed state. Monitor support through the pour, especially after rain or vibration. Stop safely for settlement and obtain the proper recovery/support response.

P72 worked paper comparison: maximum reaction 240 kN and supplied allowable pressure 300 kPa require ideal area 0.80 m². Effective 0.60 m² gives 400 kPa and fails. Changed: effective 1.0 m² gives 240 kPa, but an unverified underground vault still prevents acceptance. These computations do not establish real soil or pad design. Use actual level tolerances, not an external test's generic number.

lessons.title: Q06 — Electrical hazards and emergency boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Electrical hazards and emergency boundaries

Survey electrical hazards before positioning, unfolding, pouring, cleaning and folding. The boom, line, concrete and hose can form hazardous paths; a rubber-looking hose is not proof of insulation. Obtain the applicable clearance/protection arrangement for actual voltage and circumstances through the responsible parties. Do not use a single remembered distance for every voltage or configuration, and do not treat a spotter as permission to enter a prohibited area.

Plan the whole motion envelope, including load/boom deflection and operator distraction. Where required, establish effective observation and clear limits. Keep unauthorized people away and treat unidentified overhead lines as hazardous until appropriately verified. For contact or suspected energization, activate the site/electrical emergency plan and keep others away from the truck, hose and surrounding exposure. Do not approach to perform an unplanned rescue.

Worked: the boom clears a line at setup, but the final placing point reduces that separation beyond the approved boundary. Stop before the move and revise the plan. Changed: the utility establishes an authorized de-energized condition for specified lines, but another nearby circuit is outside that confirmation. Do not extend the confirmation to that circuit by assumption.

lessons.title: Q07 — Boom unfolding, reach and permitted attachments
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Boom unfolding, reach and permitted attachments

Identify actual boom sections, folding pattern, control directions, limits and permitted setup. Follow the prescribed unfolding sequence and clearance envelope; do not force a section past its stop or use another machine to extend reach. A concrete placing boom is not a crane. Do not lift roof trusses, equipment or other unrelated loads from it or use a crane to improvise additional boom extension.

Check approved end-hose length, filled weight, reducers and attachment limits. Include concrete weight and all specified fittings; do not compare only empty hose mass. Approved pump attachments still need correct installation, gaskets, clamps, safety pins and required restraints. Match the complete actual configuration; arithmetic cannot authorize an unapproved attachment.

P72 worked: a supplied attachment ceiling is 180 kg. Hose 55 kg, contained concrete 100 and approved fittings 15 total 170, leaving 10. Changed: an extra reducer adds 20, making 190 and exceeding by 10. This is fictional arithmetic, not an actual tip-load rating. The operator must also verify whether that reducer/configuration is permitted at all.

lessons.title: Q08 — Delivery pipes, hoses, couplings and supports
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Delivery pipes, hoses, couplings and supports

Use components rated and compatible for the actual concrete pressure, wear condition, diameter, end style and application. The lowest suitable component rating limits the assembled system. Pipe and clamp appearance alone do not establish remaining strength. Inspect, identify and verify components through the appropriate procedure. Correct gaskets, full clamp engagement and retained safety pins matter; do not substitute wire or a mismatched coupling.

Provide designed supports, anchors and routing for actual line weight, pressure effects and movement. The applicable OSHA discharge-pipe support requirement includes design for 100 percent overload; this is not permission to increase operating pressure or improvise support calculations. Avoid trip, crush and vehicle-damage exposure along the line. Use the intended single-ended hose at discharge rather than a double-ended delivery hose with metal mass at its free end.

Worked P72: pump maximum 85 bar, pipe 100, hose 80 and clamp 75 give a supplied comparison ceiling no higher than 75. Planned 82 exceeds it by 7. Changed: clamp is replaced with a compatible 100-bar unit; the hose now limits the comparison to 80, so 82 still fails by 2. Actual suitability and permitted pressure-setting methods remain required.

lessons.title: Q09 — Concrete properties, batch information and pumping plan
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Concrete properties, batch information and pumping plan

Review the actual mix designation, aggregate/pumpability information, batch time, delivery condition and applicable acceptance requirements with the responsible pour personnel. Temperature and delays can change behavior. Do not add water or admixture on personal judgment to overcome resistance; only the authorized quality process can approve a change and record it. Apparent flowability alone does not prove the concrete meets the job specification.

Match delivery and placement rates to the pump and crew without compromising support, forms or hose control. Confirm hopper feed and avoid conditions that draw air into the system. Unexpected resistance, segregation or interruption requires communication and appropriate disposition, not ever-higher pressure. Keep batch/volume/delay records accurate so the quality team can evaluate the actual placement.

Worked P72: planned volume 12 m³ at an assumed steady 24 m³/h gives 0.5 h or 30 minutes of ideal pumping, excluding startup and interruptions. Changed: deliveries support only 18 m³/h, making ideal time 40 minutes. This is scheduling arithmetic, not permission to rush a crew or accept delayed concrete without review.

lessons.title: Q10 — Truck backing, hopper and personnel protection
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Truck backing, hopper and personnel protection

Establish a safe mixer approach, backing signaler and clear exclusion from pinch points between vehicles and equipment. The driver stops when required sight or communication is lost. Do not stand behind the mixer or between moving vehicles to guide by body position. Stabilize and secure equipment under the actual procedure before discharge. Coordinate truck changes so the operator can maintain controlled feed without distraction.

Keep hopper grates and required interlocks functioning. Never reach into the hopper, agitator, valve or moving mechanism to clear material while hazardous energy can cause motion. Use the actual lockout/tagout, verification and supported maintenance procedure for access; emergency stop alone is not full isolation. Approved tools do not make reaching around a guard safe. Protect against wet-concrete contact, slips and pinch zones around chutes.

Worked: a large object rests on the hopper grate and a worker proposes lifting the grate while the agitator runs. Stop and use the authorized clearing/isolation process. Changed: the agitator appears stopped, but remote starting remains possible. Verify full required hazardous-energy control before access.

lessons.title: Q11 — Signals, remote control and positioning
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Signals, remote control and positioning

Confirm remote identity, battery condition, control directions, emergency stop and communication before operation. Secure the remote against unintended input while handling other tasks. Do not operate by a display alone when the actual boom/hose and people are not adequately observed. Use the agreed signal arrangement for blind placement and stop if directions are unclear or conflicting.

Coordinate boom sections smoothly to keep the hose controlled and avoid kinking, dragging, impact or entanglement with structure. Do not pull a hose loose with the boom. The placing crew needs a safe standing/working platform and clear escape from the hose zone. Maintain the startup/restart exclusion until flow is confirmed safe under the procedure; a signal to approach is deliberate, not inferred from silence.

Worked: the signaler disappears behind a wall and a radio message is incomplete. Stop instead of continuing the previous direction. Changed: radio is restored, but the operator cannot establish which of two crews is directing the pump. Resolve directing responsibility before motion or flow resumes.

lessons.title: Q12 — Priming and initial flow
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Priming and initial flow

Plan the approved priming method and safe discharge destination before starting. Ensure the assembled system, supports, hose type, exclusion area and concrete supply meet the actual procedure. Priming material and initial discharge need controlled containment and authorized quality disposition; they are not automatically acceptable in the structure. Keep all people a prudent safe distance from the discharge hazard as established by the actual plan.

Air in the line can compress and release suddenly, causing violent hose movement. The first stroke and restart are therefore not routine opportunities for a worker to hold the hose steady. Start and establish flow using the actual manufacturer procedure, observing the discharge from a protected position. Do not increase output blindly when discharge is absent. Only permit the placing crew to approach after the specified safe flow condition and communication are established.

Worked: the pump starts but no material appears and the hose twitches. Stop and apply the approved pressure/blockage response; do not ask a worker to grip the hose harder. Changed: steady flow is established but the primeout discharge is contaminating a drain. Stop and correct containment; successful flow does not resolve environmental exposure.

lessons.title: Q13 — Placement, monitoring and changing conditions
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Placement, monitoring and changing conditions

During placement monitor the boom/line, hopper feed, pressure behavior, crew position, ground support, weather and interacting equipment. The operator's job is continuous control, not setting a rate and leaving. Keep the hose within permitted length/configuration and avoid kinks or unapproved rigid end fittings. Coordinate any move with the crew before motion; do not let someone ride or hang on the hose.

Stop for unexpected leakage, pipe/coupling movement, loss of support, control problems or unsafe personnel exposure. Do not service or grease a moving/pressurized hazard unless the actual procedure explicitly provides a safe authorized method. The approved pour plan also considers placing rate and structural/formwork capacity; an operator cannot increase rate solely to recover schedule time.

Worked P72: fictional plan permits 20 m³/h at the receiving work area, while pump capability is 40. A request for 30 exceeds the plan by 10 and requires authorized review, not automatic compliance. Changed: a revised plan permits 30, but a pad begins settling. The separate stability problem still requires a safe stop.

lessons.title: Q14 — Interruptions, air entry and restart
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Interruptions, air entry and restart

After a pause, changed boom position, low feed or any condition that may admit air, reassess restart hazards. Concrete draining from a downward line, aging mix or restricted flow can worsen the risk. Do not assume a pause is safe because it lasted only a few minutes. Establish the proper discharge exclusion or move the boom to an approved safe restart area when the work arrangement permits and the plan requires it.

Restart under the actual manufacturer's sequence with direct observation and controlled output. If flow is absent or stops unexpectedly, stop and use the approved pressure-relief/blockage process. ACPA guidance emphasizes separation from the discharge and confirmation of steady flow; it is not a substitute for machine-specific procedure. Never rely on a person holding a hose to prevent whip or allow early approach because a supervisor is impatient.

Worked: after a delivery delay, a downward hose has drained and a finisher waits beside it. Hold restart until the required separation and procedure are in place. Changed: the finisher moves away but an unseen crew is below the discharge level. Verify the complete hazard area before pumping, not just the people visible from the cab.

lessons.title: Q15 — Blockages, residual pressure and safe recovery
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Blockages, residual pressure and safe recovery

Recognize abnormal pressure/flow, stopped discharge, hose deformation and other signs through the actual instructions. Stop instead of forcing pressure upward. Inform and clear affected personnel and apply the authorized isolation/pressure-relief sequence. Reverse strokes or a zero indication may be part of a procedure but do not automatically prove every isolated segment is depressurized. Concrete plugs can trap pressure separately.

Do not crack a clamp to test for pressure, stand in a potential discharge path or strike a loaded line. Qualified recovery must establish a safe state, supports and verified pressure control before disassembly. Inspect and reassemble correctly after correction, then treat resumed flow as a controlled restart. Preserve the cause/repair record; do not hide an incident because production eventually resumes.

Worked: the pump gauge reads zero but a plug separates the far line section. The distant section may retain pressure. Hold opening until the authorized method verifies safe conditions for that section. Changed: pressure is safely relieved, but the removed clamp is damaged. Replace/verify suitable components before restart rather than reuse the defect.

lessons.title: Q16 — Cleanout, washout and environmental control
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Cleanout, washout and environmental control

Select the actual approved cleanout method and location before the pour. Provide containment, safe supports, exclusion and appropriate tools/PPE. Different pump/line arrangements require different procedures; do not copy a high-rise or compressed-air method to a boom system. Compressed air can store substantial energy and eject plugs, cleaning devices or material. It requires its own authorized equipment, capture/retention and trained procedure; it is not a shortcut in this ordinary practical.

For maintenance/access, isolate and verify all hazardous energy before opening guards or reaching into pump components. Safely remove attachments only after support and pressure conditions permit. Washout water and cementitious waste need authorized containment/disposal; keep drains and public routes protected. For offsite cleanout, use the actual approved transport/containment plan, considering remaining material and time, not an improvised uncovered hopper trip.

Worked: the designated washout is full and the operator suggests blowing material into an open field with compressed air. Stop and obtain an approved alternative; no unplanned projectile or discharge operation. Changed: a valid containment area is found but the crew lacks the specified cleanout capture equipment. Location alone does not authorize the method.

lessons.title: Q17 — Emergency response and occupational exposure
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Emergency response and occupational exposure

Brief the response to power contact, support loss, hose whip/line failure, hopper entrapment, hydraulic injury, fire and wet-concrete exposure. Stop and control the area without entering a secondary hazard. Untrained entry into an energized area or a moving mechanism can create more casualties. Emergency stop is an immediate control, followed by the applicable isolation, rescue and medical response.

Use suitable protection and hygiene against cement burns and eye exposure, noise, heat and other actual hazards. Promptly follow the product SDS and emergency washing/medical instructions; do not wait for pain to prove harm. Do not hand-search a hydraulic leak. Suspected injection injury needs immediate professional medical attention even with a tiny puncture. Record the actual event and preserve equipment restrictions for investigation.

Worked: grout enters a worker's boot while the pour continues. Arrange safe relief/stop and prompt decontamination/medical response as appropriate rather than waiting for shift end. Changed: exposure is addressed but the hose failure that caused it is unexplained. Keep the affected equipment restricted until qualified correction and release.

lessons.title: Q18 — Folding, travel and end-of-day handover
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Folding, travel and end-of-day handover

Follow the actual shutdown/folding sequence with the complete movement envelope clear. Verify attachments removed or stowed as required, boom seated and retained, outriggers fully retracted/secured, pads/tools restrained, PTO/control state correct and residual material safely contained. Walk around the vehicle before movement; an indicator alone does not verify every pin or protruding item.

Complete the required vehicle/pump defect reports, repair needs and job records. Prepare fuel, water, lubrication and batteries for the next job through authorized safe procedures. Record actual batch/volume/interruptions and unresolved restrictions; do not sign a safe condition that was not checked. Road readiness must be reassessed for the actual return route and driver status. One good pour does not prove a safe trip home.

Worked P72: projected travel height after incorrect stow is 4.20 m, while the verified route allows 4.10; it exceeds by 0.10. Correct actual stow and remeasure rather than choose a favorable label. Changed: height is corrected but an outrigger lock is not engaged. That separate restraint defect still prevents travel. The independent practical combines all phases, including actual controlled pumping and safe cleanout, before the operating award.


---

courses.title: VUC072 | VUC072 — Instructor and practical workbook

content.title: VUC072 | VUC072 — Instructor and practical workbook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC072 — Instructor and practical workbook
lessons.body: # VUC072 — Instructor and practical workbook

lessons.title: Preparation and teaching sequence
lessons.body:
## Preparation and teaching sequence

Plan 72 hours: 16 instruction/checks, 8 application labs, 28 supervised stations, 12 integrated practice/assessment, 4 final/review and 4 remediation/records. Extend learning as needed and retain actual hours. Instructor/assessor must be competent for the actual boom pump, concrete system, cleaning method and observed tasks. Road driving requires its separate legal qualifications and assessment; public-road operation is not created as a course exercise.

Provide inspected pump truck and current actual manuals, approved inspected delivery system and end hose, suitable pads/supports, validated stable site, known safe boom envelope, protected lightweight targets and landing areas, actual approved pumpable concrete, controlled delivery/receiving crew, approved primeout/restart/cleanout containment, PPE/SDS/washing facilities, communication and emergency supplies. Pumping uses a planned nonstructural training placement or a separately approved supervised placement with all actual job controls; do not improvise a pour to fill an assessment checkbox.

Validate ground reactions/support, setup/level/sector, electrical and traffic boundaries, pipeline ratings/wear/supports, attachment filled mass, hopper guards/interlocks, controls/emergency stops, concrete batch/pumpability acceptance and waste disposition. No fault is physically introduced into a live pressurized system. Simulate air/plug/contact/settlement problems verbally or with photographs; do not deliberately cause hose whip, blockages, entrapment or instability. All normal protections remain functioning.

Diagnostic: units, pressure versus capacity, hose filled mass, pad-area comparison, signal recognition, startup separation and distinction between stop and verified isolation. Teach a complete safe sequence, practice a changed case and assess independently. Learners receive all actual limits and targets before assessment; private keys do not contain hidden operating data.

lessons.title: Application labs
lessons.body:
## Application labs

### W01 — Dispatch and route

Packet: actual-size equipment assignment, missing cleanup location and fictional 4.10 m travel height versus 4.00 m route clearance. Worked: clearance fails by 0.10 m and cleanup is independently unresolved. Changed: verified alternative route clears the vehicle but the driver qualification/duty basis is missing. Learner submits dispatch/route checklist and accurate readiness holds; no course certificate is treated as a driving license.

### W02 — Site and support

Paper reaction 210 kN, allowable pressure 250 kPa and effective area 0.70 m². Worked ideal area 0.84 m²; pressure 300 kPa fails. Changed effective area 1.0 m² gives 210, but the point lies over an unverified slab void. Learner submits calculation and a site-specific validated setup checklist. Actual lab uses safe accepted supports only. A paper pass does not approve the void or pad strength.

### W03 — Inspection and attachment

Packet: missing clamp pin, overdue elbow examination, faulty hopper interlock; fictional attachment mass hose 60 + concrete 95 + fittings 20 = 175 kg versus 190 allowable. Worked mass margin 15 does not clear any inspection fault. Changed extra fitting 25 yields 200, exceeding by 10. Actual lab safely inspects and assembles approved depressurized/supported attachments, checking compatibility, gaskets, clamps, pins and restraints.

### W04 — Pipe pressure and routing

Paper ratings pump 100 bar, pipe 110, hose 85, clamp 90; planned 92. Worked ceiling 85 and exceedance 7. Changed rated hose 100 makes clamp 90 the lowest, so 92 still fails by 2. Learner maps actual line supports, exposure and end-hose selection and verifies actual ratings. No real overpressure is applied. Required support design and actual allowed pressure are obtained through qualified procedures, not created from this arithmetic.

### W05 — Concrete supply and signals

Paper volume 15 m³ at 30 m³/h gives 30 ideal minutes; changed supply 20 m³/h gives 45. Learner reviews batch/pumpability information and writes a delay/quality referral without unauthorized water addition. Actual lab briefs mixer/placing crews, tests signals/remote identity and demonstrates safe truck-interface positioning on a controlled site; no person stands in a moving-vehicle pinch zone.

### W06 — Boom control and startup

Packet: approved setup/envelope and primeout area, safe target positions, an absent-discharge verbal inject and a person depicted in the hose zone. Worked: establish controlled startup separation and stop on abnormal discharge; do not hold the hose to suppress whip. Changed: flow is steady but containment is breached. Actual lab performs safe boom placement and normal manufacturer-directed priming/flow with the approved material and containment. Fault cases are simulated without inducing them.

### W07 — Interruptions and pressure

Packet: delayed delivery, downward line that may have drained, crew near discharge, later zero pump gauge with a hypothetical isolated plug. Worked: use the approved restart exclusion/sequence and do not infer all line sections are depressurized. Changed: verified pressure relief but damaged clamp. Hold until suitable repair/assembly/restart. Actual lab rehearses safe communication, stop and normal planned restart; blocked-line opening is a tabletop/isolated training assembly exercise, not a live induced plug.

### W08 — Cleanup and return

Packet: full washout, missing capture equipment, a proposed compressed-air shortcut and fictional 4.25 m stowed height versus 4.15 route clearance. Worked: resolve method/location and correct excess height 0.10. Changed height corrected but outrigger restraint absent. Learner demonstrates actual approved normal cleanout and stowing, with no improvised compressed-air cleanout, and completes defect/return records. No discharge to a drain or false ready status is accepted.

lessons.title: Station scoring
lessons.body:
## Station scoring

Five dimensions 0–2: correct identity/basis, preparation/method, controlled result, safety/limits and traceable record. Zero wrong/absent/unsafe, one safe but incomplete, two complete and supported. Each station requires at least 8/10, no zero and no unresolved critical error. Bypass, hazardous hopper access, unverified pressure opening, ignored electrical/support uncertainty, uncontrolled hose exposure, unauthorized boom lifting or fabricated readiness is critical. Stop actual unsafe work and require remediation plus changed independent reassessment. Numerical tolerance 0.01 stated unit; do not round failure into passing.

| Station | Required evidence | Changed task |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Dispatch/scope/role plan | Different job/cleanup arrangement |
| P02 actual | Vehicle readiness and controlled-site walkaround | Recorded defect scenario |
| P03 actual | Pump/boom/hopper/device inspection | Photographic critical fault |
| P04 actual | Site and pour-team briefing | Changed safe placing area |
| P05 actual | Validated outrigger/support/level setup | Different approved setup |
| P06 | Electrical boundary/emergency decision | Unconfirmed nearby circuit |
| P07 actual | Actual unfolding and permitted attachment verification | Different approved configuration |
| P08 actual | Depressurized supported line/hose/clamp assembly | Different compatible component |
| P09 actual | Actual batch/supply and approved rate review | Delay/quality concern scenario |
| P10 actual | Truck interface and hopper protection | Simulated approach/guard fault |
| P11 actual | Remote/signals and controlled boom/hose movement | Changed target sequence |
| P12 actual | Actual approved priming and safe initial flow | Different approved receiving area |
| P13 actual | Actual controlled concrete placement and monitoring | Changed safe placing point |
| P14 actual | Normal planned stop/restart with separation | Air-entry scenario remains verbal |
| P15 | Blockage/residual-pressure/isolation case | Plug separating gauge and remote segment |
| P16 actual | Actual approved ordinary cleanout/containment | Alternate approved washout arrangement |
| P17 | Emergency/medical/repair-release decisions | Different simulated incident |
| P18 actual | Independent I72 and actual stow/secure/return check | Physical set B |

Fourteen stations require actual performance. Dry boom control alone cannot substitute for the required normal concrete-pumping and cleanout observations. If wet operation is unavailable, issue only a limited dry-control/knowledge record, not the full operating award.

lessons.title: I72 independent practical
lessons.body:
## I72 independent practical

Prepare separate teaching T and assessment A/B plans. Validate actual equipment, operator/crew roles, site/support/level/sector, electrical clearances, full boom envelope, attachments and filled masses, delivery ratings/supports, batch acceptance, pressure/rate limits, PPE, controls, receiving and washout arrangements. Use an appropriately small planned concrete volume and safe placement area validated by the responsible instructor/pour team; record actual material and volume. There is no universal minimum volume that substitutes for demonstrating all required functions.

Set three safe boom/hose target areas with clear marked boundaries and a route requiring coordinated section movement and an approved change in height. Targets and all clearances are established from the actual machine/site plan, with people outside the motion/hose zone. Do not copy external test dimensions or attach unapproved weights/chains. Learner packet specifies all target boundaries, safe elevations and permitted contact/support conditions before work. Schedule about four hours plus familiarization; no speed score rewards rushed movement.

Independent sequence: review dispatch/vehicle/pump documents; perform inspection; survey/brief; verify site/support and electrical/traffic controls; set up and unfold; safely assemble permitted attachments; demonstrate remote and signals; move hose to all three targets without collision, dragging, kinking or unplanned contact; verify actual concrete/batch and crew readiness; perform approved priming and confirm steady flow with the hazard zone clear; conduct controlled placement at two approved receiving points; perform one normal planned stop/restart with renewed separation and observed safe flow; stop and clean through the approved ordinary method; remove/support attachments as prescribed; fold/stow/secure and complete travel/handover checks.

Pass requires every critical limit and sequence, correct response to signals, all target placements inside the predeclared safe boundaries, protected people, proper supported/retained attachments, effective guards, no pressure opening without verified safe state, controlled concrete discharge and containment, actual planned restart and safe completed cleanout/stow. All restrictions and actual observations must be recorded. A verbal fault inject during a safe pause tests recognition without creating the condition. Do not deliberately admit air, create a blockage, bypass an interlock or approach a live power line.

Assessor intervention to prevent danger fails independent performance. Safe voluntary pauses are permitted. Weather/equipment interruption is recorded separately; restore safe conditions and repeat the complete affected task. Set B changes approved target sequence, placing/containment point or compatible attachment within a newly validated plan.
