lessons.title: VUC076 — Sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC076 — Sources and coverage

Review basis: 18 November 2026. Original VNDRLY teaching and assessments, using accessible primary sources. This is not an accredited IWCF programme or evidence of full access to proprietary curricula. Publisher topic lists establish scope; they do not supply a universally applicable operating procedure.

| Source | Material used and boundary | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| [IWCF Enhanced Well Control](https://www.iwcf.org/programmes/enhanced-well-control/) | Published advanced topic list and team/simulator emphasis. Used as a coverage crosswalk, not an accreditation claim or copied curriculum. | Q01–Q16; W01–W08; P01–P16 |
| [IWCF Drilling Well Control](https://www.iwcf.org/programmes/drilling-well-control-programme/) | Distinction between operator/supervisor roles and surface/combined scope. External awards remain separate. | Q01/Q13/Q16; intake and individual role evaluation |
| [IWCF public Level 3/4 syllabus](https://www.iwcf.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/TF-0020-IWCF-Drilling-Well-Control-Syllabus-Level-3-and-4.pdf) | Document identifies July 2017 version 8; the 2025 upload path is not treated as a revision date. Selected unusual-state and equipment objectives support scope only. | Q11–Q13 |
| [IWCF syllabus framework](https://www.iwcf.org/the-iwcf-syllabus-framework/) | Outcome-based, safety-critical assessment approach. | Essential outcomes and critical-failure rules |
| [Wild Well Technical Data Book](https://d3skwd56lw9z1l.cloudfront.net/files/wildwellcontrol-files/Documents/Resources/Technical-Data-Book-English.pdf), linked by [publisher downloads](https://www.wildwell.com/about/downloads-1) | Selected pressure, volume and contingency-method references cross-check original calculations. Simplifying assumptions are explicit. Dated generic equipment criteria are not adopted. | Q02–Q10/Q13; original calculations and changed cases |
| [SLB stripping](https://glossary.slb.com/terms/s/stripping) | Pressure-contained pipe movement and force considerations; equipment-specific procedure still required. | Q07/W04/P07 |
| [SLB bullhead](https://glossary.slb.com/en/terms/b/bullhead) | Injection destination and weak-zone risk. | Q09/W05/P09 |
| [SLB reverse circulation](https://glossary.slb.com/terms/r/reverse_circulation) | Flow-path direction and return-path implications. | Q10/W06/P10 |
| [IADC WellSharp definitions revision 2](https://iadc.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/04/WSP_Definitions_rev2.pdf) | Formation-breathing terminology; no inference that apparent breathing excludes influx. Not represented as the complete current curriculum. | Q04/W02/P04 |
| [Wild Well non-shearable definition](https://www.wildwell.com/glossary/non-shearable) | Installed capability matters; sealing capability is considered separately. | Q11/P11 |
| [CSB Pryor Trust final-report release](https://www.csb.gov/csb-issues-final-report-into-fatal-gas-well-blowout/) | Public investigation summary supports barrier, detection, alarm and emergency-learning discussion. Synthetic quantities and injects are labeled original. No claim of reviewing every page of the full report. | Q14/W07/P14 |
| [BSEE January 2026 abandonment inspection criteria](https://www.bsee.gov/sites/bsee.gov/files/2026-01/A-PINCs%20%28January%202026%29.pdf) | Selected abandonment/isolation and verification entries; not a complete jurisdictional compliance audit. | Q15/W08/P15 |
| [AER well abandonment overview](https://www.aer.ca/understanding-resource-development/project-life-cycle/suspension-and-abandonment/how-are-wells-abandoned) | Lifecycle planning and remaining responsibilities. Jurisdiction-specific rules are not generalized globally. | Q15 |

lessons.title: Coverage and delivery decisions
lessons.body:
## Coverage and delivery decisions

Every Q chapter has two explained formative checks, an original controlled final case and a changed reassessment case. Matching P stations test the essential outcomes. W labs develop the calculations and decisions before evaluation; I76 integrates individual technical performance and crew communication. Horizontal geometry, volumetric control, stripping, lubricate/bleed, bullheading, reverse circulation, fingerprinting, unusual conditions, advanced equipment, incident learning and abandonment all receive instructional and assessment treatment.

The course supplies executable discrete state-board cases for teaching. Full dynamic operator/supervisor awards require observed execution on a validated simulator with its actual control mapping, well model, response criteria and approved schedules. Those equipment inputs are delivery configuration, not permission to substitute fictional classroom numbers for a field procedure. A desktop-only result is expressly limited to decision study. Surface and combined subsea scopes are distinguished, and each claimed method must be demonstrated.

No third-party examination bank is reproduced. Original private forms and keys remain outside the public package. Unavailable enhanced proprietary instructor manuals and the failed historical scanned BSEE extraction are not claimed as reviewed. The inaccessible older presentation is not relied upon. Public-source authorship is complete within these disclosed boundaries; external accreditation, learner qualification and publication are separate.

courses.title: VUC077 | VUC077 — Well Control in Design and Lifecycle Management

content.title: VUC077 | VUC077 — Well Control in Design and Lifecycle Management
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC077 — Well Control in Design and Lifecycle Management
lessons.body: # VUC077 — Well Control in Design and Lifecycle Management

lessons.title: Purpose and entry requirements
lessons.body:
## Purpose and entry requirements

This original VNDRLY/U course teaches engineers, planners and integrity personnel to make and document defensible well-control decisions throughout a well's life. It is not an IWCF award, professional engineering license, complete well-design qualification or authorization to approve a real well. Entrants need basic well design/intervention knowledge, introductory well-control competence and awareness of crew resource management. Diagnose gaps before advanced work. Use the individual project and changed oral defense to demonstrate reasoning, not attendance alone.

All numerical data below belong to fictional D77. Assigned allowable values are exercise inputs, not industry defaults. The course covers the published compulsory design/lifecycle topics and the listed optional subjects at decision-review level. Advanced material selection, structural analysis, relief-well engineering and jurisdictional approvals require qualified specialist work. Real field documents must be reviewed against applicable current law, standards, installed equipment and subsurface evidence.

lessons.title: Q01 — Design decisions as lifecycle commitments
lessons.body:
## Q01 — Design decisions as lifecycle commitments

A well design is a set of future operating possibilities and constraints. The design team must consider construction, production or injection, interventions, suspension and abandonment before selecting the initial architecture. A choice that simplifies drilling can make later isolation, surveillance or access difficult. Begin with the well's purpose, expected fluids and pressures, credible changes, environment, service life and eventual disposition. Record why alternatives were selected or rejected, who owns unresolved assumptions and what evidence is needed before each release gate.

Separate the operator's accountability, technical design authority, independent examination, contractor execution and regulator's role. A reviewer signature is evidence of a defined review, not transfer of every responsibility. Deliver a design basis, barrier strategy, operating envelope, verification plan and lifecycle handover requirements together. Keep revisions connected so a drawing change cannot leave an obsolete pressure limit in the field procedure.

**Worked case:** an existing producer is proposed for injection. The team cannot approve conversion solely because the tree pressure rating exceeds the proposed surface pressure. Fluid compatibility, pressure/thermal loads, annular isolation, monitoring and abandonment consequences need review. **Changed case:** ownership changes but service does not. Transfer actual records and unresolved integrity issues; a new company name does not reset equipment condition or remove restrictions.

lessons.title: Q02 — Subsurface evidence and pressure windows
lessons.body:
## Q02 — Subsurface evidence and pressure windows

Use offset data, geology, seismic interpretation, pore-pressure estimates, formation-strength information, faults and uncertainty to build a depth-referenced hazard model. An offset well is evidence, not a guarantee: depletion, compartmentalization and local formations can differ. Distinguish measured observations, interpreted values and conservative assumptions. State datum and true vertical depth for pressure calculations; measured length belongs in volume and friction models.

For the original D77 screening interval at 10,000 ft TVD, assigned pore-pressure equivalent is 12.0 ppg and formation-strength equivalent 14.5 ppg. Their simplified pressure equivalents are 6,240 and 7,540 psi using 0.052 × ppg × TVD. The raw difference is 1,300 psi. Assigned uncertainty reduces the usable comparison to pore upper bound 12.4 and strength lower bound 14.0: 6,448 and 7,280 psi, difference 832. Neither number is a final operating window; surge, swab, circulation and prescribed margins still matter.

**Worked case:** the forecast enters a depleted zone beneath a higher-pressure layer. Evaluate isolation and the conflicting limits rather than averaging pressures. **Changed case:** new data move pore upper bound to 13.2 while strength lower remains 14.0. The raw bounded difference falls to 416 psi. Escalate the changed design basis before committing to the old plan.

lessons.title: Q03 — Holistic architecture and combined loads
lessons.body:
## Q03 — Holistic architecture and combined loads

Casing, cement, wellhead, completion and pressure-control equipment interact. Establish load cases for construction, pressure testing, production, injection, thermal cycling, evacuation, intervention and abandonment. Burst, collapse, axial force, buckling and combined effects cannot be accepted through one nominal pressure number. Consider how an internal pressure change affects surrounding annuli and how installation tolerances affect the available barrier envelope.

An original screening card gives internal pressure 6,200 psi, external pressure 1,800 and an already-derived allowable differential of 5,000 for one stated load case. Differential is 4,400, utilization 88%, numerical residual 600. This comparison checks only that supplied criterion. It does not calculate material strength or combined-load capacity. If external pressure falls to 800, differential becomes 5,400, utilization 108% and excess 400: reject that case even though internal pressure is unchanged.

**Worked case:** the design passes a production burst check but lacks an evacuation/collapse assessment. Hold design release pending all credible load combinations. **Changed case:** a proposed alternate connector has the same size and nominal rating but unknown seal/temperature performance. Request qualified compatibility and load-envelope evidence; do not accept catalog similarity as interchangeability. Preserve assumptions in the design dossier so later changes can be tested against them.

lessons.title: Q04 — Uncertainty, sensitivity and decision gates
lessons.body:
## Q04 — Uncertainty, sensitivity and decision gates

A single best estimate hides the uncertainty that drives failure. Keep a register of uncertain inputs, source quality, plausible bounds, consequence, owner, required evidence and decision deadline. Explore physically credible combinations rather than adding unrelated extremes without explanation. Sensitivity analysis identifies which input changes the decision most; it does not prove a low-probability event impossible. A model should be reconciled with actual observations as drilling or operation proceeds.

For D77, an assigned dynamic equivalent-density increment of 0.6 ppg added to a selected 13.0 ppg fluid yields 13.6 ppg at the specified comparison location. Against lower strength bound 14.0 the raw residual is 0.4 ppg, or 208 psi at 10,000 ft. If the dynamic increment is instead 1.0, the model reaches 14.0 and leaves zero raw residual before any required margin. The team cannot turn an uncertain friction estimate into a fixed safe limit.

**Worked case:** the uncertainty owner promises better data after the casing decision. Identify whether the decision is reversible and whether the missing information could invalidate it; hold or select a justified alternative before the gate. **Changed case:** measurements narrow the range but come from an uncalibrated sensor. Verify measurement quality before claiming uncertainty reduction. Keep both the original forecast and the revised basis rather than overwriting inconvenient history.

lessons.title: Q05 — Barrier envelopes and independence
lessons.body:
## Q05 — Barrier envelopes and independence

Draw the full path from each pressure source to every potential receptor, including internal tubular paths, annuli, behind-casing communication, control lines and connections. Define the required barrier functions for each lifecycle phase and transition. A barrier element is a component of the envelope; two components do not automatically provide two complete independent barriers. Identify common dependencies such as cement placement, shared controls, power or monitoring.

For each claimed barrier, specify function, operating limits, verification method, acceptance criteria, current evidence, owner and response to impairment. State changes during displacement, testing, maintenance or equipment removal may temporarily remove a barrier. Plan the permitted transition and compensating arrangements through the applicable approval process before work begins. Do not retroactively call an unplanned loss of protection a planned transition.

**Worked case:** two valve symbols appear in series, but both depend on a failed common hydraulic supply and neither has current sealing evidence. The review cannot count two proven independent barriers. It must establish actual state and hold the affected transition. **Changed case:** valves are verified but an annular path bypasses both. Repair the envelope analysis; the number of valves inside the tubing does not isolate that path. A barrier drawing becomes useful when it predicts where fluid can travel and what evidence stops that conclusion.

lessons.title: Q06 — Cement integrity and placement evidence
lessons.body:
## Q06 — Cement integrity and placement evidence

Cement design addresses zonal isolation and the expected mechanical, thermal and chemical service. Placement depends on hole geometry, centralization, fluid compatibility, displacement efficiency, losses, contamination and temperature/pressure history. Laboratory suitability of a slurry is necessary evidence for its purpose but does not prove it was placed correctly downhole. Record planned versus actual volumes, returns, pressures, density, mixing and timing; investigate discrepancies before relying on the cement as a barrier.

Original C77 has an assigned annular volume of 180 bbl and an exercise planning allowance of 15%, giving 207 bbl. This allowance is not a universal cement excess. If the validated slurry yield is 1.5 ft³ per sack and 1 bbl is 5.615 ft³, the theoretical requirement is 774.87 sacks, rounded up to 775 for this arithmetic exercise. Actual job design must include its full volumes and mixing constraints. A revised annular estimate of 200 bbl with the same assigned allowance becomes 230 bbl and 860.9667 theoretical sacks, or 861 rounded up.

**Worked case:** pumped volume matches plan but losses occurred. Do not infer cement top or isolation from pumped volume alone; obtain the applicable evaluation and remedial decision. **Changed case:** a bond-related log is available but conditions limit its interpretation. Combine qualified interpretation with placement and test evidence; no single attractive trace proves every possible flow path sealed.

lessons.title: Q07 — Verification methods and acceptance before testing
lessons.body:
## Q07 — Verification methods and acceptance before testing

Choose a verification method for the function and differential direction it must prove. Function testing, positive pressure testing, negative/inflow testing, logging and monitoring answer different questions. A positive test does not automatically demonstrate behavior when pressure reverses. Define the configuration, instruments, stabilization requirements, duration, acceptance criteria, communication paths and response to inconsistent readings before conducting the test.

Original T77 is a desktop record, not permission to pressure-test a real well. Its assigned criterion after stabilization is pressure decrease no greater than 20 psi over ten minutes with no unexplained flow. A record from 3,000 to 2,992 psi declines 8 and satisfies only that numerical criterion. A separate unexplained flow observation prevents acceptance. Another record from 3,000 to 2,970 declines 30 and fails the assigned pressure criterion even if no visible flow is reported.

**Worked case:** the test team explains a contradictory gauge as a nuisance after seeing the result. Hold acceptance and investigate configuration/instrument behavior; do not invent a new criterion to fit the trace. **Changed case:** the planned next phase reverses the differential. The reviewer requests verification suitable for that phase rather than treating the previous positive test as universal proof. Retain raw traces and unsuccessful attempts alongside the final interpretation.

lessons.title: Q08 — Designing for influx and loss of the normal envelope
lessons.body:
## Q08 — Designing for influx and loss of the normal envelope

Design must make detection and response feasible, not merely state that the rig will handle a kick. Assess likely influx properties, pressure/volume evolution, formation limits, flow paths, BOP capability, choke/kill systems and surface handling. Establish the operating envelope and triggers for suspension or specialist support. Kick tolerance depends on geometry, fluid, influx assumptions and the chosen method; a single generic barrel threshold is not a complete design.

In a simplified static shoe comparison, assigned allowable total pressure is 5,000 psi at 7,000 ft TVD with uniform 12 ppg above it. Hydrostatic contribution is 4,368 psi and raw surface allowance 632. At 13 ppg the contribution is 4,732 and allowance 268. Equipment with a larger working-pressure rating does not increase the formation-based allowance. Gas distribution, friction and other weak points can further constrain the actual response.

**Worked case:** a larger influx than modeled threatens the verified handling path. The office team supports the site's approved response with validated data and specialists; it must not issue improvised valve instructions. **Changed case:** losses undermine the assumed hydrostatic barrier. Reassess the method and barrier state rather than simply increasing fluid density. Document stop criteria, escalation ownership and the evidence required before returning to normal operation.

lessons.title: Q09 — Lifecycle surveillance and annular-pressure interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q09 — Lifecycle surveillance and annular-pressure interpretation

A well's integrity state changes with pressure, temperature, corrosion, wear, intervention and aging. Establish surveillance that can detect relevant failure modes early enough to act. Trends require context: operating phase, fluid levels, temperature, tubing/annulus relationships, instrument calibration and prior interventions. Annular pressure can have different causes; a momentary low reading is not proof that a persistent source has disappeared.

Original A77 has an assigned annular limit of 800 psi and a separate action threshold of 650. Readings of 400,520 and 680 show that the latest value is 30 above the action threshold despite remaining 120 below the absolute assigned limit. Apply the specified response at the threshold; do not wait for the maximum. If pressure returns after an authorized diagnostic bleed, preserve the time/volume/rebuild record and assess the source. This course does not authorize bleeding an actual annulus.

**Worked case:** a dashboard is green because it compares only with the absolute maximum. Correct the operational interpretation and response logic through controlled change. **Changed case:** an annulus no longer holds its expected pressure and needs repeated top-ups. Low pressure can also indicate loss of integrity. Investigate and record additions, fluid and cross-annulus behavior instead of assuming lower means safer.

lessons.title: Q10 — Risk management and defensible acceptance
lessons.body:
## Q10 — Risk management and defensible acceptance

Begin with credible initiating events and consequences, then identify prevention, detection, control and mitigation. A risk matrix is a communication aid; its colored cell does not replace engineering requirements or prove that additional controls are unnecessary. Distinguish inherent risk, actual controls with evidence, and residual risk under stated assumptions. Include uncertainty, human performance, simultaneous operations and common causes. Assign owners and expiry/review triggers to temporary arrangements.

For an original planning exercise, a scenario likelihood category 3 and consequence category 5 gives a product score of 15. A proposed control is said to reduce likelihood to 1, yielding 5, but no reliability or implementation evidence is supplied. The arithmetic is correct; the reduction is not justified. Categories are ordinal screening labels, not measured probabilities or a quantitative expected-loss calculation.

**Worked case:** a schedule benefit is offered as the sole reason to proceed with an unresolved barrier anomaly. Require the technical and governance basis for safe disposition; production pressure does not restore a barrier. **Changed case:** a lower score is justified but a mandatory criterion still fails. Hold that criterion until corrected or a legally permitted, properly authorized alternative is established. The acceptance record must name the decision maker, evidence, limitations and review point, not merely contain signatures.

lessons.title: Q11 — Human and organizational performance
lessons.body:
## Q11 — Human and organizational performance

Office design decisions reach the worksite through drawings, programs, meetings, software and shift handovers. Every interface can lose assumptions or blur responsibility. Use plain-language operating limits, explicit hold points and closed-loop confirmation of critical changes. Invite frontline challenge before approval; personnel familiar with actual equipment may identify a control or access mismatch invisible in a design model.

The CSB Macondo investigation emphasizes management of safety-critical elements and their assurance, not reliance on personal-injury statistics as proof of major-hazard control. Apply that distinction to original D77: a team reports months without recordable injuries while barrier verification actions are overdue. The first metric cannot cancel the second. Review leading evidence such as unresolved test failures, impairment duration and quality of changes, while preserving incident/near-miss learning.

**Worked case:** a contractor uses revision B while the office has approved revision C with a different limit. Stop the affected operation at its safe state, reconcile documents and verify the team's understanding before release. **Changed case:** the right revision is present but the operator cannot explain the abort condition. Rebrief and verify comprehension. Avoid treating a signed attendance sheet as proof that a critical instruction can be executed under pressure.

lessons.title: Q12 — Corrosion and material-selection decisions
lessons.body:
## Q12 — Corrosion and material-selection decisions

Material suitability depends on the actual environment: fluid composition, water, gases, temperature, pressure, stress, erosion and foreseeable changes. Uniform wall loss is only one mechanism. Localized attack, cracking, galvanic effects and nonmetallic degradation may invalidate a simple corrosion allowance. Specify traceable material, service limits and inspection/monitoring evidence; substitutions require more than matching dimensions.

Original M77 has measured minimum wall 8.0 mm, an assigned required minimum 6.0 and a hypothetical constant uniform loss rate 0.2 mm/year. The simple time to that minimum is ten years. At 0.4 mm/year it is five. This is a sensitivity illustration, not an inspection interval or remaining-life approval. Local pits, measurement uncertainty, combined loads or changing chemistry require qualified analysis and may make either number irrelevant.

**Worked case:** CO₂/H₂S or water content differs from the design basis. Refer the change to qualified materials and well-integrity personnel and revisit the envelope before accepting continued service. **Changed case:** a replacement seal is rated for the nominal pressure but lacks compatibility at expected temperature. Hold acceptance pending exact service evidence. Retain lot/material records, approved deviations and inspection results so later reviewers can identify what was actually installed.

lessons.title: Q13 — Maintenance as preservation of barrier function
lessons.body:
## Q13 — Maintenance as preservation of barrier function

Link each safety-critical function to equipment, failure modes, preventive tasks, tests, acceptance criteria and records. Scheduling maintenance is not completion; a closed work order without test evidence may conceal an unavailable function. Consider access, isolation, spare-part suitability, competence and the temporary barrier state created by maintenance. Restore and verify the complete affected system before handing it back.

Original backlog B77 contains twelve due tasks, four completed and eight outstanding. Two outstanding tasks concern required barrier verification. Overall completion is 33.33%, but the percentage alone does not express the risk of those two. Prioritize through the actual failure consequences and operating restrictions. Deferral requires documented review, compensating measures where valid, ownership and a time/condition limit; repeatedly extending a date is not a control.

**Worked case:** a valve is replaced and its actuator moves correctly, but required sealing verification was omitted. Keep the affected function restricted until the required evidence exists. **Changed case:** the part is correct but maintenance has left a monitoring line isolated. Include configuration restoration in acceptance; a local repair can impair another protective function. Records should allow the next shift to distinguish restored, restricted and unknown status without guessing.

lessons.title: Q14 — Integrity assurance and independent challenge
lessons.body:
## Q14 — Integrity assurance and independent challenge

Assurance asks whether the management system and its evidence actually establish well integrity. Sample traceable records from design assumptions through installed configuration, tests, surveillance, anomalies and corrective action. Independence means the reviewer can challenge the decision without simply approving their own unexamined work. It does not mean the operator can delegate away responsibility. Apply the jurisdiction's actual examination and verification arrangements rather than claiming one global legal scheme.

For original audit S77, eighteen of twenty sampled records have complete traceability, giving 90%. The missing two concern a barrier transition and a material substitution. Do not report the well safe merely because the percentage is high. Evaluate the consequence of each missing record and whether the missing evidence reflects a physical or procedural failure. Close findings only after the promised correction is verified.

**Worked case:** an examiner's concern is marked closed because a response email was sent. Check whether the evidence resolves the concern and whether the affected operation remained within its restrictions. **Changed case:** the evidence is sound but refers to another well serial number. Traceability fails until the correct configuration is established. A defensible assurance report separates sampled findings, unexamined areas, residual uncertainties and recommendations.

lessons.title: Q15 — Shallow hazards and early construction
lessons.body:
## Q15 — Shallow hazards and early construction

Early hole sections may lack the formation strength and pressure-control configuration assumed for deeper operations. Assess shallow gas, water flow, unstable sediments, faults and nearby existing wells using appropriate surveys and offset records. Plan location, casing, detection, response, diversion where applicable, evacuation and equipment exposure with specialist input. Do not transpose a conventional shut-in sequence into a shallow weak-formation situation without the approved design.

MMS/BSEE Safety Alert 212 describes a shallow-gas event where an older well log contained relevant information not recognized in the new well plan. The training lesson is to reconcile all available evidence, not assume seismic alone resolves the hazard. Diverter arrangement and exposure of personnel/equipment are part of the system review. This course supplies no universal diverter size, line routing or shallow-hole depth rule.

**Worked case:** D77 seismic interpretation shows low concern, but an offset log flags a potentially gas-bearing shallow interval. Hold the hazard closeout and obtain qualified reconciliation and the appropriate revised plan. **Changed case:** a plan is approved but the actual equipment layout places vulnerable services in the predicted exposure area. Review the installed arrangement and revise controls before drilling. A documented survey is not useful if its implications never reach the rig.

lessons.title: Q16 — Suspension and abandonment from the start
lessons.body:
## Q16 — Suspension and abandonment from the start

Design for eventual isolation of every potential flow path and the evidence needed to demonstrate it. Suspension is a managed lifecycle state, not indefinite abandonment without a plan. Permanent abandonment must address subsurface isolation, annuli, materials, verification and residual responsibilities under the applicable jurisdiction. Preserve as-built geometry and condition so future work does not depend on an optimistic original drawing.

Original P77 has two proposed internal plugs but a behind-casing path is not addressed and one placement record is absent. The number of plugs is not enough to release the transition. Map the source-to-receptor routes, determine the actual barrier requirements, resolve placement and verification, and obtain the responsible approval. Avoid universal plug-length or test-pressure claims; geology, regulation and condition determine the design.

**Worked case:** pressure rebuilds after a nominally successful test. Retain the hold and investigate the source rather than discarding the new observation. **Changed case:** a suspended well has no current surveillance owner after an organizational change. Restore accountability, records and risk-based review before treating it as safely unattended. The final handover must identify what remains, how it was verified, and who carries the continuing obligations.

lessons.title: Q17 — Tertiary response and source-control readiness
lessons.body:
## Q17 — Tertiary response and source-control readiness

Plans for loss of normal control must connect technical options, logistics, command, personnel protection and environmental response. Specialist measures may include source control, capping, containment or relief-well planning as applicable. Their feasibility depends on the actual well, access, pressure/temperature/flow envelope and available resources. A telephone number or equipment brochure is not proof that an option can be deployed in time or safely.

Original R77 assigns mobilization 18 hours, transport 30 and setup/verification 12 with no overlap in this exercise: total 60 hours. A changed transport constraint adds 24, giving 84. These are planning arithmetic, not promised emergency response times. Evaluate weather, access, interfaces, specialist availability and dependencies, then identify alternatives and protective measures. Concurrent stages require an explicit justified schedule rather than silently subtracting time.

**Worked case:** the nominated capping equipment does not match the installed interface. Escalate the feasibility gap before operation, not after a blowout. **Changed case:** a relief-well concept exists but no subsurface targeting or rig access analysis supports it. Record it as unverified capability and obtain specialist work. Learners prepare an escalation and readiness review; they do not acquire authority to design or execute a relief well.

lessons.title: Q18 — Lifecycle change, project report and handover
lessons.body:
## Q18 — Lifecycle change, project report and handover

Changes in use, fluid, temperature, pressure, completion, ownership or service life can invalidate prior assumptions. A management-of-change record should identify the initiating change, affected barriers and load cases, technical evidence, approvals, implementation, training, document updates and verification before closure. Small changes can accumulate into a different operating envelope even when no individual work order looks major.

The final D77 project asks for a supported disposition, not a production-ready engineering design. Synthesize subsurface uncertainty, pressure/load screening, cement/test evidence, barrier paths, surveillance, maintenance, specialist limits and abandonment. Recommend proceed only for a clearly defined phase whose evidence is adequate; otherwise state the exact hold and evidence required. Do not conceal missing evidence with a polished executive summary.

**Worked case:** a project report recommends holding conversion because materials compatibility and annular isolation remain unverified, while allowing only already-approved surveillance within the existing envelope. That is a useful bounded decision. **Changed case:** new evidence resolves compatibility but not isolation. Revise only the resolved item and retain the other hold. Handover includes actual configuration, limits, evidence status, unresolved items, named owners and restart requirements. An oral defense with changed facts tests whether the candidate understands the report rather than reproducing a template.


---

courses.title: VUC077 | VUC077 — Application, instructor and assessment materials

content.title: VUC077 | VUC077 — Application, instructor and assessment materials
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC077 — Application, instructor and assessment materials
lessons.body: # VUC077 — Application, instructor and assessment materials

lessons.title: Delivery plan
lessons.body:
## Delivery plan

64 planned hours: 18 instruction, 12 guided laboratories, 18 independent project work, 10 observed review/defense and 6 assessment/remediation planning. The schedule is VNDRLY's design, not IWCF's minimum or accreditation. A competent well-engineering/integrity instructor facilitates; a reviewer able to challenge the candidate's technical reasoning evaluates the project. Use controlled documents, a calculator/spreadsheet, graphing tools and the fictional dossier below. No live-well manipulations, pressure tests, injected failures or physical equipment operation occur.

Entry diagnostic: explain TVD versus MD, pressure versus force, barrier versus element, an influx indicator, and why test direction matters. Review prior introductory well-control learning and role experience. Remediate gaps before advanced calculations. Allow accessible text, extra reading time and oral explanation where appropriate; independently assessed decisions and essential outcomes remain required. The authoring package is not evidence that a learner has passed.

lessons.title: D77 original project dossier
lessons.body:
## D77 original project dossier

You are reviewing a producer's proposed conversion to injection. The current approved production envelope remains in force unless the exercise explicitly says otherwise. The proposed conversion is NOT approved. No fictional data authorize real work. Use the following supplied evidence and identify missing technical work rather than inventing it.

| Record | Supplied facts | Review implication |
|---|---|---|
| D1 subsurface | Screening interval 10,000 ft TVD; nominal pore 12.0 ppg and strength 14.5; bounded pore upper 12.4/strength lower 14.0 | Evaluate bounded and dynamic margins; data quality and model remain part of decision |
| D2 dynamic screen | Selected fluid 13.0 ppg; assigned increment 0.6, possible 1.0 | Raw residual 0.4 or 0.0 ppg before required margins; no final operating approval |
| D3 structural screen | Internal 6200/external 1800 psi; supplied allowable differential 5000 for this single case |4400/88%/600 residual; external 800 changes to 5400/108%/400 excess |
| D4 shoe screen | TVD7000, assigned total limit 5000 psi; compare 12 and 13 ppg | Surface residual 632 versus 268; not full kick tolerance |
| D5 cement | Annular estimate 180 bbl; assigned allowance 15%; yield 1.5 ft³/sack; conversion 5.615 ft³/bbl; losses recorded during placement |207 bbl/775 rounded sacks is planning arithmetic; isolation evidence still unresolved |
| D6 test | Assigned stabilized criterion≤20 psi drop/10 min AND no unexplained flow; trace 3000→2992; observer reports unexplained flow | Do not accept despite 8 psi numerical decline |
| D7 barriers | Two internal valves drawn; common control supply; annular bypass path unresolved; no current sealing record for one valve | Independence, complete envelope and verification unresolved |
| D8 surveillance | Assigned annulus action 650/limit 800; trend 400,520,680 psi; pressure rebuild noted after an authorized diagnostic | Action threshold crossed; investigate under current approved response |
| D9 materials | Minimum wall 8.0 mm; assigned required 6.0; hypothetical uniform rate 0.2/year; new fluid compatibility not established | Ten-year simplified sensitivity is not a service-life approval; conversion requires specialist evidence |
| D10 maintenance |12 due tasks, 4 closed; 2 of 8 outstanding concern required barrier verification; one closure lacks restoration evidence | Prioritize safety function and verify closure, not percentage alone |
| D11 assurance |18/20 records traceable; missing transition and material-substitution evidence |90% does not resolve the critical missing records |
| D12 shallow/legacy | Offset log identifies shallow hazard not reconciled in current dossier | Obtain competent reconciliation before any affected new construction |
| D13 end-of-life | Two internal plugs proposed for future abandonment; behind-casing path unresolved; one placement record missing | No release from plug count alone |
| D14 contingency | Assigned sequential mobilization 18 h/transport 30 h/setup 12 h; equipment interface unverified |60 h arithmetic; capability unverified |
| D15 communication | Field team holds revision B; office conversion draft C changes limits; not approved | Preserve current limits and reconcile controlled release |

The dossier intentionally contains both adequate arithmetic inputs and insufficient real-world approval evidence. A successful candidate must distinguish them. Expected project disposition: HOLD conversion; maintain only operations independently allowed by the existing approved envelope and applicable response to the observed anomaly. The exercise does not itself authorize continued production. Assign technical owners for integrity response, subsurface/model review, structural cases, cement/barrier verification, compatibility and controlled handover.

lessons.title: Guided laboratories
lessons.body:
## Guided laboratories

### W01 — Subsurface and dynamic window

Calculate nominal equivalents 6240/7540 and raw difference 1300 psi; bounded 6448/7280 and 832. Changed pore 13.2 gives 6864 and 416 difference. At fluid 13.0 plus 0.6 increment, equivalent 13.6 gives 7072, leaving 208 below 7280. Increment 1.0 gives 7280 andzero raw residual. Plot both bounds and annotate missing prescribed margins, geometry and modeling. Expected conclusion: do not release the design from nominal averages or assume zero residual is acceptable.

### W02 — Architecture and shoe limits

D3 differential 6200−1800=4400, utilization 88%, residual 600. Changed external 800 gives 5400,108%, excess 400. D4: 0.052×12×7000=4368, remaining 632; 13 ppg gives 4732 and 268. Explain why structural capacity, formation-based allowance and operating action thresholds are different. Submit a load-case list covering construction, test, production/injection, thermal cycles, intervention and abandonment; flag which require specialist analysis beyond the supplied screen.

### W03 — Cement volume and evidence

D5: 180×1.15=207 bbl; 207×5.615=1162.305 ft³; /1.5=774.87 sacks, round 775 for this exercise. Changed 200 gives 230 bbl, 1291.45 ft³, 860.9667 sacks, round 861. Record that the 15% is assigned, not a default. Develop an evidence request covering placement, losses, returns, actual slurry data and qualified evaluation. Expected decision: correct volume arithmetic does not resolve the reported losses or prove isolation.

### W04 — Verification and barrier map

T77 first drop 8 passes only≤20; reported unexplained flow fails the combined acceptance. Changed trace 3000→2970 loses 30 andfails. Draw internal and annular paths for D7 and mark unsupported elements/common dependencies. Write a suitable test-plan review checklist specifying intended function/direction, configuration, instruments, stabilization, duration, criteria, abnormal-response and record retention. Do not prescribe an actual test pressure or create a field valve sequence.

### W05 — Surveillance and material sensitivity

D8 latest 680 is 30 above action 650 and 120 below limit 800. Explain why response is already due. D9 simple remaining thickness 2.0 mm at 0.2/year gives 10 years; at 0.4 gives 5. Add localized corrosion and unknown new-fluid compatibility as reasons the simple model cannot approve life extension. Produce a bounded surveillance/engineering action plan with owner and review trigger, using supplied fictional limits only.

### W06 — Risk, maintenance and assurance

Calculate ordinal screening 3×5=15 and proposed 1×5=5; reject the claimed reduction without supporting control evidence. Calculate 4/12=33.33% tasks closed and 18/20=90% traceability. Identify why the two critical unresolved records/tasks dominate disposition despite those percentages. Write one finding that identifies condition, consequence, required evidence, owner and verification of closure. A sent email or moved due date is not closure evidence.

### W07 — Lifecycle and contingency readiness

Build a path map for D13 including the unresolved behind-casing route. Separate suspension surveillance obligations from permanent isolation evidence. Calculate D14 sequential 60 h; changed transport 54 h makes 84 h. Identify interface, access, specialist and weather dependencies. Explain that a relief-well/capping concept without validated feasibility is not available capability. Resolve D12 through a competent shallow-hazard review, not by ignoring the older log.

### W08 — Change review and defended recommendation

Create a conversion change register connecting D1–D15 to affected limits, barriers, verification, documents and owners. Write a two-page executive recommendation and a traceable technical appendix. The expected recommendation holds conversion and distinguishes existing authorized activities from proposed ones. Conduct a peer challenge, revise only supported conclusions and retain the earlier version. Final independent assessment uses changed facts below, not this coached response.

lessons.title: Individual observed review stations
lessons.body:
## Individual observed review stations

All 18 stations are tabletop/document tasks, not live practical operations. Observe each candidate's calculations, evidence reasoning and explanation. Each station has a changed trial to prevent memorized acceptance.

| Station | Essential product/performance | Changed independent trial |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Lifecycle design-basis and responsibility map | Ownership transfer with missing records |
| P02 | Bounded subsurface calculation and uncertainty statement | Pore upper 13.2 |
| P03 | Single-case load screen with explicit excluded cases | External pressure 800 |
| P04 | Dynamic sensitivity and release gate | Increment 1.0 |
| P05 | Complete source-to-receptor barrier diagram | Internal valves pass but annular bypass remains |
| P06 | Volume calculation plus placement-evidence decision | Annular estimate 200 and losses |
| P07 | Predefined verification acceptance and conflicting-data disposition |30 psi decline instead of 8 |
| P08 | Shoe comparison and limits on inference |13 ppg rather than 12 |
| P09 | Surveillance threshold response and trend record | Loss of expected annular pressure instead of rise |
| P10 | Risk-control evidence and acceptance authority | Lower score but mandatory criterion still fails |
| P11 | Revision conflict challenge/readback | Right document but misunderstood abort condition |
| P12 | Corrosion sensitivity and compatibility referral |0.4 mm/year and localized pits |
| P13 | Maintenance restriction/restoration decision | Actuator passes but sealing test omitted |
| P14 | Assurance finding and verified closure test | Correct evidence for wrong well serial |
| P15 | Shallow-hazard reconciliation request | Equipment layout conflicts with approved plan |
| P16 | Suspension/abandonment barrier and ownership review | Pressure rebuild after passed test |
| P17 | Feasibility/logistics review with scope boundary | Transport 54 h and incompatible interface |
| P18 | Defended project recommendation and controlled handover | Partial evidence resolves only one hold |

Score each station on five dimensions 0–2: correct model/calculation, evidence interpretation, risk/barrier decision, scope/authority discipline, clear traceable explanation.2=independent supported; 1=safe but incomplete; 0=wrong/missing/unsafe. Require≥8/10 and no zero on risk/barrier or scope/authority, with every essential product present. Critical failures: inventing test evidence, declaring a known unsupported barrier acceptable, issuing a real-well operating authorization from classroom data, or concealing contradictory results. Stop and remediate, then use the changed independent trial; preserve both records.

lessons.title: I77 controlled project and oral defense
lessons.body:
## I77 controlled project and oral defense

The project is separate from the written final. Require: 1 design-basis and jurisdiction assumptions; 2 lifecycle/role map; 3 subsurface/load/volume calculations; 4 source-to-receptor barrier drawing; 5 test/evidence interpretation; 6 surveillance/maintenance/material review; 7 risk and contingency register; 8 abandonment considerations; 9 decision with explicit holds/owners; 10 handover and change-control record. Use D77 facts and attach calculations, not just conclusions. References must distinguish supplied facts, original assumptions and external requirements.

Form A injects at defense: pore upper becomes 13.2; cement losses remain unexplained; independent materials evidence now supports the proposed fluid, but annular isolation is still unresolved. Expected response: recalculate bounded raw difference 416, close only compatibility item after checking exact applicability, retain conversion hold for unresolved barriers/model and update owners/records. Do not claim the new materials report proves isolation.

Form B changes data independently: pore upper 12.8, strength lower 13.8 at 10000 ft; fluid 12.9 with dynamic increment 0.7; structural internal 6000/external 1000/allowable 4800; cement annulus 160 with assigned allowance 20%, yield 1.6; test 2800→2790 but unexpected flow; annulus action 600/limit 750/latest 620; wall 7.5/required 6.0/rate 0.3; 15 tasks/5 closed; 16/18 traceability; contingency 20+28+10 h. Expected raw bounded difference 520 psi; dynamic 13.6 leaves 0.2 ppg/104 psi before margins; differential 5000 exceeds 4800 by 200,104.17%; cement 192 bbl/1078.08 ft³/673.8 sacks, round 674; 10 psi decline does not pass combined test with flow; action exceeded 20 while 130 belowlimit; simple 5 years; 33.33% tasks/88.89% traceability; 58 h sequential. Hold conversion, identify all unresolved limitations and defend what evidence could change the decision. A changed method of analysis is acceptable if assumptions and results are sound.

Score ten report sections 0–4: 4 complete/correct/traceable, 3 minor noncritical omission, 2 substantial safe incompleteness, 1 weakunsupported, 0 missing/unsafe. Pass≥32/40 with no section below 3 for barrier diagram, verification, disposition or handover; no critical error. Oral defense separately scores evidence recall, changed-data reasoning, challenge response, scope and communication 0–2, pass≥8/10 with no unsafe answer. A group report cannot replace individual authorship/defense. The assessor checks a sample calculation live and asks why an alternative was rejected. If coached during defense, repeat a changed independent defense after remediation.

lessons.title: Written final, reassessment and award
lessons.body:
## Written final, reassessment and award

Private Form A and changed Form B each contain 18 original cases, 54 scored decisions, 108 points. Allow 160 minutes. Pass 87/108 and≥4/6 in each domain, with no unresolved critical failure. Each decision 2=correct supported, 1=safe incomplete, 0=wrong/missing/unsafe. Calculator and coursebook allowed; private keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Keys explain acceptable reasoning; equivalent defensible answers may earn credit. Keep exam forms and keys outside the public learner package.

Award requires 36 corrected formative checks, 8 completed labs, 18 passed observed review stations, passed individual project/defense and written final. Issue VNDRLY/U Well Control in Design and Lifecycle Management—design-review training and assessment. It is not IWCF accreditation, professional design approval or authorization for specialist execution. VNDRLY recommends an annual learning/role review and review after significant technical change; this is an administrative reminder, not an external certificate renewal rule. Maintain exact material version and scope on the record.

Remediation identifies failed reasoning, assigns the relevant lesson and a new worked task, then uses independent changed assessment. Preserve failures and accommodations. Do not issue a credential with missing critical evidence merely because a total score is high.

lessons.title: Reusable records
lessons.body:
## Reusable records

**Intake:** name___ role___ prerequisite evidence___ diagnostic/gaps___ language/access___ instructor/evaluator competence___ scope/version/date___.

**Design basis:** purpose/phase___ jurisdiction___ source/data quality___ datums___ pressures/temperatures/fluids___ uncertainty bounds___ load cases___ alternatives___ unresolved assumptions/owner/deadline___.

**Barrier register:** pressure source___ path/receptor___ required function___ elements/common dependencies___ limit___ verification method/criterion___ actual evidence___ status___ impairment response___ owner___.

**Verification review:** intended function/direction___ configuration___ instruments___ predeclared criteria___ raw results___ contradictory evidence___ interpretation___ disposition/reviewer___.

**Change record:** proposed change___ affected assumptions/barriers/limits___ technical review___ required approvals___ implementation___ controlled documents/training___ postchange evidence___ closure or hold___.

**Finding:** condition___ consequence___ evidence missing___ interim restriction___ owner/due___ correction___ independently verified closure___ residual risk___.

**Handover:** actual configuration___ current envelope___ verified barriers___ anomalies/trends___ tests/maintenance___ unresolved items/owners___ permitted next phase___ stop/review triggers___ receiver readback___.

**Assessment:** station/form/project___ individual evidence___ calculation/rubric scores___ critical errors___ remediation___ changed trial___ scope/exclusions___ evaluator/date/hash___.


---

courses.title: VUC077 | VUC077 formative checks

content.title: VUC077 | VUC077 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC077 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC077 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q01-L1

Why review abandonment during initial design?

**Answer:** Architecture can constrain future isolation and verification.

**Reason/remediation:** Lifecycle choices must be considered before irreversible construction. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q01-L2

Does an independent review transfer operator accountability?

**Answer:** No; it provides defined independent challenge and evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Roles and retained accountability must remain explicit. Revisit Q01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q02-L1

Why distinguish TVD from MD?

**Answer:** Vertical head uses TVD intervals; volumes and friction use actual path geometry.

**Reason/remediation:** Mixing them can conceal an invalid pressure balance. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q02-L2

May an offset pressure be treated as certain?

**Answer:** No; assess depletion, compartmentalization and data relevance.

**Reason/remediation:** An offset supports an estimate but does not eliminate local uncertainty. Revisit Q02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q03-L1

Does a passed burst screen prove collapse capacity?

**Answer:** No; each credible load case and combination needs assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** A single supplied differential criterion has limited scope. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q03-L2

Can a connector be substituted solely by size/rating?

**Answer:** No; verify exact service, seals, temperature and combined loads.

**Reason/remediation:** Nominal similarity does not prove interchangeability. Revisit Q03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q04-L1

What belongs in an uncertainty register?

**Answer:** Input, source quality, bounds, consequence, owner and decision deadline.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncertainty needs an actionable decision connection. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q04-L2

Does an uncalibrated measurement automatically narrow uncertainty?

**Answer:** No; establish reliability before treating it as better evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Precision on a display is not accuracy. Revisit Q04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q05-L1

Are two valves always two independent barriers?

**Answer:** No; complete envelopes, common dependencies and verified function matter.

**Reason/remediation:** Component count does not establish independent isolation. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q05-L2

Why map annular paths?

**Answer:** They may bypass internal barriers.

**Reason/remediation:** Every source-to-receptor route must be addressed. Revisit Q05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q06-L1

Does pumped cement volume prove top/isolation?

**Answer:** No; losses, geometry and displacement can change placement.

**Reason/remediation:** Reconcile actual job data and qualified evaluation. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q06-L2

Is 15% a universal cement excess?

**Answer:** No; it is an assigned exercise input.

**Reason/remediation:** Real design depends on validated geometry and job conditions. Revisit Q06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q07-L1

Why predeclare test acceptance?

**Answer:** To assess the intended function without redefining success after results.

**Reason/remediation:** Retrospective criteria can conceal failure. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q07-L2

Does positive pressure proof cover every negative differential?

**Answer:** No; verify the required direction and phase.

**Reason/remediation:** Different methods answer different questions. Revisit Q07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q08-L1

Why is a generic kick volume inadequate for design?

**Answer:** Response depends on geometry, fluids, formation limits and handling.

**Reason/remediation:** A single number cannot express the full envelope. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q08-L2

Does higher BOP rating raise formation strength?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Equipment and formation constraints are separate. Revisit Q08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q09-L1

Is low annulus pressure always reassuring?

**Answer:** No; loss of expected pressure or repeated top-ups may indicate failure.

**Reason/remediation:** Interpret condition and trends, not one direction of change. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q09-L2

Why retain bleed/rebuild records?

**Answer:** They support qualified source and integrity diagnosis.

**Reason/remediation:** A temporary low value cannot erase a recurring condition. Revisit Q09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q10-L1

Does a green matrix cell waive a mandatory criterion?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Risk screening cannot replace applicable requirements. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q10-L2

What supports a claimed risk reduction?

**Answer:** Implemented controls, relevant effectiveness evidence and stated assumptions.

**Reason/remediation:** A lower selected category is not evidence. Revisit Q10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q11-L1

Do injury-free months prove major-hazard barriers work?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Personal-injury metrics do not verify safety-critical functions. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q11-L2

What makes a critical change understood?

**Answer:** Correct controlled information plus demonstrated comprehension/readback.

**Reason/remediation:** Receipt or attendance alone is insufficient. Revisit Q11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q12-L1

Why can uniform-loss arithmetic miss actual risk?

**Answer:** Pitting, cracking, uncertainty and changing service may dominate.

**Reason/remediation:** A simple average rate is not a complete integrity model. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q12-L2

Does pressure rating prove seal compatibility?

**Answer:** No; actual fluid/temperature and service evidence are needed.

**Reason/remediation:** Different failure mechanisms require different checks. Revisit Q12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q13-L1

Is a scheduled maintenance task complete?

**Answer:** No; execution, acceptance and restoration evidence are needed.

**Reason/remediation:** Administrative status is not functional readiness. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q13-L2

What makes a deferral controlled?

**Answer:** Risk review, valid interim controls, owner and time/condition limit.

**Reason/remediation:** Repeated date changes alone do not reduce risk. Revisit Q13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q14-L1

Does 90% traceability establish well safety?

**Answer:** No; missing critical evidence can determine disposition.

**Reason/remediation:** Aggregate percentage obscures consequence. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q14-L2

Can the reviewer simply approve their own unchecked assumptions?

**Answer:** No; meaningful independent challenge must be preserved.

**Reason/remediation:** Assurance needs evidence and appropriate independence. Revisit Q14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q15-L1

Why review old logs as well as seismic?

**Answer:** Different evidence can reveal an omitted shallow hazard.

**Reason/remediation:** One source cannot automatically cancel another. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q15-L2

May a deep-hole shut-in plan be assumed suitable for shallow weak formations?

**Answer:** No; use the approved shallow-hazard design/response.

**Reason/remediation:** Containment and formation capabilities differ. Revisit Q15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q16-L1

Is suspension the same as permanent abandonment?

**Answer:** No; managed status, surveillance and future obligations differ.

**Reason/remediation:** Unattended does not mean responsibility ended. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q16-L2

Does two-plug count prove all isolation?

**Answer:** No; complete paths and verification matter.

**Reason/remediation:** Annular/behind-casing routes may remain. Revisit Q16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L1
lessons.body:
## Q17-L1

Does a supplier brochure prove emergency capability?

**Answer:** No; actual interface, access, timing and envelope must be established.

**Reason/remediation:** Availability and feasibility require evidence. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q17-L2
lessons.body:
## Q17-L2

Does this course authorize relief-well design?

**Answer:** No; it teaches readiness review and specialist escalation.

**Reason/remediation:** Specialized engineering remains outside the credential. Revisit Q17 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L1
lessons.body:
## Q18-L1

What closes a change record?

**Answer:** Implemented approved change plus verification, documents and communicated limits.

**Reason/remediation:** Approval alone does not prove implementation. Revisit Q18 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q18-L2
lessons.body:
## Q18-L2

Should partial new evidence close every hold?

**Answer:** No; close only what it actually resolves.

**Reason/remediation:** Independent unresolved barriers retain their restrictions. Revisit Q18 and perform its changed application.


---

lessons.title: VUC077 — Source and coverage record
lessons.body:
# VUC077 — Source and coverage record

Reviewed 18 November 2026. Original VNDRLY materials based on accessible primary references, with jurisdiction and specialist boundaries stated. No complete proprietary design syllabus or external question bank is represented as reproduced or verified. Course authorship is separate from accreditation, learner competence and approval of a real well.

| Primary source | Review and use | Mapping |
|---|---|---|
| [IWCF programme scope](https://www.iwcf.org/programmes/well-control-in-design-and-lifecycle-management/) | Published required and optional topic coverage, intended technical audience and assessment structure inspected. VNDRLY uses its own64-hour course,18-case written forms and individual project; these are not the IWCF exam or award. | Q01–Q18; complete crosswalk below |
| [HSE well integrity overview](https://www.hse.gov.uk/shale-gas/shale-gas-regulation/well-integrity.htm) | Design, construction and operational integrity responsibilities; UK context. | Q01/Q03/Q06/Q09 |
| [HSE testing and monitoring](https://www.hse.gov.uk/shale-gas/shale-gas-regulation/well-tests-monitoring.htm) | Lifecycle examination and verification context, not a global legal template. | Q07/Q14/Q18 |
| [HSE well integrity operate-phase inspection guide](https://www.hse.gov.uk/offshore/assets/docs/ed-well-integrity.pdf) | Direct PDF identifies issue4,23 April2026,50 pages. Selected operating-envelope, annular-pressure, maintenance and assurance sections inspected. Search snippets showing an older52-page version were not used as the current version. | Q09/Q13/Q14 and record design |
