lessons.title: VUC087 source review and coverage — 18 November 2026
lessons.body: # VUC087 source review and coverage — 18 November 2026

lessons.title: Available primary sources
lessons.body:
## Available primary sources

- OPITO 9068: https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/banksman-slinger-competence-assessment-previously-stage-3 . Public page identifies combined-role knowledge and practical competence, four units and seven-hour assessment. It specifies detailed entry routes and authenticated logbook evidence, with date-dependent historical provisions, and two-year external validity. Full controlled specification was not obtained. Our original extended development/assessment route does not replace those entry rules or confer OPITO approval. An approved centre must determine eligibility for the external scheme; no historical exception is generalized to current learners.
- HSE LOLER overview: https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/loler.htm . Context for competent planning/supervision and suitable lifting equipment in the applicable jurisdiction. Not a universal law for every country.
- HSE planning: https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/planning-organising-lifting-operations.htm . Reviewed task-proportionate planning, roles, foreseeable hazards, route/location and stability. Supports plan review rather than improvising around changes.
- HSE examination/inspection: https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/thorough-examinations-lifting-equipment.htm . Pre-use condition checks and competent thorough examination are distinct. A current report does not excuse a new defect. Actual scheme/manufacturer criteria govern; no universal inspection interval is invented here.
- OSHA slings: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.184 . Reviewed safe-use/identification and damaged-equipment boundaries. Detailed rejection limits differ by sling type; this course requires the actual applicable criteria rather than an invented single wear allowance.
- OSHA signals: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1419 . Reviewed designated signaler, stop on interrupted/unclear communication, emergency stop and operator perspective. U.S. construction scope is identified, not assumed universal.
- OSHA voice signals: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1421 . Agreed voice communication and function/direction, distance/speed and stop structure support S87 practice.
- OSHA signal-person qualification: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1428 . Knowledge and practical demonstration plus documented qualification are distinct from generic attendance. This limited initial program does not claim to complete every qualification requirement or all signal types.
- OSHA official hand-signal chart: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926SubpartCCAppA . Six selected signals are taught and practiced against the chart; other crane functions remain outside the assessed set. No proprietary chart is reproduced.
- OSHA keeping clear: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1425 . Supports reducing exposure to load/fall zones. Our training fixture uses stricter no-under-load/no-suspended-horizontal-travel boundaries and does not purport to summarize every regulatory exception.
- Crosby rigging information: https://www.thecrosbygroup.com/wp-content/uploads/catalog/2016/en-US/473.pdf . Selected static angle/load-share principles reviewed; displayed document is historical, not a current model rating. Original calculations use explicitly fictional force units and ratings. Real manufacturer tables, configuration and competent planning control actual selection. No inferred universal permission to use a shallow angle is given.

lessons.title: Coverage and evidence
lessons.body:
## Coverage and evidence

Q87-01 roles → L87 briefing/P87-01; Q87-02 plan → Z87/W87-1/P87-02; Q87-03 load/CG → A1/A2/B87/P87-03; Q87-04 geometry/rating → A3/A4/W87-2/P87-04; Q87-05 inspection → G87/P87-05; Q87-06 attachment → supported-load task/P87-06; Q87-07 signals → S87/P87-07 and two randomized sequences; Q87-08 position → Z87/P87-08; Q87-09 trial → L87/P87-09; Q87-10 landing → L87/P87-10; Q87-11 abnormal → changed cards/P87-11; Q87-12 development → F87/P87-12. Every chapter has two explained checks and its own controlled final/changed case. Six labs and I87 integrate the work.

lessons.title: Delivery and claim boundaries
lessons.body:
## Delivery and claim boundaries

Paper masses/ratings are never used for a real lift. Actual facility plan fields must be completed from identified suitable equipment before supervised practical delivery. This is a delivery control, not a pre-issued learner result. Six physical stations and eight observed review encounters are required for the training award. Actual A/B operations require competent equipment-specific plans and current movement/landing evidence. Required restricted-view signaling uses an approved relay/handover. Tandem, personnel and dynamic offshore lifts remain outside the defined scope. Materials completion, learner achievement, workplace competence and publication remain separate states.

lessons.title: Competence-specific instruction and evidence
lessons.body:
## Competence-specific instruction and evidence

Q87-01 and Q87-12 explicitly teach entry/scope and candidate-specific workplace evidence. Q87-13 teaches unequal loading/configuration changes using U87, P87-13 and controlled case 13. Q87-14 teaches independent judgment, remediation and fair review using C87/F87, P87-14 and case 14. Two authenticated jobs and two current direct operations, including at least one workplace observation, are original VNDRLY requirements, not claimed OPITO task counts. All C87 criteria and required range must be met. Common reviewed rigging instruction from VUC086 is included as refresher; this package stands alone and adds a distinct competence decision process.

courses.title: VUC088 | VNDRLY/U Banksman and Slinger Competence Reassessment

content.title: VUC088 | VNDRLY/U Banksman and Slinger Competence Reassessment
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Banksman and Slinger Competence Reassessment
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Banksman and Slinger Competence Reassessment

VUC088 · original materials · 18 November 2026

For previously assessed personnel seeking a current competence review in a declared scope. Sixteen chapters include the reviewed technical core and specific maintained-competence/change instruction. Entry requires an authenticated previous competence record and review of subsequent experience, gaps and eligibility; initial attendance alone is insufficient. Planned 44 hours includes refresher, development and independent reassessment; actual experience accumulation is additional. This is an original VNDRLY route, not OPITO 9069 approval or a replacement for its controlled entry/renewal rules.

lessons.title: Q88-01 — Define the competence scope before accepting the assessment
lessons.body:
## Q88-01 — Define the competence scope before accepting the assessment

Competence is a supported conclusion about performance in a defined role and range of conditions. It is not a reward for attendance or years of service. For this VNDRLY assessment, identify the actual equipment family, load types, signaling methods and work environment that the evidence will cover. The candidate must demonstrate both banksman and slinger duties; doing one while watching the other is not a combined-role result.

Review prior training and authenticated supervised experience before scheduling practical assessment. A résumé is an entry clue, not proof of every skill. Check the candidate's actual role in each job, supervisor identity, plan, equipment and observations. Where the records are incomplete, agree additional supervised development rather than inventing missing experience. The assessor must be technically competent and authorized for the defined scope and independent enough to make an honest decision despite production pressure.

Worked case: a candidate presents twenty lift logs, all signed by the same supervisor, but every entry says only “assisted.” Ask what the candidate actually selected, inspected, attached and signaled. Collect specific corroboration and directly observe the gaps. Changed case: the records clearly establish slinging, but the candidate has never directed a restricted-visibility movement. That outcome remains unestablished. Do not expand a certificate to include it simply because the person is experienced with the load.

This program provides refresher instruction, development exercises and a controlled competence-assessment process. The refresher is completed before the final attempt. During final assessment, the assessor may stop danger but must not coach the candidate to a pass. A safety intervention is evidence requiring remediation and a fresh independent attempt, not a hidden successful action.

lessons.title: Q88-02 — Read the lift plan and inspect the work area
lessons.body:
## Q88-02 — Read the lift plan and inspect the work area

Read the task, load identity, mass, center of gravity, lifting points, rigging configuration, equipment, route, landing location, personnel and stop conditions. Confirm the actual situation matches the plan. Look for pedestrians, vehicles, overhead services, excavations, soft ground, restricted visibility, structures, weather and simultaneous work. A route that was clear yesterday may be occupied now. Do not alter a lift plan informally to save time.

The plan must address pickup and landing, not only travel. Decide where people stand, where they retreat and how access is controlled. Verify the landing surface and supports before lifting. A load suspended while the crew searches for dunnage creates avoidable exposure. Check communications and emergency arrangements during the briefing, using questions to confirm understanding.

Worked case: plan L88 specifies an eastward route, but a delivery truck blocks the landing zone. Stop and refer the change; do not swing the load over an occupied walkway. Changed case: the route is clear but an overhead cable has appeared in the work area. Treat it as an unresolved proximity hazard and involve the competent planner; do not estimate a safe electrical clearance from memory. The learner's job is to recognize mismatch and prevent an unauthorized workaround.

lessons.title: Q88-03 — Establish load mass, center of gravity and stability
lessons.body:
## Q88-03 — Establish load mass, center of gravity and stability

Use reliable load information: identification plate, drawing, verified inventory or competent calculation. Include contents, attachments and rigging in the appropriate load calculation. A label on an empty vessel does not include residual liquid. Do not use crane behavior to discover an unknown mass. Locate the center of gravity from reliable information and understand how it affects balance and leg loading.

For a simple static load supported at two points on one horizontal line, the support nearer the center of gravity carries more vertical share. If points are 2 metres apart and the center of gravity is 0.5 metre from the left point, a 1,000-unit weight gives left share 1,000 × 1.5/2 = 750 units and right share 250. This simplified equilibrium calculation excludes dynamic effects and does not approve lifting points. The hook arrangement and rigging must follow the competent plan.

Worked case: a skid is marked 900 kg but contains 120 kg of retained material and uses 80 kg of below-hook rigging. The total specified contribution is 1,100 kg; the planner must address the actual load and configuration. Changed case: one component is removed from one side. Both mass and center of gravity may change. Do not assume an earlier balanced lift proves the modified skid will remain level. A trial lift checks an already planned arrangement; it is not a substitute for knowing the load.

lessons.title: Q88-04 — Select slings and understand angle effects
lessons.body:
## Q88-04 — Select slings and understand angle effects

Select the actual sling for load, hitch, environment and configuration using its identification and manufacturer rating. Working load limit is not breaking strength. Do not calculate a new working limit by dividing an unknown strength by a guessed safety factor. Vertical, basket and choker arrangements can have different ratings and restrictions. A doubled-looking arrangement does not automatically double capacity. Sharp edges, bend radius, temperature, chemicals and contact pressure may require specific protection or a different accessory.

For a symmetric two-leg static teaching model, with angle theta measured from horizontal, tension in each leg is W divided by twice sine theta. At 60 degrees and W = 1,000 force units, each leg carries approximately 577.35; at 30 degrees it carries 1,000. Shallower angles increase tension. Real sling tags and approved geometry govern use; do not extrapolate outside permitted angles or assume all legs share equally in a multi-leg assembly.

Worked case: two identical legs each have a 600-unit permitted axial load in the fictional chart. A 1,000-unit symmetric load at 60 degrees is below that individual limit in this simplified check, but at 45 degrees each leg would be 707.11 and fails. Other components and the lift plan still need verification. Changed case: the center of gravity moves off-center. The equal-share formula no longer applies; obtain the correct leg shares and geometry rather than dividing total load by the number of legs.

lessons.title: Q88-05 — Inspect accessories and isolate defects
lessons.body:
## Q88-05 — Inspect accessories and isolate defects

Match each accessory's identity to its rating and examination status, then inspect its present condition using the actual manufacturer's removal criteria. Look for damaged webbing, broken wires, deformation, cracks, corrosion, heat or chemical damage, damaged threads and missing or illegible identification. Different sling types have different detailed rejection rules; this course does not invent a universal allowable number of broken wires or percentage of wear.

A current examination record does not make newly damaged equipment usable. Pre-use inspection and periodic competent examination serve different purposes. Quarantine suspected defective or unidentified equipment, tag it clearly and report through the organization's process. Do not return it to the rack where another crew might use it. Repair or proof testing requires authorized arrangements; a trainee must not hammer a hook back into shape or weld a chain link.

Worked case: sling S2 has a readable rating and current examination reference, but an edge cut is visible. Remove it from the task and seek the proper disposition. Changed case: S3 looks undamaged but its identity tag is missing. Do not borrow S1's certificate or invent a rating from its color. Obtain an identifiable suitable replacement. Inspection is a decision about the specific item in front of you, not about a similar photograph.

lessons.title: Q88-06 — Attach and protect the load
lessons.body:
## Q88-06 — Attach and protect the load

Follow the planned connection points and accessory orientation. Check compatibility among hook, master link, shackle, sling and lifting point. Load must bear where the manufacturer intends; a hook latch retains the sling but is not the load-bearing seat. Avoid unintended side loading, point loading, twists, knots and improvised shortening. Do not substitute a convenient pipe or handrail for an engineered lifting point.

Keep hands out of pinch points while taking slack. Use the approved method to seat accessories without placing fingers between sling and load. Apply suitable edge protection so it remains in position as tension develops. A loose rag is not automatically adequate protection. Confirm the rigging cannot slip or release when the load changes orientation. Remove loose items or secure them through the plan before movement.

Worked case: the sling eye sits on the hook tip because the connecting link is too small. Stop and replace the incompatible arrangement; do not rely on the latch to force it into place. Changed case: the eye seats correctly but a sharp corner lies under the synthetic sling. Obtain the specified protection or revised rigging arrangement before tensioning. The correct sequence is planned connection, inspection, clearance and controlled take-up, not loading first and adjusting by hand under tension.

lessons.title: Q88-07 — Communicate by agreed hand and voice signals
lessons.body:
## Q88-07 — Communicate by agreed hand and voice signals

Agree the signal method, designated signaler, equipment identifier, operator perspective and stop response before movement. Keep signals visible and unambiguous. If communication is lost or a signal is unclear, stop safely and re-establish understanding. An emergency stop from any person must be taken seriously. Do not continue on a guessed instruction.

For the classroom's selected standard hand-signal set, stop uses one arm extended sideways with palm down moving side to side; emergency stop uses both arms similarly. Hoist uses the raised forearm and upward index finger making small circles; lower points the arm/finger down with small circles. Swing points horizontally in the intended boom direction. Slow movement adds the other hand in front of the action-signaling hand. Practice these without a suspended load and compare with the official chart. These six are a limited training set, not qualification for every crane function.

Voice commands identify the equipment where necessary and state function/direction, distance or speed, then the function stop command at completion. Example practice exchange: “Hoist up, slowly, 50 millimetres”; operator repeats the intended action; banksman gives “Hoist stop” at the planned point. Do not use “my left” from a different viewpoint. Changed application: two radios transmit conflicting movement commands. Stop, identify the designated signaler and resolve the channel/role problem before proceeding.

lessons.title: Q88-08 — Control the exclusion area and personal position
lessons.body:
## Q88-08 — Control the exclusion area and personal position

Keep people clear of the load path, potential swing and trapping zones according to the plan. Barriers, signs and briefings must work in practice. A painted line without access control may not prevent someone walking through. Position yourself to see the relevant movement, remain visible or in reliable contact with the operator and retain an escape route. Do not stand between a moving load and a fixed structure.

Tag lines may be appropriate when specified, but can introduce entanglement or pull hazards. Do not wrap a line around a hand or body, stand in a bight or try to restrain a load beyond the planned method. If the load behaves unexpectedly, stop and lower safely under the plan rather than wrestling it into position. Nobody goes under the load to untwist a sling.

Worked case: a pedestrian enters the marked zone during take-up. Give stop and prevent further movement until the zone is controlled. Changed case: the pedestrian stays outside but the banksman's retreat route is blocked by stored material. Restore a safe position before continuing. The absence of someone directly underneath does not remove crush, swing and line-of-fire hazards. In the training fixture exercise, hands remain outside the marked footprint whenever the load is suspended.

lessons.title: Q88-09 — Take slack, trial lift and respond to imbalance
lessons.body:
## Q88-09 — Take slack, trial lift and respond to imbalance

Before taking slack, confirm attachments, people clear, communications, load free to move and the planned landing ready. Take tension gradually as instructed; observe seating, protection and unexpected snagging from a safe position. Do not use a sudden pull to free a stuck load. If it does not respond as expected, stop and investigate through the supervisor.

The controlled trial lift raises an already verified load only enough for the planned balance and security check. The plan defines the height and observations. Check whether the load hangs as expected, accessories remain seated and nothing shifts or snags. If it tilts or moves unexpectedly, stop and lower to a safe supported condition before adjustment. Never put hands into loaded rigging to correct it.

Worked case: during the L88 fixture trial, one end rises before the other and the protection moves. Stop, lower to the supports and refer the discrepancy. Do not continue because the total mass is small. Changed case: the load stays level but a loose tool slides on top. Lower and secure/remove the item using the approved method. A successful initial inch of travel does not prove the entire route or landing is safe; continue observing throughout the operation.

lessons.title: Q88-10 — Travel, land and detach under control
lessons.body:
## Q88-10 — Travel, land and detach under control

Movement follows the agreed route and speed with ongoing attention to people, obstructions and changes. Avoid sudden starts, stops and side pulling. The operator controls the machine; the banksman communicates required movement and stop conditions, not improvised machine settings. If visibility changes, stop and use the planned handover or revised communication arrangement rather than walking into a hazardous position to keep seeing.

Before landing, confirm the destination, supports, stability and clearance for rigging removal. Lower under control until the load is fully supported and stable, then release tension and detach according to the plan. Do not pull a sling from beneath a load with the crane or reach under a partly supported item. Keep the hook and loose accessories controlled after detachment.

Worked case: the receiving area has only one of two required supports. Hold the lift in a safe condition under the supervisor's direction and correct the landing arrangement; do not improvise with an unstable stack. Changed case: both supports are present but the load rocks after contact. Do not detach until stability is established. For this competence assessment, planned travel and landing must be directly observed on suitable actual equipment under the site-specific L88 plan. A floor-supported rehearsal is preparation only and cannot substitute for the required movement evidence. No generic height, travel distance or load capacity is authorized by the course text.

lessons.title: Q88-11 — Manage abnormal conditions and stop/restart
lessons.body:
## Q88-11 — Manage abnormal conditions and stop/restart

Weather, visibility, communications, equipment condition, ground conditions or the load itself can change. Use the limits in the actual lift plan and equipment instructions; there is no universal wind speed in this course. A large sail area may make a load difficult to control even when a generic weather number looks acceptable. Stop and refer rather than arguing that a previous lift succeeded.

For an abnormal event, signal stop, keep clear, inform the supervisor and follow the planned safe securing or lowering method. Do not leave a suspended load unattended or attempt an improvised repair while it is loaded. If an electrical contact or other major emergency is suspected, apply the site emergency plan and keep others clear; do not approach to rescue by touching equipment. This initial course does not qualify emergency crane recovery.

Worked case: radio contact disappears halfway through a simulated move. The operator stops safely; the team restores communications and confirms a clear instruction before restart. Changed case: communication returns but a damaged shackle is reported. The restored radio does not resolve the hardware defect. Each failed control must be addressed. Restart requires the designated authority and a confirmed safe condition, not simply silence after an alarm.

lessons.title: Q88-12 — Authenticate experience and make a bounded award
lessons.body:
## Q88-12 — Authenticate experience and make a bounded award

Trace each claimed outcome to candidate-specific evidence. Record job date, plan version, equipment, load, geometry, candidate role, supervisor and the action actually observed. Check provenance through the approved employer channel and compare documents for consistency. A copied plan may be genuine while proving nothing about who performed the work. A photograph of a landed load does not establish safe signaling during travel.

This original reassessment program requires two distinct authenticated workplace jobs since the previous award covering both roles and the assessment range, plus current direct observation of the candidate performing both roles through complete planned operations. At least one required observation occurs in the actual workplace. A suitably representative assessed facility task can supply the other current observation if its conditions genuinely cover the declared scope. These are VNDRLY criteria, not a substitute for OPITO's controlled logbook or entry requirements.

Worked case: job E1 proves the candidate inspected and slung a skid; job E2 proves they signaled a different planned load through restricted visibility with an agreed relay. Current observations confirm both roles independently. Map each criterion and check the remaining range before a bounded decision. Changed case: E2 is an unverified story and no direct banksman observation exists. Withhold the combined-role award, specify the missing evidence and arrange development/assessment. Do not convert a knowledge pass into a competence pass.

The final record states assessed scope, evidence and limitations. Personnel lifting, tandem lifts, specialized offshore dynamic operations and unassessed equipment remain excluded unless a separate competent assessment explicitly covers them. Employer appointment and jurisdiction-specific qualifications remain distinct. A candidate receives a partial evidence record when requirements are incomplete, not a misleading full certificate.

lessons.title: Q88-13 — Manage unequal loading and configuration changes
lessons.body:
## Q88-13 — Manage unequal loading and configuration changes

A competent slinger notices when a convenient formula no longer describes the arrangement. Equal load sharing requires appropriate geometry and assumptions. Offset centers of gravity, unequal leg lengths, different pick elevations and rigid multi-leg assemblies can produce unequal tensions. Do not divide by four simply because four legs are attached. Use the approved lift design and manufacturer ratings; refer complex configurations rather than improvising a new design during attachment.

For an original static paper example, a 1,200-unit load has two supports 3 metres apart, with its center 1 metre from the left. Vertical shares are 800 left and 400 right. If each leg is at 60 degrees from horizontal, ideal tensions are 800/sin 60 = 923.76 left and 400/sin 60 = 461.88 right. A 900-unit left-leg allowance fails although the total load seems modest. These calculations are only a screening exercise; lateral forces, lifting-point suitability and full arrangement remain for the competent plan.

Changed example: moving the center to 1.5 metres makes the shares 600 each and ideal 60-degree tensions 692.82. That numerical improvement does not authorize moving contents or changing pick points without approval. The actual load may shift during travel, and an apparently balanced trial can conceal an insecure internal component. Verify the load is prepared as specified.

When a sling or connector is substituted, check the entire configuration, not only a larger number on the tag. A stronger component can still be geometrically incompatible or impose a harmful load direction. Stop, document the proposed substitution and obtain the required competent approval before using it.

lessons.title: Q88-14 — Assess independent performance, remediate and review
lessons.body:
## Q88-14 — Assess independent performance, remediate and review

Use observable criteria and the supplied evidence matrix to judge the candidate. Independent performance means the candidate makes the required choices and communicates the sequence without solution prompts; normal supervision and operator cooperation remain present. Neutral clarification of task wording is permitted. Telling the candidate which sling to reject or when to stop is coaching and must be recorded. A coached completion cannot support the failed criterion.

A competence result requires every mandatory criterion, specified range and authentic evidence. Written scores support underpinning knowledge but cannot compensate for a practical critical error. If the candidate loads defective gear, enters a prohibited zone, ignores an unclear command or fabricates evidence, stop and record the exact behavior. Give focused feedback, practice the gap and use a changed task for reassessment. Retain the first attempt rather than overwriting it.

Worked case: the candidate scores 90 percent on knowledge but needs a prompt to stop when a pedestrian enters. The practical boundary-control criterion is not independently met. Withhold the competence award, provide targeted training and observe a changed incursion scenario safely. Changed case: the assessor misrecords a stop that was actually given and the candidate supplies a corroborating observation. Review the evidence and correct the record transparently; provide an independent appeal route without retaliation.

Before issue, another competent reviewer checks scope, critical criteria, evidence authenticity and unresolved gaps. This is not a requirement for another software deployment. It is a review of the learner's actual assessment record at delivery. Keep blank forms blank until the learner performs. Materials completion means the course and assessment resources exist; it does not assert that any person has passed them.

lessons.title: Q88-15 — Review maintained competence and gaps since the last award
lessons.body:
## Q88-15 — Review maintained competence and gaps since the last award

Reassessment asks whether the person still demonstrates the required competence in the proposed scope. A previous certificate establishes a past decision; it does not prove uninterrupted practice, unchanged equipment or present performance. Verify the previous award's identity, scope, issuer and status, then review what happened since it was earned. Identify periods away from the role, changes in duties, equipment, procedures and health/readiness, and relevant incidents or near misses.

Separate an eligibility decision from a competence decision. A person may be eligible to attend but not yet demonstrate the required skills. A lapsed document does not automatically prove inability, but it may prevent appointment or require a different external training route. Apply the actual scheme's rules through its authorized process; do not invent a grace period or backdate a renewed award. For this original VNDRLY route, unresolved eligibility or material practice gaps lead to a documented development/assessment route before a renewal result.

Worked case: a candidate holds a prior combined-role certificate but has spent the last year on office duties and has no recent signaling evidence. Plan a refresher and supervised practice, then current direct assessment of both roles. Do not accept the old signature as a substitute. Changed case: the candidate has continuous slinger work but only observed banksman tasks. Record the asymmetric experience and address the banksman gap specifically.

Review incident history without assuming blame. A near-miss report can reveal a learning need, an equipment problem or an unclear procedure. Ask what changed and obtain evidence of the corrective action. The reassessment must test whether the candidate applies the current safe method, not whether they can recite that an investigation occurred. Retain both successful and unsuccessful evidence honestly.

lessons.title: Q88-16 — Assess changed equipment, learning and renewal boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q88-16 — Assess changed equipment, learning and renewal boundaries

A renewed result must reflect today's task. Compare the previous and current equipment, accessory system, signal conventions, route, load types and work interfaces. Use a change matrix: old condition, new condition, effect on required skill, learning needed, evidence collected and decision. Familiar appearance is not equivalence. A new radio interface or different connector can change critical actions even when the job title is unchanged.

Before the controlled attempt, provide focused learning and practice for identified changes. During the attempt, require independent decisions under the current approved plan. Include an equivalent changed case so memorized former answers do not carry the assessment. Do not deliberately create a real unsafe load or communication failure; use safe declared cues and approved controlled conditions. A failed critical response requires remediation and another independent task.

Worked case: the previous site used direct hand signals, while the current route requires an agreed radio relay. The candidate must demonstrate the current command structure, handover, operator perspective and stop-on-loss behavior. Passing the old hand-signal sequence alone is insufficient. Changed case: the new sling has a larger nominal rating but different hitch restrictions and incompatible geometry. The candidate must reject the unapproved substitution and obtain competent planning; a higher number is not proof of suitability.

At issue, state the actual reassessed scope, date, evidence, assessor and review/renewal conditions adopted by the responsible organization. Do not automatically extend an external certificate or erase a period when authorization was absent. Retain prior award and new result as separate records. If only part of the scope is demonstrated, provide an accurate limited or incomplete record; never hide the unassessed portion behind a generic renewed label.

---

courses.title: VUC088 | VUC088 reassessment workbook and assessor guide

content.title: VUC088 | VUC088 reassessment workbook and assessor guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC088 reassessment workbook and assessor guide
lessons.body: # VUC088 reassessment workbook and assessor guide

lessons.title: Entry, scope and preparation
lessons.body:
## Entry, scope and preparation

Candidate presents an authenticated previous competence award/record in the proposed scope and verified subsequent experience. Initial training attendance alone is not entry evidence for this renewal route. Assessor verifies actual task participation and physical readiness for the planned activities through the delivery organization's appropriate process. Missing evidence leads to a development plan, not a fictional pass. This original VNDRLY route does not assert satisfaction of OPITO's controlled entry/logbook rules. If an external OPITO award is sought, its approved centre must apply the actual current scheme requirements separately.

Before assessment, record equipment family, load types, operating environment, signal methods and excluded work. Competent assessor and authorized operator must understand the actual lift plans. The assessor must be qualified for the technical scope and able to judge independently. A production supervisor's desire to fill a shift cannot override evidence. Candidate may complete refresher chapters and coached practice first; controlled attempts begin only after the boundary between practice and assessment is stated.

Resources: approved lifting appliance and site, actual manuals and rated accessories, identified loads with verified lifting points/CG, competent plans L88-A/B, examination/inspection records, barriers, appropriate communications, supports, PPE, actual emergency arrangements, forms, official signal chart and segregated defect examples. Do not use damaged examples in an actual lift. No equipment rating or site clearance is inferred from this workbook.

lessons.title: Required evidence range — original VNDRLY criteria
lessons.body:
## Required evidence range — original VNDRLY criteria

Two distinct authenticated workplace jobs since the previous award, E1 and E2, must establish relevant maintained practice and cover both slinger and banksman roles. Each has plan/reference, date, equipment, load, candidate actions, supervisor identity and verification. They may precede this reassessment but must follow the previous award; neither may be invented for this course. Current direct assessment requires two complete planned operations A and B with a meaningful difference in load/configuration or route/visibility. The candidate performs both roles across those operations, with role changes only after the load is safely supported and the handover agreed. At least one current direct observation is in the actual workplace. The other may be a representative approved training facility operation that genuinely covers the declared scope.

Required range: load/CG verification; plan-based selection; inspection/rejection; supported attachment/protection; agreed hand and voice signaling; one planned restricted-view communication relay or handover; exclusion/retreat control; take-up/trial check; controlled movement; stable landing/detachment; change/stop response; accurate records. Restricted-view practice must use a competent plan and reliable agreed communication, not an improvised blind lift. If the site scope does not permit a required activity, arrange an approved representative assessment rather than pretend it occurred. No award until all required range is evidenced.

Excluded: personnel lifts, tandem/multiple-crane lifts, unplanned load rotation, emergency recovery, live electrical proximity, dynamic offshore lifts and equipment/functions not assessed. Additional scope requires its own competent plan, development and assessment. The certificate lists actual assessed scope; it is not unlimited lifting authority.

lessons.title: L88-A/B actual-operation plan record
lessons.body:
## L88-A/B actual-operation plan record

Plan/version___ Site/date___ Competent planner___ Assessor___ Authorized operator___ Candidate role for each phase___ Appliance/model/manual/configuration___ Ground/support/anchor and route verification___ Load identity/mass/contents/CG___ Below-hook accessories and chart treatment___ Designed lifting points___ Rigging IDs/type/hitch/angles/ratings___ Environment/limits___ Pickup and landing supports___ Exclusion/access control___ Safe positions/retreat___ Signal/relay/handover arrangements___ Stop and safe securing/lowering response___ Emergency arrangements___ Independent checks/approval___.

All fields must be completed using actual evidence before the operation. This course provides no generic crane chart or universal load ceiling. Each operation must be within the equipment and competent plan. The assessor observes; the authorized operator controls the machine. Use the minimum movement needed to demonstrate the planned task, with no unnecessary exposure. Do not deliberately create a real defect, unstable load, electrical hazard or uncontrolled communication failure to test the candidate.

A should use a straightforward identified load with normal visibility. B uses a materially different approved configuration/load or route and includes the planned communication relay/handover range. The candidate must know the task and decision criteria; undisclosed assessment cues concern information changes, not hidden physical hazards. A role-player may announce an obstruction while the load is safely controlled; the candidate must stop and follow the plan. Actual unsafe conditions always stop assessment immediately.

lessons.title: E88 synthetic portfolio review cards — practice only
lessons.body:
## E88 synthetic portfolio review cards — practice only

E1 practice record: 6 November, job Cedar-41, candidate inspected and attached a verified skid under supervisor N. Vale. Plan LP-41, sling IDs S11/S12, inspection record IR-41 and task-specific observation describe the candidate's actual decisions. Supervisor can be authenticated through the approved company channel. This supports the stated slinger actions, not unseen banksman work.

E2 practice record: 12 November, job Cedar-52, candidate directed a different approved load using agreed radio commands and a planned relay around a visual obstruction. Plan LP-52 and supervisor observation identify the role and stop/handover actions. This supports those banksman actions if authentic and relevant to declared scope.

E3 practice record: undated photo of a landed load with “crew did well.” No candidate role, plan or observer. It does not establish individual competence. E4 practice record: a log copied from a colleague with a different candidate identifier. Do not accept it as this candidate's work; investigate fairly and obtain actual evidence without assuming that the colleague's valid work transfers.

These cards teach evidence review only. They must never be submitted as a real learner's workplace experience. The assessor replaces them with genuine candidate records at delivery and leaves missing fields unresolved until obtained.

lessons.title: A88/B88 refresher calculation cards
lessons.body:
## A88/B88 refresher calculation cards

A1: dry skid 900 kg + contents 120 kg + below-hook rigging 80 kg = 1,100 kg stated contribution. Actual chart treatment follows the actual appliance manual. A2: 1,000 force-unit beam, pick points 2 m apart, CG 0.5 m from left → vertical shares 750 left/250 right. CG moved to 0.8 m → 600/400.

A3: symmetric two-leg W 1,000 at 60 degrees from horizontal → 577.35 axial units per leg; 45 degrees → 707.11; 30 degrees → 1,000. Fictional leg limit 600 fails the latter two. B: W 800 at 45 degrees → 565.69, failing fictional limit 550; at 60 degrees → 461.88, but changing geometry still requires competent planning. No actual lift uses these fictional ratings.

U88 unequal-load case: W 1,200, span 3 m, CG 1 m from left → vertical shares 800/400. At 60 degrees each, axial tensions 923.76/461.88. Left leg limit 900 fails. A spare marked 1,100 has an incompatible connection; reject substitution despite the larger rating. If CG becomes centered, shares 600/600 and tensions 692.82 each, but the change is a new planning condition, not learner authorization to move contents.

Changed U88-B: W 1,500, span 3 m, CG 1.2 m from left → shares 900/600. At 45 degrees each, tensions 1,272.79/848.53. Fictional limits 1,200/900 mean left fails, right is below its individual limit. The whole proposed arrangement remains held. Do not average the two tensions or borrow spare capacity from the right leg.

lessons.title: G88 condition and substitution cards
lessons.body:
## G88 condition and substitution cards

Readable tag/current report with edge cut → remove from task. Missing tag despite good appearance → do not infer rating. Deformed connector/thread damage → quarantine, no improvised repair. Correct strength but wrong hitch or incompatible geometry → not suitable until the competent approved configuration is established. Loose protection or hook-tip seating → correct only while supported/unloaded. A substituted component can change load direction and fit; approval must cover the whole arrangement, not just a nominal number.

lessons.title: S88 communication and Z88 change cues
lessons.body:
## S88 communication and Z88 change cues

Review the official selected hand signals at https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926SubpartCCAppA . Demonstrate stop, emergency stop, hoist, lower, swing and move slowly twice in different random orders, without load movement. These are the common refresher set. Add and assess every additional signal function actually needed by L88-A/B before those operations. A missing required signal prevents that task; the six selected signals do not certify all crane functions.

Agree voice commands and operator perspective before each operation. Identify the appliance when needed; use function/direction, distance/speed and function stop. Plan relay responsibility so only the agreed signal source directs movement at a time. Handover occurs in a safe stopped state and is acknowledged by operator, outgoing and incoming signaler. Loss/conflict/ambiguity means safe stop and re-established understanding.

Z1: planned landing blocked. Z2: pedestrian approaches boundary. Z3: retreat route obstructed. Z4: new overhead service on revised drawing. Z5: weather/visibility beyond actual plan. Z6: missing support. Z7: radio loss announced during a safe controlled phase. Z8: reported damaged hardware after communications restored. Each requires the appropriate stop/hold and competent resolution; fixing one does not fix the others. Do not physically introduce any danger to create the cue.

lessons.title: C88 mandatory practical criteria and decision rule
lessons.body:
## C88 mandatory practical criteria and decision rule

C1 verifies task/scope/role and actual plan. C2 verifies load/CG and configuration basis. C3 selects identified suitable rigging. C4 inspects and rejects defects. C5 attaches/protects correctly while supported. C6 establishes zone/position and maintains it. C7 communicates clear agreed signals and handovers. C8 performs controlled take-up/trial observation. C9 controls planned movement and responds to change. C10 lands stably and detaches only when safe. C11 records authentic evidence and limits. C12 demonstrates both roles and all required range independently. C13 verifies prior award and maintained-practice/gap evidence. C14 demonstrates the current changed procedures/equipment within assessed scope.

Every C criterion must be MET with direct evidence where applicable and all required range complete. C3–C10 and truthful C11 are critical: known unsafe action or fabrication prevents award. A criterion may be NOT MET or NOT OBSERVED; neither is silently converted to MET. Score each station for feedback, but no percentage can replace all-criterion competence. Assessor prompts that supply a critical decision invalidate independent evidence for that outcome.

lessons.title: F88 reusable evidence, decision and appeal record
lessons.body:
## F88 reusable evidence, decision and appeal record

Candidate___ Assessor/technical scope___ Independent reviewer___ Previous award/issuer/status verified___ Post-award practice/gaps reviewed___ Declared award scope/exclusions___ E1/E2 actual job references and authenticity checks___ L88-A/B versions___ Current workplace observation reference___.

For C1–C14: task/role/condition___ evidence ID/time___ actual behavior___ assistance/intervention___ MET/NOT MET/NOT OBSERVED___ rationale___ missing range___ remediation___ changed reassessment___ assessor/date___. Attach actual plan, condition checks, signal observations, relevant photographs only with authorization and candidate-specific witness evidence.

Overall decision___ Knowledge scores___ Practical/range completeness___ Feedback provided___ Candidate response___ Independent appeal contact/process___ Review finding___ Scope authorized for certificate___ Employer appointment separate___.

Candidate may challenge the decision verbally or in writing to the course lead; independent competent review examines preserved evidence and may uphold, correct or arrange fresh assessment. Explain this route before assessment. No retaliation or forced agreement signature. Corrections preserve original entries with author/date/reason. Sensitive readiness details and controlled keys stay outside the public learner folder under the organization's approved privacy/retention arrangements.

lessons.title: Application labs
lessons.body:
## Application labs

### W88-1 — Portfolio and scope audit

Evaluate E1–E4 and build a C88 evidence map. Model: E1 supports slinger work, E2 supports banksman work if verified; E3/E4 cannot supply missing personal competence. List the actual workplace records needed. Do not count synthetic cards as real entry evidence.

### W88-2 — Configuration clinic

Solve A88/B88/U88 and explain why a higher-rated incompatible spare is still rejected. Model: unequal left tension 923.76 exceeds 900; centered recalculation does not authorize a physical change. Draw angle references and distinguish vertical shares from axial tension.

### W88-3 — Inspection and attachment development

Practice actual safe accessory inspection and supported attachment under instructor coaching before the final. Record help given. Model: defect rejection, valid replacement, correct seating/protection and no loaded adjustment. Practice success prepares but does not pre-score the controlled attempt.

### W88-4 — Signals, relay and access control

Practice the selected and task-specific signals, then a stopped handover/relay sequence and Z cues. Model: one agreed movement source, operator perspective, clear stop and confirmed restoration. No actual dangerous blind movement is improvised.

### W88-5 — Two-role complete operation rehearsal

Under an approved plan, rehearse the sequence in both roles with safe role changes only after support. Model: plan-to-equipment match, inspection, attachment, zone, take-up, movement, stable landing and detachment. The later controlled A/B observations use independent candidate decisions.

### W88-6 — Judgment and remediation case

Candidate has 90 percent knowledge but required a prompt to stop for Z2. Model: C6/C9 independent performance not established; withhold award, target training and use a changed cue after practice. Retain the earlier attempt. Review an assessor-error challenge fairly and document correction if evidence supports it.

lessons.title: Sixteen individual stations
lessons.body:
## Sixteen individual stations

Stations 5–10 involve actual inspection/attachment/signaling/zone/movement/landing and direct equipment work; station 7 includes physical signaling. The other ten are observed evidence/planning/calculation/response/decision encounters. Score 0 absent/unsafe, 1 substantial prompting, 2 material gaps, 3 independently satisfactory, 4 robust under changed conditions. Require at least 3 each, plus every C88 criterion and range MET. A high total never compensates for critical failure or missing workplace evidence.

### P88-01 — Readiness and scope

Task: Audit E88 evidence and define the combined-role scope.

Acceptance: Authentic prior development and both roles established or gaps explicitly held; no unsupported award.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-02 — Plan and environment

Task: Review completed L88-A/B and inspect the actual route, landing and interfaces.

Acceptance: Plan matches conditions; changes referred before movement; safe positions and rescue/emergency routes preserved.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-03 — Load and center of gravity

Task: Verify actual load information and solve A88/B88 paper checks separately.

Acceptance: Contents/rigging and CG considered; paper numbers not applied to real equipment.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-04 — Configuration and limits

Task: Select actual plan-approved rigging and explain hitch/angle/component limits.

Acceptance: Correct identities and configuration; no equal-share assumption for an unequal case or unapproved substitution.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-05 — Inspection

Task: Individually inspect the actual accessories and quarantined examples.

Acceptance: Present defects/identity gaps rejected despite certificates; records and suitable replacements verified.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-06 — Attachment

Task: Independently attach and protect the supported load under the actual approved plan.

Acceptance: Seating, orientation, compatibility and protection correct; hands clear; no solution prompts.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-07 — Signaling

Task: Demonstrate agreed hand/voice signals and a planned restricted-view relay/handover rehearsal.

Acceptance: All required movement functions clear; one signal source at a time, stop on uncertainty, operator perspective maintained.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-08 — Exclusion and position

Task: Establish and maintain the actual work zone and retreat positions.

Acceptance: No fall/swing/trap exposure; controlled access and incursion stop response demonstrated.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-09 — Take-up and balance

Task: Direct or perform the assigned role in planned take-up/trial checks.

Acceptance: Smooth planned sequence, load free and secure, safe stop/lower on announced abnormal cue.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-10 — Movement and landing

Task: Perform both roles across the two planned actual operations, including route and stable landing.

Acceptance: Continuous control, safe receiving, full support before detachment; no floor-model substitution for actual movement evidence.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-11 — Change and emergency

Task: Respond to declared communication loss and changed-condition cards with the operation safely controlled.

Acceptance: Stop/secure per plan, resolve each control, no improvised recovery or restart.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-12 — Workplace evidence

Task: Authenticate two distinct jobs and map actual candidate actions.

Acceptance: At least one current direct workplace observation; both roles/range covered; no fabricated or merely crew-level evidence.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-13 — Unequal-load judgment

Task: Calculate U88 and evaluate a proposed stronger but incompatible replacement.

Acceptance: Correct unequal tensions and hold decision; configuration approval required beyond nominal strength.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

### P88-14 — Independent decision and records

Task: Complete the criterion matrix, feedback and bounded award recommendation.

Acceptance: All mandatory criteria/range supported, failed attempts retained, independent review/appeal available.

Evidence/criterion___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed reassessment___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: R88 prior-award and currency evidence cards
lessons.body:
## R88 prior-award and currency evidence cards

Synthetic practice candidate Riley Stone, ID RS-88. Prior record PR-88 shows combined-role scope for identified yard equipment and direct hand/voice signals, assessed 18 November 2024. Its issuer and status must be authenticated through an approved channel. The date alone does not establish current external validity or eligibility. Do not use this fictional record for an actual candidate.

R1: workplace job E1 dated 8 April 2026 records Riley selecting, inspecting and attaching a planned skid under a named supervisor, with plan and accessory references. R2: E2 dated 3 September 2026 records Riley directing a different load with the agreed communication arrangement and a documented stop for an obstruction. Verify actual records and candidate role at delivery; these examples only teach review. R3: candidate reports no lifting work from October 2025 to March 2026. Identify the gap, discuss practice since return and collect current evidence rather than assuming either automatic competence or permanent inability. R4: a near miss involved an ambiguous radio handover; corrective action introduced explicit stopped handover and acknowledgment. Reassessment must demonstrate that behavior, not merely read the investigation summary.

R5 changed scenario: a different candidate has only a past initial-training attendance record and no competence award. Do not issue a renewal; route to appropriate development and initial competence assessment. R6: a purported external award is expired and scheme eligibility is unresolved. Do not invent a grace period, backdate or claim external renewal. Verify the applicable route with the authorized scheme process while continuing legitimate refresher learning.

lessons.title: M88 change matrix and current-method cards
lessons.body:
## M88 change matrix and current-method cards

Old condition: direct visibility throughout. New condition: approved route includes restricted visibility and planned radio relay. Required learning/evidence: agreed source, operator perspective, stopped handover, repeat-back and stop on communication loss. The actual lift still requires the completed competent L88 plan; the card is not a blind-lift authorization.

Old accessory: identified sling with approved hitch. Proposed new accessory: higher nominal rating but a different hitch restriction and incompatible connection. Candidate must reject unapproved substitution and obtain compatible plan-approved equipment. Do not physically load the incompatible example.

Old record: paper log with supervisor signature only. Current record: candidate-specific task evidence and traceable plan/version links required. Candidate maps actual actions, not crew output. Changed signal convention or procedure must be learned before the controlled attempt; no surprise unsupported convention is introduced during a live operation.

Matrix form: previous award/scope___ old condition___ new condition___ affected criterion___ refresher/practice___ actual current evidence___ independent result___ remaining restriction___ assessor/reviewer/date___.

### W88-7 — Maintained-practice review

Evaluate R1–R6 and write the entry/competence distinction. Model: verify prior award, post-award jobs, gap and corrective action; obtain current direct performance. R5 is not a renewal candidate. R6 requires scheme-route verification, not fabricated extension. No calendar age by itself proves skill.

### W88-8 — Change and renewal decision

Use M88 and the near-miss correction to plan a current-method demonstration. Model: stopped acknowledged handover, compatible rigging and candidate-specific records must be demonstrated independently. A correct old method does not establish the changed skill. Draft a scope-bounded renewal record without backdating or implying external approval.

### P88-15 — Maintained competence and eligibility

Task: authenticate the prior record and evaluate post-award jobs, gap and incident-learning evidence using R88. Acceptance: entry versus competence distinguished; no invented grace period or automatic pass; current evidence plan addresses actual gaps. Evidence___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Assessor/date___.

### P88-16 — Changed method and bounded renewal

Task: complete M88, demonstrate the changed communication method in a safe rehearsal and justify the final scope recommendation. Acceptance: new method independently understood, incompatible substitute rejected, limitations and dates truthful. Evidence___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Assessor/date___.

lessons.title: I88 integrated competence reassessment
lessons.body:
## I88 integrated competence reassessment

Conduct L88-A/B as defined, with candidate performing both roles and all required range, one direct workplace observation, authenticated E1/E2 and individual oral explanation of U88. Fourteen dimensions correspond to C1–C14, each 0–4. Require at least 45/56, every dimension at least 3, every mandatory criterion MET, all range and no critical error. Quantitative threshold is an additional quality check, not a substitute for complete competence. Assessor stops real danger immediately. A failed attempt is retained and followed by targeted development and a changed task, not coached continuation labeled independent.

lessons.title: Delivery and credential rules
lessons.body:
## Delivery and credential rules

Planned 44 hours: refresher instruction 8; development labs 10; individual stations 10; integrated operations/evidence review 10; controlled final and administration 3; feedback/review 3. Workplace experience accumulation is additional and depends on genuine opportunities, not a fictional fixed number of hours. Breaks and necessary remedial training are additional.

Controlled final sixteen cases, three decisions each, 96 points, 150 minutes. Pass 77/96, at least 4/6 each domain and no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; keys, collaboration and generative assistance prohibited. Changed Form B after remediation. Practical failure requires fresh practical evidence; written retake alone is insufficient.

Issue “VNDRLY/U Banksman and Slinger — competence reassessed in recorded scope” only after entry/authenticity, corrected formative checks, sixteen stations, I88, all C88/range and final pass with independent competent review. Record scope, equipment, roles, dates, evidence, assessor and program/hash. If workplace evidence is absent, issue only an accurate incomplete/development record, not a competence certificate. No OPITO award or automatic employer appointment is conferred. Review when work/equipment/ability changes and follow applicable employer or external renewal rules; do not invent universal validity from this original package.


---

content.title: VUC088 | VUC088 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC088 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC088 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q88-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-01-L1

Does a log saying “assisted” prove both roles?

**Answer:** No; establish the candidate’s specific actions and scope.

**Reason/remediation:** Crew completion is not individual evidence. Revisit Q88-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-01-L2

Can a controlled assessor supply the correct critical decision and still count independence?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Record the prompt and obtain a changed independent demonstration after development. Revisit Q88-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-02-L1

The landing area is blocked. Can the crew improvise a route over a walkway?

**Answer:** No; hold and refer the plan change.

**Reason/remediation:** The approved route and exposure controls no longer match. Revisit Q88-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-02-L2

Should dunnage be found after lifting?

**Answer:** No; prepare and verify the landing first.

**Reason/remediation:** Unplanned suspension while arranging support adds risk. Revisit Q88-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-03-L1

Dry load 900 kg, contents 120, rigging 80: total contribution?

**Answer:** 1,100 kg.

**Reason/remediation:** Include the stated contributions; actual chart deductions remain equipment-specific. Revisit Q88-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-03-L2

Which support carries more when the center of gravity moves toward it?

**Answer:** The nearer support.

**Reason/remediation:** Static moments determine unequal vertical shares. Revisit Q88-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-04-L1

At 30 degrees from horizontal with symmetric W 1,000, tension per leg?

**Answer:** 1,000 force units.

**Reason/remediation:** W divided by twice sine 30 degrees; no real lift approval follows. Revisit Q88-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-04-L2

Do four legs necessarily share equally?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Geometry, stiffness and center of gravity can prevent equal sharing. Revisit Q88-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-05-L1

Current examination but visible damage: usable?

**Answer:** No; remove and refer under the applicable criteria.

**Reason/remediation:** Present condition can invalidate previously satisfactory equipment. Revisit Q88-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-05-L2

Can sling color replace a missing tag?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Identity and applicable rating must be established. Revisit Q88-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-06-L1

Does a hook latch support the load?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The load must seat in the intended load-bearing region. Revisit Q88-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-06-L2

Can a sling be shortened with a knot?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use only approved configuration/adjustment methods. Revisit Q88-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-07-L1

Radio contact is lost. Continue the last command?

**Answer:** No; stop safely and restore agreed communication.

**Reason/remediation:** Guessing can create uncontrolled movement. Revisit Q88-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-07-L2

Directions use whose perspective?

**Answer:** The operator’s agreed perspective.

**Reason/remediation:** Different viewpoints otherwise reverse intended movement. Revisit Q88-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-08-L1

Can a tag line be wrapped around the wrist?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Entanglement and pull hazards can trap the person. Revisit Q88-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-08-L2

Retreat route blocked but zone empty: continue?

**Answer:** No; restore a safe position and retreat.

**Reason/remediation:** The banksman still faces trapping risk. Revisit Q88-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-09-L1

Unexpected tilt at trial lift: correct by hand under tension?

**Answer:** No; stop and lower safely before adjustment.

**Reason/remediation:** Loaded rigging and suspended loads create crush hazards. Revisit Q88-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-09-L2

Does a trial lift establish an unknown load mass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Mass and configuration must be planned before lifting. Revisit Q88-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-10-L1

May rigging be detached while the load is rocking?

**Answer:** No; establish stable full support first.

**Reason/remediation:** Partial contact is not a safe landed condition. Revisit Q88-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-10-L2

Can the crane pull a trapped sling from beneath the load?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use the approved supported-load removal method. Revisit Q88-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-11-L1

Radio restored but hardware defect remains: restart?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Each failed control must be resolved. Revisit Q88-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-11-L2

Is one universal wind limit supplied here?

**Answer:** No; actual plan and equipment/load conditions govern.

**Reason/remediation:** Generic numbers cannot account for all configurations and sail areas. Revisit Q88-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-12-L1

Can synthetic E88 cards serve as actual workplace experience?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** They are practice resources; real authenticated candidate evidence is required. Revisit Q88-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-12-L2

A candidate has slinger evidence only. Combined-role award?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Banksman performance and required range must also be established. Revisit Q88-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-13-L1

U88 left share 800 at 60 degrees: axial tension?

**Answer:** 923.76 force units.

**Reason/remediation:** 800 divided by sine 60; it exceeds the fictional 900 allowance. Revisit Q88-13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-13-L2

Can a stronger incompatible connector be substituted?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Fit, load direction and approved configuration matter as well as rating. Revisit Q88-13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-14-L1

Does 90 percent knowledge compensate for prompted critical practical performance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Mandatory independent practical criteria remain unmet. Revisit Q88-14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-14-L2

Must an assessor correct a substantiated recording error?

**Answer:** Yes, transparently with preserved history and reasons.

**Reason/remediation:** Fair review concerns evidence, not defending the original conclusion. Revisit Q88-14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-15-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-15-L1

Does a previous award prove uninterrupted current practice?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Verify subsequent roles, gaps, changes and current independent performance. Revisit Q88-15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-15-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-15-L2

Can a lapsed external award be backdated to preserve continuity?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Apply the actual scheme route and retain truthful dates/status. Revisit Q88-15 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-16-L1
lessons.body:
## Q88-16-L1

Does a higher-rated but incompatible replacement pass selection?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Current fit, hitch and approved configuration still govern. Revisit Q88-16 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q88-16-L2
lessons.body:
## Q88-16-L2

Does knowing the old signal method prove the changed relay method?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** The current method needs learning and independent demonstration. Revisit Q88-16 and perform its changed application.


---

lessons.title: VUC088 source review and coverage — 18 November 2026
lessons.body: # VUC088 source review and coverage — 18 November 2026

lessons.title: Available primary sources
lessons.body:
## Available primary sources

- OPITO 9069: https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/banksman-slinger-competence-reassessment-previously-stage-4 . Public scope is maintained combined-role competence, four units and seven-hour reassessment, with specified prior-award entry and lapse provisions and two-year external validity. Full controlled specification was not obtained. Our original 44-hour refresher/development/reassessment route neither renews an OPITO award nor replaces its eligibility rules. External scheme status must be determined through its authorized process; no automatic grace period is inferred.
- HSE LOLER overview: https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/loler.htm . Context for competent planning/supervision and suitable lifting equipment in the applicable jurisdiction. Not a universal law for every country.
- HSE planning: https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/planning-organising-lifting-operations.htm . Reviewed task-proportionate planning, roles, foreseeable hazards, route/location and stability. Supports plan review rather than improvising around changes.
- HSE examination/inspection: https://www.hse.gov.uk/work-equipment-machinery/thorough-examinations-lifting-equipment.htm . Pre-use condition checks and competent thorough examination are distinct. A current report does not excuse a new defect. Actual scheme/manufacturer criteria govern; no universal inspection interval is invented here.
- OSHA slings: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.184 . Reviewed safe-use/identification and damaged-equipment boundaries. Detailed rejection limits differ by sling type; this course requires the actual applicable criteria rather than an invented single wear allowance.
- OSHA signals: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1419 . Reviewed designated signaler, stop on interrupted/unclear communication, emergency stop and operator perspective. U.S. construction scope is identified, not assumed universal.
- OSHA voice signals: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1421 . Agreed voice communication and function/direction, distance/speed and stop structure support S88 practice.
- OSHA signal-person qualification: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1428 . Knowledge and practical demonstration plus documented qualification are distinct from generic attendance. This limited initial program does not claim to complete every qualification requirement or all signal types.
- OSHA official hand-signal chart: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926SubpartCCAppA . Six selected signals are taught and practiced against the chart; other crane functions remain outside the assessed set. No proprietary chart is reproduced.
- OSHA keeping clear: https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1926/1926.1425 . Supports reducing exposure to load/fall zones. Our training fixture uses stricter no-under-load/no-suspended-horizontal-travel boundaries and does not purport to summarize every regulatory exception.
- Crosby rigging information: https://www.thecrosbygroup.com/wp-content/uploads/catalog/2016/en-US/473.pdf . Selected static angle/load-share principles reviewed; displayed document is historical, not a current model rating. Original calculations use explicitly fictional force units and ratings. Real manufacturer tables, configuration and competent planning control actual selection. No inferred universal permission to use a shallow angle is given.

lessons.title: Coverage and evidence
lessons.body:
## Coverage and evidence

Q88-01 roles → L88 briefing/P88-01; Q88-02 plan → Z88/W88-1/P88-02; Q88-03 load/CG → A1/A2/B88/P88-03; Q88-04 geometry/rating → A3/A4/W88-2/P88-04; Q88-05 inspection → G88/P88-05; Q88-06 attachment → supported-load task/P88-06; Q88-07 signals → S88/P88-07 and two randomized sequences; Q88-08 position → Z88/P88-08; Q88-09 trial → L88/P88-09; Q88-10 landing → L88/P88-10; Q88-11 abnormal → changed cards/P88-11; Q88-12 development → F88/P88-12. Every chapter has two explained checks and its own controlled final/changed case. Six labs and I88 integrate the work.

lessons.title: Delivery and claim boundaries
lessons.body:
## Delivery and claim boundaries

Paper masses/ratings are never used for a real lift. Actual facility plan fields must be completed from identified suitable equipment before supervised practical delivery. This is a delivery control, not a pre-issued learner result. Six physical stations and ten observed review encounters are required for the training award. Actual A/B operations require competent equipment-specific plans and current movement/landing evidence. Required restricted-view signaling uses an approved relay/handover. Tandem, personnel and dynamic offshore lifts remain outside the defined scope. Materials completion, learner achievement, workplace competence and publication remain separate states.

lessons.title: Competence-specific instruction and evidence
lessons.body:
## Competence-specific instruction and evidence

Q88-01 and Q88-12 explicitly teach entry/scope and candidate-specific workplace evidence. Q88-13 teaches unequal loading/configuration changes using U88, P88-13 and controlled case 13. Q88-14 teaches independent judgment, remediation and fair review using C88/F88, P88-14 and case 14. Two authenticated jobs and two current direct operations, including at least one workplace observation, are original VNDRLY requirements, not claimed OPITO task counts. All C88 criteria and required range must be met. Common reviewed rigging instruction from VUC086 is included as refresher; this package stands alone and adds a distinct competence decision process.

lessons.title: Renewal-specific coverage
lessons.body:
## Renewal-specific coverage

Q88-15/R88/W88-7/P88-15 teach and assess authenticated previous award, post-award practice, gaps, incident learning and eligibility versus current competence. Q88-16/M88/W88-8/P88-16 cover changed methods, independent demonstration, truthful dates and bounded renewal. Each has two explained checks and a controlled final/changed case. C13/C14 add mandatory currency/change criteria to the retained technical C1–C12. Sixteen chapters, thirty-two checks, eight labs and sixteen stations form a standalone package. Reviewed common technical content from VUC086/087 is retained in full; no prior purchase or missing refresher module is required.
