lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Blaster and Sprayer — Initial Training
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Blaster and Sprayer — Initial Training

Program VUC089. Original materials, available-source basis, 18 November 2026. This is not OPITO approval or an external award. Learners must be able to understand instructions and complete practical activity safely; provide accessible instruction without removing safety-critical performance. Twelve chapters teach supervised beginner work. Training examples C89/S89/D89 are fictional and must never control a live job.

lessons.title: Q89-1 — Role, job scope and the coating system
lessons.body:
## Q89-1 — Role, job scope and the coating system

Industrial coating work preserves a prepared substrate by applying a specified system. A visually attractive finish is not proof of adhesion, thickness or corrosion protection. A beginner works within supervision, the job specification and the equipment instructions; completing this course does not appoint an independent coating inspector or authorize confined-space entry. Identify the asset, substrate, existing coating, required preparation, each coating layer, inspection hold points and who may release them. Treat the specification, product technical data sheet (TDS), application guide, safety data sheet (SDS) and equipment manual as different documents serving different decisions. The TDS gives product application constraints; the SDS explains chemical hazards and controls; neither alone is a job permit.

Before work, compare product names, component identities, batch/shelf-life information and document revisions against the job pack. Resolve contradictions with the supervisor or coating specialist before preparing a batch. A changed product is not accepted because its color matches. Inspect access, simultaneous work, services, weather protection, ventilation and waste arrangements. Brief the crew on start, stop and emergency communication. Record outstanding hold points rather than allowing a schedule target to become authorization.

Worked example: J89 specifies system C89 on steel panel A. A storekeeper supplies component B for a different system. Although both cans say hardener, the learner quarantines the mismatch, identifies the missing compatible component and requests correction. The learner does not experiment with a small mix. Changed application: the correct product arrives but the surface-preparation release is unsigned; product availability does not release that hold. The job remains stopped at that boundary.

lessons.title: Q89-2 — Hazard recognition and containment
lessons.body:
## Q89-2 — Hazard recognition and containment

Assess the old surface as well as the new materials. Abrasion can release hazardous material from existing coatings or the substrate, even when the chosen abrasive is described as low hazard. Unknown old paint requires characterization and an approved removal plan. Do not infer absence of lead, other metals or silica from appearance. Keep neighboring workers, vehicles and occupied areas outside the affected zone. Containment, extraction and suitable cleanup arrangements are planned before work, not after dust escapes.

Use the site risk assessment to address airborne contaminants, noise, moving hoses, flying particles, slips, manual handling, access and pressure. Select controls in order: eliminate or substitute where practicable, contain and ventilate the process, manage access, then use the specified personal protection. Confirm that the dust collector and ventilation are suitable for the material and ignition risks. A domestic fan is not an engineered control for a flammable spray atmosphere. Noise protection does not replace the assessment of exposure or equipment controls.

Worked example: a panel with unidentified legacy coating is placed in the training area. The correct response is to use the known clean training panel and hold the legacy panel for investigation. Simply wearing an extra disposable mask would not resolve the unknown hazard. Changed application: the assessment is complete but the extraction failure alarm operates. Stop using the process, make equipment safe by its procedure, leave the affected area as instructed and obtain restoration and release. Do not silence the alarm to finish the last patch.

lessons.title: Q89-3 — Respiratory protection, chemicals and personal readiness
lessons.body:
## Q89-3 — Respiratory protection, chemicals and personal readiness

Respirator selection belongs to the employer's respiratory-protection program and exposure assessment. A face covering chosen by the trainee is not an adequate substitute. Where tight-fitting equipment is required, medical evaluation, suitable fit testing, training and a user seal check are distinct requirements. Facial hair or other interference at the seal is a problem to resolve before use. Supplied breathing air and its connections must be appropriate for breathing; ordinary plant compressed air is not presumed safe. Learn the actual equipment's checks, air-supply failure response and limitations before use.

Read the selected product's SDS for inhalation, skin, eye, sensitization, fire, incompatibility and first-aid information. Gloves must be suitable for the actual chemical and exposure duration, not merely described as chemical resistant. Arrange washing and contamination control so workers do not take residue into eating areas or vehicles. Keep labels with decanted materials under the applicable workplace system. Never use solvent to clean skin. Tell the instructor about a condition or discomfort affecting safe participation through the appropriate confidential route.

Worked example: a trainee's supplied-air hose has an unidentified connector that fits a nearby utility outlet. The trainee refuses connection until the designated breathing-air system and compatibility are verified. Physical fit does not establish safe air quality. Changed application: the approved respiratory equipment becomes damaged during practice. Stop and replace or repair through the authorized process; a reduced task duration does not compensate for failed protection.

lessons.title: Q89-4 — Blast equipment and pressure control
lessons.body:
## Q89-4 — Blast equipment and pressure control

Identify the actual compressor, receiver or pressure vessel, metering arrangement, hose, couplings, restraint devices, remote control, nozzle and extraction system using the manufacturer's diagram. Inspection is systematic: identity and pressure suitability, inspection status, hose condition, coupling security, restraints, controls and safe routing. Missing identity or damaged components are quarantined. A pressure rating on one part does not establish the entire assembly's suitability. Never connect, disconnect, open or repair pressurized equipment on the assumption that the supply switch being off proves zero stored energy.

The instructor demonstrates the exact manufacturer start, remote-stop and shutdown sequence on the approved training installation. The learner rehearses it unpressurized, then performs it under direct supervision after readiness checks. Verify the remote control operates as designed before production. Do not tie it open, bypass a control or use a makeshift nozzle restraint. Keep the nozzle directed into the designated safe work zone, with stable posture and controlled hose routing. Depressurization, isolation and verification precede maintenance or blockage investigation according to the actual manual.

Worked example: releasing the remote control does not stop flow during a controlled test. The instructor uses the installation's planned safe shutdown; the system is removed from service. The learner does not continue by relying on the compressor operator to guess when to stop. Changed application: a hose shows a bulge but no leak. Reject it before pressure is applied. The absence of a visible leak is not evidence that a damaged pressure component is safe.

lessons.title: Q89-5 — Surface preparation and inspection hold points
lessons.body:
## Q89-5 — Surface preparation and inspection hold points

Remove contaminants by the approved method before abrasive preparation; blasting is not a universal way to remove grease or soluble contamination. Protect surfaces and fittings not to be treated. Deal with sharp edges, weld irregularities and other specified preparation needs through the authorized procedure. Choose the approved abrasive and method for the substrate and coating system. Excessive preparation can damage thin sections or distort components, while insufficient preparation can leave weak material under the coating.

Separate three questions: cleanliness, profile and contamination. A clean-looking surface can have the wrong profile or residual salts. The job specifies the visual reference, measurement method, sampling and acceptance criteria; use the actual authorized standards or comparators where required. This package does not reproduce proprietary visual grades or supply a substitute visual acceptance standard. Practice recognizing these separate questions on labeled training samples, then perform the prescribed tests with verified instruments. Do not average away an unacceptable location unless the specified acceptance rule expressly allows that treatment.

Worked example: fictional S89 requires recorded profile values from 40 to 65 micrometres at every listed training location, with an instructor-issued cleanliness release and contamination release. Values 48, 56 and 68 fail the upper limit at the third location. The learner holds coating and asks for an approved correction; painting more thickly is not an authorized repair. Changed application: all profile values pass but the contamination release is missing. The hold remains. After preparation protect the surface and recheck if contamination, condensation or delay could invalidate its condition.

lessons.title: Q89-6 — Climate, condensation and timing
lessons.body:
## Q89-6 — Climate, condensation and timing

Measure the conditions required by the actual coating documents at the work surface, not merely a distant weather station. Air temperature, relative humidity, surface temperature and dew point affect application and cure. A surface may be colder than the surrounding air. Record instrument identity, location, time and readings, then apply the product-specific limits. This course's synthetic limits are classroom rules only; they must never be copied into a real coating specification.

Card C89 requires surface temperature at least 3 degrees Celsius above dew point, surface temperature from 10 to 35 degrees Celsius inclusive, and relative humidity no greater than 80 percent. All three conditions must pass. At surface 18, dew point 14 and humidity 74, the margin is 4 and the card permits the climate condition. At surface 16 with the same dew point the margin is 2, so application is held. A good humidity reading does not offset a failed dew-point margin. Monitor changes during work and stop when conditions leave the permitted range.

Worked example: the initial reading passes, but the next recorded surface reading is 12 with dew point 10. The margin is 2, so the learner stops application and records the affected time and area for review. Waiting until the shift ends to report it would conceal a quality uncertainty. Changed application: surface 10, dew point 7 and humidity 80 meets all inclusive training boundaries; surface 9.9 fails the minimum even though the margin may remain adequate. Real sampling frequency and restart release follow the job plan.

lessons.title: Q89-7 — Mixing, induction, pot life and batch traceability
lessons.body:
## Q89-7 — Mixing, induction, pot life and batch traceability

Identify every component before opening it. Verify the mixing basis: a volume ratio is not automatically a mass ratio because component densities may differ. Follow the product instructions for pre-mixing, combining, mixing technique, induction and any permitted thinner. Do not guess a thinner or add solvent to extend a material's life. Use clean suitable measuring equipment, capture spills and label the mixed batch with its identity and timing. Keep traceability to the component batches and the area coated.

Fictional C89 uses base and curing component at 4: 1 by volume, no thinner, 10 minutes induction and 60 minutes pot life measured from initial combination at the stated training temperature. A 5 litre batch uses 4 litres base and 1 litre curing component. For 2.5 litres use 2 and 0.5. If combined at 09:00, the earliest application is 09:10 and the discard deadline is 10:00; induction consumes part of the pot life. This card is a calculation exercise, not a recipe for actual chemicals. Real products may define timing differently and their instructions govern.

Worked example: the crew expects to apply 1.8 litres but proposes a full 5 litre batch close to the end of the allowed window. The learner plans a permitted smaller batch only if the actual product allows accurate partial mixing; otherwise the supervisor resolves packaging and waste. Changed application: a batch remains liquid after the stated pot-life deadline. Appearance does not extend the deadline. Segregate and dispose through the approved waste route instead of blending expired material into a fresh batch.

lessons.title: Q89-8 — Application technique and safe spraying
lessons.body:
## Q89-8 — Application technique and safe spraying

Set up the actual spray equipment, coating and tip using their compatible instructions. Confirm the work zone, ventilation, electrical and ignition controls, pressure suitability, guards, trigger lock and hose condition. Practice the movement first without energized discharge. During supervised application maintain the specified distance, orientation, overlap and speed appropriate to the actual system; excessive pressure is not the default cure for a poor pattern. Stop to diagnose material, tip, equipment and setup rather than compensating blindly.

Airless equipment can inject fluid through skin. Never point the gun at a person, place a hand over the tip or use a hand to find or stop a leak. Follow the manufacturer's pressure-relief and isolation procedure before clearing, servicing or changing relevant components. A small-looking injection wound needs immediate emergency medical attention; tell responders the material and mechanism and provide the SDS without delaying care. The actual manual determines the equipment sequence, not a generic sequence from another model.

Worked example: a spray pattern develops tails. The learner stops, secures and relieves the system as instructed, then asks the supervisor to review the approved setup and material condition. Reaching toward a pressurized tip is a critical failure. Changed application: a hose leak sprays onto a glove and the worker reports a pinprick. Activate the emergency response and urgent medical evaluation; do not dismiss it because bleeding is slight. Keep others clear and have the qualified person make equipment safe.

lessons.title: Q89-9 — Film thickness, coverage and material planning
lessons.body:
## Q89-9 — Film thickness, coverage and material planning

Wet film thickness is measured during application; dry film thickness is assessed after the appropriate drying or curing condition. A prediction is not a dry measurement. For the unthinned fictional coating, predicted dry thickness equals wet thickness multiplied by the volume-solids fraction. C89 has 60 percent volume solids. A target dry thickness of 150 micrometres therefore requires a nominal wet thickness of 150/0.60 = 250 micrometres. A wet reading of 200 predicts 120, not 150. Product-specific thinning, roughness, shrinkage and measurement procedures may complicate real acceptance; follow the actual specification.

For a simple flat-area estimate, theoretical coverage in square metres per litre equals 1000 times the solids fraction divided by dry thickness in micrometres. C89 at 150 gives 4 square metres per litre. Twelve square metres require 3 litres theoretically. At a stated planning transfer efficiency of 75 percent, required mixed material is 3/0.75 = 4 litres. This allowance is a planning estimate, not permission to overspray or a guarantee of yield. State whether a percentage means efficiency or additional allowance; they are different calculations.

Worked example: a planner adds 25 percent to 3 litres and obtains 3.75. That does not equal the 4 litres required at 75 percent efficiency. The learner explains the denominator and plans the correct quantity. Changed application: 20 square metres at 200 micrometres and 50 percent solids gives 2.5 square metres per litre and 8 litres theoretical; at 80 percent efficiency it requires 10 litres. Record assumptions and units so a reviewer can reproduce the calculation.

lessons.title: Q89-10 — Cure, defects, repair and acceptance
lessons.body:
## Q89-10 — Cure, defects, repair and acceptance

Dry to touch, ready for recoating and ready for service are different conditions. Use the actual product and environmental history to establish the relevant timing. A surface that feels dry may not be ready for the next coat or service. Protect completed work from contamination and damage. If a recoat window is exceeded, obtain the specified preparation or manufacturer-approved disposition; another coat does not automatically restore compliance.

Recognize runs, sags, dry spray, missed edges, pinholes, contamination and nonuniform thickness as reasons to inspect and obtain a disposition, not as universal diagnoses with one repair. Record the location, extent, coating batch and conditions. Avoid hiding defects with an unapproved extra coat. Verify gauges and use the specified measurement method, substrate correction and sampling plan. The qualified inspector or authorized release person decides acceptance under the actual specification; the beginner supplies accurate evidence.

Worked example: the fictional D89 training rule requires each recorded corrected dry reading from 130 to 170 micrometres. Readings 145,152 and 125 fail at the last location, even though their average is about 140.67. This deliberately simple rule differs from some real statistical acceptance methods and must not replace them. Changed application: readings 145,152 and 168 pass the thickness card, but a visible contaminant is embedded. Hold for review; numerical thickness alone does not accept the surface. Repair is assessed against an approved instruction and reinspection, not an erased original record.

lessons.title: Q89-11 — Shutdown, waste, fire and abnormal events
lessons.body:
## Q89-11 — Shutdown, waste, fire and abnormal events

Plan shutdown before starting. Secure the work zone, stop and depressurize equipment by its actual procedure, isolate where required, then clean using compatible approved materials. Keep waste streams identified: spent abrasive, removed coating, liquid coating, contaminated wipes and solvents may need different handling. Do not assume spent abrasive is nonhazardous because the unused abrasive was acceptable; removed material changes the waste. Prevent releases to drains, soil or nearby operations, and use the site's waste determination and disposal arrangements.

Spray areas require control of ignition sources, suitable equipment and ventilation for the material. Loss of ventilation, unexpected vapor, fire, pressure-system damage or a person entering the exclusion zone calls for the planned stop and emergency response. Workers must know the alarm, escape route, muster and who contacts emergency services. This training does not authorize firefighting, spill entry, rescue in a contaminated space or maintenance on energized equipment. Only use an extinguisher if the site's policy, training and conditions permit it; escape takes priority.

Worked example: a container of cleaning waste has no label. The learner isolates it from use and informs the responsible person instead of pouring it into a familiar waste drum. Changed application: an ignition source appears in the controlled area while spraying. Stop safely, alert the supervisor and follow the emergency plan; do not try to complete the remaining panel while someone negotiates its removal. Record the event and inspect affected work before restart.

lessons.title: Q89-12 — Integrated beginner performance and development
lessons.body:
## Q89-12 — Integrated beginner performance and development

An initial-training award records demonstrated beginner tasks under defined supervision. It is not evidence of unrestricted trade competence. The learner must connect the full workflow: correct job and materials, hazard controls, equipment readiness, preparation, inspection hold points, climate, mixing, application, thickness evidence, cleanup and handover. A learner who can calculate thickness but bypasses a pressure control has not passed. Likewise, a neat panel with fabricated readings is unacceptable.

Maintain a personal development record after training. State the task performed, supervision, equipment, product, surface, date and evidence; distinguish observing from performing. The employer plans further supervised experience and any subsequent competence assessment. Do not fill a log with anticipated tasks or treat time served alone as proof. Report changed equipment, materials or conditions so training and authorization can be reviewed.

Worked example: learner A completes all written checks but has only watched the live application. Record the knowledge achievement and the missing practical task; do not issue the full initial skills award. Learner B completes the practical work but needs coaching to recognize an expired batch. Retain that result, remediate timing decisions and reassess on a changed batch independently. Changed application: a worker trained on the recorded enclosed installation is assigned a confined tank. That assignment requires separate planning, controls and authorizations; this certificate does not extend itself to the new environment.


---

lessons.body: # VUC089 workbook, practical delivery and instructor guide

lessons.title: Entry, delivery resources and safety gates
lessons.body:
## Entry, delivery resources and safety gates

This original 40-hour initial course develops supervised beginner performance. Entry: understanding of instructions and basic measurement arithmetic, with language/access support as needed; participation fitness reviewed confidentially; no prior independent blasting qualification presumed. Instructor must be competent in the actual blasting/coating systems and assessment, with authority to stop and access to specialist advice. One learner performs each energized task at a time under direct instructor supervision; other learners remain in the approved observation area. Assessor must be able to see controls and work continuously. Increase staffing or reduce participation if supervision cannot be maintained.

Before practical delivery complete F89: site/area___ actual equipment model/manual revision___ component ratings/inspection___ substrate/coating identity___ selected abrasive___ actual product TDS/AG/SDS revisions___ respiratory-program approval___ ventilation/containment verification___ ignition controls___ environmental/waste plan___ emergency alarm/medical route___ communication___ supervisor/operator/assessor___ approved pressure/setup/method___ isolation/pressure-relief sequence reference___ surface/film acceptance methods and limits___ climate limits___ cure/recoat limits___ release signatures/date___. Unfilled safety-critical fields prevent energized practice. These are actual facility inputs, not missing authored curriculum; no generic invented pressure or chemical recipe replaces them.

Resources: approved enclosed or controlled blasting/spray facility; inspected compatible equipment and instructions; known suitable uncontaminated training steel coupons with protected edges; approved abrasive and coating; actual SDS/TDS/AG; appropriate ventilation, respiratory and other protection; verified climate/profile/wet/dry-film instruments and required visual references; labeled defect samples, safe measuring/mixing tools, waste containers and spill response; job/inspection forms and emergency communications. Provide physically accessible work arrangements that retain the same essential safety performance. Do not run real exposure, fire, injection or equipment-failure scenarios. Use printed fault cards and isolated defect samples. A water/dry trainer can support rehearsal but does not replace the actual supervised blasting and coating tasks for the full skills award.

lessons.title: Synthetic classroom cards — never a live specification
lessons.body:
## Synthetic classroom cards — never a live specification

J89: known clean steel panel A, system C89, preparation and climate hold points, named supervisor releases. Wrong-component card identifies Red-B curing component for a Red-A job. Revision card provides obsolete J89-v 1 beside approved J89-v 2; learner must verify current instruction rather than merge contradictory values.

S89: fictional profile 40–65 micrometres at EACH listed location; cleanliness and contamination releases both required. Data A48, 56, 68 fails; changed B48, 56, 62 passes profile only. No proprietary visual grade is reproduced or claimed.

C89: fictional coating 60% volume solids, base: curing 4: 1 VOLUME, no thinner, induction 10 minutes, pot life 60 minutes from combination at the stated training condition. Climate surface 10–35°C inclusive, surface minus dew point at least 3°C, RH≤80%. Target dry 150 micrometres; nominal wet 250. Actual coating selection follows F89 instead.

D89: fictional corrected dry acceptance 130–170 micrometres at EACH location. A145,152,125 fails; B145,152,168 passes thickness but a separate debris card still causes hold. Fictional recoat window 8–24 hours from application at a fixed classroom condition: a coat applied 08:00 may be recoated from 16:00 through 08:00 next day if all other card requirements remain met. At 09:00 next day, obtain specified disposition; real products may use different timing/temperature rules.

Fault cards: unknown legacy paint; extraction alarm; unidentified breathing-air connector; damaged respirator; bulging hose; failed remote stop; missing spray guard; suspected injection; wet contaminated prepared surface; expired batch; unlabeled waste. These are announced simulations, not deliberately introduced live failures.

lessons.title: Applied learning labs and worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Applied learning labs and worked solutions

### W89-1 — Plan and control the job

Use J89 and the unknown-paint/extraction cards. Produce a start/hold table with document identity, responsible release person and missing evidence. Model: component mismatch, unknown old coating and extraction failure each independently prevent start; obtain correct materials, characterization and restored approved controls. Changed task: all three resolve but surface hold is unsigned. Hold at that remaining boundary; no majority-vote release.

### W89-2 — Surface and climate decisions

Evaluate S89 A/B and C89 readings surface 18/dew 14/RH74, surface 16/dew 14/RH74, surface 10/dew 7/RH80 and surface 9.9/dew 6/RH75. Model: S89 A fails 68; B profile passes but releases still needed. Climate margins 4, 2, 3, 3.9; results pass, fail, pass, fail(minimum temperature). Learner records all conditions rather than a single green number. Changed task: passing readings followed by condensation; stop and review surface and climate again.

### W89-3 — Batch and timing

Plan C89 batches 5 litres and 2.5 litres. Model 4+1 and 2+0.5 litres. Combination 09:00 permits 09:10 start, 10:00 discard. Changed combination 14:35 permits 14:45 start, 15:35 discard. Explain why a liquid batch past deadline remains unusable under the card. Record batch IDs, actual measured quantities and times; no assumed partial-mix permission in a real product.

### W89-4 — Film and quantity

C89: 150/0.60=250 micrometres wet; 200 wet predicts 120 dry. Coverage 1000×0.60/150=4 m²/litre.12 m² needs 3 litres theoretical, 4 litres at 75% efficiency. Changed 20 m², 200 dry, 50% solids gives 400 wet, 2.5 m²/litre, 8 litres theoretical, 10 litres at 80% efficiency. Explain why adding 25% to 3 gives 3.75, not 4. State every unit and assumption.

### W89-5 — Inspect, repair and hand over

Evaluate D89 A and B plus debris card. Model: A average 140.67 does not override 125 failure; B thickness passes but debris needs disposition. Draw a panel map with failed point and repair boundary. Preserve original results, authorized repair and reinspection. Changed task: recoat 09:00 next day after 08:00 original application exceeds 24 hours; obtain actual specified disposition instead of concealing delay.

### W89-6 — Abnormal events and development

Roleplay a failed remote stop and suspected injection using isolated cards only. Model: planned shutdown/quarantine for control failure; immediate emergency medical care for suspected injection, material details without delay. Then review a learner who watched spraying but did not perform it. Model: incomplete practical record, not a full award. Changed task requires independent reassessment after coached batch-timing error; written knowledge alone cannot clear the practical gap.

lessons.title: Individual stations
lessons.body:
## Individual stations

Stations 4–11 require actual supervised physical performance; 1–3 and 12 are observed review/readiness tasks. The instructor provides teaching/practice first, then an independent assessed attempt. Record assistance; a safety prompt prevents that attempt being scored independent. Each station must pass, not merely the average.

### P89-1 — Job-pack review

Task: Compare actual job, product/component identities, revisions and hold points; process a mismatched-component card.

Acceptance: All identities and approvals traced; mismatch and missing release held.

lessons.title: I89 integrated job and scoring
lessons.body:
## I89 integrated job and scoring

Learner completes a full planned coupon job from document/control review through preparation, release, mix, application, measurement, cleanup and handover. Include one changed paper condition before an appropriate boundary, such as expired batch or falling climate margin; do not create a live hazard. Actual cure time may require a later session and a second traceable coupon prepared by the learner for dry-film inspection. Do not substitute another person's work without identifying it as a teaching specimen. Final acceptance of the learner's own application remains required.

Twelve dimensions correspond to P89-1 through 12. Score 0=absent/unsafe, 1=major coaching, 2=safe but incomplete or prompted, 3=independent acceptable, 4=independent accurate with sound explanation. Require≥39/48, each≥3, all twelve stations passed, all actual job hold points fulfilled and no critical error. Critical: bypassed pressure/respiratory/ventilation controls, unsafe discharge direction, hand near pressurized leak/tip, unauthorized chemical substitution, continued known unsafe condition, fabricated evidence or inappropriate delay of injection emergency response. Stop unsafe attempts immediately. Retain failure, teach the gap and use a changed safe task; do not coach through and call it independent.

lessons.title: Records and remediation
lessons.body:
## Records and remediation

F89-L job record: learner___ plan/revision___ equipment___ substrate___ product/components/batches___ actual mix ratio/basis/quantities___ combination/induction/discard times___ climate time/location/instrument/readings/decision___ preparation measurements/release___ application area/time___ wet readings___ cure conditions___ dry method/corrections/readings___ defects/disposition___ repair/reinspection___ waste/shutdown___ supervisor/assessor/date___. Attach coupon map and instrument verification; privacy-protect learner records.

F89-R remediation: failed criterion___ evidence___ explanation___ instruction/practice___ changed reassessment task___ independent result___ remaining restriction___ assessor___ learner acknowledgment___ review/appeal contact___. Offer review by another competent person when assessment is disputed; preserve original evidence. Accessibility adjustments may change presentation or timing where safe, but cannot waive independent physical safety tasks.

lessons.title: Delivery schedule and credential
lessons.body:
## Delivery schedule and credential

40 hours: instruction 8; labs 6; individual coached practice and stations 14; integrated job and quality records 8; controlled final/administration 2; feedback/review 2. Cure waiting outside scheduled learning is additional. Allow further practice as needed; fixed attendance does not create a pass. Final 12 cases, 36 decisions, 72 points, 120 minutes; pass 58/72, at least 4/6 eachdomain and no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; protected keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B follows remediation; practical gaps require practical reassessment.

Issue VNDRLY/U Blaster and Sprayer — Initial Training only after corrected formative checks, labs, all stations, I89 and final pass with competent reviewer signoff. Record date, scope, actual methods/equipment, assessor, program version/hash and limitations. This is an original VNDRLY award, not OPITO certification or independent workplace competence. Further supervised experience and employer task authorization remain necessary. Apply actual employer/external renewal requirements; do not invent a universal validity period. If only knowledge is completed, record that limited achievement without issuing the full skills credential.


---

content.title: VUC089 | VUC089 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC089 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC089 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q89-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-1-L1

A correct-color hardener has a different product identity. Use it?

**Answer:** No; segregate the mismatch and obtain the specified compatible component.

**Reason/remediation:** Color does not establish chemistry or approved system compatibility. Revisit Q89-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-1-L2

All materials match but surface release is absent. Start?

**Answer:** Hold at the preparation-release boundary.

**Reason/remediation:** Material readiness does not waive an inspection hold. Revisit Q89-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-2-L1

Can low-hazard abrasive make unknown old paint safe to remove?

**Answer:** No; characterize the existing coating and approve controls first.

**Reason/remediation:** Dust can originate from the substrate and coating. Revisit Q89-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-2-L2

Extraction fails during work. Finish a small area?

**Answer:** Stop safely and obtain restoration and release.

**Reason/remediation:** A small remaining area does not eliminate exposure. Revisit Q89-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-3-L1

Does a hose fitting a utility outlet prove safe breathing air?

**Answer:** No; verify the designated approved breathing-air system and compatibility.

**Reason/remediation:** Mechanical fit says nothing about air quality. Revisit Q89-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-3-L2

Can solvent be used to clean skin?

**Answer:** No; use the approved hygiene and first-aid procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** A cleaning solvent may create additional exposure and injury. Revisit Q89-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-4-L1

Remote control fails to stop flow. Continue with a helper at the compressor?

**Answer:** No; execute planned safe shutdown and remove the system from service.

**Reason/remediation:** A failed safety control cannot be replaced by improvised coordination. Revisit Q89-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-4-L2

A hose bulges without leaking. Accept?

**Answer:** No; quarantine it before pressurization.

**Reason/remediation:** Visible damage is not made safe by absence of leakage. Revisit Q89-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-5-L1

S89 values 48, 56, 68 against inclusive 40–65. Pass?

**Answer:** No; 68 fails and requires an approved disposition.

**Reason/remediation:** Each location must meet this fictional rule. Revisit Q89-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-5-L2

Profile passes but contamination release is missing. Coat?

**Answer:** No; hold.

**Reason/remediation:** Profile, cleanliness and contamination are separate requirements. Revisit Q89-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-6-L1

C89 surface 18/dew 14/RH74. Climate result?

**Answer:** Margin 4; all card conditions pass.

**Reason/remediation:** The margin, surface range and humidity must all comply. Revisit Q89-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-6-L2

Surface 16/dew 14/RH74?

**Answer:** Margin 2 fails; hold.

**Reason/remediation:** Good humidity cannot compensate for inadequate margin. Revisit Q89-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-7-L1

C89 2.5 litres at 4: 1 volume. Components?

**Answer:** 2 litres base and 0.5 litres curing component.

**Reason/remediation:** Five total parts; divide total by 5 then allocate 4 and 1. Revisit Q89-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-7-L2

Combined 09:00, induction 10 min, pot life 60 min from combination. Window?

**Answer:** Earliest 09:10; discard 10:00.

**Reason/remediation:** Induction does not restart the pot-life clock. Revisit Q89-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-8-L1

A leaking hose wets a glove and causes a pinprick. Response?

**Answer:** Treat suspected injection as an emergency and obtain immediate medical care; identify material.

**Reason/remediation:** A small wound can conceal serious injury. Revisit Q89-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-8-L2

Clear a tip while pressurized?

**Answer:** No; use the actual pressure-relief/isolation procedure first.

**Reason/remediation:** Stopping a motor alone may leave stored pressure. Revisit Q89-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-9-L1

150 micrometres dry at 60% solids. Nominal wet?

**Answer:** 250 micrometres.

**Reason/remediation:** 150/0.60; dry prediction is wet multiplied by solids fraction. Revisit Q89-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-9-L2

12 m², 150 micrometres, 60% solids, 75% efficiency. Mixed volume?

**Answer:** 4 litres.

**Reason/remediation:** Coverage 4 m²/litre; 3 litres theoretical divided by 0.75. Revisit Q89-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-10-L1

D89 corrected dry readings 145,152,125. Accept?

**Answer:** No; 125 fails the each-location 130–170 rule.

**Reason/remediation:** A passing average cannot override this specified individual rule. Revisit Q89-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-10-L2

Dry to touch means ready for service?

**Answer:** Not necessarily; verify actual cure/service criteria.

**Reason/remediation:** Different readiness stages have different requirements. Revisit Q89-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-11-L1

Spent abrasive always has the unused material waste classification?

**Answer:** No; removed coating and contaminants must be considered.

**Reason/remediation:** The waste composition differs from the unused supply. Revisit Q89-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-11-L2

Unlabeled solvent waste can go into any waste drum?

**Answer:** No; isolate and identify through the authorized process.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncontrolled mixing risks incompatibility and incorrect disposal. Revisit Q89-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q89-12-L1

Written pass and only watched application. Full skills award?

**Answer:** No; record missing practical performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Observation is not individual demonstration. Revisit Q89-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q89-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q89-12-L2

Certificate for an enclosed training installation authorizes a tank entry?

**Answer:** No; separate site/task planning and authorization are required.

**Reason/remediation:** The recorded training scope does not automatically expand. Revisit Q89-12 and perform its changed application.


---

lessons.title: VUC089 sources, coverage and limits
lessons.body:
# VUC089 sources, coverage and limits

Reviewed 18November 2026. Original VNDRLY beginner instruction and invented teaching cases; no claim of OPITO approval or exact equivalence to an inaccessible full specification. No copyrighted standard text or proprietary visual plates reproduced. US sources support stated principles in their jurisdiction; actual work must use its governing jurisdiction, employer procedures and current product/equipment documents.

Full product specification was not available. Our40-hour original package is not represented as that approved course.|Program scope,Q89-1/12|

lessons.title: Original coverage and evidence map
lessons.body:
## Original coverage and evidence map

Each Q89 chapter maps one-to-one to P89 station and its two formative checks and separate final/changed case. W89-1 integrates 1–3; W89-2 integrates 5–6; W89-3 covers 7; W89-4 covers 9; W89-5 covers 10; W89-6 integrates 4/8/11/12. I89 combines all twelve dimensions on a controlled actual coupon job. Protected final and retake files reside outside the public package.

C89, S89, D89 and all assessment numerical values are synthetic teaching rules. Film arithmetic is dimensional calculation for stated idealized conditions; real acceptance uses actual product and inspection method. No invented universal profile, dew-point, humidity, pressure, mixing, cure or dry-film acceptance limits are imposed. Proprietary visual grades/full external unit criteria are not independently verified. The package is complete as original VNDRLY initial-training materials on this available-source basis; it is not an assertion of formal external equivalence. Actual delivery, learner demonstration and credential issue are separate future events, not claimed here.

courses.title: VUC090 | VNDRLY/U Fire Warden — Competence Assessment and Refresher

content.title: VUC090 | VNDRLY/U Fire Warden — Competence Assessment and Refresher
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Fire Warden — Competence Assessment and Refresher
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Fire Warden — Competence Assessment and Refresher

VUC090. Original available-source materials, 18November 2026. For employer-nominated wardens with prior local instruction and practice; this package includes refresher teaching and controlled assessment. It does not authorize fire attack, rescue entry or technical shutdown. Full OPITO specification was not available; no external approval or exact parity is claimed.

lessons.title: Q90-1 — Appointment, boundaries and the emergency plan
lessons.body:
## Q90-1 — Appointment, boundaries and the emergency plan

A fire warden helps implement a defined emergency plan. The role does not automatically include firefighting, rescue entry, incident command or technical shutdown. Learn the employer's written appointment, area, deputy arrangement, alarm meanings, reporting route and authority. If the warden is absent, the plan must still work; identify trained cover rather than assuming someone will improvise. Assessment must test the actual role in a safe simulation, not reward confidence or job seniority.

Read the current local plan before the exercise. Locate the assigned zone, primary and alternate exits, assembly points, communications and arrangements for visitors and people needing assistance. Establish who calls emergency services and how that call is confirmed. An automatic alarm signal is not proof that responders have been contacted. Know who may authorize re-entry; a warden's headcount does not normally provide that authority. A change in layout, occupancy or process can invalidate an old briefing.

Worked example: warden Rowan covers office Zone A but a supervisor asks Rowan to search the process building after its alarm. Rowan reports the request to incident control and remains within the assigned safe evacuation role. The desire to help does not create rescue capability. Changed application: Rowan's deputy is absent on night shift. Report the coverage gap before work and implement the employer's approved alternative; do not forge a deputy signature or assume daytime arrangements cover nights.

lessons.title: Q90-2 — Prevention observations and readiness
lessons.body:
## Q90-2 — Prevention observations and readiness

A warden's routine observations can find conditions that weaken evacuation: obstructed routes, unsuitable storage, wedged fire doors, damaged signs, unreported alarm faults or changed occupancy. Report and follow up within the site's process. Do not perform unauthorized electrical repairs, alter detectors or disable alarms to avoid nuisance activations. The responsible person or competent specialist decides technical repairs and compensatory arrangements.

Check the assigned area against the local checklist while it is safe and occupied normally. Confirm exits can be used as intended and that the route leads to the designated safe place. A door that looks like an exit but opens into a locked yard is not a complete route. Record the exact location and condition, immediate safe action, notified person and completion evidence. If an impairment affects safe occupancy, escalate promptly; a report filed for next month may not be an adequate response.

Worked example: boxes obstruct the alternate corridor while the primary corridor is open. The learner arranges authorized removal and reports the defect rather than treating the alternate as optional. Changed application: the obstruction is machinery that cannot simply be moved. The learner does not create a new unassessed escape route; management must implement an approved arrangement or restrict affected occupancy. During the emergency the learner uses the current safe route and reports unavailable areas, not yesterday's checklist.

lessons.title: Q90-3 — Recognition, alarm and initial communication
lessons.body:
## Q90-3 — Recognition, alarm and initial communication

On discovering suspected fire, raise the alarm and follow the emergency plan promptly. Do not delay warning others while trying to prove the fire's size or finish a telephone conversation. Move toward safety, communicate the location and observable facts, and distinguish confirmed information from uncertainty. Avoid unsupported statements such as no one is inside when the area has not been checked. Use the site's alarm point, radio, telephone or backup method as trained.

A concise initial message identifies the caller and location, the observed condition, people at immediate risk if known, the action taken and the assistance needed. Confirm that the recipient understood the critical information. If communication fails, use the planned alternative while maintaining evacuation; do not remain in a deteriorating area repeatedly trying the same radio. Do not make a real emergency call during a drill unless the exercise plan has specifically arranged it. A real emergency overrides the drill and triggers the real response.

Worked example: the card states smoke seen through a store-room window, no person seen, alarm activated. A sound message is that smoke is observed at that location, occupancy is unconfirmed and evacuation is underway. It is not store-room clear. Changed application: the radio battery fails. Use the designated backup contact point from a safe location and report the communication problem. The assessment judges safe information transfer, not a theatrical delay to create a more dramatic scenario.

lessons.title: Q90-4 — Evacuation direction and changing routes
lessons.body:
## Q90-4 — Evacuation direction and changing routes

Give short, calm directions that people can act on: the route to use, the route to avoid and the assembly point. Position yourself where you can guide without blocking flow or becoming trapped. Encourage people to leave belongings and proceed by the designated route. Do not argue at length with a reluctant person while others need direction; use the plan, report the refusal and protect your own exit. Never physically force or restrain a person as a routine warden technique.

An indicated route may become unsafe. Do not direct people into smoke, heat or another hazard merely because an arrow or old plan points that way. Use a safe planned alternative and communicate the change. Do not enter a smoke-filled corridor to discover whether the far end is clear. Elevators are used only under the building's specifically approved evacuation arrangements, not because an ordinary passenger lift is convenient. Keep access clear for responders and do not route evacuees through an active response area.

Worked example: route E1 is marked unavailable by a smoke simulation card before the group approaches it. The learner stops that movement, directs people along approved E2 and informs control that E1 is unavailable. Changed application: E2 also becomes unavailable in a tabletop inject. The learner follows the site's contingency and calls for assistance from the safest available position; inventing a window escape or sending people through the simulated smoke is not an acceptable answer. The training site never physically blocks real escape routes.

lessons.title: Q90-5 — Safe checking, sweep limits and withdrawal
lessons.body:
## Q90-5 — Safe checking, sweep limits and withdrawal

Some plans assign wardens a limited check of accessible areas while leaving. That is not a search-and-rescue mission. Learn exactly which rooms may be checked, how the result is communicated and when to withdraw. The warden must not enter smoke, heat, hazardous process areas or any condition outside the assigned capability. Preserve an escape route and do not re-enter to complete a checklist. If an area cannot be checked safely, report it as unchecked with the reason and last known information.

Use the local method for checking safe spaces and directing occupants out. Close doors where safe and instructed without locking people in or delaying escape. Do not open a suspect door merely to improve certainty. A closed door is not proof that its room is empty. A sweep report describes what was actually observed, its time and limitations. It does not certify the building safe for re-entry or replace responder search decisions.

Worked example: the plan permits a visual check of the open office and accessible meeting room on the exit path. A store-room approach has a smoke card. Report office and meeting room checked at the stated time, store-room unchecked due to smoke, then leave. Changed application: a colleague says a visitor may be in that store-room. Immediately communicate the possible person and last known location to incident control/responders. Do not turn the possible missing person into permission for unprotected entry.

lessons.title: Q90-6 — Inclusive assistance, visitors and dignity
lessons.body:
## Q90-6 — Inclusive assistance, visitors and dignity

Plan assistance with the people concerned before an emergency. Needs may involve mobility, hearing, vision, language, temporary injury, unfamiliarity or anxiety. Do not infer a person's needs or ability from appearance. Know the individual or general evacuation arrangements, trained helpers, backup helpers and the means of communication. Share only information needed for safe assistance; medical details are not broadcast to the whole assembly group.

If a plan uses a refuge, it is a managed temporary part of the evacuation arrangement with communication and onward evacuation, not a place to leave someone indefinitely. The plan should not depend on the emergency services as the sole means of routine assisted evacuation. Only trained authorized personnel use specialized evacuation devices, and only under their approved procedure. This course does not teach improvised carrying, stair-chair operation or manual rescue. Simulate those interfaces without lifting people during assessment.

Worked example: visitor Mira uses the agreed level route E2 with a nominated helper. The helper reports Mira's arrival by identity, not merely one extra person. Changed application: the usual helper is absent. Activate the planned trained backup and inform control of any unresolved assistance need. Do not assign an untrained bystander to carry Mira down stairs. If the planned route is compromised, communicate the exact location and need through the contingency process while maintaining the safest available arrangement.

lessons.title: Q90-7 — Assembly, identity and accountability
lessons.body:
## Q90-7 — Assembly, identity and accountability

At assembly, keep people away from traffic, hazards and responder access. Use the current accountable population, not a rough crowd estimate. Include employees, contractors, visitors and others covered by the plan. Reconcile identities against reliable attendance or sign-in information, while recognizing that records may be stale. Distinguish confirmed safe, expected but unconfirmed, confirmed offsite and unknown identity. Do not remove someone from the expected list merely to make totals balance.

Duplicates and additional arrivals can make a headcount falsely reassuring. Report unresolved people promptly with name or identifier, last known location and information source. Do not wait until the entire list is perfectly formatted. Update control when new evidence changes the picture, preserving times and earlier uncertainty. No one returns inside to look for a colleague or collect a missing register. Use the plan's backup record method if the electronic system is unavailable.

Worked example: expected IDs A1–A8, C1–C3, V1–V2 total 13. The initial arrival list contains A1–A8, C1, C2, V1, V1 and unknown X. There are 13 entries but only 11 confirmed expected identities. C3 and V2 remain unconfirmed; V1 is duplicated and X needs identification. Changed application: X is verified as V2, so 12 expected identities are confirmed and C3 remains unresolved. A later verified offsite record for C3 changes the result to 12 safe at assembly plus 1 confirmed offsite, not 13 physically at assembly.

lessons.title: Q90-8 — Responder handover and information discipline
lessons.body:
## Q90-8 — Responder handover and information discipline

A useful handover states the site and incident location, observed hazard, alarm/action times, evacuation status, routes and access, unconfirmed people with last known locations, assistance needs, unchecked areas and known relevant hazards. State the source and uncertainty. Give responders the approved map or information pack where available without delaying their work. Do not guess cylinder contents, electrical isolation status or process conditions from appearance.

Maintain a clear command interface. If multiple wardens report, identify your zone and avoid claiming whole-site clearance. Confirm urgent information reached the responsible person. Keep a time-stamped log of updates so a later all-accounted report does not erase an earlier missing-person concern. Provide corrections explicitly. Warden reports support incident command; they do not authorize firefighting tactics or operational restart.

Worked example: Zone A has one unchecked store-room and C3 unconfirmed, last seen near the loading office by a named witness at 10:04. The learner hands over those facts and labels the witness report as unverified. Changed application: C3 is confirmed offsite through the approved process at 10:12. Send a correction with the new evidence and time; do not silently edit the paper list and assume responders will notice. The store-room remains unchecked even when everyone is accounted for.

lessons.title: Q90-9 — Firefighting boundaries, re-entry and recovery
lessons.body:
## Q90-9 — Firefighting boundaries, re-entry and recovery

The presence of an extinguisher does not require a warden to fight a fire. The employer's emergency policy determines whether occupants evacuate or designated trained people may attempt limited extinguisher use. This competence package assesses evacuation and coordination, not live firefighting. Never delay alarm or escape to protect property. Smoke, uncertain material, loss of exit, spreading fire or lack of training are reasons to withdraw and report rather than attempt control.

Remain at the designated safe location and prevent casual re-entry through clear instructions and the site's access-control process. Alarm silence does not mean the emergency is over. Neither an empty roll-call list nor a manager's wish to recover a laptop establishes re-entry authority. Follow the release from the person named in the actual emergency plan. After release, any equipment restart or process restoration follows its own authorized procedure.

Worked example: the alarm stops while responders are still assessing the building. The warden keeps the group at assembly and seeks the official update. Changed application: an authorized all-clear is issued for office Zone A but the workshop remains restricted. Communicate the partial release accurately; do not say the whole site is open. Record unresolved defects and welfare needs and transfer ongoing responsibilities to the appropriate owner.

lessons.title: Q90-10 — Demonstrating competence and learning from drills
lessons.body:
## Q90-10 — Demonstrating competence and learning from drills

Competence is shown by safe independent decisions in the defined role, not simply attendance at a talk. This package requires two changed simulated emergencies covering alarm, route change, limited checking, assistance, identity-based accountability and handover. The candidate receives the local plan and safe practice before assessment. The assessor records actions and exact information communicated. A correct explanation after an unsafe choice does not erase that choice.

Debrief the exercise using evidence: what happened, why it mattered, what the plan or training needs to change, who owns the action and how closure will be verified. Distinguish an individual skill gap from a defective organizational arrangement. A candidate should receive credit for identifying a missing assistance plan rather than be expected to invent one. However, claiming that an unchecked area was clear is an individual evidence failure that requires remediation and reassessment.

Worked example: the candidate guides everyone safely but reports 13 accounted from a 13-entry duplicate list. The assessor retains the accountability failure, teaches identity reconciliation and uses a changed roster. A repeat of the same memorized list is weak evidence of the corrected skill. Changed application: the candidate correctly reports an unresolved person and refuses unsafe re-entry despite pressure. That is competent boundary management, not failure to rescue. The award records the assessed site-plan/simulated scope and does not appoint the person or grant an external qualification.


---

courses.title: VUC090 | VUC090 practical assessment and instructor guide

content.title: VUC090 | VUC090 practical assessment and instructor guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC090 practical assessment and instructor guide
lessons.body: # VUC090 practical assessment and instructor guide

lessons.title: Entry and resources
lessons.body:
## Entry and resources

Candidate is nominated for the role by the employer and has completed local plan instruction and safe practice. Review relevant participation needs confidentially; no stress exposure or physical demand beyond the role is required. Assessor is competent in emergency planning, local warden duties and assessment and is independent enough to record an honest failure. Provide accessible plan/maps, interpreting or communication support as needed without removing the need to communicate critical information effectively.

Resources: safe training area with two genuinely usable exits, clearly marked exercise paths, printed plan and rosters, radio/telephone simulation, timing/log materials, roleplayers, assistance-plan cards and mock incident controller. No live fire, smoke, blocked real exits, alarm impairment, rescue lifting or real emergency call is introduced. Exercise controller briefs all participants, coordinates with facility management and maintains an immediate stop signal. Actual emergency overrides exercise. One candidate assessed as warden at a time; roleplayers may be reused but each candidate receives changed evidence and an individual record.

Before exercise fill local adaptation F90: site___ plan/revision___ assigned zone___ real exits and assembly___ exercise paths___ alarm meanings___ actual emergency number/procedure___ simulated contact___ deputy___ trained assistance resources___ safe-sweep limits___ re-entry authority___ real-emergency override___ controller/assessor___ participant briefing/consent___ accessibility/safety review___. These actual site fields are delivery inputs, not permission to substitute unreviewed procedures. Assessment scripts below are complete fictional exercises; map them safely to the facility.

lessons.title: E90 fictional exercise plan and map
lessons.body:
## E90 fictional exercise plan and map

Single-level training building. ZoneA contains open officeO, meeting roomM and store-roomS. O and M connect to corridorC. C leads west to E1 and east to E2; both lead to outdoor assemblyA. S opens fromC. Control pointK is outside besideA and clear of emergency vehicle access. All routes are level and genuinely unobstructed during practice. No process plant is entered. Warden's permitted check covers only visibly safe O/M and safe approach toS while leaving; any unsafe card terminates that check. PrimaryE1, alternateE2. Simulated alarm phrase is EXERCISE EVACUATE; real emergency uses actual local plan.

Mock controllerKai receives radio channelEX1; backup is a runner/message delivered from safe assemblyK. Kai confirms the simulated emergency-services call; learners must not call a real service. Re-entry release belongs to mock incident commanderLee after controller confirmation, not the warden. VisitorMira has agreed level-route assistance with helperJo; backupSam is trained for this fictional arrangement. No lifting device or carrying is used. If both routes are unavailable in a tabletop inject, remain in the safest available plan-defined position and report exact circumstances to control; the physical exercise stops before any real egress restriction.

lessons.title: R90 rosters and source cards
lessons.body:
## R90 rosters and source cards

RosterA expected A1–A8, C1–C3, V1–V2:13 identities. Initial arrival entries A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, C1, C2, V1, V1, X. Thirteen entries, eleven confirmed expected identities, C3 andV2 unconfirmed, duplicateV1 andunknownX. CardA2: reception verifies X isV2 using the approved identity process; now twelve confirmed expected identities, C3 still unconfirmed. CardA3: authorized attendance owner verifiesC3 left before alarm; now twelve at assembly and one confirmed offsite. Store-roomS remains unchecked regardless of person reconciliation.

RosterB expected B1–B6, D1–D4, G1–G2:12 identities. Arrival entries B1–B6, D1, D2, D2, G1, Z: 11 entries, 9 confirmed expected identities, D3/D4/G2 unconfirmed. CardB2: ZverifiedG2; ten confirmed expected identities, D3/D4 unconfirmed. CardB3: D3 arrives and identity confirmed; eleven at assembly, D4 unconfirmed. CardB4: unverified coworker saysD4 went home; insufficient to clear. CardB5: authorized attendance owner confirmsD4 offsite before alarm; twelve accounted as eleven at assembly plus one offsite. An unchecked area remains unchecked.

No real employee identities or emergency messages are used. Candidate may use calculator but must demonstrate identity reconciliation, not just arithmetic.

lessons.title: Learning labs with worked solutions
lessons.body:
## Learning labs with worked solutions

### W90-1 — Scope and readiness

Use E90 plus cards deputy absent, exit yard locked, alarm impairment and unfamiliar technical shutdown. Produce a readiness/authority table. Model: cover must be approved; incomplete exit and alarm defect escalate; technical shutdown belongs to designated trained personnel. Changed task: manager verbally says everything is fine without resolving the locked exit. Record unresolved condition, not a false release.

### W90-2 — Safe evacuation and assistance

E1 receives smoke card; O/Mare safe; Sunsafe; Joabsent. Plan immediate directions and report. Model: raise alarm, useE2, check only safe assigned spaces, reportSunchecked, activateSamfor agreed assistance. Changed task: both routes unavailable is tabletop only; use contingency/communicate and stop physical exercise, not invented climbing/carrying.

### W90-3 — Identity accounting

Complete R90 A and B at each card stage. ModelA: 13 entries/11 confirmed expected; then 12 confirmed; then 12 assembly+1 offsite. ModelB: 11 entries/9 confirmed; then 10; then 11; unverified offsite story leavesD4 unconfirmed; verified final 11 assembly+1 offsite. List missing identities each time and send urgent updates before completing administrative detail.

### W90-4 — Handover and correction

Write initial ZoneA handover: smoke atS, uncheckedS, routeE1 unavailable, E2 used, people status from current roster, assistance status, alarm/check times and known source. Changed card verifies previously missing person offsite. Model: explicit time-stamped correction preserves original report; no inference thatSwas checked or building safe. Practice speaking the message and receiving acknowledgment.

### W90-5 — Release and learning

Respond to alarm silence, manager laptop request and office-only release. Model: remain at assembly untilLee's authorized release; do not allow retrieval; communicate restricted workshop if specified. Debrief a duplicate-count failure with owner and changed reassessment. Do not blame a candidate for correctly identifying an organizational plan gap.

lessons.title: Individual stations
lessons.body:
## Individual stations

Stations 2–6 require safe physical walk-through/communication performance in the simulation; 1 and 7–10 are observed review/roleplay. None constitutes firefighting or rescue authorization. Practice precedes independent assessment; record prompts.

### P90-1 — Appointment and plan

Task: Identify assigned zone, deputy, alarm, contact, authority and exclusions from current plan.

Acceptance: No rescue/shutdown authority invented; current coverage verified.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-2 — Readiness inspection

Task: Walk a safe training route and report staged paper defects without obstructing actual egress.

Acceptance: Exact defect, owner, immediate safe action and follow-up recorded.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-3 — Alarm and message

Task: Use simulated alarm/radio and backup to give a factual initial message.

Acceptance: Prompt warning, accurate location/uncertainty and confirmed contact; no unarranged real call.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-4 — Route direction

Task: Lead roleplayers along safe marked training paths with one paper route-change inject.

Acceptance: Clear directions, approved alternate, no unsafe-route entry or delayed retrieval.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-5 — Limited check and withdrawal

Task: Perform safe assigned check and encounter an unchecked-room card.

Acceptance: Actual scope/time reported; unsafe area left unchecked and communicated.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-6 — Assistance coordination

Task: Coordinate prebriefed assistance roleplay and backup-helper inject; no carrying.

Acceptance: Consent/dignity, planned trained help, exact status and onward arrangement.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-7 — Accountability

Task: Reconcile rosterA then changed rosterB by identity.

Acceptance: Duplicate/unknown/unconfirmed/offsite distinctions correct and promptly reported.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-8 — Responder handover

Task: Deliver structured zone handover and correction to mock incident control.

Acceptance: Locations, people, unchecked areas, times, sources and uncertainty retained.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-9 — Re-entry boundary

Task: Respond to silence, manager pressure and limited-release cards.

Acceptance: Named authority respected; no unauthorized return or firefighting.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

### P90-10 — Debrief and evidence

Task: Produce action log and explain individual versus plan defect.

Acceptance: Truthful evidence, owner, closure method and reassessment plan; no fabricated clearance.

Evidence/time___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Changed remediation___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: I90 two complete changed emergency simulations
lessons.body:
## I90 two complete changed emergency simulations

ScenarioA: brief E90 and rosterA; at exercise 10:00 give smoke-atS card. Candidate must initiate alarm/message and evacuation. When route direction begins, giveE1 unavailable card. Before assistance decision, giveJoabsent card. When candidate reports assembly, issue initial rosterA, thenA2 andA3 only after candidate has reported current unresolved people. Controller asks whetherSwas clear; correct answer remains unchecked. Then give alarm-silenced card followed later by authorized office-only release. Candidate must not infer full all-clear. Controller records response order and exact statements; these times are scenario markers, not universal evacuation deadlines.

ScenarioB: changed rosterB and morning setup. Candidate starts with safeE1 but then receives E1 unavailable card and backup communication failure requiring planned safe message route. Safe O/Mcheck is allowed; Sremains unchecked. Assistance helper present but visitor initially misunderstood assembly direction; candidate confirms understanding respectfully. IssueB2–B5 sequentially after current status reports. Add manager pressure to retrieve belongings before authorized release. Candidate delivers explicit correction and ends with accurate restricted-scope report.

Each scenario scores ten dimensions correspondingP90-1 to 10, 0 = absent/unsafe, 1 = major coaching, 2 = safe but incomplete or prompted, 3 = independent acceptable, 4 = accurate independent with reasoning. Each requires≥32/40, every dimension≥3, allmandatoryactions and no critical error. Both scenarios must pass independently. Critical errors: unsafe entry/re-entry, delaying alarm for investigation, abandoning known assistance need, fabricated all-clear/unchecked-area clearance, knowingly hiding unresolved person, unapproved real emergency call or dangerous physical improvisation. Stop danger immediately. Do not average scenarios or use written marks to offset a practical failure.

lessons.title: Assessment records, remediation and credential
lessons.body:
## Assessment records, remediation and credential

F90-E: learner/appointment___ local plan/revision___ scenario/version___ start/end___ observed alarm/message___ route/changes___ checked/unchecked areas/times___ assistance arrangements/status___ expected identities___ confirmed assembly___ confirmed offsite___ duplicate/unknown___ unresolved names/last information___ handover/acknowledgment___ corrections___ release authority/scope___ scores/critical___ assessor/date___. Use attachments for rosters and log; retain original failed evidence.

F90-D: issue___ individual skill or plan defect___ action___ owner___ due/review point___ closure evidence___ changed reassessment___ result___ reviewer/date___. For failure, reteach relevant chapter, practice safely and reassess with different roster/route/assistance injects. Provide independent review/appeal through the training organization's named contact. Protect personal data and separate necessary assistance information from medical records.

24 planned hours: refresher 6, labs 4, individual stations 6, two integrated scenarios 4, final/admin 2, feedback/review 2. Additional practice is available; attendance is not competence. Final 10 cases, 30 decisions, 60 points, 90 minutes; pass 48/60, at least 4/6 each domain, no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B after remediation. Actual practical failure requires changed practical evidence.

Issue VNDRLY/U Fire Warden — competence demonstrated in recorded simulated role only after entry/local instruction, corrected formative checks, labs, all stations, both I90 scenarios and final pass, with competent reviewer signoff. Record site-plan scope, dates, assessor, program/hash, limitations and employer appointment separately. No OPITO award or automatic emergency-service/rescue authority is granted. Review after role/plan/ability changes and according to employer requirements; the external scheme's renewal period is not automatically imposed as an unsupported VNDRLY authorization.
