lessons.title: VUC090 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC090 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q90-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-1-L1

Does warden appointment authorize smoke rescue?

**Answer:** No; follow assigned evacuation role and report need to responders.

**Reason/remediation:** A title does not create protective equipment, training or rescue authority. Revisit Q90-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-1-L2

Deputy absent at night: assume day cover?

**Answer:** No; escalate and implement approved cover.

**Reason/remediation:** The plan must address the actual staffed shift. Revisit Q90-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-2-L1

Alternate exit blocked but primary open: ignore?

**Answer:** No; report and resolve through authorized arrangements.

**Reason/remediation:** A later incident may make the primary unavailable. Revisit Q90-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-2-L2

Can a warden disable a faulty detector?

**Answer:** Not without authorized procedure and competence; report impairment.

**Reason/remediation:** Disabling protection can create an unrecognized risk. Revisit Q90-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-3-L1

Smoke observed, occupancy unknown: report room clear?

**Answer:** No; state smoke and unconfirmed occupancy.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncertainty must remain visible to responders. Revisit Q90-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-3-L2

Automatic alarm proves emergency services called?

**Answer:** No; follow and confirm the plan call procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Alarm activation and successful external notification are different events. Revisit Q90-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-4-L1

E1 smoke card, approved E2 safe: direction?

**Answer:** Use E2 and report E1 unavailable.

**Reason/remediation:** A known unsafe route is not used because it is normally primary. Revisit Q90-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-4-L2

Both routes unavailable: invent window escape?

**Answer:** No; follow local contingency and communicate exact situation.

**Reason/remediation:** Unplanned escape methods can create additional harm. Revisit Q90-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-5-L1

Room cannot be safely checked: mark clear?

**Answer:** No; report unchecked, reason, time and last information.

**Reason/remediation:** A completed form must not conceal uncertainty. Revisit Q90-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-5-L2

Possible missing visitor inside: re-enter?

**Answer:** No; promptly report to incident control/responders.

**Reason/remediation:** A missing-person concern does not authorize unprotected rescue. Revisit Q90-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-6-L1

Usual trained helper absent: use untrained carrying?

**Answer:** No; activate approved trained backup/contingency.

**Reason/remediation:** Improvised carrying can injure and does not replace an assistance plan. Revisit Q90-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-6-L2

Refuge means leave person indefinitely?

**Answer:** No; maintain planned communication and onward evacuation.

**Reason/remediation:** It is part of an evacuation arrangement, not abandonment. Revisit Q90-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-7-L1

13 entries include duplicateV1 and unknownX; 13 expected. All safe?

**Answer:** No; reconcile identities, not raw count.

**Reason/remediation:** Duplicates/extras can hide missing expected people. Revisit Q90-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-7-L2

Confirmed offsite counts as physically at assembly?

**Answer:** No; record the distinct status and evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Accurate categories preserve accountability. Revisit Q90-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-8-L1

Witness last sawC3 near office; confirmed location?

**Answer:** Report as witness information with time, not confirmed current location.

**Reason/remediation:** Source and uncertainty affect response decisions. Revisit Q90-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-8-L2

New safe-location evidence: erase earlier report?

**Answer:** No; send time-stamped correction and preserve the history.

**Reason/remediation:** Responders need an explicit update. Revisit Q90-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-9-L1

Alarm silenced: allow re-entry?

**Answer:** No; await named authority release.

**Reason/remediation:** Silence does not prove conditions safe. Revisit Q90-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-9-L2

Extinguisher present: must warden fight fire?

**Answer:** No; follow employer policy and own training; evacuation role remains.

**Reason/remediation:** Equipment availability does not create authorization. Revisit Q90-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q90-10-L1

Candidate wrongly reports all accounted then explains error: erase failure?

**Answer:** No; retain, remediate and assess a changed roster independently.

**Reason/remediation:** Later explanation is not proof of correct emergency performance. Revisit Q90-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q90-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q90-10-L2

Refusal to enter smoke for missing person: automatic fail?

**Answer:** No; safe withdrawal and prompt accurate handover are correct.

**Reason/remediation:** Assessment rewards the defined safe role, not unauthorized heroics. Revisit Q90-10 and perform its changed application.


---

lessons.title: Coverage and original assessment
lessons.body:
## Coverage and original assessment

Ten chapters map to ten stations, twenty explained checks and separate ten-case final/changed retake. Five labs address scope/readiness, evacuation/assistance, identity accounting, handover and recovery. Two complete changed scenarios integrate all ten dimensions; both must pass. Synthetic E90 maps, rosters and names are original. Scenario times are not universal evacuation performance limits. Real fire, smoke, rescue entry and disabled-person carrying are excluded from safe simulation. Full materials include instructor controls, forms, remediation, appeal and bounded credential rules.

The package is complete as original VNDRLY materials on the available-source basis. Actual local adaptation, learner delivery and assessment are future uses, not claimed completed. Publication is outside this materials task.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Onshore Fire/Emergency Response Team Leader — Further Training
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Onshore Fire/Emergency Response Team Leader — Further Training

VUC091. Original materials, 18November 2026. For previously trained and appointed leaders; not initial firefighter training. Includes required professionally controlled live-fire assessment resources. No live activity performed during authoring. Full external specification unavailable; no OPITO approval or exact equivalence claimed. Synthetic numbers never replace actual operational limits.

lessons.title: Q91-1 — Further training entry and command responsibility
lessons.body:
## Q91-1 — Further training entry and command responsibility

Further training refreshes an existing team leader's demonstrated capability; it is not a shortcut for an untrained person to command a fire team. Authenticate prior relevant training, employer appointment, recent practice, medical/respiratory readiness and the scope of duties before practical assessment. A long gap or changed equipment calls for development before demanding performance. Record the gap rather than inventing a renewal or backdating a certificate.

The team leader translates incident objectives into safe tasks for a particular crew and reports to the incident command structure. The leader does not silently assume overall command or exceed the brigade's organizational remit. Know whether the team is authorized for exterior response, interior structural work, particular process hazards or other defined tasks. A request outside that scope must be clarified and escalated. The leader owns the decision to withhold or stop the crew when readiness or conditions are inadequate.

Worked case: an experienced exterior-response leader is asked to command interior structural entry without the required current capability and support. The leader reports the limitation, maintains a safe defensive posture and requests appropriate resources. Changed case: a valid certificate exists but the team has never used the newly issued breathing apparatus. The certificate does not replace equipment-specific training and checks.

lessons.title: Q91-2 — Preincident information and initial size-up
lessons.body:
## Q91-2 — Preincident information and initial size-up

Before response, learn the site layout, access, hazardous inventories, isolation interfaces, fire-water arrangements, fixed systems, occupancy and emergency communications. During initial size-up distinguish known facts from assumptions: incident location, material, people at risk, wind or smoke movement, exposures, access and escape, available resources and special hazards. Observe from a safe position. Do not enter an uncertain hazard simply to gather a better report.

Transmit a short situation report and proposed task boundary to command. Update it when conditions change. A familiar building can contain unfamiliar contractors, stored chemicals or impaired systems. Use the current preplan and technical contacts, but do not treat an old drawing as proof of current isolation or structural condition. The leader should explicitly identify the critical unknown that prevents action and what evidence or specialist resource is needed.

Worked case: a workshop alarm is accompanied by smoke and an unidentified chemical-container label. Report the unknown material and hold incompatible attack choices while command obtains identification. Changed case: the container is identified but a neighboring cylinder is exposed. Reassess the exposure and exclusion arrangement with command; knowing the first material does not resolve the second hazard.

lessons.title: Q91-3 — Objectives, risk decisions and task briefing
lessons.body:
## Q91-3 — Objectives, risk decisions and task briefing

A task order must connect objective, method, limits and withdrawal. State what the crew is to achieve, where, with which resources, under whose supervision, how to communicate and what conditions require stopping. Confirm understanding by asking the crew to repeat the critical boundaries. Avoid broad commands such as deal with it that conceal assumptions about rescue, isolation or entry.

Use the actual incident risk process. Benefit, uncertainty and available controls change together; a task that was reasonable at the start can become unacceptable. The leader should request a change or withdraw when conditions exceed the plan, rather than continue because equipment is already deployed. Offensive and defensive strategies must be coordinated through command so one crew's action does not expose another. Do not start ventilation, open boundaries or alter a process without the authorized coordinated plan.

Worked case: task is exterior exposure protection from a marked safe position, not entry. A crew member starts toward the building to improve the view. The leader recalls the member, restates the boundary and reports any loss of control. Changed case: the safe position is affected by changing conditions. Stop, withdraw/account and request a revised task; do not simply move closer to preserve the original objective.

lessons.title: Q91-4 — Personnel, equipment and readiness
lessons.body:
## Q91-4 — Personnel, equipment and readiness

Match people and equipment to the task before deployment. Check qualifications, fitness/readiness, protective ensemble, breathing equipment, communications and inspected firefighting equipment through the actual program. A spare cylinder or radio may be present but unusable or incompatible. Verify rather than count objects. Equipment defects are reported and removed from use, not hidden because the drill is about leadership.

Assign roles explicitly: team members, entry-control/accountability interface, supply support, backup/rescue resources and safety oversight as required by the actual plan and jurisdiction. A person cannot be counted simultaneously for incompatible critical duties. Interior structural and other immediately dangerous atmosphere work have specific staffing, respiratory and rescue requirements; apply the actual applicable rule and brigade procedure, not a generic arithmetic shortcut. The leader must confirm those arrangements with command before committing the crew.

Worked case: four names appear on the board, but one person is operating a critical pump and another is not qualified for the proposed duty. The leader does not equate four names with a compliant entry arrangement. Changed case: staffing is corrected but the emergency radio fails its check. Resolve communications and backup before deployment; adequate headcount alone is insufficient.

lessons.title: Q91-5 — Breathing apparatus and endurance control
lessons.body:
## Q91-5 — Breathing apparatus and endurance control

The leader checks that the crew follows the actual breathing-apparatus procedure and keeps track of the limiting member. Starting pressure, condition, work rate, return distance, alarms and reserves all matter. A nominal cylinder duration is not a promise of usable work time. Never plan to work until a low-air alarm as a routine target. Maintain crew integrity and initiate return according to the actual procedure before the limiting condition is reached.

Classroom card A91 is only arithmetic: starting indication 280 units, turnaround threshold 180 units and observed consumption 10 units/minute yields(280−180)/10=10 minutes to that threshold at a constant assumed rate. It is not a real cylinder rule or a safe entry duration. If rate increases to 20, the same allowance is 5 minutes. Real consumption changes with effort and conditions; actual procedures, alarms and safety margins govern. No classroom calculation authorizes entry.

Worked case: one member reports an unexpected pressure decrease while others appear normal. Stop the task and follow the team withdrawal/emergency procedure; do not average the cylinders. Changed case: radio contact becomes unreliable during a breathing-apparatus task. The leader applies the established lost-communication/withdrawal procedure and accounts for the crew, rather than using remaining air as justification to continue.

lessons.title: Q91-6 — Communications, accountability and crew integrity
lessons.body:
## Q91-6 — Communications, accountability and crew integrity

Track each person's identity, assignment, location, status and changes. A crew report must reflect the actual crew, not the number originally dispatched. Use closed-loop communication for critical orders: identify recipient, task/location/limits, receive acknowledgment and verify execution. Keep emergency traffic recognizable and concise. A message sent without acknowledgment may not have reached its target.

Maintain crew contact as required by the actual operation. No freelancing is permitted. Report entry, withdrawal, reassignment, rehabilitation and release to the accountability system. When a member is unaccounted for, activate the emergency process immediately with last known information; do not silently replace the name with another person to preserve a team count. The leader manages the assigned team while command coordinates broader resources.

Worked case: T1–T4 were assigned; return board showsT1, T2, T2, T4. Four entries represent three unique people andT3 is unresolved. The leader reportsT3 immediately, with last known location and task, and initiates the plan. Changed case: T3 is confirmed in medical care through the authorized channel. Update status/time explicitly; medical location is not active crew availability.

lessons.title: Q91-7 — Fire behavior, media and process interfaces
lessons.body:
## Q91-7 — Fire behavior, media and process interfaces

The leader must understand why an apparently simple fire can change rapidly. Fuel, heat, airflow, confinement and process energy affect behavior. Unexpected smoke/heat change, structural concerns, loss of control or hazardous-material uncertainty require reassessment and potentially immediate withdrawal. Do not use this refresher as a source of improvised tactics for an unfamiliar process.

Select an extinguishing or exposure-control medium only within the approved preplan, material compatibility and equipment capability. Water is not automatically suitable for every energized, reactive or liquid-fuel situation. Foam choice, concentration and application are system/material specific and may have environmental constraints. Isolation belongs to authorized process personnel and must be confirmed; a request to close a valve is not proof it is closed. Fixed-system operation, ventilation and manual attack must be coordinated so one action does not increase another crew's risk.

Worked case: a proposed medium is not confirmed compatible with an unidentified material. Hold that task and obtain technical advice while protecting people and maintaining exclusion. Changed case: a process isolation is reported requested rather than verified. Keep the distinction in the briefing and do not plan as if energy release has stopped.

lessons.title: Q91-8 — Water, foam and resource sustainability
lessons.body:
## Q91-8 — Water, foam and resource sustainability

A leader must know whether the task can be sustained and how supply failure will be communicated. Confirm actual available flow, pressure, water source, hoses, appliances and backup with qualified operators. A tank volume alone does not establish delivery capability. Hose routing must protect access and crew escape without creating uncontrolled trip or vehicle hazards. Changes in supply require prompt coordination and a safe response, not a hidden reduction in protection.

Synthetic W91 uses 1800 litres/minute available and two planned demands 700 and 600 litres/minute, leaving 500 litres/minute arithmetic margin. Adding a 700 litres/minute demand exceeds available flow by 200. This is a planning exercise only; actual hydraulic performance and safety reserve require the competent system plan. Foam card F91 assumes 3% concentrate by final solution volume.1000 litres solution requires 30 litres concentrate and 970 litres water.200 litres concentrate theoretically supports 6666.67 litres solution before losses/reserves; it does not prove usable incident duration.

Worked case: a task needs 1200 litres solution at the fictional 3%, so 36 litres concentrate. Only 30 litres are verified available. Do not label the task supplied based on container count; request additional suitable resource or revise through command. Changed case: enough concentrate exists but its compatibility/condition is unverified. Quantity does not resolve suitability.

lessons.title: Q91-9 — Leading controlled deployment and withdrawal
lessons.body:
## Q91-9 — Leading controlled deployment and withdrawal

Before movement, the leader gives the task brief, confirms readiness, communications, accountability, supply, escape and stop conditions. During deployment maintain observation of crew performance and changing conditions. Position to lead the assigned team without losing the command interface. Give clear corrections and stop unsafe action promptly. An exercise is not a reason to tolerate a real unsafe act until the assessor has finished taking notes.

Withdrawal is an organized task. Communicate it, confirm receipt, maintain crew integrity, move by the approved safe route and report all personnel/status at the designated point. If a person or route is lost, use the emergency procedure rather than assuming the crew will regroup later. A successful extinguishment does not compensate for an unaccounted member. After withdrawal do not re-enter because the original objective remains incomplete; obtain reassessment and authorization.

Worked case: the exercise controller gives a simulated supply-loss card. The leader stops the affected action, withdraws under the approved drill procedure and confirms every identity. The controller never actually removes a critical live-fire safety supply. Changed case: the team returns safely but one radio message was not acknowledged. Establish whether the other assigned group received the withdrawal order through command; do not infer scene-wide completion from your own crew's return.

lessons.title: Q91-10 — Casualty and firefighter emergency coordination
lessons.body:
## Q91-10 — Casualty and firefighter emergency coordination

A leader must rapidly recognize an emergency involving a team member and communicate identity, location, last task, condition if known and resources needed. Activate the site's emergency traffic/rescue process. Keep other crew members accounted for and avoid uncontrolled spontaneous rescue entry. The designated rescue resources and command structure manage the response within their competence and protection.

For casualty movement, first aid or medical treatment, use personnel trained and authorized for the actual task. The leader coordinates access, information and handover rather than inventing a lifting or treatment technique. A mannequin may be used in the safe exercise; no learner is trapped, exposed to smoke or deliberately deprived of air. A simulated casualty must not distract the team from a real safety issue. The real-emergency override stops training immediately.

Worked case: T3 does not respond and was last reported near a marked training prop. The leader declares the simulated emergency, provides last known information, keepsT1/T2/T4 controlled and requests the planned rescue resource. Changed case: a real learner reports chest discomfort during the exercise. Stop the exercise and activate actual medical response; do not continue treating it as a scenario inject.

lessons.title: Q91-11 — Hazardous materials, contamination and environmental control
lessons.body:
## Q91-11 — Hazardous materials, contamination and environmental control

Fire response can expose crews to smoke, debris, chemical products and contaminated runoff. Identify the hazard and the limits of the team's training. A fire-team-leader certificate does not automatically confer hazardous-material technician or incident-commander qualification. Establish or respect control zones, access and specialist advice under the actual incident plan. Do not cross a boundary to read a label when safer information routes exist.

Plan gross contamination reduction, equipment segregation and transfer to appropriate decontamination/cleaning arrangements. Protect clean areas and vehicles from contaminated equipment. Runoff containment and environmental notifications are coordinated with the responsible specialists; they must not compromise immediate life safety or create unauthorized exposure. Do not declare a substance harmless because smoke has disappeared or because a generic detector reads zero for a different hazard.

Worked case: crew gear is visibly contaminated after a simulated chemical-exposure card. The leader routes it through the approved segregation/decontamination process and records exposure information rather than loading it into the clean cab. Changed case: an unknown residue appears on equipment. Keep it segregated, obtain identification/advice and do not prescribe a cleaning chemical by guesswork.

lessons.title: Q91-12 — Rehabilitation, rotation and human performance
lessons.body:
## Q91-12 — Rehabilitation, rotation and human performance

Sustained response demands attention to fatigue, heat burden, hydration, medical needs and cognitive performance. The leader uses the actual rehabilitation and medical-monitoring arrangements and reports crew availability accurately. A person in rehabilitation is not simultaneously ready for immediate redeployment. Rest duration alone does not prove medical readiness; qualified personnel and the applicable procedure determine return to duty.

Encourage early reporting of symptoms or equipment discomfort without ridicule. Watch for confusion, unusual behavior or reduced ability to follow instructions. Stop and obtain appropriate medical assessment when indicated. Rotate tasks through command so essential functions and accountability remain covered. After a distressing incident, provide access to support and follow-up without forcing public disclosure of personal reactions.

Worked case: a crew member insists on another task but has been referred for medical assessment. The leader marks that member unavailable and requests replacement through command. Changed case: the leader is fatigued and making communication errors. Request relief and conduct an explicit handover rather than conceal the condition to finish the exercise.

lessons.title: Q91-13 — Transfer, recovery and honest records
lessons.body:
## Q91-13 — Transfer, recovery and honest records

Transfer of leadership requires a briefing and acknowledgment. State current objective, strategy, crew identities/locations/status, hazards, resources, communications, outstanding requests, limits and next decisions. Make clear when responsibility changes. A new leader arriving on scene does not automatically know what the previous leader assumed. Keep command informed of the transfer and preserve continuity in accountability.

After control or exercise completion, account for people, secure equipment through qualified operators, record defects/exposures and restore readiness only after checks. Operational restart belongs to the authorized site process, not simply to the fire team's declaration that the visible fire is out. Debrief against observations and identify corrective actions, owners and closure evidence. Preserve near misses and failed attempts; do not improve the record by rewriting them as successes.

Worked case: replacement leader receives equipment status but not thatT3 is in medical care. The handover is incomplete because crew availability is wrong. Correct it before transfer. Changed case: incident command releases the team, but a damaged hose remains mixed with serviceable equipment. Tag/segregate and record it before readiness is declared.

lessons.title: Q91-14 — Integrated further-training standard and renewal decision
lessons.body:
## Q91-14 — Integrated further-training standard and renewal decision

The learner must lead complete controlled practical scenarios as well as explain decisions. This original package requires two changed live-fire training scenarios at a professionally managed facility plus a non-live emergency/coordination exercise. Live-fire scope, prop, fuels, operating limits, safety staffing, medical cover and shutdown arrangements are approved by the facility; this course does not supply an improvised ignition recipe. Prior competence and current readiness remain prerequisites.

Assess leadership independently: briefing, resource decisions, crew control, communication, dynamic reassessment, withdrawal, accountability, casualty interface, rehabilitation and handover. Instructor intervention for safety prevents that attempt being counted independent. A high exam score cannot compensate for unsafe crew commitment or false accountability. Reassess after targeted development on a changed task; do not simply replay memorized radio lines.

Worked case: candidate controls the flame task but ignores a simulated withdrawal trigger. The attempt fails even if no one is harmed. Changed case: candidate recognizes the trigger, withdraws safely and leaves the task unfinished. That is the correct leadership decision. Issue only the scope actually demonstrated and recorded; do not claim external revalidation or employer authority from this original VNDRLY package.


---

lessons.title: VUC091 further-training instructor and practical package
lessons.body: # VUC091 further-training instructor and practical package

lessons.title: Entry and facility gate
lessons.body:
## Entry and facility gate

Authenticate prior relevant leader training/competence, employer appointment, experience since previous assessment and current equipment familiarity. Review medical/fitness and respiratory-program requirements through qualified personnel, with privacy. A novice or unresolved capability gap enters development before this further-training assessment. Accessible instruction is provided; essential protective and leadership performance is not waived.

Live scenarios occur only at a professionally operated fire-training facility with competent live-fire instructors, an independent safety function, qualified prop/fuel/system operators, adequate trained supporting crew, backup/rescue arrangements, medical response and environmental controls. Staffing is set by the facility's approved plan and applicable requirements; the assessed learner never substitutes for the independent safety/controller role. The facility must provide approved current operating procedures and the actual props/equipment suitable for the candidate's existing scope. This authored package gives learning/assessment scripts, not permission to construct a fire prop or ignite improvised fuel.

F91 readiness record: facility___ approved scenario/prop procedure and revision___ candidate scope/prerequisites___ actual fuel/medium compatibility___ operating limits___ independent safety/controller___ qualified operators___ crew/backup/rescue roles___ medical arrangements___ PPE/respiratory checks___ water/agent supply and protected reserve___ communications/backup___ accountability___ weather/environmental limits___ safe access/escape___ emergency stop/shutdown___ real-emergency override___ prebrief/rehearsal___ authorization signatures/date___. All applicable safety-critical fields must be resolved before ignition. No missing field is replaced by a synthetic course number.

Resources: approved facility and actual manuals/preplans; inspected firefighting/respiratory equipment; compatible media and supply; radios and backup; accountability board; safe casualty mannequin; site map; hazard/status cards; decontamination/rehabilitation arrangements; forms and protected assessments. No live casualty, no deliberately failed breathing apparatus, no actual removal of critical safety supply, no unplanned exposure or improvised rescue. Faults are communicated as cards while real safety systems remain intact. If a card could confuse live safety, halt the evolution and discuss it in a safe area.

lessons.title: Original scenario cards
lessons.body:
## Original scenario cards

Map S91: training propP within facility-defined controlled zone; stagingS, commandK, rehabilitationR and medicalM outside that zone at approved locations. Access/escape pathsA/B are selected and verified by facility. Candidate leads named teamT1–T4, with separately assigned safety/support/backup personnel as the actual plan requires. The four names are a fictional accountability list, not a universal staffing prescription. Technical isolation is performed/confirmed only by authorized operators. All movement and equipment parameters follow F91.

A91 arithmetic card: 280 start, 180 threshold, 10 units/minute then 20; 10 and 5 minutes respectively. Changed card 260/170/15 then 30 gives 6 and 3. These abstract units are not cylinder pressures, reserve settings or operational entry times.

W91 flow card: available 1800L/min; demands 700 and 600; 500 margin. Extra 700 exceeds by 200. Changed available 1600, demands 600 and 700; 300 margin; extra 400 exceeds by 100. No hydraulic design or actual attack-flow recommendation is implied.

F91 solution card: 3% of 1000L=30Lconcentrate+970Lwater; 1200Lneeds 36Lconcentrate; 30 available means 6 short.200Lconcentrate/0.03=6666.67Ltheoretical final solution before losses/reserves. Changed 1% of 2000L=20L+1980L; 18Lavailable means 2 short. Actual product proportioning and environmental permission govern real use.

R91 accountability: assignedT1–T4; returnT1, T2, T2, T4 meansT3 unresolved. Later verifiedT3 atmedicalM means all four located, but onlythree potentially available and even those require actual readiness/rehab release. Changed assignedU1–U5; returnU1, U2, U3, U3, U5 leavesU4 unresolved. A coworker's guess is not verification.

H91 hazards: unknown material; unverified isolation; changed wind/route; incompatible cylinder; failed radio check; simulated supply loss; missing member; contaminated gear; medical-unavailable member; fatigued leader; partial release; damaged hose. Use only safe cards or isolated defective examples.

lessons.title: Applied labs with model reasoning
lessons.body:
## Applied labs with model reasoning

### W91-1 — Entry, scope and size-up

Review prior exterior-only scope, new apparatus and unknown-container cards. Write what may proceed and what must wait. Model: authenticate scope/current readiness; no unsupported interior commitment; obtain equipment familiarization and material information through safe channels. Changed: material known but neighboring exposure new; update size-up rather than reuse old clearance.

### W91-2 — Resource and task briefing

Build a roster of qualified available roles, not a raw number. Include pump operator and medical-unavailable member; do not double-count. Draft objective/location/limits/communications/escape/stop briefing. Model: resolve missing roles and communication before task; request resources/revised objective. Changed: member attempts unauthorized ventilation; stop and coordinate through command.

### W91-3 — Endurance and supply arithmetic

Solve A91, W91, F91 with units and assumptions. Model values above. Explain why a constant-rate model and theoretical liquid volume do not establish a safe operational duration. Changed rate doubles; allowance halves. Quantity cannot offset incompatible material or degraded actual delivery.

### W91-4 — Withdrawal and identity

Apply supply-loss card in dry rehearsal; give withdrawal order, obtain acknowledgment and reconcileR91. Model: three unique return identities, notfour; T3 reported immediately with last information. ChangedUroster leavesU4 unresolved. Verified medical update changes location, not deployability.

### W91-5 — Emergency and contamination interfaces

Use missing-member card then real-symptom discussion. Model: activate planned rescue/command while controlling others; real medical concern stops exercise. Route marked gear to approved segregation and obtain technical advice. Changed: zero detector reading for unrelated gas does not clear unknown residue.

### W91-6 — Relief, handover and recovery

Draft relief briefing with member in medical, one in rehab, degraded supply and damaged hose. Model: accurate identities/status, task/hazards/limits, requests and explicit transfer; quarantine equipment; no unsupported ready declaration. Changed: partial site release does not authorize process restart.

lessons.title: I91 integrated practical scenarios
lessons.body:
## I91 integrated practical scenarios

ScenarioA live: facility-approved exterior prop evolution within candidate scope. Candidate conducts size-up, readiness and named crew brief, coordinates verified supply and compatible medium, leads planned deployment and communicates progress. At a safe decision point controller announces a simulated changing-condition trigger. Candidate must reassess and withdraw/account when required by the brief. Real prop shutdown/safety systems remain under independent operators. Candidate then manages rehab, records equipment and hands over. Assess actual leadership, not only explanation.

ScenarioB live: separate changed facility-approved evolution with different task/resource configuration and approved prop conditions. Candidate must demonstrate current equipment/crew readiness, coordinate with a mock command/technical-isolation interface and lead the authorized operation. Inject an unverified isolation or supply limitation BEFORE any dependent live action; correct response is hold/clarify. After legitimate readiness release and live task, announce planned withdrawal cue at safe point. Require named accountability and explicit changed-status handover. No actual safety impairment is introduced.

ScenarioC non-live: missing-memberR91 card, contaminated equipment card, medical-unavailable member and leader-relief requirement. Candidate sends emergency traffic with last known information, activates planned rescue interface, controls remaining crew, updates verified medical location and hands over to relief. Use mannequin only in approved safe movement, performed by trained personnel; this is not rescue-technique qualification. A real symptom overrides all scripts.

Fourteen dimensions correspond toP91-1 through 14. Score 0 = absent/unsafe, 1 = major coaching, 2 = safe but incomplete or prompted, 3 = independent acceptable, 4 = accurate independent with reasoning. Require≥45/56, each≥3, all stations and all three scenarios passed, no critical error. ScenarioA/B each separately require all applicable safety/leadership criteria met; average marks cannot offset a failed live evolution. Critical: unsupported crew commitment, bypassed protection, ignored withdrawal, unaccounted person falsely cleared, unauthorized process action, uncontrolled rescue entry, real-emergency delay or fabricated record. Stop unsafe attempts and retain evidence; targeted development and changed reassessment follow.

lessons.title: Forms and delivery
lessons.body:
## Forms and delivery

F91-T: learner/prior evidence___ plan/version___ team identities/qualifications/status___ objective/limits___ hazards/unknowns___ media/supply verification___ briefing/repeat-back___ deployment/updates___ trigger/action___ withdrawal identities___ emergency/medical/rehab___ handover/acceptance/time___ defects/exposures___ assessor scores/critical___ reviewer/date___. F91-R: gap___ observed evidence___ teaching/practice___ changed task___ independent result___ restriction___ appeal/review contact___. Preserve failed attempts and provide competent independent review when disputed.

40 planned hours: refresher 8, labs 6, stations 8, live scenarios and emergency exercise 12, final/admin 3, debrief/review 3. Facility preparation and additional remedial practice are not fictitiously counted as independent learner performance. Final 14 cases, 42 decisions, 84 points, 120 minutes; pass 68/84, at least 4/6 each domain, no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; keys, collaboration, outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B after remediation; practical failure needs changed practical evidence.

Issue VNDRLY/U Onshore Fire/Emergency Response Team Leader — Further Training only after authenticated entry, current readiness, corrected checks, labs, all stations, I91 including both live scenarios and final pass with competent review. Record actual facility, scope, equipment, dates, assessor and program/hash. No OPITO revalidation or additional employer authorization is conferred. If live practical is not delivered, record knowledge/development only and withhold full award. Renewal/review follows actual employer and applicable scheme requirements, not an invented universal permission.

lessons.title: VUC091 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC091 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q91-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-1-L1

Does a past exterior-response certificate authorize unfamiliar interior work?

**Answer:** No; verify current task-specific capability and support.

**Reason/remediation:** Scope and readiness must match the task. Revisit Q91-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-1-L2

New breathing equipment: skip familiarization because leader experienced?

**Answer:** No; complete actual equipment training/checks.

**Reason/remediation:** Experience with another system is not proof of current competence. Revisit Q91-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-2-L1

Unknown chemical: approach to read label?

**Answer:** Use safe information routes and specialist advice.

**Reason/remediation:** Information gathering must not create unsupported exposure. Revisit Q91-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-2-L2

Old drawing proves isolation?

**Answer:** No; obtain current verified status.

**Reason/remediation:** A document and a completed action are different evidence. Revisit Q91-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-3-L1

Task says exterior only; member moves toward entry. Response?

**Answer:** Recall/control member, restate limit and report as needed.

**Reason/remediation:** A crew cannot expand task scope independently. Revisit Q91-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-3-L2

Conditions exceed plan: finish first?

**Answer:** Stop/withdraw/account and seek revised task.

**Reason/remediation:** Commitment already made does not justify continued unacceptable risk. Revisit Q91-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-4-L1

Four names guarantee compliant entry staffing?

**Answer:** No; verify role availability, qualification and all applicable arrangements.

**Reason/remediation:** Incompatible critical duties cannot be double-counted. Revisit Q91-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-4-L2

Radio fails but enough personnel: deploy?

**Answer:** Resolve communication/backup first.

**Reason/remediation:** Headcount does not replace communication readiness. Revisit Q91-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-5-L1

Synthetic 280 to 180 at 10 units/minute: time?

**Answer:** 10 minutes under constant-rate assumption.

**Reason/remediation:** 100/10; not a real operational allowance. Revisit Q91-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-5-L2

Rate 20 instead?

**Answer:** 5 minutes; actual procedures still govern.

**Reason/remediation:** Consumption change halves the simple calculated time. Revisit Q91-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-6-L1

ReturnT1, T2, T2, T4 forT1–T4: all four?

**Answer:** No; three unique, T3 unresolved.

**Reason/remediation:** Duplicate records hide missing people. Revisit Q91-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-6-L2

T3 confirmed medical care: active crew?

**Answer:** No; record medical status/time and notify.

**Reason/remediation:** Accounted for is not deployable. Revisit Q91-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-7-L1

Medium compatibility unknown: use nearest hose?

**Answer:** Hold incompatible/unknown action and obtain approved advice.

**Reason/remediation:** Available medium is not necessarily suitable. Revisit Q91-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-7-L2

Isolation requested equals isolated?

**Answer:** No; verify actual completion/status.

**Reason/remediation:** Unverified process energy remains a planning uncertainty. Revisit Q91-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-8-L1

1800 available, 700+600 demand: margin?

**Answer:** 500 litres/minute.

**Reason/remediation:** 1800−1300; actual hydraulic capability remains separate. Revisit Q91-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-8-L2

3% of 1000 litres final solution?

**Answer:** 30 litres concentrate and 970 water.

**Reason/remediation:** Concentration is based on final solution volume. Revisit Q91-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-9-L1

Supply-loss card during live drill: continue for marks?

**Answer:** Follow approved stop/withdrawal and account.

**Reason/remediation:** Safe decision overrides finishing objective. Revisit Q91-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-9-L2

Own crew out means every crew out?

**Answer:** No; confirm broader withdrawal through command.

**Reason/remediation:** Team evidence does not establish scene-wide status. Revisit Q91-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-10-L1

Member unresponsive in scenario: send everyone spontaneously?

**Answer:** Activate emergency process and control remaining crew.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncoordinated rescue creates additional casualties. Revisit Q91-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-10-L2

Real chest discomfort during drill: keep acting?

**Answer:** Stop exercise and activate actual medical response.

**Reason/remediation:** Real emergency overrides simulation. Revisit Q91-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-11-L1

Unknown contaminated gear into clean cab?

**Answer:** No; segregate and use approved decontamination route.

**Reason/remediation:** Cross-contamination extends exposure. Revisit Q91-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-11-L2

Fire leader title implies hazmat technician?

**Answer:** No; verify separate capability and scope.

**Reason/remediation:** Different duties require different competence. Revisit Q91-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-12-L1

Member in medical assessment available for task?

**Answer:** No; record unavailable and request replacement.

**Reason/remediation:** Desire to work is not medical release. Revisit Q91-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-12-L2

Leader fatigued: hide it?

**Answer:** Request relief and hand over explicitly.

**Reason/remediation:** Concealed impairment undermines command decisions. Revisit Q91-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-13-L1

Handover omits medical member: complete?

**Answer:** No; correct personnel status before transfer.

**Reason/remediation:** Resource availability is essential. Revisit Q91-13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-13-L2

Damaged hose returned with good stock: ready?

**Answer:** No; tag/segregate and record.

**Reason/remediation:** Incident completion does not restore defective equipment. Revisit Q91-13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-14-L1
lessons.body:
## Q91-14-L1

Flame controlled but withdrawal trigger ignored: pass?

**Answer:** No; critical unsafe decision requires remediation/reassessment.

**Reason/remediation:** Outcome luck does not establish safe leadership. Revisit Q91-14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q91-14-L2
lessons.body:
## Q91-14-L2

Written pass without required live scenarios: full award?

**Answer:** No; record limited completion only.

**Reason/remediation:** Practical leadership evidence is mandatory. Revisit Q91-14 and perform its changed application.

lessons.body:
# VUC091 sources and coverage

Reviewed 18November 2026. Original VNDRLY further-training package for existing leaders. Full external specification unavailable; no exact OPITO parity or formal approval claimed. Real operational rules derive from jurisdiction, employer brigade scope, actual equipment and approved facility plan.

|Primary source|Use and limitation|Coverage|
|---|---|---|
|[OPITO4651](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/further-onshore-fire-emergency-response-team-leader)|Public scope identifies existing leaders and live-fire scenarios beyond normal workplace practice;prior valid leader/further certificate and fitness arrangements are external entry requirements. Our original award does not renew that external certificate.|Q91-1/14,I91|
|[OSHA1910.156](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.156)|Brigade organization,duty-matched training,more comprehensive leader instruction and special-hazard procedures support scope/readiness boundaries. Applicable US requirements must be checked for actual operation.|Q91-1/4/7|
|[OSHA1910.134](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.134)|Respirator use,seal/effectiveness,IDLH and interior structural provisions support actual-program compliance. No abstract headcount or air-arithmetic card substitutes for applicable staffing/rescue/respiratory rules.|Q91-4/5|
|[OSHA1910.120](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.120)|Hazardous-substance emergency response has distinct training/command requirements. Leader scope does not automatically equal hazmat technician or incident commander.|Q91-7/10/11|
|[USFA Field Operations Guide](https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/publications/field_operations_guide.pdf)|Historical primary guide supports resource identity/location/status tracking,crew integrity,command interface and explicit accountability. Historical referenced standards/tactics are not represented as current universal instructions.|Q91-3/6/9/13|
|[NIOSH firefighter safety overview](https://www.cdc.gov/niosh/firefighters/about/index.html)|Current overview identifies chemical,physical and psychosocial hazards,including heat burden and traumatic events. Supports exposure/welfare awareness,not medical thresholds or clearance rules.|Q91-11/12|

lessons.title: Original learning and assessment map
lessons.body:
## Original learning and assessment map

Fourteen chapters each have two explained checks and matching station/final/changed-retake case. Six labs integrate scope/size-up, resources/briefing, abstract endurance/supply arithmetic, withdrawal/accountability, emergency/contamination and handover. I91 contains two actual facility-controlled live-fire evolutions and one non-live emergency coordination scenario. Physical evidence is required in stations 4, 5, 9, 10, 11 and 14; six stations. Eight others are observed leadership/review. Written marks cannot replace live evidence.

A91, W91, F91, R91 and all exam data are original synthetic examples. No cylinder pressure/reserve, attack flow, foam product prescription, prop fuel quantity, ignition sequence or medical return-to-duty threshold is supplied as a universal rule. Facility operating inputs must be approved before delivery. Full proprietary live-fire standards and external unit detail are not independently verified. This is the user's authorized best-effort original material basis, not a claim of accreditation.

Materials include teaching, applications, practical scripts, safety gate, individual rubrics, forms, remediation, review and bounded credential. Actual delivery and learner outcomes are not claimed. Publication is separate from materials completion.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Onshore Fire/Emergency Response Team Member — Further Training
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Onshore Fire/Emergency Response Team Member — Further Training

VUC092. Original available-source materials, 18November 2026. Existing trained members only; not initial firefighter instruction. Actual professional live-fire delivery and individual assessment are required for the full learner award. No hazardous activity was performed during authoring. Full external specification unavailable; no OPITO approval or exact parity claimed.

lessons.title: Q92-1 — Existing capability and the team-member role
lessons.body:
## Q92-1 — Existing capability and the team-member role

Further training is for an existing onshore response team member whose prior training, practice and assigned duties can be authenticated. It refreshes performance under controlled conditions; it does not turn a novice into an operational firefighter. Tell the instructor about changed equipment, long gaps or participation concerns before assessment. Current fitness and respiratory-program requirements are checked through the proper qualified process, not by peer pressure.

A member works within the team leader's brief and the brigade's scope. Understand the task, location, method, limits, communications, escape and withdrawal triggers before accepting it. Ask for clarification when an instruction is ambiguous. Reporting a capability limit is a safety action, not disobedience. Do not freelance to another team, operate an unfamiliar system or assume incident command because you arrive first.

Worked example: member has practiced exterior tasks but is assigned unfamiliar interior work. State the limitation and request appropriate instruction/resource reassignment; do not learn by entering. Changed example: new radio model is issued just before the exercise. Complete familiarization and checks before the task rather than assume identical controls.

lessons.title: Q92-2 — Recognizing hazards and reporting change
lessons.body:
## Q92-2 — Recognizing hazards and reporting change

Fire scenes combine heat, smoke, energy, structural and process hazards. Members observe and communicate changes while carrying out the assigned task. Do not wait for the leader to notice every condition. Report what you see, where and how it affects your task or escape. Keep observations separate from diagnoses; an unusual sound or smoke change is a reason to report and reassess, not a basis for an invented tactical remedy.

Use the current preplan and briefing to identify excluded areas, material uncertainties, process isolation and surrounding exposures. Do not approach an unknown container or suspected hazardous area just to identify it. If a condition exceeds the task limits, stop/withdraw as trained and inform the leader. The absence of visible flame does not establish a safe atmosphere or stable structure.

Worked example: a marked route becomes affected by a controller's simulated smoke card. The member alerts the leader and follows the approved withdrawal/alternate arrangement, not the previous route by habit. Changed example: a process valve is described as isolation requested. Do not repeat that as isolated; report the exact unverified status.

lessons.title: Q92-3 — Protective equipment and readiness checks
lessons.body:
## Q92-3 — Protective equipment and readiness checks

Inspect and use the protective equipment specified by the actual task and program. Check identity, condition, compatibility and correct fit using the manufacturer's procedure. Do not hide a damaged item because the team is waiting. A successful buddy check supports but does not replace your own checks or formal respiratory fit/medical requirements. Personal protective equipment reduces specified risks; it does not make every environment acceptable.

Know the actual equipment's donning, operational checks, limitations, alarms and doffing/maintenance arrangements. Complete unfamiliar-equipment practice in a safe environment before assessment. Keep contaminated and clean equipment separate. If a component is damaged or incompatible, remove it from service through the authorized route and inform the leader of the resulting availability limit.

Worked example: a glove is damaged and a replacement interferes with another item. The member does not accept the ensemble as ready until suitable compatible protection is obtained. Changed example: facepiece seal is affected by interference. Resolve through the respiratory program; shortening the task does not repair the seal.

lessons.title: Q92-4 — Breathing apparatus, contact and withdrawal
lessons.body:
## Q92-4 — Breathing apparatus, contact and withdrawal

Follow the actual breathing-apparatus procedure and report starting condition, checks and changes as required. Maintain team contact and monitor your own equipment and condition. Tell the leader early about unexpected consumption, alarm, leakage or difficulty. Do not remove respiratory protection in a potentially hazardous area to speak more clearly or because visible smoke has reduced. Use the trained emergency/withdrawal procedure.

Nominal cylinder duration is not guaranteed work time. Classroom A92 uses an abstract indication 250 units, threshold 170 and consumption 10 units/minute: the simple allowance is 8 minutes. At 20 units/minute it is 4 minutes. These are arithmetic illustrations only, not actual pressures, reserve rules or entry permission. Real work rates, route length, alarms and the limiting member's condition govern under the actual program.

Worked example: your indication drops unexpectedly while your buddy's appears normal. Inform the leader and follow the team's stop/withdrawal procedure; do not average readings or remain to protect the schedule. Changed example: contact with the buddy is lost. Apply the trained lost-contact/emergency procedure immediately; do not continue the assigned task alone.

lessons.title: Q92-5 — Equipment handling and coordinated movement
lessons.body:
## Q92-5 — Equipment handling and coordinated movement

Refresh handling of the actual hose, branch/nozzle, connections and other assigned equipment under qualified instruction. Inspect before use and confirm compatibility and operating procedure. Secure footing and team positions matter; unexpected movement or reaction can injure people. Do not energize equipment before the team is ready or change operating settings without the agreed communication. Follow the actual equipment and facility limits rather than a generic pressure from a classroom example.

Route equipment to maintain access and escape and avoid sharp edges, traffic and entanglement. Coordinate lifting and movement with the team. If a coupling, hose or control is damaged, report and make safe through the prescribed procedure; do not attempt an improvised live repair. Release stored energy as required before disconnection or maintenance by authorized personnel.

Worked example: a hose coupling is visibly damaged during preuse inspection. Reject it and report unavailable capability; do not wait to see whether it leaks under pressure. Changed example: the team is repositioning and a member is not ready. Hold the movement/operation and obtain acknowledgment rather than treating silence as readiness.

lessons.title: Q92-6 — Media, application and task limits
lessons.body:
## Q92-6 — Media, application and task limits

Know the medium and application method selected by the approved plan and leader. Material compatibility and equipment suitability matter. Do not substitute water, foam or another agent because it is nearby. Unknown material or unverified electrical/process isolation requires clarification. An operator's request for isolation is not confirmation of completion. Coordinate with the leader rather than touching process controls without authority.

During controlled application, perform the assigned technique within your existing training and the facility procedure. Observe the effect and report unexpected behavior. Do not change strategy independently. Foam proportioning and product compatibility are specific; the arithmetic of a percentage does not validate the system or material. Environmental controls remain part of the task.

Worked example: fictional 3% solution of 500 litres consists of 15 litres concentrate and 485 litres water. This is a learning calculation, not a mixing instruction for a real product. Changed example: 2% of 800 litres is 16 litres concentrate and 784 water. Even correct quantities do not permit use of an unapproved concentrate or incompatible equipment.

lessons.title: Q92-7 — Radio discipline and personal accountability
lessons.body:
## Q92-7 — Radio discipline and personal accountability

Use clear messages with identity, location, condition and needed action. Acknowledge critical instructions and report completion or inability. Do not hide misunderstanding behind a quick affirmative response. Emergency traffic follows the local procedure and should identify the emergency and last known position without unnecessary narrative. If radio communication fails, use the trained backup/withdrawal arrangement rather than continue silently.

Check in, stay with the assigned crew and report changes of task/location/status. After withdrawal, confirm your identity at the accountability point. Do not answer for someone you have not verified. A tag or duplicate name is not a person. If a buddy is unaccounted for, report immediately with the last known information and follow the emergency process.

Worked example: return listM1, M2, M2, M4 for assignedM1–M4 has onlythree unique identities; M3 is unresolved. Do not sign all returned. Changed example: M3 is confirmed in rehabilitation. Update the location/status through the authorized channel; that does not meanM3 is ready for the next assignment.

lessons.title: Q92-8 — Controlled live task and withdrawal performance
lessons.body:
## Q92-8 — Controlled live task and withdrawal performance

Before the evolution, repeat the assigned task, limits, escape and stop signals. During the task, maintain team coordination and watch for change. Stop unsafe action and report it even when the exercise objective is unfinished. A member is assessed on safe independent performance within the team, not on whether the prop flame goes out at any cost.

When withdrawal is ordered or required by the actual procedure, acknowledge and move with the team by the approved safe route. Keep equipment and contact under control as trained, then report at the accountability point. Do not detach to recover a tool or improve a photograph. If a problem prevents withdrawal, communicate it as an emergency promptly. Never defeat a facility safety interlock or ignore the independent safety officer.

Worked example: a simulated supply-loss card is announced at a safe decision point while the real safety supply remains intact. The member follows the leader's controlled withdrawal and confirms identity. Changed example: a supervisor says finish the last bit after the emergency stop. Follow the stop and report the conflicting instruction; assessment pressure does not override safety authority.

lessons.title: Q92-9 — Casualty support and emergency signals
lessons.body:
## Q92-9 — Casualty support and emergency signals

A member must know how to call for help and assist only within trained duties. Report identity, location, last task and observable condition. Keep the rest of the crew informed and controlled. Do not launch an unprotected rescue or improvise a casualty carry. The designated rescue/medical personnel and command structure coordinate the response with suitable protection and equipment.

In practice, use a mannequin and approved handling method only with trained personnel and suitable supervision. No real person is trapped, deprived of air or exposed to create realism. A real injury or symptom immediately changes the event from exercise to actual emergency. Provide accurate information and access for medical responders; do not diagnose away a symptom or delay care to complete assessment.

Worked example: your buddy is unresponsive in a non-live card scenario. Send the trained emergency message and follow the leader/rescue plan while maintaining your own safety. Changed example: a participant reports real dizziness during the live evolution. Call the actual stop/medical response and follow the facility plan; do not classify it as a scripted card because another casualty scenario was expected.

lessons.title: Q92-10 — Contamination, hygiene and rehabilitation
lessons.body:
## Q92-10 — Contamination, hygiene and rehabilitation

Smoke, debris and response agents can contaminate equipment and people. Follow the actual clean/dirty boundary and decontamination arrangements. Do not put contaminated gloves or gear into clean vehicles or eating areas. Unknown contamination needs appropriate identification and specialist advice; do not choose a cleaning chemical by guesswork. Record possible exposure through the employer process.

Report fatigue, heat discomfort, breathing difficulty or other symptoms early. Use the designated rehabilitation and medical arrangements. Being willing to continue does not establish readiness. Remain unavailable while medical review or required recovery is incomplete, and notify the leader of that status. Support colleagues in reporting concerns without ridicule. Psychological support after distressing events is also part of responsible recovery.

Worked example: gear receives a simulated contamination tag. Route it to the designated controlled area, not the clean cab. Changed example: after a rest period you are still awaiting medical assessment. Do not accept another task; state that you remain unavailable until the appropriate release.

lessons.title: Q92-11 — Equipment recovery, records and learning
lessons.body:
## Q92-11 — Equipment recovery, records and learning

At task completion, follow the actual shutdown and equipment-restoration procedure. Inspection, cleaning, testing and replenishment are assigned to competent personnel. Tag defects and keep them separate from serviceable equipment. Do not return an item to stock just because the incident is over. Record what you actually used, observed and reported, including failures and exposure concerns.

Debrief your own actions with the team. Describe a skill gap or plan problem accurately and propose a practical correction. A log should distinguish observation, assisted practice and independent performance. Do not sign for a task performed by another member. Changes to equipment or duties require appropriate familiarization and review before future response.

Worked example: you watched a colleague operate a branch/nozzle but did not perform that task. Record observation only. Changed example: you performed it but required a safety prompt. Preserve that assisted result, practice the gap and complete a changed independent attempt; do not rewrite the first attempt as passed.

lessons.title: Q92-12 — Further-training assessment and bounded award
lessons.body:
## Q92-12 — Further-training assessment and bounded award

This package requires individual performance within two changed professionally controlled live-fire scenarios and a non-live emergency/contamination exercise. Prior competence and current readiness are prerequisites. The facility controls props, fuels, limits, safety staffing and shutdown. Written teaching and dry rehearsal support the practical work but do not replace it. Every learner must perform the required member tasks, not stand in a group while others demonstrate.

Assessment considers preparation, protection, apparatus use, equipment handling, task understanding, communication, crew integrity, withdrawal, emergency support and recovery. Critical unsafe action prevents a pass regardless of total marks. Remediate and reassess with changed conditions after safe practice. If live delivery is not available, record only the completed knowledge/development component; do not issue the full further-training award.

Worked example: learner passes theory and attends both scenarios but never handles the assigned equipment. Practical evidence is incomplete. Changed example: learner independently recognizes the stop trigger and withdraws before completing the prop objective. That is correct safe performance. The resulting VNDRLY record states actual assessed scope and does not claim OPITO renewal, leader qualification or additional employer authority.


---

lessons.title: VUC092 instructor, practice and assessment guide
lessons.body: # VUC092 instructor, practice and assessment guide

lessons.title: Delivery entry and resources
lessons.body:
## Delivery entry and resources

For existing trained onshore response members. Authenticate prior scope, practice and employer nomination; review gaps/current equipment. Qualified personnel handle fitness/medical and respiratory-program requirements privately. Provide accessible instruction and safe familiarization; do not waive essential individual performance. Instructors must be competent in actual systems, live-fire training and assessment. An independent safety/controller function, qualified prop/system operators, adequate trained team/backup and medical support remain separate from the assessed learner.

Use a professionally operated fire-training facility and its approved live-fire procedures. Resources include suitable approved props and media, inspected actual PPE/respiratory and firefighting equipment, radios/backup, accountability system, safe mannequin, clean/dirty and rehab areas, scenario cards and forms. This package does not provide an ignition recipe or authorize improvised live-fire practice. Actual fuels, operating parameters, staffing, safety reserves and limits are facility-controlled inputs.

F92 prestart: facility/procedure/revision___ candidate prior scope/current readiness___ actual prop/task___ compatible medium___ equipment manuals/checks___ PPE/respiratory approval___ qualified instructor/operator/safety roles___ supporting team/backup/rescue___ medical arrangements___ supply/reserve___ communications___ accountability___ safe routes___ environmental/weather limits___ emergency stop/shutdown___ real-emergency override___ rehearsal and briefing___ authorized signatures/date___. Resolve all applicable safety-critical fields before ignition. No live casualty, no deliberate breathing-system fault, no removed real safety supply and no physically blocked escape route. Fault cards are simulated; halt the evolution if an inject could confuse real safety.

lessons.title: S92 scenario map and data
lessons.body:
## S92 scenario map and data

Facility defines safe propP, stagingS, commandK, rehabR, medicalM and verified routesA/B. Member reports to leaderL and performs only the briefed task. Candidate IDN1 works with named trained teammatesN2–N4; this fictional list is not a universal staffing rule. Independent safety/support/backup resources are additional as actual plan requires. Any task outside prior competence is excluded until proper development/authorization.

A92 abstract endurance: 250−170=80 units; at 10 units/minute allowance 8 minutes, at 20 allowance 4. Changed 240−180=60; at 12 allowance 5, at 20 allowance 3. These are not real cylinder pressures, turnaround settings or safe entry durations. Actual procedure/alarms and condition govern.

F92 arithmetic: 500Lfinal solution at 3%=15Lconcentrate+485Lwater.800Lat 2%=16+784. Changed 600Lat 3%=18+582. No actual product proportioning instruction is inferred.

R92 initial assignedN1–N4; returnN1, N2, N2, N4 leavesN3 unresolved. CardR2 verifiesN3 inrehabR; all four located, butN3 not automatically available. Changed assignedP1–P5; returnP1, P2, P3, P3, P5 leavesP4 unresolved. Only authorized verification clears a missing status; guessing does not.

Fault cards: scope mismatch, new radio, unverified isolation, route change, damaged/incompatible PPE, unexpected apparatus indication, lost buddy contact, damaged coupling, member not ready, unknown medium, withdrawal cue, missing member, contaminated gear, medical review pending, defective recovered equipment. Use paper or isolated defect samples, never introduce real unsafe condition.

lessons.title: Applied labs with worked answers
lessons.body:
## Applied labs with worked answers

### W92-1 — Task acceptance and hazard report

Read a task outside prior scope and new-equipment card. Model: declare limitation, clarify/reassign and complete development before deployment. Report route change and isolation requested as unverified. Changed: no flame visible but unknown atmosphere; do not infer safe entry.

### W92-2 — Protection and equipment readiness

Identify defects in isolated sample/card set; rehearse actual checklist. Model: damaged glove, incompatible component, seal interference and damaged coupling each prevent readiness. Coordinate movement only after acknowledgment. Changed: equipment sound but hose obstructs escape; resolve routing before operation.

### W92-3 — Abstract endurance and solution calculation

Solve A92/F92 and show units. Model 8/4 minutes and 5/3 changed; 15+485, 16+784, 18+582 litres. State why correct arithmetic does not authorize apparatus duration or actual agent mixing. Changed: compatible quantity unavailable; report rather than substitute unknown material.

### W92-4 — Communication, withdrawal and accountability

Rehearse critical order repeat-back, withdrawal andR92. Model: three unique of four; N3 unresolved; later verified rehab changes location but not deployability. ChangedPcase has four unique andP4 unresolved. No answering for missing buddy or returning for tools.

### W92-5 — Emergency, recovery and evidence

Practice emergency message with mannequin/card, then actual-symptom override discussion. Model: planned rescue/medical interface, real issue stops exercise, contaminated gear segregated, medical-pending member unavailable. Record observed versus assisted versus independent task. Changed: prompted performance requires remediation and fresh independent evidence.

lessons.body:

lessons.title: I92 required integrated scenarios
lessons.body:
## I92 required integrated scenarios

ScenarioA live: approved facility evolution within candidate's existing scope. Candidate receives leader briefing, states limits, checks own protection/equipment, demonstrates coordinated equipment handling and assigned application, maintains contact/reports conditions, and follows planned withdrawal at controller's safe cue. Candidate personally confirms identity and completes recovery/rehab reporting. Independent safety/operator maintains all real safeguards. Observation alone is not a pass.

ScenarioB live: changed approved task/prop configuration and individual equipment role. Before dependent action, give incompatible-material or unverified-isolation card; candidate must query/hold rather than act. Once actual readiness is properly released, perform approved live role, then changed withdrawal/communication cue at safe point. Candidate preserves crew integrity, uses trained backup if needed and gives accurate accountability. No real supply loss or apparatus fault is induced.

ScenarioC non-live: missing-buddyR92 card, mannequin support under trained method, contamination tag and pending-medical status. Candidate sends emergency message, works within leader/rescue plan, segregates gear and reports unavailable status. Real symptom discussion tests actual override. No untrained lifting or deliberate exposure.

Twelve dimensions matchP92-1 through 12. Score 0 = absent/unsafe, 1 = major coaching, 2 = safe but incomplete or prompted, 3 = independent acceptable, 4 = accurate independent with reasoning. Require≥39/48, every dimension≥3, all stations and all three scenarios pass, no critical error. Both live scenarios independently meet applicable safety/member criteria; written score cannot compensate. Critical: unsupported entry, removed/bypassed protection, ignored stop, freelancing, unreported missing buddy, false accountability, unsafe discharge/handling, real-emergency delay or fabricated evidence. Stop danger immediately. Retain failure, teach/practice and reassess changed task independently.

lessons.title: Records, delivery and award
lessons.body:
## Records, delivery and award

F92-E: learner/prior evidence___ local scope/plan___ scenario/date___ task brief/repeat-back___ personal checks___ actual equipment/application task___ observations/reports___ contact/withdrawal___ own/buddy status___ emergency interface___ contamination/rehab___ recovery/defects___ observed/assisted/independent evidence___ scores/critical___ assessor/reviewer___. F92-R: gap___ evidence___ instruction/practice___ changed reassessment___ result___ remaining restriction___ review/appeal contact___. Independent competent review available; preserve original records and protect personal/medical information.

32 planned hours: refresher 6, labs 4, stations 8, live/emergency scenarios 10, final/admin 2, feedback 2. Extra practice as needed; attendance not competence. Final 12 cases, 36 decisions, 72 points, 120 minutes; pass 58/72, at least 4/6 each domain, no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; protected keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B after remediation. Practical failure requires practical reassessment.

Issue VNDRLY/U Onshore Fire/Emergency Response Team Member — Further Training only after authenticated prior scope/current readiness, corrected formative work, labs, all stations, both live and non-live I92 scenarios and final pass with competent reviewer. Record facility, actual task/equipment, dates, assessor and program/hash. No OPITO renewal, team-leader award or new employer authorization is conferred. Without live evidence issue only accurate limited-development record, not full award. Follow actual employer/scheme review requirements after changes or lapse; do not invent universal validity.

lessons.title: VUC092 formative checks
