content.title: VUC094 | VUC094 assessor and workplace workbook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC094 assessor and workplace workbook
lessons.body: # VUC094 assessor and workplace workbook

lessons.title: Delivery and evidence gates
lessons.body:
## Delivery and evidence gates

Use an assessor competent in helicopter administration, local operator procedures and evidence-based assessment. A second competent reviewer resolves sufficiency, conflicts or appeals. Verify employer authorization, current function-specific DG preparation, personnel-system instruction and relevant initial/previous competence records. The public external product sets its own entry and renewal conditions; this original outcome is not that product's certificate.

F94 context: employer/site___ operator and procedure revisions___ candidate functions/permissions___ prerequisite evidence___ system/version___ scale and weighing basis___ required manifest fields___ checking/acceptance process___ HLO/crew interfaces___ manual fallback___ DG/escalation contacts___ privacy and retention___ assessor/reviewer___ assessment dates___. The employer must supply these actual criteria; invented aircraft limits or missing approval routes cannot be filled from this workbook.

Arrange two independently observed authorized routine workplace cycles on different occasions. Observe without interfering with crew or operations. Use only approved real records with access controls; retain evidence references or redacted copies. No deliberately wrong live manifests, dangerous items, outages or emergency messages are introduced. Changed conditions below are declared simulation using a training system/paper ledger. Where workplace opportunities are unavailable, complete the learning and simulation assessments but withhold the workplace-competence outcome until actual observations are recorded. This is a delivery requirement, not a claim that authoring the package assessed a learner.

Resources: current approved forms, secure records access, actual operator interfaces and scale procedure, training ledger, safe tagged dummy bags/freight, mock HLO/crew/DG contacts, timer, calculator, private assessment forms and evidence register. Review operational readiness before each observation; stop assessment if it distracts from safe work or requires unapproved action.

lessons.title: D94 synthetic changed-condition dataset
lessons.body:
## D94 synthetic changed-condition dataset

Cycle A: H94-A, TRAIN-94, Shore–Delta–Echo, 18 November 2026. Planned departure 11:00 UTC, estimated 11:10 UTC. A1 Nia Cole, 84 kg, bag B1 9 kg, Delta; A2 Omar Reed, 79 kg, B2 6 kg, Delta; A3 Lee Park, 92 kg, B3 11 kg, Echo. Freight F1, benign training parts, 35 kg, Delta. All inputs use one stated fictional measurement basis. Original people 255 kg, bags 26 kg, freight 35 kg, combined 316 kg; three people, three bags, one freight item.

A-change 1: remove A2 and B2, yielding 231 kg and two people/two bags/one freight. A-change 2: verified replacement A4 Ada Lake at 86 kg, B4 8 kg, Delta, yields 325 kg and three people/three bags/one freight. Prepare v 1 original, v 2 removal and v 3 replacement with checked totals and distribution. Actual departure is confirmed by mock HLO at 11:18 UTC; Delta arrival is confirmed at 11:42 UTC. Offload A1, A4, B1, B4 and F1. A3/B3 continue. Add A5 Kai Hill, 73 kg, B5 7 kg, Echo. Delta–Echo inputs: people 165 kg, bags 18 kg, total 183 kg; two people, two bags, no freight.

Controller injects, separately and in order: printer unavailable after v 3; crew still has v 2; required eligibility record for a proposed extra traveler missing; a paper card describing an unmarked battery; and a route change from Echo to Shore before the second sector. Learner must distinguish proposed, held and accepted records. The proposed extra traveler and battery do not enter accepted totals. After authorized route change, current persons/items remain A3/A5 and B3/B5 but destination becomes Shore. Mock actual return to Shore at 12:26 UTC is confirmed; no Echo arrival is recorded.

Cycle B: H94-B, TRAIN-95, Shore–Foxtrot, planned 23:40 UTC on 18 November, estimated 00:05 UTC on 19 November. R1 78 kg/B1 7 kg; R2 88 kg/B2 9 kg; R3 95 kg/B3 12 kg; freight 20 kg. Initial total 309 kg: people 261, bags 28, freight 20. Remove R3 and B3: 202 kg. Add verified R4 82 kg/B4 6 kg: 290 kg. Actual departure is verified at 00:15 UTC on 19 November. Arrival remains unknown until controller supplies confirmation at 00:44 UTC. A system retry duplicates R4 arrival; learner must reconcile the actual single event with an audit trail. Separate conversion card: proposed 55 lb item = 24.94758035 kg. It is not accepted merely because a conversion is correct.

Identity inject: manifest expects X1 Pat Vale, but arriving X2 Pat Vail has a different ID. Neither is part of accepted A or B totals. Equal-count inject: expected S1/S2/S3/S4, observed S1/S2/S3/S9; four people but S4 missing and S9 unmanifested. DG and damaged-item cards remain paper only.

lessons.title: Application labs with model reasoning
lessons.body:
## Application labs with model reasoning

### W94-1 — Evidence plan and authenticity

Create F94 and an evidence matrix for all twelve domains. Model: two independent routine workplace cycles plus changed-condition simulation; named sources and candidate contribution; prior course record used only for entry. Changed: witness statement is generic and undated. Obtain authenticated details and direct evidence; do not treat it as a completed observation.

### W94-2 — Sector and identity reconciliation

Build cycle A through the changed second sector. Model: first final A1/A3/A4; next A3/A5; F1 offloaded at Delta. Final destination Shore, no Echo arrival. Resolve X1/X2 and S4/S9 holds separately. Changed: no-show occurs after check-in; reconcile associated bags and current manifest rather than marking the person transported.

### W94-3 — Mass and counts

Show A: 255+26+35=316; subtract 85 to get 231; add 94 to get 325. Onward 92+73+11+7=183. Show B: 261+28+20=309; subtract 107 to get 202; add 88 to get 290. Convert 55 lb once using 0.45359237 kg/lb. Changed: total remains equal after a replacement; identity, counts and item records still require revision. None of these totals constitutes aircraft clearance.

### W94-4 — Revision and unavailable equipment

Create current manual v 3 and distribution log during printer failure. Model: independent check, current crew and ground records, required acknowledgment, superseded v 2 identified. Changed: ground has v 3 but crew has v 2; one acknowledgment is not sufficient. If approved fallback cannot maintain required controls, hold dependent activity and escalate.

### W94-5 — Holds and operational interface

Process eligibility, unknown DG and misunderstood briefing cards. Model: safe hold, appropriate authorized route, clear status and no unsupported release. Changed: HLO clears a deck restriction while DG decision remains open. Preserve the separate hold. No actual hazardous item or live boarding instruction is used.

### W94-6 — Recovery, handover and decision

Reconcile cycle B across midnight and remove duplicate R4 through authorized correction. Model: actual departure and arrival dates/times remain distinct; one verified arrival; source and audit retained. Prepare outcome from the evidence matrix. Changed: all calculations pass but one critical revision failure remains; withhold competence and require changed independent performance.

lessons.title: Observed stations
lessons.body:
## Observed stations

Twelve individual stations; stations 4 and 6 include safe scale/item work, and ten use observed records, system tasks or roleplay. These stations supplement, not replace, the two actual workplace observations. Assess after instruction/practice; record every prompt. Each station sheet includes the fields below.

### P94-1 — Scope and entry

Task: Authenticate preparation, competence history, permissions and assessment plan.

Acceptance: Current context is defined; unsupported functions excluded.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-2 — Sector planning

Task: Build and amend two-sector records with date and time basis.

Acceptance: People/items remain coherent with current route.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-3 — Identity and boarding

Task: Resolve same-name mismatch, no-show and equal-count wrong-identity cards.

Acceptance: No unverified person is treated as boarded.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-4 — Mass verification

Task: Use authorized scale process and independently calculate changed inputs.

Acceptance: Correct source, inclusion basis, units and totals; no loading approval claim.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-5 — Manifest distribution

Task: Prepare, check, supersede and distribute current versions.

Acceptance: Required recipients confirm current information before dependent action.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-6 — Baggage and freight

Task: Reconcile actual safe item labels, weights, destination and late change.

Acceptance: Item and document agree; loading questions referred.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-7 — Dangerous goods

Task: Process paper uncertainty and damage cards through assigned function.

Acceptance: Safe hold and authorized disposition; no guessed acceptance.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-8 — HLO interface

Task: Communicate briefing, identities, holds and current manifest.

Acceptance: Closed-loop message; movement remains under operational authority.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-9 — Fallback and recovery

Task: Use approved manual record, then reconcile into training system.

Acceptance: No stale version, duplicate movement or invented arrival.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-10 — Diversion and handover

Task: Record verified diversion and transfer current status to relief.

Acceptance: Unknowns retained; current version and pending issues acknowledged.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-11 — Evidence judgment

Task: Authenticate work samples and distinguish independent, prompted and simulated work.

Acceptance: No unsupported workplace endorsement.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P94-12 — Remediation and scope

Task: Assess changed deficient task and prepare limited final outcome.

Acceptance: All mandatory controls passed; failed evidence and review retained.

Evidence/source/revision___ Independent or prompted___ Score__/4 Critical___ Corrective practice___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: I94 integrated competence decision
lessons.body:
## I94 integrated competence decision

Observe two routine workplace cycles W-A and W-B, recording actual date, context, task, candidate actions, source records, required confirmations and observer. Then run both synthetic changed cycles independently. Controller supplies information only at the stated event; never coach the answer during the assessed attempt. The learner must leave uncertain actual events unresolved until evidence arrives. A competent reviewer maps every domain to authenticated evidence and records limitations.

Twelve dimensions follow P94-1 through P94-12. Score each 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major coaching, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independently acceptable, 4 accurate independent performance with sound explanation. Each integrated assessment requires at least 39/48, every dimension at least 3, all required observations and stations passed, and no critical error. Critical errors include knowingly accepting a wrong/unmanifested person, fabricating verified weight or movement, unauthorized DG acceptance, knowingly using an obsolete manifest, directing movement outside authority or falsifying evidence. A high written score cannot offset these failures. Retain the result, remediate and reassess a changed case independently.

lessons.title: Records, teaching schedule and credential
lessons.body:
## Records, teaching schedule and credential

F94-E evidence register: domain___ workplace/simulation___ date/context___ source reference___ candidate contribution___ observer authenticity___ independent performance___ restriction/gap___. F94-M manifest: flight/aircraft/date/sector___ revision___ people/identities/destinations/masses___ bags/count/masses/destinations___ freight/details/masses___ totals___ preparer/checker___ recipients/acceptance___. F94-C revision: source/time___ affected entries___ old/new values___ version___ superseded copies___ recipient confirmation___. F94-T movement: unique identity/event___ planned/estimated/actual___ date/time basis___ source___ manual reference___ recovery correction___. F94-H handover: current flight/version/status___ pending holds___ next action/owner___ relief acknowledgment___. F94-R remediation: failed control___ teaching/practice___ changed task___ independent result___ reviewer/appeal___. Keep actual passenger information in the authorized secure system, not public course files.

Original planned preparation/assessment allocation: 32 hours, comprising instruction 6, labs 6, stations 6, simulated integrated work 6, final/feedback/review 4 and a planning allowance of 4 for workplace observation. Actual workplace access may require longer and cannot be waived by the timetable. Final: 12 cases, 36 decisions, 72 points, 120 minutes; pass 58/72, at least 4/6 in each domain and no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed, protected keys/collaboration/outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B follows remediation; practical gaps require practical reassessment.

Issue the original VNDRLY/U Helicopter Administrator — Workplace Competence outcome only after prerequisite verification, corrected learning checks, labs, all stations, two actual independent routine cycles, both changed-condition cycles, final and reviewer acceptance. Record scope, employer/operator/system, version/hash, dates, assessor, reviewer and limitations. If only simulation is available, issue a simulation completion record, not workplace competence. No OPITO award, unrestricted DG authority, aircraft release or employer appointment is conferred. Set employer-defined review and change triggers; do not copy external validity onto an unsupported award.


---

lessons.title: VUC094 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC094 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q94-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-1-L1

Ten team-signed manifests prove your individual competence?

**Answer:** No; authenticate contribution and observe independent work.

**Reason/remediation:** Volume of paperwork is not attribution or performance. Revisit Q94-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-1-L2

Current initial training proves competence on a new system?

**Answer:** No; verify local preparation and actual function.

**Reason/remediation:** Entry evidence does not establish workplace scope. Revisit Q94-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-2-L1

A route changes after the first sector. Which records change?

**Answer:** Affected people, items, destinations, sector manifest and communications.

**Reason/remediation:** Changing a title alone leaves inconsistent operational information. Revisit Q94-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-2-L2

23:50 UTC becomes 00:20 UTC next day: what must be explicit?

**Answer:** The next date and time basis, with planned and actual fields separate.

**Reason/remediation:** A time alone may attach the event to the wrong movement. Revisit Q94-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-3-L1

Four listed and four present, one substitute: acceptable?

**Answer:** Not until identity, eligibility and manifest reconciliation are resolved.

**Reason/remediation:** Equal counts can hide a wrong passenger. Revisit Q94-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-3-L2

Checked in then cancelled means arrived?

**Answer:** No; update removal and associated items through controlled reconciliation.

**Reason/remediation:** Check-in is not transport. Revisit Q94-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-4-L1

84+79+92 kg people, 9+6+11 kg bags, 35 kg freight: total?

**Answer:** 316 kg of recorded inputs.

**Reason/remediation:** 255+26+35; not aircraft loading approval. Revisit Q94-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-4-L2

Remove 79 kg and 6 kg; add 86 kg and 8 kg: new total?

**Answer:** 325 kg.

**Reason/remediation:** 316−85=231; 231+94=325. Identity and count changes also matter. Revisit Q94-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-5-L1

Current version saved but old version held by crew: complete?

**Answer:** No; deliver and confirm required current-version acceptance.

**Reason/remediation:** Saved and received are distinct. Revisit Q94-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-5-L2

Can a neat manifest with guessed weights pass?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Presentation cannot replace reliable source inputs. Revisit Q94-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-6-L1

A tool is added after weighing. What next?

**Answer:** Reverify weight, reconcile item and revise through required acceptance.

**Reason/remediation:** The earlier measurement no longer describes the item. Revisit Q94-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-6-L2

Total mass below allowance proves compartment suitability?

**Answer:** No; authorized review of item and loading constraints is still required.

**Reason/remediation:** Aggregate mass does not establish restraint or balance suitability. Revisit Q94-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-7-L1

An unmarked battery can be accepted by estimating its size?

**Answer:** No; follow the approved hold and specialist verification process.

**Reason/remediation:** Appearance does not establish capacity or carriage permission. Revisit Q94-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-7-L2

Earlier acceptance survives discovery of damage?

**Answer:** No; reassess through the operator safety/DG process.

**Reason/remediation:** New evidence can invalidate earlier assumptions. Revisit Q94-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-8-L1

Check-in complete permits admin to direct boarding?

**Answer:** No; authorized HLO/crew controls movement.

**Reason/remediation:** Administrative readiness is not deck clearance. Revisit Q94-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-8-L2

Deck restriction cleared while identity query remains: release all?

**Answer:** No; resolve the independent identity hold.

**Reason/remediation:** One clearance does not waive another control. Revisit Q94-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-9-L1

Printer fails; only old print exists. Use it?

**Answer:** No; approved current fallback or hold dependent action.

**Reason/remediation:** An outage does not validate obsolete information. Revisit Q94-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-9-L2

System restored: blindly replay manual entries?

**Answer:** No; reconcile actual events and prevent duplicates.

**Reason/remediation:** Technical success does not prove data accuracy. Revisit Q94-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-10-L1

Flight returned to Shore. Mark Echo arrived?

**Answer:** No; record actual confirmed location and time.

**Reason/remediation:** Planned destination is not actual outcome. Revisit Q94-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-10-L2

Handover may omit an unresolved query to avoid delay?

**Answer:** No; transfer current status, holds and next actions with acknowledgment.

**Reason/remediation:** Omitted uncertainty creates false confidence. Revisit Q94-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-11-L1

Simulation-only performance earns workplace competence?

**Answer:** No; record simulation scope until required workplace evidence is complete.

**Reason/remediation:** Assessment mode limits what the evidence proves. Revisit Q94-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-11-L2

A colleague prompted all decisions: independent pass?

**Answer:** No; remediate and assess a changed independent cycle.

**Reason/remediation:** Coached completion is development evidence. Revisit Q94-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q94-12-L1

Written pass offsets failed outage performance?

**Answer:** No; require changed practical evidence after remediation.

**Reason/remediation:** Knowledge and performance are separate mandatory requirements. Revisit Q94-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q94-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q94-12-L2

Employer appointment automatically follows this certificate?

**Answer:** No; appointment and external scheme recognition remain separate.

**Reason/remediation:** A credential must not overstate authority. Revisit Q94-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Complete assessment trace
lessons.body:
## Complete assessment trace

Each of twelve Q94 domains has two explained formative checks, a corresponding P94 observed station, a separate final case with three decisions and a changed retake. W94-1 authenticates evidence; W94-2 tests sector/identity; W94-3 tests mass inputs; W94-4 tests revision/fallback; W94-5 tests holds/operational interface; W94-6 tests recovery and award decisions. I94 requires two actual routine workplace cycles and both synthetic changed-condition cycles. F94 forms retain scope, actual evidence, revisions, movement status, handover and remediation. Protected exam forms and keys are outside the learner package.

lessons.title: Maintenance and limitations
lessons.body:
## Maintenance and limitations

Before delivery, verify current operator procedures, aircraft interfaces, approved weighing and manifest methods, system permissions, DG prerequisites and employer competence policy. Record revisions and assess material changes. Do not manufacture live errors or emergencies for assessment. Actual workplace performance cannot be inferred from authored materials or simulation alone. No operational records have been changed by authoring this package.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Helicopter Landing Officer — Workplace Competence
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Helicopter Landing Officer — Workplace Competence

VUC095. Original available-source normal-operations package. Actual operator procedures and supervised workplace evidence govern delivery. No external accreditation, aircraft command, unrestricted emergency-team or refuelling qualification is conferred.

lessons.title: Q95-1 — Role, preparation and assessment boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q95-1 — Role, preparation and assessment boundaries

The HLO coordinates the helideck team and the installation side of helicopter operations within the approved helideck operations manual. This is not pilot command, aircraft performance approval or unrestricted authority over every aviation task. Establish the site, aircraft interfaces, assigned duties, competent team and actual procedures before assessing performance. Initial helideck instruction followed by supervised workplace development is the expected preparation; a workplace assessment is not a shortcut around learning the role.

Confirm fitness for the planned practical activities and appropriate PPE. Identify additional qualifications needed for specialist functions such as refuelling or emergency-team leadership. This package assesses normal HLO operations and safe recognition/escalation of abnormal conditions; it does not substitute for a full specialist emergency qualification. Evidence must identify what the candidate personally did, independently, in the actual context.

Worked and changed applications: A candidate has directed practice on a mock deck but no authenticated workplace cycle. Credit practice and arrange actual observation before a workplace outcome. Changed case: the HLO is asked to perform a fuel-system repair outside authorization. Preserve the defect, obtain the authorized specialist and do not extend competence by job title.

lessons.title: Q95-2 — Operating information and local limitations
lessons.body:
## Q95-2 — Operating information and local limitations

Read current installation and aircraft-operator information before planning a movement. Identify applicable deck dimensions and load rating, markings, obstacle environment, lighting, access routes, equipment status, weather information, and any restrictions. A familiar aircraft name does not prove compatibility with today’s deck condition. Use controlled records and the operator’s acceptance process rather than memorized generic limits.

Check revisions and communicate material changes. A restriction entered after the morning briefing can invalidate earlier readiness. The HLO must know where to obtain authoritative information and who can resolve uncertainty. Do not convert a missing value into a favorable assumption. In assessment, explain the relationship between local readiness and the flight crew’s separate decisions; a helideck report is not a flight clearance.

Worked and changed applications: A training card says fictional deck mass limit 12,000 kg and proposed aircraft operating mass 12,200 kg. Flag the 200 kg exceedance and refer; do not use aircraft empty mass instead. Changed case: mass is below the card value but a compatibility field is missing. The numerical comparison alone cannot establish readiness.

lessons.title: Q95-3 — Deck inspection and foreign-object control
lessons.body:
## Q95-3 — Deck inspection and foreign-object control

Inspect the deck and access arrangements using the approved checklist before operations and after relevant changes. Look for loose objects, contamination, damaged surfaces, unsecured equipment, obstructed routes and defects in required markings, lighting or perimeter protection. Inspect only when access is safe and authorized. A checklist tick must reflect an actual observation, not memory of the last flight.

Foreign objects can move under rotor wash and harm people or aircraft. Secure or remove them through the authorized safe process; never chase a loose item toward a running aircraft. Report defects and verify correction before changing status. Maintain clear emergency and passenger routes. The assessor should see a systematic inspection, accurate findings and a controlled reinspection after correction.

Worked and changed applications: A strap is found on the marked mock landing area. Hold readiness, arrange safe removal and recheck; do not step into a live rotor area to retrieve it. Changed case: the object is removed but a slippery patch remains. Keep the separate defect open until the approved resolution is verified.

lessons.title: Q95-4 — Weather, environmental effects and motion information
lessons.body:
## Q95-4 — Weather, environmental effects and motion information

Obtain and report current required weather and, for moving decks, motion information from authorized systems or trained sources. State time, units and any sensor limitations. Wind, visibility, precipitation, turbulence, exhaust effects and vessel motion can affect operations; do not substitute a casual visual estimate for required data. The aircraft operator determines applicable flight limits and acceptance.

Check freshness and consistency. If a sensor is unavailable, use only an approved alternative with its conditions and notifications; do not invent a replacement reading. A report that was acceptable earlier may no longer describe current conditions. Recognize installation activities that change airflow or exhaust exposure and communicate them. Assessment should use synthetic values to test reporting and hold decisions without teaching fabricated universal limits.

Worked and changed applications: The exercise card requires reports no older than ten minutes. At 14:12, a 13:58 observation is fourteen minutes old and fails that fictional freshness rule. Obtain a current approved report. Changed case: a fresh report has no units or motion-source status; resolve those gaps rather than treating its timestamp as sufficient.

lessons.title: Q95-5 — Concurrent work and obstacle coordination
lessons.body:
## Q95-5 — Concurrent work and obstacle coordination

Coordinate cranes, lifts, work parties, nearby structures and other activities that could conflict with helicopter operations. Use the approved communication and work-control arrangements to establish safe status before arrival or departure. A crane operator’s acknowledgment that a message was heard is not confirmation that the crane is in the required position. Verify the actual required condition and communicate it clearly.

Consider changing or unusual obstacles and conflicting operations near more than one landing area. Do not infer that simultaneous operations are acceptable because they occurred previously. Refer to the operator’s agreed arrangements and responsible installation authority. If a conflict develops, hold or suspend the affected operation and notify the right parties. Record who confirmed the condition and when.

Worked and changed applications: A mock crane response says request received, while the status display still shows movement. The HLO must obtain verified safe status rather than announce readiness. Changed case: crane is secured but a maintenance team remains in an access route. Resolve that independent conflict before release.

lessons.title: Q95-6 — Team organization, briefing and communications
lessons.body:
## Q95-6 — Team organization, briefing and communications

Assign competent personnel to required roles, confirm equipment and communication readiness, and brief the movement plan, hazards, signals, passenger route, special arrangements and stop criteria. Identify the HLO clearly. Check understanding with concise readback or task confirmation. Staffing is determined by the approved operation and emergency arrangements, not by an invented minimum from this course.

Use the approved radio and signaling procedures. A missed or ambiguous message requires clarification; do not proceed on a guess. When communications degrade, apply the approved alternative only if all conditions are satisfied, otherwise hold. Keep a shared picture of deck status and passenger movement. The assessor should observe leadership that invites safety concerns and does not penalize a team member for reporting a defect.

Worked and changed applications: An HDA cannot repeat the assigned passenger route. Rebrief before movement rather than assuming experience will compensate. Changed case: radio failure occurs after briefing. Establish the approved fallback and required coordination, or hold; hand signals are not a blanket substitute for every missing communication.

lessons.title: Q95-7 — Arrival readiness and controlled access
lessons.body:
## Q95-7 — Arrival readiness and controlled access

Before reporting readiness, confirm deck condition, concurrent-work status, required equipment and team, current information, and controlled access. Communicate restrictions accurately to the responsible aviation and installation parties. The pilot retains aircraft decisions; the HLO does not guarantee landing safety merely by completing a local checklist. Maintain exclusion and observation throughout arrival.

People must remain outside unsafe areas until the approved aircraft-specific process authorizes access. Rotor, tail-rotor, exhaust and visibility hazards vary with aircraft and conditions. Do not teach a universal approach direction from a generic diagram. Use the operator’s current safe routes, crew indications and HLO control. A new hazard after readiness requires an immediate status update and appropriate hold.

Worked and changed applications: The deck was reported ready but loose material is then observed. Update the status promptly and prevent personnel movement; do not hide the change to avoid disruption. Changed case: someone tries to approach because the aircraft has landed. Landing alone is not permission to enter the controlled area.

lessons.title: Q95-8 — Passenger disembarkation and embarkation
lessons.body:
## Q95-8 — Passenger disembarkation and embarkation

Coordinate with flight crew before passenger movement. Confirm the authorized route, team positions, required briefing and special assistance arrangements. Maintain positive control so passengers do not wander toward hazardous areas or retrieve dropped objects. Keep baggage and other tasks from creating a competing movement path. Do not improvise aircraft emergency instructions or assistance methods.

Reconcile passenger identities and counts with the current manifest through the approved administrative interface. A matching headcount can conceal an unmanifested substitute. Resolve discrepancies before dependent movement and ensure the crew has current information. Assess calm communication and safe pacing rather than speed. The HLO must stop a developing unsafe movement, not rely on a last-second correction.

Worked and changed applications: Manifest lists six people and six appear, but one ID differs. Hold, verify and revise through the authorized process; do not accept the number alone. Changed case: a passenger drops a bag near a marked hazard boundary. Stop and arrange controlled recovery when safe rather than allowing pursuit.

lessons.title: Q95-9 — Baggage, freight and dangerous-goods interface
lessons.body:
## Q95-9 — Baggage, freight and dangerous-goods interface

Control the safe movement of bags and freight according to the operator’s loading and route instructions. Match item identity, destination, count and recorded mass; refer loading suitability to authorized personnel. Heavy or unusual items may require specific handling arrangements. Changes after weighing or manifest preparation must be reconciled before acceptance.

Recognize suspect or undeclared dangerous goods and stay within assigned training. Hold and refer uncertain items without improvised opening, packaging or classification. Keep personnel routes clear during item handling. The HLO coordinates the interface but cannot authorize a prohibited item by relabeling it as baggage. Assess the candidate’s ability to preserve a hold under time pressure and communicate the revised status.

Worked and changed applications: A toolbox is added after manifest approval. Stop the addition, obtain verified data and authorized loading/DG review, and update records. Changed case: a damaged battery is discovered among bags. Activate the applicable safety route and specialist response; do not simply move it to another bag.

lessons.title: Q95-10 — Departure checks and post-flight restoration
lessons.body:
## Q95-10 — Departure checks and post-flight restoration

Before departure, complete the approved crew coordination and confirm people, equipment and items are clear of required areas. Verify actual status rather than relying solely on a checklist completed before loading. Reconcile unresolved discrepancies and communicate any change. The HLO’s local readiness report is not an aircraft dispatch clearance.

After the movement, record actual times and relevant events, inspect when safe, restore equipment and identify defects or replenishment needs. Do not mark the deck fully ready for another flight if a required resource remains unavailable. Preserve reports, manifest references and handover information. An accurate post-flight record supports both the next movement and later investigation.

Worked and changed applications: A handling tool is missing from the count before departure. Hold and resolve its location through the safe process; do not assume it is in storage. Changed case: the aircraft departs but a required response item is defective. Record and notify the resulting readiness restriction rather than carrying forward the previous ready status.

lessons.title: Q95-11 — Equipment defects, refuelling boundaries and abnormal response
lessons.body:
## Q95-11 — Equipment defects, refuelling boundaries and abnormal response

Know the required operational and emergency equipment and the approved process for unserviceability. A minimum-equipment provision is conditional; it is not permission to ignore a defect without meeting its conditions, authority and notification requirements. If a required capability is not established, report the restriction and hold affected operations. Do not repair safety-critical systems beyond authorization.

Refuelling requires separately competent personnel, aircraft-specific procedures and the approved HLO/crew interface. This package does not train hands-on fuel delivery. Maintain the separation and controls required by the actual procedure; do not combine passenger movement and fuelling as a time-saving improvisation. For a fire, spill or other emergency, raise the alarm, protect people and initiate the established response within trained role; do not turn an assessment into uncontrolled live rescue.

Worked and changed applications: A required response resource is unavailable and no approved alternative is established. Notify responsible parties and withhold readiness. Changed case: a radio defect has a documented conditional alternative, but the alternate link has not been tested. The conditions are not yet met; a document alone is not restored capability.

lessons.title: Q95-12 — Workplace evidence, remediation and maintained competence
lessons.body:
## Q95-12 — Workplace evidence, remediation and maintained competence

Assessment must cover normal preparation, arrival, passenger/item control, departure and restoration through independent workplace observations. Use declared mock exercises for defects and unusual conditions that cannot safely be introduced into operations. Record the candidate’s actions and any prompts, supporting work products and authenticated witnesses. Simulation is valuable evidence of decisions but cannot alone prove actual workplace performance.

For this original package, require two observed routine cycles in the defined context, all stations and changed-condition exercises, and the separate final. A critical safety or integrity failure prevents a pass regardless of total score. Remediate the specific gap and assess a changed independent task. Record employer/operator scope and limitations; no OPITO credential or universal HLO appointment follows from the authored materials.

Worked and changed applications: A candidate passes written questions but directs a person into a prohibited mock area. Stop, record the critical error, re-teach and assess changed movement control before any award. Changed case: a competent HLO moves to a different deck or operator. Review local differences and obtain the necessary preparation and evidence rather than assuming every procedure transfers unchanged.


---

content.title: VUC095 | VUC095 assessor workbook and operating exercises
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC095 assessor workbook and operating exercises
lessons.body: # VUC095 assessor workbook and operating exercises

lessons.title: Safe delivery and workplace evidence
lessons.body:
## Safe delivery and workplace evidence

Assessor must be competent in HLO duties, actual helideck/operator procedures and assessment. Use an independent reviewer for sufficiency and appeals. Verify initial preparation, supervised development, fitness and required specialist scope. The public external assessment describes expected preparation without a formal prerequisite list; this original delivery plan still requires safe readiness before participation. Do not expose an unprepared learner to live operations.

F95 adaptation: site/operator___ helideck manual revision___ aircraft types/interfaces___ deck ratings/limitations___ weather/motion sources and criteria___ concurrent-work arrangements___ required team/roles___ PPE___ approved communications/signals/fallback___ movement routes and crew indications___ required emergency resources___ unserviceability conditions/authority___ passenger/manifest interface___ specialist fuelling boundaries___ emergency notifications___ assessor/reviewer/date___. All operational criteria must come from approved local sources. Synthetic numbers below are not live limits.

Require two independent authorized routine workplace observations, each covering preparation through restoration, with actual dates and records. Observe without distracting crew or changing operational conditions. Never plant foreign objects, disable radios, introduce wrong manifests, create fuel faults or manufacture emergencies on a live deck. Changed conditions use a ground-level mock/inactive area, inert aircraft outline, marked hazards, harmless dummy items, training radios isolated from operational frequencies and roleplayers. No rotor-running activity, live fuel, fire, smoke, elevated-edge exposure or actual aircraft movement is required for mock exercises.

Safety controller checks the mock area, weather, trip hazards, roleplayer readiness and stop signal. A real hazard stops the exercise immediately. Operational authority may stop workplace observation at any time. Actual operations remain governed by their approved procedures; the course does not authorize them. If workplace access is unavailable, record simulation completion only until real evidence is obtained.

lessons.title: S95 exercise resources and scripted conditions
lessons.body:
## S95 exercise resources and scripted conditions

Draw a rectangular ground-level training area with a central aircraft outline, clearly labeled rotor/tail/exhaust hazard zones, a safe waiting area W, route R to the mock passenger door, baggage staging B and exit E. These are teaching labels, not transferable aircraft approach geometry. The actual operator must supply real aircraft-specific routes for workplace assessment. Use soft markers and no real hazards. Team: candidate HLO, two mock assistants, crew roleplayer, admin roleplayer, crane/work-party contact and independent safety controller. The exercise staffing is not a prescribed operational minimum.

Card A: fictional deck comparison value 12,000 kg; proposed operating mass 11,600 kg; compatibility fields complete. Synthetic report maximum age ten minutes. At 14:05 UTC, report observed 14:00 with units/source confirmed and no sensor fault. Team/required resources initially declared available. Crane contact initially says request received; controller withholds secured confirmation until the candidate asks and the roleplayer reports verified state. A work party remains on route R until coordinated clearance. Harmless strap and paper contamination marker are found during inspection. Candidate must identify both; removing strap does not close contamination.

Inbound list: I1/I2/I3/I4; disembarkation is allowed only after mock crew readiness and route controls. Outbound list O1/O2/O3/O4/O5/O6, six tagged bags. Present O1–O5 and X9 instead of O6. Correct model: count six but O6 missing and X9 unmanifested; hold and resolve before current manifest and crew acceptance. A dropped dummy item is placed near a marked prohibited area; prevent pursuit and arrange safe recovery. Tool inventory T1/T2/T3/T4; return list initially T1/T2/T4. T3 must be located safely, not assumed stored. After departure, controller reports one required response item unavailable; next readiness remains restricted until approved resolution.

Card B changes context: fictional deck comparison value 12,400 kg; proposed mass 12,150 kg; compatibility field unresolved. Synthetic maximum report age eight minutes. At 16:00, observation is 15:53 but sensor fault is flagged. Crew has manifest v 2 while admin holds v 3. One paper card shows damaged battery. A radio fails; supplied exercise alternative requires a verified relay link and agreed mock signals. Relay is initially unavailable, so alternative conditions are not met. Later controller confirms relay test, but the battery decision remains unresolved. A spill is represented only by a paper inject before mock departure. Correct model: preserve independent holds; one resolution does not clear all hazards.

No scenario controller may convert these fictional values into authorization for actual aircraft work. Candidate records the controlled source, current status, restriction, responsible contact and resolution for every condition.

lessons.title: Application labs
lessons.body:
## Application labs

### W95-1 — Scope and evidence

Create F95 and map all twelve domains to observation or declared simulation. Model: two actual independent cycles plus changed-condition exercises; specialist functions remain separately authorized. Changed: prior certificate exists but no current local evidence. Require preparation and observation, not automatic endorsement.

### W95-2 — Readiness reasoning

Use cards A/B. Model: A mass margin 400 kg below the fictional comparison; report age five minutes meets only its time rule. Crane, work party and defects still prevent readiness. B mass margin 250 kg below; report age seven minutes meets time but sensor fault and missing compatibility remain. Changed: proposed mass 12,200 against 12,000 is a 200 kg exceedance. Never select empty mass to force a pass.

### W95-3 — Inspection and simultaneous work

Inspect mock area and obtain crane/work-party status. Model: strap, contamination and occupied route are separate findings; received message is not secured state. Recheck corrections. Changed: crane secured but another activity conflicts; apply actual coordination requirements rather than assuming clearance transfers.

### W95-4 — Team and passenger control

Brief roles, route, signals and stop criteria; conduct mock arrival and passenger sequence. Model: correct crew/HLO interface, no unauthorized approach, O6/X9 discrepancy held, dropped item recovered only safely. Changed: radio fails and one assistant misunderstands route. Resolve both before movement.

### W95-5 — Freight, defects and departure

Process late item and damaged-battery cards, tool count and conditional communication alternative. Model: specialist referral, revised records, T3 missing, relay conditions unfulfilled. Changed: relay restored while DG query remains; retain the DG hold. No actual fuel or dangerous object is handled.

### W95-6 — Restoration and evidence decision

Record actual mock events, post-flight defect and handover. Model: next-flight readiness reflects unavailable resource; evidence distinguishes candidate action from team help. Changed: written final passed but unsafe mock approach occurred. Record critical failure and require changed practical assessment, not a numerical override.

lessons.title: Observed stations
lessons.body:
## Observed stations

Twelve stations. Physical mock-area activities occur in stations 3, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10; six other stations use documents, calculations or roleplay. Actual workplace cycles are additional mandatory evidence. Practice precedes independent assessment. Record prompts rather than treating coached work as independent.

### P95-1 — Scope and preparation

Task: Verify prior development, fitness, permissions and role boundaries.

Acceptance: No unsupported specialist function or workplace claim.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-2 — Controlled operating information

Task: Compare aircraft/deck data and identify missing or conflicting criteria.

Acceptance: Actual controlled inputs used; numerical margin not treated as total approval.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-3 — Deck inspection

Task: Inspect a safe inactive/mock area and record defects, correction and recheck.

Acceptance: Systematic actual observations; no unsafe retrieval.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-4 — Weather and status report

Task: Check synthetic source, units, age and fault flags; report restrictions.

Acceptance: No guessed data or universal invented limits.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-5 — Concurrent work

Task: Roleplay crane/work-party coordination and verify actual condition.

Acceptance: Receipt distinguished from completed safe status.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-6 — Team briefing

Task: Brief mock team roles, route, hazards and stop criteria; check understanding.

Acceptance: Clear shared plan and tested approved communications.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-7 — Arrival/access control

Task: Control a safe mock deck with changed readiness and unauthorized approach.

Acceptance: Prompt status update and safe exclusion.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-8 — Passenger movement

Task: Direct mock disembarkation/boarding with identity and dropped-item injects.

Acceptance: Approved route and crew interface; no unsafe retrieval or substitute.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-9 — Items and DG interface

Task: Reconcile safe dummy bags/freight and paper suspect-item cards.

Acceptance: Correct routing/records; specialist holds preserved.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-10 — Departure/restoration

Task: Resolve tool count, clear mock area, record events and inspect after movement.

Acceptance: No assumed clearance; next readiness reflects defects.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-11 — Defect and abnormal response

Task: Apply supplied conditional alternative and mock alarm/escalation plan.

Acceptance: All conditions verified; no unauthorized repair or emergency improvisation.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P95-12 — Evidence and outcome

Task: Build authenticated evidence matrix and changed remediation plan.

Acceptance: Independent workplace and simulation scope distinguished.

Context/source/revision___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: I95 integrated assessment
lessons.body:
## I95 integrated assessment

Run both A and B as complete changed mock cycles. Controller releases injects at the relevant stage, records the candidate's decisions and does not coach. All independent holds must be tracked through resolution. Require two actual routine workplace cycles W1 and W2 with date, site, operator, candidate contribution, observer and secure evidence references. A competent reviewer checks every domain and any restrictions. Simulation success is not proof that actual workplace observation occurred.

Twelve dimensions correspond to P95-1 through P95-12. Score 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major coaching, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independently acceptable, 4 accurate and independently explained. Each integrated decision requires at least 39/48, every dimension at least 3, all stations and required cycles passed, and no critical error. Critical: knowingly false readiness, unauthorized unsafe movement, ignoring a missing person/item or active restriction, unsupported DG/fuelling authority, invented operational data or fabricated evidence. Stop the attempt, preserve the result, provide targeted teaching/practice, then assess a changed independent task. Correct safety holds are credited even if the mock flight is delayed.

lessons.title: Forms and delivery plan
lessons.body:
## Forms and delivery plan

F95-D deck record: date/time___ controlled source___ inspected area/item___ finding___ hold___ owner/action___ verified correction/reinspection___ current status___. F95-S status report: flight/date___ weather/motion source/time/units___ deck/equipment/team status___ concurrent work___ restrictions___ recipient/readback___. F95-P movement: current manifest___ expected/actual identities___ discrepancy___ bag/freight link___ briefing/assistance___ crew readiness___ HLO/team controls___ actual event___. F95-E evidence: domain___ actual/simulated___ candidate contribution___ prompts___ source/witness___ independent result___. F95-H handover: latest status___ defects/holds___ equipment restoration___ pending owner/action___ acknowledgment___. F95-R remediation: failed control___ practice___ changed assessment___ result___ reviewer/appeal___. Protect real passenger data in authorized records.

Original 40-hour planning allocation: instruction 8, labs 6, stations 8, mock integrated cycles 8, final/feedback/review 4 and workplace-observation planning allowance 6. More time/access is required if evidence is incomplete. Final has twelve cases, 36 decisions, 72 points and 120 minutes; pass 58/72, at least 4/6 in every domain and no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B follows remediation. A practical failure needs practical evidence, not just another written score.

Award original VNDRLY/U Helicopter Landing Officer — Workplace Competence only after entry/readiness verification, corrected checks, labs, all stations, both changed mock cycles, two independent workplace cycles, final and competent review. Record operator/site/aircraft-interface scope, version/hash, dates, assessor and limitations. No OPITO award, pilot authority, specialist refuelling or emergency qualification is implied. Employer appointment and continued competence review remain separate. Changes to deck, operator, equipment or duties require review of affected competence evidence.


---

courses.title: VUC095 | VUC095 formative checks

content.title: VUC095 | VUC095 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC095 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC095 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q95-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-1-L1

Mock-deck practice alone proves workplace competence?

**Answer:** No; require authenticated actual workplace performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Simulation and workplace evidence have different limits. Revisit Q95-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-1-L2

HLO title authorizes fuel-system repair?

**Answer:** No; only separately authorized competent personnel may perform it.

**Reason/remediation:** A coordinating role does not remove specialist boundaries. Revisit Q95-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-2-L1

Fictional deck limit 12,000 kg, proposed operating mass 12,200 kg: margin?

**Answer:** 200 kg exceedance; hold and refer.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not substitute empty aircraft mass to obtain a favorable comparison. Revisit Q95-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-2-L2

Mass below limit proves all compatibility?

**Answer:** No; every applicable controlled criterion must be established.

**Reason/remediation:** One passing field does not resolve missing data. Revisit Q95-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-3-L1

Loose strap found before arrival: act how?

**Answer:** Hold readiness, arrange safe removal, then recheck.

**Reason/remediation:** Foreign-object correction must not expose people to rotor hazards. Revisit Q95-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-3-L2

Strap removed but contamination remains: ready?

**Answer:** No; resolve the separate defect.

**Reason/remediation:** Closing one finding does not close every finding. Revisit Q95-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-4-L1

Report 13:58, current 14:12, fictional maximum age ten minutes: usable?

**Answer:** Age fourteen minutes, so not under that exercise rule.

**Reason/remediation:** Obtain current approved information; the ten-minute value is not universal. Revisit Q95-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-4-L2

Fresh reading without units is sufficient?

**Answer:** No; resolve units and source/status.

**Reason/remediation:** Freshness is only one part of reliable data. Revisit Q95-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-5-L1

Crane says message received: secured status proven?

**Answer:** No; verify the required actual condition.

**Reason/remediation:** Receipt is not completion. Revisit Q95-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-5-L2

Crane secured but access route occupied: ready?

**Answer:** No; resolve independent conflict.

**Reason/remediation:** Concurrent hazards must all be addressed. Revisit Q95-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-6-L1

HDA cannot explain assigned route: proceed?

**Answer:** No; rebrief and confirm understanding.

**Reason/remediation:** Experience does not substitute for a shared current plan. Revisit Q95-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-6-L2

Radio fails: all hand signals automatically adequate?

**Answer:** No; use only approved alternatives with conditions met, otherwise hold.

**Reason/remediation:** Communication functions differ. Revisit Q95-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-7-L1

Hazard appears after ready report: keep quiet?

**Answer:** No; update status immediately and control access.

**Reason/remediation:** Readiness is conditional on current conditions. Revisit Q95-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-7-L2

Aircraft landed means passengers may approach?

**Answer:** No; wait for approved crew/HLO-controlled process.

**Reason/remediation:** Landing does not remove rotor and movement hazards. Revisit Q95-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-8-L1

Six present, one wrong ID: count sufficient?

**Answer:** No; resolve identity/manifest discrepancy.

**Reason/remediation:** Equal count can mask a substitute. Revisit Q95-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-8-L2

Passenger drops item near hazard boundary: chase it?

**Answer:** No; stop and arrange safe controlled recovery.

**Reason/remediation:** Object recovery must not create injury risk. Revisit Q95-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-9-L1

Late toolbox can bypass manifest because small?

**Answer:** No; verify and reconcile through required acceptance.

**Reason/remediation:** Unrecorded additions undermine load information. Revisit Q95-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-9-L2

Damaged battery can be moved to another bag?

**Answer:** No; use operator safety/DG escalation.

**Reason/remediation:** Relabeling or moving does not resolve the hazard. Revisit Q95-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-10-L1

Tool count short before departure: assume stored?

**Answer:** No; resolve location through safe process.

**Reason/remediation:** An assumption is not a clearance check. Revisit Q95-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-10-L2

Post-flight equipment defect leaves next-flight readiness unchanged?

**Answer:** No; record and communicate restriction.

**Reason/remediation:** Previous readiness does not survive changed capability. Revisit Q95-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-11-L1

A conditional equipment alternative is documented but untested: satisfied?

**Answer:** No; verify all required conditions and communication.

**Reason/remediation:** Documentation alone is not operational capability. Revisit Q95-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-11-L2

This normal HLO package qualifies hands-on refuelling?

**Answer:** No; separate competence and aircraft-specific procedures are required.

**Reason/remediation:** Interfaces are taught without conferring specialist authority. Revisit Q95-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q95-12-L1

High written score offsets critical movement failure?

**Answer:** No; remediate and assess changed independent performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Mandatory safety controls are not averaged away. Revisit Q95-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q95-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q95-12-L2

New operator/deck needs no review after prior pass?

**Answer:** No; assess changed local requirements and scope.

**Reason/remediation:** Competence evidence is contextual. Revisit Q95-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: VUC095 source and coverage record
lessons.body:
# VUC095 source and coverage record

Reviewed 18 November 2026. Original normal-operations workplace assessment package. Full OPITO specification unavailable; no accreditation, exact parity or external certificate asserted.

| Primary source | Public findings and use | Coverage |
|---|---|---|
| [OPITO HLO workplace competence 7046](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/helicopter-landing-officer-hlo-workplace-competence-assessment-standard) | Public assessment concerns normal HLO operations, expects initial training and supervised development, lists two mandatory units, allows sufficient assessment access rather than fixed timing, and publishes two-year external validity. These facts distinguish assessment from initial instruction; original duration and award remain separate. | Q95-1 and Q95-12; evidence gates and review |
| [CAA CAP 437 current publication record](https://www.caa.co.uk/data-and-publications/publications/documents/content/cap-437/) and [official edition 9 amendment 1](https://www.caa.co.uk/media/3ccjonps/cap437-standards-for-offshore-helicopter-landing-areas-edition-9-amendm-1.pdf) | Current version dated 7 January 2026. Chapters 5–6, Appendix K and Appendix L support competent teams, controlled movement, obstacle/concurrent-work coordination, current information, passenger interfaces and conditional treatment of equipment defects. Chapter 8 provides specialist refuelling context; this package does not teach or confer hands-on fuel qualification. No generic approach direction, aircraft limit or automatic defect waiver is inferred. | Q95-2 to Q95-11; readiness, team, movement, defect and restoration exercises |
| [CAA dangerous-goods CBTA](https://www.caa.co.uk/commercial-industry/airlines/dangerous-goods/cbta-for-dangerous-goods) | Assigned functions determine required preparation; role title alone does not establish acceptance authority. | Q95-1, Q95-9, Q95-11; DG holds |

lessons.title: Trace and maintenance
lessons.body:
## Trace and maintenance

Each Q95 chapter has two explained formative checks, a corresponding P95 station, one protected three-decision final case and a changed retake. Six worked labs connect the domains to supplied mock datasets. I95 includes two changed mock cycles and evidence forms for two actual independent workplace cycles. Six stations use safe physical mock-area tasks; six are observed review/roleplay. No actual aircraft, emergency or learner performance is claimed by package creation.

Before delivery verify current local manual, aircraft interfaces, equipment requirements, weather/motion sources, communications, movement routes, concurrent-work arrangements, specialist boundaries and emergency contacts. Record applicable revisions. Synthetic comparison values and report-age rules are explicitly not live criteria. Preserve failed evidence and reassess material changes. Learner files contain no protected final answers or real passenger records.
