lessons.title: VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Initial Training
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Initial Training

VUC096. Original available-source initial instruction and simulated skills package. Full external specification unavailable. No OPITO award, workplace appointment, unrestricted firefighting, rescue, refuelling or aircraft authority is conferred.

lessons.title: Q96-1 — NUI role, preparation and limits
lessons.body:
## Q96-1 — NUI role, preparation and limits

A normally unattended installation creates a different support problem from a permanently staffed helideck. During first arrival and final departure there may be no resident deck team waiting to intervene. The approved operating concept must explain who provides information, what automated or remote safeguards exist, how the visiting team assumes duties and how the site is left. Never fill those transitions by assuming that someone else must be present.

Initial training builds knowledge and simulated skills. Employer appointment requires local preparation, experience and workplace assessment. Verify function-specific dangerous-goods preparation and required radio qualification for the jurisdiction, plus fitness for practical training. Weather reporting, refuelling, rescue and other specialist duties require their own competence. The HLO coordinates within a defined plan; the pilot retains aircraft decisions and the duty holder retains installation responsibilities.

Worked and changed applications: A first-time visitor is called HLO because they hold a generic safety certificate. Do not treat that as sufficient role preparation. Changed case: an experienced HLO transfers from a staffed deck to a NUI. Review the unattended transitions and local emergency concept rather than assuming the old staffing model still exists.

lessons.title: Q96-2 — Rules, manuals and the installation operating concept
lessons.body:
## Q96-2 — Rules, manuals and the installation operating concept

Identify the controlled helideck manual, aircraft-operator arrangements, emergency plan, equipment requirements and jurisdiction-specific rules. Record revisions and the actual assigned functions. Public standards provide context, but local criteria such as deck compatibility, required staffing, communication links and permitted operating modes must come from authorized sources. A course example is not a waiver or operating procedure.

Map responsibility across remote support, flight crew and visiting personnel for each phase. Before arrival, establish who confirms status and how uncertainty is reported. During occupancy, define who controls the helideck and emergency response. Before leaving, identify who accepts the final unattended status. If responsibilities conflict or required information is missing, hold dependent actions and obtain an authorized resolution.

Worked and changed applications: The remote contact expects the visiting team to inspect before the first landing, which is impossible. Escalate the gap in the operating concept; do not claim an inspection occurred. Changed case: a new manual revision changes the final-departure checks. Brief and apply the current revision rather than using a familiar old checklist.

lessons.title: Q96-3 — Visit planning and remote readiness
lessons.body:
## Q96-3 — Visit planning and remote readiness

Plan the visit with current flight/sector information, personnel and equipment, communications, expected duration, rescue arrangements and contingencies for delayed return. Obtain the approved current remote status, restrictions and inspection information. A green screen without source time or fault status is not enough to establish current capability. The pilot and operator need accurate information, not an unsupported all-clear.

Consider loss of communications, worsening weather, equipment defects and inability to depart as planned. Identify approved shelter, accountability, emergency contacts and escalation triggers. Do not assume a rescue resource will arrive within a fictional classroom time. Confirm what the visiting team must carry and what is available on the installation. Resolve missing safety-critical arrangements before the visit proceeds through the authorized process.

Worked and changed applications: A remote report is old and one required status field is unknown. Obtain approved current information or report the restriction; do not infer serviceability from silence. Changed case: return is delayed beyond the planned work window. Use the approved contingency and welfare arrangements while maintaining communications and accountability.

lessons.title: Q96-4 — Helicopter and helideck hazards
lessons.body:
## Q96-4 — Helicopter and helideck hazards

Recognize rotor, tail-rotor, exhaust, noise, visibility, downwash, loose-object, slip and edge hazards. Aircraft-specific movement routes and crew indications govern approach and departure from the aircraft. Do not teach one compass direction as safe for every aircraft. Keep people controlled and prevent retrieval of dropped objects into dangerous areas. Use appropriate PPE and secure loose clothing or equipment.

An unattended period can allow contamination, debris or other deterioration to develop. Report observations accurately and inspect when access is authorized and safe. Do not create exposure by attempting correction while rotors or other hazards make access unsafe. Maintain clear escape and passenger routes. Assessment uses ground-level marked hazards and harmless props; real hazards are not needed to test recognition and control.

Worked and changed applications: A dropped glove moves toward the marked mock tail-rotor area. Stop the person who starts after it and arrange safe recovery. Changed case: debris is removed but contamination still affects the route. Keep that independent issue open; a partial cleanup is not complete readiness.

lessons.title: Q96-5 — Status systems, weather and equipment information
lessons.body:
## Q96-5 — Status systems, weather and equipment information

Understand the actual status indications, remote monitoring and failure modes supplied by the installation. Distinguish confirmed serviceability from an unavailable signal, stale report or sensor fault. Weather and motion information must come from approved sources with units and time. Do not convert an absent alarm into proof that every system is functional.

Required equipment and approved alternatives are conditional. A defect must be assessed through the applicable unserviceability process, including authority and notifications. Never bypass or reset a safety system simply to remove a red indication. The HLO communicates current facts and limitations; specialist personnel diagnose or repair outside the HLO’s authorization. A changed condition after a status report requires an update.

Worked and changed applications: A fictional exercise requires a report within eight minutes; at 10:12 a 10:00 report is twelve minutes old and fails that exercise rule. Obtain current approved information. Changed case: a new report is only two minutes old but carries a sensor-fault flag. Freshness does not cure invalid data.

lessons.title: Q96-6 — First arrival and transfer to attended operations
lessons.body:
## Q96-6 — First arrival and transfer to attended operations

Follow the approved NUI first-arrival procedure and flight-crew directions. Recognize that the visiting HLO may arrive aboard the aircraft rather than already controlling the deck. The operating concept must address this without pretending a resident team is present. Initial access and establishment of local control occur only through the authorized sequence.

Once safely established, confirm the local condition and required resources, team roles, communications and access controls. Report discrepancies discovered after arrival and restrict dependent activity. Do not retrospectively describe a remote assumption as a completed physical inspection. The transition to attended operation is a deliberate handover of information and duties, not an automatic consequence of one person stepping off the aircraft.

Worked and changed applications: The team arrives and finds an item unavailable despite the remote record. Report the actual finding and apply the restriction before later movements. Changed case: the aircraft is still in a controlled phase and a team member wants to inspect behind it. Defer unsafe access and follow crew/HLO controls rather than prioritizing the checklist.

lessons.title: Q96-7 — Team briefing and communications
lessons.body:
## Q96-7 — Team briefing and communications

Brief roles, current hazards, movement routes, normal and emergency communications, accountability and stop criteria. Check understanding and make it clear who is coordinating each phase. A small visiting team must not silently assume additional specialist roles for which members are unprepared. Confirm required communication links to remote support and flight crew through approved means.

Use concise messages with location, condition, restriction and requested action. Read back critical information and distinguish receipt from completed action. When a link fails, use only the approved alternative with its conditions satisfied; otherwise hold or escalate as the plan requires. Never use an operational frequency for an unannounced training emergency. Practical exercises use isolated training communications.

Worked and changed applications: Remote support acknowledges a message but has not confirmed the required action. Obtain the actual status rather than treating acknowledgment as completion. Changed case: a team member cannot repeat the emergency muster location. Rebrief and check understanding before the team disperses.

lessons.title: Q96-8 — Passenger, baggage and freight control
lessons.body:
## Q96-8 — Passenger, baggage and freight control

Coordinate passenger movement with crew readiness, actual routes, briefing and assistance arrangements. Reconcile identities and current manifest through the approved process. Equal counts do not establish correct passengers. Keep bags and freight controlled so they do not obstruct movement or change recorded mass after weighing. Refer loading suitability and unusual items to authorized personnel.

Recognize possible dangerous goods and stay within assigned function-based preparation. Hold uncertain items, protect people and seek authorized decisions; do not invent capacity, packaging or classification. A late item is not exempt because the return aircraft is waiting. Maintain the link between person, bag, destination and sector through additions, removals and diversions.

Worked and changed applications: Expected P1/P2/P3/P4, actual P1/P2/P3/P9: four people but the wrong identity. Hold and reconcile before movement. Changed case: a toolbox is added after weighing; verify and revise through the required process rather than accepting the unchanged total.

lessons.title: Q96-9 — Emergency preplanning and available capability
lessons.body:
## Q96-9 — Emergency preplanning and available capability

Before the visit, understand the credible helicopter and installation emergencies, alarms, escape routes, muster arrangements, casualty support and remote assistance. Identify what the installed automatic systems can do and what the visiting team is actually trained and equipped to do. An automatic system does not eliminate accountability, communication or evacuation duties.

Plan for blocked access, failed equipment, delayed external response and a team member becoming unavailable. Preserve a safe escape route and do not commit personnel to a task beyond available protection or competence. Emergency actions must follow the actual plan and crew/incident-command interfaces. A course can rehearse decisions, but cannot invent a rescue capability that the installation does not possess.

Worked and changed applications: The preplan assumes a four-person response team but only two appropriately trained people are available. Escalate the mismatch before accepting the plan. Changed case: an escape route becomes unavailable. Use the approved alternative and update accountability rather than sending people toward the original route by habit.

lessons.title: Q96-10 — Installed fire systems and limits of intervention
lessons.body:
## Q96-10 — Installed fire systems and limits of intervention

Know the location, indications, activation arrangements and authorized controls of the actual NUI fire-protection system. Understand its relationship to automatic detection and remote support. Do not memorize one generic control sequence for every installation. A reported activation does not prove the hazard is fully controlled; a fault or loss of coverage must be communicated.

Manual intervention, reset or isolation is permitted only under the approved procedure by authorized personnel. Never disable protection merely because activation seems inconvenient. Initial training uses an inert simulator to practice indication recognition, alarm, communication and authorized control decisions. Hands-on firefighting, breathing apparatus, entry or casualty rescue beyond the defined training requires separate competent facilities and qualification; this course does not silently grant them.

Worked and changed applications: The simulator shows an automatic activation while the condition remains uncertain. Raise the alarm, protect people and obtain the required status; do not reset to restore a green display. Changed case: the system reports a fault before movement. Apply the approved restriction/alternative process rather than claiming the team can replace missing protection with enthusiasm.

lessons.title: Q96-11 — Initial response, casualty information and evacuation
lessons.body:
## Q96-11 — Initial response, casualty information and evacuation

On recognizing an emergency, raise the alarm through the approved route, state location and known facts, protect people and initiate the preplanned actions within your role. Avoid unsupported diagnoses or casualty counts. Coordinate with flight crew, remote support and the responsible incident authority. Keep communications clear and preserve access for responders where safe.

Account for people by identity and last confirmed location. A duplicate name cannot offset a missing person. Use approved muster or evacuation arrangements and do not send an unprotected searcher into a hazardous area. Provide casualty information and assistance within training; medical treatment, rescue entry and aircraft-specific evacuation actions require the applicable competent direction. Reassess as conditions change rather than completing an obsolete plan.

Worked and changed applications: Roster has six people; muster sheet has six entries because one person is listed twice and another is absent. Report five unique accounted for and one missing, with last known information. Changed case: the missing person is later verified at an alternate safe location. Update the record with source/time; do not erase the earlier uncertainty.

lessons.title: Q96-12 — Final departure and return to unattended state
lessons.body:
## Q96-12 — Final departure and return to unattended state

The final departure has a special transition: the visiting team leaves and local human response may no longer be available. Follow the approved shutdown, equipment restoration, access, accountability and remote handover sequence. Confirm required automatic/remote protection remains in the specified state and record unresolved defects. Do not switch off a system merely because work is finished.

Reconcile all departing people and items, current manifest and crew interface. Verify no one is left unaccounted for and no tool or equipment remains in a prohibited location. Remote acknowledgment must reflect the actual unattended status, restrictions and follow-up. If the required state cannot be established, escalate through the authorized plan rather than falsely signing completion to catch the flight.

Worked and changed applications: The team is ready to leave but a protection-status field is unknown. Hold the handover decision and obtain authorized resolution; do not fill ready by default. Changed case: all people are accounted for but one tool is missing. Resolve its location safely before declaring the relevant area clear.

lessons.title: Q96-13 — Integrated initial assessment and development
lessons.body:
## Q96-13 — Integrated initial assessment and development

The learner must demonstrate a coherent visit from planning through first arrival, attended operations, abnormal condition, emergency response and final departure. The scenario must make responsibility transitions explicit and require the learner to preserve unresolved holds. Performance is judged on safe decisions, communication, accountability and accurate records, not on how quickly the mock aircraft leaves.

Initial completion requires instruction, corrected checks, applied tasks, observed simulated performance and the separate final. It does not establish independent workplace competence or external accreditation. Record prompting and remediate specific gaps before a changed independent assessment. Employer-led local training, experience and workplace assessment follow before appointment. Preserve source limitations and revisit the package when actual procedures or assigned roles change.

Worked and changed applications: A learner passes calculations but resets an uncertain fire indication without authority. Record critical failure and reassess changed system-control decisions after remediation. Changed case: a learner correctly holds departure because accountability is unresolved. Credit the safety decision; schedule pressure is not a reason to invent completion.


---

courses.title: VUC096 | VUC096 instructor guide, simulator exercises and records

content.title: VUC096 | VUC096 instructor guide, simulator exercises and records
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC096 instructor guide, simulator exercises and records
lessons.body: # VUC096 instructor guide, simulator exercises and records

lessons.title: Prerequisites and safe resources
lessons.body:
## Prerequisites and safe resources

Instructor must understand NUI helicopter operations, emergency planning and assessment; a competent safety controller supervises physical mock work. Verify function-appropriate DG preparation, jurisdiction-required radio qualification, fitness and the learner's intended duties. Actual appointment requires further local training, experience and workplace assessment. Do not use this course as a substitute for specialist weather, refuelling, firefighting, breathing-apparatus, rescue or medical qualifications.

F96 adaptation: duty holder/site/operator___ current manual and emergency plan___ first-arrival assurance___ remote/crew/local responsibilities___ required team and roles___ approved routes___ status systems/indications___ weather/source criteria___ installed protection and authorized controls___ communication/fallback___ rescue/support/contingencies___ final-departure state___ specialist boundaries___ instructor/safety controller/date___. Actual operational requirements must be supplied before delivery of site-specific instruction; synthetic cards below never authorize flight operations.

Use a ground-level mock layout, inert aircraft outline, marked prohibited zones, safe waiting/muster areas M1 and M2, soft route markers, harmless tagged bags/tools, isolated training radios, paper status panel, roleplayers and calculator. No aircraft movement, live rotor, real fuel, fire, smoke, dangerous goods, elevated edge, water immersion or operational alarm transmission is used. Casualties are cards or lightweight mannequins moved only under an approved safe manual-handling plan; no untrained carrying of people. A real hazard stops the exercise immediately. All messages begin with the agreed exercise identifier on non-operational channels.

lessons.title: N96 complete mock installation and visit
lessons.body:
## N96 complete mock installation and visit

NUI N96 is represented by a central aircraft outline D, waiting area W, route R1 to work area K, alternate route R2, muster M1, alternate M2 and remote controller C. Diagram distances and directions have no aircraft-operational meaning. Team: candidate HLO, three visiting workers V2/V3/V4, mock crew, remote controller and independent safety controller. The four-person exercise roster is not a prescribed real minimum. The local emergency card permits alarm, safe muster, communication and authorized inert-panel decisions; it prohibits hazardous-area entry and specialist intervention. No person is sent into a simulated hazard to create a rescue opportunity.

Cycle A: planned visit 10:00–12:00 UTC. Remote report at 09:45 is reviewed at 09:57; fictional maximum age eight minutes, so it is twelve minutes old. Required protection status is unknown. Candidate must obtain current approved information and resolve the unknown through the mock authorized process before treating readiness as established. Controller then supplies a valid 09:58 report at 10:00, including confirmed required fields and no faults. This is exercise permission to continue simulation only, not actual aviation authorization.

First arrival: crew roleplayer controls access. After safe establishment, the team discovers a paper contamination marker on R1 and a harmless loose strap near a prohibited zone. Both findings must be addressed separately and reported. A team member starts toward the strap; candidate prevents unsafe pursuit. The remote controller acknowledges the message but initially does not confirm action. Candidate must obtain the actual required status and establish attended responsibilities.

Passenger/item exercise: expected P1/P2/P3/P4; present P1/P2/P3/P9. Four bodies do not resolve P4 missing/P9 unmanifested. Weight worksheet, separately: people 80/85/90 kg, bags 7/8/9 kg, freight 26 kg, total 305 kg. Remove 85 kg person and 8 kg bag: 212 kg. Add 78 kg person and 6 kg bag: 296 kg. These are synthetic recorded inputs only, not aircraft performance approval. An unmarked-battery paper card remains held until the mock authorized decision; it is not silently included in accepted totals.

Emergency A: inert panel shows automatic activation; cause unknown. A roleplayer asks for reset to allow departure. Candidate alarms, protects people, communicates facts and preserves authorization boundaries. R1 is declared unavailable; approved safe mock route R2 leads to M2. Roster H1/V2/V3/V4, initial muster H1/V2/V2/V4: three unique, V3 missing. No improvised search is permitted. Controller later confirms V3 at M1, safe, at 10:20 UTC through named source C. Candidate updates four uniquely accounted for, records source/time and retains earlier uncertainty. Controller supplies authorized emergency status resolution only after required communication; learner must not invent it.

Final departure A: tool inventory T1/T2/T3, return list T1/T2. T3 location is unresolved until controller provides verified storage evidence. Required final protection status and remote acknowledgment are initially missing. Candidate resolves each, reconciles current persons/items and hands over the actual unattended state. Sending a message without acknowledgment does not meet the exercise's handover condition.

Cycle B changes the facts: report observed 13:55, reviewed 14:00, fictional maximum seven minutes; time passes but a sensor fault remains. Primary link fails; approved alternate requires tested relay and explicit remote receipt. Relay starts unavailable. Once restored, team identifies an emergency-preplan mismatch: four trained responders required by this fictional plan, only two available. Candidate escalates rather than claiming two can perform four roles. A paper alarm and blocked M1 route require safe alternate M2. Roster B1–B6, muster B1/B2/B3/B4/B5/B5: five unique, B6 missing. Later verified B6 at safe K resolves the count. Final departure has all tools but remote handover recipient holds an old status. Candidate provides current restrictions and obtains acknowledgment. No fabricated arrival, rescue time or restored protection is allowed.

lessons.title: Worked labs
lessons.body:
## Worked labs

### W96-1 — Phase responsibility and entry

Build F96 and a matrix for before arrival, first arrival, attended work, emergency and final departure. Model: remote/crew/local duties assigned explicitly; impossible pre-landing local inspection escalated. Changed: different operator system requires local preparation before appointment.

### W96-2 — Readiness and evidence

Apply A/B reports. Model: A 09:45 to 09:57 is twelve minutes, four beyond eight; replacement age two minutes with complete valid fields. B age five minutes meets seven but sensor fault fails validity. Changed: recent report with missing required field remains incomplete. Use actual approved criteria in workplace, never these fictional values.

### W96-3 — First arrival and hazards

Roleplay crew-controlled access, local discrepancy report and attended handover. Model: no unsafe inspection while aircraft access is restricted; strap and contamination resolved separately; remote receipt distinguished from completed action. Changed: route R1 closes, use only the approved safe alternative.

### W96-4 — People, items and scope

Resolve P4/P9 mismatch and show 80+85+90+7+8+9+26=305 kg; subtract 93 to obtain 212; add 84 to obtain 296. Model: identities, bags, counts and revision accompany arithmetic; DG hold remains outside unqualified acceptance. Changed: total unchanged after substitution still requires identity reconciliation.

### W96-5 — Emergency decisions and accountability

Run panel activation and muster A. Model: no unauthorized reset; alarm and safe M2 movement; three unique with V3 missing, then four after verified update. Changed B: five unique with B6 missing. No duplicate row offsets missing identity, and no unprotected search is created.

### W96-6 — Final departure and evidence

Reconcile tools, required protection state and remote handover. Model: T3 unresolved prevents relevant clearance; unknown protection remains a hold; current recipient acknowledgment required. Changed: tools resolved but recipient has old status. Resolve distribution separately. Write an initial-training outcome that does not claim workplace competence.

lessons.title: Individual observed stations
lessons.body:
## Individual observed stations

Thirteen stations. Safe physical mock tasks occur at 4, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12; six others use documents or review. Instruction and practice come before independent assessment. Record prompts and permit safe accommodations that preserve the assessed decision/skill.

### P96-1 — Role and prerequisites

Task: Verify assigned functions, preparation, fitness and initial-training limits.

Acceptance: No premature appointment or unsupported specialist claim.

### P96-2 — Operating concept

Acceptance: No impossible first-arrival task or unowned handover.

### P96-3 — Visit readiness

Acceptance: Missing conditions held and escalated.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-4 — Hazard control

Acceptance: Both object and contamination controls demonstrated.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-5 — Status and equipment

Task: Evaluate synthetic report age, fault flags and required fields.

Acceptance: No guessed reading, bypass or generic live limit.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-6 — First-arrival transition

Task: Roleplay crew-controlled arrival and establish attended duties.

Acceptance: Safe sequence and actual local discrepancies recorded.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-7 — Briefing and links

Task: Brief team and confirm communications/action completion.

Acceptance: Understanding and link conditions verified.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-8 — People and items

Task: Reconcile identities, safe bags and paper DG query.

Acceptance: Count alone not accepted; holds remain.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-9 — Emergency preplan

Task: Map resources, routes, accountability and remote support.

Acceptance: Capability mismatch and alternative route addressed.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-10 — System response

Task: Use inert indication/control simulator for activation and fault.

Acceptance: No unauthorized reset; alarm and approved authority preserved.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-11 — Emergency coordination

Task: Run alarm, muster, casualty-information and evacuation roleplay.

Acceptance: Unique identities, uncertainty and safe boundaries maintained.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-12 — Final departure

Task: Reconcile people/tools and transfer unattended status.

Acceptance: Required protection and remote acknowledgment established.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

### P96-13 — Integrated initial result

Task: Complete changed visit cycles and evidence review.

Acceptance: Independent safe performance; initial-only award.

Source/context___ Independent actions___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed evidence___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: I96 integrated initial assessment
lessons.body:
## I96 integrated initial assessment

Each learner leads both A and B through all visit phases; rotate supporting roleplayers without assigning candidate decisions to them. Controller releases only the specified facts, logs responses and avoids coaching. Safety controller can stop at any time. Both emergency exercises must include alarm, communication, safe movement/accountability and an authorized system-status decision. There is no live-fire or unrestricted rescue claim.

Thirteen dimensions match P96-1 through P96-13. Score 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major coaching, 2 safe incomplete/prompted, 3 independently acceptable, 4 accurate independent performance with explanation. Require at least 42/52 in each integrated cycle, every dimension at least 3, all stations passed and no critical error. Critical errors: false readiness, unsafe uncontrolled movement, unauthorized protection reset/isolation, unprotected improvised rescue, invented accountability or operational data, unsupported DG/specialist authority, or fabricated evidence. Retain failed attempts and use targeted practice followed by changed independent assessment. Safe holds receive credit even when they delay the exercise flight.

lessons.title: Forms, schedule and award
lessons.body:
## Forms, schedule and award

F96-P plan: phase___ responsible person___ required information/capability___ verified source/time___ missing condition/hold___ resolution___. F96-S status: location/time___ observed/remote source___ units/faults___ current restriction___ recipient/readback___. F96-A accountability: expected unique IDs___ verified location/source/time___ missing___ duplicate/unidentified___ update___. F96-E emergency: alarm/time___ known facts/unknowns___ safe route/muster___ resources/limits___ authorized instructions___ actions/results___ handover___. F96-D departure: persons/items/tools___ required protection state___ defects/follow-up___ remote acknowledgment___ current record___. F96-R remediation: failed control___ teaching/practice___ changed task___ result___ reviewer/appeal___. Keep sensitive workplace data in authorized systems; all course examples are synthetic.

Original 40-hour allocation: instruction 8, labs 6, stations 8, integrated simulations 10, final/feedback 4, preparation/debrief 4. Add practice where needed. Final has thirteen cases, 39 decisions, 78 points, 120 minutes; pass 63/78, at least 4/6 each domain and no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; protected keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B follows remediation. Practical failure requires practical reassessment.

Issue original VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Initial Training only after prerequisite/readiness verification, corrected checks, labs, all stations, both integrated cycles, final and competent review. Record version/hash, dates, assessor, simulated scope and limits. No OPITO certificate, workplace appointment, aircraft command, specialist refuelling, rescue or unrestricted firefighting authority is conferred. Local supervised development and workplace assessment follow. If a required control is unproven, record incomplete development rather than full completion.


---

lessons.title: VUC096 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC096 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q96-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-1-L1

Generic safety certificate appoints NUI HLO?

**Answer:** No; verify role-specific preparation and later workplace assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** Initial knowledge and appointment are distinct. Revisit Q96-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-1-L2

Staffed-deck experience transfers without review?

**Answer:** No; assess unattended transitions and local plan.

**Reason/remediation:** The support model changes. Revisit Q96-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-2-L1

Visiting team can inspect before its first landing?

**Answer:** Not by assumption; the approved operating concept must address first-arrival assurance.

**Reason/remediation:** An impossible task assignment is a planning gap. Revisit Q96-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-2-L2

Old checklist remains valid after a material revision?

**Answer:** No; apply current controlled procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Familiarity does not supersede revision control. Revisit Q96-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-3-L1

Green remote screen without source time proves readiness?

**Answer:** No; verify current source and required fields.

**Reason/remediation:** Missing data is not serviceability. Revisit Q96-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-3-L2

Return delayed: assume rescue arrives at course example time?

**Answer:** No; use actual approved contingency and confirmed support.

**Reason/remediation:** Synthetic timing is not a resource guarantee. Revisit Q96-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-4-L1

Dropped glove moves toward rotor hazard: retrieve immediately?

**Answer:** No; stop pursuit and arrange safe recovery.

**Reason/remediation:** Recovery must not create exposure. Revisit Q96-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-4-L2

Debris removed but route contaminated: ready?

**Answer:** No; resolve separate condition.

**Reason/remediation:** Partial correction is not full readiness. Revisit Q96-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-5-L1

10:00 report at 10:12 with fictional eight-minute maximum: age/result?

**Answer:** Twelve minutes, four too old under that exercise rule.

**Reason/remediation:** Use approved current information, not invented live limits. Revisit Q96-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-5-L2

Two-minute-old sensor-fault report is valid?

**Answer:** Not merely because recent; resolve fault or approved alternative.

**Reason/remediation:** Freshness and validity differ. Revisit Q96-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-6-L1

Stepping off aircraft automatically establishes attended readiness?

**Answer:** No; complete authorized transition and local checks.

**Reason/remediation:** Presence alone does not establish resources or duties. Revisit Q96-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-6-L2

Post-arrival defect contradicts remote report: ignore it?

**Answer:** No; report actual finding and restrict dependent activity.

**Reason/remediation:** New evidence changes readiness. Revisit Q96-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-7-L1

Acknowledgment means action complete?

**Answer:** No; confirm actual required state.

**Reason/remediation:** Receipt and completion differ. Revisit Q96-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-7-L2

Team member does not know muster location: proceed?

**Answer:** No; rebrief and confirm understanding.

**Reason/remediation:** Emergency roles must be shared before dispersal. Revisit Q96-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-8-L1

Four expected and four present with one wrong ID: pass?

**Answer:** No; reconcile identities and manifest.

**Reason/remediation:** Count alone hides substitution. Revisit Q96-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-8-L2

Late toolbox after weighing: retain old total?

**Answer:** No; verify changed input and revise through acceptance.

**Reason/remediation:** The old measurement no longer represents the item. Revisit Q96-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-9-L1

Four-person plan with two trained people available: acceptable?

**Answer:** Not without authorized resolution of capability mismatch.

**Reason/remediation:** A paper plan cannot create resources. Revisit Q96-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-9-L2

Automatic protection removes need for muster?

**Answer:** No; accountability and communications remain.

**Reason/remediation:** Equipment response does not account for people. Revisit Q96-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-10-L1

Uncertain activation: reset to green?

**Answer:** No; follow authorized procedure and establish conditions.

**Reason/remediation:** Reset may remove needed protection. Revisit Q96-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-10-L2

This course grants BA entry and rescue authority?

**Answer:** No; separate qualification and capability are required.

**Reason/remediation:** Simulated coordination is not unrestricted intervention competence. Revisit Q96-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-11-L1

Six entries with one duplicate and one missing: all accounted?

**Answer:** No; five unique accounted for, one missing.

**Reason/remediation:** Entry count is not identity reconciliation. Revisit Q96-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-11-L2

Missing person later verified safe: what record?

**Answer:** Update identity, location, source and time while retaining history.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence resolves uncertainty without erasing it. Revisit Q96-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-12-L1

Unknown protection state at departure: fill ready?

**Answer:** No; resolve through authorized process.

**Reason/remediation:** Final departure removes local support. Revisit Q96-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-12-L2

All people found but tool missing: ignore?

**Answer:** No; resolve safely before relevant clearance.

**Reason/remediation:** People and equipment checks are separate. Revisit Q96-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-13-L1
lessons.body:
## Q96-13-L1

Written pass offsets unauthorized reset?

**Answer:** No; critical practical failure requires remediation and changed assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** Mandatory controls cannot be averaged away. Revisit Q96-13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q96-13-L2
lessons.body:
## Q96-13-L2

Correct hold delays mock flight: fail learner?

**Answer:** No; credit safe decision and assess remaining requirements.

**Reason/remediation:** Speed is subordinate to valid controls. Revisit Q96-13 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Coverage trace
lessons.body:
## Coverage trace

Thirteen chapters map one-to-one to thirteen stations, 26 explained checks, thirteen separate final cases and thirteen changed retakes. Six labs apply phase ownership, readiness, first arrival, people/items, emergency accountability and final handover. Both I96 cycles include full visit transitions and changed emergency decisions. F96 forms retain plan, status, accountability, emergency, departure and remediation evidence. Seven stations involve safe physical mock activities; six are observed review tasks. No actual learner achievement is claimed by authoring the materials.

lessons.title: Limits and maintenance
lessons.body:
## Limits and maintenance

Verify current local manual, duty-holder responsibilities, aircraft/operator interfaces, DG and radio prerequisites, installed protection, approved alternatives and emergency plan before delivery. Confirm instructor and safety-controller competence. All numerical limits, people, timings and scenarios are synthetic. No live aircraft, fuel, fire or hazardous rescue is created. Workplace assessment and employer appointment remain subsequent requirements. Reassess affected content when procedures, equipment or assigned functions change; preserve previous evidence and recorded restrictions.

content.title: VUC097 | VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Further Training
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Further Training
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Further Training

VUC097. Original available-source refresher for previously prepared personnel. Focus: changed procedures and emergency skills rarely practiced at work. No external renewal, workplace appointment or unrestricted specialist authority is conferred.

lessons.title: Q97-1 — Further-training entry and performance review
lessons.body:
## Q97-1 — Further-training entry and performance review

Further training refreshes established NUI HLO preparation and exercises events rarely encountered in normal work. It is not an accelerated initial course for an unprepared learner. Verify the relevant initial/further history, current role and local competence arrangements before entry. Review recent practice, incidents, near misses and individual gaps without treating years of service as proof that emergency skills remain current.

Agree the functions to be refreshed and the limits of the outcome. Current DG, radio, weather, refuelling and other specialist preparation remain separately governed. Check fitness for the planned safe simulations. A candidate who lacks the prerequisite foundation needs appropriate development rather than an unsupported renewal label. Record independent performance, prompts and remediation; attendance alone is not the outcome.

Worked and changed applications: A candidate has current routine work but has never practiced loss of remote support. Include that gap in assessed simulation. Changed case: the prior certificate cannot be authenticated. Verify it through the authorized process; do not issue a further-training outcome based on an unverified photograph.

lessons.title: Q97-2 — Change review and replacing outdated habits
lessons.body:
## Q97-2 — Change review and replacing outdated habits

Compare the current controlled manual, emergency plan, equipment arrangements and communications with those used at the learner’s last training. Record what changed, its operational consequence and the required action. Updates may affect role boundaries, equipment alternatives, status reporting or final-departure handover. Do not merely list new document titles; teach how a changed control alters decisions.

The current CAP 437 amendment includes a structured equipment-unserviceability reference, but local application still requires its actual conditions and authority. A newly documented alternative is not automatic permission to operate with any defect. Verify the applicable current revision and local procedure. Use a change register linking old practice, new requirement, affected roles and demonstrated understanding. Never invent a regulatory change to make a refresher appear current.

Worked and changed applications: Old practice treated a sent status message as completed handover; the current local exercise procedure requires acknowledged receipt. Demonstrate the new confirmation step. Changed case: a colleague insists the old shortcut worked last year. Explain and apply the current controlled requirement, then record the learning gap.

lessons.title: Q97-3 — Reassessing the NUI operating concept
lessons.body:
## Q97-3 — Reassessing the NUI operating concept

Revisit the responsibilities before first arrival, during occupancy and at final departure. Ask which capabilities are automatic, remote or dependent on visiting personnel, and how their availability is established. A staffed-installation assumption can creep into routine NUI work: someone imagines a resident team will handle a defect or account for a missing person. Expose those assumptions during planning.

Evaluate changes in visit duration, staffing, work scope and external support. If the planned resource or route no longer exists, the old plan is not adequate simply because the flight is booked. Define the hold, escalation owner and evidence needed to resume. A refresher should require the learner to explain how a changed operating concept affects both normal and emergency phases, not merely recite a checklist.

Worked and changed applications: The return flight is delayed while the planned remote support shift ends. Confirm replacement coverage and actual contingency arrangements rather than assuming the old contact remains available. Changed case: one trained team member is unavailable; reassess assigned duties and emergency capability before proceeding.

lessons.title: Q97-4 — Information quality under degraded conditions
lessons.body:
## Q97-4 — Information quality under degraded conditions

Experienced personnel may trust familiar dashboards too readily. Distinguish a current valid reading from stale data, a frozen display, a fault flag or a missing required field. Report source, time, units and uncertainty. A recent timestamp does not establish validity if the sensor is faulty, and absence of an alarm does not prove protection is available.

Use approved alternatives only with every required condition satisfied. If an alternate communication or measurement path fails, reassess the operating status immediately. Do not average conflicting safety-critical reports to produce a reassuring number. Determine the authoritative source and notify responsible parties. Assessment should challenge the learner with multiple individually plausible records and require a traceable decision.

Worked and changed applications: A display refreshed at 11:00 shows a measurement last captured at 10:40. At 11:03 the measurement is 23 minutes old, not three. Changed case: the alternative report is current but its location is wrong. Reject its use for the intended site and obtain appropriate information or preserve the restriction.

lessons.title: Q97-5 — Team leadership and closed-loop communication
lessons.body:
## Q97-5 — Team leadership and closed-loop communication

Refresh clear task allocation, briefing and confirmation under time pressure. State who owns each action and what completed status must be reported. Acknowledgment that a message was heard is not evidence that a valve, route, roster or remote action is in the required state. Invite challenge and keep unresolved conditions visible rather than allowing confidence or seniority to silence concerns.

During communication loss, follow the approved fallback and its limits. Do not combine fragments from different channels into an assumed instruction. A readback that changes the location or action needs correction before execution. Maintain a concise event log and handover so incoming personnel can reconstruct actual status. The exercise should test both sending an accurate message and detecting an inaccurate response.

Worked and changed applications: HLO requests confirmation that route R2 is clear; reply says R1 clear. Correct the mismatch rather than treating any clear message as success. Changed case: relief staff accepts the handover but repeats the wrong manifest version. Resolve the version and confirm understanding.

lessons.title: Q97-6 — First arrival and normal-operation drift
lessons.body:
## Q97-6 — First arrival and normal-operation drift

Refresh the approved first-arrival transition and local establishment of duties. Routine familiarity can lead to premature movement, skipped inspection or retrospective checklist completion. Observe actual conditions when access is safe, compare them with remote information and communicate discrepancies. Do not let a successful landing be treated as proof that every ground control is in place.

Maintain aircraft-specific access controls, passenger identity and item reconciliation, briefing and crew interface during attended operations. A late change or dropped object can create a new hazard after earlier checks passed. The learner must stop and update rather than rely on momentum. Assessment should use safe mock conditions that challenge habits without exposing anyone to rotors, fuel or live aircraft movement.

Worked and changed applications: A familiar route is blocked after arrival. Use the approved alternative and rebrief, not memory. Changed case: the final headcount matches but an unfamiliar substitute is present. Resolve identity and current manifest; equal count is not enough.

lessons.title: Q97-7 — Emergency preplan refresh and resource decisions
lessons.body:
## Q97-7 — Emergency preplan refresh and resource decisions

Review credible events against actual available people, protection, routes, communications and outside support. Identify tasks the team can safely perform and tasks requiring specialist resources. An emergency plan must remain achievable if a team member becomes a casualty or a route closes. Do not assign one person simultaneously to incompatible duties simply to make the staffing table balance.

Prioritize alarm, protection of people, accountability and appropriate support within the actual plan. Reassess when the situation changes. A preplanned action may become unsafe after loss of protection or blocked access. Maintain a route out and refuse unsupported entry or rescue demands. Refreshing rarely practiced skills means testing these decisions, not creating a more hazardous exercise.

Worked and changed applications: Plan assigns the same person to remote communications and a task that prevents them communicating. Identify the conflict and obtain an authorized revised arrangement. Changed case: external support estimate increases; maintain the approved safe contingency rather than attempting an untrained rescue to meet the earlier estimate.

lessons.title: Q97-8 — Protection-system failure and authorized intervention
lessons.body:
## Q97-8 — Protection-system failure and authorized intervention

Know the current installed-system indications and approved response to activation, fault and loss of remote control. The objective is to manage the condition within authority, not to make every display green. A stopped discharge or cleared alarm does not necessarily establish that the hazard is gone. Confirm actual status through the responsible process.

Do not reset, isolate or bypass protection without the required authority and verified conditions. An approved alternative remains valid only while all its conditions hold. If a conditional relay or resource fails, withdraw the assumed capability and update restrictions. Simulated control panels allow safe practice of these decisions; they do not qualify maintenance or unrestricted firefighting.

Worked and changed applications: Remote support authorizes a specific action only after condition C is confirmed, but C remains unknown. Do not execute early. Changed case: the alternative initially works and then its link fails. Reassess immediately rather than continuing under the old approval.

lessons.title: Q97-9 — Emergency command interface and evolving response
lessons.body:
## Q97-9 — Emergency command interface and evolving response

Refresh the transition from normal operations to the approved emergency structure. Send a clear initial report with location, event, people at risk, known restrictions and assistance needed. Keep facts separate from estimates. Coordinate with flight crew, remote support and the responsible incident authority; do not assume the HLO role includes all command or technical decisions.

Update priorities as routes, capability and casualty information change. Give concise task instructions, obtain confirmation and monitor effects. Avoid tunnel vision on equipment while people remain unaccounted for. If an instruction would exceed trained capability or contradict a known safety condition, clarify and escalate. The exercise should reward safe challenge and accurate uncertainty, not a theatrical rapid response.

Worked and changed applications: A controller asks for a casualty number before identities are reconciled. Report confirmed information and the unknowns, then update. Changed case: a previously safe route becomes blocked. Redirect through the approved alternative and confirm the team received the change.

lessons.title: Q97-10 — Accountability, casualty support and evacuation
lessons.body:
## Q97-10 — Accountability, casualty support and evacuation

Reconcile expected identities with verified safe locations, not raw tally marks. Track visitors, crew interfaces and any person moved for assistance. A duplicate entry cannot compensate for someone missing. Report last confirmed information to the authorized response process and do not initiate unprotected searches. Preserve the history of uncertainty and later verification.

Provide assistance within actual training and resources; medical treatment, hazardous entry and aircraft evacuation require the applicable competent direction. Use preplanned safe routes and muster or evacuation arrangements. A support delay does not create new rescue competence. In exercises, casualty cards and safe roleplay test communication and prioritization without real hazardous movement or untrained lifting.

Worked and changed applications: Expected eight people; muster has eight entries but two are duplicates, leaving six unique and two missing. State both missing identities and seek verified information. Changed case: one is confirmed at an alternate safe point; update to seven accounted for and one missing, not all clear.

lessons.title: Q97-11 — Final departure, recovery and handover after disruption
lessons.body:
## Q97-11 — Final departure, recovery and handover after disruption

After an abnormal event, final departure requires more than the ordinary checklist. Establish the current protection state, unresolved defects, people/items, records and remote ownership of follow-up. Do not leave a system disabled or an unresolved restriction unreported because the aircraft is waiting. Restoration must be verified within the approved process.

Handover should include what happened, what is confirmed now, what remains unknown, controls in effect and the responsible next owner. Confirm receipt and understanding of the current revision. Preserve event records and failed or superseded information for review. A later correction must not erase evidence of the original condition. If required unattended status cannot be achieved, escalate through the actual contingency rather than sign a false completion.

Worked and changed applications: All people are ready but a protection isolation remains open. Obtain authorized resolution and handover before declaring the required state. Changed case: remote staff acknowledges an obsolete status. Correct the version and confirm current restrictions, not just successful message delivery.

lessons.title: Q97-12 — Independent refresher evidence and continued development
lessons.body:
## Q97-12 — Independent refresher evidence and continued development

Further-training completion requires current knowledge and independent performance in changed, rarely practiced conditions. Do not reuse an earlier initial-course score as proof of today’s skill. Record prompts, missed controls and how the learner handled new information. A critical unsafe or dishonest action prevents a pass even if most routine tasks are fluent.

Use targeted remediation followed by a changed independent scenario, retaining the first result. The original VNDRLY outcome records refresher scope and does not renew an OPITO certificate or replace workplace competence assessment and employer appointment. Identify local follow-up and changes requiring additional preparation. An effective debrief produces specific actions with owners and verification, not merely a statement that communication should improve.

Worked and changed applications: The learner performs routine checks smoothly but invents a missing-person location. Record critical failure and reassess evidence-based accountability after practice. Changed case: learner correctly preserves a hold under pressure. Credit that decision and assess the remaining domains; delay alone is not failure.


---

lessons.title: VUC097 refresher instructor and simulation workbook
lessons.body: # VUC097 refresher instructor and simulation workbook

lessons.title: Entry, update review and safe delivery
lessons.body:
## Entry, update review and safe delivery

Verify authenticated relevant initial/further preparation, current role, specialist qualifications as applicable, fitness and local competence arrangements. Instructor must understand NUI operations, emergency planning and assessment; independent safety controller supervises mock exercises. A missing foundation requires appropriate initial development, not a shortened refresher pass. The original package does not renew an external certificate.

F97 context: learner/prior evidence___ current site/operator/function___ manual/emergency-plan revisions___ changes since last preparation___ recent practice/gaps___ DG/radio/weather/refuelling boundaries___ fitness___ installed protection and authorized controls___ remote support/fallback___ routes/muster___ review owner/date___. Current approved local documents define actual operations. The update register records old control, current control, source/revision, reason, affected role and demonstrated action. Use real verified changes; do not fabricate changes to legislation.

Resources: ground-level mock NUI layout, inert aircraft outline, prohibited-area markers, safe routes R1/R2, muster M1/M2, paper protection panel, harmless items, isolated training radios, controller cards, calculator, evidence forms and protected exams. No live aircraft, fuel, fire, smoke, hazardous materials, operational alarm transmission, elevated edge, water exposure or hazardous rescue. Casualty information uses cards; no untrained lifting of people. Safety controller checks layout and stops on any real risk. Explain the exercise stop signal, welfare and accommodations before practice.

lessons.title: U97 update cards
lessons.body:
## U97 update cards

U1 is a fictional local procedural change: old process recorded message sent, current process requires named recipient acknowledgment of the current revision. U2: old mock route R1 is unavailable during work; approved current route is R2. U3: an approved alternative link requires tested relay plus confirmation by remote controller; a document listing the relay does not establish availability. These cards teach change application and are not claims that every operator adopted these changes. Separately discuss the verified current CAP 437 amendment and require local applicability review rather than copying a generic waiver.

lessons.title: N97 complete changed scenarios
lessons.body:
## N97 complete changed scenarios

Cycle A: visit planned 11:00–13:00 UTC, now delayed to 15:00. Remote contact changes at 14:00. Team role plan names H1, V2, V3 and V4; V4 becomes unavailable before the exercise starts. Candidate must confirm replacement support and an achievable authorized team/contingency plan, not pretend four people remain. Controller can supply an approved revised exercise plan only after the gap is reported. No actual staffing minimum is established by this dataset.

Information card A: display refresh 11:00, measurement captured 10:40, current 11:03. Sample age 23 minutes. Fictional maximum valid sample age ten minutes, so it exceeds by thirteen. Alternate report is for NUI Z rather than intended NUI Y. Candidate must reject both as sufficient current status for Y. Controller later supplies valid Y report at 11:05 reviewed at 11:07, with required fields and no faults. This permits simulation continuation only, not real flight authorization.

Mock arrival: approved current route R2; roleplayer replies R1 clear. Candidate must correct the readback and brief all affected participants. Manifest v 4 is current; relief repeats v 3. Outbound expected P1–P6, present P1–P5 and P9. Correct count six but P6 missing/P9 unmanifested. Resolve identities and current revision before movement. A harmless object appears near a prohibited zone after readiness; control access and arrange safe recovery, not pursuit.

Emergency A: inert panel shows activation; remote instruction allows a specified simulated action only after condition C is verified. C initially unknown. Primary communication fails; alternative relay is listed but untested. Candidate must preserve conditions, establish approved communication or hold/escalate, and avoid reset. Controller later verifies C and relay; after an authorized simulated action, hazard status remains unknown until further information. Do not infer all-clear from action completion.

Roster A: A1–A8. Initial muster A1/A2/A3/A4/A5/A6/A5/A6, eight entries but six unique; A7/A8 missing. Controller verifies A7 at safe K at 11:22, giving seven accounted for and A8 missing. Later A8 is confirmed at M2 by named controller C at 11:26, giving eight. Preserve all source/time updates. No unprotected search is allowed. During response R1 is declared blocked; use approved R2/M2 and confirm the changed instruction reached everyone.

Final A: an authorized protection isolation remains unresolved, and remote recipient holds old status v 2 while v 3 records the current restriction. Candidate must obtain authorized restoration/status resolution and acknowledged current handover. An aircraft waiting is not permission to sign false unattended readiness. Retain event and correction history.

Cycle B: measurement 13:02, current 13:07, correct site, but sensor fault active; fictional time maximum seven minutes. Time passes, validity does not. Remote support is available, but the plan assigns one person both continuous communications and an incompatible physical task. Candidate must resolve that conflict. A valid alternative link is established and then fails during the emergency; its prior acceptance no longer applies. Controller supplies evolving casualty information and a second route change. Roster B1–B7, initial muster B1/B2/B3/B4/B4/B5/B6: six unique, B7 missing. B7 later verified safe at M1 at 13:20. Final status is restored, but recipient repeats an old revision; candidate must correct and confirm. Different facts require fresh decisions, not replay of cycle A answers.

lessons.title: Applied labs
lessons.body:
## Applied labs

### W97-1 — Entry and change application

Build F97 and U97 register. Model: authenticated foundation, actual gap review, old/current controls and demonstrated changed action. Changed: prior certificate valid but duties expanded. Require added function evidence rather than treating refresher as universal authorization.

### W97-2 — Information and support

Compute sample ages and separate source validity. Model: A 23 minutes, thirteen beyond fictional ten; replacement two minutes and valid. B five minutes within seven but fault invalidates sufficiency. Confirm remote shift handover and changed team plan. Changed: fresh report for wrong site remains unsuitable.

### W97-3 — Communication and habit

Roleplay R2 request/R1 response, v 4/v 3 mismatch and late object. Model: correct exact instruction, confirm all participants, update readiness and recover safely. Changed: correct readback from one member does not prove absent member received it.

### W97-4 — Conditional systems and emergency plan

Apply C and relay conditions, then loss of relay after establishment. Model: no premature action, no continued reliance on failed alternative, clear restrictions and approved escalation. Changed: authorized action completes but hazard status unknown; do not announce all-clear.

### W97-5 — Accountability and route change

Reconcile A roster: six unique/two missing, then seven/one, then eight/none using verified sources. B: six unique/one missing, then seven/none. Model: retain history and safe-response limits. Changed: count entries equals expected but duplicates remain; identity set controls the conclusion.

### W97-6 — Recovery and final decision

Resolve isolation, current revision and remote handover separately. Model: restoration evidence plus accurate acknowledgment, not merely a sent message. Write a specific development action from a failed control. Changed: written pass with fabricated location remains critical failure and requires changed independent assessment.

lessons.title: Individual stations
lessons.body:
## Individual stations

Twelve observed stations. Physical safe mock activities occur at 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11; six others are review tasks. Practice and feedback precede assessment. Record prompts and individual decisions; team success alone cannot prove the candidate's competence.

### P97-1 — Entry and gap review

Task: Authenticate prior preparation and identify rare-skill gaps.

Acceptance: Further training not substituted for initial foundation.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-2 — Change register

Task: Compare controlled old/current procedures and demonstrate changed action.

Acceptance: Actual change understood, no invented regulatory claim.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-3 — Operating concept

Task: Replan delayed visit with support changeover and missing member.

Acceptance: Responsibilities and contingencies remain achievable.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-4 — Information validity

Task: Evaluate sample time, display time, location, units and faults.

Acceptance: No stale/wrong-site data treated as valid.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-5 — Closed-loop leadership

Task: Correct route/version readback and brief all affected people.

Acceptance: Receipt and correct completion distinguished.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-6 — Normal-operation drift

Task: Control safe mock arrival, changed route and passenger discrepancy.

Acceptance: Current conditions govern, not habit.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-7 — Emergency resources

Task: Resolve incompatible duties and unavailable protection.

Acceptance: No unsupported rescue or paper-only capability.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-8 — System conditions

Task: Use inert panel to manage conditional action and failed relay.

Acceptance: Prerequisites verified; no unauthorized reset.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-9 — Evolving response

Task: Lead alarm, report and revised-route roleplay.

Acceptance: Facts/unknowns clear and team updated.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-10 — Accountability

Task: Reconcile duplicate/missing identities and verified later updates.

Acceptance: No false all-clear or unsafe search.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-11 — Recovery/handover

Task: Resolve isolation and current-status transfer before departure.

Acceptance: Restoration and acknowledgment supported by evidence.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P97-12 — Independent outcome

Task: Review gaps, changed performance and scope.

Acceptance: Critical failures not averaged away; original refresher only.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: I97 independent further-training assessment
lessons.body:
## I97 independent further-training assessment

Each candidate leads both complete cycles, including changed emergency phases. Controller releases facts at their stated point, records actions and avoids coaching. All required communication, system-condition, accountability and final-handover controls must be demonstrated. No live-fire or hazardous rescue capability is claimed from these simulations.

Twelve dimensions match the stations. Score 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major coaching, 2 safe incomplete/prompted, 3 independently acceptable, 4 accurate independent performance with explanation. Require at least 39/48 in each cycle, every dimension at least 3, all stations passed and no critical error. Critical: false readiness, invented location/event, unsafe uncontrolled movement, unauthorized reset/isolation, unsupported rescue or DG authority, or fabricated evidence. Preserve failed attempts, teach/practice the gap, then use changed independent reassessment. Correct holds are credited despite delay.

lessons.title: Forms, timing and outcome
lessons.body:
## Forms, timing and outcome

F97-C change register: old/current control___ source/revision___ affected function___ required action___ demonstrated understanding___. F97-P plan: phase/owner___ actual capability___ gap/hold___ authorized resolution___. F97-I information: site___ sample/display/current times___ units/faults___ validity decision___ recipient___. F97-A accountability: expected IDs___ verified location/source/time___ missing/duplicate___ update___. F97-E event: time___ fact/unknown___ instruction/condition___ action/result___ route/team confirmation___. F97-H handover: current revision/status___ restored capability___ remaining restriction___ owner/acknowledgment___. F97-R development: failed control___ practice___ changed result___ follow-up owner/date___ reviewer/appeal___. Protect actual operational information; examples are synthetic.

Original 32-hour allocation: update instruction 6, labs 6, stations 6, integrated scenarios 8, final/feedback 4, preparation/debrief 2. Add time for unresolved gaps. Final: twelve cases, 36 decisions, 72 points, 120 minutes; pass 58/72, at least 4/6 per domain, no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; protected keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B follows remediation. Practical failure requires practical reassessment.

Issue original VNDRLY/U HLO for Normally Unattended Installations — Further Training only after entry/readiness verification, update work, corrected checks, labs, all stations, both integrated cycles, final and competent review. Record version/hash, dates, assessor, simulated refresher scope and local follow-up. It does not renew OPITO certification, replace workplace assessment or appoint the learner. Specialist qualifications and current employer competence controls remain separate. An unproven mandatory control means incomplete further training, not an unconditional certificate.


---
