lessons.title: VUC097 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC097 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q97-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-1-L1

Further training can replace missing initial preparation?

**Answer:** No; verify foundation and provide appropriate development.

**Reason/remediation:** Refresher assumes established role preparation. Revisit Q97-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-1-L2

Years of routine work prove rare emergency skill?

**Answer:** No; assess current independent performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Frequency of service is not evidence of every skill. Revisit Q97-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-2-L1

New document title alone proves update understood?

**Answer:** No; explain and demonstrate changed decisions.

**Reason/remediation:** Change review must affect practice. Revisit Q97-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-2-L2

Conditional equipment alternative means all defects permitted?

**Answer:** No; verify exact conditions and authority.

**Reason/remediation:** A conditional provision is not a blanket waiver. Revisit Q97-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-3-L1

Remote support shift ends during delayed visit: assume coverage?

**Answer:** No; confirm replacement and contingency.

**Reason/remediation:** Support availability changes with time. Revisit Q97-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-3-L2

One member unavailable: keep old duty allocation?

**Answer:** No; reassess capability and incompatible tasks.

**Reason/remediation:** A plan must be achievable with actual resources. Revisit Q97-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-4-L1

Display refreshed 11:00, sample 10:40, current 11:03: sample age?

**Answer:** 23 minutes.

**Reason/remediation:** Display refresh is not measurement time. Revisit Q97-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-4-L2

Current report for another location is usable?

**Answer:** No; obtain appropriate site information.

**Reason/remediation:** Correct time does not cure wrong context. Revisit Q97-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-5-L1

R2 requested, R1 confirmed: proceed?

**Answer:** No; resolve route mismatch.

**Reason/remediation:** Readback must match the required action. Revisit Q97-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-5-L2

Handover repeats wrong version: completed?

**Answer:** No; correct and reconfirm.

**Reason/remediation:** Receipt without understanding is insufficient. Revisit Q97-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-6-L1

Successful landing proves local readiness?

**Answer:** No; complete authorized transition and checks.

**Reason/remediation:** Aircraft outcome does not establish every ground control. Revisit Q97-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-6-L2

Headcount matches with substitute: accept?

**Answer:** No; reconcile identities/current manifest.

**Reason/remediation:** Count and identity are separate. Revisit Q97-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-7-L1

One person assigned incompatible simultaneous duties: adequate plan?

**Answer:** No; resolve resource conflict.

**Reason/remediation:** A staffing table cannot create simultaneous capability. Revisit Q97-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-7-L2

Support delayed: attempt untrained rescue?

**Answer:** No; maintain approved safe contingency and escalate.

**Reason/remediation:** Delay does not expand competence. Revisit Q97-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-8-L1

Conditional authorization before condition verified: execute?

**Answer:** No; establish required condition first.

**Reason/remediation:** A prerequisite is not optional. Revisit Q97-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-8-L2

Alternative link fails after approval: continue?

**Answer:** No; reassess capability and restrictions.

**Reason/remediation:** Approval depends on continuing conditions. Revisit Q97-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-9-L1

Unknown casualty count: invent plausible number?

**Answer:** No; report confirmed facts and uncertainty.

**Reason/remediation:** False precision misdirects response. Revisit Q97-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-9-L2

Route changes: tell only one member?

**Answer:** No; confirm affected team receives revised instruction.

**Reason/remediation:** Shared situational awareness must stay current. Revisit Q97-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-10-L1

Eight entries, two duplicates: unique count?

**Answer:** Six, leaving two missing if eight expected.

**Reason/remediation:** Duplicates cannot replace identities. Revisit Q97-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-10-L2

One of two missing confirmed safe: all clear?

**Answer:** No; seven accounted for, one still missing.

**Reason/remediation:** Partial resolution remains partial. Revisit Q97-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-11-L1

Departure ready but protection isolation unresolved: sign complete?

**Answer:** No; obtain authorized resolution and handover.

**Reason/remediation:** Final departure removes local support. Revisit Q97-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-11-L2

Correcting a record means erase old event?

**Answer:** No; preserve audit history.

**Reason/remediation:** Traceable correction is different from concealment. Revisit Q97-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q97-12-L1

Initial score can be reused as current refresher pass?

**Answer:** No; assess changed independent performance now.

**Reason/remediation:** Historical evidence does not prove current rare skills. Revisit Q97-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q97-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q97-12-L2

Correct hold under pressure is failure due delay?

**Answer:** No; credit safe control.

**Reason/remediation:** Schedule is not the safety criterion. Revisit Q97-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Assessment trace
lessons.body:
## Assessment trace

Twelve chapters have 24 explained formative checks, twelve matching stations, twelve protected three-decision final cases and twelve changed retakes. Six labs apply change review, information quality, communications, conditional protection, accountability and recovery. I97 requires both complete changed visit/emergency cycles. Six stations use safe physical mock activity and six observed review. Forms preserve individual evidence, prompting, critical failures and changed remediation.

lessons.title: Maintenance and limits
lessons.body:
## Maintenance and limits

Before delivery verify current manuals, actual changes since prior training, installed systems, approved alternatives, local emergency plan and specialist prerequisites. Record sources and revisions. Do not invent new legal requirements or use synthetic report-age values as live limits. No live hazard or operational record change is required. Authored materials do not prove learner performance. External certification, workplace competence and employer appointment remain distinct; retain limitations and assess changed duties separately.

courses.title: VUC098 | VNDRLY/U NUI HLO / Helicopter Emergency Response Team Leader — Workplace Competence

content.title: VUC098 | VNDRLY/U NUI HLO / Helicopter Emergency Response Team Leader — Workplace Competence
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VNDRLY/U NUI HLO / Helicopter Emergency Response Team Leader — Workplace Competence
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U NUI HLO / Helicopter Emergency Response Team Leader — Workplace Competence

VUC098. Original available-source combined-role assessment materials. Actual workplace evidence and local emergency capability govern the outcome. No external accreditation, aircraft authority or specialist refuelling/rescue qualification is conferred.

lessons.title: Q98-1 — Defining the combined workplace role
lessons.body:
## Q98-1 — Defining the combined workplace role

Define precisely which HLO and emergency-team-leader duties the employer assigns on the NUI or not-permanently-attended installation. The title does not automatically grant every aviation, rescue or maintenance function. Establish the normal operating cycle, the emergency command interface and the limits of the team’s actual capability. Separate specialist helicopter refuelling training and assessment remain necessary where that work is assigned.

Review initial preparation, supervised workplace development, fitness and relevant specialist evidence before practical assessment. The public external scheme has its own entry wording; this original package still requires safe readiness. The assessor must be competent in the actual role and local procedures, and must not assess tasks that neither the candidate nor the assessor is authorized to perform. An award is a reasoned evidence decision, not an assumption based on job title.

Worked and changed applications: A candidate is competent in normal HLO routines but has no evidence for the assigned emergency-leadership duties. Do not label the combined role complete. Changed case: refuelling is added to the job description. Require separate specialist preparation and evidence rather than treating the combined title as coverage.

lessons.title: Q98-2 — Assessment plan and authentic workplace evidence
lessons.body:
## Q98-2 — Assessment plan and authentic workplace evidence

Map each duty to direct observation, authenticated work products, questioning and safe scenario evidence. Record the site, operator, equipment, procedure revision and candidate contribution. Two independent routine workplace cycles are required by this original package, alongside local emergency exercises and changed-condition assessment. A generic witness signature without task, date or independent action is insufficient.

Rare emergencies should be assessed through approved safe drills or simulation, not by creating real failures. Label simulation honestly and identify its limits. Normal workplace evidence must come from actual authorized operations; a desktop exercise cannot be relabeled as a real flight cycle. Preserve privacy using secure references or redacted records. A reviewer checks sufficiency, consistency and any conflict of interest before the outcome.

Worked and changed applications: A portfolio contains team photographs and old checklists but no attribution. Authenticate specific actions and observe the candidate independently. Changed case: one cycle was heavily prompted. Record it as development and obtain a changed independent observation rather than hiding the assistance.

lessons.title: Q98-3 — Local operating concept and transition ownership
lessons.body:
## Q98-3 — Local operating concept and transition ownership

The NUI operating concept must cover first arrival, attended work and final departure, with clear remote, crew and visiting-team responsibilities. Verify current local procedures and restrictions. An assessment should require the candidate to trace who supplies status, who accepts handover and what happens when information or capability is missing. Do not invent a resident team during unattended phases.

Check that the plan remains achievable with actual staffing, communications, installed protection and external support. If the visiting team is expected to inspect before it can arrive, identify the impossible sequence and seek authorized resolution. If the final remote recipient is unavailable, the handover requirement remains unresolved. Competence includes recognizing a broken plan and preserving a hold, not merely completing its form.

Worked and changed applications: Remote support assumes the HLO is already on site during the first landing. Correct the responsibility gap through the approved operating concept. Changed case: the return flight is delayed into a different support shift. Confirm continuity and current status before final handover.

lessons.title: Q98-4 — Readiness information and equipment conditions
lessons.body:
## Q98-4 — Readiness information and equipment conditions

Use current approved information on deck condition, aircraft interfaces, weather, motion where applicable, equipment and restrictions. Separate measurement time from display-refresh time and confirm location, units and fault status. A stale or wrong-site report is not repaired by a confident voice. The HLO supplies accurate local information; aircraft acceptance remains with the responsible operator and crew.

Apply unserviceability provisions only under their actual conditions, authority and notifications. A listed alternative must be established and remain available. If it fails, update restrictions immediately. Do not bypass a safety indication or invent a favorable reading to keep a flight moving. The assessor should trace source data and the candidate’s reasoning, including appropriate uncertainty and escalation.

Worked and changed applications: A display updates at 08:10 but the sample is from 07:45; at 08:15 the sample is thirty minutes old. Changed case: an approved relay alternative is established, then drops out. The earlier approval no longer proves required communication capability.

lessons.title: Q98-5 — Deck inspection and concurrent-work coordination
lessons.body:
## Q98-5 — Deck inspection and concurrent-work coordination

Observe systematic inspection when access is safe and authorized: loose objects, contamination, routes, required markings/equipment and current defects. Findings must have an owner, restriction and verified resolution. A ticked checklist without actual observation is not evidence. Never introduce a real foreign object or obstruction during live operations for assessment.

Coordinate cranes, work parties and other conflicting activities through approved controls. Distinguish receipt of a request from confirmation of the required actual state. A corrected crane condition does not resolve a separate blocked passenger route. The candidate must keep the current status coherent and communicate new hazards after readiness has been reported. Use safe mock injects for conditions that cannot be introduced operationally.

Worked and changed applications: Crane contact says message received, while movement continues. Obtain verified safe status before dependent readiness. Changed case: crane is secured but a route remains contaminated; preserve that separate hold and recheck correction.

lessons.title: Q98-6 — Team leadership and routine movement control
lessons.body:
## Q98-6 — Team leadership and routine movement control

Brief team roles, hazards, approved routes, communications, special passenger arrangements and stop criteria. Confirm understanding and current required staffing. Keep access controlled during arrival, disembarkation, loading, boarding and departure through the actual crew/HLO interface. Generic training diagrams do not establish a universal safe aircraft approach direction.

A competent leader notices when the plan is no longer shared. Ambiguous radio messages, changed routes or a team member who cannot repeat the task require correction. Do not proceed based on seniority or pressure. Observe how the candidate responds to a safety challenge and how instructions reach every affected person. The goal is safe coherent movement, not the shortest turnaround.

Worked and changed applications: The team is briefed on R1 but the approved route changes to R2. Rebrief and confirm before movement. Changed case: a passenger drops an object near a hazard area. Stop pursuit and arrange safe recovery rather than allowing an uncontrolled approach.

lessons.title: Q98-7 — Passenger, item and dangerous-goods reconciliation
lessons.body:
## Q98-7 — Passenger, item and dangerous-goods reconciliation

Confirm actual identities and current manifest, not just matching headcount. Reconcile removed or substituted passengers with their bags and destination. Late freight changes require verified data and authorized acceptance. The HLO coordinates the interface but does not independently approve aircraft mass/balance or accept dangerous goods beyond assigned competence.

Keep actual items controlled after weighing and match destination and sector. Recognize suspect items, preserve safe holds and use the authorized specialist route. Do not hide freight as baggage or guess battery capacity. Assess a changed identity/item case and require the candidate to explain how current information reaches crew and ground records. Arithmetic accuracy alone cannot resolve a wrong person or unaccepted item.

Worked and changed applications: Five people are expected and five present, but one ID differs. Hold and resolve identity/eligibility and current manifest. Changed case: a toolbox is added after weighing. Verify the changed input, revise records and obtain required acceptance; the earlier total is obsolete.

lessons.title: Q98-8 — Emergency preplan and actual team capability
lessons.body:
## Q98-8 — Emergency preplan and actual team capability

Review the local emergency plan against available people, installed protection, communications, escape routes and external support. Identify tasks requiring specialist competence and actions the visiting team can perform safely. A combined role title does not create breathing-apparatus, rescue or medical capability. Avoid assigning one person incompatible simultaneous duties.

Prepare for loss of a team member, blocked access, failed protection and delayed assistance. Establish stop/withdrawal criteria and the command interface. The assessor must see a realistic plan and a response to changed resources, not a copied generic document. Drills should test judgment and coordination without exposing participants to fire, smoke, rotors or hazardous entry.

Worked and changed applications: The plan assumes three trained responders but only two are available for the visit. Escalate and obtain an achievable authorized arrangement. Changed case: adequate staffing remains but one required protection resource fails; people do not automatically substitute for engineered capability.

lessons.title: Q98-9 — Emergency leadership and communication
lessons.body:
## Q98-9 — Emergency leadership and communication

At emergency onset, raise the alarm through the approved route, state location and confirmed facts, protect people and coordinate the assigned response. Keep unknowns explicit. Allocate tasks with clear owners, obtain confirmation and monitor results. Maintain communication with crew, remote support and the responsible incident authority without claiming command beyond the actual role.

Reassess priorities as conditions change. A safe route can become unavailable, a casualty report can be corrected and an alternative link can fail. Update affected personnel and confirm understanding. Challenge instructions that depend on unverified conditions or exceed capability. The assessor records the candidate’s decisions and timing context, but does not reward unsafe haste or unsupported certainty.

Worked and changed applications: A roleplayer demands a precise casualty count before reconciliation. Report confirmed people and unknowns, then update from evidence. Changed case: the instruction names the wrong muster point. Correct and confirm the current safe destination before movement.

lessons.title: Q98-10 — Protection controls, accountability and safe support
lessons.body:
## Q98-10 — Protection controls, accountability and safe support

Manage installed-system indications and authorized controls through the actual procedure. Activation, cessation or reset does not automatically prove hazard control. Verify prerequisites before any authorized action, and do not bypass or isolate protection merely to restore a ready display. Simulation uses an inert panel and documented decision conditions, not real safety-system manipulation.

Account for unique identities and verified locations, retaining missing-person information and updates. A duplicate entry cannot offset an absent person. Use approved safe response and assistance within actual training; do not send unprotected personnel to search. Give authorized responders accurate casualty and location information. The combined role requires leadership of available capability, not invention of unavailable capability.

Worked and changed applications: Expected seven people; seven tally entries include a duplicate and omit one identity. Report six unique accounted for and the missing person. Changed case: a system action is authorized only after condition C, but C is unknown. Preserve the hold while seeking verification.

lessons.title: Q98-11 — Recovery, final departure and unattended handover
lessons.body:
## Q98-11 — Recovery, final departure and unattended handover

After normal or abnormal operations, verify actual current readiness, equipment restoration, people/items and remaining restrictions. Final departure removes local personnel, so the required protection state and remote ownership must be established through the approved plan. Do not leave an unresolved isolation or unknown status concealed behind a completed checklist.

Provide a current handover with event summary, verified state, pending defects, owners and next actions. Confirm the correct recipient understands the current revision. Preserve source records and corrections for review. If required unattended state cannot be established, escalate the contingency rather than falsely signing complete. The assessor should trace the handover to actual evidence and recipient confirmation.

Worked and changed applications: All people are accounted for, but a required resource remains unavailable. Keep that restriction visible and obtain authorized disposition before the relevant readiness claim. Changed case: recipient acknowledges the wrong revision. Correct and reconfirm; transmission alone is not accurate handover.

lessons.title: Q98-12 — Competence decision, remediation and scope maintenance
lessons.body:
## Q98-12 — Competence decision, remediation and scope maintenance

Combine independent normal-work observations, local emergency drills, changed scenarios, authenticated records and knowledge evidence. Every mandatory domain must be supported. A high final score or a large portfolio does not offset a critical practical failure. Record prompts and distinguish development from independent performance. A reviewer checks the scope and evidence before an original outcome is issued.

Remediate the specific control and reassess a changed task without erasing the first failure. Record operator/site/system context, limitations and required review triggers. This original VNDRLY package does not issue OPITO certification, renew an external credential or automatically appoint the learner. Changes in duties, equipment or operating concept require review and additional evidence where needed.

Worked and changed applications: Candidate performs normal cycles independently but emergency decisions were coached. Withhold the combined outcome until changed independent emergency evidence passes. Changed case: the candidate correctly refuses an unsupported reset under pressure. Credit the control and assess remaining requirements rather than penalizing delay.


---

content.title: VUC098 | VUC098 workplace assessor and exercise workbook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC098 workplace assessor and exercise workbook
lessons.body: # VUC098 workplace assessor and exercise workbook

lessons.title: Assessment environment and safe evidence
lessons.body:
## Assessment environment and safe evidence

Use an assessor competent in the local combined HLO/HERTL role and evidence assessment, with an independent competent reviewer. Verify initial preparation, supervised development, fitness and current specialist prerequisites appropriate to duties. Public external entry wording does not remove the duty to assess safely. No learner is placed in an unprepared live role to obtain evidence.

F98 context: employer/site/operator___ normal duties___ emergency duties/command interface___ manual and emergency-plan revisions___ aircraft/system scope___ required team/protection___ first-arrival and final-departure concept___ approved communications/alternatives___ passenger/manifest interface___ specialist exclusions___ candidate preparation/fitness___ assessor/reviewer___ privacy/retention___. Actual approved procedures define operating criteria. Missing criteria are not replaced with classroom inventions.

Require two independently observed authorized routine workplace cycles W1/W2, covering preparation, arrival, people/items, departure and restoration. Record actual date, context, actions and secure source references. Require two approved local emergency drills D1/D2 that test the candidate's assigned leadership duties in the local operating concept; they may be non-hazardous simulations and must be labeled as such. The two supplied changed scenarios below provide drill scripts after local adaptation. Actual routine cycles cannot be replaced by simulation and still be called workplace competence.

Do not plant live defects, disable operational systems, alter real manifests, transmit false emergency traffic or create dangerous conditions. Observe real routine work without distracting crew. Drills use ground-level mock/inactive areas, inert aircraft and system panels, harmless props, paper casualty/DG cards, isolated radios and roleplayers. No live fire, fuel, smoke, rotor movement, elevated-edge exposure, hazardous entry or untrained casualty lifting. Independent safety controller checks readiness and stops any real risk. If local access is unavailable, record preparation/simulation only until the workplace evidence is complete.

lessons.title: E98 evidence matrix
lessons.body:
## E98 evidence matrix

For each Q98 domain record: task/context___ evidence mode___ candidate contribution___ source/revision/date___ witness/assessor___ prompts___ independent result___ critical issue___ missing evidence___ changed reassessment___ reviewer___. W1/W2 must identify distinct actual occasions. D1/D2 must identify the approved local plan, exercise authorization, safe adaptation and individual decisions. Protect real passenger and operational data in controlled systems; use redacted references in the portfolio.

lessons.title: Scenario A — NUI transition and emergency
lessons.body:
## Scenario A — NUI transition and emergency

Mock layout: aircraft outline D, waiting W, primary route R1, alternate R2, muster M1/M2, remote controller C and inert protection panel. Geometry is not a live aircraft approach guide. Team roles: candidate, two assistant roleplayers, crew, admin, remote controller and safety controller. This is exercise staffing, not a real minimum. Local adaptation supplies actual role and capability requirements.

Visit 08:00–10:00 UTC. Remote plan incorrectly assumes a resident HLO for first landing; final handover owner blank. Candidate must resolve these through the approved operating concept, not claim impossible inspection. Data: sample 07:45, display refresh 08:10, current 08:15; sample age thirty minutes. Fictional maximum age ten minutes, so twenty beyond. Alternate report wrong site. Controller supplies valid current information only after the gap is raised. Candidate records actual source and restrictions.

Mock inspection finds harmless strap and paper contamination. Crane contact initially says received while still moving; work party occupies R1. Candidate verifies actual safe conditions, resolves each hold and rebriefs approved R2 if required. Passenger list P1–P5; actual P1–P4 plus P8. Count five but P5 missing/P8 unmanifested. Freight is a harmless toolbox changed after weighing; revised data and acceptance required. Paper DG query remains held separately.

Synthetic mass worksheet: people 82/87/91 kg, bags 8/9/10 kg, freight 25 kg: people 260, bags 27, total 312 kg. Remove 87 kg person plus 9 kg bag: 216 kg. Add 79 kg person plus 7 kg bag: 302 kg. These are administrative inputs only, not aircraft clearance. Identity/count/revision changes accompany totals.

Emergency A: fictional plan requires three trained responders but only two available. Protection resource also reports fault. Candidate must address both capability gaps; resolving staffing does not close equipment failure. Inert panel action is authorized only after condition C; C starts unknown. Candidate raises alarm, protects people, reports facts/unknowns and obtains authorized directions without reset/bypass. Route instruction mistakenly names closed M1; correct to approved safe M2 and confirm readback.

Roster A1–A7; muster A1/A2/A3/A4/A5/A6/A6. Six unique, A7 missing. No unsafe search. Controller later verifies A7 safe at M2 at 09:10, giving seven accounted for with source/time recorded. C is a separate condition and remains unresolved until explicitly verified. Final departure: required isolation/status remains open and remote holds v 2 while v 3 is current. Candidate obtains authorized resolution and accurate acknowledged handover before claiming required unattended state.

lessons.title: Scenario B — Changed capability and recovery
lessons.body:
## Scenario B — Changed capability and recovery

Visit is delayed across remote shift change. Candidate must confirm replacement ownership and current contingency. Data: sample 10:02, current 10:08, correct site but sensor fault; fictional maximum age seven minutes. Six-minute age satisfies time only. Approved alternative relay is established, then fails during response. Candidate must withdraw reliance on it and update restrictions.

Normal mock movement uses route R2 after R1 obstruction. All identities correct, but bag destination wrong and damaged-battery paper query unresolved. Roleplayer pressures departure. Candidate holds independent item issues. Emergency plan has adequate people but assigns one person incompatible simultaneous tasks; candidate resolves allocation. Casualty information changes and team receives one incorrect route readback. Candidate reports verified updates and confirms correct instructions.

Roster B1–B8; initial muster B1/B2/B3/B4/B5/B6/B7/B7: seven unique, B8 missing. B8 later verified at safe K, time 10:24. Final protection restored but recipient repeats old revision. Correct and confirm. Candidate must preserve original event history and distinguish changed evidence from assumption. This cycle cannot pass by repeating A's names, counts or conditions.

lessons.title: Worked labs
lessons.body:
## Worked labs

### W98-1 — Combined scope and evidence

Build F98/E98 for normal and emergency duties. Model: W1/W2 actual independent cycles; D1/D2 approved safe local drills; separate refuelling exclusion. Changed: authentic prior evidence from different operator requires review of differences, not automatic extension.

### W98-2 — Transitions and valid status

Resolve first-arrival/final-owner gaps and calculate sample ages. Model: A thirty minutes, twenty beyond fictional ten; B six minutes within seven but fault remains. Changed: alternate for wrong site cannot substitute. Display refresh never overwrites measurement age.

### W98-3 — Readiness and movement

Inspect mock deck, verify crane/work-party conditions and brief route. Model: each defect has its own hold; received is not secured; P5/P8 mismatch held. Changed: new object after ready report requires status update and safe recovery.

### W98-4 — Items and inputs

Show 82+87+91+8+9+10+25=312; subtract 96 to obtain 216; add 86 to obtain 302. Model: revised identities/items/counts and authorized acceptance accompany arithmetic. Changed: correct total with wrong destination or unresolved DG remains unacceptable.

### W98-5 — Emergency leadership

Resolve resource mismatch, conditional C, route readback and accountability. Model: six unique/A7 missing, then seven after verified update; C remains independent. B seven unique/B8 missing, then eight. Changed: adequate people do not cure failed protection or relay.

### W98-6 — Recovery and judgment

Trace restoration, revision and recipient understanding to evidence. Model: current acknowledged status plus remaining restrictions, no false all-clear. Evaluate portfolio with coached emergency work. Changed: written pass cannot replace independent emergency evidence; retain failure and reassess changed task.

lessons.title: Stations
lessons.body:
## Stations

Twelve stations. Physical safe mock activities at 5, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 11; six review tasks. These supplement actual W1/W2 and locally adapted D1/D2. Practice precedes independent assessment; record prompts and individual performance.

### P98-1 — Combined scope

Task: Define normal and emergency duties plus specialist exclusions.

Acceptance: No evidence-free extension from title.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-2 — Authentic evidence

Task: Map and authenticate candidate work and observations.

Acceptance: Actual, simulated, independent and coached evidence distinct.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-3 — Phase ownership

Task: Trace first arrival, occupancy and final handover.

Acceptance: No impossible task or unowned transition.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-4 — Status validity

Task: Check sample time, site, units, faults and alternatives.

Acceptance: Invalid data and failed conditions remain restrictions.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-5 — Inspection/work coordination

Task: Inspect safe mock area and verify crane/work-party state.

Acceptance: Actual condition, not receipt, controls readiness.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-6 — Team/movement

Task: Brief and control mock route changes and dropped-item event.

Acceptance: All affected people understand current safe plan.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-7 — People/items

Task: Reconcile identities, safe dummy items and paper DG query.

Acceptance: Count alone insufficient; current accepted records required.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-8 — Emergency capability

Task: Review actual plan/resources and incompatible duties.

Acceptance: No invented staffing, protection or rescue capability.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-9 — Emergency leadership

Task: Lead alarm, report, tasks and revised-route drill.

Acceptance: Facts/unknowns and command boundaries maintained.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-10 — Controls/accountability

Task: Use inert conditional panel and reconcile missing/duplicate IDs.

Acceptance: No premature action or false all-clear.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-11 — Recovery/handover

Task: Verify restoration and current unattended status transfer.

Acceptance: Evidence and correct recipient acknowledgment required.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

### P98-12 — Outcome/review

Task: Evaluate all evidence and changed remediation.

Acceptance: Both role components demonstrated independently.

Source/context___ Independent action___ Score__/4 Critical___ Remediation___ Changed result___ Assessor/date___

lessons.title: I98 integrated decision and rubric
lessons.body:
## I98 integrated decision and rubric

Complete W1/W2 and both adapted D1/D2 scenarios with authenticated evidence. Controller releases facts sequentially, never coaches assessed decisions, and safety controller may stop immediately. Reviewer maps every domain to evidence and confirms both normal and emergency components. A simulation-only result remains explicitly limited.

Twelve dimensions match the stations. Score 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major coaching, 2 safe incomplete/prompted, 3 independently acceptable, 4 accurate independent performance with explanation. Require at least 39/48 for each integrated assessed cycle, every dimension at least 3, every mandatory task passed and no critical error. Critical: false readiness, unsafe access, ignored missing identity, invented status/location, unauthorized reset/isolation, unsupported rescue/DG/refuelling authority or fabricated evidence. Preserve failure, remediate and assess changed independent performance. A correct hold is credited even if it delays the exercise.

lessons.title: Forms, schedule and outcome
lessons.body:
## Forms, schedule and outcome

F98-S status: site/source/sample/display/current times___ units/faults___ decision/hold___ recipient___. F98-D deck/work control: finding___ owner___ request/actual state___ correction/recheck___. F98-P people/items: expected/actual IDs___ discrepancy___ current manifest___ bag/freight routing/mass___ acceptance___. F98-E emergency: facts/unknowns___ resources/limits___ task owner___ condition/authority___ action/result___ route/readback___. F98-A accountability: unique expected___ verified location/source/time___ missing/duplicate___ update___. F98-H recovery: current protection___ isolation/defect___ revision___ owner/acknowledgment___. F98-R remediation: gap___ practice___ changed evidence___ independent result___ reviewer/appeal___. All actual evidence is protected; examples are synthetic.

Original 40-hour planning allowance: instruction 8, labs 6, stations 6, local drills 10, final/review 4, actual workplace observation planning 6. Extend for actual access and unmet evidence; timetable never waives requirements. Final: twelve cases, 36 decisions, 72 points, 120 minutes; pass 58/72, at least 4/6 each domain and no critical error. Coursebook/calculator allowed; protected keys, collaboration and outside assistance prohibited. Changed Form B after remediation; practical failure requires practical reassessment.

Issue original VNDRLY/U NUI HLO / Helicopter Emergency Response Team Leader — Workplace Competence only after readiness verification, corrected checks, labs, all stations, W1/W2, D1/D2, final and competent review. Record actual site/operator/system/role scope, version/hash, dates, assessor/reviewer and restrictions. This does not issue OPITO certification, replace specialist refuelling qualification or automatically appoint the learner. If actual normal-work evidence is missing, record preparation/simulation only. Material changes to role, systems or procedures trigger review and additional evidence.


---

lessons.title: VUC098 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC098 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q98-1-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-1-L1

Normal HLO evidence alone proves combined emergency-leader role?

**Answer:** No; assess each assigned duty independently.

**Reason/remediation:** A combined title requires evidence across its scope. Revisit Q98-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-1-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-1-L2

Refuelling included automatically?

**Answer:** No; separate specialist training and assessment are required.

**Reason/remediation:** Role coordination is not fuel-delivery competence. Revisit Q98-1 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-2-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-2-L1

Team photo proves individual performance?

**Answer:** No; authenticate specific actions and observe independently.

**Reason/remediation:** Presence is not competence. Revisit Q98-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-2-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-2-L2

Coached cycle can be called independent?

**Answer:** No; retain as development and obtain changed independent evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Prompting changes what the evidence proves. Revisit Q98-2 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-3-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-3-L1

Remote expects resident team at first arrival: acceptable assumption?

**Answer:** No; resolve actual transition responsibilities.

**Reason/remediation:** NUI support differs from a staffed installation. Revisit Q98-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-3-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-3-L2

Final recipient unavailable: handover completed by sending?

**Answer:** No; follow approved contingency and obtain required acceptance.

**Reason/remediation:** Unowned information is not controlled transfer. Revisit Q98-3 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-4-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-4-L1

Sample 07:45, display 08:10, current 08:15: age?

**Answer:** Thirty minutes.

**Reason/remediation:** Measurement time governs age, not display refresh. Revisit Q98-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-4-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-4-L2

Alternative link fails after approval: still valid?

**Answer:** Not while required conditions are lost.

**Reason/remediation:** Capability must remain established. Revisit Q98-4 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-5-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-5-L1

Crane received request means secured?

**Answer:** No; verify actual required condition.

**Reason/remediation:** Acknowledgment and completion differ. Revisit Q98-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-5-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-5-L2

Crane corrected but route contaminated: ready?

**Answer:** No; resolve separate defect.

**Reason/remediation:** One correction does not close all holds. Revisit Q98-5 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-6-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-6-L1

Route changes after briefing: proceed by old habit?

**Answer:** No; rebrief and confirm current route.

**Reason/remediation:** Shared understanding must follow the actual plan. Revisit Q98-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-6-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-6-L2

Dropped item near hazard: let passenger retrieve?

**Answer:** No; stop pursuit and arrange safe recovery.

**Reason/remediation:** Recovery cannot justify uncontrolled exposure. Revisit Q98-6 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-7-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-7-L1

Equal people count with wrong ID: accept?

**Answer:** No; reconcile identities and manifest.

**Reason/remediation:** Count alone can hide substitution. Revisit Q98-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-7-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-7-L2

Late toolbox leaves old mass valid?

**Answer:** No; verify changed input and revise/accept.

**Reason/remediation:** Source measurement no longer matches the item. Revisit Q98-7 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-8-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-8-L1

Three-person plan with two trained people: adequate?

**Answer:** Not without authorized capability resolution.

**Reason/remediation:** Paper roles cannot create resources. Revisit Q98-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-8-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-8-L2

More people automatically replace failed engineered protection?

**Answer:** No; apply approved restriction/alternative process.

**Reason/remediation:** Capabilities are not interchangeable by assumption. Revisit Q98-8 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-9-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-9-L1

Unknown casualty count: supply estimate as fact?

**Answer:** No; report verified facts and uncertainty.

**Reason/remediation:** False certainty can misdirect response. Revisit Q98-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-9-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-9-L2

Wrong muster point readback: ignore?

**Answer:** No; correct and confirm.

**Reason/remediation:** A response is useful only if it matches the safe instruction. Revisit Q98-9 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-10-L1

Seven entries, one duplicate and one absent: unique?

**Answer:** Six accounted for, one missing.

**Reason/remediation:** Identity reconciliation controls the result. Revisit Q98-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-10-L2

Conditional action before C verified?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Required conditions are gates, not suggestions. Revisit Q98-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-11-L1

People all found but resource missing: unrestricted ready?

**Answer:** No; record and resolve capability restriction.

**Reason/remediation:** Accountability does not prove equipment readiness. Revisit Q98-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-11-L2

Recipient repeats old revision: valid handover?

**Answer:** No; correct and confirm current status.

**Reason/remediation:** Receipt is not correct understanding. Revisit Q98-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q98-12-L1

High final score offsets coached emergency performance?

**Answer:** No; require independent practical evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Knowledge and performance are separate mandatory gates. Revisit Q98-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q98-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q98-12-L2

Correctly refuses unsupported reset: penalize delay?

**Answer:** No; credit proper boundary control.

**Reason/remediation:** Schedule pressure does not create authority. Revisit Q98-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.body:
# VUC098 sources and assessment trace

Reviewed 18 November 2026. Full OPITO specification unavailable; original available-source combined-role materials, not exact external parity or accreditation.

It explicitly separates specialist refuelling preparation and assessment. Original duration, evidence rules and award here are not represented as that external certificate. | Q98-1, Q98-2, Q98-12; combined-scope and specialist boundaries |
| [CAA CAP 437 January 2026 official text](https://www.caa.co.uk/media/3ccjonps/cap437-standards-for-offshore-helicopter-landing-areas-edition-9-amendm-1.pdf) | NUI protection, normal operating interfaces and conditional equipment alternatives support local readiness and safe transition reasoning. Actual aircraft/system procedures remain controlled inputs; no generic approach route or reset sequence is prescribed. | Q98-3 to Q98-11; F98 adaptation and scenario conditions |
| [CAA offshore-location guidance](https://regulatorylibrary.caa.co.uk/965-2012/Content/Document%20Structure/05%20SPA/3%20AMC/AMC1%20SPA%20HOFO%20115%20Use%20of%20offshore.htm) | Current location information and operator context support valid data and scoped competence decisions. | Q98-3, Q98-4 and evidence context |
| [CAA DG CBTA](https://www.caa.co.uk/commercial-industry/airlines/dangerous-goods/cbta-for-dangerous-goods) | Function-specific preparation remains distinct from a combined role title. | Q98-1, Q98-7 and paper DG scenarios |

lessons.title: Complete trace
lessons.body:
## Complete trace

Twelve chapters each have two explained checks, one observed station, a protected three-decision final case and a changed retake. Six labs link scope/evidence, transitions/status, readiness/movement, item inputs, emergency leadership and recovery/judgment. W1/W2 require actual independent routine workplace cycles. D1/D2 are approved locally adapted safe emergency drills using the supplied complete scripts. Six physical mock and six review stations supplement those observations. F98/E98 forms retain attribution, prompting, source/revision, controls, accountability, handover and remediation.

lessons.title: Limits and maintenance
lessons.body:
## Limits and maintenance

No actual learner, aircraft movement, emergency or workplace record has been created by authoring. Verify current local procedures, required capability, specialist preparation and assessment authorization before delivery. Simulated defects never enter live operations. Synthetic numbers are not operational limits. The original combined-role outcome requires all evidence; normal HLO success cannot replace emergency-leadership performance, and neither qualifies specialist refuelling. Review material changes and retain previous evidence and restrictions.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Helicopter Refuelling — Initial Training
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Helicopter Refuelling — Initial Training

VUC099. Original available-source specialist initial instruction and supervised practical package. Full OPITO specification unavailable. Actual aircraft, fuel-system and quality procedures govern all practical delivery. No external accreditation or independent workplace authorization is conferred.

lessons.title: Q99-1 — Role, entry and controlled procedures
lessons.body:
## Q99-1 — Role, entry and controlled procedures

Helicopter refuelling is a specialist function. Verify prior helideck preparation, fitness and assigned responsibilities before practical training. Identify the aircraft operator, HLO, fuel operator, quality-control authority and authorized maintenance provider. The refueller must know who can accept fuel, authorize transfer, stop the task and release a quarantined system. A general HLO certificate does not establish all these skills.

Use current aircraft-specific, system-specific and fuel-quality procedures with the relevant safety data sheet. This original initial course teaches safe decisions and supervised practice; workplace competence assessment and employer authorization follow. Do not improvise a valve sequence, pressure limit or repair method from generic notes. If the required approved procedure is absent or inconsistent, hold the task and resolve the gap.

Worked and changed applications: A crew requests a rapid top-up but the operator cannot confirm the applicable procedure revision. Do not proceed on memory. Changed case: a routine inspection reveals a defect requiring invasive fuel-system work. Isolate/report through the authorized process rather than treating initial training as maintenance authorization.

lessons.title: Q99-2 — Fuel identity, properties and exposure
lessons.body:
## Q99-2 — Fuel identity, properties and exposure

Verify the required aviation turbine fuel grade and specification through approved documentation and aircraft/operator confirmation. Similar appearance does not prove identity or suitability. Fuel can present fire, vapor, skin/eye and environmental hazards; use the current SDS and actual risk controls. Never taste fuel, deliberately inhale vapor or use an open flame to identify it.

Understand why contamination, mixed product or uncertain traceability can endanger aircraft operation even when the fuel looks clear. Water, particulate matter and other contamination require defined checks and disposition. Keep containers and tools clean and compatible. Personal protection, ventilation, ignition control and spill arrangements must match the actual activity. A course cannot assign one universal exposure limit or fuel acceptance criterion to every installation.

Worked and changed applications: A container label says one grade while the release document identifies another. Quarantine and resolve identity; clear appearance does not overrule the discrepancy. Changed case: product identity is correct but the sample is suspect. Identity and quality are separate gates.

lessons.title: Q99-3 — Receipt, transport and traceability
lessons.body:
## Q99-3 — Receipt, transport and traceability

Before accepting a delivery, reconcile tank or consignment identity, product, batch, release documentation, seals, condition and required inspection evidence. Check for damage, leakage, missing labels or signs of interference. Record source and date so the fuel can be traced through storage and dispensing. A handwritten batch substitution without authorized evidence is not a correction.

Transport and lifting of fuel containers require separate competent arrangements and approved equipment; this course does not authorize crane or dangerous-goods transport duties. During receipt, preserve segregation and prevent uncertain product entering accepted stock. Apply the specified settling, sampling and release process before use. Do not shorten required controls because the next aircraft is waiting.

Worked and changed applications: Delivery tank T8 arrives with certificate for T9. Hold receipt/release and obtain authenticated reconciliation. Changed case: tank identity matches but seal integrity is uncertain. Keep the separate concern open and follow the quality authority’s process.

lessons.title: Q99-4 — Storage, segregation and stock control
lessons.body:
## Q99-4 — Storage, segregation and stock control

Maintain approved storage condition, identification, access control, drainage/containment and environmental protection. Keep accepted, quarantined and waste/reclaim material clearly separated. A valve label or screen selection must correspond to the actual intended source. Do not return suspect samples or mixed residues to usable stock without an explicitly approved recovery process.

Track receipts, dispensed volume, sampling, waste and closing stock on a consistent basis. Investigate discrepancies rather than editing totals to make the ledger balance. Temperature, measurement method and calibration can affect comparisons; record the basis and seek competent review. Stock arithmetic is a diagnostic tool, not proof of product quality.

Worked and changed applications: Opening 5,000 L plus receipt 2,000 L minus delivery 1,200 L and sampling/waste 20 L gives expected 5,780 L. If measured closing is 5,730 L, investigate a 50 L shortfall. Changed case: a receipt is entered twice; authenticate and correct with audit history, not a hidden balancing entry.

lessons.title: Q99-5 — System layout and protective functions
lessons.body:
## Q99-5 — System layout and protective functions

Trace the actual system from supply through pumps, filtration, meters, controls and delivery hose to the aircraft interface. Identify isolation points, emergency stop, deadman or equivalent control, pressure protection, bonding provisions and sample points as applicable. Explain each component’s function and what information indicates a fault. Do not assume every installation uses the same filter technology or control arrangement.

Use the approved schematic and manufacturer instructions. A protective trip is a reason to stop and investigate, not bypass. Pressure and flow limits must match the aircraft and system; never set them from a generic classroom value. Maintenance that could affect fuel quality or integrity belongs to the authorized competent provider. The learner should demonstrate safe recognition and reporting rather than unauthorized disassembly.

Worked and changed applications: Differential pressure rises beyond the actual approved criterion. Stop/hold through the procedure and seek authorized investigation; do not bypass the filter. Changed case: a zero differential reading appears unexpectedly at established flow. Investigate the abnormal indication rather than assuming zero is always ideal.

lessons.title: Q99-6 — Sampling, inspection and quality decisions
lessons.body:
## Q99-6 — Sampling, inspection and quality decisions

Sample at the required points and times using clean suitable equipment and the approved safe method. Identify sample source, batch, date/time and operator. Avoid contaminating the sample through dirty containers or poor handling. Perform the specified visual and other checks using current methods and valid equipment or test media. Appearance alone does not establish every required quality characteristic.

Understand the difference between a passing observation, an invalid test and a failed sample. Expired or mishandled test media cannot support release. Suspect results require quarantine/hold and authorized investigation, with traceable records. Do not repeatedly sample until one result looks favorable while discarding the failures. Retain and dispose of samples under the actual procedure, not by returning them casually to storage.

Worked and changed applications: A sample contains visible water or particles. Hold affected fuel and notify the quality authority rather than filtering the evidence out of the jar. Changed case: sample looks clear but required test media is expired. The check is incomplete; obtain a valid method before release.

lessons.title: Q99-7 — Pre-use equipment checks and maintenance boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q99-7 — Pre-use equipment checks and maintenance boundaries

Inspect hoses, couplings, caps, bonding equipment, controls and required emergency resources using the actual checklist. Check status of inspection, calibration and maintenance records. A damaged hose, leaking connection or unreliable control is not made acceptable by a short delivery quantity. Keep equipment clean and protected when not in use.

Distinguish routine authorized checks from invasive maintenance. Do not open pressurized equipment, replace safety-critical components or use unapproved lubricant/parts outside authorization. Safely isolate and report defects through the approved system. A repair must be verified and released by the appropriate authority before service. The practical station uses a training rig and defect cards, never a deliberately damaged live fuel system.

Worked and changed applications: A hose has a suspect bulge and the deadman does not return correctly on the approved pre-use test. Hold equipment and report both defects. Changed case: hose is replaced by authorized staff but functional verification remains incomplete. Replacement alone is not release to use.

lessons.title: Q99-8 — Fuel quantity, units and confirmation
lessons.body:
## Q99-8 — Fuel quantity, units and confirmation

Confirm the requested fuel quantity and unit with the authorized crew, including whether it means an amount to add or a final total. Distinguish liters, gallons and mass; do not silently assume US versus Imperial gallons. Use approved density and temperature basis when mass-volume conversion is required. Aircraft fuel planning and final load acceptance remain with crew.

For classroom arithmetic, mass equals volume times density when units and conditions are consistent. At an explicitly supplied 0.800 kg/L, 600 kg corresponds to 750 L. This is not a universal fuel density. Confirm calculations and meter units before transfer and record actual delivered quantity. If the request changes, repeat the required confirmation rather than relying on an earlier number.

Worked and changed applications: Crew requests 800 kg but meter is in liters; supplied approved exercise density is 0.800 kg/L, giving 1,000 L. Changed case: instruction says bring total to 800 kg, with 300 kg already aboard; the addition is 500 kg or 625 L on the same exercise basis, subject to crew confirmation.

lessons.title: Q99-9 — Bonding, ignition control and safe setup
lessons.body:
## Q99-9 — Bonding, ignition control and safe setup

Apply the actual approved bonding and connection sequence before opening or transferring fuel, and maintain required protection through disconnection. Bonding and grounding are related controls but are not interchangeable terms; a ground connection alone does not prove the required aircraft-to-system bond. Verify equipment condition and any required continuity test using the approved method and limits.

Control ignition sources, access, hose routing and emergency escape. Position equipment according to aircraft and site procedures so it does not create rotor, exhaust, trip or collision hazards. Do not create sparks as a demonstration. A missing approved bonding point or failed check is a hold, not permission to clip onto a convenient painted surface. Instructor-led practice uses an inert interface or approved rig before any supervised fuel handling.

Worked and changed applications: A bond lead looks intact but its required test is failed. Hold setup until corrected and verified. Changed case: the ground connection is present but the required aircraft bond is absent. Do not treat the ground as a substitute.

lessons.title: Q99-10 — Crew/HLO coordination and operating modes
lessons.body:
## Q99-10 — Crew/HLO coordination and operating modes

Confirm aircraft identity, fuel request, product, required quality release, communication signals and permission to begin through the approved crew/HLO interface. Establish who operates controls, monitors the aircraft connection and can stop transfer. Maintain the required view or communication throughout. Do not begin because the hose is connected if authorization has not been given.

Engine/rotor-running or passengers-on-board operations require specific approved arrangements and competent personnel; they are not a routine shortcut authorized by this course. Passenger embarkation/disembarkation must not be improvised concurrently with refuelling. Follow the applicable aircraft manual and operator controls. If required communication is lost or a hazard develops, stop through the approved process and notify.

Worked and changed applications: The crew request is confirmed but HLO reports passenger movement is beginning. Do not combine tasks to save time; restore the approved safe arrangement. Changed case: a radio fails during transfer. Apply the stop/fallback procedure, not an assumption that silence means continue.

lessons.title: Q99-11 — Transfer monitoring and abnormal stop
lessons.body:
## Q99-11 — Transfer monitoring and abnormal stop

Start and control transfer only through the actual approved sequence and authorization. Monitor quantity, flow/pressure indications, connection, leaks and communication as required. Keep required controls attended; never wedge or bypass a deadman. Stay alert to a changed request or stop signal and confirm it clearly. A smooth flow does not prove every quality or safety gate was met.

On leakage, abnormal indication, loss of communication or other stop condition, use the approved stop/emergency process, protect people and notify responsible personnel. Do not disconnect pressurized equipment or improvise repair. Restart requires the specified cause resolution, verification and renewed authorization. Do not reset a trip repeatedly until it stays running.

Worked and changed applications: A leak card is introduced during the training transfer. Stop, communicate and apply the controlled response; do not tighten an energized connection. Changed case: the leak is reported fixed but the responsible release is missing. Keep the restart hold until required evidence and authority are established.

lessons.title: Q99-12 — Post-transfer checks and records
lessons.body:
## Q99-12 — Post-transfer checks and records

Complete the approved shutdown, disconnection, bonding removal, cap security, equipment stowage and final area-clear checks in the actual required order. Confirm no hose, lead or tool remains connected or in a hazardous location. Carry out required post-transfer sampling and quality checks and obtain crew acknowledgment of actual delivery through the procedure.

Record aircraft, date/time, product/batch, meter start/end, delivered quantity and units, quality/sample references, operator and acceptance. Preserve corrections and abnormal events. A meter difference does not by itself prove what entered the aircraft if there was a leak or other discrepancy; investigate before reporting certainty. Restore system readiness and identify remaining defects for handover.

Worked and changed applications: Meter starts 12,450 L and ends 13,200 L: indicated delivery 750 L. Record units and reconcile with request and event history. Changed case: a spill occurred; do not assert all 750 L reached the aircraft without the required investigation and crew reconciliation.

lessons.title: Q99-13 — Spill, fire, misfuelling and environmental response
lessons.body:
## Q99-13 — Spill, fire, misfuelling and environmental response

Know the actual emergency stop, alarm, exclusion and spill-response plan before work. Protect people, stop transfer when safe through approved controls and notify HLO/crew and responsible responders. Do not wash fuel into drains, create ignition sources or attempt firefighting beyond training. First aid and medical referral follow actual exposure guidance and competent direction.

Suspected wrong fuel or contaminated delivery requires immediate notification and prevention of further use through the authorized aircraft/operator process. Do not conceal the issue, dilute it away or assume a small amount is harmless. Preserve batch, sample, meter and event evidence. Environmental containment, cleanup and waste handling require appropriate resources and authority; course exercises use paper injects and inert training materials.

Worked and changed applications: After transfer, paperwork reveals a product-identity mismatch. Notify immediately and preserve evidence; do not let embarrassment delay the aircraft safety response. Changed case: a spill is contained but waste disposal is unresolved. Keep it controlled under the approved process, not returned to usable fuel.

lessons.title: Q99-14 — Integrated initial performance and workplace progression
lessons.body:
## Q99-14 — Integrated initial performance and workplace progression

The learner must complete receipt/quality reasoning, pre-use checks, quantity confirmation, safe setup, supervised rig operation, abnormal stop, post-checks and records. Each gate remains independent: correct arithmetic does not compensate for wrong product, failed quality or missing bonding. The instructor records individual performance and prompting rather than relying on group attendance.

This original initial-training outcome requires supervised practical demonstration on an approved training system, including valid quality-control practice where safely provided. A tabletop-only result is recorded as theory/simulation, not full practical completion. Workplace competence and aircraft-specific authorization follow through the employer’s process. Remediate critical gaps and use changed independent assessment; do not issue an external qualification or claim actual aircraft capability from course authorship.

Worked and changed applications: Learner calculates quantity correctly but bypasses a control. Stop and withhold practical completion pending remediation and changed performance. Changed case: learner correctly refuses transfer because quality release is missing. Credit the hold and assess the remaining skills; turnaround speed does not override release gates.


---

lessons.title: VUC099 instructor guide and supervised practical workbook
lessons.body: # VUC099 instructor guide and supervised practical workbook

lessons.title: Facility, personnel and procedure gates
lessons.body:
## Facility, personnel and procedure gates

Instructor must be competent in offshore helicopter fuelling, fuel quality and the specific training system. An independent safety supervisor controls practical activity. Verify relevant helideck foundation, fitness, assigned functions and applicable specialist permissions. Use a professionally controlled training facility with an approved risk assessment, emergency/spill arrangements, suitable PPE, ventilation, ignition controls, compatible equipment and authorized waste disposal. Do not run improvised fuel exercises on an office desk or live helideck.

F99 adaptation must be completed and approved by the competent facility/system authority: fuel grade/specification/SDS___ aircraft-interface procedure___ rig manufacturer/model/manual revision___ approved training medium___ operating pressure/flow limits___ valve/connection/shutdown sequence___ bonding points/test method/acceptance___ sampling points/flush requirements/methods/test media validity___ quality criteria/hold/release authority___ settling/release conditions___ permitted maintenance___ emergency stop/alarm/spill process___ post-check/sample retention/disposal___ instructor/safety supervisor/date___. These are controlled equipment-specific inputs, not missing universal numbers to invent. If a required field cannot be established, do not perform dependent practical work.

Use a dedicated approved rig or inert aircraft interface. Manufacturer-approved nonflammable training medium may be used only in equipment explicitly designed/authorized for it; never introduce water or other substitute into an operational aviation fuel system. Actual fuel sampling/quality practice requires the competent facility's approved handling controls and valid methods. If only paper or visual sample images are available, record theory/simulation rather than full practical completion. No live-aircraft or rotor-running transfer is required by these original exercises, and none is authorized by the course text.

No deliberate leak, wrong-fuel delivery, damaged pressurized hose, control bypass, fire or vapor exposure is created. Faults are controller cards or safe simulator states. Do not open energized equipment. Emergency practice uses safe inert props and isolated communications. A real unsafe condition stops the exercise. Learners practice before independent assessment, with individualized accommodations that preserve assessed competence.

lessons.title: R99 resource set
lessons.body:
## R99 resource set

Provide current approved schematic/manual, product/SDS cards, traceable training container and seal labels, clean suitable sample equipment, valid test media/instruments, approved rig with meter and protective controls, inert aircraft connection/bonding interface, safe hose/coupling examples, defect photographs/cards, calculator, delivery/quality logs, mock crew/HLO roles, spill-response training props and protected exams. Instructor demonstrates the actual approved procedure and confirms learner understanding before operation. Maintenance tasks are restricted to those expressly authorized by F99; invasive work is discussed/referral only unless separately qualified and authorized.

lessons.title: Complete synthetic data and controller scripts
lessons.body:
## Complete synthetic data and controller scripts

Cycle A receipt: tank T8, batch B99-A, product card Jet A-1 for exercise identity only, seal S8. First certificate deliberately references T9; learner holds reconciliation. Controller then provides authenticated corrected T8 documentation, with an audit note, not a silent replacement. A separate seal-integrity card remains unresolved until authorized disposition is supplied. No actual uncertain product enters accepted stock.

Stock A: opening 5,000 L; receipt 2,000 L; planned delivery 1,200 L; sampling/waste 20 L. Expected closing 5,780 L; measured card 5,730 L, a 50 L shortfall. Investigate measurement basis, entries and losses; do not insert a balancing receipt. A later controller card identifies a documented meter-entry error only after learner requests evidence; correction retains original and source. The scenario does not claim every real discrepancy is a clerical error.

Quality cards: Q1 visible particles; Q2 clear-looking sample with expired required test media; Q3 valid identified sample/check set supplied only after the learner holds and requests authorized resolution. Q1 and Q2 cannot release fuel. Learner performs actual approved supervised sampling/check technique on the facility's known training source; paper cards test disposition separately. Record source, batch, point, time, method, result, validity, operator and release authority.

Equipment cards: hose bulge and failed deadman return; both require hold. Controller later supplies authorized repair and functional-test evidence, but bonding-check evidence is initially absent. Learner must not let one repair clear all equipment gates. Rig operation uses only F99 limits and sequence, with no deliberately damaged equipment.

Crew request A: add 960 kg, supplied approved classroom density 0.800 kg/L, meter liters. Calculated request 1,200 L. Changed instruction: final total 960 kg with 240 kg already aboard; addition 720 kg = 900 L. Require explicit readback and mock crew/HLO confirmation. Rig may use a scaled quantity specified by its approved procedure; record actual rig quantity separately from classroom 900 L. Never force a small training rig to deliver classroom volumes beyond its safe capacity.

Transfer A: after proper setup/quality/authorization, controller introduces paper leak/loss-of-communication card. Learner stops through approved controls, communicates and preserves restart hold. No real leak is created. After authorized cause-resolution and renewed permission, complete the safe rig task. Classroom meter record 20,450 to 21,350 L indicates 900 L. If spill card was active, learner must not assert all 900 L reached aircraft without reconciliation. Complete post-checks and current delivery/quality records.

Cycle B: tank T12/batch B99-B documents match, but damage/leak card triggers separate hold. Stock opening 4,800 L + receipt 1,500 L − delivery 950 L − sampling/waste 25 L = 5,325 L; measured 5,290 L gives 35 L shortfall. Product identity later confirmed but sample-source label missing; valid-looking test cannot be assigned to an assumed source. Re-establish traceable sampling.

Request B: add 800 kg at supplied 0.800 kg/L gives 1,000 L. Changed to final 800 kg with 300 kg aboard gives addition 500 kg = 625 L. Classroom meter 15,300 to 15,925 L indicates 625 L. Passenger movement is proposed during fuelling and communication later fails. Learner maintains approved separation and stop/restart controls. Post-transfer paperwork card suggests wrong product; immediate responsible notification and evidence preservation are required, not improvised dilution. Waste-disposal route is initially unknown and must be resolved without returning suspect material to stock.

lessons.title: Worked application labs
lessons.body:
## Worked application labs

### W99-1 — Scope, identity and receipt

Complete F99 and reconcile T8/T9, seal and product cards. Model: independent holds with traceable authorized resolution; current procedure and specialist boundaries. Changed: matching documents but damaged container still prevents release.

### W99-2 — Stock and units

Calculate A expected 5,780 L and 50 L shortfall; B expected 5,325 L and 35 L shortfall. Model: investigate on consistent measurement basis, preserve correction history. Changed: duplicate receipt requires authenticated correction, not a hidden balancing withdrawal.

### W99-3 — System and quality

Trace rig functions and demonstrate approved sampling. Model: Q1 failed; Q2 invalid/incomplete; Q3 only supports release if every actual required criterion and authority is satisfied. Changed: sample source missing invalidates attribution even when test result looks acceptable. Do not cherry-pick passing samples.

### W99-4 — Equipment and setup

Demonstrate safe inspections, bonding and actual approved connection sequence. Model: hose and control defects held separately; repair plus functional verification and bonding evidence required. Changed: ground connected but aircraft bond absent remains a hold. No real failed equipment is energized.

### W99-5 — Quantity and communication

Show 960/0.800=1,200 L; (960−240)/0.800=900 L; 800/0.800=1,000 L; (800−300)/0.800=625 L. Model: confirm add versus final total, units and supplied density. Changed: request says gallons without specifying type; obtain clarification rather than choose a conversion.

### W99-6 — Controlled transfer and stop

Perform actual approved training-rig cycle with mock crew/HLO authorization, attended controls and fault-card stop. Model: stop/notify, no bypass or energized repair, restart only after cause resolution and renewed authority. Changed: communication restored but authorization still absent; remain stopped.

### W99-7 — Post-checks and abnormal delivery

Complete approved disconnection/clearance, quality checks and records. Model: 900 L or 625 L indicated by classroom meters, reconciled to event history; no fabricated crew signature. Changed: wrong-product suspicion triggers immediate notification and evidence preservation, not dilution. Resolve waste under approved environmental controls.

lessons.body:
## Individual stations

Fourteen stations. Physical supervised training tasks occur at 3, 5, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12 and 13; five other stations are calculations or review. Station 13 uses inert emergency props only.
