content.title: VUC101 | VNDRLY/U Major Emergency Management — Initial Response
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Major Emergency Management — Initial Response
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Major Emergency Management — Initial Response

VUC101 • Original initial-development program • 18 November 2026

Audience: prospective emergency leaders, team members and support personnel. No prior command appointment is required for this initial course. Participants must be able to engage safely with the simulation and understand the supplied fictional plan. This is not OPITO certification or employer command authorization. Full proprietary criteria were unavailable; public product scope and regulator guidance support this original package.

Planned delivery: 32 hours over consecutive training days: 10 instruction/prebrief, 16 scenario practice and debrief, 4 application laboratories, 2 written assessment/development planning. Add time to give every learner the required manager-role practice and feedback. This is the VNDRLY schedule, not a claim to reproduce an external course duration.

Outcomes: prepare the emergency organization; establish command and objectives; evaluate uncertain evidence; delegate safely; coordinate communications, people and resources; recognize escalation; manage stress; hand over and plan development.

lessons.title: Q101-01 — Initial training and emergency leadership
lessons.body:
## Q101-01 — Initial training and emergency leadership

Major emergency management brings together decisions about people, plant, responders and outside support. The manager must establish priorities and a workable organization while events are still uncertain. This is initial development, not proof of readiness to command a particular offshore installation. Employer appointment, asset knowledge, supervised practice and any required formal competence assessment remain separate. A participant may enter as a prospective leader, team member or support person; everyone practices the manager role so that the demands of command become visible.

Start by understanding the installation emergency plan, authority hierarchy, deputy arrangements and interfaces with marine, aviation, shore and public agencies. State who is in command and how others can contact that person. If command changes, communicate the transfer, time, current objectives and outstanding decisions. Avoid two people issuing incompatible instructions under an ambiguous title. An external specialist can advise without automatically taking local command.

Worked example: a shore manager calls while the installation commander is managing a release. The call provides resources and advice but does not silently transfer incident command. The team records the request, confirms authority and resolves conflicting instructions through the plan. A missing commander triggers the designated succession arrangement, not a competition for the loudest voice.

lessons.title: Q101-02 — Preparing a usable emergency organization
lessons.body:
## Q101-02 — Preparing a usable emergency organization

A plan becomes useful when people can find the right information and carry out their roles under stress. Preparation includes current hazards, plant configuration, impairment controls, available response teams, communications, people accounting, refuge and evacuation arrangements. Check the effect of contractors, maintenance, weather and simultaneous operations. A resource list is only credible if the people, equipment and access are actually available.

Brief the team on roles, immediate responsibilities and reporting intervals. Assign operations, people/muster, communications and logging functions clearly. The leader retains the overall picture while specialists manage assigned work. Use role cards to avoid duplication and gaps. Identify backup personnel and what must happen if a key role is lost. Test communications and make essential documents available if the normal computer system fails.

Worked example: the plan lists two response teams, but the current shift has enough qualified people for one. Record one available team and revise the response options with the responsible authority. Do not divide the same personnel into two simultaneous tasks on a planning board. Preparation should reveal limitations before the alarm, not conceal them.

lessons.title: Q101-03 — Recognizing the incident and setting objectives
lessons.body:
## Q101-03 — Recognizing the incident and setting objectives

When the first report arrives, establish location, time, people at risk, nature of the hazard and reliability of the information. Activate the relevant alarm and emergency organization under the plan. Do not wait for a complete causal explanation before taking protective steps already justified by the evidence. State a small number of immediate objectives in operational terms: protect people from the threatened area, establish accountability, control the source through authorized actions and preserve a safe evacuation option.

Distinguish objectives from tactics. Protect people is an objective; sending a team through a particular route is a tactic that requires a hazard and capability assessment. Ask what could make the incident worse, what decision is time-critical and what would change the current priorities. Review objectives when new evidence arrives. A response that was reasonable five minutes earlier can become inappropriate after wind, protection or route changes.

Worked example: smoke and a missing worker are reported in a utility module. The manager activates the plan, obtains last-known-location information and asks the response leader for a safe assessment. Ordering immediate entry without knowing conditions confuses urgency with a viable rescue plan. The missing worker remains a priority while the team determines a defensible response.

lessons.title: Q101-04 — Situation assessment and decision discipline
lessons.body:
## Q101-04 — Situation assessment and decision discipline

Maintain a shared picture with confirmed facts, credible reports, assumptions and unknowns clearly distinguished. Use timestamps and sources; an old measurement on a newly refreshed display is still old. Ask for the information that affects decisions instead of collecting every detail. Make an action log that identifies decision, reason, authority, owner, deadline and result. Explain uncertainty rather than replacing it with false precision.

Consider more than one option and identify constraints: people exposed, responder capability, route availability, system status, time to escalation and reversibility. Choose an option within authority, communicate it and monitor whether it achieves the objective. Set triggers for reassessment. An unsuccessful action is new evidence, not a reason to repeat it indefinitely. Invite challenge from team members who see a discrepancy.

Worked example: a control room reports isolation commanded but no closed feedback. The decision board must show unconfirmed isolation. A plan that assumes the release has stopped is unsupported. The manager asks for the approved failed-action response, maintains restrictions and reassesses whether refuge or evacuation options are threatened.

lessons.title: Q101-05 — Command, delegation and responder protection
lessons.body:
## Q101-05 — Command, delegation and responder protection

Give tasks to named roles with a clear outcome, constraints and reporting requirement. Ask for a readback of critical instructions. Delegation does not remove the manager's responsibility to monitor progress and interactions. Avoid micromanaging specialist techniques that belong to a competent response leader, but require the information needed to judge whether the plan remains feasible.

Responder deployment must account for hazard, competence, equipment, communications, backup and withdrawal arrangements under the local plan. No course scenario authorizes improvised entry into smoke, gas, confined space, unstable structure or energized equipment. Track teams by location, task and status; record a missed report as a problem requiring action. Stop or change a tactic when conditions exceed its assumptions. Protecting a rescue capability is part of protecting casualties.

Worked example: a team reports its planned route blocked and asks to use an unassessed route. The manager does not simply say continue. Obtain the response leader's assessment of the alternative and the required safeguards. If no safe approach exists, preserve the missing-person information and escalate alternatives rather than treating the roster deficit as permission for uncontrolled exposure.

lessons.title: Q101-06 — Communications and information flow
lessons.body:
## Q101-06 — Communications and information flow

Use concise structured messages that identify sender, incident, location, hazards, actions, needs and next update. Confirm receipt of instructions that affect safety. A message can be transmitted, received, understood and acted on at different times; the log should show which stage is established. Correct wrong identifiers immediately. Keep urgent action channels clear and route routine requests to the assigned support role.

Coordinate internal, shore, vessel, aviation and public-agency communication through the plan. Provide accurate location, incident, people status, support requested and safe contact arrangements. Do not promise a landing, rescue route or arrival time that the relevant operator has not confirmed. If a primary link fails, test the approved alternate and re-establish the current instruction. Maintain an update rhythm for people waiting at muster so uncertainty does not become rumor.

Worked example: shore says a rescue asset may be available in twenty minutes. Record a provisional estimate, not confirmed rescue. Ask who will confirm dispatch and arrival. If conditions worsen before confirmation, reassess local options rather than treating the estimate as guaranteed protection.

lessons.title: Q101-07 — Accountability, casualties and welfare
lessons.body:
## Q101-07 — Accountability, casualties and welfare

Establish a reliable people baseline and track identities through muster, response duties, medical treatment and transfer. Totals support reconciliation but do not replace it. A duplicate entry can make a count appear complete while one person is missing. Require the muster coordinator to report confirmed, unconfirmed and transferred people separately, with times and sources. Preserve last-known-location information for missing people.

Medical priorities belong to appropriately trained medical personnel. The manager coordinates access, resources and evacuation requests without inventing diagnoses or treatment. Protect personal details while ensuring responders receive relevant information. Consider the welfare of people at refuge, distressed witnesses and relief personnel. Extended incidents need rest, food, communications and replacement arrangements; these should not distract from immediate life protection but must have an owner.

Worked example: a person is counted at muster and again in the medical area. Reconcile the identity and movement before declaring a second casualty or a complete roster. If a transfer is made to a vessel, record who left, destination, time and confirmation of receipt. A planned transfer is not a completed one.

lessons.title: Q101-08 — Escalation, refuge and evacuation
lessons.body:
## Q101-08 — Escalation, refuge and evacuation

A manager must recognize when the incident is outgrowing the current response. Look for loss of source control, threatened refuge, deteriorating weather, unavailable routes, failed protection or insufficient response capability. Use the plan's escalation criteria and communicate decisions early enough for the required actions to be completed. Avoid fixation on saving equipment when life-protection options are closing.

Refuge endurance and evacuation capacity depend on conditions. Compare the latest credible time available with decision, communication, preparation and movement time, including the actual plan's allowances and uncertainty. A nominal arithmetic margin is not a safe waiting period. Confirm the capacity and suitability of the available means; subtract unavailable capacity rather than counting it because it appears on a drawing. Do not send more people than an approved means can carry.

Worked example: forty people need evacuation. Two fictional means have twenty-four approved places each, but one is unavailable. Forty-eight nominal places become twenty-four available places, leaving sixteen without that option. This is a capability gap requiring urgent command action, not permission to overload. Obtain confirmed alternatives and reassess timing.

lessons.title: Q101-09 — Stress, teamwork and challenge
lessons.body:
## Q101-09 — Stress, teamwork and challenge

Stress can cause tunnel vision, rushed speech, missed messages, indecision or fixation. Recognize these patterns in yourself and the team. Use short pauses for a structured situation review when the event permits: current threats, objectives, actions, gaps and next decision. Keep language direct. Assign one owner per task and ask for a clear response. Seek relief or support when workload exceeds reliable performance.

Create conditions where a colleague can challenge an assumption without being dismissed. A challenge should identify the observed problem and consequence; the leader should acknowledge it and resolve the evidence. Do not confuse confidence with certainty. Debrief errors without humiliation so the team reports them early in a real emergency. Simulation should be demanding enough to expose decisions, not psychologically punitive.

Worked example: a communicator says the evacuation count is inconsistent while the leader is announcing all accounted for. Stop the announcement, check identities and issue a correction. Defending the earlier statement to avoid embarrassment turns a recoverable error into a dangerous shared belief.

lessons.title: Q101-10 — Stabilization, handover and recovery
lessons.body:
## Q101-10 — Stabilization, handover and recovery

Stabilization means the situation has stopped deteriorating under defined conditions; it does not mean every hazard is gone. Confirm what remains uncertain and which controls must stay in place. Formally hand over command or shift responsibility with a readback of the current state, people status, response teams, outstanding decisions, resource commitments and next review time. Inform affected parties of the transfer.

Recovery and restart follow authorized technical and management processes. Preserve isolations, permits and evidence until their disposition is approved. Do not reset an incident merely because alarms disappear. Establish welfare and communication arrangements for people affected by the event, and preserve a factual record for review. A debrief should identify both individual development and system improvements, assign owners and define how completion will be checked.

Worked example: the apparent leak has stopped after shutdown, but one valve position remains unverified and a response team has not reported back. The incoming manager must receive those unresolved facts. A handover labeled incident closed would conceal both a plant uncertainty and a people-accounting problem.

lessons.title: Q101-11 — Integrated initial practice and development
lessons.body:
## Q101-11 — Integrated initial practice and development

Initial training deliberately combines instruction, practice, feedback and repeated application. Each participant leads at least two different emergency scenarios and also experiences a support role. A written answer alone cannot demonstrate command communication, delegation or adaptation to new evidence. The instructor observes decisions and their reasoning, then gives specific feedback tied to the scenario evidence.

Use the first developmental run to identify gaps, practice changed situations and then perform an independently observed run. Separate coached practice from unprompted evidence in the record. Produce an individual development plan that states the gap, its consequence, the required practice or workplace exposure, supervisor and review point. A package certificate should describe initial training completed; it must not imply readiness for appointment as an emergency commander.

Worked example: a learner can state the escalation rule but waits too long to apply it when the simulation changes. The development plan should require practice recognizing and acting on the trigger, not simply rereading a definition. Reassess with a different event and timing so success demonstrates transfer of learning rather than recall of the script.

---

lessons.title: VUC101 instructor guide, scenario workbook and forms
lessons.body: # VUC101 instructor guide, scenario workbook and forms

lessons.title: Delivery resources and safety
lessons.body:
## Delivery resources and safety

Provide an isolated emergency-management room or accessible remote simulation environment with shared situation board, timestamped message cards, fictional installation plan, roster, resource cards, radio/voice role play, decision log and printed fallback documents. Never call real emergency services, trigger live alarms, operate plant or create physical hazards. Instructor/controller, independent observer and role players for CRO, response leader, muster, shore and relief are required. Combine roles only when identity and timing remain clear. Every learner leads A and B and supports another run; rotate assignments without reusing an already revealed assessment sequence as independent evidence.

Explain stop word, real-emergency response, privacy and recording, breaks and fitness demands. Obtain relevant fitness declaration and accommodations without asking the class to disclose private medical details. Pause unsafe/distressing simulation. Use realistic decision pressure, not intimidation. Provide interface familiarization before scoring. Additional time is required if the cohort cannot receive individual observation within the planned hours.

Instructor adaptation sheet A101: model/version___ emergency plan___ succession___ authority boundaries___ hazard/route/refuge data___ actual resource capability___ communications/fallback___ people baseline___ medical interface___ external-agency contacts (simulated)___ escalation triggers___ recovery authority___ accessibility___ controller/observer approval___. Real-asset delivery must substitute approved site information and validate all interactions. The self-contained model below supports the original initial course only.

lessons.title: Fictional plan Juniper J101
lessons.body:
## Fictional plan Juniper J101

Modules P process, U utilities, TR refuge and E evacuation point. R1 crosses P; R2 connects U to TR; R3 connects TR to E. Route status changes only through controller evidence; unknown is not safe. The learner is assigned emergency manager for the simulation. CRO operates prescribed simulated protective controls; response leader proposes tactics and confirms team capability; muster reconciles people; communicator handles outside support; recorder keeps the action board. Shore advises and provides resources but does not silently take command. Deputy succession requires announced transfer and accepted handover.

For a credible release/fire report, activate simulated emergency organization and general alarm, direct CRO to follow the relevant protective response card, establish people status and restrict affected work. A control command without required feedback stays unconfirmed. No team enters a hazard area without response-leader assessment, plan safeguards and command authorization. No person is sent physically anywhere during this exercise. Roster correction requires identity/source/time. Primary channel E, approved alternate B; confirm two-way contact and critical readback. Only the controller can supply new plant/route/resource facts.

Escalate whenever source control, refuge, route, team capability or evacuation options deteriorate. Early outside support is permitted through the communicator. Capacity cards are hard fictional approved limits; overloading is prohibited. Provisional endurance/arrival times are estimates, not promises. Recovery requires technical safeguard verification, permit/isolation resolution and authorized release; initial management training does not teach plant restart sequences.

lessons.title: Scenario A — initially controllable utility incident
lessons.body:
## Scenario A — initially controllable utility incident

Start 09:00, roster A01–A12. One qualified response team available; a second appears on an old plan but cannot be staffed. R1 unavailable, R2/R3 initially available. TR not initially threatened. One simulated medical responder available. Primary channel E functional; B can be tested. No real firefighting or treatment occurs.

At 0 minutes CRO reports smoke in U and one worker A12 last seen there. The learner must activate, establish command/objectives, obtain evidence and delegate roles. At 3 minutes CRO reports protective command sent with no feedback; learner must retain unconfirmed status and request the prescribed failure response. At 5 minutes response leader reports route R2 currently usable but requests clarity on objectives and withdrawal conditions. Learner must provide constraints without prescribing specialist entry technique. At 7 minutes muster lists A01–A10, A10, A11: eleven unique; A12 unaccounted. At 9 minutes shore asks to restart a utility to reduce production loss. Learner must reject unsupported restart and preserve command boundary. At 11 minutes communicator reads back R1 instead of R2; learner corrects it. At 13 minutes CRO supplies confirmed protective state and response leader reports incident controlled under the fictional plan, no entry needed. At 15 minutes Medic verifies A12 at the medical point with source/time; count becomes twelve. At 18 minutes controller reports no continuing smoke but one detector fault remains. Learner must distinguish stable from cleared for restart. At 20 minutes relief requests handover. Require accepted transfer, unresolved fault, people status, resource status and recovery owner. Debrief evidence and specific development needs.

Controller supplies confirmation only after the relevant request/action; do not reward assumed results. If learner orders unassessed entry, unauthorized restart or false all-accounted announcement, stop that branch and record the critical error. During developmental practice explain and rehearse the correction; a later changed unprompted run is required for independent evidence.

lessons.title: Scenario B — escalating release and loss of options
lessons.body:
## Scenario B — escalating release and loss of options

Start 14:00, roster B01–B20. Process P release reports are credible. One team available. R1 crosses P and is unavailable; R2 initially available; R3 initially available. Two fictional evacuation means each have 12 approved places; initially both listed available. TR provisional endpoint 14:30 depends on current protection. Shore rescue initially estimated 20 minutes but not dispatched. Actual simulation carries no people or equipment.

At 0 minutes activate organization and set protective objectives. At 3 minutes CRO reports source isolation attempted/unconfirmed and a continuing release indication. At 5 minutes response leader reports the planned approach unavailable; learner must reassess rather than order any-route entry. At 7 minutes muster provides B01–B18, B18, B19: nineteen unique, B20 missing. At 9 minutes one evacuation means becomes unavailable: available capacity falls from 24 to 12, gap eight. At 11 minutes shore says rescue availability is uncertain and has no confirmed arrival; learner must not build a plan around the old estimate. At 13 minutes B20 is verified at another muster point: twenty confirmed. At 15 minutes preparation/movement estimate is 11 minutes; provisional endpoint 14:30 leaves 15 minutes, nominal margin four. Immediately introduce TR intake protection failure and R3 status uncertain, invalidating the earlier planning assumptions. Learner must escalate, request confirmed alternatives and protect remaining options without overloading. At 17 minutes E fails; require tested B and a current situation update. At 19 minutes a junior role player challenges an obsolete all-clear statement on the board. Learner corrects it and redistributes workload. At 22 minutes controller provides a confirmed alternative resource under a separate approved fictional plan; the learner must request its capacity, timing, route and handover conditions rather than inventing them. Provide card ALT only on request: 20 places, ready at 14:25, access route R4 independently confirmed available by Field at 14:22, specialized operator retains tactical movement control. These facts do not restore the old TR guarantee; leader must coordinate under the updated plan and continue monitoring. End after an explicit decision, team briefing, accountability transfer plan and accepted relief, not after a cosmetic declaration of success.

lessons.title: Changed practice C
lessons.body:
## Changed practice C

Start 16:00 with 18 people C01–C18. Lists show C01–C16, C16, C17; C18 later verified by Medic. Two 10-place means, one unavailable: ten available, gap eight. Provisional refuge endpoint 16:24; at 16:12 estimated movement nine minutes gives nominal margin three, then a route-loss card invalidates it. Cause is loss of utilities with uncertain display quality rather than a repeat release. Add a missing team report, correctable channel mismatch and a shore request conflicting with local restrictions. Instructor validates tags and plan changes, gives the learner revised reference data, and observes changed decisions. Do not reuse an exact exposed sequence as a final independent run.

lessons.title: Laboratories and expected products
lessons.body:
## Laboratories and expected products

### W101-1 — Organization and activation
Prepare role/authority chart for J101, resolve the unstaffed second team and state three immediate objectives for A. Expected: one team, explicit operations/muster/communications/logging owners, command announced, life protection and accountability before production. Change: remove communicator and require a safe reallocation with monitoring preserved.

### W101-2 — Decision and communication record
Build an action log for A's unconfirmed isolation and wrong route readback. Expected: command versus achieved state separate, current route confirmed, wrong readback corrected, owner/deadline and acknowledgment recorded. Change: channel loss after transmission, requiring tested fallback and renewed current instruction.

### W101-3 — People and resources
Reconcile A, B and C. Expected unique counts initially 11, 19, 17; missing A12, B20, C18; after verified correction 12, 20, 18. B capacity 24 initially, 12 after loss, eight-person gap; C20 initially, 10 after loss, eight-person gap. Submit identities and evidence, not totals alone.

### W101-4 — Escalation and options
At B14:15 calculate 15 minus 11=4 nominal minutes. At C16:12 calculate 12 minus 9=3. Explain why protection/route loss invalidates a safe-waiting interpretation. Compare options with capacity, access, timing, uncertainty and authority. Expected: early escalation and verified alternatives, no overload or guaranteed rescue estimate.

### W101-5 — Relief and development
Produce accepted command handover and development plan from both runs. Include outstanding plant fault, people status, resource commitments, next review and recovery limits. Development entries must name observed behavior, consequence, practice, supervisor and evidence of improvement. Change: a valid colleague challenge arrives during handover; update before acceptance.

lessons.title: Observed stations and rubric
lessons.body:
## Observed stations and rubric

### P101-01 — Command boundary

Task: Establish the assigned emergency-manager role and resolve a conflicting shore instruction.

Required evidence: Authority confirmed; single current command announced; transfer recorded. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-02 — Readiness and roles

Task: Review available teams and allocate operations, muster, communications and logging.

Required evidence: No double-booking; capability gaps visible; each task has an owner. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-03 — Objectives

Task: Respond to first report and state immediate protective objectives.

Required evidence: Activation timely; objectives distinct from unsafe predetermined tactics. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-04 — Decision picture

Task: Maintain fact/assumption/unknown board through failed isolation.

Required evidence: Unconfirmed state retained; options and review triggers documented. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-05 — Delegation

Task: Assign response tasks, handle missed report and blocked route.

Required evidence: Constraints/readback/feedback clear; responder protection preserved. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-06 — Communications

Task: Correct wrong readback, test fallback and request outside support.

Required evidence: Receipt established; provisional resource timing not treated as guaranteed. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-07 — People

Task: Reconcile duplicate muster and later medical report.

Required evidence: Unique identity count correct; missing status and corrections traceable. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-08 — Escalation

Task: Recalculate options after evacuation-capacity or refuge loss.

Required evidence: Capacity/time arithmetic correct; uncertainty and early decision explicit. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-09 — Team performance

Task: Respond to challenge and overload without losing monitoring.

Required evidence: Challenge checked; workload redistributed with confirmed ownership. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-10 — Recovery

Task: Transfer command and identify unresolved recovery constraints.

Required evidence: Acceptance and communication explicit; no premature restart/closure. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

### P101-11 — Integrated development

Task: Lead both different scenarios and produce individual development plan.

Required evidence: Observed actions support result; coaching distinguished; next development specific. Record source, action/time, feedback and observer rationale.

Use 0–4 per dimension: 0 absent/unsafe; 1 major help; 2 safe but incomplete/prompted; 3 independent, sound and traceable; 4 independent with well-timed anticipation and clear reasoning. Require 36/44, every dimension at least 3, no unresolved critical error, and two manager-role scenarios satisfactory independently. Initial coached practice is developmental and separately labeled. The VNDRLY decision rule is not claimed as an external assessment rule. Critical errors: unsupported hazardous deployment, deliberate overload, false all-accounted declaration, unauthorized restart/bypass, concealment of loss of protection, or abandoning command without required transfer. Freeze unsafe simulated action, record and remediate; use a changed run to demonstrate correction.

lessons.title: Reproducible forms
lessons.body:
## Reproducible forms

O101 organization: manager/deputy___ operations___ people___ communications___ recorder___ available resources/limits___ gaps/owner___ command announced/time___.

S101 situation: time___ source___ confirmed facts___ reports___ assumptions___ unknowns___ current objectives___ threatened option___ decision trigger___ next review___.

D101 decision/action: decision/time___ reason/evidence___ options/constraints___ authority___ owner___ required feedback/deadline___ readback___ actual result___ reassessment/correction___.

P101 people: ID___ baseline___ location/source/time___ duplicate___ missing last-known___ verified correction___ transfer/destination/receipt___ coordinator update___.

R101 resources: resource/operator___ confirmed capacity___ availability/time/source___ access___ limitations___ request/confirmation___ assignment___ return/relief___.

H101 handover: current command/time___ incident/objectives___ people/responders___ plant/protection___ resources___ unresolved decisions___ recovery constraints___ next review___ incoming readback/acceptance___ parties notified___.

E101 observation: learner/role/scenario/version___ inject/action times___ station score/evidence___ coaching provided___ critical issue___ feedback___ changed demonstration___ assessor/date___.

G101 development: observed gap___ operational consequence___ needed knowledge/practice___ employer supervisor___ planned opportunity/date___ evidence required___ review result___ appointment limitation___.

lessons.title: Written assessment, remediation and completion
lessons.body:
## Written assessment, remediation and completion

Twenty-two formative checks and five labs must be corrected with explanations. Separate controlled final has 11 cases/33 decisions, 66 points, pass 53 and at least 4/6 each domain, no critical error; 120 minutes. Private keys and changed retake remain instructor-only. Review failed reasoning, practice changed examples and use the changed form without coaching. Preserve unsuccessful and successful records. Second competent reviewer handles disputed or borderline decisions using the recorded evidence, not a lowered threshold.

Issue VNDRLY/U Major Emergency Management — Initial Response Training only after all required learning, written and observed practice decisions pass. Record identity, version/hash, dates, scenario roles, assessor and individual development plan. It documents initial training and simulation performance, not independent emergency-manager competence, OPITO certification or asset appointment. Employer development continues through local familiarization, drills, supervised role experience and applicable formal assessment. The public external initial award has no expiry; do not invent an external expiry for this original certificate. Set local development/review dates based on change and performance rather than describing training as permanent operational readiness.


---

content.title: VUC101 | VUC101 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC101 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC101 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q101-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-01-L1

Does initial training appoint the emergency commander?

**Answer:** No. Appointment and asset competence remain employer responsibilities.

**Reason/remediation:** Training evidence has a defined scope. Revisit Q101-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-01-L2

Does a shore adviser automatically take command?

**Answer:** No. Confirm the plan authority and explicitly communicate any transfer.

**Reason/remediation:** Ambiguous command can produce conflicting instructions. Revisit Q101-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-02-L1

Two teams are listed but only one can be staffed. What is available?

**Answer:** One team; record the gap and revise the response options.

**Reason/remediation:** A list does not create personnel. Revisit Q101-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-02-L2

What must a delegated task include?

**Answer:** Named owner, outcome, constraints, feedback and review time.

**Reason/remediation:** Unowned tasks can disappear during escalation. Revisit Q101-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-03-L1

Must the exact failed component be known before raising the prescribed alarm?

**Answer:** No. Act on sufficient hazard evidence under the plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Perfect diagnosis can delay protection. Revisit Q101-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-03-L2

Is send a team through R1 an objective or tactic?

**Answer:** A tactic requiring route and capability assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** The objective is the protective outcome, not a predetermined method. Revisit Q101-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-04-L1

Isolation is commanded without feedback. What goes on the board?

**Answer:** Attempted/unconfirmed isolation, source/time and follow-up owner.

**Reason/remediation:** Command is not result. Revisit Q101-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-04-L2

When should an option be reviewed?

**Answer:** At its stated trigger, failed result or material new evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Continuing an obsolete option can worsen exposure. Revisit Q101-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-05-L1

A team route becomes blocked. May it use any alternative?

**Answer:** No. Obtain the competent response assessment and required safeguards.

**Reason/remediation:** Urgency does not establish route safety. Revisit Q101-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-05-L2

Does delegation remove command oversight?

**Answer:** No. Track progress, constraints and interactions.

**Reason/remediation:** Tasks can conflict or fail after assignment. Revisit Q101-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-06-L1

A rescue asset may arrive in twenty minutes. Is that confirmed protection?

**Answer:** No. Record provisional status and obtain dispatch/arrival confirmation.

**Reason/remediation:** Estimates can change. Revisit Q101-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-06-L2

A critical message has no readback. What is its state?

**Answer:** Unconfirmed; re-establish receipt and understanding through the approved channel.

**Reason/remediation:** Transmission alone is insufficient. Revisit Q101-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-07-L1

A person appears at muster and medical. Count twice?

**Answer:** No. Reconcile identity and movement.

**Reason/remediation:** Duplicate records can conceal a missing person. Revisit Q101-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-07-L2

Who directs medical treatment?

**Answer:** Appropriately qualified medical personnel.

**Reason/remediation:** Management coordinates resources without inventing treatment. Revisit Q101-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-08-L1

Forty people, two 24-place means, one unavailable: what is the gap?

**Answer:** Available capacity is 24; gap is 16.

**Reason/remediation:** Nominal capacity is not available capacity. Revisit Q101-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-08-L2

Does a three-minute nominal margin permit three minutes waiting?

**Answer:** No. Account for uncertainty and changing conditions under the plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Endurance assumptions may fail. Revisit Q101-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-09-L1

A colleague challenges all accounted. What next?

**Answer:** Pause/correct the announcement and reconcile evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Preserving face is less important than an accurate shared picture. Revisit Q101-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-09-L2

What is an early sign of overload?

**Answer:** Missed messages, fixation or incompatible simultaneous tasks.

**Reason/remediation:** Ask for support and redistribute work explicitly. Revisit Q101-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-10-L1

Alarms clear but valve state is unknown. Is recovery complete?

**Answer:** No. Retain uncertainty and apply authorized recovery checks.

**Reason/remediation:** Alarm disappearance is not verification. Revisit Q101-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-10-L2

What makes a command handover complete?

**Answer:** Explicit acceptance of current state, people, tasks, limits and next decisions, communicated to affected roles.

**Reason/remediation:** Departure alone does not transfer responsibility. Revisit Q101-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q101-11-L1

Does a coached scenario count as independent performance?

**Answer:** No. Record coaching and obtain changed unprompted evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Assessment must distinguish assistance from capability. Revisit Q101-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q101-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q101-11-L2

What should a development plan contain?

**Answer:** Specific gap, consequence, practice, supervisor and review evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** A generic promise to improve is not actionable. Revisit Q101-11 and perform its changed application.


---

# VUC101 source and coverage record

Reviewed 18 November 2026. Original VNDRLY initial training, not an OPITO-approved course or copied assessment.

| Primary source | Basis used | Coverage and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| [OPITO 7228 public product](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/major-emergency-management-initial-response-training) | Initial emergency-team development in command, control, communication and stress; each learner practices manager role in at least two scenario types; no entry prerequisite or external expiry | Q1–11 and A/B role rotation. Public external schedule is26hours; this original package plans32hours. Full proprietary criteria unavailable, so full equivalence is not asserted. |
| [HSE emergency-plan inspection guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/offshore/assets/docs/ed-evacuation-escape-rescue.pdf) | Defined emergency organization and adequate resources underpin a usable plan | Q1–2,5–8; organization/resource forms. Fictional J101 is not a real installation plan. |

All endpoints and capacities are invented exercise data, not universal limits. |
| [HSE control room design](https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeascontrol.htm) | Human/interface/team conditions affect reliable emergency control | Q4,6,9; status feedback, workload and communication exercises. Contextual guidance, not an offshore legal equivalence claim. |
| [HSE PFEER ACOP](https://www.hse.gov.uk/PuBns/books/l65.htm) | UK offshore fire/explosion and emergency-response context | Scope/adaptation boundaries; real jurisdiction and employer plan determine applicable duties. |

Coverage: Q1→P1/W1; Q2→P2/W1; Q3→P3/W1; Q4→P4/W2; Q5→P5/W2; Q6→P6/W2; Q7→P7/W3; Q8→P8/W4; Q9→P9/W5; Q10→P10/W5; Q11→P11/A/B/development record. Each domain has two explained formative questions and separate final/changed-retake three-decision cases. Stations 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 11 require observed role-play performance; 2, 7, 10 include observed record/review tasks. All 11 dimensions are assessed; neither a reading check nor a certificate substitutes for employer appointment.

Source limitations are explicit: no inaccessible full specification is represented as reviewed, no external credential awarded, and no actual learner performance claimed by authoring this package. Local data, competent delivery and documented learner evidence are required when the materials are used.

content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Offshore Muster Checker — Workplace Competence
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Offshore Muster Checker — Workplace Competence

VUC102 • Original materials • 18 November 2026

Scope: identity-based accounting at an assigned offshore muster point, reporting and transfer under the installation emergency plan. Not OPITO approval, a coordinator qualification or authority to command searches/evacuation. Full proprietary criteria were unavailable; public source scope informs this original program.

Entry to this VNDRLY workplace route requires local induction, role familiarization and safe participation in approved drills. The public external product lists no formal entry requirements; local safety preparation is not waived by that fact. Planned learning/review allocation 24 hours: 8 instruction, 4 labs, 4 guided practice, 6 observed workplace-drill evidence/review, 2 written assessment. Workplace scheduling may require longer.

Objectives: prepare current records/equipment, reach an authorized safe point, verify identities, reconcile discrepancies, report accurately, assist orderly muster, preserve identity during movement and hand over reliably.

lessons.title: Q102-01 — Role, authority and workplace readiness
lessons.body:
## Q102-01 — Role, authority and workplace readiness

A muster checker establishes who is physically present at an assigned muster point, records reliable identity evidence and reports discrepancies to the muster coordinator. The checker does not independently declare the whole installation accounted for, order a search or authorize evacuation. Learn the installation's alarm meanings, assigned point, alternate point, communications, relief arrangements and escalation path. A local role card must identify who receives reports and who can direct relocation.

Before duty, verify the current roster source, revision and time, working radio or approved alternative, forms, writing materials and any electronic reader. Know how to continue if power or network access fails. Confirm the arrangements for visitors, contractors, response personnel, people receiving assistance and those at medical facilities. A person absent from your point may be elsewhere under an authorized arrangement, but that must be confirmed rather than assumed.

Worked case: the checker receives an older printed list and a newer electronic update adding a contractor. Retain the versions, establish the authorized current baseline and tell the coordinator about any unresolved discrepancy. Do not discard the contractor because the person does not fit the old list. Workplace competence requires observed performance in approved local drills, not only this reading.

lessons.title: Q102-02 — Responding to an alarm and reaching the assigned point
lessons.body:
## Q102-02 — Responding to an alarm and reaching the assigned point

On alarm, follow the installation's emergency instructions and use the safe designated route. Collect only the role equipment the plan requires and permits; do not delay to retrieve personal property or a missing device from an unsafe area. Assess route information and report a blocked or threatened path. An alternate muster point is used according to the plan and command instruction, not chosen silently because it is convenient.

At the point, identify yourself, establish communication with the coordinator and report readiness or limitations. Keep access and escape paths clear. Organize arrivals so identity checking does not create a dangerous queue. Instructions should be short and understandable in noise or stress. If an unsafe condition threatens the point, report it immediately and follow protective relocation arrangements; accurate paperwork never requires remaining in danger.

Worked case: the main route is closed by a drill card. The checker must use the prebriefed approved alternate, report the change and establish where people are being received. Continuing to the original point through the marked hazard to preserve the expected count is a failure, even if the register is later correct.

lessons.title: Q102-03 — Verifying identity and recording presence
lessons.body:
## Q102-03 — Verifying identity and recording presence

Record a person as present only using the approved verification method. This may combine direct observation, name/identifier confirmation and an authorized electronic system. A scanned card without its holder is not proof that the person is at muster. Similar names, shared surnames, nicknames and borrowed badges require resolution through the approved identity process. Do not guess to keep the line moving.

Separate arrival time, verified presence and other reported locations. Mark entries clearly and preserve corrections. An electronic check can assist but must not erase uncertainty from a mismatch or failed device. If a person is not on the expected list, keep them safe, record the identity as unlisted/unreconciled and notify the coordinator. Do not send an unlisted person away merely because the software has no matching row.

Worked case: two workers named Sam Lee have different identifiers S14 and S41. A verbal Sam is here cannot mark both present. Confirm each individual identity and report the remaining uncertainty. If one person carries both cards, the second card remains unverified; duplicate credentials do not create a second person.

lessons.title: Q102-04 — Reconciling duplicates, missing people and roster changes
lessons.body:
## Q102-04 — Reconciling duplicates, missing people and roster changes

Use identity-based reconciliation. Compare the authorized baseline with verified arrivals and authorized location reports, retaining the distinction between what your point confirms and what the coordinator confirms elsewhere. Remove duplicate counting without deleting the evidence that produced the discrepancy. A complete numerical total can still be wrong when one identity appears twice and another is missing.

Report missing or unconfirmed identities promptly with last-known information and its source/time. Do not conduct an independent search or ask another attendee to go back into the installation. Command uses the information to decide the response. If a person later arrives or is verified elsewhere, issue a correction with time and source so the coordinator can update the installation picture. Baseline changes must be authorized and traceable; a verbal claim that someone left before the alarm is not enough to silently remove them.

Worked case: expected IDs A01–A10; received list A01–A08, A08, A09. There are ten entries but nine unique people; A10 is unconfirmed. Report nine locally verified, one duplicate and A10 unresolved. If the coordinator later confirms A10 with the medic, record that as coordinator-confirmed elsewhere, not physically present at your point.

lessons.title: Q102-05 — Communicating counts and discrepancies
lessons.body:
## Q102-05 — Communicating counts and discrepancies

Use the prescribed report format: point, time, roster version, expected identities or count, verified local count, unlisted people, duplicates, missing/unconfirmed identities, hazards and assistance needs. State what is known and what is still being checked. Obtain acknowledgment and correct a wrong readback. Keep records of both original and updated reports so a late correction does not appear to be a new person.

If communication fails, use the approved fallback and verify receipt. Do not assume a message sent through a device reached the coordinator. Avoid broadcasting unnecessary medical or personal details on an open channel; provide the operational information and use the approved private route for sensitive details. Maintain updates when the situation changes, not only at the initial count.

Worked case: the checker reports nine at Point A, but the coordinator reads nineteen. Correct the number and point immediately using the agreed clear phrasing, then obtain the correct readback. A hurried yes can add ten imaginary people to the emergency picture.

lessons.title: Q102-06 — Maintaining an orderly and accessible muster
lessons.body:
## Q102-06 — Maintaining an orderly and accessible muster

People may arrive frightened, confused, injured or unfamiliar with the location. Give calm, concise directions and explain that they must remain available for further instructions. Keep walkways clear and do not physically restrain people. Use the installation's arrangements for language, hearing, mobility or other assistance needs. Ask for the designated assistance resource; do not improvise a lift or medical treatment beyond training.

Monitor the point's conditions and attendance after the initial count. Someone who leaves for medical care, a response role or relocation must be recorded and reported under the plan. A count taken once becomes stale when people move. Report deterioration such as smoke, crowding or a blocked exit. Follow command directions and the local emergency plan if the point must be cleared.

Worked case: a person needs assistance and the assigned helper is absent. Tell the coordinator immediately and request the approved replacement arrangement. Do not mark the assistance complete because it is written on the plan. Keep the person informed and preserve safe access while the response is arranged.

lessons.title: Q102-07 — Relocation and evacuation handover
lessons.body:
## Q102-07 — Relocation and evacuation handover

Relocation creates a risk of losing or double-counting people between points. Before movement, follow the authorized instruction and verify the destination, route, responsible receiving role and communications. Record the identities transferred, departure time and receiving acknowledgment. Reconcile the receiving list with the outgoing list; a total alone cannot reveal a substitution or duplicate.

The checker supports orderly movement but does not override the responsible transport operator's capacity or safety requirements. Do not mark people evacuated when they are only queued, assigned seats or listed on a plan. Distinguish departed, received and unconfirmed transit status. If an individual cannot be accounted for at destination, report the discrepancy immediately using last-known facts without launching an unauthorized search.

Worked case: eight people leave Point A for B. B confirms seven named identities and one duplicate. Seven unique arrivals are confirmed, not eight. Retain the missing identity and transfer time and notify the coordinator. Sending another person to fill the numerical gap would not resolve the original person's location.

lessons.title: Q102-08 — Degraded systems, relief and evidence
lessons.body:
## Q102-08 — Degraded systems, relief and evidence

A failed reader, network or printer does not end the duty to account for people. Use the approved paper fallback, current available roster and explicit uncertainty reporting. Reconcile paper and electronic records when service returns; do not import duplicates or overwrite the original event times. Record which source was used and when. Device recovery is not proof that missed arrivals were captured.

During relief, transfer the point status, roster version, local identities, people confirmed elsewhere, unresolved discrepancies, movements, hazards and unacknowledged reports. The relief checker reads back critical items and accepts the duty. Preserve evidence for the drill review with appropriate privacy controls. An assessment needs actual observation and traceable records; fabricated times or retrospective signatures cannot replace them.

Worked case: a reader recovers and uploads the same six arrivals already recorded on paper. Match identities and retain a single presence record with linked sources. Do not add the two sets and report twelve. Tell the coordinator how the reconciliation was performed and what remains uncertain.

lessons.title: Q102-09 — Practice, assessment and maintaining competence
lessons.body:
## Q102-09 — Practice, assessment and maintaining competence

Competence is demonstrated in the role during approved workplace drills with the actual local arrangements. The assessor observes preparation, route response, identity verification, reconciliation, communications, assistance, transfer and relief. Synthetic exercises help teach changed conditions but cannot establish that a person can operate the actual workplace system. No live emergency is required or deliberately created.

After each drill, compare the log with observed actions and coordinator acknowledgments. Identify errors in both individual performance and the system: stale rosters, unclear point labels, poor radio coverage or inaccessible instructions. Correct the root cause, practice a changed situation and reassess without coaching. Keep a record of what was observed rather than awarding competence for attendance.

Worked case: a learner passes the written questions but has not demonstrated paper fallback or a relocation handover at the workplace. Those evidence gaps remain open. Arrange approved drills that cover them. The full workplace certificate cannot be issued merely because the coursebook and quiz are complete.

---

lessons.title: VUC102 workplace assessment workbook
lessons.body: # VUC102 workplace assessment workbook

lessons.title: Resources, supervision and safe adaptation
lessons.body:
## Resources, supervision and safe adaptation

Use the actual installation's approved drill arrangements, current muster point/alternate, role card, roster system, radio/fallback, forms and assistance procedures. The duty holder approves timing, routes and operational interfaces. A competent muster-role assessor observes; a drill controller coordinates role players and stops unsafe activity. Do not trigger an unannounced alarm, obstruct an actual escape route, simulate a missing person by hiding someone in danger, or contact real emergency services. Faults and hazards are cards or isolated training-system states. Real emergency instructions override the exercise immediately.

For classroom practice use synthetic identities, mock cards/reader, paper lists, radios on a training channel and a marked safe room. No real personal data is required. Practice can be fully simulated, but the workplace award requires two observed approved workplace drills W1/W2 using the actual local system/arrangements and changed conditions. An actual emergency is not required. If workplace access is unavailable, record theory/simulation only and leave the workplace decision open.

Adaptation F102: site/point___ ERP/role-card revision___ alarm meanings___ designated/alternate route___ relocation authority___ coordinator/callsign___ current roster source/update authority___ approved identity methods___ reader/fallback___ assistance plan___ transfer/receipt method___ reporting format___ relief___ privacy/retention___ safe drill approval/date___ assessor competence___. Fill before W1/W2; do not invent local instructions from the fictional examples.

lessons.title: Practice data A — duplicate and medical location
lessons.body:
## Practice data A — duplicate and medical location

Authorized baseline A01–A10 at Point North; coordinator callsign Muster, primary channel 1, approved fallback 2. Point North safe in this fictional model. Arrivals: A01, A02, A03, A04, A05, A06, A07, A08, A08, A09. The repeated A08 is a duplicated entry for the same person. A10 is not yet confirmed. One role player holds A10's spare badge but is not A10. Expected initial report: nine unique local, one duplicate, A10 unconfirmed; spare badge does not change that.

At minute 3 coordinator reads nineteen instead of nine. Learner corrects and obtains accurate acknowledgment. At minute 5 reader fails; use paper. At minute 7 coordinator supplies verified medical-location report for A10, source Medic, time 09:07. Expected: nine local and one confirmed elsewhere, all ten identities reconciled by coordinator evidence; never ten local. At minute 9 an unlisted person X1 arrives. Record X1 safely as unlisted/unreconciled and notify coordinator; baseline amendment requires authorized evidence. At minute 11 controller provides authorized roster revision 2 adding X1 and verification of X1 identity. Expected: baseline 11, ten local (A01–A09, X1), one elsewhere(A10). At minute 13 relief arrives before an update acknowledgment; hand over the outstanding report and current categories explicitly.

Controller must not provide the correct count before learner reconciliation. A spare-card scan is accepted by the mock reader to test whether the learner checks the actual person. If learner reports the absent holder present, record a critical error and stop that branch. All participants remain in the safe practice area.

lessons.title: Practice data B — relocation and lost receipt
lessons.body:
## Practice data B — relocation and lost receipt

Baseline B01–B12 at Point East. Current roster revision 4. Primary route is unavailable by card; approved alternate route leads to East safely. Learner reports route change and point readiness. Actual arrivals B01–B12 verified individually. B07 needs the prebriefed approved assistance arrangement; assigned helper absent. Learner requests approved replacement and keeps access clear, without improvised physical handling. Controller supplies competent replacement and confirms briefing only after request.

At minute 5 coordinator authorizes relocation to West through approved route R2; receiving checker West acknowledges readiness. Record all 12 identities departing at 10:06. Receiving list at 10:09 is B01–B10, B10, B11: eleven unique, B12 unresolved. Learner must reconcile names and report B12's last confirmed departure, not declare twelve received. At minute 11 coordinator verifies B12 at medical, source Medic at 10:11: eleven West, one medical, all twelve reconciled across locations. At minute 13 primary channel fails before acknowledgment; test fallback and repeat the current report. At minute 15 restored reader imports the same original 12 arrivals; do not add them to current presence or undo the transfer. At minute 17 relief accepts current locations, record versions and outstanding items.

lessons.title: Changed practice C
lessons.body:
## Changed practice C

Baseline C01–C14; arrival entries C01–C12, C12, C13: thirteen unique, C14 unconfirmed. Two similar-name role players have distinct IDs C03/C11. Reader fails after seven verified entries; paper fallback covers remaining arrivals. Later C14 physically arrives: fourteen local. Coordinator authorizes five named transfers C01–C05; receiver initially confirms C01–C04, C04: four unique, C05 unresolved. A later verified receipt for C05 closes the transfer. Expected final local nine, receiver five, total fourteen. Give a wrong readback and a changed alternate-point instruction. Use this changed dataset after remediation; do not coach the arithmetic during an assessed run.

lessons.title: Workplace evidence W1 and W2
lessons.body:
## Workplace evidence W1 and W2

W1 must observe preparation, safe point establishment, actual identity checking, count/report, acknowledgment and relief during an approved workplace drill. W2 changes at least three conditions and must additionally cover device/communication fallback, a roster discrepancy, assistance coordination and a named relocation/receipt exercise. Use cards for dangerous/rare conditions; actual participants follow safe approved drill movements only. If a function cannot be demonstrated safely at the site, document the gap and arrange an approved equivalent workplace exercise—not a fabricated observation.

For each drill retain site/date/ERP version, roster revision or privacy-safe trace, observer notes, report/readback times, discrepancy/correction trail, transfer record and debrief. Competent witness statements supplement but do not replace the assessor's direct observation of critical decisions. Two dates or distinct approved drill events are required by this original package. The public external specification's exact evidence rules were unavailable; this is not an assertion of its prescribed drill count.

lessons.title: Application labs
lessons.body:
## Application labs

### W102-1 — Baseline and identity
Resolve old/current roster versions and the A spare badge. Submit authorized baseline/version, nine verified identities and A10 unresolved. Explain why a scan does not establish presence. Changed task: distinguish similar-name C03/C11 and record an unlisted attendee without excluding them from safety.

### W102-2 — Reconciliation and reporting
Compute A before/after medical confirmation and revision 2. Expected 9 local+1 elsewhere=10, then 10 local+1 elsewhere=11. Role-play nineteen/nine correction and obtain acknowledgment. Submit original and corrected reports with timestamps and source. Never silently rewrite the earlier report.

### W102-3 — Movement and receipt
Reconcile B twelve departures against eleven unique receipts and one medical confirmation. Submit B12 last-known evidence and final 11West+1 medical=12. Changed C transfer: 14 initial−5 departed=9 local; 4 received+1 unconfirmed until C05 confirmation, then 9+5=14.

### W102-4 — Fallback and relief
Reconcile paper/electronic duplicates without double-counting. For six paper arrivals plus the same six electronic entries, report six unique. Prepare relief with roster version, locations, assistance, unresolved messages and corrections. Role-play explicit readback and acceptance.

lessons.title: Observed station checklist
lessons.body:
## Observed station checklist

### P102-01 — Prepare

Task: Verify local role card, current roster, communications, forms and fallback.

Required evidence: Current baseline and limits established; role boundary understood. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-02 — Reach and establish point

Task: Follow approved route/alternate, establish point and report readiness.

Required evidence: No hazard crossing or silent relocation; access kept clear. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-03 — Verify identities

Task: Check actual attendees including similar names, unlisted person and spare badge.

Required evidence: No badge-only presence; unresolved identities retained safely. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-04 — Reconcile

Task: Compare baseline with duplicates and confirmed-elsewhere report.

Required evidence: Unique counts correct; local and elsewhere separated. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-05 — Report

Task: Give point/version/time/count/discrepancy report and correct wrong readback.

Required evidence: Correct acknowledgment and fallback demonstrated. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-06 — Maintain muster

Task: Handle assistance request and subsequent authorized movement.

Required evidence: Safe access and appropriate assistance; presence updated. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-07 — Transfer

Task: Record named departure and reconcile destination receipt.

Required evidence: Missing transit identity escalated; no false received status. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-08 — Fallback and relief

Task: Use paper during device failure, reconcile restored records and hand over.

Required evidence: No double-counting; unresolved items explicitly accepted. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

### P102-09 — Workplace integration

Task: Complete two changed approved workplace drills and debrief.

Required evidence: All functions observed with authentic evidence and no critical error. Record actual actions, times, sources and assessor rationale.

lessons.title: Forms
lessons.body:
## Forms

F102 readiness: learner/site/date___ point/alternate___ ERP revision___ roster version/time/source___ equipment/fallback___ coordinator___ assistance arrangements___ limitations/report___ approval___.

I102 identity record: ID___ expected/unlisted___ verified person/method/time___ local point___ reported-elsewhere/source/time___ duplicate/mismatch___ authorized correction___ current category___.

C102 count report: point/time/version___ baseline___ unique local___ confirmed elsewhere(source)___ unlisted___ missing IDs/last-known/source___ duplicates___ hazards/assistance___ receiver/readback/time___ correction/fallback___.

T102 movement: authority/time___ route/destination___ departing IDs/time___ receiving role/readiness___ received IDs/time___ discrepancy/last-known___ coordinator notified/ack___ final reconciliation___.

H102 relief: outgoing/incoming___ current point/roster___ verified identities/locations___ unresolved items___ assistance___ transfers___ unacknowledged reports___ records handed over___ readback/acceptance/time___.

E102 observation: drill W1/W2___ local approvals/version___ station___ observed behavior/time___ trace/witness___ score/reason___ critical issue___ remediation___ changed evidence___ assessor/date___.

D102 improvement: gap___ cause___ safe changed practice___ owner/date___ evidence required___ reassessment decision___ reviewer/appeal outcome___.

lessons.title: Assessment and credential rules
lessons.body:
## Assessment and credential rules

Nine dimensions scored 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent; 1 major help; 2 safe but incomplete/prompted; 3 independent accurate traceable; 4 independent with timely anticipation. Require 29/36, each at least 3, no critical error, all functions covered across W1/W2 with critical identity/report/transfer actions satisfactory independently. Critical errors: false presence/all-accounted report, deliberate duplicate counting, unsafe route/search instruction, unapproved overload or handling, fabricated evidence, or concealed missing transfer identity. Freeze unsafe simulation, preserve evidence, remediate and use changed observation. Do not average a critical failure into a pass.

Complete 18 formative checks with corrected reasoning and 4 labs. Controlled final: 9 cases, 27 decisions, 54 points, pass 44 and at least 4/6 each, no critical error, 90 minutes. Private changed retake and keys remain outside learner package. Assessors give formative feedback, then obtain unprompted changed evidence. Second competent reviewer resolves disputed decisions using the trace, not reduced criteria.

Only after knowledge and authentic workplace evidence pass issue VNDRLY/U Offshore Muster Checker — Workplace Assessed, with learner/site, scope, package hash, drill dates, assessor and limitations. If only simulated practice exists, label the result theory/simulation and do not use workplace-assessed wording. No OPITO certificate or appointment to coordinator/commander follows. Set a two-year VNDRLY review/renewal date and require earlier review after material change or performance concern; continued local drills remain necessary. The public OPITO product also lists two-year validity, but this certificate is independent. Materials completion is not evidence of any learner's workplace completion.


---

lessons.title: VUC102 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC102 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q102-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-01-L1

May a checker declare the entire installation accounted for?

**Answer:** No. Report the assigned-point evidence to the coordinator.

**Reason/remediation:** Local observation has a limited scope. Revisit Q102-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-01-L2

An old roster omits a newly authorized contractor. What next?

**Answer:** Establish the current authorized baseline and retain/report the discrepancy.

**Reason/remediation:** An outdated list is not authority to exclude someone. Revisit Q102-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-02-L1

A designated route is blocked. Continue to preserve the planned count?

**Answer:** No. Use the approved alternate arrangements and report the change.

**Reason/remediation:** Accounting does not justify exposure. Revisit Q102-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-02-L2

Should missing equipment be retrieved from an unsafe area?

**Answer:** No. Follow the emergency plan and report the limitation.

**Reason/remediation:** Role equipment does not outrank life protection. Revisit Q102-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-03-L1

One person carries two badges. Are two people present?

**Answer:** No. Verify each actual individual.

**Reason/remediation:** A credential scan is not a second human. Revisit Q102-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-03-L2

An unlisted person arrives. Send them away?

**Answer:** No. Keep them safe, record unlisted/unreconciled identity and notify the coordinator.

**Reason/remediation:** The roster discrepancy must be resolved without exposing the person. Revisit Q102-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-04-L1

A01–A08, A08, A09 against A01–A10: count and gap?

**Answer:** Nine unique; A10 unconfirmed.

**Reason/remediation:** Ten entries include a duplicate. Revisit Q102-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-04-L2

A10 is confirmed by the coordinator at medical. Mark locally present?

**Answer:** No. Record confirmed elsewhere with source/time.

**Reason/remediation:** Location categories must remain accurate. Revisit Q102-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-05-L1

Nine is read back as nineteen. What next?

**Answer:** Correct point/count and obtain accurate readback.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncorrected acknowledgment corrupts the shared picture. Revisit Q102-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-05-L2

No acknowledgment after sending a report: is it complete?

**Answer:** No. Use the approved fallback and confirm receipt.

**Reason/remediation:** Sent is not received. Revisit Q102-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-06-L1

An assistance helper is absent. Mark assistance complete?

**Answer:** No. Request the approved replacement and report the need.

**Reason/remediation:** Planned resources may not be available. Revisit Q102-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-06-L2

Does the initial count stay current when people leave?

**Answer:** No. Record authorized movement and report updated status.

**Reason/remediation:** Presence is time-dependent. Revisit Q102-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-07-L1

Eight depart, seven unique arrive plus a duplicate. What is confirmed?

**Answer:** Seven received and one identity unresolved in transit.

**Reason/remediation:** Eight entries do not establish eight arrivals. Revisit Q102-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-07-L2

People are queued for transport. Are they evacuated?

**Answer:** No. Record the actual stage and obtain departure/receipt evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** A plan is not completed movement. Revisit Q102-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-08-L1

Six paper arrivals reappear electronically. Count twelve?

**Answer:** No. Reconcile the same six identities across sources.

**Reason/remediation:** Duplicate data is not additional people. Revisit Q102-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-08-L2

What must relief accept?

**Answer:** Current roster, identities/locations, discrepancies, movements, hazards and unacknowledged reports.

**Reason/remediation:** Duty transfer requires a reliable picture. Revisit Q102-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q102-09-L1

Written pass but no workplace fallback demonstration: complete?

**Answer:** No. Obtain the missing observed evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Knowledge does not replace workplace performance. Revisit Q102-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q102-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q102-09-L2

How should a failed drill action be reassessed?

**Answer:** Remediate its cause and observe a changed uncoached drill.

**Reason/remediation:** Repeating a memorized sequence can conceal the gap. Revisit Q102-09 and perform its changed application.


---
