lessons.title: VUC102 sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC102 sources and coverage

Reviewed 18November 2026. Original workplace-assessment materials based on accessible primary sources, not copied external criteria.

| Primary source | Verified basis | Coverage/limit |
|---|---|---|
| [OPITO7057 public product](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/offshore-muster-checker-workplace-competence-assessment-standard) | Muster-checker assessment during offshore drills/scenarios; two mandatory units, no fixed assessment duration, two-year validity, no formal entry requirements | Q1–9,W1/W2 and credential boundary. Proprietary performance criteria unavailable; no full equivalence or external approval claimed. |
| [OPITO international emergency-response competence guidance](https://opito.com/assets/6.ENGLISH_International_ER_Guidelines_Final-rev-0-Amendment-8_MASTER-June-2019.pdf) | Historical guidance connects muster-role competence with local induction, workplace assessment and continuing offshore practice | Q1,9 and workplace evidence. Document dated2019, treated as historical guidance, not newer product criteria. |
| [OPITO workplace competence framework](https://opito.com/for-centres/workplace-competence-standards) | Workplace assessment uses occupationally competent assessors and actual operational context | W1/W2 evidence and assessor requirements; VNDRLY is not represented as an approved organization. |
| [HSE emergency-plan guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/offshore/assets/docs/ed-evacuation-escape-rescue.pdf) | Emergency organization includes distinct muster checker/coordinator and command roles within an installation plan | Q1–2,5–7; local role and transfer boundaries. No site-independent route or search authority inferred. |
| [HSE PFEER ACOP](https://www.hse.gov.uk/PuBns/books/l65.htm) | UK offshore emergency-response context | Site adaptation; other jurisdictions and employer arrangements must be identified separately. |

Trace: Q1/P1/W102-1; Q2/P2/workplace establishment; Q3/P3/W102-1; Q4/P4/W102-2; Q5/P5/W102-2; Q6/P6/workplace assistance; Q7/P7/W102-3; Q8/P8/W102-4; Q9/P9/W1/W2. Each chapter has two explained checks and a protected final/changed case with three decisions. P2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 require observed practical behavior; P1, 4 include observed document/reconciliation review. All 9 dimensions remain required.

All practice identities and timings are synthetic. Actual workplace data must be handled under the site's privacy/retention controls. No actual learner drill, identity verification or credential is asserted by authoring this package. Full workplace result cannot be inferred from classroom materials or a quiz.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Offshore Muster Coordinator — Workplace Competence
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Offshore Muster Coordinator — Workplace Competence

VUC103 • Original materials •18November 2026

Purpose: coordinate reliable installation-wide people accounting under the emergency plan. This is independent VNDRLY training/assessment, not OPITO approval or incident-command authority. Full proprietary criteria were unavailable. The public 7058 entry paragraph names the checker role; this apparent wording inconsistency is not used to invent coordinator prerequisites. This original workplace route requires local induction, role/system familiarization and safe drill participation.

Planned allocation 32 hours: 10 instruction, 6 labs, 4 guided practice, 10 workplace-drill observation/review, 2 written assessment. Allow additional scheduling time to obtain authentic evidence. Objectives: establish baseline, activate points, reconcile identities, escalate missing people, report accurately, track movement/capacity, coordinate assistance and hand over a traceable picture.

lessons.title: Q103-01 — Coordinator role and command interface
lessons.body:
## Q103-01 — Coordinator role and command interface

The muster coordinator combines reports from all muster points and other authorized locations into a single, identity-based account of people. The role is broader than checking one point: it resolves cross-point duplicates, tracks missing people, communicates the current picture to command and preserves accountability during relocation or evacuation. The coordinator does not independently direct rescue tactics or override the incident commander's authority.

Know the installation plan, reporting hierarchy, alternate arrangements and deputy role. Establish who verifies medical, response-team, transport and visitor information. Reports must state source and time. A point checker may confirm local presence, while a medic confirms a person in treatment; the coordinator reconciles those facts without counting one person twice. Report uncertainty explicitly so command can make informed decisions.

Worked example: Point A reports twelve and Point B reports eight against twenty people on board. The totals appear complete, but one identity occurs at both points and one is missing. The coordinator must compare identities rather than announce all accounted. A mathematically tidy sum is not a reliable emergency picture.

lessons.title: Q103-02 — Baseline, versions and readiness
lessons.body:
## Q103-02 — Baseline, versions and readiness

Establish the authoritative people-on-board baseline and the process for approved arrivals, departures and role changes. Record version, time and source. Prepare point assignments, checker contacts, assistance arrangements, current response-team roster and medical interface. Confirm backup forms and communications before duty. A live dashboard can still display an outdated roster; check its update status and known outages.

Control changes during an incident. A claim that someone left earlier must be supported by the authorized departure record before removing that person from the baseline. Keep unresolved claims visible. Unlisted arrivals are protected and recorded while their status is reconciled; they are not excluded from accountability simply because the baseline is incomplete. Retain an audit trail so a later reviewer can reconstruct the count at each decision time.

Worked example: baseline revision 5 lists twenty-four people, and a late update adds one contractor but lacks authorization. Record the contractor as unlisted/unreconciled and seek the authorized source. Do not silently change the expected count or reject the person's presence. Once the update is verified, issue revision 6 and reconcile all point reports to that baseline.

lessons.title: Q103-03 — Activating and supervising the muster network
lessons.body:
## Q103-03 — Activating and supervising the muster network

On alarm, activate the reporting arrangements allocated to the coordinator. Confirm which checkers are at their points, which points are usable and what fallback arrangements are active. A missing checker report can reflect failed communications or an unsafe location; it does not prove zero people at that point. Assign an owner to resolve the gap and inform command of its consequence.

Set a concise reporting rhythm appropriate to the emergency plan and event. Request initial reports promptly, then updates for changed identities, movements, hazards and assistance needs. Avoid flooding checkers with duplicate demands from multiple channels. If a point relocates, retain its identity and records through the transfer and establish the receiving contact. Never instruct a checker to remain in a threatened area merely to complete a count.

Worked example: Point East is unavailable. The checker reports moving under the approved plan to West. The coordinator records the alternate arrangement, informs command and requests named transfer/receipt evidence. Treating East as missing and West's arrivals as new people would create both a false deficit and duplicates.

lessons.title: Q103-04 — Cross-point identity reconciliation
lessons.body:
## Q103-04 — Cross-point identity reconciliation

Build the global picture from unique identifiers and current verified locations. Keep local presence, confirmed elsewhere, in-transit and unconfirmed categories distinct. Resolve overlap by asking both sources for identity, time and movement evidence. Do not select the more convenient count without checking. A person can legitimately move between points, but the record must show when and where the current status was confirmed.

Use set-based thinking: the global count is the number of unique confirmed identities, not the sum of report rows. Compare that set with the authorized baseline to identify missing and extra identities. Unlisted people require a separate resolution path. Preserve original reports and append corrections. A total can exceed the baseline because of duplicates, an unlisted arrival, or both; the cause matters.

Worked example: A has P01–P10 and B has P10–P19 against P01–P20. Each point reports ten, yet the union has nineteen unique people. P10 is duplicated and P20 unconfirmed. If Medic verifies P20, the global count becomes twenty, but P10's current location still needs reconciliation for accurate movement planning.

lessons.title: Q103-05 — Missing-person and discrepancy escalation
lessons.body:
## Q103-05 — Missing-person and discrepancy escalation

A missing-person report should identify the person, last confirmed location/time, likely task if known, source reliability, relevant hazards and actions already taken to verify records. Distinguish unconfirmed because a report is missing from a confirmed absence at a checked location. Both can require urgent attention, but they are different evidence states. Give command the facts promptly; do not wait to perfect every field before reporting a serious gap.

Coordinate verification through safe, authorized channels. Do not order a checker or attendee into a hazard to find a missing colleague. Search and rescue decisions belong to command and trained response roles. When new evidence locates the person, verify the source and update command and affected checkers. Preserve the earlier discrepancy and correction times so a stale missing-person message does not continue to drive action.

Worked example: a coworker says P20 probably went to medical. Record this as an unverified lead and ask the medical interface for confirmation. Do not change P20 to accounted merely because the explanation sounds plausible. Once Medic confirms identity and location at a stated time, update the picture and obtain acknowledgment of the correction.

lessons.title: Q103-06 — Command reporting and communication resilience
lessons.body:
## Q103-06 — Command reporting and communication resilience

Report baseline version, unique confirmed total, category/location breakdown, unresolved identities, unlisted people, response-team status, assistance needs and point hazards. State the timestamp and limitations. A concise summary should let command understand both the number and the remaining uncertainty. Do not use all accounted while any required identity is unresolved, even when raw totals match.

Obtain readback for critical counts and instructions, correct errors, and log acknowledgment. Use approved fallback when a channel fails; a sent update is not necessarily received. Maintain a single controlled global record while allowing local fallback forms. Reconcile updates after service returns without importing duplicates or replacing actual event times with upload time. Protect sensitive information and use appropriate channels for medical details.

Worked example: command reads twenty-nine when the coordinator reports nineteen confirmed and one unconfirmed. Correct the statement immediately, including the baseline and unresolved identity. A simple yes to end the exchange would mislead the emergency decision maker.

lessons.title: Q103-07 — Relocation, evacuation and transport accountability
lessons.body:
## Q103-07 — Relocation, evacuation and transport accountability

Maintain accountability through every movement stage: selected, departed, received and verified at destination. Use named lists and responsible handover roles. Coordinate with command, checkers and the relevant transport operator, who retains authority over capacity and safe operation. A seat allocation or boarding list is not proof of departure, and departure is not proof of receipt.

Reconcile each movement against the previous location and global baseline. Do not remove a person from all records while in transit. If destination reports fewer unique identities than departed, retain the specific discrepancy and last-known time. Report changes to command before relying on an apparently complete evacuation total. People at medical or in response teams may have separate arrangements that must join the global record.

Worked example: twelve depart A, destination confirms eleven unique plus a duplicate. Eleven are received and one remains unconfirmed in transit. The installation total should not drop by twelve and rise by twelve automatically. Preserve the named gap until authorized evidence resolves it.

lessons.title: Q103-08 — Assistance, capacity and changing conditions
lessons.body:
## Q103-08 — Assistance, capacity and changing conditions

The coordinator helps command understand practical constraints on moving and accounting for people. Track approved assistance needs, available helpers, medical movement requirements and point capacity according to the local plan. Do not improvise medical treatment or physical handling. A planned helper who is absent is a resource gap needing resolution, not a completed arrangement.

Report threatened muster/refuge locations and unavailable transport capacity promptly. Capacity calculations use confirmed available means, not nominal equipment on a diagram. Never solve a shortfall by overloading. Time estimates and route availability can change; state assumptions and relay changes to the responsible decision maker. The coordinator provides accountability and resource facts while command decides the response.

Worked example: twenty-six people remain, two fictional means each have sixteen approved places, but one is unavailable. Available capacity is sixteen, leaving ten without that option. Report the gap and assistance needs; do not describe thirty-two nominal places as sufficient. Request confirmed alternative arrangements through command.

lessons.title: Q103-09 — Relief, records and recovery
lessons.body:
## Q103-09 — Relief, records and recovery

A coordinator handover transfers the whole accountability picture, not just a final number. Include baseline/version, unique identities by current status, unresolved discrepancies, point conditions, assistance, movements awaiting receipt, unacknowledged messages and next update. The incoming coordinator reads back critical gaps and accepts responsibility. Inform command and checkers of the change.

Preserve original reports, corrections, event times and source references under the site's privacy and retention rules. Do not delete a mistaken all-accounted report; correct it and ensure recipients received the correction. After the drill, compare records with observed movements and identify system weaknesses. Recovery does not erase the need to confirm that all transferred people were received and all response personnel have a known status.

Worked example: the system is restored and its dashboard says twenty-five, while the controlled paper record says twenty-four plus one unresolved. Reconcile identities and source times before handing over. The cleaner electronic display cannot automatically overrule the documented uncertainty.

lessons.title: Q103-10 — Workplace demonstration and continuing practice
lessons.body:
## Q103-10 — Workplace demonstration and continuing practice

The assessor must observe coordination across multiple reporting sources in approved workplace drills. Evidence includes readiness, activation, identity reconciliation, discrepancy escalation, communication, movement tracking, assistance coordination and relief. Classroom exercises teach the method but do not prove competence using the actual installation arrangements. No genuine emergency is required or created.

Use changed drills to demonstrate that the learner can cope with a lost point report, duplicate identity, baseline change and movement discrepancy. Record coaching separately from independent performance. A failed critical report requires remediation and changed reassessment. Continuing drills and review after roster-system, role or plan changes maintain competence; a certificate alone does not keep the emergency picture accurate.

Worked example: a candidate reconciles one muster point perfectly but has never coordinated a cross-point duplicate or transfer. The coordinator evidence is incomplete. Arrange approved multi-point exercises rather than awarding the broader role on the strength of checker experience alone.

---

content.title: VUC103 | VUC103 multi-point workplace workbook
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC103 multi-point workplace workbook
lessons.body: # VUC103 multi-point workplace workbook

lessons.title: Delivery and evidence setting
lessons.body:
## Delivery and evidence setting

Use the installation's approved emergency-drill arrangements, current people-on-board system, point checker contacts, communications, fallback forms, movement records and command interface. Duty holder approves safe timing and drill routes. A competent coordinator-role assessor directly observes; controller and role players cover two or more points, medical, response-team contact, command, transport and relief. No live emergency, unsafe search, blocked escape route or unauthorized alarm is created. Hazards and unavailable equipment are simulated by cards; actual participant movement follows approved safe drill routes. Stop the exercise for a real emergency.

Classroom resources: synthetic identity cards, named rosters, shared board, paper backup, isolated reader/dashboard mock-up, training radio/voice channel, clocks and forms below. Keep real personal data out of practice datasets. Explain stop word, fitness demands, breaks, accessibility, privacy and real-emergency override. Do not punish a learner with unnecessary distress or require physical handling beyond approved arrangements.

Workplace result requires two approved multi-point drill cycles W1/W2 using actual local systems and role interfaces. Simulation-only work earns only a clearly limited theory/simulation record. No authentic workplace observation is claimed by this materials package. The two-cycle rule is VNDRLY's original evidence requirement, not a claim about inaccessible external criteria.

Adaptation A103: site/ERP revision___ coordinator/deputy authority___ command interface___ baseline/update authority___ points/checkers___ roster identifiers___ medical/response-team verification___ communications/fallback___ assistance___ relocation/transport roles___ safe drill limits___ records/privacy___ assessor/approval___. Complete and validate before delivery.

lessons.title: Fictional network Cedar
lessons.body:
## Fictional network Cedar

Point North and Point South report to Coordinator, who reports to Command. Medic verifies medical locations; Response verifies assigned team identities and status. Only authorized Records can amend baseline arrivals/departures. Primary channel E; fallback B requires two-way test and readback. Checkers verify local identities; Coordinator reconciles globally; Command decides search, relocation and evacuation. Transport operator retains capacity and movement safety authority. No one enters a hazard or operates real transport in this exercise.

A report includes point/time/roster revision, named local identities, duplicates, unlisted people, unresolved identities, hazards and assistance needs. Global board categories are local point, medical/response location confirmed, in transit and unconfirmed. A person appears once in the global identity count even when multiple source reports exist. Preserve original reports and correction history.

lessons.title: Scenario A — overlapping points and baseline change
lessons.body:
## Scenario A — overlapping points and baseline change

Baseline revision 1: P01–P20. At 09:00 North reports P01–P10. South reports P10–P19. Raw rows 20; unique identities 19; P10 overlaps; P20 unconfirmed. Coordinator must identify both problems and report 19 confirmed of 20, with location overlap and missing identity. At minute 3 a coworker says P20 probably at medical; this is only a lead. At minute 5 Medic verifies P20 at medical at 09:05. Global identity count becomes 20, but P10 location still needs reconciliation. At minute 6 South corrects that P10 left South and was physically verified at North at 09:02; current location North is now confirmed with source/time.

At minute 8 X1 arrives at South unlisted. Record safe presence as unlisted/unreconciled and seek Records authority. At minute 10 Records supplies authorized revision 2 adding X1; baseline 21, North 10(P01–P10), South 10(P11–P19, X1), Medical 1(P20), total 21. At minute 12 Command reads 31 instead of 21. Correct/readback required. At minute 14 E fails before a follow-up acknowledgment; test B and repeat current picture. At minute 16 relief arrives while an assistance request for X1 has not been confirmed. Transfer that gap explicitly.

Controller does not supply the correct unique count unless debriefing. A false all-accounted declaration while P20 is unconfirmed is critical even if row totals match. Preserve action and report timing. No real missing person is created; identities are role-play cards in a safe room.

lessons.title: Scenario B — relocation, transfer and unavailable capacity
lessons.body:
## Scenario B — relocation, transfer and unavailable capacity

Baseline revision 4: B01–B24. North holds B01–B12, South B13–B24, all verified. At 10:00 North reports threatened point by card and approved command instruction to relocate to West via safe drill route R2. West checker confirms readiness. At 10:03 all 12North identities are recorded departing. At 10:06 West reports B01–B10, B10, B11:11 unique, B12 unconfirmed in transit. South remains 12. Global confirmed 23, unconfirmed 1; do not announce 24 received. At 10:08 Medic verifies B12 at medical. Picture: West 11, South 12, Medical 1, total 24.

At 10:10 one of two fictional 16-place evacuation means becomes unavailable. Available 16, gap 8 for 24 people; coordinator reports shortfall to Command, not an overload instruction. At 10:12 South reports one assistance helper absent; request verified replacement. At 10:14 Transport offers an alternative but its capacity/time are unconfirmed; record provisional, not available. At 10:16 controller supplies confirmed alternative card: 8 places, available 10:25, approved safe route R4 confirmed by Field 10:16; Command and Transport must still direct movement. At 10:18 two response personnel B23/B24 are reassigned from South to a verified response location. Update South 10, Response 2, West 11, Medical 1, total 24. At 10:20 restored dashboard imports original North 12 and South 12 as if current; reconcile event times and do not undo transfers. At 10:22 relief takes the current picture and pending movement arrangements with readback.

lessons.title: Changed remediation C
lessons.body:
## Changed remediation C

Baseline C01–C18. A reports C01–C09, B reports C09–C17:18 rows but 17 unique, C09 overlap, C18 unconfirmed. Later Medic verifies C18 and B corrects C09 current location to A. Authorized Records adds X2 and verifies C18 departed from the installation after medical transfer: baseline remains 18 but identities change. Track verified departure/receipt, not an unexplained deletion. Six named people C01–C06 transfer; receiver initially confirms C01–C05, C05: 5 unique, C06 unresolved. Later C06 verified at origin corrects departure to 5, retaining the original error. Two fictional 10-place means, one unavailable: 10 available, gap 8. Include failed primary channel, wrong readback and unverified extra scan on system recovery. Validate these changes before an uncoached assessment.

lessons.title: Workplace W1/W2 plan
lessons.body:
## Workplace W1/W2 plan

W1 observes actual baseline preparation, network activation, at least two point reports, cross-point identity reconciliation, command report and relief. W2 changes at least three conditions and covers communication/system fallback, authorized baseline change, missing/elsewhere verification, named transfer/receipt, assistance/capacity reporting and restored-record reconciliation. Dangerous conditions are inject cards, never created physically. If actual site arrangements cannot demonstrate a required function safely, arrange another approved workplace drill and keep the evidence gap open.

Retain local ERP/roster versions, approval, observation times, privacy-safe identity trace, checker and command acknowledgments, original/corrected reports, movement records and debrief. Witness information supports direct assessor observation; it does not replace observation of critical global-accounting decisions. No retrospective invented logs, signatures or event times are permitted.

lessons.title: Laboratories
lessons.body:
## Laboratories

### W103-1 — Baseline control
Use A revision 1 and unlisted X1. Produce baseline/version/change log. Expected: 20 authorized initially; X1 presence retained separately until revision 2; then 21 identities. Changed C addition plus verified departure leaves 18 but changes membership. Explain why unchanged total does not mean unchanged roster.

### W103-2 — Set reconciliation
Merge A North/South. Expected 19 unique, P10 overlap, P20 missing; after medical 20 unique but P10 location unresolved until correction. Submit named sets and source/time, not just totals. Changed C expected 17 unique, C09 overlap, C18 missing.

### W103-3 — Reporting and missing-person evidence
Draft initial command report and follow-up after verified medical location. Correct 31/21 readback and establish B fallback. Expected facts versus lead separated, current version/time stated, receipt confirmed, no unauthorized search instruction. Retain both reports.

### W103-4 — Movement and capacity
Use B. At 10:06: West 11+South 12=23 confirmed, one transit uncertainty. At 10:08: addMedical 1=24. Available capacity 16, gap 8. At 10:18: West 11+South 10+Response 2+Medical 1=24. Explain why original dashboard 24 cannot establish current locations. Changed C transfer: 5 received, one verified origin; correct departure trail.

### W103-5 — Relief and evidence review
Prepare relief using B's restored dashboard and unconfirmed alternative offer, then update with confirmed card. Identify event versus upload time, actual capacity and remaining authority steps. Submit accepted handover and two improvements with owner, due date and verification evidence.

lessons.title: Observed station dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed station dimensions

### P103-01 — Baseline readiness

Task: Establish approved baseline, contacts, point assignments and fallback records.

Required evidence: Versions and authority clear; unverified changes separated. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-02 — Network activation

Task: Collect readiness reports, resolve a missing point and coordinate an alternate.

Required evidence: Unknown is not zero; safe relocation and receiving contact confirmed. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-03 — Global reconciliation

Task: Merge named lists and resolve cross-point overlap.

Required evidence: Unique totals and missing IDs correct; current location limits retained. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-04 — Missing-person escalation

Task: Prepare command report from uncertain lead and later verification.

Required evidence: Facts/source/time distinguished; no unsafe search instruction. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-05 — Communications

Task: Report global picture, correct wrong readback and use fallback.

Required evidence: Acknowledgment of current report recorded; no false all accounted. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-06 — Movement tracking

Task: Reconcile named departures, destination receipt and medical diversion.

Required evidence: Transit discrepancy preserved until verified; no duplicate movement count. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-07 — Assistance and capacity

Task: Identify actual available capacity and missing assistance resource.

Required evidence: Shortfall accurately reported; no overload or improvised handling. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-08 — Relief and records

Task: Reconcile restored electronic data with paper and transfer responsibility.

Required evidence: Outstanding items/readbacks preserved; authentic audit trail. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-09 — Workplace integration

Task: Coordinate two changed multi-point workplace drills.

Required evidence: All role functions directly observed with traceable independent evidence. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

### P103-10 — Review and development

Task: Debrief discrepancy causes and perform changed reassessment if required.

Required evidence: Specific corrective owner/evidence; no attendance-only award. Record behavior/time, source and assessor rationale.

lessons.title: Forms for duplication
lessons.body:
## Forms for duplication

B103 baseline: version/time/source___ authorized IDs___ additions/authority___ departures/evidence___ unlisted/unverified___ revised version___ recipients/ack___.

G103 global record: ID___ baseline status___ point/source/time___ overlapping reports___ current verified location/category___ movement___ missing/lead___ verification/correction___ command update___.

N103 network: point/checker___ readiness/hazard___ current report/time___ channel/fallback___ missing report owner___ relocation/receiver___ acknowledgment___.

M103 missing-person brief: ID___ last confirmed location/time/source___ unverified lead___ relevant task/hazard___ verification action/owner___ command notified/ack___ confirmed correction/time___.

T103 transfer: command authority___ named departure list/time___ receiving role___ named receipt/time___ discrepancy___ medical/other diversion___ corrected departure___ global reconciliation___ command ack___.

R103 resource/assistance: need___ actual available means/capacity___ unavailable___ shortfall___ helper/medical constraint___ request___ confirmed alternative/source/time___ movement authority___ pending___.

H103 relief: baseline/version___ current identity/category totals___ location uncertainties___ point hazards___ missing/transit IDs___ assistance/capacity___ unacknowledged messages___ records___ incoming readback/acceptance/time___.

E103 evidence: learner/site/drill/version___ station___ observed action/time___ trace/source___ score/reason___ critical error___ coaching___ remediation___ changed observation___ assessor/reviewer/date___.

lessons.title: Scoring and decision
lessons.body:
## Scoring and decision

Ten dimensions 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent, 1 major help, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent accurate traceable, 4 independent with timely anticipation. Require 32/40, each at least 3, no critical error, all functions observed across two approved workplace drills. Critical global-accounting and movement decisions must pass independently in both where applicable. False all-accounted statements, concealed missing identity, unsafe search/route instruction, overload, fabricated evidence or unverified baseline deletion are critical. Stop unsafe simulated branches, record, remediate and reassess changed conditions; do not average them away.

Complete 20 formative checks with corrected reasoning and 5 labs. Final: 10 cases, 30 decisions, 60 points, pass 48 and at least 4/6 each, no critical error, 90 minutes. Changed final and keys are restricted instructor files. Obtain independent changed evidence after remediation; preserve unsuccessful records. An independent competent reviewer addresses appeals against documented criteria.

Award only VNDRLY/U Offshore Muster Coordinator — Workplace Assessed after authentic workplace and knowledge evidence passes. Record identity/site, scope, package hash, drill dates, assessor and renewal/review date. Set two-year original VNDRLY renewal with earlier review after material changes/performance concerns; continue local drills. Theory/simulation-only records must not say workplace assessed. No OPITO registration, incident-command appointment or actual learner completion is asserted by this authored package.


---

lessons.title: VUC103 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC103 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q103-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-01-L1

May the coordinator independently direct a hazardous search?

**Answer:** No. Provide facts to command and trained response roles.

**Reason/remediation:** Accounting responsibility does not grant tactical rescue authority. Revisit Q103-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-01-L2

Do point totals alone prove all accounted?

**Answer:** No. Reconcile unique identities across sources.

**Reason/remediation:** One duplicate can conceal one missing person. Revisit Q103-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-02-L1

An unsigned update adds a contractor. Silently change baseline?

**Answer:** No. Record unlisted presence and obtain authorized baseline confirmation.

**Reason/remediation:** Presence and baseline authority are distinct. Revisit Q103-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-02-L2

A dashboard is live but its roster is old. Which matters?

**Answer:** The authoritative roster version and update status.

**Reason/remediation:** A working screen can show stale data. Revisit Q103-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-03-L1

No report from a point: zero attendees?

**Answer:** No. Treat the point status as unknown and resolve the reporting gap.

**Reason/remediation:** Communication failure is not a count. Revisit Q103-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-03-L2

A threatened point relocates. What must be retained?

**Answer:** Identity records, authorized destination, receiving contact and transfer/receipt evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Silent relocation creates false deficits and duplicates. Revisit Q103-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-04-L1

A: P01–P10, B: P10–P19, baseline P01–P20. What is the union?

**Answer:** Nineteen unique; P10 overlap, P20 unconfirmed.

**Reason/remediation:** Summing two ten-person reports double-counts P10. Revisit Q103-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-04-L2

Medic confirms P20. Is P10 location irrelevant?

**Answer:** No. Global identity count is complete but current location overlap still needs resolution.

**Reason/remediation:** Movement planning needs accurate locations. Revisit Q103-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-05-L1

A coworker says someone probably went to medical. Accounted?

**Answer:** No. Verify through the authorized medical interface.

**Reason/remediation:** A plausible lead is not confirmation. Revisit Q103-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-05-L2

Should an urgent discrepancy wait until every detail is known?

**Answer:** No. Report known facts and uncertainty promptly, then update.

**Reason/remediation:** Delay can deprive command of critical information. Revisit Q103-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-06-L1

Command reads 29 for 19 confirmed and 1 unconfirmed. What next?

**Answer:** Correct baseline, count and unresolved identity and obtain accurate acknowledgment.

**Reason/remediation:** A wrong readback can drive unsafe decisions. Revisit Q103-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-06-L2

Does upload time replace event time?

**Answer:** No. Preserve both when different.

**Reason/remediation:** Late synchronization can distort the sequence. Revisit Q103-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-07-L1

Twelve depart, eleven unique received plus duplicate: status?

**Answer:** Eleven received, one named identity unresolved in transit.

**Reason/remediation:** Rows do not equal people. Revisit Q103-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-07-L2

Is seat allocation proof of evacuation?

**Answer:** No. Track actual departure and receipt.

**Reason/remediation:** Planned movement is not completed movement. Revisit Q103-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-08-L1

26 people, two 16-place means, one unavailable: gap?

**Answer:** Ten; only 16 places confirmed available.

**Reason/remediation:** Nominal capacity must exclude unavailable means. Revisit Q103-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-08-L2

Missing assistance helper: resolved because plan names one?

**Answer:** No. Request verified replacement arrangement.

**Reason/remediation:** Written plans do not guarantee actual resources. Revisit Q103-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-09-L1

Electronic 25 versus paper 24 plus 1 unresolved: choose electronic?

**Answer:** No. Reconcile identities and sources before changing status.

**Reason/remediation:** Display neatness is not evidence quality. Revisit Q103-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-09-L2

What does relief accept?

**Answer:** Baseline, identity/location picture, gaps, movements, conditions and unacknowledged messages.

**Reason/remediation:** A final total is insufficient. Revisit Q103-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q103-10-L1

Checker competence alone proves coordinator competence?

**Answer:** No. Observe multi-point coordination and global reconciliation.

**Reason/remediation:** Broader responsibilities require direct evidence. Revisit Q103-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q103-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q103-10-L2

Can coaching be recorded as independent performance?

**Answer:** No. Label it and obtain changed unprompted evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Assessment must distinguish assistance. Revisit Q103-10 and perform its changed application.


---

| Primary source | Verified basis | Coverage and limit |

Entry paragraph names checker rather than coordinator;no unsupported inference made. Full criteria unavailable. |
| [OPITO international ER competence guidance](https://opito.com/assets/6.ENGLISH_International_ER_Guidelines_Final-rev-0-Amendment-8_MASTER-June-2019.pdf) | Historical coordinator guidance links local induction,offshore practice and asset-owner assessment with continuing drills | Q1–2,10,W1/W2.2019guidance distinguished from current public product. |

| [HSE emergency-plan guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/offshore/assets/docs/ed-evacuation-escape-rescue.pdf) | Distinct command,muster and response roles within documented installation arrangements | Q1,3,5–8;role boundaries and movement coordination. |
| [HSE PFEER ACOP](https://www.hse.gov.uk/PuBns/books/l65.htm) | UK offshore emergency-response framework | Local adaptation only;not universal jurisdiction or a substitute ERP. |

Trace: Q1→P1/P9; Q2→P1/W103-1; Q3→P2; Q4→P3/W103-2; Q5→P4/W103-3; Q6→P5/W103-3; Q7→P6/W103-4; Q8→P7/W103-4; Q9→P8/W103-5; Q10→P9/P10/W1/W2. Each domain has two explained checks and separate final/changed three-decision cases. P2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 require observed practical coordination; P1, 3, 10 include observed records/review. All ten dimensions required.

Practice rosters, capacities, times and routes are synthetic. Actual assessment uses approved local plans and privacy-controlled evidence. The package is complete as original materials on accessible-source basis; it does not establish full proprietary equivalence, external registration or actual learner workplace completion.

content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VNDRLY/U OIM — Controlling Emergencies
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U OIM — Controlling Emergencies

VUC104 • Original employer-readiness and simulated-assessment package •18November 2026

Audience: employer-nominated OIMs, deputies or prospective appointees supported as ready for formal emergency assessment. Requires documented readiness, essential knowledge, asset-type knowledge and safe participation. Not OPITO approval, statutory appointment or independent specialist operating authority. Full proprietary criteria unavailable; public scope and regulator guidance form the source basis.

Planned preparation/assessment allocation 48 hours: 16 instruction/refresher, 8 labs, 4 asset/readiness/interface review, 16 individual scenarios/debrief, 2 written exam, 2 development planning. Adjust time for valid evidence; no time-served award. Objectives: maintain readiness, activate command, assess uncertainty, delegate safely, communicate, account for people, preserve evacuation options, manage team/stress and hand over/recover within authority.

lessons.title: Q104-01 — Employer readiness and asset-specific command
lessons.body:
## Q104-01 — Employer readiness and asset-specific command

An OIM emergency assessment sits within the employer's selection, training, experience and workplace appraisal process. It cannot establish readiness from a short simulation alone. Before formal assessment, the employer must provide a supported declaration covering readiness, essential knowledge and the relevant asset type. The assessor reviews the evidence and identifies gaps; a signed statement without supporting records is not a substitute for demonstrated preparation.

Understand the installation's major hazards, safety case or equivalent basis, operating configuration, emergency plan, command hierarchy and external interfaces. Fixed and mobile installations have different marine, structural and stability considerations. The OIM coordinates with competent marine, drilling, aviation and technical authorities rather than inventing their specialist operating actions. Identify exactly which simulated asset and role the assessment covers.

Worked case: a candidate experienced on a fixed platform is assessed on a mobile installation without evidence of the relevant asset knowledge. Do not infer competence from job title. Complete the employer-supported preparation and appropriate assessment model. The original VNDRLY certificate must describe the assessed scope and must not claim an external OIM qualification or employer appointment.

lessons.title: Q104-02 — Maintaining readiness and managing degraded protection
lessons.body:
## Q104-02 — Maintaining readiness and managing degraded protection

Readiness includes current people, capabilities, protection systems, routes, refuge, evacuation means, communications and concurrent work. Review impairments and their compensating controls with responsible specialists. Confirm that the actual shift can deliver the emergency plan. An unavailable team, isolated firewater component or failed communication channel changes feasible options and may require restrictions before an incident occurs.

Maintain a clear record of configuration and outstanding decisions. Review changing weather, marine activity, maintenance and contractor exposure. Make sure deputies and team members know their roles and succession arrangements. Preparation should reveal conflicts between planned tasks and emergency responsibilities. Do not count the same person or resource twice when simultaneous demands could occur.

Worked case: two evacuation means are shown on the plan but one is under maintenance. The OIM must know the actual available capacity and authorized compensating arrangements. Restating the nominal total does not satisfy readiness. If the planned protection cannot be maintained, escalate and restrict affected operations through the established authority rather than normalizing the impairment.

lessons.title: Q104-03 — Recognition, command activation and priorities
lessons.body:
## Q104-03 — Recognition, command activation and priorities

On receiving a credible emergency report, establish location, people at risk, hazard, source and time. Activate the emergency organization and protective measures according to the plan without waiting for perfect diagnosis. Announce command and use the designated succession process if required. Set immediate objectives that protect life, control or limit escalation and preserve viable evacuation/escape options.

Distinguish strategic objectives from specialist tactics. The OIM must understand the consequences of a proposed action and authorize it within the plan, but should not replace a competent response leader's technical method with an improvised instruction. Identify the next decision point and what evidence will trigger a change. Production and asset protection never justify concealing uncertainty about people or continuing an untenable tactic.

Worked case: a pipeline release report is credible but the failed component is unknown. Initiate the applicable emergency response, obtain control-system and field evidence, protect exposed people and request specialist support. A demand for the exact flange number before activation delays the response without making it safer.

lessons.title: Q104-04 — Assessing uncertainty and choosing effective action
lessons.body:
## Q104-04 — Assessing uncertainty and choosing effective action

Maintain a decision picture that distinguishes confirmed facts, reports, assumptions and unknowns. Evaluate evidence quality and time, including stale displays and unconfirmed verbal reports. Ask what could happen next, how quickly options might close, and which controls are verified effective. A protective command sent is not proof of its result. Reassess when feedback is missing or a condition changes.

Compare feasible options using consequences, capability, time, access and uncertainty. State the reason for the selected action and assign a responsible owner. Establish feedback and review triggers. Avoid repeating a failed strategy because effort has already been invested in it. Invite challenge from specialists and team members with contrary evidence; the command role includes resolving the evidence rather than suppressing disagreement.

Worked case: the CRO reports isolation commanded with continuing flow. Treat source control as unconfirmed and consider continued release in the strategy. A plan assuming the leak has stopped is not supported. Require the prescribed failed-action response and reassess the threat to refuge and evacuation routes.

lessons.title: Q104-05 — Delegating authority and coordinating specialists
lessons.body:
## Q104-05 — Delegating authority and coordinating specialists

Delegate a clear task, authority boundary, constraints, required report and review time to a named role. Confirm understanding. Retain oversight of interactions: a ventilation action, vessel movement or response-team deployment may affect another part of the emergency plan. Ask specialists to identify prerequisites, consequences and failure indicators before relying on an option.

Marine masters, aviation crews, well-control personnel, response leaders and medical staff retain their specialist responsibilities. The OIM coordinates the overall incident and interfaces through the plan. Do not issue an unsafe instruction because a resource appears under organizational control. If advice conflicts, clarify the evidence and authority, record the decision and obtain the required higher or specialist support.

Worked case: a vessel offers assistance but weather and approach suitability are not confirmed. Request the master's capability and constraints; do not order an approach from a control-room map alone. A resource offer is provisional until the responsible operator confirms its safe availability and the command plan integrates it.

lessons.title: Q104-06 — Communications under escalation
lessons.body:
## Q104-06 — Communications under escalation

Establish reliable internal and external communication with named roles and a shared update rhythm. Critical instructions need exact readback and acknowledgment. Keep urgent operational messages separate from routine requests and media inquiries. Use the authorized external communicator for shore support and relevant agencies, supplying identity, location, incident, people status, hazards, needs and contact arrangements.

Monitor communication failures as operational impairments. Test the approved fallback and re-establish the current instruction, not an obsolete one. A sent alert or a resource request is not confirmation of receipt or dispatch. Correct mistaken reports openly and promptly. Ensure people at muster receive appropriate updates through the designated roles so silence does not create rumor or unsafe self-directed movement.

Worked case: shore repeats forty accounted when the OIM reported forty on board and thirty-nine confirmed. Correct the distinction immediately and verify the correction. If the channel fails, retain the unresolved acknowledgment and use the approved alternative. The incorrect all-accounted statement must not remain the assumed common picture.

lessons.title: Q104-07 — People, responders and medical coordination
lessons.body:
## Q104-07 — People, responders and medical coordination

Require identity-based accountability through muster, response duties, medical treatment and transfers. Counts alone can conceal duplicates or missing people. Ask the coordinator to state confirmed identities, locations, unresolved people and source times. Provide missing-person evidence to the response decision process without automatically ordering hazardous entry. Track response teams and their withdrawal arrangements as part of the people picture.

Medical personnel direct clinical care; command arranges resources, access and external support. Verify transport and receiving arrangements before calling a medical transfer complete. Consider assistance needs and welfare during prolonged refuge or evacuation. A planned helper, seat or medical destination must be confirmed as available. Protect sensitive information while providing the facts needed for the response.

Worked case: a medic verifies a previously missing person, but a response team has not reported back. The first discrepancy may close; the installation is not automatically fully accounted for. The OIM must retain and act on the outstanding team-status uncertainty rather than allow one reassuring report to erase another problem.

lessons.title: Q104-08 — Refuge, evacuation and loss of control
lessons.body:
## Q104-08 — Refuge, evacuation and loss of control

Recognize when controlling the source is no longer a credible basis for keeping people on the installation. Use the emergency plan's escalation and evacuation criteria, current refuge condition, route availability, capacity and time. Endurance estimates depend on the incident and functioning protection; they are not guaranteed countdowns. Decisions must allow the required communication, preparation and movement with the plan's uncertainty allowances.

Confirm actual available capacity and operator suitability. Do not overload or assume an unconfirmed external rescue asset will arrive in time. Distinguish evacuation by planned means from escape arrangements when planned options fail; use the installation's procedures and competent roles rather than inventing techniques. Continue accounting for people through departure and receipt. Preserve alternative options early instead of waiting until the preferred one is lost.

Worked case: forty-eight people need evacuation and one of two thirty-place means is unavailable. Available capacity is thirty, leaving eighteen without that option. Report and address the shortfall immediately through confirmed alternatives. A nominal sixty-place design does not solve an actual thirty-place emergency capability.

lessons.title: Q104-09 — Asset-specific escalation and degraded command locations
lessons.body:
## Q104-09 — Asset-specific escalation and degraded command locations

An incident can affect structural integrity, stability, well control, pipelines, marine collision exposure or aviation operations. The OIM must recognize which specialist information and authority are needed and how those hazards threaten the overall emergency plan. This course does not teach ballast sequences, well-kill calculations, aviation control or structural acceptance limits. Use approved asset procedures and competent specialists; do not extrapolate from an unrelated installation.

Assess whether the command location remains habitable and functional. An alternate room may have different communications, information or control capability. Arrange transfer according to the plan with explicit task acceptance and current records. If life is threatened, protective movement takes precedence over perfect paperwork. Report what can no longer be controlled or verified and adapt the strategy accordingly.

Worked case: a mobile installation reports abnormal inclination while the primary control room loses displays. Obtain competent marine assessment and use the asset's emergency arrangements. Do not improvise ballast operations. State the loss of reliable control information and confirm what the alternate location can actually support.

lessons.title: Q104-10 — Stress, challenge and sustained team performance
lessons.body:
## Q104-10 — Stress, challenge and sustained team performance

Emergency command creates high workload and pressure to appear certain. Watch for fixation, rushed speech, repeated unanswered requests, missed reports or inability to delegate. Use short structured reviews to re-establish the shared picture and priorities. Allocate support and relief before fatigue undermines decisions. A team member should be able to challenge an unsafe assumption with evidence regardless of rank.

Manage your own response to bad news. A failed action is information, not disloyalty. Acknowledge corrections, revise the plan and make the new instruction clear. Avoid humiliation or blame during the response. Record what matters, delegate routine tasks and retain attention on the next time-critical decision. After the event, support welfare and a learning-focused debrief.

Worked case: a junior communicator identifies that a rescue ETA was never confirmed. The OIM should verify the claim, correct the planning assumption and reassess local options. Dismissing the challenge because the plan has already been announced converts an uncertain estimate into a dangerous false guarantee.

lessons.title: Q104-11 — Stabilization, command handover and recovery
lessons.body:
## Q104-11 — Stabilization, command handover and recovery

Define what stabilized means in the current incident and identify conditions that could reverse it. Maintain restrictions while protection, plant integrity, people status or evidence remain unresolved. Command handover requires current objectives, verified and failed actions, team/people status, external commitments, time-sensitive decisions, impairments and recovery constraints. The incoming commander accepts and critical roles are informed.

Recovery and restart require authorized technical checks, permit/isolation disposition and management release. Do not restore operation merely because alarms clear or external attention has faded. Preserve records and evidence with traceable corrections. Debrief decisions in the context of the information available at the time; identify training, interface and system changes with owners and verification evidence.

Worked case: isolation is now confirmed but a refuge damper remains faulted. The immediate source may be controlled, yet readiness for continued occupation or restart is not automatically restored. Include the fault and required decision in the handover and recovery plan.

lessons.title: Q104-12 — Independent assessment and continuing employer judgment
lessons.body:
## Q104-12 — Independent assessment and continuing employer judgment

Formal assessment requires independent performance across different emergencies, supported by prior employer readiness evidence. The assessor observes command, decision quality, delegation, communication, team performance and stress management through changing conditions. Familiarization teaches the simulator interface, not the hidden solution to the final scenario. Coaching during a run must be recorded and cannot be presented as independent evidence.

The original package requires three satisfactory emergency scenarios within a maximum of four assessed attempts. Critical unsafe decisions cannot be averaged away by strong performance elsewhere. Remediate the cause and use a changed scenario for any permitted reassessment. When attempts are exhausted, return to a documented development plan before a new assessment cycle. The employer uses the result alongside asset knowledge, workplace appraisal and experience; the simulation certificate does not replace that judgment.

Worked case: the learner manages a controllable incident and an escalation well but delays evacuation after the scenario's loss-of-control criteria are met. The third scenario is not passed because the first two were strong. Preserve the evidence, remediate the decision failure and assess a changed loss-of-control scenario within the permitted process.

---

content.title: VUC104 | VUC104 formal simulation workbook and assessor guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VUC104 formal simulation workbook and assessor guide
lessons.body: # VUC104 formal simulation workbook and assessor guide

lessons.title: Readiness dossier and facility
lessons.body:
## Readiness dossier and facility

Before assessed runs obtain employer declaration, role/asset scope, essential knowledge evidence, workplace readiness appraisal, local drill record, training/experience record and identified limitations. Verify authenticity and sufficiency; no retrospective invented evidence. A competent assessor and asset discipline expert review the dossier. Missing readiness evidence leaves formal award open. Initial learning/practice may continue safely without claiming readiness.

Use an isolated simulator or emergency-command mock-up with validated asset model, plant/route diagrams, alarm/status cards, communications, decision board, rosters and recorded traces. No connection to operational controls, live alarms or public emergency services. Controller manages injects; independent assessor observes; role players cover CRO, Response, Muster, Medic, Marine/Shore, Communicator and Relief. Asset specialist checks scenario plausibility and boundaries. Provide interface familiarization, fitness arrangements, breaks, accessibility, stop word and real-emergency override. Do not create fire, gas, unsafe movement or physical distress.

Adaptation A104: asset type/model/revision___ employer readiness reviewed___ ERP/authority/succession___ major hazards___ protective action references___ verified feedback___ impairment controls___ teams___ people baseline___ refuge assumptions___ routes___ evacuation/escape options___ marine/aviation/medical interfaces___ communications/fallback___ alternate command capability___ recovery rules___ assessor/expert approval___. Real-asset assessment uses approved local data. Fictional model below supports original VNDRLY simulation scope only; it cannot establish knowledge of an unnamed actual asset.

lessons.title: Fictional asset Harbor H104
lessons.body:
## Fictional asset Harbor H104

Fixed production installation for A/B/C. Modules P(process), U(utilities), TR(refuge), CCR(command), ACR(alternate). R1 crosses P; R2 bypasses P to TR; R3 connectsTR to  evacuation pointE. Routes only available when controller confirms. OIM commands overall response; CRO executes approved simulated protective cards; Response leader controls specialist tactics; Muster reconciles identities; Medic directs clinical matters; Marine/Shore confirms external capabilities; Communicator handles channels; Relief accepts command explicitly.

Credible release/fire triggers simulated alarm/organization and CRO response cardG: source isolation commandXV-1 with required closed feedback AND flow-zero. If either absent, source control remains unconfirmed; CRO follows failure branch and OIM reassesses continuing hazard. No bypass or improvised technical sequence. Entry needs Response assessment, required safeguards and command authorization; never actual hazardous entry. Primary channel E, fallback Btested before reliance. AlternateACRhas voice/status but no remote plant controls. Recovery requires technical safeguards, permit/isolation disposition and authorized release. Only controller provides new facts.

Asset-knowledge laboratory M104 is a separate mobile-asset discussion, not a claim that fixed-model scenarios establish mobile competence. Card: abnormal inclination, unreliable display, competent Marine available, approved mobile ERP required; learner must request specialist advice and refuse improvised ballast. Any mobile-scope formal assessment must replace/validate scenarios with the actual approved mobile model and readiness evidence.

lessons.title: Scenario A — controllable utility fire indication
lessons.body:
## Scenario A — controllable utility fire indication

Start 08:00, roster A01–A16. One response team available. R1 unavailable, R2/R3 available. TRinitially unaffected. Atminute 0CRO reports credible smoke/heat inU. Observe alarm/organization, command announcement, objectives and delegation. Atminute 3CRO reports isolation command but no result yet; OIM must not call it complete. Atminute 5 controller supplies required closed/flow-zero confirmation after appropriate request. Atminute 7Response reports the approved tactic has controlled the simulated incident with no entry needed. Atminute 9Muster lists A01–A14, A14, A15:15 unique, A16 unconfirmed. Atminute 11Medic verifies A16 atmedical, source/time; global 16. Atminute 13Shore requests restart for production; one protection sensor remains faulted. Expected recovery restriction. Atminute 15Communicator reads 16 evacuated rather than 16 accounted; correct category. Atminute 18Relief arrives. Require accepted handover of people, source control, sensor fault, team status and recovery gate. Successful source control does not excuse false people/recovery reporting.

lessons.title: Scenario B — escalating process release
lessons.body:
## Scenario B — escalating process release

Start 11:00, roster B01–B32. Two fictional 20-place means initially available. TRprovisional endpoint 11:35, conditional on protection. One team available. At 0 credible releaseP: activate and obtain source/control/person picture. At 3XV-1 command sent, no closed feedback, flow continues. At 5Response reports preferred approach blocked; OIM must reassess rather than order any-route entry. At 7Muster provides B01–B30, B30, B31:31 unique, B32 unconfirmed. At 9 one evacuation means unavailable: 20 available, gap 12. At 11Shore says rescue may arrive 11:30 but dispatch unconfirmed. At 13Medic verifies B32; count 32, locations retained. At 15 movement estimate 14 minutes: 20 minutes to provisional endpoint, nominal margin 6. Immediately inject TRprotection fault and uncertain R3; previous timing cannot be guaranteed. At 17E fails and a deputy reports wrong count 42; tested B/correction required. At 19Marine offers alternative with no capacity proof; request actual constraints. On request controller provides ALT-B: 12 places, ready 11:24, route R4 confirmed byField 11:20, operator retains movement safety, command must integrate and monitor. At 22 junior communicator challenges old rescueETAonboard; OIM must correct and reassess. End on explicit supported strategy, allocation, people/route/capacity picture and relief, not a predetermined demand for a particular real-world tactic.

lessons.title: Scenario C — loss of control and planned evacuation
lessons.body:
## Scenario C — loss of control and planned evacuation

Start 14:00, roster C01–C40. Credible major release and structural-threat card; technical specialist confirms source cannot be controlled within current response capability. Two fictional 24-place means initially available; one becomes unavailable atminute 3:24 available, gap 16. TRprovisional endpoint 14:28, not guaranteed. R1 blocked, R2 available initially, R3 uncertain. The model's escalation criterion is met: loss of source control with threatened continued occupation requires OIM to initiate the plan's evacuation decision process immediately, coordinate confirmed safe options and continue monitoring. No actual boarding or escape occurs.

Atminute 0 activate command and protective organization; technical loss-of-control report is supplied. At 3 capacity loss. At 5Muster reports C01–C38, C38, C39:39 unique, C40 unconfirmed. At 7Response cannot locate C40 safely; OIM must retain missing facts without ordering uncontrolled entry. At 9Medic confirms C40 atmedical; global 40. At 10Shore confirms alternative 16-place means ready 14:16 with operator-approved access R4 currently verified; this is a resource fact, not an instruction to ignore later change. At 12 movement estimate 12 minutes leaves 16 to provisional endpoint, nominal margin 4. Then refuge protection deteriorates: urgent reassessment, not waiting 4 minutes. At 14 primary command room becomes unsuitable by card; ACR limited capability requires safe transfer/acceptance and disclosure. At 16Transport provides departure list C01–C24 for first means; second list C25–C40. At 18 receiver confirms C01–C23, C23 forfirst: 23 unique, C24 unconfirmed; second confirms 16 unique. Total 39 received, one transit discrepancy. At 20 receiver verifies C24 withsource/time; 40 received. OIM must distinguish planned, departed and received stages. At 22 relief/shore handover preserves asset hazards and recovery prohibition. A delayed evacuation decision after explicit loss-of-control trigger is critical; do not reward a late tidy manifest as success.

lessons.title: Changed fourth-attempt scenario D
lessons.body:
## Changed fourth-attempt scenario D

After documented remediation only. Start 16:00, roster D01–D36. Utility/common-power failure makes source-control status unreliable; technical advice confirms continued occupation threatened. Two 22-place means, one unavailable: 22 available, gap 14. Provisional endpoint 16:26; at 16:10 movement 11 minutes gives 16 remaining, nominal margin 5, thenroute loss invalidates it. Muster D01–D34, D34, D35:35 unique, D36 unconfirmed; laterMedic confirms D36. Alternative 14-place resource confirmed only after capability/time/access request. Final receiver initially lacks D22 fromfirst 22 and confirmsother 14:35 received, oneunconfirmed; laterverified D22 closes 36. Include wrong readback, failed primary channel and limited ACR. Validate all changed references before use. Do not expose inject timings before assessment or coach decisions during the run.

lessons.title: Laboratories
lessons.body:
## Laboratories

### W104-1 — Readiness dossier
Review employer evidence and asset scope; identify missing mobile knowledge in a fixed-platform candidate. Submit readiness gap/owner and assessed scope. Review actual resources/impairments in H104; do not invent employer signatures.

### W104-2 — Control evidence and strategy
Build A/B decision boards separating command, result and uncertainty. Expected: B source unconfirmed, continued-release strategy and failed-action owner. Change: closed indication arrives but flow-zero missing; required confirmation still incomplete.

### W104-3 — Delegation and communications
Role-play specialist resource offer, wrong count and failed E. Submit named task/limits/feedback, capability request, tested B, correct current readback and logged acknowledgment. No specialist operating instruction is invented.

### W104-4 — People and transfers
Ainitial 15 plusverifiedmedical 1=16; B31+1=32; C39+1=40. Cfirstreceiver 23 plussecond 16=39, then 40 after C24 verification. Submit identity sets and source times. Change D35 initial, then 36; received 35 then 36.

### W104-5 — Capacity and timing
B20 available, gap 12; at 11:15 nominal 35−15−14=6 minutes. C24 available, gap 16; at 14:12 nominal 28−12−12=4. D22 available, gap 14; at 16:10 nominal 26−10−11=5. Explain why protection/route changes invalidate safe-wait interpretations and why capacity must be confirmed.

### W104-6 — Asset boundaries, relief and recovery
Use M104 mobile card to identify required specialist/ERP evidence, not ballast actions. Prepare H104 limited ACRtransfer and final recovery handover. Include unresolved protection, people stages, resource commitments and no-restart conditions. Write development actions based on observed gaps.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P104-01 — Employer readiness

Task: Review declaration and supporting asset/readiness evidence.

Required evidence: Scope and gaps explicit; no title-only readiness. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-02 — Configuration readiness

Task: Identify impaired systems, actual teams and evacuation capacity.

Required evidence: Unavailable resources excluded; compensating decisions recorded. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-03 — Activate command

Task: Respond to first credible report and announce objectives/authority.

Required evidence: Timely plan activation; life protection prioritized. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-04 — Assess and adapt

Task: Maintain evidence board through failed control feedback.

Required evidence: Facts/assumptions separate; strategy changes with evidence. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-05 — Delegate specialists

Task: Assign tasks with constraints and obtain operator capability advice.

Required evidence: No invented specialist method; clear feedback/authority. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-06 — Communicate

Task: Correct wrong count/readback and verify fallback/external support.

Required evidence: Current acknowledged picture; estimates distinguished. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-07 — Account for people

Task: Reconcile identities, medical and response-team reports.

Required evidence: No false all accounted; missing status escalated safely. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-08 — Evacuate/escalate

Task: Address lost refuge/capacity/route options.

Required evidence: Correct arithmetic and early plan decision; no overload. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-09 — Asset/degraded command

Task: Use asset specialist and transfer to limited alternate location.

Required evidence: No improvised control; limitations and acceptance explicit. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-10 — Team/stress

Task: Handle challenge, overload and relief.

Required evidence: Evidence-based correction; critical monitoring retained. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-11 — Recovery/handover

Task: Transfer unresolved protection and restart constraints.

Required evidence: Accepted command transfer; no premature closure. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P104-12 — Three-scenario judgment

Task: Complete A, B, C independently and document development.

Required evidence: Each pass supported; attempts/coaching honestly recorded. Record inject/action time, trace and assessor rationale.

lessons.title: Forms
lessons.body:
## Forms

lessons.title: Scoring, attempts and credential boundary
lessons.body:
## Scoring, attempts and credential boundary

Each of 12 dimensions 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent, 1 major assistance, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent accurate traceable, 4 independent anticipatory with clear reasoning. Require 39/48, every dimension at least 3, no critical error, and three satisfactory independent scenarios. Each scenario must pass its relevant command criteria; readiness review applies to the entire assessment. Maximum 4 assessed attempts for 3 successful scenarios; after exhaustion require further development and a new justified plan. Do not relabel a failed assessed run as practice after seeing the result.

Critical errors include unsupported hazardous deployment, deliberate overload, false all-accounted or received declaration, unauthorized bypass/restart, concealed loss of protection, unjustified delay after explicit evacuation trigger, or fabricated readiness/evidence. Freeze unsafe simulated action, retain trace and remediate. Independent competent review handles disputed evidence against unchanged criteria.

Complete 24 explained checks and 6 labs. Controlled final: 12 cases/36 decisions, 72 points, pass 58, at least 4/6 each, no critical error, 120 minutes. Changed final and keys remain instructor-only. Written pass does not substitute for scenarios or employer readiness. Issue only VNDRLY/U OIM Controlling Emergencies — Simulation Assessed, with assessed asset/model/role, package hash, dates, attempts, assessors and limits. No OPITO certificate or statutory/employer appointment follows. Public OPITO product has no formal expiry and recommends reassessment at least every 3 years; document a local review plan and earlier reassessment after material change or concern. Employer continuing competence judgment remains necessary.
