lessons.title: VUC104 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC104 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q104-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-01-L1

Does a signed readiness statement alone replace supporting evidence?

**Answer:** No. Review employer records for readiness, essential and asset knowledge.

**Reason/remediation:** A declaration needs a defensible basis. Revisit Q104-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-01-L2

Does fixed-platform experience automatically prove mobile-asset readiness?

**Answer:** No. Establish relevant asset knowledge and assessment scope.

**Reason/remediation:** Hazards and specialist interfaces differ. Revisit Q104-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-02-L1

Two planned teams but one staffed: what is available?

**Answer:** One actual team; record and address the gap.

**Reason/remediation:** Nominal resources do not create capability. Revisit Q104-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-02-L2

One evacuation means under maintenance: count its places?

**Answer:** No. Use confirmed available capacity and compensating arrangements.

**Reason/remediation:** Unavailable equipment cannot protect people. Revisit Q104-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-03-L1

Wait for exact failed component before activation?

**Answer:** No, when credible evidence meets the plan trigger.

**Reason/remediation:** Diagnosis must not delay prescribed protection. Revisit Q104-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-03-L2

Is a specialist entry technique a command objective?

**Answer:** No. Set the protective objective and obtain competent tactical assessment.

**Reason/remediation:** Command and technical method are distinct. Revisit Q104-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-04-L1

Isolation command sent but flow continues: state?

**Answer:** Unconfirmed source control.

**Reason/remediation:** Command and achieved result differ. Revisit Q104-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-04-L2

A tactic fails: repeat indefinitely?

**Answer:** No. Reassess evidence, options and escalation triggers.

**Reason/remediation:** Persistence without feedback can close safer options. Revisit Q104-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-05-L1

A vessel offers help: may OIM dictate approach?

**Answer:** No. Confirm master/operator capability and constraints through the plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Specialist safety authority remains. Revisit Q104-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-05-L2

What makes delegation effective?

**Answer:** Named role, outcome, authority limits, constraints, feedback and review.

**Reason/remediation:** Assignment without follow-up can hide failure. Revisit Q104-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-06-L1

Forty on board, thirty-nine confirmed is read as forty accounted. What next?

**Answer:** Correct immediately and obtain accurate acknowledgment.

**Reason/remediation:** Baseline and confirmed count are different. Revisit Q104-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-06-L2

Is a rescue request proof of dispatch?

**Answer:** No. Obtain confirmation and preserve uncertainty.

**Reason/remediation:** Requested resources may not be available. Revisit Q104-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-07-L1

A missing person found but team unreported: all accounted?

**Answer:** No. Retain team-status gap.

**Reason/remediation:** One resolved discrepancy does not close another. Revisit Q104-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-07-L2

Who directs medical treatment?

**Answer:** Qualified medical personnel; command coordinates resources.

**Reason/remediation:** Command role does not confer clinical competence. Revisit Q104-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-08-L1

48 people, two 30-place means, one unavailable: gap?

**Answer:** 18 people lack that option.

**Reason/remediation:** Only 30 places are available. Revisit Q104-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-08-L2

Does nominal endurance guarantee time to wait?

**Answer:** No. Conditions and protection can invalidate it.

**Reason/remediation:** Decision time must include uncertainty and action duration. Revisit Q104-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-09-L1

Abnormal inclination: improvise ballast?

**Answer:** No. Use competent marine advice and approved asset procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Unqualified actions can worsen stability. Revisit Q104-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-09-L2

Alternate room assumed full capability?

**Answer:** No. Verify its actual information, controls and communications.

**Reason/remediation:** A different location can have different limits. Revisit Q104-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-10-L1

Junior colleague challenges unconfirmed ETA. Ignore?

**Answer:** No. Check evidence and revise planning assumption.

**Reason/remediation:** Rank does not establish facts. Revisit Q104-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-10-L2

What to do with overload signs?

**Answer:** Reprioritize, delegate support and arrange relief with monitoring intact.

**Reason/remediation:** Unmanaged workload degrades decisions. Revisit Q104-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-11-L1

Source controlled but refuge protection faulted: fully recovered?

**Answer:** No. Retain impairment and authorized recovery decision.

**Reason/remediation:** One successful action is not complete readiness. Revisit Q104-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-11-L2

What completes command transfer?

**Answer:** Explicit accepted handover and notification of affected roles.

**Reason/remediation:** Leaving the room is not transfer. Revisit Q104-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q104-12-L1

Two strong scenarios cancel critical third failure?

**Answer:** No. Each required scenario must pass independently.

**Reason/remediation:** Critical decisions cannot be averaged away. Revisit Q104-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q104-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q104-12-L2

Four attempts exhausted with only two passes: award?

**Answer:** No. Further development and a new documented assessment plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Attempt limits cannot be bypassed by relabeling failures. Revisit Q104-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Onshore Control Room Operator Emergency Response
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Onshore Control Room Operator Emergency Response

VUC105 • Original materials •18November 2026

Scope: employer-nominated onshore CRO emergency simulation assessment, with supported workplace readiness. Not external OPITO approval, site appointment, public protective-action authority or specialist spill-response qualification. Full proprietary criteria unavailable; accessible primary sources inform this original package.

Planned 40 hours: 14 instruction, 6 labs, 4 readiness/interface review, 12 scenario assessment/debrief, 2 written assessment, 2 remediation planning. Allow sufficient additional time for valid evidence. Outcomes: prepare, recognize and prioritize hazards, execute/verify authorized controls, coordinate people/access/environmental information, manage degraded systems and hand over/recover reliably.

lessons.title: Q105-01 — Readiness, site knowledge and role limits
lessons.body:
## Q105-01 — Readiness, site knowledge and role limits

The onshore CRO maintains plant control and supplies reliable operational information during an emergency. The role connects process systems with the site incident commander, field responders, muster, gate/security and external-service liaison. It does not automatically include authority to direct public evacuation, specialist firefighting or medical treatment. Employer nomination and supported workplace readiness evidence must precede a formal competence award.

Know the actual plant, hazardous inventories, utility dependencies, emergency procedures, isolation boundaries, drainage/containment arrangements, access gates and neighboring exposures. Review current permits, impairments and simultaneous work at handover. A production shutdown can affect cooling, ventilation or containment; use approved procedures rather than assuming every stopped system is safer. Record limitations and obtain support when unfamiliarity or fatigue compromises the role.

Worked example: the shift sheet says emergency cooling is available but a later maintenance record shows its supply isolated. Resolve the current authorized condition and compensating arrangements before accepting it as ready. Do not let the handover's reassuring wording replace the actual protection state.

lessons.title: Q105-02 — Recognizing abnormal conditions and credible evidence
lessons.body:
## Q105-02 — Recognizing abnormal conditions and credible evidence

Use alarms, trends, field reports and equipment status to recognize a developing emergency. Separate measurement time from display refresh time, and distinguish good-quality data from failed or frozen signals. A plausible value with bad quality may not support a safety decision. Corroboration helps diagnosis but does not justify delaying a protective action already required by the response procedure.

Maintain a concise picture of affected unit, people at risk, material/energy involved, likely escalation paths and uncertainty. Know where current approved chemical information and emergency contacts are available. Do not infer safe exposure, spill treatment or public impact from a generic substance name. Obtain the relevant product/process information and competent advice through the plan.

Worked example: a high-level alarm, rising trend and field report indicate loss of containment. The operator should initiate the prescribed response and report the uncertain extent. Sending an unprotected person to inspect a suspected vapor area solely to obtain a better photograph is not a valid verification method.

lessons.title: Q105-03 — Alarm response and workload control
lessons.body:
## Q105-03 — Alarm response and workload control

An alarm is a request for assessment or action under a defined response. Acknowledgment records receipt; it does not prove the plant is safe. Prioritize by consequence, response time and independent hazards rather than processing a flood from top to bottom. Use first-out and trend information while continuing to watch for a separate threat such as cooling loss or control-room ventilation failure.

Call the assigned support operator when workload exceeds safe capacity. Give a specific task, expected feedback and review point. Keep critical monitoring owned. Do not suppress or bypass protection merely to reduce nuisance indications. Any approved shelving/suppression process must retain authorization, limits and tracking. Record unresolved actions separately from acknowledged alarms.

Worked example: a transfer-pump trip generates many dependent alarms while a reactor cooling alarm appears. The cooling alarm may be the more urgent independent hazard. Allocate support to the trip sequence and follow the cooling response instead of assuming every alarm belongs to the first event.

lessons.title: Q105-04 — Protective actions and verified results
lessons.body:
## Q105-04 — Protective actions and verified results

Identify the correct unit/tag, procedure, authority and prerequisites before acting. Execute the designated control in the simulator and verify the required feedback. A stop command is not confirmed stopped equipment; a valve selection is not confirmed isolation. Record command time, actual indication and missing evidence. Follow the approved failed-action branch and inform command when the expected state is not achieved.

Understand site-specific interactions among shutdown, cooling, ventilation, depressurization, fire protection and containment. This package supplies fictional control cards only; it does not prescribe a real plant sequence. Never force an output, defeat an interlock or restart to improve production during an unresolved emergency. Recovery needs authorized technical and management release.

Worked example: close command XV-5 is sent, but feedback is unknown and transfer flow continues. Report isolation attempted/unconfirmed and maintain the continuing-release assumption. An optimistic radio message cannot replace the confirmation required by the actual procedure.

lessons.title: Q105-05 — Containment, drainage and environmental interfaces
lessons.body:
## Q105-05 — Containment, drainage and environmental interfaces

Loss of containment can threaten people and migrate through drains, watercourses, soil or adjacent equipment. The CRO needs the site's approved containment and drainage information and must communicate credible migration paths to command and environmental responders. Do not assume all drains lead to safe containment or that a closed valve has achieved isolation without feedback.

Spill response depends on substance, quantity, compatibility, ignition/toxic hazards and trained resources. Do not improvise neutralization, dilution, absorbent selection or drain entry. Use the approved product/site response plan and competent specialist advice. Report unconfirmed containment, available capacity and uncertainty. Environmental protection is coordinated with life safety; personnel are not sent into a hazardous area merely to protect a drain.

Worked example: a synthetic bund has 18 cubic meters of verified usable capacity and already holds 7. A further 14 cubic meters may arrive: only 11 is available, so the potential shortfall is 3. These training figures identify a concern for command; they do not authorize changing a real drain or predict a live release without validated data.

lessons.title: Q105-06 — Communications, access and external responders
lessons.body:
## Q105-06 — Communications, access and external responders

Use clear messages with site identity, location/unit, hazard, known material, people status, actions, needs and contact route. Confirm critical instructions by readback. Gate/security needs the authorized safe access point and restrictions; external responders need current hazard information and a competent liaison. A gate that was safe earlier may become unsuitable after a release or wind change.

The designated authority handles external-service notification and public protective instructions according to the site plan and applicable arrangements. The CRO supplies accurate operational information and performs the notifications allocated to the role. Never assume a call was received or that a resource is dispatched because a request was sent. Test approved fallback communication and repeat the current instruction after a failure.

Worked example: responders are directed to Gate 2 but the readback says Gate 1, which lies in the affected zone. Correct the gate, verify current safe access with the responsible role and obtain exact readback. Do not let a hurried acknowledgment send responders toward an unverified hazard.

lessons.title: Q105-07 — People, contractors and control of work
lessons.body:
## Q105-07 — People, contractors and control of work

Support the site's accountability process with accurate information about operating staff, contractors, visitors, response personnel and people in medical care. Use unique identities and source times rather than raw counts. Permit suspension and actual notification to the work party are separate facts. Tell the coordinator/command when a contractor's location or receipt of instructions is unconfirmed.

The CRO does not independently order an unprotected search or certify an area safe for entry. Provide last-known location, task, isolation status and hazards to the authorized response decision. Track changes after the initial muster, including medical movement or response assignments. A person confirmed elsewhere must not be counted again at the original point.

Worked example: a permit is electronically suspended, but the maintenance team has not acknowledged. Keep the unresolved communication visible and use the approved safe contact route. Do not mark the team withdrawn just because the permit status changed on screen.

lessons.title: Q105-08 — Toxic/fire exposure and control-room habitability
lessons.body:
## Q105-08 — Toxic/fire exposure and control-room habitability

An onshore emergency can threaten occupied buildings, routes, neighboring units and people outside the immediate process area. Use the site's hazard information, validated observations and incident-command arrangements. Do not calculate a generic safe perimeter from an unverified wind reading or assume a building is protective because it is called a control room. Ventilation, doors, power and other protective features can fail.

Monitor the habitability criteria and relocation instructions in the plan. An alternate control point may have reduced control or information capability. Tell command what remains available and what cannot be verified. Shelter versus evacuation decisions depend on the actual incident and authority; this package does not prescribe a universal choice. Give timely plant facts so the responsible decision maker can act.

Worked example: the control-room intake alarm activates and required protective-damper feedback is absent. Report protection uncertain and follow the site's immediate response. Waiting for symptoms or treating an old clean air reading as proof of safety is not an acceptable substitute.

lessons.title: Q105-09 — Utility, network and common-cause failures
lessons.body:
## Q105-09 — Utility, network and common-cause failures

Loss of power, cooling, instrument air, network communication or shared sensors can affect several protective functions simultaneously. Recognize the possibility of a common cause instead of treating every symptom as an unrelated nuisance. Identify the last reliable state and use approved independent evidence. A recovered display may still contain stale values or incomplete event history.

Apply the defined degraded-mode response and preserve safeguards. Do not improvise electrical switching, bypasses or system restoration. Coordinate with competent technical roles and command. During transfer to an alternate station, verify its actual capability, assign outstanding actions and obtain acceptance. If the current location is unsafe, life protection governs; a perfect log is not a reason to remain exposed.

Worked example: network values freeze while instrument-air pressure becomes uncertain. Report both the information loss and possible control consequence. A flat trend cannot establish stable process conditions. Ask for approved independent confirmation without sending someone into an unverified hazard.

lessons.title: Q105-10 — Team performance, relief and recovery
lessons.body:
## Q105-10 — Team performance, relief and recovery

Stress and competing demands can narrow attention. Use short checkbacks on facts, uncertainty, immediate threats, action owners and the next review. Invite challenge from colleagues and act on contradictory evidence. Delegate routine communications/logging while retaining critical monitoring. Disclose mistakes promptly and use the approved correction process rather than hiding them.

Relief requires plant state, failed/confirmed controls, people and permit status, communication gaps, environmental concerns, deadlines and next actions. Obtain explicit readback and acceptance. Recovery is separate from stabilization: verify safeguards, isolations, permits and authorized restart conditions. Preserve event times and visible corrections so the record explains what was known when a decision was made.

Worked example: a relief operator hears isolation complete while the board says no feedback. Correct the misunderstanding before transfer. If the alarm later clears because the sensor fails, retain that uncertainty and do not turn it into a restart authorization.

lessons.title: Q105-11 — Three-scenario demonstration and development
lessons.body:
## Q105-11 — Three-scenario demonstration and development

Formal onshore CRO assessment requires observed performance across three different simulated emergencies, supported by employer readiness evidence. The learner must operate the interface, communicate, verify results and maintain records; narration alone is insufficient. Familiarization covers the model and controls without revealing assessment injects. Coaching is recorded separately from independent performance.

Each scenario must produce a satisfactory decision. A critical error in one is not averaged away by success in others. Remediate the reasoning or skill gap and use changed conditions for reassessment under the documented plan. Keep records of attempts, assistance and decisions. The resulting original certificate documents simulation performance in the stated model, not unrestricted authority to operate any plant or an external OPITO award.

Worked example: a learner handles a spill well but assumes a failed control-room damper is closed in the utility-loss scenario. That scenario remains unsuccessful. Review command/result verification and habitability response, then observe a changed scenario requiring the same competence without the memorized cues.

---

lessons.title: VUC105 onshore practical workbook
lessons.body: # VUC105 onshore practical workbook

lessons.title: Facility and readiness
lessons.body:
## Facility and readiness

Use an isolated onshore-process simulator or inert mock panel, plant/route/drainage diagram, alarm list, status/quality cards, training communications, people/permit records and printable forms. No production controls, live alarms, actual chemicals, drain operations or public emergency calls. Controller manages injects; independent competent CRO assessor observes; role players cover Incident Command, Field, Muster, Gate, Liaison, Technical and Relief. Employer readiness declaration and supporting workplace evidence must be reviewed before formal award. A competent site/process expert validates real-asset adaptation.

Provide safe interface familiarization, fitness arrangements, breaks, accessibility, stop word and real-emergency override. All spill/fire/toxic conditions are simulated; never expose people to prove a response. Role players do not enter a hazard. Real emergency stops training. Adaptation A105 records site/model, ERP revision, role authority, chemicals/SDS references, control cards and feedback, containment/drainage, utility dependencies, habitability, access gates, external notification roles, people/permit interfaces, fallback, alternate controls and recovery criteria. Actual plant procedures replace fictional cards before any site-specific claim.

lessons.title: Fictional plant Rowan
lessons.body:
## Fictional plant Rowan

Units T(transfer/storage), R(process), CCR(control), ALT(alternate), M(muster). Gates 1 and 2; Gate 1 lies byT, Gate 2 is alternate only when confirmed. Primary channelE, fallbackBrequires two-way verification. CRO may raise simulated site alarm, notify Command and execute response cards allocated below. Command controls responder deployment and site protective decisions; Liaison handles external services/public-agency interface; Gate receives current authorized access; Muster verifies identities; Technical provides specialist advice. CRO does not improvise spill chemistry, entry, public evacuation or electrical switching.

CardT: credible transfer release requires simulated stopP-1 and closeXV-5, then verify stopped feedback, closed feedback AND flow-zero. Any missing criterion means source control unconfirmed; notify Command, retain hazard and follow failed-action branch(no bypass/local entry). CardC: independent cooling alarm requires simulated approved cooling-response selectionCR-2 and verification of specified restored-status card; missing status escalated. CardH: CCR intake threat requires simulated protective damper commandD-1 and required position/environment confirmation; absent evidence means protection unconfirmed and immediate ERP/Command habitability response. These are invented training actions, not real operating instructions.

ALTprovides voice and independent status cards but no remote controls. Drain D7 destination is unknown until approved drawing/Technical confirms; no learner manipulates drains. Usable containment figures are controller-provided training data, not design limits. Any environmental or off-site impact is reported through assigned Command/Liaison roles. Recovery requires verified safeguards, permits/isolations and authorized release.

lessons.title: Scenario A — transfer loss and containment gap
lessons.body:
## Scenario A — transfer loss and containment gap

Start 09:00, roster A01–A10, permit W1 team contact pending. Verified usable bund 18 cubic meters, occupied 7, potential further 14:11 remaining, shortfall 3. Gate 1 affected; Gate 2 not yet confirmed. At 0 valid release indications and Field report triggerT. At 3 command responsesP-1 stopped butXV-5 feedbackunknown, flowcontinues: report unconfirmed source control. At 5 alarm flood plus independent cooling alarm: apply Cwith priority/support. At 7Technical says D7 destinationunknown: do not assume containment or improvise treatment. At 9Liaison requests responder access; Gate confirms Gate 2 safe at 09:09 but readback saysGate 1: correct and verify. At 11Muster lists A01–A08, A08, A09: 9 unique, A10 unconfirmed. At 13Medic verifies A10; global 10 with location distinction. At 15 permit W1 still no acknowledgment: retain contact/withdrawal uncertainty, escalate safe contact. At 17 primaryE fails; testB and update current status. At 19Technical provides required control confirmations but containment/cleanup disposition remains unresolved. At 21 relief accepts these constraints and no-restart gate.

lessons.title: Scenario B — utility and process-control failure
lessons.body:
## Scenario B — utility and process-control failure

Start 12:00, roster B01–B12. Network display refresh 12:00 contains 11:52 values; quality uncertain. Instrument-air/cooling states uncertain. At 0 recognize eight-minute stale data and common-cause potential; apply degraded response and notify Command. At 3 independent cooling alarm appears; apply Cbut restored-status card withheld. At 5Field asks whether area safe for repair because pump stopped: report actual unverified state, refer entry/isolation to authorized plan. At 7 permit W2 electronically suspended, team unacknowledged: do not call withdrawn. At 9Muster gives B01–B10, B10, B11:11 unique, B12 unconfirmed. At 11Technical asks for unsafe override as a temptation card; reject unauthorized action. At 13 verified Medic report B12 closes global 12. At 15 display recovers but timestamps/duplicate events need reconciliation. At 17Relief incorrectly says cooling restored; correct missing result and accept transfer only with accurate outstanding tasks. End on coherent degraded/recovery handover, not a green screen.

lessons.title: Scenario C — control-room threat and external interface
lessons.body:
## Scenario C — control-room threat and external interface

Start 15:00, roster C01–C14. CCR intake alarm valid; old clean-air value 15:00 refresh/14:48 measurement. Card H applies. At 0 raise/notify and execute assigned protective response; recognize 12-minute-old evidence. At 3D-1 command lacks position/environment confirmation. At 5Command requests capability report forALT; voice/status only, no remote controls. At 7Gate 2 becomes unavailable by card; old responder instruction must be withdrawn and alternative authorized through Liaison/Command. At 9Muster C01–C12, C12, C13:13 unique, C14 unconfirmed. At 11 verified Medic report C14:14 global. At 13 primary communications fail; tested fallback, current access/people status and unresolved protection report required. At 15Command issues approved relocation instruction; transfer tasks/records safely with explicit receiving acceptance. At 17 sensor indication clears because fault appears; do not treat as safe-air confirmation. At 19 production requests restart: retain recovery criteria and specialist verification. End with accepted handover and correct authority boundaries; no actual evacuation or exposure occurs.

lessons.title: Changed remediation D
lessons.body:
## Changed remediation D

Use after documented gap-specific development. Start 17:00, roster D01–D16 with D01–D14, D14, D15 initially: 15 unique, D16 unconfirmed, later verified by Medic. Transfer source command has closed feedbackbutflow-zero missing. Usable bund 25, occupied 11, incoming 19:14 remaining, shortfall 5. Display 17:10 refreshcontains 17:01 bad-quality value: nine minutes old. Gate 3 proposedbutunverified; reader/radio failure and limited ALTadded. Validate revised fictional response references and provide them before assessment, without revealing inject sequence. Require changed independent performance; do not count a coached replay as a pass.

lessons.title: Laboratories
lessons.body:
## Laboratories

### W105-1 — Readiness and evidence
Resolve the cooling isolation conflict and review employer/site readiness. CalculateBdata age 8 minutes andCold measurement 12 minutes. Submit source/time/quality/uncertainty and applicable response trigger. ChangedDage 9 minutes with bad quality remains unreliable.

### W105-2 — Control and alarm response
OperateT/C mock controls and record each command/result criterion. Expected missing feedback/flow-zero stays unconfirmed; independent cooling action retains owner during flood. No override. Change suppliesclosed feedbackonly, requiring remaining verification.

### W105-3 — Containment and responder information
Aremaining 18−7=11, incoming 14 creates 3 shortfall. D25−11=14, incoming 19 creates 5 shortfall. Submit units, assumptions and unknown drainage/compatibility. Role-play correct current gate/readback and external liaison without public-action or treatment improvisation.

### W105-4 — People and permits
A9 unique+verifiedmedical 1=10; B11+1=12; C13+1=14; D15+1=16. Submit identities, locations and correction times. Keep suspended-but-unacknowledged permit party status unresolved until actual confirmation. Do not infer departure from an administrative flag.

### W105-5 — Degraded control and handover
Prepare limited ALT capability statement, failed-protection report and accepted relief forC. Reconcile restored events using event/upload times. Include containment, permit, people and restart constraints. Correct deliberate relief misunderstanding before acceptance.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P105-01 — Readiness

Task: Review employer/site evidence, configuration and impairment handover.

Required evidence: Current status and limits verified; no unsupported readiness. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-02 — Evidence

Task: Assess timed/quality-tagged trends and field report.

Required evidence: Stale/bad data identified; protective action not delayed. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-03 — Alarm workload

Task: Handle flood plus independent cooling alarm.

Required evidence: Priorities and delegated monitoring clear. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-04 — Controls

Task: Operate correct mock control and verify required results.

Required evidence: Command/result separate; failure escalated; no bypass. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-05 — Containment

Task: Calculate usable remaining capacity and report uncertain drainage.

Required evidence: Correct units/shortfall; no improvised spill treatment. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-06 — Responder communication

Task: Correct gate readback and confirm liaison/fallback.

Required evidence: Current access and acknowledgment verified. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-07 — People/work

Task: Reconcile roster and unacknowledged permit team.

Required evidence: Missing identity/status accurate; no unsafe search. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-08 — Habitability

Task: Respond to intake alarm and failed damper feedback.

Required evidence: Uncertainty and immediate plan response preserved. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-09 — Degraded systems

Task: Handle common-cause outage and limited alternate station.

Required evidence: No false stability or invented control capability. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-10 — Relief/recovery

Task: Correct handover and preserve unresolved restart conditions.

Required evidence: Explicit acceptance and authorized recovery gate. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

### P105-11 — Integrated performance

Task: Complete three different independent scenarios.

Required evidence: Each decision supported by observed action/trace. Record action/time, trace and assessor rationale.

lessons.title: Scoring and original credential
lessons.body:
## Scoring and original credential

Eleven dimensions 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent, 1 major help, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent accurate traceable, 4 independent anticipatory with sound reasoning. Require 36/44, each at least 3, no critical error, and three independently satisfactory scenarios. Readiness review applies across all; each scenario must pass relevant operational criteria. Critical errors: false isolation/habitability confirmation, unauthorized bypass/restart, unsafe entry/drain/treatment instruction, false all accounted, wrong uncorrected responder access or fabricated evidence. Freeze unsafe simulated actions, record, remediate and reassess changed conditions. No maximum external attempt rule is inferred from the public source; document attempts and development without hiding failures.

Complete 22 explained checks and 5 labs. Final 11 cases/33 decisions, 66 points, pass 53, at least 4/6 each, no critical error, 120 minutes. Changed final and keys restricted. Independent reviewer addresses disputed evidence against unchanged criteria. Written pass cannot replace employer readiness or scenario performance.

Issue only VNDRLY/U Onshore CRO Emergency Response — Simulation Assessed, with learner, model/site scope, package hash, dates, assessor and limitations. Set original two-year renewal/review with earlier review after material change/concern; public OPITO7031 also lists two-year validity, but no external award is implied. Real-site appointment and ongoing competence remain employer responsibilities. Materials completion does not assert actual learner assessment or live plant action.

# VUC105 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q105-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-01-L1

Later maintenance record contradicts cooling-ready sheet. What next?

**Answer:** Resolve current authorized protection and compensating arrangements.

**Reason/remediation:** A handover label is not proof of availability. Revisit Q105-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-01-L2

Does CRO role authorize public evacuation instructions?

**Answer:** Only actions allocated by the actual plan/authority, not automatically.

**Reason/remediation:** Operational information and public command are distinct. Revisit Q105-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-02-L1

Fresh display, bad-quality old value: reliable?

**Answer:** No. State measurement age/quality and use approved independent evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Refresh is not validation. Revisit Q105-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-02-L2

Need exact leak location before prescribed protection?

**Answer:** No, if the response trigger is already met.

**Reason/remediation:** Diagnosis must not delay required action. Revisit Q105-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-03-L1

Acknowledged alarm means corrected?

**Answer:** No. Track action and verified result.

**Reason/remediation:** Receipt differs from resolution. Revisit Q105-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-03-L2

Trip flood plus independent cooling alarm: what priority?

**Answer:** Use consequence/response time and allocate support without losing cooling attention.

**Reason/remediation:** Not every alarm shares the initiating cause. Revisit Q105-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-04-L1

Close command, no feedback, flow continues: state?

**Answer:** Attempted/unconfirmed isolation.

**Reason/remediation:** Selection is not achieved state. Revisit Q105-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-04-L2

Bypass trip to restore production during emergency?

**Answer:** No. Preserve safeguards and authorized response.

**Reason/remediation:** Production pressure is not bypass authority. Revisit Q105-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-05-L1

Bund 18 usable, 7 occupied, 14 incoming: shortfall?

**Answer:** 3 cubic meters; 11 available.

**Reason/remediation:** Use usable remaining capacity, not nominal total. Revisit Q105-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-05-L2

May operator improvise spill neutralization?

**Answer:** No. Use approved product/site procedure and competent advice.

**Reason/remediation:** Compatibility and exposure hazards vary. Revisit Q105-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-06-L1

Gate 2 read asGate 1: what next?

**Answer:** Correct, verify current access and obtain exact readback.

**Reason/remediation:** Wrong access can expose responders. Revisit Q105-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-06-L2

Request sent means responders dispatched?

**Answer:** No. Obtain acknowledgment and confirmation.

**Reason/remediation:** Communication stages differ. Revisit Q105-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-07-L1

Permit suspended but contractor unacknowledged: withdrawn?

**Answer:** Not established. Resolve through safe authorized contact.

**Reason/remediation:** System status is not actual person movement. Revisit Q105-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-07-L2

Raw counts match but duplicate identity exists: all accounted?

**Answer:** No. Reconcile unique identities and missing people.

**Reason/remediation:** Totals can conceal a gap. Revisit Q105-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-08-L1

Intake protection command without feedback: safe room?

**Answer:** Unconfirmed protection; follow immediate plan response.

**Reason/remediation:** No symptoms is not proof of safety. Revisit Q105-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-08-L2

Universal shelter or evacuation choice?

**Answer:** No. Actual incident, plan and responsible authority govern.

**Reason/remediation:** Hazard pathways and protection differ. Revisit Q105-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-09-L1

Frozen trend proves stable process?

**Answer:** No. Current state may be unknown.

**Reason/remediation:** A common failure can freeze several indications. Revisit Q105-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-09-L2

Alternate station assumed same controls?

**Answer:** No. Verify actual capability and transfer limitations.

**Reason/remediation:** Location does not guarantee function. Revisit Q105-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-10-L1

Relief hears confirmed isolation but record says attempted. What next?

**Answer:** Correct and obtain accurate readback before acceptance.

**Reason/remediation:** Handover can erase uncertainty if not checked. Revisit Q105-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-10-L2

Alarm clears from sensor fault: restart?

**Answer:** No. Preserve fault and authorized recovery checks.

**Reason/remediation:** Clear indication may be invalid. Revisit Q105-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q105-11-L1

Two successful scenarios offset critical third failure?

**Answer:** No. Each required scenario must pass.

**Reason/remediation:** Critical decisions cannot be averaged. Revisit Q105-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q105-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q105-11-L2

Narration replaces simulator controls/communications?

**Answer:** No. Observe actual interface and role performance.

**Reason/remediation:** Knowledge alone is insufficient. Revisit Q105-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: VNDRLY/U Plant Manager / Incident Commander — Initial Response
lessons.body:
# VNDRLY/U Plant Manager / Incident Commander — Initial Response

VUC106 • Original initial training •18November 2026

For prospective leaders, incident-team members and support personnel. This is not OPITO approval, employer appointment or a substitute for jurisdiction-specific hazardous-material command qualifications. Full proprietary criteria unavailable; public scope and primary regulator guidance support this original package. Local role development continues after initial training.

Planned 32 hours over consecutive days: 10 instruction/prebrief, 16 scenario practice/debrief, 4 labs, 2 written review/development. Every learner leads two different scenarios and participates in support roles; add time for valid observation. Objectives: prepare, activate, assess, delegate, communicate, account for people, coordinate environmental/external interfaces, manage escalation/stress and hand over/recover.

lessons.title: Q106-01 — Initial command development and authority
lessons.body:
## Q106-01 — Initial command development and authority

This course develops initial incident-management skills for plant leaders, team members and support personnel. It does not appoint an incident commander or establish every legal qualification that a particular hazardous-material response may require. The employer must define the role, applicable jurisdiction, plant knowledge, training and demonstrated competence before assignment. A senior job title does not automatically transfer command during an incident.

Learn the site emergency organization, succession and interfaces with public responders. Identify who commands site operations, who controls specialist tactics, who communicates with external agencies and how command transfers are announced. Public responders may have statutory responsibilities distinct from the plant organization. Follow the agreed arrangements rather than assuming either party's authority disappears when the other arrives.

Worked example: a plant director arrives after a trained commander has established control. The director provides resources and advice through the structure unless an explicit authorized transfer occurs. Two simultaneous command voices can create incompatible instructions and expose people.

lessons.title: Q106-02 — Preparing the plant emergency system
lessons.body:
## Q106-02 — Preparing the plant emergency system

Preparation links hazards to practical response capability. Review inventories, process/utility dependencies, containment and drainage, occupied buildings, access routes, contractors, neighboring sites and environmental receptors. Confirm actual response teams, equipment, communications and external-support arrangements. A contact list is not proof that a resource is available now.

Assign roles for operations, safety/technical advice, people accounting, liaison, logistics and records according to the site plan. Check deputies and relief. Identify impaired protection and compensating controls before an event. Plan for failed power, network or communications and inaccessible documents. Involve the people who will use the plan so instructions remain workable under stress.

Worked example: the plan assumes two response teams, but the shift can staff one and the second vehicle is unavailable. Record the real capability, revise response options and escalate restrictions through the responsible authority. Do not count the same crew twice or call a requested mutual-aid team available before confirmation.

lessons.title: Q106-03 — Activation, priorities and first decisions
lessons.body:
## Q106-03 — Activation, priorities and first decisions

A credible report requires prompt assessment and activation of the appropriate plan. Establish location, hazard, people at risk, source/time and immediate protective actions already taken. Announce command and objectives. Protect life and prevent escalation while obtaining the information needed for the next decision. Avoid delaying an already justified alarm or notification until the exact failed component is known.

State objectives as outcomes, then select safe feasible tactics with competent advice. Controlling a leak, accounting for people and preserving safe access may require different task owners. Identify what could change the priorities and when the team will review progress. Production recovery is not an initial objective when people or protection remain uncertain.

Worked example: a transfer release is reported near a contractor work area. Activate the plan, stop exposed work through the authorized process, obtain people status and request the approved source-control response. Sending an unprotected supervisor into the area to confirm the report is not a prerequisite for protective action.

lessons.title: Q106-04 — Situation assessment and changing strategy
lessons.body:
## Q106-04 — Situation assessment and changing strategy

Maintain a shared record of confirmed facts, reports, assumptions and unknowns. Evaluate data age and quality; a refreshed dashboard may contain stale information. Ask for information that changes a decision rather than collecting every possible detail. Record options, constraints, selected action, reason, owner and expected feedback.

Monitor whether actions achieve their intended result. A shutdown command without required feedback leaves source control uncertain. If a tactic fails or conditions change, revisit the strategy. Consider interactions with adjacent units, utilities, occupied buildings, drains and off-site receptors. Do not continue a plan solely because it was publicly announced or effort has been invested in it.

Worked example: the CRO reports isolation attempted but continuing flow. The commander must retain the continuing-release assumption and reassess containment and exposure. A plan based on release stopped is unsupported, even if the control button was correctly pressed.

lessons.title: Q106-05 — Delegation and responder safety
lessons.body:
## Q106-05 — Delegation and responder safety

Delegate to named competent roles with an outcome, authority limit, constraints, reporting requirement and review time. Confirm understanding. The commander maintains the overall picture while specialist leaders control their techniques within the plan. Do not improvise firefighting, chemical treatment, confined-space entry, electrical switching or medical treatment from a management course.

Responder protection includes hazard assessment, competence, equipment, communications, backup and withdrawal criteria under applicable procedures. Track team location/status and missed reports. Stop or change a tactic when its prerequisites fail. A missing person creates urgency but does not remove the need for a defensible rescue plan. Ask specialists what can be done safely and what cannot.

Worked example: a response team reports the planned approach unsafe and requests an alternative route assessment. The commander should obtain that assessment and protect remaining options, not simply order the team to find another way in. A resource that cannot operate safely is not available for that tactic.

lessons.title: Q106-06 — External responders, neighbors and public information
lessons.body:
## Q106-06 — External responders, neighbors and public information

Establish the designated liaison with fire, medical, police, environmental and other relevant agencies under the site plan. Provide site identity, hazard information, current access, people status, actions and assistance requested. Verify receipt, dispatch and arrival separately. Correct changed gate or route information promptly. Do not assume a requested resource is confirmed.

Off-site protective instructions and public information must follow the applicable authority and agreed arrangements. The plant supplies accurate facts and required notifications; it does not invent a public evacuation zone from an unverified reading. Neighboring operations may be threatened or contribute to escalation, requiring timely liaison. Use a designated spokesperson and distinguish confirmed facts from estimates; avoid releasing personal information unnecessarily.

Worked example: responders are directed toward Gate 1, but a wind/incident update makes that access unsuitable. Notify liaison and gate staff, obtain the authorized safe alternative and confirm the responders received it. A corrected internal map does not automatically update vehicles already approaching.

lessons.title: Q106-07 — People accounting and welfare
lessons.body:
## Q106-07 — People accounting and welfare

Require unique-identity reconciliation across muster, contractors, visitors, response teams, medical and transfers. Raw totals can match the baseline while hiding a duplicate and a missing person. Ask the coordinator to state confirmed, unconfirmed and moved people with source/time. Preserve last-known-location evidence for missing people and provide it to the authorized response decision.

Medical professionals direct treatment; command coordinates access and resources. Confirm assistance arrangements and receiving destinations for transfers. Monitor welfare during extended incidents and plan relief, rest and communication. Do not call a person evacuated because a seat is allocated or a transfer requested. Departure and receipt are separate events.

Worked example: one worker appears at both muster and medical while another is absent. Reconcile the identity and movement rather than declaring the raw total complete. A later medical confirmation closes only the relevant discrepancy; an unreported response team remains a separate issue.

lessons.title: Q106-08 — Containment and environmental decisions
lessons.body:
## Q106-08 — Containment and environmental decisions

A release can migrate through drainage, water, soil or adjacent plant. Obtain approved site drawings and substance-specific information. Determine which containment is actually usable, what is already occupied and what incoming volume is credible. State uncertainty. A nominal bund capacity may not equal usable capacity during the incident.

Use competent spill/environmental advice and approved procedures. Do not improvise neutralization, dilution, mixing or opening drains. Such actions can increase exposure or spread contamination. Coordinate environmental measures with life safety and responder protection. Record notifications and specialist recommendations through the designated roles.

Worked example: a fictional containment system has 30 cubic meters usable, 12 occupied and a potential 23 additional. Remaining capacity is 18 and potential shortfall 5. Report the gap and uncertainty; do not order a hazardous drain operation merely to make the arithmetic fit. The calculation supports the decision but does not replace verified technical advice.

lessons.title: Q106-09 — Shelter, evacuation and loss of site capability
lessons.body:
## Q106-09 — Shelter, evacuation and loss of site capability

Shelter or evacuation decisions depend on the actual hazard, protective building capability, routes, timing and responsible authority. Do not assume every building provides protection or every outdoor route is safe. Monitor protection failures and loss of access. A provisional time estimate is conditional and may become invalid when ventilation, power or route availability changes.

Confirm capacity and suitability of transport and receiving arrangements. Distinguish nominal resources from available ones. Do not overload or rely on an unconfirmed arrival estimate. If the command location becomes unsuitable, transfer through the plan while disclosing the alternate location's limitations. Preserve people accountability and communication during movement.

Worked example: thirty-eight people require a movement plan and one of two twenty-four-place vehicles is unavailable. Available capacity 24 leaves 14 without that option. Obtain confirmed alternatives and reassess timing; neither an extra name on a manifest nor an optimistic ETA creates capacity.

lessons.title: Q106-10 — Stress, team performance and challenge
lessons.body:
## Q106-10 — Stress, team performance and challenge

High workload can create fixation, rushed communication and missed feedback. Use brief structured reviews: facts, threats, objectives, actions, gaps and next decision. Assign support and relief before overload becomes failure. Keep critical monitoring owned when routine calls or media requests compete for attention.

Encourage evidence-based challenge regardless of seniority. Acknowledge bad news, correct the picture and change the plan when needed. Do not defend a failed assumption to avoid embarrassment. During practice, feedback should identify observable behavior and consequences rather than label a person. Record coaching so developmental help is not mistaken for independent performance.

Worked example: a junior liaison identifies that mutual aid was requested but never confirmed. Check the evidence, correct the resource board and reassess options. Dismissing the warning because the resource was already announced can leave the plan dependent on a nonexistent capability.

lessons.title: Q106-11 — Handover, recovery and individual development
lessons.body:
## Q106-11 — Handover, recovery and individual development

Stabilization is not recovery. Retain restrictions while protection, plant integrity, permits, isolations, people or environmental status remain unresolved. Transfer command with current objectives, confirmed and failed actions, people/responders, external commitments, deadlines and recovery constraints. The incoming commander accepts and affected roles are informed.

Recovery and restart use the authorized technical and management process. Preserve original logs with visible corrections. Debrief decisions against information available at the time, identify both individual and system improvements, assign owners and define evidence of closure. Initial-course completion includes an individual development plan for local familiarization, drills and any additional role qualification.

Worked example: a learner completes two initial scenarios but lacks site chemical and external-agency knowledge. Record successful course learning within its scope and identify the remaining employer development. Do not convert an initial training certificate into a declaration of independent readiness for that plant.

---

lessons.title: VUC106 instructor and scenario workbook
lessons.body: # VUC106 instructor and scenario workbook

lessons.title: Resources and delivery safeguards
lessons.body:
## Resources and delivery safeguards

Use an isolated incident-command room or accessible remote role-play system, fictional site map, status board, named roster, resource cards, training communications, clocks and the forms below. No live alarms, public emergency calls, plant controls, chemicals, physical firefighting or transport operations. Controller manages injects; observer appraises each learner; role players provide CRO, Response, Muster, Medic, Gate, Liaison, Technical and Relief. Every learner leads both scenarios and performs a support role. Extend time when needed rather than replacing direct observation with group attendance.

Brief stop word, real-emergency override, fitness demands, accessibility, breaks, privacy and recording. Avoid unnecessary distress. Practice may be coached; label coaching and obtain changed unprompted evidence for the original course decision. A competent site/emergency instructor validates adaptation. Actual employer appointment and jurisdiction-specific role requirements remain outside an initial certificate.

Adaptation A106: site/model and plan revision___ authority/succession___ process/chemical hazards___ containment/drainage___ people/contractor arrangements___ response capability___ gate/access___ external/public-agency interfaces___ shelter/evacuation criteria___ communications/fallback___ recovery authority___ safe drill approval___ observer___. Real-site practice uses approved local information; do not infer it from this fictional model.

lessons.title: Fictional site Alder
lessons.body:
## Fictional site Alder

Units T transfer, U utilities, B occupied building and M muster. Gates G1 near T and G2 alternate. Only controller-confirmed routes are available. Learner is incident commander for the simulation. CRO applies approved simulated control card: credible transfer release requires stop/close commands with stopped, closed and flow-zero confirmation; missing feedback means source control unconfirmed. Response leader owns specialist tactical assessment; Medic owns clinical decisions; Muster reconciles identities; Liaison contacts simulated external services and competent public authority; Gate receives current safe access; Technical supplies containment/product information. No learner gives real public instructions or specialist operating sequences.

Primary channel E, approved fallback B requires two-way test. Initial emergency activation, alarm and role delegation are authorized by the model. Hazardous entry requires a competent plan and safeguards; no physical entry occurs. Recovery requires verified protection, permit/isolation resolution and authorized release. A resource request or estimate is not confirmation of capability, dispatch or arrival.

lessons.title: Scenario A — controllable transfer incident with environmental gap
lessons.body:
## Scenario A — controllable transfer incident with environmental gap

Start 09:00, roster A01–A16. One team staffed, despite an old plan listing two. Containment verified usable 30 cubic meters, occupied 12, potential further 23: remaining 18, possible shortfall 5. Drain destination unknown. G1 affected, G2 status unconfirmed.

Minute 0: CRO and Field provide credible release report near contractors. Observe activation, command, objectives and role allocation. Minute 3: source-control command sent but flow continues; require unconfirmed status and revised strategy. Minute 5: Response requests task boundaries and reports no safe entry plan yet. Learner must not order improvised entry. Minute 7: Technical confirms capacity data but not drain destination; require specialist/environmental coordination, no drain opening or chemistry improvisation. Minute 9: Muster reports A01–A14, A14, A15: fifteen unique, A16 unconfirmed. Minute 11: Medic verifies A16 at medical with time/source: sixteen global. Minute 13: Gate confirms G2 suitable at 09:13; Liaison reads G1 back. Correct and confirm responders receive current access. Minute 15: CRO supplies all required source-control feedback; environmental disposition and one protection fault remain. Minute 17: director asks for immediate restart and tries to take command without handover. Preserve authority/recovery boundaries. Minute 20: Relief accepts plant, people, environmental and resource constraints. Debrief observed strengths and specific development gaps.

lessons.title: Scenario B — escalating utility incident and threatened building
lessons.body:
## Scenario B — escalating utility incident and threatened building

Start 14:00, roster B01–B24. One qualified team; mutual aid requested but unconfirmed. Two fictional 14-place vehicles, initially available. Building B has provisional protective endpoint 14:30 dependent on stated protection; this is a training estimate, not guaranteed safety. G1 unavailable, G2 initially suitable.

Minute 0: credible utility/process incident, source state uncertain. Activate plan and obtain technical picture. Minute 3: one vehicle unavailable: fourteen available, ten-person gap. Minute 5: Response reports planned approach unsafe; obtain options without directing uncontrolled entry. Minute 7: Muster lists B01–B22, B22, B23: twenty-three unique, B24 unconfirmed. Minute 9: coworker says B24 probably at medical; retain as lead, not confirmation. Minute 11: Medic confirms B24: twenty-four global. Minute 13: Liaison says aid may arrive at 14:25 but dispatch not confirmed; learner must not count it available. Minute 15: movement estimate eleven minutes gives fifteen remaining and four nominal margin. Immediately inject ventilation failure and route uncertainty; previous timing no longer guarantees a viable option. Minute 17: G2 becomes unavailable; update responders through liaison and obtain authorized alternative. Minute 19: junior communicator challenges an obsolete aid ETA on board while media calls arrive. Expect evidence-based correction and delegated public communication. Minute 21: controller supplies alternative only after capability request: ten approved places, available 14:24, route G3 confirmed by Field at 14:21, operator retains safe-movement authority. Confirm integration and current conditions rather than assuming the old building estimate is restored. Minute 23: primary E fails; test fallback and give current command/people/access picture. End with a supported protective decision, resource/identity plan and accepted relief. No actual shelter, evacuation or public direction is enacted.

lessons.title: Changed development scenario C
lessons.body:
## Changed development scenario C

Start 16:00, roster C01–C18; reports C01–C16, C16, C17: seventeen unique, C18 unresolved, later verified physically at muster. Usable containment 35, occupied 14, potential incoming 27: remaining 21, shortfall 6 cubic meters. Two 11-place vehicles, one unavailable: eleven available, gap seven. At 16:10 provisional endpoint 16:26 and movement twelve minutes gives four nominal margin, then route loss invalidates it. Add conflicting senior instruction, unconfirmed mutual-aid capability, wrong gate readback and unresolved permit during recovery. Provide revised reference data before practice; do not reveal assessment inject sequence. Use changed unprompted performance after remediation, not a coached replay labeled independent.

lessons.title: Laboratories
lessons.body:
## Laboratories

### W106-1 — Command and capability
Create Alder role/authority chart and resource board. Expected one staffed team, aid requested/unconfirmed, explicit operations/muster/liaison/records owners. Resolve director arrival without silent transfer. Change: second team arrives but suitability unverified; count only confirmed capability.

### W106-2 — Decision and communication log
Record A's attempted control, continuing flow, containment concern and gate correction. Expected facts/assumptions distinct, owner/feedback specified, current G2 acknowledgment and recovery constraints retained. Change: G2 later unavailable; withdraw old instruction through liaison rather than only changing a map.

### W106-3 — People and environment
A fifteen unique plus verified medical one equals sixteen. B twenty-three plus one equals twenty-four. C seventeen plus verified arrival one equals eighteen. A containment 30−12=18, 23−18=5 shortfall; C35−14=21, 27−21=6. Submit named reconciliation and volume units/assumptions; no improvised treatment follows.

### W106-4 — Escalation, relief and development
B available 14/gap 10; initial timing 30−15−11=4 nominal minutes. C available 11/gap 7; 26−10−12=4. Explain invalidating changes. Prepare accepted handover, confirmed/provisional resource distinctions and individual development plan with evidence-based actions. No overload or guaranteed waiting period.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P106-01 — Authority

Task: Resolve conflicting manager instructions and command transfer.

Evidence: Single accepted command; external/specialist boundaries retained. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-02 — Preparedness

Task: Review actual teams, protection and mutual-aid status.

Evidence: No double-booking or assumed resources. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-03 — Activation

Task: Respond to credible release and set protective objectives.

Evidence: Timely plan activation; no unsafe confirmation mission. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-04 — Assessment

Task: Maintain evidence/options board through failed source control.

Evidence: Assumptions challenged and strategy updated. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-05 — Delegation

Task: Assign response tasks with constraints and feedback.

Evidence: Competent tactics and responder safety preserved. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-06 — Liaison

Task: Correct access instructions and communicate public-impact uncertainty.

Evidence: Current acknowledged facts; no invented public authority. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-07 — People

Task: Reconcile identities and medical/transfer updates.

Evidence: No false all accounted; movement stages distinct. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-08 — Environment

Task: Calculate containment gap and request specialist action.

Evidence: Correct units/assumptions; no improvised treatment. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-09 — Escalation

Task: Address unavailable transport and lost route/protection.

Evidence: Actual capacity and conditional time recognized. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-10 — Team

Task: Handle challenge and overload with role allocation.

Evidence: Evidence-based correction and critical monitoring retained. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

### P106-11 — Recovery/development

Task: Hand over constraints and produce individual development plan.

Evidence: Explicit acceptance; initial scope not overclaimed. Record behavior/time, source and observer reasoning.

lessons.title: Reproducible forms
lessons.body:
## Reproducible forms

O106 organization: commander/deputy___ role owners___ authority/specialist interfaces___ resource availability/gaps___ command transfer/acceptance/time___.

S106 situation: source/time___ facts___ assumptions/unknowns___ people/hazards___ objectives___ options/constraints___ action/reason/owner___ feedback/trigger___ revised decision___.

C106 liaison: agency/role___ hazard/site/access___ request___ acknowledgment___ capability/dispatch/arrival confirmation___ public-information authority___ changed instruction/readback___ unresolved___.

P106 people: baseline/version___ unique identities/current locations___ missing/last-known___ medical/responders___ planned/departed/received___ correction/source/time___ command acknowledgment___.

E106 environment/resources: usable/occupied/incoming volume and units___ uncertainty___ shortfall___ drainage/compatibility___ specialist advice___ actual transport/capacity___ assistance___ alternative confirmation___ decision authority___.

H106 relief/recovery: incident/objectives___ people/responders___ source/protection___ environment___ external commitments___ outstanding permits/isolations___ deadlines___ accepted transfer___ restart prerequisites___.

A106 appraisal: learner/role/scenario/version___ inject/action times___ dimension/score/evidence___ coaching___ critical error___ feedback___ changed demonstration___ observer/date___.

D106 development: observed gap___ consequence___ required practice/local knowledge/qualification___ employer supervisor___ date/opportunity___ evidence of improvement___ review result___.

lessons.title: Decision, remediation and original award
lessons.body:
## Decision, remediation and original award

Eleven dimensions scored 0–4: 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major assistance, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent sound traceable, 4 independent with timely anticipation. Require 36/44, each at least 3, no unresolved critical error and two independently satisfactory leader-role scenarios. Coached initial practice remains separate. Critical errors: unauthorized hazardous deployment, overload, false all-accounted/received report, improvised chemical/drain action, unsupported public instruction, concealed failed protection, unauthorized restart or fabricated evidence. Stop unsafe simulated action, record, remediate and observe changed performance. A competent independent reviewer resolves disputed evidence against unchanged criteria.

Complete 22 explained checks and 4 labs. Controlled final 11 cases/33 decisions, 66 points, pass 53, at least 4/6 each, no critical error, 120 minutes. Changed final/keys remain private. Retain failed attempts and coaching. Written pass is not a substitute for observed role practice.

Issue VNDRLY/U Plant Manager/Incident Commander — Initial Response Training only after the original course decision passes, with identity, version/hash, scenario roles, dates, assessor and development plan. This records initial training, not statutory hazardous-material command qualification, external OPITO approval or employer appointment. The public external initial award has no expiry; do not invent an external expiry. Set employer review/development dates for local knowledge, drills and applicable qualifications. Authoring completion is not a learner completion claim.


---

lessons.title: VUC106 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC106 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q106-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-01-L1

Senior director arrives: automatic command transfer?

**Answer:** No. Use explicit authorized transfer and announce it.

**Reason/remediation:** Rank alone does not establish current command. Revisit Q106-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-01-L2

Does initial certificate qualify every hazardous-material command role?

**Answer:** No. Employer/jurisdiction-specific requirements remain separate.

**Reason/remediation:** Course scope must not overclaim authority. Revisit Q106-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-02-L1

Mutual aid requested: available?

**Answer:** Not until capability/availability confirmed.

**Reason/remediation:** A contact list is not a deployed resource. Revisit Q106-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-02-L2

One crew assigned as two simultaneous teams: valid?

**Answer:** No. Record actual capability and resolve gap.

**Reason/remediation:** Double-booking creates fictional resources. Revisit Q106-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-03-L1

Wait for exact flange before credible-release activation?

**Answer:** No, when plan trigger is met.

**Reason/remediation:** Protective action need not await perfect diagnosis. Revisit Q106-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-03-L2

Production restart an immediate life-safety objective?

**Answer:** No. First protect people/control escalation.

**Reason/remediation:** Recovery requires separate conditions. Revisit Q106-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-04-L1

Isolation command, continued flow: assume stopped?

**Answer:** No. Retain unconfirmed source control.

**Reason/remediation:** Command is not result. Revisit Q106-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-04-L2

New evidence invalidates announced plan: what next?

**Answer:** Reassess and communicate revised strategy.

**Reason/remediation:** Prior commitment is not evidence. Revisit Q106-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-05-L1

Missing person permits unassessed entry?

**Answer:** No. Obtain competent response plan and safeguards.

**Reason/remediation:** Urgency does not remove exposure hazards. Revisit Q106-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-05-L2

Delegation needs what?

**Answer:** Named role, outcome, limits, feedback and review.

**Reason/remediation:** Untracked tasks can fail silently. Revisit Q106-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-06-L1

Gate access changes: internal map update sufficient?

**Answer:** No. Confirm liaison/responders receive current instruction.

**Reason/remediation:** Approaching crews may hold old directions. Revisit Q106-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-06-L2

Invent public evacuation zone from uncertain wind?

**Answer:** No. Follow competent authority/site arrangements.

**Reason/remediation:** Unverified estimates cannot establish public protection. Revisit Q106-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-07-L1

Duplicate muster/medical identity: count twice?

**Answer:** No. Reconcile unique identity/location.

**Reason/remediation:** Raw totals can conceal missing people. Revisit Q106-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-07-L2

Seat allocated means evacuated?

**Answer:** No. Confirm departure and receipt.

**Reason/remediation:** Planned movement is not completion. Revisit Q106-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-08-L1

Usable 30, occupied 12, incoming 23: shortfall?

**Answer:** 5 cubic meters; 18 remaining.

**Reason/remediation:** Use verified usable remaining volume. Revisit Q106-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-08-L2

Open unknown drain to avoid overflow?

**Answer:** No. Seek approved specialist response.

**Reason/remediation:** The action may spread contamination/exposure. Revisit Q106-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-09-L1

38 people, two 24-place vehicles, one unavailable: gap?

**Answer:** 14 people; 24 available.

**Reason/remediation:** Nominal 48 is not actual capacity. Revisit Q106-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-09-L2

Old shelter estimate survives ventilation failure?

**Answer:** Not guaranteed; reassess immediately.

**Reason/remediation:** Protection assumptions can fail. Revisit Q106-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-10-L1

Junior says aid unconfirmed: ignore after announcement?

**Answer:** No. Verify and correct resource assumptions.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence outranks confidence. Revisit Q106-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-10-L2

How respond to overload?

**Answer:** Delegate support, retain monitoring and arrange relief.

**Reason/remediation:** Unmanaged workload degrades decisions. Revisit Q106-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q106-11-L1

Incident stable means restart authorized?

**Answer:** No. Resolve safeguards/permits and obtain authorized release.

**Reason/remediation:** Stability is not full recovery. Revisit Q106-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q106-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q106-11-L2

Initial learner lacks site knowledge: what record?

**Answer:** Course scope plus specific employer development plan.

**Reason/remediation:** Training completion is not appointment readiness. Revisit Q106-11 and perform its changed application.


---

lessons.body:
# VUC106 sources and coverage

Reviewed 18 November 2026. Original VNDRLY initial development; no external approval or copied proprietary criteria.

| Primary source | Verified basis | Coverage and limitation |
|---|---|---|
| [OPITO9030 public product](https://opito.com/standards-and-qualifications/industry-standards-library/plant-manager-incident-commander-initial-response-training) | Initial incident-team training in command,control,communication and stress,with manager-role scenario practice;two units,26-hour public schedule,no expiry | Q1–11,A/B and development plan. Original VNDRLY32-hour schedule and two-lead-scenario decision;full proprietary criteria unavailable. |
| [HSE emergency procedures](https://www.hse.gov.uk/workplace-health/emergency-procedures.htm) | Competent designated emergency roles and site-specific arrangements | Q1–3,5–7 and adaptation. |
| [HSE spill/emergency technical guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeasspill.htm) | Site-specific containment and response planning | Q8 and volume exercises. Historical1999legal references not treated as current numbering;no generic chemical-treatment instruction copied. |
| [HSE COMAH2015 guidance](https://www.hse.gov.uk/pubns/priced/l111.pdf) | Onshore major-accident regulatory context | Local applicable arrangements;not a claim every site is within COMAH. |
| [HSE control room design](https://www.hse.gov.uk/comah/sragtech/techmeascontrol.htm) | Human/interface/team conditions affect abnormal response | Q4,9–10 and degraded-command planning. |

Not a claim this course meets HAZWOPER or current employer-specific legal requirements. |
