lessons.title: VUC107 — Cathodic Protection Tester
lessons.body:
# VUC107 — Cathodic Protection Tester

Original VNDRLY/U training materials. This is not AMPP certification or permission for electrical, excavation, hot-work or specialist design tasks.

lessons.title: Q107-01 — Role, preparation and safe boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q107-01 — Role, preparation and safe boundaries

A tester produces trustworthy measurements and identifies conditions needing a more experienced corrosion practitioner. A reading is not a design decision or proof that a whole asset is protected. Before work, identify the structure, owner, drawing revision, test-point identity, electrolyte, material, applicable procedure and person authorized to interpret results. Review the route, access, traffic, weather, communications, electrical hazards and buried services. A familiar test box may contain foreign bonds or induced voltage: familiarity does not prove it safe.

Use the instrument and leads rated for the actual environment and anticipated voltage. Inspect insulation, fuses, probes, enclosure and battery; check calibration status and function before and after the task. Do not insert a probe into an unknown terminal or open an energized rectifier cabinet merely to complete a worksheet. Electrical work, hazardous-area equipment, excavation, confined spaces and exothermic attachment require separate authorization and controls. Stop for damaged equipment, unexpected touch voltage, gas alarm, lightning, loss of safe access or uncertain asset identity. Report the incomplete test rather than inventing a value.

All hands-on teaching here uses an isolated, current-limited low-voltage simulator with accessible protected terminals. Actual field demonstrations require an approved task plan and competent supervision. Worked decision: the test point is locked and the record is due today. Photograph the identifier from a safe position, record inaccessible/not tested, notify the owner and arrange authorized access. An old reading copied into today's field creates a false maintenance record.

lessons.title: Q107-02 — Electric circuits and measurement units
lessons.body:
## Q107-02 — Electric circuits and measurement units

Voltage is potential difference, current is charge flow, resistance relates voltage to current, and power is energy per unit time. DC direction and polarity matter; AC requires the appropriate instrument mode and frequency response. Convert millivolts to volts and milliamperes to amperes before substituting into equations. For a resistive DC circuit V = IR and P = VI. Series resistances add; parallel branches share voltage and their currents add. Kirchhoff's current law expresses conservation at a junction; voltage rises and drops balance around a complete loop.

For an isolated 12 V teaching supply across 4 ohms, I = 3 A and P = 36 W. Two resistors, 4 and 8 ohms in series, give 12 ohms and 1 A. The same resistors in parallel give 1/R = 1/4 + 1/8, hence R = 2.667 ohms and total current 4.5 A. Real supplies have limits and leads have resistance; these calculations do not authorize connecting that load to an actual source.

A voltmeter is connected across points; a direct ammeter is placed in series only within a verified safe circuit. An ammeter across a voltage source can create a short. An ohmmeter must not be applied to an energized circuit. Disconnecting a bond can interrupt protection or create an unsafe potential difference, so use approved shunt/clamp methods when the procedure requires them. Work out expected range before connection. A display of 25 mV is 0.025 V, not 25 V.

lessons.title: Q107-03 — Corrosion cells, chemistry and polarization
lessons.body:
## Q107-03 — Corrosion cells, chemistry and polarization

A corrosion cell requires anodic and cathodic reactions, an electronic path and an electrolyte path. Metal dissolution occurs at the anode; reduction consumes electrons at the cathode. Electrons travel through the metal while ionic conduction closes the electrolyte path. Different metals, oxygen availability, deposits, temperature and local chemistry can establish unequal surface conditions. A single pipe can contain both anodic and cathodic regions without being attached to a visibly different metal.

Cathodic protection supplies current to shift the protected surface toward cathodic behavior. Polarization is a change in electrode potential associated with current; it is distinct from voltage drop in the surrounding electrolyte. Coatings reduce exposed area but damaged or disbonded coatings can concentrate demand or shield a surface from effective current. Neither coating appearance nor a very negative remote reading proves protection under a shield.

Faraday's relation connects charge to ideal electrochemical mass change: m = ItM/(nF). For an original ideal example, iron dissolving as Fe 2+, I = 0.010 A, t = 86400 seconds, M = 55.85 g/mol, n = 2 and F = 96485 C/mol gives about 0.250 g. This assumes that current is entirely associated with that reaction. It is not a field wall-loss prediction: current distribution, efficiency, reaction chemistry and area are unknown. A small anodic area coupled to a large cathodic area can suffer concentrated attack. Explain the mechanism before proposing any change.

lessons.title: Q107-04 — Galvanic and impressed-current systems
lessons.body:
## Q107-04 — Galvanic and impressed-current systems

A galvanic system couples a suitably active anode to the structure through a metallic connection and shared electrolyte. The anode is consumed while providing protection current. An impressed-current system uses a DC power supply, anode circuit, structure connection and electrolyte return path. In the conventional arrangement the rectifier positive terminal goes to the anodes and negative to the protected structure. Reversed connections can drive structure corrosion. Identify actual labels and drawings rather than relying on cable color.

Recognize anode beds, junction boxes, bonds, isolation devices, test leads, coupons, permanent reference cells and protective devices. Isolation limits unintended current demand; bonding may be intentional for continuity or interference control. Do not remove a bond or bypass an isolator to make a reading look better. The owner must evaluate consequences for all connected facilities.

Worked comparison: a small coated component requiring little current may be suited to a galvanic approach, while a larger demand can require controlled impressed current. This is a concept comparison, not a tester design rule. Soil resistance, coating condition, anode life, neighboring structures, power reliability and maintenance all affect selection. If output falls after rain, do not declare anode exhaustion from that observation alone. Verify equipment, record output and potentials, and refer the pattern for diagnosis. Changes to rectifier taps, anode installation or bond resistance require the authorized procedure and responsible practitioner.

lessons.title: Q107-05 — Meters and reference electrodes
lessons.body:
## Q107-05 — Meters and reference electrodes

Structure-to-electrolyte potential is measured against a reference electrode with a known, stable electrochemical potential. Copper/copper-sulfate cells are commonly used for soil/fresh-water work; suitable silver/silver-chloride cells are used in marine applications. Different filling solutions and temperatures change reference potential, so the name alone is insufficient for a conversion. Record cell type, identifier, condition and comparison result. Follow the manufacturer's preparation, storage and contamination controls. Do not substitute a random metal rod and call it an equivalent reference.

Compare a field cell against a maintained master in the same suitable electrolyte under the approved method. A large or unstable difference requires investigation, not an undocumented correction. Inspect porous contact, liquid condition, crystals where applicable, leakage and lead continuity. Keep the electrode from contamination; use proper contact with the electrolyte, not dry asphalt. A high-input-impedance voltmeter reduces loading, but poor contact can still make a high-resistance measurement unreliable.

Teaching acceptance card R107 permits a field/master difference no greater than 10 mV under its specified comparison conditions. Cell A differs by 4 mV and is stable; cell B differs by 28 mV and drifts. A passes this fictional check; quarantine B and document it. This is not a universal manufacturer tolerance. If a meter reads -0.91 V with red on structure and black on reference, reversing leads should reverse sign, not change magnitude materially. Preserve the standard connection convention in the report.

lessons.title: Q107-06 — Structure potentials, interruption and interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q107-06 — Structure potentials, interruption and interpretation

Identify the correct structure terminal, establish sound permitted contact, place the reference at the procedure's defined location and record polarity, units, position and current condition. ON readings include potential contributions from current flowing through resistive paths. Synchronized interruption can help distinguish the immediate resistive change from subsequent polarization decay, but only when relevant sources and timing are controlled. A delayed reading is not automatically an instant-OFF reading, and an un-interrupted foreign source can leave residual error.

For the training steel dataset, ON is -1.120 V, valid immediate OFF is -0.910 V, and later fully established depolarized value is -0.770 V against the same verified CSE. ON-to-OFF magnitude change is 210 mV; polarization decay magnitude is 140 mV. Do not use ON minus depolarized, 350 mV, as the polarization decay. Record the actual time series and evidence supporting the baseline rather than selecting a convenient late value.

US gas-pipeline Appendix D contains material-specific protection alternatives, including specified steel potential and polarization-shift approaches, with measurement qualifications. It is not a universal acceptance rule for every tank, ship, alloy or environment. A raw ON reading more negative than -0.85 V CSE does not alone establish compliance; voltage drops and applicability require evaluation. The tester records conditions and flags uncertainty. Coupons approximate selected exposed surfaces; their connection, area, location and interruption method affect interpretation. Never claim a coupon represents all shielded surfaces.

lessons.title: Q107-07 — Current, shunts and output checks
lessons.body:
## Q107-07 — Current, shunts and output checks

A calibrated shunt provides a known small voltage drop at a stated current. Use I = measured mV × rated A / rated mV, retaining polarity for direction. Connect a suitable voltmeter across the designated shunt terminals; do not short the shunt or open a live bond. A DC clamp requires appropriate capability, zeroing, conductor placement and range. Clamping both outgoing and returning conductors may cancel the measured field.

A 50 mV/10 A shunt reads +17.5 mV under the drawing's positive convention: current is +3.5 A. The same device at -7.5 mV indicates -1.5 A, meaning reverse direction relative to that convention, not a negative physical magnitude. Record direction with the terminal convention. Check for loose connections and contact errors only by authorized safe methods.

An isolated simulated rectifier has 18 V external output and 3 A verified current, yielding an apparent operating circuit resistance of 6 ohms and DC output power 54 W. These are operating-point values, not a complete model of electrode polarization or rectifier efficiency. Compare external readings with built-in indications and historical conditions. If panel current is 4 A but the validated shunt gives 3 A, record the discrepancy and refer instrument diagnosis. Do not adjust protection output to reconcile a faulty panel meter. Unexpected zero current can arise from power loss, open leads, poor contacts or measurement error; it is not by itself proof of one failed component.

lessons.title: Q107-08 — Soil resistivity, sampling and pH
lessons.body:
## Q107-08 — Soil resistivity, sampling and pH

Resistance is measured for a particular geometry; resistivity expresses a material property with length units. In the simplified Wenner four-pin arrangement, equal spacing a and sufficiently shallow pins support rho = 2 pi a R. Use the same length units throughout. For a = 2 m and R = 12 ohms, rho is 150.80 ohm-m, or 15080 ohm-cm. Significant pin depth, nearby buried metal, uneven contact and layered soil affect interpretation; use the applicable correction or approved method rather than applying the simple formula blindly.

Before inserting pins, obtain required utility clearance and safe access. Lay out equal spacing, verify terminal assignments, avoid lead coupling per the instrument instructions and record spacing, depth, orientation, moisture and weather. Repeat at specified spacings and directions; do not average away a meaningful difference. Soil-box testing uses the box's verified geometry factor: rho = R A/L. If A = 40 cm 2, L = 10 cm and R = 250 ohms, rho = 1000 ohm-cm. Sampling moisture and compaction must be stated because disturbed samples may differ from in-place conditions.

Single-probe resistivity methods require their instrument-specific geometry and calibration; do not reuse the Wenner multiplier. Soil pH measures acidity/alkalinity, not CP adequacy. Calibrate a suitable pH method with appropriate buffers and retain sample identity, temperature and preparation. Antimony/CSE methods require the approved conversion and limitations; an unexplained voltage is not a valid pH. Worked decision: two samples labelled the same station have different moisture and no depth record. Retain both results as qualified observations and resample; choosing the lower value creates false precision.

lessons.title: Q107-09 — Continuity, isolation, locating and interference
lessons.body:
## Q107-09 — Continuity, isolation, locating and interference

Electrical continuity means an effective metallic path; isolation intentionally interrupts selected paths. Similar potentials on opposite sides of an isolator can suggest a problem but can also occur for other reasons. Use the authorized combination of potential comparison, controlled source response and suitable isolation instruments. Do not connect an ohmmeter to an energized installation or remove surge protection without approval. AC mitigation and overvoltage devices can provide safety functions that must remain intact.

A locator can couple conductively or inductively to a structure. Verify the intended conductor and avoid signal transfer to parallel utilities. A trace is evidence supporting location, not permission to excavate. Record confidence, depth-estimate limitations and conflicts with drawings; follow the owner's locating and excavation controls.

Stray DC can enter a structure at one location and leave at another, with corrosion risk where current discharges. Time-varying sources can cause fluctuating potentials and bond current. AC exposure introduces both personnel hazards and corrosion considerations; DC protection readings alone do not resolve it. In a training log, structure potential cycles from -0.95 to -0.62 V in step with a nearby switching event while reference and contact remain stable. Preserve synchronized time records, source state and location, then refer to the responsible corrosion specialist. Do not install an improvised drain bond to a neighbor. Coordination, ownership and engineered protection are essential.

lessons.title: Q107-10 — Installation assistance, marine work and records
lessons.body:
## Q107-10 — Installation assistance, marine work and records

A tester assisting installation checks the approved drawing, material identity, anode condition, lead polarity, cable insulation and test-point labels before burial or concealment. Anode backfill and packaging must match the approved product method. Connections must provide continuity without unacceptable structure damage; coating repairs must be compatible and inspected before covering. Exothermic welding, pin brazing and other attachment methods require their own approved procedure, competent personnel and fire/structure controls. A classroom demonstration does not authorize a live pipeline attachment.

For marine drop-cell surveys, identify the approved reference type, deployment depth, position, tide/current conditions and structure connection. Control over-water access, dropped objects, entanglement and vessel operations. Lower and retrieve only by the approved arrangement; record movement and instability rather than selecting a desired reading. Marine reference scales cannot be silently substituted for soil CSE values.

A usable record contains asset/test-point identity, date/time, operator, instrument/cell IDs, procedure revision, raw readings with signs and units, locations, source/interruption states, environmental conditions, anomalies, repeat tests and disposition. Preserve original entries with traceable corrections. Worked closeout: two points fail access, one reference check fails and five readings are valid. Report all eight planned points with distinct outcomes; do not call the route complete or replace the three missing values. Restore authorized temporary test arrangements, verify the required operating state with the owner and hand over unresolved risks. An honest incomplete result enables maintenance; a fabricated complete route hides corrosion risk.

lessons.title: VUC107 workbook, observed practice and delivery
lessons.body: # VUC107 workbook, observed practice and delivery

lessons.title: Entry, resources and timetable
lessons.body:
## Entry, resources and timetable

Entry: basic arithmetic, ability to read signs/units and follow a stop-work instruction. Diagnose unit conversion and circuit understanding before practice; remediate rather than exclude a learner for unfamiliar notation. This original 40-hour schedule comprises 12 hours instruction/worked examples, 16 supervised practical hours, 6 integrated application hours, 2 review/remediation hours, 2 final-exam hours and 2 feedback/changed-demonstration hours. More time is required if safe independent performance is not achieved. Ten domains are assessed; simulator practice precedes any approved field demonstration.

Instructor: experienced corrosion practitioner competent in the particular measurements, supported by authorized electrical/field specialists where needed. Assessor observes performance directly and retains evidence; a written answer cannot stand in for instrument handling. Provide accessible written diagrams, large displays and extra reading time as appropriate without weakening safety or independent calculation requirements.

Resources: isolated current-limited simulator with protected voltage/current terminals and known resistors; rated meter and sound leads; labelled shunts; suitable DC clamp; maintained reference/master cells and comparison vessel; approved soil-resistivity instrument, clear training area, shallow pins and measured spacing; soil box with recorded dimensions; labelled samples and pH buffers/instrument; inert anode/cable/isolator models; locator training loop; marine drop-cell dry mock-up; drawings, safe-work cards and forms. No mains cabinet, live pipe attachment, uncontrolled excavation or over-water deployment is required for this course. If resources are missing, defer the relevant observed station; do not substitute a slide and claim competence.

Training card R107: reference comparison limit 10 mV under common controlled comparison conditions; equality permitted, instability not permitted. This is a fictional exercise criterion. Record actual manufacturer requirements separately in real work. Simulator uncertainty/tolerance: voltage ±0.01 V, current ±0.05 A, resistance ±1%; account for actual instrument specifications when grading physical observations. Instructor verifies safe setup and expected readings before learners enter. Do not create real electrical faults; use fault cards.

lessons.title: Worked laboratories
lessons.body:
## Worked laboratories

### W107-01 — Circuits and current

Set isolated 12 V model with 4 and 8 ohm resistors. Learner draws series and parallel arrangements before touching leads, predicts currents, selects meter modes, measures safely and compares. Series expected 1 A, parallel 4.5 A total, branches 3 and 1.5 A. A separate 50 mV/10 A shunt dataset gives 17.5 and-7.5 mV: 3.5 and-1.5 A. Instructor injects an ammeter-across-source sketch; learner rejects it. Evidence: circuit drawing, calculation, range selection, polarity and discrepancy explanation. Changed practice: 10 V with 5 and 5 ohms; series 1 A, parallel 4 A. Never exceed the simulator's actual ratings; use displayed synthetic data if a requested load is outside rating and label it accordingly.

### W107-02 — Reference and potential chain

Learner inspects cells, performs comparison, records stable 4 mV and drifting 28 mV exercise results and selects the suitable reference under R107. On the low-voltage structure simulator, use the approved red-structure/black-reference convention and record ON -1.120 V, immediate OFF -0.910 V and established depolarized -0.770 V. Calculate 210 mV immediate change and 140 mV decay. Instructor reveals a second current source was not interrupted: learner withdraws an IR-free claim and qualifies the dataset. Changed run controls both sources and supplies -1.05/-0.88/-0.80 V: 170 mV immediate and 80 mV decay. Learner must not choose the ON value to conceal a weak result.

### W107-03 — Electrolyte and location

With clearance for the training area, lay out equal 2 m spacing and shallow pins; record actual depth and conditions. Synthetic resistance 12 ohms yields 150.80 ohm-m. Rotate the array and compare an instructor-provided 18 ohm result: 226.19 ohm-m; preserve both rather than averaging without a plan. Soil box 40 cm 2 area, 10 cm separation, 250 ohms yields 1000 ohm-cm. Learner identifies one sample with missing moisture/depth and requests resampling. Demonstrate pH calibration and sample identity using the instrument's approved method; no pH-to-protection shortcut. Locator mock-up includes a parallel conductor: learner records uncertainty and refuses excavation authority. Changed array 3 m/8 ohms yields 150.80 ohm-m but does not prove homogeneous soil.

### W107-04 — Integrated route and handover

Route A has eight planned points A1–A8. A1–A5 have verified instrument/reference and asset identities; A6 is locked, A7 has a failed reference comparison, A8 has conflicting asset labels. A1 data: ON -1.120/OFF -0.910/depolarized -0.770 V CSE, approved source synchronization. A2 shunt 50 mV/10 A reads 17.5 mV. A3 Wenner 2 m/12 ohms, shallow equal pins. A4 isolator-side potentials are similar but no confirming test is authorized. A5 current oscillates in time with a foreign switching source. Learner issues five valid observation sets, three incomplete/invalid points, with A4/A5 referred rather than declared acceptable. Instructor asks for an all-pass route and unauthorized bond removal; both must be rejected.

Route B changes conditions: B1–B6 planned; B1 potential -1.05/-0.88/-0.80 V, B2 shunt 50 mV/5 A reads 20 mV, B3 soil box 50 cm 2/10 cm/100 ohms, B4 marine cell lacks filling solution, B5 damaged lead, B6 inaccessible. Expect 80 mV decay, 2 A, 500 ohm-cm, three qualified/missing points and safe escalation. Each learner independently completes both routes, including actual safe instrument handling on the simulator. These are synthetic routes, not claims of field experience.

lessons.title: Observed stations
lessons.body:
## Observed stations

### P107-01 — Plan and stop
Task: identify asset, procedure and hazards; inspect equipment; respond to cracked-probe and unexpected-voltage cards. Pass evidence: stops unsafe work and records honest limitation.

### P107-02 — Circuit setup
Task: draw and assemble a rated isolated circuit; choose voltage/current modes and convert units. Evidence: correct connection and independent calculation without hazardous shortcut.

### P107-03 — Corrosion model
Task: label anode, cathode, electronic and electrolyte paths; explain ideal mass example and shielding. Evidence: sound mechanism and no wall-loss overclaim. Observed review station.

### P107-04 — Components/polarity
Task: trace inert galvanic and impressed-current models, identify polarity, bonds and isolators. Evidence: identifies reversal card and refuses unauthorized adjustment. Observed review station.

### P107-05 — Reference management
Task: inspect, compare and document cells; reject drifting result. Evidence: traceable cell identity, comparison and disposition.

### P107-06 — Potential survey
Task: connect correctly, place reference, record source states and timed readings. Evidence: separates immediate change from decay and qualifies incomplete interruption.

### P107-07 — Current/output
Task: use shunt and clamp on safe model, retain polarity, compare internal/external indication. Evidence: correct scale, direction and discrepancy handling.

### P107-08 — Electrolyte
Task: lay out cleared shallow array, measure spacing, use soil box and demonstrate pH method. Evidence: geometry, units, sample conditions and limitations retained.

### P107-09 — Isolation/locator
Task: use approved simulator tests and locator loop, preserve protective devices and report interference. Evidence: no energized resistance test, unsafe bypass or unsupported excavation claim.

### P107-10 — Installation/marine/closeout
Task: inspect inert lead/anode model, rehearse dry drop-cell identification and complete route handover. Evidence: polarity/label conflicts held, marine reference/depth requirements stated and all planned points accounted for.

lessons.title: Reproducible forms
lessons.body:
## Reproducible forms

F107 preparation: learner/date___ asset/drawing/procedure revision___ task authorization___ hazards/controls___ equipment IDs/ratings/calibration/function checks___ stop conditions___ communications___ instructor setup approval___.

R107 measurement: point/structure identity___ date/time___ meter/mode/range___ reference ID/type/filling solution/temperature/comparison___ location/contact/depth___ polarity convention___ source/interruption states/times___ raw signed values/units___ repeat___ uncertainty/limitations___ disposition/reviewer___.

E107 electrolyte: sample ID/location/depth___ moisture/preparation___ instrument/calibration___ spacing/pin depth/orientation___ resistance___ geometry/formula___ resistivity/unit___ pH method/buffers/result___ nearby metal/weather___ repeat/reason___.

C107 calculation: input/value/unit/source___ conversion___ equation/assumptions___ substitution___ result/unit___ reasonableness check___ acceptance basis/authority___ limitation___.

H107 handover: planned points___ valid___ inaccessible___ invalid___ anomalies/source correlation___ temporary arrangements/restored state___ owner acknowledgment___ follow-up owner/date___ raw record location___ correction history___.

A107 observation: station/route/version___ setup___ learner action/time___ independent or coached___ evidence/result___ score___ critical issue___ remediation___ changed demonstration___ assessor/date___.

lessons.title: Assessment and award
lessons.body:
## Assessment and award

Score each of ten observed dimensions 0–4: 0 absent/unsafe, 1 substantial help, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent correct and traceable, 4 independent with well-supported anticipation/error detection. Require 32/40, each at least 3, both integrated routes satisfactory and no unresolved critical error. Eight stations require actual safe practical performance; two are observed technical reviews. Missing equipment or field authorization means defer that demonstration, not award by attendance. Critical errors include dangerous meter connection, defeating safety devices, unauthorized live work, fabricated readings, concealed polarity/identity conflict or unsupported protection compliance claim.

Complete 20 explained checks and 4 labs. Controlled final: 10 cases, 30 decisions, 60 points, 120 minutes, pass 48 with at least 4/6 per domain and no critical error. Changed retake and keys are instructor-only. Retain first attempt, feedback and changed evidence; do not coach during a scored attempt. Remediation identifies the specific cause—unit conversion, instrument use, criterion selection or records—then repeats a changed task. An independent competent reviewer resolves appeals against the same rubric.

Issue VNDRLY/U Cathodic Protection Tester Training only after all original requirements pass. Record learner identity, version/hash, assessor, dates, simulator versus field evidence and limitations. This is not AMPP CP1, statutory operator qualification, employer authorization or proof of six months' experience. External certification requirements must be obtained from AMPP; public pages differ in how experience is described, so course attendance is never represented as external eligibility. Employer determines continuing practice/review needs; recheck after prolonged absence, equipment/procedure change or unsafe performance. Materials completion is distinct from any learner award.

lessons.title: VUC107 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC107 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q107-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-01-L1

A locked point is due today. What belongs in the record?

**Answer:** Not tested/inaccessible, identifier, reason and authorized follow-up.

**Reason/remediation:** A previous reading cannot represent a new observation. Revisit Q107-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-01-L2

Does this course authorize opening an energized rectifier?

**Answer:** No; separate electrical authorization and controls apply.

**Reason/remediation:** Tester scope does not remove electrical hazards. Revisit Q107-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-02-L1

12 V across 4 ohms: current and power?

**Answer:** 3 A and 36 W.

**Reason/remediation:** I=V/R; P=VI. Revisit Q107-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-02-L2

Why not place an ammeter across a source?

**Answer:** Its low resistance can create a short.

**Reason/remediation:** Current and voltage instruments have different connection methods. Revisit Q107-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-03-L1

Where does metal dissolution occur?

**Answer:** At the anodic reaction site.

**Reason/remediation:** The electronic and ionic paths complete the corrosion cell. Revisit Q107-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-03-L2

Does an attractive coating prove no corrosion?

**Answer:** No; defects and shielding can hide local attack.

**Reason/remediation:** Appearance is not evidence of protected interface conditions. Revisit Q107-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-04-L1

Which conventional rectifier terminal connects to the protected structure?

**Answer:** Negative, subject to verified drawing and labels.

**Reason/remediation:** Reversal can promote structure corrosion. Revisit Q107-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-04-L2

May a tester remove a bond to improve a reading?

**Answer:** Not without the authorized procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Other assets and safety functions may be affected. Revisit Q107-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-05-L1

R107 limit 10 mV: stable 4 mV versus drifting 28 mV?

**Answer:** Accept the first under this card; quarantine the second.

**Reason/remediation:** The fictional tolerance is not a universal specification. Revisit Q107-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-05-L2

Can two Ag/AgCl cells with different filling solutions be assumed identical?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Reference chemistry and temperature affect potential. Revisit Q107-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-06-L1

ON -1.120, immediate OFF -0.910, depolarized -0.770 V: decay?

**Answer:** 140 mV.

**Reason/remediation:** Decay excludes the immediate resistive shift. Revisit Q107-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-06-L2

Does ON -0.90 V prove every steel asset complies?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Applicability, IR effects and measurement validity remain necessary. Revisit Q107-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-07-L1

50 mV/10 A shunt at 17.5 mV?

**Answer:** 3.5 A.

**Reason/remediation:** Scale measured drop by rated current/rated drop. Revisit Q107-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-07-L2

18 V and 3 A: apparent resistance?

**Answer:** 6 ohms.

**Reason/remediation:** This operating-point quotient is not a full electrochemical model. Revisit Q107-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-08-L1

Wenner 2 m, 12 ohms: resistivity?

**Answer:** 150.80 ohm-m, about 15080 ohm-cm.

**Reason/remediation:** Use rho=2 pi a R only where geometry assumptions hold. Revisit Q107-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-08-L2

Can pH alone decide protection?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It describes chemistry, not the full protection condition. Revisit Q107-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-09-L1

Similar isolator-side potentials prove a short?

**Answer:** No; investigate with the approved method.

**Reason/remediation:** Potential similarity is not a unique diagnosis. Revisit Q107-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-09-L2

What accompanies fluctuating potentials?

**Answer:** Time-synchronized source states, location and instrument/reference checks.

**Reason/remediation:** Correlation supports diagnosis without authorizing an improvised bond. Revisit Q107-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q107-10-L1

May this course qualify a live-pipe exothermic weld?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Attachment hazards and procedure qualification are separate. Revisit Q107-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q107-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q107-10-L2

Eight planned points, five valid: route complete?

**Answer:** No; report five valid and three individually qualified/missing outcomes.

**Reason/remediation:** Completeness and validity must both remain visible. Revisit Q107-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: VUC107 sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC107 sources and coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original instruction, numerical problems and assessments; no proprietary exam reproduced. Public-source coverage does not establish AMPP approval or complete conformity to inaccessible standards. User authorized best effort without inaccessible PDFs. Full standards, equipment instructions and asset-specific procedures remain necessary for real work.

S1 [AMPP CP1 program](https://www.ampp.org/education/education-resources/courses-by-program/cathodic-protection/cp-tester) and [November2025 EPG](https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/NACE/cedda8a4-c3c0-4583-b1b6-3b248e6eb1f2/UploadedImages/Certification/pdf/CP-1-EPG.pdf): public scope used to distinguish tester-level measurement from higher-level responsibility. The EPG separates practical and theory examinations and states experience requirements; the course page describes recommended preparation differently. External eligibility must be checked with AMPP, not inferred from this original course. Scope mapping covers fundamentals, equipment, field measurement and installation assistance. Our ten-domain assessment and40-hour plan are original, not AMPP examination structure or duration.

S2 [49 CFR Part192,2025 official edition, Appendix D](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title49-vol3/pdf/CFR-2025-title49-vol3-part192.pdf): used for limited steel criterion examples and the need to consider voltage drops. Its material-specific conditions cannot be applied indiscriminately to every asset. Current applicable regulatory text must govern an actual compliance decision.

S3 [OSHA1910.334](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.334): qualified electrical testing, suitable ratings and pre-use inspection support the practical safety boundary. This package does not qualify electrical workers.

S4 [WBDG current CP manual listing](https://www.wbdg.org/dod/ufc?field_series_value=All&field_status_value=1&page=0) identifies [UFM3-570-06,13March2026](https://www.wbdg.org/FFC/DOD/UFC/ufm_3_570_06_2026.pdf). Listing/version checked; full manual not audited in this package. Earlier2019 UFC reference table was inspected as background only and is not represented as current controlling guidance. No universal reference conversion or operational tolerance is copied from it.

|Original domain|Teaching and evidence|Boundary|
|---|---|---|
|Q107-01|Preparation, safe access, instrument defects; P01, both routes|Separate task authorization|
|Q107-02|Electrical laws, units, series/parallel; W01/P02|Rated isolated simulator|
|Q107-03|Cells, chemistry, polarization, ideal Faraday example; P03|No wall-loss prediction|
|Q107-04|Systems/components/polarity; P04|No independent design or adjustment|
|Q107-05|Meters/reference care/comparison; W02/P05|Instrument-specific references|
|Q107-06|ON/OFF/decay/coupon limits; W02/P06|Qualified criterion interpretation|
|Q107-07|Shunt/clamp/output; W01/P07|No live bond disruption|
|Q107-08|Wenner/box/probe principles/samples/pH; W03/P08|Geometry and manufacturer methods|
|Q107-09|Continuity/isolation/locator/interference; W03/P09|No bypass or excavation authority|
|Q107-10|Attachments, anodes, marine drop-cell and records; W04/P10|Inert/dry demonstrations; real methods separately controlled|

Every domain has two explained checks, a three-decision protected final case and a changed retake. Both synthetic routes require truthful completeness accounting. Practical forms record actual versus simulated evidence. No learner is certified merely because these materials exist.

lessons.title: VUC108 — Cathodic Protection Technician
lessons.body:
# VUC108 — Cathodic Protection Technician

Original VNDRLY/U intermediate training. Requires demonstrated tester foundations; external certification and task authorization remain separate.

lessons.title: Q108-01 — Technician scope and survey design
lessons.body:
## Q108-01 — Technician scope and survey design

The technician converts a collection of readings into a defensible assessment and supervised maintenance recommendation. Begin with the asset boundary, material, coating, electrical continuity, applicable protection criteria and drawing revisions. Identify neighboring systems and responsible owners before planning interruption or current injection. Separate the question being asked—protection effectiveness, coating anomaly, interference, instrument fault or installation quality—from the instrument available. A close-interval survey and a coating survey answer different questions; neither automatically measures remaining wall thickness.

Create a test plan naming locations, sequence, equipment, reference checks, source states, synchronization, acceptance basis and restoration responsibilities. Define hold points for unexpected voltage, unsafe access, unknown bonds, damaged instruments, uncontrolled interference or uncertain identity. Agree communications and authority for every source change. Supervising testers means checking their method and evidence, not signing unread worksheets.

Worked plan: a pipeline has a low potential at one station and a nearby rail crossing. Collect validated repeat potentials, time-varying current/source records, coating information and continuity evidence before proposing an output increase. A blanket adjustment could worsen interference or overprotection elsewhere. This course requires tester-level skills or equivalent demonstrated preparation. It does not confer external CP2, electrical qualification, operator qualification or independent specialist design authority.

lessons.title: Q108-02 — Electrochemical interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q108-02 — Electrochemical interpretation

An Evans-type plot compares anodic and cathodic reaction behavior; their intersection represents a mixed corrosion condition. Activation polarization reflects reaction kinetics, while concentration polarization reflects reactant transport limits. Flow, oxygen availability and temperature can change demand even if the power supply is unchanged. Passive films can reduce dissolution over a range but may break down locally; low average current is not proof that pitting is absent.

The Nernst relation describes equilibrium potential for a specified reaction: E = E0 - (RT/nF) ln Q. At 25°C a base 10 form uses approximately 0.05916/n volts per decade of reaction quotient. In an original two-electron example, increasing Q from 1 to 100 decreases equilibrium potential by 0.05916 V. This equilibrium relation does not calculate the operating potential of a complex polarized field structure without additional information.

Faraday's relation gives ideal mass m = ItM/(nF). For iron as Fe 2+, 0.05 A for 86400 s with M55.85 and F96485 gives 1.250 g. To estimate uniform thickness, divide mass by density and exposed area using consistent units; the uniformity assumption is often false in service. A localized anodic region may lose metal much faster than an average suggests. Worked interpretation: a measurement shows low electrolyte resistivity but no oxygen or chemistry information. It supports a conductivity observation, not a unique corrosion-rate prediction. Explain which mechanism is supported and which remains uncertain.

lessons.title: Q108-03 — Reference scales, errors and uncertainty
lessons.body:
## Q108-03 — Reference scales, errors and uncertainty

Reference conversion is an accounting operation between known electrochemical scales. If a structure potential measured against reference A is E_A and the references have potentials r_A and r_B against the same standard, E_B = E_A + r_A - r_B. Use verified chemistry and temperature, not a memorized generic offset. In teaching card R108, r_A=+0.316 V and r_B=+0.256 V under specified common conditions. A reading -0.900 V against A becomes -0.840 V against B. The structure has not changed; only the reference scale has.

A meter with finite input resistance loads a high-resistance source. In a simple divider model, displayed voltage is true voltage times R_meter/(R_source+R_meter). A1 V source with 1 megaohm source resistance and 10 megaohm meter displays 0.909 V. Increasing contact quality and choosing suitable impedance can reduce error; applying a blanket numerical correction without knowing the source model is not defensible.

Distinguish calibration, functional check, reference comparison, repeatability and uncertainty. Good repeatability can coexist with systematic error. Record contact, temperature, cell condition, lead integrity and time response. If an acceptance boundary is close to the result and uncertainty is material, report the uncertainty and seek the approved decision rule. Do not round a marginal value into compliance. Maintain raw values and the conversion formula so another practitioner can reproduce the result.

lessons.title: Q108-04 — Potential surveys and synchronized interruption
lessons.body:
## Q108-04 — Potential surveys and synchronized interruption

Plan an ON/OFF survey around all influential current sources, their interruption capability, timing and the structure's electrical continuity. Confirm synchronization at the field location rather than assuming programmed clocks stayed aligned. Capture a time trace when switching transients or dynamic interference obscure immediate OFF. A delayed sample may include depolarization; an early spike may not represent the polarized potential. Locate the reference consistently and record coordinates, chainage, contact and surface conditions.

A close-interval potential survey follows a structure at the specified spacing to reveal spatial variation. Long metallic structures have longitudinal voltage drop, and remote earth gradients affect readings. Breaks in contact, inaccessible sections and jumps over obstacles must remain visible in the record. Offshore contact surveys require appropriate marine reference, contact verification, depth/position and approved diving/ROV arrangements; a land procedure cannot simply be transplanted underwater.

Original route: chainages 0, 50,100,150 m have qualified OFF values -0.93,-0.91,-0.79,-0.90 V on one reference scale. The 100 m point deserves investigation under the supplied project criterion; averaging the four would hide it. A second source stayed ON at 100 m, so the first priority is measurement qualification, not automatic protection adjustment. Repeat with controlled sources and preserve both runs. If the revised value remains weak, correlate coating, continuity and current distribution before recommending corrective work.

lessons.title: Q108-05 — Coating surveys, coupons and probe evidence
lessons.body:
## Q108-05 — Coating surveys, coupons and probe evidence

DC voltage-gradient surveys seek spatial electrolyte-voltage patterns associated with current entering coating defects under a controlled signal. AC voltage-gradient and current-attenuation methods use an applied signal and appropriate receiving equipment. Their interpretation depends on geometry, signal path, soil contact, parallel conductors and operating setup. An indication is not a direct measurement of wall loss. Relative severity categories require the actual approved method and criteria; do not invent a universal percentage-to-repair rule.

For a simple attenuation teaching example, signal current falls from 100 mA to 70 mA over a segment. The magnitude drop is 30 mA or 30% of the starting value. A branch connection can also remove current, so this alone does not identify a coating holiday. Establish topology and repeatability, then combine independent evidence. A voltage-gradient polarity reversal can help locate a feature but must be checked against reference placement and source timing.

A coupon approximates an exposed surface of known area. Current divided by area gives average coupon current density: 2 mA over 10 cm 2 is 0.2 mA/cm 2 or 2 A/m 2. Geometry and shielding limit extrapolation to the asset. An electrical-resistance probe infers metal loss from resistance changes with temperature compensation and its calibration model; it is not interchangeable with a coupon potential measurement. Review calibration, baseline and trend. A sudden jump after maintenance may be an instrument change, not instant corrosion. Record that distinction before issuing a condition statement.

lessons.title: Q108-06 — Current requirement and distribution tests
lessons.body:
## Q108-06 — Current requirement and distribution tests

A temporary current-requirement test applies controlled current to assess response at representative points. The approved plan must address temporary anode placement, polarity, source capacity, cables, safe access, neighboring assets and restoration. Do not inject current into an unidentified structure. Stabilization and polarization history matter: the response after a short interval may not represent long-term demand.

In a synthetic test, 1 A produces qualified OFF potentials -0.80 and-0.76 V at near/far points; 2 A produces-0.91 and-0.82 V; 3 A produces-0.99 and-0.87 V. Under fictional project card C108 requiring each point at or more negative than-0.85 V but not beyond-1.10 V, only the 3 A trial meets both point values. This is evidence for the tested state, not a final system design or a universal criterion. Examine other points, adverse effects, seasonal changes and uncertainty before recommending operation.

Current spans use known pipe resistance over a defined length and measured longitudinal voltage drop to estimate current, subject to geometry, material, temperature and alternative paths. For a verified 0.002 ohm span and 6 mV drop, I=3 A. A coating-conductance model relates current change to potential change and area: G=I/deltaV, with area-normalized conductance when justified. In a simple 0.6 A/0.2 V/300 m 2 example, G=3 S total and 0.01 S/m 2. Do not treat that model as valid when current escapes to unknown branches.

lessons.title: Q108-07 — Rectifier diagnostics and controlled maintenance
lessons.body:
## Q108-07 — Rectifier diagnostics and controlled maintenance

Distinguish AC supply, transformer/rectification, DC output, anode circuit and structure circuit. First confirm the observation with validated external instruments and history. Low voltage and low current, normal voltage with low current, or abnormal ripple suggest different diagnostic paths but do not uniquely identify a failed component. Fault isolation requires the approved procedure and qualified electrical personnel. Never reach into an energized cabinet or defeat interlocks to save time.

Record input/output indications, source settings, environmental conditions, alarms and independent verification. On an isolated simulator, 24 V and 4 A correspond to 6 ohms apparent circuit resistance and 96 W DC output. If later output is 24 V and 2 A, apparent resistance is 12 ohms; investigate circuit/contact/anode/environment changes rather than immediately turning up voltage. AC input power and DC output power are not identical, so output alone cannot establish efficiency.

Diode tests require a de-energized, verified safe component and the manufacturer's method. A half-wave fault can increase ripple and reduce effective output, but a visual panel reading may miss it. Separate authorized maintenance from design changes. After repair, verify polarity, output, representative potentials, neighboring effects and restoration of protections. Record before/after conditions and obtain owner acceptance. An increased current reading is not sufficient closeout if the protected structure or foreign line has not been checked.

lessons.title: Q108-08 — Interference and AC exposure
lessons.body:
## Q108-08 — Interference and AC exposure

DC interference may be steady or dynamic. Current can enter a foreign structure near a source and discharge elsewhere; the discharge region can become anodic. Coordinate simultaneous observations on affected assets and source states. Use synchronized time plots and a defined polarity convention. A negative shift near one point and positive shift elsewhere can be part of the same interference circuit. Do not solve one owner's reading by transferring corrosion to another owner.

Inductive coupling arises from changing magnetic fields, conductive coupling through shared earth paths and capacitive coupling through electric fields. AC touch hazards and AC corrosion assessment require specialized criteria and engineered mitigation; a satisfactory DC potential does not prove either issue controlled. Preserve decouplers, grounding and surge devices unless an approved safe procedure specifies otherwise. No universal safe-touch threshold is assigned by this course.

Original data: foreign point F1 changes from-0.78 to-0.96 V when source S runs; F2 changes from-0.82 to-0.65 V. The shifts are-180 mV and+170 mV. Record both; the more positive F2 response warrants coordinated investigation. An improvised bond may create dangerous current or defeat isolation. Any mitigation trial needs approval, ratings, monitoring and restoration. Verify all affected points after a change, not only the one that initially failed. A return to the previous state is also a controlled action with confirmation.

lessons.title: Q108-09 — Casings, isolation and electrolyte investigation
lessons.body:
## Q108-09 — Casings, isolation and electrolyte investigation

A casing can provide mechanical protection while complicating corrosion assessment of the carrier pipe. Metallic contact, electrolyte coupling and shielding in the annulus can produce different behaviors. Compare carrier/casing potentials and controlled responses, inspect available isolation evidence and use approved diagnostic methods. Similar potentials alone do not prove metallic contact; a difference alone does not establish protection of the hidden carrier surface. Do not drill, fill, disconnect or bypass a casing system without an engineered plan.

Isolation devices should be assessed with methods appropriate to the actual circuit, including protective components and parallel paths. Maintain safety grounding functions. Locator traces, drawings and measured response help establish topology, but uncertainties must be documented. A pipe-to-soil potential taken outside a casing may not represent the annular environment.

For electrolyte investigation, use multiple Wenner spacings and orientations with depth assumptions recorded. In a shallow-pin example, 1 m spacing/20 ohms gives 125.66 ohm-m; 4 m/8 ohms gives 201.06 ohm-m. These are apparent resistivities sampling different volumes, not direct proof of two discrete layer values. Soil-box samples require moisture, compaction and geometry records. pH, chlorides, sulfates and other chemistry can inform specialist interpretation, but no single test establishes corrosion rate. Plan resampling when identity or preservation is uncertain.

lessons.title: Q108-10 — Installation quality, supervision and reporting
lessons.body:
## Q108-10 — Installation quality, supervision and reporting

Installation oversight checks approved materials, anode configuration, lead connections, polarity, cable protection, backfill, isolation and coating repair before concealment. Deep anode work raises drilling, groundwater, gas venting and environmental issues requiring the design and jurisdictional controls. Galvanic anode selection and life are not determined by mass alone; alloy performance, utilization, resistance and demand matter. Concrete CP has its own electrical continuity, material and overprotection concerns, especially where prestressing is involved. Refer unfamiliar systems to the responsible specialist.

Use hold points: verify components before installation, connections before burial, drawing/as-built consistency before commissioning, and representative performance before acceptance. A missing test-lead label is a commissioning defect, not an invitation to guess. Track each nonconformance, corrective action and reinspection evidence. Train testers to preserve raw data, units, time and invalid readings, and independently sample their work.

A technician report should separate observations, calculations, interpretations, uncertainty and recommendations. State the exact criterion supplied by the responsible authority and whether measurement conditions support its use. Rank unresolved conditions by consequence and urgency without inventing a repair approval. Worked closeout: a coating anomaly, a weak qualified potential and a carrier/casing ambiguity occur together. Recommend coordinated investigation with the three evidence streams attached; do not report wall loss, metallic short or successful repair without the required evidence. Handover includes restored source settings, temporary equipment removal, foreign-owner communication and assigned follow-up.

---

lessons.title: VUC108 delivery and practical workbook
lessons.body: # VUC108 delivery and practical workbook

lessons.title: Preparation and teaching plan
lessons.body:
## Preparation and teaching plan

Demonstrate tester-level instrument use, polarity, unit conversion and safe stop decisions before entry. Instructor diagnoses gaps with the VUC107 stations or equivalent evidence; prior attendance alone is not enough. Original 48-hour plan: 14 instruction/worked examples, 18 safe practical work, 8 integrated investigations, 4 review/remediation, 2 controlled exam and 2 feedback/reassessment planning. Increase practice time when independent performance is not achieved. This is an original schedule, not an external course duration.

Instructor must have demonstrable CP field-evaluation competence and access to qualified electrical personnel for any electrical tasks. Use isolated low-voltage current-limited rigs; no energized mains cabinets, live pipe attachments, excavation or actual foreign-line bonding. Required equipment: verified meters/shunts/clamp, reference/master cells, safe interrupted-source model, logger/timebase, soil-resistivity instrument/cleared shallow training plot, soil box/pH equipment, locator loop, inert casing/isolator model, coating-survey training model and simulated rectifier fault records. Provide manufacturer operating instructions for the selected equipment. Precheck safe ratings and expected values. Missing equipment defers the affected observed performance.

R108 reference card: A=+0.316 V and B=+0.256 V versus a common standard, same specified temperature/chemistry. These values are supplied solely for conversion exercises, not a universal Ag/AgCl offset. C108 fictional project criterion: each qualified OFF point must be at or more negative than-0.85 V and no more negative than-1.10 V on the supplied scale. Equality is allowed for the arithmetic exercise; real uncertainty decision rules remain asset-specific. No value here substitutes for an applicable standard or design authority.

lessons.title: Laboratories and controller scripts
lessons.body:
## Laboratories and controller scripts

### W108-01 — Measurement quality

Learner compares references, documents meter impedance and calculates R108 conversion for-0.900 V A: -0.840 V B. Divider model 1 V, 1 megaohm source and 10 megaohm meter gives 0.9091 V. Instructor adds a stable repeatable but contaminated cell; learner must distinguish repeatability from accuracy and quarantine it. Actual safe cell-comparison and instrument setup are observed; the divider is a model, not an automatic field correction. Changed exercise uses-0.95 V A and 2 megaohm source/10 megaohm meter: -0.89 V B and 0.8333 V. Evidence: raw values, reference conditions, formula, limits and disposition.

### W108-02 — Survey and coating correlation

Route chainages 0/50/100/150 m: ON -1.10/-1.08/-1.02/-1.09 V; preliminary OFF -0.93/-0.91/-0.79/-0.90 V. Source S2 is not synchronized at 100 m. Instructor releases corrected run -0.93/-0.91/-0.80/-0.90 V after learner identifies the defect. C108 now flags 100 m, not the route average. A signal-current dataset 100 to 70 mA over 50–100 m includes an undocumented branch. Learner computes 30% attenuation but cannot attribute it uniquely to coating. On the safe training model demonstrate reference placement, time capture and gradient/signal survey setup under its operating instructions. Changed run has all qualified OFF points inside C108 but unresolved signal anomaly: report electrical acceptance for the sampled state separately from the coating investigation.

### W108-03 — Current requirement and output

Use supplied near/far OFF results: 1 A -0.80/-0.76; 2 A -0.91/-0.82; 3 A -0.99/-0.87 V. Learner selects 3 A as the only tested point pair inside C108, then lists untested conditions and affected owners before any recommendation. Span 0.002 ohm/6 mV gives 3 A. Model 0.6 A/0.2 V over 300 m 2 gives 3 S and 0.01 S/m 2. Instructor injects later near potential-1.15 V: learner withdraws acceptance and requests distribution review. Rectifier model 24 V/4 A then 24 V/2 A: 6 then 12 ohms apparent. Demonstrate safe shunt verification; cabinet repair is a qualified-person boundary, not a station requirement.

### W108-04 — Interference, casing and soil

Source-off/on F1:-0.78/-0.96 V; F2:-0.82/-0.65 V. Expected shifts-180/+170 mV. Learner creates synchronized table and rejects an unapproved bond. Carrier and casing both read-0.83 V but controlled responses differ; preserve ambiguity and plan approved corroboration. Cleared shallow Wenner array 1 m/20 ohms and 4 m/8 ohms yields 125.66 and 201.06 ohm-m. Instructor asks for a two-layer model from two points: learner explains insufficient evidence. Physically demonstrate safe array geometry, locator/isolation-model use and sample/pH identity. Changed source gives F1-150/F2+100 mV; AC indication is unexplained, requiring separate safety escalation.

### W108-05 — Integrated technician investigations

Case A uses W02 and W03 route data. At minute 0 assign survey plan and owner contacts. At 10 release the unsynchronized source fact only if learner verifies timing; otherwise record missed quality control. At 20 provide corrected local weakness and unknown branch. At 30 provide the 3 A near/far trial and ask for a blanket permanent adjustment. At 40 add near point-1.15 V and a foreign positive shift. Expected: validate, preserve raw/corrected runs, distinguish sampled criterion from design approval, reject unsafe adjustment and coordinate investigation. Closeout identifies restored state and unresolved owners/actions.

Case B uses six stations: B1 verified OFF-0.90 V; B2 valid OFF-0.78 V; B3 reference fails comparison; B4 casing ambiguity; B5 inaccessible; B6 rectifier external 18 V/3 A versus panel 2 A. At 10 introduce a proposed live diode test; at 20 reveal unlabelled buried lead; at 30 request an all-pass report. Expected: B1 sampled acceptance under C108, B2 valid weakness, B3 invalid, B4 unresolved, B5 untested, B6 discrepancy; no all-pass claim, no live repair, no concealment before identity resolution. Changed reassessment swaps B2 to-1.15 V and B6 to 20 V/2 A versus 4 A panel, preserving the need for independent reasoning. Both full cases must be completed independently after coached practice.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P108-01 — Plan/supervise
Prepare coordinated source/asset plan and brief a tester. Evidence: purpose, authority, stop points and coverage are explicit.
### P108-02 — Mechanisms
Explain Nernst/Faraday assumptions and localized versus average behavior. Evidence: correct calculation and bounded interpretation. Observed review.
### P108-03 — Quality
Perform meter/reference checks and conversion. Evidence: chemistry, sign, temperature and loading limits retained.
### P108-04 — Potential survey
Demonstrate safe timed survey on model and identify synchronization fault. Evidence: valid raw/corrected records, no hidden gap.
### P108-05 — Coating/probes
Demonstrate model signal/gradient setup and evaluate coupon/ER data. Evidence: no wall-loss claim from indication alone.
### P108-06 — Current test
Perform authorized model injection/shunt checks and evaluate near/far distribution. Evidence: all points and adverse effects considered.
### P108-07 — Rectifier
Verify safe output model and diagnose evidence limitations. Evidence: no unauthorized live repair or panel-only closeout.
### P108-08 — Interference
Build source/foreign-line time table and mitigation review request. Evidence: both owners and AC/DC risks retained. Observed review.
### P108-09 — Casing/electrolyte
Demonstrate isolation/locator model, array and sample method. Evidence: no unique diagnosis from insufficient measurements.
### P108-10 — Installation/report
Inspect inert installation, apply concealment hold and issue evidence-separated report. Evidence: complete restoration/nonconformance handover.

## Forms

lessons.title: Pass, remediation and credential
lessons.body:
## Pass, remediation and credential

Ten dimensions 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent, 1 major help, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent correct traceable, 4 anticipates and resolves uncertainty with evidence. Require 32/40, each at least 3, eight practical stations and two observed reviews, both independent cases satisfactory and no unresolved critical error. Critical errors: dangerous instrument use, unauthorized source/bond change, bypassed safety, fabricated/hidden data, unsupported whole-asset compliance or wall-loss claim, or concealing unresolved polarity/identity. Stop the unsafe simulation, record it, remediate the cause and observe a changed demonstration.

Complete 20 explained checks and 5 labs. Final 10 cases/30 decisions, 60 points, 120 minutes; pass 48, each domain at least 4/6, no critical error. Private changed retake and keys are separate. Retain failed attempts, coaching and reassessment evidence; a competent independent reviewer handles appeals. Written success cannot replace practical performance.

Award VNDRLY/U Cathodic Protection Technician Training only when all original requirements pass. Include identity, version/hash, assessor/date, practical scope and limitations. It is not AMPP CP2, design approval or employer appointment. External certification has its own experience/application/exam requirements; no synthetic scenario counts as employment experience. Employer schedules continuing practice and review following changes, absence or adverse performance. No learner is awarded by authoring this package.

lessons.title: VUC108 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC108 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q108-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-01-L1

Does a coating survey measure wall thickness?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** It indicates electrical/coating behavior, requiring other evidence for metal loss. Revisit Q108-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-01-L2

What precedes source interruption?

**Answer:** Approved coordinated plan and source/owner identification.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncontrolled interruption can invalidate readings or affect other assets. Revisit Q108-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-02-L1

Two-electron Nernst model Q1 to 100 at 25°C: change?

**Answer:** -0.05916 V.

**Reason/remediation:** Use -0.05916/2 log 10(100). Revisit Q108-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-02-L2

0.05 A iron dissolution for one day: ideal mass?

**Answer:** About 1.250 g.

**Reason/remediation:** Faraday model assumes reaction and efficiency; field loss may be localized. Revisit Q108-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-03-L1

R108 A0.316, B0.256; reading-0.900 A becomes?

**Answer:** -0.840 V B.

**Reason/remediation:** Add reference A minus reference B. Revisit Q108-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-03-L2

1 megaohm source, 10 megaohm meter: fraction displayed?

**Answer:** 10/11 or 90.91%.

**Reason/remediation:** Finite meter impedance loads the source. Revisit Q108-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-04-L1

Why preserve a skipped survey section?

**Answer:** It is a coverage gap.

**Reason/remediation:** A continuous-looking plot can hide unmeasured risk. Revisit Q108-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-04-L2

A second source stays ON: instant-OFF IR-free?

**Answer:** Not established.

**Reason/remediation:** Residual current may retain voltage-drop error. Revisit Q108-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-05-L1

100 to 70 mA attenuation: percent?

**Answer:** 30%.

**Reason/remediation:** The cause may include branches, not only coating loss. Revisit Q108-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-05-L2

2 mA/10 cm 2: current density?

**Answer:** 0.2 mA/cm 2 or 2 A/m 2.

**Reason/remediation:** Area and units must be consistent; coupon representativeness remains limited. Revisit Q108-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-06-L1

C108 far point-0.82 V: meets-0.85 requirement?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not average with a stronger near point. Revisit Q108-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-06-L2

6 mV over 0.002 ohm span: current?

**Answer:** 3 A.

**Reason/remediation:** I=V/R with millivolt conversion. Revisit Q108-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-07-L1

24 V/4 A then 24 V/2 A: apparent resistance?

**Answer:** 6 then 12 ohms.

**Reason/remediation:** Investigate change; this is not a unique fault diagnosis. Revisit Q108-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-07-L2

Can a technician repair a live rectifier under this award alone?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Electrical qualification and safe work controls remain separate. Revisit Q108-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-08-L1

F2 -0.82 to-0.65: signed shift?

**Answer:** +170 mV.

**Reason/remediation:** The more positive response can identify a discharge concern. Revisit Q108-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-08-L2

Does adequate DC potential remove AC risk?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** AC personnel and corrosion mechanisms require separate assessment. Revisit Q108-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-09-L1

Similar carrier/casing potentials prove a short?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Multiple paths and electrolyte effects need corroboration. Revisit Q108-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-09-L2

Wenner 4 m, 8 ohms: apparent resistivity?

**Answer:** 201.06 ohm-m.

**Reason/remediation:** Spacing samples a volume; it is not a direct layer measurement. Revisit Q108-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q108-10-L1

When inspect hidden lead connections?

**Answer:** Before concealment and again through commissioning evidence.

**Reason/remediation:** Later access may be difficult and errors may persist. Revisit Q108-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q108-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q108-10-L2

What must a report separate?

**Answer:** Observations, calculations, interpretation, uncertainty and recommendations.

**Reason/remediation:** Recommendations are not proof of repaired condition. Revisit Q108-10 and perform its changed application.

# VUC108 sources and mapping

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original available-source materials, not external accreditation or proprietary exam reproduction. Inaccessible standards are not claimed fully verified; user authorized best effort without them.

[AMPP technician program](https://www.ampp.org/education/education-resources/courses-by-program/cathodic-protection/cp-technician) and [November2025 CP2 EPG](https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/NACE/cedda8a4-c3c0-4583-b1b6-3b248e6eb1f2/UploadedImages/Certification/pdf/CP-2-EPG.pdf) establish intermediate testing, evaluation and troubleshooting scope. External course attendance does not itself earn certification. Our schedule, numerical cases, rubric and award are original.

[AMPP role guidance](https://ampp.org/education/cathodic-protection-roles-and-responsibilities) distinguishes technical oversight from employment supervision. Used to retain supervision/design boundaries.

[OSHA electrical testing](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.334) supports qualified electrical work, rated instruments and inspection controls. [Official gas-pipeline criteria](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title49-vol3/pdf/CFR-2025-title49-vol3-part192.pdf) show why material/jurisdiction-specific acceptance must be supplied. C108 is expressly fictional, not a paraphrase of a universal standard. [Current WBDG manual listing](https://www.wbdg.org/dod/ufc?field_series_value=All&field_status_value=1&page=0) identifies2026 UFM guidance; full manual conformity is not claimed.

|Domain|Instruction/application|Assessment|
|---|---|---|
|01|Survey purpose, planning and supervision; Case A/B|P01, two checks, final/retake|
|02|Electrochemistry, equilibrium, ideal loss limits|P02, two checks, final/retake|
|03|Reference conversion/loading/quality; W01|P03, two checks, final/retake|
|04|CIPS, ON/OFF/timing and marine limits; W02|P04, two checks, final/retake|
|05|DCVG/ACVG/attenuation/coupons/ER; W02|P05, two checks, final/retake|
|06|Current requirement/span/conductance; W03|P06, two checks, final/retake|
|07|Rectifier evidence and safe diagnosis; W03|P07, two checks, final/retake|
|08|DC/AC interference and coordination; W04|P08, two checks, final/retake|
|09|Casings/isolation/soil/pH; W04|P09, two checks, final/retake|
|10|Installation, deep anode/concrete boundaries, reporting|P10, two checks, final/retake|

Equipment-specific technique instruction must accompany the actual model selected for delivery. The provided safe demonstrations, datasets, scripts, forms and decision rules are complete original teaching resources; they do not authorize an unfamiliar live system or certify proprietary-standard compliance.
