lessons.title: VUC109 — Cathodic Protection Technologist
lessons.body:
# VUC109 — Cathodic Protection Technologist

Original VNDRLY/U applied analysis and design-calculation training. External CP3 certification and engineering/task authority remain separate.

lessons.title: Q109-01 — Basis, competence and design control
lessons.body:
## Q109-01 — Basis, competence and design control

A technologist must know why a design input is credible, which calculation applies and where the result stops being valid. Start a basis document with asset geometry, materials, coating, environment, continuity, design life, operating constraints, applicable standards and owner acceptance requirements. Identify existing and foreign CP systems, electrical safety interfaces and future connections. Separate measured facts, owner-supplied assumptions and unresolved information. An attractive calculation cannot compensate for the wrong structure boundary.

This course develops original basic-to-intermediate calculation and investigation skills. Complex, critical, mixed-material, high-risk or unfamiliar structures require specialist oversight and any legally required engineering authority. Learning an impressed-current calculation does not authorize independently approving every impressed-current design. Technical supervision includes reviewing procedures and evidence from testers/technicians, not merely assigning their shifts.

Worked decision: an owner requests a single galvanic design for a coated pipe but the drawing shows a bonded tank and an unknown foreign connection. Hold the single-structure assumption. Obtain verified continuity/topology and revise the demand boundary before selecting anodes. Record who may approve assumptions and release drawings. Maintain revision control through procurement, installation and commissioning; a change in coating, material or bond can invalidate the approved basis.

lessons.title: Q109-02 — Polarization, corrosion and environmental effects
lessons.body:
## Q109-02 — Polarization, corrosion and environmental effects

Use electrochemical theory to explain field response, not to decorate a report. Activation-controlled reaction behavior can produce a linear potential-versus-log-current region; concentration limits, passive films, mixed reactions and uncompensated resistance can invalidate a simple fit. On a supplied ideal Tafel branch with slope 0.120 V per decade, a tenfold current change corresponds to 0.120 V; doubling corresponds to 0.03612 V because log 10(2)=0.3010. Do not extrapolate across a transport-limited plateau or different reaction regime.

Nernst equilibrium shifts depend on reaction quotient and temperature; Faraday mass estimates depend on reaction, current, time and efficiency. Neither alone predicts localized damage in a complex field structure. Changes in oxygen, temperature, flow, deposits and chemistry alter polarization and current demand. Amphoteric metals and high-strength materials may be harmed by excessive polarization or local chemistry; more negative is not always better.

Worked evaluation: a current increase produces little additional qualified polarization but greater ON voltage shift. Investigate resistive drop, distribution, shielding and reaction limitations instead of repeatedly increasing output. Distinguish a protected accessible surface from a shielded interface. For reinforced concrete and prestressed systems, seek the applicable specialist criteria and structural constraints. A steel pipeline criterion cannot be transplanted without justification.

lessons.title: Q109-03 — Data qualification and criteria
lessons.body:
## Q109-03 — Data qualification and criteria

A design survey should establish valid potential, resistivity, current, coating and continuity evidence over representative conditions. Check reference chemistry, comparison, temperature, contact, meter loading, sampling time, source synchronization and location. Quantify uncertainty where practical and explain missing coverage. Retain raw data and transformations. A plotted smooth line can hide skipped points or reference changes; review the acquisition record before interpreting the graph.

Select criteria from the applicable asset standard and owner requirements with qualified review. ON values may contain significant IR contributions; interruption must address influential sources and sampling behavior. Polarization decay needs a justified depolarized baseline. A coupon or probe provides local evidence with defined geometry and limitations, not a guarantee for every surface.

Fictional criterion C109 accepts qualified steel OFF values from-0.85 through-1.10 V on its stated reference scale. Values-0.90,-0.88,-0.82,-0.92 V contain a local failure even though the average is-0.88 V. If the-0.82 point has uncertain timing, first qualify/repeat it; do not claim either definitive acceptance or a unique cause from invalid data. Report criteria separately from assumptions and measurement limitations. The original training window is not a universal standard.

lessons.title: Q109-04 — Geometry, coating breakdown and current demand
lessons.body:
## Q109-04 — Geometry, coating breakdown and current demand

Calculate exposed surface from the actual geometry and include fittings, ends or attached structures when relevant. For a cylindrical lateral surface A=pi D L. Multiply area by a justified exposed fraction and current density to obtain current demand, ensuring density is expressed per exposed area when that is its definition. Some specifications express demand per total coated area; mixing those conventions applies coating reduction twice.

Original model: D=0.30 m, L=1000 m, lateral A=942.48 m 2. End-of-life exposed fraction 0.02 and exposed-area density 0.020 A/m 2 give 0.37699 A. A supplied planning factor 1.25 yields 0.47124 A. This excludes ends/fittings by the exercise definition. If the exposed fraction becomes 0.05, the same calculation gives 1.17810 A after factor. This sensitivity is more informative than reporting excessive decimals on an uncertain coating assumption.

Define initial, mean and final demand separately. Mean demand can govern capacity consumption while final demand can govern output; using mean demand for both can under-size the system. Document evidence for coating degradation, environmental variation and maintenance assumptions. Do not silently multiply unrelated conservatism factors: explain what each covers, prevent double-counting and seek review when uncertainty dominates the result.

lessons.title: Q109-05 — Galvanic output and anode capacity
lessons.body:
## Q109-05 — Galvanic output and anode capacity

A galvanic anode must satisfy both instantaneous output and useful life. A simplified output model is I=driving voltage/total circuit resistance. Resistance includes the anode environment and relevant circuit paths; polarization changes the effective driving voltage. Capacity is charge available per mass under specified alloy/environment conditions. If capacity is already an effective rated value, do not apply current efficiency again unless the definition requires it.

For an original supplied effective capacity 1100 Ah/kg, usable fraction 0.80, mean demand 0.40 A and 10 years at 8760 h/year, required mass is 0.40×8760×10/(1100×0.80)=39.82 kg. A20 kg unit provides 17600 Ah usable; two meet the mean-life requirement in this ideal model. But each unit at 0.70 V driving difference and 3.0 ohms supplies only 0.2333 A under the supplied independent-anode approximation. For final demand 0.80 A, four are needed by output. Four 20 kg units have capacity life 20.09 years at 0.40 A, but that does not prove distribution, utilization or actual environment.

Never assume closely spaced anodes act independently: mutual resistance and geometry affect output. Check installation constraints, spacing, lead resistance, product performance, utilization and end-of-life geometry. A mass-only answer is incomplete; a current-only answer may exhaust early. Procurement must match the approved alloy and performance basis, not simply nominal weight.

lessons.title: Q109-06 — Resistance, distribution and impressed-current calculations
lessons.body:
## Q109-06 — Resistance, distribution and impressed-current calculations

Resistance models are approximations tied to geometry, boundary conditions and soil assumptions. For a supplied long vertical-electrode model in homogeneous soil, R = rho/(2 pi L) × [ln(8L/d)-1]. It assumes appropriate slender geometry and isolated placement; use the actual approved design method for real installations. With rho 50 ohm-m, L3 m and d 0.10 m, the model gives 11.89 ohms. Layering, backfill, nearby metal and multiple anodes can change actual performance substantially.

A simplified impressed-current voltage requirement sums current times circuit resistance, back voltage and other specified drops, then applies the stated design allowance. For I5 A, R4 ohms, back voltage 2 V and lead drop 1 V, the base is 23 V; a supplied 20% voltage allowance gives 27.6 V. Select equipment only after ratings, environment, control range, current capacity, safety and design approval are checked. Do not treat this arithmetic as a procurement specification.

Distribution matters as much as total current. A nearby surface can be overpolarized while a remote point remains weak. Investigate anode placement, coating variation, structure resistance, current paths and shielding. Raising output may worsen the imbalance. A long-line attenuation model can describe how potential/current response decays with distance, but its constants require evidence and its boundary conditions matter. A uniform-soil model fitted to one point is not a validated whole-system prediction.

lessons.title: Q109-07 — Interference, isolation and mitigation evaluation
lessons.body:
## Q109-07 — Interference, isolation and mitigation evaluation

Build a circuit-level explanation of suspected interference using synchronized source states, structure potentials, current directions and physical topology. Include foreign owners, AC exposure, safety grounding and protective devices. Static and dynamic DC effects require different observation periods; short sampling can miss the worst state. Distinguish induction, earth conduction and capacitive coupling when evaluating AC concerns.

Mitigation choices may include source configuration, isolation correction, coordinated bonds, distributed anodes or specialist AC measures. Each changes current paths and can create a new problem. A controlled trial needs approved limits, monitoring points, authority, rollback and post-change verification across all affected systems. Never use an unapproved bond as a diagnostic convenience.

Original trial: source-on shifts foreign pointA by-0.20 V and pointB by+0.15 V. A proposed bond improvesB but drives another pointC beyond the supplied negative limit. The trial has not solved the system problem; report the tradeoff and restore or revise only under the approved plan. A satisfactory DC potential does not establish touch safety or AC corrosion control. For a high-consequence crossing with uncertain topology, specialist review is part of competent practice rather than a failure to finish arithmetic.

lessons.title: Q109-08 — Design alternatives and lifecycle decisions
lessons.body:
## Q109-08 — Design alternatives and lifecycle decisions

Compare alternatives on technical feasibility before cost. Each option must meet demand, distribution, life, access, safety, environment and maintenance requirements. Document power availability, outage behavior, monitoring, anode replacement access and ownership responsibilities. A cheaper installation that cannot be safely inspected is not equivalent to a maintainable design.

For an original economic example at 5% discount rate over 10 years, present-worth factor for an annual cost is [1-(1.05)^-10]/0.05=7.7217. OptionG costs 12000 initially plus 500 annually: present worth 15860.87. OptionI costs 8000 initially plus 1100 annually: 16493.91. G is lower by 633.04 in this narrow model. These values exclude replacements, energy escalation, downtime, risk and residual value, so they do not determine a real procurement decision. Show sensitivity rather than hiding omitted costs.

Use a requirements matrix to compare initial/final output, capacity, monitoring, interference, access and environmental constraints. Reject alternatives that fail a mandatory condition even if their cost is attractive. Record assumptions and approval owner. If both options need unresolved specialist analysis, the correct deliverable is a conditional comparison with specific missing evidence, not a false final selection.

lessons.title: Q109-09 — Installation, commissioning and acceptance
lessons.body:
## Q109-09 — Installation, commissioning and acceptance

Translate the approved basis into drawings, schedules, material specifications, inspection hold points and commissioning tests. Identify polarity, lead labels, bonds, isolators, anode locations and reference points. Before concealment, verify the installed configuration, connections, coating repairs and as-built deviations. Unapproved substitutions require engineering disposition; visual similarity is not equivalence.

Commissioning should verify continuity/isolation, equipment calibration, polarity, output control, representative potentials, interference and restoration of safety functions. Record baseline conditions and the final approved settings. Allow appropriate stabilization and document timing. Check initial and anticipated operating states; a single favorable measurement at one source setting is not enough.

Worked release: all near points meet C109, the far point is-0.80 V and one foreign line has no owner response. Do not issue unconditional acceptance. Identify the unresolved performance and coordination items, maintain the approved safe state, and assign corrective action and retest. A punch list can distinguish documentation defects from performance defects, but it cannot waive a mandatory protection criterion. Handover must include operating limits, inspection schedule, alarm response, drawings and who has authority to change settings.

lessons.title: Q109-10 — Troubleshooting, supervision and technical report
lessons.body:
## Q109-10 — Troubleshooting, supervision and technical report

Use hypotheses and discriminating tests. A current decrease may reflect an open connection, higher ground resistance, coating change, power fault or instrument error. Determine which observations distinguish those possibilities before ordering repair. Review trends against weather, maintenance, topology and operating state. Avoid changing multiple variables at once without a plan, since the cause of improvement then becomes unclear.

Technical oversight includes checking survey procedure suitability, observing a sample of field work, reviewing anomalous results and verifying calculations independently. A spreadsheet should expose formulas, units, source inputs, assumptions and revision history. Test it with known examples and edge cases; a correct total with incorrect units is not acceptable. Separate learner calculations from controlled design approval.

A defensible report contains purpose, scope, basis, field methods, data quality, calculations, alternatives, uncertainty, conclusions, recommendations and unresolved actions. Include enough raw data and references for another competent person to reproduce key results. State what is outside scope. Where a high-risk design exceeds competence, provide a precise specialist referral with the work already completed. Do not fabricate experience or claim an external credential from this training. Final authoring completion means these learning resources are ready; actual learners must still meet all assessment requirements.

---

lessons.title: VUC109 applied workbook and delivery
lessons.body: # VUC109 applied workbook and delivery

lessons.title: Entry and resources
lessons.body:
## Entry and resources

Require demonstrated technician foundations: safe measurements, reference conversion, survey validity, circuit calculations and interference interpretation. Diagnose algebra, logarithms, geometry and units before advanced work. Original 56-hour plan: 16 instruction, 16 calculation workshops, 12 integrated design/investigation, 6 observed technical defense, 3 controlled final and 3 feedback/remediation. Additional remediation is not waived to meet the schedule.

Instructor/assessor must be competent in CP analysis and the supplied design models, with specialist/engineering support for questions outside scope. All designs are synthetic and must never be issued for construction. Use calculators or transparent spreadsheets, plotted datasets, inert installation model, safe low-voltage survey demonstration, drawings and forms. Four practical stations involve data acquisition/setup or model inspection; six are observed calculation/technical-review stations. Verify learner input/formula independence rather than accepting a copied spreadsheet. Record accommodations without changing technical decision criteria.

C109 fictional qualified OFF window:-1.10 to-0.85 V inclusive on a single specified reference. R109 calculations use 8760 hours/year, stated effective capacity and utilization, independent anodes only where explicitly assumed. No coefficient is a universal design value. Real geometry, soil, product, owner criteria and specialist authority govern field work.

lessons.title: Worked applications
lessons.body:
## Worked applications

### W109-01 — Basis and data validity

Drawing A shows 0.30 m pipe 1000 m long; exercise excludes ends/fittings. The owner initially calls it isolated. Inject at 10 minutes: a bonded vessel appears but area/condition unknown. Learner must hold the original boundary and list required topology/area verification. Dataset OFF -0.90/-0.88/-0.82/-0.92 V; average-0.88 does not pass every point. Inject uncertain timing at the weak point, then a validated repeat-0.81 V. Expect qualification followed by a valid local failure and investigation, not arbitrary averaging. Demonstrate safe acquisition/reference checks on a simulator before analyzing the dataset.

### W109-02 — Demand and sensitivity

After owner clarification, use pipe lateral area only: pi×0.30×1000=942.48 m 2. Exposed fraction 0.02, density 0.020 A/m 2 exposed area, factor 1.25: 0.47124 A. Changed fraction 0.05 yields 1.17810 A. Learner labels input source, area convention, factor purpose and difference 0.70686 A. Instructor introduces a spreadsheet that multiplies fraction twice; learner repairs and retains revision history. Changed geometry 0.20 m×800 m, fraction 0.04, density 0.020, factor 1.25 yields 0.50265 A. Do not round assumptions into certainty.

### W109-03 — Anode output and life

Effective capacity 1100 Ah/kg, utilization 0.80, mean 0.40 A, 10 years, 20 kg units. Required 39.82 kg; two units meet ideal capacity. Driving difference 0.70 V and 3 ohm per-unit model gives 0.2333 A each; final 0.80 A needs four. Selected 80 kg gives 20.09 years ideal mean-load capacity. Inject anode crowding: independent-output assumption no longer established; learner cannot approve four solely from arithmetic. Changed case mean 0.30 A, 10 years, 1000 Ah/kg, 0.80 use, 20 kg units, 0.20 A/unit, final 0.70 A: 32.85 kg and four units by output. Learner documents both limiting checks and required interaction/distribution verification.

### W109-04 — Resistance, supply and alternatives

Supplied electrode model rho 50 ohm-m, L3 m, d 0.10 m gives 11.89 ohms. Learner states homogeneous/slender/isolated assumptions. Separate supply example 5 A, 4 ohms, 2 V back, 1 V lead, 20% allowance gives 27.6 V. These are unrelated teaching submodels; do not combine the 11.89 ohm electrode with the 4 ohm circuit without a justified network. Economic example 10 years/5%, factor 7.721735: G12000+500/year=15860.87; I8000+1100/year=16493.91. G lower 633.04 under stated omissions. Instructor adds inaccessible replacement location toG: learner returns to feasibility rather than selecting by cost alone.

### W109-05 — Integrated design defense and commissioning

Case A: independently produce basis, demand, anode count/life, alternatives and commissioning plan using W02/W03. At minute 15 unknown bond appears; at 30 owner supplies verified isolated scope; at 45 anode-spacing constraint invalidates independent-output assumption; at 60 commissioning dataset near-0.94/far-0.80 V and foreign shift+0.15 V. Expected: successive holds/revisions, no construction release from model alone, local/foreign investigation and explicit final unresolved actions.

Case B: pipe 0.40 m×500 m, fraction 0.03, density 0.015, factor 1.20; demand 0.33929 A. Separate approved exercise mean 0.50 A, life 15 years, capacity 1000, use 0.85, unit 25 kg, output 0.30 A/unit, final 1.10 A yields 77.29 kg and four units. Qualified commissioning near-0.91/far-0.86 V initially meetsC109; inject unapproved anode substitution and lost safety-grounding record. Learner must withhold unconditional acceptance despite favorable potentials. Changed defense uses near-1.12/far-0.86 and a resolved substitution: performance still fails. Assessor asks learner to explain every formula, assumption and authority boundary without coaching.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P109-01 — Basis
Build asset/authority register and resolve scope change. Evidence: no hidden connected demand. Review station.
### P109-02 — Electrochemistry
Calculate valid-branch shift and explain plateau/material effects. Evidence: no blind extrapolation. Review station.
### P109-03 — Measurement quality
Demonstrate safe reference/time/source verification and classify dataset. Evidence: raw/corrected records preserved. Practical station.
### P109-04 — Demand
Calculate geometry, exposed fraction, mean/final basis and sensitivity. Evidence: units and conventions explicit. Review station.
### P109-05 — Galvanic sizing
Independently check output and capacity and defend count. Evidence: upward integer selection and interaction limits. Review station.
### P109-06 — Network/supply
Use safe model to verify circuit quantities and defend supplied resistance/voltage model. Evidence: no mixing unrelated submodels. Practical station.
### P109-07 — Interference
Review coordinated trial, limits and rollback. Evidence: all owners and safety functions retained. Review station.
### P109-08 — Alternatives
Compare feasible options and present worth with omissions. Evidence: technical veto precedes cost. Review station.
### P109-09 — Commissioning
Inspect inert installed model, polarity/labels and test plan. Evidence: hold points and representative results. Practical station.
### P109-10 — Oversight/report
Observe a simulated tester setup, identify planted recording error and produce traceable report. Evidence: independent correction and handover. Practical station.

lessons.title: Reusable forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable forms

B109 basis: scope/geometry/material___ coating/demand convention___ environment___ topology/owners___ design life___ criterion/source/authority___ facts___ assumptions___ unresolved___ approval/revision___.
C109 calculation: input/value/unit/source___ equation/applicability___ conversion/substitution___ output/unit___ sensitivity___ independent check___ design implication___ limitation___.
A109 anodes: mean/final current___ life___ capacity definition___ utilization___ required mass___ unit mass/output___ capacity count___ output count___ interaction/distribution___ selected conditional count___ reviewer___.
O109 options: mandatory requirements___ evidence per option___ rejected reason___ capital/annual/replacement assumptions___ discount/horizon___ present worth___ sensitivity___ approved selection___.
K109 commissioning: drawing/material verification___ pre-concealment hold___ polarity/continuity/isolation___ source settings___ reference/timing___ representative/foreign points___ criterion/disposition___ restoration___ unresolved owner/date___.
R109 report: purpose___ methods/raw records___ validity___ calculations___ alternatives___ interpretation/uncertainty___ conclusions___ specialist referral___ recommendations___ approvals___ attachments/hash___.
E109 assessment: learner/case/version___ action/time___ independence/coaching___ dimension/score/evidence___ critical issue___ remediation___ changed evidence___ assessor/date___.

lessons.title: Completion rules
lessons.body:
## Completion rules

Ten dimensions 0–4: 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major help, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independently correct and traceable, 4 anticipates limitations and verifies alternatives. Require 32/40, each at least 3, four practical and six observed-review dimensions, both complete defenses satisfactory and no unresolved critical error. Critical: fabricated inputs/readings, unsafe electrical/source/bond action, unsupported construction approval, concealed failed criterion, defeated safety function or claiming specialist authority outside competence. Correct the cause and reassess a changed case, retaining the original failure and feedback.

Complete 20 formative checks and 5 labs. Final 10 cases/30 decisions/60 points, 180 minutes, pass 48 and at least 4/6 each, no critical error. Changed retake/keys private. An independent competent reviewer considers appeals against unchanged criteria. No written score substitutes for observed evidence.

Issue VNDRLY/U Cathodic Protection Technologist Training only after these original requirements pass, identifying learner, version/hash, assessor, date, models and practical scope. This is not AMPP CP3, professional licensure or design sign-off. External eligibility, experience and exams remain separate. Maintain employer review after changed standards/equipment, extended absence or adverse performance. Materials production is not learner completion.


---

# VUC109 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q109-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-01-L1

A bonded tank appears on a single-pipe design: proceed unchanged?

**Answer:** No; verify the electrical boundary and revise demand.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncounted connected area invalidates the basis. Revisit Q109-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-01-L2

Does this award authorize any high-risk design?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Specialist and legal engineering authority remain separate. Revisit Q109-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-02-L1

0.120 V/decade branch: doubled current shift magnitude?

**Answer:** 0.03612 V.

**Reason/remediation:** Multiply slope by log 10(2), only within the valid branch. Revisit Q109-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-02-L2

More negative always safer?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Material damage, chemistry and distribution impose limits. Revisit Q109-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-03-L1

C109 values-0.90,-0.88,-0.82,-0.92: all pass?

**Answer:** No; -0.82 fails if qualified.

**Reason/remediation:** An acceptable average hides local weakness. Revisit Q109-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-03-L2

Uncertain OFF timing: immediate adjustment?

**Answer:** First validate/repeat.

**Reason/remediation:** Invalid evidence cannot uniquely diagnose protection. Revisit Q109-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-04-L1

0.30 m diameter, 1000 m length: lateral area?

**Answer:** 942.48 m 2.

**Reason/remediation:** A=pi D L; defined example excludes ends/fittings. Revisit Q109-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-04-L2

Mean versus final demand interchangeable?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Capacity and output checks may require different demand bases. Revisit Q109-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-05-L1

0.40 A, 10 y, 1100 Ah/kg, 0.80 use: mass?

**Answer:** 39.82 kg.

**Reason/remediation:** Charge demand divided by usable capacity. Revisit Q109-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-05-L2

20 kg units at 0.2333 A each, final 0.80 A: count?

**Answer:** Four under the independent-unit model.

**Reason/remediation:** Round output requirement up; verify interaction/distribution separately. Revisit Q109-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-06-L1

5 A×4 ohms+2+1 V with 20% allowance?

**Answer:** 27.6 V.

**Reason/remediation:** Apply allowance to the stated 23 V base. Revisit Q109-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-06-L2

Why not sum individual anode outputs blindly?

**Answer:** Mutual resistance and geometry affect distribution.

**Reason/remediation:** Independent-anode approximation may fail. Revisit Q109-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-07-L1

Bond improvesB but overpolarizesC: successful?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** All affected assets/limits must be evaluated. Revisit Q109-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-07-L2

DC criterion met: AC risks solved?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Different mechanisms and safety criteria apply. Revisit Q109-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-08-L1

What precedes cost ranking?

**Answer:** Technical feasibility and mandatory requirements.

**Reason/remediation:** Cheap noncompliance is not an equivalent option. Revisit Q109-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-08-L2

Does narrow present worth include all risk?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** State omitted replacement, downtime and residual assumptions. Revisit Q109-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-09-L1

Far point-0.80 V underC109: accept near points as whole system?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Coverage and local criteria matter. Revisit Q109-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-09-L2

Material substitution can be accepted by appearance?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Approved performance/specification and engineering disposition are needed. Revisit Q109-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q109-10-L1

Why change one variable under a test plan?

**Answer:** To preserve causal evidence where practicable.

**Reason/remediation:** Uncontrolled simultaneous changes obscure diagnosis. Revisit Q109-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q109-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q109-10-L2

What makes a spreadsheet reviewable?

**Answer:** Visible inputs, units, formulas, sources and revisions.

**Reason/remediation:** A correct-looking total alone is insufficient. Revisit Q109-10 and perform its changed application.

# VUC109 sources and coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original examples, assessments and decision rules. User authorized best effort without inaccessible standards; no complete proprietary-standard conformity or external accreditation claimed.

[AMPP CP3 program](https://www.ampp.org/education/education-resources/courses-by-program/cathodic-protection/cp-technologist) establishes advanced interpretation and design-calculation focus. [March2026 EPG](https://higherlogicdownload.s3.amazonaws.com/NACE/cedda8a4-c3c0-4583-b1b6-3b248e6eb1f2/UploadedImages/Certification/pdf/CP3-Written-Exam-Preparation-Guide.pdf) is newer than the accessible2024 theory guide. It distinguishes technical oversight and specialist escalation for complex/high-risk work. The2026 version is used for scope; this package does not reproduce its exam or eligibility pathways. Our56-hour plan and assessment are original.

[AMPP role guidance](https://ampp.org/education/cathodic-protection-roles-and-responsibilities) supports the distinction between employment supervision and technical oversight. [OSHA electrical testing](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.334) supports safe qualified testing boundaries. [Official gas-pipeline criteria](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title49-vol3/pdf/CFR-2025-title49-vol3-part192.pdf) illustrate asset-specific criteria; C109 is explicitly fictional and not a regulatory substitute.

|Domain|Coverage and evidence|
|---|---|
|01|Basis/authority/topology; W01/CaseA/P01|
|02|Polarization/logarithms/environment/material limits; P02|
|03|Qualified survey/criteria/uncertainty; W01/P03|
|04|Area/coating/current/sensitivity; W02/P04|
|05|Galvanic output/capacity/life; W03/P05|
|06|Resistance/network/distribution/supply models; W04/P06|
|07|Interference/mitigation/safety/rollback; CaseA/P07|
|08|Feasibility/lifecycle/economics; W04/P08|
|09|Installation/commissioning/conditional release; CaseB/P09|
|10|Troubleshooting/supervision/report; both cases/P10|

Every domain has two explained checks and separate final/changed three-decision cases. No synthetic design is released for construction. Equipment/asset-specific procedures and specialist review remain delivery/workplace requirements, not claims fulfilled by this document.

content.title: VUC110 | VUC110 — Cathodic Protection Specialist
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. lessons.title: VUC110 — Cathodic Protection Specialist
lessons.body:
# VUC110 — Cathodic Protection Specialist

Original VNDRLY/U advanced analysis and review materials. No external CP4 credential, professional license or construction approval is conferred.

lessons.title: Q110-01 — Responsible technical practice and requirements
lessons.body:
## Q110-01 — Responsible technical practice and requirements

Specialist work begins with a complete problem definition and a record of who has authority to approve the solution. Identify assets, materials, environments, design life, consequence of failure, interfaces, operating states and applicable legal/owner requirements. Separate technical competence from professional licensure and contractual authority. An original VNDRLY training certificate cannot grant either external CP4 status or permission to sign regulated engineering work.

Develop a requirements register with source, applicability, verification method and acceptance owner. Resolve conflicts explicitly: a generic pipeline criterion may not fit a tank bottom, marine structure, concrete system or high-strength material. Identify inaccessible standards or unknown site information as limitations; do not silently invent their provisions. Plan independent review proportional to complexity and consequence.

Worked case: a proposed common power supply serves a pipeline, tank and foreign crossing. A total current calculation is insufficient because each branch has different geometry, exposure and constraints. Define branch-level criteria, isolation/grounding interfaces, monitoring, failure modes and owner coordination before accepting a common-source architecture. Preserve assumptions through revisions and establish change-control triggers for future connections or coating changes.

lessons.title: Q110-02 — Electrochemical models and material limits
lessons.body:
## Q110-02 — Electrochemical models and material limits

A useful model explains observed behavior within stated conditions. Mixed-potential analysis considers coupled anodic and cathodic reactions; activation, concentration and resistance effects can overlap. Fit polarization data only within a justified regime. A straight line on an E-log-current plot does not establish that the whole field system follows a single Tafel mechanism. Record reference scale, compensation, temperature and stabilization history.

For an ideal branch with 0.100 V/decade slope, increasing current from 0.01 to 0.10 A changes potential magnitude by 0.100 V; increasing to 0.20 A adds only 0.03010 V in the same regime. If measured ON changes continue while qualified OFF response plateaus, examine IR drop, current distribution, shielding and transport limits. Do not extrapolate through a regime change.

Material constraints include local alkalinity, coating disbondment, hydrogen effects and differing behavior of alloys or concrete reinforcement. Prestressed components require particular care and applicable specialist criteria. Current density, polarization and exposure are not interchangeable measures. An average corrosion-rate estimate can conceal pitting or localized discharge. Explain uncertainty and identify independent inspection evidence needed to assess actual damage.

lessons.title: Q110-03 — Field investigation and model validation
lessons.body:
## Q110-03 — Field investigation and model validation

Design a field campaign around competing explanations. Use representative locations, operating states, seasons where relevant, source synchronization and appropriate reference systems. Validate acquisition before calibrating a model to it. A model fitted to biased readings can appear precise while being wrong. Retain calibration data separately from independent validation data.

Review potential surveys, coating surveys, coupon/probe evidence, resistivity/chemistry, continuity, casings and foreign-source records together. Each has limitations: coating indications are not wall thickness, remote potentials may include IR, coupons sample selected geometries and sparse soil data do not uniquely define layers. Use uncertainty and sensitivity to decide which additional measurement would most reduce decision risk.

Original validation example: model predicts OFF magnitudes 0.94, 0.90, 0.86 V at three sites; measured magnitudes 0.93, 0.89, 0.78 V. Residuals measured minus predicted are-0.01,-0.01,-0.08 V. The third point suggests a local model/data problem and cannot be dismissed because the mean error is small. Verify that point's method, then investigate topology/coating/soil and revise or reject the model. Do not tune a free parameter solely to hide an unexplained discrepancy.

lessons.title: Q110-04 — Demand, capacity and lifecycle envelopes
lessons.body:
## Q110-04 — Demand, capacity and lifecycle envelopes

Define initial, mean, final and upset current demand, with the basis for coating breakdown, temperature, flow, exposure and future expansion. Capacity consumption uses time-integrated current; output equipment must satisfy the required operating envelope and distribution. Avoid applying coating factors twice or treating an effective alloy capacity as theoretical capacity and multiplying efficiency again.

For a two-stage synthetic life, current 1 A for 5 years and 2 A for 10 years consumes(1×5+2×10)×8760=219000 Ah. With supplied effective capacity 1200 Ah/kg and utilization 0.85, required mass 214.71 kg. Twelve 20 kg units provide 244800 Ah usable, but that capacity check alone says nothing about peak output, mutual resistance or location. Evaluate replacement access and actual usable geometry.

For multiple structures, sum demand only after verifying their defined electrical relationship; an isolated structure cannot be assumed protected by a neighboring source. Separate nominal demand from uncertainty allowances and document what each factor covers. Perform sensitivity on the dominant assumptions. A design with no margin to an uncertain coating estimate should not be represented as robust merely because its arithmetic balances.

lessons.title: Q110-05 — Distributed resistance and attenuation
lessons.body:
## Q110-05 — Distributed resistance and attenuation

Long structures distribute current along metal resistance and leakage to the electrolyte. A simplified uniform linear model uses longitudinal resistance r in ohm/m and shunt conductance g in S/m, giving attenuation coefficient alpha=sqrt(rg) in 1/m and characteristic resistance sqrt(r/g) in ohms. Boundary conditions determine the solution. A semi-infinite model with one feed can use potential-shift magnitude E(x)=E0 exp(-alpha x); a finite line, multiple feeds or nonlinear polarization requires a different solution.

Original model r=0.0001 ohm/m and g=0.0004 S/m gives alpha 0.0002 per m and characteristic resistance 0.5 ohm. At 1000 m, E/E0=exp(-0.2)=0.81873. For E0=0.30 V shift, the model gives 0.24562 V at 1000 m. This is a shift magnitude, not an absolute pipe potential and not a protection verdict. Adding a native potential without verifying sign, reference and polarization assumptions can create a false result.

Check dimensional consistency, boundary behavior and sensitivity before using software. As g changes with coating condition, both attenuation and source demand change. Nearby anodes, layered soil, bonds and nonlinear reactions may invalidate the uniform model. Compare predictions with independent field data and document the valid operating range. Do not use a convenient equation beyond its assumptions simply because it produces a number.

lessons.title: Q110-06 — Groundbeds and multi-anode interactions
lessons.body:
## Q110-06 — Groundbeds and multi-anode interactions

Groundbed performance depends on soil structure, anode geometry, spacing, backfill, moisture, gas management, cable resistance and neighboring facilities. Deep systems add drilling, aquifer/environmental and venting constraints. A low calculated resistance is not a complete design: current distribution, life, maintainability and interference must also be addressed.

For a simple two-anode resistance matrix, V1=R11 I1+R12 I2 and V2=R21 I1+R22 I2. With equal applied 10 V, self resistance 5 ohms and mutual resistance 1 ohm, symmetry gives each current 10/(5+1)=1.6667 A, total 3.3333 A. Ignoring interaction predicts 4 A, overstating output by 0.6667 A or 20% relative to the actual model total. The matrix is supplied teaching data, not a universal groundbed formula.

Review positive/negative cable sizing and voltage drops under the applicable electrical design rules, without treating this course as an electrical-code substitute. Inspect installation hold points and establish baseline resistance/output measurements. If field performance differs from prediction, investigate input and installation evidence before changing source settings. Parallel anodes are not automatically independent resistors; mutual effects can be material.

lessons.title: Q110-07 — Interference, AC and coordinated mitigation
lessons.body:
## Q110-07 — Interference, AC and coordinated mitigation

Map all sources, structures, bonds, isolators, grounding systems and protective devices relevant to interference. Capture dynamic conditions with a sampling plan capable of seeing their duration and peaks. Establish sign conventions and source timing before interpreting shifts. Current entering one region may leave another and create anodic risk; improving one location can worsen another.

Mitigation must consider DC corrosion, AC corrosion, touch/step safety, fault/lightning behavior and operational ownership. Decouplers and grounding devices have ratings and failure modes; they cannot be removed just to simplify CP measurements. Use qualified electrical and corrosion expertise together where their responsibilities overlap. A DC potential criterion does not establish electrical safety.

Original coordinated trial has three monitoring points. Baseline qualified OFF values are-0.90,-0.88,-0.87 V. After a bond trial they become-0.96,-0.91,-1.18 V. Fictional window C110 is-1.10 to-0.85 V, so the third point invalidates the trial despite improvement at the first two. Document current, source state, affected owners and controlled rollback. Do not leave an experimental configuration in service without approval and verification of all relevant constraints.

lessons.title: Q110-08 — Application-specific design decisions
lessons.body:
## Q110-08 — Application-specific design decisions

Different assets need different system boundaries and evidence. A buried pipeline requires continuity, coating, attenuation and crossing evaluation. A tank bottom may have shielding from liners, replacement floors or foundation layers; perimeter readings may not prove the entire underside protected. Internal water systems add water chemistry, geometry, service compatibility and access issues. Marine structures require appropriate references, salinity/temperature and hydrodynamic/current-distribution considerations.

Concrete systems require reinforcement continuity, anode compatibility and criteria appropriate to the reinforcement and structural condition. Prestressing and high-strength materials cannot be treated as ordinary buried mild steel. Mixed-metal assemblies may impose incompatible polarization limits. Identify when separate zones, monitoring or different corrosion-control methods are needed rather than forcing a single criterion onto all components.

Worked choice: a tank has a nonconductive liner separating an external anode bed from part of the bottom. Increasing rectifier output may increase remote gradients without delivering current to the shielded interface. Require geometry/material confirmation and an applicable specialist solution; do not certify the underside from one favorable perimeter reading. Document inspection access and how future performance will be verified before selecting the concept.

lessons.title: Q110-09 — Power, controls, reliability and economics
lessons.body:
## Q110-09 — Power, controls, reliability and economics

Specify the required current/voltage envelope, control range, environmental rating, monitoring, alarm behavior and safe failure state. Redundancy must address common causes: two supplies on one failed feeder do not provide independent power. Loss of communications should not be mistaken for zero corrosion risk or a known equipment state. Define who responds to alarms and how actual output is verified.

A supplied calculation requires 8 A through 3 ohms plus 2 V back potential and 2 V cable drop: 28 V base. A25% voltage allowance gives 35 V. The design still needs appropriate current rating, transient behavior, electrical protection and approved installation. For energy estimation at continuous 35 V×8 A, DC output is 280 W or 2452.8 kWh/year. AC input will be higher according to actual efficiency and auxiliaries; do not bill DC energy as measured AC consumption.

Compare lifecycle options only after technical feasibility. At 5% over 15 years, annual present-worth factor 10.37966. OptionA capital 20000 plus 1000/year gives 30379.66; optionB capital 15000 plus 1600/year gives 31607.45. The modeled difference 1227.79 favorsA but excludes replacements, downtime and residual value. Sensitivity and reliability consequences may outweigh that difference. Show omissions and decision ownership.

lessons.title: Q110-10 — Verification, change management and specialist judgment
lessons.body:
## Q110-10 — Verification, change management and specialist judgment

A complete design package includes basis, calculations, drawings, specifications, installation quality plan, commissioning criteria, operating limits and maintenance/monitoring plan. Independent review should challenge assumptions, units, model applicability, criteria and foreseeable failures, not just arithmetic. Resolve review comments with evidence and preserve the revision trail.

Commissioning verifies the installed system, not the intention of the drawing. Check materials, polarity, continuity/isolation, protections, source controls, representative potentials, foreign effects and alarm/response behavior. Record baseline data and unresolved items. A favorable test at one operating state cannot waive a failed high-demand or source-outage condition. Define acceptance authority and the safe interim state while defects are corrected.

After service changes, evaluate whether the basis remains valid: new bonds, coating damage, replaced floors, changed chemistry, altered grounding or added structures can invalidate the old assessment. Use management of change and targeted revalidation. A specialist must communicate uncertainty and refuse unsupported sign-off. This original program assesses structured analysis and judgment with synthetic cases; it does not create years of responsible-charge experience, external certification or licensure.

---

content.title: VUC110 | VUC110 specialist workbook and delivery
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC110 specialist workbook and delivery
lessons.body: # VUC110 specialist workbook and delivery

lessons.title: Entry, delivery and equipment
lessons.body:
## Entry, delivery and equipment

Require demonstrated technologist-level calculations, survey interpretation, electrochemistry and technical reporting. Diagnose logarithms, exponentials, linear equations, dimensional analysis and uncertainty before advanced work. Original 64-hour plan: 18 instruction, 18 calculation/model workshops, 16 integrated cases, 6 observed defenses, 3 final and 3 feedback/remediation. Additional practice follows demonstrated need. This is original training, not AMPP course equivalence or a substitute for responsible-charge experience.

Instructor and independent reviewer need documented competence in advanced CP design/review and the application under discussion. Use transparent calculation sheets, plotting software or calculator, controlled datasets, inert multi-branch installation model, isolated low-voltage measurement rig and source/criteria cards. No live power, actual foreign bonds or construction release. Three stations require safe model/setup/inspection performance; seven are observed analysis/defense stations. Independently verify all setup values before assessment. Label synthetic data and never merge it into real asset records.

C110 fictional qualified OFF window:-1.10 to-0.85 V inclusive. All model constants and criteria below are exercise inputs, not universal standards. Use 8760 h/year. Effective capacities already include stated electrochemical performance; utilization is applied once. The attenuation example is semi-infinite, uniform and linear; multi-anode matrix entries are supplied, not derived from a real groundbed.

lessons.title: Laboratories
lessons.body:
## Laboratories

### W110-01 — Requirements and validation

Assets: pipe P, tank T and foreign line F; owners differ. P has qualified OFF windowC110; T has a liner whose current shielding is unresolved; F requires coordinated impact assessment. Learner creates requirements/evidence/authority matrix and refuses a single summed-current acceptance. Model predictions at P1/P2/P3 are 0.94/0.90/0.86 V magnitudes, measured 0.93/0.89/0.78. Residuals-0.01/-0.01/-0.08 V. Instructor asks to deleteP3 as an outlier; learner instead verifies measurement then investigates physical/model mismatch. Changed run 0.93/0.89/0.85 within supplied±0.02 validation band supports sampled-state validation only. Demonstrate source/time/reference verification on safe model.

### W110-02 — Demand envelope and capacity

Stage 1: 1 A for 5 years; stage 2: 2 A for 10 years. Charge 219000 Ah. Effective 1200 Ah/kg, use 0.85 requires 214.71 kg. Twelve 20 kg units provide 244800 Ah; capacity margin 25800 Ah. Learner separately documents unknown peak-output/distribution and replacement assumptions. Changed demand 0.8 A4 years+1.6 A8 years gives 140160 Ah; 1000 Ah/kg, use 0.80 requires 175.2 kg and nine 20 kg units by capacity. Instructor introduces a spreadsheet applying utilization twice; learner corrects and preserves revision. No mass-only approval.

### W110-03 — Attenuation and interacting anodes

Uniform model r 0.0001 ohm/m, g 0.0004 S/m gives alpha 0.0002/m and characteristic 0.5 ohm. E0 shift 0.30 V at 1000 m gives 0.24562 V. Learner plots 0/500/1000/2000 m: 0.30/0.27145/0.24562/0.20110 V. Instructor labels the values absolute pipe potentials; learner corrects the label and explains missing baseline. Changed r 0.0004, g 0.0001, E0 .40, x 2000 gives 0.26813 V.

Separate two-anode matrix: equal 10 V, self 5 ohms, mutual 1 ohm. Solve I1=I2=1.6667 A, total 3.3333 A. Independent assumption 4 A is 20% above model total. Changed 12 V, self 4, mutual 2 gives 2 A each, total 4 A versus independent 6 A. Explain why symmetry is valid here and why unequal source/geometry needs the full simultaneous equations. Verify simple circuit quantities on an isolated rig without representing the resistor network as an actual electrolyte model.

### W110-04 — Mitigation and application review

Baseline pointsA/B/C:-0.90/-0.88/-0.87 V; trial:-0.96/-0.91/-1.18 V. C failsC110; learner documents controlled trial rejection/rollback, owners and outstanding AC safety review. TankT has a nonconductive liner and favorable perimeter value-0.95 V; no underside acceptance is justified. A concrete branch includes prestressed steel with no applicable criteria supplied; refer to appropriate specialist/structural requirements. Instructor offers a universal-criterion shortcut; learner rejects it with a precise evidence request rather than inventing a value.

### W110-05 — Reliability and lifecycle

8 A×3 ohms+2 V back+2 V lead=28 V; 25% allowance gives 35 V. Continuous DC280 W gives 2452.8 kWh/year. Learner identifies AC efficiency/auxiliary omissions. Two supplies share one feeder and one controller: list common-cause failures and required independent verification. At 5%, 15 years, factor 10.379658: A20000+1000/year=30379.66; B15000+1600/year=31607.45. Difference 1227.79 favorsA only under stated costs. Inject inaccessible anode replacement and unpriced outage consequences; learner revises comparison and does not hide omitted costs.

### W110-06 — Two integrated specialist defenses

CaseA combines pipe/tank/foreign assets fromW01 withW02/W03 calculations. At 0 issue design basis. At 15 reveal tank liner. At 30 release unexplained P3 residual. At 45 reveal mutual-anode effect. At 60 offer bond trial fromW04. At 75 ask for construction release. Expected: explicit scope/criteria, correct arithmetic, validation hold, capacity/output separation, no tank/foreign overclaim and a reviewable conditional package with exact unresolved actions. Learner defends every assumption independently.

CaseB uses current 0.8 A4 years+1.6 A8 years, capacity 1000, use 0.80, 20 kg units; attenuation r 0.0004, g 0.0001, E0 .40, x 2000; two 12 V anodes, self 4, mutual 2. At 20 disclose shared feeder; at 40 introduce unapproved substitute anode; at 60 provide favorable sampled potentials but missing foreign-owner acceptance. Expected charge 140160 Ah, mass 175.2 kg, nine capacity units, shift 0.26813 V, total matrix 4 A, with no unconditional acceptance. Changed defense replaces source data with 5 A/3 ohm/2+1 V/25% allowance and revised coating condition: 22.5 V; require change review despite previous acceptance. Both cases require completed basis, calculations, alternatives, commissioning and maintenance plan, not only oral answers.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P110-01 — Requirements/authority
Produce branch-specific register and review plan. Evidence: ownership, criteria and approval boundaries. Review.
### P110-02 — Electrochemistry
Defend model region/material limitations and changed reaction case. Evidence: no extrapolation beyond data. Review.
### P110-03 — Investigation
Demonstrate safe data-quality setup and validation comparison. Evidence: independent data and local residual preserved. Practical.
### P110-04 — Lifecycle demand
Calculate stage charge/capacity and sensitivity. Evidence: capacity/output distinction and factor definitions. Review.
### P110-05 — Attenuation
Derive units, plot supplied model and challenge boundary assumptions. Evidence: shift versus absolute potential distinguished. Review.
### P110-06 — Groundbed network
Solve interaction matrix and verify safe model readings. Evidence: no independent-anode overclaim. Practical.
### P110-07 — Mitigation
Defend coordinated trial/rollback and electrical safety interfaces. Evidence: all affected constraints. Review.
### P110-08 — Applications
Analyze tank/concrete/marine/pipeline differences. Evidence: no generic criterion substitution. Review.
### P110-09 — Reliability/economics
Calculate voltage/energy/cost and identify common causes. Evidence: feasibility and omissions explicit. Review.
### P110-10 — Acceptance/change
Inspect inert installation, identify planted label/substitution defect and issue change-controlled handover. Evidence: no false release. Practical.

lessons.title: Forms and instructor controls
lessons.body:
## Forms and instructor controls

B110 requirements: asset/owner___ material/environment___ operating states___ criterion/source/applicability___ consequence___ verification___ approval authority___ unresolved/conflict___ disposition___.
V110 validation: model/version___ assumptions/boundary___ calibration data___ independent data___ predicted/measured/residual___ uncertainty/band___ anomaly investigation___ valid range___ reviewer___.
C110 calculation: inputs/units/source___ equations___ substitution___ result___ sensitivity/edge check___ independent reviewer___ capacity/output/distribution decision___ limitations___.
M110 mitigation: affected owners/assets___ source states___ baseline/trial/current/AC evidence___ limits___ approved controls/rollback___ results at every point___ restored state___ acceptance___.
D110 design review: drawing/spec/version___ geometry/material/polarity___ hold points___ safety/environment___ commissioning/monitoring___ comments/resolution___ release status/authority___.
H110 handover: final approved settings___ baseline/limits___ alarms/response owner___ inspection schedule___ replacement access___ changes requiring review___ unresolved actions/date___ acceptance___.
A110 assessment: learner/case/version___ dimension/action/time___ independent/coached___ evidence/score___ critical error___ feedback___ changed demonstration___ assessor/reviewer/date___.

lessons.title: Decision and original award
lessons.body:
## Decision and original award

Ten dimensions 0–4: 0 absent/unsafe, 1 major assistance, 2 safe but incomplete/prompted, 3 independent correct traceable, 4 anticipates and verifies consequential limitations. Require 32/40, each at least 3, three practical/seven review dimensions, both complete case packages and defenses satisfactory, no unresolved critical error. Critical: unsafe electrical/bond action, fabricated evidence, concealed failed criterion, knowingly invalid model used for release, unsupported whole-asset approval or false external/licensure claim. Stop, record, remediate and reassess changed conditions; retain all versions and failed evidence.

Complete 20 explained checks and 6 labs. Controlled final 10 cases/30 decisions, 60 points, 180 minutes; pass 48, each at least 4/6, no critical error. Private changed retake and keys remain separate. Independent competent reviewer handles appeals without lowering criteria. Written performance cannot replace observed practical/review evidence.

Award VNDRLY/U Cathodic Protection Specialist Training only after original requirements pass, recording identity, version/hash, assessors, dates, models and limitations. Not AMPP CP4, professional registration, employment experience or authority to release construction. External eligibility changes must be checked directly with AMPP; this package does not promise eligibility. Employer maintains continuing technical development and review after changed standards, assets or adverse performance. Authoring is not learner certification.

[Role guidance](https://ampp.org/education/cathodic-protection-roles-and-responsibilities) distinguishes technical supervision. [OSHA testing controls](https://www.osha.gov/laws-regs/regulations/standardnumber/1910/1910.334) support electrical boundaries.
