lessons.title: VUC111 — NDT Level II Method Practice
lessons.body:
# VUC111 — NDT Level II Method Practice

Original VNDRLY/U common core and PT/MT/UT/RT/VT teaching tracks. External ASNT9712 and employer/regulatory authorization are separate.

lessons.title: Q111-01 — Certification scope and Level II responsibility
lessons.body:
## Q111-01 — Certification scope and Level II responsibility

Nondestructive testing evaluates selected characteristics without intentionally destroying the item. A Level II role is method- and technique-specific: competence in penetrant testing does not establish ultrasonic or radiographic competence. Define method, technique, product/sector, procedure and limitations on every assignment and credential. Distinguish an independent certification scheme from an employer's written practice and job authorization. ASNT 9712 and ASNT NDT Level II are different programs; their names must not be used interchangeably.

This original VNDRLY package includes common instruction and PT, MT, UT, RT and VT learning tracks. It does not issue ASNT 9712, grant regulatory radiation authority or create required industrial experience. Each learner's demonstrated method/technique is recorded separately. Public ASNT pages currently differ on VT availability: the program page labels it coming soon while another overview includes it. Verify availability directly before an external application; the original VT instruction remains useful without claiming that enrollment is open.

Before testing, confirm identity, current procedure, acceptance criteria, equipment capability, training/experience, vision requirements and employer authorization. A Level II may prepare an instruction within the authorized procedure, but cannot invent a new acceptance rule to clear a part. Stop when scope, safety or technique capability is uncertain. Worked decision: an MT-trained worker is asked to approve an aluminum casting by MT. Reject the method/material mismatch and refer selection of an appropriate authorized method.

lessons.title: Q111-02 — Materials, manufacturing and discontinuities
lessons.body:
## Q111-02 — Materials, manufacturing and discontinuities

Understand how manufacturing and service create the features a method may reveal. Castings can contain shrinkage, porosity and inclusions; forgings can contain laps or internal discontinuities; welds can contain lack of fusion, incomplete penetration, porosity, slag and cracking. Service can introduce fatigue, corrosion, erosion or stress-related damage. Geometry such as roots, edges, threads and material transitions can also produce indications.

An indication is a response requiring interpretation. A relevant indication arises from a condition of interest; a nonrelevant indication may arise from geometry or known structure; a false indication may arise from processing or equipment artifacts. A discontinuity is not automatically a rejectable defect. Rejection requires the applicable acceptance criteria and valid examination. Do not dismiss an unexpected response as geometry without supporting evidence.

Orientation and accessibility govern detectability. PT needs an opening to the surface; MT needs ferromagnetic material and a suitable field direction; UT depends on sound path, orientation, coupling and material response; RT depends on attenuation, geometry and projection; VT depends on access, lighting and resolution. Worked comparison: a tight planar flaw parallel to the radiation beam may be difficult to reveal by RT, while an appropriately oriented UT beam may respond strongly. Method selection must address the expected flaw, not merely the equipment on hand.

lessons.title: Q111-03 — Instructions, calibration and examination control
lessons.body:
## Q111-03 — Instructions, calibration and examination control

An executable instruction identifies the item and area, governing procedure/revision, personnel requirements, safety, equipment/consumables, preparation, settings, calibration/system checks, coverage, interpretation, acceptance, reporting and post-test actions. It must be clear enough for an authorized operator to reproduce. Copying a generic checklist without item geometry or criteria is insufficient.

Distinguish instrument calibration from a pre-use system performance check and technique calibration on representative reference standards. Record equipment IDs and validity, reference-block or comparator identity, settings, environmental conditions and checks before/after examination. If a post-check fails, determine the affected interval and reinspect under the approved process; do not assume earlier results remain valid.

Original control example: examinations E1–E6 occur between a passing 08:00 check and failing 10:00 check, with no intermediate check. Their validity is unresolved until the approved investigation defines the affected interval; simply repeating E6 is not justified. Preserve original reports and corrections. Acceptance criteria supplied in this course are fictional training cards, not ASTM/ASME/AWS/ISO provisions. Real work must use the current applicable procedure and qualified approval. Safety includes chemicals, UV exposure, electrical equipment, access, confined spaces and radiation as relevant.

lessons.title: Q111-04 — Liquid penetrant testing
lessons.body:
## Q111-04 — Liquid penetrant testing

PT uses a penetrant capable of entering surface-breaking discontinuities on suitable nonporous materials. Clean and dry the surface using the approved method without smearing metal over openings. Verify penetrant family, sensitivity/type, removal process, compatible developer, batch/expiry and temperature range. Apply penetrant uniformly, allow the specified dwell, remove excess by the correct process, dry as required, apply developer and inspect within the prescribed development interval under verified viewing conditions.

Solvent-removable, water-washable and post-emulsifiable systems have different removal controls. Excessive washing or solvent can remove penetrant from discontinuities; inadequate removal produces background that masks indications. Emulsification time and method are critical for post-emulsifiable systems. Do not mix materials from unapproved systems or improvise dwell/temperature values. Fluorescent and visible methods require their respective viewing controls and measured light conditions; record the actual procedure limits.

Interpret indication shape, size, location and behavior, distinguishing relevant bleed-out from surface contamination or process marks. Measure according to the applicable instruction, not a guessed flaw size beneath the indication. Worked training card: reject any relevant linear indication longer than 3.0 mm; a 4.0 mm linear bleed-out rejects, a 2.0 mm rounded indication requires the separate rounded criterion, and heavy background invalidates examination. Equality and classification rules must be defined. Clean/protect the part after inspection and retain traceable disposition. PT does not detect sealed subsurface flaws.

lessons.title: Q111-05 — Magnetic particle testing
lessons.body:
## Q111-05 — Magnetic particle testing

MT detects surface and near-surface discontinuities in ferromagnetic materials by observing particles accumulated at magnetic flux leakage. Confirm material suitability. Choose an authorized magnetizing technique, particle medium and viewing conditions. A field approximately perpendicular to the expected discontinuity generally improves detection; examining in two appropriate directions helps address orientation limitations. A single direction cannot justify universal coverage.

Yokes and bench systems create different field arrangements. Verify equipment performance with the prescribed checks, contact/spacing where applicable, field adequacy/direction and particle system condition. Current magnitude alone does not prove an effective field at the examination area. Avoid arc burns, overheating and unsafe electrical contact; direct-contact techniques require their specific controls. Apply particles and magnetization in the specified sequence and observe under controlled lighting.

Geometry, permeability changes and residual fields can create nonrelevant indications. Investigate without grinding away evidence or changing acceptance rules. Demagnetize when required and verify the residual field using the prescribed method; post-clean and protect the part. Worked case: a weld is tested with one yoke orientation and no field verification. A blank surface is not a valid no-defect result. Repeat under the approved technique with field/coverage checks. The course's safe yoke demonstration is not qualification for every bench/prod/coil technique.

lessons.title: Q111-06 — Ultrasonic principles and straight-beam testing
lessons.body:
## Q111-06 — Ultrasonic principles and straight-beam testing

UT introduces sound and interprets returned or transmitted signals. In pulse-echo thickness measurement, distance equals velocity times round-trip time divided by two after correct zero/delay compensation. Material, temperature, mode and geometry affect velocity. Couplant transfers sound across the interface; poor coupling can mimic loss of backwall. Frequency and probe size affect resolution, penetration and beam behavior. Near-field and beam-spread effects matter when comparing amplitudes.

For a supplied longitudinal velocity 5900 m/s and corrected round-trip time 20 microseconds, thickness is 59.0 mm. If time is not corrected for probe delay, the result can be biased. Calibrate range, zero and sensitivity with appropriate reference blocks and verify at relevant ranges. Use representative material/curvature where required. Record probe, frequency, instrument, calibration, couplant and temperature.

A reduced backwall echo may result from attenuation, roughness, coupling, geometry or a discontinuity. Check technique and compare with known features before assigning a cause. Scan with specified overlap and coverage, recording inaccessible zones. For castings/forgings, grain structure and geometry can affect scattering and detectability. Worked decision: calibration on a flat steel block is transferred to a curved coarse-grained component without procedure support. Hold the examination until technique applicability and sensitivity are established; a numeric thickness display alone is not valid evidence.

lessons.title: Q111-07 — Ultrasonic angle-beam and weld evaluation
lessons.body:
## Q111-07 — Ultrasonic angle-beam and weld evaluation

Angle-beam examination directs a refracted beam through the material to interrogate weld regions. Confirm wedge/probe identity, refracted angle, index point, range, sensitivity and applicable reference response. Snell's relation connects incident and refracted modes through their velocities, but real wedges and materials require verification rather than a nameplate assumption. Account for weld geometry, thickness, access and expected flaw orientation.

For a supplied 60-degree refracted angle in a 20 mm plate, first-leg surface distance is 20 tan 60=34.64 mm and sound path 20/cos 60=40.0 mm. A full skip surface distance is 69.28 mm. These calculations describe ideal geometry, not a flaw's exact dimensions. Locate indications with the verified index and sound path, then evaluate by the governing procedure. Mode conversion, roots and opposite-surface reflections can produce responses requiring interpretation.

DAC or other reference methods compare responses under controlled calibration; transfer corrections and material attenuation must follow the approved method. Amplitude is not automatically flaw height. Sizing techniques have their own limitations. Worked case: a response exceeds a fictional evaluation level but lies at the expected root path. Record and investigate using permitted scans/angles; do not automatically accept as root geometry or reject without applying the criterion. Advanced phased-array or TOFD techniques require separate specific training and procedures; conventional UT instruction does not silently qualify them.

lessons.title: Q111-08 — Radiographic principles, geometry and radiation boundary
lessons.body:
## Q111-08 — Radiographic principles, geometry and radiation boundary

RT forms an image from differential transmission of ionizing radiation through an object. Thickness, density, composition, beam energy, scatter and geometry influence image contrast. X-ray generators and gamma sources differ in energy/control and regulatory handling. Film, computed radiography and digital detector systems require their own acquisition and quality controls; skill with one does not automatically qualify another.

Geometric unsharpness can be modeled as Ug=F×b/a, where F is effective source size, b object-to-detector distance and a source-to-object distance in a consistent geometry. In an original example F2 mm, b 20 mm, a 400 mm givesUg 0.10 mm. Increasing a can improve geometry but changes exposure requirements. A simple inverse-square model says doubling distance reduces unattenuated intensity to one quarter; restoring receptor exposure under otherwise identical conditions requires four times exposure. Scatter, attenuation, energy and detector behavior limit simplistic calculations.

All RT exercises in this written package use inert layouts and synthetic image-quality records. Live gamma/X-ray work requires the licensed/authorized organization, trained personnel, radiation-safety program, barriers, surveys, monitoring and emergency procedures applicable to the jurisdiction. Never approach a suspected exposed or stuck source, defeat interlocks or attempt recovery. Withdraw/control access and notify the radiation-safety authority under the approved emergency plan. An NDT training pass is not radiation authorization.

lessons.title: Q111-09 — Radiographic quality, processing and interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q111-09 — Radiographic quality, processing and interpretation

Before evaluating a radiograph, verify item/area identification, orientation, coverage, technique, image-quality indicator arrangement and required image quality. An IQI demonstrates specified image-quality capability under the technique; it is not a physical replica of every possible flaw. Film processing, handling and viewing can introduce artifacts; digital systems require validated acquisition, calibration, resolution and display controls. Do not treat arbitrary image enhancement as equivalent to the original data.

Check the applicable density/contrast/resolution requirements and viewing conditions. Retain original images and processing metadata. A scratch, water mark, detector defect or stitching artifact may resemble a discontinuity. Compare location, morphology, repeated views and process evidence, but do not erase an indication merely because it is inconvenient. Planar defects may be missed when orientation is unfavorable; negative RT is bounded by technique sensitivity and coverage.

Training image card R111 supplies fictional acceptance rules and measured features. ImageA has valid quality and a 5 mm linear relevant indication; ImageB has insufficient quality; ImageC has a known processing scratch outside the part plus a 2 mm rounded relevant indication. EvaluateA against the linear criterion, rejectB as an examination before judging the part, and keepC's artifact separate from its relevant feature. A schematic is useful for reasoning but cannot replace actual image interpretation practice in a fully equipped authorized method course. Learner endorsements must reflect the actual practical evidence obtained.

lessons.title: Q111-10 — Visual testing and remote observation
lessons.body:
## Q111-10 — Visual testing and remote observation

VT is an examination method requiring defined access, lighting, resolution, surface condition and viewing geometry. Direct viewing and remote optics have different limitations. Establish item identity and coverage, clean only as permitted, verify measuring tools and document dimensions with scale and orientation. A photograph without scale or location can be visually persuasive but technically unusable.

Remote cameras/borescopes introduce distortion, perspective, depth-of-field, illumination and blind-zone issues. Verify system performance using suitable targets and the actual working configuration. A nominal pixel count does not guarantee defect resolution at the inspection distance. Record distance/angle or other procedure-required geometry, lens settings and coverage gaps. Do not infer unseen surface condition from adjacent clear images.

Worked example: a supplied image scale is 0.20 mm/pixel in the calibrated plane; a feature spans 15 pixels, giving 3.0 mm in that plane. If the feature lies out of plane or the lens distance changes, the scale may no longer apply. Repeat with valid geometry before acceptance. Distinguish discoloration, surface contamination, dimensional mismatch and suspected cracking; use the governing criterion and refer another method when needed. Access to an enclosed item may introduce confined-space or isolation hazards not removed by choosing a camera.

lessons.title: Q111-11 — Evaluation, instruction preparation and reporting
lessons.body:
## Q111-11 — Evaluation, instruction preparation and reporting

Interpretation asks what caused the indication; evaluation asks whether the identified condition meets the applicable criteria. Keep those steps separate. State the procedure and acceptance source/revision, measured indication characteristics, validity checks and disposition. A Level II instruction should specify how an authorized operator performs the defined examination, including coverage, calibration, process parameters, recording and escalation. It must not exceed the governing procedure's authority.

Original acceptance card A111: relevant linear indications longer than 3.0 mm reject; relevant rounded indications greater than 2.5 mm reject; three or more rounded indications in any 10 mm evaluation length reject; exactly 3.0 mm linear and 2.5 mm rounded meet these size limits only. A valid examination is required first. These rules are fictional and not a code excerpt. For three rounded indications of 1.0, 1.5 and 2.0 mm within 8 mm, size alone passes but grouping rejects. Record both reasoning steps.

Report coverage and limitations even when no relevant indication is found. Identify repairs/re-examinations with traceable links, retaining original results. Do not state an entire component is defect-free when only one accessible area was tested. Worked instruction defect: it says 'inspect weld and accept if good' with no revision, coverage or criteria. Return it for completion; an experienced operator's intuition cannot make it reproducible.

lessons.title: Q111-12 — Quality, ethics, practical evidence and continuing competence
lessons.body:
## Q111-12 — Quality, ethics, practical evidence and continuing competence

Quality depends on traceable personnel, equipment, procedures, consumables, specimens and records. Protect controlled examination materials and avoid coaching during scored practical work. Record actual method/technique exposure and distinguish training hours from industrial experience. Vision and continuing-activity requirements belong to the applicable scheme and employer system; do not invent compliance from classroom attendance.

When equipment or process checks fail, identify affected examinations, preserve evidence, notify the responsible authority and perform the approved retest. Pressure to meet a shipment deadline does not justify changing criteria, omitting an indication or signing another person's work. A qualified reviewer should resolve disputed interpretation using the procedure and evidence, not rank or commercial pressure.

This package provides instruction, synthetic datasets, specimen-preparation specifications, observation forms, final and changed assessments. Actual learner endorsement requires the specified supervised practical demonstrations for that method/technique; RT exposure remains within an authorized radiation program. Missing equipment means pending practical evidence, not automatic completion. Issue an original training record with exact scope and limitations, never an ASNT9712 certificate. Renewal/external eligibility and method availability must be confirmed with the current certification body. Authoring completion is separate from an individual's qualification.

---

lessons.title: VUC111 method workbooks, instruction preparation and assessment
lessons.body: # VUC111 method workbooks, instruction preparation and assessment

lessons.title: Delivery routes and resources
lessons.body:
## Delivery routes and resources

Common core 16 hours. Original method allocations: PT32, MT40, UT80, RT80, VT24; all-track plan 272 hours. These allocations are a teaching plan, not ASNT minimum-hour equivalence. Within each track allocate approximately one quarter instruction/worked examples, one half supervised practical and one quarter interpretation/instruction preparation/assessment; extend for remediation. Record actual attendance and practice by method/technique. Core may be reused, but no method endorsement is inferred from another. Diagnose arithmetic, units, drawing interpretation and safe-work understanding first. Verify applicable vision requirements through the authorized scheme/employer process.

Instructors/assessors must be qualified and experienced in the method/technique and the governing delivery procedure. A LevelIII or other properly authorized procedure authority controls actual technique instructions and acceptance references. Provide accessible written diagrams and calibrated viewing arrangements; accommodations preserve detection and independent evaluation requirements.

PT resources: approved compatible consumable system, known surface-opening reference panels, clean nonporous coupons, timer, temperature measurement, applicable visible/UV viewing meters and safety data. MT: safe approved yoke and bench training arrangements where that technique is endorsed, ferromagnetic known-discontinuity specimens, field/system indicators, particles, light meters and residual-field equipment. UT: instrument, straight/angle probes, wedges, couplant, suitable known reference blocks and mapped casting/forging/weld specimens. RT: inert geometry rig, actual authorized training image sets with known truth, viewers/display quality tools and, only at a licensed facility, approved exposure equipment/safety program. VT: known dimensional/surface specimens, calibrated gauges, illumination meter, direct/remote optics and resolution targets. Missing resources defer the method's practical endorsement.

Use A111 fictional acceptance card only for synthetic exercises: linear relevant indication>3.0 mm rejects; rounded>2.5 mm rejects; at least 3 rounded in any 10 mm evaluation length rejects. A valid exam is prerequisite. These are not code values. Actual specimens are graded against the delivery procedure's approved criteria and assessor master map, not invented field rules.

lessons.title: Instructor specimen preparation and control
lessons.body:
## Instructor specimen preparation and control

Prepare three specimens per endorsed technique: one sound with geometric distractor, one relevant planar/surface indication and one volumetric/grouped or mixed indication appropriate to the method. A qualified assessor establishes the master map independently using suitable validated methods, recording identity, coordinates, dimensions, orientations, detectable technique and uncertainty. Mark learner-facing IDs without revealing flaw locations. Do not damage production parts to create specimens. Use purchased/verified training blocks or nonservice coupons. Keep master maps private. Retire specimens whose condition changes; pre/post-check them for contamination, wear or damage.

Synthetic card set S111 provides reproducible reasoning exercises: S1 valid 4.0 mm linear indication at x 20, y 10; S2 rounded 1.0/1.5/2.0 mm at x 10/13/18, y 20; S3 valid 2.0 mm rounded at x 40, y 15 plus known artifact outside part; S4 inadequate system/image quality; S5 no relevant indications but 20% area inaccessible; S6 linear 3.0 mm and rounded 2.5 mm with no group. Coordinates in mm on a 100×50 mm coupon. These are interpretation cards, not evidence of detection skill. Learners must separately locate unknown indications on actual approved training specimens for practical endorsement.

lessons.title: Method laboratories
lessons.body:
## Method laboratories

### W111-01 — Common instruction and traceability

Issue item WELD-A, 100 mm examination length, revisionP1, method selected by authorized procedure. Learner prepares an instruction with scope, personnel, safety, equipment, preparation, parameters/checks, coverage, criteria, report and post-test actions. Controller injects revisionP2 midway and a missing acceptance page. Expected: stop/use change control, obtain authorized current basis, retain old data as such. Calibration record 08:00 pass/10:00 fail with six intervening exams requires interval investigation. Changed record has 09:30 valid check and two later exams. Evidence: executable instruction and affected-work register.

### W111-02 — PT techniques

Under the actual approved material-system procedure, demonstrate surface preparation, material identity, temperature/time controls, application, removal, developer, viewing and post-cleaning. Practice solvent-removable, water-washable and post-emulsifiable processes separately if each is to be endorsed; do not transfer timing/removal settings between them. Instructor supplies actual procedure values on a controlled worksheet before practice. Learner records dwell/development start/end and viewing measurements. Inject over-removal and heavy background using a safe training demonstration or process record; learner rejects validity and repeats appropriately.

Evaluate S1, S2, S3, S4: rejectS1 linear; rejectS2 grouping; S3 rounded meets size criterion if no other condition; S4 invalid. On three blind approved specimens, locate/map indications and apply the actual criteria. Changed exercise S6 checks equality and avoids rejecting a boundary by intuition. Score process control and detection separately; correct interpretation of a provided card cannot replace finding an unknown indication.

### W111-03 — MT techniques

Verify ferromagnetic material and actual procedure. Demonstrate yoke system checks, field adequacy/direction, required orientations, particle application, viewing, mapping and required demagnetization/residual check. For bench endorsement, separately demonstrate approved coil/head/current technique and controls with qualified supervision; no live-contact improvisation. Instructor plants a one-direction-only record and an unverified field record; both require correction before a negative result is valid. Compare a geometric indication with a known relevant one using evidence.

Blind specimen set includes differently oriented indications and a geometric distractor. Learner must achieve prescribed coverage and identify all master-map reportable indications. Record actual technique; yoke-only practice yields no bench endorsement. Changed case uses a nonferromagnetic material card, requiring method rejection rather than more magnetizing current.

### W111-04 — UT straight beam and product forms

Verify instrument/probe/reference, zero/range/sensitivity and repeat checks. Use known thicknesses 20/40/60 mm with supplied velocity 5900 m/s for arithmetic: corrected round-trip times 6.780/13.559/20.339 microseconds. Actual block velocity/geometry govern instrument setup. Scan mapped casting/forging specimens under the approved procedure, record coverage, coupling, backwall and indications. Inject loss of coupling, changed temperature and a post-calibration failure. Learner distinguishes signal validity from defect interpretation and defines affected retest interval.

Synthetic corrected 20 microseconds gives 59.0 mm; 12 gives 35.4 mm. Changed 10 gives 29.5 mm. Blind practical requires correct locations/dimensions within the approved specimen rubric, not just these arithmetic answers. Coarse material or curved geometry requires procedure-supported calibration; a convenient flat block is not automatically representative.

### W111-05 — UT weld/angle beam

Verify index, refracted angle, range, sensitivity and reference response using the approved block. Prepare scan plan covering the required weld volume and orientations; record inaccessible zones. Supplied plate 20 mm/60 degrees gives first-leg surface 34.64 mm, path 40 mm, full skip 69.28 mm. Changed 25 mm/45 degrees gives 25 mm/35.36 mm/full skip 50 mm. Demonstrate permitted scans to distinguish geometry from relevant indications and evaluate against actual criteria. Instructor injects an amplitude-to-height claim; learner rejects unsupported sizing. Conventional track does not endorse phased array orTOFD.

### W111-06 — RT geometry and image quality

Inert rig only for geometry: F2 mm, b 20 mm, a 400 mm givesUg 0.10 mm; changedF3, b 30, a 600 gives 0.15 mm. Doubling ideal distance requires fourfold exposure for equivalent receptor exposure, all else unchanged. Use controlled actual training images with verified master interpretation and image-quality records. Learner checks identity, coverage, IQI/quality, viewing/processing or digital-system data before interpreting. Evaluate S1–S6 as reasoning cards, then complete blind actual-image interpretation separately.

Technique endorsements distinguish gamma/X-ray and the actual detector system. Live acquisition practical, if part of the learner's intended scope, occurs only under the licensed facility's procedure, qualified radiation supervision and required safety equipment. Observe pre-job controls, authorized exposure sequence, surveys/monitoring, post-exposure verification and records; assessor records exact authorization and competence evidence. No live source manipulation is instructed by synthetic cards. Emergency inject is an alarm or suspected unretracted source: withdraw/control access and notify authorized safety personnel; no approach/recovery. A simulation-only record explicitly excludes live acquisition authority.

### W111-07 — VT direct and remote

Verify lighting, resolution, gauge status, surface access and geometry. Examine three mapped specimens directly and through the actual remote system where endorsed. Record visible coverage and blind zones. Calibrated scale 0.20 mm/pixel×15 pixels gives 3.0 mm; changed 0.10×28 gives 2.8 mm only if geometry remains valid. Instructor moves camera after calibration; learner repeats verification before measuring. S5 permits only a statement about the examined 80%, not the full part. An inspection photograph requires scale, identity, orientation and traceable location.

### W111-08 — Integrated instruction and quality defense

CaseA: six items with S1–S6 evidence, valid method assignments, then a post-check failure affecting items 3–6. Learner issues initial interpretations, withdraws/qualifies affected validity, plans authorized re-examination and preserves versions. A manager requests shipment before retest. Expected no false acceptance. Prepare a usable method instruction for one assigned technique and orally defend controls/criteria.

CaseB: MT request on aluminum, PT request for sealed subsurface flaw, UT curved component with unsupported calibration, RT image with failed quality, VT inaccessible surface. Learner identifies each limitation and routes to authorized procedure/method review. Changed reassessment supplies valid methods but a grouping rejection, revision conflict and missing practical evidence. Both cases test judgment across tracks; they do not grant unperformed method endorsements.

lessons.title: Observation and scoring
lessons.body:
## Observation and scoring

### P111-01 — Scope
Identify method/technique/scheme and employer authorization. Observed review.
### P111-02 — Discontinuities
Explain manufacturing/service/geometry responses and detection limits. Observed review.
### P111-03 — Instruction
Write executable controlled instruction and affected-work plan. Observed review.
### P111-04 — PT
Perform endorsed process on blind specimens and evaluate; actual practical.
### P111-05 — MT
Perform endorsed magnetization/coverage and post-test controls; actual practical.
### P111-06 — UT straight
Calibrate, scan and map approved product specimens; actual practical.
### P111-07 — UT angle
Verify geometry, scan weld and evaluate; actual practical.
### P111-08 — RT geometry/safety
Demonstrate inert layout and correct radiation-emergency decision; actual inert practical, not live authority.
### P111-09 — RT interpretation
Interpret actual controlled training images and quality data; actual image practical.
### P111-10 — VT
Perform direct/remote endorsed examination and measurement; actual practical.
### P111-11 — Evaluation/report
Apply criteria/grouping and document coverage/limitations; observed review.
### P111-12 — Quality/ethics
Handle failed checks, records, remediation and scope-limited award; observed review.

Score each dimension 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent, 1 major help, 2 safe incomplete/prompted, 3 independent correct traceable, 4 anticipates/controls errors. All-track training requires 39/48, each at least 3, seven practical/five review dimensions, both cases satisfactory and no critical error. Method-specific training record uses common core plus applicable dimensions, each at least 3 and at least 80% overall; list uncompleted methods explicitly. Detection practical additionally requires every master-map reportable indication and no unsupported acceptance; false calls must be resolved under the procedure. Do not alter master truth to pass a candidate.

Critical errors: unsafe chemical/electrical/radiation action, missed reportable indication resulting in false acceptance, fabricated check/experience, wrong method/material acceptance, concealed coverage or unauthorized criterion change. Stop unsafe work, retain evidence, remediate and use a changed specimen/case. Written final 12 cases/36 decisions, 72 points, 180 minutes, pass 58 and at least 4/6 each, no critical error. Separate changed final/keys private. Full written cross-method exam is learning evaluation, not proof of practical endorsement. Independent qualified review handles appeals.

lessons.title: Reproducible forms and award
lessons.body:
## Reproducible forms and award

N111 instruction: item/area/method/technique___ governing revision___ authorization___ hazards___ equipment/materials___ preparation___ parameters/times___ calibration/system/viewing checks___ coverage___ interpretation/acceptance___ report/post-test___ approved by___.
P111 process: learner/specimen___ instrument/probe/consumable IDs___ actual procedure limits___ measured settings/time/light/temperature___ checks before/after___ coverage___ raw indications/coordinates___ interpretation___ criterion/disposition___ limitations___.
Q111 quality event: failed check/time___ last valid___ affected items___ containment/notification___ investigation___ retest authority/results___ revised reports___ retained originals___.
E111 experience/training: method/technique___ actual training hours___ actual industrial days/evidence separately___ vision record reference___ assessor___ practical specimens/techniques___ pending scope___.
A111 assessor: master-map ID/private location___ learner observations___ required/reportable matches___ missed/false calls___ score/evidence___ critical issue___ feedback___ changed assessment___ reviewer/date___.

Issue original VNDRLY/U NDT Method Training record with exact endorsed methods/techniques, actual practical versus simulation limits, identity, version/hash, assessor/date and pending items. Never label it ASNT9712 or imply radiation authorization. External scheme training/experience/vision/exams and employer job authorization remain separate. Materials completion is not a learner certification claim.

lessons.title: VUC111 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC111 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q111-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-01-L1

Does MT qualification establish UT competence?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Methods and techniques require distinct evidence. Revisit Q111-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-01-L2

ASNT9712 and employer-based ASNT NDT LevelII identical?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Their certification and practical responsibilities differ. Revisit Q111-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-02-L1

An indication is automatically a defect?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Interpretation and applicable acceptance evaluation are required. Revisit Q111-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-02-L2

PT detects a sealed subsurface pore?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Penetrant needs a surface opening. Revisit Q111-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-03-L1

Post-check fails afterE1–E6: onlyE6 affected?

**Answer:** Not established.

**Reason/remediation:** Investigate the interval since the last valid check. Revisit Q111-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-03-L2

Can an instruction omit criteria because operator is experienced?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Reproducibility and authorized acceptance are essential. Revisit Q111-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-04-L1

Overwashing penetrant can cause what?

**Answer:** Loss of penetrant from openings and missed indications.

**Reason/remediation:** Removal process must remain controlled. Revisit Q111-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-04-L2

Heavy background: report no flaws?

**Answer:** No; examination validity is impaired.

**Reason/remediation:** Reprocess under approved method. Revisit Q111-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-05-L1

Aluminum casting suitable forMT?

**Answer:** No ordinary ferromagnetic response.

**Reason/remediation:** Confirm material and choose an appropriate authorized method. Revisit Q111-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-05-L2

One field direction proves full orientation coverage?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Discontinuity/field orientation affects detection. Revisit Q111-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-06-L1

5900 m/s, 20 microseconds round trip: thickness?

**Answer:** 59.0 mm after valid delay correction.

**Reason/remediation:** Divide round-trip distance by two. Revisit Q111-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-06-L2

Backwall loss proves a crack?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Coupling, attenuation and geometry also cause it. Revisit Q111-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-07-L1

60-degree beam, 20 mm plate: first-leg path?

**Answer:** 40 mm, surface distance 34.64 mm.

**Reason/remediation:** Use cosine/tangent with verified angle. Revisit Q111-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-07-L2

Echo amplitude equals flaw height?

**Answer:** Not automatically.

**Reason/remediation:** Sizing and calibration require the approved technique. Revisit Q111-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-08-L1

F2, b 20, a 400 mm: unsharpness?

**Answer:** 0.10 mm.

**Reason/remediation:** Ug=Fb/a. Revisit Q111-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-08-L2

Suspected stuck source: approach to inspect?

**Answer:** No; withdraw/control access and notify authorized radiation safety personnel.

**Reason/remediation:** Training is not source-recovery authority. Revisit Q111-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-09-L1

Poor IQI/quality but no indication: accept part?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Invalid examination cannot support acceptance. Revisit Q111-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-09-L2

Can a processing artifact erase a separate relevant indication?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Classify and evaluate each with evidence. Revisit Q111-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-10-L1

0.20 mm/pixel, 15 pixels: size?

**Answer:** 3.0 mm only in calibrated geometry.

**Reason/remediation:** Out-of-plane perspective invalidates the scale. Revisit Q111-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-10-L2

Remote camera sees all surfaces?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Blind zones and resolution must be documented. Revisit Q111-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-11-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-11-L1

Three small rounded indications within 8 mm underA111?

**Answer:** Reject by grouping rule.

**Reason/remediation:** Individual size compliance does not waive grouping. Revisit Q111-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-11-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-11-L2

Exactly 3.0 mm linear underA111 size rule?

**Answer:** Meets that size limit, subject to other criteria and valid exam.

**Reason/remediation:** The rule says longer than 3.0 mm. Revisit Q111-11 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-12-L1
lessons.body:
## Q111-12-L1

Can training hours be recorded as industrial experience?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Evidence categories differ. Revisit Q111-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q111-12-L2
lessons.body:
## Q111-12-L2

Missing practical equipment: award fullmethod anyway?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Practical evidence remains pending. Revisit Q111-12 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: VUC111 sources, method scope and limits
lessons.body:
# VUC111 sources, method scope and limits

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original teaching and assessment materials. No ASNT exam reproduction or claim of external certification. User authorized best effort without inaccessible standards; actual applicable technique/acceptance documents remain required for delivery and work.

[ASNT9712 LevelII](https://certification.asnt.org/certification/asnt-9712-level-ii) identifies method/technique-specific general,specific,instruction-preparation and practical components. [Examination page](https://certification.asnt.org/certification/examinations/asnt-9712-level-ii) lists current/future method blueprints; our original cases are not those exams. VT availability is inconsistent across public pages: program says coming soon,while [ASNT overview](https://www.asnt.org/me/26/8/understanding-asnt-9712) includesVT. Verify external availability rather than promising it. [Comparison](https://www.asnt.org/certification) distinguishes ASNT9712 from employer-based certification. [ISO9712:2021 listing](https://www.iso.org/standard/75614.html?browse=ics) confirms personnel-qualification scope; full proprietary clauses not audited.

[ASNT PT overview](https://www.asnt.org/what-is-nondestructive-testing/methods/liquid-penetrant-testing) supports surface-opening method limits and removal-system distinctions. [ASNT MT overview](https://www.asnt.org/what-is-nondestructive-testing/methods/magnetic-particle-testing) supports ferromagnetic/surface-near-surface scope. [NASA MT overview](https://www.nasa.gov/centers-and-facilities/white-sands/magnetic-particle-testing/) provides independent primary method context. [NRC industrial radiography toolkit](https://www.nrc.gov/materials/miau/industrial-uses/rad-toolkit) supports separate radiation-safety qualification/authorization. [NRC safety manual listing](https://www.nrc.gov/regulations-legislation/nureg-series-publications/brochures-prepared-by-nrc-staff/br0024) is historical safety background,not a substitute for current license procedures. [ASNT renewal](https://certification.asnt.org/recertification/asnt-9712-level-ii) governs external continuing requirements; no automatic external renewal is conferred here.

|Domain|Materials/evidence|
|---|---|
|01|Method/scheme/technique/authority; P01|
|02|Manufacturing/service discontinuities and orientation; P02|
|03|Instruction/calibration/validity; W01/P03|
|04|PT systems/process/evaluation; W02/P04|
|05|MT yoke/bench/field/coverage; W03/P05|
|06|UT straight/product forms/calibration; W04/P06|
|07|UT angle/weld/geometry/evaluation; W05/P07|
|08|RT physics/geometry/radiation boundary; W06/P08|
|09|RT image quality/interpretation; W06/P09|
|10|VT direct/remote/measurement; W07/P10|
|11|Criteria/grouping/instruction/report; W08/P11|
|12|Quality/ethics/practical records/award; W08/P12|

Each domain has two explained formative questions and separate final/changed cases. All-track teaching plan 272 hours is original, not claimed equivalent to external minimums. Synthetic indication cards and fictionalA111 rules teach reasoning; actual blind specimens/images and qualified observers are required for learner practical evidence. No generic training certificate covers every method automatically.

lessons.title: VUC112 — Refrigerant Handling and Section 608 Preparation
lessons.body:
# VUC112 — Refrigerant Handling and Section 608 Preparation

Original VNDRLY/U core, TypeI, TypeII andTypeIII training. EPA certification requires an EPA-approved test; no EPA credential is issued here.

lessons.title: Q112-01 — Certification, law and scope
lessons.body:
## Q112-01 — Certification, law and scope

Section 608 technician certification is earned through an EPA-approved testing organization, not by completing an unaffiliated course. TypeI covers small appliances; TypeII covers high/very-high-pressure appliances except small appliances and MVACs; TypeIII covers low-pressure appliances; Universal requires all types with the required core examination. Section 609 motor-vehicle air-conditioning requirements are a separate path. Identify the appliance and task before selecting the credential. This original VNDRLY course prepares learners and assesses safe practice; it does not issue EPA certification.

The venting prohibition and recovery obligations are not limited to ozone-depleting refrigerants; determine the actual refrigerant and applicable exemptions rather than assuming an HFC is freely ventable. De minimis releases associated with good-faith recovery are not permission for intentional discharge. Do not use a recovery machine as a reason to ignore leaks, cylinder limits or safety. Apprentice work must follow applicable supervision requirements; a training record alone does not authorize independent service.

Worked decision: a technician has TypeI and is asked to open a large high-pressure chiller. The small-appliance credential is not enough. Arrange appropriately certified and authorized personnel. Preserve certification records and verify the certifying organization. EPA credentials do not replace employer safety training, equipment-specific competence or state/local licensing.

lessons.title: Q112-02 — Environmental effects and refrigerant identity
lessons.body:
## Q112-02 — Environmental effects and refrigerant identity

CFCs and HCFCs can deplete stratospheric ozone; many refrigerants also contribute to climate warming. Ozone-depletion potential and global-warming potential describe different effects. A refrigerant with no ozone-depletion potential can still have significant climate impact or other hazards. Regulatory phaseouts, phasedowns and equipment transition rules are distinct from whether an existing appliance may be safely serviced.

Read the appliance label and service history, then verify refrigerant identity when uncertain using an appropriate method. Blends can behave differently from single-component fluids; temperature glide and fractionation affect pressure-temperature interpretation and charging method. Follow the manufacturer and refrigerant instructions, including liquid charging where specified to preserve blend composition. Never mix unknown refrigerants into a clean recovery cylinder.

Recovery removes refrigerant and stores it externally; recycling cleans recovered refrigerant for appropriate reuse; reclamation processes it to the applicable purity specification through an authorized reclaimer. These are not synonyms. Worked case: recovered fluid from an unlabeled system is offered for another customer's appliance. Quarantine and identify it; do not treat filtering as proof of reclaimed purity or legal resale. Keep source, mass, container and disposition traceable.

lessons.title: Q112-03 — Refrigeration cycle and pressure interpretation
lessons.body:
## Q112-03 — Refrigeration cycle and pressure interpretation

A basic vapor-compression cycle moves heat using evaporation at lower pressure, compression, condensation at higher pressure and expansion. Identify compressor, suction/discharge, condenser, receiver where present, metering device and evaporator before connecting equipment. Refrigerant can remain dissolved in oil or trapped behind valves; an apparently empty segment may release more vapor after warming or equalization.

Gauge pressure is relative to local atmosphere; absolute pressure is referenced to vacuum. At a supplied atmosphere 14.7 psia, a reading 0 psig is 14.7 psia, not empty space. Vacuum readings in inchesHg relative to atmosphere differ from mmHg absolute and microns.25 mmHg absolute equals 25000 microns; it is a recovery endpoint for the specified low-pressure rule, not a universal dehydration target.

Use the correct refrigerant pressure-temperature data and distinguish saturated conditions from superheated vapor or subcooled liquid. Example with supplied saturation 40°F and suction-line 55°F gives 15°F superheat; supplied condensing 110°F and liquid 95°F gives 15°F subcooling. These calculations do not diagnose charge alone; airflow, load, metering and measurement placement matter. Never use a generic pressure as proof of identity or safe opening.

lessons.title: Q112-04 — Hazards, tools and cylinders
lessons.body:
## Q112-04 — Hazards, tools and cylinders

Refrigerants can displace oxygen, cause frostbite or pressure injury, and some are flammable or toxic. Heating or contact with flame can create dangerous decomposition products. Use ventilation, PPE, compatible equipment and ignition controls according to the refrigerant and task. Do not use oxygen or compressed air to pressure-test a refrigerant circuit. Dry nitrogen testing, when authorized, requires a regulator, relief protection and pressure limits from the manufacturer/procedure.

Use recovery equipment suitable for the refrigerant and certified where required. Inspect hoses, low-loss fittings, scales, gauges and cylinders. A disposable supply cylinder must not be refilled as a recovery vessel. Verify approved refillable cylinder identity, condition, test status, pressure rating, compatibility and allowable fill by the actual refrigerant/temperature/cylinder rules. A familiar 80% volume concept is not permission to guess mass from total cylinder weight.

Worked scale card: cylinder tare 18 lb and approved maximum gross 48 lb. Current gross 42 lb leaves 6 lb permitted mass capacity under that card. A planned 8 lb recovery needs another suitable cylinder or approved transfer plan before starting. Do not bypass overfill controls or heat a cylinder with a flame. Secure and label containers, protect valves, and follow transport requirements. Unknown contents remain segregated.

lessons.title: Q112-05 — Recovery setup and verification
lessons.body:
## Q112-05 — Recovery setup and verification

Plan recovery from appliance identity, charge, pressure class, equipment date/capability, service scope and required endpoint. Isolate only as allowed; establish a path that captures trapped refrigerant without creating a hydraulic or electrical hazard. Confirm recovery-machine, cylinder and hose compatibility and purge/manage connections according to approved instructions without unnecessary venting. Monitor mass, pressure and temperature throughout.

Liquid recovery may reduce time when equipment and appliance configuration permit it; vapor recovery completes remaining removal. Do not pull liquid into equipment not designed for it or run an appliance compressor under conditions that damage it. System-dependent equipment has limitations and relies on appliance pressure or compressor operation; it is not interchangeable with self-contained recovery. Follow the actual equipment instructions.

After reaching the applicable endpoint, allow the specified stabilization/check and investigate pressure rebound. Refrigerant dissolved in oil, trapped liquid or incomplete isolation can raise pressure again. A recovery endpoint does not prove a leak-free dry system ready for charging. Worked case: the gauge reaches the target while the cylinder approaches its approved maximum; stop at the cylinder limit, change safely and complete recovery. Neither the desired schedule nor a momentary gauge value waives either requirement.

lessons.title: Q112-06 — Type I small appliances
lessons.body:
## Q112-06 — Type I small appliances

A small appliance is not merely any device with a small-looking compressor. EPA's definition includes factory manufacture, charge and hermetic sealing with five pounds or less refrigerant. Confirm the actual definition and service/disposal task. For recovery equipment made before November 15, 1993, the small-appliance requirement is 80% recovery. For equipment made on/after that date, it is 90% with a functioning appliance compressor or 80% without one; an alternative is evacuation to 4 inchesHg vacuum under the rule.

Use actual equipment instructions to establish access and recovery from both sides when needed. A nonfunctioning compressor may trap refrigerant; pressure on one side does not prove the other is empty. Avoid permanent reliance on temporary piercing access devices where the service procedure requires proper repair. Do not energize an unsafe compressor just to use a different recovery percentage.

Worked arithmetic with a known 4 lb training charge: 90% is 3.6 lb; 80% is 3.2 lb. A mass estimate alone may be unreliable if original charge is unknown or refrigerant remains in oil; follow certified-equipment practice and permitted endpoint. Record method, equipment date, compressor condition and result. Disposal arrangements require the appropriate recovery/documentation responsibilities; a sticker claiming empty is not a substitute for the required evidence.

lessons.title: Q112-07 — Type II pressure categories and service endpoints
lessons.body:
## Q112-07 — Type II pressure categories and service endpoints

Determine pressure category from the regulatory definition and refrigerant/application, not a momentary gauge reading. The required evacuation table distinguishes recovery-equipment manufacture/import date and appliance charge. For equipment on/after November 15, 1993: very-high-pressure appliances require 0 inchesHg vacuum; high-pressure below 200 lb require 0, high-pressure 200 lb or more 10; medium-pressure below 200 lb 10, medium-pressure 200 lb or more 15. For earlier equipment: very-high and high below 200 require 0; high 200 or more 4; medium below/at-or-above 200 require 4. Values are inchesHg vacuum relative to the stated standard atmosphere; do not confuse them with absolute pressure.

The appliance full-charge category is not the amount recovered today. A300 lb appliance temporarily containing 50 lb does not become a below 200 lb category. An isolated component uses the rule's applicable treatment; verify exact conditions rather than inventing an exemption. Special nonmajor-repair or leaking-appliance provisions have defined conditions and cannot be invoked for convenience; consult the current rule and document applicability before using them.

Worked selection: a qualifying medium-pressure 150 lb appliance using modern recovery equipment requires 10 inchesHg vacuum under the normal table. A high-pressure 250 lb appliance using the same equipment also requires 10. A medium-pressure 250 lb appliance requires 15. Complete stabilization and safe isolation before opening. Service dehydration and leak testing follow the appliance procedure after repair; meeting recovery law is not the whole commissioning process.

lessons.title: Q112-08 — Type III low-pressure appliances
lessons.body:
## Q112-08 — Type III low-pressure appliances

Low-pressure systems can operate below atmospheric pressure, so leaks may admit air and moisture rather than visibly release refrigerant. Noncondensables can increase condensing pressure and reduce performance; moisture can cause corrosion or other damage. Purge systems must be operated/maintained to minimize refrigerant loss under the applicable requirements. Excessive purge activity is evidence to investigate, not a normal condition to ignore.

The normal low-pressure recovery endpoint is 25 mmHg absolute for both older and newer recovery equipment. Use an appropriate absolute-pressure instrument and understand its units. Do not read 25 inchesHg vacuum as the same endpoint. Follow chiller manufacturer procedures for water circulation, freeze prevention, pressure limits and refrigerant removal. Recovery can cool water and risk freezing tubes; arbitrary heating or pressurization is unsafe.

Worked case: a chiller reaches 25 mmHg absolute then rebounds. Investigate residual refrigerant/trapped regions and procedure-required stabilization rather than immediately opening. A pressure test must respect the actual appliance rating and approved method; never apply a memorized high-pressure-system test value to a low-pressure shell. Separate recovery, leak repair, evacuation/dehydration and charging steps. Confirm safe operating condition and records before return to service.

lessons.title: Q112-09 — Leak repair and the 2026 HFC rules
lessons.body:
## Q112-09 — Leak repair and the 2026 HFC rules

Keep legal regimes distinct. Long-standing Section 608 leak-repair requirements concern specified appliances with 50 lb or more ozone-depleting refrigerant. The AIM Act emissions-reduction/reclamation rules add requirements beginning 2026 for certain appliances with 15 lb or more containing HFCs or specified substitutes. Refrigerant composition, GWP, appliance category and exclusions matter. Do not assume the old 50 lb threshold is the only rule or that a proposed exemption is already effective.

Leak-rate calculations require full charge, amount added and the applicable calculation method. For a simple annualizing exercise, rate=(added/full charge)×(365/days since relevant addition)×100. With 10 lb added to 100 lb over 90 days, the result is 40.56%/year. This is not the same as saying 40.56 lb physically leaked that day. The actual rule controls first-use periods, exclusions, method consistency, thresholds and records.

When an applicable threshold is exceeded, follow the current rule's repair, verification, inspection, retrofit/retirement and reporting requirements. Do not merely top off and erase the event. Record discovery, full-charge basis, calculation, repair and verification. The owner/operator has duties that cannot be assumed fulfilled by the technician's invoice. Worked decision: a 20 lb HFC appliance is dismissed as below 50 lb. Reassess under the current AIM applicability rules; being outside one regime does not establish exemption from another.

For the reviewed EPA summaries, trigger rates are 30% for industrial process refrigeration, 20% for commercial refrigeration and 10% for comfort cooling/other covered categories. Normal repair timing is 30 days, with 120 days where the specified industrial shutdown condition applies; initial and follow-up verification are required. Under the 2026 AIM summary, residential/light-commercial AC and heat-pump subsector equipment and qualifying substitutes atGWP53 or below are excluded from that leak-repair provision; this does not erase venting/recovery duties. Extensions and retrofit/retirement routes require their actual conditions and records, not a verbal promise to repair later. Covered commercial/IPR appliances at 500 lb or more have quarterly post-trigger inspections; smaller covered commercial/IPR and covered comfort/other equipment have annual inspections under the stated rule conditions. Verify current applicability and reporting requirements before acting.

lessons.title: Q112-10 — Reclamation, disposal, records and final service decision
lessons.body:
## Q112-10 — Reclamation, disposal, records and final service decision

Maintain a refrigerant chain of custody: appliance/source, refrigerant identity, mass, cylinder ID, recovery date, technician, equipment and destination. Separate clean known refrigerant from contaminated or mixed material. Determine when reuse is permitted and when reclamation by an EPA-certified reclaimer is required; do not sell mixed recovered material as clean product. Record disposal/recovery responsibilities for the appliance category and retain required documentation.

Service closeout includes safe electrical/mechanical state, leak testing and repair evidence, manufacturer-required evacuation/charging, final operating checks and remaining restrictions. Never charge by guesswork or substitute a refrigerant without an approved retrofit basis and legal compatibility. For blends, use the specified charging method and correct composition. Document additions/removals accurately; scale tare and units matter.

A training completion record lists core and type-specific learning/assessment. EPA certification still requires the approved examination and certifying body; this course cannot print an EPA credential. Existing certification does not remove the need to learn changed refrigerants, flammability controls or regulations. Review current EPA pages and actual rules before delivery and before a compliance decision. Authoring completion means these original materials are prepared, not that a learner or business has satisfied legal certification or reporting duties.

---

content.title: VUC112 | VUC112 practical workbook and instructor guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC112 practical workbook and instructor guide
lessons.body: # VUC112 practical workbook and instructor guide

lessons.title: Delivery
lessons.body:
## Delivery

Original 40-hour course: 12 core instruction, 6 TypeI, 8 TypeII, 6 TypeIII, 4 integrated practice, 2 controlled final, 2 feedback/remediation. Practical work is embedded in type sessions; extend until safe independent performance. Entry: basic units/arithmetic, ability to read labels/procedures and follow stop instructions. Instructor must hold appropriate EPA certification and equipment/refrigerant competence; actual refrigerant work uses authorized facilities and supervision. Classroom rigs may use inert/nonrelease simulation, but actual learner practical scope must be recorded honestly.

Provide approved compatible recovery machine, refillable cylinders, calibrated scale, gauges/absolute vacuum instrument, low-loss fittings, known training appliance circuits, manufacturer procedures, ventilation/PPE, labels, SDS and current EPA reference pages. Flammable-refrigerant practice requires explicitly suitable equipment/facility/controls; never use an ordinary rig by assumption. No intentional refrigerant venting, no oxygen/air pressure testing, no live electrical bypass. Inert models may demonstrate connection logic before supervised real recovery. Missing equipment defers the practical endorsement.

Before each station, instructor verifies refrigerant identity, appliance class/full charge, equipment date/rating, maximum cylinder mass, endpoint and safe work limits. Learner checks independently. Actual manufacturer values govern physical work; numerical cards below are synthetic. Current regulation controls any exception or compliance decision.

### W112-01 — Core identity and pressure

Cards: factory-sealed 4 lb refrigerator; large 250 lb high-pressure appliance; low-pressure chiller; MVAC; unknown blend cylinder. Learner selects credential path, identifies unknown hold and distinguishes 608/609. Calculate at 14.7 psia atmosphere: 0 psig=14.7 psia;-5 psig=9.7 psia. Supplied saturation 40°F, line 55°F gives 15°F superheat; condensing 110°F, liquid 95°F gives 15°F subcooling. Explain why these do not alone determine charge or identity. Changed values 42/60°F give 18°F superheat. Instructor offers HFC venting shortcut; learner rejects unsupported release.

### W112-02 — Cylinder and recovery setup

Tare 18 lb, max gross 48, current gross 42, planned 8 lb recovery. Capacity 6 lb, shortfall 2 lb. Learner selects second suitable cylinder, checks ratings/contents and rehearses connections on isolated rig. Demonstrate low-loss connection, scale monitoring and safe changeover under actual procedure. Inject unknown refrigerant and damaged hose; stop/segregate/remove from service. Changed card max 50, current 44, planned 9 gives 6 available/3 shortfall. No generic 80% volume assumption replaces the supplied approved mass limit.

### W112-03 — TypeI

Known 4 lb training charge, modern equipment, functioning compressor: 3.6 lb at 90%; broken compressor: 3.2 lb at 80%. Pre 1993 equipment uses 80% branch. Alternative 4 inchesHg vacuum is selected only with appropriate procedure/equipment. Demonstrate approved access and recovery on small-appliance training rig, including trapped-side check and truthful compressor condition. Inject compressor failure midplan: do not energize unsafe equipment; revise method. Changed 4.5 lb gives 4.05/3.60 lb. Actual unknown charge requires appropriate verified method, not a fabricated starting mass.

### W112-04 — TypeII table and service

Using current official table, complete selection sheet: modern very-high 0; high 150 lb 0; high 250 lb 10; medium 150 lb 10; medium 250 lb 15 inchesHg vacuum. Older equipment: 0, 0, 4, 4, 4 respectively. Full charge determines row even if less remains. Demonstrate safe recovery setup/monitoring on suitable training rig; do not physically create every pressure class. Instructor injects endpoint rebound and cylinder limit: learner pauses safely, changes container if needed, and completes required recovery. Changed high 199 versus 200 lb tests boundary 0 versus 10 with modern equipment. Any exception requires actual applicable text and documented conditions, not instructor convenience.

### W112-05 — TypeIII

Use chiller schematic/inert rig plus authorized equipment demonstration. Identify air-ingress paths, purge significance, water/freeze controls and appropriate absolute-pressure instrument. Normal endpoint 25 mmHg absolute=25000 microns. Instructor supplies 25 inchesHg vacuum display; learner rejects unit substitution. Rebound requires procedure-based investigation. Demonstrate approved sequence and records; actual low-pressure practical work requires appropriate chiller/facility and supervisor. Do not claim live competence from schematic alone. Changed case adds frequent purge and moisture concern; learner requests leak investigation and manufacturer repair/dehydration process.

### W112-06 — Leak and complete service cases

CaseA: commercial 100 lb appliance, known covered refrigerant, 10 lb added after 90 days. Annualized 40.56% exceeds supplied 20% threshold. Learner documents applicable regime/full-charge basis, repair/verification obligations and owner handover. At 10 minutes manager requests invoice-only closure; at 20 unknown cylinder appears; at 30 repair verification fails. Expected no false closure, segregation and required follow-up. CaseB: 20 lb HFC commercial appliance in 2026, not an excluded subsector, 4 lb added after 120 days: 60.83% annualized. Learner rejects old 50 lb exemption assumption, uses current AIM applicability and documents required actions. Changed calculation 2 lb/100 lb/100 days=7.30%; below supplied threshold does not erase venting/recovery/record duties. Both cases include recovery record, cylinder balance and safe return-to-service conditions.

lessons.title: Observed dimensions
lessons.body:
## Observed dimensions

### P112-01 — Scope
Select credential/task/regime and approved external exam distinction. Review.
### P112-02 — Identity
Identify/segregate refrigerant and explain recovery/recycling/reclamation. Review.
### P112-03 — Cycle/units
Trace rig and use correct pressure/temperature units. Practical.
### P112-04 — Safety/cylinder
Inspect tools/container and calculate capacity before setup. Practical.
### P112-05 — Recovery
Demonstrate approved connection/monitoring/stabilization and stop response. Practical.
### P112-06 — TypeI
Perform supervised small-appliance method and records. Practical.
### P112-07 — TypeII
Select table row and demonstrate applicable safe rig recovery. Practical.
### P112-08 — TypeIII
Demonstrate suitable low-pressure procedure/instrument/freeze controls; record actual versus simulated evidence. Practical.
### P112-09 — Leak rules
Calculate rate and distinguish applicable 2026/ODS regimes and owner duties. Review.
### P112-10 — Closeout
Reconcile mass/disposition and issue traceable limited training record. Review.

lessons.title: Forms
lessons.body:
## Forms

S112 scope: appliance/refrigerant/identity evidence___ full charge/class___ task___ credential___ applicable rule/version___ exclusions verified___ owner responsibilities___.
R112 recovery: equipmentID/date/certification/compatibility___ cylinderID/tare/max gross/start/end___ hose/checks___ method/endpoint/units___ stabilization/rebound___ amount___ anomalies___ supervisor___.
L112 leak: full-charge basis___ addition/date/prior interval___ method/formula___ rate___ applicable threshold/regime___ discovery/repair deadline basis___ repair___ initial/follow-up verification___ inspection/report/plan duties___ owner acknowledgment___.
C112 custody: source/refrigerant___ cylinder/mass___ contamination___ reuse/recycle/reclaimer/disposal route___ recipient/date___ supporting records___.
A112 assessment: learner/version/station___ actual/simulated___ procedure/equipment___ independent/coached___ evidence/score___ critical error___ remediation___ changed result___ assessor/date___.

lessons.title: Completion and award
lessons.body:
## Completion and award

Ten dimensions 0–4: 0 unsafe/absent, 1 major help, 2 safe incomplete/prompted, 3 independent correct traceable, 4 anticipates/controls errors. Require 32/40, each at least 3, six practical/four review dimensions, both integrated cases satisfactory and no unresolved critical error. Record unperformed actual appliance work separately; simulation-only completion never claims field qualification. Critical errors: intentional unlawful venting, overfill, wrong incompatible equipment, oxygen/air test, unsafe compressor/electrical action, unit-based unsafe opening, fabricated refrigerant/certification records. Stop, remediate and reassess changed conditions.

Complete 20 explained checks and 6 labs. Controlled final 10 cases/30 decisions, 60 points, 120 minutes; pass 48, each at least 4/6, no critical error. Changed retake/keys private. Keep failed attempts and reviewer decisions. Original VNDRLY/U Refrigerant Handling Training record lists core/types covered, actual practical scope, identity, version/hash, assessor/date. EPA certification is only through an approved testing organization; this record is not an EPA card. Review regulatory/refrigerant changes before subsequent delivery. Materials creation is not learner certification.


---

lessons.title: VUC112 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC112 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q112-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-01-L1

VNDRLY completion issues EPA certification?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** An EPA-approved examination/certifying organization is required. Revisit Q112-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-01-L2

TypeI covers a large high-pressure chiller?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Match credential to appliance/task. Revisit Q112-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-02-L1

Recovery, recycling, reclamation identical?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Removal, cleaning and specification-level reclamation differ. Revisit Q112-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-02-L2

Unknown refrigerant into clean cylinder?

**Answer:** No; segregate/identify.

**Reason/remediation:** Mixing destroys traceability and can create hazards. Revisit Q112-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-03-L1

0 psig at 14.7 psia atmosphere means vacuum?

**Answer:** No; 14.7 psia absolute.

**Reason/remediation:** Gauge zero is atmospheric pressure. Revisit Q112-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-03-L2

55°F line, 40°F saturation: superheat?

**Answer:** 15°F.

**Reason/remediation:** Use actual refrigerant/measurement conditions. Revisit Q112-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-04-L1

Max gross 48, current 42: capacity?

**Answer:** 6 lb under supplied card.

**Reason/remediation:** Gross includes tare; do not infer universal fill mass. Revisit Q112-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-04-L2

Oxygen pressure test acceptable?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Use only approved compatible test medium and regulated limits. Revisit Q112-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-05-L1

Target reached then rebounds: open immediately?

**Answer:** No; investigate/stabilize per procedure.

**Reason/remediation:** Trapped/dissolved refrigerant may remain. Revisit Q112-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-05-L2

Cylinder limit reached before endpoint?

**Answer:** Stop/change safely and complete recovery.

**Reason/remediation:** Neither requirement waives the other. Revisit Q112-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-06-L1

4 lb, modern equipment, functioning compressor: 90%?

**Answer:** 3.6 lb.

**Reason/remediation:** TypeI recovery branch depends on equipment/date/condition. Revisit Q112-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-06-L2

Broken compressor: 80% of 4 lb?

**Answer:** 3.2 lb.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not energize unsafe compressor to change branch. Revisit Q112-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-07-L1

Modern medium-pressure 250 lb endpoint?

**Answer:** 15 inchesHg vacuum under normal table.

**Reason/remediation:** Full charge/category/date select row. Revisit Q112-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-07-L2

300 lb appliance now 50 lb becomes small-charge category?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Full charge remains governing input. Revisit Q112-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-08-L1

25 mmHg absolute equals microns?

**Answer:** 25000 microns.

**Reason/remediation:** Not 25 inchesHg vacuum or service dehydration target. Revisit Q112-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-08-L2

Frequent purge operation should be ignored?

**Answer:** No; investigate air ingress/system condition.

**Reason/remediation:** Low-pressure leaks may admit air/moisture. Revisit Q112-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-09-L1

10 lb/100 lb over 90 days annualized?

**Answer:** 40.56%/year.

**Reason/remediation:** Apply stated formula; actual regulatory method conditions govern. Revisit Q112-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-09-L2

20 lb HFC automatically outside leak rules?

**Answer:** No; assess 2026 AIM applicability/exclusions.

**Reason/remediation:** Old 50 lb ODS threshold is not the only regime. Revisit Q112-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q112-10-L1

Recovered fluid filtered means legally reclaimed?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** Required reclaimer/specification and reuse rules remain. Revisit Q112-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q112-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q112-10-L2

Training record equals independent service authority?

**Answer:** No.

**Reason/remediation:** EPA and employer/licensing requirements remain separate. Revisit Q112-10 and perform its changed application.
