lessons.title: VUC112 primary sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC112 primary sources and coverage

Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original teaching, examples and exams. No EPA-approved test status claimed.

[Certification requirements](https://www.epa.gov/section608/section-608-technician-certification-requirements) and [technician Q&A](https://www.epa.gov/section608/epas-refrigerant-management-program-questions-and-answers-section-608-certified):credential/task distinctions and external examination route. [Service practices](https://www.epa.gov/section608/stationary-refrigeration-service-practice-requirements):normal recovery table,small-appliance percentages and low-pressure endpoint. Exceptions require actual current rule conditions;none are invented. [ODS leak repair](https://www.epa.gov/section608/stationary-refrigeration-leak-repair-requirements):50 lb scope,category thresholds and repair/verification framework. [January2026 AIM fact sheet](https://www.epa.gov/system/files/documents/2026-01/er-r-fact-sheet-leak-repair-2026-01-13_1.pdf):new15 lb covered-appliance regime,exclusions and follow-up requirements. [AIM reporting](https://www.epa.gov/hfcs/reporting-resources-emissions-reduction-reclamation-rule):owner/operator reporting distinction. [Regulatory actions](https://www.epa.gov/hfcs/regulatory-actions-managing-hfc-use-and-reuse):proposals are not treated as effective exemptions. [Sales restrictions](https://www.epa.gov/section608/questions-and-answers-about-refrigerant-sales-restriction):certification/sale context.

Mapping: Q01 scope/P01/W01; Q02 identity/P02/W01; Q03 cycle/units/P03/W01; Q04 safety/cylinders/P04/W02; Q05 recovery/P05/W02; Q06TypeI/P06/W03; Q07TypeII/P07/W04; Q08TypeIII/P08/W05; Q09 leak rules/P09/W06; Q10 records/reclamation/P10/W06. Every domain has two explained checks and protected final/changed cases. Original 40-hour plan is not an EPA requirement. Actual equipment procedures, certification and applicable current rules govern field work.

lessons.title: VUC113 — Remote Pilot and Part 107 Preparation
lessons.body:
# VUC113 — Remote Pilot and Part 107 Preparation

Original VNDRLY/U ground instruction and supervised mission practice. FAA certification, recency and operational approvals remain separate.

lessons.title: Q113-01 — Remote pilot authority and certification
lessons.body:
## Q113-01 — Remote pilot authority and certification

The remote pilot in command is responsible for the operation and must be able to direct the aircraft safely. A business request, landowner permission or automated mission does not transfer that responsibility. Part 107 generally applies to civil small unmanned aircraft below 55 pounds including everything carried. Determine the actual operation and legal basis; recreational rules are not a shortcut for work flights. A remote pilot certificate and current aeronautical knowledge are separate from aircraft registration and any airspace authorization.

Initial certification uses the FAA's applicable knowledge-test/application pathway, with a separate qualifying Part 61 pathway. Minimum age is 16 and other eligibility requirements apply. Maintain required knowledge recency within 24 calendar months through the applicable FAA process. This original VNDRLY course does not issue an FAA certificate or replace FAA recurrent training.

Before accepting a mission, verify pilot documents, recency, aircraft registration/marking, Remote ID compliance, airspace/operational permissions and employer/site requirements. A person manipulating controls under direct supervision must be supervised as the rule requires; a remote phone call is not assumed sufficient. Worked decision: the client says an inspection is urgent but the pilot's recency is not current. Delay and restore eligibility or use a qualified current pilot; urgency is not an emergency exception.

lessons.title: Q113-02 — Operating limits, right of way and waivers
lessons.body:
## Q113-02 — Operating limits, right of way and waivers

Plan visual line of sight sufficient to know position, altitude, attitude, direction and hazards, using corrective lenses as permitted. A camera feed, telemetry or binoculars does not replace the required visual capability. A visual observer supports the crew but does not authorize an otherwise prohibited operation. Yield to crewed aircraft and never interfere with airport traffic. Maintain separation and land or reposition safely when needed.

Normal Part 107 limits include 100 mph/87 knots groundspeed, 400 feetAGL with the specified within 400-foot-radius/400-feet-above-structure allowance, 3 statute miles visibility from the control station, and cloud separation 500 feet below/2000 feet horizontally. These are legal limits, not recommended operating targets. Airspace authorization may impose a lower altitude. Do not interpret structure allowance as overriding controlled-airspace limits or other hazards.

Waivers authorize only specified deviations under their conditions. An airspace authorization is not a waiver for BVLOS or operations over people. Do not operate multiple aircraft simultaneously or from moving platforms except where the applicable rule/authorization permits. Hazardous material carriage and careless/reckless operation are not ordinary inspection options. Worked case: a tower permits a higher geometric envelope but the authorization caps 120 feetAGL. The authorization cap remains controlling; do not use the structure provision to exceed it.

lessons.title: Q113-03 — Airspace, charts and authorization
lessons.body:
## Q113-03 — Airspace, charts and authorization

Identify the site using current aeronautical information, not only a consumer map. Class B, C, D and the relevant surface Class E airspace require prior authorization forPart 107 operations; ClassG does not require that specific authorization but other restrictions still apply. Read sectional symbols, airspace floors/ceilings, airport information, obstacles and terrain. Chart altitudes may be MSL while operational limits are AGL; convert using the actual local elevation.

A chart shelf labelled 40/20 represents 4000/2000 feetMSL under the supplied chart convention. At ground elevation 1500 feetMSL, a proposed 300 feetAGL flight is 1800 feetMSL, below that shelf floor at that point; this alone does not clear other airspace or restrictions. Verify boundaries, terrain changes and current chart legend. UAS facility-map grid values support authorization planning; they are not permission by themselves. Use LAANC or FAA's applicable process and comply with time, area, altitude and conditions.

Check TFRs, NOTAMs, special-use airspace, security restrictions and site-specific constraints before and during the operation as appropriate. A geofence unlock is notFAA authorization; an app's green display is not a complete briefing. Worked decision: yesterday's authorization does not cover today's time window. Obtain valid permission or change the mission lawfully; do not backdate the flight log.

lessons.title: Q113-04 — Weather products and local judgment
lessons.body:
## Q113-04 — Weather products and local judgment

Obtain current aviation weather and assess the actual site. METARs report observations; TAFs forecast conditions at specified locations/times. Decode wind direction/speed/gusts, visibility, weather, cloud layers, temperature/dew point and altimeter setting. Reports may not describe a sheltered industrial site or wind at flight altitude. Compare observation time and trend, not just an icon.

Synthetic METAR: KZZZ 181755Z 18012G20KT 3SM BKN008 18/17 A2992. It indicates 18 th day 1755UTC, wind 180 degrees 12 knots gust 20, visibility 3 statute miles, broken layer 800 feet above station, temperature 18°C/dewpoint 17°C and altimeter 29.92 inchesHg. KZZZ is fictional. At a same-elevation site, 500-foot-below-cloud separation would cap flight at 300 feetAGL under that cloud, subject to all other restrictions. Meeting 3-mile visibility exactly leaves little margin.

Thunderstorms, gust fronts, icing, fog, precipitation and turbulence can exceed aircraft/pilot capability. Buildings and terrain create mechanical turbulence. Higher density altitude can reduce lift/performance; heat and cold affect batteries. Use aircraft limits and conservative mission margins. Worked decision: surface wind 12 knots is below a 15-knot limit but gust 20 exceeds it. No-go under that supplied limit. Do not average gusts away.

lessons.title: Q113-05 — Loading, performance and energy
lessons.body:
## Q113-05 — Loading, performance and energy

Confirm total takeoff mass, center of gravity, payload security and aerodynamic effects. A camera or propeller guard can change endurance, handling and category eligibility. Manufacturer limits are necessary but not a complete risk assessment. Check propellers, motors, structure, battery health, firmware/configuration and environmental compatibility. Do not install an unapproved payload merely because it fits.

Plan energy for launch, mission, return, contingency and landing reserve. In an original example, usable mission budget 18 minutes minus 3 outbound, 4 return and 3 reserve leaves 8 minutes for inspection. Wind may make return slower than outbound; tailwind outbound can hide a difficult headwind return. Time estimates are not a guarantee of battery performance. Use actual state/temperature/load trends and early abort triggers.

For a 1000 m return at 5 m/s ground speed, time is 200 seconds or 3.33 minutes. At 2 m/s it becomes 500 seconds or 8.33 minutes. A battery plan based only on still-air speed can fail badly. Do not deliberately exhaust a battery to validate a model. Land before limits with a suitable contingency area. Record battery condition and anomalies after flight; swelling, damage or abnormal heating requires removal from use and approved handling.

lessons.title: Q113-06 — Crew resource management and fitness
lessons.body:
## Q113-06 — Crew resource management and fitness

Define remote PIC, control manipulator, visual observer and site coordinator roles. Brief flight area, altitudes, people/vehicle controls, weather, airspace conditions, communications, emergencies and authority to call an abort. Use clear concise calls and closed-loop acknowledgment. Observers must know what to watch and how to communicate immediately; they are not spectators.

Assess illness, medication, stress, alcohol, fatigue and emotion before flying. Apply applicable alcohol/drug rules and do not fly impaired even if a minimum time interval has elapsed. Distraction, client pressure and fixation on the screen can undermine see-and-avoid. Share workload without dilutingPIC responsibility. A crew member must be able to challenge unsafe continuation.

Worked brief: the observer calls 'helicopter approaching from west, low.' PIC acknowledges, maintains awareness and executes the prebriefed safe descent/landing or separation action. Do not continue the camera task until the aircraft disappears behind equipment. Record the interruption and reassess before relaunch. If communications with the observer fail, follow the planned safe response rather than assuming silence means clear airspace.

lessons.title: Q113-07 — Preflight, control links and automation
lessons.body:
## Q113-07 — Preflight, control links and automation

Inspect aircraft condition, secure attachments, battery, propellers, controls and navigation sensors. Verify registration/Remote ID state, home point, altitude reference, return-to-home settings and geofence behavior. Check command/control link, telemetry and expected loss-link actions. A software update can change settings; do not discover that during an urgent job. Understand limitations of GNSS, compass and obstacle sensors near steel structures, power lines and reflective surfaces.

Plan launch/recovery and emergency landing areas clear of people and hazards. Confirm airspace/weather/permissions immediately before flight. Test controls safely and establish visual orientation. Automatic return-to-home may climb into an authorization ceiling or obstruction if configured poorly. Set a lawful safe strategy based on the actual site; automation is not an independent pilot.

Worked example: authorization ceiling 150 feetAGL, return-to-home configured 250 feet. Correct the plan/settings before launch and verify obstacle clearance within authorized limits; do not simply reduce altitude if that would create a collision route. If no lawful safe return path exists, change the mission or do not fly. Record preflight discrepancies and their resolution.

lessons.title: Q113-08 — Night, people, vehicles and Remote ID
lessons.body:
## Q113-08 — Night, people, vehicles and Remote ID

Night operation underPart 107 requires the applicable updated knowledge/training and anti-collision lighting visible for at least 3 statute miles with sufficient flash rate, unless an applicable authorization permits otherwise. Lighting does not replace visual line of sight, weather or airspace permission. Dark adaptation, visual illusions, obstacle visibility and depth judgment require additional planning. Do not extinguish required lighting for a better photograph.

Operations over nonparticipants require the applicable rule pathway, category-compliant aircraft and operating conditions or a valid waiver. Category 1 requires 0.55 pounds or less including attachments and no exposed rotating parts that would lacerate; open-air assemblies have additional Remote ID conditions. Categories 2/3 use required eligibility/compliance and operating restrictions; Category 4 uses an airworthiness-certificated aircraft and approved limits. A low mass alone does not prove every condition met. Moving-vehicle operations have additional restrictions; do not assume a brief transit or road closure automatically authorizes it.

Remote ID compliance can involve a standard Remote ID aircraft, a broadcast module under its restrictions, or operation within an authorized FRIA under the applicable conditions. Verify actual eligibility and operating state; registration alone is not Remote ID. If requiredRemote ID fails, follow the applicable rule and safe termination requirements. Worked case: a 249 g aircraft gains a 20 g accessory and exposed blades remain. Do not claim Category 1 eligibility from its original marketed weight.

lessons.title: Q113-09 — Emergency response and reporting
lessons.body:
## Q113-09 — Emergency response and reporting

Prepare for loss link, GNSS/compass anomalies, flyaway, low battery, propulsion failure, unexpected people, crewed traffic and weather deterioration. Define actions appropriate to the aircraft and site, including safe landing areas and emergency contacts. Do not chase a malfunction into traffic or a hazardous industrial area. Protect people first and avoid creating a second emergency.

The remote PIC may deviate fromPart 107 to the extent necessary for an in-flight emergency requiring immediate action; this is not advance permission to plan an illegal flight. Preserve facts, logs and settings after an event. DetermineFAA and NTSB reporting duties separately and follow employer/site reporting. UnderPart 107, the FAA reporting rule includes serious injury/loss of consciousness or qualifying damage to property other than the small unmanned aircraft, and a 10-calendar-day deadline; apply the actual rule's damage valuation conditions. Do not invent a damage amount to avoid reporting.

Worked scenario: link loss begins while a vehicle enters the landing area. Execute the preplanned safe contingency and communicate with the site coordinator; do not rely blindly on an automatic landing zone now occupied. After landing, quarantine the aircraft if necessary, document the sequence and investigate before return to service. An apparently undamaged aircraft can still have a latent fault.

lessons.title: Q113-10 — Field inspection mission and data ethics
lessons.body:
## Q113-10 — Field inspection mission and data ethics

Plan the inspection objective and required image quality without allowing the camera task to override flight safety. Identify hazardous equipment, vents, flares, cranes, helipads, power lines, traffic and protected information. Obtain lawful site access and coordinate operations; landowner permission does not replace airspace authorization. Avoid flight paths whose failure trajectory threatens workers or critical equipment.

Use a mission sheet with route, altitude, visual coverage, people controls, weather limits, energy, emergency areas and abort triggers. Record what was actually inspected and any gaps. A photograph does not by itself establish structural integrity; refer technical interpretation to qualified personnel. Protect personal/confidential data and retain only authorized records. Do not use zoom to claim visual-line-of-sight compliance when the aircraft cannot be adequately seen.

Worked closeout: wind increases before the final tower face is photographed. Abort safely and report that face as not inspected. Reusing an old image without its date creates false evidence. The original VNDRLY training award records learning and observed practice; FAA certification, recency, aircraft compliance and mission permissions remain separate. No course-completion claim authorizes a real flight without those requirements.

lessons.title: Flight-knowledge application supplement (Q113-03/04/06/09)
lessons.body:
## Flight-knowledge application supplement (Q113-03/04/06/09)

Airport awareness begins with runway orientation, traffic pattern and approach/departure paths. Runway 18 is approximately magnetic south; 36 is the reciprocal north direction. These numbers are not assurances of active runway use. Check current airport information and traffic. Helicopters may use paths different from fixed-wing patterns. Stay clear; do not orbit an approach path because the airport is uncontrolled. A common traffic advisory frequency supports situational awareness but a radio call does not grant airspace permission. Learn standard phonetic words and unambiguous position reports; listen before transmitting, identify who you are addressing and your position/intention, and follow authorization-specific communications. Never impersonate ATC or transmit clearance instructions. In the exercise, an observer says 'traffic west' without distance or direction of travel: request clarification while taking the safe prebriefed response, rather than assuming a conflict-free route.

Read chart obstacle elevations carefully: top elevation above MSL and height above ground are different quantities. Terrain changes can alter AGL along a constant-MSL flight. A 2,400-foot MSL aircraft above 2,100-foot ground is 300 feet AGL; above 1,900-foot ground it is 500 feet AGL. A local compass/GNSS indication may be degraded near steel or electromagnetic interference. Do not fly by a single unverified sensor. A stable air mass can support haze and poor visibility; unstable air can produce turbulence and rapidly growing clouds. A small temperature/dewpoint spread suggests possible saturation if cooling occurs, not a guaranteed forecast. TAF change groups describe forecast time periods, not current observations; compare the valid period and use current observations/site conditions. Pressure altitude and temperature influence density altitude and performance; use the aircraft's performance information rather than applying a crewed-aircraft formula blindly to a multirotor.

The safety-event rule distinguishes damage to the aircraft itself from other property. For the property trigger, the repair cost includes labor and materials; the stated exception is cost not exceeding $500, or fair market value not exceeding $500 for total loss. Injury/loss-of-consciousness triggers are independent. Preserve estimates and use the current rule when evaluating an actual event. The rule's ten-calendar-day reporting period is not permission to delay emergency assistance.


---

courses.title: VUC113 | VUC113 workbook and instructor delivery

content.title: VUC113 | VUC113 workbook and instructor delivery
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC113 workbook and instructor delivery
lessons.body: # VUC113 workbook and instructor delivery

lessons.title: Program definition
lessons.body:
## Program definition
Audience: prospective commercial inspection remote pilots and field coordinators. Entry: English aviation vocabulary/numeracy support, ability to read charts, safe participation; legal pilot eligibility is separately verified. Outcomes: plan a lawful mission, interpret airspace/weather, calculate energy, configure contingencies, coordinate a crew and produce an honest closeout. Forty planned instructional hours: 10 teaching, 6 weather/chart workshops, 8 equipment/crew stations, 10 mission simulations, 4 assessment, 2 remediation. These are original course hours, not an FAA requirement. Use current FAA rules, current charts and aircraft instructions. Instructor must be competent in Part 107 and the selected equipment; any real operation requires a qualified current remote PIC and lawful operating conditions.

lessons.title: Equipment and safe delivery
lessons.body:
## Equipment and safe delivery
Supply current chart legend and a local chart for instructor demonstration, the fictional chart/weather cards below, calculator, aircraft manual, inert aircraft with batteries disconnected for physical inspection, simulator, sample registration/authorization/maintenance records and mission/log forms. Do not energize propellers in class. Simulate emergencies; do not induce flyaway, low battery or collision risk. Ground simulations do not count as observed flight skill. If actual supervised practice is included, log separately the aircraft, site, weather, authorization, PIC, learner actions and observed outcome. This course is not an FAA practical test or approved certificate issuer.

### W113-1 — Chart and altitude desk
Card A: fictional Class C shelf 40/20; ground 1,500 MSL, target 300 AGL, adjacent terrain 1,300 MSL; grid says 100 and no authorization exists. Compute 1,800 MSL at launch and 500 AGL over lower terrain if altitude remains constant. Mark the shelf relationship only; identify missing permissions, current TFR/NOTAM review and route hazards. Do not turn a synthetic chart into real navigation. Card B: 50/25 shelf, ground 2,100 MSL, target 300 AGL; result 2,400 MSL below floor at that point, still not general permission. Learner draws launch, route, boundary, obstacles and emergency landing on blank gridded paper, with north arrow, units and a legend.

### W113-2 — Weather briefing
Card A: KZZZ 181755Z 18012G20KT 3SM BKN008 18/17 A2992. Site elevation equals station; wind limit 15 knots, authorization 120 AGL. Decode each element, identify 300 AGL cloud limit and lower 120 authorization, and reject gusts. Card B: wind 8 gust 12, visibility 5 SM, BKN012, same site/limits. Identify improved margins but require current complete briefing; this is not automatic dispatch. Instructor injects a gust front and demands a reassessment. Retain the observation time and limitations.

### W113-3 — Energy and payload
Budget 18 minutes, outbound 3, return 4, reserve 3: 8 inspection minutes. A 1,000 m route at 5 m/s takes 3.33 minutes, at 2 m/s 8.33. Recompute rather than spending the reserve. Weigh an inert payload/aircraft assembly or use 249 g plus 20 g card: 269 g. Record mass, center-of-gravity/manual compatibility and category limitations. Do not infer safe lift from a scale alone.

### W113-4 — Preflight discrepancy board
Cards: cracked propeller; RTH 250 feet versus 150 authorization; home point at yesterday's site; required Remote ID not functioning; healthy aircraft but occupied emergency landing area. Learner identifies all five holds, explains corrective verification and refuses an unsafe launch. Reset simulated home point/RTH on a training interface, then explain obstacle/ceiling conflicts. Instructor changes one setting after a simulated update; learner must recheck.

### W113-5 — Crew and emergencies
Roles: PIC, observer, site coordinator. Script: minute 0 brief; minute 2 camera request beyond VLOS; minute 4 low helicopter west; minute 6 observer radio fails; minute 8 landing area occupied. Learner gives closed-loop calls, rejects VLOS shortcut and executes simulated safe responses. Observer actor responds only when specifically addressed. Debrief fixation, handoff and authority to abort. No actual hazardous flight is performed.

### W113-6 — People, night and evidence
Prepare a daytime inspection plan and a night variant. Supplied aircraft 240 g plus 25 g light with exposed blades; do not claim Category 1. Show lawful separation or an actually applicable approved pathway. Record required night/Remote ID checks without inventing eligibility. Inspect six supplied text-image cards: four current dated tank faces, one blank, one last-month image. Report four current faces and two coverage limitations; never silently substitute.

lessons.title: Observed assessment stations
lessons.body:
## Observed assessment stations
For each station score planning, execution/decision, evidence and explanation 0–2 each: 0 absent/unsafe, 1 safe but incomplete, 2 correct independently. Pass at least 7/8 each, no critical error, and all stations. Simulator and bench labels stay on the record.

### P113-01 — Eligibility review
Using fictitious pilot/aircraft documents, detect stale recency, distinguish registration and certificate, record release hold.
### P113-02 — Operating envelope
Apply authorization cap and structure rule, maintain simulated VLOS and yield to traffic.
### P113-03 — Chart desk
Compute MSL/AGL and shelf relationship, identify authorization and restriction checks using W113-1.
### P113-04 — Weather desk
Decode W113-2 and issue a reasoned no-go/go-conditional briefing with margins.
### P113-05 — Energy desk
Calculate W113-3, preserve reserve and assess payload eligibility.
### P113-06 — Crew briefing
Assign roles and respond to helicopter/communication injects with closed-loop acknowledgment.
### P113-07 — Inert preflight
Inspect equipment and settings; identify all five W113-4 discrepancies and verification steps.
### P113-08 — Night/people review
Reject unsupported Category 1 claim; identify independent night/Remote ID conditions.
### P113-09 — Emergency/reporting
Respond to occupied landing area and injury scenario; distinguish emergency help, FAA and NTSB duties.
### P113-10 — Mission closeout
Produce coverage report from W113-6 with gaps, dates and interpretation boundaries.

lessons.title: Integrated mission A — Tower inspection
lessons.body:
## Integrated mission A — Tower inspection
Fictional tower 300 feet; authorization cap 120 AGL; wind 12 gust 20 versus 15 limit; client requests 200 feet; battery budget 18 with 3/4/3 commitments; observer available; no people control established. Deliver map, authorization check, weather/energy worksheet, crew brief and dispatch decision. Expected no-go for weather, requested altitude and uncontrolled exposure; 8 minutes budget does not cure them. At inject 1 wind improves to 8 gust 12 and area is secured: reassess all conditions and keep 120 cap. At inject 2 helicopter arrives: yield and terminate/reassess safely.

lessons.title: Integrated mission B — Night revisit
lessons.body:
## Integrated mission B — Night revisit
Aircraft 240 g plus 25 g light, exposed blades; required Remote ID fault; RTH 250 versus 150 authorization; two missing images from prior job. Identify independent holds, propose a lawful corrected plan, simulate loss-link response and produce honest partial closeout. Passing requires all holds addressed or explicit no-go, no fabricated image and no claimed FAA award. Instructor varies one datum on retake rather than repeating a memorized plan.

lessons.title: Reusable forms
lessons.body:
## Reusable forms
Mission ID___ PIC/certificate/recency verified___ aircraft/registration/Remote ID___ objective___ date/time___ chart/restriction sources and times___ authorization ID/area/time/ceiling___ terrain/obstacles___ weather/limits___ mass/configuration___ route/VLOS___ energy/reserve___ people/vehicles___ crew calls___ landing/contingencies___ go/no-go/reason___ signatures___.
Preflight item___ observed condition___ defect___ hold___ correction___ independent recheck___ release decision___.
Flight/simulation log: mode___ start/end___ actual route/height___ energy___ deviations___ event time___ response___ inspection coverage/gaps___ data retention___ reporting evaluation___ assessor___.
Assessment record: station___ four scores__/2 each___ critical issue___ evidence file___ remediation___ changed retest___ assessor/date___.

lessons.title: Instruction, remediation and award rules
lessons.body:
## Instruction, remediation and award rules
Teach the worked example before practice, then use changed data and require reasoning. Provide chart/English support without giving assessment answers. Twenty explained checks are formative. Controlled final and changed retake are private: 10 cases, 30 decisions, 60 points, 48 pass and at least 4/6 each domain, no unresolved critical error; 120 minutes. Practical all ten stations and both integrated cases must pass; written success cannot waive them. Critical failures include knowingly unauthorized flight, ignoring crewed traffic, unsafe energized demonstration, fabricated records or claiming FAA certification from this award. Stop the assessment safely, reteach the failed domain and reassess with changed conditions. Preserve original failure and retest separately.
Award only an original VNDRLY/U Remote Pilot Preparation training certificate identifying assessment mode, version, date and instructor. FAA initial/recurrent processes, actual pilot authority and mission permissions remain external. No automatic expiry equivalence or assurance of FAA exam success is claimed. Instructor reviews rule/chart/aircraft changes before each delivery; changes trigger targeted refresher and reassessment as needed. Retain learner evidence privately; never place final keys in learner distribution.


---

content.title: VUC113 | VUC113 formative checks
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC113 formative checks
lessons.body:
# VUC113 formative checks

Attempt before reading the explanation. Correct errors and revisit the matching chapter/station. These are not the controlled final.

lessons.title: Q113-01-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-01-L1

A client offers landowner permission but the pilot lacks current knowledge recency. May the inspection proceed?

**Answer:** No. Establish a qualified current remote pilot and all operational permissions first.

**Reason/remediation:** Land access is different from FAA pilot eligibility. Revisit Q113-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-01-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-01-L2

Does this course issue a remote pilot certificate?

**Answer:** No; complete the applicable FAA certification pathway.

**Reason/remediation:** An original training award cannot substitute for the federal credential. Revisit Q113-01 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-02-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-02-L1

A structure would allow a geometric altitude of 500 feet, but authorization caps 120 feet AGL. Which controls?

**Answer:** 120 feet AGL, with a safe plan within all other limits.

**Reason/remediation:** The structure provision does not cancel authorization conditions. Revisit Q113-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-02-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-02-L2

Can a camera screen alone establish visual line of sight?

**Answer:** No. Maintain the required direct visual capability.

**Reason/remediation:** Telemetry does not provide adequate see-and-avoid by itself. Revisit Q113-02 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-03-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-03-L1

Ground elevation is 1,500 feet MSL and flight is 300 feet AGL. What is flight MSL?

**Answer:** 1,800 feet MSL.

**Reason/remediation:** Add local ground elevation; check all airspace layers and restrictions separately. Revisit Q113-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-03-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-03-L2

A facility map cell says 100. Is that flight permission?

**Answer:** No. Obtain required authorization and follow its actual conditions.

**Reason/remediation:** A planning grid is not an issued approval. Revisit Q113-03 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-04-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-04-L1

A same-elevation cloud base is 800 feet above station. What altitude meets 500 feet below cloud?

**Answer:** At most 300 feet AGL, subject to lower limits and safe margins.

**Reason/remediation:** 800 minus 500 is 300; terrain differences change the calculation. Revisit Q113-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-04-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-04-L2

Wind is 12 gusting 20 knots and aircraft limit is 15. Go?

**Answer:** No under that supplied limit.

**Reason/remediation:** Gusts exceed the limit; average speed is insufficient. Revisit Q113-04 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-05-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-05-L1

An 18-minute budget requires 3 outbound, 4 return and 3 reserve. Mission time?

**Answer:** 8 minutes.

**Reason/remediation:** Subtract all committed time, then monitor actual performance. Revisit Q113-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-05-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-05-L2

A 1,000 m return slows from 5 to 2 m/s. What changes?

**Answer:** Return grows from 3.33 to 8.33 minutes.

**Reason/remediation:** Distance divided by groundspeed, then divide seconds by 60. Revisit Q113-05 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-06-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-06-L1

Observer reports low helicopter traffic during photography. Priority?

**Answer:** Yield and execute the safe separation/landing response.

**Reason/remediation:** Camera objectives never outrank crewed-aircraft safety. Revisit Q113-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-06-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-06-L2

May a fatigued pilot fly just because the legal minimum rest/alcohol interval is met?

**Answer:** No if impaired or unable to operate safely.

**Reason/remediation:** Fitness is a real-time condition, not just a clock test. Revisit Q113-06 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-07-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-07-L1

RTH is 250 feet and authorization ceiling is 150. Can you launch and fix it later?

**Answer:** No. Establish and verify a safe lawful contingency before launch.

**Reason/remediation:** An automatic climb can violate permission or collide with obstacles. Revisit Q113-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-07-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-07-L2

Does obstacle sensing eliminate the need to inspect the route?

**Answer:** No. Sensors have limitations including thin wires and reflective surfaces.

**Reason/remediation:** Automation is an aid, not independent hazard clearance. Revisit Q113-07 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-08-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-08-L1

A 249 g drone gains 20 g of attachments. Can original advertised mass prove Category 1?

**Answer:** No; total is 269 g and all category conditions must be checked.

**Reason/remediation:** Attachments count; rotor injury protection also matters. Revisit Q113-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-08-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-08-L2

Is anti-collision lighting alone enough for night operation?

**Answer:** No. Training/knowledge, visibility, airspace and all other applicable conditions still apply.

**Reason/remediation:** One satisfied requirement does not authorize the whole operation. Revisit Q113-08 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-09-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-09-L1

A link-loss landing area becomes occupied. What governs?

**Answer:** Protect people using the planned safe contingency and communicate immediately.

**Reason/remediation:** Do not blindly execute automation into a changed hazard. Revisit Q113-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-09-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-09-L2

Does a site incident report replace FAA/NTSB reporting?

**Answer:** No. Evaluate each applicable reporting duty independently.

**Reason/remediation:** Different authorities have different triggers and deadlines. Revisit Q113-09 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-10-L1
lessons.body:
## Q113-10-L1

The final tower face was not inspected because of wind. What belongs in the report?

**Answer:** A clear uninspected-area limitation and reason.

**Reason/remediation:** An old image must not be presented as current evidence. Revisit Q113-10 and perform its changed application.

lessons.title: Q113-10-L2
lessons.body:
## Q113-10-L2

Does a clear photograph prove structural integrity?

**Answer:** No. Qualified technical interpretation and appropriate inspection methods are separate.

**Reason/remediation:** Image collection and engineering acceptance are different functions. Revisit Q113-10 and perform its changed application.


---

content.title: VUC113 | VUC113 sources and coverage

lessons.title: VUC113 sources and coverage
lessons.body:
# VUC113 sources and coverage
Reviewed 2026-11-18. Original instruction and synthetic scenarios; not FAA-issued training or a reproduction of an official exam.

| Primary source | Coverage and limit |
|---|---|
| [FAA pilot certification](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/become_a_drone_pilot) | Q01 eligibility and recency; current FAA process controls actual application. |
| [FAA commercial operations](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators) | Q01–03 operation framework; general summaries are not a substitute for specific current rules. |
| [14 CFR 107.51 official 2025 text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title14-vol2/pdf/CFR-2025-title14-vol2-sec107-51.pdf) | Q02 speed/altitude/weather limits. |
| [FAA airspace authorizations](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/part_107_airspace_authorizations) | Q03 authorization versus planning grids. |
| [FAA chart guide, January 2026](https://aeronav.faa.gov/user_guide/cug-complete_20260122.pdf) | Q03 chart interpretation; synthetic exercise is not a navigational chart. |
| [FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide](https://www.faa.gov/sites/faa.gov/files/regulations_policies/handbooks_manuals/aviation/remote_pilot_study_guide.pdf) | Weather, performance, radio, airport and decision-making foundations. Historical guide: old night/people restrictions must not override current specific rules. |
| [FAA AC107-2A](https://www.faa.gov/documentLibrary/media/Advisory_Circular/AC_107-2A.pdf) | Q05–09 operational explanation; advisory material does not replace regulation. |
| [FAA operations over people](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/operations_over_people) | Q08 category and night framework; verify exact aircraft eligibility and operating conditions. |
| [FAA Remote ID](https://www.faa.gov/uas/getting_started/remote_id) | Q07–08 identification pathways and constraints. |
| [FAA waivers](https://www.faa.gov/uas/commercial_operators/part_107_waivers) | Q02/08 exceptions require their own issued conditions. |
| [14 CFR107.9 official text](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/CFR-2025-title14-vol2/pdf/CFR-2025-title14-vol2-sec107-9.pdf) | Q09 reporting trigger, property exception and supervision/condition provisions on same page. |

Each Q01–10 maps to two formative checks, one final case, one changed case and its P113 station. W1 supports Q02/03; W2 Q04; W3 Q05/08; W4 Q01/07; W5 Q02/06/09; W6 Q08/10. Both integrated missions combine legal, weather, energy, crew and evidence decisions. Final answer keys remain private.

Available-source scope: full original ground-preparation and supervised/simulated mission curriculum, not a claim to reproduce every FAA exam item or provide aircraft-specific flight qualification. Real missions require current regulations, charts, permissions and equipment instructions. Night/people guidance is taken from specific current FAA pages, not outdated restrictions in the historical study guide. Proprietary aircraft performance tables are supplied by the actual operator, not invented.

lessons.title: VUC114 — Merchant Mariner Credential Preparation and Entry-Level Shipboard Readiness
lessons.body:
# VUC114 — Merchant Mariner Credential Preparation and Entry-Level Shipboard Readiness

Original VNDRLY/U instruction. USCG issuance, approved STCW training and advanced endorsement qualifications remain separate.

lessons.title: Q114-01 — Credential architecture and selecting a lawful role
lessons.body:
## Q114-01 — Credential architecture and selecting a lawful role

An MMC is a Coast Guard credential carrying specific endorsements, not a universal license to perform every shipboard job. National endorsements and STCW endorsements serve different regulatory purposes. A medical certificate and a TWIC are separate documents. A valid card in one category does not cure a missing endorsement, expired medical authority or employer familiarization. Begin with the actual vessel, route, tonnage, propulsion, position and duties; then choose the current NMC checklist for that exact capacity.

Entry-level roles include Ordinary Seafarer, Wiper and Steward's Department, with Food Handler identified separately. Older records may use Ordinary Seaman; preserve the document's wording and check the current terminology. Qualified ratings, tank-vessel responsibilities and officer positions require their own evidence and evaluations. An entry-level endorsement does not authorize independent navigation, engineering watch responsibility or cargo-transfer person-in-charge duties.

Worked example: a new hire holds Wiper but the dispatch sheet says independent engine-room watch. The correct response is to hold that assignment and have the operator verify required qualified rating/STCW and safe manning. Do not relabel the job as cleaning while expecting watch duties. This course teaches credential preparation and common entry-level shipboard readiness; it does not award an MMC or substitute for every advanced endorsement curriculum. Build an individual progression plan naming the exact next endorsement rather than promising a generic master-mariner qualification.

lessons.title: Q114-02 — Application package, identity and truthful declarations
lessons.body:
## Q114-02 — Application package, identity and truthful declarations

Use the current NMC application route and forms. CG-719B identifies the requested transaction and endorsements. Supporting forms and evidence depend on the checklist: conviction disclosure where applicable, sea service where required, drug-testing evidence, identity/citizenship and TWIC or an applicable documented exemption. Do not add fictional sea time to an entry-level application that does not require it. Sign only truthful statements and check names, dates and requested capacities across documents.

The current NMC page directs most MMC submissions through its ASAP portal, with special handling for First Class Pilot and Local Limited applicants. Medical submissions are separate; the MMC portal warns that medical applications sent there will not be processed. Older PDFs still describe REC-email workflows. Follow the current official route for the actual transaction rather than a stale checklist's mailing paragraph. Retain the submission receipt, complete package and request-for-information history securely.

Worked review: CG-719B requests Wiper, the cover sheet requests Master, the fee receipt is for another person and one page is unsigned. Stop submission, resolve the intended endorsement and identity mismatch, obtain the applicant's actual signature and reconcile the fee. An administrator must not sign the applicant's declarations or guess an answer. A complete packet is ready for evaluation, not automatically approved.

lessons.title: Q114-03 — Medical fitness, drug evidence and privacy
lessons.body:
## Q114-03 — Medical fitness, drug evidence and privacy

Medical fitness is evaluated through the Coast Guard process, not by the course instructor. Use the appropriate current CG-719K or entry-level CG-719K/E route and qualified medical practitioner. Check the issued certificate's applicable dates and restrictions. National and STCW validity can differ; maximum periods are not a personal guarantee. An applicant under 18 may have a shorter STCW medical period. An otherwise unexpired MMC does not make expired medical authority valid for the intended service.

For transactions requiring drug evidence, use a currently accepted NMC option. An approved test, qualifying random-program letter or qualifying pre-employment letter has specific timing, laboratory/MRO and content conditions. A generic employer drug screen is not necessarily acceptable. The current test pathway uses a 185-day application window and DOT-compliant evidence. Do not change collection dates, omit a refusal or treat a negative-dilute result as a routine accepted negative.

Worked example: medical certificate shows national validity through a later date but STCW validity already expired; the assignment is on a vessel to which STCW applies. Refer the person for correct renewal/evaluation and hold affected service. Store health and drug records in restricted channels, not the general crew chat. The supervisor normally needs fitness/restriction status, not unnecessary clinical details. If health changes affect safe duty, report through the applicable process rather than relying only on the printed expiry.

lessons.title: Q114-04 — Sea-service evidence and arithmetic
lessons.body:
## Q114-04 — Sea-service evidence and arithmetic

Sea service records describe actual service in an assigned vessel position. Passenger days and guessed dates are not interchangeable with qualifying service. Record vessel identity, tonnage, propulsion/power when relevant, waters/routes, capacity, dates, hours and authorized attestation. Use CG-719S where appropriate or an acceptable letter containing required information. Keep originals/copies because future endorsements may use the same history while imposing their own recency and type-of-service requirements.

NMC guidance describes the usual day as eight hours of watchstanding/day work, excluding overtime. The under-100-GRT provision can recognize an appropriate day of at least four hours under its conditions; it is not a universal four-hour rule. Time-and-a-half credit depends on an authorized and practiced two-watch arrangement and supporting evidence, not simply working twelve hours. The Coast Guard makes the credit determination. Do not double count simultaneous dates or turn transit as a passenger into deck service.

Synthetic review: 24 documented eight-hour duty days plus 6 passenger days gives 24 candidate service days, not 30. If 20 separate days are documented under an actually qualifying 1.5-credit arrangement, the arithmetic is 30 credited days, subject to evaluation. Ten ordinary overtime days remain ten under the base assumption. A spreadsheet must retain raw days and the claimed rule separately so an evaluator can audit the result. Missing signatures or vessel details are unresolved evidence, not zero-risk clerical issues.

lessons.title: Q114-05 — STCW, approved training and competence boundaries
lessons.body:
## Q114-05 — STCW, approved training and competence boundaries

Determine whether STCW applies to the intended service and which endorsement/competence standards are required. Basic Training includes personal survival, fire prevention/firefighting, elementary first aid, and personal safety/social responsibilities. Security awareness, designated security duties, survival craft, watch ratings and advanced functions are distinct requirements where applicable. Attendance at a general online safety course does not establish completion of approved practical components.

Check the exact provider/course approval and what it satisfies, the certificate identity/date, assessment evidence and applicable continued-competence route. Renewal or revalidation requirements are not identical to original qualification. Maintain a gap matrix: requirement, accepted evidence, issuing authority, currency, missing action and owner. This course's mock exercises prepare the learner; they are not Coast Guard-approved STCW assessments and must never be signed as such.

Worked case: a worker has a VNDRLY orientation certificate and an expired training record but is scheduled as a designated security-duty crew member. Do not mark the gap closed because both documents mention security. Verify the exact endorsement/training requirement and arrange approved training/evidence. Include respectful workplace and prevention/reporting of violence, bullying and harassment in readiness. Verify current flag-state implementation for formal PSSR requirements rather than assuming another country's transition policy applies to a US credential.

lessons.title: Q114-06 — Vessel familiarization, alarms and personal survival
lessons.body:
## Q114-06 — Vessel familiarization, alarms and personal survival

Before duty, locate assigned muster station, alarm meanings, escape routes, lifejacket/immersion equipment, emergency communications and immediate supervisor. Read the vessel's station bill and emergency instructions; alarm signals and duties must be learned on the actual vessel. Find alternate routes because fire, flooding or cargo can block the usual path. Report missing or damaged lifesaving equipment immediately.

Practice inspecting and donning an appropriate lifejacket on dry land using its instructions: check condition, correct size, straps/closures, attachments and fit, then explain safe use. Do not jump into water, deploy survival craft or activate distress devices in an uncontrolled class. Real survival/boat-launch drills need qualified instructors, approved arrangements and safety controls. In a person-overboard event, raise the alarm, point continuously and follow the vessel's recovery plan; do not create another casualty by jumping in unassigned.

Worked case: the primary muster route is smoke-filled. Do not enter it to preserve attendance. Use the designated safe alternate, report your location and account for others using verified information. A missing-person report is not permission for untrained enclosed-space or smoke rescue. Prepare for cold stress and exposure using the vessel's equipment/instructions; never treat a classroom certificate as proof of water-survival performance.

lessons.title: Q114-07 — Deck seamanship and stored-energy hazards
lessons.body:
## Q114-07 — Deck seamanship and stored-energy hazards

A line can move suddenly under tension, and the whole working area can be dangerous when its path changes or it parts. Keep out of bights, pinch points and potential recoil paths; painted zones alone do not define every hazard. Never straddle a loaded line, wrap it around a hand or place a foot in a coil. Maintain clear communication with the person directing the operation and know the stop signal. Use task-appropriate PPE and footing, and keep escape paths clear.

For a training rope with no load, inspect abrasion, cuts, contamination and fittings, coil safely, and practice a bowline and clove hitch under instructor observation. A bowline forms a fixed loop when properly tied/dressed for the intended benign practice; it is not authorization for personnel lifting or every load. A clove hitch can slip or need additional securing depending on use. Actual mooring/rigging follows approved equipment limits and vessel procedures. Do not improvise knots to substitute for certified lifting attachments.

Worked scene: a crew member steps inside a slack bight as the winch operator prepares to heave. Call stop, prevent tensioning and clear personnel before a new brief. Slack now does not mean safe when load is applied. Mooring plans, weather, vessel movement and coordinated commands determine the safe sequence. Do not demonstrate powered winch recovery in an unguarded classroom.

lessons.title: Q114-08 — Lookout, communications and watch handover
lessons.body:
## Q114-08 — Lookout, communications and watch handover

A lookout observes and listens continuously, reports promptly and avoids distractions. State relative direction/bearing, object type, approximate range/trend and uncertainty. A steady bearing with decreasing range indicates collision risk requiring immediate report; it is not an instruction for an entry-level lookout to independently maneuver. The responsible officer applies the navigation rules and vessel procedures using all available information. Maintain lookout even when electronic equipment is operating.

Use closed-loop communications: receive the instruction, repeat it accurately, carry out only authorized actions and report completion or inability. Ask when uncertain. Distinguish routine calls, urgent safety information and distress; do not transmit false distress or practice on live emergency channels. In simulation, identify the vessel/station, nature and location of the problem, people at risk and assistance needed. Use the vessel's actual emergency radio procedure during operations.

Handover includes position/duty, hazards, equipment defects, traffic, work permits, communications and pending actions. Do not leave a watch until properly relieved under the vessel's procedure, and do not accept a duty beyond your endorsement/training. Worked exercise: target remains 030 degrees relative while range falls from 2.0 to 1.5 nautical miles. Report constant bearing/decreasing range promptly; do not assume radar or the officer has already noticed. Fatigue or impairment in a relief must be raised before the handover is treated as complete.

lessons.title: Q114-09 — Engine-space work, isolation and fire prevention
lessons.body:
## Q114-09 — Engine-space work, isolation and fire prevention

Engine spaces combine heat, noise, moving machinery, pressure, electricity, fuels and poor escape conditions. Entry-level assistance does not authorize opening energized equipment or operating unfamiliar valves. Identify the responsible engineer, boundaries, communications and emergency exits. Report leaks, abnormal smells, vibration, temperature and alarms promptly without touching hazardous equipment to investigate.

Before maintenance, the vessel's isolation/permit procedure must control electrical, mechanical, pressure, thermal and stored energy. A stopped motor can restart; a closed valve can leak; a gauge at zero may not prove every space safe. Only trained authorized personnel isolate and verify. The entry-level worker must recognize a missing isolation and stop, not perform a test beyond competence. Enclosed spaces require the applicable entry/rescue arrangements; never enter to retrieve a coworker without authorization and safeguards.

Worked case: an oil mist leak is near a hot surface and a supervisor asks the Wiper to tighten a fitting while machinery runs. Withdraw to safety, alert the engineer and stop the unsafe task. Do not turn a small leak into an injection/burn/fire casualty. Housekeeping reduces ignition and slip hazards, but cleaning must not bypass guards or mix incompatible chemicals. For fire, raise alarm and follow assigned duties; extinguisher use is limited to trained, safe conditions with an escape route, not a duty to fight an escalating fire.

lessons.title: Q114-10 — Pollution prevention, cargo boundaries and security
lessons.body:
## Q114-10 — Pollution prevention, cargo boundaries and security

Keep oils, chemicals and waste out of the water through the vessel's approved containment, segregation and disposal procedures. Identify drains and spill pathways before work. A small leak can spread quickly; report promptly and use only authorized safe containment actions. Do not wash a spill overboard, falsify an oil record or bypass pollution-control equipment. Cargo transfer requires competent authorized personnel, communications, checks and emergency shutdown arrangements; entry-level familiarity is not a tank-vessel PIC endorsement.

Security duties depend on the vessel's plan and assigned role. Verify access through established channels, protect keys/credentials and report suspicious activity without unsafe confrontation. Do not disclose restricted security details in public training records. A badge is not proof of authorization for every space. Cyber precautions include protecting accounts, checking unexpected attachments and reporting compromised devices; never connect unknown media to control systems.

Worked scenario: an unfamiliar contractor asks an entry-level worker to open a restricted machinery space and later to sign the transfer checklist. Verify the request with the responsible officer and decline an unsupported signature. If a spill is seen, alert the designated response chain with location/material if known, exposure and safe containment status. Do not guess a substance from color or enter vapor to identify it.

lessons.title: Q114-11 — Fatigue, respectful work and incident records
lessons.body:
## Q114-11 — Fatigue, respectful work and incident records

Shipboard work depends on reliable rest, clear roles and a crew able to report danger. Record actual work/rest and follow the applicable vessel/flag requirements; never rewrite hours to make a schedule appear compliant. A person can be fatigued despite a compliant-looking record. Raise fitness concerns early and arrange safe relief. Medication, illness, alcohol or other impairment must be handled through the appropriate medical/supervisory process.

Violence, harassment, bullying and sexual misconduct are safety and welfare issues. Seek immediate safety, support the affected person, use the designated reporting routes and preserve relevant facts without gossip, retaliation or promises of absolute confidentiality. Do not require the victim to confront the alleged offender. Instructors must offer a private alternative to sensitive role-play and avoid recreating abuse. Formal reporting/legal duties are governed by current policy and law; this course does not replace them.

Incident notes should distinguish observation, reported information and inference: time, location, people, event, immediate action and unresolved questions. Worked example: you hear a bang and then see a person on deck. Record that sequence, not an invented fall from a ladder. Protect records against alteration and share only with authorized recipients. A near miss deserves learning and corrective action even when no injury occurred.

lessons.title: Q114-12 — Renewal, progression and joining-vessel release
lessons.body:
## Q114-12 — Renewal, progression and joining-vessel release

Maintain a personal credential matrix listing each endorsement, medical scope/date, TWIC status, training/competence currency, limitations and employer familiarization. Review upcoming expirations before accepting a voyage, not at the gangway. Renewal, raise of grade, increase of scope, replacement and continuity are different transactions. A document of continuity is not authority to sail; do not treat a pending application as an issued credential.

Progression begins with the desired job and current checklist, then verified service, training, assessments and examinations where required. Keep raw evidence and identify gaps honestly. Do not purchase a course solely because its title resembles an endorsement; verify current approval and exact credit. Fees and processing routes change, so use official current information and keep receipts. The Coast Guard evaluates the application and may request more evidence or deny it; course completion cannot guarantee approval.

Worked joining review: the MMC is current, national medical date is current, STCW medical date is expired and the voyage requires STCW. Hold affected joining duties until valid authority is restored; do not erase the earlier date. On release, confirm actual role, vessel familiarization and emergency assignments. VNDRLY's award documents training and assessed readiness only. It must list the scope and observed methods and must never use a Coast Guard seal or claim to be an MMC.

---

content.title: VUC114 | VUC114 practical workbook and delivery guide
content.description: Course completion records study only. Certification also requires the separately controlled examination and applicable observed assessments specified in the program. This VNDRLY/U curriculum counterpart does not award, replace, or claim accreditation by the external credential issuer.

lessons.title: VUC114 practical workbook and delivery guide
lessons.body: # VUC114 practical workbook and delivery guide

lessons.title: Audience, outcomes and schedule
lessons.body:
## Audience, outcomes and schedule
For prospective entry-level mariners and coordinators preparing an MMC packet. This complete original preparation course teaches credential selection, document integrity and common shipboard readiness. It is not every officer/rating specialty, an approved STCW course or an MMC issuer. Prerequisites: basic literacy/numeracy, ability to participate safely with accommodations; actual eligibility/medical decisions remain with the competent authority. Outcomes: produce a truthful gap-checked packet, interpret role limits, evaluate service records, demonstrate safe dry-land routines and report emergencies accurately.
Forty-eight planned hours: 12 teaching, 8 document workshops, 10 dry-land stations, 8 scenarios, 6 assessment, 4 coached remediation. Original course hours, not statutory sea service or approved-course credit. Instructor needs relevant maritime operational/credential competence; use qualified safety instructors for equipment demonstrations. No live vessel navigation, loaded mooring, water entry, fire, enclosed-space entry or energized machinery is authorized by classroom exercises.

lessons.title: Instructor kit and fictional records
lessons.body:
## Instructor kit and fictional records
Supply current NMC forms/checklists and blank specimen copies, calculator, vessel diagram, unpowered training rope, inspected dry-land lifejacket, mock radio and station bill. Use synthetic identity only; no real health/drug documents in group work. Model vessel M114 is fictional: 80 GRT, coastal service, deck/engine/steward spaces, primary muster aft and alternate forward through port passage. Port passage is normally clear; starboard passage is blocked in inject. Alarm meanings/duties come from the instructor-supplied fictional station bill and are not universal signals.

### W114-1 — Role and application desk
Applicant Alex Example, adult, requests Ordinary Seafarer. Packet cards: signed identity page matching Alex; unsigned declaration; cover sheet says Master; another person's payment receipt; training attendance certificate claiming 'MMC issued'; current checklist copy. Identify five corrections/verification tasks: signature, intended role, payment, false award claim and exact checklist completeness. Prepare a gap sheet and a truthful draft; do not submit any real application or fabricate missing evidence. Changed packet requests Wiper and includes medical forms in MMC-only channel: identify the current separate route.

### W114-2 — Medical/drug evidence desk
Card A: national medical valid to 2028-06-01, STCW date 2026-06-01; joining 2026-11-20 on STCW-applicable service. Card B: generic employer negative screen, no DOT/MRO details. Card C: valid applicable medical with 'restriction requires review' marker, no invented diagnosis. Learner identifies A as not sufficient for STCW duty, B as unverified and C as requiring authorized role compatibility review. Record status without displaying clinical details. A test aged 190 days exceeds a supplied 185-day pathway by 5; a 180-day test still requires all other evidence conditions.

### W114-3 — Service reconciliation
Dataset A: 24 distinct eight-hour deck duty dates, 6 passenger dates, 10 ordinary overtime duty dates, no overlap. Candidate base total 34, not 40 or 39. Dataset B: 20 distinct qualifying two-watch dates with verified basis for 1.5 credit and 5 ordinary days: arithmetic 35. Instructor removes authorization evidence: learner withdraws the multiplier claim pending evaluation. Dataset C: two letters both claim the same 4 dates; identify overlap and preserve raw evidence rather than summing twice. Every dataset needs vessel/capacity/route/attestation fields and final NMC evaluation caveat.

### W114-4 — Familiarization and lifejacket
Draw M114 muster routes, exits and reporting points. Fit/inspect/don a dry-land lifejacket using its instructions; instructor checks fit and closures. Inject smoke on normal route and missing coworker. Learner uses safe alternate, reports last-known facts and does not enter smoke or tank. Role-play person-overboard alarm/pointing without water entry. No approved survival-craft competence is awarded from this station.

### W114-5 — Rope and hazard layout
Place unloaded rope on floor with marked winch/bollard/escape. Learner identifies bight, pinch and potential recoil paths, removes themselves and calls stop before any simulated heaving. Inspect a labeled damaged rope sample and quarantine it. Instructor demonstrates bowline/clove hitch slowly; learner ties, dresses and explains limitations. All rope remains unloaded; no personnel lifting. Critical error is stepping into the bight after the heave warning or claiming practice knots qualify lifting.

### W114-6 — Lookout and handover
Cards at minute 0: target 030 relative, 2.0 NM; minute 2: 030, 1.5 NM; minute 3: fog signal direction uncertain; minute 4: relief appears impaired. Learner reports constant bearing/decreasing range, sound uncertainty and fitness concern, maintaining duty until safe relief. Role-play mock radio: identify vessel, location, event, people at risk and needed assistance; no live transmission. Handover must include traffic, equipment defect, pending permit and communications.

### W114-7 — Engine/pollution desk
Five cards: stopped motor without isolation; oil leak near hot surface; pressure gauge zero but trapped section not assessed; person collapsed in tank; spill near drain. For each, state immediate safe action, authorized escalation and prohibited shortcut. Correct responses never use unprotected rescue, live fitting adjustment or overboard washdown. Record factual observations and safe containment status.

### W114-8 — Joining and progression
Assemble a role-specific gap matrix from all prior cards. Add a pending renewal, mismatched issued limitation and a security-duty assignment without matching evidence. Produce joining hold/release decision and a progression plan naming actual missing evidence and responsible owner. A completed classroom packet is not a credential. Respectful-work inject: a supervisor demands altered rest times and silence about harassment. Preserve facts, safe support and proper reporting.

lessons.title: Twelve observed stations
lessons.body:
## Twelve observed stations
Each station: four criteria (preparation, action/decision, evidence, explanation), 0 absent/unsafe, 1 safe incomplete, 2 independently correct. Pass at least 7/8 each and no critical errors. Eight desk/simulation reviews and four practical demonstrations are recorded separately; practical demonstrations are lifejacket, safe rope handling/knots, communication and handover.
### P114-01 — Role selection
Match actual endorsement to assigned duties using W1; hold unsupported specialist roles.
### P114-02 — Packet integrity
Find and correct W1 defects through authorized evidence, current route and true signatures.
### P114-03 — Fitness/privacy
Evaluate W2 date/scope mismatch and restricted record handling.
### P114-04 — Service audit
Compute W3 totals, identify overlap and unsupported multiplier.
### P114-05 — Training gap review
Separate approved BT/security/advanced evidence from original course attendance.
### P114-06 — Lifejacket/muster practical
Inspect/don using instructions and show alternate route on mock layout.
### P114-07 — Rope practical
Inspect, coil, tie unloaded practice knots and avoid bight/recoil hazards.
### P114-08 — Communications practical
Give clear closed-loop traffic/emergency reports in mock-radio exercise.
### P114-09 — Engine hazard review
Identify energy/entry/fire holds and proper authority without unsafe intervention.
### P114-10 — Pollution/security review
Handle W7 spill and W8 restricted-role requests correctly.
### P114-11 — Handover practical
Perform a complete handover with fatigue concern and factual incident note.
### P114-12 — Joining review
Issue a justified hold/release-with-scope decision from exact documents.

lessons.title: Integrated case A — First coastal joining
lessons.body:
## Integrated case A — First coastal joining
Alex holds an entry-level deck endorsement. Dispatch requests tank PIC, medical STCW date is expired, drug record lacks MRO detail, packet has 24 duty plus 6 passenger days, muster familiarization not done. Produce credential matrix, service calculation, gap/owner schedule and joining decision. Expected: 24 candidate days, no unsupported PIC assignment or medical clearance, verify drug pathway and complete actual familiarization. At inject, PIC request is removed but medical gap remains: do not release merely because one issue closed.

lessons.title: Integrated case B — Onboard near miss
lessons.body:
## Integrated case B — Onboard near miss
M114 prepares to moor; worker enters bight, frayed line noted, oil leak observed near engine hot surface, relief looks impaired. Supervisor requests clean records. Learner calls stop, raises hazards, maintains role limits, arranges safe relief and records facts. Then a revised credential arrives with a route limitation inconsistent with the next voyage. Correct closeout retains operational corrective actions and a separate credential hold. Both cases require every critical hazard/gap addressed; a persuasive narrative cannot compensate for an unsafe decision.

lessons.title: Forms
lessons.body:
## Forms
Credential matrix: person ID___ intended vessel/route/role___ actual endorsement___ limitation___ medical scope/date___ TWIC status___ training/assessment evidence___ current checklist/date___ gap___ owner___ release authority___.
Service row: vessel___ GRT/power___ route___ capacity___ dates___ hours___ raw days___ overlap check___ claimed credit/rule___ attestor___ missing evidence___ evaluator outcome___.
Familiarization: station bill version___ alarms___ primary/alternate muster___ lifejacket___ exits___ supervisor___ communications___ emergency role___ defects___ learner demonstration___ instructor___.
Handover: duty/time___ hazards/traffic___ machinery/permit state___ pending actions___ relief fitness___ acknowledgment___ unresolved issue___.
Incident: time/location___ direct observation___ reported information/source___ immediate action___ persons informed___ evidence preserved___ correction/addendum___.
Assessment: station___ four scores___ critical issue___ evidence/mode___ remediation___ changed retest___ assessor/date___.

lessons.title: Assessment and credential rules
lessons.body:
## Assessment and credential rules
Twenty-four explained checks support learning; final Form A and changed Form B are restricted instructor materials. Twelve cases, 36 decisions, 72 points; pass 58/72 plus at least 4/6 each domain, no critical error; 150 minutes, calculator/coursebook permitted but no keys or collaboration. All twelve stations and both cases must pass. Unsafe rescue, loaded-line exposure, falsification, unauthorized duty or false USCG/STCW award claims are critical: stop, remediate and reassess with changed evidence. Preserve failed and retest records.
Award VNDRLY/U Merchant Mariner Credential Preparation and Entry-Level Readiness only, naming version, assessment mode/date/instructor and limits. Never an MMC, STCW endorsement, sea-service day, medical clearance or advanced-rating qualification. Instructor reviews current NMC routes/checklists before delivery and identifies changed requirements. Learner renewal/progression remains linked to actual issued records. No automatic equivalence/renewal claim.


---
